an1.1:0.2.verse: The Chapter on What Occupies the Mind

an1.1:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

an1.1:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

an1.1:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single sight that occupies a man’s mind like the sight of a woman.

an1.1:2.2.verse: The sight of a woman occupies a man’s mind.”

an1.2:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single sound that occupies a man’s mind like the sound of a woman.

an1.2:1.2.verse: The sound of a woman occupies a man’s mind.”

an1.3:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single smell that occupies a man’s mind like the smell of a woman.

an1.3:1.2.verse: The smell of a woman occupies a man’s mind.”

an1.4:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single taste that occupies a man’s mind like the taste of a woman.

an1.4:1.2.verse: The taste of a woman occupies a man’s mind.”

an1.5:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single touch that occupies a man’s mind like the touch of a woman.

an1.5:1.2.verse: The touch of a woman occupies a man’s mind.”

an1.6:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single sight that occupies a woman’s mind like the sight of a man.

an1.6:1.2.verse: The sight of a man occupies a woman’s mind.”

an1.7:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single sound that occupies a woman’s mind like the sound of a man.

an1.7:1.2.verse: The sound of a man occupies a woman’s mind.”

an1.8:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single smell that occupies a woman’s mind like the smell of a man.

an1.8:1.2.verse: The smell of a man occupies a woman’s mind.”

an1.9:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single taste that occupies a woman’s mind like the taste of a man.

an1.9:1.2.verse: The taste of a man occupies a woman’s mind.”

an1.10:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single touch that occupies a woman’s mind like the touch of a man.

an1.10:1.2.verse: The touch of a man occupies a woman’s mind.”

an1.11:0.2.verse: The Chapter on Giving Up the Hindrances

an1.11:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to sensual desire, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow like the feature of beauty.

an1.11:1.2.verse: When you apply the mind irrationally to the feature of beauty, sensual desire arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.”

an1.12:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to ill will, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow like the feature of aversion.

an1.12:1.2.verse: When you apply the mind irrationally to the feature of aversion, ill will arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.”

an1.13:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to dullness and drowsiness, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow like discontent, sloth, yawning, sleepiness after eating, and mental sluggishness.

an1.13:1.2.verse: When you have a sluggish mind, dullness and drowsiness arise, and once arisen they increase and grow.”

an1.14:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to restlessness and remorse, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow like an unsettled mind.

an1.14:1.2.verse: When your mind is unsettled, restlessness and remorse arise, and once arisen they increase and grow.”

an1.15:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to doubt, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow like irrational application of mind.

an1.15:1.2.verse: When you apply the mind irrationally, doubt arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.”

an1.16:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents sensual desire from arising, or, when it has arisen, gives it up like the feature of ugliness.

an1.16:1.2.verse: When you apply the mind rationally to the feature of ugliness, sensual desire does not arise, or, if it has already arisen, it’s given up.”

an1.17:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents ill will from arising, or, when it has arisen, gives it up like the heart’s release by love.

an1.17:1.2.verse: When you apply the mind rationally to the heart’s release by love, ill will does not arise, or, if it has already arisen, it’s given up.”

an1.18:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents dullness and drowsiness from arising, or, when they have arisen, gives them up like the elements of initiative, persistence, and vigor.

an1.18:1.2.verse: When you’re energetic, dullness and drowsiness do not arise, or, if they’ve already arisen, they’re given up.”

an1.19:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents restlessness and remorse from arising, or, when they have arisen, gives them up like a settled mind.

an1.19:1.2.verse: When the mind is settled, restlessness and remorse do not arise, or, if they’ve already arisen, they’re given up.”

an1.20:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents doubt from arising, or, when it has arisen, gives it up like rational application of mind.

an1.20:1.2.verse: When you apply the mind rationally, doubt does not arise, or, if it’s already arisen, it’s given up.”

an1.21:1.1.verse: “I don’t envision a single thing that, when undeveloped, is as unpliant as the mind.

an1.21:1.2.verse: The mind, when undeveloped, is unpliant.”

an1.22:1.1.verse: “I don’t envision a single thing that, when developed, is as pliant as the mind.

an1.22:1.2.verse: The mind, when developed, is pliant.”

an1.23:1.1.verse: “I don’t envision a single thing that, when undeveloped, leads to such great harm as the mind.

an1.23:1.2.verse: The mind, when undeveloped, leads to great harm.”

an1.24:1.1.verse: “I don’t envision a single thing that, when developed, leads to such great benefit as the mind.

an1.24:1.2.verse: The mind, when developed, leads to great benefit.”

an1.25:1.1.verse: “I don’t envision a single thing that, when undeveloped & unapparent, leads to such great harm as the mind.

an1.25:1.2.verse: The mind, when undeveloped & unapparent, leads to great harm.”

an1.26:1.1.verse: “I don’t envision a single thing that, when developed & apparent, leads to such great benefit as the mind.

an1.26:1.2.verse: The mind, when developed & apparent, leads to great benefit.”

an1.27:1.1.verse: “I don’t envision a single thing that, when undeveloped & uncultivated, leads to such great harm as the mind.

an1.27:1.2.verse: The mind, when undeveloped & uncultivated, leads to great harm.”

an1.28:1.1.verse: “I don’t envision a single thing that, when developed & cultivated, leads to such great benefit as the mind.

an1.28:1.2.verse: The mind, when developed & cultivated, leads to great benefit.”

an1.29:1.1.verse: “I don’t envision a single thing that, when undeveloped & uncultivated, brings about such suffering & stress as the mind.

an1.29:1.2.verse: The mind, when undeveloped & uncultivated, brings about suffering & stress.”

an1.30:1.1.verse: “I don’t envision a single thing that, when developed & cultivated, brings about such happiness as the mind.

an1.30:1.2.verse: The mind, when developed & cultivated, brings about happiness.”

an1.21:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so unworkable as this mind that is not developed.

an1.22:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so workable as this mind that is developed

an1.23:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not developed.

an1.23:1.2.verse: An undeveloped mind is very harmful.”

an1.24:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is developed.

an1.24:1.2.verse: A developed mind is very beneficial.”

an1.25:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not developed or manifested.

an1.25:1.2.verse: An undeveloped and unmanifested mind is very harmful.”

an1.26:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is developed and manifested.

an1.26:1.2.verse: A developed and manifested mind is very beneficial.”

an1.27:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not developed and cultivated.

an1.27:1.2.verse: An undeveloped and uncultivated mind is very harmful.”

an1.28:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is developed and cultivated.

an1.28:1.2.verse: A developed and cultivated mind is very beneficial.”

an1.29:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that brings such suffering as this mind that is not developed and cultivated.

an1.29:1.2.verse: An undeveloped and uncultivated mind brings suffering.”

an1.30:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that brings such happiness as this mind that is developed and cultivated.

an1.30:1.2.verse: A developed and cultivated mind brings happiness.”

an1.39:1.1.verse: “I don’t envision a single thing that—when untamed, unguarded, unprotected, unrestrained—leads to such great harm as the mind.

an1.39:1.2.verse: The mind—when untamed, unguarded, unprotected, unrestrained—leads to great harm.”

an1.40:1.1.verse: “I don’t envision a single thing that—when tamed, guarded, protected, restrained—leads to such great benefit as the mind.

an1.40:1.2.verse: The mind—when tamed, guarded, protected, restrained—leads to great benefit.”

an1.31:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not tamed.

an1.31:1.2.verse: An untamed mind is very harmful.”

an1.32:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is tamed.

an1.32:1.2.verse: A tamed mind is very beneficial.”

an1.33:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not guarded.

an1.33:1.2.verse: An unguarded mind is very harmful.”

an1.34:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is guarded.

an1.34:1.2.verse: A guarded mind is very beneficial.”

an1.35:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not protected.

an1.35:1.2.verse: An unprotected mind is very harmful.”

an1.36:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is protected.

an1.36:1.2.verse: A protected mind is very beneficial.”

an1.37:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not restrained.

an1.37:1.2.verse: An unrestrained mind is very harmful.”

an1.38:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is restrained.

an1.38:1.2.verse: A restrained mind is very beneficial.”

an1.39:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not tamed, guarded, protected, and restrained.

an1.39:1.2.verse: An untamed, unguarded, unprotected, and unrestrained mind is very harmful.”

an1.40:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is tamed, guarded, protected, and restrained.

an1.40:1.2.verse: A tamed, guarded, protected, and restrained mind is very beneficial.”

an1.45:1.1.verse: “Suppose there were a pool of water—sullied, turbid, and muddy. A man with good eyesight standing there on the bank would not see shells, gravel, and pebbles, or shoals of fish swimming about and resting.

an1.45:1.3.verse: Because of the sullied nature of the water.

an1.45:1.4.verse: In the same way, that a monk with a sullied mind would know his own benefit, the benefit of others, the benefit of both; that he would realize a superior human state, a truly noble distinction of knowledge & vision: Such a thing is impossible.

an1.45:1.6.verse: Because of the sullied nature of his mind.”

an1.46:1.1.verse: “Suppose there were a pool of water—clear, limpid, and unsullied. A man with good eyesight standing there on the bank would see shells, gravel, & pebbles, and also shoals of fish swimming about and resting.

an1.46:1.3.verse: Because of the unsullied nature of the water.

an1.46:1.4.verse: In the same way, that a monk with an unsullied mind would know his own benefit, the benefit of others, the benefit of both; that he would realize a superior human state, a truly noble distinction of knowledge & vision: Such a thing is possible.

an1.46:1.6.verse: Because of the unsullied nature of his mind.”

an1.47:1.1.verse: “Just as, of all trees, the balsam is foremost in terms of softness and pliancy,

an1.47:1.2.verse: in the same way I don’t envision a single thing that, when developed & cultivated, is as soft & pliant as the mind.

an1.47:1.3.verse: The mind, when developed & cultivated, is soft & pliant.”

an1.48:1.1.verse: “I don’t envision a single thing that is as quick to reverse itself as the mind—

an1.48:1.2.verse: so much so that there is no satisfactory simile for how quick to reverse itself it is.”

an1.49:1.2.verse: And it is defiled by incoming defilements.”

an1.41:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, suppose a spike of rice or barley was pointing the wrong way. If you trod on it with hand or foot, it is impossible for it to break the skin and produce blood.

an1.41:1.3.verse: Because the spike is pointing the wrong way.

an1.41:1.4.verse: In the same way, it is quite impossible for a mendicant whose mind is pointing the wrong way to break ignorance, produce knowledge, and realize extinguishment.

an1.41:1.6.verse: Because their mind is pointing the wrong way.”

an1.42:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, suppose a spike of rice or barley was pointing the right way. If you trod on it with hand or foot, it’s possible it may break the skin and produce blood.

an1.42:1.3.verse: Because the spike is pointing the right way.

an1.42:1.4.verse: In the same way, it is quite possible for a mendicant whose mind is pointing the right way to break ignorance, produce knowledge, and realize extinguishment.

an1.42:1.6.verse: Because the mind is pointing the right way.”

an1.43:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual whose mind is corrupted, I understand:

an1.43:1.2.verse: ‘If this individual were to die right now, they would be placed in hell as if delivered there.’

an1.43:1.5.verse: Corruption of mind is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

an1.44:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual whose mind is pure, I understand:

an1.44:1.2.verse: ‘If this individual were to die right now, they would be placed in heaven as if delivered there.’

an1.44:1.5.verse: Purity of mind is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

an1.45:1.1.verse: “Suppose, mendicants, there was a lake that was cloudy, murky, and muddy. A person with clear eyes standing on the bank would not see the clams and mussels, pebbles and gravel, and schools of fish swimming about or staying still.

an1.45:1.4.verse: In the same way, that a mendicant whose mind is clouded would know what’s for their own good, the good of another, or the good of both; or that they would realize any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones: this is quite impossible.

an1.46:1.1.verse: “Suppose, mendicants, there was a lake that was transparent, clear, and unclouded. A person with clear eyes standing on the bank would see the clams and mussels, pebbles and gravel, and schools of fish swimming about or staying still.

an1.46:1.4.verse: In the same way, that a mendicant whose mind is not clouded would know what’s for their own good, the good of another, or the good of both; or that they would realize any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones: this is quite possible.

an1.47:1.1.verse: “Just as, mendicants, the sandan is said to be the best kind of tree in terms of its pliability and workability,

an1.47:1.2.verse: so too, I do not see a single thing that’s as pliable and workable as this mind that is developed and cultivated.

an1.47:1.3.verse: A mind that is developed and cultivated is pliable and workable.”

an1.48:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that’s as quick to change as this mind.

an1.48:1.2.verse: So much so that it’s not easy to give a simile for how quickly the mind changes.”

an1.49:1.2.verse: But it’s corrupted by visiting corruptions.”

an1.50:1.2.verse: And it is freed from visiting corruptions.”

an1.51:1.2.verse: And it is defiled by incoming defilements.

an1.51:1.3.verse: The uninstructed run-of-the-mill person doesn’t discern that as it has come to be,

an1.51:1.4.verse: which is why I tell you that—for the uninstructed run-of-the-mill person—there is no development of the mind.”

an1.52:1.2.verse: And it is freed from incoming defilements.

an1.52:1.3.verse: The well-instructed disciple of the noble ones discerns that as it has come to be,

an1.52:1.4.verse: which is why I tell you that—for the well-instructed disciple of the noble ones—there is development of the mind.”

an1.51:1.2.verse: But it is corrupted by visiting corruptions.

an1.51:1.3.verse: An unlearned ordinary person does not truly understand this.

an1.51:1.4.verse: So I say that the unlearned ordinary person has no development of the mind.”

an1.52:1.2.verse: And it is freed from visiting corruptions.

an1.52:1.3.verse: A learned noble disciple truly understands this.

an1.52:1.4.verse: So I say that the learned noble disciple has development of the mind.”

an1.53:1.1.verse: “If, mendicants, a mendicant cultivates a mind of love even as long as a finger-snap,

an1.53:1.3.verse: a mendicant who does not lack absorption, who follows the Teacher’s instructions, who responds to advice, and who does not eat the country’s alms in vain.

an1.53:1.4.verse: How much more so those who make much of it!”

an1.54:1.1.verse: “If, mendicants, a mendicant develops a mind of love even as long as a finger-snap,

an1.54:1.3.verse: a mendicant who does not lack absorption, who follows the Teacher’s instructions, who responds to advice, and who does not eat the country’s alms in vain.

an1.54:1.4.verse: How much more so those who make much of it!”

an1.55:1.1.verse: “If, mendicants, a mendicant focuses on a mind of love even as long as a finger-snap,

an1.55:1.3.verse: a mendicant who does not lack absorption, who follows the Teacher’s instructions, who responds to advice, and who does not eat the country’s alms in vain.

an1.55:1.4.verse: How much more so those who make much of it!”

an1.56:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, intention is the leader of all things whatsoever that are unskillful, part of the unskillful, on the side of the unskillful.

an1.56:1.2.verse: Intention is the first of those things to arise, and unskillful things follow right behind.”

an1.57:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, intention is the leader of all things whatsoever that are skillful, part of the skillful, on the side of the skillful.

an1.57:1.2.verse: Intention is the first of those things to arise, and skillful things follow right behind.”

an1.58:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to unskillful qualities, or makes skillful qualities decline like negligence.

an1.58:1.2.verse: When you’re negligent, unskillful qualities arise and skillful qualities decline.”

an1.59:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or makes unskillful qualities decline like diligence.

an1.59:1.2.verse: When you’re diligent, skillful qualities arise and unskillful qualities decline.”

an1.60:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to unskillful qualities, or makes skillful qualities decline like laziness.

an1.60:1.2.verse: When you’re lazy, unskillful qualities arise and skillful qualities decline.”

an1.61:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or makes unskillful qualities decline like arousing energy.

an1.61:1.2.verse: When you’re energetic, skillful qualities arise and unskillful qualities decline.”

an1.62:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to unskillful qualities, or makes skillful qualities decline like having many wishes.

an1.62:1.2.verse: When you have many wishes, unskillful qualities arise and skillful qualities decline.”

an1.63:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or makes unskillful qualities decline like having few wishes.

an1.63:1.2.verse: When you have few wishes, skillful qualities arise and unskillful qualities decline.”

an1.64:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to unskillful qualities, or makes skillful qualities decline like lack of contentment.

an1.64:1.2.verse: When you lack contentment, unskillful qualities arise and skillful qualities decline.”

an1.65:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or makes unskillful qualities decline like contentment.

an1.65:1.2.verse: When you’re contented, skillful qualities arise and unskillful qualities decline.”

an1.66:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to unskillful qualities, or makes skillful qualities decline like irrational application of mind.

an1.66:1.2.verse: When you apply the mind irrationally, unskillful qualities arise and skillful qualities decline.”

an1.67:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or makes unskillful qualities decline like rational application of mind.

an1.67:1.2.verse: When you apply the mind rationally, skillful qualities arise and unskillful qualities decline.”

an1.68:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to unskillful qualities, or makes skillful qualities decline like lack of situational awareness.

an1.68:1.2.verse: When you lack situational awareness, unskillful qualities arise and skillful qualities decline.”

an1.69:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or makes unskillful qualities decline like situational awareness.

an1.69:1.2.verse: When you have situational awareness, skillful qualities arise and unskillful qualities decline.”

an1.70:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to unskillful qualities, or makes skillful qualities decline like bad friends.

an1.70:1.2.verse: When you have bad friends, unskillful qualities arise and skillful qualities decline.”

an1.76:1.1.verse: “Next to nothing, monks, is loss of relatives.

an1.76:1.2.verse: This is the worst loss: loss of discernment.”

an1.77:1.1.verse: “Next to nothing, monks, is increase in relatives.

an1.77:1.2.verse: This is the foremost increase: increase in discernment.

an1.77:1.3.verse: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves:

an1.77:1.4.verse: ‘We will grow in the increase of discernment.’

an1.77:1.5.verse: That’s how you should train yourselves.”

an1.78:1.1.verse: “Next to nothing, monks, is loss of wealth.

an1.78:1.2.verse: This is the worst loss: loss of discernment.”

an1.79:1.1.verse: “Next to nothing, monks, is increase in wealth.

an1.79:1.2.verse: This is the foremost increase: increase in discernment.

an1.79:1.3.verse: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves:

an1.79:1.4.verse: ‘We will grow in the increase of discernment.’

an1.79:1.5.verse: That’s how you should train yourselves.”

an1.80:1.1.verse: “Next to nothing, monks, is loss of status.

an1.80:1.2.verse: This is the worst loss: loss of discernment.”

an1.81:1.1.verse: “Next to nothing, monks, is increase in status.

an1.81:1.2.verse: This is the foremost increase: increase in discernment.

an1.81:1.3.verse: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves:

an1.81:1.4.verse: ‘We will grow in the increase of discernment.’

an1.81:1.5.verse: That’s how you should train yourselves.”

an1.71:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or makes unskillful qualities decline like good friends.

an1.71:1.2.verse: When you have good friends, skillful qualities arise and unskillful qualities decline.”

an1.72:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to unskillful qualities, or makes skillful qualities decline like pursuing bad habits and not good habits.

an1.72:1.2.verse: When you pursue bad habits and not good habits, unskillful qualities arise and skillful qualities decline.”

an1.73:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or makes unskillful qualities decline like pursuing good habits and not bad habits.

an1.73:1.2.verse: When you pursue good habits and not bad habits, skillful qualities arise and unskillful qualities decline.”

an1.74:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents the awakening factors from arising, or, if they’ve already arisen, prevents them from being fully developed like irrational application of mind.

an1.74:1.2.verse: When you apply the mind irrationally, the awakening factors don’t arise, or, if they’ve already arisen, they’re not fully developed.”

an1.75:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to the awakening factors, or, if they’ve already arisen, fully develops them like rational application of mind.

an1.75:1.2.verse: When you apply the mind rationally, the awakening factors arise, or, if they’ve already arisen, they’re fully developed.”

an1.76:1.1.verse: “Loss of relatives, mendicants, is a small thing.

an1.76:1.2.verse: Wisdom is the worst thing to lose.”

an1.77:1.1.verse: “Growth of relatives, mendicants, is a small thing.

an1.77:1.2.verse: Wisdom is the best thing to grow.

an1.77:1.3.verse: So you should train like this:

an1.78:1.1.verse: “Loss of wealth, mendicants, is a small thing.

an1.78:1.2.verse: Wisdom is the worst thing to lose.”

an1.79:1.1.verse: “Growth of wealth, mendicants, is a small thing.

an1.79:1.2.verse: Wisdom is the best thing to grow.

an1.79:1.3.verse: So you should train like this:

an1.80:1.1.verse: “Loss of fame, mendicants, is a small thing.

an1.80:1.2.verse: Wisdom is the worst thing to lose.”

an1.81:1.1.verse: “Growth of fame, mendicants, is a small thing.

an1.81:1.2.verse: Wisdom is the best thing to grow.

an1.81:1.3.verse: So you should train like this:

an1.82:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as negligence.

an1.83:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as diligence.

an1.84:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as laziness.

an1.85:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as arousing energy.

an1.86:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as having many wishes.

an1.86:1.2.verse: Having many wishes is very harmful.”

an1.87:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as having few wishes.

an1.87:1.2.verse: Having few wishes is very beneficial.”

an1.88:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as lack of contentment.

an1.88:1.2.verse: Lack of contentment is very harmful.”

an1.89:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as contentment.

an1.90:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as irrational application of mind.

an1.90:1.2.verse: Irrational application of mind is very harmful.”

an1.91:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as rational application of mind.

an1.91:1.2.verse: Rational application of mind is very beneficial.”

an1.92:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as lack of situational awareness.

an1.92:1.2.verse: Lack of situational awareness is very harmful.”

an1.93:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as situational awareness.

an1.94:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as bad friends.

an1.95:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as good friends.

an1.96:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as pursuing bad habits and not good habits.

an1.96:1.2.verse: Pursuing bad habits and not good habits is very harmful.”

an1.97:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as pursuing good habits and not bad habits.

an1.97:1.2.verse: Pursuing good habits and not bad habits is very beneficial.”

an1.98:1.1.verse: “Taking into account interior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that is so very harmful as negligence.

an1.99:1.1.verse: “Taking into account interior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that is so very beneficial as diligence.

an1.100:1.1.verse: “Taking into account interior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that is so very harmful as laziness.

an1.101:1.1.verse: “Taking into account interior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that is so very beneficial as arousing energy.

an1.102-109:1.1.verse: “Taking into account interior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that is so very harmful as having many wishes … having few wishes … lack of contentment … contentment … irrational application of mind … rational application of mind … lack of situational awareness … situational awareness …”

an1.110:1.1.verse: “Taking into account exterior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that is so very harmful as bad friends.

an1.111:1.1.verse: “Taking into account exterior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that is so very beneficial as good friends.

an1.112:1.1.verse: “Taking into account interior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that is so very harmful as pursuing bad habits and not good habits.

an1.112:1.2.verse: Pursuing bad habits and not good habits is very harmful.”

an1.113:1.1.verse: “Taking into account interior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that is so very beneficial as pursuing good habits and not bad habits.

an1.113:1.2.verse: Pursuing good habits and not bad habits is very beneficial.”

an1.114:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching like negligence.

an1.114:1.2.verse: Negligence leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.”

an1.115:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching like diligence.

an1.115:1.2.verse: Diligence leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.”

an1.116:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching like laziness.

an1.116:1.2.verse: Laziness leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.”

an1.117:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching like arousing energy.

an1.117:1.2.verse: Arousing energy leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.”

an1.118-128:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching like having many wishes … having few wishes … lack of contentment … contentment … irrational application of mind … rational application of mind … lack of situational awareness … situational awareness … bad friends … good friends … pursuing bad habits and not good habits.

an1.118-128:1.2.verse: Pursuing bad habits and not good habits leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.”

an1.129:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching like pursuing good habits and not bad habits.

an1.129:1.2.verse: Pursuing good habits and not bad habits leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching”

an1.130:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those mendicants who explain what is not the teaching as the teaching are acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

an1.130:1.2.verse: They brim with much wickedness and make the true teaching disappear.”

an1.131:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those mendicants who explain what is the teaching as not the teaching are acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

an1.131:1.2.verse: They brim with much wickedness and make the true teaching disappear.”

an1.132-139:1.1.verse: “Those mendicants who explain what is not found in the monastic law as found in the monastic law … what is found in the monastic law as not found in the monastic law … what was not spoken and stated by the Realized One as spoken and stated by the Realized One … what was spoken and stated by the Realized One as not spoken and stated by the Realized One … what was not practiced by the Realized One as practiced by the Realized One … what was practiced by the Realized One as not practiced by the Realized One … what was not prescribed by the Realized One as prescribed by the Realized One … what was prescribed by the Realized One as not prescribed by the Realized One

an1.132-139:1.2.verse: are acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

an1.132-139:1.3.verse: They brim with much wickedness and make the true teaching disappear.”

an1.140:1.1.verse: “Monks, any monks who explain not-Dhamma as not-Dhamma are practicing for the welfare of many people, for the happiness of many people, for the benefit of many people, for the welfare & happiness of human beings & devas.

an1.140:1.2.verse: They amass much merit and help this True Dhamma to remain.”

an1.141:1.1.verse: “Monks, any monks who explain Dhamma as Dhamma are practicing for the welfare of many people, for the happiness of many people, for the benefit of many people, for the welfare & happiness of human beings & devas.

an1.141:1.2.verse: They amass much merit and help this True Dhamma to remain.”

an1.140:0.2.verse: The Chapter on Not the Teaching

an1.140:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those mendicants who explain what is not the teaching as not the teaching are acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

an1.140:1.2.verse: They brim with much merit and make the true teaching continue.”

an1.141:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those mendicants who explain what is the teaching as the teaching are acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

an1.141:1.2.verse: They brim with much merit and make the true teaching continue.”

an1.142-149:1.1.verse: “Those mendicants who explain what is not found in the monastic law as not found in the monastic law … what is found in the monastic law as found in the monastic law … what was not spoken and stated by the Realized One as not spoken and stated by the Realized One … what was spoken and stated by the Realized One as spoken and stated by the Realized One … what was not practiced by the Realized One as not practiced by the Realized One … what was practiced by the Realized One as practiced by the Realized One … what was not prescribed by the Realized One as not prescribed by the Realized One … what was prescribed by the Realized One as prescribed by the Realized One …

an1.142-149:1.2.verse: are acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

an1.142-149:1.3.verse: They brim with much merit and make the true teaching continue.”

an1.150:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those mendicants who explain a non-offense as an offense are acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

an1.150:1.2.verse: They brim with much wickedness and make the true teaching disappear.”

an1.151:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those mendicants who explain an offense as a non-offense are acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

an1.151:1.2.verse: Those mendicants brim with much wickedness and make the true teaching disappear.”

an1.152-159:1.1.verse: “Those mendicants who explain a light offense as a heavy offense … a heavy offense as a light offense … a grave offense as a minor offense … a minor offense as a grave offense … a curable offense as an incurable offense … an incurable offense as a curable offense … an offense requiring amends as an offense not requiring amends … an offense not requiring amends as an offense with redress are acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

an1.152-159:1.2.verse: Those mendicants brim with much wickedness and make the true teaching disappear.”

an1.160:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those mendicants who explain a non-offense as a non-offense are acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

an1.160:1.2.verse: They brim with much merit and make the true teaching continue.”

an1.161:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those mendicants who explain an offense as an offense are acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

an1.161:1.2.verse: They brim with much merit and make the true teaching continue.”

an1.162-169:1.1.verse: “Those mendicants who explain a light offense as a light offense … a heavy offense as a heavy offense … a grave offense as a grave offense … a minor offense as a minor offense … a curable offense as a curable offense … an incurable offense as an incurable offense … an offense requiring amends as an offense requiring amends … an offense not requiring amends as an offense requiring amends

an1.162-169:1.2.verse: are acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

an1.162-169:1.3.verse: They brim with much merit and make the true teaching continue.”

an1.170:1.1.verse: “One individual, mendicants, arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

an1.170:1.3.verse: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

an1.170:1.4.verse: This is the one individual, mendicants, who arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”

an1.171:1.1.verse: “The appearance of one individual, mendicants, is rare in the world.

an1.171:1.3.verse: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

an1.171:1.4.verse: This is the one individual, mendicants, whose appearance is rare in the world.”

an1.172:1.1.verse: “One individual, mendicants, arises in the world who is an incredible human being.

an1.172:1.3.verse: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

an1.172:1.4.verse: This is the one individual, mendicants, who arises in the world who is an incredible human being.”

an1.173:1.1.verse: “The death of one individual, mendicants, is regretted by many people.

an1.173:1.3.verse: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

an1.173:1.4.verse: This is the one individual, mendicants, whose death is regretted by many people.”

an1.174:1.1.verse: “One individual, mendicants, arises in the world unique, without peer or rival, incomparable, matchless, unrivaled, unequaled, without equal, the best of men.

an1.174:1.3.verse: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

an1.174:1.4.verse: This is the one individual, mendicants, who arises in the world unique, without peer or rival, incomparable, matchless, unrivaled, unequaled, without equal, the best of men.”

an1.175-186:1.1.verse: “With the appearance of one individual, mendicants, there is the appearance of a great eye, a great light, a great radiance, and the six unsurpassable things; the realization of the four kinds of textual analysis; the penetration of many and diverse elements; the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom; the realization of the fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection.

an1.175-186:1.3.verse: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

an1.175-186:1.4.verse: This is the one individual whose appearance brings the appearance of a great eye, a great light, a great radiance, and the six unsurpassable things; the realization of the four kinds of textual analysis; the penetration of many and diverse elements; the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom; the realization of the fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection.”

an1.187:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single other individual who rightly keeps rolling the supreme Wheel of Dhamma that was rolled forth by the Realized One like Sāriputta.

an1.187:1.2.verse: Sāriputta rightly keeps rolling the supreme Wheel of Dhamma that was rolled forth by the Realized One.”

an1.188:1.1.verse: “The foremost of my monk disciples in long standing is Koṇḍañña Who Understood.

an1.193:1.1.verse: … from eminent families is Bhaddiya son of Kāḷīgodhā.

an1.194:1.1.verse: … with a charming voice is Bhaddiya the Dwarf.

an1.195:1.1.verse: … with a lion’s roar is Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer.

an1.196:1.1.verse: … who speak on the teaching is Puṇṇa son of Mantāṇī.

an1.197:1.1.verse: … who explain in detail the meaning of a brief statement is Mahākaccāna.”

an1.198:1.1.verse: “The foremost of my monk disciples in creating a mind-made body is Cūḷapanthaka.

an1.199:1.1.verse: … who are skilled in the evolution of heart is Cūḷapanthaka.

an1.200:1.1.verse: … who are skilled in the evolution of perception is Mahāpanthaka.

an1.201:1.1.verse: … who live without strife is Subhūti.

an1.202:1.1.verse: … who are worthy of a religious donation is Subhūti.

an1.203:1.1.verse: … who stay in the wilderness is Revata of the Acacia Wood.

an1.204:1.1.verse: … who practice absorption is Revata the Doubter.

an1.205:1.1.verse: … who are energetic is Soṇa Koḷivisa.

an1.206:1.1.verse: … who enunciate well is Soṇa of the Sharp Ears.

an1.207:1.1.verse: … who receive many possessions is Sīvali.

an1.208:1.1.verse: … who are committed to faith is Vakkalī.”

an1.209:1.1.verse: “The foremost of my monk disciples who want to train is Rāhula.

an1.210:1.1.verse: … who went forth out of faith is Raṭṭhapāla.

an1.211:1.1.verse: … who are the first to vote is Kuṇḍadhāna.

an1.212:1.1.verse: … who are eloquent poets is Vaṅgīsa.

an1.213:1.1.verse: … who are impressive all around is Upasena son of Vaṅgantā.

an1.214:1.1.verse: … who assign lodgings is Dabba the Mallian.

an1.215:1.1.verse: … who are beloved of the deities is Pilindavaccha.

an1.216:1.1.verse: … with swift insight is Bāhiya of the Bark Cloth.

an1.217:1.1.verse: … with brilliant speech is Kassapa the Prince.

an1.218:1.1.verse: … who have attained the methods of textual analysis is Mahākoṭṭhita.”

an1.219:1.1.verse: “The foremost of my monk disciples who are very learned is Ānanda.

an1.223:1.1.verse: … as a personal attendant is Ānanda.

an1.224:1.1.verse: … with a large congregation is Kassapa of Uruvelā.

an1.225:1.1.verse: … who inspire lay families is Kāḷudāyī.

an1.227:1.1.verse: … who recollect past lives is Sobhita.

an1.228:1.1.verse: … who have memorized the monastic law is Upāli.

an1.229:1.1.verse: … who advise the nuns is Nandaka.

an1.230:1.1.verse: … who guard the sense doors is Nanda.

an1.231:1.1.verse: … who advise the monks is Mahākappina.

an1.232:1.1.verse: … who are skilled in the fire element is Sāgata.

an1.233:1.1.verse: … who inspire eloquent teachings is Rādha.

an1.234:1.1.verse: … who wear coarse robes is Mogharāja.”

an1.235:1.1.verse: “The foremost of my nun disciples in long standing is Mahāpajāpati Gotamī.

an1.238:1.1.verse: … who have memorized the monastic law is Paṭācārā.

an1.239:1.1.verse: … who speak on the teaching is Dhammadinnā.

an1.243:1.1.verse: … with swift insight is Bhaddā of the Curly Hair.

an1.244:1.1.verse: … who recollect past lives is Bhaddā daughter of Kapila.

an1.245:1.1.verse: … who have attained great insight is Bhaddakaccānā.

an1.246:1.1.verse: … who wear coarse robes is Kisāgotamī.

an1.247:1.1.verse: … who are committed to faith is Siṅgāla’s Mother.”

an1.248:1.1.verse: “The foremost of my laymen in first going for refuge are the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika.

an1.249:1.1.verse: … as a donor is the householder Sudatta Anāthapiṇḍika.

an1.250:1.1.verse: … who speak on the teaching is the householder Citta Macchikāsaṇḍika.

an1.251:1.1.verse: … who attract a congregation by the four ways of being inclusive is Hatthaka of Āḷavī.

an1.252:1.1.verse: … who donate fine things is Mahānāma Sakka.

an1.253:1.1.verse: … who donate nice things is the householder Ugga of Vesālī.

an1.254:1.1.verse: … who attend on the Saṅgha is the householder Uggata of Elephant Village.

an1.255:1.1.verse: … who have experiential confidence is Sūrambaṭṭha.

an1.256:1.1.verse: … who have confidence in an individual is Jīvaka Komārabhacca.

an1.257:1.1.verse: … who are intimate is the householder Nakula’s father.”

an1.258:1.1.verse: “The foremost of my laywomen in first going for refuge is Sujātā the general’s daughter.

an1.259:1.1.verse: … as a donor is Visākhā, Migāra’s mother.

an1.260:1.1.verse: … who are very learned is Khujjuttarā.

an1.261:1.1.verse: … who dwell in love is Sāmāvatī.

an1.262:1.1.verse: … who practice absorption is Uttarā, Nanda’s mother.

an1.263:1.1.verse: … who give fine things is Suppavāsā the Koliyan.

an1.264:1.1.verse: … who care for the sick is the laywoman Suppiyā.

an1.265:1.1.verse: … who have experiential confidence is Kātiyānī.

an1.266:1.1.verse: … who are intimate is the householder Nakula’s mother.

an1.267:1.1.verse: … whose confidence is based on oral transmission is the laywoman Kāḷī of Kuraraghara.”

an1.268:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to take any condition as permanent. That is not possible.

an1.268:1.2.verse: But it is possible for an ordinary person to take some condition as permanent. That is possible.”

an1.269:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to take any condition as pleasant.

an1.269:1.2.verse: But it is possible for an ordinary person to take some condition as pleasant.”

an1.270:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to take anything as self.

an1.270:1.2.verse: But it is possible for an ordinary person to take something as self.”

an1.271:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to murder their mother.

an1.271:1.2.verse: But it is possible for an ordinary person to murder their mother.”

an1.272:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to murder their father.

an1.272:1.2.verse: But it is possible for an ordinary person to murder their father.”

an1.273:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to murder a perfected one.

an1.273:1.2.verse: But it is possible for an ordinary person to murder a perfected one.”

an1.274:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to injure a Realized One with malicious intent.

an1.274:1.2.verse: But it is possible for an ordinary person to injure a Realized One with malicious intent.”

an1.275:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to cause a schism in the Saṅgha.

an1.275:1.2.verse: But it is possible for an ordinary person to cause a schism in the Saṅgha.”

an1.276:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to dedicate themselves to another teacher.

an1.276:1.2.verse: But it is possible for an ordinary person to dedicate themselves to another teacher.”

an1.277:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for two perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas to arise in the same solar system at the same time.

an1.277:1.2.verse: But it is possible for just one perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, to arise in one solar system.”

an1.278:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for two wheel-turning monarchs to arise in the same solar system at the same time.

an1.278:1.2.verse: But it is possible for just one wheel-turning monarch to arise in one solar system.”

an1.279:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a woman to be a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha.

an1.279:1.2.verse: But it is possible for a man to be a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha.”

an1.280:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a woman to be a wheel-turning monarch.

an1.280:1.2.verse: But it is possible for a man to be a wheel-turning monarch.”

an1.281-283:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a woman to perform the role of Sakka, Māra, or the Divinity.

an1.281-283:1.2.verse: But it is possible for a man to perform the role of Sakka, Māra, or the Divinity.”

an1.284:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a likable, desirable, agreeable result to come from bad bodily conduct.

an1.284:1.2.verse: But it is possible for an unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable result to come from bad bodily conduct.”

an1.285-286:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a likable, desirable, agreeable result to come from bad verbal … bad mental conduct.

an1.285-286:1.2.verse: But it is possible for an unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable result to come from bad verbal … bad mental conduct.”

an1.287:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable result to come from good bodily conduct.

an1.287:1.2.verse: But it is possible for a likable, desirable, agreeable result to come from good bodily conduct.”

an1.288-289:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable result to come from good verbal … good mental conduct.

an1.288-289:1.2.verse: But it is possible for a likable, desirable, agreeable result to come from good verbal … good mental conduct.”

an1.290:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen that someone who has engaged in bad bodily conduct, could for that reason alone, when their body breaks up, after death, be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

an1.290:1.2.verse: But it is possible that someone who has engaged in bad bodily conduct could, for that reason alone, when their body breaks up, after death, be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

an1.291-292:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen that someone who has engaged in bad verbal … bad mental conduct could, for that reason alone, when their body breaks up, after death, be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

an1.291-292:1.2.verse: But it is possible that someone who has engaged in bad verbal … bad mental conduct could, for that reason alone, when their body breaks up, after death, be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

an1.293:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen that someone who has engaged in good bodily conduct could, for that reason alone, when their body breaks up, after death, be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

an1.293:1.2.verse: But it is possible that someone who has engaged in good bodily conduct could, for that reason alone, when their body breaks up, after death, be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

an1.294-295:1.1.verse: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen that someone who has engaged in good verbal … good mental conduct could, for that reason alone, when their body breaks up, after death, be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

an1.294-295:1.2.verse: But it is possible that someone who has engaged in good verbal … good mental conduct could, for that reason alone, when their body breaks up, after death, be reborn in a good place, heavenly realm.”

an1.296:1.1.verse: “One thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated, leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

an1.296:1.4.verse: This one thing, when developed and cultivated, leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.”

an1.297-305:1.1.verse: “One thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated, leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

an1.297-305:1.3.verse: Recollection of the teaching … Recollection of the Saṅgha … Recollection of ethical conduct … Recollection of generosity … Recollection of the deities … Mindfulness of breathing … Mindfulness of death … Mindfulness of the body … Recollection of peace.

an1.297-305:1.4.verse: This one thing, when developed and cultivated, leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.”

an1.306:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to unskillful qualities, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow like wrong view.

an1.306:1.2.verse: When you have wrong view, unskillful qualities arise or, when they have arisen, they increase and grow.”

an1.307:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow like right view.

an1.307:1.2.verse: When you have right view, unarisen skillful qualities arise or, when they have arisen, they increase and grow.”

an1.308:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to unskillful qualities, or makes skillful qualities decline like wrong view.

an1.308:1.2.verse: When you have wrong view, unskillful qualities arise and skillful qualities decline.”

an1.309:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or makes unskillful qualities decline like right view.

an1.309:1.2.verse: When you have right view, skillful qualities arise and unskillful qualities decline.”

an1.310:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to wrong view, and once arisen, makes it grow like irrational application of mind.

an1.310:1.2.verse: When you apply the mind irrationally, wrong view arises, and once arisen it grows.”

an1.311:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to right view, or, once it has already arisen, makes it grow like rational application of mind.

an1.311:1.2.verse: When you apply the mind rationally, right view arises, and once arisen it grows.”

an1.312:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that causes sentient beings to be reborn, when their body breaks up, after death, in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell like wrong view.

an1.312:1.2.verse: It is because they have wrong view that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

an1.313:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that causes sentient beings to be reborn, when their body breaks up, after death, in a good place, a heavenly realm like right view.

an1.313:1.2.verse: It is because they have right view that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

an1.314:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when an individual has wrong view, whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable, harmful, and suffering.

an1.314:1.4.verse: Suppose a seed of neem, angled gourd, or bitter gourd was planted in moist earth. Whatever nutrients it takes up from the earth and water would lead to its bitter, acerbic, and unpleasant taste.

an1.314:1.7.verse: In the same way, when an individual has wrong view, whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable, harmful, and suffering.

an1.315:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when an individual has right view, whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is likable, desirable, agreeable, beneficial, and pleasant.

an1.315:1.4.verse: Suppose a seed of sugarcane, fine rice, or grape was planted in moist earth. Whatever nutrients it takes up from the earth and water would lead to its sweet, pleasant, delectable flavor.

an1.315:1.7.verse: In the same way, when an individual has right view, whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is likable, desirable, agreeable, beneficial, and pleasant.

an1.328:1.1.verse: “Monks, just as even a tiny amount of feces is foul-smelling,

an1.328:1.2.verse: in the same way, I don’t praise even a tiny amount of becoming—even as much as a finger-snap.”

an1.316:1.1.verse: “One individual, mendicants, arises in the world for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

an1.316:1.3.verse: Someone with wrong view, whose perspective is distorted.

an1.316:1.4.verse: They draw many people away from the true teaching and establish them in false teachings.

an1.316:1.5.verse: This is one individual who arises in the world for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.”

an1.317:1.1.verse: “One individual, mendicants, arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

an1.317:1.3.verse: Someone with right view, whose perspective is undistorted.

an1.317:1.4.verse: They draw many people away from false teachings and establish them in the true teaching.

an1.317:1.5.verse: This is one individuals who arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”

an1.318:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very blameworthy as wrong view.

an1.318:1.2.verse: Wrong view is the most blameworthy thing of all.”

an1.319:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I do not see a single other individual who acts for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans, as that futile man, the bamboo-staffed ascetic.

an1.319:1.2.verse: Just as a trap set at the mouth of a river would bring harm, suffering, calamity, and disaster for many fish,

an1.319:1.3.verse: so too that futile man, the bamboo-staffed ascetic, is a trap for humans, it seems to me. He has arisen in the world for the harm, suffering, calamity, and disaster of many beings.”

an1.320:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, the one who encourages someone in a poorly explained teaching and training, the one who they encourage, and the one who practices accordingly all brim with much wickedness.

an1.320:1.3.verse: Because the teaching is poorly explained.”

an1.321:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, the one who encourages someone in a well explained teaching and training, the one who they encourage, and the one who practices accordingly all brim with much merit.

an1.321:1.3.verse: Because the teaching is well explained.”

an1.322:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, in a poorly explained teaching and training, the donor should know moderation, not the recipient.

an1.322:1.3.verse: Because the teaching is poorly explained.”

an1.323:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, in a well explained teaching and training, the recipient should know moderation, not the donor.

an1.323:1.3.verse: Because the teaching is well explained.”

an1.324:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, in a poorly explained teaching and training an energetic person lives in suffering.

an1.324:1.3.verse: Because the teaching is poorly explained.”

an1.325:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, in a well explained teaching and training a lazy person lives in suffering.

an1.325:1.3.verse: Because the teaching is well explained.”

an1.326:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, in a poorly explained teaching and training a lazy person lives happily.

an1.326:1.3.verse: Because the teaching is poorly explained.”

an1.327:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, in a well explained teaching and training an energetic person lives happily.

an1.327:1.3.verse: Because the teaching is well explained.”

an1.328:1.1.verse: “Just as, mendicants, even a little bit of fecal matter still stinks,

an1.328:1.2.verse: so too I don’t approve of even a little bit of continued existence, not even as long as a finger-snap.”

an1.329:1.1.verse: “Just as even a little bit of urine, or spit, or pus, or blood still stinks,

an1.329:1.2.verse: so too I don’t approve of even a little bit of continued existence, not even as long as a finger-snap.”

an1.347:1.1.verse: “Monks, just as the delightful parks, delightful groves, landscapes, & lotus ponds in this Jambudīpa are few, while the ridges & hollows, the river ravines, the tracts of stumps & thorns, the craggy irregularities are more numerous, in the same way, those who have gained the taste of the goal, the taste of the Dhamma, the taste of release are few,

an1.347:1.2.verse: while those who have not gained the taste of the goal, the taste of the Dhamma, the taste of release are more numerous.

an1.347:1.4.verse: ‘We will gain the taste of the goal, the taste of the Dhamma, the taste of release.’

an1.347:1.5.verse: That’s how you should train yourselves.”

an1.333:1.1.verse: “Just as, mendicants, in the Black Plum Tree Land the delightful parks, woods, meadows, and lotus ponds are few,

an1.333:1.2.verse: while the hilly terrain, inaccessible riverlands, stumps and thorns, and rugged mountains are many;

an1.333:1.3.verse: so too the sentient beings born on land are few, while those born in water are many.

an1.334:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings reborn as humans are few,

an1.334:1.2.verse: while those not reborn as humans are many.

an1.335:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings reborn in civilized countries are few,

an1.335:1.2.verse: while those reborn in the borderlands, among uneducated foreigners, are many.

an1.336:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings who are wise, bright, clever, and able to distinguish what is well said from what is poorly said are few,

an1.336:1.2.verse: while the sentient beings who are witless, dull, idiotic, and unable to distinguish what is well said from what is poorly said are many.

an1.337:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings who have the noble eye of wisdom are few,

an1.337:1.2.verse: while those who are ignorant and confused are many.

an1.338:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings who get to see a Realized One are few,

an1.338:1.2.verse: while those who don’t get to see a Realized One are many.

an1.339:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings who get to hear the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One are few,

an1.339:1.2.verse: while those sentient beings who don’t get to hear the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One are many.

an1.340:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings who remember the teachings they hear are few,

an1.340:1.2.verse: while those who don’t remember the teachings are many.

an1.341:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings who examine the meaning of the teachings they have memorized are few,

an1.341:1.2.verse: while those who don’t examine the meaning of the teachings are many.

an1.342:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings who understand the meaning and the teaching and practice in line with the teaching are few,

an1.342:1.2.verse: while those who understand the meaning and the teaching but don’t practice in line with the teaching are many.

an1.343:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings inspired by inspiring places are few,

an1.343:1.2.verse: while those who are uninspired are many.

an1.344:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings who, being inspired, strive effectively are few,

an1.344:1.2.verse: while those who, even though inspired, don’t strive effectively are many.

an1.345:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings who, relying on letting go, gain immersion, gain unification of mind are few,

an1.345:1.2.verse: while those who don’t gain immersion, don’t gain unification of mind relying on letting go are many.

an1.346:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings who get the best food and flavors are few,

an1.346:1.2.verse: while those who don’t get the best food and flavors, but get by with scraps in an alms bowl are many.

an1.347:1.1.verse: … so too the sentient beings who get the essence of the meaning, the essence of the teaching, and the essence of freedom are few,

an1.347:1.2.verse: while the sentient beings who don’t get the essence of the meaning, the essence of the teaching, and the essence of freedom are many.

an1.347:1.3.verse: So you should train like this:

an1.347:1.4.verse: ‘We will get the essence of the meaning, the essence of the teaching, the essence of freedom.’

an1.348-350:1.1.verse: “Just as, mendicants, in the Black Plum Tree Land the delightful parks, woods, meadows, and lotus ponds are few,

an1.348-350:1.2.verse: while the hilly terrain, inaccessible riverlands, stumps and thorns, and rugged mountains are many;

an1.348-350:1.3.verse: so too, those who die as humans and are reborn as humans are few, while those who die as humans and are reborn in hell, or the animal realm, or the ghost realm are many.”

an1.372-374:1.1.verse: “… the sentient beings who die as ghosts and are reborn as humans are few,

an1.375-377:1.1.verse: “… the sentient beings who die as ghosts and are reborn as gods are few,

an1.575:0.2.verse: The Chapter on Mindfulness of the Body

an1.575:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, anyone who brings into their mind the great ocean includes all of the streams that run into it.

an1.575:1.2.verse: In the same way, anyone who has developed and cultivated mindfulness of the body includes all of the skillful qualities that play a part in realization.”

an1.576-582:1.1.verse: “One thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated leads to great urgency … great benefit … great sanctuary from the yoke … mindfulness and awareness … gaining knowledge and vision … blissful meditation in this life … the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.

an1.576-582:1.4.verse: This one thing, when developed and cultivated, leads to great urgency … great benefit … great sanctuary from the yoke … mindfulness and awareness … gaining knowledge and vision … blissful meditation in this life … the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.”

an1.583:1.1.verse: “When one thing, mendicants, is developed and cultivated the body and mind become tranquil, thinking and considering settle down, and all of the qualities that play a part in realization are fully developed.

an1.583:1.4.verse: When this one thing is developed and cultivated, the body and mind become tranquil, thinking and considering settle down, and all of the qualities that play a part in realization are fully developed.”

an1.584:1.1.verse: “When one thing, mendicants, is developed and cultivated, unskillful qualities do not arise, and, if they’ve already arisen, they are given up.

an1.584:1.4.verse: When this one thing is developed and cultivated, unskillful qualities do not arise, and, if they’ve already arisen, they are given up.”

an1.585:1.1.verse: “When one thing, mendicants, is developed and cultivated, skillful qualities arise, and, once they’ve arisen, they increase and grow.

an1.585:1.4.verse: When this one thing is developed and cultivated, skillful qualities arise, and, once they’ve arisen, they increase and grow.”

an1.586-590:1.1.verse: “When one thing, mendicants, is developed and cultivated, ignorance is given up … knowledge arises … the conceit ‘I am’ is given up … the underlying tendencies are uprooted … the fetters are given up.

an1.586-590:1.4.verse: When this one thing is developed and cultivated, ignorance is given up … knowledge arises … the conceit ‘I am’ is given up … the underlying tendencies are uprooted … the fetters are given up.”

an1.591-592:1.1.verse: “One thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated leads to demolition by wisdom … to complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping.

an1.591-592:1.4.verse: This one thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated leads to demolition by wisdom … to complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping.”

an1.593-595:1.1.verse: “When one thing is developed and cultivated there is the penetration of many elements … the penetration of diverse elements … the analysis of many elements.

an1.593-595:1.4.verse: When this one thing is developed and cultivated there is the penetration of many elements … the penetration of diverse elements … the analysis of many elements.”

an1.596-599:1.1.verse: “One thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated leads to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry … once-return … non-return … perfection.

an1.596-599:1.4.verse: This one thing, when developed and cultivated, leads to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry … once-return … non-return … perfection.”

an1.600-615:1.1.verse: “One thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated, leads to the getting of wisdom … the growth of wisdom … the increase of wisdom … to great wisdom … to widespread wisdom … to abundant wisdom … to deep wisdom … to extraordinary wisdom … to vast wisdom … to much wisdom … to fast wisdom … to light wisdom … to laughing wisdom … to swift wisdom … to sharp wisdom … to penetrating wisdom.

an1.600-615:1.4.verse: This one thing, when developed and cultivated, leads to the getting of wisdom … the growth of wisdom … the increase of wisdom … to great wisdom … to widespread wisdom … to abundant wisdom … to deep wisdom … to extraordinary wisdom … to vast wisdom … to much wisdom … to fast wisdom … to light wisdom … to laughing wisdom … to swift wisdom … to sharp wisdom … to penetrating wisdom.”

an1.616:0.2.verse: The Chapter on Freedom From Death

an1.616:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who don’t enjoy mindfulness of the body don’t enjoy freedom from death.

an1.616:1.2.verse: Those who enjoy mindfulness of the body enjoy freedom from death.”

an1.617:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who haven’t enjoyed mindfulness of the body haven’t enjoyed freedom from death.

an1.617:1.2.verse: Those who have enjoyed mindfulness of the body have enjoyed freedom from death.”

an1.618:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who have lost mindfulness of the body have lost freedom from death.

an1.618:1.2.verse: Those who haven’t lost mindfulness of the body haven’t lost freedom from death.”

an1.619:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who have missed out on mindfulness of the body have missed out on freedom from death.

an1.619:1.2.verse: Those who have undertaken mindfulness of the body have not missed out on freedom from death.”

an1.620:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who have neglected mindfulness of the body have neglected freedom from death.

an1.620:1.2.verse: Those who have not neglected mindfulness of the body have not neglected freedom from death.”

an1.621:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who have forgotten mindfulness of the body have forgotten freedom from death.

an1.621:1.2.verse: Those who haven’t forgotten mindfulness of the body haven’t forgotten freedom from death.”

an1.622:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who haven’t cultivated mindfulness of the body haven’t cultivated freedom from death.

an1.622:1.2.verse: Those who have cultivated mindfulness of the body have cultivated freedom from death.”

an1.623:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who haven’t developed mindfulness of the body haven’t developed freedom from death.

an1.623:1.2.verse: Those who have developed mindfulness of the body have developed freedom from death.”

an1.624:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who haven’t made much of mindfulness of the body haven’t made much of freedom from death.

an1.624:1.2.verse: Those who have made much of mindfulness of the body have made much of freedom from death.”

an1.625:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who haven’t had insight into mindfulness of the body haven’t had insight into freedom from death.

an1.625:1.2.verse: Those who have had insight into mindfulness of the body have had insight into freedom from death.”

an1.626:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who haven’t completely understood mindfulness of the body haven’t completely understood freedom from death.

an1.626:1.2.verse: Those who have completely understood mindfulness of the body have completely understood freedom from death.”

an1.627:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who haven’t realized mindfulness of the body haven’t realized freedom from death.

an1.627:1.2.verse: Those who have realized mindfulness of the body have realized freedom from death.”

an1.627:1.3.verse: The thousand discourses of the Ones are complete.

an1.627:2.1.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

an1.627:2.2.verse: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

an1.627:2.4.verse: The Book of the Ones is finished.

an2.1:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

an2.1:1.5.verse: “Yes, lord,” the monks responded to him.

an2.1:2.3.verse: Penalties in the present life and penalties in lives to come.

an2.1:2.4.verse: “And which are penalties in the present life?

an2.1:2.5.verse: There is the case where a certain person sees a thief, a criminal, who, when captured by a king, they torture in many ways.

an2.1:2.6.verse: They flog him with whips, beat him with canes, beat him with clubs; they cut off his hands, cut off his feet, cut off his hands & feet; they cut off his ears, cut off his nose, cut off his ears & nose; they subject him to the ‘porridge pot,’ the ‘polished-shell shave,’ the ‘Rāhu’s mouth,’ the ‘flaming garland,’ the ‘blazing hand,’ the ‘grass-duty (ascetic),’ the ‘bark-dress (ascetic),’ the ‘burning antelope,’ the ‘meat hooks,’ the ‘coin-gouging,’ the ‘lye pickling,’ the ‘pivot on a stake,’ the ‘rolled-up bed’; they have him splashed with boiling oil, devoured by dogs, impaled alive on stakes; they have his head cut off with a sword.

an2.1:3.1.verse: “The thought occurs to him [the first man],

an2.1:3.2.verse: ‘It’s because of these sorts of evil actions that when a thief, a criminal, is captured by a king, they torture him in many ways.

an2.1:3.3.verse: They flog him with whips … they have his head cut off with a sword.

an2.1:3.4.verse: And if I were to do this sort of evil action and I, too, were captured by a king, they would torture me in many ways.

an2.1:3.5.verse: They would flog me with whips … they would have my head cut off with a sword.’

an2.1:3.6.verse: “So, fearing penalties in the present life, he doesn’t go around plundering the belongings of others.

an2.1:3.7.verse: “These, monks, are called penalties in the present life.

an2.1:4.1.verse: “And which are penalties in lives to come?

an2.1:4.2.verse: “There is the case where a certain man considers,

an2.1:4.3.verse: ‘Bodily misconduct has an evil result in a life to come. Verbal misconduct has an evil result in a life to come. Mental misconduct has an evil result in a life to come.

an2.1:4.4.verse: If I were to engage in bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, & mental misconduct,

an2.1:4.5.verse: then how could I not—on the break-up of the body, after death—re-appear in a plane of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, in hell?’

an2.1:4.6.verse: “So, fearing penalties in lives to come, he abandons bodily misconduct and develops right bodily conduct. He abandons verbal misconduct and develops right verbal conduct. He abandons mental misconduct and develops right mental conduct. He keeps himself pure.

an2.1:4.7.verse: “These, monks, are called penalties in lives to come.

an2.1:4.8.verse: These, monks, are the two penalties.

an2.1:4.10.verse: ‘We will fear penalties in the present life. We will fear penalties in lives to come. We will be wary of penalties, seeing danger in penalties.’

an2.1:4.11.verse: That’s how you should train yourselves.

an2.1:4.12.verse: It is to be expected of one who is wary of penalties, who sees danger in penalties, that he will be released from all penalties.”

an2.2:1.1.verse: “Monks, there are these two exertions that are hard to maintain in the world.

an2.2:1.3.verse: The exertion of laypeople living at home for the sake of producing cloth, almsfood, lodging, & medicinal requisites for curing the sick. And the exertion of those who have gone forth from home for the sake of relinquishing all acquisitions.

an2.2:1.4.verse: “These are the two exertions that are hard to maintain in the world.

an2.2:2.1.verse: “Of these two exertions, this is the foremost: the exertion for the sake of relinquishing all acquisitions.

an2.2:2.3.verse: ‘We will exert ourselves in the exertion for the sake of relinquishing all acquisitions.’

an2.2:2.4.verse: That’s how you should train yourselves.”

an2.5:1.1.verse: “Monks, I have known two qualities through experience:

an2.5:1.2.verse: discontent with regard to skillful qualities and unrelenting exertion.

an2.5:1.4.verse: ‘Gladly would I let the flesh & blood in my body dry up, leaving just the skin, tendons, & bones, but if I have not attained what can be reached through manly firmness, manly persistence, manly striving, there will be no relaxing my persistence.’

an2.5:1.5.verse: From this heedfulness of mine was attained awakening. From this heedfulness of mine was attained the unexcelled freedom from bondage.

an2.5:1.6.verse: “You, too, monks, should relentlessly exert yourselves, (thinking,)

an2.5:1.7.verse: ‘Gladly would we let the flesh & blood in our bodies dry up, leaving just the skin, tendons, & bones, but if we have not attained what can be reached through manly firmness, manly persistence, manly striving, there will be no relaxing our persistence.’ You, too, in no long time

an2.5:1.8.verse: will enter & remain in the supreme goal of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness, directly knowing & realizing it for yourselves in the here & now.
