an2.62:2.7.verse: And a middle or a junior mendicant also thinks:

an2.62:2.8.verse: ‘No mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior, should admonish me;

an2.62:2.9.verse: and I shouldn’t admonish any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior.

an2.62:2.10.verse: If a mendicant—whether senior, middle, or junior—were to admonish me, they wouldn’t be sympathetic, and I’d bother them by saying “No!” And anyway I wouldn’t deal with it even if I saw what I did wrong.’

an2.62:2.12.verse: That’s what it’s like living with bad people; that’s how bad people live together.

an2.62:3.1.verse: What is it like living with good people? How do good people live together?

an2.62:3.2.verse: It’s when a senior mendicant thinks:

an2.62:3.3.verse: ‘Any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior, should admonish me;

an2.62:3.4.verse: and I should admonish any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior.

an2.62:3.5.verse: If a mendicant—whether senior, middle, or junior—were to admonish me, they’d be sympathetic, so I wouldn’t bother them, but say “Thank you!” And I’d deal with it when I saw what I did wrong.’

an2.62:3.7.verse: And a middle or a junior mendicant also thinks:

an2.62:3.8.verse: ‘Any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior, may admonish me;

an2.62:3.9.verse: and I’ll admonish any mendicant, whether senior, middle, or junior.

an2.62:3.10.verse: If a mendicant—whether senior, middle, or junior—were to admonish me, they’d be sympathetic, so I wouldn’t bother them, but say “Thank you!” And I’d deal with it when I saw what I did wrong.’

an2.62:3.12.verse: That’s what it’s like living with good people; that’s how good people live together.”

an2.63:1.1.verse: “In any disciplinary issue where on both sides the endless talk, contempt for each other’s views, resentment, bitterness, and exasperation is not settled, you can expect that this disciplinary issue

an2.63:1.2.verse: will lead to lasting acrimony and enmity, and the mendicants will not live comfortably.

an2.63:2.1.verse: In any disciplinary issue where on both sides the endless talk, contempt for each other’s views, resentment, bitterness, and exasperation is well settled, you can expect that this disciplinary issue

an2.63:2.2.verse: won’t lead to lasting acrimony and enmity, and the mendicants will live comfortably.”

an2.75:1.3.verse: Pleasure with enjoyment as its object & pleasure with equanimity as its object.

an2.75:1.5.verse: And the foremost of these two pleasures is pleasure with equanimity as its object.”

an2.64:1.1.verse: “There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.

an2.64:1.3.verse: The happiness of laypeople, and the happiness of renunciates.

an2.64:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of happiness.

an2.64:1.5.verse: The better of these two kinds of happiness is the happiness of renunciates.”

an2.65:1.1.verse: “There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.

an2.65:1.3.verse: Sensual happiness and the happiness of renunciation.

an2.65:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of happiness.

an2.65:1.5.verse: The better of these two kinds of happiness is the happiness of renunciation.”

an2.66:1.1.verse: “There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.

an2.66:1.3.verse: The happiness of attachments, and the happiness of no attachments.

an2.66:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of happiness.

an2.66:1.5.verse: The better of these two kinds of happiness is the happiness of no attachments.”

an2.67:1.1.verse: “There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.

an2.67:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of happiness.

an2.67:1.5.verse: The better of these two kinds of happiness is the happiness of no defilements.”

an2.68:1.1.verse: “There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.

an2.68:1.3.verse: Happiness of the flesh and happiness not of the flesh.

an2.68:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of happiness.

an2.68:1.5.verse: The better of these two kinds of happiness is happiness not of the flesh.”

an2.69:1.1.verse: “There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.

an2.69:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of happiness.

an2.69:1.5.verse: The better of these two kinds of happiness is noble happiness.”

an2.70:1.1.verse: “There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.

an2.70:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of happiness.

an2.70:1.5.verse: The better of these two kinds of happiness is mental happiness.”

an2.71:1.1.verse: “There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.

an2.71:1.3.verse: Happiness with rapture and happiness free of rapture.

an2.71:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of happiness.

an2.71:1.5.verse: The better of these two kinds of happiness is happiness free of rapture.”

an2.72:1.1.verse: “There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.

an2.72:1.3.verse: Happiness with pleasure and happiness with equanimity.

an2.72:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of happiness.

an2.72:1.5.verse: The better of these two kinds of happiness is happiness with equanimity.”

an2.73:1.1.verse: “There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.

an2.73:1.3.verse: The happiness of immersion and the happiness without immersion.

an2.73:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of happiness.

an2.73:1.5.verse: The better of these two kinds of happiness is the happiness of immersion.”

an2.74:1.1.verse: “There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.

an2.74:1.3.verse: Happiness that relies on rapture and happiness that relies on freedom from rapture.

an2.74:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of happiness.

an2.74:1.5.verse: The better of these two kinds of happiness is happiness that relies on freedom from rapture.”

an2.75:1.1.verse: “There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.

an2.75:1.3.verse: Happiness that relies on pleasure and happiness that relies on equanimity.

an2.75:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of happiness.

an2.75:1.5.verse: The better of these two kinds of happiness is happiness that relies on equanimity.”

an2.76:1.1.verse: “There are, mendicants, these two kinds of happiness.

an2.76:1.3.verse: Happiness that relies on form and happiness that relies on the formless.

an2.76:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of happiness.

an2.76:1.5.verse: The better of these two kinds of happiness is happiness that relies on the formless.”

an2.77:1.1.verse: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with a basis, not without a basis.

an2.77:1.2.verse: By giving up that basis, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

an2.78:1.1.verse: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with a source, not without a source.

an2.78:1.2.verse: By giving up that source, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

an2.79:1.1.verse: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with a cause, not without a cause.

an2.79:1.2.verse: By giving up that cause, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

an2.80:1.1.verse: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with conditions, not without conditions.

an2.80:1.2.verse: By giving up those conditions, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

an2.81:1.1.verse: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with a reason, not without a reason.

an2.81:1.2.verse: By giving up that reason, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

an2.82:1.1.verse: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with form, not without form.

an2.82:1.2.verse: By giving up that form, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

an2.83:1.1.verse: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with feeling, not without feeling.

an2.83:1.2.verse: By giving up that feeling, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

an2.84:1.1.verse: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with perception, not without perception.

an2.84:1.2.verse: By giving up that perception, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

an2.85:1.1.verse: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with consciousness, not without consciousness.

an2.85:1.2.verse: By giving up that consciousness, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

an2.86:1.1.verse: “Bad, unskillful qualities, mendicants, arise with a conditioned basis, not without a conditioned basis.

an2.86:1.2.verse: By giving up that conditioned basis, those bad, unskillful qualities do not occur.”

an2.87:1.3.verse: Freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom.

an2.91:1.3.verse: Views favoring existence and views favoring nonexistence.

an2.94:1.3.verse: Being hard to admonish and having bad friends.

an2.95:1.3.verse: Being easy to admonish and having good friends.

an2.96:1.3.verse: Skill in the elements and skill in application of mind.

an2.97:1.3.verse: Skill in offenses and skill in resolving offenses.

an2.98:1.3.verse: The one who takes up a burden that hasn’t fallen to him, and the one who doesn’t take up a burden that has.
One who carries the burden of what has not come to pass, and one who doesn’t carry the burden of what has come to pass.

an2.99:1.3.verse: One who doesn’t carry the burden of what has not come to pass, and one who carries the burden of what has come to pass.

an2.99:1.4.verse: These are the two who are astute.”

an2.100:1.3.verse: One who perceives what is unallowable as allowable, and one who perceives what is allowable as unallowable.

an2.101:1.3.verse: One who perceives what is unallowable as unallowable, and one who perceives what is allowable as allowable.

an2.101:1.4.verse: These are the two who are astute.”

an2.102:1.3.verse: One who perceives a non-offense as an offense, and one who perceives an offense as a non-offense.

an2.103:1.3.verse: One who perceives a non-offense as a non-offense, and one who perceives an offense as an offense.

an2.103:1.4.verse: These are the two who are astute.”

an2.104:1.3.verse: One who perceives what is not the teaching as the teaching, and one who perceives the teaching as not the teaching.

an2.105:1.3.verse: One who perceives the teaching as the teaching, and one who perceives what is not the teaching as not the teaching.

an2.105:1.4.verse: These are the two who are astute.”

an2.106:1.3.verse: One who perceives what is not the training as the training, and one who perceives what is the training as not the training.

an2.107:1.3.verse: One who perceives what is not the training as not the training, and one who perceives what is the training as the training.

an2.107:1.4.verse: These are the two who are astute.”

an2.108:1.3.verse: One who is remorseful over something they shouldn’t be, and one who isn’t remorseful over something they should be.

an2.108:1.4.verse: These are the two whose defilements grow.”

an2.109:1.3.verse: One who isn’t remorseful over something they shouldn’t be, and one who is remorseful over something they should be.

an2.109:1.4.verse: These are the two whose defilements don’t grow.”

an2.110:1.3.verse: One who perceives what is unallowable as allowable, and one who perceives what is allowable as unallowable.

an2.110:1.4.verse: These are the two whose defilements grow.”

an2.111:1.3.verse: One who perceives what is unallowable as unallowable, and one who perceives what is allowable as allowable.

an2.111:1.4.verse: These are the two whose defilements don’t grow.”

an2.112:1.3.verse: One who perceives an offense as a non-offense, and one who perceives a non-offense as an offense.

an2.112:1.4.verse: These are the two whose defilements grow.”

an2.113:1.3.verse: One who perceives an offense as an offense, and one who perceives a non-offense as a non-offense.

an2.113:1.4.verse: These are the two whose defilements don’t grow.”

an2.114:1.3.verse: One who perceives what is not the teaching as the teaching, and one who perceives the teaching as not the teaching.

an2.114:1.4.verse: These are the two whose defilements grow.”

an2.115:1.3.verse: One who perceives the teaching as the teaching, and one who perceives what is not the teaching as not the teaching.

an2.115:1.4.verse: These are the two whose defilements don’t grow.”

an2.116:1.3.verse: One who perceives what is not the training as the training, and one who perceives what is the training as not the training.

an2.116:1.4.verse: These are the two whose defilements grow.”

an2.117:1.3.verse: One who perceives what is not the training as not the training, and one who perceives what is the training as the training.

an2.117:1.4.verse: These are the two whose defilements don’t grow.”

an2.118:0.2.verse: 11. Hopes That Are Hard to Give Up

an2.119:1.1.verse: “Monks, these two people are hard to find in the world.

an2.119:1.3.verse: The one who is first to do a kindness, and the one who is grateful for a kindness done and feels obligated to repay it.

an2.119:1.4.verse: These two people are hard to find in the world.”

an2.121:1.1.verse: “Monks, these two persons rarely have enough.

an2.121:1.3.verse: One who piles [hoards] gain & gain, and one who spends [squanders] gain & gain.

an2.121:1.4.verse: These two persons rarely have enough.”

an2.125:1.1.verse: “Monks, there are these two conditions for the arising of wrong view.

an2.125:1.3.verse: The voice of another and inappropriate attention.

an2.125:1.4.verse: These are the two conditions for the arising of wrong view.”

an2.126:1.1.verse: “Monks, there are these two conditions for the arising of right view.

an2.126:1.3.verse: The voice of another and appropriate attention.

an2.126:1.4.verse: These are the two conditions for the arising of right view.”

an2.118:0.2.verse: The Chapter on Hopes That Are Hard to Give Up

an2.118:1.1.verse: “These two hopes are hard to give up.

an2.118:1.3.verse: The hope for wealth and the hope for long life.

an2.118:1.4.verse: These are two hopes that are hard to give up.”

an2.119:1.1.verse: “These two individuals are rare in the world.

an2.119:1.3.verse: One who takes the initiative, and one who is grateful and thankful.

an2.119:1.4.verse: These are the two individuals who are rare in the world.”

an2.120:1.1.verse: “These two individuals are rare in the world.

an2.120:1.3.verse: One who is satisfied, and one who satisfies others.

an2.120:1.4.verse: These are the two individuals who are rare in the world.”

an2.121:1.1.verse: “These two individuals are hard to satisfy in the world.

an2.121:1.3.verse: One who continually hoards wealth, and one who continually wastes wealth.

an2.121:1.4.verse: These are the two individuals who are hard to satisfy in the world.”

an2.122:1.1.verse: “These two individuals are easy to satisfy in the world.

an2.122:1.3.verse: One who does not continually hoard wealth, and one who does not continually waste wealth.

an2.122:1.4.verse: These are the two individuals who are easy to satisfy in the world.”

an2.123:1.1.verse: “There are two conditions for the arising of greed.

an2.123:1.3.verse: The feature of beauty and irrational application of mind.

an2.123:1.4.verse: These are the two conditions for the arising of greed.”

an2.124:1.1.verse: “There are two conditions for the arising of hate.

an2.124:1.3.verse: The feature of harshness and irrational application of mind.

an2.124:1.4.verse: These are the two conditions for the arising of hate.”

an2.125:1.1.verse: “There are two conditions for the arising of wrong view.

an2.125:1.3.verse: The voice of another and irrational application of mind.

an2.125:1.4.verse: These are the two conditions for the arising of wrong view.”

an2.126:1.1.verse: “There are two conditions for the arising of right view.

an2.126:1.3.verse: The voice of another and rational application of mind.

an2.126:1.4.verse: These are the two conditions for the arising of right view.”

an2.127:1.3.verse: A light offense and a heavy offense.

an2.128:1.3.verse: An offense with corrupt intention and an offense without corrupt intention.

an2.129:1.3.verse: A curable offense and an incurable offense.

an2.135:1.1.verse: “Endowed with two qualities, the fool—incompetent, a person of no integrity—keeps himself injured & impaired. He’s blameworthy, open to being blamed by the observant, & generates much demerit.

an2.135:1.3.verse: “Without investigating it, without examining it, he shows confidence in a matter that merits skepticism.

an2.135:1.4.verse: Without investigating it, without examining it, he shows skepticism toward a matter that merits confidence.

an2.135:1.5.verse: “Endowed with these two qualities, the fool—incompetent, a person of no integrity—keeps himself injured & impaired. He’s blameworthy, open to being blamed by the observant, & generates much demerit.

an2.135:2.1.verse: “Endowed with two qualities, the wise person—competent, a person of integrity—keeps himself uninjured & unimpaired. He’s blameless, not open to being blamed by the observant, & generates much merit.

an2.135:2.3.verse: “Investigating it, examining it, he shows skepticism toward a matter that merits skepticism.

an2.135:2.4.verse: Investigating it, examining it, he shows confidence in a matter that merits confidence.

an2.135:2.5.verse: “Endowed with these two qualities, the wise person—competent, a person of integrity—keeps himself uninjured & unimpaired. He’s blameless, not open to being blamed by the observant, & generates much merit.”

an2.130:1.2.verse: ‘May I be like Sāriputta and Moggallāna!’

an2.130:1.3.verse: These are a standard and a measure for my monk disciples, that is, Sāriputta and Moggallāna.”

an2.131:1.2.verse: ‘May I be like the nuns Khemā and Uppalavaṇṇā!’

an2.131:1.3.verse: These are a standard and a measure for my nun disciples, that is, the nuns Khemā and Uppalavaṇṇā.”

an2.132:1.2.verse: ‘May I be like the householder Citta and Hatthaka of Āḷavī!’

an2.132:1.3.verse: These are a standard and a measure for my male lay followers, that is, the householder Citta and Hatthaka of Āḷavī.”

an2.133:1.2.verse: ‘May I be like the laywomen Khujjuttarā and Veḷukaṇṭakī, Nanda’s mother!’

an2.133:1.3.verse: These are a standard and a measure for my female lay disciples, that is, the laywomen Khujjuttarā and Veḷukaṇṭakī, Nanda’s mother.”

an2.134:1.1.verse: “When a foolish, incompetent untrue person has two qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

an2.134:1.3.verse: Without examining or scrutinizing, they praise those deserving of criticism

an2.134:1.4.verse: and they criticize those deserving of praise.

an2.134:1.5.verse: When a foolish, incompetent untrue person possesses these two qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

an2.134:2.1.verse: When an astute, competent true person has two qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.

an2.134:2.3.verse: After examining and scrutinizing, they criticize those deserving of criticism

an2.134:2.4.verse: and they praise those deserving of praise.

an2.134:2.5.verse: When an astute, competent true person possesses these two qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.”

an2.135:1.1.verse: “When a foolish, incompetent untrue person has two qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

an2.135:1.3.verse: Without examining or scrutinizing, they arouse faith in things that are dubious,

an2.135:1.4.verse: and they don’t arouse faith in things that are inspiring.

an2.135:1.5.verse: When a foolish, incompetent untrue person possesses these two qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

an2.135:2.1.verse: When an astute, competent true person has two qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.

an2.135:2.3.verse: After examining or scrutinizing, they don’t arouse faith in things that are dubious,

an2.135:2.4.verse: and they do arouse faith in things that are inspiring.

an2.135:2.5.verse: When an astute, competent true person possesses these two qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.”

an2.136:1.1.verse: “When a foolish, incompetent untrue person acts wrongly toward two people they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

an2.136:1.4.verse: When a foolish, incompetent untrue person acts wrongly toward these two people they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

an2.145:1.3.verse: Riches in things of the flesh and riches in the teaching.

an2.146:1.3.verse: Enjoyment of things of the flesh and enjoyment of the teaching.

an2.146:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of enjoyment.

an2.147:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of sharing.

an2.148:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of inclusion.

an2.150:1.4.verse: These are the two kinds of sympathy.

an2.153:1.5.verse: The better of these two quests is the quest for the teaching.”

an2.225-229:1.4.verse: When they have these two things, some people—when their body breaks up, after death—are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

an2.230-279:1.1.verse: “These two things are unskillful … are skillful … are blameworthy … are blameless … have suffering as outcome … have happiness as outcome … result in suffering … result in happiness … are hurtful … are not hurtful.

an2.230-279:1.4.verse: These are the two things that are not hurtful.”

an2.280:0.2.verse: The Chapter of Abbreviated Texts on Monastic Law

an2.280:1.1.verse: “For two reasons the Realized One laid down training rules for his disciples.

an2.280:1.3.verse: For the well-being and comfort of the Saṅgha … For keeping difficult individuals in check and for the comfort of good-hearted mendicants … For restraining defilements that affect this life and protecting against defilements that affect lives to come … For restraining threats to this life and protecting against threats to lives to come … For restraining faults that affect this life and protecting against faults that affect lives to come … For restraining hazards that affect this life and protecting against hazards that affect lives to come … For restraining unskillful qualities that affect this life and protecting against unskillful qualities that affect lives to come … Out of sympathy for laypeople and for breaking up factions of mendicants with corrupt wishes … For inspiring confidence in those without it, and increasing confidence in those who have it … For the continuation of the true teaching and the support of the training.

an2.280:1.4.verse: These are the two reasons why the Realized One laid down training rules for his disciples.”

an2.281-309:1.1.verse: “For two reasons the Realized One laid down for his disciples the monastic code … the recitation of the monastic code … the suspension of the recitation of the monastic code … the invitation to admonish … the setting aside of the invitation to admonish … the disciplinary act of condemnation … placing under dependence … banishment … reconciliation … debarment … probation … being sent back to the beginning … penance … reinstatement … restoration … removal … ordination … an act with a motion … an act with a motion and one announcement … an act with a motion and three announcements … laying down what was not previously laid down … amending what was laid down … the settling of a disciplinary matter by the following methods: face-to-face … through recollection … because of past insanity … acting according to what has been admitted … majority decision … further penalty …  covering over as if with grass.

an2.281-309:1.3.verse: For the well-being and comfort of the Saṅgha … For keeping difficult individuals in check and for the comfort of good-hearted mendicants … For restraining defilements that affect this life and protecting against defilements that affect lives to come … For restraining threats to this life and protecting against threats to lives to come … For restraining faults that affect this life and protecting against faults that affect lives to come … For restraining hazards that affect this life and protecting against hazards that affect lives to come … For restraining unskillful qualities that affect this life and protecting against unskillful qualities that affect lives to come … Out of sympathy for laypeople and for breaking up factions of mendicants with corrupt wishes … For inspiring confidence in those without it, and increasing confidence in those who have it … For the continuation of the true teaching and the support of the training.

an2.281-309:1.4.verse: These are the two reasons why the Realized One laid down the settlement of a disciplinary matter by covering over with grass for his disciples.”

an2.310-319:0.2.verse: The Chapter of Abbreviated Texts Beginning with Greed

an2.310-319:1.1.verse: “For insight into greed, two things should be developed.

an2.310-319:1.4.verse: For insight into greed, these two things should be developed.”

an2.310-319:2.1.verse: “For the complete understanding … finishing … giving up … ending … vanishing … fading away … cessation … giving away … letting go of greed, two things should be developed.”

an2.320-479:1.1.verse: “Of hate … delusion … anger … acrimony … disdain … contempt … jealousy … stinginess … deceit … deviousness … obstinacy … aggression … conceit … arrogance … vanity … negligence … for insight … complete understanding … finishing … giving up … ending … vanishing … fading away … cessation … giving away … letting go … two things should be developed.

an2.320-479:1.4.verse: For the letting go of negligence, these two things should be developed.”

an2.320-479:2.1.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

an2.320-479:2.2.verse: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

an2.320-479:2.4.verse: The Book of the Twos is finished.

an3.1:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

an3.1:1.5.verse: “Yes, lord,” the monks responded to him.

an3.1:2.1.verse: “Monks, whatever dangers arise all arise from a fool, and not from a wise person.

an3.1:2.2.verse: Whatever disasters arise all arise from a fool, and not from a wise person.

an3.1:2.3.verse: Whatever troubles arise all arise from a fool, and not from a wise person.

an3.1:2.4.verse: “Just as a fire, released from a house of reeds or a house of grass, burns even gabled houses, plastered inside & out, draft-free, with close-fitting doors & windows shut against the wind;

an3.1:2.5.verse: in the same way, whatever dangers arise all arise from a fool, and not from a wise person.

an3.1:2.6.verse: Whatever disasters arise all arise from a fool, and not from a wise person.

an3.1:2.7.verse: Whatever troubles arise all arise from a fool and not from a wise person.

an3.1:3.1.verse: “Thus, monks, a fool brings danger; a wise person brings no danger.

an3.1:3.2.verse: A fool brings disasters; a wise person brings no disasters.

an3.1:3.3.verse: A fool brings trouble; a wise person brings no trouble.

an3.1:3.4.verse: “There is no danger from a wise person. There are no disasters from a wise person. There is no trouble from a wise person.

an3.1:4.2.verse: ‘We will avoid the three things that, endowed with which, one is to be recognized as a fool. We will undertake & maintain the three things that, endowed with which, one is to be recognized as a wise person.’

an3.1:4.3.verse: That’s how you should train yourselves.”

an3.1:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

an3.1:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

an3.1:2.1.verse: “Whatever dangers there are, all come from the foolish, not from the astute.

an3.1:2.2.verse: Whatever perils there are, all come from the foolish, not from the astute.

an3.1:2.3.verse: Whatever hazards there are, all come from the foolish, not from the astute.

an3.1:2.4.verse: It’s like a fire that spreads from a hut made of reeds or grass, and burns down even a bungalow, plastered inside and out, draft-free, with doors fastened and windows shuttered.

an3.1:2.5.verse: In the same way, whatever dangers there are, all come from the foolish, not from the astute.

an3.1:2.6.verse: Whatever perils there are, all come from the foolish, not from the astute.

an3.1:2.7.verse: Whatever hazards there are, all come from the foolish, not from the astute.

an3.1:3.1.verse: So, the fool is dangerous, but the astute person is safe.

an3.1:3.2.verse: The fool is perilous, but the astute person is not.

an3.1:3.3.verse: The fool is hazardous, but the astute person is not.

an3.1:3.4.verse: There’s no danger, peril, or hazard that comes from the astute.

an3.1:4.1.verse: So you should train like this:

an3.1:4.2.verse: ‘We will shun the three things by which a fool is known, and we will proceed having undertaken the three things by which an astute person is known.’

an3.2:1.1.verse: “Monks, a fool is characterized by his/her actions. A wise person is characterized by his/her actions. It is through the activities of one’s life that one’s discernment shines.

an3.2:1.2.verse: “A person endowed with three things is to be recognized as a fool.

an3.2:1.4.verse: Bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct.

an3.2:1.5.verse: A person endowed with these three things is to be recognized as a fool.

an3.2:2.1.verse: “A person endowed with three things is to be recognized as a wise person.

an3.2:2.3.verse: Good bodily conduct, good verbal conduct, good mental conduct.

an3.2:2.4.verse: A person endowed with these three things is to be recognized as a wise person.

an3.2:3.2.verse: ‘We will avoid the three things that, endowed with which, one is to be recognized as a fool. We will undertake & maintain the three things that, endowed with which, one is to be recognized as a wise person.’

an3.2:3.3.verse: That’s how you should train yourselves.”

an3.2:1.1.verse: “A fool is characterized by their deeds, and an astute person is characterized by their deeds, for wisdom shines in its traces.

an3.2:1.2.verse: A fool is known by three things.

an3.2:1.4.verse: Bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

an3.2:1.5.verse: These are the three things by which a fool is known.

an3.2:2.1.verse: An astute person is known by three things.

an3.2:2.3.verse: Good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

an3.2:2.4.verse: These are the three things by which an astute person is known.

an3.2:3.1.verse: So you should train like this:

an3.2:3.2.verse: ‘We will shun the three things by which a fool is known, and we will proceed having undertaken the three things by which an astute person is known.’

an3.3:1.1.verse: “There are these three characteristics, signs, and manifestations of a fool.

an3.3:1.3.verse: A fool thinks poorly, speaks poorly, and acts poorly.

an3.3:1.4.verse: If a fool didn’t think poorly, speak poorly, and act poorly, then how would the astute know of them:

an3.3:1.5.verse: ‘This worthy one is a fool, an untrue person’?

an3.3:1.6.verse: But since a fool does think poorly, speak poorly, and act poorly, then the astute do know of them:

an3.3:1.7.verse: ‘This worthy one is a fool, an untrue person’.

an3.3:1.8.verse: These are the three characteristics, signs, and manifestations of a fool.

an3.3:2.1.verse: There are these three characteristics, signs, and manifestations of an astute person.

an3.3:2.3.verse: An astute person thinks well, speaks well, and acts well.

an3.3:2.4.verse: If an astute person didn’t think well, speak well, and act well, then how would the astute know of them:

an3.3:2.5.verse: ‘This worthy one is astute, a true person’?

an3.3:2.6.verse: But since an astute person does think well, speak well, and act well, then the astute do know of them:

an3.3:2.7.verse: ‘This worthy one is astute, a true person’.

an3.3:2.8.verse: These are the three characteristics, signs, and manifestations of an astute person.

an3.4:1.1.verse: “A fool is known by three things.

an3.4:1.3.verse: They don’t recognize when they’ve made a mistake. When they do recognize it they don’t deal with it properly. And when someone else confesses a mistake to them, they don’t accept it properly.

an3.4:1.4.verse: These are the three things by which a fool is known.

an3.4:2.1.verse: An astute person is known by three things.

an3.4:2.3.verse: They recognize when they’ve made a mistake. When they recognize it they deal with it properly. And when someone else confesses a mistake to them, they accept it properly.

an3.4:2.4.verse: These are the three things by which an astute person is known.

an3.5:1.1.verse: “Monks, a person endowed with three qualities is to be recognized as a fool.

an3.5:1.3.verse: He formulates a question inappropriately. He answers a question inappropriately. When another answers a question appropriately—having chosen circumscribed, coherent words & phrases—he doesn’t approve of it.

an3.5:1.4.verse: A person endowed with these three qualities is to be recognized as a fool.

an3.5:2.1.verse: “Monks, a person endowed with three qualities is to be recognized as a wise person.

an3.5:2.3.verse: He formulates a question appropriately. He answers a question appropriately. When another answers a question appropriately—having chosen circumscribed, coherent words & phrases—he approves of it.

an3.5:2.4.verse: A person endowed with these three qualities is to be recognized as a wise person.”

an3.5:1.1.verse: “A fool is known by three things.

an3.5:1.3.verse: They ask a question irrationally. They answer a question irrationally. And when someone else answers a question rationally—with well-rounded, coherent, and relevant words and phrases—they disagree with it.

an3.5:1.4.verse: These are the three things by which a fool is known.

an3.5:2.1.verse: An astute person is known by three things.

an3.5:2.3.verse: They ask a question rationally. They answer a question rationally. And when someone else answers a question rationally—with well-rounded, coherent, and relevant words and phrases—they agree with it.

an3.5:2.4.verse: These are the three things by which an astute person is known.

an3.6:1.1.verse: “A fool is known by three things.

an3.6:1.3.verse: Unskillful deeds by way of body, speech, and mind.

an3.6:1.4.verse: These are the three things by which a fool is known.

an3.6:2.1.verse: An astute person is known by three things.

an3.6:2.3.verse: Skillful deeds by way of body, speech, and mind.

an3.6:2.4.verse: These are the three things by which an astute person is known.

an3.7:1.1.verse: “A fool is known by three things.

an3.7:1.3.verse: Blameworthy deeds by way of body, speech, and mind. … An astute person is known by blameless deeds by way of body, speech, and mind. …”

an3.8:1.1.verse: “A fool is known by three things.

an3.8:1.3.verse: Hurtful deeds by way of body, speech, and mind. … An astute person is known by kind deeds by way of body, speech, and mind.

an3.8:1.4.verse: These are the three things by which an astute person is known.

an3.8:2.1.verse: So you should train like this:

an3.8:2.2.verse: ‘We will shun the three qualities by which a fool is known, and we will proceed having undertaken the three qualities by which an astute person is known.’

an3.9:1.1.verse: “When a foolish, incompetent, untrue person has three qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

an3.9:1.3.verse: Bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

an3.9:1.4.verse: When a foolish, incompetent untrue person possesses these three qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

an3.9:2.1.verse: When an astute, competent true person has three qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.

an3.9:2.3.verse: Good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

an3.9:2.4.verse: When an astute, competent true person possesses these three qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.”

an3.10:1.1.verse: “Monks, when one is endowed with three qualities, without abandoning three impurities, then as if one had been carried off, one would thus be placed in hell.

an3.10:1.3.verse: One is unvirtuous and hasn’t abandoned the impurity of being unvirtuous.

an3.10:1.4.verse: One is envious and hasn’t abandoned the impurity of envy.

an3.10:1.5.verse: One is stingy and hasn’t abandoned the impurity of stinginess.

an3.10:1.6.verse: When one is endowed with these three qualities, without abandoning these three impurities, then as if one had been carried off, one would thus be placed in hell.

an3.10:2.1.verse: “Monks, when one is endowed with three qualities, having abandoned three impurities, then as if one had been carried off, one would thus be placed in heaven.

an3.10:2.3.verse: One is virtuous and has abandoned the impurity of being unvirtuous.

an3.10:2.4.verse: One is not envious and has abandoned the impurity of envy.

an3.10:2.5.verse: One is not stingy and has abandoned the impurity of stinginess.

an3.10:2.6.verse: When one is endowed with these three qualities, having abandoned these three impurities, then as if one had been carried off, one would thus be placed in heaven.”

an3.10:1.1.verse: “Anyone who has three qualities, and has not given up three stains, is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an3.10:1.3.verse: They’re unethical, and haven’t given up the stain of immorality.

an3.10:1.4.verse: They’re jealous, and haven’t given up the stain of jealousy.

an3.10:1.5.verse: They’re stingy, and haven’t given up the stain of stinginess.

an3.10:1.6.verse: Anyone who possesses these three qualities, and has not given up these three stains, is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an3.10:2.1.verse: Anyone who has three qualities, and has given up three stains, is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an3.10:2.3.verse: They’re ethical, and have given up the stain of immorality.

an3.10:2.4.verse: They’re not jealous, and have given up the stain of jealousy.

an3.10:2.5.verse: They’re not stingy, and have given up the stain of stinginess.

an3.10:2.6.verse: Anyone who possesses these three qualities, and has given up these three stains, is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an3.11:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a well-known mendicant with three qualities is acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

an3.11:1.3.verse: They encourage deeds of body and speech, as well as principles, that aren’t in line with good qualities.

an3.11:1.4.verse: A well-known mendicant who possesses these three qualities is acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

an3.11:2.1.verse: A well-known mendicant with three qualities is acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

an3.11:2.3.verse: They encourage deeds of body and speech, as well as principles, that are in line with good qualities.

an3.11:2.4.verse: A well-known mendicant who possesses these three qualities is acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”

an3.12:1.1.verse: “Monks, these three things are to be remembered by a head-anointed noble-warrior king throughout life.

an3.12:1.4.verse: This is the first thing that is to be remembered by a head-anointed noble-warrior king throughout life.

an3.12:2.1.verse: “Then again, the place where he was head-anointed as a noble-warrior king:

an3.12:2.2.verse: This is the second thing that is to be remembered by a head-anointed noble-warrior king throughout life.

an3.12:3.1.verse: “Then again, the place where, having won the battle, he then emerged victorious and ruled at the head of the battle:

an3.12:3.2.verse: This is the third thing that is to be remembered by a head-anointed noble-warrior king throughout life.

an3.12:3.3.verse: “These, monks, are the three things to be remembered by a head-anointed noble-warrior king throughout life.

an3.12:4.1.verse: “In the same way, these three things are to be remembered by a monk throughout life.

an3.12:4.3.verse: “The place where, shaving off his hair & beard, clothing himself in the ochre robe, he goes forth from the home life into homelessness:

an3.12:4.4.verse: This is the first thing that is to be remembered by a monk throughout life.

an3.12:5.1.verse: “Then again, the place where he discerns, as it has come to be, ‘This is stress’ … ‘This is the origination of stress’ … ‘This is the cessation of stress’ … ‘This is the path of practice leading to the cessation of stress’:

an3.12:5.2.verse: This is the second thing that is to be remembered by a monk throughout life.

an3.12:6.1.verse: “Then again, the place where, through the ending of effluents, he enters & remains in the effluent-free awareness-release & discernment-release, directly knowing & realizing it for himself right in the here-&-now:

an3.12:6.2.verse: This is the third thing that is to be remembered by a monk throughout life.

an3.12:6.3.verse: “These, monks, are the three things to be remembered by a monk throughout life.”

an3.12:1.1.verse: “An anointed aristocratic king should commemorate three places as long as he lives.

an3.12:2.1.verse: The place he was anointed as king.

an3.12:3.1.verse: The place where he won victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.

an3.12:3.3.verse: These are the three places an anointed king should commemorate as long as he lives.

an3.12:4.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant should commemorate three places as long as they live.

an3.12:4.3.verse: The place where the mendicant shaved off their hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and went forth from the lay life to homelessness.

an3.12:5.1.verse: The place where the mendicant truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

an3.12:6.1.verse: The place where the mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an3.12:6.3.verse: These are the three places a mendicant should commemorate as long as they live.”

an3.13:1.1.verse: “These three individuals are found in the world.

an3.13:1.3.verse: The hopeless, the hopeful, and the one who has done away with hope.

an3.13:1.4.verse: And what, mendicants, is a hopeless individual?

an3.13:1.5.verse: It’s when an individual is reborn in a low family—a family of corpse-workers, bamboo-workers, hunters, chariot-makers, or scavengers—poor, with little to eat or drink, where life is tough, and food and shelter are hard to find.

an3.13:1.6.verse: And they’re ugly, unsightly, deformed, sickly—one-eyed, crippled, lame, or half-paralyzed. They don’t get to have food, drink, clothes, and vehicles; garlands, fragrances, and makeup; or bed, house, and lighting.

an3.13:1.8.verse: ‘They say the aristocrats have anointed the aristocrat named so-and-so as king.’

an3.13:1.10.verse: ‘Oh, when will the aristocrats anoint me too as king?’

an3.13:1.11.verse: This is called a hopeless individual.

an3.13:2.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is a hopeful individual?

an3.13:2.2.verse: It’s when someone is the eldest son of an anointed aristocratic king. He has not yet been anointed, but is eligible, and has been confirmed in the succession.

an3.13:2.4.verse: ‘They say that the aristocrats have anointed the aristocrat named so-and-so as king.’

an3.13:2.6.verse: ‘Oh, when will the aristocrats anoint me too as king?’

an3.13:2.7.verse: This is called a hopeful individual.

an3.13:3.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is an individual who has done away with hope?

an3.13:3.2.verse: It’s when a king has been anointed.

an3.13:3.4.verse: ‘They say that the aristocrats have anointed the aristocrat named so-and-so as king.’

an3.13:3.6.verse: ‘Oh, when will the aristocrats anoint me too as king?’

an3.13:3.8.verse: Because the former hope he had to be anointed has now died down.

an3.13:3.9.verse: This is called an individual who has done away with hope.

an3.13:3.10.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.

an3.13:4.1.verse: In the same way, these three individuals are found among the mendicants.

an3.13:4.3.verse: The hopeless, the hopeful, and the one who has done away with hope.

an3.13:4.4.verse: And what, mendicants, is a hopeless individual?

an3.13:4.5.verse: It’s when an individual is unethical, of bad qualities, filthy, with suspicious behavior, underhand, no true ascetic or spiritual practitioner—though claiming to be one—rotten inside, festering, and depraved.

an3.13:4.7.verse: ‘They say that the mendicant named so-and-so has realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’

an3.13:4.9.verse: ‘Oh, when will I too realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with my own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’

an3.13:4.10.verse: This is called a hopeless individual.

an3.13:5.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is a hopeful individual?

an3.13:5.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, of good character.

an3.13:5.4.verse: ‘They say that the mendicant named so-and-so has realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’

an3.13:5.6.verse: ‘Oh, when will I too realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with my own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’

an3.13:5.7.verse: This is called a hopeful individual.

an3.13:6.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is an individual who has done away with hope?

an3.13:6.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant is a perfected one, who has ended all defilements.

an3.13:6.4.verse: ‘They say that the mendicant named so-and-so has realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’

an3.13:6.6.verse: ‘Oh, when will I too realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with my own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’

an3.13:6.8.verse: Because the former hope they had to be freed has now died down.

an3.13:6.9.verse: This is called an individual who has done away with hope.

an3.13:6.10.verse: These are the three individuals found among the mendicants.”

an3.14:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, even a wheel-turning monarch, a just and principled king, does not wield power without having their own king.”

an3.14:1.2.verse: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha:

an3.14:1.3.verse: “But who is the king of the wheel-turning monarch, the just and principled king?”

an3.14:1.4.verse: “It is principle, monk,” said the Buddha.

an3.14:1.5.verse: “Monk, a wheel-turning monarch provides just protection and security for his court, relying only on principle—honoring, respecting, and venerating principle, having principle as his flag, banner, and authority.

an3.14:2.1.verse: He provides just protection and security for his aristocrats, vassals, troops, brahmins and householders, people of town and country, ascetics and brahmins, beasts and birds.

an3.14:2.2.verse: When he has done this, he wields power only in a principled manner.

an3.14:2.3.verse: And this power cannot be undermined by any human enemy.

an3.14:3.1.verse: In the same way, monk, a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, a just and principled king, provides just protection and security regarding bodily actions, relying only on principle—honoring, respecting, and venerating principle, having principle as his flag, banner, and authority.

an3.14:3.2.verse: ‘This kind of bodily action should be cultivated. This kind of bodily action should not be cultivated.’

an3.14:4.1.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One … provides just protection and security regarding verbal actions, saying:

an3.14:4.2.verse: ‘This kind of verbal action should be cultivated. This kind of verbal action should not be cultivated.’ … And regarding mental actions:

an3.14:4.3.verse: ‘This kind of mental action should be cultivated. This kind of mental action should not be cultivated.’

an3.14:5.1.verse: And when a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha has provided just protection and security regarding actions of body, speech, and mind, he rolls forth the supreme Wheel of Dhamma.

an3.14:5.2.verse: And that wheel cannot be rolled back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.”

an3.15:1.1.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Vārāṇasī in the Deer Park at Isipatana.

an3.15:1.4.verse: “Yes, lord,” the monks responded to him.

an3.15:2.1.verse: “Once, monks, there was a king named Pacetana.

an3.15:2.2.verse: One day King Pacetana said to his chariot maker,

an3.15:2.3.verse: ‘My good chariot maker, in six months time from now a battle will take place.

an3.15:2.4.verse: Can you make me a new pair of chariot wheels?’

an3.15:2.5.verse: “‘Yes, your majesty, I can,’ the chariot maker replied to the king.

an3.15:2.6.verse: “Then in six months minus six days the chariot maker finished one wheel.

an3.15:2.8.verse: ‘In six days time from now the battle will take place. Will the pair of chariot wheels be finished?’

an3.15:2.9.verse: “‘Your majesty, in these six months minus six days, I have finished one wheel.’

an3.15:2.10.verse: ‘But can you finish the second wheel in these six days?’

an3.15:2.11.verse: ‘Yes, your majesty, I can,’ the chariot maker replied to the king. Then, after finishing the second wheel in six days, the chariot maker took the pair of wheels to the king and, on arrival, said to him,

an3.15:2.12.verse: ‘Here is your new pair of chariot wheels all finished, your majesty.’

an3.15:2.13.verse: “‘And what is the difference between your wheel that took six months minus six days to finish, and your wheel that took six days to finish?

an3.15:2.14.verse: I don’t see any difference between them at all.’

an3.15:2.15.verse: “‘There is a difference between them, your majesty.

an3.15:3.1.verse: Then the chariot maker took the chariot wheel that took six days to finish and set it rolling.

an3.15:3.2.verse: Going as far as its momentum carried it, it twirled around and around and fell to the ground.

an3.15:3.3.verse: But then he took the chariot wheel that took six months minus six days to finish and set it rolling.

an3.15:3.4.verse: Going as far as its momentum carried it, it stood still as if fixed on an axle.

an3.15:4.1.verse: “‘Now what is the reason, my good chariot maker, what is the cause, why the chariot wheel that took six days to finish, when set rolling, goes as far as its momentum carries it and then, twirling around and around, falls to the ground?

an3.15:4.2.verse: And what is the reason, what is the cause, why the chariot wheel that took six months minus six days to finish, when set rolling, goes as far as its momentum carries it and then stands still as if fixed on an axle?’

an3.15:4.3.verse: “‘Your majesty, as for the wheel that took six days to finish, its rim is crooked, with faults & flaws. Its spokes are crooked, with faults & flaws. Its hub is crooked, with faults & flaws.

an3.15:4.4.verse: Because its rim… spokes… (&) hub are crooked, with faults & flaws, when set rolling it goes as far as its momentum carries it and then, twirling around and around, falls to the ground.

an3.15:4.5.verse: But as for the wheel that took six months minus six days to finish, its rim is not crooked, with no faults or flaws. Its spokes are not crooked, with no faults or flaws. Its hub is not crooked, with no faults or flaws.

an3.15:4.6.verse: Because its rim… spokes… (&) hub are not crooked, with no faults or flaws, when set rolling it goes as far as its momentum carries it and then stands still as if fixed on an axle.’

an3.15:5.1.verse: “Now, monks, the thought may occur to you that

an3.15:5.2.verse: the chariot maker on that occasion was someone else,

an3.15:5.3.verse: but it shouldn’t be seen in that way.

an3.15:5.4.verse: I myself was the chariot maker on that occasion.

an3.15:5.5.verse: I was skilled in dealing with the crookedness, the faults, the flaws of wood.

an3.15:5.6.verse: Now I am a worthy one, rightly self-awakened, skilled in dealing with the crookedness, faults, & flaws of bodily action; skilled in dealing with the crookedness, faults, & flaws of verbal action; skilled in dealing with the crookedness, faults, & flaws of mental action.

an3.15:5.7.verse: “Any monk or nun in whom the crookedness, faults, & flaws of bodily action are not abandoned; the crookedness, faults, & flaws of verbal action are not abandoned; the crookedness, faults, & flaws of mental action are not abandoned has fallen away from this Dhamma & Vinaya, just like the wheel that took six days to finish.

an3.15:6.1.verse: But any monk or nun in whom the crookedness, faults, & flaws of bodily action are abandoned; the crookedness, faults, & flaws of verbal action are abandoned; the crookedness, faults, & flaws of mental action are abandoned stands firm in this Dhamma & Vinaya, just like the wheel that took six months minus six days to finish.

an3.15:7.2.verse: ‘We will abandon crookedness, faults, & flaws in bodily action. We will abandon crookedness, faults, & flaws in verbal action. We will abandon crookedness, faults, & flaws in mental action.’

an3.15:7.3.verse: That’s how you should train yourselves.”

an3.15:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

an3.15:1.2.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

an3.15:2.1.verse: “Once upon a time, there was a king named Pacetana.

an3.15:2.2.verse: Then King Pacetana addressed his chariot-maker,

an3.15:2.3.verse: ‘In six months’ time, my good chariot-maker, there will be a battle.

an3.15:2.4.verse: Are you able to make me a new pair of wheels?’

an3.15:2.5.verse: ‘I can, Your Majesty,’ replied the chariot-maker.

an3.15:2.6.verse: Then, when it was six days less than six months later, the chariot-maker had finished one wheel.

an3.15:2.7.verse: Then King Pacetana addressed his chariot-maker,

an3.15:2.8.verse: ‘In six days’ time there will be a battle. Is my new pair of wheels finished?’

an3.15:2.9.verse: ‘Now that it is six days less than six months, Your Majesty, I have finished one wheel.’

an3.15:2.10.verse: ‘Are you able to finish the second wheel in these six days?’

an3.15:2.11.verse: Saying, ‘I can, Your Majesty,’ the chariot-maker finished the second wheel in six days. Taking the pair of wheels he went up to King Pacetana, and said this to the king,

an3.15:2.12.verse: ‘Your Majesty, these are your two new wheels, finished.’

an3.15:2.13.verse: ‘But, my good chariot-maker, what is the difference between the wheel that was finished in six days less than six months, and the wheel finished in just six days?

an3.15:2.14.verse: Because I can’t see any difference between them.’

an3.15:2.15.verse: ‘But, Your Majesty, there is a difference.

an3.15:3.1.verse: Then the chariot-maker rolled forth the wheel that had been finished in six days.

an3.15:3.2.verse: It rolled as far as the original impetus took it, then wobbled and fell down.

an3.15:3.3.verse: Then he rolled forth the wheel that had been finished in six days less than six months.

an3.15:3.4.verse: It rolled as far as the original impetus took it, then stood still as if fixed to an axle.

an3.15:4.1.verse: ‘But what is the cause, my good chariot-maker, what is the reason why the wheel that was finished in six days wobbled and fell,

an3.15:4.2.verse: while the one that was finished in six days less than six months stood still as if fixed to an axle?’

an3.15:4.3.verse: ‘The wheel that was finished in six days, Your Majesty, is crooked, flawed, and defective in rim, spoke, and hub.

an3.15:4.4.verse: That’s why it wobbled and fell.

an3.15:4.5.verse: The wheel that was finished in six days less than six months, Your Majesty, is not crooked, flawed, and defective in rim, spoke, and hub.

an3.15:4.6.verse: That’s why it stood still as if fixed to an axle.’

an3.15:5.2.verse: ‘Surely that chariot-maker must have been someone else at that time?’

an3.15:5.3.verse: But you should not see it like that.

an3.15:5.4.verse: I myself was the chariot-maker at that time.

an3.15:5.5.verse: Then I was skilled in the crooks, flaws, and defects of wood.

an3.15:5.6.verse: Now that I am a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, I am skilled in the crooks, flaws, and defects of actions by body, speech, and mind.

an3.15:5.7.verse: Whatever monk or nun has not given up the crooks, flaws, and defects of body, speech, and mind has fallen from the teaching and training, just like the wheel that was finished in six days.

an3.15:6.1.verse: Whatever monk or nun has given up the crooks, flaws, and defects of body, speech, and mind is established in the teaching and training, just like the wheel that was finished in six days less than six months.

an3.15:7.1.verse: So you should train like this:

an3.15:7.2.verse: ‘We will give up the crooks, flaws, and defects of body, speech, and mind.’

an3.16:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has three things their practice is a sure bet, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.

an3.16:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant guards the sense doors, eats in moderation, and is dedicated to wakefulness.

an3.16:2.1.verse: And how does a mendicant guard the sense doors?

an3.16:2.2.verse: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

an3.16:2.3.verse: If the faculty of sight were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of sight, and achieving its restraint.

an3.16:2.4.verse: When they hear a sound with their ears …

an3.16:2.5.verse: When they smell an odor with their nose …

an3.16:2.6.verse: When they taste a flavor with their tongue …

an3.16:2.7.verse: When they feel a touch with their body …

an3.16:2.8.verse: When they know an idea with their mind, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

an3.16:2.9.verse: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of mind, and achieving its restraint.

an3.16:2.10.verse: That’s how a mendicant guards the sense doors.

an3.16:3.1.verse: And how does a mendicant eat in moderation?

an3.16:3.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant reflects rationally on the food that they eat:

an3.16:3.3.verse: ‘Not for fun, indulgence, adornment, or decoration, but only to sustain this body, to avoid harm, and to support spiritual practice. In this way, I shall put an end to old discomfort and not give rise to new discomfort, and I will have the means to keep going, blamelessness, and a comfortable abiding.’

an3.16:3.4.verse: That’s how a mendicant eats in moderation.

an3.16:4.1.verse: And how is a mendicant dedicated to wakefulness?

an3.16:4.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant practices walking and sitting meditation by day, purifying their mind from obstacles. In the first watch of the night, they continue to practice walking and sitting meditation. In the middle watch, they lie down in the lion’s posture—on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other—mindful and aware, and focused on the time of getting up. In the last watch, they get up and continue to practice walking and sitting meditation, purifying their mind from obstacles.

an3.16:4.3.verse: This is how a mendicant is dedicated to wakefulness.

an3.16:4.4.verse: When a mendicant possesses these three things their practice is a sure bet, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.”

an3.17:1.1.verse: “These three things, mendicants, lead to hurting yourself, hurting others, and hurting both.

an3.17:1.3.verse: Bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

an3.17:1.4.verse: These are three things that lead to hurting yourself, hurting others, and hurting both.

an3.17:2.1.verse: These three things, mendicants, don’t lead to hurting yourself, hurting others, or hurting both.

an3.17:2.3.verse: Good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

an3.17:2.4.verse: These are three things that don’t lead to hurting yourself, hurting others, or hurting both.”

an3.18:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, if wanderers who follow another religion were to ask you:

an3.18:1.2.verse: ‘Reverend, do you lead the spiritual life with the ascetic Gotama so that you can be reborn in the realm of the gods?’

an3.18:1.3.verse: Being questioned like this, wouldn’t you be horrified, repelled, and disgusted?”

an3.18:1.5.verse: “So it seems that you are horrified, repelled, and disgusted by heavenly lifespan, beauty, happiness, glory, and sovereignty.

an3.18:1.6.verse: How much more then should you be horrified, embarrassed, and disgusted by bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.”

an3.19:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a shopkeeper who has three factors is unable to acquire more wealth or to increase the wealth they’ve already acquired.

an3.19:1.3.verse: It’s when a shopkeeper doesn’t carefully focus on their work in the morning, at midday, and in the afternoon.

an3.19:1.4.verse: A shopkeeper who has these three factors is unable to acquire more wealth or to increase the wealth they’ve already acquired.

an3.19:2.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant with three qualities is unable to acquire more skillful qualities or to increase the skillful qualities they’ve already acquired.

an3.19:2.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t carefully focus on a meditation subject as a basis of immersion in the morning, at midday, and in the afternoon.

an3.19:2.4.verse: A mendicant who possesses these three qualities is unable to acquire more skillful qualities or to increase the skillful qualities they’ve already acquired.

an3.19:3.1.verse: A shopkeeper who has three factors is able to acquire more wealth or to increase the wealth they’ve already acquired.

an3.19:3.3.verse: It’s when a shopkeeper carefully focuses on their work in the morning, at midday, and in the afternoon.

an3.19:3.4.verse: A shopkeeper who has these three factors is able to acquire more wealth or to increase the wealth they’ve already acquired.

an3.19:4.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant with three qualities is able to acquire more skillful qualities or to increase the skillful qualities they’ve already acquired.

an3.19:4.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant carefully focuses on a meditation subject as a basis of immersion in the morning, at midday, and in the afternoon.

an3.19:4.4.verse: A mendicant who possesses these three qualities is able to acquire more skillful qualities or to increase the skillful qualities they’ve already acquired.”

an3.20:1.1.verse: “Monks, a shopkeeper endowed with three factors will, in no long time, achieve greatness & abundance in terms of wealth.

an3.20:1.3.verse: There is the case where a shopkeeper has a good eye, is astute, & is consummate in his backing.

an3.20:1.4.verse: “And how does a shopkeeper have a good eye?

an3.20:1.5.verse: There is the case where a shopkeeper knows of an item:

an3.20:1.6.verse: ‘This item can be bought at this price and sold at this price; the cost will be this much, and the profit this much.’

an3.20:1.7.verse: This is how a shopkeeper has a good eye.

an3.20:2.2.verse: There is the case where a shopkeeper is skilled in buying & selling an item.

an3.20:2.3.verse: This is how a shopkeeper is astute.

an3.20:3.1.verse: “And how is a shopkeeper consummate in his backing?

an3.20:3.2.verse: There is the case where householders or householders’ sons know of a shopkeeper,

an3.20:3.3.verse: ‘This shopkeeper has a good eye & is astute. He is capable of supporting his wife & children and repaying our investment at regular intervals.’

an3.20:3.5.verse: ‘Here, my friend, having made wealth from this, support your wife & children and repay us at regular intervals.’

an3.20:3.6.verse: This is how a shopkeeper is consummate in his backing.

an3.20:3.7.verse: “A shopkeeper endowed with these three factors will, in no long time, achieve greatness & abundance in terms of wealth.

an3.20:4.1.verse: “Monks, a monk endowed with three factors will, in no long time, achieve greatness & abundance in terms of skillful qualities.

an3.20:4.3.verse: There is the case where a monk has a good eye, is astute, & is consummate in his backing.

an3.20:4.4.verse: “And how does a monk have a good eye?

an3.20:4.5.verse: There is the case where a monk discerns, as it has come to be, that ‘This is stress’… ‘This is the origination of stress’… ‘This is the cessation of stress’… ‘This is the path of practice leading to the cessation of stress.’

an3.20:4.6.verse: This is how a monk has a good eye.

an3.20:5.2.verse: There is the case where a monk keeps his persistence aroused for abandoning unskillful qualities and taking on skillful qualities. He is steadfast, solid in his effort, not shirking his duties with regard to skillful qualities.

an3.20:5.3.verse: This is how a monk is astute.

an3.20:6.1.verse: “And how is a monk consummate in his backing?

an3.20:6.2.verse: There is the case where a monk—approaching at regular intervals those monks who are learned, to whom the tradition has come down, who have memorized the suttas, memorized the Vinaya, memorized the mātikas [lists of Dhamma topics]—asks & questions them,

an3.20:6.3.verse: ‘How is this, venerable sirs? What is the meaning of this?’

an3.20:6.4.verse: Those venerable ones make open what isn’t open, make plain what isn’t plain, dispel doubt on various doubtful points.

an3.20:6.5.verse: This is how a monk is consummate in his backing.

an3.20:6.6.verse: “Monks, a monk endowed with these three factors will, in no long time, achieve greatness & abundance in terms of skillful qualities.”

an3.20:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a shopkeeper who has three factors soon acquires great and abundant wealth.

an3.20:1.3.verse: It’s when a shopkeeper sees clearly, is indefatigable, and has supporters.

an3.20:1.4.verse: And how does a shopkeeper see clearly?

an3.20:1.5.verse: It’s when a shopkeeper knows of a product:

an3.20:1.6.verse: ‘This product is bought at this price and is selling at this price. With this much investment, it’ll bring this much profit.’

an3.20:1.7.verse: That’s how a shopkeeper sees clearly.

an3.20:2.1.verse: And how is a shopkeeper indefatigable?

an3.20:2.2.verse: It’s when a shopkeeper is skilled in buying and selling products.

an3.20:2.3.verse: That’s how a shopkeeper is indefatigable.

an3.20:3.1.verse: And how does a shopkeeper have supporters?

an3.20:3.2.verse: It’s when rich, affluent, and wealthy householders or householders’ children know of him:

an3.20:3.3.verse: ‘This good shopkeeper sees clearly and is indefatigable. They are capable of providing for their wives and children, and paying us back from time to time.’

an3.20:3.4.verse: They deposit money with the shopkeeper, saying:

an3.20:3.5.verse: ‘With this, my good shopkeeper, earn money to provide for your wives and children, and pay us back from time to time.’

an3.20:3.6.verse: That’s how a shopkeeper has supporters.

an3.20:3.7.verse: A shopkeeper who has these three factors soon acquires great and abundant wealth.

an3.20:4.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant with three qualities soon acquires great and abundant skillful qualities.

an3.20:4.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant sees clearly, is indefatigable, and has supporters.

an3.20:4.4.verse: And how does a mendicant see clearly?

an3.20:4.5.verse: It’s when a mendicant truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

an3.20:4.6.verse: That’s how a mendicant sees clearly.

an3.20:5.1.verse: And how is a mendicant indefatigable?

an3.20:5.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They are strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

an3.20:5.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is indefatigable.

an3.20:6.1.verse: And how does a mendicant have supporters?

an3.20:6.2.verse: It’s when from time to time a mendicant goes up to those mendicants who are very learned—inheritors of the heritage, who have memorized the teachings, the monastic law, and the outlines—and asks them questions:

an3.20:6.3.verse: ‘Why, sir, does it say this? What does that mean?’

an3.20:6.4.verse: Those venerables reveal what is hidden, clarify what is unclear, and dispel doubt regarding the many doubtful matters.

an3.20:6.5.verse: That’s how a mendicant has supporters.

an3.20:6.6.verse: A mendicant with these three qualities soon acquires great and abundant skillful qualities.”

an3.21:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

an3.21:1.3.verse: Then Venerable Saviṭṭha and Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

an3.21:1.4.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side and Venerable Sāriputta said to Venerable Saviṭṭha,

an3.21:2.1.verse: “Reverend Saviṭṭha, these three individuals are found in the world.

an3.21:2.3.verse: The direct witness, the one attained to view, and the one freed by faith.

an3.21:2.4.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.

an3.21:2.5.verse: Of these three individuals, who do you believe to be the finest?”

an3.21:3.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, these three individuals are found in the world.

an3.21:3.3.verse: The direct witness, the one attained to view, and the one freed by faith.

an3.21:3.4.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.

an3.21:3.5.verse: Of these three individuals, I believe the individual freed by faith to be finest.

an3.21:3.7.verse: Because this individual’s faculty of faith is extraordinary.”

an3.21:4.2.verse: “Reverend Koṭṭhita, these three people are found in the world.

an3.21:4.4.verse: The direct witness, the one attained to view, and the one freed by faith.

an3.21:4.5.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.

an3.21:4.6.verse: Of these three individuals, who do you believe to be the finest?”

an3.21:5.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, these three individuals are found in the world.

an3.21:5.3.verse: The direct witness, the one attained to view, and the one freed by faith.

an3.21:5.4.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.

an3.21:5.5.verse: Of these three individuals, I believe the direct witness to be finest.

an3.21:5.7.verse: Because this individual’s faculty of immersion is extraordinary.”

an3.21:6.2.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, these three individuals are found in the world.

an3.21:6.4.verse: The direct witness, the one attained to view, and the one freed by faith.

an3.21:6.5.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.

an3.21:6.6.verse: Of these three individuals, who do you believe to be the finest?”

an3.21:7.1.verse: “Reverend Koṭṭhita, these three people are found in the world.

an3.21:7.3.verse: The direct witness, the one attained to view, and the one freed by faith.

an3.21:7.4.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.

an3.21:7.5.verse: Of these three individuals, I believe the individual attained to view to be finest.

an3.21:7.7.verse: Because this individual’s faculty of wisdom is extraordinary.”

an3.21:8.1.verse: Then Sāriputta said to Saviṭṭha and Mahākoṭṭhita,

an3.21:8.2.verse: “Each of us has spoken from the heart.

an3.21:8.3.verse: Come, reverends, let’s go to the Buddha, and tell him about this.

an3.21:8.4.verse: As he answers, so we’ll remember it.”

an3.21:8.6.verse: Then Sāriputta, Saviṭṭha, and Mahākoṭṭhita went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side.

an3.21:8.7.verse: Then Sāriputta told the Buddha of all they had discussed.

an3.21:9.1.verse: “In this matter, Sāriputta, it’s not easy to categorically declare that

an3.21:9.2.verse: one of these three individuals is finest.

an3.21:9.3.verse: In some cases, an individual freed by faith is practicing for perfection, while the direct witness and the one attained to view are once-returners or non-returners.

an3.21:10.1.verse: In this matter, it’s not easy to categorically declare that

an3.21:10.2.verse: one of these three individuals is finest.

an3.21:10.3.verse: In some cases, a direct witness is practicing for perfection, while the one freed by faith and the one attained to view are once-returners or non-returners.

an3.21:11.1.verse: In this matter, it’s not easy to categorically declare that

an3.21:11.2.verse: one of these three individuals is finest.

an3.21:11.3.verse: In some cases, one attained to view is practicing for perfection, while the one freed by faith and the direct witness are once-returners or non-returners.

an3.21:12.1.verse: In this matter, it’s not easy to categorically declare that

an3.21:12.2.verse: one of these three individuals is finest.”

an3.22:1.1.verse: “There are these three types of sick people to be found existing in the world.

an3.22:1.3.verse: There is the case of the sick person who—regardless of whether he does or does not receive amenable food, regardless of whether he does or does not receive amenable medicine, regardless of whether he does or does not receive proper nursing—will not recover from that illness.

an3.22:2.1.verse: There is the case of the sick person who—regardless of whether he does or does not receive amenable food, regardless of whether he does or does not receive amenable medicine, regardless of whether he does or does not receive proper nursing—will recover from that illness.

an3.22:3.1.verse: There is the case of the sick person who will recover from that illness if he receives amenable food, amenable medicine, & proper nursing, but not if he doesn’t.

an3.22:4.1.verse: “Now, it is because of the sick person who will recover from that illness if he receives amenable food, amenable medicine, & proper nursing—but not if he doesn’t—that food for the sick has been allowed, medicine for the sick has been allowed, nursing for the sick has been allowed.

an3.22:4.2.verse: And it is because there is this sort of sick person that the other sorts of sick persons are to be nursed as well [on the chance that they may actually turn out to need and benefit from such nursing].

an3.22:4.3.verse: “These are the three types of sick people to be found existing in the world.

an3.22:5.1.verse: “In the same way, these three types of people, like the three types of sick people, are to be found existing in the world.

an3.22:5.3.verse: There is the case of the person who—regardless of whether he does or doesn’t get to see the Tathāgata, regardless of whether he does or doesn’t get to hear the Dhamma & Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata—will not alight on the lawfulness, the rightness of skillful qualities.

an3.22:6.1.verse: There is the case of the person who—regardless of whether he does or doesn’t get to see the Tathāgata, regardless of whether he does or doesn’t get to hear the Dhamma & Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata—will alight on the lawfulness, the rightness of skillful qualities.

an3.22:7.1.verse: There is the case of the person who will alight on the lawfulness, the rightness of skillful qualities if he gets to see the Tathāgata and gets to hear the Dhamma & Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, but not if he doesn’t.

an3.22:8.1.verse: “Now, it is because of the person who will alight on the lawfulness, the rightness of skillful qualities if he gets to see the Tathāgata and gets to hear the Dhamma & Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata—but not if he doesn’t—that the teaching of the Dhamma has been allowed.

an3.22:8.2.verse: And it is because there is this sort of person that the other sorts of persons are to be taught the Dhamma as well [on the chance that they may actually turn out to need and benefit from the teaching].

an3.22:8.3.verse: “These are the three types of people, like the three types of sick people, to be found existing in the world.”

an3.22:1.1.verse: “These three patients are found in the world.

an3.22:1.3.verse: In some cases a patient won’t recover from an illness, regardless of whether or not they get suitable food and medicines, and a capable carer.

an3.22:2.1.verse: In some cases a patient will recover from an illness, regardless of whether or not they get suitable food and medicines, and a capable carer.

an3.22:3.1.verse: In some cases a patient can recover from an illness, but only if they get suitable food and medicines, and a capable carer, and not if they don’t get these things.

an3.22:4.1.verse: Now, it’s for the sake of the last patient—who will recover only if they get suitable food and medicines, and a capable carer—that food, medicines, and a carer are prescribed.

an3.22:4.2.verse: But also, for the sake of this patient, the other patients should be looked after.

an3.22:4.3.verse: These are the three kinds of patients found in the world.

an3.22:5.1.verse: In the same way, these three individuals similar to patients are found in the world.

an3.22:5.3.verse: Some people don’t step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities, regardless of whether or not they get to see a Realized One, and to hear the teaching and training that he proclaims.

an3.22:6.1.verse: Some people do step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities, regardless of whether or not they get to see a Realized One, and to hear the teaching and training that he proclaims.

an3.22:7.1.verse: Some people can step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities, but only if they get to see a Realized One, and to hear the teaching and training that he proclaims, and not when they don’t get those things.

an3.22:8.1.verse: Now, it’s for the sake of this last individual that teaching the Dhamma is prescribed, that is, the one who can step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities, but only if they get to see a Realized One, and to hear the teaching and training that he proclaims.

an3.22:8.2.verse: But also, for the sake of this individual, the other people should be taught Dhamma.

an3.22:8.3.verse: These are the three individuals similar to patients found in the world.”
