an3.23:1.1.verse: “These three individuals are found in the world.

an3.23:1.3.verse: Firstly, a certain individual makes hurtful choices by way of body, speech, and mind.

an3.23:1.4.verse: Having made these choices, they’re reborn in a hurtful world,

an3.23:1.6.verse: Touched by hurtful contacts, they experience hurtful feelings that are absolutely painful—like the beings in hell.

an3.23:2.1.verse: Furthermore, another individual makes pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind.

an3.23:2.2.verse: Having made these choices, they are reborn in a pleasing world,

an3.23:2.4.verse: Touched by pleasing contacts, they experience pleasing feelings of absolute happiness—like the gods of universal beauty.

an3.23:3.1.verse: Furthermore, another individual makes both hurtful and pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind.

an3.23:3.2.verse: Having made these choices, they are reborn in a world that is both hurtful and pleasing,

an3.23:3.3.verse: where hurtful and pleasing contacts strike them.

an3.23:3.4.verse: Touched by both hurtful and pleasing contacts, they experience both hurtful and pleasing feelings that are a mixture of pleasure and pain—like humans, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.

an3.23:3.5.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.”

an3.24:1.1.verse: “Monks, these three persons are one’s great benefactors.

an3.24:1.3.verse: “The person through whom one has gone to the Buddha for refuge, has gone to the Dhamma for refuge, has gone to the Saṅgha for refuge:

an3.24:2.1.verse: “Further, the person through whom one discerns, as it has come to be, that ‘This is stress’… ‘This is the origination of stress’… ‘This is the cessation of stress’… ‘This is the path of practice leading to the cessation of stress’:

an3.24:3.1.verse: “Further, the person through whom one—with the ending of effluents—enters & remains in the effluent-free awareness-release & discernment-release, having directly known & realized it for himself right in the here & now:

an3.24:3.3.verse: “These three persons, monks, are one’s great benefactors.

an3.24:4.1.verse: And I tell you: One has no other benefactor greater than these three.

an3.24:4.2.verse: And I tell you, too, that it’s not easy for one to repay these three benefactors by bowing down, by rising up in greeting, by raising one’s hands palm-to-palm in front of the heart, by performing services in line with seniority, or by presenting them with robes, almsfood, lodging, or medicinal requisites used for curing the sick.”

an3.24:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these three individuals are very helpful to another.

an3.24:1.3.verse: The individual who has enabled you to go for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.

an3.24:1.4.verse: This individual is very helpful to another.

an3.24:2.1.verse: Furthermore, the individual who has enabled you to truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

an3.24:2.2.verse: This individual is very helpful to another.

an3.24:3.1.verse: Furthermore, the individual who has enabled you to realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with your own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an3.24:3.2.verse: This individual is very helpful to another.

an3.24:3.3.verse: These are the three individuals who are very helpful to another individual.

an3.24:4.1.verse: And I say that there is no one more helpful to another than these three individuals.

an3.24:4.2.verse: And I also say that it’s not easy to repay these three individuals by bowing down to them, rising up for them, greeting them with cupped palms, and observing proper etiquette for them; or by providing them with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.”

an3.25:1.1.verse: “These three individuals are found in the world.

an3.25:1.3.verse: An individual with a mind like an open sore, an individual with a mind like lightning, and an individual with a mind like diamond.

an3.25:1.4.verse: And who has a mind like an open sore?

an3.25:1.5.verse: It’s an individual who is irritable and bad-tempered.

an3.25:1.6.verse: Even when lightly criticized they lose their temper, becoming annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, and they display annoyance, hate, and bitterness.

an3.25:1.7.verse: They’re like a festering sore, which, when you hit it with a stick or a stone, discharges even more.

an3.25:1.8.verse: In the same way, an individual is irritable and bad-tempered.

an3.25:1.9.verse: Even when lightly criticized they lose their temper, becoming annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, and they display annoyance, hate, and bitterness.

an3.25:1.10.verse: This is called an individual with a mind like an open sore.

an3.25:2.1.verse: And who has a mind like lightning?

an3.25:2.2.verse: It’s an individual who truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

an3.25:2.3.verse: They’re like a person with keen eyes in the dark of the night, who sees by a flash of lightning.

an3.25:2.4.verse: In the same way, an individual truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

an3.25:2.5.verse: This is called an individual with a mind like lightning.

an3.25:3.1.verse: And who has a mind like diamond?

an3.25:3.2.verse: It’s an individual who realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an3.25:3.3.verse: It’s like a diamond, which can’t be cut by anything at all, not even a gem or a stone.

an3.25:3.4.verse: In the same way, an individual realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom … in this very life …

an3.25:3.5.verse: This is called an individual with a mind like diamond.

an3.25:3.6.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.”

an3.26:1.1.verse: “These three individuals are found in the world.

an3.26:1.3.verse: There is an individual you shouldn’t associate with, accompany, or attend.

an3.26:1.4.verse: There is an individual you should associate with, accompany, and attend.

an3.26:1.5.verse: There is an individual you should associate with, accompany, and attend with honor and respect.

an3.26:1.6.verse: Who is the individual you shouldn’t associate with, accompany, or attend?

an3.26:1.7.verse: It’s an individual who is inferior in terms of ethics, immersion, and wisdom.

an3.26:1.8.verse: You shouldn’t associate with, accompany, or attend such an individual, except out of kindness and sympathy.

an3.26:2.1.verse: Who is the individual you should associate with, accompany, and attend?

an3.26:2.2.verse: It’s an individual who is similar in terms of ethics, immersion, and wisdom.

an3.26:2.3.verse: You should associate with, accompany, and attend such an individual.

an3.26:2.5.verse: Thinking, ‘Since our ethical conduct is similar, we can discuss ethics, the conversation will flow, and we’ll both be at ease.

an3.26:2.6.verse: Since our immersion is similar, we can discuss immersion, the conversation will flow, and we’ll both be at ease.

an3.26:2.7.verse: Since our wisdom is similar, we can discuss wisdom, the conversation will flow, and we’ll both be at ease.’

an3.26:2.8.verse: That’s why you should associate with, accompany, and attend such an individual.

an3.26:3.1.verse: Who is the individual you should associate with, accompany, and attend with honor and respect?

an3.26:3.2.verse: It’s an individual who is superior in terms of ethics, immersion, and wisdom.

an3.26:3.3.verse: You should associate with, accompany, and attend such an individual with honor and respect.

an3.26:3.5.verse: Thinking, ‘I’ll fulfill the entire spectrum of ethical conduct I haven’t yet fulfilled, or support with wisdom in every situation the ethical conduct I’ve already fulfilled.

an3.26:3.6.verse: I’ll fulfill the entire spectrum of immersion I haven’t yet fulfilled, or support with wisdom in every situation the immersion I’ve already fulfilled.

an3.26:3.7.verse: I’ll fulfill the entire spectrum of wisdom I haven’t yet fulfilled, or support with wisdom in every situation the wisdom I’ve already fulfilled.’

an3.26:3.8.verse: That’s why you should associate with, accompany, and attend this individual with honor and respect.

an3.26:3.9.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.

an3.26:4.1.verse: A man who associates with an inferior goes downhill,

an3.26:4.2.verse: but associating with an equal, you’ll never decline;

an3.26:4.3.verse: following the best, you’ll quickly rise up,

an3.26:4.4.verse: so you should keep company with people better than you.”

an3.27:1.1.verse: “These three individuals are found in the world.

an3.27:1.3.verse: There is an individual you should be disgusted by, and you shouldn’t associate with, accompany, or attend them.

an3.27:1.4.verse: There is an individual you should regard with equanimity, and you shouldn’t associate with, accompany, or attend them.

an3.27:1.5.verse: There is an individual you should associate with, accompany, and attend.

an3.27:1.6.verse: Who is the individual you should be disgusted by, and not associate with, accompany, or attend?

an3.27:1.7.verse: It’s an individual who is unethical, of bad qualities, filthy, with suspicious behavior, underhand, no true ascetic or spiritual practitioner—though claiming to be one—rotten inside, festering, and depraved.

an3.27:1.8.verse: You should be disgusted by such an individual, and you shouldn’t associate with, accompany, or attend them.

an3.27:1.10.verse: Even if you don’t follow the example of such an individual, you still get a bad reputation:

an3.27:1.11.verse: ‘That individual has bad friends, companions, and associates.’

an3.27:1.12.verse: They’re like a snake that’s been living in a pile of dung. Even if it doesn’t bite, it’ll still rub off on you.

an3.27:1.13.verse: In the same way, even if you don’t follow the example of such an individual, you still get a bad reputation:

an3.27:1.14.verse: ‘That individual has bad friends, companions, and associates.’

an3.27:1.15.verse: That’s why you should be disgusted by such an individual, and you shouldn’t associate with, accompany, or attend them.

an3.27:2.1.verse: Who is the individual you should regard with equanimity, and not associate with, accompany, or attend?

an3.27:2.2.verse: It’s an individual who is irritable and bad-tempered.

an3.27:2.3.verse: Even when lightly criticized they lose their temper, becoming annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, and they display annoyance, hate, and bitterness.

an3.27:2.4.verse: They’re like a festering sore, which, when you hit it with a stick or a stone, discharges even more.

an3.27:2.5.verse: In the same way, someone is irritable and bad-tempered.

an3.27:2.6.verse: They’re like a firebrand of pale-moon ebony, which, when you hit it with a stick or a stone, sizzles and crackles even more.

an3.27:2.7.verse: In the same way, someone is irritable and bad-tempered.

an3.27:2.8.verse: They’re like a sewer, which, when you stir it with a stick or a stone, stinks even more.

an3.27:2.9.verse: In the same way, an individual is irritable and bad-tempered.

an3.27:2.10.verse: Even when lightly criticized they lose their temper, becoming annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, and they display annoyance, hate, and bitterness.

an3.27:2.11.verse: You should regard such an individual with equanimity, and you shouldn’t associate with, accompany, or attend them.

an3.27:2.13.verse: Thinking, ‘They might abuse or insult me, or do me harm.’

an3.27:2.14.verse: That’s why you should regard such an individual with equanimity, and you shouldn’t associate with, accompany, or attend them.

an3.27:3.1.verse: Who is the individual you should associate with, accompany, and attend?

an3.27:3.2.verse: It’s an individual who is ethical, of good character.

an3.27:3.3.verse: You should associate with, accompany, and attend such an individual.

an3.27:3.5.verse: Even if you don’t follow the example of such an individual, you still get a good reputation:

an3.27:3.6.verse: ‘That individual has good friends, companions, and associates.’

an3.27:3.7.verse: That’s why you should associate with, accompany, and attend such an individual.

an3.27:3.8.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.

an3.27:4.1.verse: A man who associates with an inferior goes downhill,

an3.27:4.2.verse: but associating with an equal, you’ll never decline;

an3.27:4.3.verse: following the best, you’ll quickly rise up,

an3.27:4.4.verse: so you should keep company with people better than you.”

an3.28:1.1.verse: “These three individuals are found in the world.

an3.28:1.3.verse: One with speech like dung, one with speech like flowers, and one with speech like honey.

an3.28:1.4.verse: And who has speech like dung?

an3.28:1.5.verse: It’s an individual who is summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness: ‘Please, my man, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ So they deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

an3.28:1.6.verse: This is called an individual with speech like dung.

an3.28:2.1.verse: And who has speech like flowers?

an3.28:2.2.verse: It’s an individual who is summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness: ‘Please, my man, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I see.’ So they don’t deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

an3.28:2.3.verse: This is called an individual with speech like flowers.

an3.28:3.1.verse: And who has speech like honey?

an3.28:3.2.verse: It’s an individual who gives up harsh speech.

an3.28:3.3.verse: They speak in a way that’s mellow, pleasing to the ear, endearing, going to the heart, polite, and likable and agreeable to the people.

an3.28:3.4.verse: This is called an individual with speech like honey.

an3.28:3.5.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.”

an3.29:1.1.verse: “These three individuals are found in the world.

an3.29:1.3.verse: The blind, the one-eyed, and the two-eyed.

an3.29:1.5.verse: It’s someone who doesn’t have the kind of vision that’s needed to acquire more wealth or to increase the wealth they’ve already acquired.

an3.29:1.6.verse: Nor do they have the kind of vision that’s needed to know the difference between qualities that are skillful and unskillful, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, and those with a portion of dark or bright.

an3.29:1.7.verse: This is called a blind individual.

an3.29:2.1.verse: Who is the individual with one eye?

an3.29:2.2.verse: It’s someone who has the kind of vision that’s needed to acquire more wealth and to increase the wealth they’ve already acquired.

an3.29:2.3.verse: But they don’t have the kind of vision that’s needed to know the difference between qualities that are skillful and unskillful, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, and those with a portion of dark or bright.

an3.29:2.4.verse: This is called a one-eyed individual.

an3.29:3.1.verse: Who is the individual with two eyes?

an3.29:3.2.verse: It’s someone who has the kind of vision that’s needed to acquire more wealth and to increase the wealth they’ve already acquired.

an3.29:3.3.verse: And they have the kind of vision that’s needed to know the difference between skillful and unskillful, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, or qualities on the side of dark and bright.

an3.29:3.5.verse: This is called a two-eyed individual.

an3.29:3.6.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.

an3.29:4.3.verse: They hold a losing hand on both counts,

an3.29:4.4.verse: those who are blind, with ruined eyes.

an3.29:6.3.verse: the young man’s skilled at piling up money,

an3.29:6.5.verse: From here they go to hell—

an3.29:7.1.verse: And now the two-eyed is explained,

an3.29:7.4.verse: money acquired by their own hard work.

an3.29:8.1.verse: They give with best of intentions,

an3.29:8.3.verse: They go to a good place,

an3.29:9.3.verse: But you should keep the two-eyed close,

an3.30:1.1.verse: “Monks, there are these three types of persons to be found existing in the world.

an3.30:1.3.verse: The person of upside down discernment, the person of lap discernment, and the person of wide-open discernment.

an3.30:1.4.verse: “And which is the person of upside-down discernment?

an3.30:1.5.verse: There is the case where a person, having gone to a monastery, often listens to the Dhamma in the presence of the monks.

an3.30:1.6.verse: The monks teach him the Dhamma admirable in the beginning, admirable in the middle, admirable in the end. They expound the holy life both in its particulars & in its meaning, entirely perfect, surpassingly pure.

an3.30:1.7.verse: He, while sitting in that seat, doesn’t attend to the beginning of that talk, doesn’t attend to the middle, doesn’t attend to the end.

an3.30:1.8.verse: Having gotten up from that seat, he doesn’t attend to the beginning of that talk, doesn’t attend to the middle, doesn’t attend to the end.

an3.30:1.9.verse: Just as when a pot is turned upside down, water poured there runs off and doesn’t stay;

an3.30:1.10.verse: in the same way, there is the case where a person, having gone to a monastery, often listens to the Dhamma in the presence of the monks.

an3.30:1.11.verse: The monks teach him the Dhamma admirable in the beginning, admirable in the middle, admirable in the end. They expound the holy life both in its particulars & in its meaning, entirely perfect, surpassingly pure.

an3.30:1.12.verse: He, while sitting in that seat, doesn’t attend to the beginning of that talk, doesn’t attend to the middle, doesn’t attend to the end.

an3.30:1.13.verse: Having gotten up from that seat, he doesn’t attend to the beginning of that talk, doesn’t attend to the middle, doesn’t attend to the end.

an3.30:1.14.verse: This is called a person of upside down discernment.

an3.30:2.1.verse: “And which is the person of lap discernment?

an3.30:2.2.verse: There is the case where a person, having gone to a monastery, often listens to the Dhamma in the presence of the monks.

an3.30:2.3.verse: The monks teach him the Dhamma admirable in the beginning, admirable in the middle, admirable in the end. They expound the holy life both in its particulars & in its meaning, entirely perfect, surpassingly pure.

an3.30:2.4.verse: He, while sitting in that seat, attends to the beginning of that talk, attends to the middle, attends to the end.

an3.30:2.5.verse: But having gotten up from that seat, he doesn’t attend to the beginning of that talk, doesn’t attend to the middle, doesn’t attend to the end.

an3.30:2.6.verse: Just as when a person has various foods strewn over his lap—

an3.30:2.7.verse: sesame seeds, husked rice, cakes, & jujubes—

an3.30:2.8.verse: and when getting up, his mindfulness lapsed, he would scatter them;

an3.30:2.9.verse: in the same way, there is the case where a person, having gone to a monastery, often listens to the Dhamma in the presence of the monks.

an3.30:2.10.verse: The monks teach him the Dhamma admirable in the beginning, admirable in the middle, admirable in the end. They expound the holy life both in its particulars & in its meaning, entirely perfect, surpassingly pure.

an3.30:2.11.verse: He, while sitting in that seat, attends to the beginning of that talk, attends to the middle, attends to the end.

an3.30:2.12.verse: But having gotten up from that seat, he doesn’t attend to the beginning of that talk, doesn’t attend to the middle, doesn’t attend to the end.

an3.30:2.13.verse: This is called a person of lap discernment.

an3.30:3.1.verse: “And which is the person of wide open discernment?

an3.30:3.2.verse: There is the case where a person, having gone to a monastery, often listens to the Dhamma in the presence of the monks.

an3.30:3.3.verse: The monks teach him the Dhamma admirable in the beginning, admirable in the middle, admirable in the end. They expound the holy life both in its particulars & in its meaning, entirely perfect, surpassingly pure.

an3.30:3.4.verse: He, while sitting in that seat, attends to the beginning of that talk, attends to the middle, attends to the end.

an3.30:3.5.verse: And having gotten up from that seat, attends to the beginning of that talk, attends to the middle, attends to the end.

an3.30:3.6.verse: Just as when a pot is set right side up, water poured there stays and doesn’t run off;

an3.30:3.7.verse: in the same way, there is the case where a person, having gone to a monastery, often listens to the Dhamma in the presence of the monks.

an3.30:3.8.verse: The monks teach him the Dhamma admirable in the beginning, admirable in the middle, admirable in the end. They expound the holy life both in its particulars & in its meaning, entirely perfect, surpassingly pure.

an3.30:3.9.verse: He, while sitting in that seat, attends to the beginning of that talk, attends to the middle, attends to the end.

an3.30:3.10.verse: And having gotten up from that seat, attends to the beginning of that talk, attends to the middle, attends to the end.

an3.30:3.11.verse: This is called a person of wide open discernment.”

an3.30:3.12.verse: These are the three types of persons to be found existing in the world.

an3.30:4.1.verse: A man of upside down discernment—

an3.30:4.4.verse: in the presence of the monks,

an3.30:5.2.verse: like the beginning, middle, or end of a talk,

an3.30:6.2.verse: is said to be better than that one.

an3.30:6.4.verse: in the presence of the monks,

an3.30:7.1.verse: while sitting in that seat, grasps the words

an3.30:7.2.verse: of the beginning, middle, & end of the talk,

an3.30:7.4.verse: he doesn’t discern anything like that,

an3.30:8.1.verse: But a man of wide open discernment

an3.30:8.2.verse: is said to be better than those ones.

an3.30:8.4.verse: in the presence of the monks,

an3.30:9.1.verse: while sitting in that seat, he grasps the words

an3.30:9.2.verse: of the beginning, middle, & end of the talk.

an3.30:10.2.verse: Practicing the Dhamma in line with the Dhamma,

an3.30:1.1.verse: “These three individuals are found in the world.

an3.30:1.3.verse: One with upside-down wisdom, one with wisdom on their lap, and one with widespread wisdom.

an3.30:1.4.verse: And who is the individual with upside-down wisdom?

an3.30:1.5.verse: It’s an individual who often goes to the monastery to hear the teaching in the presence of the mendicants.

an3.30:1.6.verse: The mendicants teach them Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And they reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

an3.30:1.7.verse: But even while sitting there, that person doesn’t apply the mind to the beginning, middle, or end of the discussion.

an3.30:1.8.verse: And when they rise from their seat, they don’t apply the mind to the beginning, middle, or end of the discussion.

an3.30:1.9.verse: It’s like when a pot full of water is tipped over, so the water drains out and doesn’t stay.

an3.30:1.10.verse: In the same way, an individual often goes to the monastery to hear the teaching in the presence of the mendicants.

an3.30:1.11.verse: The mendicants teach them Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And they reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

an3.30:1.12.verse: But even while sitting there, that person doesn’t apply the mind to the discussion in the beginning, middle, or end.

an3.30:1.13.verse: And when they rise from their seat, they don’t apply the mind to the beginning, middle, or end of the discussion.

an3.30:1.14.verse: This is called an individual with upside-down wisdom.

an3.30:2.1.verse: And who is the individual with wisdom on their lap?

an3.30:2.2.verse: It’s an individual who often goes to the monastery to hear the teaching in the presence of the mendicants.

an3.30:2.3.verse: The mendicants teach them Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And they reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

an3.30:2.4.verse: While sitting there, that person applies the mind to the discussion in the beginning, middle, and end.

an3.30:2.5.verse: But when they rise from their seat, they don’t apply the mind to the beginning, middle, or end of the discussion.

an3.30:2.6.verse: It’s like a person who has different kinds of food crammed on their lap—

an3.30:2.7.verse: such as sesame, rice, sweets, or jujube—

an3.30:2.8.verse: so that if they rise from the seat without mindfulness, everything gets scattered.

an3.30:2.9.verse: In the same way, an individual often goes to the monastery to hear the teaching in the presence of the mendicants.

an3.30:2.10.verse: The mendicants teach them Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And they reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

an3.30:2.11.verse: While sitting there, that person applies the mind to the discussion in the beginning, middle, and end.

an3.30:2.12.verse: But when they rise from their seat, they don’t apply the mind to the beginning, middle, or end of the discussion.

an3.30:2.13.verse: This is called an individual with wisdom on their lap.

an3.30:3.1.verse: And who is the individual with widespread wisdom?

an3.30:3.2.verse: It’s an individual who often goes to the monastery to hear the teaching in the presence of the mendicants.

an3.30:3.3.verse: The mendicants teach them Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And they reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

an3.30:3.4.verse: While sitting there, they apply the mind to the discussion in the beginning, middle, and end.

an3.30:3.5.verse: And when they rise from their seat, they continue to apply the mind to the beginning, middle, or end of the discussion.

an3.30:3.6.verse: It’s like when a pot full of water is set straight, so the water stays and doesn’t drain out.

an3.30:3.7.verse: In the same way, an individual often goes to the monastery to hear the teaching in the presence of the mendicants.

an3.30:3.8.verse: The mendicants teach them Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And they reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

an3.30:3.9.verse: While sitting there, they apply the mind to the discussion in the beginning, middle, and end.

an3.30:3.10.verse: And when they rise from their seat, they continue to apply the mind to the beginning, middle, or end of the discussion.

an3.30:3.11.verse: This is called an individual with widespread wisdom.

an3.30:3.12.verse: These are the three individuals found in the world.

an3.30:4.2.verse: is a simpleton and cannot see,

an3.30:6.1.verse: the individual with wisdom on their lap

an3.30:6.2.verse: is better than that, it’s said;

an3.30:7.1.verse: such a person can only learn

an3.30:7.4.verse: but they’ve only grasped the phrasing,

an3.30:7.5.verse: for when they rise their understanding fails,

an3.30:7.6.verse: and what they’ve learned is lost.

an3.30:8.2.verse: is better than that, it’s said;

an3.30:9.4.verse: and when they’ve grasped the phrasing,

an3.30:10.1.verse: they remember it with the best of intentions.

an3.30:10.3.verse: practicing in line with the teaching,

an3.30:10.4.verse: would make an end of suffering.”

an3.31:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with divinity.

an3.31:1.2.verse: A family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with the first tutors.

an3.31:1.3.verse: A family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with those worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods.

an3.31:1.4.verse: ‘Divinity’ is a term for your parents.

an3.31:1.5.verse: ‘First tutors’ is a term for your parents.

an3.31:1.6.verse: ‘Worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods’ is a term for your parents.

an3.31:1.8.verse: Parents are very helpful to their children, they raise them, nurture them, and show them the world.

an3.31:2.3.verse: They’re worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods from their children,

an3.31:3.2.verse: would revere them and honor them

an3.31:4.3.verse: in this life they’re praised by the astute,

an3.31:4.4.verse: and they depart to rejoice in heaven.”

an3.32:1.1.verse: Then Ven. Ānanda went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, bowed down to him and sat to one side. As he was sitting there, he said to the Blessed One,

an3.32:2.1.verse: “Lord, could it be that a monk would have a concentration-attainment of such a sort that, with regard to this conscious body, he would have no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession, that with regard to all external themes [topics of concentration] he would have no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession,

an3.32:2.2.verse: and that he would enter & remain in the awareness-release & discernment-release in which there is no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession for one entering & remaining in it?”

an3.32:2.3.verse: “It could be, Ānanda, that a monk would have a concentration-attainment of such a sort that, with regard to this conscious body, he would have no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession, that with regard to all external themes [topics of concentration] he would have no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession,

an3.32:2.4.verse: and that he would enter & remain in the awareness-release & discernment-release in which there is no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession for one entering & remaining in it.”

an3.32:3.1.verse: “But how, lord, could a monk have a concentration-attainment of such a sort that, with regard to this conscious body, he would have no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession, that with regard to all external themes [topics of concentration] he would have no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession,

an3.32:3.2.verse: and that he would enter & remain in the awareness-release & discernment-release in which there is no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession for one entering & remaining in it?”

an3.32:4.1.verse: “There is the case, Ānanda, where a monk is percipient in this way:

an3.32:4.2.verse: ‘This is peace, this is exquisite—the pacification of all fabrications; the relinquishing of all acquisitions; the ending of craving; dispassion; cessation; unbinding.’

an3.32:4.3.verse: This is how a monk would have a concentration-attainment of such a sort that, with regard to this conscious body, he would have no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession, that with regard to all external themes [topics of concentration] he would have no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession,

an3.32:4.4.verse: and that he would enter & remain in the awareness-release & discernment-release in which there is no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession for one entering & remaining in it.

an3.32:5.1.verse: “And it was in reference to this that I said, in Puṇṇaka’s Questions in the Pārāyana [Sn 5:3]:

an3.32:6.2.verse: the high & low in the world, for whom there is nothing perturbing in the world—

an3.32:6.4.verse: he, I tell you, has crossed over birth & aging.”

an3.32:1.1.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

an3.32:2.1.verse: “Could it be, sir, that a mendicant might gain a state of immersion such that there’s no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit for this conscious body; and no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit for externally for all signs;

an3.32:2.2.verse: and that they’d live having attained the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit are no more?”

an3.32:2.3.verse: “It could be, Ānanda, that a mendicant gains a state of immersion such that they have no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit for this conscious body; and no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit for externally for all signs;

an3.32:2.4.verse: and that they’d live having attained the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit are no more.”

an3.32:4.2.verse: ‘This is peaceful; this is sublime—that is, the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.’

an3.32:4.3.verse: That’s how, Ānanda, a mendicant might gain a state of immersion such that there’s no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit for this conscious body; and no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit for externally for all signs;

an3.32:4.4.verse: and that they’d live having achieved the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit are no more.

an3.32:5.1.verse: And Ānanda, this is what I was referring to in ‘The Way to the Far Shore’, in ‘The Questions of Puṇṇaka’ when I said:

an3.32:6.1.verse: ‘Having appraised the world high and low,

an3.32:6.2.verse: there is nothing in the world that disturbs them.

an3.32:6.3.verse: Peaceful, unclouded, untroubled, with no need for hope—

an3.32:6.4.verse: they’ve crossed over rebirth and old age, I declare.’”

an3.33:1.1.verse: Then Ven. Sāriputta went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, bowed down to him and sat to one side. As he was sitting there, the Blessed One said to him,

an3.33:1.2.verse: “Sāriputta, I could teach the Dhamma in brief,

an3.33:1.3.verse: I could teach the Dhamma in detail,

an3.33:1.4.verse: I could teach the Dhamma in brief & in detail,

an3.33:1.5.verse: but those who would understand the Dhamma are hard to find.”

an3.33:1.6.verse: “This is the time, Blessed One, this is the time, One Well Gone,

an3.33:1.7.verse: that the Blessed One should teach the Dhamma in brief, should teach the Dhamma in detail, should teach the Dhamma in brief & in detail.

an3.33:1.8.verse: There will be those who would understand.”

an3.33:2.2.verse: ‘There will be no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession with regard to this conscious body. There will be no I-making or mine-making conceit-obsession with regard to all external themes [topics of concentration]. We will enter & remain in the awareness-release & discernment-release where there is no I-making or my-making conceit-obsession for one entering & remaining in it.’

an3.33:2.3.verse: That’s how you should train yourselves.

an3.33:3.1.verse: When there is in a monk no I-making or my-making conceit-obsession with regard to this conscious body, no I-making or my-making conceit-obsession with regard to all external themes, and when he enters & remains in the awareness-release & discernment-release where there is no I-making or my-making conceit-obsession for one entering & remaining in it,

an3.33:3.3.verse: a monk who has cut through craving, has ripped off the fetter, and—from rightly breaking through conceit—has put an end to suffering & stress.

an3.33:3.4.verse: “And it was in reference to this that I said, in Udaka’s Questions in the Pārāyana [Sn 5:13]:

an3.33:4.2.verse: both of sensual desires, & of unhappiness,

an3.33:5.2.verse: with inspection of mental qualities swift in the forefront:

an3.33:5.3.verse: That I call the gnosis of emancipation,

an3.33:1.1.verse: Then Venerable Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

an3.33:1.4.verse: maybe both in brief and in detail.

an3.33:1.5.verse: But it’s hard to find anyone who understands.”

an3.33:1.6.verse: “Now is the time, Blessed One! Now is the time, Holy One!

an3.33:1.7.verse: Let the Buddha teach Dhamma in brief, in detail, and both in brief and in detail.

an3.33:1.8.verse: There will be those who understand the teaching!”

an3.33:2.1.verse: “So, Sāriputta, you should train like this:

an3.33:2.2.verse: ‘There’ll be no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit for this conscious body; and no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit externally for all signs; and we’ll live having achieved the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit are no more.’

an3.33:3.1.verse: When a mendicant has no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit for this conscious body; and no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit externally for all signs; and they live having attained the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit are no more—

an3.33:3.3.verse: a mendicant who has cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit has made an end of suffering.

an3.33:3.4.verse: And Sāriputta, this is what I was referring to in ‘The Way to the Far Shore’, in ‘The Questions of Udaya’ when I said:

an3.33:5.3.verse: this, I declare, is liberation by enlightenment,

an3.34:1.1.verse: “Monks, these three are causes for the origination of actions.

an3.34:1.3.verse: Greed is a cause for the origination of actions. Aversion is a cause for the origination of actions. Delusion is a cause for the origination of actions.

an3.34:2.1.verse: “Any action performed with greed—born of greed, caused by greed, originating from greed: Wherever one’s selfhood [atta-bhāva] turns up, there that action will ripen.

an3.34:2.2.verse: Where that action ripens, there one will experience its fruit, either in this very life that has arisen or further along in the sequence.

an3.34:3.1.verse: “Any action performed with aversion—born of aversion, caused by aversion, originating from aversion: Wherever one’s selfhood turns up, there that action will ripen.

an3.34:3.2.verse: Where that action ripens, there one will experience its fruit, either in this very life that has arisen or further along in the sequence.

an3.34:4.1.verse: “Any action performed with delusion—born of delusion, caused by delusion, originating from delusion: Wherever one’s selfhood turns up, there that action will ripen.

an3.34:4.2.verse: Where that action ripens, there one will experience its fruit, either in this very life that has arisen or further along in the sequence.

an3.34:5.1.verse: “Just as when seeds are not broken, not rotten, not damaged by wind & heat, capable of sprouting, well-buried, planted in well-prepared soil,

an3.34:5.2.verse: and the rain-god would offer good streams of rain:

an3.34:5.3.verse: Those seeds would thus come to growth, increase, & abundance.

an3.34:5.4.verse: In the same way, any action performed with greed—born of greed, caused by greed, originating from greed: Wherever one’s selfhood turns up, there that action will ripen.

an3.34:5.5.verse: Where that action ripens, there one will experience its fruit, either in this very life that has arisen or further along in the sequence.

an3.34:6.2.verse: performed with delusion—born of delusion, caused by delusion, originating from delusion: Wherever one’s selfhood turns up, there that action will ripen.

an3.34:6.3.verse: Where that action ripens, there one will experience its fruit, either in this very life that has arisen or further along in the sequence.

an3.34:6.4.verse: “These are three causes for the origination of actions.

an3.34:7.1.verse: “Now, these three are (further) causes for the origination of actions.

an3.34:7.3.verse: Non-greed is a cause for the origination of actions. Non-aversion is a cause for the origination of actions. Non-delusion is a cause for the origination of actions.

an3.34:8.1.verse: “Any action performed with non-greed—born of non-greed, caused by non-greed, originating from non-greed: When greed is gone, that action is thus abandoned, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising.

an3.34:9.1.verse: “Any action performed with non-aversion—born of non-aversion, caused by non-aversion, originating from non-aversion: When aversion is gone, that action is thus abandoned, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising.

an3.34:10.1.verse: “Any action performed with non-delusion—born of non-delusion, caused by non-delusion, originating from non-delusion: When delusion is gone, that action is thus abandoned, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising.

an3.34:11.1.verse: “Just as when seeds are not broken, not rotten, not damaged by wind & heat, capable of sprouting, well-buried, planted in well-prepared soil,

an3.34:11.2.verse: and a man would burn them with fire

an3.34:11.3.verse: and, burning them with fire, would make them into fine ashes.

an3.34:11.4.verse: Having made them into fine ashes, he would winnow them before a high wind or wash them away in a swift-flowing stream.

an3.34:11.5.verse: Those seeds would thus be destroyed at the root, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising.

an3.34:11.6.verse: “In the same way, any action performed with non-greed—born of non-greed, caused by non-greed, originating from non-greed: When greed is gone, that action is thus abandoned, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising.

an3.34:12.2.verse: performed with non-delusion—born of non-delusion, caused by non-delusion, originating from non-delusion: When delusion is gone, that action is thus abandoned, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development,

an3.34:12.4.verse: “These, monks, are three causes for the origination of action.”

an3.34:13.3.verse: born of greed, born of aversion, & born of delusion,

an3.34:14.3.verse: giving rise to clear knowledge, he sheds

an3.34:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these three sources that give rise to deeds.

an3.34:1.3.verse: Greed, hate, and delusion are sources that give rise to deeds.

an3.34:2.1.verse: Any deed that emerges from greed—born, sourced, and originated from greed—ripens where that new incarnation is born.

an3.34:2.2.verse: And wherever that deed ripens, its result is experienced—either in the present life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

an3.34:3.1.verse: Any deed that emerges from hate—born, sourced, and originated from hate—ripens where that new incarnation is born.

an3.34:3.2.verse: And wherever that deed ripens, its result is experienced—either in the present life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

an3.34:4.1.verse: Any deed that emerges from delusion—born, sourced, and originated from delusion—ripens where that new incarnation is born.

an3.34:4.2.verse: And wherever that deed ripens, its result is experienced—either in the present life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

an3.34:5.1.verse: Suppose some seeds were intact, unspoiled, not weather-damaged, fertile, and well-kept. They’re sown in a well-prepared, productive field,

an3.34:5.2.verse: and the heavens provide plenty of rain.

an3.34:5.3.verse: Then those seeds would grow, increase, and mature.

an3.34:5.4.verse: In the same way, any deed that emerges from greed—born, sourced, and originated from greed—ripens where that new incarnation is born.

an3.34:5.5.verse: And wherever that deed ripens, its result is experienced—either in the present life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

an3.34:6.1.verse: Any deed that emerges from hate …

an3.34:6.2.verse: Any deed that emerges from delusion—born, sourced, and originated from delusion—ripens where that new incarnation is born.

an3.34:6.3.verse: And wherever that deed ripens, its result is experienced—either in the present life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

an3.34:6.4.verse: These are three sources that give rise to deeds.

an3.34:7.1.verse: Mendicants, there are these three sources that give rise to deeds.

an3.34:7.3.verse: Contentment, love, and understanding are sources that give rise to deeds.

an3.34:8.1.verse: Any deed that emerges from contentment—born, sourced, and originated from contentment—is given up when greed is done away with. It’s cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

an3.34:9.1.verse: Any deed that emerges from love—born, sourced, and originated from love—is abandoned when hate is done away with. It’s cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

an3.34:10.1.verse: Any deed that emerges from understanding—born, sourced, and originated from understanding—is abandoned when delusion is done away with. It’s cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

an3.34:11.1.verse: Suppose some seeds were intact, unspoiled, not damaged by wind and sun, fertile, and well-kept.

an3.34:11.2.verse: But someone would burn them with fire,

an3.34:11.4.verse: and whisk away the ashes in a strong wind, or glide them down a swift stream.

an3.34:11.5.verse: Then those seeds would be cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

an3.34:11.6.verse: In the same way, any deed that emerges from contentment—born, sourced, and originated from contentment—is abandoned when greed is done away with. It’s cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

an3.34:12.1.verse: Any deed that emerges from love …

an3.34:12.2.verse: Any deed that emerges from understanding—born, sourced, and originated from understanding—is abandoned when delusion is done away with.

an3.34:12.3.verse: It’s cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

an3.34:12.4.verse: These are three sources that give rise to deeds.

an3.34:13.2.verse: out of greed, hate, or delusion,

an3.34:13.5.verse: are to be experienced right here,

an3.34:14.3.verse: of the outcome of greed, hate, and delusion,

an3.35:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Āḷavī on a spread of leaves by a cattle track in a siṁsapā forest.

an3.35:1.3.verse: Then Hatthaka of Āḷavī, out roaming & rambling for exercise, saw the Blessed One sitting on a spread of leaves by the cattle track in the siṁsapā forest.

an3.35:1.4.verse: On seeing him, he went to him and, on arrival, having bowed down to him, sat to one side. As he was sitting there he said to the Blessed One,

an3.35:1.5.verse: “Lord, I hope the Blessed One has slept in ease.”

an3.35:1.6.verse: “Yes, young man. I have slept in ease.

an3.35:1.7.verse: Of those in the world who sleep in ease, I am one.”

an3.35:2.1.verse: “But cold, lord, is the winter night. The ‘Between-the-Eights’ is a time of snowfall. Hard is the ground trampled by cattle hooves. Thin is the spread of leaves. Sparse are the leaves in the trees. Thin are your ochre robes. And cold blows the Verambhā wind.

an3.35:2.2.verse: Yet still the Blessed One says,

an3.35:2.3.verse: ‘Yes, young man. I have slept in ease.

an3.35:2.4.verse: Of those in the world who sleep in ease, I am one.’”

an3.35:3.1.verse: “In that case, young man, I will question you in return. Answer as you see fit.

an3.35:3.2.verse: Now, what do you think? Suppose a householder or householder’s son has a house with a gabled roof, plastered inside & out, draft-free, with close-fitting door & windows shut against the wind.

an3.35:3.3.verse: Inside he has a throne-like bed spread with a long-fleeced coverlet, a white wool coverlet, an embroidered coverlet, a rug of kadali-deer hide, with a canopy above, & red cushions on either side;

an3.35:3.4.verse: and there a lamp would be burning,

an3.35:3.5.verse: and his four wives, with their many charms, would be attending to him.

an3.35:3.6.verse: Would he sleep in ease, or not?

an3.35:3.7.verse: Or how does this strike you?”

an3.35:3.8.verse: “Yes, lord, he would sleep in ease.

an3.35:3.9.verse: Of those in the world who sleep in ease, he would be one.”

an3.35:4.1.verse: “But what do you think, young man?

an3.35:4.2.verse: Might there arise in that householder or householder’s son any bodily fevers or fevers of mind born of passion so that—burned with those passion-born fevers—he would sleep miserably?”

an3.35:5.1.verse: “As for those passion-born fevers—burned with which the householder or householder’s son would sleep miserably—that passion has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising.

an3.35:6.1.verse: “Now, what do you think, young man?

an3.35:6.2.verse: Might there arise in that householder or householder’s son any bodily fevers or fevers of mind born of aversion so that—burned with those aversion-born fevers—he would sleep miserably?” “Yes, lord.” “As for those aversion-born fevers—burned with which the householder or householder’s son would sleep miserably—that aversion has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising. Therefore he sleeps in ease. “Now, what do you think, young man? Might there arise in that householder or householder’s son any bodily fevers or fevers of mind

an3.35:6.3.verse: born of delusion so that—burned with those delusion-born fevers—he would sleep miserably?”

an3.35:7.1.verse: “As for those delusion-born fevers—burned with which the householder or householder’s son would sleep miserably—that delusion has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising.

an3.35:8.3.verse: who doesn’t adhere to sensual pleasures,

an3.35:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Āḷavī, on a mat of leaves by a cow-path in a rosewood grove.

an3.35:1.3.verse: Then as Hatthaka of Āḷavī was going for a walk he saw the Buddha sitting on that mat of leaves.

an3.35:1.4.verse: He went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said,

an3.35:1.5.verse: “Sir, I trust the Buddha slept well?”

an3.35:1.7.verse: I am one of those who sleep at ease in the world.”

an3.35:2.1.verse: “The winter nights are cold, sir, and it’s the week of mid-winter, when the snow falls. Rough is the ground trampled under the cows’ hooves, and thin is the mat of leaves. The leaves are sparse on the trees, the ocher robes are cold, and cold blows the north wind.

an3.35:2.4.verse: I am one of those who sleep at ease in the world.’”

an3.35:3.1.verse: “Well then, prince, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.

an3.35:3.2.verse: What do you think? Take the case of a householder or his son, who lives in a bungalow, plastered inside and out, draft-free, with door fastened and window shuttered.

an3.35:3.3.verse: His couch is spread with woolen covers—shag-piled, pure white, or embroidered with flowers—and spread with a fine deer hide. It has a canopy above and red pillows at both ends.

an3.35:3.4.verse: An oil lamp is burning there,

an3.35:3.5.verse: while his four wives attend to him in all manner of agreeable ways.

an3.35:3.6.verse: What do you think, prince, would he sleep at ease, or not?

an3.35:3.7.verse: Or how do you see this?”

an3.35:3.9.verse: Of those who sleep at ease in the world, he would be one.”

an3.35:4.2.verse: Is it not possible that a fever born of greed—physical or mental—might arise in that householder or householder’s son, burning him so he sleeps badly?”

an3.35:5.1.verse: “The greed that burns that householder or householder’s son, making them sleep badly, has been cut off at the root by the Realized One, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

an3.35:5.2.verse: That’s why I sleep at ease.

an3.35:6.2.verse: Is it not possible that a fever born of hate …

an3.35:6.3.verse: or a fever born of delusion—physical or mental—might arise in that householder or householder’s son, burning him so he sleeps badly?”

an3.35:7.1.verse: “The delusion that burns that householder or householder’s son, making them sleep badly, has been cut off at the root by the Realized One, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

an3.35:7.2.verse: That’s why I sleep at ease.
