an4.61:4.1.verse: The third thing, having got wealth and fame, is the wish: ‘May I live long, keeping alive for a long time!’

an4.61:5.1.verse: The fourth thing, having got wealth, fame, and long life, is the wish: ‘When my body breaks up, after death, may I be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm!’

an4.61:5.2.verse: These are the four things, which are likable, desirable, and agreeable, but hard to get in the world.

an4.61:6.1.verse: These next four things lead to the getting of those four things.

an4.61:6.3.verse: Accomplishment in faith, ethics, generosity, and wisdom.

an4.61:7.1.verse: And what is accomplishment in faith?

an4.61:7.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

an4.61:7.3.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

an4.61:7.4.verse: This is called accomplishment in faith.

an4.61:8.1.verse: And what is accomplishment in ethics?

an4.61:8.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

an4.61:8.3.verse: This is called accomplishment in ethics.

an4.61:9.1.verse: And what is accomplishment in generosity?

an4.61:9.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

an4.61:9.3.verse: This is called accomplishment in generosity.

an4.61:10.1.verse: And what is accomplishment in wisdom?

an4.61:10.2.verse: When your heart is mastered by covetousness and immoral greed, you do what you shouldn’t, and fail to do what you should.

an4.61:10.3.verse: Your fame and happiness fall to dust.

an4.61:10.4.verse: When your heart is mastered by ill will …

an4.61:10.10.verse: doubt, you do what you shouldn’t, and fail to do what you should.

an4.61:10.11.verse: Your fame and happiness fall to dust.

an4.61:11.1.verse: Knowing that ‘covetousness and immoral greed are corruptions of the mind’, that noble disciple gives them up.

an4.61:11.5.verse: ‘doubt is a corruption of the mind’, that noble disciple gives it up.

an4.61:12.1.verse: When a noble disciple has given up these things,

an4.61:12.6.verse: they’re called ‘a noble disciple of great wisdom, of widespread wisdom, who sees what matters, and is accomplished in wisdom’.

an4.61:12.7.verse: This is called accomplishment in wisdom.

an4.61:12.8.verse: These are the four things that lead to the getting of the four things, which are likable, desirable, and agreeable, but hard to get in the world.

an4.61:13.1.verse: There are four fitting deeds that a noble disciple does with the legitimate wealth he has earned by his efforts and initiative, built up with his own hands, gathered by the sweat of the brow.

an4.61:13.3.verse: To start with, with his legitimate wealth he makes himself happy and pleased, keeping himself properly happy.

an4.61:13.4.verse: He makes his mother and father happy …

an4.61:13.5.verse: He makes his children, partners, bondservants, workers, and staff happy …

an4.61:13.6.verse: He makes his friends and colleagues happy …

an4.61:13.7.verse: This is his first usage within means on a deserved and fitting cause.

an4.61:14.1.verse: Furthermore, with his legitimate wealth he defends himself against threats from such things as fire, flood, rulers, bandits, or unloved heirs.

an4.61:14.3.verse: This is his second usage within means on a deserved and fitting cause.

an4.61:15.1.verse: Furthermore, with his legitimate wealth he makes five spirit-offerings:

an4.61:15.2.verse: to relatives, guests, ancestors, king, and deities.

an4.61:15.3.verse: This is his third expenditure in an appropriate sphere on a deserved and fitting cause.

an4.61:16.1.verse: Furthermore, with his legitimate wealth he establishes an uplifting religious donation for ascetics and brahmins—those who refrain from intoxication and negligence, are settled in patience and gentleness, and who tame, calm, and extinguish themselves—that’s conducive to heaven, ripens in happiness, and leads to heaven.

an4.61:16.2.verse: This is his fourth usage within means on a deserved and fitting cause.

an4.61:17.1.verse: These are the four fitting deeds that a noble disciple does with the legitimate wealth he has earned by his efforts and initiative, built up with his own hands, gathered by the sweat of the brow.

an4.61:17.2.verse: Whatever wealth is spent on something other than these four fitting deeds is said to not be usage within means on a deserved and fitting cause.

an4.61:17.3.verse: But whatever wealth is spent on these four fitting deeds is said to be usage within means on a deserved and fitting cause.

an4.61:18.1.verse: ‘I’ve enjoyed my wealth, supporting those who depend on me;

an4.61:18.5.verse: I have served the ethical and

an4.61:19.4.verse: I don’t regret what I’ve done.’

an4.61:20.1.verse: A mortal man who recollects this

an4.61:20.2.verse: stands firm in the teaching of the noble ones.

an4.61:20.4.verse: and they depart to rejoice in heaven.”

an4.62:1.1.verse: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

an4.62:2.1.verse: “Householder, these four kinds of happiness can be earned by a layperson who enjoys sensual pleasures, depending on time and occasion.

an4.62:2.3.verse: The happiness of ownership, using wealth, debtlessness, and blamelessness.

an4.62:3.1.verse: And what is the happiness of ownership?

an4.62:3.2.verse: It’s when a gentleman owns legitimate wealth that he has earned by his own efforts and initiative, built up with his own hands, gathered by the sweat of the brow.

an4.62:3.3.verse: When he reflects on this, he’s filled with pleasure and happiness.

an4.62:3.4.verse: This is called ‘the happiness of ownership’.

an4.62:4.1.verse: And what is the happiness of using wealth?

an4.62:4.2.verse: It’s when a gentleman uses his legitimate wealth, and makes merit with it.

an4.62:4.3.verse: When he reflects on this, he’s filled with pleasure and happiness.

an4.62:4.4.verse: This is called ‘the happiness of using wealth’.

an4.62:5.1.verse: And what is the happiness of debtlessness?

an4.62:5.2.verse: It’s when a gentleman owes no debt, large or small, to anyone.

an4.62:5.3.verse: When he reflects on this, he’s filled with pleasure and happiness.

an4.62:5.4.verse: This is called ‘the happiness of debtlessness’.

an4.62:6.1.verse: And what is the happiness of blamelessness?

an4.62:6.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has blameless conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

an4.62:6.3.verse: When he reflects on this, he’s filled with pleasure and happiness.

an4.62:6.4.verse: This is called ‘the happiness of blamelessness’.

an4.62:6.5.verse: These four kinds of happiness can be earned by a layperson who enjoys sensual pleasures, depending on time and occasion.

an4.62:7.2.verse: and the extra happiness of possession,

an4.62:7.3.verse: a mortal enjoying the happiness of using wealth,

an4.62:8.1.verse: Discerning clearly, a clever person knows

an4.62:8.3.verse: the other kind is not worth a sixteenth part

an4.63:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with divinity.

an4.63:1.2.verse: A family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with the first tutors.

an4.63:1.3.verse: A family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with the elder gods.

an4.63:1.4.verse: A family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with those worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods.

an4.63:2.1.verse: ‘Divinity’ is a term for your parents.

an4.63:2.2.verse: ‘First tutors’ is a term for your parents.

an4.63:2.3.verse: ‘Elder gods’ is a term for your parents.

an4.63:2.4.verse: ‘Worthy of an offering dedicated to the gods’ is a term for your parents.

an4.63:2.6.verse: Parents are very helpful to their children, they raise them, nurture them, and show them the world.

an4.63:3.3.verse: They’re worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods from their children,

an4.63:4.2.verse: would revere them and honor them

an4.63:5.3.verse: they’re praised in this life by the astute,

an4.63:5.4.verse: and they depart to rejoice in heaven.”

an4.64:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.64:1.3.verse: They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, and lie.

an4.64:1.4.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.64:2.4.verse: astute people don’t praise these things.”

an4.65:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.65:1.3.verse: There are those whose estimation of and confidence in others is based on their appearance, on their voice, on their mortification, and on principle.

an4.65:1.4.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.

an4.65:2.2.verse: and those swayed by a voice,

an4.65:2.3.verse: are full of desire and greed;

an4.65:3.3.verse: the fool shut in on every side,

an4.65:3.4.verse: gets carried away by a voice.

an4.65:4.4.verse: they’re also carried away by a voice.

an4.65:5.4.verse: they don’t get carried away by a voice.”

an4.66:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.66:1.3.verse: The greedy, the hateful, the delusional, and the conceited.

an4.66:1.4.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.

an4.66:2.1.verse: Full of desire for desirable things,

an4.66:3.1.verse: Born of greed, born of hate,

an4.66:4.1.verse: If you act out of these qualities, that’s what you become.

an4.66:4.3.verse: are blind, with no eyes to see,

an4.66:4.4.verse: and they never imagine that this could be so.”

an4.67:1.1.verse: At one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.

an4.67:1.2.verse: Then at that time near Sāvatthī a certain monk was bitten by a snake and died.

an4.67:1.3.verse: Then a great many monks approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, they sat down on one side. While sitting on one side those monks said this to the Fortunate One:

an4.67:1.4.verse: “Here, reverend Sir, near Sāvatthī, a certain monk has been bitten by a snake and has died”.

an4.67:2.1.verse: “Surely, monks, that monk did not suffuse the four royal families of snakes with a mind (full of) friendliness.

an4.67:2.2.verse: For if, monks, that monk had suffused the four royal families of snakes with a mind (full of) friendliness then that monk, monks, would not have been bitten by a snake and died.

an4.67:3.1.verse: Who are the four royal families of snakes?

an4.67:3.2.verse: The Virūpakkha royal family of snakes, the Erāpatha royal family of snakes, the Chabyāputta royal family of snakes, the Kaṇhāgotamaka royal family of snakes.

an4.67:3.3.verse: Surely, monks, that monk did not suffuse these four royal families of snakes with a mind (full of) friendliness.

an4.67:3.4.verse: For if, monks, that monk had suffused these four royal families of snakes with a mind (full of) friendliness, then that monk, monks, would not have been bitten by a snake and died.

an4.67:4.1.verse: I allow you, monks, to suffuse these four royal families of snakes with a mind (full of) friendliness, to guard yourselves, to protect yourselves, to safeguard yourselves.”

an4.67:5.1.verse: I am friendly with the Virūpakkhas,

an4.67:5.2.verse: with the Erāpathas I am friendly,

an4.67:5.3.verse: I am friendly with the Chabyāputtas,

an4.67:6.1.verse: I am friendly with those without feet,

an4.67:6.2.verse: with those with two feet I am friendly,

an4.67:6.3.verse: I am friendly with those with four feet,

an4.67:6.4.verse: with those with many feet I am friendly.

an4.67:7.1.verse: May the one without feet not hurt me,

an4.67:7.2.verse: may the one with two feet not hurt me,

an4.67:7.3.verse: may the one with four feet not hurt me,

an4.67:7.4.verse: may the one with many feet not hurt me.

an4.67:8.1.verse: May all beings, all living creatures,

an4.67:8.2.verse: all who are born, in their entirety,

an4.67:8.4.verse: may nothing bad come to anyone.

an4.67:10.3.verse: I have made this protection, I have made this safeguard,

an4.67:10.6.verse: I revere the seven Perfect Sambuddhas.”

an4.67:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

an4.67:1.2.verse: Now, at that time a monk in Sāvatthī passed away due to a snake bite.

an4.67:1.3.verse: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

an4.67:1.4.verse: “Sir, a monk in Sāvatthī has passed away due to a snake bite.”

an4.67:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, that monk mustn’t have spread a mind of love to the four royal snake families.

an4.67:2.2.verse: If he had, he wouldn’t have died due to a snake bite.

an4.67:3.2.verse: The royal snake families of Virūpakkha, Erāpatha, Chabyāputta, and Kaṇhāgotamaka. …

an4.67:4.1.verse: Mendicants, I urge you to spread a mind of love to the four royal snake families, for your own safety, security, and protection.

an4.67:7.1.verse: May the footless not harm me!

an4.67:7.2.verse: May I not be harmed by the two-footed!

an4.67:7.3.verse: May the four-footed not harm me!

an4.67:7.4.verse: May I not be harmed by the many-footed!

an4.67:8.1.verse: All sentient beings, all living things,

an4.67:8.3.verse: may they see only nice things,

an4.67:8.4.verse: may bad not come to anyone.

an4.67:10.3.verse: I’ve made this safeguard, I’ve made this protection:

an4.67:10.5.verse: And so I revere the Blessed One,

an4.67:10.6.verse: I revere the seven perfectly awakened Buddhas.”

an4.68:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain, not long after Devadatta had left.

an4.68:1.2.verse: There the Buddha spoke to the mendicants about Devadatta:

an4.68:1.3.verse: “Possessions, honor, and popularity came to Devadatta for his own ruin and downfall.

an4.68:4.1.verse: or a reed, all of which bear fruit to their own ruin and downfall …

an4.68:5.1.verse: It’s like a mule, which becomes pregnant to its own ruin and downfall.

an4.68:5.2.verse: In the same way, possessions, honor, and popularity came to Devadatta for his own ruin and downfall.

an4.68:6.1.verse: The banana plant is destroyed by its own fruit,

an4.68:6.2.verse: as are the bamboo and the reed.

an4.69:1.3.verse: The efforts to restrain, to give up, to develop, and to preserve.

an4.69:1.4.verse: And what, mendicants, is the effort to restrain?

an4.69:1.5.verse: It’s when you generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise.

an4.69:1.6.verse: This is called the effort to restrain.

an4.69:2.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is the effort to give up?

an4.69:2.2.verse: It’s when you generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities are given up.

an4.69:2.3.verse: This is called the effort to give up.

an4.69:3.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is the effort to develop?

an4.69:3.2.verse: It’s when you generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities arise.

an4.69:3.3.verse: This is called the effort to develop.

an4.69:4.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is the effort to preserve?

an4.69:4.2.verse: It’s when you generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.

an4.69:4.3.verse: This is called the effort to preserve.

an4.69:5.4.verse: taught by the Kinsman of the Sun.

an4.69:5.5.verse: Any mendicant who keenly applies these

an4.69:5.6.verse: may attain the ending of suffering.”

an4.70:1.1.verse: “At a time when kings are unprincipled, royal officials become unprincipled.

an4.70:1.2.verse: When royal officials are unprincipled, brahmins and householders become unprincipled.

an4.70:1.3.verse: When brahmins and householders are unprincipled, the people of town and country become unprincipled.

an4.70:1.4.verse: When the people of town and country are unprincipled, the courses of the moon and sun become erratic.

an4.70:1.5.verse: … the courses of the stars and constellations …

an4.70:1.8.verse: the seasons and years become erratic.

an4.70:1.9.verse: … the blowing of the winds becomes erratic and chaotic.

an4.70:1.11.verse: … the heavens don’t provide enough rain.

an4.70:1.13.verse: When people eat crops that have ripened erratically, they become short-lived, ugly, weak, and sickly.

an4.70:2.1.verse: At a time when kings are principled, royal officials become principled.

an4.70:2.3.verse: people of town and country become principled.

an4.70:2.4.verse: When the people of town and country are principled, the courses of the sun and moon become regular.

an4.70:2.8.verse: the seasons and years become regular.

an4.70:2.9.verse: … the blowing of the winds becomes regular and orderly.

an4.70:2.11.verse: … the heavens provide plenty of rain.

an4.70:2.12.verse: When the heavens provide plenty of rain, the crops ripen well.

an4.70:2.13.verse: When people eat crops that have ripened well, they become long-lived, beautiful, strong, and healthy.

an4.70:3.2.verse: if the bull goes off course,

an4.70:3.4.verse: because their leader is off course.

an4.70:4.4.verse: what do you expect the rest to do?

an4.70:6.4.verse: what do you expect the rest to do?

an4.70:6.5.verse: The whole country sleeps at ease,

an4.71:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has four things their practice is a sure bet, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.

an4.71:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, learned, energetic, and wise.

an4.71:1.4.verse: When a mendicant possesses these four things their practice is a sure bet, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.”

an4.72:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has four things their practice is a sure bet, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.

an4.72:1.3.verse: Thoughts of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness; and right view.

an4.72:1.4.verse: When a mendicant possesses these four things their practice is a sure bet, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.”

an4.73:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, an untrue person can be known by four qualities.

an4.73:1.3.verse: To start with, an untrue person speaks ill of another even when not asked, let alone when asked.

an4.73:1.4.verse: But when summoned for questioning they speak ill of another in full detail, not leaving anything out.

an4.73:1.5.verse: That’s how to know that this is an untrue person.

an4.73:2.1.verse: Furthermore, an untrue person doesn’t speak well of another even when asked, let alone when not asked.

an4.73:2.2.verse: But when summoned for questioning they speak well of another without giving the full details, leaving many things out.

an4.73:2.3.verse: That’s how to know that this is an untrue person.

an4.73:3.1.verse: Furthermore, an untrue person doesn’t speak ill of themselves even when asked, let alone when not asked.

an4.73:3.2.verse: But when summoned for questioning they speak ill of themselves without giving the full details, leaving many things out.

an4.73:3.3.verse: That’s how to know that this is an untrue person.

an4.73:4.1.verse: Furthermore, an untrue person speaks well of themselves even when not asked, let alone when asked.

an4.73:4.2.verse: But when summoned for questioning they speak well of themselves in full detail, not leaving anything out.

an4.73:4.3.verse: That’s how to know that this is an untrue person.

an4.73:4.4.verse: An untrue person can be known by these four qualities.

an4.73:5.1.verse: A true person can be known by four qualities.

an4.73:5.3.verse: To start with, a true person doesn’t speak ill of another even when asked, let alone when not asked.

an4.73:5.4.verse: But when summoned for questioning they speak ill of another without giving the full details, leaving many things out.

an4.73:5.5.verse: That’s how to know that this is a true person.

an4.73:6.1.verse: Furthermore, a true person speaks well of another even when not asked, let alone when asked.

an4.73:6.2.verse: But when summoned for questioning they speak well of another in full detail, not leaving anything out.

an4.73:6.3.verse: That’s how to know that this is a true person.

an4.73:7.1.verse: Furthermore, a true person speaks ill of themselves even when not asked, let alone when asked.

an4.73:7.2.verse: But when led on by questions they speak ill of themselves in full detail, not leaving anything out.

an4.73:7.3.verse: That’s how to know that this is a true person.

an4.73:8.1.verse: Furthermore, a true person doesn’t speak well of themselves even when asked, let alone when not asked.

an4.73:8.2.verse: But when summoned for questioning they speak well of themselves without giving the full details, leaving many things out.

an4.73:8.3.verse: That’s how to know that this is a true person.

an4.73:8.4.verse: A true person can be known by these four qualities.

an4.73:9.1.verse: It’s like a bride on the day or night she’s first brought to her husband’s home. Right away she sets up a keen sense of conscience and prudence for her mother and father in law, her husband, and even the bondservants, workers, and staff.

an4.73:9.2.verse: But after some time, because of living together and familiarity, she’ll even say to her mother and father in law, or to her husband:

an4.73:9.4.verse: In the same way, on the day or night a mendicant first goes forth from the lay life to homelessness, right away they set up a keen sense of conscience and prudence for the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, and even the monastery workers and novices.

an4.73:9.5.verse: But after some time, because of living together and familiarity, they’ll even say to their tutor or mentor:

an4.73:9.7.verse: So you should train like this:

an4.73:9.8.verse: ‘We will live with hearts like that of a newly wedded bride.’

an4.74:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four things are the best.

an4.74:1.3.verse: The best ethics, immersion, wisdom, and freedom.

an4.74:1.4.verse: These are the four things that are the best.”

an4.75:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four things are the best.

an4.75:1.3.verse: The best form, feeling, perception, and existence.

an4.75:1.4.verse: These are the four things that are the best.”

an4.76:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying between a pair of sal trees in the sal forest of the Mallas at Upavattana near Kusinārā at the time of his full extinguishment.

an4.76:1.2.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

an4.76:2.1.verse: “Perhaps even a single mendicant has doubt or uncertainty regarding the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice. So ask, mendicants! Don’t regret it later, thinking:

an4.76:2.2.verse: ‘We were in the Teacher’s presence and we weren’t able to ask the Buddha a question.’”

an4.76:2.3.verse: When this was said, the mendicants kept silent.

an4.76:3.1.verse: For a second time the Buddha addressed the mendicants: …

an4.76:3.4.verse: For a second time, the mendicants kept silent.

an4.76:4.1.verse: For a third time the Buddha addressed the mendicants: …

an4.76:4.4.verse: For a third time, the mendicants kept silent.

an4.76:5.1.verse: Then the Buddha said to the mendicants:

an4.76:5.2.verse: “Mendicants, perhaps you don’t ask out of respect for the Teacher. So let a friend tell a friend.”

an4.76:5.3.verse: When this was said, the mendicants kept silent.

an4.76:5.4.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha:

an4.76:5.6.verse: I am quite confident that there’s not even a single mendicant in this Saṅgha who has doubt or uncertainty regarding the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice.”

an4.76:6.1.verse: “Ānanda, you speak from faith. But the Realized One knows that there’s not even a single mendicant in this Saṅgha who has doubt or uncertainty regarding the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice.

an4.76:6.2.verse: Even the last of these five hundred mendicants is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

an4.77:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four things are unthinkable. They should not be thought about, and anyone who tries to think about them will go mad or get frustrated.

an4.77:1.5.verse: The domain of one in absorption …

an4.77:1.11.verse: These are the four unthinkable things. They should not be thought about, and anyone who tries to think about them will go mad or get frustrated.”

an4.78:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four ways of purifying a religious donation.

an4.78:1.3.verse: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by the giver, not the recipient.

an4.78:1.4.verse: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by the recipient, not the giver.

an4.78:1.5.verse: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by neither the giver nor the recipient.

an4.78:1.6.verse: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by both the giver and the recipient.

an4.78:2.1.verse: And how is a religious donation purified by the giver, not the recipient?

an4.78:2.2.verse: It’s when the giver is ethical, of good character, but the recipient is unethical, of bad character.

an4.78:3.1.verse: And how is a religious donation purified by the recipient, not the giver?

an4.78:3.2.verse: It’s when the giver is unethical, of bad character, but the recipient is ethical, of good character.

an4.78:4.1.verse: And how is a religious donation purified by neither the giver nor the recipient?

an4.78:4.2.verse: It’s when both the giver and the recipient are unethical, of bad character.

an4.78:5.1.verse: And how is a religious donation purified by both the giver and the recipient?

an4.78:5.2.verse: It’s when both the giver and the recipient are ethical, of good character.

an4.78:5.4.verse: These are the four ways of purifying a religious donation.”

an4.79:1.1.verse: Then Venerable Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

an4.79:1.2.verse: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why for different people the same kind of business undertaking might fail,

an4.79:2.1.verse: “Sāriputta, take a case where someone goes to an ascetic or brahmin and invites them to ask for what they need. But they fail to give what’s requested.

an4.79:2.2.verse: When they’ve passed away from that life, if they’re reborn in this place, whatever business they undertake fails.

an4.79:3.1.verse: Take a case where someone goes to an ascetic or brahmin and invites them to ask for what they need. They give what’s requested, but don’t meet expectations.

an4.79:3.2.verse: When they’ve passed away from that life, if they’re reborn in this place, whatever business they undertake doesn’t meet expectations.

an4.79:4.1.verse: Take a case where someone goes to an ascetic or brahmin and invites them to ask for what they need. They give what’s requested, meeting expectations.

an4.79:4.2.verse: When they’ve passed away from that life, if they’re reborn in this place, whatever business they undertake meets expectations.

an4.79:5.1.verse: Take a case where someone goes to an ascetic or brahmin and invites them to ask for what they need. They give what’s requested, exceeding expectations.

an4.79:5.2.verse: When they’ve passed away from that life, if they’re reborn in this place, whatever business they undertake exceeds expectations.

an4.79:6.1.verse: This is the cause, this is the reason why for different people the same kind of business undertaking might fail,

an4.80:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

an4.80:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

an4.80:2.1.verse: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why ladies don’t attend council meetings, work for a living, or travel to Persia?”

an4.80:2.6.verse: This is the cause, this is the reason why ladies don’t attend council meetings, work for a living, or travel to Persia.”

an4.81:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.81:1.3.verse: They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, and lie.

an4.81:1.4.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.81:2.1.verse: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an4.81:2.3.verse: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, or lie.

an4.81:2.4.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an4.82:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.82:1.3.verse: They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.

an4.82:1.4.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.82:2.1.verse: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an4.82:2.3.verse: They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.

an4.82:2.4.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an4.83:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.83:1.3.verse: Without examining or scrutinizing, they praise those deserving of criticism,

an4.83:1.4.verse: and they criticize those deserving of praise.

an4.83:1.5.verse: They arouse faith in things that are dubious, and they don’t arouse faith in things that are inspiring.

an4.83:1.6.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.83:2.1.verse: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an4.83:2.3.verse: After examining and scrutinizing, they criticize those deserving of criticism,

an4.83:2.4.verse: and they praise those deserving of praise.

an4.83:2.5.verse: They don’t arouse faith in things that are dubious,

an4.83:2.6.verse: and they do arouse faith in things that are inspiring.

an4.83:2.7.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an4.84:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.84:1.3.verse: They value anger, or denigration, or material things, or honor rather than the true teaching.

an4.84:1.4.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.84:2.1.verse: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an4.84:2.3.verse: They value the true teaching rather than anger, or denigration, or material things, or honor.

an4.84:2.4.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an4.85:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.85:1.5.verse: the light bound for darkness, and

an4.85:2.1.verse: And how is an individual dark and bound for darkness?

an4.85:2.2.verse: It’s when an individual is reborn in a low family—a family of corpse-workers, bamboo-workers, hunters, chariot-makers, or scavengers—poor, with little to eat or drink, where life is tough, and food and shelter are hard to find.

an4.85:2.3.verse: And they’re ugly, unsightly, deformed, sickly—one-eyed, crippled, lame, or half-paralyzed. They don’t get to have food, drink, clothes, and vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; or bed, house, and lighting.

an4.85:2.4.verse: And they do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

an4.85:2.5.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

an4.85:2.6.verse: That’s how an individual is dark and bound for darkness.

an4.85:3.1.verse: And how is an individual dark and bound for light?

an4.85:3.2.verse: It’s when an individual is reborn in a low family …

an4.85:3.4.verse: But they do good things by way of body, speech, and mind.

an4.85:3.5.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

an4.85:3.6.verse: That’s how an individual is dark and bound for light.

an4.85:4.1.verse: And how is an individual light and bound for darkness?

an4.85:4.2.verse: It’s when an individual is reborn in an eminent family—a well-to-do family of aristocrats, brahmins, or householders—rich, affluent, and wealthy, with lots of gold and silver, lots of property and assets, and lots of money and grain.

an4.85:4.3.verse: And they’re attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty. They get to have food, drink, clothes, and vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

an4.85:4.4.verse: But they do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

an4.85:4.5.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

an4.85:4.6.verse: That’s how an individual is light and bound for darkness.

an4.85:5.1.verse: And how is an individual light and bound for light?

an4.85:5.2.verse: It’s when an individual is reborn in an eminent family …

an4.85:5.4.verse: And they do good things by way of body, speech, and mind.

an4.85:5.5.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

an4.85:5.6.verse: That’s how an individual is light and bound for light.

an4.85:5.7.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.86:1.1.verse: “These four individuals are found in the world.

an4.86:1.3.verse: One sunk low who sinks lower,

an4.86:1.4.verse: one sunk low who rises high,

an4.86:1.5.verse: one risen high who sinks low, and

an4.86:1.6.verse: one risen high who rises higher.

an4.86:1.7.verse: … These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.87:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.87:1.3.verse: The confirmed ascetic, the white lotus ascetic, the pink lotus ascetic, and the delicate ascetic of ascetics.

an4.87:2.1.verse: And how is an individual a confirmed ascetic?

an4.87:2.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant is a practicing trainee,

an4.87:2.3.verse: who lives aspiring to the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

an4.87:2.4.verse: It’s like the eldest son of an anointed aristocratic king. He has not yet been anointed, but is eligible, and has been confirmed in the succession.

an4.87:2.5.verse: In the same way, a mendicant is a practicing trainee, who lives aspiring to the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

an4.87:2.6.verse: That’s how an individual is a confirmed ascetic.

an4.87:3.1.verse: And how is an individual a white lotus ascetic?

an4.87:3.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements. But they don’t have direct meditative experience of the eight liberations.

an4.87:3.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a white lotus ascetic.

an4.87:4.1.verse: And how is an individual a pink lotus ascetic?

an4.87:4.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom … in this very life … And they have direct meditative experience of the eight liberations.

an4.87:4.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a pink lotus ascetic.

an4.87:5.1.verse: And how is an individual a delicate ascetic of ascetics?

an4.87:5.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant usually uses only what they’ve been invited to accept—robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick—rarely using them without invitation.

an4.87:5.3.verse: When living with other spiritual practitioners, they usually find themselves treated agreeably by them by way of body, speech, and mind, and rarely disagreeably.

an4.87:5.4.verse: And they are usually presented with agreeable things by them, rarely with disagreeable ones.

an4.87:5.5.verse: They’re healthy, so the various unpleasant feelings—stemming from disorders of bile, phlegm, wind, or their conjunction; or caused by change in weather, by not taking care of yourself, by exertion, or as the result of past deeds—usually don’t come up.

an4.87:5.6.verse: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

an4.87:5.7.verse: And they realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom … in this very life …

an4.87:5.8.verse: That’s how an individual is a delicate ascetic of ascetics.

an4.87:6.1.verse: And if anyone should be rightly called a delicate ascetic of ascetics, it’s me.

an4.87:6.2.verse: For I usually use only what I’ve been invited to accept …

an4.87:6.3.verse: When living with other mendicants, I am usually treated agreeably by them.  …

an4.87:6.5.verse: I get the four absorptions when I want, without trouble or difficulty.

an4.87:6.6.verse: And I’ve realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom … in this very life …

an4.87:7.1.verse: So if anyone should be rightly called a delicate ascetic of ascetics, it’s me.

an4.87:7.2.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.88:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.88:1.3.verse: The confirmed ascetic, the white lotus ascetic, the pink lotus ascetic, and the delicate ascetic of ascetics.

an4.88:2.1.verse: And how is an individual a confirmed ascetic?

an4.88:2.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant—with the ending of three fetters—is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

an4.88:2.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a confirmed ascetic.

an4.88:3.1.verse: And how is an individual a white lotus ascetic?

an4.88:3.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant—with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion—is a once-returner. They come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.

an4.88:3.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a white lotus ascetic.

an4.88:4.1.verse: And how is an individual a pink lotus ascetic?

an4.88:4.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant—with the ending of the five lower fetters—is reborn spontaneously. They’re extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.

an4.88:4.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a pink lotus ascetic.

an4.88:5.1.verse: And how is an individual a delicate ascetic of ascetics?

an4.88:5.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an4.88:5.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a delicate ascetic of ascetics.

an4.88:5.4.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.89:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.89:1.3.verse: The confirmed ascetic, the white lotus ascetic, the pink lotus ascetic, and the delicate ascetic of ascetics.

an4.89:2.1.verse: And how is an individual a confirmed ascetic?

an4.89:2.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant has right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

an4.89:2.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a confirmed ascetic.

an4.89:3.1.verse: And how is an individual a white lotus ascetic?

an4.89:3.2.verse: It’s when they have right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom. But they don’t have direct meditative experience of the eight liberations.

an4.89:3.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a white lotus ascetic.

an4.89:4.1.verse: And how is an individual a pink lotus ascetic?

an4.89:4.2.verse: It’s when they have right view … and right freedom. And they do have direct meditative experience of the eight liberations.

an4.89:4.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a pink lotus ascetic.

an4.89:5.1.verse: And how is an individual a delicate ascetic of ascetics?

an4.89:5.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant usually uses only what they’ve been invited to accept … And if anyone should be rightly called a delicate ascetic of ascetics, it’s me.

an4.89:5.3.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.90:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.90:1.3.verse: The confirmed ascetic, the white lotus ascetic, the pink lotus ascetic, and the delicate ascetic of ascetics.

an4.90:2.1.verse: And how is an individual a confirmed ascetic?

an4.90:2.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant is a trainee who hasn’t achieved their heart’s desire, but lives aspiring to the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

an4.90:2.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a confirmed ascetic.

an4.90:3.1.verse: And how is an individual a white lotus ascetic?

an4.90:3.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant meditates observing rise and fall in the five grasping aggregates.

an4.90:3.3.verse: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the disappearance of form.

an4.90:3.7.verse: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.’

an4.90:3.8.verse: But they don’t have direct meditative experience of the eight liberations.

an4.90:3.9.verse: That’s how an individual is a white lotus ascetic.

an4.90:4.1.verse: And how is an individual a pink lotus ascetic?

an4.90:4.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant meditates observing rise and fall in the five grasping aggregates.

an4.90:4.3.verse: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the disappearance of form.

an4.90:4.7.verse: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.’

an4.90:4.8.verse: And they have direct meditative experience of the eight liberations.

an4.90:4.9.verse: That’s how an individual is a pink lotus ascetic.

an4.90:5.1.verse: And how is an individual a delicate ascetic of ascetics?

an4.90:5.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant usually uses only what they’ve been invited to accept … And if anyone should be rightly called a delicate ascetic of ascetics, it’s me.

an4.90:5.3.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.91:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.91:1.5.verse: a god surrounded by titans, and

an4.91:2.1.verse: And how is an individual a titan surrounded by titans?

an4.91:2.2.verse: It’s when an individual is unethical, of bad character, and their followers are the same.

an4.91:2.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a titan surrounded by titans.

an4.91:3.1.verse: And how is an individual a titan surrounded by gods?

an4.91:3.2.verse: It’s when an individual is unethical, of bad character, but their followers are ethical, of good character.

an4.91:3.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a titan surrounded by gods.

an4.91:4.1.verse: And how is an individual a god surrounded by titans?

an4.91:4.2.verse: It’s when an individual is ethical, of good character, but their followers are unethical, of bad character.

an4.91:4.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a god surrounded by titans.

an4.91:5.1.verse: And how is an individual a god surrounded by gods?

an4.91:5.2.verse: It’s when an individual is ethical, of good character, and their followers are the same.

an4.91:5.3.verse: That’s how an individual is a god surrounded by gods.

an4.91:5.4.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.92:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.92:1.3.verse: One individual has internal serenity of heart, but not the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

an4.92:1.4.verse: One individual has the higher wisdom of discernment of principles, but not internal serenity of heart.

an4.92:1.5.verse: One individual has neither internal serenity of heart, nor the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

an4.92:1.6.verse: One individual has both internal serenity of heart, and the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

an4.92:1.7.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.93:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.93:1.3.verse: One individual has internal serenity of heart, but not the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

an4.93:1.4.verse: One individual has the higher wisdom of discernment of principles, but not internal serenity of heart.

an4.93:1.5.verse: One individual has neither internal serenity of heart, nor the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

an4.93:1.6.verse: One individual has both internal serenity of heart, and the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

an4.93:2.1.verse: As for the individual who has serenity but not discernment: grounded on serenity, they should practice meditation to get discernment.

an4.93:2.2.verse: After some time they have both serenity and discernment.

an4.93:3.1.verse: As for the individual who has discernment but not serenity: grounded on discernment, they should practice meditation to get serenity.

an4.93:3.2.verse: After some time they have both discernment and serenity.

an4.93:4.1.verse: As for the individual who has neither serenity nor discernment: in order to get those skillful qualities, they should apply extraordinary enthusiasm, effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness.

an4.93:4.2.verse: Suppose your clothes or head were on fire. In order to extinguish it, you’d apply extraordinary enthusiasm, effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness.

an4.93:4.3.verse: In the same way, in order to get those skillful qualities, that individual should apply extraordinary enthusiasm …

an4.93:4.4.verse: After some time they have both serenity and discernment.

an4.93:5.1.verse: As for the individual who has both serenity and discernment: grounded on those skillful qualities, they should practice meditation further to end the defilements.

an4.93:5.2.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.94:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.94:1.3.verse: One individual has internal serenity of heart, but not the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

an4.94:1.4.verse: One individual has the higher wisdom of discernment of principles, but not internal serenity of heart.

an4.94:1.5.verse: One individual has neither internal serenity of heart, nor the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

an4.94:1.6.verse: One individual has both internal serenity of heart, and the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

an4.94:2.1.verse: As for the individual who has serenity but not discernment: they should approach someone who has discernment and ask:

an4.94:2.5.verse: They would answer from their own experience:

an4.94:2.6.verse: ‘This is how conditions should be seen, comprehended, and discerned.’

an4.94:2.7.verse: After some time they have both serenity and discernment.

an4.94:3.1.verse: As for the individual who has discernment but not serenity: they should approach someone who has serenity and ask:

an4.94:3.2.verse: ‘Reverend, how should the mind be stilled?

an4.94:3.5.verse: How should it be immersed in samādhi?’

an4.94:3.6.verse: They would answer from their own experience:

an4.94:3.7.verse: ‘Reverend, this is how the mind should be stilled, settled, unified, and immersed in samādhi.’

an4.94:3.8.verse: After some time they have both discernment and serenity.

an4.94:4.1.verse: As for the individual who has neither serenity nor discernment: they should approach someone who has serenity and discernment and ask:

an4.94:4.2.verse: ‘Reverend, how should the mind be stilled?

an4.94:4.5.verse: How should it be immersed in samādhi?’

an4.94:4.9.verse: They would answer as they’ve seen and known:

an4.94:4.10.verse: ‘Reverend, this is how the mind should be stilled, settled, unified, and immersed in samādhi. And this is how conditions should be seen, comprehended, and discerned.’

an4.94:4.11.verse: After some time they have both serenity and discernment.

an4.94:5.1.verse: As for the individual who has both serenity and discernment: grounded on those skillful qualities, they should practice meditation further to end the defilements.

an4.94:5.2.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.95:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.95:1.3.verse: One who practices to benefit neither themselves nor others;

an4.95:1.4.verse: one who practices to benefit others, but not themselves;

an4.95:1.5.verse: one who practices to benefit themselves, but not others; and

an4.95:1.6.verse: one who practices to benefit both themselves and others.

an4.95:2.1.verse: Suppose there was a firebrand for lighting a funeral pyre, burning at both ends, and smeared with dung in the middle. It couldn’t be used as timber either in the village or the wilderness.

an4.95:2.2.verse: The individual who practices to benefit neither themselves nor others is like this, I say.

an4.95:3.1.verse: The individual who practices to benefit others, but not themselves, is better than that.

an4.95:3.2.verse: The individual who practices to benefit themselves, but not others, is better than both of those.

an4.95:3.3.verse: But the individual who practices to benefit both themselves and others is the foremost, best, chief, highest, and finest of the four.

an4.95:4.1.verse: From a cow comes milk, from milk comes curds, from curds come butter, from butter comes ghee, and from ghee comes cream of ghee. And the cream of ghee is said to be the best of these.

an4.95:4.2.verse: In the same way, the individual who practices to benefit both themselves and others is the foremost, best, chief, highest, and finest of the four.

an4.95:4.3.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.96:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.96:1.3.verse: One who practices to benefit themselves, but not others;

an4.96:1.4.verse: one who practices to benefit others, but not themselves;

an4.96:1.5.verse: one who practices to benefit neither themselves nor others; and

an4.96:1.6.verse: one who practices to benefit both themselves and others.

an4.96:2.1.verse: And how does an individual practice to benefit themselves, but not others?

an4.96:2.2.verse: It’s when an individual practices to remove their own greed, hate, and delusion, but doesn’t encourage others to do the same.

an4.96:2.5.verse: That’s how an individual practices to benefit themselves, but not others.

an4.96:3.1.verse: And how does an individual practice to benefit others, but not themselves?

an4.96:3.2.verse: It’s when an individual doesn’t practice to remove their own greed, hate, and delusion, but encourages others to remove theirs.

an4.96:3.5.verse: That’s how an individual practices to benefit others, but not themselves.

an4.96:4.1.verse: And how does an individual practice to benefit neither themselves nor others?

an4.96:4.2.verse: It’s when an individual doesn’t practice to remove their own greed, hate, and delusion, nor do they encourage others to remove theirs.

an4.96:4.5.verse: That’s how an individual practices to benefit neither themselves nor others.

an4.96:5.1.verse: And how does an individual practice to benefit both themselves and others?

an4.96:5.2.verse: It’s when an individual practices to remove their own greed, hate, and delusion, and encourages others to remove theirs.

an4.96:5.5.verse: That’s how an individual practices to benefit both themselves and others.

an4.96:5.6.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.97:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.97:1.3.verse: One who practices to benefit themselves, but not others;

an4.97:1.4.verse: one who practices to benefit others, but not themselves;

an4.97:1.5.verse: one who practices to benefit neither themselves nor others; and

an4.97:1.6.verse: one who practices to benefit both themselves and others.

an4.97:2.1.verse: And how does an individual practice to benefit themselves, but not others?

an4.97:2.2.verse: It’s when an individual is quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings. They readily memorize the teachings they’ve heard. They examine the meaning of teachings they’ve memorized. Understanding the meaning and the teaching, they practice in line with the teaching.

an4.97:2.3.verse: But they’re not a good speaker and do not enunciate well. Their voice isn’t polished, clear, articulate, and doesn’t express the meaning. They don’t educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire their spiritual companions.

an4.97:2.4.verse: That’s how an individual practices to benefit themselves, but not others.

an4.97:3.1.verse: And how does an individual practice to benefit others, but not themselves?

an4.97:3.2.verse: It’s when an individual is not quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings. …

an4.97:3.4.verse: That’s how an individual practices to benefit others, but not themselves.

an4.97:4.1.verse: And how does an individual practice to benefit neither themselves nor others?

an4.97:4.2.verse: It’s when an individual is not quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings. …

an4.97:4.3.verse: Nor are they a good speaker. …

an4.97:4.4.verse: That’s how an individual practices to benefit neither themselves nor others.

an4.97:5.1.verse: And how does an individual practice to benefit both themselves and others?

an4.97:5.2.verse: It’s when an individual is quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings. …

an4.97:5.4.verse: That’s how an individual practices to benefit both themselves and others.

an4.97:5.5.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.98:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.98:1.3.verse: One who practices to benefit themselves, but not others;

an4.98:1.4.verse: one who practices to benefit others, but not themselves;

an4.98:1.5.verse: one who practices to benefit neither themselves nor others; and

an4.98:1.6.verse: one who practices to benefit both themselves and others.

an4.98:1.7.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.99:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.99:1.3.verse: One who practices to benefit themselves, but not others;

an4.99:1.4.verse: one who practices to benefit others, but not themselves;

an4.99:1.5.verse: one who practices to benefit neither themselves nor others; and

an4.99:1.6.verse: one who practices to benefit both themselves and others.

an4.99:2.1.verse: And how does an individual practice to benefit themselves, but not others?

an4.99:2.2.verse: It’s when an individual doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor. But they don’t encourage others to do the same.

an4.99:2.7.verse: That’s how an individual practices to benefit themselves, but not others.

an4.99:3.1.verse: And how does an individual practice to benefit others, but not themselves?

an4.99:3.2.verse: It’s when an individual kills living creatures, steals, commits sexual misconduct, lies, and consumes intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor. But they encourage others to not do these things.

an4.99:3.7.verse: That’s how an individual practices to benefit others, but not themselves.

an4.99:4.1.verse: And how does a person practice to benefit neither themselves nor others?

an4.99:4.2.verse: It’s when an individual kills, etc. … and doesn’t encourage others to not do these things.

an4.99:4.3.verse: That’s how an individual practices to benefit neither themselves nor others.

an4.99:5.1.verse: And how does an individual practice to benefit both themselves and others?

an4.99:5.2.verse: It’s when an individual doesn’t kill, etc. … and encourages others to do the same.

an4.99:5.3.verse: That’s how an individual practices to benefit both themselves and others.

an4.99:5.4.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.100:1.1.verse: Then the wanderer Potaliya went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

an4.100:1.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and the Buddha said to him:

an4.100:2.1.verse: “Potaliya, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.100:2.3.verse: One individual criticizes those deserving of criticism at the right time, truthfully and correctly. But they don’t praise those deserving of praise at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

an4.100:2.4.verse: Another individual praises those deserving of praise … But they don’t criticize those deserving of criticism …

an4.100:2.5.verse: Another individual doesn’t praise those deserving of praise … Nor do they criticize those deserving of criticism …

an4.100:2.6.verse: Another individual criticizes those deserving of criticism at the right time, truthfully and correctly. And they praise those deserving of praise at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

an4.100:2.7.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.

an4.100:2.8.verse: Of these four individuals, who do you believe to be the finest?”

an4.100:3.8.verse: “Worthy Gotama, of these four individuals, it is the individual who neither praises those deserving of praise at the right time, truthfully and correctly; nor criticizes those deserving of criticism at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

an4.100:3.9.verse: That is the individual I believe to be the finest.

an4.100:3.11.verse: Because, worthy Gotama, equanimity is the best.”

an4.100:4.3.verse: “Potaliya, of these four individuals, it is the individual who criticizes those deserving of criticism at the right time, truthfully and correctly; and praises those deserving of praise at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

an4.100:4.4.verse: That is the individual I consider to be the finest.

an4.100:4.6.verse: Because, Potaliya, understanding of time and context is the best.”

an4.100:5.3.verse: “Worthy Gotama, of these four individuals, it is the individual who criticizes those deserving of criticism at the right time, truthfully and correctly; and praises those deserving of praise at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

an4.100:5.4.verse: That is the individual I believe to be the finest.

an4.100:5.6.verse: Because, worthy Gotama, understanding of time and context is the best.

an4.100:6.2.verse: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

an4.100:6.3.verse: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

an4.100:6.4.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

an4.101:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

an4.101:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

an4.101:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of clouds.

an4.101:2.5.verse: one neither thunders nor rains, and

an4.101:2.7.verse: These are the four kinds of clouds.

an4.101:2.8.verse: In the same way, these four individuals similar to clouds are found in the world.

an4.101:2.12.verse: one neither thunders nor rains, and

an4.101:3.1.verse: And how does an individual thunder but not rain?

an4.101:3.2.verse: It’s when an individual is a talker, not a doer.

an4.101:3.3.verse: That’s how an individual thunders but doesn’t rain.

an4.101:3.4.verse: That individual is like a cloud that thunders but doesn’t rain, I say.

an4.101:4.1.verse: And how does an individual rain but not thunder?

an4.101:4.2.verse: It’s when an individual is a doer, not a talker. …

an4.101:5.1.verse: And how does an individual neither thunder nor rain?

an4.101:5.2.verse: It’s when an individual is neither a talker nor a doer. …

an4.101:6.1.verse: And how does an individual both thunder and rain?

an4.101:6.2.verse: It’s when an individual is both a talker and a doer. …

an4.101:6.6.verse: These four individuals similar to clouds are found in the world.”

an4.102:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of clouds.

an4.102:1.5.verse: one neither thunders nor rains, and

an4.102:1.7.verse: These are the four kinds of clouds.

an4.102:1.8.verse: In the same way, these four individuals similar to clouds are found in the world.

an4.102:1.12.verse: one neither thunders nor rains, and

an4.102:2.1.verse: And how does an individual thunder but not rain?

an4.102:2.2.verse: It’s when an individual memorizes the teaching—

an4.102:2.3.verse: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

an4.102:2.4.verse: But they don’t truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

an4.102:2.5.verse: That’s how an individual thunders but doesn’t rain.

an4.102:2.6.verse: That individual is like a cloud that thunders but doesn’t rain, I say.

an4.102:3.1.verse: And how does an individual rain but not thunder?

an4.102:3.2.verse: It’s when an individual doesn’t memorize the teaching …

an4.102:3.4.verse: But they truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

an4.102:4.1.verse: And how does an individual neither thunder nor rain?

an4.102:4.2.verse: It’s when an individual doesn’t memorize the teaching …

an4.102:4.4.verse: Nor do they truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

an4.102:5.1.verse: And how does an individual both thunder and rain?

an4.102:5.2.verse: It’s when an individual memorizes the teaching …

an4.102:5.4.verse: And they truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

an4.102:5.8.verse: These four individuals similar to clouds are found in the world.”

an4.103:1.8.verse: In the same way, these four individuals similar to pots are found in the world.

an4.103:2.1.verse: And how is an individual covered but hollow?

an4.103:2.2.verse: It’s when an individual is impressive when going out and coming back, when looking ahead and aside, when bending and extending the limbs, and when bearing the outer robe, bowl and robes.

an4.103:2.3.verse: But they don’t truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

an4.103:2.4.verse: That’s how an individual is covered but hollow.

an4.103:2.5.verse: That individual is like a pot that’s covered but hollow, I say.

an4.103:3.1.verse: And how is an individual uncovered but full?

an4.103:3.2.verse: It’s when an individual is not impressive …

an4.103:3.3.verse: But they truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

an4.103:4.1.verse: And how is an individual uncovered and hollow?

an4.103:4.2.verse: It’s when an individual is not impressive …

an4.103:4.3.verse: Nor do they truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

an4.103:5.1.verse: And how is an individual covered and full?

an4.103:5.2.verse: It’s when an individual is impressive …

an4.103:5.3.verse: And they truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

an4.103:5.7.verse: These four individuals similar to pots are found in the world.”

an4.104:1.8.verse: In the same way, these four individuals similar to lakes are found in the world.

an4.104:1.10.verse: One is shallow but appears deep,

an4.104:1.11.verse: one is deep but appears shallow,

an4.104:3.1.verse: And how is an individual deep but appears shallow?

an4.105:1.10.verse: One is unripe but seems ripe,

an4.105:1.12.verse: one is unripe and seems unripe, and
