an4.107:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of mice.

an4.107:1.3.verse: One makes a hole but doesn’t live in it,

an4.107:1.4.verse: one lives in a hole but doesn’t make it,

an4.107:1.5.verse: one neither makes a hole nor lives in it, and

an4.107:1.6.verse: one both makes a hole and lives in it.

an4.107:1.7.verse: These are the four kinds of mice.

an4.107:1.8.verse: In the same way, these four individuals similar to mice are found in the world.

an4.107:1.10.verse: One makes a hole but doesn’t live in it,

an4.107:1.11.verse: one lives in a hole but doesn’t make it,

an4.107:1.12.verse: one neither makes a hole nor lives in it, and

an4.107:1.13.verse: one both makes a hole and lives in it.

an4.107:2.1.verse: And how does an individual make a hole but not live in it?

an4.107:2.2.verse: It’s when an individual memorizes the teaching—

an4.107:2.3.verse: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

an4.107:2.4.verse: But they don’t really understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

an4.107:2.5.verse: That’s how an individual makes a hole but doesn’t live in it.

an4.107:2.6.verse: That individual is like a mouse that makes a hole but doesn’t live in it, I say.

an4.107:3.1.verse: And how does an individual live in a hole but not make it?

an4.107:3.2.verse: It’s when an individual doesn’t memorize the teaching …

an4.107:3.4.verse: But they really understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

an4.107:4.1.verse: And how does an individual neither make a hole nor live in it?

an4.107:4.2.verse: It’s when an individual doesn’t memorize the teaching …

an4.107:4.4.verse: Nor do they really understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

an4.107:5.1.verse: And how does an individual both make a hole and live in it?

an4.107:5.2.verse: It’s when an individual memorizes the teaching …

an4.107:5.4.verse: And they really understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

an4.107:5.8.verse: These four individuals similar to mice are found in the world.”

an4.108:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of oxen.

an4.108:1.3.verse: One hostile to its own herd, not others;

an4.108:1.4.verse: one hostile to other herds, not its own;

an4.108:1.5.verse: one hostile to both its own herd and others; and

an4.108:1.6.verse: one hostile to neither its own herd nor others.

an4.108:1.7.verse: These are the four kinds of oxen.

an4.108:1.8.verse: In the same way, these four individuals similar to oxen are found in the world.

an4.108:1.10.verse: One hostile to their own herd, not others;

an4.108:1.11.verse: one hostile to other herds, not their own;

an4.108:1.12.verse: one hostile to both their own herd and others; and

an4.108:1.13.verse: one hostile to neither their own herd nor others.

an4.108:2.1.verse: And how is an individual hostile to their own herd, not others?

an4.108:2.2.verse: It’s when an individual intimidates their own followers, not the followers of others.

an4.108:2.3.verse: That’s how an individual is hostile to their own herd, not others.

an4.108:2.4.verse: That individual is like an ox that’s hostile to its own herd, not others.

an4.108:3.1.verse: And how is an individual hostile to other herds, not their own?

an4.108:3.2.verse: It’s when an individual intimidates the followers of others, not their own. …

an4.108:4.1.verse: And how is an individual hostile to both their own herd and others?

an4.108:4.2.verse: It’s when an individual intimidates their own followers and the followers of others. …

an4.108:5.1.verse: And how is an individual hostile to neither their own herd nor others?

an4.108:5.2.verse: It’s when an individual doesn’t intimidate their own followers or the followers of others.

an4.108:5.6.verse: These four individuals similar to oxen are found in the world.”

an4.109:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of tree.

an4.109:1.3.verse: One is a softwood surrounded by softwoods,

an4.109:1.4.verse: one is a softwood surrounded by hardwoods,

an4.109:1.5.verse: one is a hardwood surrounded by softwoods, and

an4.109:1.6.verse: one is a hardwood surrounded by hardwoods.

an4.109:1.7.verse: These are the four kinds of tree.

an4.109:1.8.verse: In the same way, these four individuals similar to trees are found in the world.

an4.109:1.10.verse: One is a softwood surrounded by softwoods,

an4.109:1.11.verse: one is a softwood surrounded by hardwoods,

an4.109:1.12.verse: one is a hardwood surrounded by softwoods, and

an4.109:1.13.verse: one is a hardwood surrounded by hardwoods.

an4.109:2.1.verse: And how is an individual a softwood surrounded by softwoods?

an4.109:2.2.verse: It’s when an individual is unethical, of bad character,

an4.109:2.3.verse: and their followers are the same.

an4.109:2.4.verse: That’s how an individual is a softwood surrounded by softwoods.

an4.109:2.5.verse: That individual is like a softwood tree that’s surrounded by softwoods, I say.

an4.109:3.1.verse: And how is an individual a softwood surrounded by hardwoods?

an4.109:3.2.verse: It’s when an individual is unethical, of bad character,

an4.109:3.3.verse: but their followers are ethical, of good character. …

an4.109:4.1.verse: And how is an individual a hardwood surrounded by softwoods?

an4.109:4.2.verse: It’s when an individual is ethical, of good character,

an4.109:4.3.verse: but their followers are unethical, of bad character. …

an4.109:5.1.verse: And how is an individual a hardwood surrounded by hardwoods?

an4.109:5.2.verse: It’s when an individual is ethical, of good character,

an4.109:5.3.verse: and their followers are the same.

an4.109:5.7.verse: These four individuals similar to trees are found in the world.”

an4.110:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of viper.

an4.110:1.3.verse: One whose venom is fast-acting but not lethal,

an4.110:1.4.verse: one whose venom is lethal but not fast-acting,

an4.110:1.5.verse: one whose venom is both fast-acting and lethal, and

an4.110:1.6.verse: one whose venom is neither fast-acting nor lethal.

an4.110:1.7.verse: These are the four kinds of viper.

an4.110:1.8.verse: In the same way, these four individuals similar to vipers are found in the world.

an4.110:1.10.verse: One whose venom is fast-acting but not lethal,

an4.110:1.11.verse: one whose venom is lethal but not fast-acting,

an4.110:1.12.verse: one whose venom is both fast-acting and lethal, and

an4.110:1.13.verse: one whose venom is neither fast-acting nor lethal.

an4.110:2.1.verse: And how is an individual’s venom fast-acting but not lethal?

an4.110:2.2.verse: It’s when an individual is often angry,

an4.110:2.3.verse: but their anger doesn’t linger long.

an4.110:2.4.verse: That’s how an individual’s venom is fast-acting but not lethal.

an4.110:2.5.verse: That individual is like a viper whose venom is fast-acting but not lethal.

an4.110:3.1.verse: And how is an individual’s venom lethal but not fast-acting?

an4.110:3.2.verse: It’s when an individual is not often angry,

an4.110:3.3.verse: but their anger lingers for a long time.

an4.110:4.1.verse: And how is an individual’s venom both fast-acting and lethal?

an4.110:4.2.verse: It’s when an individual is often angry,

an4.110:4.3.verse: and their anger lingers for a long time.

an4.110:5.1.verse: And how is an individual’s venom neither fast-acting nor lethal?

an4.110:5.2.verse: It’s when an individual is not often angry,

an4.110:5.3.verse: and their anger doesn’t linger long.

an4.110:5.7.verse: These four individuals similar to vipers are found in the world.”

an4.111:1.1.verse: Then Kesi the horse trainer went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

an4.111:1.2.verse: “Kesi, you’re known as a horse trainer.

an4.111:1.3.verse: Just how do you guide a horse in training?”

an4.111:1.4.verse: “Sir, I guide a horse in training sometimes gently, sometimes harshly, and sometimes both gently and harshly.”

an4.111:1.5.verse: “Kesi, what do you do with a horse in training that doesn’t follow these forms of training?”

an4.111:1.7.verse: “In that case, sir, I kill it.

an4.111:1.9.verse: So that I don’t disgrace my tutor’s community.

an4.111:2.1.verse: But sir, the Buddha is the supreme guide for those fit for training.

an4.111:2.2.verse: Just how do you guide a person in training?”

an4.111:2.3.verse: “Kesi, I guide a person in training sometimes gently, sometimes harshly, and sometimes both gently and harshly.

an4.111:2.5.verse: ‘This is good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind. This is the result of good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind. This is life as a god. This is life as a human.’

an4.111:2.7.verse: ‘This is bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind. This is the result of bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind. This is life in hell. This is life as an animal. This is life as a ghost.’

an4.111:3.1.verse: The both gentle and harsh way is this:

an4.111:3.2.verse: ‘This is good conduct … this is bad conduct …’”

an4.111:4.1.verse: “Sir, what do you do with a person in training who doesn’t follow these forms of training?”

an4.111:4.2.verse: “In that case, Kesi, I kill them.”

an4.111:4.3.verse: “Sir, it’s not appropriate for the Buddha to kill living creatures.

an4.111:4.7.verse: it’s not appropriate for a Realized One to kill living creatures.

an4.111:4.8.verse: But when a person in training doesn’t follow any of these forms of training, the Realized One doesn’t think they’re worth advising or instructing, and neither do their sensible spiritual companions.

an4.111:4.9.verse: For it is killing in the training of the Noble One

an4.111:4.10.verse: when the Realized One doesn’t think they’re worth advising or instructing, and neither do their sensible spiritual companions.”

an4.111:5.2.verse: when the Realized One doesn’t think they’re worth advising or instructing, and neither do their sensible spiritual companions.

an4.111:5.3.verse: Excellent, sir! … From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

an4.112:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a fine royal thoroughbred with four factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and reckoned a factor of kingship.

an4.112:1.4.verse: A fine royal thoroughbred with these four factors is worthy of a king. …

an4.112:2.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant with four qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

an4.112:2.4.verse: A mendicant with these four qualities … is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

an4.113:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four fine thoroughbreds are found in the world.

an4.113:1.3.verse: One fine thoroughbred is moved to act when it sees the shadow of the goad, thinking:

an4.113:1.4.verse: ‘What task will the horse trainer have me do today? How should I respond?’

an4.113:1.5.verse: Some fine thoroughbreds are like that.

an4.113:1.6.verse: This is the first fine thoroughbred found in the world.

an4.113:2.1.verse: Furthermore, one fine thoroughbred isn’t moved to act when it sees the shadow of the goad, but only when its hairs are struck, thinking:

an4.113:2.2.verse: ‘What task will the horse trainer have me do today? How should I respond?’

an4.113:2.3.verse: Some fine thoroughbreds are like that.

an4.113:2.4.verse: This is the second fine thoroughbred found in the world.

an4.113:3.1.verse: Furthermore, one fine thoroughbred isn’t moved to act when it sees the shadow of the goad, nor when its hairs are struck, but only when its hide is struck, thinking:

an4.113:3.2.verse: ‘What task will the horse trainer have me do today? How should I respond?’

an4.113:3.3.verse: Some fine thoroughbreds are like that.

an4.113:3.4.verse: This is the third fine thoroughbred found in the world.

an4.113:4.1.verse: Furthermore, one fine thoroughbred isn’t moved to act when it sees the shadow of the goad, nor when its hairs are struck, nor when its hide is struck, but only when its bone is struck, thinking:

an4.113:4.2.verse: ‘What task will the horse trainer have me do today? How should I respond?’

an4.113:4.3.verse: Some fine thoroughbreds are like that.

an4.113:4.4.verse: This is the fourth fine thoroughbred found in the world.

an4.113:4.5.verse: These are the four fine thoroughbreds found in the world.

an4.113:5.1.verse: In the same way, these four fine thoroughbred people are found in the world.

an4.113:5.3.verse: One fine thoroughbred person hears about

an4.113:5.4.verse: the suffering or death of a woman or man in such-and-such village or town.

an4.113:5.5.verse: They’re moved to act by this,

an4.113:5.7.verse: Applying themselves, they directly realize the ultimate truth, and see it with penetrating wisdom.

an4.113:5.8.verse: This individual is like the fine thoroughbred

an4.113:5.9.verse: that’s shaken when it sees the shadow of the goad.

an4.113:5.10.verse: Some fine thoroughbred people are like that.

an4.113:5.11.verse: This is the first fine thoroughbred person found in the world.

an4.113:6.1.verse: Furthermore, one fine thoroughbred person doesn’t hear about

an4.113:6.2.verse: the suffering or death of a woman or man in such-and-such village or town, but they see it themselves.

an4.113:6.3.verse: They’re moved to act by this,

an4.113:6.5.verse: Applying themselves, they directly realize the ultimate truth, and see it with penetrating wisdom.

an4.113:6.6.verse: This person is like the fine thoroughbred that’s moved to act

an4.113:6.8.verse: Some fine thoroughbred people are like that.

an4.113:6.9.verse: This is the second fine thoroughbred person found in the world.

an4.113:7.1.verse: Furthermore, one fine thoroughbred person doesn’t hear about

an4.113:7.2.verse: the suffering or death of a woman or man in such-and-such village or town, nor do they see it themselves, but it happens to their own relative or family member.

an4.113:7.3.verse: They’re moved to act by this,

an4.113:7.5.verse: Applying themselves, they directly realize the ultimate truth, and see it with penetrating wisdom.

an4.113:7.6.verse: This person is like the fine thoroughbred that’s moved to act

an4.113:7.8.verse: Some fine thoroughbred people are like that.

an4.113:7.9.verse: This is the third fine thoroughbred person found in the world.

an4.113:8.1.verse: Furthermore, one fine thoroughbred person doesn’t hear about

an4.113:8.2.verse: the suffering or death of a woman or man in such-and-such village or town, nor do they see it themselves, nor does it happen to their own relative or family member, but they themselves are afflicted with physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.

an4.113:8.3.verse: They’re moved to act by this,

an4.113:8.5.verse: Applying themselves, they directly realize the ultimate truth, and see it with penetrating wisdom.

an4.113:8.6.verse: This person is like the fine thoroughbred that’s moved to act

an4.113:8.8.verse: Some fine thoroughbred people are like that.

an4.113:8.9.verse: This is the fourth fine thoroughbred person found in the world.

an4.113:8.10.verse: These are the four fine thoroughbred people found in the world.”

an4.114:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a royal bull elephant with four factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.

an4.114:1.3.verse: A royal bull elephant listens, destroys, endures, and goes fast.

an4.114:2.1.verse: And how does a royal bull elephant listen?

an4.114:2.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens to whatever task the elephant trainer has it do,

an4.114:2.3.verse: whether or not it has done it before.

an4.114:2.5.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant listens.

an4.114:3.1.verse: And how does a royal bull elephant destroy?

an4.114:3.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant in battle destroys elephants with their riders, horses with their riders, chariots and charioteers, and foot soldiers.

an4.114:3.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant destroys.

an4.114:4.1.verse: And how does a royal bull elephant endure?

an4.114:4.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant in battle endures being struck by spears, swords, arrows, and axes; it endures the thunder of the drums, kettledrums, horns, and cymbals.

an4.114:4.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant endures.

an4.114:5.1.verse: And how does a royal bull elephant go fast?

an4.114:5.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant swiftly goes in whatever direction the elephant trainer sends it,

an4.114:5.3.verse: whether or not it has been there before.

an4.114:5.5.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant goes fast.

an4.114:5.6.verse: A royal bull elephant with four factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.

an4.114:6.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant with four qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

an4.114:6.3.verse: A mendicant listens, destroys, endures, and goes fast.

an4.114:7.1.verse: And how does a mendicant listen?

an4.114:7.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens when the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One is being taught.

an4.114:8.1.verse: And how does a mendicant destroy?

an4.114:8.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t tolerate a sensual, malicious, or cruel thought. They don’t tolerate any bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen, but give them up, dispel them, eliminate them, and obliterate them.

an4.114:9.1.verse: And how does a mendicant endure?

an4.114:9.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant endures cold, heat, hunger, and thirst; the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles; rude and unwelcome criticism; and they put up with physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.

an4.114:10.1.verse: And how does a mendicant go fast?

an4.114:10.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant swiftly goes in the direction they’ve never gone before in all this long time; that is, the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.

an4.114:10.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant goes fast.

an4.114:10.4.verse: A mendicant with these four qualities … is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

an4.115:1.3.verse: There is a thing that’s unpleasant to do,

an4.115:1.5.verse: There is a thing that’s unpleasant to do,

an4.115:1.7.verse: There is a thing that’s pleasant to do,

an4.115:1.9.verse: There is a thing that’s pleasant to do,

an4.115:2.1.verse: Take the thing that’s unpleasant to do,

an4.115:2.3.verse: This is regarded as a thing that shouldn’t be done on both grounds:

an4.115:2.6.verse: and because doing it proves harmful.

an4.115:2.8.verse: This is regarded as a thing that shouldn’t be done on both grounds.

an4.115:3.1.verse: Next, take the thing that’s unpleasant to do,

an4.115:3.3.verse: It is here that you can tell who is foolish and who is astute in regard to human strength, energy, and vigor.

an4.115:3.5.verse: ‘Despite the fact that this thing is unpleasant to do,

an4.115:3.10.verse: ‘Even though this thing is unpleasant to do,

an4.115:4.1.verse: Next, take the thing that’s pleasant to do,

an4.115:4.3.verse: It is here that you can tell who is foolish and who is astute in regard to human strength, energy, and vigor.

an4.115:4.5.verse: ‘Even though this thing is pleasant to do,

an4.115:4.10.verse: ‘Despite the fact that this thing is pleasant to do,

an4.115:5.1.verse: Next, take the thing that’s pleasant to do, and doing it proves beneficial.

an4.115:5.2.verse: This is regarded as a thing that should be done on both grounds:

an4.115:5.4.verse: and because doing it proves beneficial.

an4.115:5.5.verse: This is regarded as a thing that should be done on both grounds.

an4.116:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you should be diligent in four situations.

an4.116:1.3.verse: Give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind; and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

an4.116:1.9.verse: Give up wrong view; and develop right view.

an4.116:2.1.verse: A mendicant who has done these things does not fear death in lives to come.”

an4.117:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, in your own way you should practice diligence, mindfulness, and guarding of the mind in four situations.

an4.117:1.3.verse: ‘May my mind not be aroused by things that arouse greed.’ In your own way you should practice diligence, mindfulness, and guarding of the mind.

an4.117:1.4.verse: ‘May my mind not be angered by things that provoke hate.’ …

an4.117:1.5.verse: ‘May my mind not be deluded by things that promote delusion.’ …

an4.117:1.6.verse: ‘May my mind not be intoxicated by things that intoxicate.’ …

an4.117:2.1.verse: When a mendicant’s mind is no longer affected by greed, hate, delusion, or intoxication because they’ve got rid of these things, they don’t shake, tremble, quake, or get nervous, nor are they persuaded by the teachings of other ascetics.”

an4.118:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a faithful gentleman should go to see these four inspiring places.

an4.118:1.3.verse: Thinking: ‘Here the Realized One was born!’—that is an inspiring place.

an4.118:1.4.verse: Thinking: ‘Here the Realized One became awakened as a supreme fully awakened Buddha!’—that is an inspiring place.

an4.118:1.5.verse: Thinking: ‘Here the Realized One rolled forth the supreme Wheel of Dhamma!’—that is an inspiring place.

an4.118:1.6.verse: Thinking: ‘Here the Realized One was fully quenched in the element of extinguishment, with no residue!’—that is an inspiring place.

an4.118:1.7.verse: These are the four inspiring places that a faithful gentleman should go to see.”

an4.119:1.3.verse: The perils of rebirth, old age, sickness, and death.

an4.120:1.3.verse: The perils of fire, water, kings, and bandits.

an4.121:1.3.verse: The fears of guilt, shame, punishment, and going to a bad place.

an4.121:2.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is the fear of guilt?

an4.121:2.3.verse: ‘If I were to do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind, wouldn’t I blame myself for my conduct?’

an4.121:2.4.verse: Being afraid of guilt, they give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, keeping themselves pure.

an4.121:2.5.verse: This is called the fear of guilt.

an4.121:3.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is the fear of shame?

an4.121:3.3.verse: ‘If I were to do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind, wouldn’t others blame me for my conduct?’

an4.121:3.4.verse: Being afraid of shame, they give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, keeping themselves pure.

an4.121:3.5.verse: This is called the fear of shame.

an4.121:4.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is the fear of punishment?

an4.121:4.2.verse: It’s when someone sees that the kings have arrested a bandit, a criminal, and subjected them to various punishments—

an4.121:4.3.verse: whipping, caning, and clubbing; cutting off hands or feet, or both; cutting off ears or nose, or both; the ‘porridge pot’, the ‘shell-shave’, the ‘Rāhu’s mouth’, the ‘garland of fire’, the ‘burning hand’, the ‘bulrush twist’, the ‘bark dress’, the ‘antelope’, the ‘meat hook’, the ‘coins’, the ‘caustic pickle’, the ‘twisting bar’, the ‘straw mat’; being splashed with hot oil, being fed to the hounds, being impaled alive, and being beheaded.

an4.121:5.2.verse: ‘If I were to do the same kind of bad deed, the kings would punish me in the same way.’ …

an4.121:5.4.verse: Being afraid of punishment, they don’t steal the belongings of others.

an4.121:5.5.verse: They give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, keeping themselves pure.

an4.121:5.6.verse: This is called the fear of punishment.

an4.121:6.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is the fear of rebirth in a bad place?

an4.121:6.3.verse: ‘Bad conduct of body, speech, or mind has a bad result in the next life.

an4.121:6.4.verse: If I were to do such bad things, when my body breaks up, after death, I’d be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.’

an4.121:6.5.verse: Being afraid of rebirth in a bad place, they give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, keeping themselves pure.

an4.121:6.6.verse: This is called the fear of rebirth in a bad place.

an4.122:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, anyone who enters the water should anticipate four dangers.

an4.122:1.3.verse: The dangers of waves, gharials, whirlpools, and sharks.

an4.122:1.4.verse: These are the four dangers that anyone who enters the water should anticipate.

an4.122:1.5.verse: In the same way, a gentleman gone forth from the lay life to homelessness in this teaching and training should anticipate four dangers.

an4.122:1.7.verse: The dangers of waves, gharials, whirlpools, and sharks.

an4.122:2.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is the danger of waves?

an4.122:2.2.verse: It’s when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness, thinking:

an4.122:2.3.verse: ‘I’m swamped by rebirth, old age, and death; by sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. I’m swamped by suffering, mired in suffering.

an4.122:2.4.verse: Hopefully I can make an end to this entire mass of suffering.’

an4.122:2.5.verse: When they’ve gone forth, their spiritual companions advise and instruct them:

an4.122:2.6.verse: ‘You should go out like this, and come back like that. You should look to the front like this, and to the side like that. You should contract your limbs like this, and extend them like that. This is how you should bear your outer robe, bowl, and robes.’

an4.122:2.8.verse: ‘Formerly, as laypeople, we advised and instructed others.

an4.122:2.9.verse: And now these mendicants—who you’d think were our children or grandchildren—imagine they can advise and instruct us!’

an4.122:2.10.verse: Angry and upset, they resign the training and return to a lesser life.

an4.122:2.11.verse: This is called a mendicant who resigns the training and returns to a lesser life for fear of the danger of waves.

an4.122:2.12.verse: ‘Danger of waves’ is a term for anger and distress.

an4.122:2.13.verse: This is called the danger of waves.

an4.122:3.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is the danger of gharials?

an4.122:3.2.verse: It’s when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness …

an4.122:3.5.verse: When they’ve gone forth, their spiritual companions advise and instruct them:

an4.122:3.6.verse: ‘You may eat, consume, taste, and drink these things, but not those. You may eat what’s allowable, but not what’s unallowable. You may eat at the right time, but not at the wrong time.’

an4.122:3.8.verse: ‘Formerly, as laypeople, we used to eat, consume, taste, and drink what we wanted, not what we didn’t want.

an4.122:3.12.verse: We ate and drank both allowable and unallowable things, at the right time and the wrong time.

an4.122:3.13.verse: And these faithful householders give us delicious fresh and cooked foods at the wrong time of day. But these guys imagine they can gag our mouths!’

an4.122:3.14.verse: Angry and upset, they resign the training and return to a lesser life.

an4.122:3.15.verse: This is called a mendicant who resigns the training and returns to a lesser life for fear of the danger of gharials.

an4.122:3.16.verse: ‘Danger of gharials’ is a term for gluttony.

an4.122:3.17.verse: This is called the danger of gharials.

an4.122:4.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is the danger of whirlpools?

an4.122:4.2.verse: It’s when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness …

an4.122:4.5.verse: When they’ve gone forth, they robe up in the morning and, taking their bowl and robe, enter a village or town for alms without guarding body, speech, and mind, without establishing mindfulness, and without restraining the sense faculties.

an4.122:4.6.verse: There they see a householder or their child amusing themselves, supplied and provided with the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

an4.122:4.8.verse: ‘Formerly, as laypeople, we amused ourselves, supplied and provided with the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

an4.122:4.9.verse: And it’s true that my family is wealthy.

an4.122:4.10.verse: I can both enjoy my wealth and make merit.

an4.122:4.11.verse: Why don’t I resign the training and return to a lesser life, so I can enjoy my wealth and make merit?’

an4.122:4.12.verse: They resign the training and return to a lesser life.

an4.122:4.13.verse: This is called a mendicant who resigns the training and returns to a lesser life for fear of the danger of whirlpools.

an4.122:4.14.verse: ‘Danger of whirlpools’ is a term for the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

an4.122:4.15.verse: This is called the danger of whirlpools.

an4.122:5.1.verse: And what, mendicants, is the danger of sharks?

an4.122:5.2.verse: It’s when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness …

an4.122:5.5.verse: When they’ve gone forth, they robe up in the morning and, taking their bowl and robe, enter a village or town for alms without guarding body, speech, and mind, without establishing mindfulness, and without restraining the sense faculties.

an4.122:5.6.verse: There they see a lady scantily clad, with revealing clothes.

an4.122:5.8.verse: so they resign the training and return to a lesser life.

an4.122:5.9.verse: This is called a mendicant who resigns the training and returns to a lesser life because they’re afraid of the danger of sharks.

an4.122:5.10.verse: ‘Danger of sharks’ is a term for ladies.

an4.122:5.11.verse: This is called the danger of sharks.

an4.122:5.12.verse: These are the four dangers that a gentleman gone forth from the lay life to homelessness in this teaching and training should anticipate.”

an4.123:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.123:1.3.verse: Take an individual who, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

an4.123:1.4.verse: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.

an4.123:1.5.verse: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the Divinity’s host.

an4.123:1.6.verse: The lifespan of the gods of the Divinity’s host is one eon.

an4.123:1.7.verse: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.

an4.123:1.8.verse: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.

an4.123:1.9.verse: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.

an4.123:2.1.verse: Furthermore, take an individual who, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, enters and remains in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

an4.123:2.2.verse: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.

an4.123:2.3.verse: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of sublime luminosity.

an4.123:2.4.verse: The lifespan of the gods of sublime luminosity is two eons.

an4.123:2.5.verse: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.

an4.123:2.6.verse: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.

an4.123:2.7.verse: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.

an4.123:3.1.verse: Furthermore, take an individual who, with the fading away of rapture, enters and remains in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

an4.123:3.2.verse: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.

an4.123:3.3.verse: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of universal beauty.

an4.123:3.4.verse: The lifespan of the gods of universal beauty is four eons.

an4.123:3.5.verse: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.

an4.123:3.6.verse: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.

an4.123:3.7.verse: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.

an4.123:4.1.verse: Furthermore, take an individual who, with the giving up of pleasure and pain, and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, enters and remains in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

an4.123:4.2.verse: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.

an4.123:4.3.verse: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of abundant fruit.

an4.123:4.4.verse: The lifespan of the gods of abundant fruit is five hundred eons.

an4.123:4.5.verse: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.

an4.123:4.6.verse: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.

an4.123:4.7.verse: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.

an4.123:4.8.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.124:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.124:1.3.verse: Take an individual who, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption …

an4.124:1.4.verse: They contemplate the phenomena there—included in form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness—as impermanent, as suffering, as diseased, as a boil, as a dart, as gloom, as an affliction, as alien, as breaking apart, as empty, as not-self.

an4.124:1.5.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the pure abodes.

an4.124:1.6.verse: This rebirth is distinct from that of ordinary people.

an4.124:2.1.verse: Furthermore, take an individual who, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, enters and remains in the second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption …

an4.124:2.2.verse: They contemplate the phenomena there—included in form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness—as impermanent, as suffering, as diseased, as a boil, as a dart, as gloom, as an affliction, as alien, as breaking apart, as empty, as not-self.

an4.124:2.3.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the pure abodes.

an4.124:2.4.verse: This rebirth is distinct from that of ordinary people.

an4.124:2.5.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

an4.125:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.

an4.125:1.3.verse: Firstly, an individual meditates spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

an4.125:1.4.verse: They enjoy this and like it and find it rewarding.

an4.125:1.5.verse: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the Divinity’s host.

an4.125:1.6.verse: The lifespan of the gods of the Divinity’s host is one eon.

an4.125:1.7.verse: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.

an4.125:1.8.verse: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.

an4.125:1.9.verse: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.

an4.125:2.1.verse: Furthermore, an individual meditates spreading a heart full of compassion … They’re reborn in the company of the gods of sublime luminosity. The lifespan of the gods of sublime luminosity is two eons.

an4.125:2.2.verse: Furthermore, an individual meditates spreading a heart full of rejoicing … They’re reborn in the company of the gods of universal beauty. The lifespan of the gods of universal beauty is four eons.

an4.125:2.3.verse: Furthermore, an individual meditates spreading a heart full of equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

an4.125:2.4.verse: They enjoy this and like it and find it rewarding.

an4.125:2.5.verse: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die

an4.125:2.7.verse: they’re reborn in the company of the gods of abundant fruit.

an4.125:2.8.verse: The lifespan of the gods of abundant fruit is five hundred eons.

an4.125:2.9.verse: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.

an4.125:2.10.verse: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.

an4.125:2.11.verse: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.

an4.125:2.12.verse: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
