an4.200:11.1.verse: And how does a mendicant push back?

an4.200:11.2.verse: It’s when someone abuses, annoys, or argues with a mendicant, and the mendicant abuses, annoys, or argues back at them.

an4.200:11.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant pushes back.

an4.200:12.1.verse: And how does a mendicant not push back?

an4.200:12.2.verse: It’s when someone abuses, annoys, or argues with a mendicant, and the mendicant doesn’t abuse, annoy, or argue back at them.

an4.200:12.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant doesn’t push back.

an4.200:13.1.verse: And how does a mendicant fume?

an4.200:13.2.verse: When there is the concept ‘I am’, there are the concepts ‘I am such’, ‘I am thus’, ‘I am otherwise’; ‘I am fleeting’, ‘I am lasting’; ‘mine’, ‘such is mine’, ‘thus is mine’, ‘otherwise is mine’; ‘also mine’, ‘such is also mine’, ‘thus is also mine’, ‘otherwise is also mine’; ‘I will be’, ‘I will be such’, ‘I will be thus’, ‘I will be otherwise’.

an4.200:14.1.verse: And how does a mendicant not fume?

an4.200:14.2.verse: When there is no concept ‘I am’, there are no concepts ‘I am such’, ‘I am thus’, ‘I am otherwise’; ‘I am fleeting’, ‘I am lasting’; ‘mine’, ‘such is mine’, ‘thus is mine’, ‘otherwise is mine’; ‘also mine’, ‘such is also mine’, ‘thus is also mine’, ‘otherwise is also mine’; ‘I will be’, ‘I will be such’, ‘I will be thus’, ‘I will be otherwise’.

an4.200:14.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant doesn’t fume.

an4.200:15.1.verse: And how is a mendicant ignited?

an4.200:15.2.verse: When there is the concept ‘I am because of this’, there are the concepts ‘I am such because of this’, ‘I am thus because of this’, ‘I am otherwise because of this’; ‘I am fleeting because of this’, ‘I am lasting because of this’; ‘mine because of this’, ‘such is mine because of this’, ‘thus is mine because of this’, ‘otherwise is mine because of this’; ‘also mine because of this’, ‘such is also mine because of this’, ‘thus is also mine because of this’, ‘otherwise is also mine because of this’; ‘I will be because of this’, ‘I will be such because of this’, ‘I will be thus because of this’, ‘I will be otherwise because of this’.

an4.200:15.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is ignited.

an4.200:16.1.verse: And how is a mendicant not ignited?

an4.200:16.2.verse: When there is no concept ‘I am because of this’, there are no concepts ‘I am such because of this’, ‘I am thus because of this’, ‘I am otherwise because of this’; ‘I am fleeting because of this’, ‘I am lasting because of this’; ‘mine because of this’, ‘such is mine because of this’, ‘thus is mine because of this’, ‘otherwise is mine because of this’; ‘also mine because of this’, ‘such is also mine because of this’, ‘thus is also mine because of this’, ‘otherwise is also mine because of this’; ‘I will be because of this’, ‘I will be such because of this’, ‘I will be thus because of this’, ‘I will be otherwise because of this’.

an4.200:16.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is not ignited.

an4.200:17.1.verse: And how does a mendicant burn up?

an4.200:17.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant hasn’t given up the conceit ‘I am’, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.

an4.200:17.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is burned up.

an4.200:18.1.verse: And how does a mendicant not burn up?

an4.200:18.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant has given up the conceit ‘I am’, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.

an4.200:18.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is not burned up.”

an4.201:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you an untrue person and an even more untrue person,

an4.201:1.2.verse: a true person and an even truer person.

an4.201:1.3.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

an4.201:2.2.verse: It’s someone who kills living creatures, steals, commits sexual misconduct, lies, and consumes intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

an4.201:2.3.verse: This is called an untrue person.

an4.201:3.1.verse: And what is an even more untrue person?

an4.201:3.2.verse: It’s someone who kills living creatures, steals, commits sexual misconduct, lies, and consumes intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor. And they encourage others to do these things.

an4.201:3.7.verse: This is called an even more untrue person.

an4.201:4.1.verse: And what is a true person?

an4.201:4.2.verse: It’s someone who doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

an4.201:4.3.verse: This is called a true person.

an4.201:5.1.verse: And what is an even truer person?

an4.201:5.2.verse: It’s someone who doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor. And they encourage others to refrain from these things.

an4.201:5.7.verse: This is called an even truer person.”

an4.202:1.2.verse: a true person and an even truer person.

an4.202:4.1.verse: And what is a true person?

an4.202:4.2.verse: It’s someone who is faithful, conscientious, prudent, learned, energetic, mindful, and wise.

an4.222:1.1.verse: “When a foolish, incompetent untrue person has four qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

an4.222:2.3.verse: Good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and right view.

an4.222:2.4.verse: When an astute, competent true person possesses these four qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.”

an4.229:1.1.verse: “A foolish person … brims with much wickedness. … They’re faithless, unethical, shameless, and imprudent. … An astute person … brims with much merit. … They’re faithful, ethical, conscientious, and prudent. …”

an4.230:1.1.verse: “A foolish person … brims with much wickedness. … They’re faithless, unethical, lazy, and witless. … An astute person … brims with much merit. … They’re faithful, ethical, energetic, and wise.

an4.230:1.2.verse: When an astute, competent true person possesses these four qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.”

an4.231:1.3.verse: A poet who thoughtfully composes their own work, a poet who repeats the oral transmission, a poet who educates, and a poet who improvises.

an4.232:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I declare these four kinds of deeds, having realized them with my own insight.

an4.232:1.3.verse: There are dark deeds with dark results.

an4.232:1.4.verse: There are bright deeds with bright results.

an4.232:1.5.verse: There are dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results.

an4.232:1.6.verse: There are neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.

an4.232:1.7.verse: These are the four kinds of deeds that I declare, having realized them with my own insight.”

an4.233:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I declare these four kinds of deeds, having realized them with my own insight.

an4.233:1.3.verse: There are dark deeds with dark results;

an4.233:1.5.verse: dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results; and

an4.233:1.6.verse: neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.

an4.233:2.1.verse: And what are dark deeds with dark results?

an4.233:2.2.verse: It’s when someone makes hurtful choices by way of body, speech, and mind.

an4.233:2.3.verse: Having made these choices, they’re reborn in a hurtful world,

an4.233:2.5.verse: Touched by hurtful contacts, they experience hurtful feelings that are absolutely painful—like the beings in hell.

an4.233:2.6.verse: These are called dark deeds with dark results.

an4.233:3.1.verse: And what are bright deeds with bright results?

an4.233:3.2.verse: It’s when someone makes pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind.

an4.233:3.3.verse: Having made these choices, they’re reborn in a pleasing world,

an4.233:3.5.verse: Touched by pleasing contacts, they experience pleasing feelings of absolute happiness—like the gods of universal beauty.

an4.233:3.6.verse: These are called bright deeds with bright results.

an4.233:4.1.verse: And what are dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results?

an4.233:4.2.verse: It’s when someone makes both hurtful and pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind.

an4.233:4.3.verse: Having made these choices, they are reborn in a world that is both hurtful and pleasing,

an4.233:4.4.verse: where hurtful and pleasing contacts strike them.

an4.233:4.5.verse: Touched by both hurtful and pleasing contacts, they experience both hurtful and pleasing feelings that are a mixture of pleasure and pain—like humans, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.

an4.233:4.6.verse: These are called dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results.

an4.233:5.1.verse: And what are neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds?

an4.233:5.2.verse: It’s the intention to give up dark deeds with dark results, bright deeds with bright results, and both dark and bright deeds with both dark and bright results.

an4.233:5.3.verse: These are called neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.

an4.233:5.4.verse: These are the four kinds of deeds that I declare, having realized them with my own insight.”

an4.234:1.1.verse: Then Sikhāmoggallāna the brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

an4.234:1.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, Sikhāmoggallāna sat down to one side, and said to the Buddha:

an4.234:2.1.verse: “Worthy Gotama, a few days ago the student Soṇakāyana came to me and said:

an4.234:2.2.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama advocates not doing any deeds. So he teaches the annihilation of the world!’

an4.234:2.3.verse: The world exists through deeds, and it remains because deeds are undertaken.”

an4.234:3.1.verse: “Brahmin, I can’t recall even seeing the student Soṇakāyana,

an4.234:3.2.verse: so how could we possibly have had such a discussion?

an4.234:3.3.verse: I declare these four kinds of deeds, having realized them with my own insight.

an4.234:3.5.verse: There are dark deeds with dark results;

an4.234:3.7.verse: dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results; and

an4.234:3.8.verse: neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.

an4.234:4.1.verse: And what are dark deeds with dark results?

an4.234:4.2.verse: It’s when someone makes hurtful choices by way of body, speech, and mind. …

an4.234:4.5.verse: Touched by hurtful contacts, they experience hurtful feelings that are absolutely painful—like the beings in hell.

an4.234:4.6.verse: These are called dark deeds with dark results.

an4.234:5.1.verse: And what are bright deeds with bright results?

an4.234:5.2.verse: It’s when someone makes pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind. …

an4.234:5.5.verse: Touched by pleasing contacts, they experience pleasing feelings of absolute happiness—like the gods of universal beauty.

an4.234:5.6.verse: These are called bright deeds with bright results.

an4.234:6.1.verse: And what are dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results?

an4.234:6.2.verse: It’s when someone makes both hurtful and pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind. …

an4.234:6.5.verse: Touched by both hurtful and pleasing contacts, they experience both hurtful and pleasing feelings that are a mixture of pleasure and pain—like humans, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.

an4.234:6.6.verse: These are called dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results.

an4.234:7.1.verse: And what are neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds?

an4.234:7.2.verse: It’s the intention to give up dark deeds with dark results, bright deeds with bright results, and both dark and bright deeds with both dark and bright results.

an4.234:7.3.verse: These are called neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.

an4.234:7.4.verse: These are the four kinds of deeds that I declare, having realized them with my own insight.”

an4.235:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I declare these four kinds of deeds, having realized them with my own insight.

an4.235:1.3.verse: There are dark deeds with dark results;

an4.235:1.5.verse: dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results; and

an4.235:1.6.verse: neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.

an4.235:1.7.verse: And what are dark deeds with dark results?

an4.235:1.8.verse: It’s when someone kills living creatures, steals, commits sexual misconduct, lies, and consumes intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

an4.235:1.9.verse: These are called dark deeds with dark results.

an4.235:2.1.verse: And what are bright deeds with bright results?

an4.235:2.2.verse: It’s when someone doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

an4.235:2.3.verse: These are called bright deeds with bright results.

an4.235:3.1.verse: And what are dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results?

an4.235:3.2.verse: It’s when someone makes both hurtful and pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind. These are called dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results.

an4.235:4.1.verse: And what are neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds?

an4.235:4.2.verse: It’s the intention to give up dark deeds with dark results, bright deeds with bright results, and both dark and bright deeds with both dark and bright results. These are called neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.

an4.235:4.3.verse: These are the four kinds of deeds that I declare, having realized them with my own insight.”

an4.236:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I declare these four kinds of deeds, having realized them with my own insight.

an4.236:1.3.verse: There are dark deeds with dark results;

an4.236:1.5.verse: dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results; and

an4.236:1.6.verse: neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.

an4.236:2.1.verse: And what are dark deeds with dark results?

an4.236:2.2.verse: It’s when someone murders their mother or father or a perfected one. They maliciously shed the blood of a Realized One. Or they cause a schism in the Saṅgha.

an4.236:2.3.verse: These are called dark deeds with dark results.

an4.236:3.1.verse: And what are bright deeds with bright results?

an4.236:3.2.verse: It’s when someone doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, or commit sexual misconduct. They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re content, kind-hearted, with right view.

an4.236:3.3.verse: These are called bright deeds with bright results.

an4.236:4.1.verse: And what are dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results?

an4.236:4.2.verse: It’s when someone makes both hurtful and pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind. These are called dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results.

an4.236:5.1.verse: And what are neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds?

an4.236:5.2.verse: It’s the intention to give up dark deeds with dark results, bright deeds with bright results, and both dark and bright deeds with both dark and bright results. These are called neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.

an4.236:5.3.verse: These are the four kinds of deeds that I declare, having realized them with my own insight.”

an4.237:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I declare these four kinds of deeds, having realized them with my own insight.

an4.237:1.3.verse: There are dark deeds with dark results;

an4.237:1.5.verse: dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results; and

an4.237:1.6.verse: neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.

an4.237:2.1.verse: And what are dark deeds with dark results?

an4.237:2.2.verse: It’s when someone makes hurtful choices by way of body, speech, and mind. These are called dark deeds with dark results.

an4.237:3.1.verse: And what are bright deeds with bright results?

an4.237:3.2.verse: It’s when someone makes pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind. These are called bright deeds with bright results.

an4.237:4.1.verse: And what are dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results?

an4.237:4.2.verse: It’s when someone makes both hurtful and pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind. These are called dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results.

an4.237:5.1.verse: And what are neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds?

an4.237:5.2.verse: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

an4.237:5.3.verse: These are called neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.

an4.237:5.4.verse: These are the four kinds of deeds that I declare, having realized them with my own insight.”

an4.238:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I declare these four kinds of deeds, having realized them with my own insight. …

an4.238:1.2.verse: And what are dark deeds with dark results? It’s when someone makes hurtful choices by way of body, speech, and mind. These are called dark deeds with dark results.

an4.238:2.1.verse: And what are bright deeds with bright results?

an4.238:2.2.verse: It’s when someone makes pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind. These are called bright deeds with bright results.

an4.238:3.1.verse: And what are dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results?

an4.238:3.2.verse: It’s when someone makes both hurtful and pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind. These are called dark and bright deeds with dark and bright results.

an4.238:4.1.verse: And what are neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds?

an4.238:4.2.verse: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

an4.238:4.3.verse: These are called neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.

an4.238:4.4.verse: These are the four kinds of deeds that I declare, having realized them with my own insight.”

an4.239:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.239:1.3.verse: Blameworthy deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, and blameworthy view.

an4.239:1.4.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.239:2.1.verse: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an4.239:2.3.verse: Blameless deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, and blameless view.

an4.239:2.4.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an4.240:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.240:1.3.verse: Hurtful deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, and hurtful view.

an4.240:1.4.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.240:2.1.verse: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an4.240:2.3.verse: Pleasing deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, and pleasing view.

an4.240:2.4.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an4.241:1.1.verse: “‘Only here is there a first ascetic, here a second ascetic, here a third ascetic, and here a fourth ascetic.

an4.241:1.2.verse: Other sects are empty of ascetics.’

an4.241:1.3.verse: This, mendicants, is how you should rightly roar your lion’s roar.

an4.241:2.1.verse: And who is the first ascetic?

an4.241:2.2.verse: It’s a mendicant who—with the ending of three fetters—is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

an4.241:3.1.verse: And who is the second ascetic?

an4.241:3.2.verse: It’s a mendicant who—with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion—is a once-returner. They come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.

an4.241:4.1.verse: And who is the third ascetic?

an4.241:4.2.verse: It’s a mendicant who—with the ending of the five lower fetters—is reborn spontaneously. They’re extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.

an4.241:5.1.verse: And who is the fourth ascetic?

an4.241:5.2.verse: It’s a mendicant who realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an4.241:6.1.verse: ‘Only here is there a first ascetic, here a second ascetic, here a third ascetic, and here a fourth ascetic.

an4.241:6.2.verse: Other sects are empty of ascetics.’

an4.241:6.3.verse: This, mendicants, is how you should rightly roar your lion’s roar.”

an4.242:0.3.verse: Benefits of Relying on a True Person

an4.242:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you can expect four benefits from relying on a true person.

an4.242:1.3.verse: Growth in noble ethics, immersion, wisdom, and freedom.

an4.242:1.4.verse: You can expect these four benefits from relying on a true person.”

an4.243:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

an4.243:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

an4.243:1.3.verse: “Well, Ānanda, has that disciplinary issue been settled yet?”

an4.243:1.5.verse: Venerable Anuruddha’s protégé Bāhiya remains entirely committed to creating a schism in the Saṅgha.

an4.243:1.6.verse: But Anuruddha doesn’t think to say a single word about it.”

an4.243:2.1.verse: “But Ānanda, since when has Anuruddha been involved in disciplinary issues in the midst of the Saṅgha?

an4.243:2.2.verse: Shouldn’t you, together with Sāriputta and Moggallāna, settle all disciplinary issues that come up?

an4.243:3.1.verse: A bad monk sees four reasons to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

an4.243:3.3.verse: Take an unethical monk, of bad qualities, filthy, with suspicious behavior, underhand, no true ascetic or spiritual practitioner—though claiming to be one—rotten inside, festering, and depraved.

an4.243:3.5.verse: ‘Suppose the monks know that I’m a bad monk …

an4.243:3.6.verse: If they’re in harmony, they’ll expel me,

an4.243:3.7.verse: but if they’re divided they won’t.’

an4.243:3.8.verse: A bad monk sees this as the first reason to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

an4.243:4.1.verse: Furthermore, a bad monk has wrong view, he’s attached to an extremist view.

an4.243:4.3.verse: ‘Suppose the monks know that I have wrong view …

an4.243:4.4.verse: If they’re in harmony they’ll expel me,

an4.243:4.5.verse: but if they’re divided they won’t.’

an4.243:4.6.verse: A bad monk sees this as the second reason to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

an4.243:5.1.verse: Furthermore, a bad monk has wrong livelihood and earns a living by wrong livelihood.

an4.243:5.3.verse: ‘Suppose the monks know that I have wrong livelihood …

an4.243:5.4.verse: If they’re in harmony they’ll expel me,

an4.243:5.5.verse: but if they’re divided they won’t.’

an4.243:5.6.verse: A bad monk sees this as the third reason to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

an4.243:6.1.verse: Furthermore, a bad monk desires material things, honor, and admiration.

an4.243:6.3.verse: ‘Suppose the monks know that I desire material things, honor, and admiration.

an4.243:6.4.verse: If they’re in harmony they won’t honor, respect, revere, or venerate me,

an4.243:6.5.verse: but if they’re divided they will.’

an4.243:6.6.verse: A bad monk sees this as the fourth reason to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

an4.243:6.7.verse: A bad monk sees these four reasons to relish schism in the Saṅgha.”

an4.244:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four perils of offenses.

an4.244:1.3.verse: Suppose they were to arrest a bandit, a criminal and present him to the king, saying:

an4.244:1.4.verse: ‘Your Majesty, this is a bandit, a criminal.

an4.244:1.7.verse: ‘Go, my men, and tie this man’s arms tightly behind his back with a strong rope. Shave his head and march him from street to street and square to square to the beating of a harsh drum. Then take him out the south gate and there, to the south of the city, chop off his head.’

an4.244:1.8.verse: The king’s men would do as they were told.

an4.244:1.10.verse: ‘This man must have done a truly bad and reprehensible deed, a capital offense.

an4.244:1.12.verse: There’s no way I’d ever do such a bad and reprehensible deed, a capital offense.’

an4.244:1.13.verse: In the same way, take any monk or nun who has set up such an acute perception of peril regarding expulsion offenses.

an4.244:1.14.verse: It can be expected that if they haven’t committed an expulsion offense they won’t, and if they committed one they will deal with it properly.

an4.244:2.1.verse: Suppose a man was to put on a black cloth, mess up his hair, and put a club on his shoulder. Then he approaches a large crowd and says:

an4.244:2.2.verse: ‘Sirs, I’ve done a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of clubbing. I submit to your pleasure.’

an4.244:2.4.verse: ‘This man must have done a truly bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of clubbing. …

an4.244:2.7.verse: There’s no way I’d ever do such a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of clubbing.’

an4.244:2.8.verse: In the same way, take any monk or nun who has set up such an acute perception of peril regarding suspension offenses. It can be expected that if they haven’t committed a suspension offense they won’t, and if they committed one they will deal with it properly.

an4.244:3.1.verse: Suppose a man was to put on a black cloth, mess up his hair, and put a sack of ashes on his shoulder. Then he approaches a large crowd and says:

an4.244:3.2.verse: ‘Sirs, I’ve done a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of a sack of ashes.

an4.244:3.5.verse: ‘This man must have done a truly bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of a sack of ashes. …

an4.244:3.9.verse: There’s no way I’d ever do such a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of a sack of ashes.’

an4.244:3.10.verse: In the same way, take any monk or nun who has set up such an acute perception of peril regarding confessable offenses. It can be expected that if they haven’t committed a confessable offense they won’t, and if they committed one they will deal with it properly.

an4.244:4.1.verse: Suppose a man was to put on a black cloth and mess up his hair. Then he approaches a large crowd and says:

an4.244:4.2.verse: ‘Sirs, I’ve done a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of criticism.

an4.244:4.5.verse: ‘This man must have done a truly bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of criticism. …

an4.244:4.9.verse: There’s no way I’d ever do such a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of criticism.’

an4.244:4.10.verse: In the same way, take any monk or nun who has set up such an acute perception of peril regarding confessable offenses. It can be expected that if they haven’t committed a confessable offense they won’t, and if they committed one they will deal with it properly.

an4.244:4.11.verse: These are the four perils of offenses.”

an4.245:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, this spiritual life is lived with training as its benefit, with wisdom as its overseer, with freedom as its core, and with mindfulness as its ruler.

an4.245:1.2.verse: And how is training its benefit?

an4.245:1.3.verse: Firstly, I laid down for my disciples the training that deals with supplementary regulations in order to inspire confidence in those without it and to increase confidence in those who have it.

an4.245:1.4.verse: They undertake whatever supplementary regulations I have laid down, keeping them intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred.

an4.245:2.1.verse: Furthermore, I laid down for my disciples the training that deals with the fundamentals of the spiritual life in order to rightly end suffering in every way.

an4.245:2.2.verse: They undertake whatever training that deals with the fundamentals of the spiritual life I have laid down, keeping it intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred.

an4.245:2.3.verse: That’s how training is its benefit.

an4.245:3.1.verse: And how is wisdom its overseer?

an4.245:3.2.verse: I taught the Dhamma to my disciples in order to rightly end suffering in every way.

an4.245:3.3.verse: They examine with wisdom any teachings I taught them.

an4.245:3.4.verse: That’s how wisdom is its overseer.

an4.245:4.1.verse: And how is freedom its core?

an4.245:4.2.verse: I taught the Dhamma to my disciples in order to rightly end suffering in every way.

an4.245:4.3.verse: They experience through freedom any teachings I taught them.

an4.245:4.4.verse: That’s how freedom is its core.

an4.245:5.1.verse: And how is mindfulness its ruler?

an4.245:5.2.verse: Mindfulness is well established in oneself: ‘In this way I’ll fulfill the training dealing with supplementary regulations, or support with wisdom in every situation the training dealing with supplementary regulations I’ve already fulfilled.’

an4.245:5.3.verse: Mindfulness is well established in oneself: ‘In this way I’ll fulfill the training dealing with the fundamentals of the spiritual life, or support with wisdom in every situation the training dealing with the fundamentals of the spiritual life I’ve already fulfilled.’

an4.245:5.4.verse: Mindfulness is well established in oneself: ‘In this way I’ll examine with wisdom the teaching that I haven’t yet examined, or support with wisdom in every situation the teaching I’ve already examined.’

an4.245:5.5.verse: Mindfulness is well established in oneself: ‘In this way I’ll experience through freedom the teaching that I haven’t yet experienced, or support with wisdom in every situation the teaching I’ve already experienced.’

an4.245:5.6.verse: That’s how mindfulness is its ruler.

an4.245:5.7.verse: ‘This spiritual life is lived with training as its benefit, with wisdom as its overseer, with freedom as its core, and with mindfulness as its ruler.’

an4.245:5.8.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”

an4.246:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four ways of lying down.

an4.246:1.3.verse: The ways a corpse, a pleasure seeker, a lion, and a Realized One lie down.

an4.246:1.4.verse: And how does a corpse lie down?

an4.246:1.5.verse: Corpses usually lie flat on their backs.

an4.246:1.6.verse: This is called the way a corpse lies down.

an4.246:2.1.verse: And how does a pleasure seeker lie down?

an4.246:2.2.verse: Pleasure seekers usually lie down on their left side.

an4.246:2.3.verse: This is called the way a pleasure seeker lies down.

an4.246:3.1.verse: And how does a lion lie down?

an4.246:3.2.verse: The lion, king of beasts, lies down on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other, with his tail tucked between his thighs.

an4.246:3.3.verse: When he wakes, he lifts his front quarters and checks his hind quarters.

an4.246:3.4.verse: If he sees that any part of his body is disordered or displaced, he is displeased.

an4.246:3.5.verse: But if he sees that no part of his body is disordered or displaced, he is pleased.

an4.246:3.6.verse: This is called the way a lion lies down.

an4.246:4.1.verse: And how does a Realized One lie down?

an4.246:4.2.verse: It’s when a Realized One, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.

an4.246:4.3.verse: This is called the way a Realized One lies down.

an4.246:4.4.verse: These are the four ways of lying down.”

an4.247:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four are worthy of a monument.

an4.247:1.3.verse: A Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha; an independent Buddha; a disciple of a Realized One; and a wheel-turning monarch.

an4.247:1.4.verse: These four are worthy of a monument.”

an4.248:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four things lead to the growth of wisdom.

an4.248:1.3.verse: Associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, rational application of mind, and practicing in line with the teaching.

an4.248:1.4.verse: These four things lead to the growth of wisdom.”

an4.249:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four things are very helpful to a human being.

an4.249:1.3.verse: Associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, rational application of mind, and practicing in line with the teaching.

an4.249:1.4.verse: These four things are very helpful to a human being.”

an4.250:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four ignoble expressions.

an4.250:1.3.verse: Saying you’ve seen, heard, thought, or known something, but you haven’t.

an4.250:1.4.verse: These are the four ignoble expressions.”

an4.251:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four noble expressions.

an4.251:1.3.verse: Saying you haven’t seen, heard, thought, or known something, and you haven’t.

an4.251:1.4.verse: These are the four noble expressions.”

an4.252:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four ignoble expressions.

an4.252:1.3.verse: Saying you haven’t seen, heard, thought, or known something, and you have.

an4.252:1.4.verse: These are the four ignoble expressions.”

an4.253:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four noble expressions.

an4.253:1.3.verse: Saying you’ve seen, heard, thought, or known something, and you have.

an4.253:1.4.verse: These are the four noble expressions.”

an4.254:1.3.verse: There are things that should be completely understood by direct knowledge.

an4.254:1.4.verse: There are things that should be given up by direct knowledge.

an4.254:1.5.verse: There are things that should be developed by direct knowledge.

an4.254:1.6.verse: There are things that should be realized by direct knowledge.

an4.254:2.1.verse: And what are the things that should be completely understood by direct knowledge?

an4.254:2.3.verse: These are called the things that should be completely understood by direct knowledge.

an4.254:3.1.verse: And what are the things that should be given up by direct knowledge?

an4.254:3.2.verse: Ignorance and craving for continued existence.

an4.254:3.3.verse: These are called the things that should be given up by direct knowledge.

an4.254:4.1.verse: And what are the things that should be developed by direct knowledge?

an4.254:4.3.verse: These are called the things that should be developed by direct knowledge.

an4.254:5.1.verse: And what are the things that should be realized by direct knowledge?

an4.254:5.3.verse: These are called the things that should be realized by direct knowledge.

an4.255:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four ignoble searches.

an4.255:1.3.verse: Someone liable to old age searches only for what grows old.

an4.255:1.4.verse: Someone liable to sickness searches only for what gets sick.

an4.255:1.5.verse: Someone liable to death searches only for what dies.

an4.255:1.6.verse: Someone liable to become corrupted searches only for what is defiled.

an4.255:1.7.verse: These are the four ignoble searches.

an4.255:2.1.verse: There are these four noble searches.

an4.255:2.3.verse: Someone who is liable to grow old, knowing the drawback in what grows old, searches for that which is free of old age, the supreme sanctuary from the yoke, extinguishment.

an4.255:2.4.verse: Someone who is liable to get sick, knowing the drawback in what gets sick, searches for that which is free of sickness, the supreme sanctuary from the yoke, extinguishment.

an4.255:2.5.verse: Someone who is liable to die, knowing the drawback in what dies, searches for that which is free of death, the supreme sanctuary from the yoke, extinguishment.

an4.255:2.6.verse: Someone liable to become corrupted, knowing the drawback in what is defiled, searches for the undefiled supreme sanctuary from the yoke, extinguishment.

an4.255:2.7.verse: These are the four noble searches.”

an4.256:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four ways of being inclusive.

an4.256:1.3.verse: Giving, kindly words, taking care, and equality.

an4.256:1.4.verse: These are the four ways of being inclusive.”

an4.257:1.1.verse: Then Venerable Māluṅkyaputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

an4.257:2.1.verse: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

an4.257:2.2.verse: “Well now, Māluṅkyaputta, what are we to say to the young monks,

an4.257:2.3.verse: when even an old man like you, elderly and senior, asks the Realized One for brief advice?”

an4.257:2.4.verse: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief! May the Holy One teach me the Dhamma in brief! Hopefully I can understand the meaning of what the Buddha says! Hopefully I can be an heir of the Buddha’s teaching!”

an4.257:3.1.verse: “Māluṅkyaputta, there are four things that give rise to craving in a mendicant.

an4.257:3.6.verse: or rebirth in this or that state.

an4.257:3.7.verse: These are the four things that give rise to craving in a mendicant.

an4.257:3.8.verse: That craving is given up by a mendicant, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future. Then they’re called a mendicant who has cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit has made an end of suffering.”

an4.257:4.1.verse: When Māluṅkyaputta had been given this advice by the Buddha, he rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

an4.257:4.2.verse: Then Māluṅkyaputta, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

an4.257:4.3.verse: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

an4.257:4.4.verse: And Venerable Māluṅkyaputta became one of the perfected.

an4.258:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when families don’t stay wealthy for long, it’s always for one or more of these four reasons.

an4.258:1.3.verse: They don’t look for what’s lost; they don’t repair old things; they eat and drink too much; or they put an unethical woman or man in charge.

an4.258:1.4.verse: When families don’t stay wealthy for long, it’s always for one or more of these four reasons.

an4.258:2.1.verse: When families do stay wealthy for long, it’s always for one or more of these four reasons.

an4.258:2.3.verse: They look for what’s lost; they repair old things; they eat and drink in moderation; and they put an ethical woman or man in charge.

an4.258:2.4.verse: When families do stay wealthy for long, it’s always for one or more of these four reasons.”

an4.259:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a fine royal thoroughbred with four factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and reckoned a factor of kingship.

an4.259:1.3.verse: It’s when a fine royal thoroughbred is beautiful, strong, fast, and well-proportioned.

an4.259:1.4.verse: A fine royal thoroughbred with these four factors is worthy of a king. …

an4.259:2.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant with four qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

an4.259:2.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is beautiful, strong, fast, and well proportioned.

an4.259:3.1.verse: And how is a mendicant beautiful?

an4.259:3.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

an4.259:3.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is beautiful.

an4.259:4.1.verse: And how is a mendicant strong?

an4.259:4.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They are strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

an4.259:4.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is strong.

an4.259:5.1.verse: And how is a mendicant fast?

an4.259:5.2.verse: It’s when they truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

an4.259:5.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is fast.

an4.259:6.1.verse: And how is a mendicant well proportioned?

an4.259:6.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant receives robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

an4.259:6.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is well proportioned.

an4.259:7.1.verse: A mendicant with these four qualities … is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

an4.260:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a fine royal thoroughbred with four factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and reckoned a factor of kingship.

an4.260:1.3.verse: It’s when a fine royal thoroughbred is beautiful, strong, fast, and well-proportioned.

an4.260:1.4.verse: A fine royal thoroughbred with these four factors is worthy of a king. …

an4.260:2.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant with four qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

an4.260:2.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is beautiful, strong, fast, and well proportioned.

an4.260:3.1.verse: And how is a mendicant beautiful?

an4.260:3.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

an4.260:3.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is beautiful.

an4.260:4.1.verse: And how is a mendicant strong?

an4.260:4.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They are strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

an4.260:4.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is strong.

an4.260:5.1.verse: And how is a mendicant fast?

an4.260:5.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an4.260:5.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is fast.

an4.260:6.1.verse: And how is a mendicant well proportioned?

an4.260:6.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant receives robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

an4.260:6.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is well proportioned.

an4.260:7.1.verse: A mendicant with these four qualities … is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

an4.261:1.3.verse: The powers of energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

an4.262:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has four qualities they’re not ready to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

an4.262:1.3.verse: They have sensual, malicious, and cruel thoughts; or they’re witless, dull, and idiotic.

an4.262:1.4.verse: When a mendicant possesses these four qualities they’re not ready to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

an4.262:2.1.verse: When a mendicant has four qualities they’re ready to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

an4.262:2.3.verse: They have thoughts of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness; and they’re wise, bright, and clever.

an4.262:2.4.verse: When a mendicant possesses these four qualities they’re ready to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.”

an4.263:1.1.verse: “When a foolish, incompetent untrue person has four qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

an4.263:1.3.verse: Blameworthy deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, and blameworthy view.

an4.263:1.4.verse: When a foolish, incompetent untrue person possesses these four qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

an4.263:2.1.verse: When an astute, competent true person has four qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.

an4.263:2.3.verse: Blameless deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, and blameless view.

an4.263:2.4.verse: When an astute, competent true person possesses these four qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.”

an4.264:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.264:1.3.verse: They themselves kill living creatures; they encourage others to kill living creatures; they approve of killing living creatures; and they praise killing living creatures.

an4.264:1.4.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.264:2.1.verse: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an4.264:2.3.verse: They don’t themselves kill living creatures; they encourage others to not kill living creatures; they approve of not killing living creatures; and they praise not killing living creatures.

an4.264:2.4.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an4.265:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an4.265:1.4.verse: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there. …

an4.266:2.1.verse: They don’t themselves commit sexual misconduct …”

an4.273:2.1.verse: They themselves have right view; they encourage others to have right view; they approve of right view; and they praise right view.

an4.273:2.2.verse: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an4.274:1.1.verse: “For insight into greed, four things should be developed.

an4.274:1.3.verse: Firstly, a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

an4.274:1.4.verse: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings … mind … principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

an4.274:1.5.verse: For insight into greed, these four things should be developed.”

an4.275:1.1.verse: “For insight into greed, four things should be developed.

an4.275:1.3.verse: Firstly, a mendicant generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise.

an4.275:1.4.verse: …so that unskillful qualities that have arisen are given up … so that skillful qualities arise … so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.

an4.275:1.5.verse: For insight into greed, these four things should be developed.”

an4.276:1.1.verse: “For insight into greed, four things should be developed.

an4.276:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort.

an4.276:1.4.verse: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to energy …

an4.276:1.7.verse: For insight into greed, these four things should be developed.”

an4.277-303:1.1.verse: “For the complete understanding … finishing … giving up … ending … vanishing … fading away … cessation … giving away … letting go of greed, four things should be developed.”

an4.304-783:1.1.verse: “Of hate … delusion … anger … acrimony … disdain … contempt … jealousy … stinginess … deceit … deviousness … obstinacy … aggression … conceit … arrogance … vanity … negligence … for insight … complete understanding … finishing … giving up … ending … vanishing … fading away … cessation … giving away … letting go … four things should be developed.”

an4.304-783:1.5.verse: The Book of the Fours is finished.

an5.1:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

an5.1:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

an5.1:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five powers of a trainee.

an5.1:2.3.verse: The powers of faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.

an5.1:2.4.verse: These are the five powers of a trainee.

an5.1:3.1.verse: So you should train like this:

an5.1:3.2.verse: ‘We will have the trainee’s powers of faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.’

an5.1:3.4.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

an5.1:3.5.verse: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

an5.2:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five powers of a trainee.

an5.2:1.3.verse: The powers of faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.

an5.2:2.1.verse: And what is the power of faith?

an5.2:2.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

an5.2:2.3.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

an5.2:2.4.verse: This is called the power of faith.

an5.2:3.1.verse: And what is the power of conscience?

an5.2:3.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has a conscience. They’re conscientious about bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and conscientious about having any bad, unskillful qualities.

an5.2:3.3.verse: This is called the power of conscience.

an5.2:4.1.verse: And what is the power of prudence?

an5.2:4.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple is prudent. They’re prudent when it comes to bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and prudent when it comes to acquiring any bad, unskillful qualities.

an5.2:4.3.verse: This is called the power of prudence.

an5.2:5.1.verse: And what is the power of energy?

an5.2:5.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

an5.2:5.3.verse: This is called the power of energy.

an5.2:6.1.verse: And what is the power of wisdom?

an5.2:6.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

an5.2:6.3.verse: This is called the power of wisdom.

an5.2:6.4.verse: These are the five powers of a trainee.

an5.2:7.1.verse: So you should train like this:

an5.2:7.2.verse: ‘We will have the trainee’s powers of faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.’

an5.3:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has five qualities they live unhappily in this very life—with distress, anguish, and fever—and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a bad rebirth.

an5.3:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is faithless, shameless, imprudent, lazy, and witless.

an5.3:1.4.verse: When a mendicant possesses these five qualities they live unhappily in this very life—with distress, anguish, and fever—and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a bad rebirth.

an5.3:2.1.verse: When a mendicant has five qualities they live happily in this very life—without distress, anguish, or fever—and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a good rebirth.

an5.3:2.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is faithful, conscientious, prudent, energetic, and wise.

an5.3:2.4.verse: When a mendicant possesses these five qualities they live happily in this very life—without distress, anguish, or fever—and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a good rebirth.”

an5.4:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an5.4:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is faithless, shameless, imprudent, lazy, and witless.

an5.4:1.4.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an5.4:2.1.verse: A mendicant with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an5.4:2.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is faithful, conscientious, prudent, energetic, and wise.

an5.4:2.4.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an5.5:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, any monk or nun who resigns the training and returns to a lesser life deserves rebuttal and criticism on five legitimate grounds in this very life.

an5.5:1.3.verse: ‘You had no faith, conscience, prudence, energy, or wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’

an5.5:1.4.verse: Any monk or nun who resigns the training and returns to a lesser life deserves rebuttal and criticism on these five legitimate grounds in this very life.

an5.5:2.1.verse: Any monk or nun who lives the full and pure spiritual life in pain and sadness, weeping, with tearful face, deserves praise on five legitimate grounds in this very life.

an5.5:2.3.verse: ‘You had faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.’

an5.5:2.4.verse: Any monk or nun who lives the full and pure spiritual life in pain and sadness, weeping, with tearful face, deserves praise on these five legitimate grounds in this very life.”

an5.6:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you don’t become unskillful as long as faith is established in skillful qualities.

an5.6:1.2.verse: But when faith vanishes and faithlessness takes over,

an5.6:2.1.verse: You don’t become unskillful as long as conscience … prudence … energy … wisdom is established in skillful qualities.

an5.6:5.2.verse: But when wisdom vanishes and witlessness takes over,

an5.7:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, sentient beings are mostly charmed by sensual pleasures.

an5.7:1.2.verse: When a gentleman has abandoned the scythe and flail and gone forth from the lay life to homelessness, they’re qualified to be called ‘a faithful renunciate from a good family’.

an5.7:1.4.verse: Because a youth can get sensual pleasures of this kind or that.

an5.7:1.5.verse: Now, all sensual pleasures are just reckoned as ‘sensual pleasures’, regardless of whether they’re inferior, average, or superior.

an5.7:1.6.verse: Suppose there was a little baby boy who, because of his nursemaid’s negligence, puts a stick or stone in his mouth.

an5.7:1.7.verse: The nursemaid would very quickly notice

an5.7:1.8.verse: and try to take it out.

an5.7:1.9.verse: If that didn’t work, she’d cradle his head with her left hand, and take it out using a hooked finger of her right hand, even if it drew blood.

an5.7:1.11.verse: I admit she’d know, ‘This will distress the child,

an5.7:1.13.verse: Still, it should be done by a nursemaid who wants what’s best for him, out of kindness and sympathy.

an5.7:1.14.verse: And when the boy has grown up and has enough sense, his nursemaid would not be concerned about him, thinking:

an5.7:1.15.verse: ‘The boy can look after himself. He won’t be negligent.’

an5.7:2.1.verse: In the same way, I still need to look after a mendicant who hasn’t finished developing faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities.

an5.7:2.2.verse: But when a mendicant has finished developing faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom regarding skillful qualities, I need not be concerned, thinking:

an5.7:2.3.verse: ‘They can look after themselves. They won’t be negligent.’”

an5.8:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities fails, and doesn’t establish themselves in the true teaching.

an5.8:1.7.verse: witless fails, and doesn’t establish themselves in the true teaching.

an5.8:1.8.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities fails, and doesn’t establish themselves in the true teaching.

an5.8:2.1.verse: A mendicant with five qualities doesn’t fail, and establishes themselves in the true teaching.

an5.8:2.7.verse: wise doesn’t fail, and establishes themselves in the true teaching.

an5.8:2.8.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities doesn’t fail, and establishes themselves in the true teaching.”

an5.9:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a disrespectful and irreverent mendicant with five qualities fails, and doesn’t establish themselves in the true teaching.

an5.9:1.3.verse: A disrespectful and irreverent mendicant who is faithless …

an5.9:1.7.verse: witless fails, and doesn’t establish themselves in the true teaching.

an5.9:1.8.verse: A disrespectful and irreverent mendicant with these five qualities fails, and doesn’t establish themselves in the true teaching.

an5.9:2.1.verse: A respectful and reverent mendicant with five qualities doesn’t fail, and establishes themselves in the true teaching.

an5.9:2.3.verse: A respectful and reverent mendicant who is faithful …

an5.9:2.7.verse: wise doesn’t fail, and establishes themselves in the true teaching.

an5.9:2.8.verse: A respectful and reverent mendicant with these five qualities doesn’t fail, and establishes themselves in the true teaching.”

an5.10:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a disrespectful and irreverent mendicant with five qualities can’t achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training.

an5.10:1.3.verse: A disrespectful and irreverent mendicant who is faithless …

an5.10:1.7.verse: witless can’t achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training.

an5.10:1.8.verse: A disrespectful and irreverent mendicant with these five qualities can’t achieve growth, improvement, or maturity in this teaching and training.

an5.10:2.1.verse: A respectful and reverent mendicant with five qualities can achieve growth, improvement, and maturity in this teaching and training.

an5.10:2.3.verse: A respectful and reverent mendicant who is faithful …

an5.10:2.4.verse: conscientious … prudent … energetic … wise can achieve growth, improvement, and maturity in this teaching and training.

an5.10:2.5.verse: A respectful and reverent mendicant with these five qualities can achieve growth, improvement, and maturity in this teaching and training.”

an5.11:1.1.verse: “I claim to have attained perfection and consummation of insight regarding teachings not learned before from another.

an5.11:1.2.verse: The Realized One has five powers of a Realized One. With these he claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and turns the divine wheel.

an5.11:1.4.verse: The powers of faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.

an5.11:1.5.verse: These are the five powers of a Realized One. With these he claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and turns the divine wheel.”

an5.12:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five powers of a trainee.

an5.12:1.3.verse: The powers of faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.

an5.12:1.4.verse: These are the five powers of a trainee.

an5.12:1.5.verse: Of these five powers of a trainee, the power of wisdom is the chief. It holds and binds everything together.

an5.12:2.1.verse: It’s like a bungalow. The roof-peak is the chief point, which holds and binds everything together.

an5.12:2.2.verse: In the same way, of these five powers of a trainee, the power of wisdom is the chief. It holds and binds everything together.

an5.12:3.1.verse: So you should train like this:

an5.12:3.2.verse: ‘We will have the trainee’s powers of faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.’

an5.13:1.3.verse: The powers of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

an5.14:1.3.verse: The powers of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

an5.14:2.1.verse: And what is the power of faith?

an5.14:2.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

an5.14:2.3.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

an5.14:2.4.verse: This is called the power of faith.

an5.14:3.1.verse: And what is the power of energy?

an5.14:3.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

an5.14:3.3.verse: This is called the power of energy.

an5.14:4.1.verse: And what is the power of mindfulness?

an5.14:4.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple is mindful. They have utmost mindfulness and alertness, and can remember and recall what was said and done long ago.

an5.14:4.3.verse: This is called the power of mindfulness.

an5.14:5.1.verse: And what is the power of immersion?

an5.14:5.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

an5.14:5.3.verse: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

an5.14:5.4.verse: And with the fading away of rapture, they enter and remain in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

an5.14:5.5.verse: With the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

an5.14:5.6.verse: This is called the power of immersion.

an5.14:6.1.verse: And what is the power of wisdom?

an5.14:6.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

an5.14:6.3.verse: This is called the power of wisdom.

an5.15:1.3.verse: The powers of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

an5.15:1.4.verse: And where should the power of faith be seen?

an5.15:1.5.verse: In the four factors of stream-entry.

an5.15:1.7.verse: And where should the power of energy be seen?

an5.15:1.10.verse: And where should the power of mindfulness be seen?

an5.15:1.11.verse: In the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

an5.15:1.13.verse: And where should the power of immersion be seen?

an5.15:1.16.verse: And where should the power of wisdom be seen?

an5.16:1.3.verse: The powers of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

an5.16:1.5.verse: Of these five powers, the power of wisdom is the chief. It holds and binds everything together.

an5.16:1.6.verse: It’s like a bungalow. The roof-peak is the chief point, which holds and binds everything together.

an5.16:1.7.verse: In the same way, of these five powers, the power of wisdom is the chief. It holds and binds everything together.”

an5.17:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is practicing for their own welfare, but not that of others.

an5.17:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is personally accomplished in ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom. But they don’t encourage others in these qualities.

an5.17:1.8.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is practicing for their own welfare, but not that of others.”

an5.18:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is practicing for the welfare of others, but not their own.

an5.18:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is not personally accomplished in ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, or the knowledge and vision of freedom. But they encourage others in these qualities.

an5.18:1.8.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is practicing for the welfare of others, but not their own.”

an5.19:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is practicing neither for their own welfare, nor that of others.

an5.19:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is not personally accomplished in ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, or the knowledge and vision of freedom. Nor do they encourage others in these qualities.

an5.19:1.8.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is practicing neither for their own welfare, nor that of others.”

an5.20:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is practicing for both their own welfare and that of others.

an5.20:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is personally accomplished in ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom. And they encourage others in these qualities.

an5.20:1.7.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is practicing both for their own welfare and that of others.”

an5.21:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, it is quite impossible for a disrespectful and irreverent mendicant with incompatible lifestyle to fulfill the practice dealing with supplementary regulations regarding their spiritual companions.

an5.21:1.2.verse: Without fulfilling the practice dealing with supplementary regulations, it’s impossible to fulfill the practice of a trainee.

an5.21:1.3.verse: Without fulfilling the practice of a trainee, it’s impossible to fulfill ethics.

an5.21:1.4.verse: Without fulfilling ethics, it’s impossible to fulfill right view.

an5.21:1.5.verse: Without fulfilling right view, it’s impossible to fulfill right immersion.

an5.21:2.1.verse: But it is quite possible for a respectful and reverent mendicant with compatible lifestyle to fulfill the practice dealing with supplementary regulations regarding their spiritual companions.

an5.21:2.2.verse: Having fulfilled the practice dealing with supplementary regulations, it’s possible to fulfill the practice of a trainee.

an5.21:2.3.verse: Having fulfilled the practice of a trainee, it’s possible to fulfill ethics.

an5.21:2.4.verse: Having fulfilled ethics, it’s possible to fulfill right view.

an5.21:2.5.verse: Having fulfilled right view, it’s possible to fulfill right immersion.”

an5.22:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, it is quite impossible for a disrespectful and irreverent mendicant with incompatible lifestyle to fulfill the practice dealing with supplementary regulations regarding their spiritual companions.

an5.22:1.2.verse: Without fulfilling the practice dealing with supplementary regulations, it’s impossible to fulfill the practice of a trainee.

an5.22:1.3.verse: Without fulfilling the practice of a trainee, it’s impossible to fulfill the entire spectrum of ethics.

an5.22:1.4.verse: Without fulfilling the entire spectrum of ethics, it’s impossible to fulfill the entire spectrum of immersion.

an5.22:1.5.verse: Without fulfilling the entire spectrum of immersion, it’s impossible to fulfill the entire spectrum of wisdom.

an5.22:2.1.verse: But it is quite possible for a respectful and reverent mendicant with compatible lifestyle to fulfill the practice dealing with supplementary regulations regarding their spiritual companions.

an5.22:2.2.verse: Having fulfilled the practice dealing with supplementary regulations, it’s possible to fulfill the practice of a trainee.

an5.22:2.3.verse: Having fulfilled the practice of a trainee, it’s possible to fulfill the entire spectrum of ethics.

an5.22:2.4.verse: Having fulfilled the entire spectrum of ethics, it’s possible to fulfill the entire spectrum of immersion.

an5.22:2.5.verse: Having fulfilled the entire spectrum of immersion, it’s possible to fulfill the entire spectrum of wisdom.”

an5.23:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five corruptions of native gold. When native gold is corrupted by these it’s not pliable, workable, or radiant, but is brittle and not completely ready for working.

an5.23:1.3.verse: Iron, copper, tin, lead, and silver.

an5.23:1.4.verse: When native gold is corrupted by these five corruptions it’s not pliable, workable, or radiant, but is brittle and not completely ready for working.

an5.23:1.5.verse: But when native gold is free of these five corruptions it becomes pliable, workable, and radiant, not brittle, and ready to be worked.

an5.23:1.6.verse: Then the goldsmith can successfully create any kind of ornament they want, whether a ring, earrings, a necklace, or a golden garland.

an5.23:2.1.verse: In the same way, there are these five corruptions of the mind. When the mind is corrupted by these it’s not pliable, workable, or radiant. It’s brittle, and not rightly immersed in samādhi for the ending of defilements.

an5.23:2.3.verse: Sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.

an5.23:2.4.verse: These are the five corruptions of the mind. When the mind is corrupted by these it’s not pliable, workable, or radiant. It’s brittle, and not rightly immersed in samādhi for the ending of defilements.

an5.23:2.5.verse: But when the mind is free of these five corruptions it’s pliable, workable, and radiant. It’s not brittle, and is rightly immersed in samādhi for the ending of defilements.

an5.23:2.6.verse: You extend your mind to realize by insight each and every thing that can be realized by insight; and you are capable of realizing those things, since each and every one is within range.

an5.23:3.1.verse: If you wish: ‘May I wield the many kinds of psychic power—multiplying myself and becoming one again; materializing and dematerializing; going unobstructed through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; diving in and out of the earth as if it were water; walking on water as if it were earth; flying cross-legged through the sky like a bird; touching and stroking with the hand the sun and moon, so mighty and powerful, controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity.’

an5.23:3.2.verse: You’re capable of realizing it, since each and every one is within range.

an5.23:4.1.verse: If you wish: ‘With clairaudience that is purified and superhuman, may I hear both kinds of sounds, human and heavenly, whether near or far.’

an5.23:4.2.verse: You’re capable of realizing it, since each and every one is within range.

an5.23:5.1.verse: If you wish: ‘May I understand the minds of other beings and individuals, having encompassed them with my mind.

an5.23:5.2.verse: May I understand mind with greed as “mind with greed”,

an5.23:5.3.verse: and mind without greed as “mind without greed”;

an5.23:5.4.verse: mind with hate as “mind with hate”,

an5.23:5.5.verse: and mind without hate as “mind without hate”;

an5.23:5.6.verse: mind with delusion as “mind with delusion”,

an5.23:5.7.verse: and mind without delusion as “mind without delusion”;

an5.23:5.12.verse: mind that is not supreme as “mind that is not supreme”,

an5.23:5.13.verse: and mind that is supreme as “mind that is supreme”;

an5.23:5.14.verse: mind immersed in samādhi as “mind immersed in samādhi”,

an5.23:5.15.verse: and mind not immersed in samādhi as “mind not immersed in samādhi”;

an5.23:5.18.verse: You’re capable of realizing it, since each and every one is within range.

an5.23:6.1.verse: If you wish: ‘May I recollect many kinds of past lives. That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. May I remember: “There, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn somewhere else. There, too, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn here.” May I recollect my many past lives, with features and details.’

an5.23:6.2.verse: You’re capable of realizing it, since each and every one is within range.

an5.23:7.1.verse: If you wish: ‘With clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, may I see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place—and understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds: “These dear beings did bad things by way of body, speech, and mind. They denounced the noble ones; they had wrong view; and they chose to act out of that wrong view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell. These dear beings, however, did good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They never denounced the noble ones; they had right view; and they chose to act out of that right view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.” And so, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, may I see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. And may I understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.’

an5.23:7.2.verse: You’re capable of realizing it, since each and every one is within range.

an5.23:8.1.verse: If you wish: ‘May I realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with my own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’

an5.23:8.2.verse: You’re capable of realizing it, since each and every one is within range.”

an5.24:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, an unethical person, who lacks ethics, has destroyed a vital condition for right immersion.

an5.24:1.2.verse: When there is no right immersion, one who lacks right immersion has destroyed a vital condition for true knowledge and vision.

an5.24:1.3.verse: When there is no true knowledge and vision, one who lacks true knowledge and vision has destroyed a vital condition for disillusionment and dispassion.

an5.24:1.4.verse: When there is no disillusionment and dispassion, one who lacks disillusionment and dispassion has destroyed a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.

an5.24:1.5.verse: Suppose there was a tree that lacked branches and foliage.

an5.24:1.6.verse: Its shoots, bark, softwood, and heartwood would not grow to fullness.

an5.24:1.7.verse: In the same way, an unethical person, who lacks ethics, has destroyed a vital condition for right immersion.

an5.24:1.8.verse: When there is no right immersion, one who lacks right immersion has destroyed a vital condition for true knowledge and vision.

an5.24:1.9.verse: When there is no true knowledge and vision, one who lacks true knowledge and vision has destroyed a vital condition for disillusionment and dispassion.

an5.24:1.10.verse: When there is no disillusionment and dispassion, one who lacks disillusionment and dispassion has destroyed a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.

an5.24:2.1.verse: An ethical person, who has fulfilled ethics, has fulfilled a vital condition for right immersion.

an5.24:2.2.verse: When there is right immersion, one who has fulfilled right immersion has fulfilled a vital condition for true knowledge and vision.

an5.24:2.3.verse: When there is true knowledge and vision, one who has fulfilled true knowledge and vision has fulfilled a vital condition for disillusionment and dispassion.

an5.24:2.4.verse: When there is disillusionment and dispassion, one who has fulfilled disillusionment and dispassion has fulfilled a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.

an5.24:2.5.verse: Suppose there was a tree that was complete with branches and foliage. Its shoots, bark, softwood, and heartwood would all grow to fullness.

an5.24:2.6.verse: In the same way, an ethical person, who has fulfilled ethics, has fulfilled a vital condition for right immersion.

an5.24:2.7.verse: When there is right immersion, one who has fulfilled right immersion has fulfilled a vital condition for true knowledge and vision.

an5.24:2.8.verse: When there is true knowledge and vision, one who has fulfilled true knowledge and vision has fulfilled a vital condition for disillusionment and dispassion.

an5.24:2.9.verse: When there is disillusionment and dispassion, one who has fulfilled disillusionment and dispassion has fulfilled a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.”

an5.25:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when right view is supported by five factors it has freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom as its fruit and benefit.

an5.25:2.2.verse: It’s when right view is supported by ethics, learning, discussion, serenity, and discernment.

an5.25:2.3.verse: When right view is supported by these five factors it has freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom as its fruit and benefit.”

an5.26:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five opportunities for freedom. If a mendicant stays diligent, keen, and resolute at these times, their mind is freed, their defilements are ended, and they arrive at the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

an5.26:2.2.verse: Firstly, the Teacher or a respected spiritual companion teaches Dhamma to a mendicant.

an5.26:2.3.verse: In whatever way the Teacher or a respected spiritual companion teaches Dhamma to that mendicant, they always feel inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma.

an5.26:2.6.verse: When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil.

an5.26:2.7.verse: When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss.

an5.26:2.8.verse: And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.

an5.26:2.9.verse: This is the first opportunity for freedom. If a mendicant stays diligent, keen, and resolute at this time, their mind is freed, their defilements are ended, and they arrive at the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

an5.26:3.1.verse: Furthermore, it may be that neither the Teacher nor a respected spiritual companion teaches Dhamma to a mendicant. But the mendicant teaches Dhamma in detail to others as they learned and memorized it.

an5.26:3.2.verse: In whatever way that mendicant teaches Dhamma in detail to others as they learned and memorized it, they always feel inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma.

an5.26:3.5.verse: When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil.

an5.26:3.6.verse: When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss.

an5.26:3.7.verse: And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.

an5.26:3.8.verse: This is the second opportunity for freedom. …

an5.26:4.1.verse: Furthermore, it may be that neither the Teacher nor … the mendicant teaches Dhamma. But the mendicant rehearses the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it.

an5.26:4.2.verse: In whatever way that mendicant rehearses the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it, they always feel inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma.
