an5.57:1.7.verse: ‘I am the owner of my deeds and heir to my deeds. Deeds are my womb, my relative, and my refuge.

an5.57:1.8.verse: I shall be the heir of whatever deeds I do, whether good or bad.’

an5.57:1.9.verse: A woman or a man, a layperson or a renunciate should often review this.

an5.57:2.1.verse: What is the advantage for a woman or a man, a layperson or a renunciate of often reviewing this: ‘I am liable to grow old, I am not exempt from old age’?

an5.57:2.2.verse: There are sentient beings who, intoxicated with the vanity of youth, do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

an5.57:2.3.verse: Reviewing this subject often, they entirely give up the vanity of youth, or at least reduce it.

an5.57:2.4.verse: This is the advantage for a woman or a man, a layperson or a renunciate of often reviewing this: ‘I am liable to grow old, I am not exempt from old age’.

an5.57:3.1.verse: What is the advantage of often reviewing this: ‘I am liable to get sick, I am not exempt from sickness’?

an5.57:3.2.verse: There are sentient beings who, drunk on the vanity of health, do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

an5.57:3.3.verse: Reviewing this subject often, they entirely give up the vanity of health, or at least reduce it.

an5.57:3.4.verse: This is the advantage of often reviewing this: ‘I am liable to get sick, I am not exempt from sickness’.

an5.57:4.1.verse: What is the advantage of often reviewing this: ‘I am liable to die, I am not exempt from death’?

an5.57:4.2.verse: There are sentient beings who, drunk on the vanity of life, do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

an5.57:4.3.verse: Reviewing this subject often, they entirely give up the vanity of life, or at least reduce it.

an5.57:4.4.verse: This is the advantage of often reviewing this: ‘I am liable to die, I am not exempt from death’.

an5.57:5.1.verse: What is the advantage of often reviewing this: ‘I must be parted and separated from all I hold dear and beloved’?

an5.57:5.2.verse: There are sentient beings who, aroused by desire and lust for their dear and beloved, do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

an5.57:5.3.verse: Reviewing this subject often, they entirely give up desire and lust for their dear and beloved, or at least reduce it.

an5.57:5.4.verse: This is the advantage of often reviewing this: ‘I must be parted and separated from all I hold dear and beloved’.

an5.57:6.1.verse: What is the advantage of often reviewing like this: ‘I am the owner of my deeds and heir to my deeds. Deeds are my womb, my relative, and my refuge.

an5.57:6.2.verse: I shall be the heir of whatever deeds I do, whether good or bad’?

an5.57:6.3.verse: There are sentient beings who do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

an5.57:6.4.verse: Reviewing this subject often, they entirely give up bad conduct, or at least reduce it.

an5.57:6.5.verse: This is the advantage for a woman or a man, a layperson or a renunciate of often reviewing like this: ‘I am the owner of my deeds and heir to my deeds. Deeds are my womb, my relative, and my refuge.

an5.57:6.6.verse: I shall be the heir of whatever deeds I do, whether good or bad.’

an5.57:7.2.verse: ‘It’s not just me who is liable to grow old, not being exempt from old age. For all sentient beings grow old according to their nature, as long as they come and go, pass away and are reborn.’

an5.57:7.3.verse: When they review this subject often, the path is born in them.

an5.57:7.4.verse: They cultivate, develop, and make much of it.

an5.57:7.5.verse: By doing so, they give up the fetters and eliminate the underlying tendencies.

an5.57:8.1.verse: ‘It’s not just me who is liable to get sick, not being exempt from sickness. For all sentient beings get sick according to their nature, as long as they come and go, pass away and are reborn.’

an5.57:8.2.verse: When they review this subject often, the path is born in them.

an5.57:8.3.verse: They cultivate, develop, and make much of it.

an5.57:8.4.verse: By doing so, they give up the fetters and eliminate the underlying tendencies.

an5.57:9.1.verse: ‘It’s not just me who is liable to die, not being exempt from death. For all sentient beings die according to their nature, as long as they come and go, pass away and are reborn.’

an5.57:9.2.verse: When they review this subject often, the path is born in them.

an5.57:9.3.verse: They cultivate, develop, and make much of it.

an5.57:9.4.verse: By doing so, they give up the fetters and eliminate the underlying tendencies.

an5.57:10.1.verse: ‘It’s not just me who must be parted and separated from all I hold dear and beloved. For all sentient beings must be parted and separated from all they hold dear and beloved, as long as they come and go, pass away and are reborn.’

an5.57:10.2.verse: When they review this subject often, the path is born in them.

an5.57:10.3.verse: They cultivate, develop, and make much of it.

an5.57:10.4.verse: By doing so, they give up the fetters and eliminate the underlying tendencies.

an5.57:11.1.verse: ‘It’s not just me who shall be the owner of my deeds and heir to my deeds.

an5.57:11.2.verse: For all sentient beings shall be the owners of their deeds and heirs to their deeds, as long as they come and go, pass away and are reborn.’

an5.57:11.3.verse: When they review this subject often, the path is born in them.

an5.57:11.4.verse: They cultivate, develop, and make much of it.

an5.57:11.5.verse: By doing so, they give up the fetters and eliminate the underlying tendencies.

an5.57:12.2.verse: and so are old age and death.

an5.57:12.3.verse: Though this is how their nature is,

an5.57:13.1.verse: If I were to be disgusted

an5.57:13.2.verse: with creatures whose nature is such,

an5.57:13.3.verse: it would not be appropriate for me,

an5.57:13.4.verse: since my life is just the same.

an5.57:14.2.verse: I understood the truth without attachments.

an5.57:16.4.verse: I’m committed to the spiritual life.”

an5.58:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

an5.58:1.2.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Vesālī for alms.

an5.58:1.3.verse: Then after the meal, on his return from almsround, he plunged deep into the Great Wood and sat at the root of a tree for the day’s meditation.

an5.58:2.1.verse: Now at that time several Licchavi youths took strung bows and, escorted by a pack of hounds, were going for a walk in the Great Wood when they saw the Buddha seated at the root of a tree.

an5.58:2.2.verse: When they saw him, they put down their strung bows, dispatched their hounds to one side, and went up to him. They bowed and silently paid homage to the Buddha with cupped palms.

an5.58:3.1.verse: Now at that time Mahānāma the Licchavi was going for a walk in the Great Wood when he saw those Licchavi youths silently paying homage to the Buddha with cupped palms.

an5.58:3.2.verse: Seeing this, he went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side,

an5.58:3.4.verse: “They will become Vajjis! They will become Vajjis!”

an5.58:4.1.verse: “But Mahānāma, why do you say that

an5.58:4.3.verse: “Sir, these Licchavi youths are violent, harsh, and brash.

an5.58:4.4.verse: Whenever sweets are left out for families—sugarcane, jujube fruits, pancakes, pies, or fritters—they filch them and eat them up.

an5.58:4.5.verse: And they hit women and girls of good families on their backs.

an5.58:4.6.verse: But now they’re silently paying homage to the Buddha with cupped palms.”

an5.58:5.2.verse: “Mahānāma, you can expect only growth, not decline, when you find five qualities in any gentleman—whether he’s an anointed aristocratic king, an appointed or hereditary official, an army general, a village chief, a guild chief, or a ruler of his own clan.

an5.58:6.2.verse: Firstly, a gentleman uses his legitimate wealth—earned by his efforts and initiative, built up with his own hands, gathered by the sweat of the brow—to honor, respect, esteem, and venerate his mother and father.

an5.58:6.3.verse: Honored in this way, his mother and father love him with a good heart, wishing:

an5.58:6.4.verse: ‘Live long! Stay alive for a long time!’

an5.58:6.5.verse: When a gentleman is loved by his mother and father, you can expect only growth, not decline.

an5.58:7.1.verse: Furthermore, a gentleman uses his legitimate wealth to honor, respect, esteem, and venerate his wives and children, bondservants, workers, and staff.

an5.58:7.2.verse: Honored in this way, his wives and children, bondservants, workers, and staff love him with a good heart, wishing:

an5.58:7.3.verse: ‘Live long! Stay alive for a long time!’

an5.58:7.4.verse: When a gentleman is loved by his wives and children, bondservants, workers, and staff, you can expect only growth, not decline.

an5.58:8.1.verse: Furthermore, a gentleman uses his legitimate wealth to honor, respect, esteem, and venerate those who work the neighboring fields, and those he does business with.

an5.58:8.2.verse: Honored in this way, those who work the neighboring fields, and those he does business with love him with a good heart, wishing:

an5.58:8.3.verse: ‘Live long! Stay alive for a long time!’

an5.58:8.4.verse: When a gentleman is loved by those who work the neighboring fields, and those he does business with, you can expect only growth, not decline.

an5.58:9.1.verse: Furthermore, a gentleman uses his legitimate wealth to honor, respect, esteem, and venerate the deities who receive spirit-offerings.

an5.58:9.2.verse: Honored in this way, the deities who receive spirit-offerings love him with a good heart, wishing:

an5.58:9.3.verse: ‘Live long! Stay alive for a long time!’

an5.58:9.4.verse: When a gentleman is loved by the deities, you can expect only growth, not decline.

an5.58:10.1.verse: Furthermore, a gentleman uses his legitimate wealth to honor, respect, esteem, and venerate ascetics and brahmins.

an5.58:10.2.verse: Honored in this way, ascetics and brahmins love him with a good heart, wishing:

an5.58:10.3.verse: ‘Live long! Stay alive for a long time!’

an5.58:10.4.verse: When a gentleman is loved by ascetics and brahmins, you can expect only growth, not decline.

an5.58:11.1.verse: You can expect only growth, not decline, when you find these five qualities in any gentleman—

an5.58:11.2.verse: whether he’s an anointed aristocratic king, an appointed or hereditary official, an army general, a village chief, a guild chief, or a ruler of his own clan.

an5.58:12.1.verse: He’s always dutiful to his mother and father,

an5.58:12.2.verse: and for the good of his wives and children.

an5.58:12.3.verse: He looks after those in his household,

an5.58:12.4.verse: and those dependent on him for their livelihood.

an5.58:13.2.verse: looks after the welfare of relatives—

an5.58:13.3.verse: both those who have passed away,

an5.58:14.1.verse: While living at home, an astute person

an5.58:14.2.verse: uses legitimate means to give rise to joy

an5.58:15.3.verse: They praise him in this life,

an5.58:15.4.verse: and he departs to rejoice in heaven.”

an5.59:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, it’s hard to find someone gone forth when old who has five qualities.

an5.59:1.3.verse: It’s hard to find someone gone forth when old who is sophisticated, well-presented, and learned, who can teach Dhamma, and has memorized the monastic law.

an5.59:1.4.verse: It’s hard to find someone gone forth when old who possesses these five qualities.”

an5.60:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, it’s hard to find someone gone forth when old who has five qualities.

an5.60:1.3.verse: It’s hard to find someone gone forth when old who is easy to admonish, retains what they learn, and learns respectfully, who can teach the Dhamma, and has memorized the monastic law.

an5.60:1.4.verse: It’s hard to find someone gone forth when old who possesses these five qualities.”

an5.61:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are very fruitful and beneficial. They have freedom from death as their objective and culmination.

an5.61:1.3.verse: The perceptions of ugliness, death, drawbacks, repulsiveness of food, and dissatisfaction with the whole world.

an5.61:1.4.verse: These five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are very fruitful and beneficial. They have freedom from death as their objective and culmination.”

an5.62:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are very fruitful and beneficial. They have freedom from death as their objective and culmination.

an5.62:1.3.verse: The perceptions of impermanence, not-self, death, repulsiveness of food, and dissatisfaction with the whole world.

an5.62:1.4.verse: These five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are very fruitful and beneficial. They have freedom from death as their objective and culmination.”

an5.63:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a male noble disciple who grows in five ways grows nobly, taking on what is essential and excellent in this life.

an5.63:1.3.verse: He grows in faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

an5.63:1.4.verse: A male noble disciple who grows in these five ways grows nobly, taking on what is essential and excellent in this life.

an5.63:2.1.verse: He who grows in faith and ethics,

an5.63:2.2.verse: wisdom, and both generosity and learning—

an5.63:2.3.verse: a good man such as he sees clearly,

an5.63:2.4.verse: and takes on what is essential for himself in this life.”

an5.64:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a female noble disciple who grows in five ways grows nobly, taking on what is essential and excellent in this life.

an5.64:1.3.verse: She grows in faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

an5.64:1.4.verse: A female noble disciple who grows in these five ways grows nobly, taking on what is essential and excellent in this life.

an5.64:2.1.verse: She who grows in faith and ethics,

an5.64:2.2.verse: wisdom, and both generosity and learning—

an5.64:2.3.verse: a virtuous laywoman such as she

an5.64:2.4.verse: takes on what is essential for herself in this life.”

an5.65:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is fit to hold a discussion with their spiritual companions.

an5.65:1.3.verse: A mendicant is personally accomplished in ethics, and answers questions that come up when discussing accomplishment in ethics.

an5.65:1.4.verse: They’re personally accomplished in immersion, and they answer questions that come up when discussing accomplishment in immersion.

an5.65:1.5.verse: They’re personally accomplished in wisdom, and they answer questions that come up when discussing accomplishment in wisdom.

an5.65:1.6.verse: They’re personally accomplished in freedom, and they answer questions that come up when discussing accomplishment in freedom.

an5.65:1.7.verse: They’re personally accomplished in the knowledge and vision of freedom, and they answer questions that come up when discussing accomplishment in the knowledge and vision of freedom.

an5.65:1.8.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is fit to hold a discussion with their spiritual companions.”

an5.66:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is fit to share their life with their spiritual companions.

an5.66:1.3.verse: A mendicant is personally accomplished in ethics, and answers questions posed when discussing accomplishment in ethics.

an5.66:1.4.verse: They’re personally accomplished in immersion, and they answer questions posed when discussing accomplishment in immersion.

an5.66:1.5.verse: They’re personally accomplished in wisdom, and they answer questions posed when discussing accomplishment in wisdom.

an5.66:1.6.verse: They’re personally accomplished in freedom, and they answer questions posed when discussing accomplishment in freedom.

an5.66:1.7.verse: They’re personally accomplished in the knowledge and vision of freedom, and they answer questions posed when discussing accomplishment in the knowledge and vision of freedom.

an5.66:1.8.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is fit to share their life with their spiritual companions.”

an5.67:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, any monk or nun who develops and cultivates five qualities can expect one of two results:

an5.67:1.2.verse: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.

an5.67:2.2.verse: A mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort …

an5.67:2.3.verse: A mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to energy, and active effort …

an5.67:2.4.verse: A mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to mental development, and active effort …

an5.67:2.5.verse: A mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to inquiry, and active effort.

an5.67:2.6.verse: And the fifth is sheer vigor.

an5.67:2.7.verse: Any monk or nun who develops and cultivates these five qualities can expect one of two results:

an5.67:2.8.verse: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”

an5.68:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, before my awakening—when I was still not awake but intent on awakening—I developed and cultivated five things.

an5.68:1.3.verse: The basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort …

an5.68:1.4.verse: the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to energy, and active effort …

an5.68:1.5.verse: the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to mental development, and active effort …

an5.68:1.6.verse: the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to inquiry, and active effort.

an5.68:1.7.verse: And the fifth is sheer vigor.

an5.68:1.8.verse: When I had developed and cultivated these five things, with vigor as fifth,

an5.68:1.9.verse: I extended the mind to realize by insight each and every thing that can be realized by insight; and I was capable of realizing those things, since each and every one was within range.

an5.68:2.1.verse: If I wished: ‘May I multiply myself and become one again … controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity.’

an5.68:2.2.verse: I was capable of realizing it, since each and every one is within range.

an5.68:3.1.verse: If I wished: … ‘May I realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with my own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’

an5.68:3.2.verse: I was capable of realizing it, since each and every one is within range.”

an5.69:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five things, when developed and cultivated, lead solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

an5.69:2.2.verse: A mendicant meditates observing the ugliness of the body, perceives the repulsiveness of food, perceives dissatisfaction with the whole world, observes the impermanence of all conditions, and has well established the perception of their own death.

an5.69:2.3.verse: These five things, when developed and cultivated, lead solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.”

an5.70:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five things, when developed and cultivated, lead to the ending of defilements.

an5.70:1.3.verse: A mendicant meditates observing the ugliness of the body, perceives the repulsiveness of food, perceives dissatisfaction with the whole world, observes the impermanence of all conditions, and has well established the perception of their own death.

an5.70:1.4.verse: These five things, when developed and cultivated, lead to the ending of defilements.”

an5.71:0.3.verse: Freedom of Heart is the Fruit (1st)

an5.71:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five things, when developed and cultivated, have freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom as their fruit and benefit.

an5.71:2.2.verse: A mendicant meditates observing the ugliness of the body, perceives the repulsiveness of food, perceives dissatisfaction with the whole world, observes the impermanence of all conditions, and has well established the perception of their own death.

an5.71:2.3.verse: These five things, when developed and cultivated, have freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom as their fruit and benefit.

an5.71:2.4.verse: When a mendicant has freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom,

an5.71:2.5.verse: such a mendicant is one who is called ‘one who has lifted the cross-bar’, ‘one who has filled in the moat’, ‘one who has pulled up the pillar’, ‘one who is unimpeded’, and also ‘a noble one with banner lowered and burden dropped, detached’.

an5.71:3.1.verse: And how has a mendicant lifted the cross-bar?

an5.71:3.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant has given up ignorance, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.

an5.71:3.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant has lifted the cross-bar.

an5.71:4.1.verse: And how has a mendicant filled in the moat?

an5.71:4.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant has given up transmigrating through births in future lives, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.

an5.71:4.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant has filled in the moat.

an5.71:5.1.verse: And how has a mendicant pulled up the pillar?

an5.71:5.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant has given up craving, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.

an5.71:5.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant has pulled up the pillar.

an5.71:6.1.verse: And how is a mendicant unimpeded?

an5.71:6.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant has given up the five lower fetters, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them, so they’re unable to arise in the future.

an5.71:6.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is unimpeded.

an5.71:7.1.verse: And how is a mendicant a noble one with with banner lowered and burden dropped, detached?

an5.71:7.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant has given up the conceit ‘I am’, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.

an5.71:7.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant is a noble one with banner lowered and burden dropped, detached.”

an5.72:0.3.verse: Freedom of Heart is the Fruit (2nd)

an5.72:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five things, when developed and cultivated, have freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom as their fruit and benefit.

an5.72:1.3.verse: The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of giving up, and the perception of fading away.

an5.72:1.4.verse: These five things, when developed and cultivated, have freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom as their fruit and benefit.

an5.72:1.5.verse: When a mendicant has freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom,

an5.72:1.6.verse: such a mendicant is one who is called ‘one who has lifted the cross-bar’, ‘one who has filled in the moat’, ‘one who has pulled up the pillar’, ‘one who is unimpeded’, and also ‘a noble one with banner lowered and burden dropped, detached’. …”

an5.73:0.3.verse: One Who Lives by the Teaching (1st)

an5.73:1.1.verse: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

an5.73:1.2.verse: “Sir, they speak of ‘one who lives by the teaching’.

an5.73:1.3.verse: How is a mendicant who lives by the teaching defined?”

an5.73:2.1.verse: “Mendicant, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

an5.73:2.2.verse: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

an5.73:2.3.verse: They spend too much time studying that teaching. They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.73:2.4.verse: That mendicant is called one who studies a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.73:3.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant teaches Dhamma in detail to others as they learned and memorized it.

an5.73:3.2.verse: They spend too much time advocating that teaching. They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.73:3.3.verse: That mendicant is called one who advocates a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.73:4.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant rehearses the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it.

an5.73:4.2.verse: They spend too much time reciting that teaching. They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.73:4.3.verse: That mendicant is called one who rehearses a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.73:5.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant thinks about and considers the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it.

an5.73:5.2.verse: They spend too much time thinking about that teaching. They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.73:5.3.verse: That mendicant is called one who thinks a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.73:6.1.verse: Take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

an5.73:6.2.verse: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

an5.73:6.3.verse: They don’t spend too much time studying that teaching. They don’t neglect retreat, and they’re committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.73:6.4.verse: That’s how a mendicant is one who lives by the teaching.

an5.73:7.1.verse: So, mendicant, I’ve taught you the one who studies a lot, the one who advocates a lot, the one who rehearses a lot, the one who thinks a lot, and the one who lives by the teaching.

an5.73:7.2.verse: Out of sympathy, I’ve done what a teacher should do who wants what’s best for their disciples.

an5.73:7.3.verse: Here are these roots of trees, and here are these empty huts. Practice absorption, mendicant! Don’t be negligent! Don’t regret it later! This is my instruction to you.”

an5.74:0.3.verse: One Who Lives by the Teaching (2nd)

an5.74:1.1.verse: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

an5.74:1.2.verse: “Sir, they speak of ‘one who lives by the teaching’.

an5.74:1.3.verse: How is a mendicant who lives by the teaching defined?”

an5.74:2.1.verse: “Mendicant, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

an5.74:2.2.verse: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

an5.74:2.3.verse: But they don’t understand the higher meaning.

an5.74:2.4.verse: That mendicant is called one who studies a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.74:3.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant teaches Dhamma in detail to others as they learned and memorized it. But they don’t understand the higher meaning.

an5.74:3.2.verse: That mendicant is called one who advocates a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.74:4.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant rehearses the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it. But they don’t understand the higher meaning.

an5.74:4.2.verse: That mendicant is called one who rehearses a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.74:5.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant thinks about and considers the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it. But they don’t understand the higher meaning.

an5.74:5.2.verse: That mendicant is called one who thinks a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.74:6.1.verse: Take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

an5.74:6.2.verse: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

an5.74:6.3.verse: And they do understand the higher meaning.

an5.74:6.4.verse: That’s how a mendicant is one who lives by the teaching.

an5.74:7.1.verse: So, mendicant, I’ve taught you the one who studies a lot, the one who advocates a lot, the one who rehearses a lot, the one who thinks a lot, and the one who lives by the teaching.

an5.74:7.2.verse: Out of sympathy, I’ve done what a teacher should do who wants what’s best for their disciples.

an5.74:7.3.verse: Here are these roots of trees, and here are these empty huts. Practice absorption, mendicant! Don’t be negligent! Don’t regret it later! This is my instruction to you.”

an5.75:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five warriors are found in the world.

an5.75:1.3.verse: Firstly, one warrior falters and founders at the mere sight of a cloud of dust. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

an5.75:1.5.verse: This is the first warrior found in the world.

an5.75:2.1.verse: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust,

an5.75:2.2.verse: but he falters and founders at the mere sight of a banner’s crest. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

an5.75:2.4.verse: This is the second warrior found in the world.

an5.75:3.1.verse: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest,

an5.75:3.2.verse: but he falters and founders at the mere sound of turmoil. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

an5.75:3.4.verse: This is the third warrior found in the world.

an5.75:4.1.verse: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil,

an5.75:4.2.verse: but he’s killed or injured when blows are struck.

an5.75:4.4.verse: This is the fourth warrior found in the world.

an5.75:5.1.verse: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil and being struck.

an5.75:5.2.verse: He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.

an5.75:5.4.verse: This is the fifth warrior found in the world.

an5.75:5.5.verse: These are the five warriors found in the world.

an5.75:6.1.verse: In the same way, these five individuals similar to warriors are found among the monks.

an5.75:6.3.verse: Firstly, one monk falters and founders at the mere sight of a cloud of dust. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.75:6.4.verse: Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.

an5.75:6.7.verse: ‘In such-and-such village or town there’s a woman or a girl who is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.’

an5.75:6.8.verse: Hearing this, he falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.75:6.9.verse: Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.

an5.75:7.1.verse: I say that this individual is like the warrior who falters and founders at the mere sight of a cloud of dust.

an5.75:7.4.verse: This is the first individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.75:8.1.verse: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust,

an5.75:8.2.verse: but at the mere sight of a banner’s crest he falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.75:8.3.verse: Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.

an5.75:8.5.verse: It’s when a monk doesn’t hear:

an5.75:8.6.verse: ‘In such-and-such village or town there’s a woman or a girl who is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.’

an5.75:8.7.verse: But he sees for himself a woman or a girl who is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.

an5.75:8.8.verse: Seeing her, he falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.75:8.9.verse: Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.

an5.75:9.1.verse: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust,

an5.75:9.2.verse: but he falters and founders at the mere sight of a banner’s crest.

an5.75:9.5.verse: This is the second individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.75:10.1.verse: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest,

an5.75:10.2.verse: but he falters and founders at the mere sound of turmoil. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.75:10.3.verse: Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.

an5.75:10.5.verse: It’s when a mendicant who has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut is approached by a lady. She smiles, chats, laughs, and teases him.

an5.75:10.6.verse: He falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.75:10.7.verse: Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.

an5.75:11.1.verse: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest,

an5.75:11.2.verse: but he falters and founders at the mere sound of turmoil.

an5.75:11.5.verse: This is the third individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.75:12.1.verse: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil,

an5.75:12.2.verse: but he’s killed or injured when blows are struck.

an5.75:12.4.verse: It’s when a mendicant who has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut is approached by a lady. She sits right by him, lies down, or embraces him.

an5.75:12.5.verse: Without resigning the training and declaring his inability to continue, he indulges in sex.

an5.75:13.1.verse: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil, but is killed or injured when blows are struck.

an5.75:13.4.verse: This is the fourth individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.75:14.1.verse: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil, and being struck. He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.

an5.75:14.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant who has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut is approached by a lady. She sits right by him, lies down, or embraces him.

an5.75:14.4.verse: But he disentangles and frees himself, and goes wherever he wants.

an5.75:14.5.verse: He frequents a secluded lodging—a wilderness, the root of a tree, a hill, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a forest, the open air, a heap of straw.

an5.75:15.1.verse: Gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, he sits down cross-legged, sets his body straight, and brings mindfulness to the present.

an5.75:15.2.verse: Giving up covetousness for the world, he meditates with a heart rid of covetousness, cleansing the mind of covetousness.

an5.75:15.3.verse: Giving up ill will and malevolence, he meditates with a mind rid of ill will, full of sympathy for all living beings, cleansing the mind of ill will.

an5.75:15.4.verse: Giving up dullness and drowsiness, he meditates with a mind rid of dullness and drowsiness, perceiving light, mindful and aware, cleansing the mind of dullness and drowsiness.

an5.75:15.5.verse: Giving up restlessness and remorse, he meditates without restlessness, his mind settled internally, cleansing the mind of restlessness and remorse.

an5.75:15.6.verse: Giving up doubt, he meditates having gone beyond doubt, not undecided about skillful qualities, cleansing the mind of doubt.

an5.75:15.7.verse: He gives up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.

an5.75:15.8.verse: Then, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, he enters and remains in the first absorption …

an5.75:15.9.verse: second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.

an5.75:16.1.verse: When his mind has become immersed in samādhi like this—purified, bright, flawless, rid of corruptions, pliable, workable, steady, and imperturbable—he extends it toward knowledge of the ending of defilements.

an5.75:16.2.verse: He truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

an5.75:16.3.verse: He truly understands: ‘These are defilements’ … ‘This is the origin of defilements’ … ‘This is the cessation of defilements’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of defilements’.

an5.75:16.4.verse: Knowing and seeing like this, his mind is freed from the defilements of sensuality, desire to be reborn, and ignorance.

an5.75:16.5.verse: When he’s freed, he knows he’s freed.

an5.75:16.6.verse: He understands: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

an5.75:17.1.verse: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil and being struck. He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.

an5.75:17.4.verse: This is the fifth individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.75:17.5.verse: These five individuals similar to warriors are found among the monks.”

an5.76:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five warriors are found in the world.

an5.76:1.3.verse: Firstly, one warrior dons his sword and shield, fastens his bow and arrows, and plunges into the thick of battle.

an5.76:1.4.verse: He strives and struggles in the battle,

an5.76:1.5.verse: but his foes kill him and finish him off.

an5.76:1.7.verse: This is the first warrior found in the world.

an5.76:2.1.verse: Furthermore, one warrior dons his sword and shield, fastens his bow and arrows, and plunges into the thick of battle.

an5.76:2.2.verse: He strives and struggles in the battle,

an5.76:2.4.verse: He’s carried off and taken to his relatives,

an5.76:2.5.verse: but he dies on the road before he reaches them.

an5.76:2.7.verse: This is the second warrior found in the world.

an5.76:3.1.verse: Furthermore, one warrior dons his sword and shield, fastens his bow and arrows, and plunges into the thick of battle.

an5.76:3.2.verse: He strives and struggles in the battle,

an5.76:3.4.verse: He’s carried off and taken to his relatives,

an5.76:3.5.verse: who nurse him and care for him.

an5.76:3.6.verse: But he dies of his injuries while in their care.

an5.76:3.8.verse: This is the third warrior found in the world.

an5.76:4.1.verse: Furthermore, one warrior dons his sword and shield, fastens his bow and arrows, and plunges into the thick of battle.

an5.76:4.2.verse: He strives and struggles in the battle,

an5.76:4.4.verse: He’s carried off and taken to his relatives,

an5.76:4.5.verse: who nurse him and care for him.

an5.76:4.6.verse: And while in their care, he recovers from his injuries.

an5.76:4.8.verse: This is the fourth warrior found in the world.

an5.76:5.1.verse: Furthermore, one warrior dons his sword and shield, fastens his bow and arrows, and plunges into the thick of battle.

an5.76:5.2.verse: He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.

an5.76:5.4.verse: This is the fifth warrior found in the world.

an5.76:5.5.verse: These are the five warriors found in the world.

an5.76:6.1.verse: In the same way, these five individuals similar to warriors are found among the monks.

an5.76:6.3.verse: Firstly, a mendicant lives supported by a town or village.

an5.76:6.4.verse: He robes up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, enters a village or town for alms without guarding body, speech, and mind, without establishing mindfulness, and without restraining the sense faculties.

an5.76:6.5.verse: There he sees a lady scantily clad, with revealing clothes.

an5.76:6.7.verse: and, without resigning the training and declaring his inability to continue, he indulges in sex.

an5.76:7.1.verse: I say that this individual is like the warrior who is killed and finished off by his foes. Some individuals are like that.

an5.76:7.2.verse: This is the first individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.76:8.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant lives supported by a town or village.

an5.76:8.2.verse: He robes up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, enters a village or town for alms without guarding body, speech, and mind, without establishing mindfulness, and without restraining the sense faculties.

an5.76:8.3.verse: There he sees a lady scantily clad, with revealing clothes.

an5.76:8.5.verse: and his body and mind burn with it.

an5.76:8.7.verse: ‘Why don’t I visit the monastery and tell the monks:

an5.76:8.8.verse: “Reverends, I am overcome with lust, mired in lust. I am unable to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.76:8.9.verse: I declare my inability to continue training. I resign it and will return to a lesser life.”’

an5.76:8.10.verse: But while traveling on the road, before he reaches the monastery he declares his inability to continue training. He resigns and returns to a lesser life.

an5.76:9.1.verse: I say that they are like the warrior who is taken to his relatives for care, but he dies on the road before he reaches them. Some individuals are like that.

an5.76:9.2.verse: This is the second individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.76:10.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant lives supported by a town or village.

an5.76:10.2.verse: He robes up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, enters a village or town for alms without guarding body, speech, and mind, without establishing mindfulness, and without restraining the sense faculties.

an5.76:10.3.verse: There he sees a lady scantily clad, with revealing clothes.

an5.76:10.5.verse: and his body and mind burn with it.

an5.76:10.7.verse: ‘Why don’t I visit the monastery and tell the monks:

an5.76:10.8.verse: “Reverends, I am overcome with lust, mired in lust. I am unable to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.76:10.9.verse: I declare my inability to continue training. I resign and will return to a lesser life.”’

an5.76:10.10.verse: He goes to the monastery and tells the monks:

an5.76:10.11.verse: ‘Reverends, I am overcome with lust, mired in lust. I am unable to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.76:10.12.verse: I declare my inability to continue training. I disavow it and will return to a lesser life.’

an5.76:11.1.verse: His spiritual companions advise and instruct him:

an5.76:11.2.verse: ‘Reverend, the Buddha says that sensual pleasures give little gratification and much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks.

an5.76:11.3.verse: With the similes of a skeleton …

an5.76:11.10.verse: a butcher’s knife and chopping board …

an5.76:11.12.verse: a cobra’s head, the Buddha says that sensual pleasures give little gratification and much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks.

an5.76:11.13.verse: Be happy with the spiritual life.

an5.76:11.14.verse: Venerable, please don’t declare your inability to continue training, resign it and return to a lesser life.’

an5.76:12.1.verse: When thus advised and instructed by his spiritual companions, he says:

an5.76:12.2.verse: ‘Reverends, even though the Buddha says that sensual pleasures give little gratification and much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks,

an5.76:12.3.verse: I am unable to keep up the spiritual life. I declare my inability to continue training. I resign it and will return to a lesser life.’

an5.76:12.4.verse: Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.

an5.76:13.1.verse: I say that they are like the warrior who dies of his injuries while in the care of his relatives. Some individuals are like that.

an5.76:13.2.verse: This is the third individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.76:14.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant lives supported by a town or village.

an5.76:14.2.verse: He robes up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, enters a village or town for alms without guarding body, speech, and mind, without establishing mindfulness, and without restraining the sense faculties.

an5.76:14.3.verse: There he sees a lady scantily clad, with revealing clothes.

an5.76:14.5.verse: and his body and mind burn with it.

an5.76:14.7.verse: ‘Why don’t I visit the monastery and tell the monks:

an5.76:14.8.verse: “Reverends, I am overcome with lust, mired in lust. I am unable to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.76:14.9.verse: I declare my inability to continue training. I resign it and will return to a lesser life.”’

an5.76:14.10.verse: He goes to the monastery and tells the monks:

an5.76:14.11.verse: ‘Reverends, I am overcome with lust, mired in lust. I am unable to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.76:14.12.verse: I declare my inability to continue training. I resign it and will return to a lesser life.’

an5.76:15.1.verse: His spiritual companions advise and instruct him:

an5.76:15.2.verse: ‘Reverend, the Buddha says that sensual pleasures give little gratification and much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks.

an5.76:15.3.verse: With the simile of a skeleton …

an5.76:15.4.verse: a scrap of meat … a grass torch … a pit of glowing coals … a dream … borrowed goods … fruit on a tree … a butcher’s knife and chopping board … swords and spears … a cobra’s head, the Buddha says that sensual pleasures give little gratification and much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks.

an5.76:15.5.verse: Be happy with the spiritual life.

an5.76:15.6.verse: Venerable, please don’t declare your inability to continue training, resign it and return to a lesser life.’

an5.76:16.1.verse: When thus advised and instructed by his spiritual companions, he says:

an5.76:16.2.verse: ‘I’ll make an attempt, reverends, I’ll struggle, I’ll be happy.

an5.76:16.3.verse: I won’t now declare my inability to continue training, resign it and return to a lesser life.’

an5.76:17.1.verse: I say that this individual is like the warrior who recovers from his injuries while in the care of his relatives.

an5.76:17.3.verse: This is the fourth individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.76:18.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant lives supported by a town or village.

an5.76:18.2.verse: He robes up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, enters a village or town, guarding body, speech, and mind, establishing mindfulness, and restraining the sense faculties.

an5.76:18.3.verse: Seeing a sight with his eyes, he doesn’t get caught up in the features and details.

an5.76:18.4.verse: If the faculty of sight were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, he practices restraint, protecting the faculty of sight, and achieving its restraint.

an5.76:18.5.verse: Hearing a sound with his ears …

an5.76:18.6.verse: Smelling an odor with his nose …

an5.76:18.7.verse: Tasting a flavor with his tongue …

an5.76:18.8.verse: Encountering a touch with his body …

an5.76:18.9.verse: Knowing an idea with his mind, he doesn’t get caught up in the features and details.

an5.76:18.10.verse: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, he practices restraint, protecting the faculty of mind, and achieving its restraint.

an5.76:18.11.verse: Then after the meal, on his return from almsround,

an5.76:18.12.verse: he frequents a secluded lodging—a wilderness, the root of a tree, a hill, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a forest, the open air, a heap of straw.

an5.76:18.13.verse: Gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, he sits down cross-legged, sets his body straight, and brings mindfulness to the present.

an5.76:18.14.verse: He gives up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.

an5.76:18.15.verse: Then, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, he enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.

an5.76:19.1.verse: When his mind has become immersed in samādhi like this—purified, bright, flawless, rid of corruptions, pliable, workable, steady, and imperturbable—he extends it toward knowledge of the ending of defilements.

an5.76:19.2.verse: He truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’. He truly understands: ‘These are defilements’ … ‘This is the origin of defilements’ … ‘This is the cessation of defilements’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of defilements’. Knowing and seeing like this, his mind is freed from the defilements of sensuality, desire to be reborn, and ignorance. When he’s freed, he knows he’s freed.

an5.76:19.3.verse: He understands: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

an5.76:20.1.verse: I say that this individual is like the warrior who dons his sword and shield, fastens his bow and arrows, and plunges into the thick of battle. He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.

an5.76:20.3.verse: This is the fifth individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.76:20.4.verse: These five individuals similar to warriors are found among the monks.”

an5.77:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, seeing these five future perils is quite enough for a wilderness mendicant to meditate diligently, keenly, and resolutely for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

an5.77:2.3.verse: ‘Currently I’m living alone in a wilderness.

an5.77:2.5.verse: I might get bitten by a snake, a scorpion, or a centipede.

an5.77:2.6.verse: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.

an5.77:2.7.verse: I’d better rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

an5.77:2.8.verse: This is the first future peril …

an5.77:3.2.verse: ‘Currently I’m living alone in a wilderness.

an5.77:3.4.verse: I might stumble off a cliff, or get food poisoning, or suffer a disturbance of bile, phlegm, or piercing winds.

an5.77:3.5.verse: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.

an5.77:3.6.verse: I’d better rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

an5.77:3.7.verse: This is the second future peril …

an5.77:4.2.verse: ‘Currently I’m living alone in a wilderness.

an5.77:4.4.verse: I might encounter wild beasts—a lion, a tiger, a leopard, a bear, or a hyena—which might take my life.

an5.77:4.5.verse: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.

an5.77:4.6.verse: I’d better rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

an5.77:4.7.verse: This is the third future peril …

an5.77:5.2.verse: ‘Currently I’m living alone in a wilderness.

an5.77:5.4.verse: I might encounter youths escaping a crime or on their way to commit one, and they might take my life.

an5.77:5.5.verse: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.

an5.77:5.6.verse: I’d better rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

an5.77:5.7.verse: This is the fourth future peril …

an5.77:6.2.verse: ‘Currently I’m living alone in a wilderness.

an5.77:6.3.verse: But in a wilderness there are savage monsters who might take my life.

an5.77:6.4.verse: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.

an5.77:6.5.verse: I’d better rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

an5.77:6.6.verse: This is the fifth future peril …

an5.77:7.1.verse: These are the five future perils, seeing which is quite enough for a wilderness mendicant to meditate diligently, keenly, and resolutely for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.”

an5.78:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, seeing these five future perils is quite enough for a mendicant to meditate diligently, keenly, and resolutely for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

an5.78:1.4.verse: ‘Currently I’m a youth, young, with pristine black hair, blessed with youth, in the prime of life.

an5.78:1.5.verse: But there will come a time when this body is struck with old age.

an5.78:1.6.verse: When you’re old, overcome by old age, it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas, and it’s not easy to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

an5.78:1.7.verse: Before that unlikable, undesirable, and disagreeable thing happens,

an5.78:1.8.verse: I’d better preempt it by rousing up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized. That way, when it happens, I’ll live comfortably even though I’m old.’

an5.78:1.9.verse: This is the first future peril …

an5.78:2.2.verse: ‘Currently, I’m rarely ill or unwell. My stomach digests well, being neither too hot nor too cold, but just right, and fit for meditation.

an5.78:2.3.verse: But there will come a time when this body is struck with sickness.

an5.78:2.4.verse: When you’re sick, overcome by sickness, it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas, and it’s not easy to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

an5.78:2.5.verse: Before that unlikable, undesirable, and disagreeable thing happens,

an5.78:2.6.verse: I’d better preempt it by rousing up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized. That way, when it happens, I’ll live comfortably even though I’m sick.’

an5.78:2.7.verse: This is the second future peril …

an5.78:3.2.verse: ‘Currently, there’s plenty of food, a good harvest, so it’s easy to get almsfood, and easy to keep going by collecting alms.

an5.78:3.3.verse: But there will come a time of famine, a bad harvest, when it’s hard to get almsfood, and not easy to keep going by collecting alms.

an5.78:3.4.verse: In a time of famine, people move to where there’s plenty of food,

an5.78:3.5.verse: where they live crowded and cramped together.

an5.78:3.6.verse: When you live crowded and cramped together, it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas, and it’s not easy to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

an5.78:3.7.verse: Before that unlikable, undesirable, and disagreeable thing happens,

an5.78:3.8.verse: I’d better preempt it by rousing up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized. That way, when it happens, I’ll live comfortably even though there’s a famine.’

an5.78:3.9.verse: This is the third future peril …

an5.78:4.2.verse: ‘Currently, people live in harmony, appreciating each other, without dispute, blending like milk and water, and regarding each other with kindly eyes.

an5.78:4.3.verse: But there will come a time of peril due to turmoil in the wilds, so the countryfolk mount their vehicles and flee everywhere.

an5.78:4.4.verse: In a time of peril, people move to where there’s sanctuary,

an5.78:4.5.verse: where they live crowded and cramped together.

an5.78:4.6.verse: When you live crowded and cramped together, it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas, and it’s not easy to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

an5.78:4.7.verse: Before that unlikable, undesirable, and disagreeable thing happens,

an5.78:4.8.verse: I’d better preempt it by rousing up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized. That way, when it happens, I’ll live comfortably even in a time of peril.’

an5.78:4.9.verse: This is the fourth future peril …

an5.78:5.2.verse: ‘Currently, the Saṅgha lives comfortably, in harmony, appreciating each other, without dispute, with one recitation.

an5.78:5.3.verse: But there will come a time of schism in the Saṅgha.

an5.78:5.4.verse: When there is schism in the Saṅgha, it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas, and it’s not easy to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

an5.78:5.5.verse: Before that unlikable, undesirable, and disagreeable thing happens,

an5.78:5.6.verse: I’d better preempt it by rousing up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized. That way, when it happens, I’ll live comfortably even though there’s schism in the Saṅgha.’

an5.78:5.7.verse: This is the fifth future peril …

an5.78:6.1.verse: These are the five future perils, seeing which is quite enough for a mendicant to meditate diligently, keenly, and resolutely for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.”

an5.79:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five future perils have not currently arisen, but they will arise in the future.

an5.79:1.2.verse: You should look out for them

an5.79:1.3.verse: and try to give them up.

an5.79:2.2.verse: In a future time there will be mendicants who have not developed their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

an5.79:2.4.verse: but be unable to guide them in the higher ethics, mind, and wisdom.

an5.79:2.5.verse: They too will not develop their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

an5.79:2.7.verse: but be unable to guide them in the higher ethics, mind, and wisdom.

an5.79:2.8.verse: They too will not develop their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

an5.79:2.9.verse: And that is how corrupt training comes from corrupt teachings,

an5.79:2.10.verse: and corrupt teachings come from corrupt training.

an5.79:2.11.verse: This is the first future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

an5.79:3.1.verse: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who have not developed their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

an5.79:3.2.verse: They will give dependence to others,

an5.79:3.3.verse: but be unable to guide them in the higher ethics, mind, and wisdom.

an5.79:3.4.verse: They too will not develop their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

an5.79:3.5.verse: They too will give dependence to others,

an5.79:3.6.verse: but be unable to guide them in the higher ethics, mind, and wisdom.

an5.79:3.7.verse: They too will not develop their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

an5.79:3.8.verse: And that is how corrupt training comes from corrupt teachings,

an5.79:3.9.verse: and corrupt teachings come from corrupt training.

an5.79:3.10.verse: This is the second future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

an5.79:4.1.verse: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who have not developed their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

an5.79:4.2.verse: In discussion about the teachings and elaborations they’ll fall into dark ideas without realizing it.

an5.79:4.3.verse: And that is how corrupt training comes from corrupt teachings,

an5.79:4.4.verse: and corrupt teachings come from corrupt training.

an5.79:4.5.verse: This is the third future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

an5.79:5.1.verse: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who have not developed their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

an5.79:5.2.verse: When discourses spoken by the Realized One—deep, profound, transcendent, dealing with emptiness—are being recited they won’t want to listen. They won’t actively listen or try to understand, nor will they think those teachings are worth learning and memorizing.

an5.79:5.3.verse: But when discourses composed by poets—poetry, with fancy words and phrases, composed by outsiders or spoken by disciples—are being recited they will want to listen. They’ll actively listen and try to understand, and they’ll think those teachings are worth learning and memorizing.

an5.79:5.4.verse: And that is how corrupt training comes from corrupt teachings,

an5.79:5.5.verse: and corrupt teachings come from corrupt training.

an5.79:5.6.verse: This is the fourth future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

an5.79:6.1.verse: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who have not developed their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

an5.79:6.2.verse: The senior mendicants will be indulgent and slack, leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion, not rousing energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

an5.79:6.3.verse: Those who come after them will follow their example.

an5.79:6.4.verse: They too will become indulgent and slack, leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion, not rousing energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

an5.79:6.5.verse: And that is how corrupt training comes from corrupt teachings,

an5.79:6.6.verse: and corrupt teachings come from corrupt training.

an5.79:6.7.verse: This is the fifth future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

an5.79:7.1.verse: These are the five future perils that have not currently arisen, but will arise in the future.

an5.79:7.2.verse: You should look out for them,

an5.79:7.3.verse: and try to give them up.”

an5.80:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five future perils have not currently arisen, but they will arise in the future.

an5.80:1.2.verse: You should look out for them

an5.80:1.3.verse: and try to give them up.

an5.80:2.2.verse: In a future time there will be mendicants who like nice robes.

an5.80:2.3.verse: They will neglect the practice of wearing rag robes and the practice of frequenting remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

an5.80:2.4.verse: They will come down to the villages, towns, and capital cities and make their homes there. And they will employ many kinds of improper solicitation for the sake of a robe.

an5.80:2.5.verse: This is the first future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

an5.80:3.1.verse: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who like nice almsfood.

an5.80:3.2.verse: They will neglect the practice of walking for almsfood and the practice of frequenting remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

an5.80:3.3.verse: They will come down to the villages, towns, and capital cities and make their home there. And they will employ many kinds of improper solicitation for the sake of almsfood.

an5.80:3.4.verse: This is the second future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

an5.80:4.1.verse: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who like nice lodgings.

an5.80:4.2.verse: They will neglect the practice of staying at the root of a tree and the practice of frequenting remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

an5.80:4.3.verse: They will come down to the villages, towns, and capital cities and make their home there. And they will employ many kinds of improper solicitation for the sake of lodgings.

an5.80:4.4.verse: This is the third future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

an5.80:5.1.verse: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who mix closely with nuns, trainee nuns, and novice nuns.

an5.80:5.2.verse: In such conditions, it can be expected that

an5.80:5.3.verse: they will lead the spiritual life dissatisfied, or commit one of the corrupt offenses, or resign the training and return to a lesser life.

an5.80:5.4.verse: This is the fourth future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

an5.80:6.1.verse: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who mix closely with monastery attendants and novices.

an5.80:6.2.verse: In such conditions it can be expected that

an5.80:6.3.verse: they will engage in storing up goods for their own use, and making obvious hints about digging the earth and cutting plants.

an5.80:6.4.verse: This is the fifth future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

an5.80:7.1.verse: These are the five future perils that have not currently arisen, but will arise in the future.

an5.80:7.2.verse: You should look out for them

an5.80:7.3.verse: and try to give them up.”

an5.81:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a senior mendicant with five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

an5.81:1.3.verse: They desire the desirable, they hate the hateful, they’re deluded by the delusory, they’re annoyed by the annoying, and they’re intoxicated by the intoxicating.

an5.81:1.4.verse: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is disliked and disagreeable by their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

an5.81:2.1.verse: A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.

an5.81:2.3.verse: They don’t desire the desirable, they don’t hate the hateful, they’re not deluded by the delusory, they’re not annoyed by the annoying, and they’re not intoxicated by the intoxicating.

an5.81:2.4.verse: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”

an5.82:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a senior mendicant with five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

an5.82:1.3.verse: They’re not free of greed, hate, and delusion; they are offensive and contemptuous.

an5.82:1.4.verse: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

an5.82:2.1.verse: A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.

an5.82:2.3.verse: They’re free of greed, hate, and delusion; they’re not offensive and contemptuous.

an5.82:2.4.verse: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”

an5.83:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a senior mendicant with five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

an5.83:1.3.verse: They use deceit, flattery, hinting, and belittling, and they use material things to chase after other material things.

an5.83:1.4.verse: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

an5.83:2.1.verse: A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.

an5.83:2.3.verse: They don’t use deceit, flattery, hinting, or belittling, and they don’t use material things to chase after other material things.

an5.83:2.4.verse: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”

an5.84:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a senior mendicant with five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

an5.84:1.3.verse: They’re faithless, shameless, imprudent, lazy, and witless.

an5.84:1.4.verse: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

an5.84:2.1.verse: A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.

an5.84:2.3.verse: They’re faithful, conscientious, prudent, energetic, and wise.

an5.84:2.4.verse: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”

an5.85:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a senior mendicant with five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

an5.85:1.3.verse: They can’t endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

an5.85:1.4.verse: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

an5.85:2.1.verse: A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.

an5.85:2.3.verse: They can endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

an5.85:2.4.verse: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”

an5.86:0.3.verse: Attaining the Methods of Textual Analysis

an5.86:1.1.verse: “A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.

an5.86:1.3.verse: They have attained the textual analysis of meaning, text, definition, and eloquence.

an5.86:1.4.verse: And they are deft and tireless in a diverse spectrum of duties for their spiritual companions, understanding how to go about things in order to complete and organize the work.

an5.86:1.5.verse: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”

an5.87:1.1.verse: “A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.

an5.87:1.3.verse: They’re ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

an5.87:1.4.verse: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

an5.87:1.5.verse: They’re a good speaker who enunciates well, with a polished, clear, and articulate voice that expresses the meaning.

an5.87:1.6.verse: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

an5.87:1.7.verse: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an5.87:1.8.verse: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”

an5.88:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a senior mendicant who has five qualities is acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of of gods and humans.

an5.88:2.2.verse: They are long standing and have long gone forth.

an5.88:2.3.verse: They’re well-known, famous, with a large following that includes both laypeople and renunciates.

an5.88:2.4.verse: They receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

an5.88:2.5.verse: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

an5.88:2.6.verse: But they have wrong view and distorted perspective. They draw many people away from the true teaching and establish them in false teachings.

an5.88:2.7.verse: People follow their example, thinking that the senior mendicant is long standing and has long gone forth. Or that they’re well-known, famous, with a large following that includes both laypeople and renunciates. Or that they receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick. Or that they’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned.

an5.88:2.8.verse: A senior mendicant who possesses these five qualities is acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

an5.88:3.1.verse: A senior mendicant who has five qualities is acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

an5.88:4.2.verse: They are long standing and have long gone forth.

an5.88:4.3.verse: They’re well-known, famous, with a large following, including both laypeople and renunciates.

an5.88:4.4.verse: They receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

an5.88:4.5.verse: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

an5.88:4.6.verse: And they have right view and an undistorted perspective. They draw many people away from false teachings and establish them in the true teaching.

an5.88:4.7.verse: People follow their example, thinking that the senior mendicant is long standing and has long gone forth. Or that they’re well-known, famous, with a large following that includes both laypeople and renunciates. Or that they receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick. Or that they’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned.

an5.88:4.8.verse: A senior mendicant who possesses these five qualities is acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”

an5.89:1.1.verse: “These five things lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.89:1.3.verse: They relish work, talk, sleep, and company. And they don’t review the extent of their mind’s freedom.

an5.89:1.4.verse: These five things lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.89:2.1.verse: These five things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.89:2.3.verse: They don’t relish work, talk, sleep, and company. And they review the extent of their mind’s freedom.

an5.89:2.4.verse: These five things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.”

an5.90:1.1.verse: “These five things lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.90:1.3.verse: Firstly, a mendicant trainee has many duties and responsibilities, and is competent in many tasks.

an5.90:1.4.verse: They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.90:1.5.verse: This is the first thing that leads to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.90:2.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee spends too much time doing trivial work.

an5.90:2.2.verse: They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.90:2.3.verse: This is the second thing that leads to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.90:3.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee mixes closely with laypeople and renunciates, socializing inappropriately like a layperson.

an5.90:3.2.verse: They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.90:3.3.verse: This is the third thing that leads to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.90:4.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee enters the town at the wrong time, and returns too late in the day.

an5.90:4.2.verse: They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.90:4.3.verse: This is the fourth thing that leads to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.90:5.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee doesn’t get to take part in talk about self-effacement that helps open the heart, when they want, without trouble or difficulty. That is,

an5.90:5.2.verse: talk about fewness of wishes, contentment, seclusion, aloofness, arousing energy, ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.

an5.90:5.3.verse: They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.90:5.4.verse: This is the fifth thing that leads to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.90:5.5.verse: These five things lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.90:6.1.verse: These five things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.90:6.3.verse: Firstly, a mendicant trainee doesn’t have many duties and responsibilities, even though they are competent in many tasks.

an5.90:6.4.verse: They don’t neglect retreat, and are committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.90:6.5.verse: This is the first thing that doesn’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.90:7.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee doesn’t waste their day doing trivial work.

an5.90:7.2.verse: They don’t neglect retreat, and are committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.90:7.3.verse: This is the second thing that doesn’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.90:8.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee doesn’t mix closely with laypeople and renunciates, socializing inappropriately like a layperson.

an5.90:8.2.verse: They don’t neglect retreat, and are committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.90:8.3.verse: This is the third thing that doesn’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.90:9.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee doesn’t enter the village too early or return too late in the day.

an5.90:9.2.verse: They don’t neglect retreat, and are committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.90:9.3.verse: This is the fourth thing that doesn’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.90:10.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee gets to take part in talk about self-effacement that helps open the heart, when they want, without trouble or difficulty. That is,

an5.90:10.2.verse: talk about fewness of wishes, contentment, seclusion, aloofness, arousing energy, ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.

an5.90:10.3.verse: They don’t neglect retreat, and are committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.90:10.4.verse: This is the fifth thing that doesn’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

an5.90:10.5.verse: These five things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.”

an5.91:1.3.verse: Accomplishment in faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

an5.92:1.3.verse: Accomplishment in ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.

an5.93:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are five ways of declaring enlightenment.

an5.93:1.3.verse: One declares enlightenment out of stupidity and folly.

an5.93:1.4.verse: Or because of corrupt wishes, being of wishful temperament.

an5.93:1.5.verse: Or because of madness and mental disorder.

an5.93:1.8.verse: These are the five ways of declaring enlightenment.”

an5.94:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five ways of living comfortably.

an5.94:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

an5.94:1.4.verse: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption …

an5.94:1.5.verse: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an5.94:1.6.verse: These are the five ways of living comfortably.”
