an5.95:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant who has five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.

an5.95:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant has attained the textual analysis of meaning, text, definition, and eloquence, and they review the extent of their mind’s freedom.

an5.95:1.4.verse: A mendicant who has these five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.”

an5.96:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant cultivating mindfulness of breathing who has five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.

an5.96:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant has few obligations and duties, and is unburdensome and contented with life’s necessities.

an5.96:1.4.verse: They eat little, not devoted to filling their stomach.

an5.96:1.5.verse: They are rarely drowsy, and are dedicated to wakefulness.

an5.96:1.6.verse: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

an5.96:1.7.verse: They review the extent of their mind’s freedom.

an5.96:1.8.verse: A mendicant cultivating mindfulness of breathing who has these five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.”

an5.97:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant developing mindfulness of breathing who has five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.

an5.97:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant has few concerns and duties, and is unburdensome and contented with life’s necessities.

an5.97:1.4.verse: They eat little, not devoted to filling their stomach.

an5.97:1.5.verse: They are rarely drowsy, and are dedicated to wakefulness.

an5.97:1.6.verse: They get to take part in talk about self-effacement that helps open the heart, when they want, without trouble or difficulty. That is,

an5.97:1.7.verse: talk about fewness of wishes, contentment, seclusion, keeping your distance, arousing energy, ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.

an5.97:1.8.verse: They review the extent of their mind’s freedom.

an5.97:1.9.verse: A mendicant developing mindfulness of breathing who has these five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.”

an5.98:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant practicing mindfulness of breathing who has five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.

an5.98:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant has few obligations and duties, and is unburdensome and contented with life’s necessities.

an5.98:1.4.verse: They eat little, not devoted to filling their stomach.

an5.98:1.5.verse: They are rarely drowsy, and are dedicated to wakefulness.

an5.98:1.6.verse: They live in the wilderness, in remote lodgings.

an5.98:1.7.verse: They review the extent of their mind’s freedom.

an5.98:1.8.verse: A mendicant practicing mindfulness of breathing who has these five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.”

an5.99:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, toward evening the lion, king of beasts, emerges from his den,

an5.99:1.4.verse: and roars his lion’s roar three times.

an5.99:1.5.verse: Then he sets out on the hunt.

an5.99:1.6.verse: If he strikes an elephant, he does it carefully, not carelessly.

an5.99:1.10.verse: or any smaller creatures—even a hare or a cat—he does it carefully, not carelessly.

an5.99:1.12.verse: Thinking: ‘May I not lose my way.’

an5.99:2.1.verse: ‘Lion’ is a term for the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

an5.99:2.2.verse: When the Realized One teaches Dhamma to an assembly, this is his lion’s roar.

an5.99:2.3.verse: When the Realized One teaches the monks …

an5.99:2.7.verse: or ordinary people—even food-carriers and hunters—he teaches them carefully, not carelessly.

an5.99:2.9.verse: Because the Realized One has respect and reverence for the teaching.”

an5.100:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

an5.100:1.3.verse: At that time the Koliyan named Kakudha—Venerable Mahāmoggallāna’s supporter—had recently passed away and been reborn in a certain host of mind-made gods.

an5.100:1.4.verse: His incarnation was two or three times the size of a Magadhan village with its fields.

an5.100:1.5.verse: But with that incarnation he didn’t obstruct himself or others.

an5.100:2.1.verse: Then the godling Kakudha went up to Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,

an5.100:2.2.verse: “Sir, this fixed desire arose in Devadatta:

an5.100:2.4.verse: And as that thought arose, Devadatta lost that psychic power.”

an5.100:2.5.verse: That is what the godling Kakudha said.

an5.100:2.6.verse: Then he bowed and respectfully circled Mahāmoggallāna, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

an5.100:3.1.verse: Then Mahāmoggallāna went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

an5.100:5.1.verse: “But Moggallāna, did you encompass the godling Kakudha’s mind, and know that

an5.100:5.2.verse: everything he says is correct and not otherwise?”

an5.100:5.7.verse: Now that futile man Devadatta will expose himself by his own deeds.

an5.100:6.1.verse: Moggallāna, there are these five teachers found in the world.

an5.100:6.3.verse: Firstly, some teacher with impure conduct claims: ‘I am pure in ethics. My ethical conduct is pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

an5.100:6.5.verse: ‘This teacher has impure ethical conduct, but claims to be ethically pure.

an5.100:6.6.verse: They wouldn’t like it if we were to tell the laypeople.

an5.100:6.7.verse: And how could we treat them in a way that they don’t like?

an5.100:6.8.verse: But they consent to robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

an5.100:6.9.verse: They themselves will be recognized by their own deeds.’

an5.100:6.10.verse: The disciples of such a teacher cover up their teacher’s conduct,

an5.100:6.11.verse: and the teacher expects them to do so.

an5.100:7.1.verse: Furthermore, some teacher with impure livelihood claims: ‘I am pure in livelihood. My livelihood is pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

an5.100:7.3.verse: ‘This teacher has impure livelihood, but claims to have pure livelihood.

an5.100:7.4.verse: They wouldn’t like it if we were to tell the laypeople.

an5.100:7.5.verse: And how could we treat them in a way that they don’t like?

an5.100:7.6.verse: But they consent to robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

an5.100:7.7.verse: They themselves will be recognized by their own deeds.’

an5.100:7.8.verse: The disciples of such a teacher cover up their teacher’s livelihood,

an5.100:7.9.verse: and the teacher expects them to do so.

an5.100:8.1.verse: Furthermore, some teacher with impure teaching claims: ‘I am pure in teaching. My teaching is pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

an5.100:8.3.verse: ‘This teacher has impure teaching, but claims to have pure teaching.

an5.100:8.4.verse: They wouldn’t like it if we were to tell the laypeople.

an5.100:8.5.verse: And how could we treat them in a way that they don’t like?

an5.100:8.6.verse: But they consent to robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

an5.100:8.7.verse: They themselves will be recognized by their own deeds.’

an5.100:8.8.verse: The disciples of such a teacher cover up their teacher’s teaching,

an5.100:8.9.verse: and the teacher expects them to do so.

an5.100:9.1.verse: Furthermore, some teacher with impure answers claims: ‘I am pure in how I answer. My answers are pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

an5.100:9.3.verse: ‘This teacher has impure answers, but claims to have pure answers.

an5.100:9.4.verse: They wouldn’t like it if we were to tell the laypeople.

an5.100:9.5.verse: And how could we treat them in a way that they don’t like?

an5.100:9.6.verse: But they consent to robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

an5.100:9.7.verse: They themselves will be recognized by their own deeds.’

an5.100:9.8.verse: The disciples of such a teacher cover up their teacher’s answers,

an5.100:9.9.verse: and the teacher expects them to do so.

an5.100:10.1.verse: Furthermore, some teacher with impure knowledge and vision claims: ‘I am pure in knowledge and vision. My knowledge and vision are pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

an5.100:10.3.verse: ‘This teacher has impure knowledge and vision, but claims to have pure knowledge and vision.

an5.100:10.4.verse: They wouldn’t like it if we were to tell the laypeople.

an5.100:10.5.verse: And how could we treat them in a way that they don’t like?

an5.100:10.6.verse: But they consent to robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

an5.100:10.7.verse: They themselves will be recognized by their own deeds.’

an5.100:10.8.verse: The disciples of such a teacher cover up their teacher’s knowledge and vision,

an5.100:10.9.verse: and the teacher expects them to do so.

an5.100:10.10.verse: These are the five teachers found in the world.

an5.100:11.1.verse: But Moggallāna, I have pure ethical conduct, and I claim: ‘I am pure in ethical conduct. My ethical conduct is pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

an5.100:11.2.verse: My disciples don’t cover up my conduct, and I don’t expect them to.

an5.100:11.3.verse: I have pure livelihood, and I claim: ‘I am pure in livelihood. My livelihood is pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

an5.100:11.4.verse: My disciples don’t cover up my livelihood, and I don’t expect them to.

an5.100:11.5.verse: I have pure teaching, and I claim: ‘I am pure in teaching. My teaching is pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

an5.100:11.6.verse: My disciples don’t cover up my teaching, and I don’t expect them to.

an5.100:11.7.verse: I have pure answers, and I claim: ‘I am pure in how I answer. My answers are pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

an5.100:11.8.verse: My disciples don’t cover up my answers, and I don’t expect them to.

an5.100:11.9.verse: I have pure knowledge and vision, and I claim: ‘I am pure in knowledge and vision. My knowledge and vision are pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

an5.100:11.10.verse: My disciples don’t cover up my knowledge and vision, and I don’t expect them to.”

an5.101:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five qualities make a trainee self-assured.

an5.101:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is faithful, ethical, learned, energetic, and wise.

an5.101:2.1.verse: A person of faith doesn’t have the insecurities of someone who lacks faith.

an5.101:2.2.verse: So this quality makes a trainee self-assured.

an5.101:3.1.verse: An ethical person doesn’t have the insecurities of someone who is unethical.

an5.101:3.2.verse: So this quality makes a trainee self-assured.

an5.101:4.1.verse: A learned person doesn’t have the insecurities of a person of little learning.

an5.101:4.2.verse: So this quality makes a trainee self-assured.

an5.101:5.1.verse: An energetic person doesn’t have the insecurities of a lazy person.

an5.101:5.2.verse: So this quality makes a trainee self-assured.

an5.101:6.1.verse: A wise person doesn’t have the insecurities of someone who is witless.

an5.101:6.2.verse: So this quality makes a trainee self-assured.

an5.101:6.3.verse: These are the five qualities that make a trainee self-assured.”

an5.102:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, even if a monk is of impeccable character, he might be suspected and distrusted as a ‘bad monk’ for five reasons.

an5.102:2.2.verse: It’s when a monk resorts to prostitutes, widows, voluptuous girls, eunuchs, or nuns for alms.

an5.102:3.1.verse: Even if a monk is of impeccable character, he might be suspected and distrusted as a ‘bad monk’ for these five reasons.”

an5.103:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a master thief with five factors breaks into houses, plunders wealth, steals from isolated buildings, and commits highway robbery.

an5.103:1.3.verse: A master thief relies on rough ground, on thick cover, and on the powerful; they pay bribes, and they act alone.

an5.103:2.1.verse: And how does a master thief rely on rough ground?

an5.103:2.2.verse: It’s when a master thief relies on inaccessible riverlands or rugged mountains.

an5.103:2.3.verse: That’s how a master thief relies on rough ground.

an5.103:3.1.verse: And how does a master thief rely on thick cover?

an5.103:3.2.verse: It’s when a master thief relies on thick grass, thick trees, a blind spot, or a large forest grove.

an5.103:3.3.verse: That’s how a master thief relies on thick cover.

an5.103:4.1.verse: And how does a master thief rely on the powerful?

an5.103:4.2.verse: It’s when a master thief relies on rulers or their chief ministers.

an5.103:4.4.verse: ‘If anyone accuses me of anything, these rulers or their chief ministers will speak in my defense in the case.’

an5.103:4.6.verse: That’s how a master thief relies on the powerful.

an5.103:5.1.verse: And how does a master thief pay bribes?

an5.103:5.2.verse: It’s when a master thief is rich, affluent, and wealthy.

an5.103:5.4.verse: ‘If anyone accuses me of anything, I’ll settle it with a bribe.’

an5.103:5.6.verse: That’s how a master thief pays bribes.

an5.103:6.1.verse: And how does a master thief act alone?

an5.103:6.2.verse: It’s when a master thief carries out robbery all alone.

an5.103:6.4.verse: So that their secret plans are not leaked to others.

an5.103:6.5.verse: That’s how a master thief acts alone.

an5.103:7.1.verse: A master thief with these five factors breaks into houses, plunders wealth, steals from isolated buildings, and commits highway robbery.

an5.103:8.1.verse: In the same way, when a bad mendicant has five qualities, they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

an5.103:8.3.verse: A bad mendicant relies on rough ground, on thick cover, and on the powerful; they pay bribes, and they act alone.

an5.103:9.1.verse: And how does a bad mendicant rely on rough ground?

an5.103:9.2.verse: It’s when a bad mendicant has unethical conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

an5.103:9.3.verse: That’s how a bad mendicant relies on rough ground.

an5.103:10.1.verse: And how does a bad mendicant rely on thick cover?

an5.103:10.2.verse: It’s when a bad mendicant has wrong view, he’s attached to an extremist view.

an5.103:10.3.verse: That’s how a bad mendicant relies on thick cover.

an5.103:11.1.verse: And how does a bad mendicant rely on the powerful?

an5.103:11.2.verse: It’s when a bad mendicant relies on rulers or their chief ministers.

an5.103:11.4.verse: ‘If anyone accuses me of anything, these rulers or their chief ministers will speak in my defense in the case.’

an5.103:11.6.verse: That’s how a bad mendicant relies on the powerful.

an5.103:12.1.verse: And how does a bad mendicant pay bribes?

an5.103:12.2.verse: It’s when a bad mendicant receives robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

an5.103:12.4.verse: ‘If anyone accuses me of anything, I’ll settle it with a bribe.’

an5.103:12.6.verse: That’s how a bad mendicant pays bribes.

an5.103:13.1.verse: And how does a bad mendicant act alone?

an5.103:13.2.verse: It’s when a bad mendicant dwells alone in the borderlands.

an5.103:13.3.verse: They visit families there to acquire material things.

an5.103:13.4.verse: That’s how a bad mendicant acts alone.

an5.103:14.1.verse: When a bad mendicant possesses these five qualities, they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.”

an5.104:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is a delicate ascetic of ascetics.

an5.104:2.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant usually uses only what they’ve been invited to accept—robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick—rarely using them without invitation.

an5.104:2.3.verse: When living with other spiritual practitioners, they usually find themselves treated agreeably by them by way of body, speech, and mind, and rarely disagreeably.

an5.104:2.4.verse: And they are usually presented with agreeable things by them, rarely with disagreeable ones.

an5.104:2.5.verse: They’re healthy, so the various unpleasant feelings—stemming from disorders of bile, phlegm, wind, or their conjunction; or caused by change in weather, by not taking care of themselves, by exertion, or as the result of past deeds—usually don’t come up.

an5.104:2.6.verse: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

an5.104:2.7.verse: And they realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an5.104:2.8.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is a delicate ascetic of ascetics.

an5.104:3.1.verse: And if anyone should be rightly called a delicate ascetic of ascetics, it’s me.

an5.104:3.2.verse: For I usually use only what I’ve been invited to accept.

an5.104:3.3.verse: When living with other mendicants, I am usually treated agreeably by them.

an5.104:3.4.verse: And I usually present them with agreeable things.

an5.104:3.6.verse: I get the four absorptions when I want, without trouble or difficulty.

an5.104:3.7.verse: And I’ve realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom … in this very life …

an5.104:4.1.verse: So if anyone should be rightly called a delicate ascetic of ascetics, it’s me.”

an5.105:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five ways of living comfortably.

an5.105:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with kindness by way of body, speech, and mind, both in public and in private.

an5.105:1.4.verse: They live according to the precepts shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. Those precepts are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

an5.105:1.5.verse: They live according to the view shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. That view is noble and emancipating, and delivers one who applies it to the complete ending of suffering.

an5.105:1.6.verse: These are the five ways of living comfortably.”

an5.106:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

an5.106:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

an5.106:2.1.verse: “Sir, how could a mendicant live comfortably while staying in a monastic community?”

an5.106:2.2.verse: “It’s when a mendicant is accomplished in their own ethical conduct, but they don’t urge others to be ethical.

an5.106:2.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant could live comfortably while staying in a monastic community.”

an5.106:3.1.verse: “But sir, could there be another way for a mendicant to live comfortably while staying in a monastic community?”

an5.106:3.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is accomplished in their own ethical conduct, but they don’t urge others to be ethical.

an5.106:3.4.verse: And they watch themselves, but don’t watch others.

an5.106:3.5.verse: That’s how a mendicant could live comfortably while staying in a monastic community.”

an5.106:4.1.verse: “But sir, could there be another way for a mendicant to live comfortably while staying in a monastic community?”

an5.106:4.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is accomplished in their own ethical conduct, but they don’t urge others to be ethical.

an5.106:4.4.verse: And they watch themselves, but don’t watch others.

an5.106:4.5.verse: And they’re not well-known, but aren’t bothered by that.

an5.106:4.6.verse: That’s how a mendicant could live comfortably while staying in a monastic community.”

an5.106:5.1.verse: “But sir, could there be another way for a mendicant to live comfortably while staying in a monastic community?”

an5.106:5.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is accomplished in their own ethical conduct, but they don’t urge others to be ethical.

an5.106:5.4.verse: And they watch themselves, but don’t watch others.

an5.106:5.5.verse: And they’re not well-known, but aren’t bothered by that.

an5.106:5.6.verse: And they get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

an5.106:5.7.verse: That’s how a mendicant could live comfortably while staying in a monastic community.”

an5.106:6.1.verse: “But sir, might there be another way for a mendicant to live comfortably while staying in a monastic community?”

an5.106:6.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is accomplished in their own ethical conduct, but they don’t urge others to be ethical.

an5.106:6.4.verse: And they watch themselves, but don’t watch others.

an5.106:6.5.verse: And they’re not well-known, but aren’t bothered by that.

an5.106:6.6.verse: And they get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

an5.106:6.7.verse: And they realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an5.106:6.8.verse: That’s how a mendicant could live comfortably while staying in a monastic community.

an5.106:7.1.verse: And I say that there is no better or finer way of living comfortably than this.”

an5.107:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

an5.107:2.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant is accomplished in ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.

an5.107:3.1.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

an5.108:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

an5.108:2.2.verse: It’s when they have the entire spectrum of the adept’s ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and knowledge and vision of freedom.

an5.108:2.3.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities … is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

an5.109:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is at ease in any quarter.

an5.109:1.3.verse: It’s when mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

an5.109:1.4.verse: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

an5.109:1.5.verse: They’re content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

an5.109:1.6.verse: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

an5.109:1.7.verse: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an5.109:1.8.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is at ease in any quarter.”

an5.110:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has five qualities they’re ready to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

an5.110:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

an5.110:1.4.verse: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s totally full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, reciting them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

an5.110:1.5.verse: They live with energy roused up. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

an5.110:1.6.verse: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

an5.110:1.7.verse: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an5.110:1.8.verse: When a mendicant possesses these five qualities they’re ready to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.”

an5.111:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities who visits families is disliked and disagreeable, not respected or admired.

an5.111:1.3.verse: They act as though they’re close to people they hardly know. They give away things they don’t own. They over-associate with close friends. They whisper in the ear. And they ask for too much.

an5.111:1.4.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities who visits families is disliked and disagreeable, not respected or admired.

an5.111:2.1.verse: A mendicant with five qualities who visits families is dear and beloved, respected and admired.

an5.111:2.3.verse: They don’t act as though they’re close to people they hardly know. They don’t give away things they don’t own. They don’t over-associate with close friends. They don’t whisper in the ear. And they don’t ask for too much.

an5.111:2.4.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities who visits families is dear and beloved, respected and admired.”

an5.112:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you shouldn’t take a second monk with five qualities.

an5.112:1.3.verse: They walk too far away or too close behind. They don’t take your bowl when it’s full. They don’t warn you when your speech is bordering on an offense. They keep on interrupting while you’re speaking. And they’re witless, dull, and idiotic.

an5.112:1.4.verse: You shouldn’t take a second monk these five qualities.

an5.112:2.1.verse: You should take a second monk with five qualities.

an5.112:2.3.verse: They don’t walk too far away or too close behind. They take your bowl when it is full. They warn you when your speech is bordering on an offense. They don’t interrupt while you’re speaking. And they’re wise, bright, and clever.

an5.112:2.4.verse: You should take a second monk with these five qualities.”

an5.113:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant who has five qualities can’t enter and remain in right immersion.

an5.113:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant can’t endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

an5.113:1.4.verse: A mendicant who possesses these five qualities can’t enter and remain in right immersion.

an5.113:2.1.verse: A mendicant who has five qualities can enter and remain in right immersion.

an5.113:2.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant can endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

an5.113:2.4.verse: A mendicant who possesses these five qualities can enter and remain in right immersion.”

an5.114:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Magadhans at Andhakavinda.

an5.114:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

an5.114:2.1.verse: “Ānanda, those mendicants who are junior, recently gone forth, newly come to this teaching and training should be encouraged, supported, and established in five things.

an5.114:2.3.verse: They should be encouraged, supported, and established in restraint in the monastic code: ‘Reverends, please be ethical. Live restrained in the monastic code, conducting yourselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, keep the rules you’ve undertaken.’

an5.114:3.1.verse: They should be encouraged, supported, and established in sense restraint: ‘Reverends, please live with sense doors guarded, mindfully alert and on guard, with protected mind, having a heart protected by mindfulness.’

an5.114:4.1.verse: They should be encouraged, supported, and established in limiting their speech: ‘Reverends, please speak little. Put a limit on your speech.’

an5.114:5.1.verse: They should be encouraged, supported, and established in retreat: ‘Reverends, please live in the wilderness. Frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.’

an5.114:6.1.verse: They should be encouraged, supported, and established in right perspective: ‘Reverends, please hold right view and have right perspective.’

an5.114:6.2.verse: Those mendicants who are junior, recently gone forth, newly come to this teaching and training should be encouraged, supported, and established by you in these five things.”

an5.115:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a nun with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an5.115:1.3.verse: She is stingy with dwellings, families, material things, praise, and the teaching.

an5.115:1.4.verse: A nun with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an5.115:2.1.verse: A nun with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an5.115:2.3.verse: She is not stingy with dwellings, families, material things, praise, or the teaching.

an5.115:2.4.verse: A nun with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an5.116:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a nun with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an5.116:1.3.verse: Without examining or scrutinizing, she praises those deserving of criticism,

an5.116:1.4.verse: and criticizes those deserving of praise.

an5.116:1.5.verse: She arouses faith in things that are dubious,

an5.116:1.6.verse: and doesn’t arouse faith in things that are inspiring.

an5.116:1.7.verse: And she wastes gifts given in faith.

an5.116:1.8.verse: A nun with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an5.116:2.1.verse: A nun with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an5.116:2.3.verse: After examining and scrutinizing, she criticizes those deserving of criticism,

an5.116:2.4.verse: and praises those deserving of praise.

an5.116:2.5.verse: She doesn’t arouse faith in things that are dubious,

an5.116:2.6.verse: and does arouse faith in things that are inspiring.

an5.116:2.7.verse: And she doesn’t waste gifts given in faith.

an5.116:2.8.verse: A nun with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an5.121:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

an5.121:1.2.verse: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and went to the infirmary, where

an5.121:1.3.verse: he saw a certain mendicant who was weak and sick.

an5.121:1.4.verse: He sat down on the seat spread out,

an5.121:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, if a weak and sick mendicant does not neglect five things, it can be expected that

an5.121:2.2.verse: they will soon realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an5.121:3.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant meditates observing the ugliness of the body, perceives the repulsiveness of food, perceives dissatisfaction with the whole world, observes the impermanence of all conditions, and has well established the perception of their own death.

an5.121:3.3.verse: If a weak and sick mendicant does not neglect these five things, it can be expected that

an5.121:3.4.verse: they will soon realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”

an5.122:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, any monk or nun who develops and cultivates five qualities can expect one of two results:

an5.122:1.2.verse: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.

an5.122:2.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant has well established mindfulness inside themselves in order to understand the arising and passing away of phenomena, meditates observing the ugliness of the body, perceives the repulsiveness of food, perceives dissatisfaction with the whole world, and observes the impermanence of all conditions.

an5.122:2.3.verse: Any monk or nun who develops and cultivates these five qualities can expect one of two results:

an5.122:2.4.verse: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”

an5.123:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a patient with five qualities is hard to care for.

an5.123:1.3.verse: They do what is unsuitable. They don’t know moderation in what is suitable. They don’t take their medicine. Though their carer wants what’s best for them, they don’t accurately report their symptoms by saying when they’re getting worse, getting better, or staying the same. And they cannot endure physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.

an5.123:1.4.verse: A patient with these five qualities is hard to care for.

an5.123:2.1.verse: A patient with five qualities is easy to care for.

an5.123:2.3.verse: They do what is suitable. They know moderation in what is suitable. They take their medicine. Because their carer wants what’s best for them, they accurately report their symptoms by saying when they’re getting worse, getting better, or staying the same. And they can endure physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.

an5.123:2.4.verse: A patient with these five qualities is easy to care for.”

an5.124:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a carer with five qualities is not competent to care for a patient.

an5.124:1.4.verse: They don’t know what is suitable and unsuitable, so they supply what is unsuitable and remove what is suitable.

an5.124:1.5.verse: They care for the sick for the sake of material benefits, not out of love.

an5.124:1.6.verse: They’re disgusted to remove feces, urine, vomit, or spit.

an5.124:1.7.verse: They’re unable to educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire the patient with a Dhamma talk from time to time.

an5.124:1.8.verse: A carer with these five qualities is not competent to care for a patient.

an5.124:2.1.verse: A carer with five qualities is competent to care for a patient.

an5.124:2.4.verse: They know what is suitable and unsuitable, so they remove what is unsuitable and supply what is suitable.

an5.124:2.5.verse: They care for the sick out of love, not for the sake of material benefits.

an5.124:2.6.verse: They’re not disgusted to remove feces, urine, vomit, or spit.

an5.124:2.7.verse: They’re able to educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire the patient with a Dhamma talk from time to time.

an5.124:2.8.verse: A carer with these five qualities is competent to care for a patient.”

an5.125:1.3.verse: Doing what is unsuitable, not knowing moderation in what is suitable, eating food unfit for consumption, activity at unsuitable times, and unchastity.

an5.125:1.4.verse: These are the five things that impede longevity.

an5.125:2.3.verse: Doing what is suitable, knowing moderation in what is suitable, eating food fit for consumption, activity at suitable times, and chastity.

an5.125:2.4.verse: These are the five things that promote longevity.”

an5.126:1.3.verse: Doing what is unsuitable, not knowing moderation in what is suitable, eating food unfit for consumption, unethical behavior, and bad friends.

an5.126:1.4.verse: These are the five things that impede longevity.

an5.126:2.3.verse: Doing what is suitable, knowing moderation in what is suitable, eating food fit for consumption, ethical conduct, and good friends.

an5.126:2.4.verse: These are the five things that promote longevity.”

an5.127:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is not fit to live apart from a Saṅgha community.

an5.127:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is not content with any kind of robe, almsfood, lodging, and medicines and supplies for the sick. And they have a lot of sensual thoughts.

an5.127:1.4.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is not fit to live apart from a Saṅgha community.

an5.127:2.1.verse: A mendicant with five qualities is fit to live apart from a Saṅgha community.

an5.127:2.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is content with any kind of robe, almsfood, lodging, and medicines and supplies for the sick. And they think a lot about renunciation.

an5.127:2.4.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is fit to live apart from a Saṅgha community.”

an5.128:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five kinds of suffering for an ascetic.

an5.128:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is not content with any kind of robe, almsfood, lodging, and medicines and supplies for the sick. And they lead the spiritual life dissatisfied.

an5.128:1.4.verse: These are five kinds of suffering for an ascetic.

an5.128:2.1.verse: There are these five kinds of happiness for an ascetic.

an5.128:2.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is content with any kind of robe, almsfood, lodging, and medicines and supplies for the sick. And they lead the spiritual life satisfied.

an5.128:2.4.verse: These are five kinds of happiness for an ascetic.”

an5.129:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five fatal wounds lead to a place of loss, to hell.

an5.129:1.3.verse: Murdering your mother or father or a perfected one; maliciously shedding the blood of a Realized One; and causing a schism in the Saṅgha.

an5.129:1.4.verse: These five fatal wounds lead to a place of loss, to hell.”

an5.130:1.3.verse: Loss of relatives, wealth, health, ethics, and view.

an5.130:1.4.verse: It is not because of loss of relatives, wealth, or health that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

an5.130:1.5.verse: It is because of loss of ethics or view that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

an5.130:2.3.verse: Endowment with relatives, wealth, health, ethics, and view.

an5.130:2.4.verse: It is not because of endowment with relatives, wealth, or health that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

an5.130:2.5.verse: It is because of endowment with ethics or view that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

an5.131:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, possessing five factors a wheel-turning monarch wields power only in a principled manner.

an5.131:1.2.verse: And this power cannot be undermined by any human enemy.

an5.131:2.2.verse: A wheel-turning monarch knows what is right, knows principle, knows moderation, knows the right time, and knows the assembly.

an5.131:2.3.verse: A wheel-turning monarch who possesses these five factors wields power only in a principled manner.

an5.131:2.4.verse: And this power cannot be undermined by any human enemy.

an5.131:3.1.verse: In the same way, possessing five qualities a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha rolls forth the supreme Wheel of Dhamma only in a principled manner.

an5.131:3.2.verse: And that wheel cannot be rolled back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.

an5.131:4.2.verse: A Realized One knows what is right, knows principle, knows moderation, knows the right time, and knows the assembly.

an5.131:4.3.verse: Possessing these five qualities a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha rolls forth the supreme Wheel of Dhamma only in a principled manner.

an5.131:4.4.verse: And that wheel cannot be rolled back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.”

an5.132:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, possessing five factors a wheel-turning monarch’s eldest son continues to wield the power set in motion by his father only in a principled manner.

an5.132:1.2.verse: And this power cannot be undermined by any human enemy.

an5.132:2.2.verse: A wheel-turning monarch’s oldest son knows what is right, knows principle, knows moderation, knows the right time, and knows the assembly.

an5.132:2.3.verse: A wheel-turning monarch’s oldest son who possesses these five factors continues to wield the power set in motion by his father only in a principled manner.

an5.132:2.4.verse: And this power cannot be undermined by any human enemy.

an5.132:3.1.verse: In the same way, possessing five qualities Sāriputta rightly keeps rolling the supreme Wheel of Dhamma that was rolled forth by the Realized One.

an5.132:3.2.verse: And that wheel cannot be turned back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.

an5.132:4.2.verse: Sāriputta knows what is right, knows principle, knows moderation, knows the right time, and knows the assembly.

an5.132:4.3.verse: Possessing these five qualities Sāriputta rightly keeps rolling the supreme Wheel of Dhamma that was rolled forth by the Realized One.

an5.132:4.4.verse: And that wheel cannot be turned back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.”

an5.133:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, even a wheel-turning monarch, a just and principled king, does not wield power without having their own king.”

an5.133:1.2.verse: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,

an5.133:1.3.verse: “But who is the king of the wheel-turning monarch, the just and principled king?”

an5.133:1.4.verse: “It is principle, monk,” said the Buddha.

an5.133:2.1.verse: “Monk, a wheel-turning monarch provides just protection and security for his court, relying only on principle—honoring, respecting, and venerating principle, having principle as his flag, banner, and authority.

an5.133:3.1.verse: He provides just protection and security for his aristocrats, vassals, troops, brahmins and householders, people of town and country, ascetics and brahmins, beasts and birds.

an5.133:3.2.verse: When he has done this, he wields power only in a principled manner.

an5.133:3.3.verse: And this power cannot be undermined by any human enemy.

an5.133:4.1.verse: In the same way, monk, a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, a just and principled king, provides just protection and security for the monks, relying only on principle—honoring, respecting, and venerating principle, having principle as his flag, banner, and authority.

an5.133:4.2.verse: ‘This kind of bodily action should be cultivated. This kind of bodily action should not be cultivated.

an5.133:4.3.verse: This kind of verbal action should be cultivated. This kind of verbal action should not be cultivated.

an5.133:4.4.verse: This kind of mental action should be cultivated. This kind of mental action should not be cultivated.

an5.133:4.5.verse: This kind of livelihood should be cultivated. This kind of livelihood should not be cultivated.

an5.133:4.6.verse: This kind of village or town should be cultivated. This kind of village or town should not be cultivated.’

an5.133:5.1.verse: In the same way, monk, a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, a just and principled king, provides just protection and security for the nuns … laymen … laywomen, relying only on principle—honoring, respecting, and venerating principle, having principle as his flag, banner, and authority.

an5.133:5.2.verse: ‘This kind of bodily action should be cultivated. This kind of bodily action should not be cultivated.

an5.133:5.3.verse: This kind of verbal action should be cultivated. This kind of verbal action should not be cultivated.

an5.133:5.4.verse: This kind of mental action should be cultivated. This kind of mental action should not be cultivated.

an5.133:5.5.verse: This kind of livelihood should be cultivated. This kind of livelihood should not be cultivated.

an5.133:5.6.verse: This kind of village or town should be cultivated. This kind of village or town should not be cultivated.’

an5.133:6.1.verse: When a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha has provided just protection and security for the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, he rolls forth the supreme Wheel of Dhamma only in a principled manner.

an5.133:6.2.verse: And that wheel cannot be rolled back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.”

an5.134:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, with five factors an anointed aristocratic king lives in his own realm, no matter what region he lives in.

an5.134:2.2.verse: An anointed aristocratic king is well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

an5.134:2.3.verse: He is rich, affluent, and wealthy, with a full treasury and storehouses.

an5.134:2.4.verse: He is powerful, having an army of four divisions that is obedient and carries out instructions.

an5.134:2.5.verse: He has a commander who is astute, competent, and intelligent, able to think issues through as they bear upon the past, future, and present.

an5.134:2.6.verse: These four things bring his glory to fruition.

an5.134:2.7.verse: With these five qualities, including glory, an anointed aristocratic king lives in his own realm, no matter what direction he lives in.

an5.134:2.9.verse: Because that is how it is for victors.

an5.134:3.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant with five qualities lives with mind freed, no matter what region they live in.

an5.134:3.3.verse: It’s when mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

an5.134:3.4.verse: This is like the anointed aristocratic king’s impeccable birth.

an5.134:3.5.verse: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

an5.134:3.6.verse: This is like the anointed aristocratic king being rich, affluent, and wealthy, with full treasury and storehouses.

an5.134:3.7.verse: They live with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

an5.134:3.8.verse: This is like the anointed aristocratic king having power.

an5.134:3.9.verse: They’re wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

an5.134:3.10.verse: This is like the anointed aristocratic king having a commander.

an5.134:3.11.verse: These four qualities bring their freedom to fruition.

an5.134:3.12.verse: With these five qualities, including freedom, they live in their own realm, no matter what region they live in.

an5.134:3.14.verse: Because that is how it is for those whose mind is free.”

an5.135:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, an anointed aristocratic king’s eldest son with five factors aspires to kingship.

an5.135:1.3.verse: It’s when an anointed aristocratic king’s eldest son is well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

an5.135:1.4.verse: He is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.

an5.135:1.5.verse: He is dear and beloved to his parents.

an5.135:1.6.verse: He is dear and beloved to the people of town and country.

an5.135:1.7.verse: He is trained and skilled in the arts of anointed aristocratic kings, such as elephant riding, horse riding, driving a chariot, archery, and swordsmanship.

an5.135:2.2.verse: ‘I’m well born on both my mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

an5.135:2.3.verse: Why shouldn’t I aspire to kingship?

an5.135:2.4.verse: I’m attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.

an5.135:2.5.verse: Why shouldn’t I aspire to kingship?

an5.135:2.6.verse: I’m dear and beloved to my parents.

an5.135:2.7.verse: Why shouldn’t I aspire to kingship?

an5.135:2.8.verse: I’m dear and beloved to the people of town and country.

an5.135:2.9.verse: Why shouldn’t I aspire to kingship?

an5.135:2.10.verse: I’m trained and skilled in the arts of anointed aristocratic kings, such as elephant riding, horse riding, driving a chariot, archery, and swordsmanship.

an5.135:2.11.verse: Why shouldn’t I aspire to kingship?’

an5.135:2.12.verse: An anointed aristocratic king’s eldest son with these five factors aspires to kingship.

an5.135:3.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant with five qualities aspires to end the defilements.

an5.135:3.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

an5.135:3.4.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

an5.135:3.5.verse: They are rarely ill or unwell. Their stomach digests well, being neither too hot nor too cold, but just right, and fit for meditation.

an5.135:3.6.verse: They’re not devious or deceitful. They reveal themselves honestly to the Teacher or sensible spiritual companions.

an5.135:3.7.verse: They live with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

an5.135:3.8.verse: They’re wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

an5.135:4.2.verse: ‘I am a person of faith; I have faith in the Realized One’s awakening …

an5.135:4.4.verse: Why shouldn’t I aspire to end the defilements?

an5.135:4.5.verse: I’m rarely ill or unwell. My stomach digests well, being neither too hot nor too cold, but just right, and fit for meditation.

an5.135:4.6.verse: Why shouldn’t I aspire to end the defilements?

an5.135:4.7.verse: I’m not devious or deceitful. I reveal myself honestly to the Teacher or sensible spiritual companions.

an5.135:4.8.verse: Why shouldn’t I aspire to end the defilements?

an5.135:4.9.verse: I live with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. I’m strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

an5.135:4.10.verse: Why shouldn’t I aspire to end the defilements?

an5.135:4.11.verse: I’m wise. I have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

an5.135:4.12.verse: Why shouldn’t I aspire to end the defilements?’

an5.135:4.13.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities aspires to end the defilements.”

an5.136:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, an anointed aristocratic king’s eldest son with five factors aspires to become a viceroy.

an5.136:1.3.verse: It’s when an anointed aristocratic king’s eldest son is well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

an5.136:1.4.verse: He is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.

an5.136:1.5.verse: He is dear and beloved to his parents.

an5.136:1.6.verse: He is dear and beloved to the armed forces.

an5.136:1.7.verse: He is astute, competent, and intelligent, able to think issues through as they bear upon the past, future, and present.

an5.136:2.6.verse: dear and beloved to my parents …

an5.136:2.8.verse: dear and beloved to the armed forces …

an5.136:2.10.verse: I’m astute, competent, and intelligent, able to think issues through as they bear upon the past, future, and present.

an5.136:2.11.verse: Why shouldn’t I aspire to become a viceroy?’

an5.136:2.12.verse: An anointed aristocratic king’s eldest son with these five factors aspires to become a viceroy.

an5.136:3.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant with five qualities aspires to end the defilements.

an5.136:3.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

an5.136:3.4.verse: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s totally full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, reciting them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

an5.136:3.5.verse: Their mind is firmly established in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

an5.136:3.6.verse: They live with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

an5.136:3.7.verse: They’re wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

an5.136:4.10.verse: wise. I have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

an5.136:4.11.verse: Why shouldn’t I aspire to end the defilements?’

an5.136:4.12.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities aspires to end the defilements.”

an5.137:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five sleep little at night, staying mostly awake.

an5.137:1.3.verse: A woman longing for a man.

an5.137:1.4.verse: A man longing for a woman.

an5.137:1.5.verse: A thief longing for their loot.

an5.137:1.6.verse: A king busy with his duties.

an5.137:1.7.verse: A mendicant longing for freedom from the yoke.

an5.137:1.8.verse: These five sleep little at night, staying mostly awake.”

an5.138:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a royal bull elephant with five factors eats food, takes up space, drops dung, and takes a ticket, yet is still reckoned a royal bull elephant.

an5.138:1.3.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant can’t endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

an5.138:1.4.verse: A royal bull elephant with these five factors eats food, takes up space, drops dung, and takes a ticket, yet is still reckoned a royal bull elephant.

an5.138:2.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant with five qualities eats food, takes up space, tramples beds and chairs, and takes a ticket, yet is still reckoned a mendicant.

an5.138:2.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant can’t endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

an5.138:2.4.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities eats food, takes up space, tramples beds and chairs, and takes a ticket, yet is still reckoned a mendicant.”

an5.139:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a royal bull elephant with five factors is not worthy of a king, not fit to serve a king, and is not reckoned a factor of kingship.

an5.139:1.3.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant can’t endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

an5.139:2.1.verse: And how is it that a royal bull elephant can’t endure sights?

an5.139:2.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant gone to battle falters and founders at the sight of a division of elephants, of cavalry, of chariots, or of infantry. It doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

an5.139:2.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant can’t endure sights.

an5.139:3.1.verse: And how is it that a royal bull elephant can’t endure sounds?

an5.139:3.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant gone to battle falters and founders at the sound of a division of elephants, of cavalry, of chariots, or of infantry, or the thunder of the drums, kettledrums, horns, and cymbals. It doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

an5.139:3.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant can’t endure sounds.

an5.139:4.1.verse: And how is it that a royal bull elephant can’t endure smells?

an5.139:4.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant gone to battle falters and founders when it smells the odor of the feces and urine of battle-hardened, pedigree royal bull elephants. It doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

an5.139:4.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant can’t endure smells.

an5.139:5.1.verse: And how is it that a royal bull elephant can’t endure tastes?

an5.139:5.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant gone to battle falters and founders when it misses a meal of grass and water, or it misses two, three, four, or five meals. It doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

an5.139:5.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant can’t endure tastes.

an5.139:6.1.verse: And how is it that a royal bull elephant can’t endure touches?

an5.139:6.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant gone to battle falters and founders when struck by a swift arrow, or by two, three, four, or five swift arrows. It doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

an5.139:6.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant can’t endure touches.

an5.139:7.1.verse: A royal bull elephant with these five factors is not worthy of a king, not fit to serve a king, and is not reckoned a factor of kingship.

an5.139:8.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant with five qualities is not worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, not worthy of hospitality, not worthy of a religious donation, not worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is not the supreme field of merit for the world.

an5.139:8.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant can’t endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

an5.139:9.1.verse: And how is it that a mendicant can’t endure sights?

an5.139:9.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, seeing a sight with their eyes, is aroused by a desirable sight, so is not able to still the mind.

an5.139:9.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant can’t endure sights.

an5.139:10.1.verse: And how is it that a mendicant can’t endure sounds?

an5.139:10.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, hearing a sound with their ears, is aroused by a desirable sound, so is not able to still the mind.

an5.139:10.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant can’t endure sounds.

an5.139:11.1.verse: And how is it that a mendicant can’t endure smells?

an5.139:11.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, smelling an odor with their nose, is aroused by a desirable smell, so is not able to still the mind.

an5.139:11.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant can’t endure smells.

an5.139:12.1.verse: And how is it that a mendicant can’t endure tastes?

an5.139:12.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, tasting a flavor with their tongue, is aroused by desirable tastes, so is not able to still the mind.

an5.139:12.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant can’t endure tastes.

an5.139:13.1.verse: And how is it that a mendicant can’t endure touches?

an5.139:13.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, encountering a touch with their body, is aroused by a desirable touch, so is not able to still the mind.

an5.139:13.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant can’t endure touches.

an5.139:14.1.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is not worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, not worthy of hospitality, not worthy of a religious donation, not worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is not the supreme field of merit for the world.

an5.139:15.3.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant can endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

an5.139:16.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant can endure sights.

an5.139:17.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant can endure sounds.

an5.139:18.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant can endure smells.

an5.139:19.1.verse: And how is it that a royal bull elephant can endure tastes?

an5.139:19.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant gone to battle does not falter or founder when it misses a meal of grass and water, or it misses two, three, four, or five meals. It stays firm, and plunges into battle.

an5.139:19.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant can endure tastes.

an5.139:20.1.verse: And how is it that a royal bull elephant can endure touches?

an5.139:20.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant gone to battle does not falter or founder when struck by a swift arrow, or by two, three, four, or five swift arrows. It stays firm, and plunges into battle.

an5.139:20.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant can endure touches.

an5.139:23.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, seeing a sight with their eyes, is not aroused by a desirable sight, so is able to still the mind.

an5.139:26.1.verse: And how is it that a mendicant can endure tastes?

an5.139:26.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, tasting a flavor with their tongue, is not aroused by desirable tastes, so is able to still the mind.

an5.139:26.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant can endure tastes.

an5.139:27.1.verse: And how is it that a mendicant can endure touches?

an5.139:27.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, encountering a touch with their body, is not aroused by a desirable touch, so is able to still the mind.

an5.139:27.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant can endure touches.

an5.139:28.1.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

an5.140:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a royal bull elephant with five factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.

an5.140:1.3.verse: A royal bull elephant listens, destroys, protects, endures, and goes fast.

an5.140:2.1.verse: And how does a royal bull elephant listen?

an5.140:2.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens to whatever task the elephant trainer has it do,

an5.140:2.3.verse: whether or not it has done it before.

an5.140:2.5.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant listens.

an5.140:3.1.verse: And how does a royal bull elephant destroy?

an5.140:3.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant in battle destroys elephants with their riders, horses with their riders, chariots and charioteers, and foot soldiers.

an5.140:3.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant destroys.

an5.140:4.1.verse: And how does a royal bull elephant protect?

an5.140:4.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant in battle protects its fore-quarters and hind-quarters, its fore-feet and hind-feet, and its head, ears, tusks, trunk, tail, and rider.

an5.140:4.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant protects.

an5.140:5.1.verse: And how does a royal bull elephant endure?

an5.140:5.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant in battle endures being struck by spears, swords, arrows, and axes; it endures the thunder of the drums, kettledrums, horns, and cymbals.

an5.140:5.3.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant endures.

an5.140:6.1.verse: And how does a royal bull elephant go fast?

an5.140:6.2.verse: It’s when a royal bull elephant swiftly goes in whatever direction the elephant trainer sends it,

an5.140:6.3.verse: whether or not it has been there before.

an5.140:6.5.verse: That’s how a royal bull elephant goes fast.

an5.140:7.1.verse: A royal bull elephant with these five factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.

an5.140:8.1.verse: In the same way, a mendicant with five qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

an5.140:8.3.verse: A mendicant listens, destroys, protects, endures, and goes fast.

an5.140:9.1.verse: And how does a mendicant listen?

an5.140:9.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens when the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One is being taught.

an5.140:10.1.verse: And how does a mendicant destroy?

an5.140:10.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t tolerate a sensual, malicious, or cruel thought. They don’t tolerate any bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen, but give them up, dispel them, calm them, eliminate them, and obliterate them.

an5.140:11.1.verse: And how does a mendicant protect?

an5.140:11.2.verse: When a mendicant sees a sight with the eyes, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

an5.140:11.3.verse: If the faculty of sight were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of sight, and achieving its restraint.

an5.140:11.4.verse: Hearing a sound with their ears …

an5.140:11.5.verse: Smelling an odor with their nose …

an5.140:11.6.verse: Tasting a flavor with their tongue …

an5.140:11.7.verse: Encountering a touch with their body …

an5.140:11.8.verse: Knowing an idea with their mind, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

an5.140:11.9.verse: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of mind, and achieving its restraint.

an5.140:12.1.verse: And how does a mendicant endure?

an5.140:12.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant endures cold, heat, hunger, and thirst; the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles; rude and unwelcome criticism; and puts up with physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.

an5.140:13.1.verse: And how does a mendicant go fast?

an5.140:13.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant swiftly goes in the direction they’ve never gone before in all this long time; that is, the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.

an5.140:13.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant goes fast.

an5.140:14.1.verse: A mendicant with these five qualities … is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

an5.141:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five individuals are found in the world.

an5.141:1.3.verse: One gives then scorns, one lives together then scorns, one is gullible for gossip, one is impulsive, and one is dull and stupid.

an5.141:2.1.verse: And how does an individual give then scorn?

an5.141:2.2.verse: It’s when an individual gives an individual robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

an5.141:2.6.verse: They give to them, then they scorn them.

an5.141:2.7.verse: That’s how an individual gives then scorns.

an5.141:3.1.verse: And how does an individual live together then scorn?

an5.141:3.2.verse: It’s when an individual lives with someone else for two or three years.

an5.141:3.3.verse: They live together with them, then they scorn them.

an5.141:3.4.verse: That’s how an individual lives together then scorns.

an5.141:4.1.verse: And how is an individual gullible for gossip?

an5.141:4.2.verse: It’s when they’re very quick to believe what a certain individual says in praise or criticism of another.

an5.141:4.3.verse: That’s how an individual is gullible for gossip.

an5.141:5.1.verse: And how is an individual impulsive?

an5.141:5.2.verse: It’s when a certain individual is fickle in faith, devotion, fondness, and confidence.

an5.141:5.3.verse: That’s how an individual is impulsive.

an5.141:6.1.verse: And how is an individual dull and stupid?

an5.141:6.2.verse: It’s when they don’t know the difference between qualities that are skillful and unskillful, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, and those with a portion of dark or bright.

an5.141:6.3.verse: That’s how an individual is dull and stupid.

an5.141:6.4.verse: These are the five individuals found in the world.”

an5.142:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five individuals are found in the world.

an5.142:1.3.verse: One individual transgresses and regrets it.

an5.142:1.4.verse: And they don’t truly understand the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where those arisen bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.

an5.142:2.1.verse: One individual transgresses and doesn’t regret it.

an5.142:3.1.verse: One individual doesn’t transgress yet still feels regret.

an5.142:4.1.verse: One individual neither transgresses nor regrets.

an5.142:5.1.verse: One individual neither transgresses nor regrets.

an5.142:5.2.verse: And they do understand where those arisen bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.

an5.142:6.1.verse: Take the case of the individual who transgresses and regrets it.

an5.142:6.2.verse: And they don’t truly understand the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where those arisen bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.

an5.142:6.4.verse: ‘Venerable, the defilements born of transgression are found in you, and the defilements born of regret grow. You would do well to give up the defilements born of transgression and dispel the defilements born of regret, and then develop the mind and wisdom.

an5.142:6.5.verse: In this way you’ll become just like the fifth individual.’

an5.142:7.1.verse: Take the case of the individual who transgresses and doesn’t regret it.

an5.142:7.4.verse: ‘Venerable, the defilements born of transgression are found in you, but the defilements born of regret don’t grow. You would do well to give up the defilements born of transgression, and then develop the mind and wisdom.

an5.142:7.5.verse: In this way you’ll become just like the fifth individual.’

an5.142:8.1.verse: Take the case of the individual who doesn’t transgress yet feels regret.

an5.142:8.4.verse: ‘Venerable, the defilements born of transgression are not found in you, yet the defilements born of regret grow. You would do well to dispel the defilements born of regret, and then develop the mind and wisdom.

an5.142:8.5.verse: In this way you’ll become just like the fifth individual.’

an5.142:9.1.verse: Take the case of the individual who neither transgresses nor regrets.

an5.142:9.4.verse: ‘Venerable, the defilements born of transgression are not found in you, and the defilements born of regret don’t grow. You would do well to develop the mind and wisdom.

an5.142:9.5.verse: In this way you’ll become just like the fifth individual.’

an5.142:10.1.verse: And so, mendicants, when these four individuals are advised and instructed by comparison with the fifth individual, they gradually attain the ending of defilements.”

an5.143:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

an5.143:1.2.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Vesālī for alms.

an5.143:1.3.verse: Now at that time around five hundred Licchavis were sitting together at the Sārandada Shrine, and this discussion came up among them,

an5.143:1.4.verse: “The appearance of five treasures is rare in the world.

an5.143:1.6.verse: The elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, and the householder-treasure.

an5.143:1.7.verse: The appearance of these five treasures is rare in the world.”

an5.143:2.1.verse: Then those Licchavis sent a man out on to the road, saying,

an5.143:2.2.verse: “My man, please tell us when you see the Buddha.”

an5.143:2.3.verse: That man saw the Buddha coming off in the distance.

an5.143:2.4.verse: He went to the Licchavis and said,

an5.143:2.5.verse: “Sirs, the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha is coming.

an5.143:3.1.verse: Then those Licchavis went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,

an5.143:4.1.verse: “Please go to the Sārandada Shrine, out of sympathy.”

an5.143:4.3.verse: Then the Buddha went up to the Sārandada Shrine. He sat down on the seat spread out and said to the Licchavis,

an5.143:4.4.verse: “Licchavis, what were you sitting talking about just now? What conversation was left unfinished?”

an5.143:4.5.verse: “Well, sir, this discussion came up among us while we were sitting together:

an5.143:4.6.verse: ‘The appearance of five treasures is rare in the world. …’”

an5.143:5.1.verse: “You Licchavis are so fixated on sensual pleasures, that’s the only discussion that came up!

an5.143:5.2.verse: Licchavis, the appearance of five treasures is rare in the world.

an5.143:5.4.verse: The appearance of a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha.

an5.143:5.5.verse: A teacher of the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One.

an5.143:5.6.verse: An individual who understands the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One.

an5.143:5.7.verse: An individual who practices in line with the teaching.

an5.143:5.8.verse: An individual who is grateful and thankful.

an5.143:5.9.verse: The appearance of these five treasures is rare in the world.”

an5.144:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāketa in Tikaṇḍakī Wood.

an5.144:1.2.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

an5.144:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, a mendicant would do well to meditate from time to time perceiving the following: the repulsive in the unrepulsive,

an5.144:2.3.verse: the repulsive in both the unrepulsive and the repulsive, and

an5.144:2.4.verse: the unrepulsive in both the repulsive and the unrepulsive.

an5.144:2.5.verse: A mendicant would do well to meditate from time to time staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive.

an5.144:3.1.verse: For what reason should a mendicant meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive?

an5.144:3.2.verse: ‘May greed not arise in me for things that arouse greed.’

an5.144:3.3.verse: A mendicant should meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive for this reason.

an5.144:4.1.verse: For what reason should a mendicant meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive?

an5.144:4.2.verse: ‘May hate not arise in me for things that provoke hate.’ …

an5.144:5.1.verse: For what reason should a mendicant meditate perceiving the repulsive in both the unrepulsive and the repulsive?

an5.144:5.2.verse: ‘May greed not arise in me for things that arouse greed. May hate not arise in me for things that provoke hate.’ …

an5.144:6.1.verse: For what reason should a mendicant meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in both the repulsive and the unrepulsive?

an5.144:6.2.verse: ‘May hate not arise in me for things that provoke hate. May greed not arise in me for things that arouse greed.’ …

an5.144:7.1.verse: For what reason should a mendicant meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive?

an5.144:7.2.verse: ‘May no greed for things that arouse greed, hate for things that provoke hate, or delusion for things that promote delusion arise in me in any way at all.’

an5.144:7.3.verse: For this reason a mendicant should meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive.”

an5.145:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, someone with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an5.145:1.3.verse: They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, and consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

an5.145:1.4.verse: Someone with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an5.145:2.1.verse: Someone with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an5.145:2.3.verse: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

an5.145:2.4.verse: Someone with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an5.146:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you shouldn’t associate with a mendicant friend who has five qualities.

an5.146:1.3.verse: They start up work projects. They take up disciplinary issues. They conflict with leading mendicants. They like long and aimless wandering. They’re unable to educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire you from time to time with a Dhamma talk.

an5.146:1.4.verse: Mendicants, you shouldn’t associate with a mendicant friend who possesses these five qualities.

an5.146:2.1.verse: You should associate with a mendicant friend who has five qualities.

an5.146:2.3.verse: They don’t start up work projects. They don’t take up disciplinary issues. They don’t conflict with leading mendicants. They don’t like long and aimless wandering. They’re able to educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire you from time to time with a Dhamma talk.

an5.146:2.4.verse: You should associate with a mendicant friend who possesses these five qualities.”

an5.147:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five gifts of an untrue person.

an5.147:1.3.verse: They give carelessly. They give thoughtlessly. They don’t give with their own hand. They give the dregs. They give without consideration for consequences.

an5.147:1.4.verse: These are the five gifts of an untrue person.

an5.147:2.1.verse: There are these five gifts of a true person.

an5.147:2.3.verse: They give carefully. They give thoughtfully. They give with their own hand. They don’t give the dregs. They give with consideration for consequences.

an5.147:2.4.verse: These are the five gifts of a true person.”

an5.148:1.1.verse: “There are these five gifts of a true person.

an5.148:1.3.verse: They give a gift out of faith. They give a gift carefully. They give a gift at the right time. They give a gift with no strings attached. They give a gift without damaging themselves or others.

an5.148:2.1.verse: Having given a gift out of faith, in whatever place the result of that gift manifests they become rich, affluent, and wealthy. And they’re attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.

an5.148:3.1.verse: Having given a gift carefully, in whatever place the result of that gift manifests they become rich, affluent, and wealthy.

an5.148:3.2.verse: And their children, wives, bondservants, servants, and workers want to listen. They actively listen and try to understand.

an5.148:4.1.verse: Having given a gift at the right time, in whatever place the result of that gift manifests they become rich, affluent, and wealthy.

an5.148:4.2.verse: And when the time is right, their needs are amply satisfied.

an5.148:5.1.verse: Having given a gift with no strings attached, in whatever place the result of that gift manifests they become rich, affluent, and wealthy.

an5.148:5.2.verse: And their mind tends to enjoy the five refined kinds of sensual stimulation.

an5.148:6.1.verse: Having given a gift without damaging themselves or others, in whatever place the result of that gift manifests they become rich, affluent, and wealthy.

an5.148:6.2.verse: And no damage comes to their property from anywhere, whether fire, flood, rulers, bandits, or unloved heirs.

an5.148:6.3.verse: These are the five gifts of a true person.”
