an8.22:12.3.verse: He informed the Buddha of all he had discussed with the householder Uggata of Elephant Village. The Buddha said:

an8.22:13.2.verse: When I declared that the householder Uggata of Elephant Village was someone who has eight amazing and incredible qualities, I was referring to the same eight qualities that he rightly explained to you.

an8.22:13.3.verse: You should remember the householder Uggata of Elephant Village as someone who has these eight amazing and incredible qualities.”

an8.23:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Āḷavī, at Āḷavī’s premier shrine.

an8.23:1.2.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

an8.23:1.3.verse: “Mendicants, you should remember the householder Hatthaka of Āḷavī as someone who has seven amazing and incredible qualities.

an8.23:1.12.verse: You should remember the householder Hatthaka of Āḷavī as someone who possesses these seven amazing and incredible qualities.”

an8.23:1.13.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

an8.23:1.14.verse: When he had spoken, the Holy One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling.

an8.23:2.1.verse: Then a certain mendicant robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of the householder Hatthaka of Āḷavī, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

an8.23:2.2.verse: Then Hatthaka went up to that mendicant, bowed, and sat down to one side. The mendicant said to Hatthaka:

an8.23:3.1.verse: “Respectable sir, the Buddha declared that you have seven amazing and incredible qualities.

an8.23:3.10.verse: The Buddha declared that you possess these seven amazing and incredible qualities.”

an8.23:3.11.verse: “But sir, I trust that no white-clothed lay people were present?”

an8.23:3.12.verse: “No, there weren’t any white-clothed lay people present.”

an8.23:4.1.verse: Then that mendicant, after taking almsfood in Hatthaka of Āḷavī’s home, rose from his seat and left.

an8.23:4.2.verse: Then after the meal, on his return from almsround, he went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him of what he had discussed with the householder Hatthaka. The Buddha said:

an8.23:7.3.verse: He doesn’t want his own good qualities to be made known to others.

an8.23:7.4.verse: Well then, mendicant, you should remember the householder Hatthaka of Āḷavī as someone who has this eighth amazing and incredible quality, that is, fewness of wishes.”

an8.24:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Āḷavī, at Āḷavī’s premier shrine.

an8.24:1.2.verse: Then the householder Hatthaka of Āḷavī, escorted by around five hundred lay followers, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to Hatthaka:

an8.24:1.4.verse: How do you bring together such a large congregation?”

an8.24:1.5.verse: “Sir, I bring together such a large congregation by using the four ways of being inclusive as taught by the Buddha.

an8.24:1.7.verse: can be included by a gift, I include them by giving a gift.

an8.24:1.9.verse: can be included by kindly words, I include them by kindly words.

an8.24:1.11.verse: can be included by taking care of them, I include them by caring for them.

an8.24:1.13.verse: can be included by equality, I include them by treating them equally.

an8.24:1.14.verse: But also, worthy sir, my family is wealthy.

an8.24:1.15.verse: They wouldn’t think that a poor person was worth listening to in the same way.”

an8.24:1.17.verse: This is the right way to bring together a large congregation.

an8.24:1.18.verse: Whether in the past, future, or present, all those who have brought together a large congregation have done so by using these four ways of being inclusive.”

an8.24:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired Hatthaka of Āḷavī with a Dhamma talk, after which he got up from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

an8.24:2.2.verse: Then, not long after Hatthaka had left, the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

an8.24:2.3.verse: “Mendicants, you should remember the householder Hatthaka of Āḷavī as someone who has eight amazing and incredible qualities.

an8.24:2.13.verse: You should remember the householder Hatthaka of Āḷavī as someone who possesses these eight amazing and incredible qualities.”

an8.25:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

an8.25:1.2.verse: Then Mahānāma the Sakyan went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

an8.25:1.3.verse: “Sir, how is a lay follower defined?”

an8.25:1.4.verse: “Mahānāma, when you’ve gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha,

an8.25:1.5.verse: you’re considered to be a lay follower.”

an8.25:2.1.verse: “But how is an ethical lay follower defined?”

an8.25:2.2.verse: “When a lay follower doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor,

an8.25:2.3.verse: they’re considered to be an ethical lay follower.”

an8.25:3.1.verse: “But how do we define a lay follower who is practicing to benefit themselves, not others?”

an8.25:3.2.verse: “A lay follower is accomplished in faith, but doesn’t encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:3.3.verse: They’re accomplished in ethical conduct, but don’t encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:3.4.verse: They’re accomplished in generosity, but don’t encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:3.5.verse: They like to see the mendicants, but don’t encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:3.6.verse: They like to hear the true teaching, but don’t encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:3.7.verse: They readily memorize the teachings they’ve heard, but don’t encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:3.8.verse: They examine the meaning of the teachings they’ve memorized, but don’t encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:3.9.verse: Understanding the meaning and the teaching, they practice in line with the teaching, but they don’t encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:3.10.verse: That’s how we define a lay follower who is practicing to benefit themselves, not others.”

an8.25:4.1.verse: “But how do we define a lay follower who is practicing to benefit both themselves and others?”

an8.25:4.2.verse: “A lay follower is accomplished in faith and encourages others to do the same.

an8.25:4.3.verse: They’re accomplished in ethical conduct and encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:4.4.verse: They’re accomplished in generosity and encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:4.5.verse: They like to see the mendicants and encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:4.6.verse: They like to hear the true teaching and encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:4.7.verse: They readily memorize the teachings they’ve heard and encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:4.8.verse: They examine the meaning of the teachings they’ve memorized and encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:4.9.verse: Understanding the meaning and the teaching, they practice in line with the teaching and they encourage others to do the same.

an8.25:4.10.verse: That’s how we define a lay follower who is practicing to benefit both themselves and others.”

an8.26:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in Jīvaka’s Mango Grove.

an8.26:1.2.verse: Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

an8.26:1.3.verse: “Sir, how is a lay follower defined?”

an8.26:1.4.verse: “Jīvaka, when you’ve gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha,

an8.26:1.5.verse: you’re considered to be a lay follower.”

an8.26:2.1.verse: “But how is an ethical lay follower defined?”

an8.26:2.2.verse: “When a lay follower doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor,

an8.26:2.3.verse: they’re considered to be an ethical lay follower.”

an8.26:3.1.verse: “But how do we define a lay follower who is practicing to benefit themselves, not others?”

an8.26:3.2.verse: “A lay follower is accomplished in faith, but doesn’t encourage others to do the same. They’re accomplished in ethical conduct … they’re accomplished in generosity … they like to see the mendicants … they like to hear the true teaching … they memorize the teachings … they examine the meaning …

an8.26:3.3.verse: Understanding the meaning and the teaching, they practice in line with the teaching, but they don’t encourage others to do the same.

an8.26:3.4.verse: That’s how we define a lay follower who is practicing to benefit themselves, not others.”

an8.26:4.1.verse: “But how do we define a lay follower who is practicing to benefit both themselves and others?”

an8.26:4.2.verse: “A lay follower is accomplished in faith and encourages others to do the same.

an8.26:4.3.verse: They’re accomplished in ethical conduct and encourage others to do the same.

an8.26:4.4.verse: They’re accomplished in generosity and encourage others to do the same.

an8.26:4.5.verse: They like to see the mendicants and encourage others to do the same.

an8.26:4.6.verse: They like to hear the true teaching and encourage others to do the same.

an8.26:4.7.verse: They readily memorize the teachings they’ve heard and encourage others to do the same.

an8.26:4.8.verse: They examine the meaning of the teachings they’ve memorized and encourage others to do the same.

an8.26:4.9.verse: Understanding the meaning and the teaching, they practice in line with the teaching and they encourage others to do the same.

an8.26:4.10.verse: That’s how we define a lay follower who is practicing to benefit both themselves and others.”

an8.27:1.3.verse: Crying is the power of babies. Anger is the power of ladies. Weapons are the power of bandits. Authority is the power of rulers. Complaining is the power of fools. Reason is the power of the astute. Reflection is the power of the learned. Patience is the power of ascetics and brahmins.

an8.28:1.1.verse: Then Venerable Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

an8.28:1.2.verse: “Sāriputta, how many powers does a mendicant who has ended the defilements have that qualify them to claim:

an8.28:1.4.verse: “Sir, a mendicant who has ended the defilements has eight powers that qualify them to claim:

an8.28:2.2.verse: Firstly, a mendicant with defilements ended has clearly seen with right wisdom all conditions as truly impermanent.

an8.28:2.3.verse: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim:

an8.28:3.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has clearly seen with right wisdom that sensual pleasures are truly like a pit of glowing coals.

an8.28:3.2.verse: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim:

an8.28:4.1.verse: Furthermore, the mind of a mendicant with defilements ended slants, slopes, and inclines to seclusion. They’re withdrawn, loving renunciation, and have totally eliminated defiling influences.

an8.28:4.2.verse: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim:

an8.28:5.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

an8.28:5.2.verse: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim:

an8.28:6.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the four bases of psychic power …

an8.28:6.5.verse: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim:

an8.28:7.1.verse: A mendicant who has ended the defilements possesses these eight powers that qualify them to claim:

an8.29:1.1.verse: “‘Now is the time! Now is the time!’ So says an unlearned ordinary person. But they don’t know whether it’s time or not.

an8.29:1.2.verse: Mendicants, there are eight lost opportunities for spiritual practice.

an8.29:1.4.verse: Firstly, a Realized One has arisen in the world—perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed. He teaches the Dhamma leading to peace, extinguishment, awakening, as proclaimed by the Holy One.

an8.29:1.5.verse: But an individual has been reborn in hell.

an8.29:1.6.verse: This is the first lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

an8.29:2.1.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world … He teaches the Dhamma leading to peace, extinguishment, awakening, as proclaimed by the Holy One.

an8.29:2.2.verse: But an individual has been reborn in the animal realm. This is the second lost opportunity …

an8.29:3.1.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world …

an8.29:3.2.verse: But an individual has been reborn in the ghost realm. This is the third lost opportunity …

an8.29:4.1.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world …

an8.29:4.2.verse: But an individual has been reborn in one of the long-lived orders of gods. This is the fourth lost opportunity …

an8.29:5.1.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world …

an8.29:5.2.verse: But an individual has been reborn in the borderlands, among uneducated foreigners, where monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen do not go. This is the fifth lost opportunity …

an8.29:6.1.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world … And an individual is reborn in a central country. But they have wrong view and distorted perspective:

an8.29:6.2.verse: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’ This is the sixth lost opportunity …

an8.29:7.1.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world …

an8.29:7.2.verse: And an individual is reborn in a central country. But they’re witless, dull, idiotic, and unable to distinguish what is well said from what is poorly said.

an8.29:7.3.verse: This is the seventh lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

an8.29:8.1.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has not arisen in the world …

an8.29:8.2.verse: So he doesn’t teach the Dhamma leading to peace, extinguishment, awakening, as proclaimed by the Holy One. And an individual is reborn in a central country. And they’re wise, bright, clever, and able to distinguish what is well said from what is poorly said.

an8.29:8.3.verse: This is the eighth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

an8.29:9.1.verse: There are these eight lost opportunities for spiritual practice.

an8.29:10.1.verse: Mendicants, there is just one opportunity for spiritual practice.

an8.29:10.3.verse: It’s when a Realized One has arisen in the world, perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.

an8.29:10.4.verse: He teaches the Dhamma leading to peace, extinguishment, awakening, as proclaimed by the Holy One. And an individual is reborn in a central country. And they’re wise, bright, clever, and able to distinguish what is well said from what is poorly said.

an8.29:10.5.verse: This is the one opportunity for spiritual practice.

an8.29:11.1.verse: When you’ve gained the human state,

an8.29:11.2.verse: and the true teaching has been so well proclaimed,

an8.29:11.3.verse: those who don’t seize the moment

an8.29:12.1.verse: For many wrong times are spoken of,

an8.29:13.1.verse: If you find yourself in their presence,

an8.29:13.2.verse: so hard to find in the world,

an8.29:13.3.verse: and if you’ve gained a human birth,

an8.29:13.4.verse: and the teaching of the Dhamma;

an8.29:13.5.verse: that’s enough to make an effort,

an8.29:13.6.verse: for a personage who desires self-knowledge.

an8.29:14.1.verse: How is the true teaching to be understood

an8.29:14.2.verse: so that the moment doesn’t pass you by?

an8.29:14.3.verse: For if you miss your moment

an8.29:14.4.verse: you’ll grieve when sent to hell.

an8.29:15.3.verse: you’ll regret it for a long time,

an8.29:15.4.verse: like the merchant in the story of the past.

an8.29:16.2.verse: a failure in the true teaching,

an8.29:17.1.verse: Those who’ve gained the human state

an8.29:17.2.verse: when the true teaching has been so well proclaimed,

an8.29:17.3.verse: and have completed what the Teacher taught—

an8.29:17.4.verse: or will do so, or are doing so now—

an8.29:18.1.verse: have realized the right time in the world

an8.29:18.3.verse: You should live guarded, ever mindful,

an8.29:19.3.verse: proclaimed by the Realized One, the Clear-eyed One,

an8.29:19.4.verse: and taught by the Kinsman of the Sun.

an8.29:20.1.verse: Having cut off all underlying tendencies

an8.29:20.2.verse: that follow those drifting in Māra’s dominion,

an8.29:20.3.verse: they’re the ones in this world who’ve truly crossed over,

an8.29:20.4.verse: having reached the ending of defilements.”

an8.30:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Bhaggas at Crocodile’s Bellow, in the deer park at Bhesakaḷā’s Wood.

an8.30:1.2.verse: And at that time Venerable Anuruddha was staying in the land of the Cetīs in the Park of the East-Raftered Hall.

an8.30:1.3.verse: Then as Anuruddha was in private retreat this thought came to his mind:

an8.30:1.4.verse: “This teaching is for those of few wishes, not those of many wishes.

an8.30:1.5.verse: It’s for the contented, not those who lack contentment.

an8.30:1.6.verse: It’s for the secluded, not those who enjoy company.

an8.30:1.7.verse: It’s for the energetic, not the lazy.

an8.30:1.8.verse: It’s for the mindful, not the unmindful.

an8.30:1.9.verse: It’s for those with immersion, not those without immersion.

an8.30:1.10.verse: It’s for the wise, not the witless.”

an8.30:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha knew Anuruddha’s train of thought. As easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from the deer park at Bhesakaḷā’s Wood in the land of the Bhaggas and reappeared in front of Anuruddha in the Park of the East-Raftered Hall in the land of the Cetīs,

an8.30:2.2.verse: and sat down on the seat spread out.

an8.30:2.3.verse: Anuruddha bowed to the Buddha and sat down to one side.

an8.30:3.2.verse: It’s good that you reflect on these thoughts of a great man:

an8.30:3.3.verse: ‘This teaching is for those of few wishes, not those of many wishes.

an8.30:3.4.verse: It’s for the contented, not those who lack contentment.

an8.30:3.5.verse: It’s for the secluded, not those who enjoy company.

an8.30:3.6.verse: It’s for the energetic, not the lazy.

an8.30:3.7.verse: It’s for the mindful, not the unmindful.

an8.30:3.8.verse: It’s for those with immersion, not those without immersion.

an8.30:3.9.verse: It’s for the wise, not the witless.’

an8.30:3.10.verse: Well then, Anuruddha, you should also reflect on the following eighth thought of a great man:

an8.30:3.11.verse: ‘This teaching is for those who don’t enjoy proliferating and don’t like to proliferate, not for those who enjoy proliferating and like to proliferate.’

an8.30:4.1.verse: First you’ll reflect on these eight thoughts of a great man. Then as far as you want, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, you’ll enter and remain in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

an8.30:5.1.verse: You’ll enter and remain in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

an8.30:6.1.verse: You’ll enter and remain in the third absorption, where you’ll meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

an8.30:7.1.verse: With the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, you’ll enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

an8.30:8.1.verse: First you’ll reflect on these eight thoughts of a great man, and you’ll get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when you want, without trouble or difficulty. Then as you live contented, your rag robe will seem to you like a chest full of garments of different colors seems to a householder or householder’s child.

an8.30:8.2.verse: It will be for your enjoyment, relief, and comfort, and for alighting upon extinguishment.

an8.30:9.1.verse: As you live contented, your scraps of almsfood will seem to you like boiled fine rice with the dark grains picked out, served with many soups and sauces seems to a householder or householder’s child.

an8.30:9.2.verse: It will be for your enjoyment, relief, and comfort, and for alighting upon extinguishment.

an8.30:10.1.verse: As you live contented, your lodging at the root of a tree will seem to you like a bungalow, plastered inside and out, draft-free, with door fastened and window shuttered seems to a householder or householder’s child.

an8.30:10.2.verse: It will be for your enjoyment, relief, and comfort, and for alighting upon extinguishment.

an8.30:11.1.verse: As you live contented, your grass mat for lodging will seem to you like a couch spread with woolen covers—shag-piled, pure white, or embroidered with flowers—and spread with a fine deer hide, with a canopy above and red pillows at both ends seems to a householder or householder’s child.

an8.30:11.2.verse: It will be for your enjoyment, relief, and comfort, and for alighting upon extinguishment.

an8.30:12.1.verse: As you live contented your rancid urine as medicine will seem to you like various medicines—ghee, butter, oil, honey, and molasses—seem to a householder or householder’s child.

an8.30:12.2.verse: It will be for your enjoyment, relief, and comfort, and for alighting upon extinguishment.

an8.30:12.3.verse: Well then, Anuruddha, for the next rainy season residence you should stay right here in the land of the Cetīs in the Park of the East-Raftered Hall.”

an8.30:13.1.verse: After advising Anuruddha like this, the Buddha—as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, vanished from the Park of the East-Raftered Hall in the land of the Cetīs and reappeared in the deer park at Bhesakaḷā’s Wood in the land of the Bhaggas at Crocodile’s Bellow.

an8.30:13.2.verse: He sat down on the seat spread out

an8.30:13.4.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the eight thoughts of a great man. Listen …

an8.30:13.5.verse: And what are the eight thoughts of a great man?

an8.30:13.6.verse: This teaching is for those of few wishes, not those of many wishes.

an8.30:13.7.verse: It’s for the contented, not those who lack contentment.

an8.30:13.8.verse: It’s for the secluded, not those who enjoy company.

an8.30:13.9.verse: It’s for the energetic, not the lazy.

an8.30:13.10.verse: It’s for the mindful, not the unmindful.

an8.30:13.11.verse: It’s for those with immersion, not those without immersion.

an8.30:13.12.verse: It’s for the wise, not the witless.

an8.30:13.13.verse: It’s for those who don’t enjoy proliferating and don’t like to proliferate, not for those who enjoy proliferating and like to proliferate.

an8.30:14.1.verse: ‘This teaching is for those of few wishes, not those of many wishes.’

an8.30:14.2.verse: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

an8.30:14.3.verse: A mendicant with few wishes doesn’t wish: ‘May they know me as having few wishes!’ When contented, they don’t wish: ‘May they know me as contented!’ When secluded, they don’t wish: ‘May they know me as secluded!’ When energetic, they don’t wish: ‘May they know me as energetic!’ When mindful, they don’t wish: ‘May they know me as mindful!’ When immersed, they don’t wish: ‘May they know me as immersed!’ When wise, they don’t wish: ‘May they know me as wise!’ When not enjoying proliferation, they don’t wish: ‘May they know me as one who doesn’t enjoy proliferating!’

an8.30:14.4.verse: ‘This teaching is for those of few wishes, not those of many wishes.’

an8.30:14.5.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

an8.30:15.1.verse: ‘This teaching is for the contented, not those who lack contentment.’ That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

an8.30:15.2.verse: It’s for a mendicant who’s content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

an8.30:15.3.verse: ‘This teaching is for the contented, not those who lack contentment.’

an8.30:15.4.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

an8.30:16.1.verse: ‘This teaching is for the secluded, not those who enjoy company.’ That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

an8.30:16.2.verse: It’s for a mendicant who lives secluded. But monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, rulers and their chief ministers, monastics of other religions and their disciples go to visit them.

an8.30:16.3.verse: With a mind slanting, sloping, and inclining to seclusion, withdrawn, and loving renunciation, that mendicant invariably gives a talk concerned only with sending them away.

an8.30:16.4.verse: ‘This teaching is for the secluded, not those who enjoy company.’

an8.30:16.5.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

an8.30:17.1.verse: ‘This teaching is for the energetic, not the lazy.’ That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

an8.30:17.2.verse: It’s for a mendicant who lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

an8.30:17.3.verse: ‘This teaching is for the energetic, not the lazy.’

an8.30:17.4.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

an8.30:18.1.verse: ‘This teaching is for the mindful, not the unmindful.’

an8.30:18.2.verse: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

an8.30:18.3.verse: It’s for a mendicant who’s mindful. They have utmost mindfulness and alertness, and can remember and recall what was said and done long ago.

an8.30:18.4.verse: ‘This teaching is for the mindful, not the unmindful.’

an8.30:18.5.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

an8.30:19.1.verse: ‘This teaching is for those with immersion, not those without immersion.’

an8.30:19.2.verse: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

an8.30:19.3.verse: It’s for a mendicant who, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.

an8.30:19.4.verse: ‘This teaching is for those with immersion, not those without immersion.’

an8.30:19.5.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

an8.30:20.1.verse: ‘This teaching is for the wise, not the witless.’

an8.30:20.2.verse: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

an8.30:20.3.verse: It’s for a mendicant who’s wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

an8.30:20.4.verse: ‘This teaching is for the wise, not the witless.’

an8.30:20.5.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

an8.30:21.1.verse: ‘This teaching is for those who don’t enjoy proliferating and don’t like to proliferate, not for those who enjoy proliferating and like to proliferate.’

an8.30:21.2.verse: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

an8.30:21.3.verse: It’s for a mendicant whose mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided regarding the cessation of proliferation.

an8.30:21.4.verse: ‘This teaching is for those who don’t enjoy proliferating and don’t like to proliferate, not for those who enjoy proliferating and like to proliferate.’

an8.30:21.5.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”

an8.30:22.1.verse: Then Anuruddha stayed the next rainy season residence right there in the land of the Cetīs in the Park of the East-Raftered Hall.

an8.30:22.2.verse: And Anuruddha, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

an8.30:22.3.verse: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

an8.30:22.4.verse: And Venerable Anuruddha became one of the perfected.

an8.30:22.5.verse: And on the occasion of attaining perfection he recited these verses:

an8.30:23.2.verse: the supreme Teacher in the world

an8.30:23.3.verse: came to me in a mind-made body,

an8.30:25.4.verse: and have fulfilled the Buddha’s instructions.”

an8.31:1.3.verse: Someone might give a gift after insulting the recipient.

an8.31:1.4.verse: Or they give out of fear.

an8.31:1.5.verse: Or they give thinking, ‘They gave to me.’

an8.31:1.6.verse: Or they give thinking, ‘They’ll give to me.’

an8.31:1.7.verse: Or they give thinking, ‘It’s good to give.’

an8.31:1.8.verse: Or they give thinking, ‘I cook, they don’t. It wouldn’t be right for me to not give to them.’

an8.31:1.9.verse: Or they give thinking, ‘By giving this gift I’ll get a good reputation.’

an8.31:1.10.verse: Or they give thinking, ‘This is an adornment and requisite for the mind.’

an8.32:1.3.verse: For this, they say, is the path of the gods,

an8.32:1.4.verse: which leads to the heavenly realm.”

an8.33:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these eight grounds for giving.

an8.33:1.3.verse: Someone might give a gift out of favoritism or hostility or stupidity or cowardice. Or they give thinking, ‘Giving was practiced by my father and my father’s father. It would not be right for me to abandon this traditional family custom.’ Or they give thinking, ‘After I’ve given this gift, when my body breaks up, after death, I’ll be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’ Or they give thinking, ‘When giving this gift my mind becomes clear, and I become happy and joyful.’ Or they give a gift thinking, ‘This is an adornment and requisite for the mind.’

an8.33:1.4.verse: These are the eight grounds for giving.”

an8.34:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when a field has eight factors a seed sown in it is not very fruitful or rewarding or productive.

an8.34:1.2.verse: What eight factors does it have?

an8.34:1.3.verse: It’s when a field has mounds and ditches. It has stones and gravel. It’s salty. It doesn’t have deep furrows. And it’s not equipped with water inlets, water outlets, irrigation channels, and boundaries.

an8.34:1.4.verse: When a field has these eight factors a seed sown in it is not fruitful or rewarding or productive.

an8.34:2.1.verse: In the same way, when an ascetic or brahmin has eight factors a gift given to them is not very fruitful or beneficial or brilliant or bountiful.

an8.34:2.2.verse: What eight factors do they have?

an8.34:2.3.verse: It’s when an ascetic or brahmin has wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

an8.34:2.4.verse: When an ascetic or brahmin has these eight factors a gift given to them is not very fruitful or beneficial or brilliant or bountiful.

an8.34:3.1.verse: When a field has eight factors a seed sown in it is very fruitful and rewarding and productive.

an8.34:3.2.verse: What eight factors does it have?

an8.34:3.3.verse: It’s when a field doesn’t have mounds and ditches. It doesn’t have stones and gravel. It’s not salty. It has deep furrows. And it’s equipped with water inlets, water outlets, irrigation channels, and boundaries.

an8.34:3.4.verse: When a field has these eight factors a seed sown in it is very fruitful and rewarding and productive.

an8.34:4.1.verse: In the same way, when an ascetic or brahmin has eight factors a gift given to them is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.

an8.34:4.2.verse: What eight factors do they have?

an8.34:4.3.verse: It’s when an ascetic or brahmin has right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

an8.34:4.4.verse: When an ascetic or brahmin has these eight factors a gift given to them is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.

an8.34:5.2.verse: and the seed sown in it is excellent,

an8.34:5.4.verse: the crop of grain will be excellent.

an8.34:6.1.verse: The absence of crop loss is excellent,

an8.34:7.1.verse: So too, when you give excellent food

an8.34:7.4.verse: for what you did was excellent.

an8.34:8.1.verse: So if a person wants excellence,

an8.34:8.3.verse: You should frequent those with excellent wisdom,

an8.34:8.4.verse: so that your own excellence will flourish.

an8.34:10.2.verse: and having attained excellence of view,

an8.34:10.3.verse: one who excels in mind proceeds,

an8.34:10.4.verse: relying on excellence in the path.

an8.34:11.2.verse: and attaining the excellence of extinguishment,

an8.35:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these eight rebirths by giving.

an8.35:1.3.verse: First, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

an8.35:1.4.verse: Whatever they give they expect back.

an8.35:1.5.verse: They see a well-to-do aristocrat or brahmin or householder amusing themselves, supplied and provided with the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

an8.35:1.7.verse: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of well-to-do aristocrats or brahmins or householders!’

an8.35:1.8.verse: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it.

an8.35:1.9.verse: As they’ve settled for less and not developed further, their thought leads to rebirth there.

an8.35:1.10.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of well-to-do aristocrats or brahmins or householders.

an8.35:1.11.verse: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.

an8.35:1.12.verse: The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their purity.

an8.35:2.1.verse: Next, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins …

an8.35:2.2.verse: Whatever they give they expect back.

an8.35:2.4.verse: ‘The gods of the four great kings are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

an8.35:2.6.verse: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods of the four great kings!’ …

an8.35:2.9.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the four great kings.

an8.35:2.10.verse: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.

an8.35:2.11.verse: The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their purity.

an8.35:3.1.verse: Next, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins …

an8.35:3.2.verse: Whatever they give they expect back.

an8.35:3.8.verse: ‘The gods who control what is created by others are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

an8.35:3.10.verse: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods who control what is created by others!’

an8.35:3.11.verse: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it.

an8.35:3.12.verse: As they’ve settled for less and not developed further, their thought leads to rebirth there.

an8.35:3.13.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods who control what is created by others.

an8.35:3.14.verse: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.

an8.35:3.15.verse: The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their purity.

an8.35:4.1.verse: Next, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

an8.35:4.2.verse: Whatever they give they expect back.

an8.35:4.4.verse: ‘The gods of the Divinity’s host are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

an8.35:4.6.verse: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods of the Divinity’s host!’

an8.35:4.7.verse: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it.

an8.35:4.8.verse: As they’ve settled for less and not developed further, their thought leads to rebirth there.

an8.35:4.9.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the Divinity’s host.

an8.35:4.10.verse: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.

an8.35:4.11.verse: And for those free of desire, not those with desire.

an8.35:4.12.verse: The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their freedom from desire.

an8.35:4.13.verse: These are the eight rebirths by giving.”

an8.36:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these three grounds for making merit.

an8.36:1.3.verse: Giving, ethical conduct, and meditation are all grounds for making merit.

an8.36:2.1.verse: First, someone has practiced a little giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit, but they haven’t got as far as meditation as a ground for making merit.

an8.36:2.2.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn among disadvantaged humans.

an8.36:3.1.verse: Next, someone has practiced a moderate amount of giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit, but they haven’t got as far as meditation as a ground for making merit.

an8.36:3.2.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn among well-off humans.

an8.36:4.1.verse: Next, someone has practiced to an extraordinary degree giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit, but they haven’t got as far as meditation as a ground for making merit.

an8.36:4.2.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the four great kings.

an8.36:4.3.verse: There, the four great kings themselves have practiced giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit to a greater degree than the other gods. So they surpass them in ten respects:

an8.36:4.4.verse: heavenly lifespan, beauty, happiness, glory, sovereignty, sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

an8.36:5.1.verse: Next, someone has practiced to an extraordinary degree giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit, but they haven’t got as far as meditation as a ground for making merit.

an8.36:5.2.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the thirty-three.

an8.36:5.3.verse: There, Sakka, lord of gods, has practiced giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit to a greater degree than the other gods. So he surpasses them in ten respects …

an8.36:6.1.verse: Next, someone has practiced to an extraordinary degree giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit, but they haven’t got as far as meditation as a ground for making merit.

an8.36:6.2.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of Yama.

an8.36:6.3.verse: There, the godling Suyāma has practiced giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit to a greater degree than the other gods. So he surpasses them in ten respects …

an8.36:7.1.verse: Next, someone has practiced to an extraordinary degree giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit, but they haven’t got as far as meditation as a ground for making merit.

an8.36:7.2.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the joyful gods.

an8.36:7.3.verse: There, the godling Santusita has practiced giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit to a greater degree than the other gods. So he surpasses them in ten respects …

an8.36:8.1.verse: Next, someone has practiced to an extraordinary degree giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit, but they haven’t got as far as meditation as a ground for making merit.

an8.36:8.2.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods who love to create.

an8.36:8.3.verse: There, the godling Sunimmita has practiced giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit to a greater degree than the other gods. So he surpasses them in ten respects …

an8.36:9.1.verse: Next, someone has practiced to an extraordinary degree giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit, but they haven’t got as far as meditation as a ground for making merit.

an8.36:9.2.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods who control what is created by others.

an8.36:9.3.verse: There, the godling Vasavattī has practiced giving and ethical conduct as grounds for making merit to a greater degree than the other gods. So he surpasses them in ten respects:

an8.36:9.4.verse: heavenly lifespan, beauty, happiness, glory, sovereignty, sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

an8.36:9.5.verse: These are the three grounds for making merit.”

an8.37:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these eight gifts of a true person.

an8.37:1.3.verse: Their gift is pure, good quality, timely, appropriate, intelligent, and regular. While giving their heart is confident, and afterwards they’re uplifted.

an8.37:1.4.verse: These are the eight gifts of a true person.

an8.37:2.1.verse: He gives pure, good quality, and timely gifts

an8.37:2.4.verse: who are fertile fields of merit.

an8.37:3.2.verse: giving away many things of the flesh.

an8.37:4.1.verse: An intelligent person sacrifices like this,

an8.37:4.2.verse: faithful, with a mind of letting go.

an8.37:4.3.verse: Such an astute person is reborn

an8.38:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a true person is born in a family for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the people.

an8.38:1.2.verse: For the benefit, welfare, and happiness of mother and father; children and partners; bondservants, workers, and staff; friends and colleagues; departed ancestors; the king; the deities; and ascetics and brahmins.

an8.38:2.1.verse: It’s like a great rain cloud, which nourishes all the crops for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the people.

an8.38:2.2.verse: In the same way, a true person is born in a family for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the people. …

an8.38:3.1.verse: A wise person living at home

an8.38:3.3.verse: Neither by day or at night do they neglect

an8.38:4.1.verse: They venerate them in accord with the teaching,

an8.38:4.3.verse: One of settled faith and good nature

an8.38:5.3.verse: Good for the king, good for the gods,

an8.38:5.4.verse: and good for relatives and comrades.

an8.38:6.1.verse: In fact, they’re good for everyone,

an8.38:6.2.verse: well grounded in the true teaching.

an8.38:6.3.verse: Rid of the stain of stinginess,

an8.38:6.4.verse: they’ll enjoy a world of grace.”

an8.39:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these eight kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness. They nurture happiness and are conducive to heaven, ripening in happiness and leading to heaven. They lead to what is likable, desirable, agreeable, to welfare and happiness.

an8.39:1.3.verse: Firstly, a noble disciple has gone for refuge to the Buddha.

an8.39:1.4.verse: This is the first kind of overflowing merit …

an8.39:2.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple has gone for refuge to the teaching.

an8.39:2.2.verse: This is the second kind of overflowing merit …

an8.39:3.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple has gone for refuge to the Saṅgha.

an8.39:3.2.verse: This is the third kind of overflowing merit …

an8.39:3.3.verse: Mendicants, these five gifts are great, primordial, long-standing, customary, and traditional. They are uncorrupted, as they have been since the beginning. They’re not being corrupted now nor will they be. Sensible ascetics and brahmins don’t look down on them.

an8.39:3.5.verse: Firstly, a noble disciple gives up killing living creatures.

an8.39:3.6.verse: By so doing they give to countless sentient beings the gift of freedom from fear, enmity, and ill will.

an8.39:3.7.verse: And they themselves also enjoy unlimited freedom from fear, enmity, and ill will.

an8.39:3.8.verse: This is the first gift that is a great offering, primordial, long-standing, customary, and traditional. It is uncorrupted, as it has been since the beginning. It’s not being corrupted now nor will it be. Sensible ascetics and brahmins don’t look down on it.

an8.39:3.9.verse: This is the fourth kind of overflowing merit …

an8.39:4.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple gives up stealing. …

an8.39:4.2.verse: This is the fifth kind of overflowing merit …

an8.39:5.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple gives up sexual misconduct. …

an8.39:5.2.verse: This is the sixth kind of overflowing merit …

an8.39:6.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple gives up lying. …

an8.39:6.2.verse: This is the seventh kind of overflowing merit …

an8.39:7.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple gives up intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

an8.39:7.2.verse: By so doing they give to countless sentient beings the gift of freedom from fear, enmity, and ill will.

an8.39:7.3.verse: And they themselves also enjoy unlimited freedom from fear, enmity, and ill will.

an8.39:7.4.verse: This is the fifth gift that is a great offering, primordial, long-standing, customary, and traditional. It is uncorrupted, as it has been since the beginning. It’s not being corrupted now nor will it be. Sensible ascetics and brahmins don’t look down on it.

an8.39:7.5.verse: This is the eighth kind of overflowing merit …

an8.39:8.1.verse: These are the eight kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness. They nurture happiness and are conducive to heaven, ripening in happiness and leading to heaven. They lead to what is likable, desirable, agreeable, to welfare and happiness.”

an8.40:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, the killing of living creatures, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

an8.40:1.2.verse: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is a short lifespan.

an8.40:2.1.verse: Stealing, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

an8.40:2.2.verse: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is loss of wealth.

an8.40:3.1.verse: Sexual misconduct, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

an8.40:3.2.verse: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is rivalry and enmity.

an8.40:4.1.verse: Lying, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

an8.40:4.2.verse: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is false accusations.

an8.40:5.1.verse: Backbiting, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

an8.40:5.2.verse: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is being divided against friends.

an8.40:6.1.verse: Harsh speech, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

an8.40:6.2.verse: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is hearing disagreeable things.

an8.40:7.1.verse: Talking nonsense, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

an8.40:7.2.verse: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is that no one takes what you say seriously.

an8.40:8.1.verse: Drinking beer and wine, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

an8.40:8.2.verse: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is madness.”

an8.41:0.3.verse: The Sabbath With Eight Factors, In Brief

an8.41:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

an8.41:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

an8.41:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, the observance of the sabbath with its eight factors is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.

an8.41:2.2.verse: And how should it be observed?

an8.41:2.3.verse: It’s when a noble disciple reflects:

an8.41:2.4.verse: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They are scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

an8.41:2.5.verse: I, too, for this day and night will give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. I’ll be scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

an8.41:2.6.verse: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’

an8.41:3.1.verse: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up stealing. They take only what’s given, and expect only what’s given. They keep themselves clean by not thieving.

an8.41:3.2.verse: I, too, for this day and night will give up stealing. I’ll take only what’s given, and expect only what’s given. I’ll keep myself clean by not thieving.

an8.41:3.3.verse: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’

an8.41:4.1.verse: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up unchastity. They are chaste, set apart, refraining from the vulgar act of sex.

an8.41:4.2.verse: I, too, for this day and night will give up unchastity. I will be chaste, set apart, refraining from the vulgar act of sex.

an8.41:4.3.verse: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’

an8.41:5.1.verse: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up lying. They speak the truth and stick to the truth. They’re honest and dependable, and don’t trick the world with their words.

an8.41:5.2.verse: I, too, for this day and night will give up lying. I’ll speak the truth and stick to the truth. I’ll be honest and dependable, and won’t trick the world with my words.

an8.41:5.3.verse: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’

an8.41:6.1.verse: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

an8.41:6.2.verse: I, too, for this day and night will give up intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

an8.41:6.3.verse: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’

an8.41:7.1.verse: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones eat in one part of the day, abstaining from eating at night and from food at the wrong time.

an8.41:7.2.verse: I, too, for this day and night will eat in one part of the day, abstaining from eating at night and food at the wrong time.

an8.41:7.3.verse: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’

an8.41:8.1.verse: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up seeing shows of dancing, singing, and music; and attiring and adorning themselves with garlands, fragrance, and makeup.

an8.41:8.2.verse: I, too, for this day and night will give up seeing shows of dancing, singing, and music; and attiring and adorning myself with garlands, fragrance, and makeup.

an8.41:8.3.verse: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’

an8.41:9.1.verse: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up high and luxurious beds. They sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

an8.41:9.2.verse: I, too, for this day and night will give up high and luxurious beds. I’ll sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

an8.41:9.3.verse: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’

an8.41:10.1.verse: The observance of the sabbath with its eight factors in this way is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.”

an8.42:0.3.verse: The Sabbath With Eight Factors, In Detail

an8.42:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, the observance of the sabbath with its eight factors is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.

an8.42:1.2.verse: And how should it be observed?

an8.42:1.3.verse: It’s when a noble disciple reflects:

an8.42:1.4.verse: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They are scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

an8.42:1.5.verse: I, too, for this day and night will give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. I’ll be scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

an8.42:1.6.verse: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’

an8.42:2.1.verse: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up high and luxurious beds. They sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

an8.42:2.2.verse: I, too, for this day and night will give up high and luxurious beds. I’ll sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

an8.42:2.3.verse: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’

an8.42:2.5.verse: The observance of the sabbath with its eight factors in this way is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.

an8.42:3.2.verse: Suppose you were to rule as sovereign lord over these sixteen great countries—Aṅga, Magadha, Kāsi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Cetī, Vaccha, Kuru, Pañcāla, Maccha, Sūrasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhāra, and Kamboja—full of the seven treasures.

an8.42:3.3.verse: This wouldn’t be worth a sixteenth part of the sabbath with its eight factors.

an8.42:3.5.verse: Because human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.

an8.42:4.1.verse: Fifty years in the human realm is one day and night for the gods of the four great kings.

an8.42:4.2.verse: Thirty such days make up a month.

an8.42:4.3.verse: Twelve such months make up a year.

an8.42:4.4.verse: The lifespan of the gods of the four great kings is five hundred of these heavenly years.

an8.42:4.5.verse: It’s possible that some woman or man who has observed the eight-factored sabbath will—when their body breaks up, after death—be reborn in the company of the gods of the four great kings.

an8.42:4.6.verse: This is what I was referring to when I said:

an8.42:4.7.verse: ‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’

an8.44:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

an8.44:1.2.verse: Then the layman Vāseṭṭha went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

an8.44:1.3.verse: “Vāseṭṭha, the observance of the sabbath with its eight factors is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful …

an8.44:1.4.verse: blameless, they go to a heavenly place.”

an8.44:2.1.verse: When he said this, Vāseṭṭha said to the Buddha:

an8.44:2.2.verse: “If my loved ones—relatives and kin—were to observe this sabbath with its eight factors, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.

an8.44:2.3.verse: If all the aristocrats, brahmins, peasants, and menials were to observe this sabbath with its eight factors, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.”

an8.44:3.1.verse: “That’s so true, Vāseṭṭha! That’s so true, Vāseṭṭha!

an8.44:3.2.verse: If all the aristocrats, brahmins, peasants, and menials were to observe this sabbath with its eight factors, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.

an8.44:3.3.verse: If the whole world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—were to observe this sabbath with its eight factors, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.

an8.44:3.4.verse: If these great sal trees were to observe this sabbath with its eight factors, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness—if they were sentient.

an8.44:3.5.verse: How much more then a human being!”

an8.46:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

an8.46:1.2.verse: Now at that time Venerable Anuruddha had gone into retreat for the day’s meditation.

an8.46:1.3.verse: Then several deities of the Agreeable Host went up to Venerable Anuruddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:

an8.46:1.4.verse: “Honorable Anuruddha, we are the deities called ‘Agreeable’. We wield authority and control over three things.

an8.46:1.5.verse: We can turn any color we want on the spot.

an8.46:1.6.verse: We can get any voice that we want on the spot.

an8.46:1.7.verse: We can get any pleasure that we want on the spot.

an8.46:1.8.verse: We are the deities called ‘Agreeable’. We wield authority and control over these three things.”

an8.46:2.2.verse: “If only these deities would all turn blue, of blue color, clad in blue, adorned with blue!”

an8.46:2.3.verse: Then those deities, knowing Anuruddha’s thought, all turned blue.

an8.46:3.2.verse: “If only these deities would all turn yellow …”

an8.46:3.3.verse: “If only these gods would all turn red …”

an8.46:3.4.verse: “If only these gods would all turn white …”

an8.46:3.5.verse: Then those deities, knowing Anuruddha’s thought, all turned white.

an8.46:4.1.verse: Then one of those deities sang, one danced, and one snapped her fingers.

an8.46:4.2.verse: Suppose there was a quintet made up of skilled musicians who had practiced well and kept excellent rhythm. They’d sound graceful, tantalizing, sensuous, endearing, and intoxicating.

an8.46:4.3.verse: In the same way the performance by those deities sounded graceful, tantalizing, sensuous, endearing, and intoxicating.

an8.46:4.4.verse: But Venerable Anuruddha averted his senses.

an8.46:5.1.verse: Then those deities, thinking “Master Anuruddha isn’t enjoying this,” vanished right there.

an8.46:5.2.verse: Then in the late afternoon, Anuruddha came out of retreat and went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened, adding:

an8.46:9.2.verse: “How many qualities do ladies have so that—when their body breaks up, after death—they are reborn in company with the Gods of the Agreeable Host?”

an8.46:10.1.verse: “Anuruddha, when they have eight qualities ladies—when their body breaks up, after death—are reborn in company with the Gods of the Agreeable Host.

an8.46:10.3.verse: Take the case of a lady whose mother and father give her to a husband wanting what’s best for her, out of kindness and sympathy. She would get up before him and go to bed after him, and be obliging, behaving nicely and speaking politely.

an8.46:11.1.verse: She honors, respects, esteems, and venerates those her husband respects, such as

an8.46:11.2.verse: mother and father, and ascetics and brahmins.

an8.46:11.3.verse: And when they arrive she serves them with a seat and water.

an8.46:12.1.verse: She’s deft and tireless in her husband’s household duties, such as knitting and sewing. She understands how to go about things in order to complete and organize the work.

an8.46:13.1.verse: She knows what work her husband’s domestic bondservants, servants, and workers have completed, and what they’ve left incomplete.

an8.46:13.2.verse: She knows who is sick, and who is fit or unwell. She distributes to each a fair portion of fresh and cooked foods.

an8.46:14.1.verse: She ensures that any income her husband earns is guarded and protected, whether money, grain, silver, or gold. She doesn’t overspend, steal, waste, or lose it.

an8.46:15.1.verse: She’s a lay follower who has gone for refuge to the Buddha, his teaching, and the Saṅgha.

an8.46:16.2.verse: She doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

an8.46:17.2.verse: She lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

an8.46:18.1.verse: When they possess these eight qualities ladies—when their body breaks up, after death—are reborn in company with the Gods of the Agreeable Host.

an8.46:19.1.verse: She’d never look down on her husband,

an8.46:19.2.verse: who’s always eager to work hard,

an8.46:20.1.verse: And a good woman never scolds her husband

an8.46:21.1.verse: She gets up early, works tirelessly,

an8.46:22.1.verse: A lady who fulfills these duties

an8.48:2.3.verse: Take the case of a lady whose mother and father give her to a husband wanting what’s best for her, out of kindness and sympathy. She would get up before him and go to bed after him, and be obliging, behaving nicely and speaking politely.

an8.48:3.2.verse: mother and father, and ascetics and brahmins.

an8.48:3.3.verse: And when they arrive she serves them with a seat and water.

an8.48:4.1.verse: She’s deft and tireless in her husband’s household duties, such as knitting and sewing. She understands how to go about things in order to complete and organize the work.

an8.48:5.1.verse: She knows what work her husband’s domestic bondservants, servants, and workers have completed, and what they’ve left incomplete.

an8.48:5.2.verse: She knows who is sick, and who is fit or unwell. She distributes to each a fair portion of fresh and cooked foods.

an8.48:6.1.verse: She ensures that any income her husband earns is guarded and protected, whether money, grain, silver, or gold. She doesn’t overspend, steal, waste, or lose it.

an8.48:7.1.verse: She’s a lay follower who has gone for refuge to the Buddha, his teaching, and the Saṅgha.

an8.48:8.2.verse: She doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

an8.48:9.1.verse: She’s generous. She lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

an8.48:10.1.verse: When they possess these eight qualities ladies—when their body breaks up, after death—are reborn in company with the Gods of the Agreeable Host.

an8.48:11.1.verse: She’d never look down on her husband,

an8.48:11.2.verse: who’s always eager to work hard,

an8.48:12.1.verse: And a good woman never scolds her husband

an8.48:13.1.verse: She gets up early, works tirelessly,

an8.48:14.1.verse: A lady who fulfills these duties

an8.49:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

an8.49:1.2.verse: Then Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side.

an8.49:2.1.verse: “Visākhā, a lady who has four qualities is practicing to win in this life, and she succeeds at it.

an8.49:2.3.verse: It’s when a lady is well-organized at work, manages the domestic help, acts lovingly toward her husband, and preserves his earnings.

an8.49:3.1.verse: And how is a lady well-organized at work?

an8.49:3.2.verse: It’s when she’s deft and tireless in doing domestic duties for her husband, such as knitting and sewing. She understands how to go about things in order to complete and organize the work.

an8.49:3.3.verse: That’s how a lady is well-organized at work.

an8.49:4.1.verse: And how does a lady manage the domestic help?

an8.49:4.2.verse: It’s when she knows what work her husband’s domestic bondservants, servants, and workers have completed, and what they’ve left incomplete.

an8.49:4.3.verse: She knows who is sick, and who is fit or unwell. She distributes to each a fair portion of fresh and cooked foods.

an8.49:4.4.verse: That’s how a lady manages the domestic help.

an8.49:5.1.verse: And how does a lady act lovingly toward her husband?

an8.49:5.2.verse: It’s when a lady would not transgress in any way that her husband would not consider agreeable, even for the sake of her own life.

an8.49:5.3.verse: That’s how a lady acts lovingly toward her husband.

an8.49:6.1.verse: And how does a lady preserve his earnings?

an8.49:6.2.verse: It’s when she ensures that any income her husband earns is guarded and protected, whether money, grain, silver, or gold. She doesn’t overspend, steal, waste, or lose it.

an8.49:6.3.verse: That’s how a lady preserves his earnings.

an8.49:6.4.verse: A lady who possesses these four qualities is practicing to win in this life, and she succeeds at it.

an8.49:7.1.verse: A lady who has four qualities is practicing to win in the next life, and she succeeds at it.

an8.49:7.3.verse: It’s when a lady is accomplished in faith, ethics, generosity, and wisdom.

an8.49:8.1.verse: And how is a lady accomplished in faith?

an8.49:8.2.verse: It’s when a lady has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

an8.49:8.3.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

an8.49:8.4.verse: That’s how a lady is accomplished in faith.

an8.49:9.1.verse: And how is a lady accomplished in ethics?

an8.49:9.2.verse: It’s when a lady doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

an8.49:9.3.verse: That’s how a lady is accomplished in ethics.

an8.49:10.1.verse: And how is a lady accomplished in generosity?

an8.49:10.2.verse: It’s when she lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

an8.49:10.3.verse: That’s how a lady is accomplished in generosity.

an8.49:11.1.verse: And how is a lady accomplished in wisdom?

an8.49:11.2.verse: It’s when a lady is wise. She has the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

an8.49:11.3.verse: That’s how a lady is accomplished in wisdom.

an8.49:12.1.verse: A lady who possesses these four qualities is practicing to win in the next life, and she succeeds at it.

an8.49:15.1.verse: And so, a lady in whom

an8.49:16.3.verse: a virtuous laywoman such as she

an8.49:16.4.verse: is reborn in the realm of the Agreeable Gods.”

an8.51:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

an8.51:1.2.verse: Then Mahāpajāpati Gotamī went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:

an8.51:1.3.verse: “Sir, please let ladies gain the going forth from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

an8.51:1.5.verse: Don’t endorse the going forth for ladies from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

an8.51:3.1.verse: For a third time, Mahāpajāpati Gotamī said to the Buddha:

an8.51:3.2.verse: “Sir, please let ladies gain the going forth from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

an8.51:3.4.verse: Don’t endorse the going forth for ladies from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

an8.51:4.1.verse: Then Mahāpajāpati Gotamī thought, “The Buddha does not permit ladies to go forth.” Miserable and sad, weeping, with a tearful face, she bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on her right, before leaving.

an8.51:5.1.verse: When the Buddha had stayed in Kapilavatthu as long as he pleased, he set out for Vesālī.

an8.51:5.2.verse: Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Vesālī,

an8.51:5.3.verse: where he stayed at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

an8.51:5.4.verse: Then Mahāpajāpati Gotamī had her hair shaved, and dressed in ocher robes. Together with several Sakyan ladies she set out for Vesālī.

an8.51:5.5.verse: Traveling stage by stage, she arrived at Vesālī and went to the Great Wood, the hall with the peaked roof.

an8.51:5.6.verse: Then Mahāpajāpati Gotamī stood crying outside the gate, her feet swollen, her limbs covered with dust, miserable and sad, with tearful face.

an8.51:6.1.verse: Venerable Ānanda saw her standing there,

an8.51:6.3.verse: “Gotamī, why do you stand crying outside the gate, your feet swollen, your limbs covered with dust, miserable and sad, with tearful face?”

an8.51:6.4.verse: “Honorable Ānanda, it’s because the Buddha does not permit ladies to go forth in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

an8.51:6.5.verse: “Well then, Gotamī, wait here an hour while I ask the Buddha to grant the going forth for ladies.”

an8.51:7.1.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

an8.51:7.2.verse: “Sir, Mahāpajāpati Gotamī is standing crying outside the gate, her feet swollen, her limbs covered with dust, miserable and sad, with tearful face.

an8.51:7.3.verse: She says that it’s because the Buddha does not permit ladies to go forth.

an8.51:7.4.verse: Sir, please let ladies gain the going forth from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

an8.51:7.6.verse: Don’t endorse the going forth for ladies from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

an8.51:8.2.verse: For a third time, Ānanda said to the Buddha:

an8.51:8.3.verse: “Sir, please let ladies gain the going forth from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

an8.51:8.5.verse: Don’t endorse the going forth for ladies from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

an8.51:9.2.verse: “The Buddha does not permit ladies to go forth.

an8.51:9.3.verse: Why don’t I try another approach?”

an8.51:9.4.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha,

an8.51:9.5.verse: “Sir, is a lady able to realize the fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection once she has gone forth?”

an8.51:9.7.verse: “If a lady is able to realize the fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection once she has gone forth.

an8.51:9.8.verse: Sir, Mahāpajāpati has been very helpful to the Buddha. As his aunt, she raised him, nurtured him, and gave him her milk.

an8.51:9.9.verse: When the Buddha’s birth mother passed away, she nurtured him at her own breast.

an8.51:9.10.verse: Sir, please let ladies gain the going forth from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

an8.51:10.1.verse: “Ānanda, if Mahāpajāpati Gotamī accepts these eight principles of respect, that will be her ordination.

an8.51:11.1.verse: A nun, even if she has been ordained for a hundred years, should bow down to a monk who was ordained that very day. She should rise up for him, greet him with cupped palms, and observe proper etiquette toward him.

an8.51:11.2.verse: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

an8.51:12.1.verse: A nun should not commence the rainy season residence in a monastery without monks.

an8.51:12.2.verse: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

an8.51:13.1.verse: Each fortnight the nuns should expect two things from the community of monks:

an8.51:13.2.verse: the date of the sabbath, and visiting for advice.

an8.51:13.3.verse: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

an8.51:14.1.verse: After completing the rainy season residence the nuns should invite admonition from the communities of both monks and nuns in regard to anything that was

an8.51:14.3.verse: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

an8.51:15.1.verse: A nun who has committed a grave offense should undergo penance in the communities of both monks and nuns for a fortnight.

an8.51:15.2.verse: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

an8.51:16.1.verse: A trainee nun who has trained in the six rules for two years should seek ordination from the communities of both monks and nuns.

an8.51:16.2.verse: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

an8.51:17.1.verse: A nun should not abuse or insult a monk in any way.

an8.51:17.2.verse: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

an8.51:18.1.verse: From this day forth it is forbidden for nuns to criticize monks, but it is not forbidden for monks to criticize nuns.

an8.51:18.2.verse: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

an8.51:19.1.verse: If Mahāpajāpati Gotamī accepts these eight principles of respect, that will be her ordination.”

an8.51:20.1.verse: Then Ānanda, having learned these eight principles of respect from the Buddha himself, went to Mahāpajāpati Gotamī and said:

an8.51:21.1.verse: “Gotamī, if you accept eight principles of respect, that will be your ordination.

an8.51:22.1.verse: A nun, even if she has been ordained for a hundred years, should bow down to a monk who was ordained that very day. She should rise up for him, greet him with cupped palms, and observe proper etiquette toward him.

an8.51:22.2.verse: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts. …

an8.51:23.1.verse: From this day forth it is forbidden for nuns to criticize monks, but it is not forbidden for monks to criticize nuns.

an8.51:23.2.verse: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

an8.51:23.3.verse: If you accept these eight principles of respect, that will be your ordination.”

an8.51:24.1.verse: “Ānanda, suppose there was a woman or man who was young, youthful, and fond of adornments, and had bathed their head. After getting a garland of lotuses, jasmine, or liana flowers, they would take them in both hands and place them on the crown of the head.

an8.51:24.2.verse: In the same way, sir, I accept these eight principles of respect as not to be transgressed so long as life lasts.”

an8.51:25.1.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

an8.51:25.2.verse: “Sir, Mahāpajāpati Gotamī has accepted the eight principles of respect as not to be transgressed so long as life lasts.”

an8.51:26.1.verse: “Ānanda, if ladies had not gained the going forth from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One, the spiritual life would have lasted long. The true teaching would have remained for a thousand years.

an8.51:26.2.verse: But since they have gained the going forth, now the spiritual life will not last long.

an8.51:26.3.verse: The true teaching will remain only five hundred years.

an8.51:27.1.verse: It’s like those families with many women and few men. They’re easy prey for bandits and grain-jar thieves.

an8.51:27.2.verse: In the same way, the spiritual life does not last long in a teaching and training where ladies gain the going forth.

an8.51:28.1.verse: It’s like a field full of rice. Once the disease called ‘white bones’ attacks, it doesn’t last long.

an8.51:28.2.verse: In the same way, the spiritual life does not last long in a teaching and training where ladies gain the going forth.

an8.51:29.1.verse: It’s like a field full of sugarcane. Once the disease called ‘red rot’ attacks, it doesn’t last long.

an8.51:29.2.verse: In the same way, the spiritual life does not last long in a teaching and training where ladies gain the going forth.

an8.51:30.1.verse: As a man might build a dyke around a large lake as a precaution against the water overflowing,

an8.51:30.2.verse: in the same way as a precaution I’ve prescribed the eight principles of respect as not to be transgressed so long as life lasts.”

an8.52:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

an8.52:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

an8.52:1.3.verse: “Sir, how many qualities should a monk have to be deemed an adviser for nuns?”

an8.52:2.1.verse: “Ānanda, a monk with eight qualities may be deemed an adviser for nuns.

an8.52:2.3.verse: Firstly, a monk is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

an8.52:2.4.verse: They’re learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s totally full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, reciting them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

an8.52:2.5.verse: Both monastic codes have been passed down to them in detail, well analyzed, well mastered, well evaluated in both the rules and accompanying material.

an8.52:2.6.verse: They’re a good speaker who enunciates well. Their voice is polished, clear, articulate, and expresses the meaning.

an8.52:2.7.verse: They’re able to educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire the community of nuns.

an8.52:2.8.verse: They’re liked and agreeable to most of the nuns.

an8.52:2.9.verse: They have never previously sexually harassed any woman wearing the ocher robe who has gone forth in the Buddha’s name.

an8.52:2.10.verse: They have been ordained for twenty years or more.

an8.52:2.11.verse: A monk with these eight qualities may be deemed an adviser for nuns.”
