an10.99:17.1.verse: They give up talking nonsense. Their words are timely, true, and meaningful, in line with the teaching and training. They say things at the right time which are valuable, reasonable, succinct, and beneficial.

an10.99:18.1.verse: They refrain from injuring plants and seeds.

an10.99:18.2.verse: They eat in one part of the day, abstaining from eating at night and food at the wrong time.

an10.99:18.3.verse: They refrain from seeing shows of dancing, singing, and music.

an10.99:18.4.verse: They refrain from attiring and adorning themselves with garlands, fragrance, and makeup.

an10.99:18.5.verse: They refrain from high and luxurious beds.

an10.99:18.6.verse: They refrain from receiving gold and currency,

an10.99:18.15.verse: They refrain from running errands and messages;

an10.99:18.19.verse: mutilation, murder, abduction, banditry, plunder, and violence.

an10.99:19.1.verse: They’re content with robes to look after the body and almsfood to look after the belly.

an10.99:19.2.verse: Wherever they go, they set out taking only these things.

an10.99:19.3.verse: They’re like a bird: wherever it flies, wings are its only burden.

an10.99:19.4.verse: In the same way, a mendicant is content with robes to look after the body and almsfood to look after the belly. Wherever they go, they set out taking only these things.

an10.99:19.5.verse: When they have this spectrum of noble ethics, they experience a blameless happiness inside themselves.

an10.99:20.1.verse: When they see a sight with their eyes, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

an10.99:20.2.verse: If the faculty of sight were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of sight, and achieving its restraint.

an10.99:20.3.verse: When they hear a sound with their ears …

an10.99:20.4.verse: When they smell an odor with their nose …

an10.99:20.5.verse: When they taste a flavor with their tongue …

an10.99:20.6.verse: When they feel a touch with their body …

an10.99:20.7.verse: When they know an idea with their mind, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

an10.99:20.8.verse: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of mind, and achieving its restraint.

an10.99:20.9.verse: When they have this noble sense restraint, they experience an unsullied bliss inside themselves.

an10.99:21.1.verse: They act with situational awareness when going out and coming back; when looking ahead and aside; when bending and extending the limbs; when bearing the outer robe, bowl and robes; when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; when urinating and defecating; when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and keeping silent.

an10.99:22.1.verse: When they have this spectrum of noble ethics, this noble sense restraint, and this noble mindfulness and situational awareness,

an10.99:22.2.verse: they frequent a secluded lodging—a wilderness, the root of a tree, a hill, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a forest, the open air, a heap of straw.

an10.99:22.3.verse: Gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, they sit down cross-legged, set their body straight, and bring mindfulness to the present.

an10.99:23.1.verse: Giving up covetousness for the world, they meditate with a heart rid of covetousness, cleansing the mind of covetousness.

an10.99:23.2.verse: Giving up ill will and malevolence, they meditate with a mind rid of ill will, full of sympathy for all living beings, cleansing the mind of ill will.

an10.99:23.3.verse: Giving up dullness and drowsiness, they meditate with a mind rid of dullness and drowsiness, perceiving light, mindful and aware, cleansing the mind of dullness and drowsiness.

an10.99:23.4.verse: Giving up restlessness and remorse, they meditate without restlessness, their mind settled internally, cleansing the mind of restlessness and remorse.

an10.99:23.5.verse: Giving up doubt, they meditate having gone beyond doubt, not undecided about skillful qualities, cleansing the mind of doubt.

an10.99:24.1.verse: They give up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.

an10.99:24.2.verse: Then, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, they enter and remain in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

an10.99:24.4.verse: Isn’t this state better than what they had before?”

an10.99:25.1.verse: “When my disciples see this quality inside themselves they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest. But so far they haven’t achieved their heart’s goal.

an10.99:26.1.verse: Furthermore, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, a mendicant enters and remains in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

an10.99:26.3.verse: Isn’t this state better than what they had before?”

an10.99:27.1.verse: “When my disciples see this quality inside themselves they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest. But so far they haven’t achieved their heart’s goal.

an10.99:28.1.verse: Furthermore, with the fading away of rapture, a mendicant enters and remains in the third absorption. They meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

an10.99:28.3.verse: Isn’t this state better than what they had before?”

an10.99:29.1.verse: “When my disciples see this quality inside themselves they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest. But so far they haven’t achieved their heart’s goal.

an10.99:30.1.verse: Furthermore, with the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, a mendicant enters and remains in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness. …” …

an10.99:31.1.verse: “Furthermore, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, a mendicant enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.

an10.99:31.3.verse: Isn’t this state better than what they had before?”

an10.99:32.1.verse: “When my disciples see this quality inside themselves they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest. But so far they haven’t achieved their heart’s goal.

an10.99:33.1.verse: Furthermore, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, a mendicant enters and remains in the dimension of infinite consciousness. …” …

an10.99:34.1.verse: “Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness. …” …

an10.99:35.1.verse: “Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, aware that ‘this is peaceful, this is sublime’, they enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

an10.99:35.3.verse: Isn’t this state better than what they had before?”

an10.99:36.1.verse: “When my disciples see this quality inside themselves they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest. But so far they haven’t achieved their heart’s goal.

an10.99:37.1.verse: Furthermore, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, they enter and remain in the cessation of perception and feeling. And, having seen with wisdom, their defilements come to an end.

an10.99:37.3.verse: Isn’t this state better than what they had before?”

an10.99:38.1.verse: “When my disciples see this quality inside themselves they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest. And they have achieved their heart’s goal.

an10.99:38.2.verse: Come on, Upāli, stay with the Saṅgha.

an10.99:38.3.verse: If you stay with the Saṅgha you’ll be comfortable.”

an10.100:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, without giving up ten things you can’t realize perfection.

an10.100:1.3.verse: Greed, hate, delusion, anger, acrimony, disdain, contempt, jealousy, stinginess, and conceit.

an10.100:1.4.verse: Without giving up these ten things you can’t realize perfection.

an10.100:2.1.verse: After giving up ten things you can realize perfection.

an10.100:2.3.verse: Greed, hate, delusion, anger, acrimony, disdain, contempt, jealousy, stinginess, and conceit.

an10.100:2.4.verse: After giving up these ten things you can realize perfection.”

an10.101:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when these three perceptions for ascetics are developed and cultivated they fulfill seven things.

an10.101:1.3.verse: ‘I have secured freedom from class.’ ‘My livelihood is tied up with others.’ ‘My behavior should be different.’

an10.101:1.4.verse: When these three perceptions for ascetics are developed and cultivated they fulfill seven things.

an10.101:2.2.verse: Their deeds and behavior are always consistent with the precepts. They’re content, kind-hearted, and humble. They want to train. They use the necessities of life after reflecting on their purpose. They’re energetic.

an10.101:2.3.verse: When those three perceptions for ascetics are developed and cultivated they fulfill these seven things.”

an10.102:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when the seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they fulfill three knowledges.

an10.102:1.3.verse: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

an10.102:1.4.verse: When these seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they fulfill three knowledges.

an10.102:1.6.verse: It’s when a mendicant recollects their many kinds of past lives.

an10.102:1.7.verse: That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. They recollect their many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

an10.102:1.8.verse: With clairvoyance that is purified and surpasses the human, they understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

an10.102:1.9.verse: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

an10.102:1.10.verse: When those seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they fulfill these three knowledges.”

an10.103:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, relying on the wrong way leads to failure, not success.

an10.103:1.2.verse: And how does relying on the wrong way lead to failure, not success?

an10.103:1.3.verse: Wrong view produces wrong purpose. Wrong purpose produces wrong speech. Wrong speech produces wrong action. Wrong action produces wrong livelihood. Wrong livelihood produces wrong effort. Wrong effort produces wrong mindfulness. Wrong mindfulness produces wrong immersion. Wrong immersion produces wrong knowledge. Wrong knowledge produces wrong freedom.

an10.103:1.4.verse: That’s how relying on the wrong way leads to failure, not success.

an10.103:2.1.verse: Relying on the right way leads to success, not failure.

an10.103:2.2.verse: And how does relying on the right way lead to success, not failure?

an10.103:2.3.verse: Right view produces right purpose. Right purpose produces right speech. Right speech produces right action. Right action produces right livelihood. Right livelihood produces right effort. Right effort produces right mindfulness. Right mindfulness produces right immersion. Right immersion produces right knowledge. Right knowledge produces right freedom.

an10.103:2.4.verse: That’s how relying on the right way leads to success, not failure.”

an10.104:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, consider an individual who has wrong view, purpose, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, immersion, knowledge, and freedom.

an10.104:1.2.verse: Whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable, harmful, and suffering.

an10.104:2.1.verse: Suppose a seed of neem, angled gourd, or bitter gourd was planted in moist earth. Whatever nutrients it takes up from the earth and water would lead to its bitter, acerbic, and unpleasant taste.

an10.104:2.4.verse: In the same way, consider an individual who has wrong view, purpose, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, immersion, knowledge, and freedom.

an10.104:2.5.verse: Whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable, harmful, and suffering.

an10.104:3.1.verse: Consider an individual who has right view, purpose, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, immersion, knowledge, and freedom. Whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is likable, desirable, agreeable, beneficial, and pleasant.

an10.104:4.1.verse: Suppose a seed of sugarcane, fine rice, or grape was planted in moist earth. Whatever nutrients it takes up from the earth and water would lead to its sweet, pleasant, delectable flavor.

an10.104:4.4.verse: In the same way, consider an individual who has right view, purpose, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, immersion, knowledge, and freedom.

an10.104:4.5.verse: Whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is likable, desirable, agreeable, beneficial, and pleasant.

an10.105:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, ignorance leads the attainment of unskillful qualities, with lack of conscience and prudence following along.

an10.105:1.2.verse: An ignoramus, sunk in ignorance, produces wrong view. Wrong view produces wrong purpose. Wrong purpose produces wrong speech. Wrong speech produces wrong action. Wrong action produces wrong livelihood. Wrong livelihood produces wrong effort. Wrong effort produces wrong mindfulness. Wrong mindfulness produces wrong immersion. Wrong immersion produces wrong knowledge. Wrong knowledge produces wrong freedom.

an10.105:2.1.verse: Knowledge leads the attainment of skillful qualities, with conscience and prudence following along.

an10.105:2.2.verse: A knowing one, firm in knowledge, produces right view. Right view produces right purpose. Right purpose produces right speech. Right speech produces right action. Right action produces right livelihood. Right livelihood produces right effort. Right effort produces right mindfulness. Right mindfulness produces right immersion. Right immersion produces right knowledge. Right knowledge produces right freedom.”

an10.106:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these ten grounds for wearing away.

an10.106:1.3.verse: For one of right view, wrong view is worn away.

an10.106:1.4.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong view are worn away.

an10.106:1.5.verse: And because of right view, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.106:2.1.verse: For one of right purpose, wrong purpose is worn away.

an10.106:2.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong purpose are worn away.

an10.106:2.3.verse: And because of right purpose, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.106:3.1.verse: For one of right speech, wrong speech is worn away.

an10.106:3.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong speech are worn away.

an10.106:3.3.verse: And because of right speech, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.106:4.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong action are worn away.

an10.106:4.3.verse: And because of right action, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.106:5.1.verse: For one of right livelihood, wrong livelihood is worn away.

an10.106:5.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong livelihood are worn away.

an10.106:5.3.verse: And because of right livelihood, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.106:6.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong effort are worn away.

an10.106:6.3.verse: And because of right effort, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.106:7.1.verse: For one of right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is worn away.

an10.106:7.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong mindfulness are worn away.

an10.106:7.3.verse: And because of right mindfulness, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.106:8.1.verse: For one of right immersion, wrong immersion is worn away.

an10.106:8.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong immersion are worn away.

an10.106:8.3.verse: And because of right immersion, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.106:9.1.verse: For one of right knowledge, wrong knowledge is worn away.

an10.106:9.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong knowledge are worn away.

an10.106:9.3.verse: And because of right knowledge, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.106:10.1.verse: For one of right freedom, wrong freedom is worn away.

an10.106:10.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong freedom are worn away.

an10.106:10.3.verse: And because of right freedom, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.106:11.1.verse: These are the ten grounds for wearing away.”

an10.107:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, in the southern lands there is a ceremony named ‘bone-washing’.

an10.107:1.2.verse: There they have food, drink, snacks, meals, refreshments, and beverages, as well as dancing, singing, and music.

an10.107:1.3.verse: There is such a washing, I don’t deny it.

an10.107:1.4.verse: But that washing is low, crude, ordinary, ignoble, and pointless. It doesn’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

an10.107:2.1.verse: I will teach a noble washing that leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment. Relying on that washing, sentient beings who are liable to rebirth, old age, and death, to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are freed from all these things.

an10.107:2.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

an10.107:4.1.verse: For one of right view, wrong view is washed away.

an10.107:4.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong view are washed away.

an10.107:4.3.verse: And because of right view, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.107:5.1.verse: For one of right purpose, wrong purpose is washed away. …

an10.107:5.2.verse: For one of right speech, wrong speech is washed away. …

an10.107:5.3.verse: For one of right action, wrong action is washed away. …

an10.107:5.4.verse: For one of right livelihood, wrong livelihood is washed away. …

an10.107:5.5.verse: For one of right effort, wrong effort is washed away. …

an10.107:5.6.verse: For one of right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is washed away. …

an10.107:5.7.verse: For one of right immersion, wrong immersion is washed away. …

an10.107:5.8.verse: For one of right knowledge, wrong knowledge is washed away. …

an10.107:6.1.verse: For one of right freedom, wrong freedom is washed away.

an10.107:6.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong freedom are washed away.

an10.107:6.3.verse: And because of right freedom, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.107:6.4.verse: This is the noble washing that leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment. Relying on this washing, sentient beings who are liable to rebirth, old age, and death, to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are freed from all these things.”

an10.108:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, doctors prescribe a purgative for eliminating illnesses stemming from disorders of bile, phlegm, and wind.

an10.108:1.2.verse: There is such a purgative, I don’t deny it.

an10.108:1.3.verse: But this kind of purgative sometimes works and sometimes fails.

an10.108:2.1.verse: I will teach a noble purgative that works without fail. Relying on that purgative, sentient beings who are liable to rebirth, old age, and death, to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are freed from all these things.

an10.108:2.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

an10.108:3.1.verse: “And what is the noble purgative that works without fail?

an10.108:4.1.verse: For one of right view, wrong view is purged.

an10.108:4.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are purged.

an10.108:4.3.verse: And because of right view, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.108:5.1.verse: For one of right purpose, wrong purpose is purged. …

an10.108:5.2.verse: For one of right speech, wrong speech is purged. …

an10.108:5.3.verse: For one of right action, wrong action is purged. …

an10.108:5.5.verse: For one of right effort, wrong effort is purged. …

an10.108:5.6.verse: For one of right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is purged. …

an10.108:5.7.verse: For one of right immersion, wrong immersion is purged. …

an10.108:5.8.verse: For one of right knowledge, wrong knowledge is purged. …

an10.108:6.1.verse: For one of right freedom, wrong freedom is purged.

an10.108:6.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong freedom are purged.

an10.108:6.3.verse: And because of right freedom, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.109:2.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak. …

an10.109:4.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are vomited up.

an10.109:4.3.verse: And because of right view, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.109:5.7.verse: For one of right immersion, wrong immersion is vomited up. …

an10.109:5.8.verse: For one of right knowledge, wrong knowledge is vomited up. …

an10.109:6.1.verse: For one of right freedom, wrong freedom is vomited up.

an10.109:6.2.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong freedom are vomited up.

an10.110:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these ten qualities should be blown away.

an10.110:1.3.verse: For one of right view, wrong view is blown away.

an10.110:1.4.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are blown away.

an10.110:1.5.verse: And because of right view, many skillful qualities are fully developed.

an10.110:2.1.verse: For one of right purpose, wrong purpose is blown away. …

an10.110:2.2.verse: For one of right speech, wrong speech is blown away. …

an10.110:2.3.verse: For one of right action, wrong action is blown away. …

an10.110:2.4.verse: For one of right livelihood, wrong livelihood is blown away. …

an10.111:1.1.verse: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

an10.111:2.1.verse: “Sir, they speak of the one called ‘an adept’.

an10.111:2.2.verse: How is an adept mendicant defined?”

an10.111:2.3.verse: “Mendicant, it’s when a mendicant has an adept’s right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

an10.111:2.4.verse: That’s how a mendicant is an adept.”

an10.112:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are ten qualities of an adept.

an10.112:1.3.verse: An adept’s right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

an10.112:1.4.verse: These are the ten qualities of an adept.”

an10.113:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you should know bad principles with bad results.

an10.113:1.2.verse: And you should know good principles with good results.

an10.113:1.3.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.

an10.113:2.1.verse: And what are bad principles with bad results?

an10.113:2.2.verse: Wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.

an10.113:2.3.verse: These are called bad principles with bad results.

an10.113:3.1.verse: And what are good principles with good results?

an10.113:3.2.verse: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

an10.113:3.3.verse: These are called good principles with good results.

an10.113:4.1.verse: ‘You should know bad principles with bad results.

an10.113:4.2.verse: And you should know good principles with good results.

an10.113:4.3.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

an10.113:4.4.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”

an10.114:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you should know bad principles and good principles.

an10.114:1.2.verse: And you should know bad results and good results.

an10.114:1.3.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.

an10.114:2.1.verse: So what are bad principles? What are good principles? What are bad results? And what are good results?

an10.114:3.1.verse: Wrong view is a bad principle.

an10.114:3.2.verse: Right view is a good principle.

an10.114:3.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are bad results.

an10.114:3.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right view are good results.

an10.114:4.1.verse: Wrong purpose is a bad principle.

an10.114:4.2.verse: Right purpose is a good principle.

an10.114:4.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong purpose are bad results.

an10.114:4.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right purpose are good results.

an10.114:5.1.verse: Wrong speech is a bad principle.

an10.114:5.2.verse: Right speech is a good principle.

an10.114:5.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong speech are bad results.

an10.114:5.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right speech are good results.

an10.114:6.1.verse: Wrong action is a bad principle.

an10.114:6.2.verse: Right action is a good principle.

an10.114:6.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong action are bad results.

an10.114:6.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right action are good results.

an10.114:7.1.verse: Wrong livelihood is a bad principle.

an10.114:7.2.verse: Right livelihood is a good principle.

an10.114:7.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong livelihood are bad results.

an10.114:7.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right livelihood are good results.

an10.114:8.1.verse: Wrong effort is a bad principle.

an10.114:8.2.verse: Right effort is a good principle.

an10.114:8.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong effort are bad results.

an10.114:8.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right effort are good results.

an10.114:9.1.verse: Wrong mindfulness is a bad principle.

an10.114:9.2.verse: Right mindfulness is a good principle.

an10.114:9.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong mindfulness are bad results.

an10.114:9.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right mindfulness are good results.

an10.114:10.1.verse: Wrong immersion is a bad principle.

an10.114:10.2.verse: Right immersion is a good principle.

an10.114:10.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong immersion are bad results.

an10.114:10.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right immersion are good results.

an10.114:11.1.verse: Wrong knowledge is a bad principle.

an10.114:11.2.verse: Right knowledge is a good principle.

an10.114:11.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong knowledge are bad results.

an10.114:11.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right knowledge are good results.

an10.114:12.1.verse: Wrong freedom is a bad principle.

an10.114:12.2.verse: Right freedom is a good principle.

an10.114:12.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong freedom are bad results.

an10.114:12.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right freedom are good results.

an10.114:13.1.verse: ‘You should know bad principles and good principles.

an10.114:13.2.verse: And you should know bad results and good results.

an10.114:13.3.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

an10.114:13.4.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”

an10.115:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you should know bad principles and good principles.

an10.115:1.2.verse: And you should know bad results and good results.

an10.115:1.3.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.”

an10.115:1.4.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

an10.115:1.5.verse: When he had spoken, the Holy One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling.

an10.115:2.1.verse: Soon after the Buddha left, those mendicants considered,

an10.115:2.2.verse: “The Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail.

an10.115:2.6.verse: Who can explain in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha?”

an10.115:3.2.verse: “This Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions.

an10.115:3.3.verse: He is capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha.

an10.115:3.4.verse: Let’s go to him, and ask him about this matter.

an10.115:3.5.verse: As he answers, so we’ll remember it.”

an10.115:4.1.verse: Then those mendicants went to Ānanda, and exchanged greetings with him.

an10.115:4.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side. They told him what had happened, and said,

an10.115:8.1.verse: “Reverends, suppose there was a person in need of heartwood. And while wandering in search of heartwood he’d come across a large tree standing with heartwood. But he’d pass over the roots and trunk, imagining that the heartwood should be sought in the branches and leaves.

an10.115:8.2.verse: Such is the consequence for the venerables. Though you were face to face with the Buddha, you bypassed him, imagining that you should ask me about this matter.

an10.115:8.3.verse: For he is the Buddha, the one who knows and sees. He is vision, he is knowledge, he is the manifestation of principle, he is the manifestation of divinity. He is the preacher, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the bestower of freedom from death, the lord of truth, the Realized One.

an10.115:8.4.verse: That was the time to approach the Buddha and ask about this matter.

an10.115:8.5.verse: You should have remembered it in line with the Buddha’s answer.”

an10.115:9.1.verse: “Certainly he is the Buddha, the one who knows and sees. He is vision, he is knowledge, he is the manifestation of principle, he is the manifestation of divinity. He is the preacher, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the bestower of freedom from death, the lord of truth, the Realized One.

an10.115:9.2.verse: That was the time to approach the Buddha and ask about this matter.

an10.115:9.3.verse: We should have remembered it in line with the Buddha’s answer.

an10.115:9.4.verse: Still, Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions.

an10.115:9.5.verse: You are capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha.

an10.115:9.6.verse: Please explain this, if it’s no trouble.”

an10.115:10.1.verse: “Then listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

an10.115:11.1.verse: “Reverends, the Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:

an10.115:11.2.verse: ‘You should know bad principles and good principles.

an10.115:11.3.verse: And you should know bad results and good results.

an10.115:11.4.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

an10.115:12.1.verse: So what are bad principles? What are good principles? What are bad results? And what are good results?

an10.115:13.1.verse: Wrong view is a bad principle.

an10.115:13.2.verse: Right view is a good principle.

an10.115:13.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are bad results.

an10.115:13.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right view are good results.

an10.115:14.1.verse: Wrong purpose is a bad principle.

an10.115:14.2.verse: Right purpose is a good principle. …

an10.115:14.3.verse: Wrong speech is a bad principle.

an10.115:14.4.verse: Right speech is a good principle. …

an10.115:14.5.verse: Wrong action is a bad principle.

an10.115:14.6.verse: Right action is a good principle. …

an10.115:14.7.verse: Wrong livelihood is a bad principle.

an10.115:14.8.verse: Right livelihood is a good principle. …

an10.115:14.9.verse: Wrong effort is a bad principle.

an10.115:14.10.verse: Right effort is a good principle. …

an10.115:14.11.verse: Wrong mindfulness is a bad principle.

an10.115:14.12.verse: Right mindfulness is a good principle. …

an10.115:14.13.verse: Wrong immersion is a bad principle.

an10.115:14.14.verse: Right immersion is a good principle. …

an10.115:14.15.verse: Wrong knowledge is a bad principle.

an10.115:14.16.verse: Right knowledge is a good principle. …

an10.115:15.1.verse: Wrong freedom is a bad principle.

an10.115:15.2.verse: Right freedom is a good principle.

an10.115:15.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong freedom are bad results.

an10.115:15.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right freedom are good results.

an10.115:16.1.verse: The Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:

an10.115:16.2.verse: ‘You should know bad principles and good principles …

an10.115:16.3.verse: and practice accordingly.’ And this is how I understand the detailed meaning of this summary recital.

an10.115:16.4.verse: If you wish, you may go to the Buddha and ask him about this.

an10.115:16.5.verse: You should remember it in line with the Buddha’s answer.”

an10.115:17.1.verse: “Yes, reverend,” said those mendicants, approving and agreeing with what Ānanda said. Then they rose from their seats and went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. Then they said:

an10.115:21.1.verse: “Sir, we went to Ānanda and asked him about this matter.

an10.115:21.2.verse: And Ānanda clearly explained the meaning to us in this manner, with these words and phrases.”

an10.115:22.4.verse: If you came to me and asked this question, I would answer it in exactly the same way as Ānanda.

an10.115:22.5.verse: That is what it means, and that’s how you should remember it.”

an10.116:1.1.verse: Then the wanderer Ajita went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

an10.116:1.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha,

an10.116:2.1.verse: “Worthy Gotama, we have a spiritual companion called ‘Astute’.

an10.116:2.2.verse: He has worked out around five hundred arguments by which followers of other religions will know when they’ve been refuted.”

an10.116:3.1.verse: Then the Buddha said to the mendicants,

an10.116:3.2.verse: “Mendicants, do you remember this Astute’s points?”

an10.116:3.3.verse: “Now is the time, Blessed One! Now is the time, Holy One!

an10.116:3.4.verse: Let the Buddha speak and the mendicants will remember it.”

an10.116:4.1.verse: “Well then, mendicants, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

an10.116:5.1.verse: “Mendicants, take a certain someone who rebuts and quashes unprincipled statements with unprincipled statements. This delights an unprincipled assembly,

an10.116:5.3.verse: ‘He is truly astute! He is truly astute!’

an10.116:6.1.verse: Someone else rebuts and quashes principled statements with unprincipled statements. This delights an unprincipled assembly,

an10.116:6.3.verse: ‘He is truly astute! He is truly astute!’

an10.116:7.1.verse: Someone else rebuts and quashes principled and unprincipled statements with unprincipled statements. This delights an unprincipled assembly,

an10.116:7.3.verse: ‘He is truly astute! He is truly astute!’

an10.116:8.1.verse: Mendicants, you should know bad principles and good principles.

an10.116:8.2.verse: And you should know bad results and good results.

an10.116:8.3.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.

an10.116:9.1.verse: So what are bad principles? What are good principles? What are bad results? And what are good results?

an10.116:9.2.verse: Wrong view is a bad principle.

an10.116:9.3.verse: Right view is a good principle.

an10.116:9.4.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are bad results.

an10.116:9.5.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right view are good results.

an10.116:10.1.verse: Wrong purpose is a bad principle.

an10.116:10.2.verse: Right purpose is a good principle. …

an10.116:10.3.verse: Wrong speech is a bad principle.

an10.116:10.4.verse: Right speech is a good principle. …

an10.116:10.5.verse: Wrong action is a bad principle.

an10.116:10.6.verse: Right action is a good principle. …

an10.116:10.7.verse: Wrong livelihood is a bad principle.

an10.116:10.8.verse: Right livelihood is a good principle. …

an10.116:10.9.verse: Wrong effort is a bad principle.

an10.116:10.10.verse: Right effort is a good principle. …

an10.116:10.11.verse: Wrong mindfulness is a bad principle.

an10.116:10.12.verse: Right mindfulness is a good principle. …

an10.116:10.13.verse: Wrong immersion is a bad principle.

an10.116:10.14.verse: Right immersion is a good principle. …

an10.116:10.15.verse: Wrong knowledge is a bad principle.

an10.116:10.16.verse: Right knowledge is a good principle. …

an10.116:11.1.verse: Wrong freedom is a bad principle.

an10.116:11.2.verse: Right freedom is a good principle.

an10.116:11.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong freedom are bad results.

an10.116:11.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right freedom are good results.

an10.116:12.1.verse: ‘You should know bad principles and good principles.

an10.116:12.2.verse: And you should know bad results and good results.

an10.116:12.3.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

an10.116:12.4.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”

an10.117:1.1.verse: Then Saṅgārava the brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

an10.117:1.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

an10.117:1.3.verse: “Worthy Gotama, what is the near shore? And what is the far shore?”

an10.117:1.4.verse: “Wrong view is the near shore, brahmin, and right view is the far shore.

an10.117:1.5.verse: Wrong purpose is the near shore, and right purpose is the far shore.

an10.117:1.6.verse: Wrong speech is the near shore, and right speech is the far shore.

an10.117:1.7.verse: Wrong action is the near shore, and right action is the far shore.

an10.117:1.8.verse: Wrong livelihood is the near shore, and right livelihood is the far shore.

an10.117:1.9.verse: Wrong effort is the near shore, and right effort is the far shore.

an10.117:1.10.verse: Wrong mindfulness is the near shore, and right mindfulness is the far shore.

an10.117:1.11.verse: Wrong immersion is the near shore, and right immersion is the far shore.

an10.117:1.12.verse: Wrong knowledge is the near shore, and right knowledge is the far shore.

an10.117:1.13.verse: Wrong freedom is the near shore, and right freedom is the far shore.

an10.117:1.14.verse: This is the near shore, and this is the far shore.

an10.119:1.1.verse: Now, at that time it was the sabbath. The brahmin Jānussoṇi had bathed his head and dressed in a new pair of linen robes. Holding a handful of fresh grass, he stood to one side not far from the Buddha.

an10.119:2.3.verse: “Brahmin, why have you bathed your head and dressed in a new pair of linen robes? Why are you standing to one side holding a handful of fresh grass?

an10.119:2.4.verse: What’s going on today with the brahmin clan?”

an10.119:2.5.verse: “Worthy Gotama, today is the ceremony of descent for the brahmin clan.”

an10.119:3.1.verse: “But how do the brahmins observe the ceremony of descent?”

an10.119:3.2.verse: “Well, worthy Gotama, on the sabbath the brahmins bathe their heads and dress in a new pair of linen robes. They make a heap of fresh cow dung and spread it with green grass. Then they make their beds between the boundary and the fire chamber.

an10.119:3.3.verse: That night they rise three times and worship the fire with cupped palms:

an10.119:3.5.verse: And they serve the fire with abundant ghee, oil, and butter.

an10.119:3.6.verse: And when the night has passed they serve the brahmins with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

an10.119:3.7.verse: That’s how the brahmins observe the ceremony of descent.”

an10.119:4.1.verse: “The ceremony of descent observed by the brahmins is quite different from that observed in the training of the Noble One.”

an10.119:4.2.verse: “But worthy Gotama, how is the ceremony of descent observed in the training of the Noble One?

an10.119:4.3.verse: Worthy Gotama, please teach me this.”

an10.119:5.1.verse: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

an10.119:6.3.verse: in both this life and the next.’

an10.119:15.3.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up wrong freedom,

an10.119:15.5.verse: This is the ceremony of descent in the training of the Noble One.”

an10.119:16.1.verse: “The ceremony of descent observed by the brahmins is quite different from that observed in the training of the Noble One.

an10.119:16.2.verse: And, worthy Gotama, the ceremony of descent observed by the brahmins is not worth a sixteenth part of a master of the ceremony of descent observed in the training of the Noble One.

an10.119:16.4.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

an10.120:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the noble descent.

an10.120:1.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak. …

an10.120:1.3.verse: And what is the noble descent?

an10.120:1.4.verse: It’s when a noble disciple reflects:

an10.120:1.6.verse: in both this life and the next.’

an10.120:1.7.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up wrong view,

an10.120:1.18.verse: in both this life and the next.’

an10.120:1.19.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up wrong freedom,

an10.120:1.21.verse: This is called the noble descent.”

an10.121:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, the dawn is the forerunner and harbinger of the sunrise.

an10.121:1.2.verse: In the same way right view is the forerunner and harbinger of skillful qualities.

an10.121:1.3.verse: Right view produces right purpose. Right purpose produces right speech. Right speech produces right action. Right action produces right livelihood. Right livelihood produces right effort. Right effort produces right mindfulness. Right mindfulness produces right immersion. Right immersion produces right knowledge. Right knowledge produces right freedom.”

an10.122:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these ten things, when developed and cultivated, lead to the ending of defilements.

an10.122:1.3.verse: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

an10.122:1.4.verse: These ten things, when developed and cultivated, lead to the ending of defilements.”

an10.123:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these ten things are not purified and cleansed apart from the Holy One’s training.

an10.123:1.3.verse: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

an10.123:1.4.verse: These ten things are not purified and cleansed apart from the Holy One’s training.”

an10.124:1.3.verse: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

an10.124:1.4.verse: These are the ten things that don’t arise apart from the Holy One’s training.”

an10.126:1.4.verse: These are the ten things that don’t culminate in the removal of greed, hate, and delusion apart from the Holy One’s training.”

an10.134:2.6.verse: This is called what is good.”

an10.135:1.8.verse: This is called the teaching of the noble ones.”
