an10.150:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle to cultivate and the principle not to cultivate. …

an10.150:1.3.verse: And what is the principle not to cultivate?

an10.150:1.4.verse: Wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.

an10.150:1.5.verse: This is called the principle not to cultivate.

an10.150:1.6.verse: And what is the principle to cultivate?

an10.150:1.7.verse: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

an10.150:1.8.verse: This is called the principle to cultivate.”

an10.151:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle to develop and the principle not to develop. …

an10.151:1.3.verse: And what is the principle not to develop?

an10.151:1.4.verse: Wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.

an10.151:1.5.verse: This is called the principle not to develop.

an10.151:1.6.verse: And what is the principle to develop?

an10.151:1.7.verse: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

an10.151:1.8.verse: This is called the principle to develop.”

an10.152:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle to make much of and the principle not to make much of. …

an10.152:1.3.verse: And what is the principle not to make much of?

an10.152:1.4.verse: Wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.

an10.152:1.5.verse: This is called the principle not to make much of.

an10.152:1.6.verse: And what is the principle to make much of?

an10.152:1.7.verse: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

an10.152:1.8.verse: This is called the principle to make much of.”

an10.153:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle to recollect and the principle not to recollect. …

an10.153:1.3.verse: And what is the principle not to recollect?

an10.153:1.4.verse: Wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.

an10.153:1.5.verse: This is called the principle not to recollect.

an10.153:1.6.verse: And what is the principle to recollect?

an10.153:1.7.verse: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

an10.153:1.8.verse: This is called the principle to recollect.”

an10.154:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle to realize and the principle not to realize. …

an10.154:1.3.verse: And what is the principle not to realize?

an10.154:1.4.verse: Wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.

an10.154:1.5.verse: This is called the principle not to realize.

an10.154:1.6.verse: And what is the principle to realize?

an10.154:1.7.verse: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

an10.154:1.8.verse: This is called the principle to realize.”

an10.155:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you should not associate with an individual who has ten qualities.

an10.155:1.3.verse: Wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.

an10.155:1.4.verse: You should not associate with an individual who has these ten qualities.

an10.155:2.1.verse: You should associate with an individual who has ten qualities.

an10.155:2.3.verse: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

an10.155:2.4.verse: You should associate with an individual who has these ten qualities.”

an10.156-166:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you should not frequent an individual who has ten qualities. …

an10.156-166:2.4.verse: Right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

an10.156-166:2.5.verse: An individual who has these ten qualities brims with much merit.”

an10.167:1.1.verse: Now, at that time it was the sabbath. The brahmin Jānussoṇi had bathed his head and dressed in a new pair of linen robes. Holding a handful of fresh grass, he stood to one side not far from the Buddha.

an10.167:2.3.verse: “Brahmin, why have you bathed your head and dressed in a new pair of linen robes? Why are you standing to one side holding a handful of fresh grass?

an10.167:2.4.verse: What’s going on today with the brahmin clan?”

an10.167:2.5.verse: “Worthy Gotama, today is the ceremony of descent for the brahmin clan.”

an10.167:3.1.verse: “But how do the brahmins observe the ceremony of descent?”

an10.167:3.2.verse: “Well, worthy Gotama, on the sabbath the brahmins bathe their heads and dress in a new pair of linen robes. They make a heap of fresh cow dung and spread it with green grass. Then they make their beds between the boundary and the fire chamber.

an10.167:3.3.verse: That night they rise three times and worship the fire with cupped palms:

an10.167:3.5.verse: And they serve the fire with abundant ghee, oil, and butter.

an10.167:3.6.verse: And when the night has passed they serve the brahmins with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

an10.167:3.7.verse: That’s how the brahmins observe the ceremony of descent.”

an10.167:4.1.verse: “The ceremony of descent observed by the brahmins is quite different from that observed in the training of the Noble One.”

an10.167:4.2.verse: “But worthy Gotama, how is the ceremony of descent observed in the training of the Noble One?

an10.167:4.3.verse: Worthy Gotama, please teach me this.”

an10.167:5.1.verse: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

an10.167:6.2.verse: ‘Killing living creatures has a bad result in the present life and in lives to come.’

an10.167:6.3.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up killing living creatures,

an10.167:6.4.verse: they descend from killing living creatures.

an10.167:7.2.verse: in the present life and in lives to come.’

an10.167:7.3.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up stealing,

an10.167:8.2.verse: in the present life and in lives to come.’

an10.167:8.3.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up sexual misconduct,

an10.167:9.2.verse: in the present life and in lives to come.’

an10.167:9.3.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up lying,

an10.167:10.2.verse: in the present life and in lives to come.’

an10.167:10.3.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up backbiting,

an10.167:11.2.verse: in the present life and in lives to come.’

an10.167:11.3.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up harsh speech,

an10.167:12.2.verse: in the present life and in lives to come.’

an10.167:12.3.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up talking nonsense,

an10.167:13.2.verse: in the present life and in lives to come.’

an10.167:13.3.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up covetousness,

an10.167:14.2.verse: in the present life and in lives to come.’

an10.167:14.3.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up ill will,

an10.167:15.2.verse: in the present life and in lives to come.’

an10.167:15.3.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up wrong view,

an10.167:15.5.verse: This is the ceremony of descent in the training of the Noble One.”

an10.167:16.1.verse: “The ceremony of descent observed by the brahmins is quite different from that observed in the training of the Noble One.

an10.167:16.2.verse: And, worthy Gotama, the ceremony of descent observed by the brahmins is not worth a sixteenth part of the ceremony of descent observed in the training of the Noble One.

an10.167:16.4.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

an10.168:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the noble descent.

an10.168:1.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

an10.168:2.1.verse: “And what, mendicants, is the noble descent?

an10.168:2.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple reflects:

an10.168:2.3.verse: ‘Killing living creatures has a bad result

an10.168:2.4.verse: in the present life and in lives to come.’

an10.168:2.5.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up killing living creatures,

an10.168:2.6.verse: they descend from killing living creatures.

an10.168:3.2.verse: in the present life and in lives to come.’

an10.168:3.3.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up stealing,

an10.168:11.1.verse: … ‘Wrong view has a bad result both in the present life and in lives to come.’

an10.168:11.2.verse: Reflecting like this, they give up wrong view,

an10.168:11.4.verse: This is called the noble descent.”

an10.169:1.1.verse: Then Saṅgārava the brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

an10.169:1.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

an10.169:2.1.verse: “Worthy Gotama, what is the near shore? And what is the far shore?”

an10.169:2.2.verse: “Killing living creatures is the near shore, brahmin, and not killing living creatures is the far shore.

an10.169:2.3.verse: Stealing is the near shore, and not stealing is the far shore.

an10.169:2.4.verse: Sexual misconduct is the near shore, and refraining from sexual misconduct is the far shore.

an10.169:2.5.verse: Lying is the near shore, and not lying is the far shore.

an10.169:2.6.verse: Divisive speech is the near shore, and refraining from divisive speech is the far shore.

an10.169:2.7.verse: Harsh speech is the near shore, and refraining from harsh speech is the far shore.

an10.169:2.8.verse: Talking nonsense is the near shore, and refraining from talking nonsense is the far shore.

an10.169:2.9.verse: Covetousness is the near shore, and contentment is the far shore.

an10.169:2.10.verse: Ill will is the near shore, and good will is the far shore.

an10.169:2.11.verse: Wrong view is the near shore, and right view is the far shore.

an10.169:2.12.verse: This is the near shore, and this is the far shore.

an10.169:3.2.verse: who cross to the far shore.

an10.169:4.1.verse: When the teaching is well explained,

an10.169:4.4.verse: Death’s dominion so hard to pass.

an10.169:5.2.verse: an astute person would develop the bright.

an10.169:5.4.verse: in seclusion, where joy is hard,

an10.169:6.3.verse: an astute person would cleanse themselves

an10.169:7.1.verse: And those whose minds are rightly developed

an10.169:7.6.verse: they are quenched in this world.”

an10.170:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the near shore and the far shore.

an10.170:1.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak. …

an10.170:1.3.verse: And what, mendicants, is the near shore? What is the far shore?

an10.170:1.4.verse: Killing living creatures is the near shore, mendicants, and not killing living creatures is the far shore.

an10.170:1.5.verse: Stealing is the near shore, and not stealing is the far shore.

an10.170:1.6.verse: Sexual misconduct is the near shore, and refraining from sexual misconduct is the far shore.

an10.170:1.7.verse: Lying is the near shore, and not lying is the far shore.

an10.170:1.8.verse: Divisive speech is the near shore, and refraining from divisive speech is the far shore.

an10.170:1.9.verse: Harsh speech is the near shore, and refraining from harsh speech is the far shore.

an10.170:1.10.verse: Talking nonsense is the near shore, and refraining from talking nonsense is the far shore.

an10.170:1.11.verse: Covetousness is the near shore, and contentment is the far shore.

an10.170:1.12.verse: Ill will is the near shore, and good will is the far shore.

an10.170:1.13.verse: Wrong view is the near shore, and right view is the far shore.

an10.170:1.14.verse: This is the near shore, and this is the far shore.

an10.170:2.2.verse: who cross to the far shore.

an10.170:3.1.verse: When the teaching is well explained,

an10.170:3.4.verse: Death’s dominion so hard to pass.

an10.170:4.2.verse: an astute person would develop the bright.

an10.170:4.4.verse: in seclusion, where joy is hard,

an10.170:5.2.verse: Having given up sensual pleasures, owning nothing,

an10.170:5.3.verse: an astute person would cleanse themselves

an10.170:6.1.verse: And those whose minds are rightly developed

an10.170:6.6.verse: they are quenched in this world.”

an10.171:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you should know bad principles with bad results.

an10.171:1.2.verse: And you should know good principles with good results.

an10.171:1.3.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.

an10.171:2.1.verse: And what are bad principles with bad results?

an10.171:2.2.verse: Killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; covetousness, ill will, and wrong view.

an10.171:2.3.verse: These are called bad principles with bad results.

an10.171:3.1.verse: And what are good principles with good results?

an10.171:3.2.verse: Refraining from killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; refraining from speech that’s false, divisive, harsh, or nonsensical; contentment, good will, and right view.

an10.171:3.3.verse: These are called good principles with good results.

an10.171:4.1.verse: ‘You should know bad principles with bad results.

an10.171:4.2.verse: And you should know good principles with good results.

an10.171:4.3.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

an10.171:4.4.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”

an10.172:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you should know bad principles and good principles.

an10.172:1.2.verse: And you should know bad results and good results.

an10.172:1.3.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.”

an10.172:1.4.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

an10.172:1.5.verse: When he had spoken, the Holy One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling.

an10.172:2.1.verse: Soon after the Buddha left, those mendicants considered,

an10.172:2.2.verse: “The Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail.

an10.172:2.3.verse: ‘You should know bad principles and good principles.

an10.172:2.4.verse: And you should know bad results and good results.

an10.172:2.5.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

an10.172:2.6.verse: Who can explain in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha?”

an10.172:3.2.verse: “This Venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions.

an10.172:3.3.verse: He is capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha.

an10.172:3.4.verse: Let’s go to him, and ask him about this matter.

an10.172:3.5.verse: As he answers, so we’ll remember it.”

an10.172:4.1.verse: Then those mendicants went to Mahākaccāna, and exchanged greetings with him.

an10.172:4.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side. They told him what had happened, and said,

an10.172:8.1.verse: “Reverends, suppose there was a person in need of heartwood. And while wandering in search of heartwood he’d come across a large tree standing with heartwood. But he’d pass over the roots and trunk, imagining that the heartwood should be sought in the branches and leaves.

an10.172:8.2.verse: Such is the consequence for the venerables. Though you were face to face with the Buddha, you bypassed him, imagining that you should ask me about this matter.

an10.172:8.3.verse: For he is the Buddha, the one who knows and sees. He is vision, he is knowledge, he is the manifestation of principle, he is the manifestation of divinity. He is the preacher, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the bestower of freedom from death, the lord of truth, the Realized One.

an10.172:8.4.verse: That was the time to approach the Buddha and ask about this matter.

an10.172:8.5.verse: You should have remembered it in line with the Buddha’s answer.”

an10.172:9.1.verse: “Certainly he is the Buddha, the one who knows and sees. He is vision, he is knowledge, he is the manifestation of principle, he is the manifestation of divinity. He is the preacher, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the bestower of freedom from death, the lord of truth, the Realized One.

an10.172:9.2.verse: That was the time to approach the Buddha and ask about this matter.

an10.172:9.3.verse: We should have remembered it in line with the Buddha’s answer.

an10.172:9.4.verse: Still, Venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions.

an10.172:9.5.verse: He is capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary recital given by the Buddha.

an10.172:9.6.verse: Please explain this, if it’s no trouble.”

an10.172:10.1.verse: “Well then, reverends, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

an10.172:11.1.verse: “Reverends, the Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:

an10.172:11.2.verse: ‘You should know bad principles and good principles …

an10.172:12.1.verse: So what are bad principles? What are good principles?

an10.172:12.2.verse: What are bad results? And what are good results?

an10.172:12.3.verse: Killing living creatures is a bad principle.

an10.172:12.4.verse: Not killing living creatures is a good principle.

an10.172:12.5.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by killing living creatures are bad results.

an10.172:12.6.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of not killing living creatures are good results.

an10.172:13.2.verse: Not stealing is a good principle.

an10.172:13.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by stealing are bad results.

an10.172:13.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of not stealing are good results.

an10.172:14.1.verse: Sexual misconduct is a bad principle.

an10.172:14.2.verse: Refraining from sexual misconduct is a good principle.

an10.172:14.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by sexual misconduct are bad results.

an10.172:14.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of refraining from sexual misconduct are good results.

an10.172:15.2.verse: Not lying is a good principle.

an10.172:15.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by lying are bad results.

an10.172:15.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of not lying are good results.

an10.172:16.2.verse: Refraining from divisive speech is a good principle.

an10.172:16.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by backbiting are bad results.

an10.172:16.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of refraining from divisive speech are good results.

an10.172:17.1.verse: Harsh speech is a bad principle.

an10.172:17.2.verse: Refraining from harsh speech is a good principle.

an10.172:17.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by harsh speech are bad results.

an10.172:17.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of refraining from harsh speech are good results.

an10.172:18.1.verse: Talking nonsense is a bad principle.

an10.172:18.2.verse: Refraining from talking nonsense is a good principle.

an10.172:18.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by talking nonsense are bad results.

an10.172:18.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of refraining from talking nonsense are good results.

an10.172:19.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by covetousness are bad results.

an10.172:19.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of contentment are good results.

an10.172:20.1.verse: Ill will is a bad principle.

an10.172:20.2.verse: Good will is a good principle.

an10.172:20.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by ill will are bad results.

an10.172:20.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of good will are good results.

an10.172:21.1.verse: Wrong view is a bad principle.

an10.172:21.2.verse: Right view is a good principle.

an10.172:21.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are bad results.

an10.172:21.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right view are good results.

an10.172:22.1.verse: The Buddha gave this brief summary recital, then entered his dwelling without explaining the meaning in detail:

an10.172:22.2.verse: ‘You should know bad principles and good principles …

an10.172:22.4.verse: And this is how I understand the detailed meaning of this summary recital.

an10.172:22.5.verse: If you wish, you may go to the Buddha and ask him about this.

an10.172:22.6.verse: You should remember it in line with the Buddha’s answer.”

an10.172:23.1.verse: “Yes, reverend,” said those mendicants, approving and agreeing with what Mahākaccāna said. Then they rose from their seats and went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. Then they said:

an10.172:27.1.verse: “Sir, we went to Mahākaccāna and asked him about this matter.

an10.172:27.2.verse: And Mahākaccāna clearly explained the meaning to us in this manner, with these words and phrases.”

an10.172:28.2.verse: Mahākaccāna is astute, he has great wisdom.

an10.172:28.3.verse: If you came to me and asked this question, I would answer it in exactly the same way as Mahākaccāna.

an10.172:28.4.verse: That is what it means, and that’s how you should remember it.”

an10.173:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you should know bad principles and good principles.

an10.173:1.2.verse: And you should know bad results and good results.

an10.173:1.3.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.

an10.173:2.1.verse: So what are bad principles? What are good principles? What are bad results? And what are good results?

an10.173:2.3.verse: Killing living creatures is a bad principle.

an10.173:2.4.verse: Refraining from killing living creatures is a good principle.

an10.173:2.5.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by killing living creatures are bad results.

an10.173:2.6.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of not killing living creatures are good results.

an10.173:3.2.verse: Refraining from stealing is a good principle. …

an10.173:3.3.verse: Sexual misconduct is a bad principle.

an10.173:3.4.verse: Refraining from sexual misconduct is a good principle. …

an10.173:3.6.verse: Refraining from lying is a good principle. …

an10.173:3.8.verse: Refraining from divisive speech is a good principle. …

an10.173:3.9.verse: Harsh speech is a bad principle.

an10.173:3.10.verse: Refraining from harsh speech is a good principle. …

an10.173:3.11.verse: Talking nonsense is a bad principle.

an10.173:3.12.verse: Refraining from talking nonsense is a good principle. …

an10.173:3.15.verse: Ill will is a bad principle.

an10.173:3.16.verse: Good will is a good principle. …

an10.173:4.1.verse: Wrong view is a bad principle.

an10.173:4.2.verse: Right view is a good principle.

an10.173:4.3.verse: And the many bad, unskillful qualities produced by wrong view are bad results.

an10.173:4.4.verse: And the many skillful qualities fully developed because of right view are good results.

an10.173:5.1.verse: ‘You should know bad principles and good principles.

an10.173:5.2.verse: And you should know bad results and good results.

an10.173:5.3.verse: Knowing these things, your practice should follow the good principles with good results.’

an10.173:5.4.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”

an10.174:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I say that killing living creatures is threefold:

an10.174:1.2.verse: caused by greed, hate, or delusion.

an10.174:2.1.verse: I say that stealing is threefold:

an10.174:2.2.verse: caused by greed, hate, or delusion.

an10.174:3.1.verse: I say that sexual misconduct is threefold:

an10.174:3.2.verse: caused by greed, hate, or delusion.

an10.174:4.1.verse: I say that lying is threefold:

an10.174:4.2.verse: caused by greed, hate, or delusion.

an10.174:5.1.verse: I say that backbiting is threefold:

an10.174:5.2.verse: caused by greed, hate, or delusion.

an10.174:6.1.verse: I say that harsh speech is threefold:

an10.174:6.2.verse: caused by greed, hate, or delusion.

an10.174:7.1.verse: I say that talking nonsense is threefold:

an10.174:7.2.verse: caused by greed, hate, or delusion.

an10.174:8.1.verse: I say that covetousness is threefold:

an10.174:8.2.verse: caused by greed, hate, or delusion.

an10.174:9.1.verse: I say that ill will is threefold:

an10.174:9.2.verse: caused by greed, hate, or delusion.

an10.174:10.1.verse: I say that wrong view is threefold:

an10.174:10.2.verse: caused by greed, hate, or delusion.

an10.174:10.3.verse: And so greed, hate, and delusion are sources and origins for deeds.

an10.174:10.4.verse: With the ending of greed, hate, and delusion, the sources of deeds are ended.”

an10.175:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, this teaching provides a bypass, it doesn’t lack a bypass.

an10.175:1.2.verse: And how does this teaching provide a bypass, not lacking a bypass?

an10.175:1.3.verse: Not killing living creatures bypasses killing living creatures.

an10.175:1.5.verse: Refraining from sexual misconduct bypasses sexual misconduct.

an10.175:1.7.verse: Refraining from divisive speech bypasses divisive speech.

an10.175:1.8.verse: Refraining from harsh speech bypasses harsh speech.

an10.175:1.9.verse: Refraining from talking nonsense bypasses talking nonsense.

an10.175:1.13.verse: That’s how this teaching provides a bypass, it doesn’t lack a bypass.”

an10.176:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Pāvā in Cunda the smith’s mango grove.

an10.176:1.3.verse: Then Cunda the smith went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

an10.176:1.4.verse: “Cunda, whose purity do you believe in?”

an10.176:1.5.verse: “Sir, I believe in the purity advocated by the western brahmins garlanded with aquatic flowers who carry pitchers, serve the sacred flame, and immerse themselves in water.”

an10.176:2.1.verse: “But Cunda, what kind of purity do these western brahmins advocate?”

an10.176:2.2.verse: “The western brahmins encourage their disciple like this:

an10.176:2.3.verse: ‘Please, my man, rising early you should stroke the earth from your bed.

an10.176:2.4.verse: If you don’t stroke the earth, stroke fresh cow dung.

an10.176:2.5.verse: If you don’t stroke fresh cow dung, stroke green grass.

an10.176:2.6.verse: If you don’t stroke green grass, serve the sacred flame.

an10.176:2.7.verse: If you don’t serve the sacred flame, revere the sun with cupped palms.

an10.176:2.8.verse: If you don’t revere the sun with cupped palms, immerse yourself in water three times, including at dusk.’

an10.176:2.9.verse: The western brahmins advocate this kind of purity.”

an10.176:3.1.verse: “The purity advocated by the western brahmins is quite different from that in the training of the Noble One.”

an10.176:3.2.verse: “But what, sir, is purity in the training of the Noble One?

an10.176:4.1.verse: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

an10.176:5.1.verse: “Cunda, impurity is threefold by way of body,

an10.176:5.3.verse: and threefold by way of mind.

an10.176:6.1.verse: And how is impurity threefold by way of body?

an10.176:6.2.verse: It’s when someone kills living creatures. They’re violent, bloody-handed, a hardened killer, merciless to all living beings.

an10.176:7.1.verse: They steal. With the intention to commit theft, they take the wealth or belongings of others from village or wilderness.

an10.176:8.1.verse: They commit sexual misconduct. They have relations with women who have their mother, father, both mother and father, brother, sister, relatives, or clan as guardian. They have relations with a woman who is protected on principle, or who has a husband, or whose violation is punishable by law, or even one who has been garlanded as a token of betrothal.

an10.176:9.1.verse: This is the threefold impurity by way of body.

an10.176:10.1.verse: And how is impurity fourfold by way of speech?

an10.176:10.2.verse: It’s when someone lies. They’re summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness: ‘Please, my friend, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ So they deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

an10.176:11.1.verse: They backbite. They repeat in one place what they heard in another so as to divide people against each other. And so they divide those who are harmonious, supporting division, delighting in division, loving division, speaking words that promote division.

an10.176:12.1.verse: They speak harshly. They use the kinds of words that are cruel, nasty, hurtful, offensive, bordering on anger, not leading to immersion.

an10.176:13.1.verse: They talk nonsense. Their speech is untimely, and is neither factual nor beneficial. It has nothing to do with the teaching or the training. Their words have no value, and are untimely, unreasonable, rambling, and pointless.

an10.176:13.2.verse: This is the fourfold impurity by way of speech.

an10.176:14.1.verse: And how is impurity threefold by way of mind?

an10.176:14.2.verse: It’s when someone is covetous. They covet the wealth and belongings of others: ‘Oh, if only their belongings were mine!’

an10.176:15.1.verse: They have ill will and malicious intentions: ‘May these sentient beings be killed, slaughtered, slain, destroyed, or annihilated!’

an10.176:16.1.verse: They have wrong view. Their perspective is distorted:

an10.176:16.2.verse: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

an10.176:16.3.verse: This is the threefold impurity by way of mind.

an10.176:17.1.verse: These are the ten ways of doing unskillful deeds.

an10.176:17.2.verse: When you have these ten ways of doing unskillful deeds, then if you rise early, whether or not you stroke the earth from your bed, you’re still impure.

an10.176:18.1.verse: Whether or not you stroke fresh cow dung, you’re still impure.

an10.176:19.1.verse: Whether or not you stroke green grass, you’re still impure.

an10.176:20.1.verse: Whether or not you serve the sacred flame, you’re still impure.

an10.176:21.1.verse: Whether or not you revere the sun with cupped palms, you’re still impure.

an10.176:22.1.verse: Whether or not you immerse yourself in water three times, you’re still impure.

an10.176:22.3.verse: These ten ways of doing unskillful deeds are impure and make things impure.

an10.176:23.1.verse: It’s because of those who do these ten kinds of unskillful deeds that hell, the animal realm, the ghost realm, or any other bad places are found.

an10.176:24.1.verse: Cunda, purity is threefold by way of body,

an10.176:24.3.verse: and threefold by way of mind.

an10.176:25.1.verse: And how is purity threefold by way of body?

an10.176:25.2.verse: It’s when someone gives up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They’re scrupulous and kind, living full of sympathy for all living beings.

an10.176:26.1.verse: They give up stealing. They don’t, with the intention to commit theft, take the wealth or belongings of others from village or wilderness.

an10.176:27.1.verse: They give up sexual misconduct. They don’t have relations with women who have their mother, father, both mother and father, brother, sister, relatives, or clan as guardian. They don’t have relations with a woman who is protected on principle, or who has a husband, or whose violation is punishable by law, or even one who has been garlanded as a token of betrothal.

an10.176:28.1.verse: This is the threefold purity by way of body.

an10.176:29.1.verse: And how is purity fourfold by way of speech?

an10.176:29.2.verse: It’s when someone gives up lying. They’re summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness: ‘Please, my friend, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I see.’ So they don’t deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

an10.176:30.1.verse: They give up backbiting. They don’t repeat in one place what they heard in another so as to divide people against each other. Instead, they reconcile those who are divided and support those who are united, delighting in harmony, loving harmony, speaking words that promote harmony.

an10.176:31.1.verse: They give up harsh speech. They speak in a way that’s mellow, pleasing to the ear, endearing, going to the heart, polite, and likable and agreeable to the people.

an10.176:32.1.verse: They give up talking nonsense. Their words are timely, true, and meaningful, in line with the teaching and training.

an10.176:32.2.verse: They say things at the right time which are valuable, reasonable, succinct, and beneficial.

an10.176:33.1.verse: This is the fourfold purity by way of speech.

an10.176:34.1.verse: And how is purity threefold by way of mind?

an10.176:34.2.verse: It’s when someone is content. They don’t covet the wealth and belongings of others: ‘Oh, if only their belongings were mine!’

an10.176:35.1.verse: They have a kind heart and loving intentions: ‘May these sentient beings live free of enmity and ill will, untroubled and happy!’

an10.176:36.1.verse: They have right view, an undistorted perspective:

an10.176:36.2.verse: ‘There is meaning in giving, sacrifice, and offerings. There are fruits and results of good and bad deeds. There is an afterlife. There are such things as mother and father, and beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there are ascetics and brahmins who are rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describe the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

an10.176:37.1.verse: This is the threefold purity by way of mind.

an10.176:38.1.verse: These are the ten ways of doing skillful deeds.

an10.176:38.2.verse: When you have these ten ways of doing skillful deeds, then if you rise early, whether or not you stroke the earth from your bed, you’re still pure.

an10.176:39.1.verse: Whether or not you stroke fresh cow dung, you’re still pure.

an10.176:40.1.verse: Whether or not you stroke green grass, you’re still pure.

an10.176:41.1.verse: Whether or not you serve the sacred flame, you’re still pure.

an10.176:42.1.verse: Whether or not you revere the sun with cupped palms, you’re still pure.

an10.176:43.1.verse: Whether or not you immerse yourself in water three times, you’re still pure.

an10.176:43.3.verse: These ten ways of doing skillful deeds are pure and make things pure.

an10.176:44.1.verse: It’s because of those who do these ten kinds of skillful deeds that gods, humans, or any other good places are found.”

an10.176:45.1.verse: When he said this, Cunda the smith said to the Buddha,

an10.176:45.3.verse: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

an10.177:1.1.verse: Then the brahmin Jānussoṇi went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

an10.177:1.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha,

an10.177:2.2.verse: give gifts and perform memorial rites for the dead:

an10.177:2.3.verse: ‘May this gift aid my departed relatives and kin. May they partake of this gift.’

an10.177:2.4.verse: But does this gift really aid departed relatives and kin?

an10.177:2.5.verse: Do they actually partake of it?”

an10.177:2.6.verse: “It aids them if the conditions are right, brahmin, but not if the conditions are wrong.”

an10.177:3.1.verse: “Then, worthy Gotama, what are the right and wrong conditions?”

an10.177:3.2.verse: “Brahmin, take someone who kills living creatures, steals, and commits sexual misconduct. They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re covetous, malicious, with wrong view.

an10.177:3.3.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in hell.

an10.177:3.4.verse: There they survive feeding on the food of the hell beings.

an10.177:3.5.verse: The conditions there are wrong, so the gift does not aid the one who lives there.

an10.177:4.1.verse: Take someone else who kills living creatures … and has wrong view.

an10.177:4.2.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the animal realm.

an10.177:4.3.verse: There they survive feeding on the food of the beings in the animal realm.

an10.177:4.4.verse: The conditions there too are wrong, so the gift does not aid the one who lives there.

an10.177:5.1.verse: Take someone else who doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, or commit sexual misconduct. They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re contented, kind-hearted, with right view.

an10.177:5.2.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the human realm.

an10.177:5.3.verse: There they survive feeding on human food.

an10.177:5.4.verse: The conditions there too are wrong, so the gift does not aid the one who lives there.

an10.177:6.1.verse: Take someone else who doesn’t kill living creatures … and has right view.

an10.177:6.2.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods.

an10.177:6.3.verse: There they survive feeding on the food of the gods.

an10.177:6.4.verse: The conditions there too are wrong, so the gift does not aid the one who lives there.

an10.177:7.1.verse: Take someone else who kills living creatures … and has wrong view.

an10.177:7.2.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the ghost realm.

an10.177:7.3.verse: There they survive feeding on the food of the beings in the ghost realm. Or else they survive feeding on what friends and colleagues, relatives and kin provide them with from here.

an10.177:7.4.verse: The conditions there are right, so the gift aids the one who lives there.”

an10.177:8.1.verse: “But worthy Gotama, who partakes of that gift if the departed relative is not reborn in that place?”

an10.177:8.2.verse: “Other departed relatives reborn there will partake of that gift.”

an10.177:9.1.verse: “But who partakes of the gift when neither that relative nor other relatives have been reborn in that place?”

an10.177:9.2.verse: “It’s impossible, brahmin, it cannot happen that that place is vacant of departed relatives in all this long time.

an10.177:9.3.verse: It’s never fruitless for the donor.”

an10.177:10.1.verse: “Does the worthy Gotama propose this even when the conditions are wrong?”

an10.177:10.2.verse: “I propose this even when the conditions are wrong.

an10.177:10.3.verse: Take someone who kills living creatures, steals, and commits sexual misconduct. They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re covetous, malicious, with wrong view.

an10.177:10.4.verse: They give to ascetics or brahmins such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

an10.177:10.5.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of elephants.

an10.177:10.6.verse: There they get to have food and drink, garlands and various adornments.

an10.177:11.1.verse: Since in this life they killed living creatures … and had wrong view, they were reborn in the company of elephants.

an10.177:11.2.verse: Since they gave to ascetics or brahmins … they get to have food and drink, garlands and various adornments.

an10.177:12.1.verse: Take someone else who kills living creatures … and has wrong view.

an10.177:12.2.verse: They give to ascetics or brahmins …

an10.177:12.3.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of horses. …

an10.177:12.6.verse: There they get to have food and drink, garlands and various adornments.

an10.177:13.1.verse: Since in this life they killed living creatures … and had wrong view, they were reborn in the company of dogs.

an10.177:13.2.verse: Since they gave to ascetics or brahmins … they get to have food and drink, garlands and various adornments.

an10.177:14.1.verse: Take someone else who doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, or commit sexual misconduct. They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re contented, kind-hearted, with right view.

an10.177:14.2.verse: They give to ascetics or brahmins …

an10.177:14.3.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the human realm.

an10.177:14.4.verse: There they get to have the five kinds of human sensual stimulation.

an10.177:15.1.verse: Since in this life they didn’t kill living creatures … and had right view, they were reborn in the company of humans.

an10.177:15.2.verse: Since they gave to ascetics or brahmins … they get to have the five kinds of human sensual stimulation.

an10.177:16.1.verse: Take someone else who doesn’t kill living creatures … and has right view.

an10.177:16.2.verse: They give to ascetics or brahmins …

an10.177:16.3.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods.

an10.177:16.4.verse: There they get to have the five kinds of heavenly sensual stimulation.

an10.177:17.1.verse: Since in this life they didn’t kill living creatures … and had right view, they were reborn in the company of the gods.

an10.177:17.2.verse: Since they gave to ascetics or brahmins … they get to have the five kinds of heavenly sensual stimulation.

an10.177:17.3.verse: It’s never fruitless for the donor.”

an10.177:18.2.verse: This is quite enough to justify giving gifts and performing memorial rites for the dead, since it’s never fruitless for the donor.”

an10.177:18.3.verse: “That’s so true, brahmin. It’s never fruitless for the donor.”

an10.177:19.2.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

an10.178:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you what is good and what is not good.

an10.178:1.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

an10.178:2.2.verse: Killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; covetousness, ill will, and wrong view.

an10.178:2.3.verse: This is called what is not good.

an10.178:3.2.verse: Refraining from killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; refraining from speech that’s false, divisive, harsh, or nonsensical; contentment, good will, and right view.

an10.178:3.3.verse: This is called what is good.”

an10.179:0.3.verse: The Teaching of the Noble Ones

an10.179:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the teaching of the noble ones, and what is not the teaching of the noble ones.

an10.179:1.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak. …

an10.179:1.3.verse: And what is not the teaching of the noble ones?

an10.179:1.6.verse: This is called what is not the teaching of the noble ones.

an10.179:2.1.verse: And what is the teaching of the noble ones?

an10.179:2.4.verse: This is called the teaching of the noble ones.”

an10.180:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the skillful and the unskillful …

an10.181:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the beneficial and the harmful. …

an10.182:1.1.verse: “I will teach you what is the teaching and what is not the teaching. …

an10.182:1.3.verse: And what is not the teaching?

an10.182:1.6.verse: This is called what is not the teaching.

an10.183:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the defiled principle and the undefiled. …

an10.183:1.3.verse: And what is the defiled principle?

an10.183:1.6.verse: This is called the defiled principle.

an10.183:2.1.verse: And what is the undefiled principle?

an10.183:2.4.verse: This is called the undefiled principle.”

an10.184:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the blameworthy principle and the blameless. …

an10.184:1.3.verse: And what is the blameworthy principle?

an10.184:1.6.verse: This is called the blameworthy principle.

an10.184:2.1.verse: And what is the blameless principle?

an10.184:2.4.verse: This is called the blameless principle.”

an10.185:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the mortifying principle and the unmortifying. …

an10.185:1.3.verse: And what is the mortifying principle?

an10.185:1.6.verse: This is called the mortifying principle.

an10.185:2.1.verse: And what is the unmortifying principle?

an10.185:2.4.verse: This is called the unmortifying principle.”

an10.186:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle that leads to accumulation and that which leads to dispersal. …

an10.186:1.3.verse: And what is the principle that leads to accumulation?

an10.186:1.6.verse: This is called the principle that leads to accumulation.

an10.186:2.1.verse: And what is the principle that leads to dispersal?

an10.186:2.4.verse: This is called the principle that leads to dispersal.”

an10.187:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle that has suffering as outcome, and that which has happiness as outcome. …

an10.187:1.3.verse: And what is the principle whose outcome is suffering?

an10.187:1.6.verse: This is the principle whose outcome is suffering.

an10.187:2.1.verse: And what is the principle whose outcome is happiness?

an10.187:2.4.verse: This is the principle whose outcome is happiness.”

an10.188:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle that results in suffering and that which results in happiness. …

an10.188:1.3.verse: And what is the principle that results in suffering?

an10.188:1.6.verse: This is called the principle that results in suffering.

an10.188:2.1.verse: And what is the principle that results in happiness?

an10.188:2.4.verse: This is called the principle that results in happiness.”

an10.189:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the noble path and the ignoble path. …

an10.189:1.3.verse: And what is the ignoble path?

an10.189:1.6.verse: This is called the ignoble path.

an10.189:2.1.verse: And what is the noble path?

an10.189:2.4.verse: This is called the noble path.”

an10.190:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the dark path and the bright path. …

an10.190:1.3.verse: And what is the dark path?

an10.190:1.6.verse: This is called the dark path.

an10.190:2.1.verse: And what is the bright path?

an10.190:2.4.verse: This is called the bright path.”

an10.191:1.1.verse: “I will teach you what is the true teaching and what is not the true teaching. …

an10.191:1.3.verse: And what is not the true teaching?

an10.191:1.6.verse: This is called what is not the true teaching.

an10.191:2.1.verse: And what is the true teaching?

an10.191:2.4.verse: This is called the true teaching.”

an10.192:0.3.verse: The Teaching of the True Persons

an10.192:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the teaching of the true persons and the teaching of the untrue persons.

an10.192:1.3.verse: And what is the teaching of the untrue persons?

an10.192:1.6.verse: This is the teaching of the untrue persons.

an10.192:2.1.verse: And what is the teaching of the true persons?

an10.192:2.4.verse: This is the teaching of the true persons.”

an10.193:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle to activate and the principle not to activate. …

an10.193:1.3.verse: And what is the principle not to activate?

an10.193:1.6.verse: This is called the principle not to activate.

an10.193:2.1.verse: And what is the principle to activate?

an10.193:2.4.verse: This is called the principle to activate.”

an10.194:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle to cultivate and the principle not to cultivate. …

an10.194:1.3.verse: And what is the principle not to cultivate?

an10.194:1.6.verse: This is called the principle not to cultivate.

an10.194:2.1.verse: And what is the principle to cultivate?

an10.194:2.4.verse: This is called the principle to cultivate.”

an10.195:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle to develop and the principle not to develop. …

an10.195:1.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.

an10.195:1.3.verse: And what is the principle not to develop?

an10.195:1.6.verse: This is called the principle not to develop.

an10.195:2.1.verse: And what is the principle to develop?

an10.195:2.4.verse: This is called the principle to develop.”

an10.196:0.3.verse: Principles That Should Be Made Much Of

an10.196:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle to make much of and the principle not to make much of. …

an10.196:1.3.verse: And what is the principle not to make much of?

an10.196:1.6.verse: This is called the principle not to make much of.

an10.196:2.1.verse: And what is the principle to make much of?

an10.196:2.4.verse: This is called the principle to make much of.”

an10.197:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle to recollect and the principle not to recollect. …

an10.197:1.3.verse: And what is the principle not to recollect?

an10.197:1.6.verse: This is called the principle not to recollect.

an10.197:2.1.verse: And what is the principle to recollect?

an10.197:2.4.verse: This is called the principle to recollect.”

an10.198:1.1.verse: “I will teach you the principle to realize and the principle not to realize. …

an10.198:1.3.verse: And what is the principle not to realize?

an10.198:1.6.verse: This is called the principle not to realize.

an10.198:2.1.verse: And what is the principle to realize?

an10.198:2.4.verse: This is called the principle to realize.”

an10.199-210:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, you should not associate with an individual who possesses ten qualities.

an10.199-210:1.3.verse: They kill living creatures, steal, and commit sexual misconduct. They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re covetous, malicious, with wrong view.

an10.199-210:1.4.verse: You should not associate with an individual who possesses these ten qualities.

an10.199-210:2.1.verse: You should associate with an individual who possesses ten qualities.

an10.199-210:2.3.verse: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, or commit sexual misconduct. They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. They’re contented, kind-hearted, with right view.

an10.199-210:2.4.verse: You should associate with an individual who possesses these ten qualities.”

an10.199-210:3.1.verse: “Mendicants, you should not frequent an individual who possesses ten qualities …

an10.199-210:4.1.verse: “An individual who possesses these ten qualities brims with much wickedness. …

an10.199-210:4.2.verse: An individual who possesses these ten qualities brims with much merit.

an10.199-210:4.4.verse: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, or commit sexual misconduct. They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. They’re contented, kind-hearted, with right view.

an10.199-210:4.5.verse: An individual who possesses these ten qualities brims with much merit.”

an10.211:1.1.verse: “Someone with ten qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an10.211:1.3.verse: It’s when someone kills living creatures. They’re violent, bloody-handed, a hardened killer, merciless to all living beings.

an10.211:2.1.verse: They steal. With the intention to commit theft, they take the wealth or belongings of others from village or wilderness.

an10.211:3.1.verse: They commit sexual misconduct. They have relations with women who have their mother, father, both mother and father, brother, sister, relatives, or clan as guardian. They have relations with a woman who is protected on principle, or who has a husband, or whose violation is punishable by law, or even one who has been garlanded as a token of betrothal.

an10.211:4.1.verse: They lie. They’re summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness: ‘Please, my man, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ So they deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

an10.211:5.1.verse: They backbite. They repeat in one place what they heard in another so as to divide people against each other. And so they divide those who are harmonious, supporting division, delighting in division, loving division, speaking words that promote division.

an10.211:6.1.verse: They speak harshly. They use the kinds of words that are cruel, nasty, hurtful, offensive, bordering on anger, not leading to immersion.

an10.211:7.1.verse: They talk nonsense. Their speech is untimely, and is neither factual nor beneficial. It has nothing to do with the teaching or the training. Their words have no value, and are untimely, unreasonable, rambling, and pointless.

an10.211:8.1.verse: They’re covetous. They covet the wealth and belongings of others: ‘Oh, if only their belongings were mine!’

an10.211:9.1.verse: They have ill will and malicious intentions: ‘May these sentient beings be killed, slaughtered, slain, destroyed, or annihilated!’

an10.211:10.1.verse: They have wrong view. Their perspective is distorted:

an10.211:11.1.verse: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

an10.211:11.2.verse: Someone with these ten qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an10.211:12.1.verse: Someone with ten qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an10.211:12.3.verse: It’s when someone gives up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They’re scrupulous and kind, living full of sympathy for all living beings.

an10.211:13.1.verse: They give up stealing. They don’t, with the intention to commit theft, take the wealth or belongings of others from village or wilderness.

an10.211:14.1.verse: They give up sexual misconduct. They don’t have relations with women who have their mother, father, both mother and father, brother, sister, relatives, or clan as guardian. They don’t have relations with a woman who is protected on principle, or who has a husband, or whose violation is punishable by law, or even one who has been garlanded as a token of betrothal.

an10.211:15.1.verse: They give up lying. They’re summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness: ‘Please, my man, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I see.’ So they don’t deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

an10.211:16.1.verse: They give up backbiting. They don’t repeat in one place what they heard in another so as to divide people against each other. Instead, they reconcile those who are divided and support those who are united, delighting in harmony, loving harmony, speaking words that promote harmony.

an10.211:17.1.verse: They give up harsh speech. They speak in a way that’s mellow, pleasing to the ear, endearing, going to the heart, polite, and likable and agreeable to the people.

an10.211:18.1.verse: They give up talking nonsense. Their words are timely, true, and meaningful, in line with the teaching and training. They say things at the right time which are valuable, reasonable, succinct, and beneficial.

an10.211:19.1.verse: They’re content. They don’t covet the wealth and belongings of others: ‘Oh, if only their belongings were mine!’

an10.211:20.1.verse: They have a kind heart and loving intentions: ‘May these sentient beings live free of enmity and ill will, untroubled and happy!’

an10.211:21.1.verse: They have right view, an undistorted perspective:

an10.211:21.2.verse: ‘There is meaning in giving, sacrifice, and offerings. There are fruits and results of good and bad deeds. There is an afterlife. There are such things as mother and father, and beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there are ascetics and brahmins who are rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describe the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

an10.211:22.1.verse: Someone with these ten qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

an10.216:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you an exposition of the teaching on creepy creatures.

an10.216:1.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

an10.216:2.1.verse: “What is the exposition of the teaching on creepy creatures?

an10.216:2.2.verse: Sentient beings are the owners of their deeds and heir to their deeds. Deeds are their womb, their relative, and their refuge.

an10.216:2.3.verse: They shall be the heir of whatever deeds they do, whether good or bad.

an10.216:3.1.verse: Take a certain someone who kills living creatures. They’re violent, bloody-handed, a hardened killer, merciless to all living beings.

an10.216:3.2.verse: They’re creepy in body, speech, and mind.

an10.216:3.3.verse: Doing crooked deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, their destiny and rebirth are crooked.

an10.216:4.1.verse: Someone whose destiny and rebirth is crooked is reborn in one of two places, I say:

an10.216:4.2.verse: in an absolutely painful hell, or among the species of creepy animals.

an10.216:4.3.verse: And what are the species of creepy animals?

an10.216:4.4.verse: Snakes, scorpions, centipedes, mongooses, cats, mice, owls, or whatever other species of animal that creep away when they see humans.

an10.216:4.5.verse: This is how a being is born from a being.

an10.216:4.6.verse: For your deeds determine your rebirth,

an10.216:4.7.verse: and when you’re reborn contacts strike you.

an10.216:4.8.verse: This is why I say that sentient beings are heirs to their deeds.

an10.216:5.12.verse: They’re creepy in body, speech, and mind.

an10.216:5.13.verse: Doing crooked deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, their destiny and rebirth are crooked.

an10.216:6.1.verse: Someone whose destiny and rebirth is crooked is reborn in one of two places, I say:

an10.216:6.2.verse: in an absolutely painful hell, or among the species of creepy animals.

an10.216:6.3.verse: And what are the species of creepy animals?

an10.216:6.4.verse: Snakes, scorpions, centipedes, mongooses, cats, mice, owls, or whatever other species of animal that creep away when they see humans.

an10.216:6.5.verse: This is how a being is born from a being.

an10.216:6.6.verse: For your deeds determine your rebirth,

an10.216:6.7.verse: and when you’re reborn contacts strike you.

an10.216:6.8.verse: This is why I say that sentient beings are heirs to their deeds.

an10.216:6.9.verse: Sentient beings are the owners of their deeds and heir to their deeds. Deeds are their womb, their relative, and their refuge.

an10.216:6.10.verse: They shall be the heir of whatever deeds they do, whether good or bad.

an10.216:7.1.verse: Take a certain someone who gives up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They’re scrupulous and kind, living full of sympathy for all living beings.

an10.216:7.2.verse: They’re not creepy in body, speech, and mind.

an10.216:7.3.verse: Doing virtuous deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, their destiny and rebirth is virtuous.

an10.216:8.1.verse: Someone whose destiny and rebirth is virtuous is reborn in one of two places, I say:

an10.216:8.2.verse: in a heaven of absolute happiness, or in an eminent well-to-do family of aristocrats, brahmins, or householders—rich, affluent, and wealthy, with lots of gold and silver, lots of property and assets, and lots of money and grain.

an10.216:8.3.verse: This is how a being is born from a being.

an10.216:8.4.verse: For your deeds determine your rebirth,

an10.216:8.5.verse: and when you’re reborn contacts strike you.

an10.216:8.6.verse: This is why I say that sentient beings are heirs to their deeds.

an10.216:9.1.verse: Take someone else who gives up stealing …

an10.216:9.12.verse: They’re not creepy in body, speech, and mind.

an10.216:9.13.verse: Doing virtuous deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, their destiny and rebirth is virtuous.

an10.216:10.2.verse: in a heaven of absolute happiness, or in an eminent well-to-do family of aristocrats, brahmins, or householders—rich, affluent, and wealthy, with lots of gold and silver, lots of property and assets, and lots of money and grain.

an10.216:10.3.verse: This is how a being is born from a being.

an10.216:11.3.verse: This is the exposition of the teaching on creepy creatures.”

an10.217:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I don’t say that intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated are eliminated without being experienced.

an10.217:1.2.verse: And that may be in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

an10.217:1.3.verse: But in any case, there is no making an end of suffering without experiencing intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated, I say.

an10.217:2.1.verse: Now, there are three kinds of corruption and failure of bodily action that have unskillful intention, with suffering as their outcome and result.

an10.217:2.2.verse: There are four kinds of corruption and failure of verbal action that have unskillful intention, with suffering as their outcome and result.

an10.217:2.3.verse: There are three kinds of corruption and failure of mental action that have unskillful intention, with suffering as their outcome and result.

an10.217:3.1.verse: And what are the three kinds of corruption and failure of bodily action?

an10.217:3.2.verse: It’s when someone kills living creatures. They’re violent, bloody-handed, a hardened killer, merciless to all living beings.

an10.217:4.1.verse: They steal. With the intention to commit theft, they take the wealth or belongings of others from village or wilderness.

an10.217:5.1.verse: They commit sexual misconduct. They have relations with women who have their mother, father, both mother and father, brother, sister, relatives, or clan as guardian. They have relations with a woman who is protected on principle, or who has a husband, or whose violation is punishable by law, or even one who has been garlanded as a token of betrothal.

an10.217:6.1.verse: These are the three kinds of corruption and failure of bodily action.

an10.217:7.1.verse: And what are the four kinds of corruption and failure of verbal action?

an10.217:7.2.verse: It’s when someone lies. They’re summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness:

an10.217:7.3.verse: ‘Please, my man, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ So they deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

an10.217:8.1.verse: They backbite. They repeat in one place what they heard in another so as to divide people against each other. And so they divide those who are harmonious, supporting division, delighting in division, loving division, speaking words that promote division.

an10.217:9.1.verse: They speak harshly. They use the kinds of words that are cruel, nasty, hurtful, offensive, bordering on anger, not leading to immersion.

an10.217:10.1.verse: They talk nonsense. Their speech is untimely, and is neither factual nor beneficial. It has nothing to do with the teaching or the training. Their words have no value, and are untimely, unreasonable, rambling, and pointless.

an10.217:11.1.verse: These are the four kinds of corruption and failure of verbal action.

an10.217:12.1.verse: And what are the three kinds of corruption and failure of mental action?

an10.217:12.2.verse: It’s when someone is covetous. They covet the wealth and belongings of others: ‘Oh, if only their belongings were mine!’

an10.217:13.1.verse: They have ill will and malicious intentions: ‘May these sentient beings be killed, slaughtered, slain, destroyed, or annihilated!’

an10.217:14.1.verse: They have wrong view. Their perspective is distorted:

an10.217:14.2.verse: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

an10.217:15.1.verse: These are the three kinds of corruption and failure of mental action.

an10.217:16.1.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, sentient beings are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell because of these three kinds of corruption and failure of bodily action, these four kinds of corruption and failure of verbal action, or these three kinds of corruption and failure of mental action that have unskillful intention, with suffering as their outcome and result.

an10.217:17.1.verse: It’s like throwing sure-bet dice: they always fall the right side up.

an10.217:17.2.verse: In the same way, when their body breaks up, after death, sentient beings are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell because of these three kinds of corruption and failure of bodily action, these four kinds of corruption and failure of verbal action, or these three kinds of corruption and failure of mental action that have unskillful intention, with suffering as their outcome and result.

an10.217:18.1.verse: I don’t say that intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated are eliminated without being experienced.

an10.217:18.2.verse: And that may be in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

an10.217:18.3.verse: But in any case, there is no making an end of suffering without experiencing intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated, I say.

an10.217:19.1.verse: Now, there are three kinds of successful bodily action that have skillful intention, with happiness as their outcome and result.

an10.217:19.2.verse: There are four kinds of successful verbal action that have skillful intention, with happiness as their outcome and result.

an10.217:19.3.verse: There are three kinds of successful mental action that have skillful intention, with happiness as their outcome and result.

an10.217:20.1.verse: And what are the three kinds of successful bodily action?

an10.217:20.2.verse: It’s when someone gives up killing living creatures. They renounce the rod and the sword. They’re scrupulous and kind, living full of sympathy for all living beings.

an10.217:21.1.verse: They don’t steal. They don’t, with the intention to commit theft, take the wealth or belongings of others from village or wilderness.

an10.217:22.1.verse: They give up sexual misconduct. They don’t have relations with women who have their mother, father, both mother and father, brother, sister, relatives, or clan as guardian. They don’t have relations with a woman who is protected on principle, or who has a husband, or whose violation is punishable by law, or even one who has been garlanded as a token of betrothal.

an10.217:23.1.verse: These are the three kinds of successful bodily action.

an10.217:24.1.verse: And what are the four kinds of successful verbal action?

an10.217:24.2.verse: It’s when someone gives up lying. They’re summoned to a council, an assembly, a family meeting, a guild, or to the royal court, and asked to bear witness: ‘Please, my friend, say what you know.’ Not knowing, they say ‘I don’t know.’ Knowing, they say ‘I know.’ Not seeing, they say ‘I don’t see.’ And seeing, they say ‘I see.’ So they don’t deliberately lie for the sake of themselves or another, or for some trivial worldly reason.

an10.217:25.1.verse: They give up backbiting. They don’t repeat in one place what they heard in another so as to divide people against each other. Instead, they reconcile those who are divided and support those who are united, delighting in harmony, loving harmony, speaking words that promote harmony.

an10.217:26.1.verse: They give up harsh speech. They speak in a way that’s mellow, pleasing to the ear, endearing, going to the heart, polite, and likable and agreeable to the people.

an10.217:27.1.verse: They give up talking nonsense. Their words are timely, true, and meaningful, in line with the teaching and training. They say things at the right time which are valuable, reasonable, succinct, and beneficial.

an10.217:28.1.verse: These are the four kinds of successful verbal action.

an10.217:29.1.verse: And what are the three kinds of successful mental action?

an10.217:29.2.verse: It’s when someone is content. They don’t covet the wealth and belongings of others: ‘Oh, if only their belongings were mine!’

an10.217:30.1.verse: They have a kind heart and loving intentions: ‘May these sentient beings live free of enmity and ill will, untroubled and happy!’

an10.217:31.1.verse: They have right view, an undistorted perspective:

an10.217:31.2.verse: ‘There is meaning in giving, sacrifice, and offerings. There are fruits and results of good and bad deeds. There is an afterlife. There are such things as mother and father, and beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there are ascetics and brahmins who are rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describe the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

an10.217:32.1.verse: These are the three kinds of successful mental action.

an10.217:33.1.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, sentient beings are reborn in a good place, in heaven because of these three kinds of successful bodily action, these four kinds of successful verbal action, or these three kinds of successful mental action that have skillful intention, with happiness as their outcome and result.

an10.217:34.1.verse: It’s like throwing unfaling dice: they always fall the right side up.

an10.217:34.2.verse: In the same way, when their body breaks up, after death, sentient beings are reborn in a good place, in heaven because of these three kinds of successful bodily action, these four kinds of successful verbal action, or these three kinds of successful mental action that have skillful intention, with happiness as their outcome and result.

an10.217:34.3.verse: I don’t say that intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated are eliminated without being experienced.

an10.217:34.4.verse: And that may be in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

an10.217:34.5.verse: But in any case, there is no making an end of suffering without experiencing intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated, I say.”

an10.219:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I don’t say that intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated are eliminated without being experienced.

an10.219:1.2.verse: And that may be in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

an10.219:1.3.verse: But in any case, there is no making an end of suffering without experiencing intentional deeds that have been performed and accumulated, I say.

an10.219:2.1.verse: That noble disciple is rid of desire, rid of ill will, unconfused, aware, and mindful. They meditate spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

an10.219:3.2.verse: ‘Formerly my mind was limited and undeveloped. Now it’s limitless and well developed. Whatever limited deeds I’ve done don’t remain or persist there.’

an10.219:4.2.verse: Suppose a child had developed the heart’s release by love from their childhood on. Would they still do any bad deed?”

an10.219:5.1.verse: “Not doing any bad deed, would they still experience any suffering?”

an10.219:5.3.verse: For if they don’t do any bad deed, from where would suffering afflict them?”

an10.219:6.1.verse: “This heart’s release by love should be developed by women or men.

an10.219:6.2.verse: For neither women nor men take this body with them when they go.

an10.219:6.3.verse: The mind is what’s inside mortal beings.

an10.219:6.5.verse: ‘Whatever bad deeds I have done in the past with this deed-born body I will experience here.

an10.219:6.6.verse: It will not follow me to my next life.’

an10.219:6.7.verse: The heart’s release by love developed in this way leads to non-return for a wise mendicant here who has not penetrated to a higher freedom.

an10.219:7.1.verse: They meditate spreading a heart full of compassion …

an10.219:7.2.verse: They meditate spreading a heart full of rejoicing …

an10.219:7.3.verse: They meditate spreading a heart full of equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth.

an10.219:7.4.verse: In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

an10.219:8.2.verse: ‘Formerly my mind was limited and undeveloped. Now it’s limitless and well developed. Whatever limited deeds I’ve done don’t remain or persist there.’

an10.219:9.2.verse: Suppose a child had developed the heart’s release by equanimity from their childhood on. Would they still do any bad deed?”

an10.219:10.1.verse: “Not doing any bad deed, would they still experience any suffering?”

an10.219:10.3.verse: For if they don’t do any bad deed, from where would suffering afflict them?”

an10.219:11.1.verse: “This heart’s release by equanimity should be developed by women or men.

an10.219:11.2.verse: For neither women nor men take this body with them when they go.

an10.219:11.3.verse: The mind is what’s inside mortal beings.

an10.219:11.5.verse: ‘Whatever bad deeds I have done in the past with this deed-born body I will experience here.

an10.219:11.6.verse: It will not follow me to my next life.’

an10.219:11.7.verse: The heart’s release by equanimity developed in this way leads to non-return for a wise mendicant here who has not penetrated to a higher freedom.”

an10.220:1.1.verse: Then a certain brahmin went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

an10.220:1.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

an10.220:1.3.verse: “What is the cause, worthy Gotama, what is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell?”

an10.220:1.4.verse: “Unprincipled and immoral conduct is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

an10.220:2.1.verse: “But what is the cause, worthy Gotama, what is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm?”

an10.220:2.2.verse: “Principled and moral conduct is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

an10.220:3.1.verse: “I don’t understand the detailed meaning of what the worthy Gotama has said in brief.

an10.220:3.2.verse: Please, worthy Gotama, teach me this matter so I can understand the detailed meaning.”

an10.220:3.3.verse: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

an10.220:4.1.verse: “Brahmin, unprincipled and immoral conduct is threefold by way of body,

an10.220:4.3.verse: and threefold by way of mind.

an10.220:5.1.verse: And how is unprincipled and immoral conduct threefold by way of body? …

an10.220:5.2.verse: That’s how unprincipled and immoral conduct is threefold by way of body.

an10.220:6.1.verse: And how is unprincipled and immoral conduct fourfold by way of speech? …

an10.220:6.2.verse: That’s how unprincipled and immoral conduct is fourfold by way of speech.

an10.220:7.1.verse: And how is unprincipled and immoral conduct threefold by way of mind? …

an10.220:7.2.verse: That’s how unprincipled and immoral conduct is threefold by way of mind.

an10.220:7.3.verse: That’s how unprincipled and immoral conduct is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

an10.220:8.1.verse: Principled and moral conduct is threefold by way of body,

an10.220:8.3.verse: and threefold by way of mind.

an10.220:9.1.verse: And how is principled and moral conduct threefold by way of body? …

an10.220:9.2.verse: That’s how principled and moral conduct is threefold by way of body.

an10.220:10.1.verse: And how is principled and moral conduct fourfold by way of speech? …

an10.220:10.2.verse: That’s how principled and moral conduct is fourfold by way of speech.

an10.220:11.1.verse: And how is principled and moral conduct threefold by way of mind? …

an10.220:11.2.verse: That’s how principled and moral conduct is threefold by way of mind.

an10.220:11.3.verse: That’s how principled and moral conduct is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

an10.220:12.2.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

an10.221:1.1.verse: “Someone with ten qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an10.221:1.3.verse: They kill living creatures, steal, and commit sexual misconduct. They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re covetous, malicious, with wrong view.

an10.221:1.4.verse: Someone with these ten qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

an10.221:2.1.verse: Someone with ten qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.

an10.221:2.3.verse: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, or commit sexual misconduct. They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. They’re contented, kind-hearted, with right view.

an10.221:2.4.verse: Someone with these ten qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
