dn3:2.3.18.verse: These are the four causes of quitting this supreme knowledge and conduct.

dn3:2.4.2.verse: Is this supreme knowledge and conduct seen in your own denomination?”

dn3:2.4.4.verse: Who am I and my denomination compared with the supreme knowledge and conduct?

dn3:2.4.7.verse: Since you’re not managing to obtain this supreme knowledge and conduct, have you with your denomination plunged into a wilderness region carrying your pack with a shoulder-pole, thinking

dn3:2.4.8.verse: you will get by eating fallen fruit?”

dn3:2.4.11.verse: Have you with your denomination … plunged into a wilderness region carrying a spade and basket, thinking

dn3:2.4.12.verse: you will get by eating tubers and fruit?”

dn3:2.4.15.verse: Have you with your denomination … set up a fire chamber in the neighborhood of a village or town and dwelt there serving the sacred flame?”

dn3:2.4.18.verse: Have you with your denomination … set up a four-doored fire chamber at the crossroads and dwelt there, thinking:

dn3:2.4.19.verse: ‘When an ascetic or brahmin comes from the four quarters, I will honor them as best I can’?”

dn3:2.5.1.verse: “So you with your denomination are not only inferior to the supreme knowledge and conduct,

dn3:2.5.2.verse: you are even inferior to the four causes of quitting the supreme knowledge and conduct.

dn3:2.5.3.verse: But you have been told this by your tutor, the brahmin Pokkharasāti:

dn3:2.5.4.verse: ‘Who are these shavelings, fake ascetics, primitives, black spawn from the feet of our kinsman compared with conversation with the brahmins of the three knowledges?’ Yet he himself has not even fulfilled one of the quittings!

dn3:2.5.5.verse: See, Ambaṭṭha, how your tutor Pokkharasāti has wronged you.

dn3:2.6.0.verse: 6. Being Like the Seers of the Past

dn3:2.6.1.verse: Pokkharasāti lives off an endowment provided by King Pasenadi of Kosala.

dn3:2.6.2.verse: But the king won’t even grant him an audience face to face.

dn3:2.6.3.verse: When he consults, he does so behind a curtain.

dn3:2.6.4.verse: Why wouldn’t the king grant a face to face audience with someone who’d receive his legitimate presentation of food?

dn3:2.6.5.verse: See, Ambaṭṭha, how your tutor Pokkharasāti has wronged you.

dn3:2.7.2.verse: Suppose King Pasenadi was holding consultations with warrior-chiefs or chieftains while sitting on an elephant’s neck or on horseback, or while standing on the mat in a chariot.

dn3:2.7.3.verse: And suppose he’d get down from that place and stand aside.

dn3:2.7.4.verse: Then along would come a worker or their bondservant, who’d stand in the same place and continue the consultation:

dn3:2.7.5.verse: ‘This is what King Pasenadi says, and this too is what the king says.’

dn3:2.7.6.verse: Though he spoke the king’s words and gave the king’s advice,

dn3:2.7.7.verse: does that qualify him to be the king or the king’s minister?”

dn3:2.8.1.verse: “In the same way, Ambaṭṭha, the ancient seers of the brahmins were Aṭṭhaka, Vāmaka, Vāmadeva, Vessāmitta, Yamadaggi, Aṅgīrasa, Bhāradvāja, Vāseṭṭha, Kassapa, and Bhagu. They were the authors and propagators of the hymns. Their hymnal was sung and propagated and compiled in ancient times; and these days, brahmins continue to sing and chant it, chanting what was chanted and teaching what was taught.

dn3:2.8.2.verse: You might imagine that, since you’ve learned their hymns by heart in your own denomination, that makes you a seer or someone on the path to becoming a seer. But that is not possible.

dn3:2.9.2.verse: According to what you have heard from elderly and senior brahmins, the tutors of tutors,

dn3:2.9.4.verse: nicely bathed and anointed, with hair and beard dressed, bedecked with jewels, earrings, and bracelets, dressed in white—amuse themselves, supplied and provided with the five kinds of sensual stimulation, like you do today in your denomination?”

dn3:2.10.2.verse: “Did they eat boiled fine rice, garnished with clean meat, with the dark grains picked out, served with many soups and sauces, like you do today in your denomination?”

dn3:2.10.5.verse: “Did they amuse themselves with girls wearing thongs that show off their curves, like you do today in your denomination?”

dn3:2.10.8.verse: “Did they drive about in chariots drawn by mares with plaited manes, whipping and lashing them onward with long goads, like you do today in your denomination?”

dn3:2.10.11.verse: “Did they get men with long swords to guard them in fortresses with moats dug and barriers in place, like you do today in your denomination?”

dn3:2.10.13.verse: “So, Ambaṭṭha, in your own denomination you are neither a seer nor someone on the path to becoming a seer.

dn3:2.10.14.verse: Whoever has any doubt or uncertainty about me, let them ask me and I will clear up their doubts with my answer.”

dn3:2.11.1.verse: Then the Buddha left his dwelling and proceeded to begin walking mindfully,

dn3:2.11.3.verse: Then while walking beside the Buddha, Ambaṭṭha scrutinized his body for the thirty-two marks of a great man.

dn3:2.11.4.verse: He saw all of them except two,

dn3:2.11.6.verse: whether the private parts are sheathed in a foreskin, and the largeness of the tongue.

dn3:2.12.1.verse: Then it occurred to the Buddha,

dn3:2.12.2.verse: “This student Ambaṭṭha sees all the marks except two,

dn3:2.12.4.verse: whether the private parts are sheathed in a foreskin, and the largeness of the tongue.”

dn3:2.12.5.verse: Then the Buddha used his psychic power to will that Ambaṭṭha would see his private parts sheathed in a foreskin.

dn3:2.12.6.verse: And he stuck out his tongue and stroked back and forth on his ear holes and nostrils, and covered his entire forehead with his tongue.

dn3:2.12.8.verse: “The ascetic Gotama possesses the thirty-two marks completely, lacking none.”

dn3:2.12.10.verse: “Well, now, sir, I must go. I have many duties, and much to do.”

dn3:2.12.12.verse: Then Ambaṭṭha mounted his chariot drawn by mares and left.

dn3:2.13.1.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Pokkharasāti had come out from Ukkaṭṭhā together with a large group of brahmins and was sitting in his own park just waiting for Ambaṭṭha.

dn3:2.14.1.verse: He went by carriage as far as the terrain allowed, then descended and approached the brahmin Pokkharasāti on foot. He bowed and sat down to one side, and Pokkharasāti said to him:

dn3:2.14.2.verse: “I hope, dear Ambaṭṭha, you saw the worthy Gotama?”

dn3:2.14.4.verse: “Well, does he live up to his reputation or not?”

dn3:2.14.7.verse: The worthy Gotama possesses the thirty-two marks completely, lacking none.”

dn3:2.14.8.verse: “And did you have some discussion with him?”

dn3:2.14.10.verse: “And what kind of discussion did you have with him?”

dn3:2.14.11.verse: Then Ambaṭṭha informed Pokkharasāti of all they had discussed.

dn3:2.15.2.verse: “Oh, our bloody fake scholar, our fake learned man, who pretends to be proficient in the three Vedas! A man who behaves like this ought, when their body breaks up, after death, to be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

dn3:2.15.3.verse: It’s only because you repeatedly attacked the worthy Gotama like that that he kept bringing up charges against us!”

dn3:2.15.4.verse: Angry and upset, he kicked Ambaṭṭha over,

dn3:2.15.5.verse: and wanted to go and see the Buddha right away.

dn3:2.16.1.verse: Then those brahmins said to Pokkharasāti,

dn3:2.16.2.verse: “It’s much too late to visit the ascetic Gotama today.

dn3:2.16.4.verse: So Pokkharasāti had delicious fresh and cooked foods prepared in his own home. Then he mounted a carriage and, with attendants carrying torches, set out from Ukkaṭṭhā for the forest near Icchānaṅgala.

dn3:2.17.1.verse: He went by carriage as far as the terrain allowed, then descended and entered the monastery on foot. He went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him. When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha,

dn3:2.17.2.verse: “Master Gotama, has my resident pupil, the student Ambaṭṭha, come here?”

dn3:2.17.4.verse: “And did you have some discussion with him?”

dn3:2.17.6.verse: “And what kind of discussion did you have with him?”

dn3:2.17.7.verse: Then the Buddha informed Pokkharasāti of all they had discussed.

dn3:2.17.8.verse: Then Pokkharasāti said to the Buddha,

dn3:2.17.9.verse: “Ambaṭṭha is a fool, worthy Gotama. Please forgive him.”

dn3:2.17.10.verse: “May the student Ambaṭṭha be happy, brahmin.”

dn3:2.18.1.verse: Then Pokkharasāti scrutinized the Buddha’s body for the thirty-two marks of a great man.

dn3:2.18.2.verse: He saw all of them except two,

dn3:2.18.4.verse: whether the private parts are sheathed in a foreskin, and the largeness of the tongue.

dn3:2.18.5.verse: Then it occurred to the Buddha,

dn3:2.18.6.verse: “Pokkharasāti sees all the marks except two,

dn3:2.18.8.verse: whether the private parts are sheathed in a foreskin, and the largeness of the tongue.”

dn3:2.18.9.verse: Then the Buddha used his psychic power to will that Pokkharasāti would see his private parts sheathed in a foreskin.

dn3:2.18.10.verse: And he stuck out his tongue and stroked back and forth on his ear holes and nostrils, and covered his entire forehead with his tongue.

dn3:2.19.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama possesses the thirty-two marks completely, lacking none.”

dn3:2.19.4.verse: “Would the worthy Gotama together with the mendicant Saṅgha please accept today’s meal from me?”

dn3:2.20.1.verse: Then, knowing that the Buddha had consented, Pokkharasāti announced the time to him,

dn3:2.20.2.verse: “It’s time, worthy Gotama, the meal is ready.”

dn3:2.20.3.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of Pokkharasāti together with the mendicant Saṅgha, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

dn3:2.20.4.verse: Then Pokkharasāti served and satisfied the Buddha with his own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods, while his young students served the Saṅgha.

dn3:2.20.5.verse: When the Buddha had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, Pokkharasāti took a low seat and sat to one side.

dn3:2.21.1.verse: Then the Buddha taught him step by step, with

dn3:2.21.2.verse: a talk on giving, ethical conduct, and heaven. He revealed the drawbacks of sensual pleasures, so sordid and corrupt, and the benefit of renunciation.

dn3:2.21.3.verse: And when the Buddha knew that Pokkharasāti’s mind was ready, pliable, rid of hindrances, elated, and confident he revealed the special teaching of the Buddhas:

dn3:2.21.4.verse: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

dn3:2.21.5.verse: Just as a clean cloth rid of stains would properly absorb dye,

dn3:2.21.6.verse: in that very seat the stainless, immaculate vision of the Dhamma arose in the brahmin Pokkharasāti:

dn3:2.21.7.verse: “Everything that is liable to arise is liable to cease.”

dn3:2.22.0.verse: 9. Pokkharasāti Declares Himself a Lay Follower

dn3:2.22.1.verse: Then Pokkharasāti saw, attained, understood, and fathomed the Dhamma. He went beyond doubt, got rid of indecision, and became self-assured and independent of others regarding the Teacher’s instructions. He said to the Buddha,

dn3:2.22.3.verse: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, just so has the worthy Gotama made the Teaching clear in many ways.

dn3:2.22.4.verse: Together with my children, wives, retinue, and ministers, I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

dn3:2.22.5.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.

dn3:2.22.6.verse: Just as the worthy Gotama visits other devoted families in Ukkaṭṭhā, may he visit mine.

dn3:2.22.7.verse: The brahmin boys and girls there will bow to you, rise in your presence, give you a seat and water, and gain confidence in their hearts. That will be for their lasting welfare and happiness.”

dn3:2.22.8.verse: “That’s nice of you to say, householder.”

dn4:1.0.verse: 1. The Brahmins and Householders of Campā

dn4:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Aṅgas together with a large Saṅgha of five hundred mendicants when he arrived at Campā,

dn4:1.3.verse: where he stayed by the banks of the Gaggarā Lotus Pond.

dn4:1.4.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Soṇadaṇḍa was living in Campā. It was a crown property given by King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, teeming with living creatures, full of hay, wood, water, and grain, a royal park endowed to a brahmin.

dn4:2.1.verse: The brahmins and householders of Campā heard:

dn4:2.2.verse: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—has arrived at Campā and is staying on the banks of the Gaggarā Lotus Pond.

dn4:2.4.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

dn4:2.5.verse: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

dn4:2.6.verse: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

dn4:2.7.verse: It’s good to see such perfected ones.”

dn4:2.8.verse: Then, exiting Campā, they formed into companies and headed to the Gaggarā Lotus Pond.

dn4:3.1.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Soṇadaṇḍa had retired to the upper floor of his stilt longhouse for his midday nap.

dn4:3.2.verse: He saw the brahmins and householders heading for the lotus pond,

dn4:3.4.verse: “My butler, why are the brahmins and householders headed for the Gaggarā Lotus Pond?”

dn4:3.5.verse: “The ascetic Gotama has arrived at Campā and is staying on the banks of the Gaggarā Lotus Pond.

dn4:3.7.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

dn4:3.8.verse: They’re going to see that worthy Gotama.”

dn4:3.9.verse: “Well then, go to the brahmins and householders and say to them:

dn4:3.11.verse: you to wait, as he will also go to see the ascetic Gotama.’”

dn4:3.12.verse: “Yes, worthy sir,” replied the butler, and did as he was asked.

dn4:4.1.verse: Now at that time around five hundred brahmins from abroad were residing in Campā on some business.

dn4:4.3.verse: the brahmin Soṇadaṇḍa was going to see the ascetic Gotama.

dn4:4.4.verse: They approached Soṇadaṇḍa and said to him,

dn4:4.5.verse: “Is it really true that you are going to see the ascetic Gotama?”

dn4:5.2.verse: It’s not appropriate for you to go to see the ascetic Gotama.

dn4:5.3.verse: For if you do so, your reputation will diminish and his will increase.

dn4:5.4.verse: For this reason it’s not appropriate for you to go to see the ascetic Gotama;

dn4:5.5.verse: it’s appropriate that he comes to see you.

dn4:5.6.verse: You are well born on both your mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a pure vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

dn4:5.7.verse: For this reason it’s not appropriate for you to go to see the ascetic Gotama;

dn4:5.8.verse: it’s appropriate that he comes to see you.

dn4:5.10.verse: You recite and remember the hymns, and have mastered the three Vedas, together with their vocabularies and ritual performance, their phonology and word classification, and the testaments as fifth. You know them word-by-word, and their grammar. You are well versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man. …

dn4:5.11.verse: You are attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty. You have divine looks and lustre, remarkable to behold. …

dn4:5.12.verse: You are ethical, mature in ethical conduct. …

dn4:5.13.verse: You’re a good speaker who enunciates well, with a polished, clear, and articulate voice that expresses the meaning. …

dn4:5.14.verse: You’re the tutor of tutors for many, and teach three hundred young students to recite the hymns. Many students come from various districts and countries for the sake of the hymns, wishing to learn the hymns. …

dn4:5.15.verse: You’re old, elderly and senior, advanced in years, and have reached the final stage of life.

dn4:5.16.verse: The ascetic Gotama is young, and has newly gone forth. …

dn4:5.17.verse: You’re honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed by King Bimbisāra of Magadha …

dn4:5.19.verse: You live in Campā, a crown property given by King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, teeming with living creatures, full of hay, wood, water, and grain, a royal park endowed to a brahmin.

dn4:5.21.verse: For this reason, too, it’s not appropriate for you to go to see the ascetic Gotama;

dn4:5.22.verse: it’s appropriate that he comes to see you.”

dn4:6.1.verse: When they had spoken, Soṇadaṇḍa said to those brahmins:

dn4:6.2.verse: “Well then, gentlemen, listen to why it’s appropriate for me to go to see the ascetic Gotama,

dn4:6.3.verse: and it’s not appropriate for him to come to see me.

dn4:6.4.verse: He is well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

dn4:6.5.verse: For this reason it’s not appropriate for the ascetic Gotama to come to see me;

dn4:6.6.verse: rather, it’s appropriate for me to go to see him.

dn4:6.7.verse: When he went forth he abandoned a large family circle. …

dn4:6.8.verse: When he went forth he abandoned abundant gold, both coined and uncoined, stored above and below ground. …

dn4:6.9.verse: He went forth from the lay life to homelessness while still a youth, young, with pristine black hair, blessed with youth, in the prime of life. …

dn4:6.10.verse: Though his mother and father wished otherwise, weeping with tearful faces, he shaved off his hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and went forth from the lay life to homelessness. …

dn4:6.11.verse: He is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty. He has divine looks and lustre, remarkable to behold. …

dn4:6.12.verse: He is ethical, possessing ethical conduct that is noble and skillful. …

dn4:6.13.verse: He’s a good speaker who enunciates well, with a polished, clear, and articulate voice that expresses the meaning. …

dn4:6.15.verse: He has ended sensual desire, and is rid of caprice. …

dn4:6.16.verse: He teaches the efficacy of deeds and action. He doesn’t wish any harm upon the community of brahmins. …

dn4:6.17.verse: He went forth from an eminent family of unbroken aristocratic lineage. …

dn4:6.18.verse: He went forth from a rich, affluent, and wealthy family. …

dn4:6.19.verse: People come from distant lands and distant countries to question him. …

dn4:6.20.verse: Many thousands of deities have gone for refuge for life to him. …

dn4:6.22.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’ …

dn4:6.23.verse: He has the thirty-two marks of a great man. …

dn4:6.24.verse: He is welcoming, congenial, polite, smiling, open, the first to speak. …

dn4:6.25.verse: He’s honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed by the four assemblies. …

dn4:6.26.verse: Many gods and humans are devoted to him. …

dn4:6.27.verse: While he is residing in a village or town, non-human entities do not harass them. …

dn4:6.28.verse: He leads an order and a community, and tutors a community, and is said to be the best of the various religious founders. He didn’t come by his fame in the same ways as those other ascetics and brahmins.

dn4:6.29.verse: Rather, he came by his fame due to his supreme knowledge and conduct. …

dn4:6.30.verse: King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha and his wives and children have gone for refuge for life to the ascetic Gotama. …

dn4:6.31.verse: King Pasenadi of Kosala and his wives and children have gone for refuge for life to the ascetic Gotama. …

dn4:6.32.verse: The brahmin Pokkharasāti and his wives and children have gone for refuge for life to the ascetic Gotama. …

dn4:6.33.verse: He’s honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed by King Bimbisāra of Magadha …

dn4:6.36.verse: The ascetic Gotama has arrived at Campā and is staying at the Gaggarā Lotus Pond.

dn4:6.37.verse: Any ascetic or brahmin who comes to stay in our village district is our guest,

dn4:6.38.verse: and should be honored and respected as such.

dn4:6.41.verse: For this reason, too, it’s not appropriate for the worthy Gotama to come to see me;

dn4:6.42.verse: rather, it’s appropriate for me to go to see him.

dn4:6.43.verse: This is the extent of the worthy Gotama’s praise that I have memorized. But his praises are not confined to this,

dn4:6.44.verse: for the praise of the worthy Gotama is limitless.”

dn4:6.45.verse: When he had spoken, those brahmins said to him,

dn4:6.46.verse: “According to Soṇadaṇḍa’s praises, if the worthy Gotama were staying within a hundred leagues, it’d be worthwhile for a faithful gentleman to go to see him, even if he had to carry his own provisions in a knapsack.”

dn4:6.47.verse: “Well then, gentlemen, let’s all go to see the ascetic Gotama.”

dn4:7.1.verse: Then Soṇadaṇḍa together with a large group of brahmins approached the Gaggarā Lotus Pond.

dn4:8.1.verse: But as he reached the far side of the forest, this thought came to mind,

dn4:8.2.verse: “Suppose I was to ask the ascetic Gotama a question.

dn4:8.4.verse: ‘Brahmin, you shouldn’t ask your question like that. This is how you should ask it.’ And the assembly might disparage me for that:

dn4:8.5.verse: ‘Soṇadaṇḍa is foolish and incompetent. He’s not able to ask the ascetic Gotama a rational question.’

dn4:8.6.verse: And when you’re disparaged by the assembly, your reputation diminishes.

dn4:8.7.verse: When your reputation diminishes, your wealth also diminishes.

dn4:8.8.verse: But my wealth relies on my reputation.

dn4:8.9.verse: Or if the ascetic Gotama asks me a question, I might not satisfy him with my answer.

dn4:8.11.verse: ‘Brahmin, you shouldn’t answer the question like that. This is how you should answer it.’ And the assembly might disparage me for that:

dn4:8.12.verse: ‘Soṇadaṇḍa is foolish and incompetent. He’s not able to satisfy the ascetic Gotama’s mind with his answer.’

dn4:8.13.verse: And when you’re disparaged by the assembly, your reputation diminishes.

dn4:8.14.verse: When your reputation diminishes, your wealth also diminishes.

dn4:8.15.verse: But my wealth relies on my reputation.

dn4:8.16.verse: On the other hand, if I were to turn back after having come so far without having seen the ascetic Gotama, the assembly might disparage me for that:

dn4:8.17.verse: ‘Soṇadaṇḍa is foolish and incompetent. He’s stuck-up and scared. He doesn’t dare to go and see the ascetic Gotama. For how on earth can he turn back after having come so far without having seen the ascetic Gotama!’

dn4:8.18.verse: And when you’re disparaged by the assembly, your reputation diminishes.

dn4:8.19.verse: When your reputation diminishes, your wealth also diminishes.

dn4:8.20.verse: But my wealth relies on my reputation.”

dn4:9.1.verse: Then Soṇadaṇḍa went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

dn4:9.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side.

dn4:9.3.verse: Before sitting down to one side, some of the brahmins and householders of Campā bowed, some exchanged greetings and polite conversation, some held up their cupped palms toward the Buddha, some announced their name and clan, while some kept silent.

dn4:10.1.verse: But while sitting there, Soṇadaṇḍa continued to be plagued by many second thoughts. He thought,

dn4:10.16.verse: “If only the ascetic Gotama would ask me about my own tutor’s scriptural heritage of the three Vedas! Then I could definitely satisfy his mind with my answer.”

dn4:11.1.verse: Then, knowing Soṇadaṇḍa’s train of thought, it occurred to the Buddha,

dn4:11.2.verse: “This brahmin Soṇadaṇḍa is troubled by his own thoughts.

dn4:11.3.verse: Why don’t I ask him about his own tutor’s scriptural heritage of the three Vedas?”

dn4:11.5.verse: “Brahmin, how many factors must a brahmin possess for the brahmins to describe him as a brahmin;

dn4:11.6.verse: and so that when he says ‘I am a brahmin’ he speaks rightly, without falling into falsehood?”

dn4:12.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama has asked me about exactly what I wanted, what I wished for, what I desired, what I yearned for; that is, my own scriptural heritage.

dn4:12.4.verse: I can definitely satisfy his mind with my answer.”

dn4:13.1.verse: Then Soṇadaṇḍa straightened his back, looked around the assembly, and said to the Buddha,

dn4:13.2.verse: “Worthy Gotama, a brahmin must possess five factors for the brahmins to describe him as a brahmin;

dn4:13.3.verse: and so that when he says ‘I am a brahmin’ he speaks rightly, without falling into falsehood.

dn4:13.5.verse: It’s when a brahmin is well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

dn4:13.6.verse: He recites and remembers the hymns, and has mastered the three Vedas, together with their vocabularies and ritual performance, their phonology and word classification, and the testaments as fifth. He knows them word-by-word, and their grammar. He is well versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man.

dn4:13.7.verse: He is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty. He has divine looks and lustre, remarkable to behold.

dn4:13.8.verse: He is ethical, mature in ethical conduct.

dn4:13.9.verse: He’s astute and intelligent, being the first or second to hold the sacrificial ladle.

dn4:13.10.verse: These are the five factors which a brahmin must possess for the brahmins to describe him as a brahmin;

dn4:13.11.verse: and so that when he says ‘I am a brahmin’ he speaks rightly, without falling into falsehood.”

dn4:14.1.verse: “But brahmin, is it possible to set aside one of these five factors and still rightly describe someone as a brahmin?”

dn4:14.4.verse: We could leave appearance out of the five factors.

dn4:14.10.verse: A brahmin must possess the remaining four factors for the brahmins to rightly describe him as a brahmin.”

dn4:15.1.verse: “But brahmin, is it possible to set aside one of these four factors and still rightly describe someone as a brahmin?”

dn4:15.4.verse: We could leave the hymns out of the four factors.

dn4:15.5.verse: For what do the hymns matter?

dn4:15.9.verse: A brahmin must possess the remaining three factors for the brahmins to rightly describe him as a brahmin.”

dn4:16.1.verse: “But brahmin, is it possible to set aside one of these three factors and still rightly describe someone as a brahmin?”

dn4:16.4.verse: We could leave birth out of the three factors.

dn4:16.6.verse: It’s when a brahmin is ethical, mature in ethical conduct;

dn4:16.7.verse: and he’s astute and intelligent, being the first or second to hold the sacrificial ladle.

dn4:16.8.verse: A brahmin must possess these two factors for the brahmins to rightly describe him as a brahmin.”

dn4:17.1.verse: When he had spoken, those brahmins said to him,

dn4:17.2.verse: “Please don’t say that, worthy Soṇadaṇḍa, please don’t say that!

dn4:17.3.verse: You’re just condemning appearance, the hymns, and birth! You’re totally going over to the ascetic Gotama’s doctrine!”

dn4:18.1.verse: So the Buddha said to them,

dn4:18.3.verse: Soṇadaṇḍa is unlearned, a poor speaker, witless, and not capable of debating with me about this, then leave him aside and you can debate with me.

dn4:18.5.verse: he’s learned, a good speaker who enunciates well, astute, and capable of debating with me about this, then you should stand aside and let him debate with me.”

dn4:19.1.verse: When he said this, Soṇadaṇḍa said to the Buddha,

dn4:19.2.verse: “Let it be, worthy Gotama, be silent. I myself will respond to them in a legitimate manner.”

dn4:19.3.verse: Then he said to those brahmins,

dn4:19.4.verse: “Don’t say this, good fellows, don’t say this:

dn4:19.5.verse: ‘You’re just condemning appearance, the hymns, and birth! You’re totally going over to the ascetic Gotama’s doctrine!’

dn4:19.6.verse: I’m not condemning appearance, hymns, or birth.”

dn4:20.1.verse: Now at that time Soṇadaṇḍa’s nephew, the young student Aṅgaka was sitting in that assembly.

dn4:20.2.verse: Then Soṇadaṇḍa said to those brahmins,

dn4:20.3.verse: “Gentlemen, do you see my nephew, the young student Aṅgaka?”

dn4:20.5.verse: “Aṅgaka is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty. He has divine looks and lustre, remarkable to behold. There’s no one in this assembly so good-looking, apart from the ascetic Gotama.

dn4:20.6.verse: Aṅgaka recites and remembers the hymns, and has mastered the three Vedas, together with their vocabularies and ritual performance, their phonology and word classification, and the testaments as fifth. He knows them word-by-word, and their grammar. He is well versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man.

dn4:20.7.verse: And I am the one who teaches him the hymns.

dn4:20.8.verse: Aṅgaka is well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

dn4:20.9.verse: And I know his mother and father.

dn4:20.10.verse: But if Aṅgaka were to kill living creatures, steal, commit adultery, lie, and drink liquor, then what’s the use of his appearance, his hymns, or his birth?

dn4:20.11.verse: It’s when a brahmin is ethical, mature in ethical conduct;

dn4:20.12.verse: and he’s astute and intelligent, being the first or second to hold the sacrificial ladle.

dn4:20.13.verse: A brahmin must possess these two factors for the brahmins to rightly describe him as a brahmin.”

dn4:21.0.verse: 6. The Discussion of Ethics and Wisdom

dn4:21.1.verse: “But brahmin, is it possible to set aside one of these two factors and still rightly describe someone as a brahmin?”

dn4:21.4.verse: For wisdom is cleansed by ethics, and ethics are cleansed by wisdom.

dn4:21.5.verse: Ethics and wisdom always go together.

dn4:21.6.verse: An ethical person is wise, and a wise person ethical.

dn4:21.7.verse: And ethics and wisdom are said to be the best things in the world.

dn4:21.8.verse: It’s just like when you clean one hand with the other, or clean one foot with the other.

dn4:21.9.verse: In the same way, wisdom is cleansed by ethics, and ethics are cleansed by wisdom.

dn4:21.10.verse: Ethics and wisdom always go together.

dn4:21.11.verse: An ethical person is wise, and a wise person ethical.

dn4:21.12.verse: And ethics and wisdom are said to be the best things in the world.”

dn4:22.1.verse: “That’s so true, brahmin, that’s so true! For wisdom is cleansed by ethics, and ethics are cleansed by wisdom.

dn4:22.2.verse: Ethics and wisdom always go together.

dn4:22.3.verse: An ethical person is wise, and a wise person ethical.

dn4:22.4.verse: And ethics and wisdom are said to be the best things in the world.

dn4:22.5.verse: It’s just like when you clean one hand with the other, or clean one foot with the other.

dn4:22.6.verse: In the same way, wisdom is cleansed by ethics, and ethics are cleansed by wisdom.

dn4:22.7.verse: Ethics and wisdom always go together.

dn4:22.8.verse: An ethical person is wise, and a wise person ethical.

dn4:22.9.verse: And ethics and wisdom are said to be the best things in the world.

dn4:22.10.verse: But what, brahmin, is that ethical conduct?

dn4:22.12.verse: “That’s all I know about this matter, worthy Gotama.

dn4:22.13.verse: May the worthy Gotama himself please clarify the meaning of this.”

dn4:23.1.verse: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

dn4:23.4.verse: “It’s when a Realized One arises in the world, perfected, a fully awakened Buddha …

dn4:23.5.verse: That’s how a mendicant is accomplished in ethics.

dn4:23.6.verse: This, brahmin, is that ethical conduct. …

dn4:23.7.verse: They enter and remain in the first absorption …

dn4:23.11.verse: They project and extend the mind toward knowledge and vision …

dn4:23.13.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’

dn4:24.0.verse: 7. Soṇadaṇḍa Declares Himself a Lay Follower

dn4:24.1.verse: When he had spoken, Soṇadaṇḍa said to the Buddha,

dn4:24.3.verse: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the Teaching clear in many ways.

dn4:24.4.verse: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

dn4:24.5.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.

dn4:24.6.verse: Would you and the mendicant Saṅgha please accept tomorrow’s meal from me?”

dn4:24.8.verse: Then, knowing that the Buddha had consented, Soṇadaṇḍa rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

dn4:24.9.verse: And when the night had passed Soṇadaṇḍa had delicious fresh and cooked foods prepared in his own home. Then he had the Buddha informed of the time, saying,

dn4:24.10.verse: “It’s time, worthy Gotama, the meal is ready.”

dn4:25.1.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of Soṇadaṇḍa together with the mendicant Saṅgha, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

dn4:25.2.verse: Then Soṇadaṇḍa served and satisfied the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha with his own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

dn4:26.1.verse: When the Buddha had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, Soṇadaṇḍa took a low seat and sat to one side.

dn4:26.2.verse: Seated to one side he said to the Buddha:

dn4:26.3.verse: “Worthy Gotama, if, when I have gone to an assembly, I rise from my seat and bow to the worthy Gotama, that assembly might disparage me for that.

dn4:26.4.verse: And when you’re disparaged by the assembly, your reputation diminishes.

dn4:26.5.verse: When your reputation diminishes, your wealth also diminishes.

dn4:26.6.verse: But my wealth relies on my reputation.

dn4:26.7.verse: If, when I have gone to an assembly, I raise my cupped palms, please take it that I have risen from my seat.

dn4:26.8.verse: And if I undo my turban, please take it that I have bowed.

dn4:26.9.verse: And the worthy Gotama, if, when I am in a carriage, I get down from my carriage and bow to the worthy Gotama, that assembly might disparage me for that.

dn4:26.12.verse: If, when I am in a carriage, I hold up my goad, please take it that I have got down from my carriage.

dn4:26.13.verse: And if I lower my parasol, please take it that I have bowed.”

dn4:27.1.verse: Then the Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired the brahmin Soṇadaṇḍa with a Dhamma talk, after which he rose from his seat and left.

dn5:1.0.verse: 1. The Brahmins and Householders of Khāṇumata

dn5:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Magadhans together with a large Saṅgha of five hundred mendicants when he arrived at a village of the Magadhan brahmins named Khāṇumata.

dn5:1.3.verse: There he stayed nearby at Ambalaṭṭhikā.

dn5:1.4.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Kūṭadanta was living in Khāṇumata. It was a crown property given by King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, teeming with living creatures, full of hay, wood, water, and grain, a royal park endowed to a brahmin.

dn5:1.5.verse: Now at that time Kūṭadanta had prepared a great sacrifice.

dn5:1.6.verse: Bulls, bullocks, heifers, goats and rams—seven hundred of each—had been led to the post for the sacrifice.

dn5:2.1.verse: The brahmins and householders of Khāṇumata heard:

dn5:2.2.verse: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—has arrived at Khāṇumata and is staying at Ambalaṭṭhikā.

dn5:2.4.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

dn5:2.5.verse: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

dn5:2.6.verse: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

dn5:2.7.verse: It’s good to see such perfected ones.”

dn5:2.8.verse: Then, exiting Khāṇumata, they formed into companies and headed to Ambalaṭṭhikā.

dn5:3.1.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Kūṭadanta had retired to the upper floor of his stilt longhouse for his midday nap.

dn5:3.2.verse: He saw the brahmins and householders heading for Ambalaṭṭhikā,

dn5:3.4.verse: “My butler, why are the brahmins and householders headed for Ambalaṭṭhikā?”

dn5:3.5.verse: “The ascetic Gotama has arrived at Khāṇumata and is staying at Ambalaṭṭhikā.

dn5:3.7.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

dn5:3.8.verse: They’re going to see that worthy Gotama.”

dn5:4.3.verse: the ascetic Gotama knows how to accomplish the sacrifice with three modes and sixteen accessories.

dn5:4.5.verse: but I wish to perform a great sacrifice.

dn5:4.6.verse: Why don’t I ask him how to accomplish the sacrifice with three modes and sixteen accessories?”

dn5:4.8.verse: “Well then, go to the brahmins and householders and say to them:

dn5:4.10.verse: you to wait, as he will also go to see the ascetic Gotama.’”

dn5:4.11.verse: “Yes, worthy sir,” replied the butler, and did as he was asked.

dn5:5.1.verse: Now at that time several hundred brahmins were residing in Khāṇumata

dn5:5.2.verse: thinking to participate in Kūṭadanta’s sacrifice.

dn5:5.4.verse: Kūṭadanta was going to see the ascetic Gotama.

dn5:5.5.verse: They approached Kūṭadanta and said to him:

dn5:5.6.verse: “Is it really true that you are going to see the ascetic Gotama?”

dn5:6.2.verse: It’s not appropriate for you to go to see the ascetic Gotama.

dn5:6.3.verse: For if you do so, your reputation will diminish and his will increase.

dn5:6.4.verse: For this reason it’s not appropriate for you to go to see the ascetic Gotama;

dn5:6.5.verse: it’s appropriate that he comes to see you.

dn5:6.6.verse: You are well born on both your mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

dn5:6.7.verse: For this reason it’s not appropriate for you to go to see the ascetic Gotama;

dn5:6.8.verse: it’s appropriate that he comes to see you.

dn5:6.9.verse: You’re rich, affluent, and wealthy, with lots of property and assets, and lots of money and grain …

dn5:6.10.verse: You recite and remember the hymns, and have mastered the three Vedas, together with their vocabularies and ritual performance, their phonology and word classification, and the testaments as fifth. You know them word-by-word, and their grammar. You are well versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man. …

dn5:6.11.verse: You are attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty. You have divine looks and lustre, remarkable to behold. …

dn5:6.12.verse: You are ethical, mature in ethical conduct. …

dn5:6.13.verse: You’re a good speaker who enunciates well, with a polished, clear, and articulate voice that expresses the meaning. …

dn5:6.14.verse: You’re the tutor of tutors for many, and teach three hundred young students to recite the hymns. Many students come from various districts and countries for the sake of the hymns, wishing to learn the hymns. …

dn5:6.15.verse: You’re old, elderly and senior, advanced in years, and have reached the final stage of life.

dn5:6.16.verse: The ascetic Gotama is young, and has newly gone forth. …

dn5:6.17.verse: You’re honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed by King Bimbisāra of Magadha …

dn5:6.19.verse: You live in Khāṇumata, a crown property given by King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, teeming with living creatures, full of hay, wood, water, and grain, a royal park endowed to a brahmin.

dn5:6.20.verse: For this reason it’s not appropriate for you to go to see the ascetic Gotama;

dn5:6.21.verse: it’s appropriate that he comes to see you.”

dn5:7.1.verse: When they had spoken, Kūṭadanta said to those brahmins:

dn5:7.2.verse: “Well then, gentlemen, listen to why it’s appropriate for me to go to see the ascetic Gotama,

dn5:7.3.verse: and it’s not appropriate for him to come to see me.

dn5:7.4.verse: He is well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

dn5:7.5.verse: For this reason it’s not appropriate for the ascetic Gotama to come to see me;

dn5:7.6.verse: rather, it’s appropriate for me to go to see him.

dn5:7.7.verse: When he went forth he abandoned a large family circle. …

dn5:7.8.verse: When he went forth he abandoned abundant gold, both coined and uncoined, stored above and below ground. …

dn5:7.9.verse: He went forth from the lay life to homelessness while still a youth, young, with pristine black hair, blessed with youth, in the prime of life. …

dn5:7.10.verse: Though his mother and father wished otherwise, weeping with tearful faces, he shaved off his hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and went forth from the lay life to homelessness. …

dn5:7.11.verse: He is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty. He has divine looks and lustre, remarkable to behold. …

dn5:7.12.verse: He is ethical, possessing ethical conduct that is noble and skillful. …

dn5:7.13.verse: He’s a good speaker who enunciates well, with a polished, clear, and articulate voice that expresses the meaning. …

dn5:7.15.verse: He has ended sensual desire, and is rid of caprice. …

dn5:7.16.verse: He teaches the efficacy of deeds and action. He doesn’t wish any harm upon the community of brahmins. …

dn5:7.17.verse: He went forth from an eminent family of unbroken aristocratic lineage. …

dn5:7.18.verse: He went forth from a rich, affluent, and wealthy family. …

dn5:7.19.verse: People come from distant lands and distant countries to question him. …

dn5:7.20.verse: Many thousands of deities have gone for refuge for life to him. …

dn5:7.22.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’ …

dn5:7.23.verse: He has the thirty-two marks of a great man. …

dn5:7.24.verse: He is welcoming, congenial, polite, smiling, open, the first to speak. …

dn5:7.25.verse: He’s honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed by the four assemblies. …

dn5:7.26.verse: Many gods and humans are devoted to him. …

dn5:7.27.verse: While he is residing in a village or town, non-human entities do not harass them. …

dn5:7.28.verse: He leads an order and a community, and tutors a community, and is said to be the best of the various religious founders. He didn’t come by his fame in the same ways as those other ascetics and brahmins.

dn5:7.29.verse: Rather, he came by his fame due to his supreme knowledge and conduct. …

dn5:7.30.verse: King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha and his wives and children have gone for refuge for life to the ascetic Gotama. …

dn5:7.31.verse: King Pasenadi of Kosala and his wives and children have gone for refuge for life to the ascetic Gotama. …

dn5:7.32.verse: The brahmin Pokkharasāti and his wives and children have gone for refuge for life to the ascetic Gotama. …

dn5:7.33.verse: He’s honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed by King Bimbisāra of Magadha …

dn5:7.36.verse: The ascetic Gotama has arrived at Khāṇumata and is staying at Ambalaṭṭhikā.

dn5:7.37.verse: Any ascetic or brahmin who comes to stay in our village district is our guest,

dn5:7.38.verse: and should be honored and respected as such.

dn5:7.41.verse: For this reason, too, it’s not appropriate for Worthy Gotama to come to see me;

dn5:7.42.verse: rather, it’s appropriate for me to go to see him.

dn5:7.43.verse: This is the extent of the worthy Gotama’s praise that I have memorized. But his praises are not confined to this,

dn5:7.44.verse: for the praise of the worthy Gotama is limitless.”

dn5:7.45.verse: When he had spoken, those brahmins said to him,

dn5:7.46.verse: “According to Kūṭadanta’s praises, if the worthy Gotama were staying within a hundred leagues, it’d be worthwhile for a faithful gentleman to go to see him, even if he had to carry his own provisions in a knapsack.”

dn5:7.47.verse: “Well then, gentlemen, let’s all go to see the ascetic Gotama.”

dn5:8.0.verse: 4. The Story of King Mahāvijita’s Sacrifice

dn5:8.1.verse: Then Kūṭadanta together with a large group of brahmins went to Ambalaṭṭhikā, approached the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

dn5:8.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side.

dn5:8.3.verse: Before sitting down to one side, some of the brahmins and householders of Khāṇumata bowed, some exchanged greetings and polite conversation, some held up their cupped palms toward the Buddha, some announced their name and clan, while some kept silent.

dn5:9.3.verse: you know how to accomplish the sacrifice with three modes and sixteen accessories.

dn5:9.5.verse: but I wish to perform a great sacrifice.

dn5:9.6.verse: Please teach me how to accomplish the sacrifice with three modes and sixteen accessories.”

dn5:9.7.verse: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

dn5:10.1.verse: “Once upon a time, brahmin, there was a king named Mahāvijita. He was rich, affluent, and wealthy, with lots of gold and silver, lots of property and assets, lots of money and grain, and a full treasury and storehouses.

dn5:10.2.verse: Then as King Mahāvijita was in private retreat this thought came to his mind:

dn5:10.3.verse: ‘I have achieved human wealth, and reign after conquering this vast territory. Why don’t I hold a large sacrifice? That will be for my lasting welfare and happiness.’

dn5:10.4.verse: Then he summoned the brahmin high priest and said to him:

dn5:10.5.verse: ‘Just now, brahmin, as I was in private retreat this thought came to mind,

dn5:10.6.verse: “I have achieved human wealth, and reign after conquering this vast territory. Why don’t I perform a great sacrifice? That will be for my lasting welfare and happiness.”

dn5:10.7.verse: Brahmin, I wish to perform a great sacrifice.

dn5:10.8.verse: Please instruct me. It will be for my lasting welfare and happiness.’

dn5:11.1.verse: When he had spoken, the brahmin high priest said to him:

dn5:11.2.verse: ‘Sir, the king’s realm is harried and oppressed. Raiding of villages, towns, and cities has been seen, and infesting of highways.

dn5:11.3.verse: But if the king were to extract more taxes while his realm is thus harried and oppressed, he would not be doing his duty.

dn5:11.5.verse: “I’ll eradicate this plague of savages by execution or imprisonment or confiscation or condemnation or banishment!” But that’s not the right way to eradicate this plague of savages.

dn5:11.6.verse: Those who remain after the killing will return to harass the king’s realm.

dn5:11.7.verse: Rather, here is a plan, relying on which the plague of savages will be properly uprooted.

dn5:11.8.verse: So let the king provide seed and fodder for those in the realm who work in growing crops and raising cattle.

dn5:11.9.verse: Let the king provide funding for those who work in trade.

dn5:11.10.verse: Let the king guarantee food and wages for those in government service.

dn5:11.11.verse: Then the people, occupied with their own work, will not harass the realm.

dn5:11.12.verse: The king’s revenues will be great.

dn5:11.13.verse: When the country is secured as a sanctuary, free of being harried and oppressed, the happy people, with joy in their hearts, dancing with children at their breast, will dwell as if their houses were wide open.’

dn5:11.14.verse: The king agreed with the high priest’s advice and followed his recommendation.

dn5:11.19.verse: Then the king summoned the brahmin high priest and said to him:

dn5:11.20.verse: ‘I have eradicated the plague of savages. And relying on your plan my revenue is now great.

dn5:11.21.verse: Since the country is secured as a sanctuary, free of being harried and oppressed, the happy people, with joy in their hearts, dancing with children at their breast, dwell as if their houses were wide open.

dn5:11.22.verse: Brahmin, I wish to perform a great sacrifice.

dn5:11.23.verse: Please instruct me. It will be for my lasting welfare and happiness.’

dn5:12.1.verse: ‘In that case, let the king announce this throughout the realm to the aristocrat vassals of both town and country; the ministers and councillors of both town and country; the well-to-do brahmins of both town and country; and the well-off householders of both town and country.

dn5:12.2.verse: “I wish to perform a great sacrifice. Please grant your approval, worthy sirs; it will be for my lasting welfare and happiness.”’

dn5:12.3.verse: The king agreed with the high priest’s advice and followed his recommendation.

dn5:12.4.verse: And all of the people who were thus informed responded by saying:

dn5:12.5.verse: ‘May the king perform a sacrifice! It is time for a sacrifice, Great King.’

dn5:12.9.verse: And so these four consenting factions became accessories to the sacrifice.

dn5:13.2.verse: He was well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

dn5:13.3.verse: He was attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty. He had divine looks and lustre, remarkable to behold.

dn5:13.4.verse: He was rich, affluent, and wealthy, with lots of gold and silver, lots of property and assets, lots of money and grain, and a full treasury and storehouses.

dn5:13.5.verse: He was powerful, having an army of four divisions that was obedient and carried out instructions. He’d probably prevail over his enemies just with his reputation.

dn5:13.6.verse: He was faithful, generous, a donor, his door always open. He was a well-spring of support, making merit with ascetics and brahmins, for paupers, vagrants, supplicants, and beggars.

dn5:13.7.verse: He was very learned in diverse fields of learning. He understood the meaning of diverse statements, saying:

dn5:13.8.verse: ‘This is what that statement means; that is what this statement means.’

dn5:13.9.verse: He was astute, competent, and intelligent, able to think issues through as they bear upon the past, future, and present.

dn5:13.10.verse: These are the eight factors that King Mahāvijita possessed.

dn5:13.11.verse: And so these eight factors also became accessories to the sacrifice.

dn5:14.1.verse: And the brahmin high priest had four factors.

dn5:14.2.verse: He was well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

dn5:14.3.verse: He recited and remembered the hymns, and had mastered the three Vedas, together with their vocabularies and ritual performance, their phonology and word classification, and the testaments as fifth. He knew them word-by-word, and their grammar. He was well versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man.

dn5:14.4.verse: He was ethical, mature in ethical conduct.

dn5:14.5.verse: He was astute, competent, and intelligent, being the first or second to hold the sacrificial ladle.

dn5:14.6.verse: These are the four factors that the brahmin high priest possessed.

dn5:14.7.verse: And so these four factors also became accessories to the sacrifice.

dn5:15.1.verse: Next, before the sacrifice, the brahmin high priest taught the three modes to the king.

dn5:15.2.verse: ‘Now, though the king wants to perform a great sacrifice, he might have certain regrets, thinking:

dn5:15.3.verse: “I shall lose a great fortune,” or

dn5:15.5.verse: “I am losing a great fortune,” or

dn5:15.7.verse: “I have lost a great fortune.” But the king should not harbor such regrets.’

dn5:15.8.verse: These are the three modes that the brahmin high priest taught to the king before the sacrifice.

dn5:16.1.verse: Next, before the sacrifice, the brahmin high priest dispelled the king’s regret regarding the recipients in ten respects:

dn5:16.2.verse: ‘There will come to the sacrifice those who kill living creatures and those who refrain from killing living creatures.

dn5:16.3.verse: As to those who kill living creatures, the outcome of that is theirs alone.

dn5:16.4.verse: But as to those who refrain from killing living creatures, it is for their sakes that the king should sacrifice, relinquish, rejoice, and gain confidence in his heart.

dn5:16.5.verse: There will come to the sacrifice those who steal …

dn5:16.13.verse: have wrong view and those who have right view.

dn5:16.14.verse: As to those who have wrong view, the outcome of that is theirs alone.

dn5:16.15.verse: But as to those who have right view, it is for their sakes that the king should sacrifice, relinquish, rejoice, and gain confidence in his heart.’

dn5:16.16.verse: These are the ten respects in which the high priest dispelled the king’s regret regarding the recipients before the sacrifice.

dn5:17.1.verse: Next, while the king was performing the great sacrifice, the brahmin high priest educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired the king’s mind in sixteen respects:

dn5:17.2.verse: ‘Now, while the king is performing the great sacrifice, someone might say,

dn5:17.3.verse: “King Mahāvijita performs a great sacrifice, but he did not announce it to the aristocrat vassals of town and country.

dn5:17.4.verse: That’s the kind of great sacrifice that this king performs.”

dn5:17.5.verse: Those who speak against the king in this way have no legitimacy.

dn5:17.6.verse: For the king did indeed announce it to the aristocrat vassals of town and country.

dn5:17.7.verse: Let the king know this as a reason to sacrifice, relinquish, rejoice, and gain confidence in his heart.

dn5:17.8.verse: While the king is performing the great sacrifice, someone might say,

dn5:17.9.verse: “King Mahāvijita performs a great sacrifice, but he did not announce it to the aristocrat vassals; the ministers and councillors; the well-to-do brahmins; and the well-off householders. That’s the kind of great sacrifice that this king performs.”

dn5:17.10.verse: Those who speak against the king in this way have no legitimacy.

dn5:17.11.verse: For the king did indeed announce it to all these people.

dn5:17.12.verse: Let the king know this too as a reason to sacrifice, relinquish, rejoice, and gain confidence in his heart.

dn5:17.13.verse: While the king is performing the great sacrifice, someone might say

dn5:17.14.verse: that he does not possess the eight factors.

dn5:17.27.verse: Those who speak against the king in this way have no legitimacy.

dn5:17.28.verse: For the king does indeed possess the eight factors.

dn5:17.29.verse: Let the king know this too as a reason to sacrifice, relinquish, rejoice, and gain confidence in his heart.

dn5:17.30.verse: While the king is performing the great sacrifice, someone might say

dn5:17.31.verse: that the high priest does not possess the four factors.

dn5:17.42.verse: Those who speak against the king in this way have no legitimacy.

dn5:17.43.verse: For the high priest does indeed possess the four factors.

dn5:17.44.verse: Let the king know this too as a reason to sacrifice, relinquish, rejoice, and gain confidence in his heart.’

dn5:17.45.verse: These are the sixteen respects in which the high priest educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired the king’s mind while he was performing the sacrifice.

dn5:18.1.verse: And brahmin, in that sacrifice no cattle were killed, no goats or sheep were killed, and no chickens or pigs were killed. There was no slaughter of various kinds of creatures. No trees were felled for the sacrificial post. No grass was reaped to strew over the place of sacrifice.

dn5:18.2.verse: No bondservants, servants, or workers did their jobs under threat of punishment and danger, weeping with tearful faces.

dn5:18.3.verse: Those who wished to work did so, while those who did not wish to did not.

dn5:18.4.verse: They did the work they wanted to, and did not do what they didn’t want to.

dn5:18.5.verse: The sacrifice was completed with just ghee, oil, butter, curds, honey, and molasses.

dn5:19.1.verse: Then the aristocrat vassals, ministers and councillors, well-to-do brahmins, and well-off householders came to the king bringing abundant wealth and said,

dn5:19.2.verse: ‘Your Majesty, this abundant wealth is specially for you alone; may Your Majesty accept it!’

dn5:19.3.verse: ‘There’s enough raised for me through regular taxes. Let this be for you; and here, take even more!’

dn5:19.5.verse: When the king turned them down, they withdrew to one side to think up a plan,

dn5:19.6.verse: ‘It wouldn’t be proper for us to take this abundant wealth back to our own homes.

dn5:19.7.verse: King Mahāvijita is performing a great sacrifice. Let us make an offering as an auxiliary sacrifice.’

dn5:20.1.verse: Then the aristocrat vassals of town and country set up gifts to the east of the sacrificial enclosure.

dn5:20.2.verse: The ministers and councillors of town and country set up gifts to the south of the sacrificial enclosure.

dn5:20.3.verse: The well-to-do brahmins of town and country set up gifts to the west of the sacrificial enclosure.

dn5:20.4.verse: The well-off householders of town and country set up gifts to the north of the sacrificial enclosure.

dn5:20.5.verse: And brahmin, in that sacrifice too no cattle were killed, no goats were killed, and no chickens or pigs were killed. There was no slaughter of various kinds of creatures. No trees were felled for the sacrificial post. No grass was reaped to strew over the place of sacrifice.

dn5:20.6.verse: No bondservants, servants, or workers did their jobs under threat of punishment and danger, weeping with tearful faces.

dn5:20.7.verse: Those who wished to work did so, while those who did not wish to did not.

dn5:20.8.verse: They did the work they wanted to, and did not do what they didn’t want to.

dn5:20.9.verse: The sacrifice was completed with just ghee, oil, butter, curds, honey, and molasses.

dn5:20.10.verse: And so there were four consenting factions, eight factors possessed by King Mahāvijita, four factors possessed by the high priest,

dn5:20.12.verse: Brahmin, this is called the sacrifice accomplished with three modes and sixteen accessories.”

dn5:21.1.verse: When he said this, those brahmins made an uproar,

dn5:21.2.verse: “Hooray for such sacrifice! Hooray for the accomplishment of such sacrifice!”

dn5:21.3.verse: But the brahmin Kūṭadanta sat in silence.

dn5:21.4.verse: So those brahmins said to him,

dn5:21.5.verse: “How can you not applaud the ascetic Gotama’s fine words?”

dn5:21.6.verse: “It’s not that I don’t applaud what he said.

dn5:21.7.verse: If anyone didn’t applaud such fine words, their head would explode!

dn5:21.8.verse: But, gentlemen, it occurs to me that

dn5:21.9.verse: the ascetic Gotama does not say:

dn5:21.10.verse: ‘So I have heard’ or ‘It ought to be like this.’

dn5:21.12.verse: ‘So it was then, this is how it was then.’

dn5:21.14.verse: the ascetic Gotama at that time must have been King Mahāvijita, the owner of the sacrifice, or else the brahmin high priest who facilitated the sacrifice for him.

dn5:21.15.verse: Does the worthy Gotama recall having performed such a sacrifice, or having facilitated it, and then, when his body broke up, after death, being reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm?”

dn5:21.16.verse: “I do recall that, brahmin. For I myself was the brahmin high priest at that time who facilitated the sacrifice.”

dn5:22.0.verse: 5. A Regular Gift as a Propitious Sacrifice.

dn5:22.1.verse: “But Worthy Gotama, apart from that sacrifice accomplished with three modes and sixteen accessories, is there any other sacrifice that has fewer obligations and undertakings, yet is more fruitful and beneficial?”

dn5:22.4.verse: “The regular gifts as propitious sacrifice given specially to ethical renunciates;

dn5:22.5.verse: this sacrifice, brahmin, has fewer obligations and undertakings, yet is more fruitful and beneficial.”

dn5:23.1.verse: “What is the cause, Worthy Gotama, what is the reason why those regular gifts as propitious sacrifice have fewer obligations and undertakings, yet are more fruitful and beneficial, compared with the sacrifice accomplished with three modes and sixteen accessories?”

dn5:23.2.verse: “Because neither perfected ones nor those who are on the path to perfection will attend such a sacrifice.

dn5:23.4.verse: Because beatings and throttlings are seen there.

dn5:23.5.verse: But the regular gifts as propitious sacrifice given specially to ethical renunciates;

dn5:23.6.verse: perfected ones and those who are on the path to perfection will attend such a sacrifice.

dn5:23.8.verse: Because no beatings and throttlings are seen there.

dn5:23.9.verse: This is the cause, brahmin, this is the reason why those regular gifts as propitious sacrifice have fewer obligations and undertakings, yet are more fruitful and beneficial, compared with the sacrifice accomplished with three modes and sixteen accessories.”

dn5:24.1.verse: “But Worthy Gotama, apart from that sacrifice accomplished with three modes and sixteen accessories and those regular gifts as propitious sacrifice, is there any other sacrifice that has fewer obligations and undertakings, yet is more fruitful and beneficial?”

dn5:24.4.verse: “When someone gives a dwelling specially for the Saṅgha of the four quarters.”

dn5:25.1.verse: “But is there any other sacrifice that has fewer obligations and undertakings, yet is more fruitful and beneficial?”

dn5:25.4.verse: “When someone with confident heart goes for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.”

dn5:26.1.verse: “But is there any other sacrifice that has fewer obligations and undertakings, yet is more fruitful and beneficial?”

dn5:26.4.verse: “When someone with a confident heart undertakes the training rules

dn5:26.5.verse: to refrain from killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.”

dn5:27.1.verse: “But is there any other sacrifice that has fewer obligations and undertakings, yet is more fruitful and beneficial?”

dn5:27.4.verse: It’s when a Realized One arises in the world, perfected, a fully awakened Buddha …

dn5:27.5.verse: That’s how a mendicant is accomplished in ethics. …

dn5:27.6.verse: They enter and remain in the first absorption …

dn5:27.7.verse: This sacrifice has fewer obligations and undertakings than the former, yet is more fruitful and beneficial. …

dn5:27.8.verse: They enter and remain in the second absorption …

dn5:27.11.verse: This sacrifice has fewer obligations and undertakings than the former, yet is more fruitful and beneficial. …

dn5:27.12.verse: They project and extend the mind toward knowledge and vision …

dn5:27.13.verse: This sacrifice has fewer obligations and undertakings than the former, yet is more fruitful and beneficial.

dn5:27.14.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’

dn5:27.15.verse: This sacrifice has fewer obligations and undertakings than the former, yet is more fruitful and beneficial.

dn5:27.16.verse: And, brahmin, there is no other accomplishment of sacrifice which is better and finer than this.”

dn5:28.0.verse: 6. Kūṭadanta Declares Himself a Lay Follower

dn5:28.1.verse: When he had spoken, Kūṭadanta said to the Buddha,

dn5:28.3.verse: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the Teaching clear in many ways.

dn5:28.4.verse: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

dn5:28.5.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.

dn5:28.6.verse: And these bulls, bullocks, heifers, goats, and rams—seven hundred of each—I release them, I grant them life! Let them eat green grass and drink cool water, and may a cool breeze blow upon them!”

dn5:29.0.verse: 7. The Realization of the Fruit of Stream-Entry

dn5:29.1.verse: Then the Buddha taught Kūṭadanta step by step, with

dn5:29.2.verse: a talk on giving, ethical conduct, and heaven. He revealed the drawbacks of sensual pleasures, so sordid and corrupt, and the benefit of renunciation.

dn5:29.3.verse: And when he knew that Kūṭadanta’s mind was ready, pliable, rid of hindrances, elated, and confident he revealed the special teaching of the Buddhas:

dn5:29.4.verse: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

dn5:29.5.verse: Just as a clean cloth rid of stains would properly absorb dye,

dn5:29.6.verse: in that very seat the stainless, immaculate vision of the Dhamma arose in the brahmin Kūṭadanta:

dn5:29.7.verse: “Everything that is liable to arise is liable to cease.”

dn5:30.1.verse: Then Kūṭadanta saw, attained, understood, and fathomed the Dhamma. He went beyond doubt, got rid of indecision, and became self-assured and independent of others regarding the Teacher’s instructions. He said to the Buddha,

dn5:30.2.verse: “Would the worthy Gotama together with the mendicant Saṅgha please accept tomorrow’s meal from me?”

dn5:30.4.verse: Then, knowing that the Buddha had consented, Kūṭadanta rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

dn5:30.5.verse: And when the night had passed Kūṭadanta had delicious fresh and cooked foods prepared in his own sacrificial enclosure. Then he had the Buddha informed of the time, saying,

dn5:30.6.verse: “It’s time, worthy Gotama, the meal is ready.”

dn5:30.7.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the sacrificial enclosure of Kūṭadanta together with the mendicant Saṅgha, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

dn5:30.8.verse: Then Kūṭadanta served and satisfied the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha with his own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

dn5:30.9.verse: When the Buddha had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, Kūṭadanta took a low seat and sat to one side.

dn5:30.10.verse: Then the Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired him with a Dhamma talk, after which he rose from his seat and left.

dn6:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

dn6:1.3.verse: Now at that time several brahmin emissaries from Kosala and Magadha were residing in Vesālī on some business.

dn6:1.5.verse: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—is staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

dn6:1.7.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

dn6:1.8.verse: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

dn6:1.9.verse: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

dn6:1.10.verse: It’s good to see such perfected ones.”

dn6:2.1.verse: Then they went to the hall with the peaked roof in the Great Wood to see the Buddha.

dn6:2.2.verse: Now, at that time Venerable Nāgita was the Buddha’s attendant.

dn6:2.3.verse: The brahmin emissaries went up to him and said,

dn6:2.4.verse: “Worthy Nāgita, where is the worthy Gotama at present?

dn6:2.5.verse: For we want to see him.”

dn6:2.6.verse: “It’s the wrong time to see the Buddha; he is on retreat.”

dn6:2.7.verse: So right there the brahmin emissaries sat down to one side, thinking,

dn6:2.8.verse: “We’ll go only after we’ve seen the worthy Gotama.”

dn6:3.1.verse: Oṭṭhaddha the Licchavi together with a large assembly of Licchavis also approached Nāgita at the hall with the peaked roof. He bowed, stood to one side, and said to Nāgita,

dn6:3.2.verse: “Honorable Nāgita, where is the Blessed One at present, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha?

dn6:3.3.verse: For we want to see him.”

dn6:3.4.verse: “It’s the wrong time to see the Buddha; he is on retreat.”

dn6:3.5.verse: So right there Oṭṭhaddha also sat down to one side, thinking,

dn6:3.6.verse: “I’ll go only after I’ve seen the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.”

dn6:4.1.verse: Then the novice Sīha approached Nāgita. He bowed, stood to one side, and said to Nāgita,

dn6:4.2.verse: “Honorable Kassapa, these several brahmin emissaries from Kosala and Magadha, and also Oṭṭhaddha the Licchavi together with a large assembly of Licchavis, have come here to see the Buddha. It’d be good if these people got to see the Buddha.”

dn6:4.3.verse: “Well then, Sīha, tell the Buddha yourself.”

dn6:4.4.verse: “Yes, sir,” replied Sīha. He went to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and told him of the people waiting to see him, adding:

dn6:4.6.verse: “Sir, it’d be good if these people got to see the Buddha.”

dn6:4.7.verse: “Well then, Sīha, spread out a seat in the shade of the dwelling.”

dn6:4.8.verse: “Yes, sir,” replied Sīha, and he did so.

dn6:4.9.verse: Then the Buddha left his dwelling and sat in the shade of the dwelling on the seat spread out.

dn6:5.1.verse: Then the brahmin emissaries went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

dn6:5.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side.

dn6:5.3.verse: Oṭṭhaddha the Licchavi together with a large assembly of Licchavis also went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. Oṭṭhaddha said to the Buddha, “Sir, a few days ago Sunakkhatta the Licchavi came to me and said:

dn6:5.4.verse: ‘Mahāli, soon I will have been living in dependence on the Buddha for three years. I see heavenly sights that are pleasant, sensual, and arousing, but I don’t hear heavenly sounds that are pleasant, sensual, and arousing.’

dn6:5.5.verse: The heavenly sounds that Sunakkhatta cannot hear: do such sounds really exist or not?”

dn6:5.7.verse: “Such sounds really do exist, but Sunakkhatta cannot hear them.”

dn6:6.1.verse: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why Sunakkhatta cannot hear them, even though they really do exist?”

dn6:6.2.verse: “Mahāli, take a mendicant who has developed immersion to the eastern quarter in one aspect: so as to see heavenly sights but not to hear heavenly sounds.

dn6:6.3.verse: When they have developed immersion for that purpose,

dn6:6.4.verse: they see heavenly sights but don’t hear heavenly sounds.

dn6:6.6.verse: Because that is how it is for a mendicant who develops immersion in that way.

dn6:7.1.verse: Furthermore, take a mendicant who has developed immersion to the southern quarter in one aspect …

dn6:7.8.verse: That is how it is for a mendicant who develops immersion in that way.

dn6:8.1.verse: Take a mendicant who has developed immersion to the eastern quarter in one aspect: so as to hear heavenly sounds but not to see heavenly sights.

dn6:8.2.verse: When they have developed immersion for that purpose,

dn6:8.3.verse: they hear heavenly sounds but don’t see heavenly sights.

dn6:8.5.verse: Because that is how it is for a mendicant who develops immersion in that way.

dn6:9.1.verse: Furthermore, take a mendicant who has developed immersion to the southern quarter in one aspect …

dn6:9.8.verse: That is how it is for a mendicant who develops immersion in that way.

dn6:10.1.verse: Take a mendicant who has developed immersion to the eastern quarter in both aspects: so as to hear heavenly sounds and see heavenly sights.

dn6:10.2.verse: When they have developed immersion for that purpose,

dn6:10.3.verse: they see heavenly sights and hear heavenly sounds.

dn6:10.5.verse: Because that is how it is for a mendicant who develops immersion in that way.

dn6:11.1.verse: Furthermore, take a mendicant who has developed immersion to the southern quarter in both aspects …

dn6:11.8.verse: That is how it is for a mendicant who develops immersion in that way.

dn6:11.9.verse: This is the cause, Mahāli, this is the reason why Sunakkhatta cannot hear heavenly sounds that are pleasant, sensual, and arousing, even though they really do exist.”

dn6:12.1.verse: “Surely the mendicants must lead the spiritual life under the Buddha for the sake of realizing such a development of immersion?”

dn6:12.2.verse: “No, Mahāli, the mendicants don’t lead the spiritual life under me for the sake of realizing such a development of immersion.

dn6:12.3.verse: There are other things that are finer, for the sake of which the mendicants lead the spiritual life under me.”

dn6:13.1.verse: “But sir, what are those finer things?”

dn6:13.2.verse: “Firstly, Mahāli, with the ending of three fetters a mendicant is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

dn6:13.3.verse: This is one of the finer things for the sake of which the mendicants lead the spiritual life under me.

dn6:13.4.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant—with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion—is a once-returner. They come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.

dn6:13.5.verse: This too is one of the finer things.

dn6:13.6.verse: Furthermore, with the ending of the five lower fetters, a mendicant is reborn spontaneously and will become extinguished there, not liable to return from that world.

dn6:13.7.verse: This too is one of the finer things.

dn6:13.8.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and lives having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

dn6:13.9.verse: This too is one of the finer things.

dn6:13.10.verse: These are the finer things, for the sake of which the mendicants lead the spiritual life under me.”

dn6:14.1.verse: “But, sir, is there a path and a practice for realizing these things?”

dn6:14.4.verse: “It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

dn6:14.5.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

dn6:14.6.verse: This is the path and the practice for realizing these things.

dn6:15.1.verse: This one time, Mahāli, I was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

dn6:15.3.verse: the wanderer Muṇḍiya and Jāliya, the pupil of the wood-bowl ascetic—came and exchanged greetings with me.

dn6:15.4.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they stood to one side and said to me:

dn6:15.5.verse: ‘Reverend Gotama, are the soul and the body one and the same, or is the soul one thing, the body another?’

dn6:16.1.verse: ‘Well then, reverends, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.’

dn6:16.4.verse: ‘Take the case when a Realized One arises in the world, perfected, a fully awakened Buddha …

dn6:16.5.verse: That’s how a mendicant is accomplished in ethics. …

dn6:16.7.verse: They enter and remain in the first absorption.

dn6:16.8.verse: When a mendicant knows and sees like this, would it be appropriate to say of them:

dn6:16.9.verse: “The soul and the body are one and the same” or “The soul is one thing, the body another”?’

dn6:16.12.verse: ‘But reverends, I know and see like this.

dn6:16.14.verse: “The soul and the body are one and the same” or “The soul and the body are different things”. …

dn6:17.1.verse: They enter and remain in the second absorption …

dn6:17.4.verse: When a mendicant knows and sees like this, would it be appropriate to say of them:

dn6:17.5.verse: “The soul and the body are one and the same” or “The soul is one thing, the body another”?’

dn6:17.8.verse: ‘But reverends, I know and see like this.

dn6:17.10.verse: “The soul and the body are one and the same” or “The soul is one thing, the body another”. …

dn6:18.1.verse: They project and extend the mind toward knowledge and vision …

dn6:18.2.verse: When a mendicant knows and sees like this, would it be appropriate to say of them:

dn6:18.3.verse: “The soul and the body are one and the same” or “The soul is one thing, the body another”?’

dn6:18.7.verse: ‘But reverends, I know and see like this.

dn6:18.9.verse: “The soul and the body are one and the same” or “The soul is one thing, the body another”. …

dn6:19.1.verse: They understand: “… there is nothing further for this place.”

dn6:19.2.verse: When a mendicant knows and sees like this, would it be appropriate to say of them:

dn6:19.3.verse: “The soul and the body are one and the same” or “The soul is one thing, the body another”?’

dn6:19.6.verse: ‘But reverends, I know and see like this.

dn6:19.8.verse: “The soul and the body are one and the same” or “The soul is one thing, the body another”.’”

dn6:19.9.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

dn6:19.10.verse: Satisfied, Oṭṭhaddha the Licchavi approved what the Buddha said.

dn7:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

dn7:1.3.verse: Now at that time two renunciates—

dn7:1.4.verse: the wanderer Muṇḍiya and Jāliya, the pupil of the wood-bowl ascetic—came to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

dn7:1.5.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they stood to one side and said to the Buddha,

dn7:1.6.verse: “Reverend Gotama, are the soul and the body one and the same, or is the soul one thing, the body another?”

dn7:1.7.verse: “Well then, reverends, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

dn7:2.1.verse: “Take the case when a Realized One arises in the world, perfected, a fully awakened Buddha …

dn7:2.2.verse: That’s how a mendicant is accomplished in ethics. …

dn7:2.4.verse: They enter and remain in the first absorption …

dn7:2.5.verse: When a mendicant knows and sees like this, would it be appropriate to say of them:

dn7:2.6.verse: ‘The soul and the body are one and the same’ or ‘The soul is one thing, the body another’?”

dn7:2.9.verse: “But reverends, I know and see like this.

dn7:2.11.verse: ‘The soul and the body are one and the same’ or ‘The soul is one thing, the body another’. …

dn7:3.1.verse: They enter and remain in the second absorption …
