dn16:5.22.2.verse: “If I have the Mallas pay homage to the Buddha one by one, they won’t be finished before first light.

dn16:5.22.3.verse: I’d better separate them family by family and then have them pay homage, saying:

dn16:5.22.4.verse: ‘Sir, the Malla named so-and-so with children, wives, retinue, and ministers bows with his head to your feet.’”

dn16:5.22.5.verse: And so that’s what he did.

dn16:5.22.7.verse: So by this means Ānanda got the Mallas to finish paying homage to the Buddha in the first watch of the night.

dn16:5.23.1.verse: Now at that time a wanderer named Subhadda was residing near Kusinārā.

dn16:5.23.3.verse: on that very day, in the last watch of the night, will be the full extinguishment of the ascetic Gotama.

dn16:5.23.5.verse: “I have heard that brahmins of the past who were elderly and senior, the tutors of tutors, said:

dn16:5.23.6.verse: ‘Only rarely do Realized Ones arise in the world, perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas.’

dn16:5.23.7.verse: And this very day, in the last watch of the night, will be the full extinguishment of the ascetic Gotama.

dn16:5.23.8.verse: This state of uncertainty has come up in me.

dn16:5.23.9.verse: I am quite confident that the Buddha is capable of teaching me so that I can give up this state of uncertainty.”

dn16:5.24.1.verse: Then Subhadda went to the Mallian sal grove at Upavattana, approached Ānanda, and said to him,

dn16:5.24.2.verse: “Worthy Ānanda, I have heard that brahmins of the past who were elderly and senior, the tutors of tutors, said:

dn16:5.24.3.verse: ‘Only rarely do Realized Ones arise in the world, perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas.’

dn16:5.24.4.verse: And this very day, in the last watch of the night, will be the full extinguishment of the ascetic Gotama.

dn16:5.24.5.verse: This state of uncertainty has come up in me.

dn16:5.24.6.verse: I am quite confident that the Buddha is capable of teaching me so that I can give up this state of uncertainty.

dn16:5.24.7.verse: Worthy Ānanda, please let me see the ascetic Gotama.”

dn16:5.24.8.verse: When he had spoken, Ānanda said,

dn16:5.24.9.verse: “Enough, Reverend Subhadda, do not trouble the Realized One. He is tired.”

dn16:5.24.11.verse: For a third time, Subhadda asked Ānanda, and a third time Ānanda refused.

dn16:5.25.1.verse: The Buddha heard that discussion between Ānanda and Subhadda.

dn16:5.25.3.verse: “Enough, Ānanda, don’t obstruct Subhadda; let him see the Realized One.

dn16:5.25.4.verse: For whatever he asks me, he will only be looking to understand, not to trouble me.

dn16:5.25.5.verse: And he will quickly understand any answer I give to his question.”

dn16:5.25.6.verse: So Ānanda said to the wanderer Subhadda,

dn16:5.25.7.verse: “Go, Reverend Subhadda, the Buddha is making time for you.”

dn16:5.26.1.verse: Then the wanderer Subhadda went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him. When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

dn16:5.26.2.verse: “Worthy Gotama, there are those ascetics and brahmins who lead an order and a community, and tutor a community. They’re well-known and famous religious founders, deemed holy by many people.

dn16:5.26.3.verse: Namely: Pūraṇa Kassapa, the bamboo-staffed ascetic Gosāla, Ajita of the hair blanket, Pakudha Kaccāyana, Sañjaya Belaṭṭhiputta, and the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan.

dn16:5.26.4.verse: According to their own claims, did all of them have direct knowledge, or none of them, or only some?”

dn16:5.26.7.verse: I shall teach you the Dhamma.

dn16:5.26.8.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

dn16:5.27.1.verse: “Subhadda, in whatever teaching and training the noble eightfold path is not found, there is no ascetic found, no second ascetic, no third ascetic, and no fourth ascetic.

dn16:5.27.2.verse: In whatever teaching and training the noble eightfold path is found, there is an ascetic found, a second ascetic, a third ascetic, and a fourth ascetic.

dn16:5.27.3.verse: In this teaching and training the noble eightfold path is found. Only here is there an ascetic, here a second ascetic, here a third ascetic, and here a fourth ascetic. Other sects are empty of ascetics.

dn16:5.27.4.verse: Were these mendicants to practice well, the world would not be empty of perfected ones.

dn16:5.27.5.verse: I was twenty-nine years of age, Subhadda,

dn16:5.27.6.verse: when I went forth to discover what is skillful.

dn16:5.27.9.verse: Teacher of the references for the systematic teaching:

dn16:5.27.10.verse: outside of here there is no ascetic,

dn16:5.27.14.verse: Other sects are empty of ascetics.

dn16:5.27.15.verse: Were these mendicants to practice well, the world would not be empty of perfected ones.”

dn16:5.28.1.verse: When he had spoken, Subhadda said to the Buddha,

dn16:5.28.3.verse: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, the Buddha has made the teaching clear in many ways.

dn16:5.28.4.verse: I go for refuge to the Buddha, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

dn16:5.28.5.verse: Sir, may I receive the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence?”

dn16:5.29.1.verse: “Subhadda, if someone formerly ordained in another sect wishes to take the going forth, the ordination in this teaching and training, they must spend four months on probation. When four months have passed, if the mendicants are satisfied, they’ll give the going forth, the ordination into monkhood.

dn16:5.29.2.verse: However, I have recognized individual differences in this matter.”

dn16:5.29.3.verse: “Sir, if four months probation are required in such a case, I’ll spend four years on probation. When four years have passed, if the mendicants are satisfied, let them give me the going forth, the ordination into monkhood.”

dn16:5.29.4.verse: Then the Buddha said to Ānanda,

dn16:5.29.5.verse: “Well then, Ānanda, give Subhadda the going forth.”

dn16:5.30.2.verse: “You’re so fortunate, Reverand Ānanda, so very fortunate,

dn16:5.30.3.verse: to be anointed here in the Teacher’s presence as his pupil!”

dn16:5.30.4.verse: And the wanderer Subhadda received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

dn16:5.30.5.verse: Not long after his ordination, Venerable Subhadda, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

dn16:5.30.6.verse: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

dn16:5.30.7.verse: And Venerable Subhadda became one of the perfected.

dn16:5.30.8.verse: He was the last personal disciple of the Buddha.

dn16:6.1.1.verse: Then the Buddha addressed Venerable Ānanda:

dn16:6.1.2.verse: “Now, Ānanda, some of you might think:

dn16:6.1.3.verse: ‘The teacher’s dispensation has passed. Now we have no Teacher.’

dn16:6.1.4.verse: But you should not see it like this.

dn16:6.1.5.verse: The teaching and training that I have taught and pointed out for you shall be your Teacher after my passing.

dn16:6.2.1.verse: After my passing, mendicants ought not address each other as ‘reverend’, as they do today.

dn16:6.2.2.verse: A more senior mendicant ought to address a more junior mendicant by name or clan, or by saying ‘reverend’.

dn16:6.2.3.verse: A more junior mendicant ought to address a more senior mendicant using ‘sir’ or ‘venerable’.

dn16:6.3.1.verse: If it wishes, after my passing the Saṅgha may abolish the lesser and minor training rules.

dn16:6.4.1.verse: After my passing, give the divine punishment to the mendicant Channa.”

dn16:6.4.2.verse: “But sir, what is the divine punishment?”

dn16:6.4.4.verse: but the mendicants should not correct, advise, or instruct him.”

dn16:6.5.1.verse: Then the Buddha said to the mendicants,

dn16:6.5.2.verse: “Perhaps even a single mendicant has doubt or uncertainty regarding the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice. So ask, mendicants! Don’t regret it later, thinking:

dn16:6.5.3.verse: ‘We were in the Teacher’s presence and we weren’t able to ask the Buddha a question.’”

dn16:6.5.4.verse: When this was said, the mendicants kept silent.

dn16:6.6.2.verse: For a third time the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

dn16:6.6.3.verse: “Perhaps even a single mendicant has doubt or uncertainty regarding the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice. So ask, mendicants! Don’t regret it later, thinking:

dn16:6.6.4.verse: ‘We were in the Teacher’s presence and we weren’t able to ask the Buddha a question.’”

dn16:6.6.5.verse: For a third time, the mendicants kept silent.

dn16:6.6.6.verse: Then the Buddha said to the mendicants,

dn16:6.6.7.verse: “Mendicants, perhaps you don’t ask out of respect for the Teacher. So let a friend tell a friend.”

dn16:6.6.8.verse: When this was said, the mendicants kept silent.

dn16:6.6.9.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha,

dn16:6.6.10.verse: “It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing! I am quite confident that there is not even a single mendicant in this Saṅgha who has doubt or uncertainty regarding the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice.”

dn16:6.6.11.verse: “Ānanda, you speak out of faith. But the Realized One knows that there is not even a single mendicant in this Saṅgha who has doubt or uncertainty regarding the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice.

dn16:6.6.12.verse: Even the last of these five hundred mendicants is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

dn16:6.7.1.verse: Then the Buddha said to the mendicants:

dn16:6.7.2.verse: “Come now, mendicants, I say to you all:

dn16:6.7.4.verse: These were the Realized One’s last words.

dn16:6.8.1.verse: Then the Buddha entered the first absorption. Emerging from that, he entered the second absorption. Emerging from that, he successively entered into and emerged from the third absorption, the fourth absorption, the dimension of infinite space, the dimension of infinite consciousness, the dimension of nothingness, and the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. Then he entered the cessation of perception and feeling.

dn16:6.8.2.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda said to Venerable Anuruddha,

dn16:6.8.3.verse: “Honorable Anuruddha, has the Buddha become fully quenched?”

dn16:6.8.4.verse: “No, Reverend Ānanda. He has entered the cessation of perception and feeling.”

dn16:6.9.1.verse: Then the Buddha emerged from the cessation of perception and feeling and entered the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. Emerging from that, he successively entered into and emerged from the dimension of nothingness, the dimension of infinite consciousness, the dimension of infinite space, the fourth absorption, the third absorption, the second absorption, and the first absorption. Emerging from that, he successively entered into and emerged from the second absorption and the third absorption. Then he entered the fourth absorption. Emerging from that the Buddha immediately became fully extinguished.

dn16:6.10.1.verse: When the Buddha was fully quenched, along with the full extinguishment there was a great earthquake, awe-inspiring and hair-raising, and thunder cracked the sky.

dn16:6.10.14.verse: When the Buddha was fully quenched, Venerable Anuruddha spoke this verse:

dn16:6.10.16.verse: for the unaffected one of steady heart.

dn16:6.10.19.verse: He put up with painful feelings

dn16:6.10.23.verse: When the Buddha was fully quenched, Venerable Ānanda spoke this verse:

dn16:6.10.26.verse: When the Buddha, endowed with all fine qualities,

dn16:6.10.28.verse: When the Buddha was fully quenched, some of the mendicants there who were not free of desire, with arms raised, falling down like their feet were chopped off, rolling back and forth, lamented: “Too soon the Blessed One has become fully quenched! Too soon the Holy One has become fully quenched! Too soon the Eye of the World has vanished!”

dn16:6.10.29.verse: But the mendicants who were free of desire endured, mindful and aware, thinking,

dn16:6.10.30.verse: “Conditions are impermanent. How could it possibly be otherwise?”

dn16:6.11.2.verse: “Enough, reverends, do not grieve or lament.

dn16:6.11.3.verse: Did the Buddha not prepare us for this when he explained that

dn16:6.11.4.verse: we must be parted and separated from all we hold dear and beloved?

dn16:6.11.5.verse: How could it possibly be so that what is born, created, conditioned, and liable to wear out should not wear out?

dn16:6.11.7.verse: “But sir, what kind of deities are you thinking of?”

dn16:6.11.8.verse: “There are, Ānanda, deities—both in space and on the earth—who are aware of the earth. With hair disheveled and arms raised, they fall down like their feet were chopped off, rolling back and forth, lamenting:

dn16:6.11.9.verse: ‘Too soon the Blessed One has become fully quenched! Too soon the Holy One has become fully quenched! Too soon the Eye of the World has vanished!’

dn16:6.11.12.verse: But the deities who are free of desire endure, mindful and aware, thinking:

dn16:6.11.13.verse: ‘Conditions are impermanent. How could it possibly be otherwise?’”

dn16:6.11.14.verse: Ānanda and Anuruddha spent the rest of the night talking about Dhamma.

dn16:6.12.2.verse: “Go, Ānanda, into Kusinārā and inform the Mallas:

dn16:6.12.3.verse: ‘Vāseṭṭhas, the Buddha has become fully quenched.

dn16:6.12.5.verse: “Yes, sir,” replied Ānanda. Then, in the morning, he robed up and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Kusinārā with a companion.

dn16:6.12.6.verse: Now at that time the Mallas of Kusinārā were sitting together at the town hall still on the same business.

dn16:6.12.7.verse: Ānanda went up to them, and announced,

dn16:6.12.8.verse: “Vāseṭṭhas, the Buddha has become fully quenched.

dn16:6.12.10.verse: When they heard what Ānanda had to say, the Mallas, their sons, daughters-in-law, and wives became distraught, saddened, and grief-stricken. And some, with hair disheveled and arms raised, falling down like their feet were chopped off, rolling back and forth, lamented,

dn16:6.12.11.verse: “Too soon the Blessed One has become fully quenched! Too soon the Holy One has become fully quenched! Too soon the Eye of the World has vanished!”

dn16:6.13.0.verse: 37. The Rites of Venerating the Buddha’s Corpse

dn16:6.13.1.verse: Then the Mallas ordered their men,

dn16:6.13.2.verse: “So then, lads, collect fragrances and garlands, and all the musical instruments in Kusinārā.”

dn16:6.13.3.verse: Then—taking those fragrances and garlands, all the musical instruments, and five hundred pairs of garments—they went to the Mallian sal grove at Upavattana and approached the Buddha’s corpse. They spent the day honoring, respecting, revering, and venerating the Buddha’s corpse with dance and song and music and garlands and fragrances, and making awnings and setting up pavilions.

dn16:6.13.5.verse: “It’s too late to cremate the Buddha’s corpse today. Let’s do it tomorrow.”

dn16:6.13.6.verse: But they spent the next day the same way, and so too the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth days.

dn16:6.14.1.verse: Then on the seventh day they thought,

dn16:6.14.2.verse: “Honoring, respecting, revering, and venerating the Buddha’s corpse with dance and song and music and garlands and fragrances, let us carry it to the south of the town, and cremate it there outside the town.”

dn16:6.14.3.verse: Now at that time eight of the leading Mallas, having bathed their heads and dressed in unworn clothes, said,

dn16:6.14.4.verse: “We shall lift the Buddha’s corpse.” But they were unable to do so.

dn16:6.14.6.verse: “What is the cause, Honorable Anuruddha, what is the reason why these eight Mallian chiefs are unable to lift the Buddha’s corpse?”

dn16:6.14.8.verse: “Vāseṭṭhas, you have one plan, but the deities have a different one.”

dn16:6.15.1.verse: “But sir, what is the deities’ plan?”

dn16:6.15.3.verse: carry the Buddha’s corpse to the south of the town while venerating it with dance and song and music and garlands and fragrances, and cremate it there outside the town.

dn16:6.15.5.verse: carry the Buddha’s corpse to the north of the town while venerating it with heavenly dance and song and music and garlands and fragrances. Then they plan to enter the town by the northern gate, carry it through the center of the town, leave by the eastern gate, and cremate it there at the Mallian shrine named Coronation.”

dn16:6.15.6.verse: “Sir, let it be as the deities plan.”

dn16:6.16.1.verse: Now at that time the whole of Kusinārā was covered knee-deep with the flowers of the Flame Tree, without gaps even on the filth and rubbish heaps.

dn16:6.16.2.verse: Then the deities and the Mallas of Kusinārā carried the Buddha’s corpse to the north of the town while venerating it with heavenly and human dance and song and music and garlands and fragrances. Then they entered the town by the northern gate, carried it through the center of the town, left by the eastern gate, and deposited the corpse there at the Mallian shrine named Coronation.

dn16:6.17.1.verse: Then the Mallas said to Ānanda,

dn16:6.17.2.verse: “Honorable Ānanda, how do we proceed when it comes to the Realized One’s corpse?”

dn16:6.17.3.verse: “Proceed in the same way as they do for the corpse of a wheel-turning monarch.”

dn16:6.17.4.verse: “But how do they proceed with a wheel-turning monarch’s corpse?”

dn16:6.17.5.verse: “They wrap a wheel-turning monarch’s corpse with unworn cloth, then with uncarded cotton, then again with unworn cloth.

dn16:6.17.6.verse: In this way they wrap the corpse with five hundred double-layers. Then they place it in an iron casket filled with oil and close it up with another casket. Then, having built a funeral pyre out of all kinds of aromatics, they cremate the corpse.

dn16:6.17.7.verse: They build a monument for the wheel-turning monarch at the crossroads.

dn16:6.17.8.verse: That’s how they proceed with a wheel-turning monarch’s corpse.

dn16:6.17.9.verse: Proceed in the same way with the Realized One’s corpse.

dn16:6.17.10.verse: A monument for the Realized One is to be built at the crossroads.

dn16:6.17.11.verse: When someone there lifts up garlands or fragrance or powder, or bows, or inspires confidence in their heart, that will be for their lasting welfare and happiness.”

dn16:6.18.1.verse: Then the Mallas ordered their men,

dn16:6.18.3.verse: So the Mallas wrapped the Buddha’s corpse,

dn16:6.18.4.verse: and placed it in an iron casket filled with oil. Then, having built a funeral pyre out of all kinds of aromatics, they lifted the corpse on to the pyre.

dn16:6.19.1.verse: Now at that time Venerable Mahākassapa was traveling along the road from Pāvā to Kusinārā together with a large Saṅgha of five hundred mendicants.

dn16:6.19.2.verse: Then he left the road and sat at the root of a tree.

dn16:6.19.3.verse: Now at that time a certain Ājīvaka ascetic had picked up a Flame Tree flower in Kusinārā and was traveling along the road to Pāvā.

dn16:6.19.4.verse: Mahākassapa saw him coming off in the distance and said to him,

dn16:6.19.5.verse: “Reverend, might you know about our Teacher?”

dn16:6.19.6.verse: “Yes, reverend. Seven days ago the ascetic Gotama was fully quenched.

dn16:6.19.7.verse: From there I picked up this Flame Tree flower.”

dn16:6.19.8.verse: Some of the mendicants there who were not free of desire, with arms raised, falling down like their feet were chopped off, rolling back and forth, lamented,

dn16:6.19.9.verse: “Too soon the Blessed One has become fully quenched! Too soon the Holy One has become fully quenched! Too soon the Eye of the World has vanished!”

dn16:6.19.10.verse: But the mendicants who were free of desire endured, mindful and aware, thinking,

dn16:6.19.11.verse: “Conditions are impermanent. How could it possibly be otherwise?”

dn16:6.20.1.verse: Now at that time a monk named Subhadda, who had gone forth when old, was sitting in that assembly.

dn16:6.20.3.verse: “Enough, reverends, do not grieve or lament. We’re well rid of that Great Ascetic. And we are harried:

dn16:6.20.4.verse: ‘This is allowable for you; this is not allowable for you.’

dn16:6.20.5.verse: Well, now we shall do what we want and not do what we don’t want.”

dn16:6.20.6.verse: Then Venerable Mahākassapa addressed the mendicants,

dn16:6.20.7.verse: “Enough, reverends, do not grieve or lament.

dn16:6.20.8.verse: Did the Buddha not prepare us for this when he explained that

dn16:6.20.9.verse: we must be parted and separated from all we hold dear and beloved?

dn16:6.20.10.verse: How could it possibly be so that what is born, created, conditioned, and liable to wear out should not wear out, even the Realized One’s body?”

dn16:6.21.1.verse: Now at that time four of the leading Mallas, having bathed their heads and dressed in unworn clothes, said,

dn16:6.21.2.verse: “We shall light the Buddha’s funeral pyre.” But they were unable to do so.

dn16:6.21.4.verse: “What is the cause, Venerable Anuruddha, what is the reason why these four Mallian chiefs are unable to light the Buddha’s funeral pyre?”

dn16:6.21.6.verse: “Vāseṭṭhas, the deities have a different plan.”

dn16:6.21.7.verse: “But sir, what is the deities’ plan?”

dn16:6.21.9.verse: Venerable Mahākassapa is traveling along the road from Pāvā to Kusinārā together with a large Saṅgha of five hundred mendicants.

dn16:6.21.10.verse: The Buddha’s funeral pyre shall not burn until he bows with his head to the Buddha’s feet.”

dn16:6.21.11.verse: “Sir, let it be as the deities plan.”

dn16:6.22.1.verse: Then Venerable Mahākassapa arrived at the Mallian shrine named Coronation at Kusinārā and approached the Buddha’s funeral pyre. Arranging his robe over one shoulder and raising his joined palms, he respectfully circled the Buddha three times, keeping him on his right, and bowed with his head to the Buddha’s feet.

dn16:6.22.2.verse: And the five hundred mendicants did likewise.

dn16:6.22.3.verse: And when Mahākassapa and the five hundred mendicants bowed the Buddha’s funeral pyre burst into flames all by itself.

dn16:6.23.1.verse: And when the Buddha’s corpse was cremated no ash or soot was found from outer or inner skin, flesh, sinews, or synovial fluid.

dn16:6.23.3.verse: It’s like when ghee or oil blaze and burn, and neither ashes nor soot are found.

dn16:6.23.4.verse: In the same way, when the Buddha’s corpse was cremated no ash or soot was found from outer or inner skin, flesh, sinews, or synovial fluid.

dn16:6.23.6.verse: And of those five hundred pairs of garments only two were not burnt: the innermost and the outermost.

dn16:6.23.7.verse: But when the Buddha’s corpse was consumed the funeral pyre was extinguished by a stream of water that appeared in the sky,

dn16:6.23.8.verse: by water dripping from the sal trees,

dn16:6.23.9.verse: and by the Mallas’ fragrant water.

dn16:6.23.10.verse: Then the Mallas made a cage of spears for the Buddha’s relics in the town hall and surrounded it with a buttress of bows. For seven days they honored, respected, revered, and venerated them with dance and song and music and garlands and fragrances.

dn16:6.24.1.verse: King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha, heard

dn16:6.24.2.verse: that the Buddha had become fully quenched at Kusinārā.

dn16:6.24.3.verse: He sent an envoy to the Mallas of Kusinārā:

dn16:6.24.4.verse: “The Buddha was an aristocrat and so am I. I too deserve a share of the Buddha’s relics. I will build a monument for them and conduct a memorial service.”

dn16:6.24.5.verse: The Licchavis of Vesālī also heard

dn16:6.24.6.verse: that the Buddha had become fully quenched at Kusinārā.

dn16:6.24.7.verse: They sent an envoy to the Mallas of Kusinārā:

dn16:6.24.8.verse: “The Buddha was an aristocrat and so are we. We too deserve a share of the Buddha’s relics. We will build a monument for them and conduct a memorial service.”

dn16:6.24.9.verse: The Sakyans of Kapilavatthu also heard

dn16:6.24.10.verse: that the Buddha had become fully quenched at Kusinārā.

dn16:6.24.11.verse: They sent an envoy to the Mallas of Kusinārā:

dn16:6.24.12.verse: “The Buddha was our foremost relative. We too deserve a share of the Buddha’s relics. We will build a monument for them and conduct a memorial service.”

dn16:6.24.13.verse: The Bulis of Allakappa also heard

dn16:6.24.14.verse: that the Buddha had become fully quenched at Kusinārā.

dn16:6.24.15.verse: They sent an envoy to the Mallas of Kusinārā:

dn16:6.24.16.verse: “The Buddha was an aristocrat and so are we. We too deserve a share of the Buddha’s relics. We will build a monument for them and conduct a memorial service.”

dn16:6.24.17.verse: The Koliyans of Rāmagāma also heard

dn16:6.24.18.verse: that the Buddha had become fully quenched at Kusinārā.

dn16:6.24.19.verse: They sent an envoy to the Mallas of Kusinārā:

dn16:6.24.20.verse: “The Buddha was an aristocrat and so are we. We too deserve a share of the Buddha’s relics. We will build a monument for them and conduct a memorial service.”

dn16:6.24.21.verse: The brahmin of Veṭhadīpa also heard

dn16:6.24.22.verse: that the Buddha had become fully quenched at Kusinārā.

dn16:6.24.23.verse: He sent an envoy to the Mallas of Kusinārā:

dn16:6.24.24.verse: “The Buddha was an aristocrat and I am a brahmin. I too deserve a share of the Buddha’s relics. I will build a monument for them and conduct a memorial service.”

dn16:6.24.25.verse: The Mallas of Pāvā also heard

dn16:6.24.26.verse: that the Buddha had become fully quenched at Kusinārā.

dn16:6.24.27.verse: They sent an envoy to the Mallas of Kusinārā:

dn16:6.24.28.verse: “The Buddha was an aristocrat and so are we. We too deserve a share of the Buddha’s relics. We will build a monument for them and conduct a memorial service.”

dn16:6.25.1.verse: When they had spoken, the Mallas of Kusinārā said to those various groups:

dn16:6.25.2.verse: “The Buddha was fully quenched in our village district. We will not give away a share of his relics.”

dn16:6.25.3.verse: Then Doṇa the brahmin said to those various groups:

dn16:6.25.4.verse: “Hear, worthy sirs, a single word from me.

dn16:6.25.6.verse: It would not be good to fight over

dn16:6.25.7.verse: a share of the supreme individual’s relics.

dn16:6.25.8.verse: Let us make eight portions, worthy sirs,

dn16:6.25.10.verse: Let there be monuments far and wide,

dn16:6.25.11.verse: so many folk may gain faith in the Clear-eyed One!”

dn16:6.25.12.verse: “Well then, brahmin, you yourself should fairly divide the Buddha’s relics in eight portions.”

dn16:6.25.13.verse: “Yes, worthy sirs,” replied Doṇa to those various groups. He divided the relics as asked and said to them,

dn16:6.25.14.verse: “Worthy sirs, please give me the urn, and I shall build a monument for it and conduct a memorial service.”

dn16:6.25.15.verse: So they gave Doṇa the urn.

dn16:6.26.3.verse: They sent an envoy to the Mallas of Kusinārā:

dn16:6.26.4.verse: “The Buddha was an aristocrat, and so are we. We too deserve a share of the Buddha’s relics. We will build a monument for them and conduct a memorial service.”

dn16:6.26.5.verse: “There is no portion of the Buddha’s relics left, they have already been portioned out.

dn16:6.27.10.verse: and the Moriyas of Pippalivana built monuments for them and conducted memorial services.

dn16:6.27.11.verse: Thus there were eight monuments for the relics, a ninth for the urn, and a tenth for the embers.

dn16:6.27.12.verse: That is how it was in the old days.

dn16:6.28.1.verse: There were eight shares of the Clear-eyed One’s relics.

dn16:6.28.2.verse: Seven were worshiped in the Black Plum Tree Land.

dn16:6.28.3.verse: But one share of the most excellent of men

dn16:6.28.4.verse: was worshiped in Rāmagāma by a dragon king.

dn16:6.28.5.verse: One tooth is venerated by the gods of the Third Heaven,

dn16:6.28.6.verse: and one is worshiped in the city of Gandhāra;

dn16:6.28.7.verse: another one in the realm of the Kaliṅga King,

dn16:6.28.8.verse: and one is worshiped by a dragon king.

dn16:6.28.9.verse: Through their glory this rich earth

dn16:6.28.10.verse: is adorned with the best of offerings.

dn16:6.28.12.verse: is well honored by the honorable.

dn16:6.28.13.verse: It’s venerated by lords of gods, dragons, and fairies;

dn16:6.28.14.verse: and likewise venerated by the finest lords of men.

dn16:6.28.15.verse: Honor it with cupped palms when you get the chance,

dn16:6.28.16.verse: for a Buddha is rare even in a hundred eons.
