dn25:20.5.verse: ‘Surely, householder, you should know better! With whom does the ascetic Gotama converse? With whom does he engage in discussion? With whom does he achieve lucidity of wisdom?

dn25:20.6.verse: Staying in empty huts has destroyed the ascetic Gotama’s wisdom. Not frequenting assemblies, he is unable to hold a discussion. He just lurks on the periphery.

dn25:20.7.verse: He’s just like a one-eyed cow, circling around and lurking on the periphery.

dn25:20.9.verse: Please, householder, let the ascetic Gotama come to this assembly. I’ll sink him with just one question! I’ll roll him over and wrap him up like a hollow pot!’

dn25:20.10.verse: Now the Blessed One, perfected and fully awakened, has arrived here. Why don’t you send him out of the assembly to the periphery like a one-eyed cow? Why don’t you sink him with just one question? Why don’t you roll him over and wrap him up like a hollow pot?”

dn25:20.11.verse: When he said this, Nigrodha sat silent, dismayed, shoulders drooping, downcast, depressed, with nothing to say.

dn25:21.1.verse: Knowing this, the Buddha said to him,

dn25:21.2.verse: “Is it really true, Nigrodha—are those your words?”

dn25:21.3.verse: “It’s true, sir, those are my words. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of me.”

dn25:21.5.verse: Have you heard that wanderers of the past who were elderly and senior, the tutors of tutors, said that

dn25:21.6.verse: when the perfected ones, the fully awakened Buddhas of the past came together, they made an uproar, a colossal racket as they sat and talked about all kinds of low topics,

dn25:21.8.verse: like you do in your denomination these days?

dn25:21.9.verse: Or did they say that the Buddhas frequented remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest that are quiet and still, far from the madding crowd, remote from human settlements, and fit for retreat, like I do these days?”

dn25:21.10.verse: “I have heard that wanderers of the past who were elderly and senior, said that

dn25:21.11.verse: when the perfected ones, the fully awakened Buddhas of the past came together, they didn’t make an uproar,

dn25:21.13.verse: like I do in my denomination these days.

dn25:21.14.verse: They said that the Buddhas of the past frequented remote lodgings in the wilderness, like the Buddha does these days.”

dn25:21.15.verse: “Nigrodha, you are a sensible and mature man. Did it not occur to you:

dn25:21.16.verse: ‘The Blessed One is awakened, tamed, serene, crossed over, and quenched. And he teaches Dhamma for awakening, taming, serenity, crossing over, and extinguishment’?”

dn25:22.0.verse: 5. The Culmination of the Spiritual Path

dn25:22.2.verse: “I made a mistake, sir. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of me to speak in that way.

dn25:22.3.verse: Please, sir, accept my mistake for what it is, so I will restrain myself in future.”

dn25:22.4.verse: “Indeed, Nigrodha, you made a mistake. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of you to speak in that way.

dn25:22.5.verse: But since you have recognized your mistake for what it is, and have dealt with it properly, I accept it.

dn25:22.6.verse: For it is growth in the training of the Noble One to recognize a mistake for what it is, deal with it properly, and commit to restraint in the future.

dn25:22.7.verse: Nigrodha, this is what I say:

dn25:22.8.verse: Let a sensible person come—neither devious nor deceitful, a person of integrity. I teach and instruct them.

dn25:22.9.verse: By practicing as instructed they will realize the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life, in seven years. They will live having achieved with their own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

dn25:22.11.verse: Let a sensible person come—neither devious nor deceitful, a person of integrity. I teach and instruct them.

dn25:22.12.verse: By practicing as instructed they will realize the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life, in six years …

dn25:22.30.verse: Let a sensible person come—neither devious nor deceitful, a person of integrity. I teach and instruct them.

dn25:22.31.verse: By practicing as instructed they will realize the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life, in seven days.

dn25:23.2.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama speaks like this because he wants pupils.’

dn25:23.3.verse: But you should not see it like this.

dn25:23.4.verse: Let your tutor remain your tutor.

dn25:23.6.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama speaks like this because he wants us to give up our recitation.’

dn25:23.7.verse: But you should not see it like this.

dn25:23.8.verse: Let your recitation remain as it is.

dn25:23.10.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama speaks like this because he wants us to give up our livelihood.’

dn25:23.11.verse: But you should not see it like this.

dn25:23.12.verse: Let your livelihood remain as it is.

dn25:23.14.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama speaks like this because he wants us to start doing things that are unskillful and considered unskillful in our denomination.’

dn25:23.15.verse: But you should not see it like this.

dn25:23.16.verse: Let those things that are unskillful and considered unskillful in your denomination remain as they are.

dn25:23.18.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama speaks like this because he wants us to stop doing things that are skillful and considered skillful in our denomination.’

dn25:23.19.verse: But you should not see it like this.

dn25:23.20.verse: Let those things that are skillful and considered skillful in your denomination remain as they are.

dn25:23.21.verse: I do not speak for any of these reasons.

dn25:23.22.verse: Nigrodha, there are things that are unskillful, corrupting, leading to future lives, hurtful, resulting in suffering and future rebirth, old age, and death. I teach Dhamma so that those things may be given up.

dn25:23.23.verse: When you practice accordingly, corrupting qualities will be given up in you and cleansing qualities will grow. You’ll enter and remain in the fullness and abundance of wisdom, having realized it with your own insight in this very life.”

dn25:24.1.verse: When this was said, those wanderers sat silent, dismayed, shoulders drooping, downcast, depressed, with nothing to say, as if their minds were possessed by Māra.

dn25:24.2.verse: Then it occurred to the Buddha,

dn25:24.3.verse: “All these silly people have been touched by the Wicked One!

dn25:24.4.verse: For not even a single one thinks,

dn25:24.5.verse: ‘Come, let us lead the spiritual life under the ascetic Gotama for the sake of enlightenment—for what do seven days matter?’”

dn25:24.6.verse: Then the Buddha, having roared his lion’s roar in the lady Udumbarikā’s monastery for wanderers, rose into the air and landed on Vulture’s Peak.

dn25:24.7.verse: Meanwhile, the householder Sandhāna went right back to Rājagaha.

dn26:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Magadhans at Mātulā.

dn26:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

dn26:1.7.verse: “Mendicants, live as your own island, your own refuge, with no other refuge. Let the teaching be your island and your refuge, with no other refuge.

dn26:1.8.verse: And how does a mendicant do this?

dn26:1.9.verse: They meditate observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

dn26:1.10.verse: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

dn26:1.12.verse: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

dn26:1.13.verse: That’s how a mendicant lives with themselves as island and refuge, without other refuge; with the teachings as island and refuge, without other refuge.

dn26:1.14.verse: You should roam inside your own territory, the domain of your fathers.

dn26:1.15.verse: If you roam inside your own territory, the domain of your fathers, Māra won’t find a vulnerability or get an opportunity.

dn26:1.16.verse: It is due to undertaking skillful qualities that merit grows.

dn26:2.1.verse: Once upon a time, mendicants, there was a king named Daḷhanemi who was a wheel-turning monarch, a just and principled king. His dominion extended to all four sides, he achieved stability in the country, and he possessed the seven treasures.

dn26:2.2.verse: He had the following seven treasures:

dn26:2.3.verse: the wheel, the elephant, the horse, the jewel, the woman, the householder, and the commander as the seventh treasure.

dn26:2.4.verse: He had over a thousand sons who were valiant and heroic, crushing the armies of his enemies.

dn26:2.5.verse: After conquering this land girt by sea, he reigned by principle, without rod or sword.

dn26:3.1.verse: Then, after many years, many hundred years, many thousand years had passed, King Daḷhanemi addressed one of his men,

dn26:3.2.verse: ‘My man, when you see that the heavenly wheel-treasure has receded back from its place, please tell me.’

dn26:3.4.verse: After many thousand years had passed, that man saw that the heavenly wheel-treasure had receded back from its place. So he went to King Daḷhanemi and said,

dn26:3.5.verse: ‘Please Your Majesty, you should know that your heavenly wheel-treasure has receded back from its place.’

dn26:3.6.verse: So the king summoned the crown prince and said,

dn26:3.7.verse: ‘Dear prince, my heavenly wheel-treasure has receded back from its place.

dn26:3.9.verse: when this happens to a wheel-turning monarch, he does not have long to live.

dn26:3.10.verse: I have enjoyed human pleasures. Now it is time for me to seek heavenly pleasures.

dn26:3.11.verse: Come, dear prince, rule this land surrounded by ocean!

dn26:3.12.verse: I shall shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness.’

dn26:3.13.verse: And so, after carefully instructing the crown prince in kingship, King Daḷhanemi shaved off his hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and went forth from the lay life to homelessness.

dn26:3.14.verse: Seven days later the heavenly wheel-treasure vanished.

dn26:4.1.verse: Then a certain man approached the newly anointed aristocrat king and said,

dn26:4.2.verse: ‘Please Your Majesty, you should know that the heavenly wheel-treasure has vanished.’

dn26:4.3.verse: At that the king was unhappy and experienced unhappiness.

dn26:4.4.verse: He went to the royal seer and said,

dn26:4.5.verse: ‘Please Your Majesty, you should know that the heavenly wheel-treasure has vanished.’

dn26:4.6.verse: When he said this, the royal seer said to him,

dn26:4.7.verse: ‘Don’t be unhappy at the vanishing of the wheel-treasure. My dear, the wheel-treasure is not inherited from your father.

dn26:4.8.verse: Come now, my dear, proceed in the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch.

dn26:4.9.verse: If you do so, it’s possible that—on a fifteenth day sabbath, having bathed your head and gone upstairs in the royal longhouse to observe the sabbath—the heavenly wheel-treasure will appear to you, with a thousand spokes, with rim and hub, complete in every detail.’

dn26:5.0.verse: 2.1. The Noble Duty of a Wheel-Turning Monarch

dn26:5.1.verse: ‘But Your Majesty, what is the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch?’

dn26:5.2.verse: ‘Well then, my dear, relying only on principle—honoring, respecting, and venerating principle, having principle as your flag, banner, and authority—provide just protection and security for your court, troops, aristocrats, vassals, brahmins and householders, people of town and country, ascetics and brahmins, beasts and birds.

dn26:5.3.verse: Do not let injustice prevail in the realm.

dn26:5.4.verse: Provide money to the penniless in the realm.

dn26:5.5.verse: And there are ascetics and brahmins in the realm who refrain from intoxication and negligence, are settled in patience and gentleness, and who tame, calm, and extinguish themselves. From time to time you should go up to them and ask and learn:

dn26:5.6.verse: “Sirs, what is skillful? What is unskillful? What is blameworthy? What is blameless? What should be cultivated? What should not be cultivated? Doing what leads to my lasting harm and suffering? Doing what leads to my lasting welfare and happiness?”

dn26:5.7.verse: Having heard them, you should shun what is unskillful and proceed having undertaken what is skillful.

dn26:5.8.verse: This is the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch.’

dn26:5.10.verse: ‘Yes, Your Majesty,’ replied the new king to the royal seer. And he proceeded in the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch.

dn26:5.11.verse: While he was proceeding in that duty, on a fifteenth day sabbath, he had bathed his head and gone upstairs in the royal longhouse to observe the sabbath.

dn26:5.12.verse: And the heavenly wheel-treasure appeared to him, with a thousand spokes, with rim and hub, complete in every detail.

dn26:5.14.verse: ‘I have heard that when the heavenly wheel-treasure appears to a king in this way, he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn26:5.15.verse: Am I then a wheel-turning monarch?’

dn26:6.1.verse: Then the anointed king, rising from his seat and arranging his robe over one shoulder, took a ceremonial vase in his left hand and besprinkled the wheel-treasure with his right hand, saying,

dn26:6.2.verse: ‘Roll forth, O wheel-treasure! Triumph, O wheel-treasure!’

dn26:6.3.verse: Then the wheel-treasure rolled toward the east. And the king followed it together with his army of four divisions. In whatever place the wheel-treasure stood still, there the king came to stay together with his army.

dn26:6.4.verse: And any opposing rulers of the eastern quarter came to the wheel-turning monarch and said,

dn26:6.5.verse: ‘Come, Great King! Welcome, Great King! We are yours, Great King, instruct us.’

dn26:6.7.verse: ‘Do not kill living creatures. Do not steal. Do not commit sexual misconduct. Do not lie. Do not drink liquor. Maintain the current level of taxation.’

dn26:6.8.verse: And so the opposing rulers of the eastern quarter became his vassals.

dn26:7.1.verse: Then the wheel-treasure, having plunged into the eastern ocean and emerged again, rolled toward the south. …

dn26:7.2.verse: Having plunged into the southern ocean and emerged again, it rolled toward the west. …

dn26:7.9.verse: Having plunged into the western ocean and emerged again, it rolled toward the north, followed by the king together with his army of four divisions.

dn26:7.10.verse: In whatever place the wheel-treasure stood still, there the king came to stay together with his army.

dn26:7.11.verse: And any opposing rulers of the northern quarter came to the wheel-turning monarch and said,

dn26:7.12.verse: ‘Come, Great King! Welcome, Great King! We are yours, Great King, instruct us.’

dn26:7.14.verse: ‘Do not kill living creatures. Do not steal. Do not commit sexual misconduct. Do not lie. Do not drink liquor. Maintain the current level of taxation.’

dn26:7.15.verse: And so the rulers of the northern quarter became his vassals.

dn26:7.16.verse: And then the wheel-treasure, having triumphed over this land surrounded by ocean, returned to the royal capital. There it stood still by the gate to the royal compound at the High Court as if fixed to an axle, illuminating the royal compound.

dn26:8.6.verse: and a seventh time, a wheel-turning monarch was established in exactly the same way. And after many years the seventh wheel-turning monarch went forth, handing the realm over to the crown prince.

dn26:8.18.verse: Seven days later the heavenly wheel-treasure vanished.

dn26:9.1.verse: Then a certain man approached the newly anointed aristocrat king and said,

dn26:9.2.verse: ‘Please Your Majesty, you should know that the heavenly wheel-treasure has vanished.’

dn26:9.3.verse: At that the king was unhappy and experienced unhappiness.

dn26:9.4.verse: But he didn’t go to the royal seer and ask about the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch.

dn26:9.5.verse: He just governed the country according to his own ideas.

dn26:9.6.verse: So governed, the country’s people did not prosper like before, as they had when former kings proceeded in the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch.

dn26:9.7.verse: Then the ministers and councillors, the treasurers and chief ministers, military officers, guardsmen, and professional advisers gathered and said to the king,

dn26:9.8.verse: ‘Your Majesty, when governed according to your own ideas, the country’s people do not prosper like before, as they did when former kings proceeded in the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch.

dn26:9.9.verse: In your realm are found ministers and councillors, treasurers and chief ministers, military officers, guardsmen, and professional advisers—both ourselves and others—who remember the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch.

dn26:9.10.verse: Please, Your Majesty, ask us about the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch.

dn26:10.1.verse: So the anointed king asked the assembled ministers and councillors, treasurers and chief ministers, military officers, guardsmen, and professional advisers about the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch.

dn26:10.3.verse: After listening to them, he provided just protection and security. But he did not provide money to the penniless in the realm.

dn26:10.5.verse: When poverty was widespread, a certain person stole from others, with the intention to commit theft.

dn26:10.7.verse: and presented him to the king, saying,

dn26:10.8.verse: ‘Your Majesty, this person stole from others with the intention to commit theft.’

dn26:10.9.verse: The king said to that person,

dn26:10.10.verse: ‘Is it really true, my man, that you stole from others with the intention to commit theft?’

dn26:10.14.verse: So the king provided some money to that person, saying,

dn26:10.15.verse: ‘With this money, my man, keep yourself alive, and provide for your mother and father, partners and children. Work for a living, and establish an uplifting religious donation for ascetics and brahmins that’s conducive to heaven, ripens in happiness, and leads to heaven.’

dn26:11.1.verse: But then another man stole something from others.

dn26:11.3.verse: and presented him to the king, saying,

dn26:11.4.verse: ‘Your Majesty, this person stole from others.’

dn26:11.5.verse: The king said to that person,

dn26:11.6.verse: ‘Is it really true, my man, that you stole from others?’

dn26:11.10.verse: So the king provided some money to that person, saying,

dn26:11.11.verse: ‘With this money, my man, keep yourself alive, and provide for your mother and father, partners and children. Work for a living, and establish an uplifting religious donation for ascetics and brahmins that’s conducive to heaven, ripens in happiness, and leads to heaven.’

dn26:12.2.verse: ‘It seems the king is providing money to anyone who steals from others!’

dn26:12.5.verse: So then another man stole something from others.

dn26:12.7.verse: and presented him to the king, saying,

dn26:12.8.verse: ‘Your Majesty, this person stole from others.’

dn26:12.9.verse: The king said to that person,

dn26:12.10.verse: ‘Is it really true, my man, that you stole from others?’

dn26:12.15.verse: ‘If I provide money to anyone who steals from others, it will only increase the stealing.

dn26:12.16.verse: I’d better make an end of this person, finish him off, and chop off his head.’

dn26:12.18.verse: ‘Well then, lads, tie this man’s arms tightly behind his back with a strong rope. Shave his head and march him from street to street and square to square to the beating of a harsh drum. Then take him out the south gate and make an end of him, finish him off, and chop off his head.’

dn26:12.19.verse: ‘Yes, Your Majesty,’ they replied, and did as he commanded.

dn26:13.2.verse: ‘It seems the king is chopping the head off anyone who steals from others!’

dn26:13.4.verse: ‘We’d better have sharp swords made. Then when we steal from others, we’ll make an end of them, finish them off, and chop off their heads.’

dn26:13.5.verse: They had sharp swords made. Then they started to attack villages, towns, and cities, and to infest the highways.

dn26:13.6.verse: And they chopped the heads off anyone they stole from.

dn26:14.1.verse: And so, mendicants, from not providing money to the penniless, poverty became widespread. When poverty was widespread, theft became widespread. When theft was widespread, swords became widespread. When swords were widespread, killing living creatures became widespread. And for the sentient beings among whom killing was widespread, their lifespan and beauty declined.

dn26:14.2.verse: Those people lived for 80,000 years, but their children lived for 40,000 years.

dn26:14.3.verse: Among the humans who lived for 40,000 years, a certain person stole something from others.

dn26:14.5.verse: and presented him to the king, saying,

dn26:14.6.verse: ‘Your Majesty, this person stole from others.’

dn26:14.7.verse: The king said to that person,

dn26:14.8.verse: ‘Is it really true, my man, that you stole from others?’

dn26:14.9.verse: ‘No, Your Majesty,’ he said, deliberately lying.

dn26:15.1.verse: And so, mendicants, from not providing money to the penniless, poverty, theft, swords, and killing became widespread. When killing was widespread, lying became widespread. And for the sentient beings among whom lying was widespread, their lifespan and beauty declined.

dn26:15.2.verse: Those people who lived for 40,000 years had children who lived for 20,000 years.

dn26:15.3.verse: Among the humans who lived for 20,000 years, a certain person stole something from others.

dn26:15.4.verse: Someone else reported this to the king,

dn26:15.5.verse: ‘Your Majesty, the person named so-and-so stole from others,’ he said, going behind his back.

dn26:16.1.verse: And so, mendicants, from not providing money to the penniless, poverty, theft, swords, killing, and lying became widespread. When lying was widespread, backbiting became widespread. And for the sentient beings among whom backbiting was widespread, their lifespan and beauty declined.

dn26:16.2.verse: Those people who lived for 20,000 years had children who lived for 10,000 years.

dn26:17.1.verse: Among the humans who lived for 10,000 years, some were beautiful, some were ugly.

dn26:17.2.verse: And the ugly beings, coveting the beautiful ones, had relations with the wives of others.

dn26:17.3.verse: And so, mendicants, from not providing money to the penniless, poverty, theft, swords, killing, lying, and backbiting became widespread. When backbiting was widespread, sexual misconduct became widespread. And for the sentient beings among whom sexual misconduct was widespread, their lifespan and beauty declined.

dn26:17.4.verse: Those people who lived for 10,000 years had children who lived for 5,000 years.

dn26:17.5.verse: Among the humans who lived for 5,000 years, two things became widespread:

dn26:17.7.verse: For the sentient beings among whom these two things were widespread, their lifespan and beauty declined.

dn26:17.8.verse: Those people who lived for 5,000 years had some children who lived for 2,500 years, while others lived for 2,000 years.

dn26:17.9.verse: Among the humans who lived for 2,500 years, desire and ill will became widespread.

dn26:17.10.verse: For the sentient beings among whom desire and ill will were widespread, their lifespan and beauty declined.

dn26:17.11.verse: Those people who lived for 2,500 years had children who lived for 1,000 years.

dn26:17.12.verse: Among the humans who lived for 1,000 years, wrong view became widespread.

dn26:17.13.verse: For the sentient beings among whom wrong view was widespread, their lifespan and beauty declined.

dn26:17.14.verse: Those people who lived for 1,000 years had children who lived for five hundred years.

dn26:17.15.verse: Among the humans who lived for five hundred years, three things became widespread:

dn26:17.16.verse: illicit desire, immoral greed, and wrong religious teachings.

dn26:17.17.verse: For the sentient beings among whom these three things were widespread, their lifespan and beauty declined.

dn26:17.18.verse: Those people who lived for five hundred years had some children who lived for two hundred and fifty years, while others lived for two hundred years.

dn26:17.19.verse: Among the humans who lived for two hundred and fifty years, these things became widespread:

dn26:17.20.verse: lack of due respect for mother and father, ascetics and brahmins, and failure to honor the elders in the family.

dn26:18.1.verse: And so, mendicants, from not providing money to the penniless, all these things became widespread—poverty,

dn26:18.11.verse: illicit desire, immoral greed, and wrong religious teachings,

dn26:18.12.verse: and lack of due respect for mother and father, ascetics and brahmins, and failure to honor the elders in the family.

dn26:18.13.verse: For the sentient beings among whom these things were widespread, their lifespan and beauty declined.

dn26:18.14.verse: Those people who lived for two hundred and fifty years had children who lived for a hundred years.

dn26:19.0.verse: 5. When People Live for Ten Years

dn26:19.1.verse: There will come a time, mendicants, when these people will have children who live for ten years.

dn26:19.2.verse: Among the humans who live for ten years, girls will be marriageable at five.

dn26:19.4.verse: ghee, butter, oil, honey, molasses, and salt.

dn26:19.5.verse: The best kind of food will be finger millet,

dn26:19.6.verse: just as fine rice with meat is the best kind of food today.

dn26:19.8.verse: The ten ways of doing skillful deeds will totally disappear, and the ten ways of doing unskillful deeds will explode in popularity.

dn26:19.9.verse: Those humans will not even have the word ‘skillful’, still less anyone who does what is skillful.

dn26:19.10.verse: And anyone who disrespects mother and father, ascetics and brahmins, and fails to honor the elders in the family will be venerated and praised,

dn26:19.11.verse: just as the opposite is venerated and praised today.

dn26:20.1.verse: There’ll be no recognition of the status of mother, aunts, or wives and partners of tutors and respected people.

dn26:20.2.verse: The world will become dissolute, like goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, and hounds and jackals.

dn26:20.3.verse: They’ll be full of hostility toward each other, with acute ill will, malevolence, and thoughts of murder.

dn26:20.4.verse: Even a mother will feel like this for her child, and the child for its mother,

dn26:20.5.verse: father for child, child for father,

dn26:20.6.verse: brother for sister, and sister for brother.

dn26:20.7.verse: They’ll be just like a deer hunter when he sees a deer—full of hostility, ill will, malevolence, and thoughts of killing.

dn26:21.1.verse: Among the humans who live for ten years, there will be an interregnum of swords lasting seven days.

dn26:21.2.verse: During that time they will see each other as beasts.

dn26:21.3.verse: Sharp swords will appear in their hands,

dn26:21.4.verse: with which they’ll take each other’s life, crying, ‘It’s a beast! It’s a beast!’

dn26:21.5.verse: But then some of those beings will think,

dn26:21.6.verse: ‘Let us neither kill nor be killed! Why don’t we hide in thick grass, thick jungle, thick trees, inaccessible riverlands, or rugged mountains and survive on forest roots and fruits?’

dn26:21.8.verse: When those seven days have passed, having emerged from their hiding places and embraced each other, they will come together and cry in one voice,

dn26:21.9.verse: ‘Fantastic, dear foe, you live! Fantastic, dear foe, you live!’

dn26:21.12.verse: ‘It’s because we undertook unskillful things that we suffered such an extensive loss of our relatives.

dn26:21.14.verse: What skillful thing should we do?

dn26:21.15.verse: Why don’t we refrain from killing living creatures? Having undertaken this skillful thing we’ll live by it.’

dn26:21.17.verse: Because of undertaking this skillful thing, their lifespan and beauty will grow.

dn26:21.18.verse: Those people who live for ten years will have children who live for twenty years.

dn26:22.2.verse: ‘Because of undertaking this skillful thing, our lifespan and beauty are growing.

dn26:22.3.verse: Why don’t we do even more skillful things?

dn26:22.4.verse: What skillful thing should we do?

dn26:22.5.verse: Why don’t we refrain from stealing …

dn26:22.11.verse: Why don’t we give up covetousness …

dn26:22.15.verse: illicit desire, immoral greed, and wrong religious teachings.

dn26:22.16.verse: Why don’t we pay due respect to mother and father, ascetics and brahmins, honoring the elders in our families? Having undertaken this skillful thing we’ll live by it.’

dn26:22.18.verse: Because of undertaking this skillful thing, their lifespan and beauty will grow.

dn26:22.19.verse: Those people who live for twenty years will have children who live for forty years.

dn26:22.20.verse: Those people who live for forty years will have children who live for eighty years,

dn26:22.21.verse: then a hundred and sixty years,

dn26:23.3.verse: Among the humans who live for 80,000 years, girls will be marriageable at five hundred.

dn26:23.5.verse: Among the humans who live for 80,000 years, there will be just three afflictions: greed, starvation, and old age.

dn26:23.6.verse: The Black Plum Tree Land will be successful and prosperous. The villages, towns, and capital cities will be no more than a chicken’s flight apart.

dn26:23.7.verse: And the land will be so full of humans you’d think they were squashed together, like a thicket of rushes or reeds.

dn26:23.8.verse: The royal capital will be Varanasi, renamed Ketumatī. And it will be successful and prosperous, populous and full of people, with plenty of food.

dn26:23.9.verse: There will be 84,000 cities in the Black Plum Tree Land, with the royal capital of Ketumatī foremost.

dn26:24.1.verse: And in the royal capital of Ketumatī a king named Saṅkha will arise, a wheel-turning monarch, a just and principled king. His dominion will extend to all four sides, he will achieve stability in the country, and possess the seven treasures.

dn26:24.2.verse: He will have the following seven treasures:

dn26:24.3.verse: the wheel, the elephant, the horse, the jewel, the woman, the householder, and the commander as the seventh treasure.

dn26:24.4.verse: He will have over a thousand sons who are valiant and heroic, crushing the armies of his enemies.

dn26:24.5.verse: After conquering this land girt by sea, he will reign by principle, without rod or sword.

dn26:25.0.verse: 8. The Arising of the Buddha Metteyya

dn26:25.1.verse: And the Blessed One named Metteyya will arise in the world—perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed—

dn26:25.2.verse: just as I have arisen today.

dn26:25.3.verse: He will realize with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and make it known to others, just as I do today.

dn26:25.4.verse: He will teach the Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he will reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure,

dn26:25.6.verse: He will lead a Saṅgha of many thousand mendicants, just as I lead a Saṅgha of many hundreds today.

dn26:26.1.verse: Then King Saṅkha will have the sacrificial post once built by King Mahāpanāda raised up.

dn26:26.2.verse: Having reigned, he will abdicate, offering charity to ascetics and brahmins, paupers, vagrants, supplicants, and beggars. Then, having shaved off his hair and beard and dressed in ocher robes, he will go forth from the lay life to homelessness in the Buddha Metteyya’s presence.

dn26:26.3.verse: Soon after going forth, living withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, he will realize the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He will live having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

dn26:27.1.verse: Mendicants, live as your own island, your own refuge, with no other refuge. Let the teaching be your island and your refuge, with no other refuge.

dn26:27.2.verse: And how does a mendicant do this?

dn26:27.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

dn26:27.4.verse: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

dn26:27.6.verse: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

dn26:27.7.verse: That’s how a mendicant lives with themselves as island and refuge, without other refuge; with the teachings as island and refuge, without other refuge.

dn26:28.0.verse: 9. On Long Life and Beauty for Mendicants

dn26:28.1.verse: Mendicants, you should roam inside your own territory, the domain of your fathers.

dn26:28.2.verse: Doing so, you will grow in lifespan, beauty, happiness, wealth, and power.

dn26:28.3.verse: And what is long life for a mendicant?

dn26:28.4.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort.

dn26:28.5.verse: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to energy, and active effort.

dn26:28.6.verse: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to mental development, and active effort.

dn26:28.7.verse: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to inquiry, and active effort.

dn26:28.8.verse: Having developed and cultivated these four bases of psychic power they may, if they wish, live for the proper lifespan or what’s left of it.

dn26:28.9.verse: This is long life for a mendicant.

dn26:28.10.verse: And what is beauty for a mendicant?

dn26:28.11.verse: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

dn26:28.12.verse: This is beauty for a mendicant.

dn26:28.13.verse: And what is happiness for a mendicant?

dn26:28.14.verse: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

dn26:28.15.verse: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption …

dn26:28.18.verse: This is happiness for a mendicant.

dn26:28.19.verse: And what is wealth for a mendicant?

dn26:28.20.verse: It’s when a monk meditates spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

dn26:28.21.verse: They meditate spreading a heart full of compassion …

dn26:28.23.verse: equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

dn26:28.24.verse: This is wealth for a mendicant.

dn26:28.25.verse: And what is power for a mendicant?

dn26:28.26.verse: It’s when a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

dn26:28.27.verse: This is power for a mendicant.

dn26:28.28.verse: Mendicants, I do not see a single power so hard to defeat as the power of Māra.

dn26:28.29.verse: It is due to undertaking skillful qualities that merit grows.”

dn26:28.30.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

dn26:28.31.verse: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

dn27:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

dn27:1.3.verse: Now at that time Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja were living on probation among the mendicants in hopes of being ordained.

dn27:1.4.verse: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came downstairs from the longhouse and was walking mindfully in the open air, beneath the shade of the longhouse.

dn27:2.3.verse: “Reverend Bhāradvāja, the Buddha is walking mindfully in the open air, beneath the shade of the longhouse.

dn27:2.4.verse: Come, reverend, let’s go to the Buddha.

dn27:2.5.verse: Hopefully we’ll get to hear a Dhamma talk from him.”

dn27:2.7.verse: So they went to the Buddha, bowed, and walked beside him.

dn27:3.1.verse: Then the Buddha said to Vāseṭṭha,

dn27:3.2.verse: “Vāseṭṭha, you are both brahmins by birth and family, and have gone forth from the lay life to homelessness from a brahmin family. I hope you don’t have to suffer abuse and insults from the brahmins.”

dn27:3.3.verse: “Actually, sir, the brahmins do insult and abuse us with their typical insults to the fullest extent, holding nothing back.”

dn27:3.4.verse: “But how do the brahmins insult you?”

dn27:3.6.verse: ‘Only brahmins are the best class; other classes are inferior.

dn27:3.7.verse: Only brahmins are the light class; other classes are dark.

dn27:3.8.verse: Only brahmins are purified, not others.

dn27:3.9.verse: Only brahmins are the Divinity’s bosom sons, born from his mouth, born of the Divinity, created by the Divinity, heirs of the Divinity.

dn27:3.10.verse: You’ve both abandoned the best class to join an inferior class, namely these shavelings, fake ascetics, primitives, black spawn from the feet of our kinsman.

dn27:3.11.verse: This is not right, it’s not proper!’

dn27:3.12.verse: That’s how the brahmins insult us.”

dn27:4.1.verse: “Actually, Vāseṭṭha, the brahmins are forgetting their tradition when they say this to you.

dn27:4.6.verse: For brahmin women are seen menstruating, being pregnant, giving birth, and breast-feeding.

dn27:4.7.verse: Yet even though they’re born from a brahmin womb they say:

dn27:4.8.verse: ‘Only brahmins are the best class; other classes are inferior.

dn27:4.9.verse: Only brahmins are the light class; other classes are dark.

dn27:4.10.verse: Only brahmins are purified, not others.

dn27:4.11.verse: Only brahmins are the Divinity’s bosom sons, born from his mouth, born of the Divinity, created by the Divinity, heirs of the Divinity.’

dn27:4.12.verse: They misrepresent the brahmins, speak falsely, and brim with much wickedness.

dn27:5.1.verse: Vāseṭṭha, there are these four classes:

dn27:5.3.verse: Some aristocrats kill living creatures, steal, and commit sexual misconduct. They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, and nonsensical. And they’re covetous, malicious, with wrong view.

dn27:5.4.verse: These things are unskillful, blameworthy, not to be cultivated, unworthy of the noble ones—and are reckoned as such. They are dark deeds with dark results, criticized by sensible people. Such things are exhibited in some aristocrats.

dn27:5.5.verse: And they are also seen among some brahmins,

dn27:6.1.verse: But some aristocrats refrain from killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct. They refrain from speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, and nonsensical. And they’re content, kind-hearted, with right view.

dn27:6.2.verse: These things are skillful, blameless, to be cultivated, worthy of the noble ones—and are reckoned as such. They are bright deeds with bright results, praised by sensible people. Such things are exhibited in some aristocrats.

dn27:6.3.verse: And they are also seen among some brahmins,

dn27:7.1.verse: Both these things occur like this, mixed up in these four classes—the dark and the bright, that which is praised and that which is criticized by sensible people. Yet of this the brahmins say:

dn27:7.2.verse: ‘Only brahmins are the best class; other classes are inferior.

dn27:7.3.verse: Only brahmins are the light class; other classes are dark.

dn27:7.4.verse: Only brahmins are purified, not others.

dn27:7.5.verse: Only brahmins are the Divinity’s bosom sons, born from his mouth, born of the Divinity, created by the Divinity, heirs of the Divinity.’

dn27:7.8.verse: Because any mendicant from these four classes who is perfected—with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment—is said to be foremost by virtue of principle, not against principle.

dn27:7.9.verse: For principle, Vāseṭṭha, is the best thing for people in both this life and the next.

dn27:7.10.verse: And here’s a way to understand how this is so.

dn27:8.1.verse: King Pasenadi of Kosala knows that

dn27:8.2.verse: the ascetic Gotama has gone forth from the neighboring clan of the Sakyans.

dn27:8.3.verse: And the Sakyans are his vassals.

dn27:8.4.verse: The Sakyans show deference to King Pasenadi by bowing down, rising up, greeting him with cupped palms, and observing proper etiquette for him.

dn27:8.5.verse: Now, King Pasenadi shows the same kind of deference to the Realized One. But he doesn’t think: ‘The ascetic Gotama is well-born, I am ill-born.

dn27:8.6.verse: He is powerful, I am weak.

dn27:8.7.verse: He is handsome, I am ugly.

dn27:8.8.verse: He is illustrious, I am insignificant.’

dn27:8.9.verse: Rather, in showing such deference to the Realized One he is only honoring, respecting, and venerating principle.

dn27:8.10.verse: And here’s another way to understand how principle is the best thing for people in both this life and the next.

dn27:9.1.verse: Vāseṭṭha, you have different births, names, clans, and families, yet have gone forth from the lay life to homelessness.

dn27:9.2.verse: When they ask you what you are, you claim to be ascetics who follow the Sakyan.

dn27:9.3.verse: But only when someone has faith in the Realized One—settled, rooted, and planted deep, strong, not to be shifted by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world—is it appropriate for them to say:

dn27:9.4.verse: ‘I am the Buddha’s bosom son, born from his mouth, born of principle, created by principle, heir to principle.’

dn27:9.6.verse: For these are terms for the Realized One: ‘the embodiment of principle’, and ‘the embodiment of divinity’, and ‘the manifestation of principle’, and ‘the manifestation of divinity’.

dn27:10.1.verse: There comes a time when, Vāseṭṭha, after a very long period has passed, this cosmos contracts.

dn27:10.2.verse: As the cosmos contracts, sentient beings are mostly headed for the realm of sublime luminosity.

dn27:10.3.verse: There they are mind-made, feeding on rapture, self-radiant, wandering in midair, steadily glorious, and they remain like that for a very long time.

dn27:10.4.verse: There comes a time when, after a very long period has passed, this cosmos expands.

dn27:10.5.verse: As the cosmos expands, sentient beings mostly pass away from that host of luminous deities and come back to this realm.

dn27:10.6.verse: Here they are mind-made, feeding on rapture, self-radiant, wandering in midair, steadily glorious, and they remain like that for a very long time.

dn27:11.1.verse: But the single mass of water at that time was utterly dark.

dn27:11.2.verse: The moon and sun were not found, nor were stars and constellations, day and night, months and fortnights, years and seasons, or male and female. Beings were simply known as ‘beings’.

dn27:11.3.verse: After a very long period had passed, the earth’s nectar curdled in the water.

dn27:11.4.verse: It appeared just like the curd on top of hot milk-rice as it cools.

dn27:11.6.verse: It was beautiful, fragrant, and delicious, like ghee or butter.

dn27:11.7.verse: And it was as sweet as pure dwarf-bee honey.

dn27:11.9.verse: Now, one of those beings was reckless.

dn27:11.10.verse: Thinking, ‘Oh my, what might this be?’ they tasted the earth’s nectar with their finger.

dn27:11.11.verse: They enjoyed it, and craving was born in them.

dn27:11.12.verse: And other beings, following that being’s example, tasted the earth’s nectar with their fingers.

dn27:11.13.verse: They too enjoyed it, and craving was born in them.

dn27:12.1.verse: Then those beings started to eat the earth’s nectar, breaking it into lumps.

dn27:12.4.verse: And with the vanishing of their radiance the moon and sun appeared,

dn27:12.7.verse: and so were months and fortnights,

dn27:12.9.verse: So far had the world evolved once more.

dn27:13.1.verse: Then those beings eating the earth’s nectar, with that as their food and nourishment, remained for a very long time.

dn27:13.2.verse: But so long as they ate that earth’s nectar, their bodies became more solid and they diverged in appearance;

dn27:13.4.verse: And the beautiful beings looked down on the ugly ones:

dn27:13.5.verse: ‘We’re more beautiful, they’re the ugly ones!’

dn27:13.6.verse: And the vanity of the beautiful ones made the earth’s nectar vanish.

dn27:13.9.verse: ‘Oh, what a taste! Oh, what a taste!’

dn27:13.10.verse: And even today when people get something tasty they say:

dn27:13.11.verse: ‘Oh, what a taste! Oh, what a taste!’

dn27:13.12.verse: They’re just remembering an ancient primordial saying, but they don’t understand what it means.

dn27:14.1.verse: When the earth’s nectar had vanished, ground-fungus appeared to those beings.

dn27:14.2.verse: It appeared just like a mushroom.

dn27:14.3.verse: It was beautiful, fragrant, and delicious, like ghee or butter.

dn27:14.4.verse: And it was as sweet as pure dwarf-bee honey.

dn27:14.5.verse: Then those beings started to eat the ground-fungus.

dn27:14.6.verse: With that as their food and nourishment, they remained for a very long time.

dn27:14.7.verse: But so long as they ate that ground-fungus, their bodies became more solid and they diverged in appearance;

dn27:14.9.verse: And the beautiful beings looked down on the ugly ones:

dn27:14.10.verse: ‘We’re more beautiful, they’re the ugly ones!’

dn27:14.11.verse: And the vanity of the beautiful ones made the ground-fungus vanish.

dn27:14.13.verse: When the ground-fungus had vanished, bursting pods appeared, like the fruit of the kadam tree.

dn27:14.14.verse: They were beautiful, fragrant, and delicious, like ghee or butter.

dn27:14.15.verse: And they were as sweet as pure dwarf-bee honey.

dn27:15.1.verse: Then those beings started to eat the bursting pods.

dn27:15.2.verse: With that as their food and nourishment, they remained for a very long time.

dn27:15.3.verse: But so long as they ate those bursting pods, their bodies became more solid and they diverged in appearance;

dn27:15.5.verse: And the beautiful beings looked down on the ugly ones:

dn27:15.6.verse: ‘We’re more beautiful, they’re the ugly ones!’

dn27:15.7.verse: And the vanity of the beautiful ones made the bursting pods vanish.

dn27:15.9.verse: ‘Oh, what we’ve lost! Oh, what we’ve lost—those bursting pods!’

dn27:15.10.verse: And even today when people experience suffering they say:

dn27:15.11.verse: ‘Oh, what we’ve lost! Oh, what we’ve lost!’

dn27:15.12.verse: They’re just remembering an ancient primordial saying, but they don’t understand what it means.

dn27:16.1.verse: When the bursting pods had vanished, ripe untilled rice appeared to those beings. It had no powder or husk, pure and fragrant, with only the rice-grain.

dn27:16.2.verse: What they took for supper at dusk, by daybreak had grown back and ripened.

dn27:16.3.verse: And what they took for breakfast at daybreak had grown back and ripened by the evening,

dn27:16.5.verse: Then those beings eating the ripe untilled rice, with that as their food and nourishment, remained for a very long time.

dn27:16.7.verse: But so long as they ate that ripe untilled rice, their bodies became more solid and they diverged in appearance. And female characteristics appeared on women, while male characteristics appeared on men.

dn27:16.8.verse: Women spent too much time gazing at men, and men at women.

dn27:16.9.verse: They became lustful, and their bodies burned with fever.

dn27:16.10.verse: Due to this fever they had sex with each other.

dn27:16.11.verse: Those who saw them having sex pelted them with dirt, clods, or cow-dung, saying,

dn27:16.13.verse: How on earth can one being do that to another?’

dn27:16.14.verse: And even today people in some countries, when carrying a bride off, pelt her with dirt, clods, or cow-dung.

dn27:16.15.verse: They’re just remembering an ancient primordial saying, but they don’t understand what it means.

dn27:17.1.verse: What was deemed as unprincipled at that time, these days is deemed as principled.

dn27:17.2.verse: The beings who had sex together weren’t allowed to enter a village or town for one or two months.

dn27:17.3.verse: Ever since they excessively threw themselves into immorality,

dn27:17.4.verse: they started to make buildings to hide their immoral deeds.

dn27:17.5.verse: Then one of those beings of idle disposition thought,

dn27:17.6.verse: ‘Oh my, why should I be bothered to gather rice at dusk for supper, and at daybreak for breakfast?

dn27:17.7.verse: Why don’t I gather rice for supper and breakfast all at once?’

dn27:17.9.verse: Then one of the other beings approached that being and said,

dn27:17.10.verse: ‘Come, good being, we shall go to gather rice.’

dn27:17.11.verse: ‘There’s no need, good being! I gathered rice for supper and breakfast all at once.’

dn27:17.12.verse: So that being, following their example, gathered rice for two days all at once, thinking: ‘This seems fine.’

dn27:17.13.verse: Then one of the other beings approached that being and said,

dn27:17.14.verse: ‘Come, good being, we shall go to gather rice.’

dn27:17.15.verse: ‘There’s no need, good being! I gathered rice for two days all at once.’

dn27:17.16.verse: So that being, following their example, gathered rice for four days all at once, thinking: ‘This seems fine.’

dn27:17.17.verse: Then one of the other beings approached that being and said,

dn27:17.18.verse: ‘Come, good being, we shall go to gather rice.’

dn27:17.19.verse: ‘There’s no need, good being! I gathered rice for four days all at once.’

dn27:17.20.verse: So that being, following their example, gathered rice for eight days all at once, thinking: ‘This seems fine.’

dn27:17.21.verse: But when they started to store up rice to eat,

dn27:17.22.verse: the rice grains became wrapped in powder and husk,

dn27:17.23.verse: it didn’t grow back after reaping, leaving a trace showing, and the rice stood in clumps.

dn27:18.1.verse: Then those beings gathered together and bemoaned,

dn27:18.2.verse: ‘Oh, how wicked things have appeared among beings!

dn27:18.3.verse: For we used to be mind-made, feeding on rapture, self-radiant, wandering in midair, steadily glorious, and we remained like that for a very long time.

dn27:18.4.verse: After a very long period had passed, the earth’s nectar curdled in the water.

dn27:18.10.verse: But due to bad, unskillful things among us, the earth’s nectar vanished,

dn27:18.26.verse: and now the rice grains have become wrapped in powder and husk, it doesn’t grow back after reaping, traces are left showing, and the rice stands in clumps.

dn27:18.27.verse: We’d better divide up the rice and lay down boundaries.’

dn27:19.1.verse: Now, one of those beings was reckless. While guarding their own share they took another’s share without it being given, and ate it.

dn27:19.2.verse: They grabbed the one who had done this and said,

dn27:19.3.verse: ‘You have done a bad thing, good being, in that while guarding your own share you took another’s share without it being given, and ate it.

dn27:19.4.verse: Do not do such a thing again.’

dn27:19.7.verse: For a third time they did the same thing, and were told not to continue.

dn27:19.11.verse: And then they struck that being, some with fists, others with stones, and still others with rods.

dn27:19.12.verse: From that day on stealing was found, and blame, and lying, and the taking up of rods.

dn27:20.1.verse: Then those beings gathered together and bemoaned,

dn27:20.2.verse: ‘Oh, how wicked things have appeared among beings, in that stealing is found, and blaming and lying and the taking up of rods!

dn27:20.3.verse: Why don’t we elect one being who would rightly accuse those who deserve it, blame those who deserve it, and expel those who deserve it?

dn27:20.4.verse: We shall pay them with a share of rice.’

dn27:20.5.verse: Then those beings approached the being among them who was most attractive, good-looking, lovely, and illustrious, and said,

dn27:20.6.verse: ‘Come, good being, rightly accuse those who deserve it, blame those who deserve it, and banish those who deserve it.

dn27:20.7.verse: We shall pay you with a share of rice.’

dn27:20.8.verse: ‘Yes, worthy sirs,’ replied that being. They acted accordingly,

dn27:20.9.verse: and were paid with a share of rice.

dn27:21.1.verse: ‘Elected by the populace’, Vāseṭṭha, is the meaning of ‘popularly elected’, the first term applied to them.

dn27:21.2.verse: ‘Lord of the fields’ is the meaning of ‘aristocrat’, the second term applied to them.

dn27:21.3.verse: ‘They please others with principle’ is the meaning of ‘king’, the third term applied to them.

dn27:21.4.verse: And that, Vāseṭṭha, is how the ancient primordial terms for the circle of aristocrats were created; for those very beings, not others; for those like them, not unlike; by virtue of principle, not against principle.

dn27:21.5.verse: For principle, Vāseṭṭha, is the best thing for people in both this life and the next.

dn27:22.1.verse: Then some of those same beings thought,

dn27:22.2.verse: ‘Oh, how wicked things have appeared among beings, in that stealing is found, and blaming and lying and the taking up of rods and banishment!

dn27:22.3.verse: Why don’t we set aside bad, unskillful things?’

dn27:22.5.verse: ‘They set aside bad, unskillful things’ is the meaning of ‘brahmin’, the first term applied to them.

dn27:22.6.verse: They built leaf huts in a wilderness region where they meditated pure and bright, without lighting cooking fires or digging the soil. They came down at daybreak for breakfast and at dusk for supper to the village, town, or royal capital seeking a meal.

dn27:22.7.verse: When they had obtained food they continued to meditate in the leaf huts.

dn27:22.8.verse: When people noticed this they said,

dn27:22.9.verse: ‘These beings build leaf huts in a wilderness region where they meditate pure and bright, without lighting cooking fires or digging the soil. They come down at daybreak for breakfast and at dusk for supper to the village, town, or royal capital seeking a meal.

dn27:22.10.verse: When they have obtained food they continue to meditate in the leaf huts.’

dn27:22.11.verse: ‘They meditate’ is the meaning of ‘meditator’, the second term applied to them.

dn27:23.1.verse: But some of those beings were unable to keep up with their meditation in the leaf huts in the wilderness. They came down to the neighborhood of a village or town where they dwelt compiling texts.

dn27:23.2.verse: When people noticed this they said,

dn27:23.3.verse: ‘These beings were unable to keep up with their meditation in the leaf huts in the wilderness. They came down to the neighborhood of a village or town where they dwelt compiling texts. Now they don’t meditate.’

dn27:23.4.verse: ‘Now they don’t meditate’ is the meaning of ‘reciter’, the third term applied to them.

dn27:23.5.verse: What was deemed as worse at that time, these days is deemed as best.

dn27:23.6.verse: And that, Vāseṭṭha, is how the ancient primordial terms for the circle of brahmins were created; for those very beings, not others; for those like them, not unlike; by virtue of principle, not against principle.

dn27:23.7.verse: For principle, Vāseṭṭha, is the best thing for people in both this life and the next.

dn27:24.1.verse: Some of those same beings, taking up an active sex life, applied themselves to various jobs.

dn27:24.2.verse: ‘Having taken up an active sex life, they apply themselves to various jobs’ is the meaning of ‘peasant’, the term applied to them.

dn27:24.3.verse: And that, Vāseṭṭha, is how the ancient primordial term for the circle of peasants was created; for those very beings, not others; for those like them, not unlike; by virtue of principle, not against principle.

dn27:24.4.verse: For principle, Vāseṭṭha, is the best thing for people in both this life and the next.

dn27:25.1.verse: The remaining beings lived by venal hunting and minor tasks.

dn27:25.2.verse: ‘They live by venal hunting and minor tasks’ is the meaning of ‘menial’, the term applied to them.

dn27:25.3.verse: And that, Vāseṭṭha, is how the ancient primordial term for the circle of menials was created; for those very beings, not others; for those like them, not unlike; by virtue of principle, not against principle.

dn27:25.4.verse: For principle, Vāseṭṭha, is the best thing for people in both this life and the next.

dn27:26.1.verse: There came a time when an aristocrat,

dn27:26.5.verse: or menial, deprecating their own vocation, went forth from the lay life to homelessness, thinking,

dn27:26.7.verse: From these four circles, Vāseṭṭha, the circle of ascetics was created; for those very beings, not others; for those like them, not unlike; by virtue of principle, not against principle.

dn27:26.8.verse: For principle, Vāseṭṭha, is the best thing for people in both this life and the next.

dn27:27.5.verse: or ascetic may do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind. They have wrong view, and they act out of that wrong view. And because of that, when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

dn27:28.5.verse: or ascetic may do good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They have right view, and they act out of that right view. And because of that, when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

dn27:29.5.verse: or ascetic may do mixed things by way of body, speech, and mind. They have mixed view, and they act out of that mixed view. And because of that, when their body breaks up, after death, they experience both pleasure and pain.

dn27:30.0.verse: 15. The Qualities on the Side of Awakening

dn27:30.5.verse: or ascetic who is restrained in body, speech, and mind, and develops the seven qualities on the side of awakening, becomes extinguished in this very life.

dn27:31.1.verse: Any mendicant from these four classes who is perfected—with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment—is said to be the foremost by virtue of principle, not against principle.

dn27:31.2.verse: For principle, Vāseṭṭha, is the best thing for people in both this life and the next.

dn27:32.1.verse: The divinity Sanaṅkumāra also spoke this verse:

dn27:32.3.verse: who take clan as the standard.

dn27:32.4.verse: But one accomplished in knowledge and conduct

dn27:32.5.verse: is first among gods and humans.’

dn27:32.6.verse: That verse was well sung by the Divinity Sanaṅkumāra, not poorly sung; well spoken, not poorly spoken; beneficial, not harmful, and I agree with it.

dn27:32.8.verse: The aristocrat is best among people

dn27:32.9.verse: who take clan as the standard.

dn27:32.10.verse: But one accomplished in knowledge and conduct

dn27:32.11.verse: is first among gods and humans.”

dn27:32.12.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

dn27:32.13.verse: Satisfied, Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja approved what the Buddha said.

dn28:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Nāḷandā in Pāvārika’s Mango Grove.

dn28:1.3.verse: Then Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

dn28:1.4.verse: “Sir, I have such confidence in the Buddha that I believe there’s no other ascetic or brahmin—whether past, future, or present—whose direct knowledge is superior to the Buddha when it comes to awakening.”

dn28:1.5.verse: “That’s a grand and bold statement, Sāriputta. You’ve roared a definitive, categorical lion’s roar, saying:

dn28:1.6.verse: ‘I have such confidence in the Buddha that

dn28:1.7.verse: I believe there’s no other ascetic or brahmin—whether past, future, or present—whose direct knowledge is superior to the Buddha when it comes to awakening.’

dn28:1.8.verse: What about all the perfected ones, the fully awakened Buddhas who lived in the past? Have you encompassed their minds to know that

dn28:1.9.verse: those Buddhas had such ethics, or such qualities, or such wisdom, or such meditation, or such freedom?”

dn28:1.11.verse: “And what about all the perfected ones, the fully awakened Buddhas who will live in the future? Have you encompassed their minds to know that

dn28:1.12.verse: those Buddhas will have such ethics, or such qualities, or such wisdom, or such meditation, or such freedom?”

dn28:1.14.verse: “And what about me, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha at present? Have you encompassed my mind to know that

dn28:1.15.verse: I have such ethics, or such qualities, or such wisdom, or such meditation, or such freedom?”

dn28:1.17.verse: “In that case, Sāriputta, given that you don’t encompass the minds of Buddhas past, future, or present,

dn28:1.18.verse: what then are you doing, making such a grand and bold statement, roaring such a definitive, categorical lion’s roar?”

dn28:2.1.verse: “Sir, though I don’t encompass the minds of Buddhas past, future, and present,

dn28:2.2.verse: still I understand this by inference from the teaching.

dn28:2.3.verse: Suppose there was a king’s frontier citadel with fortified embankments, ramparts, and arches, and a single gate.

dn28:2.4.verse: And it has a gatekeeper who is astute, competent, and intelligent. He keeps strangers out and lets known people in.

dn28:2.5.verse: As he walks around the patrol path, he doesn’t see a hole or cleft in the wall, not even one big enough for a cat to slip out.

dn28:2.7.verse: ‘Whatever sizable creatures enter or leave the citadel, all of them do so via this gate.’

dn28:2.8.verse: In the same way, I understand this by inference from the teaching:

dn28:2.9.verse: ‘All the perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas—whether past, future, or present—give up the five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom. Their mind is firmly established in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. They correctly develop the seven awakening factors. And they awaken to the supreme perfect awakening.’

dn28:2.12.verse: Sir, once I approached the Buddha to listen to the teaching.

dn28:2.13.verse: He explained Dhamma with its higher and higher stages, with its better and better stages, with its dark and bright sides.

dn28:2.14.verse: When I directly knew a certain principle of those teachings, in accordance with how I was taught, I came to a conclusion about the teachings. I had confidence in the Teacher:

dn28:2.15.verse: ‘The Blessed One is a fully awakened Buddha. The teaching is well explained. The Saṅgha is practicing well.’

dn28:3.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches skillful qualities is unsurpassable.

dn28:3.2.verse: This consists of such skillful qualities as

dn28:3.3.verse: the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, and the noble eightfold path.

dn28:3.4.verse: By these a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

dn28:3.5.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to skillful qualities.

dn28:3.6.verse: The Buddha understands this without exception. There is nothing to be understood beyond this whereby another ascetic or brahmin might be superior in direct knowledge to the Buddha when it comes to skillful qualities.

dn28:4.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches the description of the sense fields is unsurpassable.

dn28:4.2.verse: There are these six interior and exterior sense fields.

dn28:4.3.verse: The eye and sights, the ear and sounds, the nose and smells, the tongue and tastes, the body and touches, and the mind and ideas.

dn28:4.4.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to describing the sense fields.

dn28:4.5.verse: The Buddha understands this without exception. There is nothing to be understood beyond this whereby another ascetic or brahmin might be superior in direct knowledge to the Buddha when it comes to describing the sense fields.

dn28:5.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches the conception of the embryo is unsurpassable.

dn28:5.2.verse: There are these four kinds of conception.

dn28:5.3.verse: Firstly, someone is unaware when conceived in their mother’s womb, unaware as they remain there, and unaware as they emerge. This is the first kind of conception.

dn28:5.4.verse: Furthermore, someone is aware when conceived in their mother’s womb, but unaware as they remain there, and unaware as they emerge. This is the second kind of conception.

dn28:5.5.verse: Furthermore, someone is aware when conceived in their mother’s womb, aware as they remain there, but unaware as they emerge. This is the third kind of conception.

dn28:5.6.verse: Furthermore, someone is aware when conceived in their mother’s womb, aware as they remain there, and aware as they emerge. This is the fourth kind of conception.

dn28:5.7.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to the conception of the embryo.

dn28:6.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches the different ways of revealing is unsurpassable.

dn28:6.2.verse: There are these four ways of revealing.

dn28:6.3.verse: Firstly, someone reveals by means of a sign,

dn28:6.4.verse: ‘This is what you’re thinking, such is your thought, and thus is your state of mind.’

dn28:6.5.verse: And even if they reveal this many times, it turns out exactly so, not otherwise.

dn28:6.6.verse: This is the first way of revealing.

dn28:6.7.verse: Furthermore, someone reveals after hearing it from humans or non-humans or deities,

dn28:6.8.verse: ‘This is what you’re thinking, such is your thought, and thus is your state of mind.’

dn28:6.9.verse: And even if they reveal this many times, it turns out exactly so, not otherwise.

dn28:6.10.verse: This is the second way of revealing.

dn28:6.11.verse: Furthermore, someone reveals by hearing the sound of thought spreading as someone thinks and considers,

dn28:6.12.verse: ‘This is what you’re thinking, such is your thought, and thus is your state of mind.’

dn28:6.13.verse: And even if they reveal this many times, it turns out exactly so, not otherwise.

dn28:6.14.verse: This is the third way of revealing.

dn28:6.15.verse: Furthermore, someone comprehends the mind of one who has attained the immersion that’s free of placing the mind and keeping it connected. They understand,

dn28:6.16.verse: ‘Judging by the way this worthy’s intentions are directed, immediately after this mind state, they’ll think this thought.’

dn28:6.17.verse: And even if they reveal this many times, it turns out exactly so, not otherwise.

dn28:6.18.verse: This is the fourth way of revealing.

dn28:6.19.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to the ways of revealing.

dn28:7.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches the attainments of vision is unsurpassable.

dn28:7.2.verse: There are these four attainments of vision.

dn28:7.3.verse: Firstly, some ascetic or brahmin—by dint of keen, resolute, committed, and diligent effort, and right application of mind—experiences an immersion of the heart of such a kind that they examine their own body up from the soles of the feet and down from the tips of the hairs, wrapped in skin and full of many kinds of filth.

dn28:7.4.verse: ‘In this body there is head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, diaphragm, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, undigested food, feces, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, urine.’

dn28:7.5.verse: This is the first attainment of vision.

dn28:7.6.verse: Furthermore, some ascetic or brahmin experiences that immersion and examines their own body.

dn28:7.7.verse: ‘In this body there is head hair … urine.’

dn28:7.8.verse: Going further, they examine a person’s bones with skin, flesh, and blood.

dn28:7.9.verse: This is the second attainment of vision.

dn28:7.10.verse: Furthermore, some ascetic or brahmin experiences that immersion and examines their own body.

dn28:7.11.verse: ‘In this body there is head hair … urine.’

dn28:7.12.verse: Going further, they examine a person’s bones with skin, flesh, and blood.

dn28:7.13.verse: And they understand of a person that their stream of consciousness is consistent on both sides: established in both this world and the next.

dn28:7.14.verse: This is the third attainment of vision.

dn28:7.15.verse: Furthermore, some ascetic or brahmin experiences that immersion and examines their own body.

dn28:7.16.verse: ‘In this body there is head hair … urine.’

dn28:7.17.verse: Going further, they examine a person’s bones with skin, flesh, and blood.

dn28:7.18.verse: They understand of a person that their stream of consciousness is consistent on both sides: not established in either this world or the next.

dn28:7.19.verse: This is the fourth attainment of vision.

dn28:7.20.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to attainments of vision.

dn28:8.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches the description of individuals is unsurpassable.

dn28:8.3.verse: One freed both ways, one freed by wisdom, a direct witness, one attained to view, one freed by faith, a follower of teachings, a follower by faith.

dn28:8.4.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to the description of individuals.

dn28:9.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches the kinds of striving is unsurpassable.

dn28:9.2.verse: There are these seven awakening factors: the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

dn28:9.3.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to the kinds of striving.

dn28:10.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches the ways of practice is unsurpassable.

dn28:10.4.verse: pleasant practice with slow insight, and

dn28:10.6.verse: Of these, the painful practice with slow insight is said to be inferior both ways: because it’s painful and because it’s slow.

dn28:10.7.verse: The painful practice with swift insight is said to be inferior because it’s painful.

dn28:10.8.verse: The pleasant practice with slow insight is said to be inferior because it’s slow.

dn28:10.9.verse: But the pleasant practice with swift insight is said to be superior both ways: because it’s pleasant and because it’s swift.

dn28:10.10.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to the ways of practice.

dn28:11.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches behavior in speech is unsurpassable.

dn28:11.2.verse: It’s when someone doesn’t use speech that’s connected with lying, or divisive, or backbiting, or aggressively trying to win.

dn28:11.3.verse: They speak only wise counsel, valuable and timely.

dn28:11.4.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to behavior in speech.

dn28:12.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches a person’s ethical behavior is unsurpassable.

dn28:12.2.verse: It’s when someone is honest and faithful. They don’t use deceit, flattery, hinting, or belittling, and they don’t use material things to chase after other material things. They guard the sense doors and eat in moderation. They’re fair, dedicated to wakefulness, tireless, energetic, and meditative. They have good memory, eloquence, rememberance, retention, and thoughtfulness. They’re not greedy for sensual pleasures. They are mindful and alert.

dn28:12.3.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to a person’s ethical behavior.

dn28:13.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches the different degrees of responsiveness to instruction is unsurpassable.

dn28:13.2.verse: There are these four degrees of responsiveness to instruction.

dn28:13.3.verse: The Buddha knows by investigating inside another individual:

dn28:13.4.verse: ‘By practicing as instructed this individual will, with the ending of three fetters, become a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.’

dn28:13.5.verse: The Buddha knows by investigating inside another individual:

dn28:13.6.verse: ‘By practicing as instructed this individual will, with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, become a once-returner. They will come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.’

dn28:13.7.verse: The Buddha knows by investigating inside to another individual:

dn28:13.8.verse: ‘By practicing as instructed this individual will, with the ending of the five lower fetters, be reborn spontaneously. They will be extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.’

dn28:13.9.verse: The Buddha knows by investigating inside another individual:

dn28:13.10.verse: ‘By practicing as instructed this individual will realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’

dn28:13.11.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to the different degrees of responsiveness to instruction.

dn28:14.0.verse: 1.11. The Knowledge and Freedom of Others

dn28:14.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches the knowledge and freedom of other individuals is unsurpassable.

dn28:14.2.verse: The Buddha knows by investigating inside another individual:

dn28:14.3.verse: ‘With the ending of three fetters this individual will become a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.’

dn28:14.4.verse: The Buddha knows by investigating inside another individual:

dn28:14.5.verse: ‘With the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, this individual will become a once-returner. They will come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.’

dn28:14.6.verse: The Buddha knows by investigating inside another individual:

dn28:14.7.verse: ‘With the ending of the five lower fetters, this individual will be reborn spontaneously. They will be extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.’

dn28:14.8.verse: The Buddha knows by investigating inside another individual:

dn28:14.9.verse: ‘This individual will realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’

dn28:14.10.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to the knowledge and freedom of other individuals.

dn28:15.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches eternalist doctrines is unsurpassable.

dn28:15.2.verse: There are these three eternalist doctrines.

dn28:15.3.verse: Firstly, some ascetic or brahmin—by dint of keen, resolute, committed, and diligent effort, and right application of mind—experiences an immersion of the heart of such a kind that they recollect many hundreds of thousands of past lives,

dn28:15.6.verse: ‘I know that in the past the cosmos expanded or contracted.

dn28:15.7.verse: I don’t know whether in the future the cosmos will expand or contract.

dn28:15.8.verse: The self and the cosmos are eternal, barren, steady as a mountain peak, standing firm like a pillar. They remain the same for all eternity, while these sentient beings wander and transmigrate and pass away and rearise.’

dn28:15.9.verse: This is the first eternalist doctrine.

dn28:15.10.verse: Furthermore, some ascetic or brahmin—by dint of keen, resolute, committed, and diligent effort, and right application of mind—experiences an immersion of the heart of such a kind that they recollect their past lives for as many as ten eons of the expansion and contraction of the cosmos,

dn28:15.13.verse: ‘I know that in the past the cosmos expanded or contracted.

dn28:15.14.verse: I don’t know whether in the future the cosmos will expand or contract.

dn28:15.15.verse: The self and the cosmos are eternal, barren, steady as a mountain peak, standing firm like a pillar.

dn28:15.16.verse: They remain the same for all eternity, while these sentient beings wander and transmigrate and pass away and rearise.’

dn28:15.17.verse: This is the second eternalist doctrine.

dn28:15.18.verse: Furthermore, some ascetic or brahmin—by dint of keen, resolute, committed, and diligent effort, and right application of mind—experiences an immersion of the heart of such a kind that they recollect their past lives for as many as forty eons of the expansion and contraction of the cosmos,

dn28:15.21.verse: ‘I know that in the past the cosmos expanded or contracted.

dn28:15.22.verse: I don’t know whether in the future the cosmos will expand or contract.

dn28:15.23.verse: The self and the cosmos are eternal, barren, steady as a mountain peak, standing firm like a pillar.

dn28:15.24.verse: They remain the same for all eternity, while these sentient beings wander and transmigrate and pass away and rearise.’

dn28:15.25.verse: This is the third eternalist doctrine.

dn28:15.26.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to eternalist doctrines.

dn28:16.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches the knowledge of recollecting past lives is unsurpassable.

dn28:16.2.verse: It’s when some ascetic or brahmin—by dint of keen, resolute, committed, and diligent effort, and right application of mind—experiences an immersion of the heart of such a kind that they recollect their many kinds of past lives.

dn28:16.3.verse: That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. They remember:

dn28:16.4.verse: ‘There, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn somewhere else. There, too, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn here.’ And so they recollect their many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

dn28:16.5.verse: Sir, there are gods whose lifespan cannot be reckoned or calculated.

dn28:16.6.verse: Still, no matter what incarnation they have previously been reborn in—whether formed or formless or percipient or non-percipient or neither percipient nor non-percipient—

dn28:16.7.verse: they recollect their many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

dn28:16.8.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to the knowledge of recollecting past lives.

dn28:17.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches the knowledge of the death and rebirth of sentient beings is unsurpassable.
