dn28:17.2.verse: It’s when some ascetic or brahmin—by dint of keen, resolute, committed, and diligent effort, and right application of mind—experiences an immersion of the heart of such a kind that with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—

dn28:17.3.verse: inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds: ‘These dear beings did bad things by way of body, speech, and mind. They denounced the noble ones; they had wrong view; and they chose to act out of that wrong view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell. These dear beings, however, did good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They never denounced the noble ones; they had right view; and they chose to act out of that right view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’ And so, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

dn28:17.4.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to the knowledge of death and rebirth.

dn28:18.1.verse: And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches psychic power is unsurpassable.

dn28:18.2.verse: There are these two kinds of psychic power.

dn28:18.3.verse: There are psychic powers that are accompanied by defilements and attachments, and are said to be ignoble.

dn28:18.4.verse: And there are psychic powers that are free of defilements and attachments, and are said to be noble.

dn28:18.5.verse: What are the psychic powers that are accompanied by defilements and attachments, and are said to be ignoble?

dn28:18.6.verse: It’s when some ascetic or brahmin—by dint of keen, resolute, committed, and diligent effort, and right application of mind—experiences an immersion of the heart of such a kind that they wield the many kinds of psychic power:

dn28:18.7.verse: multiplying themselves and becoming one again; materializing and dematerializing; going unobstructed through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; diving in and out of the earth as if it were water; walking on water as if it were earth; flying cross-legged through the sky like a bird; touching and stroking with the hand the sun and moon, so mighty and powerful; controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity.

dn28:18.8.verse: These are the psychic powers that are accompanied by defilements and attachments, and are said to be ignoble.

dn28:18.9.verse: But what are the psychic powers that are free of defilements and attachments, and are said to be noble?

dn28:18.10.verse: It’s when, if a mendicant wishes: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

dn28:18.11.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

dn28:18.12.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

dn28:18.13.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive and the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

dn28:18.14.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

dn28:18.15.verse: These are the psychic powers that are free of defilements and attachments, and are said to be noble.

dn28:18.16.verse: This is unsurpassable when it comes to psychic powers.

dn28:18.17.verse: The Buddha understands this without exception. There is nothing to be understood beyond this whereby another ascetic or brahmin might be superior in direct knowledge to the Buddha when it comes to psychic powers.

dn28:19.1.verse: The Buddha has achieved what should be achieved by a faithful gentleman by being energetic and strong, by human strength, energy, vigor, and exertion.

dn28:19.2.verse: The Buddha doesn’t indulge in sensual pleasures, which are low, crude, ordinary, ignoble, and pointless. And he doesn’t indulge in self-mortification, which is painful, ignoble, and pointless.

dn28:19.3.verse: He gets the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when he wants, without trouble or difficulty.

dn28:19.5.verse: Sir, if they were to ask me,

dn28:19.6.verse: ‘Reverend Sāriputta, is there any other ascetic or brahmin—whether past, future, or present—whose direct knowledge is superior to the Buddha when it comes to awakening?’ I would tell them ‘No.’

dn28:19.9.verse: But if they were to ask me,

dn28:19.10.verse: ‘Reverend Sāriputta, is there any other ascetic or brahmin—whether past or future—whose direct knowledge is equal to the Buddha when it comes to awakening?’ I would tell them ‘Yes.’

dn28:19.12.verse: But if they were to ask: ‘Reverend Sāriputta, is there any other ascetic or brahmin at present whose direct knowledge is equal to the Buddha when it comes to awakening?’ I would tell them ‘No.’

dn28:19.13.verse: But if they were to ask me,

dn28:19.14.verse: ‘But why does Venerable Sāriputta grant this in respect of some but not others?’ I would answer them like this,

dn28:19.15.verse: ‘Reverends, I have heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

dn28:19.16.verse: “The perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas of the past were equal in awakening to myself.”

dn28:19.17.verse: And I have heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

dn28:19.18.verse: “The perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas of the future will be equal in awakening to myself.”

dn28:19.19.verse: And I have also heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

dn28:19.20.verse: “It’s impossible for two perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas to arise in the same solar system at the same time.”’

dn28:19.21.verse: Answering this way, I trust that I repeated what the Buddha has said, and didn’t misrepresent him with an untruth. I trust my explanation was in line with the teaching, and that there are no legitimate grounds for rebuttal or criticism.”

dn28:19.22.verse: “Indeed, Sāriputta, in answering this way you repeat what I’ve said, and don’t misrepresent me with an untruth. Your explanation is in line with the teaching, and there are no legitimate grounds for rebuttal or criticism.”

dn28:20.1.verse: When he had spoken, Venerable Udāyī said to the Buddha,

dn28:20.2.verse: “It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing! The Realized One has so few wishes, such contentment, such self-effacement!

dn28:20.3.verse: For even though the Realized One has such power and might, he will not make a display of himself.

dn28:20.4.verse: If the wanderers following other religions were to see even a single one of these qualities in themselves they’d carry around a banner to that effect.

dn28:20.5.verse: It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing! The Realized One has so few wishes, such contentment, such self-effacement!

dn28:20.6.verse: For even though the Realized One has such power and might, he will not make a display of himself.”

dn28:20.7.verse: “See, Udāyī, how the Realized One has so few wishes, such contentment, such self-effacement.

dn28:20.8.verse: For even though the Realized One has such power and might, he will not make a display of himself.

dn28:20.9.verse: If the wanderers following other religions were to see even a single one of these qualities in themselves they’d carry around a banner to that effect.

dn28:20.10.verse: See, Udāyī, how the Realized One has so few wishes, such contentment, such self-effacement.

dn28:20.11.verse: For even though the Realized One has such power and might, he will not make a display of himself.”

dn28:21.1.verse: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Sāriputta,

dn28:21.2.verse: “So Sāriputta, you should frequently speak this exposition of the teaching to the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen.

dn28:21.3.verse: Though there will be some futile people who have doubt or uncertainty regarding the Realized One, when they hear this exposition of the teaching they’ll give up that doubt or uncertainty.”

dn28:21.4.verse: That’s how Venerable Sāriputta declared his confidence in the Buddha’s presence.

dn28:21.5.verse: And that’s why the name of this discussion is “Inspiring Confidence”.

dn29:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans in a stilt longhouse in a mango grove belonging to those Sakyans named Vedhaññā.

dn29:1.3.verse: Now at that time the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan had recently passed away at Pāvā.

dn29:1.4.verse: With his passing the Jain ascetics split, dividing into two factions, fighting, quarreling, and disputing, continually wounding each other with barbed words:

dn29:1.5.verse: “You don’t understand this teaching and training. I understand this teaching and training. What, you understand this teaching and training? You’re practicing wrong. I’m practicing right. I stay on topic, you don’t. You said last what you should have said first. You said first what you should have said last. What you’ve thought so much about has been disproved. Your doctrine is refuted. Go on, save your doctrine! You’re trapped; get yourself out of this—if you can!”

dn29:1.6.verse: You’d think there was nothing but slaughter going on among the Jain ascetics.

dn29:1.7.verse: And the Jain Ñātika’s white-clothed lay disciples were disillusioned, dismayed, and disappointed in the Jain ascetics. They were equally disappointed with a teaching and training so poorly explained and poorly propounded, not emancipating, not leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is not a fully awakened Buddha, with broken monument and without a refuge.

dn29:2.1.verse: And then, after completing the rainy season residence near Pāvā, the novice Cunda went to see Venerable Ānanda at Sāma village. He bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

dn29:2.5.verse: “Reverend Cunda, we should see the Buddha about this matter.

dn29:2.6.verse: Come, let’s go to the Buddha and tell him about this.”

dn29:3.1.verse: Then Ānanda and Cunda went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

dn29:4.1.verse: “That’s what happens, Cunda, when a teaching and training is poorly explained and poorly propounded, not emancipating, not leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is not a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:4.2.verse: Take the case where a teacher is not awakened, and the teaching is poorly explained and poorly propounded, not emancipating, not leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is not a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:4.3.verse: A disciple in that teaching does not practice in line with the teaching, does not practice following that procedure, does not live in line with the teaching. They proceed having turned away from that teaching.

dn29:4.4.verse: You should say this to them,

dn29:4.5.verse: ‘You’re fortunate, reverend, you’re so very fortunate!

dn29:4.6.verse: For your teacher is not awakened, and their teaching is poorly explained and poorly propounded, not emancipating, not leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is not a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:4.7.verse: But you don’t practice in line with that teaching, you don’t practice following that procedure, you don’t live in line with the teaching. You proceed having turned away from that teaching.’

dn29:4.8.verse: In such a case the teacher and the teaching are to blame, but the disciple deserves praise.

dn29:4.9.verse: Suppose someone was to say to such a disciple,

dn29:4.10.verse: ‘Come on, venerable, practice as taught and pointed out by your teacher.’

dn29:4.11.verse: The one who encourages, the one who they encourage, and the one who practices accordingly all brim with much wickedness.

dn29:4.13.verse: It’s because that teaching and training is poorly explained and poorly propounded, not emancipating, not leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is not a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:5.1.verse: Take the case where a teacher is not awakened, and the teaching is poorly explained and poorly propounded, not emancipating, not leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is not a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:5.2.verse: A disciple in that teaching practices in line with the teaching, practices following that procedure, lives in line with the teaching. They proceed having undertaken that teaching.

dn29:5.3.verse: You should say this to them,

dn29:5.4.verse: ‘It’s your loss, reverend, it’s your misfortune! For your teacher is not awakened, and their teaching is poorly explained and poorly propounded, not emancipating, not leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is not a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:5.5.verse: And you practice in line with that teaching, you practice following that procedure, you live in line with the teaching. You proceed having undertaken that teaching.’

dn29:5.6.verse: In such a case the teacher, the teaching, and the disciple are all to blame.

dn29:5.7.verse: Suppose someone was to say to such a disciple,

dn29:5.8.verse: ‘Clearly the venerable is practicing systematically and will succeed in that system.’

dn29:5.9.verse: The one who praises, the one who they praise, and the one who, being praised, rouses up even more energy all brim with much wickedness.

dn29:5.11.verse: It’s because that teaching and training is poorly explained and poorly propounded, not emancipating, not leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is not a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:6.1.verse: Take the case where a teacher is awakened, and the teaching is well explained and well propounded, emancipating, leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:6.2.verse: A disciple in that teaching does not practice in line with the teaching, does not practice following that procedure, does not live in line with the teaching. They proceed having turned away from that teaching.

dn29:6.3.verse: You should say this to them,

dn29:6.4.verse: ‘It’s your loss, reverend, it’s your misfortune! For your teacher is awakened, and their teaching is well explained and well propounded, emancipating, leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:6.5.verse: But you don’t practice in line with that teaching, you don’t practice following that procedure, you don’t live in line with the teaching. You proceed having turned away from that teaching.’

dn29:6.6.verse: In such a case the teacher and the teaching deserve praise, but the disciple is to blame.

dn29:6.7.verse: Suppose someone was to say to such a disciple,

dn29:6.8.verse: ‘Come on, venerable, practice as taught and pointed out by your teacher.’

dn29:6.9.verse: The one who encourages, the one who they encourage, and the one who practices accordingly all brim with much merit.

dn29:6.11.verse: It’s because that teaching and training is well explained and well propounded, emancipating, leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:7.1.verse: Take the case where a teacher is awakened, and the teaching is well explained and well propounded, emancipating, leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:7.2.verse: A disciple in that teaching practices in line with the teaching, practices following that procedure, lives in line with the teaching. They proceed having undertaken that teaching.

dn29:7.3.verse: You should say this to them,

dn29:7.4.verse: ‘You’re fortunate, reverend, you’re so very fortunate!

dn29:7.5.verse: For your teacher is awakened, and their teaching is well explained and well propounded, emancipating, leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:7.6.verse: And you practice in line with that teaching, you practice following that procedure, you live in line with the teaching. You proceed having undertaken that teaching.’

dn29:7.7.verse: In such a case the teacher, the teaching, and the disciple all deserve praise.

dn29:7.8.verse: Suppose someone was to say to such a disciple,

dn29:7.9.verse: ‘Clearly the venerable is practicing systematically and will succeed in that system.’

dn29:7.10.verse: The one who praises, the one who they praise, and the one who, being praised, rouses up even more energy all brim with much merit.

dn29:7.12.verse: It’s because that teaching and training is well explained and well propounded, emancipating, leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:8.1.verse: Take the case where a teacher arises in the world who is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha. The teaching is well explained and well propounded, emancipating, leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is fully awakened.

dn29:8.2.verse: But the disciples have not been educated in the meaning of that good teaching. And the spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure has not been disclosed and divulged to them; its sayings have not all been collected; and it has not been fully revealed with its demonstrable basis among gods and humans.

dn29:8.3.verse: And then their teacher passes away.

dn29:8.4.verse: When such a teacher has passed away the disciples are tormented by regrets.

dn29:8.6.verse: They think: ‘Our teacher was perfected, a fully awakened Buddha. His teaching was well explained, but we were not educated in its meaning. And the spiritual practice was not fully disclosed and divulged to us; its sayings have not all been collected; and it has not been fully revealed with its demonstrable basis among gods and humans.

dn29:8.7.verse: And then our teacher passed away.’

dn29:8.8.verse: When such a teacher has passed away the disciples are tormented by regrets.

dn29:9.1.verse: Take the case where a teacher arises in the world who is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha. The teaching is well explained and well propounded, emancipating, leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is fully awakened.

dn29:9.2.verse: The disciples have been educated in the meaning of that good teaching. And the spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure has been disclosed and divulged to them; its sayings have all been collected; and it has been fully revealed with its demonstrable basis among gods and humans.

dn29:9.3.verse: And then their teacher passes away.

dn29:9.4.verse: When such a teacher has passed away the disciples are free of regrets.

dn29:9.6.verse: They think: ‘Our teacher was perfected, a fully awakened Buddha.

dn29:9.8.verse: we were educated in its meaning, and the spiritual practice was fully revealed to us.

dn29:9.9.verse: And then our teacher passed away.’

dn29:9.10.verse: When such a teacher has passed away the disciples are free of regrets.

dn29:10.0.verse: 5. On the Incomplete Spiritual Path, Etc.

dn29:10.1.verse: Now suppose, Cunda, that a spiritual path possesses those factors. But the teacher is not senior, long standing, long gone forth, advanced in years, and reached the final stage of life.

dn29:10.2.verse: Then that spiritual path is incomplete in that respect.

dn29:10.3.verse: But when a spiritual path possesses those factors and the teacher is senior,

dn29:10.4.verse: then that spiritual path is complete in that respect.

dn29:11.1.verse: Now suppose that a spiritual path possesses those factors and the teacher is senior. But there are no senior monk disciples who are competent, educated, self-assured, have attained sanctuary from the yoke,

dn29:11.2.verse: who can rightly explain the true teaching, and who can legitimately and completely refute the doctrines of others that come up, and teach with a demonstrable basis.

dn29:11.3.verse: Then that spiritual path is incomplete in that respect.

dn29:12.1.verse: But when a spiritual path possesses those factors and the teacher is senior and there are competent senior monks,

dn29:12.3.verse: then that spiritual path is complete in that respect.

dn29:12.4.verse: Now suppose that a spiritual path possesses those factors and the teacher is senior and there are competent senior monks.

dn29:12.6.verse: But there are no competent middle monks,

dn29:12.15.verse: There are white-clothed laywomen enjoying sensual pleasures, but the spiritual path is not successful and prosperous, extensive, popular, widespread, and fully revealed among gods and humans …

dn29:12.16.verse: the spiritual path is successful and prosperous, extensive, popular, widespread, and fully revealed among gods and humans, but it has not reached the peak of material things and fame.

dn29:12.17.verse: Then that spiritual path is incomplete in that respect.

dn29:13.1.verse: But when a spiritual path possesses those factors and the teacher is senior and there are competent senior monks,

dn29:13.12.verse: and the spiritual path is successful and prosperous, extensive, popular, widespread, and fully revealed among gods and humans, and it has reached the peak of material things and fame,

dn29:13.13.verse: then that spiritual path is complete in that respect.

dn29:14.1.verse: I, Cunda, am a teacher who has arisen in the world today, perfected and fully awakened.

dn29:14.2.verse: The teaching is well explained and well propounded, emancipating, leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is fully awakened.

dn29:14.3.verse: My disciples have been educated in the meaning of that good teaching. And the spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure has been disclosed and divulged to them with all its collected sayings, with its demonstrable basis, fully revealed among gods and humans.

dn29:14.4.verse: I am a teacher today who is senior, long standing, long gone forth, advanced in years, and have reached the final stage of life.

dn29:15.1.verse: I have today disciples who are competent senior monks,

dn29:15.12.verse: Today my spiritual path is successful and prosperous, extensive, popular, widespread, and fully revealed among gods and humans.

dn29:16.1.verse: Of all the teachers in the world today, Cunda, I don’t see even a single one who has reached the peak of material things and fame like me.

dn29:16.2.verse: Of all the spiritual communities and groups in the world today, Cunda, I don’t see even a single one who has reached the pinnacle of material things and fame like the mendicant Saṅgha.

dn29:16.4.verse: And if there’s any spiritual path of which it may be rightly said that

dn29:16.5.verse: it’s endowed with all good qualities, complete in all good qualities, neither too little nor too much, well explained, whole, complete, and fully revealed,

dn29:16.6.verse: it’s of this spiritual path that this should be said.

dn29:16.8.verse: Uddaka son of Rāma used to say:

dn29:16.10.verse: But seeing what does one not see?

dn29:16.11.verse: You can see the blade of a well-sharpened razor, but not the edge.

dn29:16.14.verse: But that saying of Uddaka’s is low, crude, ordinary, ignoble, and pointless, as it’s only about a razor.

dn29:16.15.verse: If there’s anything of which it may be rightly said:

dn29:16.16.verse: ‘Seeing, one does not see,’ it’s of this that it should be said.

dn29:16.18.verse: Seeing what does one not see?

dn29:16.19.verse: One sees this: a spiritual path endowed with all good qualities, complete in all good qualities, neither too little nor too much, well explained, whole, complete, and fully revealed.

dn29:16.20.verse: One does not see this: anything that, were it to be removed, would make it purer.

dn29:16.21.verse: One does not see this: anything that, were it to be added, would make it more complete.

dn29:17.0.verse: 6. Teachings Should be Recited in Concert

dn29:17.1.verse: So, Cunda, you should all come together and recite in concert, without disputing, those things I have taught you from my direct knowledge, comparing meaning with meaning and phrasing with phrasing, so that this spiritual path may last for a long time. That would be for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

dn29:17.2.verse: And what are those things I have taught from my direct knowledge?

dn29:17.3.verse: They are the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, and the noble eightfold path.

dn29:17.4.verse: These are the things I have taught from my own direct knowledge.

dn29:18.1.verse: Suppose one of those spiritual companions who is training in harmony and mutual appreciation, without disputing, were to recite the teaching in the Saṅgha.

dn29:18.3.verse: ‘This venerable misconstrues the meaning and mistakes the phrasing.’

dn29:18.4.verse: You should neither approve nor reject them, but say,

dn29:18.5.verse: ‘Reverend, if this is the meaning, the phrasing may either be this or that: which is more fitting? And if this is the phrasing, the meaning may be either this or that: which is more fitting?’

dn29:18.7.verse: ‘This phrasing fits the meaning better than that. And this meaning fits the phrasing better than that.’

dn29:18.8.verse: Without flattering or rebuking them, you should carefully persuade them by examining that meaning and that phrasing.

dn29:19.1.verse: Suppose another spiritual companion were to recite the teaching in the Saṅgha.

dn29:19.3.verse: ‘This venerable misconstrues the meaning but gets the phrasing right.’

dn29:19.4.verse: You should neither approve nor reject them, but say,

dn29:19.5.verse: ‘Reverend, if this is the phrasing, the meaning may be either this or that: which is more fitting?’

dn29:19.7.verse: ‘This meaning fits the phrasing better than that.’

dn29:19.8.verse: Without flattering or rebuking, you should carefully persuade them by examining that meaning.

dn29:20.1.verse: Suppose another spiritual companion were to recite the teaching in the Saṅgha.

dn29:20.3.verse: ‘This venerable construes the meaning correctly but mistakes the phrasing.’

dn29:20.4.verse: You should neither approve nor reject them, but say,

dn29:20.5.verse: ‘Reverend, if this is the meaning, the phrasing may be either this or that: which is more fitting?’

dn29:20.7.verse: ‘This phrasing fits the meaning better than that.’

dn29:20.8.verse: Without flattering or rebuking, you should carefully persuade them by examining that phrasing.

dn29:21.1.verse: Suppose another spiritual companion were to recite the teaching in the Saṅgha.

dn29:21.3.verse: ‘This venerable construes the meaning correctly and gets the phrasing right.’

dn29:21.4.verse: Saying ‘Good!’ you should express approval and appreciation of that mendicant’s statement,

dn29:21.6.verse: ‘We are fortunate, reverend, so very fortunate

dn29:21.7.verse: to see a venerable such as yourself, so well-versed in the meaning and the phrasing, as one of our spiritual companions!’

dn29:22.1.verse: Cunda, I do not teach you solely for restraining defilements that affect this life.

dn29:22.2.verse: Nor do I teach solely for protecting against defilements that affect lives to come.

dn29:22.3.verse: I teach both for restraining defilements that affect this life and

dn29:22.4.verse: protecting against defilements that affect lives to come.

dn29:22.5.verse: And that’s why I have allowed robes for you that suffice

dn29:22.6.verse: only for the sake of warding off cold and heat; for warding off the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles; and for covering up the private parts.

dn29:22.7.verse: I have allowed almsfood for you that suffices

dn29:22.8.verse: only to sustain this body, avoid harm, and support spiritual practice; so that you will put an end to old discomfort and not give rise to new discomfort, and will keep on living blamelessly and at ease.

dn29:22.9.verse: I have allowed lodgings for you that suffice

dn29:22.10.verse: only for the sake of warding off cold and heat; for warding off the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles; to shelter from harsh weather and to enjoy retreat.

dn29:22.11.verse: I have allowed medicines and supplies for the sick for you that suffice

dn29:22.12.verse: only for the sake of warding off the pains of illness and to promote good health.

dn29:23.1.verse: It’s possible that wanderers of other religions might say,

dn29:23.2.verse: ‘The ascetics who follow the Sakyan live indulging in pleasure.’

dn29:23.5.verse: For there are many different kinds of indulgence in pleasure.’

dn29:23.6.verse: These four kinds of indulgence in pleasure, Cunda, are low, crude, ordinary, ignoble, and pointless. They don’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

dn29:23.8.verse: It’s when some fool makes themselves happy and pleased by killing living creatures.

dn29:23.9.verse: This is the first kind of indulgence in pleasure.

dn29:23.10.verse: Furthermore, someone makes themselves happy and pleased by theft.

dn29:23.11.verse: This is the second kind of indulgence in pleasure.

dn29:23.12.verse: Furthermore, someone makes themselves happy and pleased by lying.

dn29:23.13.verse: This is the third kind of indulgence in pleasure.

dn29:23.14.verse: Furthermore, someone amuses themselves, supplied and provided with the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

dn29:23.15.verse: This is the fourth kind of indulgence in pleasure.

dn29:23.16.verse: These are the four kinds of indulgence in pleasure that are low, crude, ordinary, ignoble, and pointless. They don’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

dn29:24.1.verse: It’s possible that wanderers of other religions might say,

dn29:24.2.verse: ‘The ascetics who follow the Sakyan live indulging in pleasure in these four ways.’

dn29:24.4.verse: It isn’t right to say that about you; it misrepresents you with an untruth.

dn29:24.5.verse: Cunda, these four kinds of indulgence in pleasure lead solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

dn29:24.7.verse: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

dn29:24.8.verse: This is the first kind of indulgence in pleasure.

dn29:24.9.verse: Furthermore, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, a mendicant enters and remains in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

dn29:24.10.verse: This is the second kind of indulgence in pleasure.

dn29:24.11.verse: Furthermore, with the fading away of rapture, a mendicant enters and remains in the third absorption. They meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

dn29:24.12.verse: This is the third kind of indulgence in pleasure.

dn29:24.13.verse: Furthermore, with the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, a mendicant enters and remains in the fourth absorption. It is without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

dn29:24.14.verse: This is the fourth kind of indulgence in pleasure.

dn29:24.15.verse: These are the four kinds of indulgence in pleasure which lead solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

dn29:24.16.verse: It’s possible that wanderers of other religions might say,

dn29:24.17.verse: ‘The ascetics who follow the Sakyan live indulging in pleasure in these four ways.’

dn29:24.19.verse: It’s right to say that about you; it doesn’t misrepresent you with an untruth.

dn29:25.0.verse: 10. The Benefits of Indulgence in Pleasure

dn29:25.1.verse: It’s possible that wanderers of other religions might say,

dn29:25.2.verse: ‘How many fruits and benefits may be expected by those who live indulging in pleasure in these four ways?’

dn29:25.4.verse: ‘Four benefits may be expected by those who live indulging in pleasure in these four ways.

dn29:25.6.verse: Firstly, with the ending of three fetters a mendicant becomes a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

dn29:25.7.verse: This is the first fruit and benefit.

dn29:25.8.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant—with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion—becomes a once-returner. They come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.

dn29:25.9.verse: This is the second fruit and benefit.

dn29:25.10.verse: Furthermore, with the ending of the five lower fetters, a mendicant is reborn spontaneously and will become extinguished there, not liable to return from that world.

dn29:25.11.verse: This is the third fruit and benefit.

dn29:25.12.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and lives having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

dn29:25.13.verse: This is the fourth fruit and benefit.

dn29:25.14.verse: These four benefits may be expected by those who live indulging in pleasure in these four ways.’

dn29:26.1.verse: It’s possible that wanderers of other religions might say,

dn29:26.2.verse: ‘The ascetics who follow the Sakyan are fickle.’

dn29:26.4.verse: ‘Reverends, these things have been taught and pointed out for his disciples by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, not to be transgressed so long as life lasts.

dn29:26.5.verse: Suppose there was an Indra’s pillar or an iron pillar with deep foundations, firmly embedded, imperturbable and unshakable.

dn29:26.6.verse: In the same way, these things have been taught and pointed out for his disciples by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, not to be transgressed so long as life lasts.

dn29:26.7.verse: A mendicant who is perfected—with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment—can’t transgress in nine respects.

dn29:26.8.verse: A mendicant with defilements ended can’t deliberately take the life of a living creature, take something with the intention to steal, have sex, tell a deliberate lie, or store up goods for their own enjoyment like they used to as a layperson. And they can’t make decisions prejudiced by favoritism, hostility, stupidity, or cowardice.

dn29:26.9.verse: A mendicant who is perfected can’t transgress in these nine respects.’

dn29:27.1.verse: It’s possible that wanderers of other religions might say,

dn29:27.2.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama demonstrates boundless knowledge and vision of the past, but not of the future. What’s up with that?’

dn29:27.3.verse: Those wanderers, like incompetent fools, seem to imagine that one kind of knowledge and vision can be demonstrated by means of another kind of knowledge and vision.

dn29:27.4.verse: Regarding the past, the Realized One has knowledge stemming from memory.

dn29:27.5.verse: He recollects as far as he wants.

dn29:27.6.verse: Regarding the future, the Realized One has the knowledge born of awakening:

dn29:27.7.verse: ‘This is my last rebirth; now there’ll be no more future lives.’

dn29:28.1.verse: If a question about the past is untrue, false, and pointless, the Realized One does not reply.

dn29:28.2.verse: If a question about the past is true and correct, but pointless, he does not reply.

dn29:28.3.verse: If a question about the past is true, correct, and beneficial, he knows the right time to reply.

dn29:28.4.verse: And the Realized One replies to questions about the future or the present in the same way.

dn29:28.8.verse: And so the Realized One has speech that’s well-timed, true, meaningful, in line with the teaching and training. That’s why he’s called the ‘Realized One’.

dn29:29.1.verse: In this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—whatever is seen, heard, thought, known, attained, sought, and explored by the mind, all that has been understood by the Realized One.

dn29:29.2.verse: That’s why he’s called the ‘Realized One’.

dn29:29.3.verse: From the night when the Realized One awakens to the supreme perfect awakening until the night he becomes fully extinguished—in the element of extinguishment with no residue—everything he speaks, says, and expresses is real, not otherwise.

dn29:29.4.verse: That’s why he’s called the ‘Realized One’.

dn29:29.5.verse: The Realized One does as he says, and says as he does.

dn29:29.6.verse: Since this is so, that’s why he’s called the ‘Realized One’.

dn29:29.7.verse: In this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—the Realized One is the vanquisher, the unvanquished, the universal seer, the wielder of power.

dn29:30.1.verse: It’s possible that wanderers of other religions might say,

dn29:30.2.verse: ‘Is this your view: “A realized one still exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile”?’

dn29:30.4.verse: ‘Reverend, this has not been declared by the Buddha.’

dn29:30.7.verse: ‘Then is this your view: “A realized one no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile”?’

dn29:30.9.verse: ‘This too has not been declared by the Buddha.’

dn29:30.12.verse: ‘Then is this your view: “A realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile”?’

dn29:30.14.verse: ‘This too has not been declared by the Buddha.’

dn29:30.17.verse: ‘Then is this your view: “A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile”?’

dn29:30.19.verse: ‘This too has not been declared by the Buddha.’

dn29:31.2.verse: ‘But why has this not been declared by the ascetic Gotama?’

dn29:31.4.verse: ‘Because it’s not beneficial or relevant to the fundamentals of the spiritual life. It doesn’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment. That’s why it hasn’t been declared by the Buddha.’

dn29:32.1.verse: It’s possible that wanderers of other religions might say,

dn29:32.2.verse: ‘But what has been declared by the ascetic Gotama?’

dn29:32.4.verse: ‘What has been declared by the Buddha is this: “This is suffering”—“This is the origin of suffering”—“This is the cessation of suffering”—“This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.”’

dn29:33.2.verse: ‘But why has this been declared by the ascetic Gotama?’

dn29:33.4.verse: ‘Because it’s beneficial and relevant to the fundamentals of the spiritual life. It leads to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment. That’s why it has been declared by the Buddha.’

dn29:34.1.verse: Cunda, I have explained to you as they should be explained the views that some rely on regarding the first beginning.

dn29:34.2.verse: Shall I explain them to you in the wrong way?

dn29:34.3.verse: I have explained to you as they should be explained the views that some rely on regarding the final end.

dn29:34.4.verse: Shall I explain them to you in the wrong way?

dn29:34.5.verse: What are the views that some rely on regarding the first beginning?

dn29:34.7.verse: There are some ascetics and brahmins who have this doctrine and view:

dn29:34.8.verse: ‘The self and the cosmos are eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’

dn29:34.9.verse: There are some ascetics and brahmins who have this doctrine and view:

dn29:34.10.verse: ‘The self and the cosmos are not eternal,

dn29:34.11.verse: or both eternal and not eternal,

dn29:34.12.verse: or neither eternal nor not eternal.

dn29:34.13.verse: The self and the cosmos are made by oneself,

dn29:34.15.verse: or made by both oneself and another,

dn29:34.16.verse: or they have arisen anomalously, not made by oneself or another.

dn29:34.19.verse: or both eternal and not eternal,

dn29:34.20.verse: or neither eternal nor not eternal.

dn29:34.21.verse: Pleasure and pain are made by oneself,

dn29:34.23.verse: or made by both oneself and another,

dn29:34.24.verse: or they have arisen anomalously, not made by oneself or another. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’

dn29:35.1.verse: Regarding this, I go up to the ascetics and brahmins whose view is that

dn29:35.2.verse: the self and the cosmos are eternal,

dn29:35.5.verse: “The self and the cosmos are eternal”?’

dn29:35.7.verse: This is the only truth, anything else is futile,’

dn29:35.10.verse: Because there are beings who have different opinions on this topic.

dn29:35.11.verse: I don’t see any such expositions that are equal to my own, still less superior.

dn29:35.12.verse: Rather, I am the one who is superior when it comes to the higher exposition.

dn29:36.1.verse: Regarding this, I go up to the ascetics and brahmins who assert all the other views as described above.

dn29:36.22.verse: And in each case, I don’t grant that.

dn29:36.24.verse: Because there are beings who have different opinions on this topic.

dn29:36.25.verse: I don’t see any such expositions that are equal to my own, still less superior.

dn29:36.26.verse: Rather, I am the one who is superior when it comes to the higher exposition.

dn29:36.27.verse: These are the views that some rely on regarding the first beginning.

dn29:37.1.verse: What are the views that some rely on regarding the final end?

dn29:37.3.verse: There are some ascetics and brahmins who have this doctrine and view:

dn29:37.4.verse: ‘The self is healthy after death, and formed …

dn29:37.12.verse: or the self is annihilated and destroyed when the body breaks up, and doesn’t exist after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’

dn29:38.1.verse: Regarding this, I go up to the ascetics and brahmins whose view is that,

dn29:38.2.verse: ‘The self is formed and healthy after death,’

dn29:38.5.verse: “The self is formed and healthy after death”?’

dn29:38.7.verse: This is the only truth, anything else is futile,’

dn29:38.10.verse: Because there are beings who have different opinions on this topic.

dn29:38.11.verse: I don’t see any such expositions that are equal to my own, still less superior.

dn29:38.12.verse: Rather, I am the one who is superior when it comes to the higher exposition.

dn29:39.1.verse: Regarding this, I go up to the ascetics and brahmins who assert all the other views as described above.

dn29:39.14.verse: And in each case, I don’t grant that.

dn29:39.16.verse: Because there are beings who have different opinions on this topic.

dn29:39.17.verse: I don’t see any such expositions that are equal to my own, still less superior.

dn29:39.18.verse: Rather, I am the one who is superior when it comes to the higher exposition.

dn29:39.19.verse: These are the views that some rely on regarding the final end, which I have explained to you as they should be explained.

dn29:39.20.verse: Shall I explain them to you in the wrong way?

dn29:40.1.verse: I have taught and pointed out the four kinds of mindfulness meditation for giving up and going beyond all these views of the first beginning and the final end.

dn29:40.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

dn29:40.4.verse: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

dn29:40.6.verse: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

dn29:40.7.verse: These are the four kinds of mindfulness meditation that I have taught for giving up and going beyond all these views of the first beginning and the final end.”

dn29:41.1.verse: Now at that time Venerable Upavāṇa was standing behind the Buddha fanning him.

dn29:41.4.verse: This exposition of the teaching is impressive, sir,

dn29:41.5.verse: it is very impressive. Sir, what is the name of this exposition of the teaching?”

dn29:41.6.verse: “Well then, Upavāṇa, you may remember this exposition of the teaching as ‘The Impressive Discourse’.”

dn29:41.7.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

dn29:41.8.verse: Satisfied, Venerable Upavāṇa approved what the Buddha said.

dn30:0.2.verse: The Marks of a Great Man

dn30:1.1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

dn30:1.1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

dn30:1.1.7.verse: “There are thirty-two marks of a great man. A great man who possesses these has only two possible destinies, no other.

dn30:1.1.8.verse: If he stays at home he becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch, a just and principled king. His dominion extends to all four sides, he achieves stability in the country, and he possesses the seven treasures.

dn30:1.1.9.verse: He has the following seven treasures:

dn30:1.1.10.verse: the wheel, the elephant, the horse, the jewel, the woman, the householder, and the commander as the seventh treasure.

dn30:1.1.11.verse: He has over a thousand sons who are valiant and heroic, crushing the armies of his enemies.

dn30:1.1.12.verse: After conquering this land girt by sea, he reigns by principle, without rod or sword.

dn30:1.1.13.verse: But if he goes forth from the lay life to homelessness, he becomes a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, who has cast off the world’s veil.

dn30:1.2.1.verse: And what are the thirty-two marks?

dn30:1.2.5.verse: On the soles of his feet there are thousand-spoked wheels, with rims and hubs, complete in every detail.

dn30:1.2.8.verse: His hands and feet are soft and tender.

dn30:1.2.9.verse: He has serried hands and feet.

dn30:1.2.10.verse: The tops of his feet are arched.

dn30:1.2.11.verse: His calves are like those of an antelope.

dn30:1.2.12.verse: When standing upright and not bending over, the palms of both hands touch the knees.

dn30:1.2.13.verse: His private parts are sheathed in a foreskin.

dn30:1.2.14.verse: He is golden colored; his skin shines like lustrous gold.

dn30:1.2.15.verse: He has delicate skin, so delicate that dust and dirt don’t stick to his body.

dn30:1.2.16.verse: His hairs grow one per pore.

dn30:1.2.17.verse: His hairs stand up; they’re blue-black and curl clockwise.

dn30:1.2.18.verse: His body is tall and straight-limbed.

dn30:1.2.19.verse: He has bulging muscles in seven places.

dn30:1.2.20.verse: His chest is like that of a lion.

dn30:1.2.21.verse: He is filled out between the shoulders.

dn30:1.2.22.verse: He has the proportional circumference of a banyan tree: the span of his arms equals the height of his body.

dn30:1.2.25.verse: His jaw is like that of a lion.

dn30:1.2.31.verse: He has the voice of the Divinity, like a cuckoo’s call.

dn30:1.2.33.verse: He has eyelashes like a cow’s.

dn30:1.2.34.verse: Between his eyebrows there grows a tuft, soft and white like cotton-wool.

dn30:1.2.35.verse: The crown of his head is like a turban.

dn30:1.3.1.verse: These are the thirty-two marks of a great man. A great man who possesses these has only two possible destinies, no other.

dn30:1.3.4.verse: Seers who are outsiders remember these marks, but they do not know

dn30:1.3.5.verse: the specific deeds performed in the past to obtain each mark.

dn30:1.4.1.verse: In some past lives, past existences, past abodes the Realized One was reborn as a human being. He firmly and persistently undertook skillful behaviors such as good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, giving and sharing, taking precepts, observing the sabbath, paying due respect to mother and father, ascetics and brahmins, honoring the elders in the family, and various other things pertaining to skillful behaviors.

dn30:1.4.2.verse: Due to performing, accumulating, heaping up, and amassing those deeds, when his body broke up, after death, he was reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

dn30:1.4.3.verse: There he surpassed the other gods in ten respects: heavenly lifespan, beauty, happiness, glory, sovereignty, sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

dn30:1.4.4.verse: When he passed away from there and came back to this place he obtained this mark of a great man:

dn30:1.4.6.verse: He places his foot on the ground evenly, raises it evenly, and touches the ground evenly with the whole sole of his foot.

dn30:1.5.1.verse: Possessing this mark, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:1.5.2.verse: He has the following seven treasures:

dn30:1.5.3.verse: the wheel, the elephant, the horse, the jewel, the woman, the householder, and the commander as the seventh treasure.

dn30:1.5.4.verse: He has over a thousand sons who are valiant and heroic, crushing the armies of his enemies.

dn30:1.5.5.verse: After conquering this land girt by sea—free of harassment by bandits, successful and prosperous, safe, blessed, free of pests—he reigns by principle, without rod or sword.

dn30:1.5.6.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:1.5.7.verse: He can’t be stopped by any human foe or enemy.

dn30:1.5.8.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:1.5.9.verse: But if he goes forth from the lay life to homelessness, he becomes a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, who has cast off the world’s veil.

dn30:1.5.10.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:1.5.11.verse: He can’t be stopped by any foe or enemy whether internal or external; nor by greed, hate, or delusion; nor by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.

dn30:1.5.12.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:1.6.3.verse: purity, precepts, and observing the sabbath;

dn30:1.6.5.verse: firmly undertaking these things, he lived accordingly.

dn30:1.6.6.verse: By means of these deeds he went to heaven,

dn30:1.6.7.verse: where he enjoyed happiness and merriment.

dn30:1.6.8.verse: After passing away from there to here,

dn30:1.6.9.verse: he steps evenly on this rich earth.

dn30:1.6.11.verse: that there is no stopping one of such even tread,

dn30:1.6.13.verse: That’s the meaning shown by this mark.

dn30:1.6.14.verse: While living at home he cannot be stopped,

dn30:1.6.15.verse: he defeats his foes, and cannot be beaten.

dn30:1.6.16.verse: Due to the fruit of that deed,

dn30:1.6.17.verse: he cannot be stopped by any human.

dn30:1.6.18.verse: But if one such chooses the life gone forth,

dn30:1.6.20.verse: not even the best can ever stop him;

dn30:1.6.21.verse: this is the nature of the supreme man.”

dn30:1.7.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:1.7.2.verse: He conveyed happiness to many people, casting out threats, terror, and danger, providing just protection and security, and giving gifts with all the trimmings.

dn30:1.7.3.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:1.7.4.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained this mark:

dn30:1.7.5.verse: on the soles of his feet there are thousand-spoked wheels, with rims and hubs, complete in every detail and well divided inside.

dn30:1.8.1.verse: Possessing this mark, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:1.8.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:1.8.4.verse: of brahmins and householders, people of town and country, treasurers and chief ministers, military officers, guardsmen, ministers, councillors, rulers, tax beneficiaries, and princes.

dn30:1.8.5.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:1.8.6.verse: But if he goes forth from the lay life to homelessness, he becomes a fully awakened Buddha.

dn30:1.8.7.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:1.8.9.verse: of monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, gods, humans, titans, dragons, and centaurs.

dn30:1.8.10.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:1.9.3.verse: he brought happiness to many people,

dn30:1.9.4.verse: ridding them of fear, terror, and danger,

dn30:1.9.6.verse: By means of these deeds he went to heaven,

dn30:1.9.7.verse: where he enjoyed happiness and merriment.

dn30:1.9.8.verse: After passing away from there to here,

dn30:1.9.9.verse: wheels on his two feet are found,

dn30:1.9.12.verse: seeing the prince with the hundred-fold mark of merits,

dn30:1.9.13.verse: that he’d have a following, subduing foes,

dn30:1.9.14.verse: which is why he has wheels all rimmed around.

dn30:1.9.15.verse: If one such doesn’t choose the life gone forth,

dn30:1.9.16.verse: he’ll roll the wheel and rule the land.

dn30:1.9.17.verse: The aristocrats will be his vassals,

dn30:1.9.19.verse: But if one such chooses the life gone forth,

dn30:1.9.21.verse: the gods, humans, titans, Sakka, and monsters;

dn30:1.9.22.verse: centaurs and dragons, birds and beasts,

dn30:1.9.24.verse: the supreme, honored by gods and humans.”

dn30:1.10.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:1.10.2.verse: He gave up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. He was scrupulous and kind, living full of sympathy for all living beings.

dn30:1.10.3.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:1.10.4.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained these three marks:

dn30:1.10.5.verse: he has stretched heels, long fingers, and his body is tall and straight-limbed.

dn30:1.11.1.verse: Possessing these marks, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:1.11.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:1.11.3.verse: He’s long-lived, preserving his life for a long time. No human foe or enemy is able to take his life before his time.

dn30:1.11.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:1.11.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:1.11.6.verse: He’s long-lived, preserving his life for a long time. No foes or enemies—nor any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or anyone in the world—is able to take his life before his time.

dn30:1.11.7.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:1.12.2.verse: “Realizing for himself the horrors of death,

dn30:1.12.3.verse: he refrained from killing other creatures.

dn30:1.12.4.verse: By that good conduct he went to heaven,

dn30:1.12.5.verse: where he enjoyed the fruit of deeds well done.

dn30:1.12.6.verse: Passing away, on his return to here,

dn30:1.12.8.verse: his stretched heels are abundant and long,

dn30:1.12.9.verse: and like the Divinity, he’s straight and beautiful, with well-formed limbs.

dn30:1.12.10.verse: Fair of arm, youthful, of good posture and breeding,

dn30:1.12.11.verse: his fingers are soft and tender and long.

dn30:1.12.12.verse: By these three marks of an excellent man,

dn30:1.12.13.verse: they indicated that the prince’s life would be long:

dn30:1.12.14.verse: ‘As a householder he will live long;

dn30:1.12.15.verse: longer still if he goes forth, due to

dn30:1.12.16.verse: mastery in the development of psychic power.

dn30:1.12.17.verse: Thus this is the sign of long life.’”

dn30:1.13.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:1.13.2.verse: He was a donor of delicious and tasty cooked and fresh foods, and drinks that were sweet and succulent.

dn30:1.13.3.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:1.13.4.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained this mark: he has bulging muscles in seven places.

dn30:1.13.5.verse: Both hands, both feet, both shoulders, and his chest are all bulging.

dn30:1.14.1.verse: Possessing this mark, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:1.14.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:1.14.3.verse: He gets delicious and tasty cooked and fresh foods, and drinks that are sweet and succulent.

dn30:1.14.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:1.14.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:1.14.6.verse: He gets delicious and tasty cooked and fresh foods, and drinks that are sweet and succulent.

dn30:1.14.7.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:1.15.2.verse: “He used to give the very best of flavors—

dn30:1.15.5.verse: he rejoiced long in the Garden of Delight.

dn30:1.15.6.verse: On returning to here, he is rounded in seven places,

dn30:1.15.7.verse: and tender hands and feet are found.

dn30:1.15.8.verse: The soothsayers expert in signs declared:

dn30:1.15.9.verse: ‘He’ll get tasty foods of all sorts

dn30:1.15.10.verse: as a householder, that’s what that means.

dn30:1.15.11.verse: But even if he goes forth he’ll get the same,

dn30:1.15.12.verse: supreme in gaining tasty foods of all sorts,

dn30:1.15.13.verse: cutting all bonds of the lay life.’”

dn30:1.16.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:1.16.2.verse: He brought people together using the four ways of being inclusive:

dn30:1.16.3.verse: giving, kindly words, taking care, and equality.

dn30:1.16.4.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:1.16.5.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained these two marks:

dn30:1.16.6.verse: his hands and feet are soft and tender, and they are serried.

dn30:1.17.1.verse: Possessing these marks, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:1.17.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:1.17.3.verse: His retinue is inclusive, cohesive, and well-managed. This includes brahmins and householders, people of town and country, treasurers and chief ministers, military officers, guardsmen, ministers, councillors, rulers, tax beneficiaries, and princes.

dn30:1.17.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:1.17.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:1.17.6.verse: His retinue is inclusive and well-managed. This includes monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, gods, humans, titans, dragons, and centaurs.

dn30:1.17.7.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:1.18.4.verse: such action and conduct as brought people together,

dn30:1.18.5.verse: he went to heaven due to his esteemed virtue.

dn30:1.18.6.verse: Passing away, on his return to here,

dn30:1.18.8.verse: hands and feet so tender and serried,

dn30:1.18.10.verse: His retinue is loyal and manageable,

dn30:1.18.11.verse: staying agreeably all over this broad land.

dn30:1.18.14.verse: But if he gives up all sensual enjoyments,

dn30:1.18.15.verse: as victor he speaks Dhamma to the people.

dn30:1.18.16.verse: Devoted, they respond to his words;

dn30:1.18.17.verse: after listening, they practice in line with the teaching.”

dn30:1.19.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:1.19.2.verse: His speech was meaningful and principled. He educated many people, bringing welfare and happiness, offering the teaching.

dn30:1.19.3.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:1.19.4.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained these two marks:

dn30:1.19.5.verse: the tops of his feet are arched and his hairs stand up.

dn30:1.20.1.verse: Possessing these marks, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:1.20.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:1.20.3.verse: He is the foremost, best, chief, highest, and finest of those who enjoy sensual pleasures.

dn30:1.20.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:1.20.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:1.20.6.verse: He is the foremost, best, chief, highest, and finest of all sentient beings.

dn30:1.20.7.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:1.21.3.verse: moving the people with his explanations.

dn30:1.21.4.verse: He brought welfare and happiness to creatures,

dn30:1.21.7.verse: he advanced to heaven and there rejoiced.

dn30:1.21.8.verse: On return to here two marks are found,

dn30:1.21.12.verse: Swollen with flesh and blood, encased in skin,

dn30:1.21.14.verse: If that sort lives in the home, he becomes

dn30:1.21.15.verse: the best of those who enjoy sensual pleasures.

dn30:1.21.16.verse: There’ll be none better than him;

dn30:1.21.17.verse: he’ll proceed having mastered all the Black Plum Tree Land.

dn30:1.21.18.verse: But going forth the peerless renunciate

dn30:1.21.19.verse: turns into the best of all creatures.

dn30:1.21.20.verse: There’ll be none better than him,

dn30:1.21.21.verse: he’ll live having mastered the whole world.”

dn30:1.22.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:1.22.2.verse: He was a thorough teacher of a profession, a branch of knowledge, conduct, or action, thinking:

dn30:1.22.3.verse: ‘How might they quickly learn and practice, without getting exhausted?’

dn30:1.22.4.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:1.22.5.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained this mark:

dn30:1.22.6.verse: his calves are like those of an antelope.

dn30:1.23.1.verse: Possessing this mark, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:1.23.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:1.23.3.verse: He quickly obtains the things worthy of a king, the factors, supports, and things befitting a king.

dn30:1.23.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:1.23.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:1.23.6.verse: He quickly obtains the things worthy of an ascetic, the factors, supports, and things befitting an ascetic.

dn30:1.23.7.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:1.24.3.verse: he thought of how they might easily learn.

dn30:1.24.5.verse: he taught them things that harm no one at all.

dn30:1.24.6.verse: Having done that skillful deed whose outcome is happiness,

dn30:1.24.7.verse: he gains prominent and elegant calves.

dn30:1.24.9.verse: he’s covered in delicate rising hairs.

dn30:1.24.10.verse: They say that individual has antelope calves,

dn30:1.24.11.verse: and that this is the mark of swift success.

dn30:1.24.12.verse: If he desires the things fitting the household life,

dn30:1.24.13.verse: not going forth, they’ll quickly be his.

dn30:1.24.14.verse: But if one such chooses the life gone forth,

dn30:1.24.16.verse: the peerless renunciate will quickly find

dn30:1.25.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:1.25.2.verse: He approached an ascetic or brahmin and asked:

dn30:1.25.3.verse: ‘Sirs, what is skillful? What is unskillful? What is blameworthy? What is blameless? What should be cultivated? What should not be cultivated? Doing what leads to my lasting harm and suffering? Doing what leads to my lasting welfare and happiness?’

dn30:1.25.4.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:1.25.5.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained this mark:

dn30:1.25.6.verse: he has delicate skin, so delicate that dust and dirt don’t stick to his body.

dn30:1.26.1.verse: Possessing this mark, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:1.26.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:1.26.3.verse: He has great wisdom. Of those who enjoy sensual pleasures, none is his equal or better in wisdom.

dn30:1.26.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:1.26.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:1.26.6.verse: He has great wisdom, widespread wisdom, laughing wisdom, swift wisdom, sharp wisdom, and penetrating wisdom. No sentient being is his equal or better in wisdom.

dn30:1.26.7.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:1.27.3.verse: eager to understand, he asked questions.

dn30:1.27.4.verse: Keen to learn, he waited on renunciates,

dn30:1.27.5.verse: heeding their explanation with pure intent.

dn30:1.27.6.verse: Due to that deed of acquiring wisdom,

dn30:1.27.7.verse: as a human being his skin is delicate.

dn30:1.27.8.verse: At his birth the soothsayers expert in signs prophesied:

dn30:1.27.10.verse: If one such doesn’t choose the life gone forth,

dn30:1.27.11.verse: he’ll roll the wheel and rule the land.

dn30:1.27.12.verse: Among those with material things who have been educated,

dn30:1.27.13.verse: none equal or better than him is found.

dn30:1.27.14.verse: But if one such chooses the life gone forth,

dn30:1.27.16.verse: gaining wisdom that’s supreme and distinguished,

dn30:1.27.17.verse: the one of superb, vast intelligence attains awakening.”

dn30:1.28.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:1.28.3.verse: Even when heavily criticized he didn’t lose his temper, become annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, or display annoyance, hate, and bitterness.

dn30:1.28.4.verse: He donated soft and delicate mats and blankets, and cloaks of delicate linen, cotton, silk, and wool.

dn30:1.28.5.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:1.28.6.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained this mark:

dn30:1.28.7.verse: he is golden colored; his skin shines like lustrous gold.

dn30:1.29.1.verse: Possessing this mark, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:1.29.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:1.29.3.verse: He obtains soft and delicate mats and blankets, and delicate cloaks of linen, cotton, silk, and wool.

dn30:1.29.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:1.29.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:1.29.6.verse: He obtains soft and delicate mats and blankets, and cloaks of delicate linen, cotton, silk, and wool.

dn30:1.29.7.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:1.30.2.verse: “Fixated on good will, he gave gifts.

dn30:1.30.3.verse: In an earlier life he poured forth cloth

dn30:1.30.5.verse: like a god pouring rain on this broad earth.

dn30:1.30.6.verse: So doing he passed from here to heaven,

dn30:1.30.7.verse: where he enjoyed the fruits of deeds well done.

dn30:1.30.8.verse: Here he wins a figure shining like honey-yellow gold,

dn30:1.30.9.verse: like Indra, the finest of gods.

dn30:1.30.10.verse: If that man stays in the house, not wishing to go forth,

dn30:1.30.11.verse: he conquers and rules this vast, broad earth,

dn30:1.30.12.verse: together with the seven treasures here.

dn30:1.30.13.verse: He gets immaculate, delicate, pure skin,

dn30:1.30.14.verse: receiving clothing, cloth, and the finest cloaks

dn30:1.30.15.verse: if he chooses the life gone forth.

dn30:1.30.16.verse: For he still partakes of past deed’s fruit;

dn30:1.30.17.verse: what’s been done is never lost.”

dn30:1.31.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:1.31.2.verse: He reunited long-lost and long-separated relatives, friends, loved ones, and comrades.

dn30:1.31.3.verse: He reunited mother with child and child with mother; father with child and child with father; brother with brother, brother with sister, sister with brother, and sister with sister, bringing them together with rejoicing.

dn30:1.31.4.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:1.31.5.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained this mark:

dn30:1.31.6.verse: his private parts are sheathed in a foreskin.

dn30:1.32.1.verse: Possessing this mark, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:1.32.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:1.32.3.verse: He has many sons, over a thousand sons who are valiant and heroic, crushing the armies of his enemies.

dn30:1.32.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:1.32.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:1.32.6.verse: He has many sons, many thousands of sons who are valiant and heroic, crushing the armies of his enemies.

dn30:1.32.7.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:1.33.6.verse: By means of these deeds he went to heaven,

dn30:1.33.7.verse: where he enjoyed happiness and merriment.

dn30:1.33.8.verse: After passing away from there to here,

dn30:1.33.9.verse: his private parts are sheathed in a foreskin.

dn30:1.33.14.verse: But if he lives the renunciate life

dn30:1.33.15.verse: he has even more sons following his word.

dn30:1.33.17.verse: that’s the meaning shown by this mark.”

dn30:1.33.18.verse: The first recitation section is complete.

dn30:2.1.0.verse: 15–16. Equal Proportions and Touching the Knees

dn30:2.1.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:2.1.2.verse: Examining the gathered population, he knew what they had in common and what was their own; he knew each person, and he knew the distinctions between people.

dn30:2.1.3.verse: In each case, he made appropriate distinctions between people: ‘This one deserves that; that one deserves this.’

dn30:2.1.4.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:2.1.5.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained these two marks:

dn30:2.1.6.verse: he has the proportional circumference of a banyan tree; and when standing upright and not bending over, the palms of both hands touch the knees.

dn30:2.2.1.verse: Possessing these marks, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:2.2.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:2.2.3.verse: He is rich, affluent, and wealthy, with lots of gold and silver, lots of property and assets, lots of money and grain, and a full treasury and storehouses.

dn30:2.2.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:2.2.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:2.2.6.verse: He is rich, affluent, and wealthy.

dn30:2.2.7.verse: He has these kinds of wealth:

dn30:2.2.8.verse: the wealth of faith, ethics, conscience, prudence, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

dn30:2.2.9.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:2.3.2.verse: “Examining the many people in a community,

dn30:2.3.3.verse: he weighed, evaluated, and judged each case:

dn30:2.3.5.verse: That’s how he used to draw distinctions between people.

dn30:2.3.7.verse: he can touch his knees with both hands.

dn30:2.3.8.verse: With the remaining ripening of the fruit of good deeds,

dn30:2.3.9.verse: his circumference was that of a great tree.

dn30:2.3.10.verse: Learned experts in the many different

dn30:2.3.13.verse: many different things that householders deserve.

dn30:2.3.14.verse: Here there are many suitable pleasures

dn30:2.3.15.verse: for the ruler of the land to enjoy as householder.

dn30:2.3.16.verse: But if he gives up all sensual enjoyments,

dn30:2.3.17.verse: he will gain the supreme, highest peak of wealth.’”

dn30:2.4.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:2.4.2.verse: He wanted what’s best, the welfare, the comfort, and sanctuary of the people, thinking:

dn30:2.4.3.verse: ‘How might they flourish in faith, ethics, learning, generosity, teachings, and wisdom; in wealth and grain, fields and land, birds and beasts, children and partners; in bondservants, workers, and staff; in family, friends, and kin?’

dn30:2.4.4.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:2.4.5.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained these three marks:

dn30:2.4.6.verse: his chest is like that of a lion; he is filled out between the shoulders.; and his torso is cylindrical.

dn30:2.5.1.verse: Possessing these marks, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:2.5.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:2.5.3.verse: He’s not liable to decline. He doesn’t decline in wealth and grain, fields and land, birds and beasts, children and partners; in bondservants, workers, and staff; in family, friends, and kin. He doesn’t decline in any of his accomplishments.

dn30:2.5.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:2.5.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:2.5.6.verse: He’s not liable to decline. He doesn’t decline in faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom. He doesn’t decline in any of his accomplishments.

dn30:2.5.7.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:2.6.2.verse: “His wish was this: ‘How may others not decline

dn30:2.6.3.verse: in faith, ethics, learning, and intelligence,

dn30:2.6.4.verse: in generosity, teachings, and much good else,

dn30:2.6.5.verse: in coin and grain, fields and lands,

dn30:2.6.8.verse: in strength, and both beauty and happiness?’

dn30:2.6.9.verse: And so he ever desired their success.

dn30:2.6.10.verse: His chest was shaped like that of a lion,

dn30:2.6.11.verse: filled out between the shoulders, and torso cylindrical.

dn30:2.6.12.verse: Due to the well-done deeds of the past,

dn30:2.6.13.verse: he had that portent of non-decline.

dn30:2.6.14.verse: Even as layman he grows in coin and grain,

dn30:2.6.16.verse: But once gone forth, owning nothing, he attains

dn30:2.6.17.verse: the supreme awakening which may never decline.”

dn30:2.7.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:2.7.2.verse: He would never hurt any sentient being with fists, stones, rods, or swords.

dn30:2.7.3.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:2.7.4.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained this mark: he has ridged taste buds. His raised taste receptors, originating in the throat, disperse evenly.

dn30:2.8.1.verse: Possessing this mark, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:2.8.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:2.8.3.verse: He is rarely ill or unwell. His stomach digests well, being neither too hot nor too cold.

dn30:2.8.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:2.8.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:2.8.6.verse: He is rarely ill or unwell. His stomach digests well, being neither too hot nor too cold, but just right, and fit for meditation.

dn30:2.8.7.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:2.9.2.verse: “Not with fist or rod or stone,

dn30:2.9.3.verse: or sword or beating to death,

dn30:2.9.6.verse: For that very reason he rejoiced in heaven after passing away,

dn30:2.9.7.verse: finding happiness as a fruit of happy deeds.

dn30:2.9.8.verse: With taste receptors prominent and evenly spreading nutrition,

dn30:2.9.9.verse: on his return here he has ridged taste buds.

dn30:2.9.10.verse: That’s why the clever prophets said:

dn30:2.9.13.verse: That’s the meaning shown by this mark.’”

dn30:2.10.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:2.10.2.verse: When looking at others he didn’t glare, look askance, or avert his eyes. Being straightforward, he reached out to others with straightforward intentions, looking at people with kindly eyes.

dn30:2.10.3.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:2.10.4.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained these two marks:

dn30:2.10.5.verse: his eyes are indigo, and he has eyelashes like a cow’s.

dn30:2.11.1.verse: Possessing these marks, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:2.11.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:2.11.3.verse: The people look on him with kindly eyes. He is dear and beloved to the brahmins and householders, people of town and country, treasurers and chief ministers, military officers, guardsmen, ministers, councillors, rulers, tax beneficiaries, and princes.

dn30:2.11.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:2.11.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:2.11.6.verse: The people look on him with kindly eyes. He is dear and beloved to the monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, gods, humans, titans, dragons, and centaurs.

dn30:2.11.7.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:2.12.2.verse: “With not a glare or glance askance,

dn30:2.12.5.verse: looking at people with kindly eyes.

dn30:2.12.6.verse: In good rebirths he enjoyed the fruit

dn30:2.12.8.verse: But here he has a cow’s eyelashes,

dn30:2.12.9.verse: and indigo eyes so fair to see.

dn30:2.12.13.verse: he’d be looked upon with kindly eyes.

dn30:2.12.14.verse: Even as a householder he’d be regarded kindly,

dn30:2.12.16.verse: But if he becomes an ascetic, not lay,

dn30:2.12.17.verse: as destroyer of sorrow he’ll be loved by many.”

dn30:2.13.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:2.13.2.verse: He was the leader and forerunner of people in skillful behaviors such as good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, giving and sharing, taking precepts, observing the sabbath, paying due respect to mother and father, ascetics and brahmins, honoring the elders in the family, and various other things pertaining to skillful behaviors.

dn30:2.13.3.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:2.13.4.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained this mark:

dn30:2.13.5.verse: the crown of his head is like a turban.

dn30:2.14.1.verse: Possessing this mark, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:2.14.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:2.14.3.verse: He has a large following of brahmins and householders, people of town and country, treasurers and chief ministers, military officers, guardsmen, ministers, councillors, rulers, tax beneficiaries, and princes.

dn30:2.14.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:2.14.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?

dn30:2.14.6.verse: He has a large following of monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, gods, humans, titans, dragons, and centaurs.

dn30:2.14.7.verse: That’s what he obtains as Buddha.”

dn30:2.15.2.verse: “Among people of good conduct, he was the leader,

dn30:2.15.3.verse: devoted to a life of principle among the principled.

dn30:2.15.5.verse: and he experienced the fruit of good deeds in heaven.

dn30:2.15.7.verse: he gains a head crowned like a turban.

dn30:2.15.8.verse: The experts in omens and signs prophesied:

dn30:2.15.9.verse: ‘He will be leader of the people.

dn30:2.15.10.verse: Assistants serve him here among men,

dn30:2.15.11.verse: as they did for him then in the past.

dn30:2.15.12.verse: If he becomes an aristocrat, ruler of the land,

dn30:2.15.13.verse: he’ll gain the service of the people.

dn30:2.15.14.verse: But if that man goes forth,

dn30:2.15.15.verse: he’ll be sophisticated, proficient in the teachings.

dn30:2.15.16.verse: Devoted to the virtues of his instruction,

dn30:2.15.17.verse: the people will become his followers.’”

dn30:2.16.0.verse: 24–25. One Hair Per Pore, and a Tuft

dn30:2.16.1.verse: “Mendicants, in some past lives the Realized One was reborn as a human being.

dn30:2.16.2.verse: He refrained from lying. He spoke the truth and stuck to the truth. He was honest and dependable, and didn’t trick the world with his words.

dn30:2.16.3.verse: Due to performing those deeds he was reborn in a heavenly realm.

dn30:2.16.4.verse: When he came back to this place he obtained these two marks:

dn30:2.16.5.verse: his hairs grow one per pore, and between his eyebrows there grows a tuft, soft and white like cotton-wool.

dn30:2.17.1.verse: Possessing these marks, if he stays at home he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.

dn30:2.17.2.verse: And what does he obtain as king?

dn30:2.17.3.verse: He has many close adherents among the brahmins and householders, people of town and country, treasurers and chief ministers, military officers, guardsmen, ministers, councillors, rulers, tax beneficiaries, and princes.

dn30:2.17.4.verse: That’s what he obtains as king.

dn30:2.17.5.verse: And what does he obtain as Buddha?
