dn33:2.1.137.verse: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.

dn33:2.1.138.verse: This is the fifth opportunity for freedom.

dn33:2.1.139.verse: Five perceptions that ripen in freedom:

dn33:2.1.140.verse: the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of giving up, and the perception of fading away.

dn33:2.1.141.verse: These are the teachings grouped by five that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

dn33:2.1.142.verse: You should all recite these in concert.

dn33:2.2.1.verse: There are teachings grouped by six that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

dn33:2.2.2.verse: You should all recite these in concert.

dn33:2.2.3.verse: What are the teachings grouped by six?

dn33:2.2.5.verse: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

dn33:2.2.7.verse: sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

dn33:2.2.9.verse: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind consciousness.

dn33:2.2.11.verse: contact through the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

dn33:2.2.13.verse: feeling born of contact through the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

dn33:2.2.15.verse: perceptions of sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

dn33:2.2.17.verse: intention regarding sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

dn33:2.2.19.verse: craving for sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

dn33:2.2.21.verse: A mendicant lacks respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, the training, diligence, and hospitality.

dn33:2.2.23.verse: A mendicant has respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, the training, diligence, and hospitality.

dn33:2.2.25.verse: Seeing a sight with their eyes, one is preoccupied with a sight that’s a basis for happiness.

dn33:2.2.26.verse: Hearing a sound with their ears …

dn33:2.2.27.verse: Smelling an odor with their nose …

dn33:2.2.28.verse: Tasting a flavor with their tongue …

dn33:2.2.29.verse: Encountering a touch with their body …

dn33:2.2.30.verse: Knowing an idea with their mind, one is preoccupied with an idea that’s a basis for happiness.

dn33:2.2.32.verse: Seeing a sight with their eyes, one is preoccupied with a sight that’s a basis for sadness. …

dn33:2.2.33.verse: Knowing an idea with their mind, one is preoccupied with an idea that’s a basis for sadness.

dn33:2.2.35.verse: Seeing a sight with their eyes, one is preoccupied with a sight that’s a basis for equanimity. …

dn33:2.2.36.verse: Knowing an idea with their mind, one is preoccupied with an idea that’s a basis for equanimity.

dn33:2.2.38.verse: Firstly, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with bodily kindness, both in public and in private.

dn33:2.2.39.verse: This warm-hearted quality makes for fondness and respect, conducing to inclusion, harmony, and unity, without quarreling.

dn33:2.2.40.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with verbal kindness, both in public and in private.

dn33:2.2.41.verse: This too is a warm-hearted quality.

dn33:2.2.42.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with mental kindness, both in public and in private.

dn33:2.2.43.verse: This too is a warm-hearted quality.

dn33:2.2.44.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant shares without reservation any material things they have gained by legitimate means, even the food placed in the alms-bowl, using them in common with their ethical spiritual companions.

dn33:2.2.45.verse: This too is a warm-hearted quality.

dn33:2.2.46.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant lives according to the precepts shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. Those precepts are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

dn33:2.2.47.verse: This too is a warm-hearted quality.

dn33:2.2.48.verse: They live according to the view shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. That view is noble and emancipating, and delivers one who applies it to the complete ending of suffering.

dn33:2.2.49.verse: This warm-hearted quality too makes for fondness and respect, conducing to inclusion, harmony, and unity, without quarreling.

dn33:2.2.51.verse: Firstly, a mendicant is irritable and acrimonious.

dn33:2.2.52.verse: Such a mendicant lacks respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and they don’t fulfill the training.

dn33:2.2.53.verse: They create a dispute in the Saṅgha, which is for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

dn33:2.2.54.verse: If you see such a root of dispute in yourselves or others, you should try to give up this bad thing.

dn33:2.2.55.verse: If you don’t see it, you should practice so that it doesn’t come up in the future.

dn33:2.2.56.verse: That’s how to give up this bad root of dispute, so it doesn’t come up in the future.

dn33:2.2.57.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant is offensive and contemptuous …

dn33:2.2.60.verse: They have corrupt wishes and wrong view …

dn33:2.2.61.verse: They’re attached to their own views, holding them tight, and refusing to let go.

dn33:2.2.64.verse: If you see such a root of dispute in yourselves or others, you should try to give up this bad thing.

dn33:2.2.65.verse: If you don’t see it, you should practice so that it doesn’t come up in the future.

dn33:2.2.66.verse: That’s how to give up this bad root of dispute, so it doesn’t come up in the future.

dn33:2.2.68.verse: earth, water, fire, air, space, and consciousness.

dn33:2.2.71.verse: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by love. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

dn33:2.2.72.verse: Yet somehow ill will still occupies my mind.’

dn33:2.2.73.verse: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! Don’t say that. Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say that.

dn33:2.2.74.verse: It’s impossible, reverend, it cannot happen that the heart’s release by love has been developed and properly implemented,

dn33:2.2.75.verse: yet somehow ill will still occupies the mind.

dn33:2.2.76.verse: For it is the heart’s release by love that is the escape from ill will.’

dn33:2.2.78.verse: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by compassion. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

dn33:2.2.79.verse: Yet somehow the thought of harming still occupies my mind.’

dn33:2.2.80.verse: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

dn33:2.2.83.verse: For it is the heart’s release by compassion that is the escape from thoughts of harming.’

dn33:2.2.85.verse: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by rejoicing. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

dn33:2.2.86.verse: Yet somehow discontent still occupies my mind.’

dn33:2.2.87.verse: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

dn33:2.2.90.verse: For it is the heart’s release by rejoicing that is the escape from discontent.’

dn33:2.2.92.verse: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by equanimity. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

dn33:2.2.93.verse: Yet somehow desire still occupies my mind.’

dn33:2.2.94.verse: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

dn33:2.2.97.verse: For it is the heart’s release by equanimity that is the escape from desire.’

dn33:2.2.99.verse: ‘I’ve developed the signless release of the heart. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

dn33:2.2.100.verse: Yet somehow my consciousness still follows after signs.’

dn33:2.2.101.verse: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

dn33:2.2.104.verse: For it is the signless release of the heart that is the escape from all signs.’

dn33:2.2.106.verse: ‘I’m rid of the conceit “I am”. And I don’t regard anything as “I am this”.

dn33:2.2.107.verse: Yet somehow the dart of doubt and indecision still occupies my mind.’

dn33:2.2.108.verse: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! Don’t say that. Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say that.

dn33:2.2.109.verse: It’s impossible, reverend, it cannot happen that the conceit “I am” has been done away with, and nothing is regarded as “I am this”,

dn33:2.2.110.verse: yet somehow the dart of doubt and indecision still occupy the mind.

dn33:2.2.111.verse: For it is the uprooting of the conceit “I am” that is the escape from the dart of doubt and indecision.’

dn33:2.2.113.verse: the unsurpassable seeing, listening, acquisition, training, service, and recollection.

dn33:2.2.115.verse: the recollection of the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, ethics, generosity, and the deities.

dn33:2.2.117.verse: A mendicant, seeing a sight with their eyes, is neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

dn33:2.2.118.verse: Hearing a sound with their ears … Smelling an odor with their nose … Tasting a flavor with their tongue … Encountering a touch with their body …

dn33:2.2.119.verse: Knowing an idea with their mind, they’re neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

dn33:2.2.121.verse: Someone born into a dark class gives rise to a dark result.

dn33:2.2.122.verse: Someone born into a dark class gives rise to a bright result.

dn33:2.2.123.verse: Someone born into a dark class gives rise to extinguishment, which is neither dark nor bright.

dn33:2.2.124.verse: Someone born into a bright class gives rise to a bright result.

dn33:2.2.125.verse: Someone born into a bright class gives rise to a dark result.

dn33:2.2.126.verse: Someone born into a bright class gives rise to extinguishment, which is neither dark nor bright.

dn33:2.2.128.verse: the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of giving up, the perception of fading away, and the perception of cessation.

dn33:2.2.129.verse: These are the teachings grouped by six that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

dn33:2.2.130.verse: You should all recite these in concert.

dn33:2.3.1.verse: There are teachings grouped by seven that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

dn33:2.3.2.verse: You should all recite these in concert.

dn33:2.3.3.verse: What are the teachings grouped by seven?

dn33:2.3.4.verse: Seven riches of the noble ones:

dn33:2.3.5.verse: the riches of faith, ethics, conscience, prudence, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

dn33:2.3.7.verse: mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

dn33:2.3.9.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, and right mindfulness.

dn33:2.3.11.verse: a mendicant is faithless, shameless, imprudent, unlearned, lazy, unmindful, and witless.

dn33:2.3.13.verse: a mendicant is faithful, conscientious, prudent, learned, energetic, mindful, and wise.

dn33:2.3.14.verse: Seven aspects of the teachings of the true persons:

dn33:2.3.15.verse: a mendicant knows the teachings, knows the meaning, knows themselves, knows moderation, knows the right time, knows assemblies, and knows individuals.

dn33:2.3.17.verse: A mendicant has a keen enthusiasm to undertake the training …

dn33:2.3.23.verse: to penetrate theoretically. And they don’t lose these desires in the future.

dn33:2.3.25.verse: the perception of impermanence, the perception of not-self, the perception of ugliness, the perception of drawbacks, the perception of giving up, the perception of fading away, and the perception of cessation.

dn33:2.3.27.verse: faith, energy, conscience, prudence, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

dn33:2.3.29.verse: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and diverse in perception, such as human beings, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.

dn33:2.3.30.verse: This is the first plane of consciousness.

dn33:2.3.31.verse: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and unified in perception, such as the gods reborn in the Divinity’s host through the first absorption.

dn33:2.3.32.verse: This is the second plane of consciousness.

dn33:2.3.33.verse: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and diverse in perception, such as the gods of sublime luminosity.

dn33:2.3.34.verse: This is the third plane of consciousness.

dn33:2.3.35.verse: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and unified in perception, such as the gods of universal beauty.

dn33:2.3.36.verse: This is the fourth plane of consciousness.

dn33:2.3.37.verse: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond perceptions of form. With the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite space.

dn33:2.3.38.verse: This is the fifth plane of consciousness.

dn33:2.3.39.verse: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite space. Aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

dn33:2.3.40.verse: This is the sixth plane of consciousness.

dn33:2.3.41.verse: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness. Aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they have been reborn in the dimension of nothingness.

dn33:2.3.42.verse: This is the seventh plane of consciousness.

dn33:2.3.43.verse: Seven individuals worthy of a religious donation:

dn33:2.3.44.verse: one freed both ways, one freed by wisdom, a direct witness, one attained to view, one freed by faith, a follower of teachings, and a follower by faith.

dn33:2.3.46.verse: sensual desire, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, desire for continued existence, and ignorance.

dn33:2.3.48.verse: attraction, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, desire for continued existence, and ignorance.

dn33:2.3.49.verse: Seven means of settling any disciplinary issues that might arise:

dn33:2.3.50.verse: Resolution face-to-face to be applied. Resolution through recollection to be granted. Resolution because of past insanity to be granted. Acting according to what has been admitted. Majority decision. Further penalty. Covering over as if with grass.

dn33:2.3.51.verse: These are the teachings grouped by seven that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

dn33:2.3.52.verse: You should all recite these in concert.

dn33:2.3.53.verse: The second recitation section is complete.

dn33:3.1.1.verse: There are teachings grouped by eight that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

dn33:3.1.2.verse: You should all recite these in concert.

dn33:3.1.3.verse: What are the teachings grouped by eight?

dn33:3.1.5.verse: wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

dn33:3.1.7.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

dn33:3.1.8.verse: Eight individuals worthy of a religious donation:

dn33:3.1.9.verse: The stream-enterer and the one practicing to realize the fruit of stream-entry. The once-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of once-return. The non-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of non-return. The perfected one, and the one practicing for perfection.

dn33:3.1.11.verse: Firstly, a mendicant has some work to do.

dn33:3.1.13.verse: ‘I have some work to do. But while doing it my body will get tired. I’d better have a lie down.’

dn33:3.1.14.verse: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

dn33:3.1.15.verse: This is the first ground for laziness.

dn33:3.1.16.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has done some work.

dn33:3.1.18.verse: ‘I’ve done some work. But while working my body got tired. I’d better have a lie down.’

dn33:3.1.19.verse: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy …

dn33:3.1.20.verse: This is the second ground for laziness.

dn33:3.1.21.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has to go on a journey.

dn33:3.1.23.verse: ‘I have to go on a journey. But while walking my body will get tired. I’d better have a lie down.’

dn33:3.1.24.verse: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy …

dn33:3.1.25.verse: This is the third ground for laziness.

dn33:3.1.26.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has gone on a journey.

dn33:3.1.28.verse: ‘I’ve gone on a journey. But while walking my body got tired. I’d better have a lie down.’

dn33:3.1.29.verse: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy …

dn33:3.1.30.verse: This is the fourth ground for laziness.

dn33:3.1.31.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has wandered for alms, but they didn’t get to fill up on as much food as they like, coarse or fine.

dn33:3.1.33.verse: ‘I’ve wandered for alms, but I didn’t get to fill up on as much food as I like, coarse or fine. My body is tired and unfit for work. I’d better have a lie down.’

dn33:3.1.34.verse: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy …

dn33:3.1.35.verse: This is the fifth ground for laziness.

dn33:3.1.36.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has wandered for alms, and they got to fill up on as much food as they like, coarse or fine.

dn33:3.1.38.verse: ‘I’ve wandered for alms, and I got to fill up on as much food as I like, coarse or fine. My body is heavy and unfit for work, like I’ve just eaten a load of beans. I’d better have a lie down.’

dn33:3.1.39.verse: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy …

dn33:3.1.40.verse: This is the sixth ground for laziness.

dn33:3.1.41.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant feels a little sick.

dn33:3.1.43.verse: ‘I feel a little sick. Lying down would be good for me. I’d better have a lie down.’

dn33:3.1.45.verse: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy …

dn33:3.1.46.verse: This is the seventh ground for laziness.

dn33:3.1.47.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has recently recovered from illness.

dn33:3.1.49.verse: ‘I’ve recently recovered from illness. My body is weak and unfit for work. I’d better have a lie down.’

dn33:3.1.50.verse: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

dn33:3.1.51.verse: This is the eighth ground for laziness.

dn33:3.1.53.verse: Firstly, a mendicant has some work to do.

dn33:3.1.55.verse: ‘I have some work to do. While working it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

dn33:3.1.56.verse: They rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

dn33:3.1.57.verse: This is the first ground for arousing energy.

dn33:3.1.58.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has done some work.

dn33:3.1.60.verse: ‘I’ve done some work. While I was working I wasn’t able to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’

dn33:3.1.62.verse: This is the second ground for arousing energy.

dn33:3.1.63.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has to go on a journey.

dn33:3.1.65.verse: ‘I have to go on a journey. While walking it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’

dn33:3.1.68.verse: This is the third ground for arousing energy.

dn33:3.1.69.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has gone on a journey.

dn33:3.1.71.verse: ‘I’ve gone on a journey. While I was walking I wasn’t able to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’

dn33:3.1.73.verse: This is the fourth ground for arousing energy.

dn33:3.1.74.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has wandered for alms, but they didn’t get to fill up on as much food as they like, coarse or fine.

dn33:3.1.76.verse: ‘I’ve wandered for alms, but I didn’t get to fill up on as much food as I like, coarse or fine. My body is light and fit for work. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’

dn33:3.1.78.verse: This is the fifth ground for arousing energy.

dn33:3.1.79.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has wandered for alms, and they got to fill up on as much food as they like, coarse or fine.

dn33:3.1.81.verse: ‘I’ve wandered for alms, and I got to fill up on as much food as I like, coarse or fine. My body is strong and fit for work. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’

dn33:3.1.83.verse: This is the sixth ground for arousing energy.

dn33:3.1.84.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant feels a little sick.

dn33:3.1.86.verse: ‘I feel a little sick. It’s possible this illness will worsen. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’

dn33:3.1.88.verse: This is the seventh ground for arousing energy.

dn33:3.1.89.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has recently recovered from illness.

dn33:3.1.91.verse: ‘I’ve recently recovered from illness. It’s possible the illness will come back. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

dn33:3.1.92.verse: They rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

dn33:3.1.93.verse: This is the eighth ground for arousing energy.

dn33:3.1.95.verse: Someone might give a gift after insulting the recipient. Or they give out of fear. Or they give thinking, ‘They gave to me.’ Or they give thinking, ‘They’ll give to me.’ Or they give thinking, ‘It’s good to give.’ Or they give thinking, ‘I cook, they don’t. It wouldn’t be right for me to not give to them.’ Or they give thinking, ‘By giving this gift I’ll get a good reputation.’ Or they give thinking, ‘This is an adornment and requisite for the mind.’

dn33:3.1.98.verse: First, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

dn33:3.1.99.verse: Whatever they give they expect back.

dn33:3.1.100.verse: They see an affluent aristocrat or brahmin or householder amusing themselves, supplied and provided with the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

dn33:3.1.102.verse: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of well-to-do aristocrats or brahmins or householders!’

dn33:3.1.103.verse: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it. As they’ve settled for less and not developed further, their thought leads to rebirth there.

dn33:3.1.104.verse: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.

dn33:3.1.105.verse: The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their purity.

dn33:3.1.106.verse: Next, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins.

dn33:3.1.107.verse: Whatever they give they expect back.

dn33:3.1.109.verse: ‘The gods of the four great kings are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

dn33:3.1.111.verse: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods of the four great kings!’

dn33:3.1.112.verse: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it. As they’ve settled for less and not developed further, their thought leads to rebirth there.

dn33:3.1.113.verse: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.

dn33:3.1.114.verse: The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their purity.

dn33:3.1.115.verse: Next, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins.

dn33:3.1.116.verse: Whatever they give they expect back.

dn33:3.1.121.verse: the gods who love to create …

dn33:3.1.122.verse: the gods who control what is created by others are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

dn33:3.1.124.verse: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods who control what is created by others!’

dn33:3.1.125.verse: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it. As they’ve settled for less and not developed further, their thought leads to rebirth there.

dn33:3.1.126.verse: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.

dn33:3.1.127.verse: The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their purity.

dn33:3.1.128.verse: Next, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

dn33:3.1.129.verse: Whatever they give they expect back.

dn33:3.1.131.verse: ‘The gods of the Divinity’s host are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

dn33:3.1.133.verse: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods of the Divinity’s host!’

dn33:3.1.134.verse: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it. As they’ve settled for less and not developed further, their thought leads to rebirth there.

dn33:3.1.135.verse: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.

dn33:3.1.136.verse: And for those free of desire, not those with desire.

dn33:3.1.137.verse: The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their freedom from desire.

dn33:3.1.139.verse: the assemblies of aristocrats, brahmins, householders, and ascetics. An assembly of the gods of the four great kings. An assembly of the gods of the thirty-three. An assembly of Māras. An assembly of divinities.

dn33:3.1.141.verse: gain and loss, fame and disgrace, blame and praise, pleasure and pain.

dn33:3.1.143.verse: Perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limited, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

dn33:3.1.144.verse: This is the first dimension of mastery.

dn33:3.1.145.verse: Perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limitless, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

dn33:3.1.147.verse: This is the second dimension of mastery.

dn33:3.1.148.verse: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limited, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

dn33:3.1.149.verse: This is the third dimension of mastery.

dn33:3.1.150.verse: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limitless, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

dn33:3.1.151.verse: This is the fourth dimension of mastery.

dn33:3.1.152.verse: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are blue, with blue color and blue appearance.

dn33:3.1.153.verse: They’re like a flax flower that’s blue, with blue color and blue appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, blue, with blue color and blue appearance.

dn33:3.1.154.verse: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

dn33:3.1.155.verse: This is the fifth dimension of mastery.

dn33:3.1.156.verse: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance.

dn33:3.1.157.verse: They’re like a champak flower that’s yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance.

dn33:3.1.158.verse: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

dn33:3.1.159.verse: This is the sixth dimension of mastery.

dn33:3.1.160.verse: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are red, with red color and red appearance.

dn33:3.1.161.verse: They’re like a scarlet mallow flower that’s red, with red color and red appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, red, with red color and red appearance.

dn33:3.1.162.verse: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

dn33:3.1.163.verse: This is the seventh dimension of mastery.

dn33:3.1.164.verse: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are white, with white color and white appearance.

dn33:3.1.165.verse: They’re like the morning star that’s white, with white color and white appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, white, with white color and white appearance.

dn33:3.1.166.verse: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

dn33:3.1.167.verse: This is the eighth dimension of mastery.

dn33:3.1.169.verse: Having physical form, they see forms.

dn33:3.1.171.verse: Not perceiving physical form internally, they see forms externally.

dn33:3.1.175.verse: Going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite space.

dn33:3.1.177.verse: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

dn33:3.1.179.verse: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness.

dn33:3.1.181.verse: Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, they enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

dn33:3.1.183.verse: Going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, they enter and remain in the cessation of perception and feeling.

dn33:3.1.185.verse: These are the teachings grouped by eight that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

dn33:3.1.186.verse: You should all recite these in concert.

dn33:3.2.1.verse: There are teachings grouped by nine that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

dn33:3.2.2.verse: You should all recite these in concert.

dn33:3.2.3.verse: What are the teachings grouped by nine?

dn33:3.2.5.verse: Thinking: ‘They did wrong to me,’ you harbor resentment.

dn33:3.2.6.verse: Thinking: ‘They are doing wrong to me’ …

dn33:3.2.8.verse: ‘They did wrong by someone I love’ …

dn33:3.2.9.verse: ‘They are doing wrong by someone I love’ …

dn33:3.2.10.verse: ‘They will do wrong by someone I love’ …

dn33:3.2.13.verse: Thinking: ‘They will help someone I dislike,’ you harbor resentment.

dn33:3.2.14.verse: Nine ways to get rid of resentment:

dn33:3.2.15.verse: Thinking: ‘They did wrong to me, but what can I possibly do?’ you get rid of resentment.

dn33:3.2.16.verse: Thinking: ‘They are doing wrong to me …’ …

dn33:3.2.18.verse: ‘They did wrong by someone I love …’ …

dn33:3.2.19.verse: ‘They are doing wrong by someone I love …’ …

dn33:3.2.20.verse: ‘They will do wrong by someone I love …’ …

dn33:3.2.23.verse: Thinking: ‘They will help someone I dislike, but what can I possibly do?’ you get rid of resentment.

dn33:3.2.25.verse: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and diverse in perception, such as human beings, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.

dn33:3.2.26.verse: This is the first abode of sentient beings.

dn33:3.2.27.verse: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and unified in perception, such as the gods reborn in the Divinity’s host through the first absorption.

dn33:3.2.28.verse: This is the second abode of sentient beings.

dn33:3.2.29.verse: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and diverse in perception, such as the gods of sublime luminosity.

dn33:3.2.30.verse: This is the third abode of sentient beings.

dn33:3.2.31.verse: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and unified in perception, such as the gods of universal beauty.

dn33:3.2.32.verse: This is the fourth abode of sentient beings.

dn33:3.2.33.verse: There are sentient beings that are non-percipient and do not experience anything, such as the gods who are non-percipient beings.

dn33:3.2.34.verse: This is the fifth abode of sentient beings.

dn33:3.2.35.verse: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond perceptions of form. With the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite space.

dn33:3.2.36.verse: This is the sixth abode of sentient beings.

dn33:3.2.37.verse: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite space. Aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

dn33:3.2.38.verse: This is the seventh abode of sentient beings.

dn33:3.2.39.verse: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness. Aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they have been reborn in the dimension of nothingness.

dn33:3.2.40.verse: This is the eighth abode of sentient beings.

dn33:3.2.41.verse: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of nothingness. They have been reborn in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

dn33:3.2.42.verse: This is the ninth abode of sentient beings.

dn33:3.2.43.verse: Nine lost opportunities for spiritual practice:

dn33:3.2.44.verse: Firstly, a Realized One has arisen in the world. He teaches the Dhamma leading to peace, extinguishment, awakening, as proclaimed by the Holy One.

dn33:3.2.45.verse: But that individual has been reborn in hell.

dn33:3.2.46.verse: This is the first lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

dn33:3.2.47.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world …

dn33:3.2.48.verse: But that individual has been reborn in the animal realm.

dn33:3.2.49.verse: This is the second lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

dn33:3.2.50.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world …

dn33:3.2.51.verse: But an individual has been reborn in the ghost realm.

dn33:3.2.52.verse: This is the third lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

dn33:3.2.53.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world …

dn33:3.2.54.verse: But that individual has been reborn among the titans.

dn33:3.2.55.verse: This is the fourth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

dn33:3.2.56.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world …

dn33:3.2.57.verse: But that individual has been reborn in one of the long-lived orders of gods.

dn33:3.2.58.verse: This is the fifth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

dn33:3.2.59.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world …

dn33:3.2.60.verse: But that individual has been reborn in the borderlands, among uneducated foreigners, where monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen do not go.

dn33:3.2.61.verse: This is the sixth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

dn33:3.2.62.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world …

dn33:3.2.63.verse: And an individual is reborn in a central country. But they have wrong view and distorted perspective:

dn33:3.2.64.verse: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

dn33:3.2.65.verse: This is the seventh lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

dn33:3.2.66.verse: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world …

dn33:3.2.67.verse: And an individual is reborn in a central country. But they’re witless, dull, idiotic, and unable to distinguish what is well said from what is poorly said.

dn33:3.2.68.verse: This is the eighth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

dn33:3.2.69.verse: Furthermore, no Realized One has arisen in the world,

dn33:3.2.70.verse: so there is no teaching of the Dhamma leading to peace, extinguishment, awakening, as proclaimed by the Holy One. But an individual is reborn in a central country. And they’re wise, bright, clever, and able to distinguish what is well said from what is poorly said.

dn33:3.2.71.verse: This is the ninth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

dn33:3.2.73.verse: A mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

dn33:3.2.74.verse: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

dn33:3.2.75.verse: And with the fading away of rapture, they enter and remain in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

dn33:3.2.76.verse: With the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

dn33:3.2.77.verse: Going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite space.

dn33:3.2.78.verse: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

dn33:3.2.79.verse: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness.

dn33:3.2.80.verse: Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, they enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

dn33:3.2.81.verse: Going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, they enter and remain in the cessation of perception and feeling.

dn33:3.2.83.verse: For someone who has attained the first absorption, sensual perceptions have ceased.

dn33:3.2.84.verse: For someone who has attained the second absorption, the placing of the mind and keeping it connected have ceased.

dn33:3.2.85.verse: For someone who has attained the third absorption, rapture has ceased.

dn33:3.2.86.verse: For someone who has attained the fourth absorption, breathing has ceased.

dn33:3.2.87.verse: For someone who has attained the dimension of infinite space, the perception of form has ceased.

dn33:3.2.88.verse: For someone who has attained the dimension of infinite consciousness, the perception of the dimension of infinite space has ceased.

dn33:3.2.89.verse: For someone who has attained the dimension of nothingness, the perception of the dimension of infinite consciousness has ceased.

dn33:3.2.90.verse: For someone who has attained the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, the perception of the dimension of nothingness has ceased.

dn33:3.2.91.verse: For someone who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, perception and feeling have ceased.

dn33:3.2.92.verse: These are the teachings grouped by nine that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

dn33:3.2.93.verse: You should all recite these in concert.

dn33:3.3.1.verse: There are teachings grouped by ten that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

dn33:3.3.2.verse: You should all recite these in concert.

dn33:3.3.3.verse: What are the teachings grouped by ten?

dn33:3.3.4.verse: Ten qualities that serve as protector:

dn33:3.3.5.verse: Firstly, a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

dn33:3.3.7.verse: This is a quality that serves as protector.

dn33:3.3.8.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant is very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

dn33:3.3.10.verse: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

dn33:3.3.11.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has good friends, companions, and associates.

dn33:3.3.13.verse: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

dn33:3.3.14.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant is easy to admonish, having qualities that make them easy to admonish. They’re patient, and take instruction respectfully.

dn33:3.3.16.verse: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

dn33:3.3.17.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant is deft and tireless in a diverse spectrum of duties for their spiritual companions, understanding how to go about things in order to complete and organize the work.

dn33:3.3.19.verse: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

dn33:3.3.20.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant loves the teachings and is a delight to converse with, being full of joy in the teaching and training.

dn33:3.3.22.verse: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

dn33:3.3.23.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant is content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

dn33:3.3.25.verse: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

dn33:3.3.26.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They are strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

dn33:3.3.28.verse: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

dn33:3.3.29.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant is mindful. They have utmost mindfulness and alertness, and can remember and recall what was said and done long ago.

dn33:3.3.31.verse: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

dn33:3.3.32.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

dn33:3.3.34.verse: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

dn33:3.3.36.verse: Someone perceives the meditation on universal earth above, below, across, undivided and limitless.

dn33:3.3.37.verse: They perceive the meditation on universal water …

dn33:3.3.45.verse: They perceive the meditation on universal consciousness above, below, across, undivided and limitless.

dn33:3.3.46.verse: Ten ways of doing unskillful deeds:

dn33:3.3.47.verse: killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; covetousness, ill will, and wrong view.

dn33:3.3.48.verse: Ten ways of doing skillful deeds:

dn33:3.3.49.verse: refraining from killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; refraining from speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; contentment, good will, and right view.

dn33:3.3.50.verse: Ten abodes of the noble ones:

dn33:3.3.51.verse: A mendicant has given up five factors, possesses six factors, has a single guard, has four supports, has cast aside idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth, has totally given up searching, has unsullied intentions, has stilled the physical process, and is well freed in mind and well freed by wisdom.

dn33:3.3.52.verse: And how has a mendicant given up five factors?

dn33:3.3.53.verse: It’s when a mendicant has given up sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.

dn33:3.3.54.verse: That’s how a mendicant has given up five factors.

dn33:3.3.55.verse: And how does a mendicant possess six factors?

dn33:3.3.56.verse: A mendicant, seeing a sight with their eyes, is neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

dn33:3.3.57.verse: Hearing a sound with their ears … Smelling an odor with their nose … Tasting a flavor with their tongue … Encountering a touch with their body …

dn33:3.3.58.verse: Knowing an idea with their mind, they’re neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

dn33:3.3.59.verse: That’s how a mendicant possesses six factors.

dn33:3.3.60.verse: And how does a mendicant have a single guard?

dn33:3.3.61.verse: It’s when a mendicant’s heart is guarded by mindfulness.

dn33:3.3.62.verse: That’s how a mendicant has a single guard.

dn33:3.3.63.verse: And how does a mendicant have four supports?

dn33:3.3.64.verse: After appraisal, a mendicant uses some things, endures some things, avoids some things, and dispels some things.

dn33:3.3.65.verse: That’s how a mendicant has four supports.

dn33:3.3.66.verse: And how has a mendicant cast aside idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth?

dn33:3.3.67.verse: Different ascetics and brahmins have different idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth. A mendicant has cast out, cast aside, thrown out, discarded, let go of, given up, and relinquished all these.

dn33:3.3.68.verse: That’s how a mendicant has cast aside idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth.

dn33:3.3.69.verse: And how has a mendicant totally given up searching?

dn33:3.3.70.verse: It’s when they’ve given up searching for sensual pleasures, for continued existence, and for a spiritual path.

dn33:3.3.71.verse: That’s how a mendicant has totally given up searching.

dn33:3.3.72.verse: And how does a mendicant have unsullied intentions?

dn33:3.3.73.verse: It’s when they’ve given up sensual, malicious, and cruel intentions.

dn33:3.3.74.verse: That’s how a mendicant has unsullied intentions.

dn33:3.3.75.verse: And how has a mendicant stilled the physical process?

dn33:3.3.76.verse: It’s when, with the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

dn33:3.3.77.verse: That’s how a mendicant has stilled the physical process.

dn33:3.3.78.verse: And how is a mendicant well freed in mind?

dn33:3.3.79.verse: It’s when a mendicant’s mind is freed from greed, hate, and delusion.

dn33:3.3.80.verse: That’s how a mendicant is well freed in mind.

dn33:3.3.81.verse: And how is a mendicant well freed by wisdom?

dn33:3.3.82.verse: It’s when a mendicant understands: ‘I’ve given up greed, hate, and delusion, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them, so they’re unable to arise in the future.’

dn33:3.3.85.verse: That’s how a mendicant’s mind is well freed by wisdom.

dn33:3.3.87.verse: an adept’s right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

dn33:3.3.88.verse: Reverends, these are the teachings grouped by ten that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

dn33:3.3.89.verse: You should all recite these in concert, without disputing, so that this spiritual path may last for a long time. That would be for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”

dn33:3.4.1.verse: Then the Buddha got up and said to Venerable Sāriputta,

dn33:3.4.3.verse: It’s good that you’ve taught this exposition of the reciting in concert.”

dn33:3.4.4.verse: That is what Venerable Sāriputta said, and the Teacher concurred.

dn33:3.4.5.verse: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what Sāriputta said.

dn34:1.1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Campā on the banks of the Gaggarā Lotus Pond together with a large Saṅgha of five hundred mendicants.

dn34:1.1.8.verse: up to ten for attaining extinguishment,

dn34:1.1.9.verse: for making an end of suffering,

dn34:1.2.1.verse: Reverends, one thing is helpful, one thing should be developed, one thing should be completely understood, one thing should be given up, one thing makes things worse, one thing leads to distinction, one thing is hard to comprehend, one thing should be produced, one thing should be directly known, one thing should be realized.

dn34:1.2.5.verse: What one thing should be developed?

dn34:1.2.6.verse: Mindfulness of the body that is full of pleasure.

dn34:1.2.8.verse: What one thing should be completely understood?

dn34:1.2.9.verse: Contact, which is accompanied by defilements and fuels grasping.

dn34:1.2.11.verse: What one thing should be given up?

dn34:1.2.14.verse: What one thing makes things worse?

dn34:1.2.17.verse: What one thing leads to distinction?

dn34:1.2.20.verse: What one thing is hard to comprehend?

dn34:1.2.21.verse: The heart’s immersion of immediate result.

dn34:1.2.23.verse: What one thing should be produced?

dn34:1.2.26.verse: What one thing should be directly known?

dn34:1.2.27.verse: All sentient beings are sustained by food.

dn34:1.2.29.verse: What one thing should be realized?

dn34:1.2.30.verse: The unshakable release of the heart.

dn34:1.2.32.verse: So these ten things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.

dn34:1.3.1.verse: Two things are helpful, two things should be developed, two things should be completely understood, two things should be given up, two things make things worse, two things lead to distinction, two things are hard to comprehend, two things should be produced, two things should be directly known, two things should be realized.

dn34:1.3.5.verse: What two things should be developed?

dn34:1.3.8.verse: What two things should be completely understood?

dn34:1.3.11.verse: What two things should be given up?

dn34:1.3.12.verse: Ignorance and craving for continued existence.

dn34:1.3.14.verse: What two things make things worse?

dn34:1.3.15.verse: Being hard to admonish and having bad friends.

dn34:1.3.17.verse: What two things lead to distinction?

dn34:1.3.18.verse: Being easy to admonish and having good friends.

dn34:1.3.20.verse: What two things are hard to comprehend?

dn34:1.3.21.verse: The causes and reasons for the corruption of sentient beings, and the causes and reasons for the purification of sentient beings.

dn34:1.3.23.verse: What two things should be produced?

dn34:1.3.25.verse: knowledge of ending, and knowledge of non-arising.

dn34:1.3.27.verse: What two things should be directly known?

dn34:1.3.29.verse: the conditioned element and the unconditioned element.

dn34:1.3.31.verse: What two things should be realized?

dn34:1.3.34.verse: So these twenty things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.

dn34:1.4.3.verse: Associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, and practicing in line with the teaching.

dn34:1.4.5.verse: What three things should be developed?

dn34:1.4.7.verse: Immersion with placing the mind and keeping it connected. Immersion without placing the mind, merely keeping it connected. Immersion without placing the mind or keeping it connected.

dn34:1.4.9.verse: What three things should be completely understood?

dn34:1.4.13.verse: What three things should be given up?

dn34:1.4.15.verse: craving for sensual pleasures, craving for continued existence, and craving for nonexistence.

dn34:1.4.17.verse: What three things make things worse?

dn34:1.4.21.verse: What three things lead to distinction?

dn34:1.4.25.verse: What three things are hard to comprehend?

dn34:1.4.27.verse: Renunciation is the escape from sensual pleasures. The formless is the escape from form. Cessation is the escape from whatever is created, conditioned, and dependently originated.

dn34:1.4.29.verse: What three things should be produced?

dn34:1.4.31.verse: knowledge regarding the past portion, the future portion, and the present portion.

dn34:1.4.33.verse: What three things should be directly known?

dn34:1.4.35.verse: the sensual realm, the realm of luminous form, and the formless realm.

dn34:1.4.37.verse: What three things should be realized?

dn34:1.4.39.verse: recollection of past lives, knowledge of the death and rebirth of sentient beings, and knowledge of the ending of defilements.

dn34:1.4.41.verse: So these thirty things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.

dn34:1.5.4.verse: living in a suitable region, relying on true persons, being rightly resolved in oneself, and past merit.

dn34:1.5.6.verse: What four things should be developed?

dn34:1.5.7.verse: The four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

dn34:1.5.8.verse: A mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

dn34:1.5.9.verse: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

dn34:1.5.11.verse: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

dn34:1.5.13.verse: What four things should be completely understood?

dn34:1.5.15.verse: edible food, whether solid or subtle; contact is the second, mental intention the third, and consciousness the fourth.

dn34:1.5.17.verse: What four things should be given up?

dn34:1.5.19.verse: sensuality, desire for rebirth, views, and ignorance.

dn34:1.5.21.verse: What four things make things worse?

dn34:1.5.23.verse: the yokes of sensuality, desire for rebirth, views, and ignorance.

dn34:1.5.25.verse: What four things lead to distinction?

dn34:1.5.27.verse: unyoking from the yokes of sensuality, desire for rebirth, views, and ignorance.

dn34:1.5.29.verse: What four things are hard to comprehend?

dn34:1.5.31.verse: immersion liable to decline, stable immersion, immersion that leads to distinction, and immersion that leads to penetration.

dn34:1.5.33.verse: What four things should be produced?

dn34:1.5.35.verse: knowledge of the teaching, inferential knowledge, knowledge of encompassing, and conventional knowledge.

dn34:1.5.37.verse: What four things should be directly known?

dn34:1.5.39.verse: suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.

dn34:1.5.41.verse: What four things should be realized?

dn34:1.5.42.verse: Four fruits of the ascetic life:

dn34:1.5.45.verse: So these forty things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.

dn34:1.6.4.verse: A mendicant has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

dn34:1.6.5.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

dn34:1.6.6.verse: They are rarely ill or unwell. Their stomach digests well, being neither too hot nor too cold, but just right, and fit for meditation.

dn34:1.6.7.verse: They’re not devious or deceitful. They reveal themselves honestly to the Teacher or sensible spiritual companions.

dn34:1.6.8.verse: They live with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

dn34:1.6.9.verse: They’re wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

dn34:1.6.11.verse: What five things should be developed?

dn34:1.6.13.verse: pervasion with rapture, pervasion with pleasure, pervasion with mind, pervasion with light, and the basis for reviewing.

dn34:1.6.15.verse: What five things should be completely understood?

dn34:1.6.17.verse: form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

dn34:1.6.19.verse: What five things should be given up?

dn34:1.6.21.verse: sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.

dn34:1.6.23.verse: What five things make things worse?

dn34:1.6.25.verse: Firstly, a mendicant has doubts about the Teacher. They’re uncertain, undecided, and lacking confidence.

dn34:1.6.26.verse: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

dn34:1.6.28.verse: This is the first kind of hard-heartedness.

dn34:1.6.29.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant has doubts about the teaching …

dn34:1.6.32.verse: A mendicant is angry and upset with their spiritual companions, resentful and closed off.

dn34:1.6.33.verse: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

dn34:1.6.34.verse: This is the fifth kind of hard-heartedness.

dn34:1.6.36.verse: What five things lead to distinction?

dn34:1.6.38.verse: faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

dn34:1.6.40.verse: What five things are hard to comprehend?

dn34:1.6.42.verse: A mendicant focuses on sensual pleasures, but on that their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

dn34:1.6.43.verse: But when they focus on renunciation, on that their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

dn34:1.6.44.verse: Their mind is in a good state, well developed, well risen, well freed, and well detached from sensual pleasures.

dn34:1.6.45.verse: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of sensual pleasures, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

dn34:1.6.46.verse: This is how the escape from sensual pleasures is explained.

dn34:1.6.47.verse: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on ill will, but their mind does not leap forth …

dn34:1.6.48.verse: But when they focus on good will, their mind leaps forth …

dn34:1.6.49.verse: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from ill will.

dn34:1.6.50.verse: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of ill will, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

dn34:1.6.51.verse: This is how the escape from ill will is explained.

dn34:1.6.52.verse: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on harming, but their mind does not leap forth …

dn34:1.6.53.verse: But when they focus on compassion, their mind leaps forth …

dn34:1.6.54.verse: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from harming.

dn34:1.6.55.verse: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of harming, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

dn34:1.6.56.verse: This is how the escape from harming is explained.

dn34:1.6.57.verse: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on form, but their mind does not leap forth …

dn34:1.6.58.verse: But when they focus on the formless, their mind leaps forth …

dn34:1.6.59.verse: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from forms.

dn34:1.6.60.verse: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of form, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

dn34:1.6.61.verse: This is how the escape from forms is explained.

dn34:1.6.62.verse: Take a case where a mendicant focuses on substantial reality, but their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

dn34:1.6.63.verse: But when they focus on the cessation of substantial reality, their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

dn34:1.6.64.verse: Their mind is in a good state, well developed, well risen, well freed, and well detached from substantial reality.

dn34:1.6.65.verse: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of substantial reality, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

dn34:1.6.66.verse: This is how the escape from substantial reality is explained.

dn34:1.6.68.verse: What five things should be produced?

dn34:1.6.70.verse: The following knowledges arise for you personally: ‘This immersion is blissful now, and results in bliss in the future.’

dn34:1.6.71.verse: ‘This immersion is noble and not of the flesh.’

dn34:1.6.72.verse: ‘This immersion is not cultivated by reprobates.’

dn34:1.6.73.verse: ‘This immersion is peaceful and sublime and tranquil and unified, not held in place by forceful suppression.’

dn34:1.6.74.verse: ‘I mindfully enter into and emerge from this immersion.’

dn34:1.6.76.verse: What five things should be directly known?

dn34:1.6.78.verse: Firstly, the Teacher or a respected spiritual companion teaches Dhamma to a mendicant.

dn34:1.6.79.verse: That mendicant feels inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma, no matter how the Teacher or a respected spiritual companion teaches it.

dn34:1.6.80.verse: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.

dn34:1.6.81.verse: This is the first opportunity for freedom.

dn34:1.6.82.verse: Furthermore, it may be that neither the Teacher nor a respected spiritual companion teaches Dhamma to a mendicant. But the mendicant teaches Dhamma in detail to others as they learned and memorized it.

dn34:1.6.83.verse: That mendicant feels inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma, no matter how they teach it in detail to others as they learned and memorized it.

dn34:1.6.84.verse: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.

dn34:1.6.85.verse: This is the second opportunity for freedom.

dn34:1.6.86.verse: Furthermore, it may be that neither the Teacher nor … the mendicant teaches Dhamma. But the mendicant rehearses the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it.

dn34:1.6.87.verse: That mendicant feels inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma, no matter how they rehearse it in detail as they learned and memorized it.

dn34:1.6.88.verse: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.

dn34:1.6.89.verse: This is the third opportunity for freedom.

dn34:1.6.90.verse: Furthermore, it may be that neither the Teacher nor … the mendicant teaches Dhamma … nor does the mendicant rehearse the teaching.

dn34:1.6.91.verse: But the mendicant thinks about and considers the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it.

dn34:1.6.92.verse: That mendicant feels inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma, no matter how they think about and consider it in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it.

dn34:1.6.93.verse: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.

dn34:1.6.94.verse: This is the fourth opportunity for freedom.

dn34:1.6.95.verse: Furthermore, it may be that neither the Teacher nor … the mendicant teaches Dhamma … nor does the mendicant rehearse the teaching … or think about it.

dn34:1.6.96.verse: But a meditation subject as a basis of immersion is properly grasped, focused on, borne in mind, and penetrated with wisdom.

dn34:1.6.97.verse: That mendicant feels inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma, no matter how a meditation subject as a basis of immersion is properly grasped, focused on, borne in mind, and penetrated with wisdom.

dn34:1.6.98.verse: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.

dn34:1.6.99.verse: This is the fifth opportunity for freedom.

dn34:1.6.101.verse: What five things should be realized?

dn34:1.6.103.verse: ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and knowledge and vision of freedom.

dn34:1.6.105.verse: So these fifty things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.

dn34:1.7.4.verse: Firstly, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with bodily kindness, both in public and in private.

dn34:1.7.5.verse: This warm-hearted quality makes for fondness and respect, conducing to inclusion, harmony, and unity, without quarreling.

dn34:1.7.6.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with verbal kindness.

dn34:1.7.7.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with mental kindness.

dn34:1.7.8.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant shares without reservation any material things they have gained by legitimate means, even the food placed in the alms-bowl, using them in common with their ethical spiritual companions.

dn34:1.7.9.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant lives according to the precepts shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. Those precepts are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

dn34:1.7.10.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant lives according to the view shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. That view is noble and emancipating, and delivers one who applies it to the complete ending of suffering.

dn34:1.7.11.verse: This warm-hearted quality makes for fondness and respect, conducing to inclusion, harmony, and unity, without quarreling.

dn34:1.7.13.verse: What six things should be developed?

dn34:1.7.15.verse: the recollection of the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, ethics, generosity, and the deities.

dn34:1.7.17.verse: What six things should be completely understood?

dn34:1.7.19.verse: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

dn34:1.7.21.verse: What six things should be given up?

dn34:1.7.23.verse: craving for sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

dn34:1.7.25.verse: What six things make things worse?

dn34:1.7.27.verse: A mendicant lacks respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, the training, diligence, and hospitality.

dn34:1.7.29.verse: What six things lead to distinction?

dn34:1.7.31.verse: A mendicant has respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, the training, diligence, and hospitality.

dn34:1.7.33.verse: What six things are hard to comprehend?

dn34:1.7.36.verse: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by love. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

dn34:1.7.37.verse: Yet somehow ill will still occupies my mind.’

dn34:1.7.38.verse: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! Don’t say that. Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say that.

dn34:1.7.39.verse: It’s impossible, reverend, it cannot happen that the heart’s release by love has been developed and properly implemented,

dn34:1.7.40.verse: yet somehow ill will still occupies the mind.

dn34:1.7.41.verse: For it is the heart’s release by love that is the escape from ill will.’

dn34:1.7.43.verse: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by compassion. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

dn34:1.7.44.verse: Yet somehow the thought of harming still occupies my mind.’

dn34:1.7.45.verse: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

dn34:1.7.46.verse: For it is the heart’s release by compassion that is the escape from thoughts of harming.’

dn34:1.7.48.verse: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by rejoicing. …

dn34:1.7.49.verse: Yet somehow discontent still occupies my mind.’

dn34:1.7.50.verse: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

dn34:1.7.51.verse: For it is the heart’s release by rejoicing that is the escape from discontent.’

dn34:1.7.53.verse: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by equanimity. …

dn34:1.7.54.verse: Yet somehow desire still occupies my mind.’

dn34:1.7.55.verse: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

dn34:1.7.56.verse: For it is the heart’s release by equanimity that is the escape from desire.’

dn34:1.7.58.verse: ‘I’ve developed the signless release of the heart. …

dn34:1.7.59.verse: Yet somehow my consciousness still follows after signs.’

dn34:1.7.60.verse: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

dn34:1.7.61.verse: For it is the signless release of the heart that is the escape from all signs.’

dn34:1.7.63.verse: ‘I’m rid of the conceit “I am”. And I don’t regard anything as “I am this”.

dn34:1.7.64.verse: Yet somehow the dart of doubt and indecision still occupies my mind.’

dn34:1.7.65.verse: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! Don’t say that. Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say that.

dn34:1.7.66.verse: It’s impossible, reverend, it cannot happen that the conceit “I am” has been done away with, and nothing is regarded as “I am this”,

dn34:1.7.67.verse: yet somehow the dart of doubt and indecision still occupy the mind.

dn34:1.7.68.verse: For it is the uprooting of the conceit “I am” that is the escape from the dart of doubt and indecision.’

dn34:1.7.70.verse: What six things should be produced?

dn34:1.7.72.verse: A mendicant, seeing a sight with their eyes, is neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

dn34:1.7.73.verse: Hearing a sound with their ears …

dn34:1.7.74.verse: Smelling an odor with their nose …

dn34:1.7.75.verse: Tasting a flavor with their tongue …

dn34:1.7.76.verse: Encountering a touch with their body …

dn34:1.7.77.verse: Knowing an idea with their mind, they’re neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

dn34:1.7.79.verse: What six things should be directly known?

dn34:1.7.81.verse: the unsurpassable seeing, listening, acquisition, training, service, and recollection.

dn34:1.7.83.verse: What six things should be realized?

dn34:1.7.85.verse: A mendicant wields the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying themselves and becoming one again; materializing and dematerializing; going unobstructed through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; diving in and out of the earth as if it were water; walking on water as if it were earth; flying cross-legged through the sky like a bird; touching and stroking with the hand the sun and moon, so mighty and powerful; controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity.

dn34:1.7.86.verse: With clairaudience that is purified and superhuman, they hear both kinds of sounds, human and heavenly, whether near or far.

dn34:1.7.87.verse: They understand the minds of other beings and individuals, having encompassed them with their own mind.

dn34:1.7.90.verse: They recollect many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

dn34:1.7.91.verse: With clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

dn34:1.7.92.verse: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

dn34:1.7.94.verse: So these sixty things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.

dn34:1.8.3.verse: Seven riches of the noble ones:

dn34:1.8.4.verse: the riches of faith, ethics, conscience, prudence, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

dn34:1.8.6.verse: What seven things should be developed?

dn34:1.8.8.verse: mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

dn34:1.8.10.verse: What seven things should be completely understood?

dn34:1.8.12.verse: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and diverse in perception, such as human beings, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.

dn34:1.8.13.verse: This is the first plane of consciousness.

dn34:1.8.14.verse: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and unified in perception, such as the gods reborn in the Divinity’s host through the first absorption.

dn34:1.8.15.verse: This is the second plane of consciousness.

dn34:1.8.16.verse: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and diverse in perception, such as the gods of sublime luminosity.

dn34:1.8.17.verse: This is the third plane of consciousness.

dn34:1.8.18.verse: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and unified in perception, such as the gods of universal beauty.

dn34:1.8.19.verse: This is the fourth plane of consciousness.

dn34:1.8.20.verse: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond perceptions of form. With the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite space.

dn34:1.8.21.verse: This is the fifth plane of consciousness.

dn34:1.8.22.verse: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite space. Aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

dn34:1.8.23.verse: This is the sixth plane of consciousness.

dn34:1.8.24.verse: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness. Aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they have been reborn in the dimension of nothingness.

dn34:1.8.25.verse: This is the seventh plane of consciousness.

dn34:1.8.27.verse: What seven things should be given up?

dn34:1.8.29.verse: sensual desire, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, desire for continued existence, and ignorance.

dn34:1.8.31.verse: What seven things make things worse?

dn34:1.8.33.verse: a mendicant is faithless, shameless, imprudent, unlearned, lazy, unmindful, and witless.

dn34:1.8.35.verse: What seven things lead to distinction?

dn34:1.8.37.verse: a mendicant is faithful, conscientious, prudent, learned, energetic, mindful, and wise.

dn34:1.8.39.verse: What seven things are hard to comprehend?

dn34:1.8.40.verse: Seven aspects of the teachings of the true persons:

dn34:1.8.41.verse: a mendicant knows the teachings, knows the meaning, knows themselves, knows moderation, knows the right time, knows assemblies, and knows individuals.

dn34:1.8.43.verse: What seven things should be produced?

dn34:1.8.45.verse: the perception of impermanence, the perception of not-self, the perception of ugliness, the perception of drawbacks, the perception of giving up, the perception of fading away, and the perception of cessation.

dn34:1.8.47.verse: What seven things should be directly known?

dn34:1.8.49.verse: A mendicant has a keen enthusiasm to undertake the training …

dn34:1.8.55.verse: to penetrate theoretically. And they don’t lose these desires in the future.

dn34:1.8.57.verse: What seven things should be realized?

dn34:1.8.58.verse: Seven powers of one who has ended the defilements.

dn34:1.8.59.verse: Firstly, a mendicant with defilements ended has clearly seen with right wisdom all conditions as truly impermanent.

dn34:1.8.60.verse: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim: ‘My defilements have ended.’

dn34:1.8.61.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has clearly seen with right wisdom that sensual pleasures are truly like a pit of glowing coals. …

dn34:1.8.63.verse: Furthermore, the mind of a mendicant with defilements ended slants, slopes, and inclines to seclusion. They’re withdrawn, loving renunciation, and have totally eliminated defiling influences. …

dn34:1.8.65.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. …

dn34:1.8.67.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the five faculties. …

dn34:1.8.69.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the seven awakening factors. …

dn34:1.8.71.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the noble eightfold path. …

dn34:1.8.72.verse: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim:

dn34:1.8.75.verse: So these seventy things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.

dn34:1.8.76.verse: The first recitation section is complete.

dn34:2.1.3.verse: There are eight causes and reasons that lead to acquiring the wisdom fundamental to the spiritual life, and to its increase, growth, development, and fulfillment once it has been acquired.

dn34:2.1.5.verse: It’s when a mendicant lives relying on the Teacher or a spiritual companion in a teacher’s role. And they set up a keen sense of conscience and prudence for them, with warmth and respect.

dn34:2.1.7.verse: When a mendicant lives relying on the Teacher or a spiritual companion in a teacher’s role—with a keen sense of conscience and prudence for them, with warmth and respect—from time to time they go and ask them questions:

dn34:2.1.10.verse: Those venerables clarify what is unclear, reveal what is obscure, and dispel doubt regarding the many doubtful matters.

dn34:2.1.12.verse: After hearing that teaching they perfect withdrawal of both body and mind.

dn34:2.1.14.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

dn34:2.1.16.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant is very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

dn34:2.1.18.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They are strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

dn34:2.1.20.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant is mindful. They have utmost mindfulness and alertness, and can remember and recall what was said and done long ago.

dn34:2.1.22.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant meditates observing rise and fall in the five grasping aggregates.

dn34:2.1.23.verse: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the disappearance of form.

dn34:2.1.24.verse: Such is feeling, such is the origin of feeling, such is the disappearance of feeling.

dn34:2.1.25.verse: Such is perception, such is the origin of perception, such is the disappearance of perception.

dn34:2.1.26.verse: Such are choices, such is the origin of choices, such is the disappearance of choices.

dn34:2.1.27.verse: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.’

dn34:2.1.30.verse: What eight things should be developed?

dn34:2.1.31.verse: The noble eightfold path, that is:
