ps3.9:25.1.verse: Imehi cattālīsāya ākārehi anulomikaṁ khantiṁ paṭilabhantassa, imehi cattālīsāya ākārehi sammattaniyāmaṁ okkamantassa kati aniccānupassanā, kati dukkhānupassanā, kati anattānupassanā?

ps3.10:1.1.verse: Nicchāto, mokkho vimokkho, vijjāvimutti, adhisīlaṁ, adhicittaṁ, adhipaññā, passaddhi, ñāṇaṁ, dassanaṁ, visuddhi, nekkhammaṁ, nissaraṇaṁ, paviveko, vosaggo, cariyā, jhānavimokkho, bhāvanā, adhiṭṭhānaṁ, jīvitaṁ. [19]

ps3.10:2.1.verse: Nicchātoti nekkhammena kāmacchandato nicchāto, abyāpādena byāpādato nicchāto …pe…

ps3.10:4.1.verse: Vijjāvimuttīti nekkhammaṁ vijjatīti vijjā, kāmacchandato muccatīti vimutti.

ps3.10:4.4.verse: Abyāpādo vijjatīti vijjā, byāpādato vimuccatīti vimutti.

ps3.10:4.7.verse: arahattamaggo vijjatīti vijjā, sabbakilesehi muccatīti vimutti.

ps3.10:5.1.verse: Adhisīlaṁ adhicittaṁ adhipaññāti nekkhammena kāmacchandaṁ, saṁvaraṭṭhena sīlavisuddhi, avikkhepaṭṭhena cittavisuddhi, dassanaṭṭhena diṭṭhivisuddhi.

ps3.10:5.6.verse: arahattamaggena sabbakilese saṁvaraṭṭhena sīlavisuddhi, avikkhepaṭṭhena cittavisuddhi.

ps3.10:6.1.verse: Passaddhīti nekkhammena kāmacchandaṁ paṭippassambheti, abyāpādena byāpādaṁ paṭippassambheti …pe…

ps3.10:7.1.verse: Ñāṇanti kāmacchandassa pahīnattā nekkhammaṁ ñātaṭṭhena ñāṇaṁ;

ps3.10:8.1.verse: Dassananti kāmacchandassa pahīnattā nekkhammaṁ diṭṭhattā dassanaṁ.

ps3.10:10.3.verse: Yaṁ kho pana kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ, nirodho tassa nekkhammaṁ.

ps3.10:11.3.verse: Yaṁ kho pana kiñci bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ, nirodho tassa nissaraṇaṁ.

ps3.10:16.1.verse: Bhāvanā adhiṭṭhānaṁ jīvitanti kāmacchandaṁ pajahanto nekkhammaṁ bhāvetīti—

ps3.10:16.5.verse: Svāyaṁ evaṁ bhāvanāsampanno adhiṭṭhānasampanno samaṁ jīvati, no visamaṁ;

ps3.10:16.9.verse: Svāyaṁ evaṁ bhāvanāsampanno adhiṭṭhānasampanno ājīvasampanno yaññadeva parisaṁ upasaṅkamati—

ps3.10:16.10.verse: yadi khattiyaparisaṁ yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṁ yadi gahapatiparisaṁ yadi samaṇaparisaṁ—

ps3.10:16.13.verse: Tathā hi so bhāvanāsampanno adhiṭṭhānasampanno ājīvasampanno.

ps3.10:17.19.verse: Svāyaṁ evaṁ bhāvanāsampanno adhiṭṭhānasampanno samaṁ jīvati, no visamaṁ;

ps3.10:17.23.verse: Svāyaṁ evaṁ bhāvanāsampanno adhiṭṭhānasampanno ājīvasampanno yaññadeva parisaṁ upasaṅkamati—

ps3.10:17.24.verse: yadi khattiyaparisaṁ yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṁ yadi gahapatiparisaṁ yadi samaṇaparisaṁ—

ps3.10:17.27.verse: Tathā hi so bhāvanāsampanno adhiṭṭhānasampanno ājīvasampannoti.

pv1:1.1.verse: Homage to the Blessed, Noble, and Perfectly Enlightened One.

pv1:2.3.verse: A gift is like a seed,

pv1:2.4.verse: And from this, the fruit grows.

pv1:3.1.verse: The seed is sown in the field,

pv1:3.2.verse: For the benefit of the departed and the donor.

pv1:3.4.verse: And the donor grows in merit.

pv1:4.1.verse: Having done what's wholesome in this way,

pv1:4.4.verse: One goes to the ground of heaven.

pv1:5.1.verse: This is the first (Discourse), The Simile of the Field.

snp1.1:1.1.verse: A monk who removes anger when it appears,

snp1.1:1.2.verse: as one removes a serpent’s venom using medicines,

snp1.1:1.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:1.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:2.1.verse: A monk who completely cuts off passion,

snp1.1:2.2.verse: like a lotus plant dropping its flowers,

snp1.1:2.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:2.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:3.1.verse: A monk who has completely severed craving,

snp1.1:3.2.verse: who has dried up the swiftly flowing river,

snp1.1:3.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:3.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:4.1.verse: A monk who completely destroys conceit,

snp1.1:4.2.verse: like a flood destroys a fragile bamboo bridge,

snp1.1:4.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:4.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:5.1.verse: A monk who sees no value in states of being,

snp1.1:5.2.verse: as one does not find flowers on fig trees,

snp1.1:5.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:5.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:6.1.verse: A monk in whom there is no anger,

snp1.1:6.2.verse: who has completely gone beyond both being and non-being,

snp1.1:6.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:6.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:7.1.verse: A monk who has completely blown away their thoughts,

snp1.1:7.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:7.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:8.1.verse: A monk who neither goes too far nor goes back,

snp1.1:8.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:8.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:9.1.verse: A monk who neither goes too far nor goes back,

snp1.1:9.2.verse: who knows that the world is completely false,

snp1.1:9.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:9.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:10.1.verse: A monk who neither goes too far nor goes back,

snp1.1:10.2.verse: who is free of greed, knowing it to be completely false,

snp1.1:10.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:10.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:11.1.verse: A monk who neither goes too far nor goes back,

snp1.1:11.2.verse: who is free of passion, knowing it to be completely false,

snp1.1:11.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:11.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:12.1.verse: A monk who neither goes too far nor goes back,

snp1.1:12.2.verse: who is free of hatred, knowing it to be completely false,

snp1.1:12.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:12.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:13.1.verse: A monk who neither goes too far nor goes back,

snp1.1:13.2.verse: who is free of delusion, knowing it to be completely false,

snp1.1:13.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:13.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:14.1.verse: A monk who has no subconscious tendencies,

snp1.1:14.2.verse: who has eliminated the unwholesome roots,

snp1.1:14.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:14.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:15.1.verse: A monk who has no anxiety whatsoever

snp1.1:15.2.verse: about this life or the next,

snp1.1:15.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:15.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:16.1.verse: A monk who has no desire whatsoever

snp1.1:16.2.verse: based on which one might be bound to existence,

snp1.1:16.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:16.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:17.1.verse: A monk who has discarded the five hindrances,

snp1.1:17.2.verse: who is untroubled, free of doubt, unafflicted,

snp1.1:17.3.verse: relinquishes both the here and the beyond

snp1.1:17.4.verse: like a snake shedding its decayed skin.

snp1.1:1.1.verse: The monk who subdues his arisen anger

snp1.1:1.2.verse: as, with herbs, snake-venom once it has spread;

snp1.1:1.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:1.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:2.1.verse: The monk who has cut off passion without leaving a trace,

snp1.1:2.2.verse: as he would, plunging into a lake, a lotus;

snp1.1:2.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:2.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:3.1.verse: The monk who has cut off craving without leaving a trace,

snp1.1:3.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:3.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:4.1.verse: The monk who has uprooted conceit without leaving a trace,

snp1.1:4.2.verse: as a great flood, a very weak bridge made of reeds;

snp1.1:4.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:4.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:5.1.verse: The monk seeing in states of becoming no essence,

snp1.1:5.2.verse: as he would, when examining fig trees, no flowers;

snp1.1:5.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:5.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:6.1.verse: The monk with no inner anger,

snp1.1:6.2.verse: who has thus gone beyond becoming & not-;

snp1.1:6.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:6.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:7.1.verse: The monk whose discursive thoughts are dispersed,

snp1.1:7.2.verse: well-dealt with inside, without leaving a trace;

snp1.1:7.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:7.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:8.1.verse: The monk who hasn’t slipped past or held back,

snp1.1:8.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:8.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:9.1.verse: The monk who hasn’t slipped past or held back,

snp1.1:9.2.verse: knowing with regard to the world that “All this is unreal”;

snp1.1:9.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:9.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:10.1.verse: The monk who hasn’t slipped past or held back,

snp1.1:10.2.verse: without greed, as “All this is unreal”;

snp1.1:10.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:10.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:11.1.verse: The monk who hasn’t slipped past or held back,

snp1.1:11.2.verse: without passion, as “All this is unreal”;

snp1.1:11.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:11.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:12.1.verse: The monk who hasn’t slipped past or held back,

snp1.1:12.2.verse: without aversion, as “All this is unreal”;

snp1.1:12.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:12.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:13.1.verse: The monk who hasn’t slipped past or turned back,

snp1.1:13.2.verse: without delusion, as “All this is unreal”;

snp1.1:13.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:13.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:14.1.verse: The monk in whom there are no obsessions

snp1.1:14.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:14.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:15.1.verse: The monk in whom there’s nothing born of disturbance,

snp1.1:15.2.verse: that would lead him back to this shore;

snp1.1:15.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:15.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:16.1.verse: The monk in whom there’s nothing born of the underbrush,

snp1.1:16.2.verse: that would act as a cause for binding him to becoming;

snp1.1:16.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:16.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:17.1.verse: The monk who’s abandoned five hindrances,

snp1.1:17.2.verse: who, untroubled, de-arrowed, has crossed over doubt;

snp1.1:17.3.verse: sloughs off the near shore & far—

snp1.1:17.4.verse: as a snake, its decrepit old skin.

snp1.1:1.1.verse: When anger surges, they drive it out,

snp1.1:1.2.verse: as with medicine a cobra’s spreading venom.

snp1.1:1.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:1.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:2.2.verse: like a lotus plucked flower and stalk.

snp1.1:2.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:2.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:3.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:3.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:4.2.verse: as a fragile bridge of reeds by a great flood.

snp1.1:4.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:4.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:5.1.verse: In future lives they find no worth,

snp1.1:5.2.verse: as an inspector of fig trees finds no flower.

snp1.1:5.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:5.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:6.2.verse: passed beyond any kind of existence.

snp1.1:6.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:6.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:7.1.verse: Their mental vibrations are cleared away,

snp1.1:7.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:7.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:8.1.verse: They have not run too far nor run back,

snp1.1:8.2.verse: but have gone beyond all this proliferation.

snp1.1:8.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:8.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:9.1.verse: They have not run too far nor run back,

snp1.1:9.2.verse: for they know that nothing in the world is what it seems.

snp1.1:9.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:9.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:10.1.verse: They have not run too far nor run back,

snp1.1:10.2.verse: knowing nothing is what it seems, free of greed.

snp1.1:10.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:10.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:11.1.verse: They have not run too far nor run back,

snp1.1:11.2.verse: knowing nothing is what it seems, free of lust.

snp1.1:11.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:11.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:12.1.verse: They have not run too far nor run back,

snp1.1:12.2.verse: knowing nothing is what it seems, free of hate.

snp1.1:12.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:12.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:13.1.verse: They have not run too far nor run back,

snp1.1:13.2.verse: knowing nothing is what it seems, free of delusion.

snp1.1:13.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:13.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:14.1.verse: They have no underlying tendencies at all,

snp1.1:14.2.verse: and are rid of unskillful roots,

snp1.1:14.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:14.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:15.1.verse: They have nothing born of distress at all

snp1.1:15.2.verse: to make them to return to the near shore.

snp1.1:15.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:15.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:16.1.verse: No snarl grows in them at all,

snp1.1:16.2.verse: that would shackle them to a new life.

snp1.1:16.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:16.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.1:17.1.verse: They’ve given up the five hindrances,

snp1.1:17.2.verse: untroubled, rid of indecision, free of thorns.

snp1.1:17.3.verse: Such a mendicant sheds the near shore and the far,

snp1.1:17.4.verse: as a serpent its old worn-out skin.

snp1.2:1.1.verse: “I have prepared cooked rice and fresh milk,”

snp1.2:1.3.verse: “I stay constantly at the shore of the great river,

snp1.2:1.4.verse: “I have a closed hut with a fire kindled;

snp1.2:1.5.verse: “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

snp1.2:2.1.verse: “I have no anger and no corruption,”

snp1.2:2.3.verse: “I stay one night at the shore of the great river,

snp1.2:2.4.verse: “I have an open hut with the fire extinguished;

snp1.2:2.5.verse: “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

snp1.2:3.3.verse: “In the marshes and meadows where the cattle roam,

snp1.2:3.4.verse: “When it rained in the past, they could endure;

snp1.2:3.5.verse: “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

snp1.2:4.3.verse: “It crossed over to the far shore, it went past the deluge;

snp1.2:4.4.verse: “I have no need of a raft;

snp1.2:4.5.verse: “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

snp1.2:5.3.verse: “For a long time, she has been a pleasant co-resident,

snp1.2:5.4.verse: “I have never heard anything evil from her;

snp1.2:5.5.verse: “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

snp1.2:6.3.verse: “For a long time, it has been thoroughly developed and well-trained,

snp1.2:6.4.verse: “No evil can be found in me;

snp1.2:6.5.verse: “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

snp1.2:7.1.verse: “I have a servant that I hired myself,”

snp1.2:7.4.verse: “I have never heard anything evil from them;

snp1.2:7.5.verse: “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

snp1.2:8.1.verse: “I am not the servant of anyone,”

snp1.2:8.3.verse: “I travel the entire world with what I have gained,

snp1.2:8.5.verse: “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

snp1.2:9.1.verse: “There is a cow and a suckling calf,”

snp1.2:9.3.verse: “There is the herd-mother with her offspring,

snp1.2:9.5.verse: “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

snp1.2:10.1.verse: “There is no cow and no suckling calf,”

snp1.2:10.5.verse: “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

snp1.2:11.1.verse: “The post is firmly entrenched and does not wobble,”

snp1.2:11.3.verse: “The ropes are made of new and well-made twine,

snp1.2:11.4.verse: “It is not possible for the calves to break them;

snp1.2:11.5.verse: “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

snp1.2:12.1.verse: “Like a bull that has broken its bonds,”

snp1.2:12.3.verse: “Like an elephant that has burst through rotten vines,

snp1.2:12.4.verse: “I will never again enter a womb;

snp1.2:12.5.verse: “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

snp1.2:13.1.verse: Flooding both the low ground and the high ground,

snp1.2:13.2.verse: a great raincloud poured down rain.

snp1.2:13.3.verse: After hearing the rain from the angels,

snp1.2:14.1.verse: “It is a gain for us, and not a small one,

snp1.2:15.1.verse: “I am a cow-herd, and I listen,

snp1.2:15.2.verse: “I will live the spiritual life following the Sublime One,

snp1.2:16.1.verse: “One who has children delights because of their children,”

snp1.2:16.3.verse: “One who has cattle delights because of their cattle,

snp1.2:16.4.verse: “Possessions are the delight of a person,

snp1.2:16.5.verse: “One who has no possessions has no delight.”

snp1.2:17.1.verse: “One who has children sorrows because of their children,”

snp1.2:17.3.verse: “One who has cattle sorrows because of their cattle,

snp1.2:17.4.verse: “Possessions are the the sorrow of a person,

snp1.2:17.5.verse: “One who has no possessions has no sorrow.”

snp1.2:1.1.verse: “The rice is cooked, my milking done.

snp1.2:1.3.verse: I live with my people along the banks of the Mahi;

snp1.2:1.4.verse: my hut is roofed, my fire lit:

snp1.2:1.5.verse: So if you want, rain-god, go ahead & rain.”

snp1.2:2.3.verse: I live for one night along the banks of the Mahi;

snp1.2:2.4.verse: my hut’s roof is open, my fire out.

snp1.2:2.5.verse: So if you want, rain-god, go ahead & rain.”

snp1.2:3.1.verse: “No mosquitoes or gadflies are to be found.

snp1.2:3.3.verse: The cows range in the marshy meadow where the grasses flourish.

snp1.2:3.4.verse: They could stand the rain if it came:

snp1.2:3.5.verse: So if you want, rain-god, go ahead & rain.”

snp1.2:4.1.verse: “A raft, well-made, has been lashed together.

snp1.2:4.3.verse: Having crossed over, gone to the far shore, I’ve subdued the flood.

snp1.2:4.4.verse: No need for a raft is to be found:

snp1.2:4.5.verse: So if you want, rain-god, go ahead & rain.”

snp1.2:5.3.verse: is charming, has lived with me long.

snp1.2:5.4.verse: I hear no evil about her at all:

snp1.2:5.5.verse: So if you want, rain-god, go ahead & rain.”

snp1.2:6.3.verse: has long been nurtured, well tamed.

snp1.2:6.4.verse: No evil is to be found in me:

snp1.2:6.5.verse: So if you want, rain-god, go ahead & rain.”

snp1.2:7.3.verse: My sons live in harmony, free from disease.

snp1.2:7.4.verse: I hear no evil about them at all:

snp1.2:7.5.verse: So if you want, rain-god, go ahead & rain.”

snp1.2:8.3.verse: I wander the whole world on the reward [of my Awakening].

snp1.2:8.4.verse: No need for earnings is to be found:

snp1.2:8.5.verse: So if you want, rain-god, go ahead & rain.”

snp1.2:9.4.verse: & a great bull, the leader of the herd:

snp1.2:9.5.verse: So if you want, rain-god, go ahead & rain.”

snp1.2:10.1.verse: “There are no cows, no young bulls,

snp1.2:10.3.verse: no cows in calf or breeding cows,

snp1.2:10.4.verse: no great bull, the leader of the herd:

snp1.2:10.5.verse: So if you want, rain-god, go ahead & rain.”

snp1.2:11.4.verse: not even young bulls could break:

snp1.2:11.5.verse: So if you want, rain-god, go ahead & rain.”

snp1.2:12.1.verse: “Having broken my bonds like a great bull,

snp1.2:12.3.verse: like a great elephant tearing a rotting vine,

snp1.2:12.4.verse: I never again will lie in the womb:

snp1.2:12.5.verse: So if you want, rain-god, go ahead & rain.”

snp1.2:13.2.verse: The great cloud rained down straightaway,

snp1.2:14.2.verse: that we’ve gazed on the Blessed One!

snp1.2:14.3.verse: We go to him, the One with Eyes, for refuge.

snp1.2:14.4.verse: May you be our teacher, Great Sage.

snp1.2:15.2.verse: Let’s follow the holy life under the One Well-Gone.

snp1.2:15.3.verse: Gone to the far shore of aging & death,

snp1.2:15.4.verse: let’s put an end to suffering & stress.”

snp1.2:16.1.verse: “Those with children delight because of their children.

snp1.2:16.3.verse: Those with cattle delight because of their cows.

snp1.2:16.4.verse: A person’s delight comes from acquisitions,

snp1.2:16.5.verse: for a person with no acquisitions doesn’t delight.”

snp1.2:17.1.verse: “Those with children grieve precisely because of their children.

snp1.2:17.3.verse: Those with cattle grieve precisely because of their cows.

snp1.2:17.4.verse: A person’s grief comes from acquisitions,

snp1.2:17.5.verse: for a person with no acquisitions doesn’t grieve.”

snp1.2:1.1.verse: “I’ve boiled my rice and drawn my milk,”

snp1.2:1.3.verse: “I stay with my family along the bank of the Mahī.

snp1.2:1.4.verse: My hut is roofed, my sacred fire kindled:

snp1.2:1.5.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.”

snp1.2:2.1.verse: “I boil not with anger and have drawn out hard-heartedness,”

snp1.2:2.3.verse: “I stay for one night along the bank of the Mahī.

snp1.2:2.4.verse: My hut is wide open, my fire is quenched:

snp1.2:2.5.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.”

snp1.2:3.3.verse: “cows graze on the lush meadow grass.

snp1.2:3.4.verse: They get by even when the rain comes:

snp1.2:3.5.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.”

snp1.2:4.1.verse: “I bound a raft and prepared it well,”

snp1.2:4.3.verse: “and with it I crossed over, went to the far shore, and dispelled the flood.

snp1.2:4.4.verse: Now I have no need for a raft:

snp1.2:4.5.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.”

snp1.2:5.4.verse: I hear nothing bad about her:

snp1.2:5.5.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.”

snp1.2:6.4.verse: Nothing bad is found in me:

snp1.2:6.5.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.”

snp1.2:7.4.verse: I hear nothing bad about them:

snp1.2:7.5.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.”

snp1.2:8.3.verse: “with what I have earned I wander the world.

snp1.2:8.4.verse: I have no need for wages:

snp1.2:8.5.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.”

snp1.2:9.4.verse: I’ve also got a bull, captain of the herd here:

snp1.2:9.5.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.”

snp1.2:10.3.verse: “no cows in calf or breeding cows.

snp1.2:10.4.verse: I haven’t got a bull, captain of the herd here:

snp1.2:10.5.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.”

snp1.2:11.3.verse: “The grass halters are new and well-woven,

snp1.2:11.4.verse: not even the sucklings can break them:

snp1.2:11.5.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.”

snp1.2:12.1.verse: “Like a bull I broke the bonds,”

snp1.2:12.3.verse: “like an elephant I snapped the vine.

snp1.2:12.4.verse: I will never lie in a womb again:

snp1.2:12.5.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.”

snp1.2:13.1.verse: Right then a vast cloud rained forth,

snp1.2:14.1.verse: “It is no small gain for us

snp1.2:14.2.verse: that we have seen the Buddha.

snp1.2:14.3.verse: We come to you for refuge, Clear-eyed One.

snp1.2:14.4.verse: O great sage, please be our Teacher.

snp1.2:15.2.verse: shall lead the spiritual life under the Holy One.

snp1.2:15.4.verse: we shall make an end of suffering.”

snp1.2:16.4.verse: For attachments are a man’s delight;

snp1.2:17.4.verse: For attachments are a man’s sorrow;

snp1.2:17.5.verse: without attachments there are no sorrows.”

snp1.3:1.1.verse: Renouncing violence for all living beings,

snp1.3:1.2.verse: harming not even one of them,

snp1.3:1.3.verse: you would not wish for offspring, so how a companion?

snp1.3:2.1.verse: For a person by nature entangled there are affections;

snp1.3:2.2.verse: on the heels of affection, this pain.

snp1.3:2.3.verse: Seeing the drawback born of affection,

snp1.3:3.1.verse: One whose mind is enmeshed in sympathy for friends & companions,

snp1.3:5.1.verse: As a deer in the wilds, unfettered,

snp1.3:5.2.verse: goes for forage wherever it wants:

snp1.3:6.1.verse: You are prey to requests in the midst of companions,

snp1.3:6.2.verse: when staying at home, when going out wandering—

snp1.3:6.3.verse: Valuing the freedom that no one else covets,

snp1.3:7.1.verse: There is sporting & love in the midst of companions,

snp1.3:7.3.verse: Feeling disgust at the prospect of parting from those who’d be dear,

snp1.3:8.1.verse: Without resistance in all four directions,

snp1.3:9.1.verse: They are hard to please, some of those gone forth,

snp1.3:9.2.verse: as well as those living the household life.

snp1.3:9.3.verse: Being unconcerned with the offspring of others,

snp1.3:10.2.verse: like a kovilara tree that has shed its leaves,

snp1.3:10.3.verse: the enlightened one, cutting all household ties,

snp1.3:11.1.verse: If you gain an astute companion,

snp1.3:12.1.verse: If you don’t gain an astute companion,

snp1.3:12.3.verse: wander alone like a king renouncing his conquered kingdom,

snp1.3:12.4.verse: like the elephant in the Mataṅga wilds, [his herd].

snp1.3:13.2.verse: Those on a par, or better, should be chosen as friends.

snp1.3:13.3.verse: If they’re not to be found, living faultlessly,

snp1.3:14.3.verse: clinking, clashing, two on an arm,

snp1.3:15.1.verse: [Thinking:] “In the same way, if I were to live with another,

snp1.3:15.2.verse: there would be conversation or attachment.”

snp1.3:16.1.verse: Because sensual pleasures, elegant, honeyed, & charming,

snp1.3:16.2.verse: bewitch the mind with their manifold forms—

snp1.3:16.3.verse: seeing this drawback in sensual strings—

snp1.3:17.2.verse: disease, an arrow, a danger for me.”

snp1.3:17.3.verse: Seeing this danger in sensual strings,

snp1.3:19.1.verse: As a great white elephant, renouncing his herd,

snp1.3:19.3.verse: lives in the wilds wherever he wants,

snp1.3:20.1.verse: “There’s no way that one delighting in company

snp1.3:20.3.verse: Heeding the words of the Kinsman of the Sun,

snp1.3:21.2.verse: the sure way attained, the path gained,

snp1.3:21.3.verse: [realizing:] “Unled by others, I have knowledge arisen,”

snp1.3:22.1.verse: With no greed, no deceit, no thirst,

snp1.3:22.3.verse: with no inclinations for all the world, every world,

snp1.3:23.2.verse: disregarding the goal, intent on the discordant way.

snp1.3:23.3.verse: Don’t associate yourself with someone heedless & hankering.

snp1.3:24.1.verse: Consort with one who is learned, who maintains the Dhamma,

snp1.3:24.3.verse: Knowing the meanings, subdue your perplexity,

snp1.3:25.1.verse: Free from longing, finding no pleasure

snp1.3:25.2.verse: in the world’s sport, ardor, or sensual bliss,

snp1.3:25.3.verse: abstaining from adornment, speaking the truth,

snp1.3:27.1.verse: “This is a bondage. There’s little happiness here,

snp1.3:27.2.verse: next to no enjoyment, all the more suffering & pain.

snp1.3:27.3.verse: This is a boil”: Knowing this, circumspect,

snp1.3:28.2.verse: like a fish in the water tearing a net,

snp1.3:28.3.verse: like a fire not coming back to what’s burnt,

snp1.3:30.2.verse: like a coral tree that has shed its leaves,

snp1.3:30.3.verse: going forth in the ochre robe,

snp1.3:31.1.verse: Showing no greed for flavors, not wanton,

snp1.3:31.2.verse: going from house to house for alms

snp1.3:31.3.verse: with mind unenmeshed in this family or that,

snp1.3:33.1.verse: Turning your back on pleasure & pain,

snp1.3:34.1.verse: With persistence aroused for the highest goal’s attainment,

snp1.3:34.2.verse: with mind unsmeared, not lazy in action,

snp1.3:34.3.verse: firm in effort, with steadfastness & strength arisen,

snp1.3:35.2.verse: constantly living the Dhamma in line with the Dhamma,

snp1.3:35.3.verse: comprehending the danger in states of becoming,

snp1.3:36.1.verse: Intent on the ending of craving & heedful,

snp1.3:36.2.verse: neither drooling nor dumb, but learned, mindful,

snp1.3:37.1.verse: Unstartled, like a lion at sounds.

snp1.3:37.2.verse: Unsnared, like the wind in a net.

snp1.3:37.3.verse: Unsmeared, like a lotus in water:

snp1.3:38.1.verse: Like a lion—forceful, strong in fang,

snp1.3:38.2.verse: living as a conqueror, the king of beasts—

snp1.3:39.1.verse: At the right time consorting with the release

snp1.3:39.2.verse: through goodwill, compassion, empathetic joy, equanimity,

snp1.3:39.3.verse: unobstructed by all the world, any world,

snp1.3:40.1.verse: Having let go of passion, aversion, delusion;

snp1.3:40.3.verse: unfazed at the ending of life,

snp1.3:41.1.verse: People follow & associate for a motive.

snp1.3:41.2.verse: Friends without a motive these days are rare.

snp1.3:41.3.verse: They’re shrewd for their own ends, & impure.

snp1.3:41.5.verse: The third: the Rhinoceros Horn Discourse.

snp1.3:1.1.verse: When you’ve laid down violence toward all creatures,

snp1.3:1.2.verse: not harming even a single one,

snp1.3:1.3.verse: don’t wish for a child, let alone a companion:

snp1.3:1.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:2.1.verse: Those with close relationships have affection,

snp1.3:2.3.verse: Seeing this danger born of affection,

snp1.3:2.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:3.1.verse: When feelings for friends and loved ones

snp1.3:3.2.verse: are tied up in selfish love, you miss out on the goal.

snp1.3:3.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:4.1.verse: As a spreading bamboo gets entangled,

snp1.3:4.2.verse: so does concern for partners and children.

snp1.3:4.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:5.1.verse: As a wild deer loose in the forest

snp1.3:5.3.verse: a smart person looking for freedom would

snp1.3:5.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:6.1.verse: When among friends, whether staying in place

snp1.3:6.2.verse: or going on a journey, you’re always on call.

snp1.3:6.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:7.1.verse: Among friends you have fun and games,

snp1.3:7.2.verse: and for children you are full of fondness.

snp1.3:7.3.verse: Though loathe to depart from those you hold dear,

snp1.3:7.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:8.1.verse: At ease in any quarter, unresisting,

snp1.3:8.2.verse: content with whatever comes your way;

snp1.3:8.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:9.1.verse: Even some renunciates are hard to please,

snp1.3:9.2.verse: as are some layfolk dwelling at home.

snp1.3:9.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:10.1.verse: Having shed the marks of the home life,

snp1.3:10.2.verse: like the fallen leaves of the Shady Orchid Tree;

snp1.3:10.3.verse: having cut the bonds of the home life, a hero would

snp1.3:10.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:11.1.verse: If you find an alert companion,

snp1.3:11.2.verse: an attentive friend to live happily together,

snp1.3:11.4.verse: wander with them, joyful and mindful.

snp1.3:12.1.verse: If you find no alert companion,

snp1.3:12.2.verse: an attentive friend to live happily together,

snp1.3:12.3.verse: then, like a king who flees his conquered realm,

snp1.3:12.4.verse: wander alone like a tusker in the wilds.

snp1.3:13.1.verse: Clearly we praise the blessing of a friend,

snp1.3:13.2.verse: it’s good to be with friends your equal or better.

snp1.3:13.3.verse: But failing to find them, eating blamelessly,

snp1.3:13.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:14.1.verse: Though made of shining gold, well-finished by a smith,

snp1.3:14.2.verse: when two bracelets share the same arm

snp1.3:14.3.verse: they clash up against each other. Seeing this,

snp1.3:14.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:15.1.verse: Thinking, “So too, if I had a partner,

snp1.3:15.3.verse: Seeing this peril in the future,

snp1.3:15.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:16.1.verse: Sensual pleasures are diverse, sweet, delightful;

snp1.3:16.2.verse: appearing in disguise they disturb the mind.

snp1.3:16.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:17.1.verse: This is a calamity, a boil, a disaster,

snp1.3:17.2.verse: an illness, a dart, and a danger for me.

snp1.3:17.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:18.1.verse: Heat and cold, hunger and thirst,

snp1.3:18.2.verse: wind and sun, flies and reptiles:

snp1.3:18.3.verse: having put up with all these things,

snp1.3:18.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:19.1.verse: As a full-grown elephant, lotus-fond, magnificent,

snp1.3:19.3.verse: stays as it pleases in the forest,

snp1.3:19.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:20.1.verse: It’s impossible for one who delights in company

snp1.3:20.3.verse: Heeding the speech of the Kinsman of the Sun,

snp1.3:20.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:21.1.verse: Thinking, “I have left twisted views behind,

snp1.3:21.2.verse: reached the sure way, and gained the path;

snp1.3:21.3.verse: I’ve given rise to knowledge, and need no one to guide me”,

snp1.3:21.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:22.1.verse: No greed, no guile, no thirst, no slur,

snp1.3:22.2.verse: dross and delusion is smelted off;

snp1.3:22.3.verse: free of hoping for anything in the world,

snp1.3:22.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:23.2.verse: blind to the good, habitually immoral.

snp1.3:23.3.verse: Don’t befriend the heedless and the hankering, but

snp1.3:23.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:24.1.verse: Spend time with the learned who have memorized the teachings,

snp1.3:24.3.verse: When you understand the meanings and have dispelled doubt,

snp1.3:24.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:25.1.verse: When you realize that worldly fun and games

snp1.3:25.2.verse: and pleasure are inadequate, unconcerned with them,

snp1.3:25.3.verse: as one unadorned, a speaker of truth,

snp1.3:25.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:26.3.verse: having given up sensual pleasures to this extent,

snp1.3:26.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:27.1.verse: “This is a chain. Here there’s hardly any happiness,

snp1.3:27.2.verse: little gratification, and it’s full of drawbacks.

snp1.3:27.3.verse: It’s a hook.” Knowing this, a thoughtful person would

snp1.3:27.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:28.2.verse: like a fish that tears the net and swims free,

snp1.3:28.3.verse: or a fire not returning to ground it has burned,

snp1.3:28.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:29.3.verse: not festering or burning with desire,

snp1.3:29.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:30.1.verse: Having shed the marks of the home life,

snp1.3:30.2.verse: like the fallen leaves of the Orchid Tree,

snp1.3:30.3.verse: and gone forth in the ocher robe,

snp1.3:30.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:31.1.verse: Not wanton, nor rousing greed for tastes,

snp1.3:31.2.verse: providing for no other, wandering indiscriminately for alms,

snp1.3:31.3.verse: not attached to this family or that,

snp1.3:31.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:32.1.verse: When you’ve given up five mental obstacles,

snp1.3:32.3.verse: and cut off affection and hate, being independent,

snp1.3:32.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:33.1.verse: When you’ve put pleasure and pain behind you,

snp1.3:33.3.verse: and gained equanimity serene and pure,

snp1.3:33.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:34.1.verse: With energy roused to reach the ultimate goal,

snp1.3:34.2.verse: not sluggish in mind or lazy,

snp1.3:34.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:35.2.verse: always living in line with the teaching,

snp1.3:35.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:36.1.verse: One whose aim is the ending of craving—

snp1.3:36.3.verse: who has appraised the teaching and is assured, destined for awakening, should

snp1.3:36.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:37.1.verse: Like a lion not startled by sounds,

snp1.3:37.2.verse: like wind not caught in a net,

snp1.3:37.3.verse: like water not sticking to a lotus,

snp1.3:37.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:38.1.verse: Like the fierce-fanged lion, king of beasts,

snp1.3:38.2.verse: who wanders as conqueror and victor,

snp1.3:38.3.verse: you should frequent remote lodgings, and

snp1.3:38.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:39.3.verse: Not upset by anything in the world,

snp1.3:39.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:40.1.verse: Having given up greed, hate, and delusion,

snp1.3:40.3.verse: unafraid at the end of life,

snp1.3:40.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.3:41.1.verse: They befriend you and serve you for their own sake;

snp1.3:41.2.verse: these days it’s hard to find friends lacking ulterior motive.

snp1.3:41.4.verse: live alone like a horned rhino.

snp1.4:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying among the Magadhans in Dakkhiṇāgiri near the brahman village of Ekanāḷā.

snp1.4:1.3.verse: Now at that time approximately 500 of the brahman Kasi [Plowing] Bhāradvāja’s plows were yoked at the sowing time.

snp1.4:1.4.verse: Then, in the early morning, after adjusting his lower robe and carrying his bowl & outer robe, the Blessed One went to where Kasi Bhāradvāja was working.

snp1.4:1.5.verse: Now at that time Kasi Bhāradvāja’s food-distribution was underway.

snp1.4:1.6.verse: So the Blessed One went to Kasi Bhāradvāja’s food-distribution and, on arrival, stood to one side.

snp1.4:2.1.verse: Kasi Bhāradvāja saw the Blessed One standing for alms,

snp1.4:2.2.verse: and on seeing him, said to him,

snp1.4:2.3.verse: “I, contemplative, plow & sow. Having plowed & sown, I eat.

snp1.4:2.4.verse: You, too, contemplative, should plow & sow. Having plowed & sown, you (will) eat.”

snp1.4:3.1.verse: “I, too, brahman, plow & sow. Having plowed & sown, I eat.”

snp1.4:3.2.verse: “But, contemplative, we don’t see the Master Gotama’s yoke or plow, plowshare, goad, or oxen,

snp1.4:3.3.verse: and yet the Master Gotama says this:

snp1.4:3.4.verse: ‘I, too, brahman, plow & sow. Having plowed & sown, I eat.’”

snp1.4:4.1.verse: Then Kasi Bhāradvāja addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

snp1.4:5.2.verse: but we don’t see your plowing.

snp1.4:5.3.verse: Being asked, tell us about your plowing

snp1.4:5.4.verse: so that we may know your plowing.”

snp1.4:6.3.verse: shame my pole, mind my yoke-tie,

snp1.4:7.1.verse: Guarded in body, guarded in speech,

snp1.4:7.2.verse: restrained in terms of belly & food,

snp1.4:8.2.verse: bearing me toward rest from the yoke,

snp1.4:8.4.verse: to where, having gone, one doesn’t grieve.

snp1.4:9.1.verse: That’s how my plowing is plowed.

snp1.4:9.2.verse: It has as its fruit the deathless.

snp1.4:9.4.verse: one is unyoked from all suffering & stress.”

snp1.4:10.1.verse: Then Kasi Bhāradvāja, having heaped up milk-rice in a large bronze serving bowl, offered it to the Blessed One, [saying,]

snp1.4:10.4.verse: for the Master Gotama plows the plowing that has as its fruit the deathless.”

snp1.4:11.1.verse: “What’s been chanted over with verses shouldn’t be eaten by me.

snp1.4:11.2.verse: That’s not the nature, brahman, of one who’s seen rightly.

snp1.4:11.3.verse: What’s been chanted over with verses Awakened Ones reject.

snp1.4:11.4.verse: That being their Dhamma, brahman, this is their way of life.

snp1.4:12.2.verse: his effluents ended, his anxiety stilled—

snp1.4:12.3.verse: serve him with other food & drink,

snp1.4:12.4.verse: for that is the field for one looking for merit.”

snp1.4:13.1.verse: “Then to whom, Master Gotama, should I give this milk-rice?”

snp1.4:13.2.verse: “Brahman, I don’t see that person in this world—with its devas, Māras, & Brahmās, in this generation with its contemplatives & brahmans, its royalty & commonfolk—by whom this milk-rice, having been eaten, would be rightly digested, aside from a Tathāgata or a Tathāgata’s disciple.

snp1.4:13.3.verse: In that case, brahman, throw the milk-rice away in a place without vegetation, or dump it in water with no living beings.”

snp1.4:14.1.verse: So Kasi Bhāradvāja dumped the milk-rice in water with no living beings.

snp1.4:14.2.verse: And the milk-rice, when dropped in the water, hissed & sizzled, seethed & steamed.

snp1.4:14.3.verse: Just as an iron ball heated all day, when tossed in the water, hisses & sizzles, seethes & steams,

snp1.4:14.4.verse: in the same way the milk-rice, when dropped in the water, hissed & sizzled, seethed & steamed.

snp1.4:15.1.verse: Then Kasi Bhāradvāja—in awe, his hair standing on end—went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, throwing himself down with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, said to him,

snp1.4:15.3.verse: Just as if he were to place upright what was overturned, to reveal what was hidden, to show the way to one who was lost, or to carry a lamp into the dark so that those with eyes could see forms, in the same way has Master Gotama—through many lines of reasoning—made the Dhamma clear.

snp1.4:15.4.verse: I go to Master Gotama for refuge, to the Dhamma, & to the Saṅgha of monks. May Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward, for life.

snp1.4:15.5.verse: Let me obtain the Going-forth in Master Gotama’s presence, let me obtain Acceptance (into the Bhikkhu Saṅgha).”

snp1.4:16.1.verse: Then the brahman Kasi Bhāradvāja obtained the Going-forth in the Blessed One’s presence, he obtained Acceptance.

snp1.4:16.2.verse: And not long after his Acceptance—dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, & resolute—he in no long time reached & remained in the supreme goal of the holy life, for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness, knowing & realizing it for himself in the here-&-now.

snp1.4:16.3.verse: He knew: “Birth is ended, the holy life fulfilled, the task done. There is nothing further for the sake of this world.”

snp1.4:16.4.verse: And so Ven. Bhāradvāja became another one of the arahants.

snp1.4:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Magadhans in the Southern Hills near the brahmin village of Ekanāḷa.

snp1.4:1.3.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Farmer had harnessed around five hundred plows, it being the season for sowing.

snp1.4:1.4.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to where Bhāradvāja the Farmer was working.

snp1.4:1.5.verse: Now at that time Bhāradvāja the Farmer was distributing food.

snp1.4:1.6.verse: Then the Buddha went to where the distribution was taking place and stood to one side.

snp1.4:2.1.verse: Bhāradvāja the Farmer saw him standing for alms

snp1.4:2.3.verse: “I plough and sow, ascetic, and then I eat.

snp1.4:2.4.verse: You too should plough and sow, then you may eat.”

snp1.4:3.1.verse: “I too plough and sow, brahmin, and then I eat.”

snp1.4:3.2.verse: “I don’t see the worthy Gotama with a yoke or plow or plowshare or goad or oxen, yet he says:

snp1.4:3.4.verse: ‘I too plough and sow, brahmin, and then I eat.’”

snp1.4:4.1.verse: Then Bhāradvāja the Farmer addressed the Buddha in verse:

snp1.4:5.2.verse: but I don’t see you farming.

snp1.4:5.3.verse: Tell me your farming when asked,

snp1.4:5.4.verse: so I can recognize your farming.”

snp1.4:6.1.verse: “Faith is my seed, fervor my rain,

snp1.4:6.2.verse: and wisdom is my yoke and plough.

snp1.4:6.3.verse: Conscience is my draft-pole, mind my strap,

snp1.4:7.2.verse: I restrict my intake of food.

snp1.4:7.3.verse: I use truth as my scythe,

snp1.4:8.2.verse: transporting me to sanctuary from the yoke.

snp1.4:8.4.verse: to where there is no sorrow.

snp1.4:9.1.verse: That’s how to do the farming

snp1.4:9.2.verse: that has freedom from death as its fruit.

snp1.4:10.1.verse: Then Bhāradvāja the Farmer poured milk-rice in a large bronze cup and presented it to the Buddha:

snp1.4:10.2.verse: “May the worthy Gotama eat the milk-rice!

snp1.4:10.3.verse: The worthy one is a farmer.

snp1.4:10.4.verse: For the worthy Gotama does the farming that has freedom from death as its fruit.”

snp1.4:11.1.verse: “Food enchanted by a verse isn’t fit for me to eat.

snp1.4:11.2.verse: That’s not the principle of those who see, brahmin.

snp1.4:11.3.verse: The Buddhas cast aside things enchanted with verses.

snp1.4:11.4.verse: Since there is such a principle, brahmin, that’s how they live.

snp1.4:12.1.verse: Serve with other food and drink

snp1.4:12.2.verse: the consummate one, the great seer,

snp1.4:12.3.verse: with defilements ended and remorse stilled.

snp1.4:12.4.verse: For he is the field for the seeker of merit.”

snp1.4:13.1.verse: “Then, worthy Gotama, to whom should I give the milk-rice?”

snp1.4:13.2.verse: “Brahmin, I don’t see anyone in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—who can properly digest this milk-rice, except the Realized One or one of his disciples.

snp1.4:13.3.verse: Well then, brahmin, throw out the milk-rice where there is little that grows, or drop it into water that has no living creatures.”

snp1.4:14.1.verse: So Bhāradvāja the Farmer dropped the milk-rice in water that had no living creatures.

snp1.4:14.2.verse: And when the milk-rice was placed in the water, it sizzled and hissed, steaming and fuming.

snp1.4:14.3.verse: Suppose there was an iron cauldron that had been heated all day. If you placed it in the water, it would sizzle and hiss, steaming and fuming.

snp1.4:14.4.verse: In the same way, when the milk-rice was placed in the water, it sizzled and hissed, steaming and fuming.

snp1.4:15.1.verse: Then Bhāradvāja the Farmer, shocked and awestruck, went up to the Buddha, bowed down with his head to the Buddha’s feet, and said,

snp1.4:15.3.verse: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

snp1.4:15.4.verse: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

snp1.4:15.5.verse: May I receive the going forth, the ordination in the worthy Gotama’s presence?”

snp1.4:16.1.verse: And Bhāradvāja the Farmer received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

snp1.4:16.2.verse: Not long after his ordination, Venerable Bhāradvāja, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

snp1.4:16.3.verse: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

snp1.4:16.4.verse: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.

snp1.5:1.1.verse: “I ask the sage of abundant discernment,

snp1.5:1.3.verse: awakened, lord of the Dhamma, free of craving,

snp1.5:1.4.verse: supreme among two-legged beings, best of charioteers:

snp1.5:1.5.verse: How many contemplatives are there in the world? Please tell me.”

snp1.5:2.3.verse: Being asked in person, I disclose them to you:

snp1.5:2.5.verse: one who lives by the path, and the path-corrupter.”

snp1.5:3.1.verse: “Whom do the awakened call the path-victor?

snp1.5:3.3.verse: How is one unequaled in pointing out the path?

snp1.5:3.4.verse: When asked, tell me about the one who lives by the path.

snp1.5:3.5.verse: Then disclose the path-corrupter to me.”

snp1.5:4.2.verse: is refreshed in unbinding, devoid of greed,

snp1.5:4.3.verse: a guide to the world along with its devas:

snp1.5:4.4.verse: The awakened call such a person path-victor.

snp1.5:5.1.verse: Whoever here knowing the foremost as foremost,

snp1.5:5.2.verse: who points out, who analyzes the Dhamma right here,

snp1.5:5.3.verse: he, the cutter of doubt, the sage unperturbed,

snp1.5:5.4.verse: is called the second of monks: path-explainer.

snp1.5:6.2.verse: lives by the path, restrained, mindful,

snp1.5:6.4.verse: is called the third of monks: with the path as his life.

snp1.5:7.1.verse: Making a façade of good practices,

snp1.5:7.2.verse: brash, reckless, a corrupter of families,

snp1.5:7.4.verse: & going about as a counterfeit: he is a path-corrupter.

snp1.5:8.1.verse: And when any householder understands these,

snp1.5:8.2.verse: —an instructed disciple of the noble ones, discerning—

snp1.5:8.3.verse: knowing, ‘Not all are like that one,’

snp1.5:8.4.verse: seeing one like that doesn’t kill his conviction.

snp1.5:8.5.verse: For how would one equate the corrupt with the uncorrupt,

snp1.5:1.1.verse: “I ask the sage abounding in wisdom,”

snp1.5:1.3.verse: “the Buddha, master of the teaching, free of craving,

snp1.5:1.4.verse: best of men, excellent charioteer, please tell me this:

snp1.5:1.5.verse: how many ascetics are there in the world?”

snp1.5:2.1.verse: “There are four ascetics, not a fifth.”

snp1.5:2.3.verse: “Being asked to bear witness, I will explain them to you:

snp1.5:3.1.verse: “Who is a path-victor according to the Buddhas?”

snp1.5:3.3.verse: “and how is one an unequaled explainer of the path?

snp1.5:3.4.verse: Tell me when asked about one who lives the path,

snp1.5:4.3.verse: a guide for the world with its gods.

snp1.5:4.4.verse: The Buddhas say one such is victor of the path.

snp1.5:5.2.verse: they explain and analyze the teaching right here.

snp1.5:5.3.verse: That sage unstirred, with doubt cut off,

snp1.5:5.4.verse: is the second mendicant, I say, the teacher of the path.

snp1.5:6.1.verse: Living restrained and mindful on the path

snp1.5:6.2.verse: of the well-taught passage of teaching,

snp1.5:6.4.verse: is the third mendicant, I say, the path-liver.

snp1.5:7.1.verse: Dressed like one true to their vows,

snp1.5:7.2.verse: pushy, rude, a corrupter of families,

snp1.5:7.4.verse: the path-wrecker’s life is a sham.

snp1.5:8.3.verse: knows that ‘They are not all like that one’.

snp1.5:8.4.verse: So when they see them they don’t lose their faith.

snp1.5:8.5.verse: For how could one equate them—

snp1.5:8.6.verse: the corrupt with the uncorrupt, the pure with the impure?”

snp1.6:1.2.verse: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.

snp1.6:1.3.verse: Then a certain god, towards the end of the night, whose surpassing beauty lit up the whole of Jeta’s Wood, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he stood on one side.

snp1.6:1.4.verse: While standing on one side that god recited a verse to the Fortunate One:

snp1.6:2.2.verse: regarding the man going to ruin -

snp1.6:2.3.verse: we have come to ask the Fortunate One,

snp1.6:2.4.verse: what is the cause of ruination?”

snp1.6:3.1.verse: “The thriving man is easy to know,

snp1.6:3.2.verse: the ruining man is easy to know,

snp1.6:3.3.verse: the thriving man loves the Dhamma,

snp1.6:3.4.verse: the ruining man hates the Dhamma.”

snp1.6:4.1.verse: “Indeed it is so, this we know,

snp1.6:4.2.verse: this is the first ruin (of man).

snp1.6:4.4.verse: what is the second cause of ruin?”

snp1.6:5.2.verse: he does not endear the good,

snp1.6:5.3.verse: he is pleased with the Dhamma of the bad,

snp1.6:5.4.verse: that is a cause of ruination.”

snp1.6:6.1.verse: “Indeed it is so, this we know,

snp1.6:6.2.verse: this is the second ruin (of man).

snp1.6:6.4.verse: what is the third cause of ruin?”

snp1.6:7.1.verse: “That man who is fond of sleep, fond of society,

snp1.6:7.4.verse: that is a cause of ruination.”

snp1.6:8.1.verse: “Indeed it is so, this we know,

snp1.6:8.2.verse: this is the third ruin (of man).

snp1.6:8.4.verse: what is the fourth cause of ruin?”

snp1.6:9.1.verse: “He who, when his mother or father has grown old,

snp1.6:9.3.verse: though having much, does not support them,

snp1.6:9.4.verse: that is a cause of ruination.”

snp1.6:10.1.verse: “Indeed it is so, this we know,

snp1.6:10.2.verse: this is the fourth ruin (of man).

snp1.6:10.4.verse: what is the fifth cause of ruin?”

snp1.6:11.1.verse: ° “He who deceives a brahmin, or an ascetic,

snp1.6:11.4.verse: that is a cause of ruination.”

snp1.6:12.1.verse: “Indeed it is so, this we know,

snp1.6:12.2.verse: this is the fifth ruin (of man).

snp1.6:12.4.verse: what is the sixth cause of ruin?”

snp1.6:13.2.verse: who has gold, who has food,

snp1.6:13.3.verse: but who eats his sweetmeats alone,

snp1.6:13.4.verse: that is a cause of ruination.”

snp1.6:14.1.verse: “Indeed it is so, this we know,

snp1.6:14.2.verse: this is the sixth ruin (of man).

snp1.6:14.4.verse: what is the seventh cause of ruin?”

snp1.6:15.1.verse: “That man who is proud of his birth,

snp1.6:15.4.verse: that is a cause of ruination.”

snp1.6:16.1.verse: “Indeed it is so, this we know,

snp1.6:16.2.verse: this is the seventh ruin (of man).

snp1.6:16.4.verse: what is the eighth cause of ruin?”

snp1.6:17.4.verse: that is a cause of ruination.”

snp1.6:18.1.verse: “Indeed it is so, this we know,

snp1.6:18.2.verse: this is the eighth ruin (of man).

snp1.6:18.4.verse: what is the ninth cause of ruin?”

snp1.6:19.1.verse: “(He who is) not satisfied with his own wives,

snp1.6:19.3.verse: and is seen with other mens’ wives,

snp1.6:19.4.verse: that is a cause of ruination.”

snp1.6:20.1.verse: “Indeed it is so, this we know,

snp1.6:20.2.verse: this is the ninth ruin (of man).

snp1.6:20.4.verse: what is the tenth cause of ruin?”

snp1.6:21.1.verse: “A man who, being past his youth,

snp1.6:21.2.verse: brings home a young girl (for his wife),

snp1.6:21.4.verse: that is a cause of ruination.”

snp1.6:22.1.verse: “Indeed it is so, this we know,

snp1.6:22.2.verse: this is the tenth ruin (of man).

snp1.6:22.4.verse: what is the eleventh cause of ruin?”

snp1.6:23.1.verse: “A woman given to drink, a spendthrift,

snp1.6:23.2.verse: or a man of similar sort,

snp1.6:23.4.verse: that is a cause of ruination.”

snp1.6:24.1.verse: “Indeed it is so, this we know,

snp1.6:24.2.verse: this is the eleventh ruin (of man).

snp1.6:24.4.verse: what is the twelfth cause of ruin?”

snp1.6:25.1.verse: “One who is poor, but has great craving,

snp1.6:25.2.verse: who is born in a family of nobles,

snp1.6:25.3.verse: and who wants to be king,

snp1.6:25.4.verse: that is a cause of ruination.

snp1.6:26.1.verse: The wise man who reflects on (the cause of) these ruins

snp1.6:26.3.verse: a noble one, endowed with insight,

snp1.6:1.2.verse: at one time the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

snp1.6:1.3.verse: Then a certain deva, in the far extreme of the night, her extreme radiance lighting up the entirety of Jeta’s Grove, went to the Blessed One. On arrival, having bowed down to him, she stood to one side.

snp1.6:1.4.verse: As she was standing there, she addressed him with a verse:

snp1.6:2.3.verse: having come to question the Blessed One:

snp1.6:2.4.verse: What is the way leading to decline?”

snp1.6:3.1.verse: “Easily known is the one of good prospects;

snp1.6:3.2.verse: easily known,1 the one in decline.

snp1.6:3.3.verse: The one of good prospects loves the Dhamma,

snp1.6:3.4.verse: the one in decline detests it.”

snp1.6:4.1.verse: “We know, indeed, that that is so.

snp1.6:4.2.verse: That’s the first one in decline.

snp1.6:4.3.verse: May the Blessed One tell the second:

snp1.6:4.4.verse: What is the way leading to decline?”

snp1.6:5.2.verse: the good he doesn’t hold dear.

snp1.6:5.3.verse: He approves of the ideas of the wicked:

snp1.6:5.4.verse: That is the way leading to decline.”

snp1.6:6.1.verse: “We know, indeed, that that is so.

snp1.6:6.2.verse: That’s the second one in decline.

snp1.6:6.3.verse: May the Blessed One tell the third:

snp1.6:6.4.verse: What is the way leading to decline?”

snp1.6:7.4.verse: That is the way leading to decline.”

snp1.6:8.1.verse: “We know, indeed, that that is so.

snp1.6:8.2.verse: That’s the third one in decline.

snp1.6:8.3.verse: May the Blessed One tell the fourth:

snp1.6:8.4.verse: What is the way leading to decline?”

snp1.6:9.3.verse: though capable, one doesn’t support them:

snp1.6:9.4.verse: That is the way leading to decline.”

snp1.6:10.1.verse: “We know, indeed, that that is so.

snp1.6:10.2.verse: That’s the fourth one in decline.

snp1.6:10.3.verse: May the Blessed One tell the fifth:

snp1.6:10.4.verse: What is the way leading to decline?”

snp1.6:11.3.verse: whoever deceives them with a lie:

snp1.6:11.4.verse: That is the way leading to decline.”

snp1.6:12.1.verse: “We know, indeed, that that is so.

snp1.6:12.2.verse: That’s the fifth one in decline.

snp1.6:12.3.verse: May the Blessed One tell the sixth:

snp1.6:12.4.verse: What is the way leading to decline?”

snp1.6:13.4.verse: That is the way leading to decline.”

snp1.6:14.1.verse: “We know, indeed, that that is so.

snp1.6:14.2.verse: That’s the sixth one in decline.

snp1.6:14.3.verse: May the Blessed One tell the seventh:

snp1.6:14.4.verse: What is the way leading to decline?”

snp1.6:15.1.verse: “The man proud of his birth, proud of his wealth,

snp1.6:15.4.verse: That is the way leading to decline.”

snp1.6:16.1.verse: “We know, indeed, that that is so.

snp1.6:16.2.verse: That’s the seventh one in decline.

snp1.6:16.3.verse: May the Blessed One tell the eighth:

snp1.6:16.4.verse: What is the way leading to decline?”

snp1.6:17.1.verse: “The man debauched with women, debauched in drink,

snp1.6:17.4.verse: That is the way leading to decline.”

snp1.6:18.1.verse: “We know, indeed, that that is so.

snp1.6:18.2.verse: That’s the eighth one in decline.

snp1.6:18.3.verse: May the Blessed One tell the ninth:

snp1.6:18.4.verse: What is the way leading to decline?”

snp1.6:19.4.verse: That is the way leading to decline.”

snp1.6:20.1.verse: “We know, indeed, that that is so.

snp1.6:20.2.verse: That’s the ninth one in decline.

snp1.6:20.3.verse: May the Blessed One tell the tenth:

snp1.6:20.4.verse: What is the way leading to decline?”

snp1.6:21.2.verse: a man takes a young woman with timbara-fruit breasts,

snp1.6:21.3.verse: and, jealous of her, doesn’t sleep:

snp1.6:21.4.verse: That is the way leading to decline.”

snp1.6:22.1.verse: “We know, indeed, that that is so.

snp1.6:22.2.verse: That’s the tenth one in decline.

snp1.6:22.3.verse: May the Blessed One tell the eleventh:

snp1.6:22.4.verse: What is the way leading to decline?”

snp1.6:23.2.verse: or a man of that sort—

snp1.6:23.4.verse: That is the way leading to decline.”

snp1.6:24.1.verse: “We know, indeed, that that is so.

snp1.6:24.2.verse: That’s the eleventh one in decline.

snp1.6:24.3.verse: May the Blessed One tell the twelfth:

snp1.6:24.4.verse: What is the way leading to decline?”

snp1.6:25.1.verse: “One of meager means but great craving,

snp1.6:25.4.verse: That is the way leading to decline.

snp1.6:26.1.verse: These ones in decline in the world,

snp1.6:26.5.verse: The Discourse on Decline, the sixth.

snp1.6:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

snp1.6:1.3.verse: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side.

snp1.6:1.4.verse: Standing to one side, that deity addressed the Buddha in verse:

snp1.6:2.3.verse: We have come to ask you, sir:

snp1.6:3.2.verse: understanding downfall is just as easy.

snp1.6:3.3.verse: One who loves the teaching succeeds,

snp1.6:3.4.verse: but a hater of the teaching meets their downfall.”

snp1.6:4.3.verse: Tell us the second, Blessed One:

snp1.6:5.2.verse: he has no love for the good.

snp1.6:5.3.verse: He believes the teaching of the bad;

snp1.6:5.4.verse: and that leads to his downfall.”

snp1.6:6.3.verse: Tell us the third, Blessed One:

snp1.6:7.2.verse: a man who does no work;

snp1.6:7.4.verse: and that leads to his downfall.”

snp1.6:8.3.verse: Tell us the fourth, Blessed One:

snp1.6:9.1.verse: “Though able, he does not look after

snp1.6:9.4.verse: and that leads to his downfall.”

snp1.6:10.3.verse: Tell us the fifth, Blessed One:

snp1.6:11.4.verse: and that leads to his downfall.”

snp1.6:12.3.verse: Tell us the sixth, Blessed One:

snp1.6:13.4.verse: and that leads to his downfall.”

snp1.6:14.3.verse: Tell us the seventh, Blessed One:

snp1.6:15.3.verse: looks down on his own family,

snp1.6:15.4.verse: and that leads to his downfall.”

snp1.6:16.3.verse: Tell us the eighth, Blessed One:

snp1.6:17.3.verse: wastes all that he has earned,

snp1.6:17.4.verse: and that leads to his downfall.”

snp1.6:18.3.verse: Tell us the ninth, Blessed One:

snp1.6:19.4.verse: and that leads to his downfall.”

snp1.6:20.3.verse: Tell us the tenth, Blessed One:

snp1.6:21.2.verse: marries a girl with budding breasts;

snp1.6:21.4.verse: and that leads to his downfall.”

snp1.6:22.3.verse: Tell us the eleventh, Blessed One:

snp1.6:23.3.verse: who’s a drunkard and a wastrel,

snp1.6:23.4.verse: and that leads to his downfall.”

snp1.6:24.3.verse: Tell us the twelfth, Blessed One:

snp1.6:25.1.verse: “A man of little wealth and strong craving,

snp1.6:25.4.verse: and that leads to his downfall.

snp1.6:26.1.verse: Seeing these downfalls in the world,

snp1.6:26.4.verse: will enjoy a world of grace.”

snp1.7:1.2.verse: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.

snp1.7:1.3.verse: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

snp1.7:1.4.verse: Then at that time in the brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja’s residence the (sacrificial) fire was burning, and the offering had been taken up.

snp1.7:1.5.verse: Then, as the Fortunate One was going from house to house for alms in Sāvatthī, he approached the brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja’s residence.

snp1.7:2.1.verse: The brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja saw the Fortunate One coming from afar,

snp1.7:2.2.verse: and having seen him, he said this to the Fortunate One:

snp1.7:3.1.verse: After this was said, the Fortunate One said this to the brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja:

snp1.7:3.2.verse: “But do you know, brahmin, what an outcaste is, or what things make one an outcaste?”

snp1.7:3.3.verse: “I certainly do not know, reverend Gotama, what an outcaste is, or what things make one an outcaste.

snp1.7:3.4.verse: It would be good for me if the reverend Gotama would preach the Dhamma so that I may know what an outcaste is, and what things make one an outcaste.”

snp1.7:3.5.verse: “Then listen, brahmin, apply your mind well, and I will speak.”

snp1.7:3.6.verse: “Yes, reverend,” the brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja replied to the Fortunate One,

snp1.7:3.7.verse: and the Fortunate One said this:

snp1.7:4.1.verse: “That man who is angry, who has enmity,

snp1.7:4.3.verse: who has wrong views, and is deceitful,

snp1.7:4.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:5.1.verse: Whether once born, or twice born,

snp1.7:5.2.verse: he who is violent to creatures here,

snp1.7:5.3.verse: who has no sympathy with creatures,

snp1.7:5.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:6.3.verse: who is well known as an oppressor,

snp1.7:6.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:7.1.verse: ° (He who), whether in the village or the wilderness,

snp1.7:7.2.verse: takes by theft what is not given,

snp1.7:7.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:8.1.verse: He who has taken on a debt,

snp1.7:8.2.verse: and when pressed (to pay it) runs away,

snp1.7:8.3.verse: saying: “There is no debt due to you,”

snp1.7:8.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:9.3.verse: along the path, takes that trifle,

snp1.7:9.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:10.1.verse: That man who, for his own sake,

snp1.7:10.2.verse: for the sake of others, or for wealth,

snp1.7:10.3.verse: when asked to bear witness, speaks falsely,

snp1.7:10.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:11.2.verse: with the wives of friends or relatives,

snp1.7:11.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:12.1.verse: He who, when his mother or father has grown old,

snp1.7:12.3.verse: though having much, does not support them,

snp1.7:12.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:13.1.verse: ° He who strikes, or annoys with words,

snp1.7:13.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:14.1.verse: He who, when he is asked what is good,

snp1.7:14.2.verse: teaches that which is not good,

snp1.7:14.3.verse: who conceals things when he gives advice,

snp1.7:14.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:15.1.verse: He who, having done a bad deed,

snp1.7:15.2.verse: longs thus: “May they not know about me,”

snp1.7:15.3.verse: he who conceals what he is doing,

snp1.7:15.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:16.1.verse: He who, having gone to another’s family,

snp1.7:16.3.verse: does not return the honour when (his benefactor) comes,

snp1.7:16.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:17.1.verse: ° He who deceives a brahmin, or an ascetic,

snp1.7:17.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:18.1.verse: ° He who annoys with words a brahmin, or an ascetic,

snp1.7:18.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:19.1.verse: He who speaks to those who are bad here,

snp1.7:19.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:20.3.verse: who is debased through his own conceit,

snp1.7:20.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:21.2.verse: who has bad longings, is selfish, crafty,

snp1.7:21.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:22.2.verse: or else one of his disciples,

snp1.7:22.4.verse: he one should know as an outcaste.

snp1.7:23.1.verse: He who, not being a Worthy One

snp1.7:23.2.verse: claims that he is a Worthy One,

snp1.7:23.3.verse: is a thief in the world with its brahmās,

snp1.7:23.4.verse: he is the worst of the outcastes.

snp1.7:23.5.verse: These, indeed, are said to be outcastes,

snp1.7:23.6.verse: those whom I have explained to you.

snp1.7:24.1.verse: One is not an outcaste by birth,

snp1.7:24.2.verse: by birth one is not a brahmin,

snp1.7:24.3.verse: by deeds one becomes an outcaste,

snp1.7:24.4.verse: one becomes a brahmin by deeds.

snp1.7:25.1.verse: You can know it also by this,

snp1.7:26.1.verse: This Mātaṅga attained the highest repute,

snp1.7:26.2.verse: which was very hard to obtain,

snp1.7:27.1.verse: He ascended the way going to the gods,

snp1.7:27.3.verse: and having put away sensual desire,

snp1.7:27.4.verse: he went to the brahma worlds.

snp1.7:27.6.verse: from being reborn in the brahma worlds.

snp1.7:28.1.verse: Brahmins, though born in a family of scholars,

snp1.7:29.2.verse: in the next life they have an unhappy destiny.

snp1.7:30.1.verse: One is not an outcaste by birth,

snp1.7:30.2.verse: by birth one is not a brahmin,

snp1.7:30.3.verse: by deeds one becomes an outcaste,

snp1.7:30.4.verse: one becomes a brahmin by deeds.”

snp1.7:31.1.verse: After this was said, the brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja said this to the Fortunate One:

snp1.7:31.3.verse: Please bear it in mind, reverend Gotama, that I am a lay disciple who has gone for refuge from today forward for as long as I have the breath of life.”

snp1.7:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

snp1.7:1.3.verse: Then, in the early morning, after adjusting his lower robe and carrying his bowl & outer robe, he entered Sāvatthī for alms.

snp1.7:1.4.verse: Now at that time, in the house of the brahman Aggika Bhāradvāja, a (sacrificial) fire was burning and an offering was lifted up.

snp1.7:1.5.verse: Then the Blessed One, going through Sāvatthī on a methodical almsround,1 approached the house of Aggika Bhāradvāja.

snp1.7:2.1.verse: Aggika Bhāradvāja saw the Blessed One coming from afar

snp1.7:2.2.verse: and, on seeing him, said to him:

snp1.7:3.1.verse: When this was said, the Blessed One said to the brahman Aggika Bhāradvāja,

snp1.7:3.2.verse: “But do you know, brahman, what an outcaste is, or the actions that make one an outcaste?”

snp1.7:3.3.verse: “No, in fact, Master Gotama, I don’t know what an outcaste is, or the actions that make one an outcaste.

snp1.7:3.4.verse: It would be good if Master Gotama taught me the Dhamma so that I would know what an outcaste is and the actions that make one an outcaste.”

snp1.7:3.5.verse: “In that case, brahman, listen and pay close attention. I will speak.”

snp1.7:3.6.verse: “As you say, master,” the brahman Aggika Bhāradvāja responded to the Blessed One.

snp1.7:4.3.verse: deceitful, and defective in his views:

snp1.7:5.2.verse: whoever here harms a living being,

snp1.7:5.3.verse: who has no sympathy for a living being:

snp1.7:7.3.verse: takes in a manner of theft:

snp1.7:9.2.verse: strikes a person going along a road,

snp1.7:10.1.verse: Whatever man, for his own sake, the sake of another,

snp1.7:10.3.verse: tells a lie when asked to bear witness:

snp1.7:11.1.verse: Whoever, with the wives of relatives or friends,

snp1.7:11.3.verse: by force or with their consent:

snp1.7:13.3.verse: and reviles them with his speech:

snp1.7:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

snp1.7:3.5.verse: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

snp1.7:3.6.verse: “Yes, worthy sir,” Bhāradvāja the Fire-Worshiper replied.

snp1.8:1.1.verse: What should be done by one skilled in goodness,

snp1.10:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Āḷavī in the haunt of the Āḷavaka yakkha.

snp1.10:1.3.verse: Then the Āḷavaka yakkha went to the Blessed One and on arrival said to him:

snp1.10:1.5.verse: [Saying,] “All right, my friend,” the Blessed One went out.

snp1.10:1.7.verse: “All right, my friend,” the Blessed One went in.

snp1.10:2.2.verse: A third time, the Āḷavaka yakkha said to the Blessed One,

snp1.10:2.4.verse: “All right, my friend,” the Blessed One went out.

snp1.10:2.6.verse: “All right, my friend,” the Blessed One went in.

snp1.10:3.1.verse: Then a fourth time, the Āḷavaka yakkha said to the Blessed One,

snp1.10:3.4.verse: Do what you have to do.”

snp1.10:4.1.verse: “I will ask you a question, contemplative.

snp1.10:4.2.verse: If you can’t answer me, I will hurl out your mind or rip open your heart or, grabbing you by the feet, hurl you across the Ganges.”

snp1.10:5.1.verse: “My friend, I see no one in the cosmos with its devas, Māras, & Brahmās, in this generation with its contemplatives & brahmans, its royalty & commonfolk, who could hurl out my mind or rip open my heart or, grabbing me by the feet, hurl me across the Ganges.

snp1.10:5.2.verse: But nevertheless, ask me what you wish.”

snp1.10:5.3.verse: Then the Āḷavaka yakkha addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

snp1.10:6.1.verse: “What is a person’s highest wealth here?

snp1.10:7.4.verse: Living with discernment, one’s life is called best.”

snp1.10:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Āḷavī in the haunt of the native spirit Āḷavaka.

snp1.10:1.3.verse: Then the native spirit Āḷavaka went up to the Buddha, and said to him:

snp1.10:1.5.verse: Saying, “All right, respectable sir,” the Buddha went out.

snp1.10:1.7.verse: Saying, “All right, respectable sir,” the Buddha went in.

snp1.10:2.2.verse: And for a third time the native spirit Āḷavaka said to the Buddha,

snp1.10:2.4.verse: Saying, “All right, respectable sir,” the Buddha went out.

snp1.10:2.6.verse: Saying, “All right, respectable sir,” the Buddha went in.

snp1.10:3.1.verse: And for a fourth time the native spirit Āḷavaka said to the Buddha,

snp1.10:3.3.verse: “No, respectable sir, I won’t get out.

snp1.10:4.1.verse: “I will ask you a question, ascetic.

snp1.10:4.2.verse: If you don’t answer me, I’ll drive you insane, or explode your heart, or grab you by the feet and throw you to the far shore of the Ganges!”

snp1.10:5.1.verse: “I don’t see anyone in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans who could do that to me.

snp1.10:5.2.verse: But anyway, ask what you wish.”

snp1.10:5.3.verse: Then the native spirit Āḷavaka addressed the Buddha in verse:

snp1.10:6.2.verse: What brings happiness when practiced well?

snp1.10:6.3.verse: What’s the sweetest taste of all?

snp1.10:6.4.verse: The one they say has the best life: how do they live?”

snp1.10:7.1.verse: “Faith here is a person’s best wealth.

snp1.10:7.2.verse: The teaching brings happiness when practiced well.

snp1.10:7.3.verse: Truth is the sweetest taste of all.

snp1.10:7.4.verse: The one they say has the best life lives by wisdom.”

snp1.10:10.6.verse: when passing from this world to the next?”
