snp1.10:14.1.verse: Go ahead, ask others as well,

snp1.10:14.2.verse: there are many ascetics and brahmins.

snp1.10:14.3.verse: See whether anything better is found

snp1.10:14.4.verse: than truth, principle, generosity, and patience.”

snp1.10:15.4.verse: what’s good for lives to come.

snp1.10:16.1.verse: It was truly for my benefit

snp1.10:16.2.verse: that the Buddha came to stay at Āḷavī.

snp1.10:16.4.verse: where a gift is very fruitful.

snp1.10:17.2.verse: village to village, town to town,

snp1.10:17.4.verse: and the clear rightness of the teaching!”

snp1.11:2.4.verse: the body isn’t seen for what it is:

snp1.11:3.1.verse: filled with intestines, filled with stomach,

snp1.11:3.2.verse: with the lump of the liver, & bladder,

snp1.11:5.1.verse: On top of that, in nine streams,

snp1.11:5.2.verse: filth is always flowing from it:

snp1.11:6.2.verse: from the mouth it vomits—now vomit,

snp1.11:6.4.verse: from the body, beads of sweat.

snp1.11:7.1.verse: And on top of that, its hollow head

snp1.11:8.3.verse: cast away in a charnel ground,

snp1.11:8.4.verse: even relatives don’t care for it.

snp1.11:9.4.verse: along with any other animals there.

snp1.11:10.1.verse: Having heard the Awakened One’s words,

snp1.11:11.1.verse: As this is, so is that.

snp1.11:11.4.verse: he should let desire for the body fade away.

snp1.11:12.4.verse: the unfallen, undying1 state of unbinding.

snp1.11:14.1.verse: On the basis of a body like this,

snp1.11:14.2.verse: whoever would think to exalt himself

snp1.11:14.4.verse: what is that if not blindness?

snp1.11:14.5.verse: The Discourse on Victory, the eleventh.

snp1.11:0.2.verse: Victory Over Desire for the Body

snp1.11:1.4.verse: these are the movements of the body.

snp1.11:2.1.verse: Linked together by bones and sinews,

snp1.11:2.2.verse: plastered over with flesh and hide,

snp1.11:2.4.verse: the body is not seen as it is.

snp1.11:3.1.verse: It’s full of guts and belly,

snp1.11:5.3.verse: There is muck from the eyes,

snp1.11:6.4.verse: And from the body, sweat and waste.

snp1.11:7.1.verse: Then there is the hollow head

snp1.11:9.3.verse: It’s devoured by crows and vultures,

snp1.11:10.4.verse: for they see it as it is.

snp1.11:11.2.verse: as that is, so is this.”

snp1.11:11.3.verse: They’d blanch desire for the body

snp1.11:12.3.verse: has found the peace free of death,

snp1.11:12.4.verse: extinguishment, the state that does not pass.

snp1.11:13.1.verse: This two-legged body is dirty and stinking,

snp1.11:13.3.verse: and oozing all over the place—

snp1.11:14.1.verse: And if, on account of such a body,

snp1.11:14.4.verse: what is that but a failure to see?

snp1.12:1.2.verse: a home gives birth to dust.2

snp1.12:1.3.verse: Free from a home, free from intimacy:

snp1.12:1.4.verse: Such is the vision of the sage.3

snp1.12:2.1.verse: Who, destroying what’s born, wouldn’t plant (again)

snp1.12:2.3.verse: They call him the wandering, solitary sage.

snp1.12:2.4.verse: He, the great seer, has seen the state of peace.

snp1.12:3.1.verse: Considering the ground, crushing the seed,

snp1.12:3.3.verse: —truly a sage— seer of the ending of birth,

snp1.12:3.4.verse: abandoning conjecture, he cannot be classified.

snp1.12:4.2.verse: not longing for any one anywhere

snp1.12:4.3.verse: —truly a sage— with no coveting, without greed,

snp1.12:4.4.verse: he does not build,6 for he has gone beyond.

snp1.12:5.2.verse: with regard to all things: unsmeared,

snp1.12:5.3.verse: abandoning all, in the ending of craving, released:

snp1.12:5.4.verse: The enlightened call him a sage.

snp1.12:6.1.verse: With discernment his strength, well-endowed in habit & practice,

snp1.12:6.3.verse: released from attachments, free from rigidity, free from effluent7:

snp1.12:6.4.verse: The enlightened call him a sage.

snp1.12:7.3.verse: unstartled, like a lion at sounds,

snp1.12:7.4.verse: uncaught, like the wind in a net,

snp1.12:7.5.verse: unsmeared, like a lotus in water,8

snp1.12:7.6.verse: leader of others, by others unled:

snp1.12:7.7.verse: The enlightened call him a sage.

snp1.12:8.1.verse: Who becomes like the pillar at a bathing ford,9

snp1.12:8.3.verse: he, without passion, his senses well-centered:

snp1.12:8.4.verse: The enlightened call him a sage.

snp1.12:9.1.verse: Truly poised, straight as a shuttle,10

snp1.12:9.4.verse: The enlightened call him a sage.

snp1.12:10.1.verse: Restrained in mind, he does no evil.

snp1.12:10.4.verse: The enlightened call him a sage.

snp1.12:11.1.verse: From the best, the middling, the leftovers,

snp1.12:11.2.verse: he receives alms, sustaining himself on what others give,

snp1.12:11.4.verse: The enlightened call him a sage.

snp1.12:12.1.verse: The wandering sage abstaining from sex,

snp1.12:12.2.verse: in youth bound by no one,

snp1.12:12.3.verse: abstaining from intoxication12 & complacency, totally apart:

snp1.12:12.4.verse: The enlightened call him a sage.

snp1.12:13.1.verse: Knowing the world, seeing the highest goal,

snp1.12:13.3.verse: his chains broken, unattached, without effluent:

snp1.12:13.4.verse: The enlightened call him a sage.

snp1.12:14.1.verse: These two are different, they dwell far apart:

snp1.12:14.2.verse: the householder supporting a wife and the unselfish one, of good practices.

snp1.12:14.3.verse: Slaying other beings, the householder is unrestrained.

snp1.12:14.4.verse: Constantly the sage protects other beings, is controlled.

snp1.12:15.1.verse: Just as the crested, blue-necked peacock,

snp1.12:15.2.verse: when flying, never matches the wild goose in speed,

snp1.12:15.3.verse: even so the householder never keeps up with the monk—

snp1.12:15.4.verse: the sage secluded in the forest, doing jhāna.

snp1.12:15.5.verse: The Discourse on the Sage, the twelfth.

snp1.12:16.2.verse: the Rhinoceros Horn, and Kasi Bhāradvāja,

snp1.12:16.4.verse: the Outcaste, and the Development of Goodwill.

snp1.12:2.1.verse: Having cut down what’s grown, they wouldn’t replant,

snp1.12:2.2.verse: nor would they nurture what’s growing.

snp1.12:2.3.verse: That’s who they call a sage wandering alone,

snp1.12:2.4.verse: the great seer has seen the state of peace.

snp1.12:3.1.verse: Having appraised the fields and measured the seeds,

snp1.12:3.2.verse: they wouldn’t nurture them with moisture.

snp1.12:3.3.verse: Truly that sage who sees the ending of rebirth

snp1.12:3.4.verse: has left speculation behind and is beyond reckoning.

snp1.12:4.1.verse: Understanding all the planes of rebirth,

snp1.12:4.2.verse: not wanting a single one of them;

snp1.12:4.3.verse: truly that sage freed of greed

snp1.12:4.4.verse: need not swim, for they have reached the far shore.

snp1.12:5.1.verse: The vanquisher of all, knower of all, so very intelligent,

snp1.12:5.2.verse: unsullied in the midst of all things,

snp1.12:5.3.verse: has given up all, freed in the ending of craving:

snp1.12:5.4.verse: that’s who the attentive know as a sage.

snp1.12:6.1.verse: Strong in wisdom, with precepts and observances intact,

snp1.12:6.4.verse: that’s who the attentive know as a sage.

snp1.12:7.2.verse: is unshaken by blame and praise—

snp1.12:7.3.verse: like a lion not startled by sounds,

snp1.12:7.4.verse: like wind not caught in a net,

snp1.12:7.5.verse: like water not sticking to a lotus.

snp1.12:7.6.verse: Leader of others, not by others led:

snp1.12:7.7.verse: that’s who the attentive know as a sage.

snp1.12:8.1.verse: Steady as a post in a bathing-place

snp1.12:8.2.verse: when others speak endlessly against them,

snp1.12:8.3.verse: freed of greed, with senses stilled:

snp1.12:8.4.verse: that’s who the attentive know as a sage.

snp1.12:9.3.verse: discerning the just and the unjust:

snp1.12:9.4.verse: that’s who the attentive know as a sage.

snp1.12:10.2.verse: young or middle-aged, the sage is self-controlled.

snp1.12:10.3.verse: Irreproachable, he does not insult anyone:

snp1.12:10.4.verse: that’s who the attentive know as a sage.

snp1.12:11.1.verse: When one who lives on charity receives alms,

snp1.12:11.2.verse: from the top, the middle, or the leftovers,

snp1.12:11.3.verse: they think it unworthy to praise or put down:

snp1.12:11.4.verse: that’s who the attentive know as a sage.

snp1.12:12.1.verse: The sage lives refraining from sex,

snp1.12:12.2.verse: even when young is not tied down,

snp1.12:12.3.verse: refraining from indulgence and negligence, freed:

snp1.12:12.4.verse: that’s who the attentive know as a sage.

snp1.12:13.1.verse: Understanding the world, the seer of the ultimate goal,

snp1.12:13.2.verse: the unaffected one, having crossed the flood and the ocean,

snp1.12:13.3.verse: has cut the ties, unattached and undefiled:

snp1.12:13.4.verse: that’s who the attentive know as a sage.

snp1.12:14.1.verse: The two are not the same, far apart in lifestyle and conduct—

snp1.12:14.2.verse: the householder providing for a wife, and the selfless one true to their vows.

snp1.12:14.3.verse: The unrestrained householder kills other creatures,

snp1.12:14.4.verse: while the restrained sage always protects living creatures.

snp1.12:15.1.verse: As the crested blue-necked peacock flying through the sky

snp1.12:15.2.verse: never approaches the speed of the swan,

snp1.12:15.3.verse: so the householder cannot compete with the mendicant,

snp1.12:15.4.verse: the sage meditating secluded in the woods.

snp2.1:1.1.verse: Whatever beings have come together here,

snp2.1:1.2.verse: whether of the earth or in the firmament,

snp2.1:1.3.verse: may the minds of all those beings be happy,

snp2.1:1.4.verse: and may they listen carefully to what is said.

snp2.1:2.1.verse: Therefore, all of you beings, be attentive,

snp2.1:2.2.verse: be friendly towards this generation of men,

snp2.1:2.3.verse: they who bring offerings by day and by night,

snp2.1:2.4.verse: therefore, being heedful, you must protect them.

snp2.1:3.1.verse: Whatever riches there are - here or elsewhere

snp2.1:3.2.verse: or in the heavens - that excellent treasure

snp2.1:3.3.verse: is not equal unto the Realised One,

snp2.1:3.4.verse: this excellent treasure is in the Buddha:

snp2.1:3.5.verse: by virtue of this truth may there be safety!

snp2.1:4.2.verse: which the concentrated Sakyan sage attained,

snp2.1:4.3.verse: there is nothing that is equal to that state,

snp2.1:4.4.verse: this excellent treasure is in the Dhamma:

snp2.1:4.5.verse: by virtue of this truth may there be safety!

snp2.1:5.1.verse: That which the Buddha, the Great One, praised as pure,

snp2.1:5.2.verse: the concentration said to have prompt (result),

snp2.1:5.3.verse: no equal to that concentration is found,

snp2.1:5.4.verse: this excellent treasure is in the Dhamma:

snp2.1:5.5.verse: by virtue of this truth may there be safety!

snp2.1:6.1.verse: Those eight individuals praised by the good,

snp2.1:6.2.verse: there are these four pairs (of individuals),

snp2.1:6.3.verse: those disciples of the Happy One are worthy of gifts,

snp2.1:6.4.verse: those things that have been given to them have great fruits,

snp2.1:6.5.verse: this excellent treasure is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:6.6.verse: by virtue of this truth may there be safety!

snp2.1:7.1.verse: Those who have firm and devoted minds,

snp2.1:7.2.verse: without sense desire in Gotama's dispensation,

snp2.1:7.3.verse: those who have attained, and entered the deathless,

snp2.1:7.4.verse: are enjoying emancipation, gained for free,

snp2.1:7.5.verse: this excellent treasure is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:7.6.verse: by virtue of this truth may there be safety!

snp2.1:8.1.verse: Just as a locking post stuck fast in the earth

snp2.1:8.2.verse: does not waver on account of the four winds,

snp2.1:8.3.verse: in the same way, I say, is the true person,

snp2.1:8.4.verse: the one who sees the noble truths completely,

snp2.1:8.5.verse: this excellent treasure is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:8.6.verse: by virtue of this truth may there be safety!

snp2.1:9.1.verse: Those who clearly distinguish the noble truths,

snp2.1:9.2.verse: which were well preached by the one with deep wisdom,

snp2.1:9.3.verse: however great they become in heedlessness

snp2.1:9.4.verse: still they do not take up an eighth existence,

snp2.1:9.5.verse: this excellent treasure is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:9.6.verse: by virtue of this truth may there be safety!

snp2.1:10.2.verse: there are a triad of things that are given up:

snp2.1:10.4.verse: and whatever (grasping at) virtue and practices there is.

snp2.1:11.1.verse: He is free from (rebirth in) the four lower worlds,

snp2.1:11.2.verse: he is incapable of the six great crimes.

snp2.1:11.3.verse: this excellent treasure is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:11.4.verse: by virtue of this truth may there be safety!

snp2.1:12.1.verse: Whatever bad action there is that he performs

snp2.1:12.2.verse: by way of body, or of speech, or of mind,

snp2.1:12.3.verse: he is incapable of covering it up,

snp2.1:12.4.verse: this incapacity is said of one who has seen the state (of peace),

snp2.1:12.5.verse: this excellent treasure is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:12.6.verse: by virtue of this truth may there be safety!

snp2.1:13.1.verse: Just like a tall woodland tree crowned with blossom

snp2.1:13.2.verse: in the summer months, in the early summer,

snp2.1:13.3.verse: in the same way he preached the Dhamma which is best,

snp2.1:13.4.verse: which goes to Nibbāna, the highest benefit,

snp2.1:13.5.verse: this excellent treasure is in the Buddha:

snp2.1:13.6.verse: by virtue of this truth may there be safety!

snp2.1:14.1.verse: The best one, knowing the best, giving the best, brought the best,

snp2.1:14.2.verse: brought the best, unsurpassed he preached the best Dhamma.

snp2.1:14.3.verse: this excellent treasure is in the Buddha:

snp2.1:14.4.verse: by virtue of this truth may there be safety!

snp2.1:15.1.verse: The old is destroyed, and nothing new is produced,

snp2.1:15.2.verse: (their) minds are unexcited by future rebirth,

snp2.1:15.3.verse: they have destroyed the seeds, and have no desire for growth,

snp2.1:15.4.verse: the wise are still, just as this lamp (is still),

snp2.1:15.5.verse: this excellent treasure is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:15.6.verse: by virtue of this truth may there be safety!

snp2.1:16.1.verse: Whatever beings have come together here,

snp2.1:16.2.verse: whether of the earth or in the firmament,

snp2.1:16.3.verse: the Realised One is revered by gods and men,

snp2.1:16.4.verse: we honour the Buddha - may there be safety!

snp2.1:17.1.verse: Whatever beings have come together here,

snp2.1:17.2.verse: whether of the earth or in the firmament,

snp2.1:17.3.verse: the Realised One is revered by gods and men,

snp2.1:17.4.verse: we honour the Dhamma - may there be safety!

snp2.1:18.1.verse: Whatever beings have come together here,

snp2.1:18.2.verse: whether of the earth or in the firmament,

snp2.1:18.3.verse: the Realised One is revered by gods and men,

snp2.1:18.4.verse: we honour the Saṅgha - may there be safety!

snp2.1:5.4.verse: This, too, is an exquisite treasure in the Dhamma.

snp2.1:5.5.verse: By this truth may there be well-being.

snp2.1:6.1.verse: The eight persons, praised by those at peace—

snp2.1:6.3.verse: They, disciples of the One Well-Gone, deserve offerings.

snp2.1:6.4.verse: What is given to them bears great fruit.

snp2.1:6.5.verse: This, too, is an exquisite treasure in the Saṅgha.

snp2.1:6.6.verse: By this truth may there be well-being.

snp2.1:7.3.verse: on attaining their goal, plunge into the deathless,

snp2.1:7.4.verse: freely enjoying the liberation they’ve gained.

snp2.1:7.5.verse: This, too, is an exquisite treasure in the Saṅgha.

snp2.1:7.6.verse: By this truth may there be well-being.

snp2.1:8.2.verse: that even the four winds cannot shake:

snp2.1:8.3.verse: That, I tell you, is like the person of integrity,

snp2.1:8.5.verse: This, too, is an exquisite treasure in the Saṅgha.

snp2.1:8.6.verse: By this truth may there be well-being.

snp2.1:9.1.verse: Those who have seen clearly the noble truths

snp2.1:9.2.verse: well-taught by the one deeply discerning—

snp2.1:9.3.verse: regardless of what [later] might make them heedless—

snp2.1:9.4.verse: will come to no eighth state of becoming,3

snp2.1:9.5.verse: This, too, is an exquisite treasure in the Saṅgha.

snp2.1:9.6.verse: By this truth may there be well-being.

snp2.1:10.1.verse: At the moment of attaining sight,

snp2.1:11.1.verse: One is completely released from the four states of deprivation,5

snp2.1:11.2.verse: and incapable of committing the six great wrongs.6

snp2.1:11.3.verse: This, too, is an exquisite treasure in the Saṅgha.

snp2.1:11.4.verse: By this truth may there be well-being.
