snp2.1:12.5.verse: This, too, is an exquisite treasure in the Saṅgha.

snp2.1:12.6.verse: By this truth may there be well-being.

snp2.1:13.1.verse: Like a forest grove with flowering tops

snp2.1:13.2.verse: in the first month of the heat of the summer,

snp2.1:13.3.verse: so is the foremost Dhamma he taught,

snp2.1:13.4.verse: for the highest benefit, leading to unbinding.

snp2.1:13.5.verse: This, too, is an exquisite treasure in the Buddha.

snp2.1:13.6.verse: By this truth may there be well-being.

snp2.1:14.2.verse: unsurpassed, he taught the foremost Dhamma.

snp2.1:14.3.verse: This, too, is an exquisite treasure in the Buddha.

snp2.1:14.4.verse: By this truth may there be well-being.

snp2.1:15.1.verse: Ended the old, there is no new taking birth.

snp2.1:15.2.verse: Dispassioned their minds toward future becoming,

snp2.1:15.3.verse: they, with no seed, no desire for growth,

snp2.1:15.4.verse: enlightened, go out like this flame.7

snp2.1:15.5.verse: This, too, is an exquisite treasure in the Saṅgha.

snp2.1:15.6.verse: By this truth may there be well-being.

snp2.1:16.3.verse: the Tathāgata worshipped by beings human & divine—

snp2.1:16.4.verse: let us pay homage to the Buddha. May there be well-being.

snp2.1:17.3.verse: the Tathāgata worshipped by beings human & divine—

snp2.1:17.4.verse: let us pay homage to the Dhamma. May there be well-being.

snp2.1:18.3.verse: the Tathāgata worshipped by beings human & divine—

snp2.1:18.4.verse: let us pay homage to the Saṅgha. May there be well-being.

snp2.1:1.2.verse: on the ground or in the sky:

snp2.1:1.3.verse: may beings all be of happy heart,

snp2.1:1.4.verse: and listen carefully to what is said.

snp2.1:2.1.verse: So pay heed, all you beings,

snp2.1:2.3.verse: who day and night bring offerings;

snp2.1:3.1.verse: There’s no wealth in this life or the next,

snp2.1:3.2.verse: no sublime gem in the heavens,

snp2.1:3.4.verse: This sublime gem is in the Buddha:

snp2.1:3.5.verse: by this truth, may you be well!

snp2.1:4.1.verse: Ending, dispassion, the undying, the sublime,

snp2.1:4.2.verse: attained by the Sakyan Sage immersed in samādhi;

snp2.1:4.3.verse: there is nothing equal to that Dhamma.

snp2.1:4.4.verse: This sublime gem is in the Dhamma:

snp2.1:4.5.verse: by this truth, may you be well!

snp2.1:5.1.verse: The purity praised by the highest Buddha

snp2.1:5.2.verse: is said to be the “immersion with immediate fruit”;

snp2.1:5.3.verse: no equal to that immersion is found.

snp2.1:5.4.verse: This sublime gem is in the Dhamma:

snp2.1:5.5.verse: by this truth, may you be well!

snp2.1:6.1.verse: The eight individual persons praised by the good

snp2.1:6.2.verse: are the four pairs of the Holy One’s disciples;

snp2.1:6.3.verse: they are worthy of religious donations,

snp2.1:6.4.verse: what’s given to them is very fruitful.

snp2.1:6.5.verse: This sublime gem is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:6.6.verse: by this truth, may you be well!

snp2.1:7.3.verse: they’ve attained the goal, plunged into freedom from death,

snp2.1:7.4.verse: and enjoy the quenching they’ve freely gained.

snp2.1:7.5.verse: This sublime gem is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:7.6.verse: by this truth, may you be well!

snp2.1:8.1.verse: As Indra’s pillar rooted in earth

snp2.1:8.2.verse: is not shaken by the four winds,

snp2.1:8.3.verse: I say a true person is like this,

snp2.1:8.4.verse: who sees the noble truths in experience.

snp2.1:8.5.verse: This sublime gem is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:8.6.verse: by this truth, may you be well!

snp2.1:9.1.verse: Those who fathom the noble truths

snp2.1:9.2.verse: taught by the one of deep wisdom,

snp2.1:9.3.verse: do not take an eighth life,

snp2.1:9.4.verse: even if they are hugely negligent.

snp2.1:9.5.verse: This sublime gem is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:9.6.verse: by this truth, may you be well!

snp2.1:11.1.verse: They’re freed from the four places of loss,

snp2.1:11.3.verse: This sublime gem is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:11.4.verse: by this truth, may you be well!

snp2.1:12.1.verse: Even if they do a bad deed

snp2.1:12.3.verse: they are unable to conceal it;

snp2.1:12.4.verse: this, it’s said, is the inability of one who has seen the truth.

snp2.1:12.5.verse: This sublime gem is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:12.6.verse: by this truth, may you be well!

snp2.1:13.1.verse: Like a tall forest tree crowned with flowers

snp2.1:13.2.verse: in the first month of summer;

snp2.1:13.3.verse: that’s how he taught the superb Dhamma,

snp2.1:13.4.verse: leading to extinguishment, the ultimate benefit.

snp2.1:13.5.verse: This sublime gem is in the Buddha:

snp2.1:13.6.verse: by this truth, may you be well!

snp2.1:14.1.verse: The superb, knower of the superb, giver of the superb, bringer of the superb;

snp2.1:14.3.verse: This sublime gem is in the Buddha:

snp2.1:14.4.verse: by this truth, may you be well!

snp2.1:15.1.verse: The old is ended, nothing new is produced;

snp2.1:15.2.verse: their minds have no desire for future rebirth.

snp2.1:15.3.verse: Withered are the seeds, there’s no desire for growth,

snp2.1:15.4.verse: those attentive ones are extinguished like this lamp.

snp2.1:15.5.verse: This sublime gem is in the Saṅgha:

snp2.1:15.6.verse: by this truth, may you be well!

snp2.1:16.2.verse: on the ground or in the sky:

snp2.1:16.3.verse: the Realized One is honored by gods and humans!

snp2.1:16.4.verse: We bow to the Buddha! May you be safe!

snp2.1:17.2.verse: on the ground or in the sky:

snp2.1:17.3.verse: the Realized One is honored by gods and humans!

snp2.1:17.4.verse: We bow to the Dhamma! May you be safe!

snp2.1:18.2.verse: on the ground or in the sky:

snp2.1:18.3.verse: the Realized One is honored by gods and humans!

snp2.1:18.4.verse: We bow to the Saṅgha! May you be safe!

snp2.2:1.1.verse: “Those peacefully eating millet, Job’s-tears, green gram,

snp2.2:1.3.verse: obtained in line with the Dhamma,

snp2.2:1.4.verse: don’t desire sensual-pleasures or tell falsehoods.

snp2.2:2.1.verse: But when eating what is well-made, well-prepared,

snp2.2:2.4.verse: Kassapa, one consumes a raw stench.

snp2.2:3.1.verse: ‘Raw stench is not proper for me,’

snp2.2:3.2.verse: Yet you, kinsman of Brahmā, say,

snp2.2:3.4.verse: and the well-prepared fleshes of birds.

snp2.2:3.5.verse: So I ask you, Kassapa, the meaning of that:

snp2.2:3.6.verse: Of what sort is ‘raw stench’ for you?”

snp2.2:4.3.verse: useless recitations, associating with the wives of others:

snp2.2:4.4.verse: This is a raw stench, not the eating of meat.

snp2.2:5.1.verse: Those people here who are unrestrained in sensuality,

snp2.2:5.2.verse: greedy for flavors, mixed together with what’s impure,

snp2.2:5.4.verse: This is a raw stench, not the eating of meat.

snp2.2:6.1.verse: Those who are rough, pitiless, eating the flesh off your back,

snp2.2:6.3.verse: habitually ungenerous, giving to no one:

snp2.2:6.4.verse: This is a raw stench, not the eating of meat.

snp2.2:7.3.verse: conceit & pride, befriending those of no integrity:

snp2.2:7.4.verse: This is a raw stench, not the eating of meat.

snp2.2:8.1.verse: Those of evil habits, debt-repudiators, informers,

snp2.2:8.3.verse: vile men who do evil things:

snp2.2:8.4.verse: This is a raw stench, not the eating of meat.

snp2.2:9.1.verse: Those people here who are unrestrained toward beings,

snp2.2:9.2.verse: taking what’s others’, intent on injury,

snp2.2:9.4.verse: This is a raw stench, not the eating of meat.

snp2.2:10.1.verse: Those who are very greedy, constantly intent

snp2.2:10.2.verse: on hindering and killing; beings who, after passing away,

snp2.2:10.3.verse: go to darkness, fall headfirst into hell:

snp2.2:10.4.verse: This is a raw stench, not the eating of meat.

snp2.2:11.2.verse: no nakedness, no shaven head, no tangled hair,

snp2.2:11.3.verse: no rough animal skins, no performance of fire oblations,

snp2.2:11.4.verse: or the many austerities to become an immortal in the world,

snp2.2:11.5.verse: no chants, no oblations, no performance of sacrifices at the proper season—

snp2.2:11.6.verse: purify a mortal who hasn’t crossed over doubt.

snp2.2:12.1.verse: One should go about guarded with regard to those things, one’s faculties understood,

snp2.2:12.2.verse: standing firm in the Dhamma, delighting in being straightforward & mild.

snp2.2:12.4.verse: the enlightened one isn’t smeared by what’s heard or seen.”

snp2.2:13.1.verse: Thus this meaning, the Blessed One, again & again

snp2.2:13.2.verse: explained it. The one who had mastered chants understood it.

snp2.2:13.4.verse: free from raw stench, unfettered, indomitable3—proclaimed it.

snp2.2:14.1.verse: Hearing the Awakened One’s well-spoken word—

snp2.2:14.2.verse: free from raw stench, dispelling all stress—

snp2.2:14.3.verse: the one with lowered mind paid homage to the Tathāgata,

snp2.2:14.4.verse: chose the Going Forth right there.

snp2.2:1.4.verse: They don’t lie to get what they want.

snp2.2:2.1.verse: But when you eat delicious food,

snp2.2:2.2.verse: nicely cooked and prepared, and offered by others,

snp2.2:2.3.verse: enjoying a dish of fine rice,

snp2.2:3.2.verse: so you said, O brahmin only by kin.

snp2.2:3.3.verse: Yet here you are enjoying a dish of fine rice,

snp2.2:3.4.verse: well prepared with the flesh of fowl.

snp2.2:3.6.verse: what do you take to be putrefaction?”

snp2.2:4.4.verse: this is putrefaction, not eating meat.

snp2.2:5.2.verse: greedy for tastes, mixed up in impurity,

snp2.2:5.4.verse: this is putrefaction, not eating meat.

snp2.2:6.2.verse: pitiless and arrogant betrayers of friends,

snp2.2:6.4.verse: this is putrefaction, not eating meat.

snp2.2:7.4.verse: this is putrefaction, not eating meat.

snp2.2:8.4.verse: this is putrefaction, not eating meat.

snp2.2:9.1.verse: People here who can’t stop harming living creatures,

snp2.2:9.2.verse: taking from others, intent on hurting,

snp2.2:9.3.verse: immoral, cruel, harsh, lacking regard for others:

snp2.2:9.4.verse: this is putrefaction, not eating meat.

snp2.2:10.2.verse: and addicted to evil—those beings pass into darkness,

snp2.2:10.4.verse: this is putrefaction, not eating meat.

snp2.2:11.1.verse: Not fish or flesh or fasting,

snp2.2:11.2.verse: nudity or baldness, or dreadlocks or dirt,

snp2.2:11.3.verse: not rough hides or serving the sacred flame,

snp2.2:11.4.verse: or the many endless mortifications in the world,

snp2.2:11.5.verse: not hymns or oblations, sacrifices or seasonal observances,

snp2.2:11.6.verse: will cleanse a mortal not free of doubt.

snp2.2:12.1.verse: Guarding the streams of sense impressions, wander with faculties understood,

snp2.2:12.2.verse: standing on the teaching, delighting in integrity and tenderness.

snp2.2:12.3.verse: The attentive have slipped their chains and given up all suffering;

snp2.2:12.4.verse: they don’t cling to the seen and the heard.”

snp2.2:13.1.verse: The Buddha explained this matter to him again and again,

snp2.2:13.2.verse: until the master of hymns understood it.

snp2.2:13.3.verse: It was illustrated with colorful verses

snp2.2:13.4.verse: by the sage free of putrefaction, unattached, hard to trace.

snp2.2:14.1.verse: Having heard the fine words of the Buddha,

snp2.2:14.2.verse: that are free of putrefaction, casting aside all suffering;

snp2.2:14.3.verse: humbled, he bowed to the Realized One,

snp2.2:14.4.verse: and right away begged to go forth.

snp2.3:1.1.verse: One who, flouting, despising a sense of shame,

snp2.3:1.3.verse: but not grasping what he could do [to help]:

snp2.3:1.4.verse: Know him as “Not one of mine.”

snp2.3:2.2.verse: speaks endearing words to which he doesn’t conform,

snp2.3:3.1.verse: He’s not a friend who’s always wary,

snp2.3:3.2.verse: suspecting a split, focusing just on your weakness.

snp2.3:3.3.verse: But him on whom you can depend, like a child on its parent’s breast:

snp2.3:3.4.verse: That’s a true friend whom others can’t split from you.

snp2.3:4.1.verse: The conditions that make for joy,

snp2.3:4.4.verse: for one carrying the manly burden.

snp2.3:5.3.verse: one is freed from evil, devoid of distress,

snp2.3:5.4.verse: refreshed with the savor of rapture in the Dhamma.1

snp2.3:1.3.verse: but not following up in deeds—

snp2.3:1.4.verse: know they’re not on your side.

snp2.3:2.1.verse: Some say nice things to their friends

snp2.3:3.3.verse: One on whom you rest, like a child on the breast,

snp2.3:3.4.verse: is a true friend, not split from you by others.

snp2.3:4.1.verse: One whose reward is the fruit

snp2.3:4.2.verse: of bearing the burden of service

snp2.3:5.1.verse: One who has drunk the nectar of seclusion

snp2.3:5.3.verse: free of stress, free of evil,

snp2.3:5.4.verse: drinks the joyous nectar of Dhamma.

snp2.4:1.2.verse: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.

snp2.4:1.3.verse: Then a certain god, towards the end of the night, whose surpassing beauty lit up the whole of Jeta’s Wood, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he stood on one side.

snp2.4:1.4.verse: While standing on one side that god addressed the Fortunate One with a verse:

snp2.4:2.1.verse: “Many are the gods and the men

snp2.4:2.2.verse: who have thought about the blessings

snp2.4:2.4.verse: now please say what is the supreme blessing.”

snp2.4:4.3.verse: aspiring in a right way oneself:

snp2.4:5.2.verse: and being disciplined and well trained,

snp2.4:5.3.verse: and whatever words are well spoken:

snp2.4:6.1.verse: Attendance on one's mother and father,

snp2.4:6.2.verse: looking after one’s wife and children,

snp2.4:6.3.verse: with works that are not agitating:

snp2.4:7.1.verse: Giving, and living by the Dhamma,

snp2.4:9.3.verse: listening to Dhamma at the right time:

snp2.4:10.1.verse: Being patient and easily spoken to,

snp2.4:10.3.verse: discussing Dhamma at the right time:

snp2.4:12.1.verse: He whose mind does not waver,

snp2.4:12.2.verse: when it is touched by things of this world,

snp2.4:13.4.verse: for them this is the supreme blessing.”

snp2.4:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

snp2.4:1.3.verse: Then a certain deva, in the far extreme of the night, her extreme radiance lighting up the entirety of Jeta’s Grove, went to the Blessed One. On arrival, having bowed down to him, she stood to one side.

snp2.4:1.4.verse: As she was standing there, she addressed him with a verse:

snp2.4:3.3.verse: paying homage to those worthy of homage:

snp2.4:4.2.verse: having made merit in the past,

snp2.4:6.2.verse: assistance to one’s wife and children,

snp2.4:9.3.verse: hearing the Dhamma on timely occasions:

snp2.4:10.3.verse: discussing the Dhamma on timely occasions:

snp2.4:12.1.verse: When touched by the ways of the world,3

snp2.4:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

snp2.4:1.3.verse: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side.

snp2.4:1.4.verse: That deity addressed the Buddha in verse:

snp2.4:3.2.verse: but to fraternize with the wise,

snp2.4:3.3.verse: and honoring those worthy of honor:

snp2.4:4.2.verse: having made merit in the past,

snp2.4:9.3.verse: and timely listening to the teaching:

snp2.4:10.3.verse: and timely discussion of the teaching:

snp2.5:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying in Gayā at Ṭaṅkitamañca, the haunt of Suciloma the yakkha.

snp2.5:1.3.verse: And on that occasion Khara the yakkha and Suciloma the yakkha passed by not far from the Blessed One.

snp2.5:1.4.verse: Then Khara the yakkha said to Suciloma the yakkha:

snp2.5:1.6.verse: “That’s not a contemplative. That’s a fake contemplative.

snp2.5:1.7.verse: I’ll find out whether that’s a contemplative or a fake contemplative.”

snp2.5:2.1.verse: So Suciloma the yakkha approached the Blessed One and on arrival leaned his body up against the Blessed One.

snp2.5:2.2.verse: The Blessed One leaned his body away.

snp2.5:2.3.verse: So Suciloma the yakkha said to the Blessed One:

snp2.5:2.5.verse: “No, I’m not afraid of you, friend,

snp2.5:2.6.verse: just that your touch is evil.”

snp2.5:3.1.verse: “I will ask you a question, contemplative.

snp2.5:3.2.verse: If you can’t answer me, I will hurl out your mind or rip open your heart or, grabbing you by the feet, hurl you across the Ganges.”

snp2.5:4.1.verse: “My friend, I see no one in the cosmos with its devas, Māras, & Brahmās, in this generation with its contemplatives & brahmans, its royalty & commonfolk, who could hurl out my mind or rip open my heart or, grabbing me by the feet, hurl me across the Ganges.

snp2.5:4.2.verse: But nevertheless, ask me what you wish.”

snp2.5:4.3.verse: So Suciloma the yakkha addressed the Blessed One in verse:

snp2.5:5.2.verse: Displeasure, delight, horripilation are born from what?

snp2.5:5.3.verse: Arising from what do thoughts fling the mind around,

snp2.5:6.1.verse: “Passion & aversion come from this1 as a cause;

snp2.5:6.2.verse: displeasure, delight, horripilation are born from this;

snp2.5:6.3.verse: arising from this thoughts fling the mind around,

snp2.5:7.1.verse: They’re born from affection arisen from the mind, from oneself,2

snp2.5:7.2.verse: like the trunk-born (shoots) of a banyan tree,

snp2.5:7.4.verse: like a māluva vine spread in a forest.

snp2.5:8.1.verse: Those who discern where it’s born

snp2.5:8.3.verse: They cross over this flood, so hard to cross,

snp2.5:8.4.verse: never crossed before, for the sake of no further becoming.”

snp2.5:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Gayā on the cut-stone ledge in the haunt of Spiky the native spirit.

snp2.5:1.3.verse: Now at that time the native spirits Shaggy and Spiky were passing by not far from the Buddha.

snp2.5:1.7.verse: I’ll soon find out whether he’s an ascetic or a faker.”

snp2.5:2.1.verse: Then Spiky went up to the Buddha and leaned up against his body,

snp2.5:2.3.verse: Then Spiky said to the Buddha,

snp2.5:3.1.verse: “I will ask you a question, ascetic.

snp2.5:3.2.verse: If you don’t answer me, I’ll drive you insane, or explode your heart, or grab you by the feet and throw you to the far shore of the Ganges!”

snp2.5:4.1.verse: “I don’t see anyone in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans who could do that to me.

snp2.5:4.2.verse: But anyway, ask what you wish.”

snp2.5:4.3.verse: Then Spiky addressed the Buddha in verse:

snp2.5:5.1.verse: “Where do greed and hate come from?

snp2.5:5.2.verse: From where spring discontent, desire, and terror?

snp2.5:5.3.verse: Where do the mind’s thoughts originate,

snp2.5:5.4.verse: like a crow let loose by boys.”

snp2.5:6.2.verse: from here spring discontent, desire, and terror;

snp2.5:6.3.verse: here’s where the mind’s thoughts originate,

snp2.5:6.4.verse: like a crow let loose by boys.

snp2.5:7.1.verse: Born of affection, originating in oneself,

snp2.5:7.2.verse: like prop roots sprouting from a banyan;

snp2.5:7.3.verse: the many kinds of attachment to sensual pleasures

snp2.5:7.4.verse: are like camel’s foot creeper creeping through the woods.

snp2.5:8.1.verse: Those who understand where they come from

snp2.5:8.3.verse: They cross this flood so hard to cross,

snp2.5:8.4.verse: not crossed before, so as to not be reborn.”

snp2.6:1.1.verse: Living the Dhamma life, living the holy life:

snp2.6:1.2.verse: This, they say, is the highest power.

snp2.6:2.2.verse: delighting in injury, a stupid beast,

snp2.6:3.4.verse: even when proclaimed by the Awakened One.

snp2.6:4.4.verse: to be the path that leads to hell.

snp2.6:5.2.verse: from womb to womb, from darkness to darkness,

snp2.6:7.1.verse: Monks, whoever you know to be like this,

snp2.6:7.3.verse: evil in his desires, evil in his resolves,

snp2.6:9.3.verse: Having swept away those of evil desires,

snp2.6:10.4.verse: you will put an end to suffering & stress.2

snp2.6:1.1.verse: A righteous life, a spiritual life,

snp2.6:1.2.verse: they call this the supreme treasure.

snp2.6:1.4.verse: from the lay life to homelessness

snp2.6:3.1.verse: A mendicant who loves to quarrel,

snp2.6:3.3.verse: doesn’t even know what’s been explained

snp2.6:3.4.verse: in the Dhamma taught by the Buddha.

snp2.6:4.4.verse: is the path that leads to hell.

snp2.6:5.2.verse: passing from womb to womb, from darkness to darkness,

snp2.6:6.4.verse: for it’s hard to clean one full of grime.

snp2.6:7.1.verse: Mendicants, knowing that someone is like this,

snp2.6:7.3.verse: of corrupt wishes and wicked intent,

snp2.6:9.2.verse: they’re not ascetics, they just think they are.

snp2.6:9.3.verse: When you’ve thrown out those of corrupt wishes,

snp2.6:10.4.verse: you’ll make an end of suffering.

snp2.7:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

snp2.7:1.3.verse: Then many Kosalan brahmans of great means—old, aged, advanced in years, having come to the last stage of life—approached the Blessed One. On arrival, they exchanged courteous greetings with him.

snp2.7:1.4.verse: After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, they sat to one side. As they were sitting there, they said to him:

snp2.7:1.5.verse: “Master Gotama, do brahmans at present live in conformity with the brahman principles of ancient brahmans?”

snp2.7:1.6.verse: “No, brahmans. Brahmans at present don’t live in conformity with the brahman principles of ancient brahmans.”

snp2.7:1.7.verse: “It would be good if Master Gotama described the brahman principles of ancient brahmans, if it wouldn’t burden him.”

snp2.7:1.8.verse: “In that case, brahmans, listen and pay close attention. I will speak.”

snp2.7:1.9.verse: “As you say, master,” the brahmans of great means responded to the Blessed One.

snp2.7:2.3.verse: Abandoning the five strings of sensuality,

snp2.7:2.4.verse: they practiced for their own benefit.

snp2.7:3.3.verse: They had study as their wealth.

snp2.7:4.1.verse: They did not despise what was prepared for them:

snp2.7:6.1.verse: Brahmans were not to be violated,

snp2.7:6.2.verse: not to be beaten, protected by law,2

snp2.7:6.4.verse: from the doors of any home.

snp2.7:7.3.verse: Brahmans of old practiced the search

snp2.7:8.2.verse: nor did they buy their wives.

snp2.7:8.4.verse: having come together, they found joy together.

snp2.7:10.1.verse: They praised: the holy life, virtue,

snp2.7:13.1.verse: They asked for rice, bedding, cloth, butter & oil.

snp2.7:13.4.verse: from that they performed the sacrifice.

snp2.7:14.1.verse: And in setting up the sacrifice,

snp2.7:16.3.verse: brahmans, in line with their principles,

snp2.7:16.4.verse: were committed to standards of what should & shouldn’t be done.

snp2.7:16.5.verse: As long as this lasted in the world,

snp2.7:17.1.verse: But a perversion came among them.

snp2.7:19.2.verse: joined with groups of excellent women—

snp2.7:21.2.verse: by the brahmans, lord of charioteers,

snp2.7:21.3.verse: the horse sacrifice, the human sacrifice,

snp2.7:24.1.verse: And they, receiving the wealth there,

snp2.7:24.2.verse: found joy together in hoarding it.

snp2.7:24.6.verse: they went up to Okkāka again.

snp2.7:25.4.verse: This is a requisite for beings.

snp2.7:26.2.verse: by the brahmans, lord of charioteers,

snp2.7:27.1.verse: Not with their hooves or horns

snp2.7:27.5.verse: but the king, grabbing them by the horns,

snp2.7:28.4.verse: when the knife fell on the cows.

snp2.7:29.1.verse: Three were the diseases before then:

snp2.7:30.4.verse: the sacrificers fall away from the Dhamma.

snp2.7:31.3.verse: Where people see such a thing,

snp2.7:32.1.verse: With the Dhamma perishing in this way,

snp2.7:32.3.verse: noble warriors are split far apart,

snp2.7:33.2.verse: and any others protected by clan,

snp2.7:33.3.verse: repudiating the doctrine of their birth,

snp2.7:34.1.verse: When this was said, those brahmans of great means said to the Blessed One:

snp2.7:34.2.verse: “Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent! Just as if he were to place upright what was overturned, to reveal what was hidden, to show the way to one who was lost, or to carry a lamp into the dark so that those with eyes could see forms, in the same way has Master Gotama—through many lines of reasoning—made the Dhamma clear.

snp2.7:34.3.verse: We go to Master Gotama for refuge, to the Dhamma, & to the Saṅgha of monks. May Master Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge from this day forward, for life.”

snp2.7:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

snp2.7:1.3.verse: Then several old and well-to-do brahmins of Kosala—elderly and senior, who were advanced in years and had reached the final stage of life—went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

snp2.7:1.4.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

snp2.7:1.5.verse: “Worthy Gotama, are the ancient principles of the brahmins exhibited these days among brahmins?”

snp2.7:1.7.verse: “If you wouldn’t mind, Worthy Gotama, please teach us the ancient principles of the brahmins.”

snp2.7:1.8.verse: “Well then, brahmins, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

snp2.7:2.3.verse: Having given up the five sensual stimuli,

snp2.7:2.4.verse: they lived for their own true good.

snp2.7:3.1.verse: Brahmins used to own no cattle,

snp2.7:3.3.verse: Chanting was their money and grain,

snp2.7:3.4.verse: which they guarded as a gift from god.

snp2.7:4.3.verse: People believed that food prepared in faith

snp2.7:6.1.verse: Brahmins used to be inviolable and

snp2.7:6.3.verse: No one ever turned them away

snp2.7:7.4.verse: their quest for knowledge and conduct.

snp2.7:8.2.verse: nor did they purchase a wife.

snp2.7:9.1.verse: Brahmins never approached their wives for sex

snp2.7:9.3.verse: the fertile phase of the menstrual cycle

snp2.7:11.1.verse: He who was supreme among them,

snp2.7:12.1.verse: Training in line with their duties,

snp2.7:14.3.verse: Like a mother, father, or brother,

snp2.7:16.1.verse: The brahmins were delicate and tall,

snp2.7:16.3.verse: They were keen on all the duties

snp2.7:16.5.verse: So long as they continued in the world,

snp2.7:17.2.verse: little by little when they saw

snp2.7:17.4.verse: and the ladies in all their finery.

snp2.7:18.1.verse: Their chariots were harnessed with thoroughbreds,

snp2.7:18.4.verse: were neatly divided section by section.

snp2.7:19.1.verse: They were lavished with herds of cattle,

snp2.7:19.2.verse: and furnished with bevies of lovely ladies.

snp2.7:20.1.verse: They compiled hymns to that end,

snp2.7:20.3.verse: ‘You have plenty of money and grain.

snp2.7:20.4.verse: Sacrifice! For you have much treasure.

snp2.7:20.5.verse: Sacrifice! For you have much money.’

snp2.7:21.2.verse: the king, chief of charioteers, performed

snp2.7:21.4.verse: the sacrifices of the ‘casting of the yoke-pin’, the ‘royal soma drinking’, and the ‘unimpeded’.

snp2.7:21.5.verse: When he had carried out these sacrifices,

snp2.7:21.6.verse: he gave riches to the brahmins.

snp2.7:22.1.verse: There were cattle, bedding, and clothes,

snp2.7:22.2.verse: and ladies in all their finery;

snp2.7:23.3.verse: Having furnished them with different grains,

snp2.7:23.4.verse: he gave riches to the brahmins.

snp2.7:24.1.verse: When they got hold of that wealth,

snp2.7:24.2.verse: they arranged to store it up.

snp2.7:24.3.verse: Falling under the sway of desire,

snp2.7:24.5.verse: They compiled hymns to that end,

snp2.7:24.6.verse: approached King Okkāka once more and said,

snp2.7:25.4.verse: as they are essential for creatures.

snp2.7:25.5.verse: Sacrifice! For you have much treasure.

snp2.7:25.6.verse: Sacrifice! For you have much money.’

snp2.7:27.1.verse: Neither with feet nor with horns

snp2.7:27.2.verse: do cows harm anyone at all.

snp2.7:27.5.verse: But taking them by the horns,

snp2.7:27.6.verse: the king slew them with a sword.

snp2.7:28.1.verse: At that the gods and the ancestors,

snp2.7:28.2.verse: with Indra, the titans and monsters,

snp2.7:28.3.verse: roared out: ‘This is a crime against nature!’

snp2.7:28.4.verse: as the sword fell on the cows.

snp2.7:29.1.verse: There used to be three kinds of illness:

snp2.7:29.3.verse: But due to the slaughter of cows,

snp2.7:31.1.verse: And that is how this mean old practice

snp2.7:31.3.verse: Wherever they see such a thing,

snp2.7:32.4.verse: and wives looked down on their husbands.

snp2.7:33.1.verse: Aristocrats and brahmins only by kin,

snp2.7:33.2.verse: and others protected by their clan,

snp2.7:33.4.verse: fell under the sway of sensual pleasures.”

snp2.7:34.1.verse: When he had spoken, those well-to-do brahmins said to the Buddha,

snp2.7:34.3.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge for life.”

snp2.8:1.2.verse: —as the devas, Indra—one from whom you might learn the Dhamma,

snp2.8:1.4.verse: confident in you, shows you the Dhamma.

snp2.8:2.2.verse: practicing the Dhamma in line with the Dhamma,

snp2.8:2.4.verse: heedful, befriending a teacher like that.

snp2.8:3.1.verse: But if you consort with a piddling fool

snp2.8:3.2.verse: who hasn’t come to the goal, and is envious,

snp2.8:3.3.verse: without having cleared up the Dhamma right here,

snp2.8:3.4.verse: you’ll go to death with your doubts unresolved.

snp2.8:4.1.verse: Like a man gone down to a river—

snp2.8:4.3.verse: and swept away in the current:

snp2.8:4.4.verse: How can he help others across?

snp2.8:5.1.verse: Even so: he who hasn’t cleared up the Dhamma,

snp2.8:5.2.verse: attended to the meaning of what the learned say,

snp2.8:5.3.verse: himself not knowing, his doubts uncrossed:

snp2.8:5.4.verse: How can he get others to comprehend?

snp2.8:6.1.verse: But as one who’s embarked on a sturdy boat,

snp2.8:6.3.verse: would carry many others across there,

snp2.8:6.4.verse: knowing the needed techniques, skillful, thoughtful.

snp2.8:7.3.verse: can, knowing, get other people to comprehend—

snp2.8:7.4.verse: when the conditions have arisen for them to lend ear.

snp2.8:8.1.verse: So: you should befriend a person of integrity—

snp2.8:8.3.verse: Practicing so as to know the goal,

snp2.8:8.4.verse: having experienced the Dhamma, you get bliss.

snp2.8:1.1.verse: If you would learn the teaching from someone,

snp2.8:1.2.verse: honor them as the gods honor Indra.

snp2.8:1.3.verse: Then they will have confidence in you,

snp2.8:1.4.verse: and being learned, they reveal the teaching.

snp2.8:2.2.verse: practicing in line with that teaching

snp2.8:2.4.verse: through diligently sticking close to such a person.

snp2.8:3.1.verse: But associating with a petty fool

snp2.8:3.2.verse: who falls short of the goal, jealous,

snp2.8:3.3.verse: then unable to discern the teaching in this life,

snp2.8:3.4.verse: one proceeds to death still plagued by doubts.

snp2.8:4.1.verse: It’s like a man who has plunged into a river,

snp2.8:4.3.verse: As they are swept away downstream,

snp2.8:4.4.verse: how could they help others across?

snp2.8:5.1.verse: Just so, one unable to discern the teaching,

snp2.8:5.2.verse: who hasn’t studied the meaning under the learned,

snp2.8:5.3.verse: not knowing it oneself, still plagued by doubts,

snp2.8:5.4.verse: how could they help others to contemplate?

snp2.8:6.1.verse: But one who has embarked on a strong boat

snp2.8:6.3.verse: would bring many others across there

snp2.8:7.1.verse: So too one who understands—a knowledge master,

snp2.8:7.4.verse: so long as they are prepared to listen carefully.

snp2.8:8.1.verse: That’s why you should spend time with a true person,

snp2.8:8.3.verse: Having understood the meaning, putting it into practice,

snp2.8:8.4.verse: one who understands the teaching would find happiness.

snp2.9:1.3.verse: would a person become rightly based

snp2.9:2.1.verse: “One should be respectful of one’s superiors1 & not envious;

snp2.9:2.2.verse: should have a sense of the time for seeing teachers;2

snp2.9:2.3.verse: should value the opportunity when a talk on Dhamma’s in progress;

snp2.9:2.4.verse: should listen intently to well-spoken words;

snp2.9:3.1.verse: should go at the proper time,

snp2.9:3.2.verse: humbly, casting off arrogance, to one’s teacher’s presence;

snp2.9:3.3.verse: the Dhamma, its meaning, restraint, & the holy life—

snp2.9:4.2.verse: established in Dhamma, with a sense of how to investigate Dhamma,

snp2.9:4.3.verse: one should not speak in ways destructive of Dhamma,3

snp2.9:4.4.verse: should guide oneself with true, well-spoken words.

snp2.9:5.4.verse: one should go about free of intoxication, with steadfast mind.

snp2.9:6.1.verse: Understanding’s the heartwood of well-spoken words;

snp2.9:6.2.verse: concentration, the heartwood of learning & understanding.

snp2.9:6.3.verse: When a person is hasty & heedless

snp2.9:7.1.verse: While those who delight in the Dhamma taught by the noble ones,

snp2.9:7.2.verse: are unsurpassed in word, action, & mind.

snp2.9:7.3.verse: They, established in calm, composure, & concentration,

snp2.9:7.4.verse: have reached what discernment & learning have as their heartwood.”4

snp2.9:1.3.verse: would a person lay the foundations right,

snp2.9:2.2.verse: they’d know the time to visit their respected teachers.

snp2.9:2.3.verse: Treasuring the chance for a Dhamma talk,

snp2.9:2.4.verse: they’d listen carefully to the well-spoken words.

snp2.9:3.1.verse: At the right time, they’d enter the vicinity of their respected teachers

snp2.9:3.2.verse: in placid manner, leaving obstinacy behind.

snp2.9:3.3.verse: They’d call to mind and put into practice

snp2.9:3.4.verse: the meaning, the teaching, self-control, and the spiritual life.

snp2.9:4.1.verse: Delighting in the teaching, enjoying the teaching,

snp2.9:4.2.verse: standing on the teaching, evaluating the teaching,

snp2.9:4.3.verse: they’d never say anything that degraded the teaching,

snp2.9:4.4.verse: but would be guided by genuine words well-spoken.

snp2.9:5.1.verse: Giving up mirth, muttered prayer, weeping, ill will,

snp2.9:5.4.verse: they’d wander free of vanity, steadfast.

snp2.9:6.1.verse: Understanding is the essence of well-spoken words,

snp2.9:6.2.verse: stillness is the essence of learning and understanding.

snp2.9:6.3.verse: Wisdom and learning do not flourish

snp2.9:6.4.verse: in a hasty and negligent person.

snp2.9:7.1.verse: Those happy with the teaching proclaimed by the Noble One

snp2.9:7.2.verse: are supreme in speech, mind, and deed.

snp2.9:7.3.verse: Abiding in peace, gentleness, and stillness,

snp2.9:7.4.verse: they’ve realized the essence of learning and wisdom.”

snp2.10:1.3.verse: And what sleep is there for the afflicted,

snp2.10:2.2.verse: Train firmly for the sake of peace.

snp2.10:2.3.verse: Don’t let the king of death, —seeing you heedless—

snp2.10:2.4.verse: deceive you, bring you under his sway.

snp2.10:3.4.verse: don’t let the moment pass by.

snp2.10:3.5.verse: Those for whom the moment is past

snp2.10:4.2.verse: comes from heedlessness, has heedlessness on its heels.

snp2.10:1.2.verse: What’s the point in your sleeping?

snp2.10:1.4.verse: when inflicted by an arrow strike?

snp2.10:2.3.verse: The King of Death has caught you heedless—

snp2.10:2.4.verse: don’t let him fool you under his sway.

snp2.10:3.4.verse: Don’t let the moment pass you by.

snp2.10:3.5.verse: For if you miss your moment

snp2.10:3.6.verse: you’ll grieve when sent to hell.

snp2.10:4.4.verse: pluck out the dart from yourself.

snp2.11:1.2.verse: do you not despise the wise man?

snp2.11:1.3.verse: Is the one who holds up the torch for human beings

snp2.11:2.2.verse: I don’t despise the wise man.

snp2.11:2.3.verse: The one who holds up the torch for human beings

snp2.11:3.3.verse: going forth from home through conviction,

snp2.11:3.4.verse: be one who puts an end to suffering & stress.

snp2.11:5.4.verse: Don’t be one who returns to the world.

snp2.11:6.3.verse: have mindfulness immersed in the body,

snp2.11:7.3.verse: Develop the mind in the unattractive—

snp2.11:8.3.verse: Then, from having broken through conceit,

snp2.11:9.1.verse: In this way, the Blessed One often instructed Ven. Rāhula3 with these verses.

snp2.11:1.2.verse: even for the man of wisdom?

snp2.11:1.3.verse: Do you honor he who holds aloft

snp2.11:2.3.verse: I always honor he who holds aloft

snp2.11:3.1.verse: “One who’s given up the five sensual stimulations,

snp2.11:3.3.verse: and who’s left the home life out of faith—

snp2.11:3.4.verse: let them make an end to suffering!

snp2.11:5.4.verse: don’t come back to this world again.

snp2.11:6.1.verse: Be restrained in the monastic code

snp2.11:6.3.verse: With mindfulness immersed in the body,

snp2.11:7.4.verse: meditate on the ugly aspects of the body.

snp2.11:8.2.verse: give up the tendency to conceit;

snp2.11:9.1.verse: That is how the Buddha regularly advised Venerable Rāhula with these verses.

snp2.12:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Āḷavī at the Aggāḷava shrine.

snp2.12:1.3.verse: And on that occasion Ven. Vaṅgīsa’s1 preceptor, an elder named Nigrodha Kappa, had recently totally unbound at the Aggāḷava shrine.

snp2.12:1.4.verse: Then as Ven. Vaṅgīsa was alone in seclusion, this train of thought arose in his awareness:

snp2.12:1.5.verse: “Has my preceptor totally unbound, or has he not totally unbound?”

snp2.12:1.6.verse: Then, emerging from his seclusion in the late afternoon, Ven. Vaṅgīsa went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, having bowed down to him, sat to one side. As he was sitting there, he said to the Blessed One,

snp2.12:1.7.verse: “Just now, as I was alone in seclusion, this train of thought arose in my awareness:

snp2.12:1.8.verse: ‘Has my preceptor totally unbound, or has he not totally unbound?’”

snp2.12:1.9.verse: Then, arranging his robe over one shoulder and placing his hands palm-to-palm over his heart toward the Blessed One, Ven. Vaṅgīsa addressed the Blessed One in verses:

snp2.12:2.1.verse: “We ask the Teacher of supreme discernment,

snp2.12:2.2.verse: who has cut off uncertainty in the here-&-now:

snp2.12:2.3.verse: A monk has died at the Aggāḷava shrine—

snp2.12:2.4.verse: well-known, prestigious, with mind fully unbound.

snp2.12:3.2.verse: given by you, Blessed One, to that brahman.

snp2.12:3.3.verse: He went about revering you, intent on release,

snp2.12:3.4.verse: with persistence aroused, seeing the firm Dhamma.

snp2.12:4.2.verse: we all, too, want to know:

snp2.12:4.3.verse: ready to hear are our ears.

snp2.12:4.4.verse: You, our teacher: you are unexcelled.

snp2.12:5.1.verse: Cut through our uncertainty. Tell me this,

snp2.12:5.2.verse: make known, One of discernment deep, that he was totally unbound.

snp2.12:5.3.verse: Speak in our midst, All-around Eye,

snp2.12:5.4.verse: like Thousand-eyed Sakka, in the midst of the devas.3

snp2.12:6.1.verse: Here, whatever snares there are, paths of delusion,

snp2.12:6.2.verse: siding with not-knowing, bases of uncertainty:

snp2.12:6.3.verse: on reaching the Tathāgata, they don’t exist,

snp2.12:6.4.verse: as that Eye is the foremost of men.

snp2.12:7.1.verse: For if no man were ever to disperse defilements—

snp2.12:7.2.verse: as the wind, a dark mass of clouds—

snp2.12:7.3.verse: the whole world would be enveloped in darkness.

snp2.12:7.4.verse: Even brilliant people wouldn’t shine bright.

snp2.12:8.1.verse: But the enlightened are makers of light.

snp2.12:8.2.verse: Thus I think you’re that, enlightened one.

snp2.12:8.3.verse: We have come to one who knows through clear-seeing.

snp2.12:8.4.verse: Make Kappa shine in our assembly.

snp2.12:9.1.verse: Quickly, handsome one, stir your handsome voice.

snp2.12:9.2.verse: Like a swan,4 stretching out (its neck), call gently

snp2.12:9.4.verse: We all listen to you, sitting upright.

snp2.12:10.1.verse: Pleading, I shall get the pure one to speak,

snp2.12:10.2.verse: he whose birth & death are abandoned entirely.

snp2.12:10.3.verse: People run-of-the-mill haven’t the power to bring about what they desire,

snp2.12:10.4.verse: but Tathāgatas have the power to bring about what they have pondered.

snp2.12:11.2.verse: is rightly-grasped, you of discernment rightly straight.

snp2.12:11.4.verse: knowing, don’t delude us, one of discernment supreme.

snp2.12:12.1.verse: Understanding the noble Dhamma from high to low,

snp2.12:12.2.verse: knowing, don’t delude us, hero supreme.

snp2.12:12.3.verse: As if distressed in mind by the heat in the summer,

snp2.12:12.4.verse: I long for the water of your speech: rain down a torrent.5

snp2.12:13.1.verse: Was the holy life he led in line with his aim?

snp2.12:13.2.verse: Kappa—was it not in any way in vain?

snp2.12:13.3.verse: Did he unbind with no fuel remaining?6

snp2.12:13.4.verse: Let us hear how he was released.”

snp2.12:14.1.verse: “Here he cut off craving for name-&-form,

snp2.12:14.3.verse: the current of the Dark One, the long-time obsession.

snp2.12:14.4.verse: He has crossed over birth & death.”

snp2.12:14.5.verse: So spoke the Blessed One, excelling in five.7

snp2.12:15.3.verse: Surely, my question was not in vain,

snp2.12:15.4.verse: nor was I deceived by the brahman.

snp2.12:16.1.verse: As he spoke, so he acted:

snp2.12:16.2.verse: he was a disciple of the One Awakened.

snp2.12:16.3.verse: He has cut through the net

snp2.12:17.4.verse: the realm of Death so very hard to cross.”

snp2.12:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Āḷavī, at Āḷavī’s premier shrine.

snp2.12:1.3.verse: Now at that time it was not long after Venerable Vaṅgīsa’s mentor, the senior monk named Nigrodhakappa, had become fully quenched.

snp2.12:1.4.verse: Then as Vaṅgīsa was in private retreat this thought came to his mind:

snp2.12:1.5.verse: “Has my mentor become quenched or not?”

snp2.12:1.6.verse: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Vaṅgīsa came out of retreat and went to the Buddha. He bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

snp2.12:1.7.verse: “Just now, sir, as I was in private retreat this thought came to mind.

snp2.12:1.8.verse: ‘Has my mentor become quenched or not?’”

snp2.12:1.9.verse: Then Venerable Vaṅgīsa rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha, and addressed him in verse:

snp2.12:2.1.verse: “I ask the Teacher unrivaled in wisdom,

snp2.12:2.2.verse: who has cut off all doubts in this very life:

snp2.12:2.3.verse: a monk has died at Āḷavī’s premier shrine,

snp2.12:2.4.verse: who was well-known, famous, and quenched.

snp2.12:3.2.verse: it was given to that brahmin by you, Blessed One.

snp2.12:3.3.verse: He wandered in your honor, yearning for freedom,

snp2.12:3.4.verse: energetic, a resolute Seer of Truth.

snp2.12:4.2.verse: we all wish to know about that disciple.

snp2.12:4.3.verse: Our ears are eager to hear,

snp2.12:4.4.verse: for you are the most excellent teacher.

snp2.12:5.1.verse: Cut off our doubt, declare this to us;

snp2.12:5.2.verse: your wisdom is vast, tell us of his quenching!

snp2.12:5.4.verse: like the thousand-eyed Sakka in the midst of the gods!

snp2.12:6.1.verse: Whatever ties there are, or paths to delusion,

snp2.12:6.2.verse: or things on the side of unknowing, or that are bases of doubt

snp2.12:6.3.verse: vanish on reaching a Realized One,

snp2.12:6.4.verse: for his eye is the best of all people’s.

snp2.12:7.1.verse: If no man were ever to disperse corruptions,

snp2.12:7.2.verse: like the wind dispersing the stormclouds,

snp2.12:7.3.verse: darkness would shroud the whole world;

snp2.12:7.4.verse: not even brilliant men would shine.

snp2.12:8.1.verse: The attentive are bringers of light;

snp2.12:8.2.verse: my hero, that is what I think of you.

snp2.12:8.3.verse: We’ve come for your discernment and knowledge:

snp2.12:8.4.verse: here in this assembly, declare to us about Kappāyana.

snp2.12:9.1.verse: Swiftly send forth your sweet, sweet voice,

snp2.12:9.2.verse: like a goose stretching its neck, gently honking,

snp2.12:9.4.verse: alert, we all listen to you.

snp2.12:10.1.verse: You have entirely abandoned birth and death;

snp2.12:10.2.verse: curbed and pure, I urge you, speak the Dhamma!

snp2.12:10.3.verse: For ordinary people have no wish-granter,

snp2.12:10.4.verse: but Realized Ones have a comprehensibility-granter.

snp2.12:11.1.verse: Your answer is definitive, and we will adopt it,

snp2.12:11.3.verse: We raise our cupped palms one last time,

snp2.12:11.4.verse: one of unrivaled wisdom, don’t deliberately confuse us.

snp2.12:12.1.verse: Knowing the teaching of the noble ones from top to bottom,

snp2.12:12.2.verse: one of unrivaled energy, don’t deliberately confuse us.

snp2.12:12.3.verse: As a man baking in the summer sun would long for water,

snp2.12:12.4.verse: I long for your voice, so let the sound rain  forth.

snp2.12:13.1.verse: Surely Kappāyana did not lead the spiritual life in vain?

snp2.12:13.3.verse: or did he still have a residue?

snp2.12:13.4.verse: Let us hear what kind of liberation he had!”

snp2.12:14.1.verse: “He cut off craving for name and form right here,”

snp2.12:14.3.verse: “the river of darkness that had long lain within him.

snp2.12:14.4.verse: He has entirely crossed over birth and death.”

snp2.12:14.5.verse: So declared the Blessed One, the leader of the five.

snp2.12:15.1.verse: “Now that I have heard your words,

snp2.12:15.2.verse: seventh of seers, I am confident.

snp2.12:15.3.verse: My question, it seems, was not in vain,

snp2.12:15.4.verse: the brahmin did not deceive me.

snp2.12:16.1.verse: As he said, so he did—

snp2.12:16.2.verse: he was a disciple of the Buddha.

snp2.12:16.3.verse: He cut the net of death the deceiver,

snp2.12:17.3.verse: He has indeed gone far beyond

snp2.12:17.4.verse: Death’s dominion so hard to pass.”

snp2.13:1.1.verse: “I ask the sage of abundant discernment,

snp2.13:1.2.verse: crossed over to the far shore, totally unbound, steadfast in mind:

snp2.13:1.4.verse: how does one wander rightly in the world?”1

snp2.13:2.4.verse: whose fault of omens is completely abandoned:

snp2.13:2.5.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:3.1.verse: A monk should subdue passion for sensualities human

snp2.13:3.3.verse: Having gone past becoming, and met with the Dhamma,

snp2.13:3.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:4.2.verse: a monk should abandon anger & meanness.

snp2.13:4.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:5.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:6.1.verse: He finds no essence in acquisitions,

snp2.13:6.3.verse: independent is he, by others unled:

snp2.13:6.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:7.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:8.1.verse: A monk who’d not gloat, ‘He venerates me,’

snp2.13:8.3.verse: or be elated on receiving food from another:

snp2.13:8.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:9.3.verse: he, having crossed over doubt, de-arrowed,

snp2.13:9.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:10.1.verse: Having found what’s appropriate for himself,

snp2.13:10.2.verse: the monk wouldn’t harm anyone in the world,

snp2.13:10.3.verse: having found the Dhamma as it actually is,

snp2.13:10.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:11.1.verse: In whom there are no obsessions,

snp2.13:11.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:12.2.verse: beyond reach of every road to passion,

snp2.13:12.3.verse: tamed, totally unbound, steadfast in mind:

snp2.13:12.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:13.2.verse: not following factions among those who are factious,

snp2.13:13.3.verse: enlightened; his greed, aversion, & irritation subdued:

snp2.13:13.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:14.1.verse: Victorious, pure, his roof opened up,3

snp2.13:14.2.verse: a master of dhammas, gone beyond & unperturbed,

snp2.13:14.3.verse: skilled in the knowledge of fabrication-cessation:

snp2.13:14.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:15.1.verse: Gone beyond speculations about futures & pasts,

snp2.13:15.2.verse: and—having passed by—purified in his discernment,

snp2.13:15.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.

snp2.13:16.1.verse: Knowing the state, meeting the Dhamma,

snp2.13:16.2.verse: seeing the opened-up, when his effluents are abandoned

snp2.13:16.3.verse: from the ending of all acquisitions:

snp2.13:16.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.”

snp2.13:17.1.verse: “Yes, Blessed One, that’s just how it is.

snp2.13:17.3.verse: gone totally beyond all things conducive for fetters5,

snp2.13:17.4.verse: he would wander rightly in the world.”

snp2.13:1.1.verse: “I ask the sage abounding in wisdom—

snp2.13:1.3.verse: when a mendicant has left home, casting aside sensuality,

snp2.13:1.4.verse: what’s the right way to wander the world?”

snp2.13:2.3.verse: “about celestial portents, dreams, or bodily marks;

snp2.13:2.4.verse: with the stain of superstitions left behind,

snp2.13:3.3.verse: with rebirth transcended and truth comprehended,

snp2.13:4.2.verse: a mendicant gives up anger and stinginess;

snp2.13:4.3.verse: with favoring and opposing left behind,

snp2.13:5.1.verse: When the loved and the unloved are both left behind,

snp2.13:5.2.verse: not grasping or dependent on anything;

snp2.13:5.3.verse: freed from all things that fetter,

snp2.13:6.2.verse: rid of desire for things they’ve acquired,

snp2.13:6.3.verse: independent, needing no one to guide them,

snp2.13:7.1.verse: Not hostile in speech, mind, or deed,

snp2.13:7.3.verse: Aspiring to the state of extinguishment,

snp2.13:8.1.verse: Not gloating that, ‘they bow to me’;

snp2.13:8.2.verse: though reviled, they’d still stay in touch;

snp2.13:8.3.verse: not besotted when getting food from others,

snp2.13:9.1.verse: When greed and craving to live again are cast off,

snp2.13:9.2.verse: a mendicant refrains from violence and abduction;

snp2.13:9.3.verse: rid of indecision, free of thorns,

snp2.13:10.1.verse: Knowing what is suitable for themselves,

snp2.13:10.2.verse: a mendicant would hurt no one in the world;

snp2.13:10.3.verse: understanding the teaching in line with the truth,

snp2.13:11.1.verse: They have no underlying tendencies at all,

snp2.13:11.2.verse: and are rid of unskillful roots;

snp2.13:11.3.verse: free of hope, with no need for hope,

snp2.13:13.1.verse: Faithful, learned, seer of the sure path,

snp2.13:13.2.verse: an attentive one joins no faction among sects;

snp2.13:13.3.verse: rid of greed, hate, and aversion,

snp2.13:14.1.verse: A purified victor with veil cast off,

snp2.13:14.2.verse: among worldly things master, transcendent, stilled;

snp2.13:14.3.verse: expert in knowledge of conditions’ cessation,

snp2.13:15.1.verse: They’re over speculating on the future or past,

snp2.13:15.2.verse: and understand what it means to be pure;

snp2.13:15.3.verse: freed from all the sense fields,

snp2.13:16.1.verse: The state of peace is understood, the truth is comprehended,

snp2.13:16.2.verse: they’ve openly seen defilements cast off;

snp2.13:16.3.verse: and with the ending of all attachments,

snp2.13:17.1.verse: “Clearly, Blessed One, it is just as you say.

snp2.13:17.2.verse: One who lives like this is a tamed mendicant,

snp2.13:17.3.verse: passed beyond all fetters and yokes:

snp2.14:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

snp2.14:1.3.verse: Then Dhammika the lay follower, together with 500 other lay followers, approached the Blessed One and, on arrival, having bowed down to him, sat to one side. As he was sitting there, he addressed the Blessed One in verses:

snp2.14:2.2.verse: How-acting does one become a good disciple—

snp2.14:2.3.verse: either one gone from home into homelessness,

snp2.14:2.4.verse: or a lay follower with a home?

snp2.14:3.1.verse: For you discern the destination & future course

snp2.14:3.2.verse: of the world along with its devas—

snp2.14:3.3.verse: there is no one equal to you in seeing the subtle goal;

snp2.14:3.4.verse: for they call you foremost, awakened.

snp2.14:4.1.verse: Understanding all knowledge, the whole Dhamma,1

snp2.14:4.2.verse: you proclaim it to beings with sympathetic mind.

snp2.14:4.3.verse: Your roof opened up,2 All-around Eye,3

snp2.14:4.4.verse: you, stainless, illumine the whole world.

snp2.14:5.1.verse: He came to your presence—Erāvaṇa, the nāga king,4

snp2.14:5.3.verse: Having consulted with you, having heard, he understood,

snp2.14:6.3.verse: To him, too, you spoke when asked.

snp2.14:6.4.verse: And he too, having heard, was satisfied.

snp2.14:7.1.verse: And these sectarians, debaters by habit,

snp2.14:7.3.verse: don’t overtake you in terms of discernment,

snp2.14:7.4.verse: as a person standing doesn’t catch up with one going quickly.

snp2.14:8.1.verse: And these brahmans, debaters by habit,

snp2.14:8.3.verse: all depend on you for the meaning,

snp2.14:8.4.verse: and any others who consider themselves debaters.

snp2.14:9.1.verse: For this Dhamma is subtle & blissful.

snp2.14:9.2.verse: This, Blessed One, well set-forth by you:

snp2.14:9.3.verse: We all want to hear it.

snp2.14:9.4.verse: Tell it to us, Excellent Awakened, when asked.

snp2.14:10.1.verse: All these monks are sitting together—

snp2.14:10.2.verse: and the lay followers, right there—to hear.

snp2.14:10.3.verse: Let them listen to the Dhamma awakened to by one who is stainless,

snp2.14:10.4.verse: as the devas listen to Vasavant’s6 well-spoken word.”

snp2.14:11.1.verse: “Listen to me, monks. I will let you hear

snp2.14:11.2.verse: the Dhamma of polishing away. Live by it,7 all of you.

snp2.14:11.3.verse: May those who are thoughtful, seeing the purpose,

snp2.14:11.4.verse: partake of the duties proper for one gone forth.

snp2.14:12.1.verse: A monk should surely not wander at the wrong time.

snp2.14:12.2.verse: He should go for alms in the village at the right time.

snp2.14:12.3.verse: For attachments get attached to one going at the wrong time.

snp2.14:12.4.verse: That’s why they don’t wander at the wrong time, the awakened.

snp2.14:13.4.verse: one should, at the right time, enter for alms.

snp2.14:14.1.verse: Having received alms in proper season,

snp2.14:14.2.verse: a monk, returning alone, should sit down in solitude.

snp2.14:14.3.verse: Pondering what’s inside, his mind-state collected,

snp2.14:14.4.verse: he should not let his heart wander outside.

snp2.14:15.1.verse: If he should converse with a disciple,

snp2.14:15.3.verse: he should utter the exquisite Dhamma,

snp2.14:15.4.verse: and not divisive speech or disparagement of others.

snp2.14:16.2.verse: We don’t praise those of limited discernment.

snp2.14:16.3.verse: Attachments get attached on account of this & that,

snp2.14:16.4.verse: for they send their minds far away from there.

snp2.14:17.1.verse: Almsfood, a dwelling, a place to sit & lie down,

snp2.14:17.2.verse: and water for washing dust from his robe—

snp2.14:17.3.verse: having heard the Dhamma taught by the One Well-Gone,

snp2.14:17.4.verse: the disciple of foremost discernment should resort to these, having considered.

snp2.14:18.1.verse: So then, in almsfood, a place to sit & lie down,

snp2.14:18.2.verse: and water for washing dust from his robe—

snp2.14:18.3.verse: a monk should stay unsmeared by these things,

snp2.14:18.4.verse: like a water-drop on a lotus.

snp2.14:19.2.verse: I will tell you how-acting one becomes a good disciple,

snp2.14:19.4.verse: can’t be managed by those wealthy in property.

snp2.14:20.1.verse: One should not kill a living being, nor have it killed,

snp2.14:20.3.verse: laying aside violence toward all living creatures,

snp2.14:20.4.verse: both the firm & unfirm in the world.

snp2.14:21.1.verse: Then the disciple should avoid, consciously,

snp2.14:21.3.verse: should not have it taken nor condone its taking.

snp2.14:21.4.verse: He should avoid all (taking of) what’s not given.

snp2.14:22.1.verse: The observant person should avoid uncelibate behavior

snp2.14:22.2.verse: like a pit of glowing embers.

snp2.14:22.3.verse: But if he’s incapable of celibate behavior,

snp2.14:22.4.verse: he should not transgress with the wife of another.

snp2.14:23.1.verse: When gone to an audience hall or assembly,

snp2.14:23.2.verse: or one-on-one, he should not tell a lie,

snp2.14:23.3.verse: nor have it told, nor condone its being told.

snp2.14:24.1.verse: Any householder who approves of this Dhamma

snp2.14:24.3.verse: nor have others drink it, nor condone its being drunk,

snp2.14:24.4.verse: knowing that it ends in madness.

snp2.14:25.1.verse: For from intoxication, fools do evil things

snp2.14:25.2.verse: and get others, heedless, to do them.

snp2.14:25.3.verse: One should avoid this opening to demerit—

snp2.14:26.1.verse: One should not kill a living being,

snp2.14:26.2.verse: take what’s not given, tell a lie, nor be a drinker.

snp2.14:26.3.verse: One should abstain from uncelibate behavior—sexual intercourse—

snp2.14:26.4.verse: should not eat at night, a meal at the wrong time,

snp2.14:27.1.verse: should not wear a garland or use scents,

snp2.14:27.2.verse: should sleep on a bed, on the ground, or on a mat,

snp2.14:27.3.verse: for this, they say, is the eightfold uposatha,

snp2.14:27.4.verse: proclaimed by the Awakened One who has gone to the end of suffering & stress.

snp2.14:28.2.verse: the eightfold uposatha on the fourteenth, fifteenth, & eighth

snp2.14:28.3.verse: of the fortnight,8 and on special days of the fortnight,

snp2.14:29.1.verse: the observant person at dawn after the uposatha,

snp2.14:29.3.verse: should share food & drink, as is proper,

snp2.14:30.1.verse: One should righteously support mother & father,

snp2.14:30.3.verse: One heedful in this householder protocol

snp2.14:30.4.verse: goes to the devas called Self-radiant.”

snp2.14:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

snp2.14:1.3.verse: Then the lay follower Dhammika, together with five hundred lay followers, went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and addressed him in verse:

snp2.14:2.1.verse: “I ask you, Gotama, whose wisdom is vast:

snp2.14:2.2.verse: what does one do to become a good disciple,

snp2.14:2.3.verse: both one who has left the home,

snp2.14:2.4.verse: and the lay followers staying at home?

snp2.14:3.1.verse: For you understand the course and destiny

snp2.14:3.2.verse: of the world with all its gods.

snp2.14:3.3.verse: There is no equal to you who sees the subtle meaning,

snp2.14:3.4.verse: for you are the Buddha most excellent, they say.

snp2.14:4.2.verse: you reveal the teaching out of sympathy for beings.

snp2.14:4.3.verse: All-seer, you have cast off the veil,

snp2.14:4.4.verse: and immaculate, you dazzle the whole world.

snp2.14:5.1.verse: The dragon king Erāvaṇa, hearing you called ‘Victor’,

snp2.14:5.3.verse: He consulted with you then, having heard your words,

snp2.14:6.2.verse: approached to ask about the teaching.

snp2.14:6.3.verse: You also answered him, O attentive one,

snp2.14:6.4.verse: and hearing you he too was consoled.

snp2.14:7.1.verse: Those monastics of other religions given to debate,

snp2.14:7.3.verse: all fail to overtake you in wisdom,

snp2.14:7.4.verse: like a standing man next to a sprinter.

snp2.14:8.2.verse: some of whom are quite senior,

snp2.14:8.3.verse: all end up beholden to you for the meaning,

snp2.14:8.4.verse: and others too who think themselves debaters.

snp2.14:9.1.verse: So subtle and pleasant is the teaching

snp2.14:9.2.verse: that is well proclaimed by you, Blessed One.

snp2.14:9.3.verse: It’s all we long to hear. So when asked,

snp2.14:9.4.verse: O Best of Buddhas, tell us!

snp2.14:10.2.verse: and the layfolk too are here to listen.

snp2.14:10.3.verse: Let them hear the teaching the immaculate one discovered,

snp2.14:10.4.verse: like gods listening to the fine words of Vāsava.”

snp2.14:11.1.verse: “Listen to me, mendicants, I will educate you

snp2.14:11.2.verse: in the cleansing teaching; all bear it in mind.

snp2.14:11.3.verse: A thoughtful person, seeing the meaning,

snp2.14:11.4.verse: would adopt the deportment proper to a renunciate.

snp2.14:12.1.verse: No way would a mendicant go out at the wrong time;

snp2.14:12.2.verse: at the right time, they’d walk the village for alms.

snp2.14:12.3.verse: For chains bind one who wanders at the wrong time,

snp2.14:12.4.verse: which is why the Buddhas avoid it.

snp2.14:13.1.verse: Sights, sounds, tastes, smells, and touches,

snp2.14:13.4.verse: and enter for the morning meal at the right time.

snp2.14:14.1.verse: After receiving alms for the day,

snp2.14:14.2.verse: on returning a mendicant would sit in private alone.

snp2.14:14.3.verse: Inwardly reflective, they’d curb their mind

snp2.14:14.4.verse: from outside things, keeping themselves collected.

snp2.14:15.1.verse: Should they converse with a disciple,

snp2.14:15.2.verse: with anyone else, or with a mendicant,

snp2.14:15.3.verse: they’d bring up only the sublime teaching,

snp2.14:16.2.verse: but we praise not those of little wisdom.

snp2.14:16.3.verse: In place after place they are bound in chains,

snp2.14:16.4.verse: for they send their mind over there far away.

snp2.14:17.1.verse: Alms, a dwelling, a bed and seat,

snp2.14:17.2.verse: and water for rinsing the dust from the cloak—

snp2.14:17.3.verse: after hearing the teaching of the Holy One,

snp2.14:17.4.verse: a disciple of outstanding wisdom would use these after appraisal.

snp2.14:18.1.verse: That’s why, when it comes to alms and lodgings,

snp2.14:18.2.verse: and water for rinsing the dust from the cloak,

snp2.14:18.3.verse: a mendicant is unsullied in the midst of these things,

snp2.14:18.4.verse: like a droplet on a lotus-leaf.

snp2.14:19.1.verse: Now I shall tell you the householder’s duty,

snp2.14:19.2.verse: doing which one becomes a good disciple.

snp2.14:19.3.verse: For one burdened with possessions does not get to realize

snp2.14:19.4.verse: the whole of the mendicant’s practice.

snp2.14:20.1.verse: They’d not kill any creature, nor have them killed,

snp2.14:20.2.verse: nor grant permission for others to kill.

snp2.14:20.3.verse: They’ve laid aside violence toward all creatures

snp2.14:20.4.verse: frail or firm that there are in the world.

snp2.14:21.1.verse: Next, a disciple would avoid knowingly

snp2.14:21.2.verse: taking anything not given at all,

snp2.14:21.3.verse: they’d not get others to do it, nor grant them permission to steal;

snp2.14:22.1.verse: A sensible person would avoid the unchaste life,

snp2.14:22.2.verse: like a burning pit of coals.

snp2.14:22.3.verse: But if unable to remain chaste,

snp2.14:22.4.verse: they’d not transgress with another’s partner.

snp2.14:23.2.verse: or one on one, they would not lie.

snp2.14:23.3.verse: They’d not get others to lie, nor grant them permission to lie;

snp2.14:24.2.verse: would not consume liquor or drink.

snp2.14:24.3.verse: They’d not get others to drink, nor grant them permission to drink;

snp2.14:25.1.verse: For drunken fools do bad things,

snp2.14:25.4.verse: the maddening, deluding frolic of fools.

snp2.14:26.1.verse: You shouldn’t kill living creatures, or steal,

snp2.14:26.4.verse: and don’t eat at night, the wrong time.

snp2.14:27.1.verse: Not wearing garlands or applying fragrance,

snp2.14:27.2.verse: you should sleep on a low bed, or a mat on the ground.

snp2.14:27.3.verse: This is the eight-factored sabbath, they say,

snp2.14:27.4.verse: revealed by the Buddha, who has gone to suffering’s end.

snp2.14:28.1.verse: Then having rightly undertaken the sabbath

snp2.14:28.2.verse: complete in all its eight factors

snp2.14:28.3.verse: on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and eighth of the fortnight,

snp2.14:28.4.verse: as well as on the fortnightly special displays,

snp2.14:29.2.verse: a clever person, rejoicing with confident heart,

snp2.14:29.4.verse: to the mendicant Saṅgha as is fitting.

snp2.14:30.1.verse: One should rightfully support one’s parents,

snp2.14:30.3.verse: A diligent layperson observing these duties

snp3.1:1.2.verse: how he went forth, the One with Eyes,

snp3.1:2.3.verse: while going forth is the open air,

snp3.1:3.2.verse: he avoided evil deeds in body.

snp3.1:4.1.verse: Then he, the Buddha, went to Rājagaha,

snp3.1:4.2.verse: the mountain fortress of the Magadhans,

snp3.1:5.3.verse: and on seeing him, consummate in marks,

snp3.1:6.4.verse: looking only a plow-length before him,

snp3.1:7.2.verse: This one’s not like one from a lowly lineage:

snp3.1:7.4.verse: to see where this monk will go.”

snp3.1:8.4.verse: Where will his dwelling place be?

snp3.1:9.1.verse: As he went from house to house—

snp3.1:10.1.verse: Then he, the sage, completing his alms round,

snp3.1:10.4.verse: That’s where his dwelling will be.

snp3.1:11.1.verse: Seeing him go to his dwelling place,

snp3.1:12.3.verse: sits like a tiger, a bull,

snp3.1:12.4.verse: a lion in a mountain cleft.”

snp3.1:13.2.verse: the noble-warrior king, by royal coach,

snp3.1:14.1.verse: Going as far as the coach would go,

snp3.1:14.2.verse: the noble-warrior king got down from the coach,

snp3.1:16.2.verse: in the first stage of youth,

snp3.1:17.2.verse: in the vanguard of an army, arrayed with an elephant squadron.

snp3.1:17.3.verse: I offer you wealth: Enjoy it.

snp3.1:17.4.verse: I ask your birth: Inform me.”

snp3.1:18.2.verse: by the foothills of the Himalayas,

snp3.1:18.3.verse: is a country consummate in energy & wealth,

snp3.1:19.3.verse: From that lineage I have gone forth,

snp3.1:19.4.verse: but not in hope of sensuality.

snp3.1:1.2.verse: with the example of the Clear-eyed One,

snp3.1:1.3.verse: the course of inquiry that led to

snp3.1:2.3.verse: ‘The life of one gone forth is like an open space.’

snp3.1:5.3.verse: Noticing that he was endowed with marks,

snp3.1:6.4.verse: he looks just a plough’s length in front.

snp3.1:7.2.verse: unlike one from a low family.

snp3.1:7.3.verse: Let the king’s messengers run out,

snp3.1:7.4.verse: and find where the mendicant will go.’

snp3.1:8.4.verse: Where shall he find a place to stay?’

snp3.1:9.2.verse: sense doors guarded and well restrained,

snp3.1:10.3.verse: He betook himself to Mount Paṇḍava,

snp3.1:10.4.verse: thinking, ‘Here is the place I shall stay.’

snp3.1:11.1.verse: Seeing that he had arrived at a place to stay,

snp3.1:12.2.verse: is on the east flank of Mount Paṇḍava.

snp3.1:12.3.verse: There he sits, like a tiger or a bull,

snp3.1:12.4.verse: like a lion in a mountain cave.’

snp3.1:14.1.verse: He went as far as vehicles could go,

snp3.1:16.2.verse: a lad in the prime of life.

snp3.3:1.5.verse: “Yes, lord,” the monks responded to him.

snp3.3:2.1.verse: “Monks, speech endowed with four characteristics is well-spoken, not poorly spoken—faultless & not to be faulted by the observant.

snp3.3:2.3.verse: There is the case where a monk says only what is well-spoken, not what is poorly spoken; only what is just, not what is unjust; only what is endearing, not what is unendearing; only what is true, not what is false.

snp3.3:2.4.verse: Speech endowed with these four characteristics is well-spoken, not poorly spoken—faultless & not to be faulted by the observant.”

snp3.3:2.5.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

snp3.3:2.6.verse: Having said this, the One Well-Gone, the Teacher, said further:

snp3.3:3.1.verse: “The calm say that what is well-spoken is best;

snp3.3:3.2.verse: second, that one should say what is just, not unjust;

snp3.3:3.4.verse: fourth,          what is true, not false.”

snp3.3:4.1.verse: Then Ven. Vaṅgīsa,1 rising from his seat, arranging his robe over one shoulder, faced the Blessed One with his hands palm-to-palm in front of his heart and said,

snp3.3:4.2.verse: “An inspiration has come to me, Blessed One! An inspiration has come to me, One Well-Gone!”

snp3.3:4.3.verse: “Let the inspiration come to you, Vaṅgīsa,” the Blessed One said.

snp3.3:4.4.verse: Then Ven. Vaṅgīsa praised the Blessed One to his face with these fitting verses:

snp3.3:6.3.verse: Speech when it brings no evil

snp3.3:7.4.verse: —so say the calm— are firmly established on truth.

snp3.3:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

snp3.3:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

snp3.3:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, speech that has four factors is well spoken, not poorly spoken. It’s blameless and is not criticized by sensible people.

snp3.3:2.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant speaks well, not poorly; their speech is principled, not unprincipled; they speak pleasantly, not unpleasantly; and they speak truthfully, not falsely.

snp3.3:2.4.verse: Speech with these four factors is well spoken, not poorly spoken. It’s blameless and is not criticized by sensible people.”

snp3.3:2.5.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

snp3.3:2.6.verse: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

snp3.3:3.1.verse: “Good people say well-spoken words are foremost;

snp3.3:3.2.verse: second, speech ought be principled, not unprincipled;

snp3.3:3.4.verse: and fourth, speak truthfully, not falsely.”

snp3.3:4.1.verse: Then Venerable Vaṅgīsa rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha, and said,

snp3.3:4.2.verse: “I feel inspired to speak, Blessed One! I feel inspired to speak, Holy One!”

snp3.3:4.3.verse: “Then speak as you feel inspired,” said the Buddha.

snp3.3:4.4.verse: Then Vaṅgīsa extolled the Buddha in his presence with fitting verses:

snp3.3:5.4.verse: such speech is truly well spoken.

snp3.3:6.4.verse: that bring nothing bad to others.

snp3.3:7.3.verse: Good people say the teaching and meaning

snp3.3:8.1.verse: The words spoken by the Buddha

snp3.3:8.3.verse: for making an end of suffering,

snp3.3:8.4.verse: this really is the best kind of speech.”

snp3.4:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying among the Kosalans on the bank of the River Sundarikā.

snp3.4:1.3.verse: And on that occasion, the brahman Sundarika Bhāradvāja was offering a fire sacrifice and performing a fire oblation on the bank of the River Sundarikā.

snp3.4:1.4.verse: Then, having offered the fire sacrifice and performed the fire oblation, he got up from his seat and looked around to the four directions, (thinking,)

snp3.4:1.5.verse: “Who should eat the remains of the offering?”

snp3.4:1.6.verse: He saw the Blessed One sitting not far away at the root of a tree with his head covered.

snp3.4:1.7.verse: On seeing him, he took the remains of the offering in his left hand and his water-pot in his right, and went to the Blessed One.

snp3.4:2.1.verse: Then the Blessed One, at the sound of the brahman Sundarika Bhāradvāja’s footsteps, uncovered his head.

snp3.4:2.2.verse: The brahman Sundarika Bhāradvāja (thinking,) “This venerable one is shaven. This venerable one is a shaveling,” wanted to turn back.

snp3.4:2.3.verse: But then the thought occurred to him,

snp3.4:2.4.verse: “Still, there are some brahmans who are shaven. What if, having approached him, I were to ask his caste?”

snp3.4:2.5.verse: So he went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, asked:

snp3.4:3.1.verse: Then the Blessed One addressed the brahman Sundarika Bhāradvāja in verse:

snp3.4:4.1.verse: “I’m not a brahman or king’s son,

snp3.4:4.2.verse: not a merchant, or anyone at all.2

snp3.4:4.3.verse: Comprehending the clan of the run-of-the-mill,3

snp3.4:4.4.verse: having nothing, I wander by means of wisdom in the world.

snp3.4:5.1.verse: Wearing my outer robe, I wander without home,

snp3.4:5.2.verse: my hair     shaven off, my mind          entirely unbound,

snp3.4:5.4.verse: You ask me an inappropriate question about clan.”

snp3.4:6.1.verse: “But, sir, brahmans surely inquire of brahmans,

snp3.4:7.3.verse: I ask you the three lines of the Sāvitti

snp3.4:8.2.verse: did seers, men, noble warriors, & brahmans

snp3.4:8.3.verse: —many of them here in the world— (first) arrange sacrifices to devas?”

snp3.4:9.1.verse: “Whoever has attained the end, an attainer-of-knowledge,

snp3.4:9.2.verse: should receive an oblation at the time of a sacrifice, his (sacrifice), I say, would succeed.”5

snp3.4:10.3.verse: for we have seen an attainer-of-knowledge like you.

snp3.4:10.4.verse: It’s from not seeing those like you

snp3.4:10.5.verse: that someone else eats the sacrificial cake.”

snp3.4:11.1.verse: “Therefore, brahman, as you are seeking your benefit,

snp3.4:11.3.verse: Perhaps you may find here one at peace, with no anger, no desire, no affliction:

snp3.4:12.2.verse: I desire to sacrifice, but I don’t understand

snp3.4:12.4.verse: Teach me, sir. Tell me that.”

snp3.4:13.1.verse: “In that case, brahman, lend ear. I will teach you the Dhamma.

snp3.4:14.1.verse: Don’t inquire about birth.6 Inquire about conduct.

snp3.4:14.2.verse: As from wood, a fire is born,7

snp3.4:14.3.verse: so a sage, even from lowly birth

snp3.4:14.4.verse: —steadfast, restrained through a sense of shame— becomes a thoroughbred.

snp3.4:15.1.verse: One tamed by truth, endowed with self-control,

snp3.4:15.2.verse: attained to the end of knowledge, having fulfilled the holy life:

snp3.4:15.3.verse: To him, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,8

snp3.4:15.4.verse: to him a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.4:16.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.4:16.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.4:17.1.verse: Those devoid of passion, their faculties well-centered,

snp3.4:17.2.verse: released like the moon from the grasp of an eclipse:

snp3.4:17.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.4:17.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.4:18.1.verse: Unattached, they wander in the world,

snp3.4:18.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.4:18.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.4:19.2.verse: who knows the end of birth & death,

snp3.4:19.3.verse: totally unbound, cool as a pool of water:

snp3.4:19.4.verse: The Tathāgata deserves9 the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:20.3.verse: the Tathāgata of infinite discernment, not smeared here or beyond:

snp3.4:20.4.verse: The Tathāgata deserves the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:21.1.verse: In whom no deceptiveness dwells, no conceit,

snp3.4:21.3.verse: his anger dispelled, his mind entirely unbound,

snp3.4:21.4.verse: a brahman who has abandoned the stain of grief:

snp3.4:21.5.verse: The Tathāgata deserves the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:22.1.verse: He has abandoned the homes of the mind,

snp3.4:22.4.verse: The Tathāgata deserves the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:23.1.verse: Centered, he’s crossed over the flood,

snp3.4:23.2.verse: he knows the Dhamma through the highest view,

snp3.4:23.3.verse: effluents ended, bearing his last body:

snp3.4:23.4.verse: The Tathāgata deserves the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:24.1.verse: Whose effluent of becoming and harsh speech

snp3.4:24.2.verse: are destroyed, finished, do not exist—

snp3.4:24.3.verse: he, an attainer-of-knowledge, everywhere totally released10,

snp3.4:24.4.verse: The Tathāgata deserves the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:25.1.verse: Gone beyond snares, for whom there are no snares,

snp3.4:25.2.verse: who, among those attached to conceit, is unattached to conceit,

snp3.4:25.3.verse: comprehending stress along with its field & its site11,

snp3.4:25.4.verse: The Tathāgata deserves the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:26.2.verse: gone beyond the views known by others,

snp3.4:26.3.verse: who has no supports, no mental objects13 at all:

snp3.4:26.4.verse: The Tathāgata deserves the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:27.1.verse: In whom, having understood them, phenomena from high to low

snp3.4:27.2.verse: are destroyed, finished, do not exist14—

snp3.4:27.3.verse: at peace, released in the ending of clinging:

snp3.4:27.4.verse: The Tathāgata deserves the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:28.1.verse: Seeing the end & ending of fetters & birth,

snp3.4:28.2.verse: having dispelled the path of passion without trace,

snp3.4:28.4.verse: The Tathāgata deserves the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:29.1.verse: Who doesn’t contemplate self by means of self,15

snp3.4:29.3.verse: truly unperturbed, free from rigidity, free from doubt:

snp3.4:29.4.verse: The Tathāgata deserves the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:30.1.verse: Who has no conditions for delusion,

snp3.4:30.2.verse: with knowledge & vision of all phenomena

snp3.4:30.4.verse: having attained the unexcelled self-awakening, auspicious—

snp3.4:30.5.verse: to that extent is the purity of a spirit17:

snp3.4:30.6.verse: The Tathāgata deserves the sacrificial cake.”

snp3.4:31.1.verse: “And may my offering be a true offering

snp3.4:31.2.verse: from having obtained an attainer-of-knowledge like you.

snp3.4:31.3.verse: As Brahmā is my witness, may the Blessed One accept,

snp3.4:31.4.verse: may the Blessed One eat, my sacrificial cake.”

snp3.4:32.2.verse: shouldn’t be eaten by me. That’s not the nature, brahman, of one who’s seen rightly.

snp3.4:32.3.verse: What’s been chanted over with verses Awakened Ones reject.

snp3.4:32.4.verse: That being their Dhamma, brahman, this is their way of life.

snp3.4:33.3.verse: his effluents     ended, his anxiety     stilled,

snp3.4:33.4.verse: for that is the field for one looking for merit.”

snp3.4:34.1.verse: “It’s well, Blessed One, how I understand

snp3.4:34.2.verse: who should eat the offering of one like me,

snp3.4:34.3.verse: whom I should seek at the time of sacrifice

snp3.4:36.4.verse: When one like this has come to the sacrifice,

snp3.4:37.1.verse: then, subduing scorn, with hands palm-to-palm

snp3.4:37.4.verse: In this way the offerings will succeed.”

snp3.4:38.3.verse: unexcelled          in all the world, recipient          for all the world21

snp3.4:38.4.verse: deserves          the sacrificial cake. A gift given to you, master, bears great fruit.”

snp3.4:39.1.verse: Then the brahman Sundarika Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One,

snp3.4:39.3.verse: Just as if he were to place upright what was overturned, to reveal what was hidden, to show the way to one who was lost, or to carry a lamp into the dark so that those with eyes could see forms, in the same way has Master Gotama—through many lines of reasoning—made the Dhamma clear.

snp3.4:39.4.verse: I go to Master Gotama for refuge, to the Dhamma, & to the Saṅgha of monks.

snp3.4:39.5.verse: Let me obtain the Going-forth in Master Gotama’s presence, let me obtain Acceptance (into the Bhikkhu Saṅgha).”

snp3.4:39.6.verse: Then the brahman Sundarika Bhāradvāja obtained the Going-forth in the Blessed One’s presence, he obtained Acceptance. And not long after his Acceptance—dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, & resolute—he in no long time reached & remained in the supreme goal of the holy life, for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness, knowing & realizing it for himself in the here-&-now. He knew: “Birth is ended, the holy life fulfilled, the task done. There is nothing further for the sake of this world.”

snp3.4:39.7.verse: And so Ven. Sundarika Bhāradvāja became another one of the arahants.
