snp3.4:39.8.verse: The Sundarika Bhāradvāja Sutta, the fourth.

snp3.4:0.2.verse: With Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā on the Sacrificial Cake

snp3.4:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the Kosalan lands on the bank of the Sundarikā River.

snp3.4:1.3.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā was serving the sacred flame and performing the fire sacrifice on the bank of the Sundarikā.

snp3.4:1.4.verse: Then he rose from his seat and surveyed the four quarters, wondering,

snp3.4:1.5.verse: “Now who might eat the leftovers of this oblation?”

snp3.4:1.6.verse: He saw the Buddha meditating at the root of a certain tree with his robe pulled over his head.

snp3.4:1.7.verse: Taking the leftovers of the oblation in his left hand and a pitcher in the right he approached the Buddha.

snp3.4:2.1.verse: When he heard Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā’s footsteps the Buddha uncovered his head.

snp3.4:2.2.verse: Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā thought, “This man is shaven, he is shaven!” And he wanted to turn back.

snp3.4:2.4.verse: “Even some brahmins are shaven. Why don’t I go to him and ask about his birth?”

snp3.4:2.5.verse: Then the brahmin Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā went up to the Buddha, and said to him,

snp3.4:3.1.verse: Then the Buddha addressed Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā in verse:

snp3.4:4.1.verse: “I am no brahmin, nor am I a ruler,

snp3.4:4.3.verse: Fully understanding the clan of ordinary people,

snp3.4:4.4.verse: I wander in the world owning nothing, reflective.

snp3.4:5.1.verse: Clad in my cloak, I wander without home,

snp3.4:5.3.verse: Since I’m unburdened by sons of Manu,

snp3.4:5.4.verse: it’s inappropriate to ask me about clan.”

snp3.4:6.1.verse: “Actually sir, when brahmins meet they politely

snp3.4:6.2.verse: ask each other whether they are brahmins.”

snp3.4:7.1.verse: “Well, if you say that you’re a brahmin,

snp3.4:7.3.verse: I shall question you on that Sāvitrī Prayer,

snp3.4:7.4.verse: with its three lines and twenty-four syllables.”

snp3.4:8.1.verse: “On what grounds have seers and men,

snp3.4:8.2.verse: aristocrats and brahmins here in the world

snp3.4:8.3.verse: performed so many different sacrifices to the gods?”

snp3.4:9.1.verse: “During a sacrifice, should a past-master, a knowledge master,

snp3.4:9.2.verse: receive an oblation, it profits the donor, I say.”

snp3.4:10.1.verse: “Then clearly my oblation will be profitable,”

snp3.4:10.3.verse: “since I have met such a knowledge master.

snp3.4:10.4.verse: It’s because I’d never met anyone like you

snp3.4:10.5.verse: that others ate the sacrificial cake.”

snp3.4:11.1.verse: “So then, brahmin, since you have approached me

snp3.4:11.2.verse: as a seeker of the good, ask.

snp3.4:11.3.verse: Perhaps you may find here someone intelligent,

snp3.4:11.4.verse: peaceful, unclouded, untroubled, with no need for hope.”

snp3.4:12.2.verse: and wish to perform a sacrifice. Please advise me,

snp3.4:12.4.verse: where an oblation is profitable; tell me this.”

snp3.4:13.1.verse: “Well then, brahmin, listen up, I will teach you the Dhamma.

snp3.4:14.1.verse: Don’t ask about birth, ask about conduct;

snp3.4:14.2.verse: for the fire of Jātaveda is born from sticks.

snp3.4:14.3.verse: A steadfast sage, even though from a low class family,

snp3.4:14.4.verse: is a thoroughbred checked by conscience.

snp3.4:15.1.verse: Tamed by truth, fulfilled by taming,

snp3.4:15.2.verse: a complete knowledge master who has completed the spiritual journey—

snp3.4:15.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.4:15.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.4:16.1.verse: Those who have left sensuality behind, wandering homeless,

snp3.4:16.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.4:16.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.4:17.1.verse: Those freed of greed, with senses stilled,

snp3.4:17.2.verse: like the moon released from the eclipse—

snp3.4:17.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.4:17.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.4:18.2.verse: always mindful, calling nothing their own—

snp3.4:18.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.4:18.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.4:19.1.verse: Having left sensuality behind, wandering triumphant,

snp3.4:19.2.verse: knowing the end of rebirth and death,

snp3.4:19.3.verse: quenched and cool as a lake:

snp3.4:19.4.verse: the Realized One is worthy of the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:20.1.verse: Good among the good, far from the bad,

snp3.4:20.2.verse: the Realized One has infinite wisdom.

snp3.4:20.3.verse: Unsullied in this life and the next:

snp3.4:20.4.verse: the Realized One is worthy of the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:21.1.verse: In whom dwells no deceit or conceit,

snp3.4:21.2.verse: rid of greed, unselfish, with no need for hope,

snp3.4:21.4.verse: a brahmin rid of sorrow’s stain:

snp3.4:21.5.verse: the Realized One is worthy of the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:22.1.verse: He has given up the mind’s home,

snp3.4:22.2.verse: and has no possessions at all.

snp3.4:22.3.verse: Not grasping to this life or the next:

snp3.4:22.4.verse: the Realized One is worthy of the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:23.1.verse: Serene, he has crossed the flood,

snp3.4:23.2.verse: and has understood the teaching with ultimate view.

snp3.4:23.3.verse: With defilements ended, bearing his final body:

snp3.4:23.4.verse: the Realized One is worthy of the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:24.1.verse: In whom desire to be reborn, and caustic speech

snp3.4:24.2.verse: are cleared and ended, and are no more;

snp3.4:24.4.verse: the Realized One is worthy of the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:25.1.verse: He has slipped his chains, he’s chained no more,

snp3.4:25.2.verse: among those caught in conceit he is free of conceit;

snp3.4:25.3.verse: he has fully understood suffering with its field and ground:

snp3.4:25.4.verse: the Realized One is worthy of the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:26.1.verse: Not relying on hope, seeing seclusion,

snp3.4:26.2.verse: well past the views proclaimed by others.

snp3.4:26.3.verse: In him there are no supporting conditions at all:

snp3.4:26.4.verse: the Realized One is worthy of the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:27.1.verse: He has comprehended all things, high and low,

snp3.4:27.2.verse: cleared them and ended them, so they are no more.

snp3.4:27.3.verse: Peaceful, freed in the ending of grasping:

snp3.4:27.4.verse: the Realized One is worthy of the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:28.1.verse: He sees the ending of rebirth’s fetter,

snp3.4:28.2.verse: and has cast aside all manner of desire.

snp3.4:28.4.verse: the Realized One is worthy of the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:29.1.verse: Not seeing himself in terms of a self,

snp3.4:29.2.verse: he is stilled, sincere, and steadfast.

snp3.4:29.4.verse: the Realized One is worthy of the sacrificial cake.

snp3.4:30.1.verse: He harbors no delusions within at all,

snp3.4:30.2.verse: he has insight into all things.

snp3.4:30.4.verse: attained to the state of grace, the supreme awakening.

snp3.4:30.5.verse: That’s how the purity of a spirit is defined:

snp3.4:30.6.verse: the Realized One is worthy of the sacrificial cake.”

snp3.4:31.1.verse: “Let my oblation be a true offering,

snp3.4:31.2.verse: since I have found such a knowledge master!

snp3.4:31.3.verse: I see divinity in person! Accept my offering, Blessed One:

snp3.4:32.1.verse: “Food enchanted by a verse isn’t fit for me to eat.

snp3.4:32.2.verse: That’s not the principle of those who see, brahmin.

snp3.4:32.3.verse: The Buddhas cast aside things enchanted with verses.

snp3.4:32.4.verse: Since there is such a principle, brahmin, that’s how they live.

snp3.4:33.1.verse: Serve with other food and drink

snp3.4:33.2.verse: the consummate one, the great seer,

snp3.4:33.3.verse: with defilements ended and remorse stilled.

snp3.4:33.4.verse: For he is the field for the seeker of merit.”

snp3.4:34.2.verse: now that I have found your teaching,

snp3.4:34.3.verse: when I look for someone during a sacrifice,

snp3.4:34.4.verse: who should eat the religious donation of one like me?”

snp3.4:35.3.verse: who is liberated from sensual pleasures,

snp3.4:35.4.verse: and who has cast aside dullness.

snp3.4:36.1.verse: One who has erased perimeters and limits,

snp3.4:36.4.verse: When such a person comes to the sacrifice,

snp3.4:37.3.verse: and venerate them with food and drink,

snp3.4:37.4.verse: and in this way your religious donation will succeed.”

snp3.4:38.1.verse: “The Buddha is worthy of the sacrificial cake,

snp3.4:38.2.verse: he is the supreme field of merit,

snp3.4:38.3.verse: recipient of gifts from the whole world;

snp3.4:38.4.verse: what’s given to the worthy one is very fruitful.”

snp3.4:39.1.verse: Then the brahmin Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā said to the Buddha,

snp3.4:39.3.verse: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

snp3.4:39.4.verse: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

snp3.4:39.5.verse: May I receive the going forth, the ordination in the worthy Gotama’s presence?”

snp3.4:39.6.verse: And the brahmin Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

snp3.4:39.7.verse: And soon after, he became one of the perfected.

snp3.5:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Rājagaha on Vulture Peak Mountain.

snp3.5:1.3.verse: Then the young brahman Māgha went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, exchanged courteous greetings with him.

snp3.5:1.4.verse: After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, he sat to one side.

snp3.5:1.5.verse: As he was sitting there, he said to the Blessed One,

snp3.5:2.1.verse: “Master Gotama, I am generous, a master of giving, magnanimous, responsive to requests.

snp3.5:2.3.verse: Having searched for wealth righteously, then—with wealth righteously gained, righteously acquired—I give to one, I give to two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, one hundred, and to more.

snp3.5:2.4.verse: Thus giving, thus sacrificing, do I produce much merit?”

snp3.5:3.1.verse: “Certainly, young man, thus giving, thus sacrificing, you produce much merit.

snp3.5:3.2.verse: Anyone who is generous, a master of giving, magnanimous, responsive to requests,

snp3.5:3.4.verse: and, having searched for wealth righteously, then—with wealth righteously gained, righteously acquired—gives to one, to two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, one hundred, and to more, produces much merit.”

snp3.5:3.5.verse: Then the young brahman Māgha addressed the Blessed One in verse:

snp3.5:4.3.verse: wearing ochre robes, wandering without home:

snp3.5:4.4.verse: When a householder responsive to requests, a master of giving,

snp3.5:4.5.verse: makes a sacrifice in hopes of merit, looking for merit,

snp3.5:4.6.verse: giving food & drink to others here,

snp3.5:4.7.verse: how is the offering purified for the one making the sacrifice?”

snp3.5:5.1.verse: “When a householder responsive to requests, a master of giving,

snp3.5:5.3.verse: makes a sacrifice in hopes of merit, looking for merit,

snp3.5:5.4.verse: giving food & drink to others here:

snp3.5:5.5.verse: Such a person achieves his aim in terms of the recipient.”

snp3.5:6.1.verse: “When a householder responsive to requests, a master of giving,

snp3.5:6.3.verse: makes a sacrifice in hopes of merit, looking for merit,

snp3.5:6.4.verse: giving food & drink to others here:

snp3.5:6.5.verse: Point out to me the recipient.”

snp3.5:7.1.verse: “Those who, unadhering,1 wander in the world,

snp3.5:7.2.verse: having nothing, fully accomplished, their minds restrained:

snp3.5:7.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:7.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.5:8.1.verse: Those who have cut all fetters & bonds,

snp3.5:8.2.verse: tamed, released, with no afflictions, no desires:

snp3.5:8.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:8.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.5:9.1.verse: Those released from all fetters & bonds,

snp3.5:9.2.verse: tamed, released, with no afflictions, no desires:

snp3.5:9.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:9.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.5:10.2.verse: their holy life fulfilled, their effluents ended:

snp3.5:10.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:10.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.5:11.1.verse: Those in whom no deceptiveness dwells, no conceit,

snp3.5:11.2.verse: their holy life fulfilled, their effluents ended:

snp3.5:11.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:11.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.5:12.1.verse: Those devoid of greed, unpossessive, undesiring,

snp3.5:12.2.verse: their holy life fulfilled, their effluents ended:

snp3.5:12.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:12.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.5:13.1.verse: Those who aren’t prey to cravings,

snp3.5:13.2.verse: who wander without possessiveness, having crossed over the flood:

snp3.5:13.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:13.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.5:15.1.verse: Those who, having abandoned sensuality, wander without home,

snp3.5:15.2.verse: their minds well-restrained, straight as a shuttle:

snp3.5:15.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:15.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.5:16.1.verse: Those devoid of passion, their faculties well-centered,

snp3.5:16.2.verse: released like the moon from the grasp of an eclipse:

snp3.5:16.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:16.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.5:17.1.verse: Having calmed themselves, those devoid of passion, unprovoked,

snp3.5:17.2.verse: who have no (future) destinations, having abandoned them here:

snp3.5:17.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:17.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.5:18.1.verse: Having abandoned birth & death without trace,

snp3.5:18.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:18.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.5:19.1.verse: They who, with themselves as refuge, wander in the world,

snp3.5:19.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:19.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.5:20.1.verse: They who know here, as it really is—

snp3.5:20.2.verse: ‘This is the last birth, there is no further becoming’:

snp3.5:20.3.verse: To them, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:20.4.verse: to them a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.

snp3.5:21.1.verse: An attainer-of-knowledge,2 delighting in jhāna, mindful,

snp3.5:21.2.verse: attained to self-awakening, the refuge of many:

snp3.5:21.3.verse: To him, at the right time, you should bestow an offering,

snp3.5:21.4.verse: to him a brahman aiming at merit should sacrifice.”

snp3.5:22.1.verse: “Yes, my question was not in vain.

snp3.5:22.3.verse: You, Blessed One, have pointed out the recipient.

snp3.5:22.4.verse: You know this here, as it really is,

snp3.5:22.5.verse: because this Dhamma has been experienced by you.

snp3.5:23.1.verse: When a householder responsive to requests, a master of giving,

snp3.5:23.2.verse: makes a sacrifice in hopes of merit, looking for merit,

snp3.5:23.3.verse: giving food & drink to others here:

snp3.5:23.4.verse: Point out to me, Blessed One, the consummation of the sacrifice.”

snp3.5:24.4.verse: For one sacrificing, the sacrifice is the object, the support.3

snp3.5:24.5.verse: Taking a stand there, he abandons faults.4

snp3.5:25.2.verse: developing a mind of goodwill, immeasurable;

snp3.5:25.4.verse: should pervade all the directions immeasurably.”

snp3.5:26.2.verse: By means of what mind does one go to the Brahmā world?

snp3.5:26.3.verse: Say this, sage, when asked by me who doesn’t know.

snp3.5:26.4.verse: As the Blessed One is my witness, I have seen Brahmā today,

snp3.5:26.5.verse: for you are equal to Brahmā for us—it’s true!

snp3.5:26.6.verse: How, shining one, does one reappear in the Brahmā world?”

snp3.5:27.1.verse: “Whoever sacrifices with the threefold sacrifice consummation,5

snp3.5:27.3.verse: such a one would achieve his aim in terms of the recipient.

snp3.5:27.4.verse: Having thus sacrificed rightly, one responsive to requests

snp3.5:27.5.verse: reappears, I say, in the Brahmā world.”5

snp3.5:28.1.verse: When this was said, the young brahman Māgha said to the Blessed One:

snp3.5:28.2.verse: “Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent! Just as if he were to place upright what was overturned, to reveal what was hidden, to show the way to one who was lost, or to carry a lamp into the dark so that those with eyes could see forms, in the same way has Master Gotama—through many lines of reasoning—made the Dhamma clear. I go to Master Gotama for refuge, to the Dhamma, & to the Saṅgha of monks. May Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge

snp3.5:28.3.verse: from this day forward, for life.”

snp3.5:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

snp3.5:1.3.verse: Then the student Māgha approached the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

snp3.5:1.4.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side,

snp3.5:2.1.verse: “I’m a giver, worthy Gotama, a donor; I am bountiful and committed to charity.

snp3.5:2.2.verse: I seek wealth in a principled manner,

snp3.5:2.3.verse: and with that legitimate wealth I give to one person, to two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred people or even more.

snp3.5:2.4.verse: Giving and sacrificing like this, worthy Gotama, do I brim with much merit?”

snp3.5:3.2.verse: A giver or donor who is bountiful and committed to charity,

snp3.5:3.3.verse: who seeks wealth in a principled manner,

snp3.5:3.4.verse: and with that legitimate wealth gives to one person, or up to a hundred people or even more, brims with much merit.”

snp3.5:3.5.verse: Then Māgha addressed the Buddha in verse:

snp3.5:4.4.verse: Suppose a lay donor who is committed to charity

snp3.5:4.5.verse: makes a sacrifice seeking merit, looking for merit,

snp3.5:4.6.verse: giving food and drink to others here:

snp3.5:5.1.verse: “Suppose a lay donor who is committed to charity,”

snp3.5:5.3.verse: “makes a sacrifice seeking merit, looking for merit,

snp3.5:5.4.verse: giving food and drink to others here:

snp3.5:5.5.verse: such a one would succeed due to those who are worthy of donations.”

snp3.5:6.1.verse: “Suppose a lay donor who is committed to charity,”

snp3.5:6.3.verse: “makes a sacrifice seeking merit, looking for merit,

snp3.5:6.4.verse: giving food and drink to others here:

snp3.5:6.5.verse: explain to me who is worthy of donations.”

snp3.5:7.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:7.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:8.1.verse: Those who have cut off all fetters and bonds,

snp3.5:8.2.verse: tamed, liberated, untroubled, with no need for hope:

snp3.5:8.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:8.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:9.1.verse: Those who are released from all fetters,

snp3.5:9.2.verse: tamed, liberated, untroubled, with no need for hope:

snp3.5:9.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:9.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:10.1.verse: Having given up greed, hate, and delusion,

snp3.5:10.2.verse: with defilements ended, the spiritual journey completed:

snp3.5:10.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:10.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:11.1.verse: Those in whom dwells no deceit or conceit,

snp3.5:11.2.verse: with defilements ended, the spiritual journey completed:

snp3.5:11.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:11.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:12.1.verse: Those rid of greed, unselfish, with no need for hope,

snp3.5:12.2.verse: with defilements ended, the spiritual journey completed:

snp3.5:12.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:12.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:13.1.verse: Those not fallen prey to cravings,

snp3.5:13.2.verse: who, having crossed the flood, live unselfishly:

snp3.5:13.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:13.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:14.1.verse: Those with no craving at all in the world

snp3.5:14.2.verse: for any state of existence in this life or the next:

snp3.5:14.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:14.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:15.1.verse: Those who have left sensuality behind, wandering homeless,

snp3.5:15.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:15.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:16.1.verse: Those freed of greed, with senses stilled,

snp3.5:16.2.verse: like the moon released from the eclipse:

snp3.5:16.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:16.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:17.1.verse: Those assuaged ones free of greed and anger,

snp3.5:17.2.verse: for whom there are no destinies, being rid of them in this life:

snp3.5:17.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:17.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:18.1.verse: They’ve given up rebirth and death completely,

snp3.5:18.2.verse: and have gone beyond all indecision:

snp3.5:18.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:18.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:19.1.verse: Those who live as their own island,

snp3.5:19.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:19.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:20.1.verse: Those here who know this to be true:

snp3.5:20.2.verse: ‘This is my last life, there are no future lives’:

snp3.5:20.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:20.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.

snp3.5:21.1.verse: A knowledge master, loving absorption, mindful,

snp3.5:21.2.verse: who has reached awakening and is a refuge for many:

snp3.5:21.3.verse: that is where a brahmin seeking merit

snp3.5:21.4.verse: should bestow a timely oblation as sacrifice.”

snp3.5:22.1.verse: “Clearly my questions were not in vain!”

snp3.5:22.3.verse: “The Buddha has explained to me who is worthy of donations.

snp3.5:22.4.verse: You are the one here who knows this to be true,

snp3.5:22.5.verse: for truly you understand this matter.

snp3.5:23.1.verse: Suppose a lay donor who is committed to charity

snp3.5:23.2.verse: makes a sacrifice seeking merit, looking for merit,

snp3.5:23.3.verse: giving food and drink to others here:

snp3.5:23.4.verse: explain to me how to accomplish the sacrifice.”

snp3.5:24.3.verse: “be clear and confident in every way.

snp3.5:24.4.verse: Sacrifice is the ground standing upon which

snp3.5:25.1.verse: One free of greed, rid of anger,

snp3.5:25.2.verse: developing a heart of limitless love,

snp3.5:25.3.verse: spreads that limitlessness in every direction,

snp3.5:26.2.verse: How can one go to the realm of divinity oneself?

snp3.5:26.3.verse: I do not know, so please tell me when asked,

snp3.5:26.4.verse: for the Buddha is the divinity I see in person today!

snp3.5:26.5.verse: To us you are truly the equal of divinity.

snp3.5:26.6.verse: Brilliant One, how is one reborn in the realm of divinity?”

snp3.5:27.1.verse: “One who accomplishes the sacrifice with three modes,”

snp3.5:27.3.verse: “such a one would succeed due to those who are worthy of donations.

snp3.5:27.4.verse: Sacrificing like this, one rightly committed to charity

snp3.5:27.5.verse: is reborn in the realm of divinity, I say.”

snp3.5:28.1.verse: When he had spoken, the student Māgha said to the Buddha,

snp3.5:28.3.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

snp3.6:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Forest, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary.

snp3.6:1.3.verse: Now on that occasion, questions had been assigned to Sabhiya the wanderer by a devatā who was a former relative of his:

snp3.6:1.4.verse: “Sabhiya, if any contemplative or brahman, when asked these questions, answers them, live the holy life in his presence.”

snp3.6:2.1.verse: Then Sabhiya the wanderer, having learned these questions in the presence of that devatā, went to those who had communities & groups, who were the teachers of groups, well-known, prestigious, founders of sects, well-regarded by people at large—i.e.,

snp3.6:2.2.verse: Pūraṇa Kassapa, Makkhali Gosāla, Ajita Kesakambalin, Pakudha Kaccāyana, Sañjaya Velaṭṭhaputta, & the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta—

snp3.6:2.4.verse: But they, being asked the questions by Sabhiya the wanderer, were unable to answer.

snp3.6:2.5.verse: Unable to answer, they showed anger, aversion, & displeasure,

snp3.6:2.6.verse: and even turned the questions back on Sabhiya the wanderer.

snp3.6:3.1.verse: The thought occurred to Sabhiya the wanderer,

snp3.6:3.2.verse: “These venerable contemplatives & brahmans with communities & groups, who are the teachers of groups, well-known, prestigious, founders of sects, well-regarded by people at large—i.e.,

snp3.6:3.4.verse: when asked these questions by me are unable to answer.

snp3.6:3.5.verse: Unable to answer, they show anger, aversion, & displeasure;

snp3.6:3.6.verse: and even turn the questions back on me.

snp3.6:3.7.verse: What if I were to revert to the lower life and partake of sensual pleasures?”

snp3.6:4.1.verse: But then the thought occurred to him,

snp3.6:4.2.verse: “There is still this Gotama the contemplative. He has a community & group, he is the teacher of a group, well-known, prestigious, founder of a sect, well-regarded by people at large.

snp3.6:4.3.verse: What if I, having gone to him, were to ask him these questions?”

snp3.6:5.1.verse: Then the thought occurred to Sabhiya the wanderer,

snp3.6:5.2.verse: “Now, those venerable contemplatives & brahmans—old, elderly, aged, along in their years, at an advanced stage of life, elders, senior, long gone forth, with communities & groups, teachers of groups, well-known, prestigious, founders of sects, well-regarded by people at large—i.e.,

snp3.6:5.4.verse: even they, when asked these questions by me, were unable to answer.

snp3.6:5.5.verse: Unable to answer, they showed anger, aversion, & displeasure, and even turned the questions back on me.

snp3.6:5.6.verse: So how could this Gotama the contemplative answer when asked these questions?

snp3.6:5.7.verse: He is both young in age and newly gone forth.”

snp3.6:6.1.verse: But then the thought occurred to him,

snp3.6:6.2.verse: “Gotama the contemplative is not to be despised as ‘young’ or treated with contempt.

snp3.6:6.3.verse: Even though young, he is of great power & great might.1 What if I, having gone to him, were to ask him these questions?”

snp3.6:7.1.verse: So Sabhiya the wanderer set out, headed for Rājagaha.

snp3.6:7.2.verse: Wandering by stages, he arrived at where the Blessed One was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Forest, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary. On arrival, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Blessed One.

snp3.6:7.3.verse: After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, he sat to one side.

snp3.6:7.4.verse: As he was sitting there, he addressed the Blessed One in verse:

snp3.6:8.4.verse: Put an end to them, when asked them by me.

snp3.6:8.5.verse: Answer me     one-by-one, in line with the Dhamma.”

snp3.6:9.4.verse: I will put an end to them, when asked them by you.

snp3.6:9.5.verse: I will answer you     one-by-one, in line with the Dhamma.

snp3.6:11.1.verse: Then the thought occurred to Sabhiya the wanderer,

snp3.6:11.3.verse: how even the leave, of which I didn’t receive even a little bit from other contemplatives & brahmans, has been granted to me by Gotama the contemplative.”

snp3.6:11.4.verse: Gratified, joyful, exultant, enraptured, & happy, he asked the Blessed One a question:

snp3.6:12.1.verse: “Having attained what is one said to be a monk?

snp3.6:12.3.verse: In what way is one composed? And how is one said to be tamed?

snp3.6:12.5.verse: Answer, Blessed One, when I’ve asked you.”

snp3.6:13.1.verse: “By means of the path accomplished by himself,

snp3.6:13.3.verse: having gone to total unbinding, having crossed over doubt;

snp3.6:13.5.verse: having fulfilled [the task], further-becoming ended: He is a monk.2

snp3.6:14.2.verse: he harms no one in all the world.

snp3.6:14.4.verse: he has no swellings3: He is composed.

snp3.6:15.2.verse: within & without, with regard to all the world,4

snp3.6:15.3.verse: disenchanted with this world & the next,

snp3.6:15.4.verse: he awaits his time,5 developed: He’s tamed.

snp3.6:16.3.verse: having done away with dust & blemish —pure—

snp3.6:16.4.verse: he has attained the ending of birth: He is called awakened.”6

snp3.6:17.1.verse: Then Sabhiya the wanderer—delighting in and approving of the Blessed One’s words—gratified, joyful, exultant, enraptured & happy, asked the Blessed One a further question:

snp3.6:18.1.verse: “Having attained what is one said to be a brahman?

snp3.6:18.3.verse: In what way is one a contemplative, and how is one ‘washed’?

snp3.6:18.4.verse: How is one called a nāga?

snp3.6:18.5.verse: Answer, Blessed One, when I’ve asked you.”

snp3.6:19.5.verse: independent, Such: He’s called a brahman.

snp3.6:20.2.verse: dustless, having known this world & the next,

snp3.6:20.4.verse: he is truly called a contemplative8— Such.

snp3.6:21.2.verse: within & without, in     all the world,

snp3.6:21.3.verse: with regard to the theories of beings human & divine,

snp3.6:21.4.verse: he goes to no theory: He’s said to be ‘washed.’9

snp3.6:22.1.verse: He does no misdeed10 at all in the world.

snp3.6:22.4.verse: truly he’s called a nāga— Such.”

snp3.6:23.1.verse: Then Sabhiya the wanderer—delighting in and approving of the Blessed One’s words—gratified, joyful, exultant, enraptured & happy, asked the Blessed One a further question:

snp3.6:24.1.verse: “Whom do the awakened call a field-victor?

snp3.6:24.3.verse: In what way is one skilled and how is one wise?

snp3.6:24.4.verse: And how is one called by the name of ‘sage’?

snp3.6:24.5.verse: Answer, Blessed One, when I’ve asked you.”

snp3.6:25.3.verse: heavenly, human, and fields of the Brahmās—

snp3.6:25.4.verse: freed from the root bonds of all fields,

snp3.6:25.5.verse: he’s truly called a field-victor— Such.

snp3.6:26.3.verse: freed from the root bonds of all storehouses,

snp3.6:27.2.verse: within & without, one of pure discernment

snp3.6:28.2.verse: within & without, in all the world,

snp3.6:28.3.verse: he is worshipped by beings human & divine.

snp3.6:28.4.verse: Having transcended snares & nets, he is a sage.”

snp3.6:29.1.verse: Then Sabhiya the wanderer—delighting in and approving of the Blessed One’s words—gratified, joyful, exultant, enraptured & happy, asked the Blessed One a further question:

snp3.6:30.1.verse: “Having attained what is one said to be an attainer-of-knowledge?

snp3.6:30.3.verse: In what way is one well-tested, and how is one persistent?

snp3.6:30.4.verse: Why is one named a thoroughbred?

snp3.6:30.5.verse: Answer, Blessed One, when I’ve asked you.”

snp3.6:31.3.verse: those of contemplatives, those of brahmans—

snp3.6:31.4.verse: devoid of passion for all feelings,14

snp3.6:31.5.verse: gone beyond knowledge: He’s an attainer-of-knowledge.

snp3.6:32.2.verse: within & without, the root of disease,

snp3.6:32.3.verse: freed from the root bond of disease,

snp3.6:33.2.verse: gone beyond the suffering of hell, he’s one with persistence.

snp3.6:33.4.verse: is rightly called a hero16— Such.

snp3.6:34.1.verse: One truly whose bonds are cut

snp3.6:34.2.verse: within & without, the root of snares,

snp3.6:34.3.verse: freed from all the root bonds of snares,

snp3.6:34.4.verse: truly he’s called a thoroughbred— Such.”

snp3.6:35.1.verse: Then Sabhiya the wanderer—delighting in and approving of the Blessed One’s words—gratified, joyful, exultant, enraptured & happy, asked the Blessed One a further question:

snp3.6:36.1.verse: “Having attained what is one said to be learned?

snp3.6:36.3.verse: In what way is one noble, and how is one a person of good conduct?

snp3.6:36.4.verse: Why is one named a wanderer?

snp3.6:36.5.verse: Answer, Blessed One, when I’ve asked you.”

snp3.6:37.1.verse: “Having heard, having directly known every Dhamma for the sake of direct knowing17 in the world,

snp3.6:37.4.verse: having conquered, free of doubt, released

snp3.6:37.5.verse: everywhere, everywhere without trouble, one is said to be learned.18

snp3.6:38.2.verse: knowing, he does not come to lie in the womb,

snp3.6:38.3.verse: dispelling mud and the three types of perception,19

snp3.6:38.4.verse: he goes to no theory: He is called noble.

snp3.6:39.1.verse: Whoever here has attained attainment with regard to good conduct,

snp3.6:39.2.verse: all-skillful, who has learned the Dhamma,

snp3.6:39.3.verse: unattached everywhere, everywhere his mind released,

snp3.6:39.4.verse: he has no irritation: He is one of good conduct.

snp3.6:40.1.verse: Avoiding whatever action there is that ripens in suffering & stress

snp3.6:40.2.verse: —above, below, and even all around in the middle—

snp3.6:40.4.verse: he has put an all-around end to deceptiveness, conceit, greed, anger,

snp3.6:40.6.verse: He’s called a wanderer, attained to attainment.”20

snp3.6:41.1.verse: Then Sabhiya the wanderer—delighting in and approving of the Blessed One’s words—gratified, joyful, exultant, enraptured & happy—got up from his seat and, arranging his upper robe over his shoulder and placing his hands palm-to-palm over his heart toward the Blessed One, praised the Blessed One face-to-face with fitting verses:

snp3.6:42.1.verse: “Of the three & the sixty views leading downward,21

snp3.6:42.2.verse: resting on the teachings of contemplatives, O Deeply Discerning,

snp3.6:42.3.verse: dependent on perceptions & words of perceptions,

snp3.6:42.4.verse: you have dispelled them and crossed the flood of darkness.

snp3.6:43.1.verse: You have gone     to the end, you have gone     to the further shore of suffering & stress.

snp3.6:43.2.verse: You are a noble one, rightly self-awakened. I would imagine that you have ended the effluents.

snp3.6:43.4.verse: ender of suffering, you have brought me across.

snp3.6:44.1.verse: When you learned of my doubt,

snp3.6:44.2.verse: you brought me across my uncertainty. Homage to you,

snp3.6:44.3.verse: sage attained to the attainment of sagacity’s ways.

snp3.6:44.4.verse: Free from rigidity, Kinsman of the Sun, you’re composed.

snp3.6:45.2.verse: you have answered, One with Eyes.

snp3.6:45.3.verse: Yes, you are a sage, rightly self-awakened.

snp3.6:47.1.verse: In your words, Nāga of nāgas,

snp3.6:48.1.verse: Homage to you, O thoroughbred man,

snp3.6:48.2.verse: Homage to you, O superlative man,23

snp3.6:48.3.verse: in the world with its devas

snp3.6:48.4.verse: there’s no one to compare with you.24

snp3.6:49.2.verse: You: Sage who has conquered Māra.

snp3.6:49.4.verse: having crossed over, bring this generation across.

snp3.6:50.3.verse: you are a lion free of clinging,

snp3.6:51.6.verse: Sabhiya venerates them, the feet of the Teacher.25”

snp3.6:52.1.verse: Then Sabhiya the wanderer, bending his head to the Blessed One’s feet, said to him:

snp3.6:52.2.verse: “Magnificent, lord! Magnificent! Just as if he were to place upright what was overturned, to reveal what was hidden, to show the way to one who was lost, or to set out a lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes could see forms, in the same way has the Blessed One—through many lines of reasoning—made the Dhamma clear.

snp3.6:52.3.verse: I go to the Blessed One for refuge, to the Dhamma, & to the Saṅgha of monks.

snp3.6:52.4.verse: Let me obtain the Going-forth in the Blessed One’s presence, let me obtain Acceptance.”

snp3.6:53.1.verse: “Anyone, Sabhiya, who has previously belonged to another sect and who desires the Going-forth & Acceptance into this Dhamma & Vinaya, must first undergo probation for four months. If, at the end of four months, the monks feel so moved, they give him the Going-forth & accept him into the monk’s state.

snp3.6:53.2.verse: But I know distinctions among individuals in this matter.”

snp3.6:54.1.verse: “Lord, if that is so, I am willing to undergo probation for four years. If, at the end of four years, the monks feel so moved, let them give me the Going-forth & accept me into the monk’s state.”

snp3.6:54.2.verse: Then Sabhiya the wanderer obtained the Going-forth in the Blessed One’s presence, he obtained Acceptance. And not long after his Acceptance—dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, & resolute—he in no long time reached & remained in the supreme goal of the holy life, for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness, knowing & realizing it for himself in the here-&-now. He knew: “Birth is ended, the holy life fulfilled, the task done. There is nothing further for the sake of this world.”

snp3.6:54.3.verse: And so Ven. Sabhiya became another one of the arahants.

snp3.6:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

snp3.6:1.3.verse: Now at that time the wanderer Sabhiya had been presented with several questions by a deity who was a former blood relation, saying:

snp3.6:1.4.verse: “Sabhiya, you should live the spiritual life with whatever ascetic or brahmin answers these questions.”

snp3.6:2.1.verse: Then Sabhiya, after learning those questions in the presence of that deity, approached those ascetics and brahmins who led an order and a community, and taught a community, who were well-known and famous religious founders, deemed holy by many people. That is,

snp3.6:2.2.verse: Pūraṇa Kassapa, the bamboo-staffed ascetic Gosāla, Ajita of the hair blanket, Pakudha Kaccāyana, Sañjaya Belaṭṭhiputta, and the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan.

snp3.6:2.3.verse: And he asked them those questions,

snp3.6:2.4.verse: but they were stumped by them.

snp3.6:3.6.verse: they questioned me in return on that matter.

snp3.6:3.7.verse: Why don’t I return to a lesser life so I can enjoy sensual pleasures?”

snp3.6:4.2.verse: “This ascetic Gotama also leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people.

snp3.6:4.3.verse: Why don’t I ask him these questions?”

snp3.6:5.2.verse: “Even those ascetics and brahmins who are elderly and senior, who are advanced in years and have reached the final stage of life; who are senior, long standing, long gone forth; who lead an order and a community, and tutor a community; who are well-known and famous religious founders, deemed holy by many people—that is

snp3.6:5.5.verse: They displayed annoyance, hate, and bitterness, and even questioned me in return.

snp3.6:5.6.verse: How can the ascetic Gotama possibly answer my questions,

snp3.6:5.7.verse: since he is so young in age and newly gone forth?”

snp3.6:6.2.verse: “An ascetic should not be looked down upon or disparaged because they are young.

snp3.6:6.3.verse: Though young, the ascetic Gotama has great psychic power and might. Why don’t I ask him these questions?”

snp3.6:7.1.verse: Then Sabhiya set out for Rājagaha.

snp3.6:7.2.verse: Traveling stage by stage, he came to Rājagaha, the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground. He went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

snp3.6:7.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side,

snp3.6:7.4.verse: and addressed the Buddha in verse:

snp3.6:8.1.verse: “I’ve come full of  doubts and uncertainties,”

snp3.6:8.5.verse: Answer my questions in turn, in accordance with the truth.”

snp3.6:9.4.verse: I shall solve them for you,

snp3.6:9.5.verse: answering your questions in turn, in accordance with the truth.

snp3.6:11.3.verse: Where those other ascetics and brahmins didn’t even give me a chance, the Buddha has invited me.”

snp3.6:11.4.verse: Uplifted and elated, full of rapture and happiness, he asked this question.

snp3.6:12.1.verse: “What must one attain to be called a mendicant?”

snp3.6:12.3.verse: “How is one ‘gentle’, how said to be ‘tamed’?

snp3.6:12.4.verse: How is one declared to be ‘awakened’?

snp3.6:12.5.verse: May the Buddha please answer my question.”

snp3.6:13.1.verse: “When by the path they have walked themselves,”

snp3.6:13.4.verse: giving up desire for existence or nonexistence,

snp3.6:13.5.verse: their journey complete, their rebirths ended: that is a mendicant.

snp3.6:14.2.verse: they don’t harm anyone in the world.

snp3.6:14.3.verse: An ascetic who has crossed over, unclouded,

snp3.6:14.4.verse: who has no pretensions, is gentle.

snp3.6:15.2.verse: inside and out in the whole world.

snp3.6:15.3.verse: Having pierced through this world and the next,

snp3.6:16.1.verse: They have examined the eons in their entirety,

snp3.6:16.2.verse: and both sides of transmigration—passing away and rebirth.

snp3.6:16.4.verse: the one they call ‘awakened’ has attained the end of rebirth.”

snp3.6:17.1.verse: And then, having approved and agreed with what the Buddha said, uplifted and elated, full of rapture and happiness, Sabhiya asked another question:

snp3.6:18.1.verse: “What must one attain to be called ‘brahmin’?”

snp3.6:18.3.verse: “Why is one an ‘ascetic’, and how a ‘bathed initiate’?

snp3.6:18.4.verse: How is one declared to be a ‘giant’?

snp3.6:18.5.verse: May the Buddha please answer my question.”

snp3.6:20.1.verse: An assuaged one who has given up good and evil,

snp3.6:20.2.verse: stainless, understanding this world and the next,

snp3.6:21.1.verse: Having washed off all bad things

snp3.6:21.2.verse: inside and out in the whole world,

snp3.6:21.3.verse: among gods and humans bound to creations,

snp3.6:21.4.verse: the one they call ‘washed’ does not return to creation.

snp3.6:22.1.verse: They do nothing monstrous at all in the world,

snp3.6:23.1.verse: And then Sabhiya asked another question:

snp3.6:24.1.verse: “Who is a ‘field-victor’ according to the Buddhas?”

snp3.6:24.3.verse: “Why is one ‘skillful’, and how ‘an astute scholar’?

snp3.6:24.4.verse: How is one declared to be a ‘sage’?

snp3.6:24.5.verse: May the Buddha please answer my question.”

snp3.6:25.1.verse: “They are victors on the fields of deeds in their entirety,”

snp3.6:25.3.verse: “the fields of gods, humans, and divinities;

snp3.6:25.4.verse: released from the root bondage to all fields:

snp3.6:26.1.verse: They have examined the coffers in their entirety,

snp3.6:26.2.verse: the coffers of gods, humans, and divinities;

snp3.6:26.3.verse: released from the root bondage to all coffers:

snp3.6:27.2.verse: both inside and out; understanding purity,

snp3.6:27.3.verse: they have left dark and bright behind:

snp3.6:27.4.verse: one such is rightly called ‘an astute scholar’.

snp3.6:28.1.verse: Understanding the nature of the bad and the good

snp3.6:28.2.verse: inside and out in the whole world;

snp3.6:28.3.verse: one worthy of honor by gods and humans,

snp3.6:28.4.verse: who has escaped from the net and the chain: that is a sage.”

snp3.6:29.1.verse: And then Sabhiya asked another question:

snp3.6:30.1.verse: “What must one attain to be called ‘knowledge master’?”

snp3.6:30.3.verse: “Why is one ‘studied’, and how is one ‘heroic’?

snp3.6:30.5.verse: May the Buddha please answer my question.”

snp3.6:31.1.verse: “They have examined knowledges in their entirety,”

snp3.6:31.3.verse: “those that are current among ascetics and brahmins;

snp3.6:31.4.verse: rid of greed for all feelings,

snp3.6:31.5.verse: having left all knowledges behind: that is a knowledge master.

snp3.6:32.1.verse: Having studied proliferation and name & form

snp3.6:32.2.verse: inside and out—the root of disease;

snp3.6:32.3.verse: released from the root bondage to all disease:

snp3.6:33.2.verse: heroic, he escapes from the suffering of hell;

snp3.6:34.2.verse: the root of clinging inside and out;

snp3.6:34.3.verse: released from the root bondage to all clinging:

snp3.6:35.1.verse: And then Sabhiya asked another question:

snp3.6:36.1.verse: “What must one attain to be called ‘scholar’?”

snp3.6:36.3.verse: “Why is one ‘noble’, and how is one ‘well conducted’?

snp3.6:36.5.verse: May the Buddha please answer my question.”

snp3.6:37.3.verse: “and has known for themselves what in the world is blameworthy and blameless;

snp3.6:38.1.verse: Having cut off defilements and clingings,

snp3.6:38.2.verse: being wise, they enter no womb.

snp3.6:38.3.verse: They’ve cast aside the bog of the three perceptions,

snp3.6:38.4.verse: the one they call ‘noble’ does not return to creation.

snp3.6:39.1.verse: One here who is accomplished and skillful in all forms of good conduct;

snp3.6:39.3.verse: everywhere not stuck, freed in mind,

snp3.6:39.4.verse: who has no aversion: they are ‘well-conducted’.

snp3.6:40.2.verse: having banished any deed that results in suffering,

snp3.6:40.3.verse: deceit and conceit, as well as greed and anger,

snp3.6:40.5.verse: They have made a limit on name and form;

snp3.6:40.6.verse: the one they call a ‘wanderer’ has reached their destination.”

snp3.6:41.1.verse: And then, having approved and agreed with what the Buddha said, uplifted and elated, full of rapture and happiness, Sabhiya rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha, and extolled the Buddha in his presence with fitting verses:

snp3.6:42.1.verse: “O one of vast wisdom, there are three and sixty opinions

snp3.6:42.2.verse: based on the doctrines of ascetics:

snp3.6:42.3.verse: they are expressions of perception, based on perception.

snp3.6:42.4.verse: Having dispelled them all, you passed over the dark flood.

snp3.6:43.1.verse: You have gone to the end, gone beyond suffering,

snp3.6:43.2.verse: you are perfected, a fully awakened Buddha; I think you have ended defilements.

snp3.6:43.4.verse: ender of suffering—you brought me across!

snp3.6:44.2.verse: you brought me beyond doubt—homage to you!

snp3.6:44.3.verse: A sage, accomplished in the ways of sagacity,

snp3.6:44.4.verse: you are gentle, not hardhearted, O Kinsman of the Sun.

snp3.6:45.1.verse: Any doubts that I once had,

snp3.6:45.2.verse: you have answered for me, O Clear-eyed One.

snp3.6:45.3.verse: Clearly you are a sage, an Awakened One,

snp3.6:45.4.verse: there are no hindrances in you.

snp3.6:46.2.verse: is blown away and mown down.

snp3.6:47.1.verse: O giant among giants, O great hero,

snp3.6:48.2.verse: Homage to you, supreme among men!

snp3.6:48.3.verse: In the world with its gods,

snp3.6:49.1.verse: You are the Buddha, you are the Teacher,

snp3.6:49.2.verse: you are the sage who has overcome Māra;

snp3.6:49.3.verse: you have cut off the underlying tendencies,

snp3.6:49.4.verse: you’ve crossed over, and you bring humanity across.

snp3.6:50.3.verse: you are a lion free of grasping,

snp3.6:50.4.verse: with fear and dread given up.

snp3.6:51.2.verse: to which water does not stick,

snp3.6:51.5.verse: Stretch out your feet, great hero:

snp3.6:52.1.verse: Then the wanderer Sabhiya bowed with his head to the Buddha’s feet and said,

snp3.6:52.3.verse: I go for refuge to the Buddha, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

snp3.6:52.4.verse: Sir, may I receive the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence?”

snp3.6:53.1.verse: “Sabhiya, if someone formerly ordained in another sect wishes to take the going forth, the ordination in this teaching and training, they must spend four months on probation. When four months have passed, if the mendicants are satisfied, they’ll give the going forth, the ordination into monkhood.

snp3.6:53.2.verse: However, I recognize individual differences in this matter.”

snp3.6:54.1.verse: “Sir, if four months probation are required in such a case, I’ll spend four years on probation. When four years have passed, if the mendicants are satisfied, let them give me the going forth, the ordination into monkhood.”

snp3.6:54.2.verse: And the wanderer Sabhiya received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

snp3.6:54.3.verse: And Venerable Sabhiya became one of the perfected.

snp3.7:1.2.verse: on one occasion, while the Blessed One was wandering on a tour among the Aṅguttarāpans with a large Saṅgha of monks, approximately 1,250 monks in all, he arrived at an Aṅguttarāpan town named Āpaṇa.

snp3.7:1.3.verse: Keṇiya the coiled hair ascetic heard it said,

snp3.7:1.4.verse: “Gotama the contemplative—a son of the Sakyans, gone forth from the Sakyan clan—on a wandering tour among the Aṅguttarāpans with a large Saṅgha of monks, approximately 1,250 monks in all—has arrived at Āpaṇa.

snp3.7:1.5.verse: And of that Master Gotama this fine reputation has spread:

snp3.7:1.6.verse: ‘He is indeed a Blessed One, worthy & rightly self-awakened, consummate in clear-knowing & conduct, well-gone, an expert with regard to the cosmos, unexcelled trainer of people fit to be tamed, teacher of devas & human beings, awakened, blessed.’

snp3.7:1.7.verse: He makes known—having realized it through direct knowledge—this world with its devas, Māras, & Brahmās, this generation with its contemplatives & brahmans, its rulers & commonfolk;

snp3.7:1.8.verse: he explains the Dhamma admirable in the beginning, admirable in the middle, admirable in the end; he expounds the holy life both in its particulars & in its essence, entirely perfect, surpassingly pure.

snp3.7:1.9.verse: It is good to see such a worthy one.”

snp3.7:2.1.verse: So Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, exchanged courteous greetings with him.

snp3.7:2.2.verse: After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, he sat to one side.1

snp3.7:2.3.verse: As he was sitting there, the Blessed One instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged him with a talk on Dhamma.

snp3.7:2.4.verse: Then Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic—instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged with the Blessed One’s talk on Dhamma—said to him,

snp3.7:2.5.verse: “Master Gotama, may the Blessed One acquiesce to my meal tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha of monks.”

snp3.7:2.6.verse: When this was said, the Blessed One said to him,

snp3.7:2.7.verse: “The Saṅgha of monks is large, Keṇiya, approximately 1,250 monks in all, and you are strongly confident in brahmans.”

snp3.7:3.1.verse: A second time, Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic said to the Blessed One,

snp3.7:3.2.verse: “Even though the Saṅgha of monks is large, Master Gotama, approximately 1,250 monks in all, and I am strongly confident in brahmans,

snp3.7:3.3.verse: may Master Gotama acquiesce to my meal tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha of monks.”

snp3.7:3.4.verse: A second time, the Blessed One said to Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic,

snp3.7:3.5.verse: “The Saṅgha of monks is large, Keṇiya, approximately 1,250 monks in all, and you are strongly confident in brahmans.”

snp3.7:4.1.verse: A third time, Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic said to the Blessed One,

snp3.7:4.2.verse: “Master Gotama, even though the Saṅgha of monks is large, approximately 1,250 monks in all, and I am strongly confident in brahmans,

snp3.7:4.3.verse: may Master Gotama acquiesce to my meal tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha of monks.”

snp3.7:4.4.verse: The Blessed One acquiesced with silence.

snp3.7:4.5.verse: Then Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic, understanding the Blessed One’s acquiescence, got up from his seat and returned to his own ashram. On arrival, he addressed his friends & companions, his relatives & kinsmen:

snp3.7:4.6.verse: “Listen to me, venerable friends & companions, relatives & kinsmen:

snp3.7:4.7.verse: I have invited Gotama the contemplative together with a Saṅgha of monks, approximately 1,250 monks in all, for the meal tomorrow.

snp3.7:4.8.verse: Give me bodily assistance for that.”

snp3.7:4.9.verse: “As you say, master,” his friends & companions, relatives & kinsmen responded to him. Some of them dug out ovens, some split wood, some washed dishes, some set out a water pot, some arranged seats,

snp3.7:4.10.verse: while Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic arranged a pavilion of garlands himself.

snp3.7:5.1.verse: Now on that occasion Sela the brahman was staying at Āpaṇa. He was a master of the Three Vedas with their vocabularies, liturgy, phonology, etymology, & histories as a fifth; skilled in philology & grammar, he was fully versed in cosmology and in the marks of a Great Man. He was instructing 300 young brahmans in the (Vedic) mantras.

snp3.7:6.2.verse: Then, as he—surrounded by 300 young brahmans—was walking and wandering about to exercise his legs, he arrived at the ashram of Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic.

snp3.7:6.3.verse: He saw that some of the people in the ashram were digging out ovens, some were splitting wood… while Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic was arranging a pavilion of garlands himself.

snp3.7:6.4.verse: On seeing this, he said to Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic,

snp3.7:6.5.verse: “Could it be that Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic is giving a son or daughter in marriage, or is he setting up a great sacrifice, or is Seniya Bimbisāra, the king of Magadha, invited for tomorrow together with his army?”

snp3.7:7.1.verse: “No, Sela, it’s not that I’m giving a son or daughter in marriage, nor that Seniya Bimbisāra, the king of Magadha, is invited for tomorrow together with his army.

snp3.7:7.2.verse: But I am setting up a great sacrifice.

snp3.7:7.3.verse: There is Gotama the contemplative—a son of the Sakyans, gone forth from the Sakyan clan—who, on a wandering tour among the Aṅguttarāpans with a large Saṅgha of monks, approximately 1,250 monks in all, has arrived at Āpaṇa.

snp3.7:7.4.verse: And of that Master Gotama this fine reputation has spread: ‘He is indeed a Blessed One, worthy & rightly self-awakened, consummate in clear-knowing & conduct, well-gone, an expert with regard to the cosmos, unexcelled trainer of people fit to be tamed, teacher of devas & human beings,

snp3.7:7.6.verse: He has been invited by me for the meal tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha of monks.”

snp3.7:8.1.verse: Then the thought occurred to Sela the brahman,

snp3.7:8.2.verse: “Even just this word is hard to come by in the world: ‘Awakened.’

snp3.7:8.3.verse: Now, these 32 marks of a Great Man have come down in our mantras. For a Great Man endowed with them, two future courses, and no other, exist.

snp3.7:8.4.verse: If he inhabits a home, he will become a wheel-turning king, righteous, a king through righteousness, a conqueror of the four quarters, a stabilizer of his countryside endowed with the seven treasures.

snp3.7:8.6.verse: the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the adviser-treasure as the seventh.

snp3.7:8.7.verse: He will have a thousand sons, valiant, heroic in body, crushers of enemy armies.

snp3.7:8.8.verse: He will dwell, having conquered the earth to the edge of the sea, by means of Dhamma, without rod, without sword.

snp3.7:8.9.verse: But if he goes forth from the home life into homelessness, he will become a worthy one, rightly self-awakened, with his roof opened in the world.2

snp3.7:8.10.verse: Master Keṇiya, where is he staying now, that Master Gotama, worthy & rightly self-awakened?”

snp3.7:9.1.verse: When this was said, Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic lifted his right arm and said to Sela the brahman,

snp3.7:9.2.verse: “There, by the dark green line of the forest.”

snp3.7:9.3.verse: Then Sela the brahman, together with the 300 young brahmans, headed toward the Blessed One.

snp3.7:9.4.verse: Then he addressed the young brahmans,

snp3.7:9.5.verse: “Come noiselessly, masters, placing a footstep in a footstep.

snp3.7:9.6.verse: These Blessed Ones are hard to approach, like a lion wandering alone.

snp3.7:9.7.verse: And when I engage Gotama the contemplative in counsel, don’t break into the middle of my talk.

snp3.7:9.8.verse: Wait until the end of my talk.”

snp3.7:10.1.verse: Then Sela the brahman went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, exchanged courteous greetings with him.

snp3.7:10.2.verse: After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, he sat to one side.

snp3.7:10.3.verse: As he was sitting there, he looked for the 32 marks of a Great Man in the Blessed One’s body.

snp3.7:10.4.verse: He saw most of the 32 marks of a Great Man in the Blessed One’s body, except for two.

snp3.7:10.5.verse: About the two marks he was doubtful, uncertain, undecided, and wasn’t reassured:

snp3.7:10.6.verse: about the male organ being in a sheath, and about the size of the tongue.

snp3.7:11.1.verse: The thought occurred to the Blessed One,

snp3.7:11.2.verse: “Sela the brahman sees most of my marks of a Great Man, except for two.

snp3.7:11.3.verse: About the two marks he is doubtful, uncertain, undecided, and isn’t reassured:

snp3.7:11.4.verse: about the male organ being in a sheath, and about the size of the tongue.”

snp3.7:11.5.verse: So the Blessed One willed a willing of power such that Sela the brahman saw that the Blessed One’s male organ was in a sheath.

snp3.7:11.6.verse: And then, extending his tongue, the Blessed One licked both ear-holes and nostrils back and forth, and covered his whole forehead with his tongue.

snp3.7:12.1.verse: The thought occurred to Sela the brahman,

snp3.7:12.2.verse: “Gotama the contemplative’s 32 marks of a Great Man are complete and not incomplete.

snp3.7:12.3.verse: But I don’t know whether he is awakened or not.

snp3.7:12.4.verse: Still, I have heard the aged line of teachers, along in their years, say:

snp3.7:12.5.verse: ‘Blessed Ones, worthy & rightly self-awakened, reveal themselves when their praise is spoken.’

snp3.7:12.6.verse: What if I were to praise Gotama the contemplative face-to-face with fitting verses?”

snp3.7:12.7.verse: So Sela the brahman praised the Blessed One face-to-face with fitting verses:

snp3.7:13.3.verse: Blessed One, you have a golden complexion,

snp3.7:13.4.verse: you have white teeth, you’re vigorous.

snp3.7:14.1.verse: The characteristics of a well-born man,

snp3.7:14.2.verse: the marks of a Great Man,

snp3.7:15.1.verse: Clear your eyes, good your face,

snp3.7:15.3.verse: In the midst of a community of contemplatives

snp3.7:16.1.verse: A monk admirable to look at,

snp3.7:16.3.verse: but what use is the contemplative state

snp3.7:16.4.verse: for you, so superlative in appearance?

snp3.7:17.1.verse: You deserve to be a king,

snp3.7:17.4.verse: sovereign lord of the Jambu grove.4

snp3.7:18.3.verse: King of kings, monarch of human beings:

snp3.7:19.4.verse: I turn the wheel with Dhamma—

snp3.7:19.5.verse: the wheel whose turning can’t be stopped.”

snp3.7:21.1.verse: But who, master, is your general,

snp3.7:21.2.verse: the disciple right below the teacher?

snp3.7:21.4.verse: the Dhamma-wheel set rolling by you?”

snp3.7:25.2.verse: I am one whose appearance in the world

snp3.7:26.4.verse: having overmastered all enemies, I rejoice, with no fear from anywhere.”

snp3.7:27.2.verse: how he speaks, this One with Eyes,

snp3.7:27.4.verse: He roars like a lion in the forest.

snp3.7:28.3.verse: Who, even one of a dark birth,7 on seeing him,

snp3.7:29.1.verse: Whoever wants to     may follow me.

snp3.7:29.4.verse: in the presence of the one of foremost discernment.”

snp3.7:30.2.verse: in the message of the Rightly Self-Awakened One,

snp3.7:30.3.verse: we, too, will here go forth

snp3.7:30.4.verse: in the presence of the one of foremost discernment.”

snp3.7:31.2.verse: request, with hands palm-to-palm over the heart:

snp3.7:32.4.verse: where the Going-forth is not in vain

snp3.7:32.5.verse: for a heedful person who trains.”

snp3.7:33.1.verse: Then Sela the brahman, together with his following, obtained the Going-forth in the Blessed One’s presence, he obtained Acceptance.

snp3.7:33.2.verse: Then, as the night was ending, Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic, having had choice staple & non-staple foods prepared in his own ashram, announced the time to the Blessed One,

snp3.7:33.3.verse: “It is time, master Gotama. The meal is ready.”

snp3.7:33.4.verse: Then, early in the morning, the Blessed One—after adjusting his lower robe and carrying his bowl & outer robe—went together with a Saṅgha of monks to Keṇiya’s ashram. On arrival, he sat down on an arranged seat.

snp3.7:34.1.verse: Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic, with his own hand, served & satisfied the Blessed One & the Saṅgha of monks with choice staple & non-staple foods.

snp3.7:34.2.verse: Then, when the Blessed One had eaten and had rinsed his bowl & hands, Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic took a lower seat and sat to one side.

snp3.7:34.3.verse: As he was sitting there, the Blessed One expressed approval of him with these verses:

snp3.7:35.1.verse: “The fire oblation is the chief of sacrifices,

snp3.7:35.2.verse: the Sāvitti,     the chief of Vedic hymns,8

snp3.7:35.3.verse: a king,          chief among human beings,

snp3.7:36.1.verse: the moon,     chief of the zodiac stars,

snp3.7:36.2.verse: the sun,          chief of things that burn,9

snp3.7:36.3.verse: and for those who sacrifice, wishing for merit,

snp3.7:37.1.verse: Then, having expressed approval of Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic with these verses, the Blessed One got up from his seat and left.

snp3.7:37.2.verse: Then Ven. Sela, together with his following—dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, & resolute—in no long time reached & remained in the supreme goal of the holy life, for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness, knowing & realizing it for himself in the here-&-now. He knew: “Birth is ended, the holy life fulfilled, the task done. There is nothing further for the sake of this world.”

snp3.7:37.3.verse: And so Ven. Sela, together with his following, became another one of the arahants.

snp3.7:38.1.verse: Then Ven. Sela, together with his following, went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder and extending his hands palm-to-palm over the heart toward the Blessed One, addressed him in verse:

snp3.7:39.1.verse: “This is the eighth day since coming for refuge,

snp3.7:39.4.verse: we have tamed ourselves with your message.

snp3.7:40.2.verse: You: Sage who has conquered Māra.

snp3.7:40.4.verse: having crossed over, bring this generation across.

snp3.7:41.3.verse: you are a lion free of clinging,

snp3.7:42.2.verse: stand with hands palm-to-palm over the heart.

snp3.7:42.4.verse: The nāgas venerate them, the feet of the Teacher.”10

snp3.7:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was wandering together with a large Saṅgha of 1,250 mendicants in the land of the Aṅguttarāpans when he arrived at a town of theirs named Āpaṇa.

snp3.7:1.4.verse: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—has arrived at Āpaṇa, together with a large Saṅgha of 1,250 mendicants.

snp3.7:1.6.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

snp3.7:1.7.verse: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

snp3.7:1.8.verse: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

snp3.7:1.9.verse: It’s good to see such perfected ones.”

snp3.7:2.1.verse: So Keṇiya approached the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

snp3.7:2.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side.

snp3.7:2.3.verse: The Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired him with a Dhamma talk.

snp3.7:2.4.verse: Then he said to the Buddha,

snp3.7:2.5.verse: “Would Worthy Gotama together with the mendicant Saṅgha please accept tomorrow’s meal from me?”

snp3.7:2.6.verse: When he said this, the Buddha said to him,

snp3.7:2.7.verse: “The Saṅgha is large, Keṇiya; there are 1,250 mendicants. And you are devoted to the brahmins.”

snp3.7:3.1.verse: For a second time, Keṇiya asked the Buddha to accept a meal offering.

snp3.7:3.2.verse: “Never mind that the Saṅgha is large, with 1,250 mendicants, and that I am devoted to the brahmins.

snp3.7:3.3.verse: Would Worthy Gotama together with the mendicant Saṅgha please accept tomorrow’s meal from me?”

snp3.7:3.4.verse: And for a second time, the Buddha gave the same reply.

snp3.7:4.1.verse: For a third time, Keṇiya asked the Buddha to accept a meal offering.

snp3.7:4.2.verse: “Never mind that the Saṅgha is large, with 1,250 mendicants, and that I am devoted to the brahmins.

snp3.7:4.3.verse: Would Worthy Gotama together with the mendicant Saṅgha please accept tomorrow’s meal from me?”

snp3.7:4.5.verse: Then, knowing that the Buddha had consented, Keṇiya rose from his seat and went to his own hermitage. There he addressed his friends and colleagues, relatives and kin,

snp3.7:4.6.verse: “My friends and colleagues, relatives and kin: please listen!

snp3.7:4.7.verse: The ascetic Gotama together with the mendicant Saṅgha has been invited by me for tomorrow’s meal.

snp3.7:4.8.verse: Please help me out with the manual preparations.”

snp3.7:4.9.verse: “Yes, worthy sir,” they replied. Some dug ovens, some chopped wood, some washed dishes, some set up a water jar, and some spread out seats.

snp3.7:4.10.verse: Meanwhile, Keṇiya set up the pavilion himself.

snp3.7:5.1.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Sela was residing in Āpaṇa. He had mastered the three Vedas, together with their vocabularies and ritual performance, their phonology and word classification, and the testaments as fifth. He knew them word-by-word, and their grammar. He was well versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man. And he was teaching three hundred young students to recite the hymns.

snp3.7:6.1.verse: And at that time Keṇiya was devoted to Sela.

snp3.7:6.2.verse: Then Sela, while going for a walk escorted by the three hundred young students, approached Keṇiya’s hermitage.

snp3.7:6.3.verse: He saw the preparations going on,

snp3.7:6.5.verse: “Worthy Keṇiya, is your son or daughter being married? Or are you setting up a grand sacrifice? Or has King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha been invited for tomorrow’s meal?”

snp3.7:7.1.verse: “There is no marriage, Worthy Sela, and the king is not coming.

snp3.7:7.2.verse: Rather, I am setting up a grand sacrifice.

snp3.7:7.3.verse: The ascetic Gotama has arrived at Āpaṇa, together with a large Saṅgha of 1,250 mendicants.

snp3.7:7.5.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

snp3.7:7.6.verse: He has been invited by me for tomorrow’s meal together with the mendicant Saṅgha.”

snp3.7:8.2.verse: “It’s hard to even find the word ‘awakened one’ in the world.

snp3.7:8.3.verse: The thirty-two marks of a great man have been handed down in our hymns. A great man who possesses these has only two possible destinies, no other.

snp3.7:8.4.verse: If he stays at home he becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch, a just and principled king. His dominion extends to all four sides, he achieves stability in the country, and he possesses the seven treasures.

snp3.7:8.5.verse: He has the following seven treasures:

snp3.7:8.6.verse: the wheel, the elephant, the horse, the jewel, the woman, the householder, and the commander as the seventh treasure.

snp3.7:8.7.verse: He has over a thousand sons who are valiant and heroic, crushing the armies of his enemies.

snp3.7:8.8.verse: After conquering this land girt by sea, he reigns by principle, without rod or sword.

snp3.7:8.9.verse: But if he goes forth from the lay life to homelessness, he becomes a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, who has cast off the world’s veil.”

snp3.7:8.10.verse: He said, “But Keṇiya, where is the Blessed One at present, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha?”

snp3.7:9.1.verse: When he said this, Keṇiya pointed with his right arm and said,

snp3.7:9.2.verse: “There, worthy Sela, at that line of blue forest.”

snp3.7:9.3.verse: Then Sela, together with his young students, approached the Buddha.

snp3.7:9.4.verse: He said to his young students,

snp3.7:9.6.verse: For the Buddhas are intimidating, like a lion living alone.

snp3.7:9.7.verse: When I’m consulting with the ascetic Gotama, don’t interrupt.

snp3.7:10.1.verse: Then Sela went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

snp3.7:10.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side,

snp3.7:10.3.verse: and scrutinized the Buddha’s body for the thirty-two marks of a great man.

snp3.7:10.4.verse: He saw all of them except two,

snp3.7:10.6.verse: whether the private parts were sheathed in a foreskin, and the largeness of the tongue.

snp3.7:11.1.verse: Then it occurred to the Buddha,

snp3.7:11.2.verse: “Sela sees all the marks except two,

snp3.7:11.4.verse: whether the private parts are sheathed in a foreskin, and the largeness of the tongue.”

snp3.7:11.5.verse: The Buddha used his psychic power to will that Sela would see his private parts sheathed in a foreskin.

snp3.7:11.6.verse: And he stuck out his tongue and stroked back and forth on his ear holes and nostrils, and covered his entire forehead with his tongue.

snp3.7:12.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama possesses the thirty-two marks completely, lacking none.

snp3.7:12.3.verse: But I don’t know whether or not he is an awakened one.

snp3.7:12.4.verse: I have heard that brahmins of the past who were elderly and senior, the tutors of tutors, said,

snp3.7:12.5.verse: ‘Those who are perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas reveal themselves when praised.’

snp3.7:12.6.verse: Why don’t I extoll him in his presence with fitting verses?”

snp3.7:12.7.verse: Then Sela extolled the Buddha in his presence with fitting verses:

snp3.7:13.2.verse: you’re radiant, handsome, lovely to behold;

snp3.7:13.4.verse: with teeth so white; you’re strong.

snp3.7:14.3.verse: the marks of a great man,

snp3.7:14.4.verse: are all found on your body.

snp3.7:15.1.verse: Your eyes are clear, your face is fair,

snp3.7:15.3.verse: In the midst of the Saṅgha of ascetics,

snp3.7:16.1.verse: You’re a mendicant fine to see,

snp3.7:16.2.verse: with skin that shines like lustrous gold.

snp3.7:33.1.verse: And the brahmin Sela together with his assembly received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

snp3.7:33.2.verse: And when the night had passed Keṇiya had delicious fresh and cooked foods prepared in his own hermitage. Then he had the Buddha informed of the time, saying,

snp3.7:33.3.verse: “It’s time, worthy Gotama, the meal is ready.”

snp3.7:33.4.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to Keṇiya’s hermitage, where he sat down on the seat spread out together with the Saṅgha of mendicants.

snp3.7:34.1.verse: Then Keṇiya served and satisfied the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha with his own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

snp3.7:34.2.verse: When the Buddha had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, Keṇiya took a low seat and sat to one side.

snp3.7:34.3.verse: The Buddha expressed his appreciation with these verses:

snp3.7:37.1.verse: When the Buddha had expressed his appreciation to Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic with these verses, he rose from his seat and left.

snp3.7:37.2.verse: Then Venerable Sela and his assembly, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. They lived having achieved with their own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

snp3.7:37.3.verse: And Venerable Sela together with his assembly became perfected.

snp3.7:38.1.verse: Then Sela with his assembly went to the Buddha. He arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his joined palms toward the Buddha, and said:

snp3.9:1.3.verse: And on that occasion many well-known wealthy brahmans were dwelling in Icchānaṅgala, i.e.,

snp3.9:1.4.verse: Caṅkī the brahman, Tārukkha the brahman, Pokkharasāti the brahman, Jānusoṇin the brahman, Todeyya the brahman, and many other well-known wealthy brahmans.

snp3.9:1.5.verse: Then, while the young brahmans Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja were walking and wandering about to exercise their legs, this conversation arose between them:

snp3.9:2.2.verse: “When one is well-born on both sides, the mother’s & the father’s, is of pure descent for seven generations of fathers—uncriticized & irreproachable in the telling of one’s birth:

snp3.9:2.3.verse: It’s to that extent that one is a brahman.”

snp3.9:3.2.verse: “When one is virtuous & consummate in one’s practices,

snp3.9:3.3.verse: it’s to that extent that one is a brahman.”

snp3.9:3.4.verse: But neither was the young brahman Bhāradvāja able to win over the young brahman Vāseṭṭha, nor was the young brahman Vāseṭṭha able to win over the young brahman Bhāradvāja.

snp3.9:4.1.verse: Then the young brahman Vāseṭṭha said to the young brahman Bhāradvāja,

snp3.9:4.2.verse: “Bhāradvāja, this Gotama the contemplative—a son of the Sakyans, gone forth from the Sakyan clan—is staying at Icchānaṅgala in the Icchānaṅgala forest grove.

snp3.9:4.3.verse: And of that Master Gotama this fine reputation has spread:

snp3.9:4.4.verse: ‘He is indeed a Blessed One, worthy & rightly self-awakened, consummate in clear-knowing & conduct, well-gone, an expert with regard to the cosmos, unexcelled trainer of people fit to be tamed, teacher of devas & human beings, awakened, blessed.’

snp3.9:4.5.verse: Come, let’s go to Gotama the contemplative and, on arrival, ask him about this matter.

snp3.9:4.6.verse: However he answers, that’s how we’ll hold it.”

snp3.9:4.7.verse: “As you say, master,” the young brahman Bhāradvāja responded to the young brahman Vāseṭṭha.

snp3.9:5.1.verse: So the young brahmans Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, exchanged courteous greetings with him.

snp3.9:5.2.verse: After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, they sat to one side.

snp3.9:69.1.verse: When this was said, the young brahmans Vāseṭṭha & Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One:

snp3.9:69.2.verse: “Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent! snp3.9:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in a forest near Icchānaṅgala.

snp3.9:1.3.verse: Now at that time several very well-known well-to-do brahmins were residing in Icchānaṅgala. They included

snp3.9:1.4.verse: the brahmins Caṅkī, Tārukkha, Pokkharasāti, Jānussoṇi, Todeyya, and others.

snp3.9:1.5.verse: Then as the students Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja were going for a walk they began to discuss the question:

snp3.9:2.2.verse: “When you’re well born on both your mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation—

snp3.9:3.2.verse: “When you’re ethical and accomplished in doing your duties—

snp3.9:3.4.verse: But neither was able to persuade the other.

snp3.9:4.2.verse: “Worthy Bhāradvāja, the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—is staying in a forest near Icchānaṅgala.

snp3.9:4.4.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

snp3.9:4.5.verse: Come, let’s go to see him and ask him about this matter.

snp3.9:4.6.verse: As he answers, so we’ll remember it.”

snp3.9:5.1.verse: So they went to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

snp3.9:22.5.verse: none of these are defined by birth

snp3.9:22.6.verse: as it is for other species.

snp3.9:28.4.verse: as a bandit, not a brahmin.

snp3.9:29.4.verse: as a warrior, not a brahmin.

snp3.9:30.4.verse: as a sacrificer, not a brahmin.

snp3.9:31.4.verse: as a ruler, not a brahmin.
