snp3.12:42.4.verse: there is no origination of suffering.

snp3.12:43.2.verse: that suffering is caused by perturbation,

snp3.12:44.3.verse: ‘For the dependent there is quivering’: this is the first contemplation.

snp3.12:44.4.verse: ‘For the independent there’s no agitation’: this is the second contemplation.

snp3.12:44.5.verse: When a mendicant meditates in this way they can expect enlightenment or non-return.”

snp3.12:44.6.verse: Then the Teacher went on to say:

snp3.12:45.3.verse: goes from this state to another,

snp3.12:47.3.verse: ‘Formless states are more peaceful than states of form’: this is the first contemplation.

snp3.12:47.4.verse: ‘Cessation is more peaceful than formless states’: this is the second contemplation.

snp3.12:47.5.verse: When a mendicant meditates in this way they can expect enlightenment or non-return.”

snp3.12:47.6.verse: Then the Teacher went on to say:

snp3.12:48.1.verse: “There are beings in the realm of luminous form,

snp3.12:48.2.verse: and others stuck in the formless.

snp3.12:49.1.verse: But the people who completely understand form,

snp3.12:50.3.verse: ‘What this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—focuses on as true, the noble ones have clearly seen with right wisdom to be actually false’: this is the first contemplation.

snp3.12:50.4.verse: ‘What this world focuses on as false, the noble ones have clearly seen with right wisdom to be actually true’: this is the second contemplation.

snp3.12:50.5.verse: When a mendicant meditates in this way they can expect enlightenment or non-return.”

snp3.12:50.6.verse: Then the Teacher went on to say:

snp3.12:51.1.verse: “See how the world with its gods

snp3.12:52.2.verse: it turns out to be something else.

snp3.12:52.3.verse: And that is what is false in it,

snp3.12:52.4.verse: for the ephemeral is deceptive by nature.

snp3.12:53.2.verse: the noble ones know it as truth.

snp3.12:54.1.verse: “Suppose, monks, they questioned you thus: ‘Could there be another way to contemplate the pairs?’

snp3.12:54.4.verse: ‘What this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—focuses on as happiness, the noble ones have clearly seen with right wisdom to be actually suffering’: this is the first contemplation.

snp3.12:54.5.verse: ‘What this world focuses on as suffering, the noble ones have clearly seen with right wisdom to be actually happiness’: this is the second contemplation.

snp3.12:54.6.verse: When a mendicant meditates rightly contemplating a pair of teachings in this way—diligent, keen, and resolute—they can expect one of two results:

snp3.12:54.7.verse: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”

snp3.12:54.8.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

snp3.12:54.9.verse: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

snp3.12:55.2.verse: touches, and ideas, the lot of them—

snp3.12:55.4.verse: as long as you can say that they exist.

snp3.12:56.1.verse: For all the world with its gods,

snp3.12:56.2.verse: this is what they deem happiness.

snp3.12:56.4.verse: is deemed as suffering for them.

snp3.12:57.1.verse: The noble ones have seen as happiness

snp3.12:57.3.verse: This insight by those who see

snp3.12:58.2.verse: the noble ones say is suffering.

snp3.12:58.4.verse: the noble ones know as happiness.

snp3.12:59.1.verse: See, this teaching is hard to understand,

snp3.12:59.3.verse: There is darkness for the shrouded;

snp3.12:59.4.verse: blackness for those who don’t see.

snp3.12:60.2.verse: like light for those who see.

snp3.12:60.3.verse: Though close, they do not understand,

snp3.12:60.4.verse: those fools inexpert in the teaching.

snp3.12:61.1.verse: They’re mired in desire for continued existence,

snp3.12:61.2.verse: flowing along the stream of lives,

snp3.12:61.4.verse: this teaching isn’t easy for them to understand.

snp3.12:62.1.verse: Who, apart from the noble ones,

snp3.12:62.2.verse: is qualified to understand this state?

snp3.12:63.1.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

snp3.12:63.2.verse: Satisfied, the monks approved what the Buddha said.

snp3.12:63.3.verse: And while this discourse was being spoken, the minds of sixty monks were freed from defilements by not grasping.

snp4.1:1.1.verse: If one, longing for sensual pleasure,

snp4.1:1.4.verse: The mortal gets what he wants.

snp4.1:2.4.verse: he’s afflicted, as if shot with an arrow.

snp4.1:3.2.verse: —as he would, with his foot, the head of a snake—

snp4.1:4.4.verse: a man who is greedy for these

snp4.1:6.3.verse: Letting them go, he’d cross over the flood

snp4.1:6.4.verse: like one who, having bailed out the boat, has reached the far shore.

snp4.1:1.1.verse: If a mortal desires sensual pleasure

snp4.1:2.1.verse: But for that personage in the throes of pleasure,

snp4.1:2.4.verse: it inflicts them like an arrow strike.

snp4.1:4.1.verse: There are many objects of sensual desire:

snp4.1:4.2.verse: fields, lands, and gold; cattle and horses;

snp4.1:4.3.verse: slaves and servants; women and relatives.

snp4.1:4.4.verse: When a man lusts over these,

snp4.1:5.4.verse: like water in a leaky boat.

snp4.1:6.1.verse: That’s why a personage, ever mindful,

snp4.1:6.3.verse: Give them up and cross the flood,

snp4.1:6.4.verse: as a bailed-out boat reaches the far shore.

snp4.2:1.1.verse: Staying attached to the cave, covered heavily over,

snp4.2:1.4.verse: for sensual pleasures, sensual desires, in the world, are not lightly let go.

snp4.2:2.1.verse: Those chained by desire, bound by becoming’s allure,

snp4.2:2.2.verse: aren’t easily released for there’s no liberation by others.

snp4.2:2.4.verse: on hunger for sensual pleasures here or before—

snp4.2:3.1.verse: greedy for sensual pleasures, busy, deluded,

snp4.2:3.2.verse: ungenerous, entrenched in the discordant way,

snp4.2:3.4.verse: “What will we be when we pass on from here?”

snp4.2:4.1.verse: So a person should train right here-&-now.

snp4.2:4.2.verse: Whatever you know as discordant in the world,

snp4.2:4.3.verse: don’t, for its sake, act discordantly,

snp4.2:4.4.verse: for that life, the enlightened say, is short.

snp4.2:5.1.verse: I see them, in the world, floundering around,

snp4.2:5.2.verse: people immersed in craving for states of becoming.

snp4.2:5.3.verse: Base people moan in the mouth of death,

snp4.2:5.4.verse: their craving, for states of becoming & not-, unallayed.

snp4.2:6.1.verse: See them, floundering in their sense of mine,

snp4.2:6.2.verse: like fish in the puddles of a dried-up stream—

snp4.2:6.3.verse: and, seeing this, live with no mine,

snp4.2:6.4.verse: not forming attachment for states of becoming.

snp4.2:7.2.verse: comprehending sensory contact, with no greed.

snp4.2:7.3.verse: Doing nothing for which he himself would rebuke himself,

snp4.2:7.4.verse: the enlightened person doesn’t adhere to what’s seen, to what’s heard.

snp4.2:8.1.verse: Comprehending perception, he’d cross over the flood—

snp4.2:8.2.verse: the sage not stuck on possessions.

snp4.2:8.3.verse: Then, with arrow removed, living heedfully,

snp4.2:8.4.verse: he longs for neither—this world, the next.

snp4.2:1.1.verse: Trapped in a cave, thickly overspread,

snp4.2:1.3.verse: That sort is far from seclusion,

snp4.2:1.4.verse: for sensual pleasures in the world are not easy to give up.

snp4.2:2.1.verse: The chains of desire, the bonds of life’s pleasures

snp4.2:2.2.verse: are hard to escape, for one cannot free another.

snp4.2:2.3.verse: Looking to the past or the future,

snp4.2:2.4.verse: they pray for these pleasures or former ones.

snp4.2:3.1.verse: Greedy, fixated, infatuated by sensual pleasures,

snp4.2:3.3.verse: When led to suffering they lament,

snp4.2:3.4.verse: “What will become of us when we pass away from here?”

snp4.2:4.1.verse: That’s why a personage should train in this life:

snp4.2:4.2.verse: should you know that anything in the world is wrong,

snp4.2:4.3.verse: don’t act wrongly on account of that;

snp4.2:4.4.verse: for the attentive say this life is short.

snp4.2:5.1.verse: I see the world’s population floundering,

snp4.2:5.2.verse: given to craving for future lives.

snp4.2:5.3.verse: Base men wail in the jaws of death,

snp4.2:5.4.verse: not rid of craving for life after life.

snp4.2:6.2.verse: like fish in puddles of a dried-up stream.

snp4.2:6.4.verse: forming no attachment to future lives.

snp4.2:7.1.verse: Rid of desire for both ends,

snp4.2:7.2.verse: having completely understood contact, free of greed,

snp4.2:7.3.verse: doing nothing for which they’d blame themselves,

snp4.2:7.4.verse: the attentive don’t cling to the seen and the heard.

snp4.2:8.1.verse: Having completely understood perception and having crossed the flood,

snp4.2:8.2.verse: the sage, not clinging to possessions,

snp4.2:8.3.verse: with dart plucked out, living diligently,

snp4.2:8.4.verse: does not hope for this world or the next.

snp4.3:1.1.verse: There are some who dispute corrupted at heart,

snp4.3:1.2.verse: and those who dispute their hearts set on truth,

snp4.3:1.3.verse: but a sage doesn’t enter a dispute that’s arisen,

snp4.3:1.4.verse: which is why he has no rigidity anywhere at all.

snp4.3:2.1.verse: Now, how would one overcome his own views?

snp4.3:2.2.verse: led on by desire, entrenched in his likes,

snp4.3:2.4.verse: He’d dispute in line with the way that he knows.

snp4.3:3.1.verse: Whoever, of his own practices, habits,

snp4.3:3.3.verse: is, say the skilled, ignoble by nature—

snp4.3:3.4.verse: he who speaks of himself of his own accord.

snp4.3:4.1.verse: But a monk at peace, fully unbound in himself,

snp4.3:4.2.verse: not boasting of his habits —“That’s how I am”—

snp4.3:4.3.verse: he, say the skilled, is noble by nature—

snp4.3:4.4.verse: he with no vanity anywhere in the world.

snp4.3:5.3.verse: when he sees it to his own advantage—

snp4.3:5.4.verse: relies on a peace dependent on the provoked.

snp4.3:6.1.verse: Because entrenchments in views aren’t easily overcome

snp4.3:6.2.verse: when considering what’s grasped among doctrines,

snp4.3:6.3.verse: that’s why a person, in light of these very entrenchments,

snp4.3:7.1.verse: Now, one who is cleansed has nothing anywhere in the world—

snp4.3:7.2.verse: no theorized view about states of becoming or not-,

snp4.3:7.4.verse: by what means would he go? He isn’t involved,

snp4.3:8.1.verse: for one who’s involved enters into disputes over doctrines.

snp4.3:8.2.verse: But how—in connection with what—would you argue with one uninvolved?

snp4.3:8.3.verse: He has nothing embraced or rejected,

snp4.3:8.4.verse: has sloughed off every view right here—every one.

snp4.3:1.2.verse: while others speak set on truth.

snp4.3:1.3.verse: When disputes come up a sage does not get involved,

snp4.3:1.4.verse: which is why they’ve no barrenness at all.

snp4.3:2.1.verse: How can you transcend your own view

snp4.3:2.2.verse: when you’re led by preference, dogmatic in belief?

snp4.3:2.4.verse: you’d speak according to your notion.

snp4.3:3.2.verse: of their own precepts and vows.

snp4.3:3.3.verse: They have an ignoble nature, say those who are skilled,

snp4.3:3.4.verse: since they speak on themselves of their own accord.

snp4.3:4.2.verse: never boasts “thus am I” of their precepts.

snp4.3:4.3.verse: They have a noble nature, say those who are skilled,

snp4.3:4.4.verse: who have no pretensions about anything in the world.

snp4.3:5.1.verse: For one who formulates and creates teachings,

snp4.3:5.2.verse: and promotes them despite their defects,

snp4.3:5.3.verse: if they see an advantage for themselves,

snp4.3:5.4.verse: they become dependent on that, relying on unstable peace.

snp4.3:6.1.verse: It’s not easy to get over dogmatic views

snp4.3:6.2.verse: adopted after judging among the teachings.

snp4.3:6.3.verse: That’s why, among all these dogmas, a person

snp4.3:6.4.verse: ditches one teaching and takes up another.

snp4.3:7.1.verse: The cleansed one has no formulated view

snp4.3:7.2.verse: at all in the world about the different realms.

snp4.3:7.3.verse: Having given up illusion and conceit,

snp4.3:7.4.verse: by what path would they go? They are not involved.

snp4.3:8.1.verse: For one who gets involved is embroiled in disputes about teachings—

snp4.3:8.2.verse: but how to dispute with the uninvolved? About what?

snp4.3:8.3.verse: For picking up and putting down is not what they do;

snp4.3:8.4.verse: they have shaken off all views in this very life.

snp4.4:1.1.verse: “I see the pure, the supreme, free from disease.

snp4.4:1.2.verse: It’s in connection with what’s seen that a person’s purity is.”

snp4.4:1.4.verse: & remaining focused on purity, one falls back on that knowledge.

snp4.4:2.1.verse: If it’s in connection with what is seen that a person’s purity is,

snp4.4:2.2.verse: or if stress is abandoned in connection with knowledge,

snp4.4:2.3.verse: then a person with acquisitions is purified in connection with something else,

snp4.4:2.4.verse: for his view betrays that in the way he asserts it.

snp4.4:3.1.verse: No brahman says purity comes in connection with anything else—

snp4.4:3.2.verse: in what’s seen, heard, sensed, habits or practices—

snp4.4:3.4.verse: not creating anything here, he’s let go of what he’d embraced.

snp4.4:4.1.verse: Abandoning what’s first, they depend on what’s next.

snp4.4:4.2.verse: Following perturbation, they don’t cross over the bond.

snp4.4:4.4.verse: —like a monkey releasing a branch to seize at another—

snp4.4:5.1.verse: a person undertaking practices on his own,

snp4.4:5.2.verse: goes high & low, latched onto perception.

snp4.4:5.3.verse: But having clearly known through vedas, having encountered the Dhamma,

snp4.4:5.4.verse: one deeply discerning doesn’t go high & low.

snp4.4:6.1.verse: He’s enemy-free with regard to all things

snp4.4:6.3.verse: —one who has seen in this way, who goes around open—

snp4.4:6.4.verse: By whom, with what, should he be pigeonholed here in the world?

snp4.4:7.3.verse: Untying the tied-up knot of grasping,

snp4.4:7.4.verse: they don’t form a desire anywhere in the world.

snp4.4:8.1.verse: The brahman gone beyond territories, has nothing that

snp4.4:8.3.verse: Unimpassionate for passion, not impassioned for dis-,

snp4.4:8.4.verse: he has nothing here that he’s grasped as supreme.

snp4.4:1.2.verse: it is vision that grants a person purity.”

snp4.4:1.3.verse: Recalling this notion of the ultimate,

snp4.4:1.4.verse: they believe in the notion that there is one who observes purity.

snp4.4:2.1.verse: If a person were granted purity through what is seen,

snp4.4:2.2.verse: or if by a notion they could give up suffering,

snp4.4:2.3.verse: then one with attachments is purified by another:

snp4.4:2.4.verse: their view betrays them as one who asserts thus.

snp4.4:3.1.verse: The brahmin speaks not of purity from another

snp4.4:3.2.verse: in terms of what has been seen, heard, or thought; or by precepts or vows.

snp4.4:3.3.verse: They are unsullied in the midst of good and evil,

snp4.4:3.4.verse: letting go what was picked up, without creating anything new here.

snp4.4:4.1.verse: Having let go the last they lay hold of the next;

snp4.4:4.2.verse: following impulse, they don’t pass the chain.

snp4.4:4.3.verse: They grab on and let loose like a monkey

snp4.4:5.1.verse: Having undertaken their own vows, a personage

snp4.4:5.2.verse: visits various teachers, being attached to perception.

snp4.4:5.3.verse: One who knows, having comprehended the truth through the knowledges,

snp4.4:5.4.verse: does not visit various teachers, being of vast wisdom.

snp4.4:6.1.verse: They are remote from all things

snp4.4:6.4.verse: how could anyone in this world judge them?

snp4.4:7.1.verse: They don’t make things up or promote them,

snp4.4:7.2.verse: or speak of the uttermost purity.

snp4.4:7.3.verse: After untying the tight knot of grasping

snp4.4:7.4.verse: they long for nothing in the world.

snp4.4:8.1.verse: The brahmin has stepped over the perimeter;

snp4.4:8.2.verse: knowing and seeing, they adopt nothing.

snp4.4:8.3.verse: Neither in love with passion nor besotted by dispassion,

snp4.4:8.4.verse: there is nothing here they adopt as the ultimate.

snp4.5:1.2.verse: a person makes them the utmost thing in the world,

snp4.5:1.3.verse: &, from that, calls all others inferior

snp4.5:1.4.verse: and so he’s not gone beyond disputes.

snp4.5:2.1.verse: When he sees his own advantage

snp4.5:2.2.verse: in what’s seen, heard, sensed, or in habits & practices,

snp4.5:2.4.verse: he sees all else, all others, as inferior.

snp4.5:3.1.verse: That, too, say the skilled, is a binding knot:

snp4.5:3.2.verse: that in dependence on which you regard another as inferior.

snp4.5:3.3.verse: on what’s seen, heard, or sensed,

snp4.5:3.4.verse: or on habits & practices, a monk shouldn’t be dependent.

snp4.5:4.1.verse: nor should he theorize a view in the world

snp4.5:4.2.verse: in connection with knowledge or habits & practices;

snp4.5:4.4.verse: shouldn’t think himself inferior or superlative.

snp4.5:5.1.verse: Abandoning what he’d embraced, not clinging,

snp4.5:5.2.verse: he doesn’t make himself dependent even in connection with knowledge;

snp4.5:5.3.verse: doesn’t follow a faction among those who are split;

snp4.5:5.4.verse: doesn’t fall back on any view whatsoever.

snp4.5:6.1.verse: One who isn’t inclined toward either side

snp4.5:6.4.verse: when considering what’s grasped among doctrines,

snp4.5:7.1.verse: with regard to what’s seen, heard, or sensed,

snp4.5:7.4.verse: By whom, with what, should he be pigeonholed here in the world?

snp4.5:8.3.verse: A brahman not led by habits or practices,

snp4.5:8.4.verse: gone to the beyond —Such— doesn’t fall back.

snp4.5:1.1.verse: If, maintaining that theirs is the “ultimate” view,

snp4.5:1.2.verse: a personage makes it out to be highest in the world;

snp4.5:1.3.verse: then they declare all others are “lesser”;

snp4.5:1.4.verse: that’s why they’re not beyond disputes.

snp4.5:2.1.verse: If they see an advantage for themselves

snp4.5:2.2.verse: in what’s seen, heard, or thought; or in precepts or vows,

snp4.5:2.3.verse: in that case, having adopted that one alone,

snp4.5:2.4.verse: they see all others as inferior.

snp4.5:3.1.verse: Those who are skilled say that, too, is a knot,

snp4.5:3.2.verse: relying on which people see others as lesser.

snp4.5:3.3.verse: That’s why a mendicant ought not rely

snp4.5:3.4.verse: on what’s seen, heard, or thought, or on precepts and vows.

snp4.5:4.1.verse: Nor would they form a view about the world

snp4.5:4.2.verse: through a notion or through precepts and vows.

snp4.5:4.3.verse: They would never represent themselves as “equal”,

snp4.5:5.1.verse: What was picked up has been set down and is not grasped again;

snp4.5:5.2.verse: they form no dependency even on notions.

snp4.5:5.3.verse: They follow no side among the factions,

snp4.5:5.4.verse: and believe in no view at all.

snp4.5:6.1.verse: One here who has no wish for either end—

snp4.5:6.2.verse: for any state of existence in this life or the next—

snp4.5:6.3.verse: has adopted no dogma at all

snp4.5:7.1.verse: For them not even the tiniest idea is formulated here

snp4.5:7.2.verse: regarding what is seen, heard, or thought.

snp4.5:7.3.verse: That brahmin does not grasp any view—

snp4.5:7.4.verse: how could anyone in this world judge them?

snp4.5:8.1.verse: They don’t make things up or promote them,

snp4.5:8.2.verse: and don’t subscribe to any of the doctrines.

snp4.5:8.3.verse: The brahmin has no need to be led by precept or vow;

snp4.5:8.4.verse: gone to the far shore, one such does not return.

snp4.6:1.2.verse: You die this side of a century,

snp4.6:1.3.verse: but even if you live past,

snp4.6:2.1.verse: People grieve for what they see as mine,

snp4.6:2.2.verse: for nothing possessed is constant, nothing is constantly possessed.

snp4.6:2.3.verse: Seeing this separation simply as it is,

snp4.6:2.4.verse: one shouldn’t follow the household life.

snp4.6:3.4.verse: shouldn’t incline to be devoted to mine-ness.

snp4.6:4.1.verse: what he met in a dream,

snp4.6:4.2.verse: Just as a man doesn’t see on awakening,

snp4.6:4.3.verse: even so, those he held dear,

snp4.6:4.4.verse: he doesn’t see when they are dead —their time done—.

snp4.6:5.2.verse: people are called by this name or that,

snp4.6:5.4.verse: to be pointed to when they are dead.

snp4.6:6.2.verse: are not let go by those greedy for mine,

snp4.6:6.3.verse: so sages, letting go of possessions,

snp4.6:7.3.verse: They say it’s congenial for him,

snp4.6:7.4.verse: he who wouldn’t, in any realm, display self.

snp4.6:8.4.verse: like water on a white lotus, do not adhere.

snp4.6:9.1.verse: As a water bead on a lotus leaf,

snp4.6:9.2.verse: as water on a red lily, doesn’t adhere,

snp4.6:9.4.verse: to the seen, the heard, or the sensed;

snp4.6:10.2.verse: in connection with the seen, the heard, or the sensed.

snp4.6:10.3.verse: In no other way does he wish for purity,

snp4.6:10.4.verse: for he neither takes on passion nor puts it away.

snp4.6:1.2.verse: you die before a hundred years.

snp4.6:1.3.verse: Even if you live a little longer,

snp4.6:1.4.verse: you still die of old age.

snp4.6:2.2.verse: yet there is no such thing as permanent possessions.

snp4.6:2.3.verse: Separation is a fact of life; when you see this,

snp4.6:2.4.verse: you wouldn’t stay living at home.

snp4.6:3.1.verse: Whatever a person thinks of as belonging to them,

snp4.6:3.2.verse: that too is given up when they die.

snp4.6:3.3.verse: Knowing this, an astute follower of mine

snp4.6:3.4.verse: would not be bent on ownership.

snp4.6:4.1.verse: Just as, upon awakening, a person does not see

snp4.6:4.2.verse: what they encountered in a dream;

snp4.6:4.3.verse: so too you do not see your loved ones

snp4.6:4.4.verse: when they are dead and gone.

snp4.6:5.1.verse: You used to see and hear those folk,

snp4.6:5.2.verse: and call them by their name.

snp4.6:5.3.verse: Yet the name is all that’s left to tell

snp4.6:5.4.verse: of a personage when they’re gone.

snp4.6:6.1.verse: Those who are greedy for belongings

snp4.6:6.2.verse: don’t give up sorrow, lamentation, and stinginess.

snp4.6:6.3.verse: That’s why the sages, seers of sanctuary,

snp4.6:7.1.verse: For a mendicant who lives withdrawn,

snp4.6:7.4.verse: to not show themselves in a home.

snp4.6:8.2.verse: they don’t form likes or dislikes.

snp4.6:8.4.verse: slip off them like water from a leaf.

snp4.6:9.1.verse: Like a droplet slips from a lotus-leaf,

snp4.6:9.2.verse: like water from a lotus flower;

snp4.6:9.3.verse: the sage doesn’t cling to that

snp4.6:9.4.verse: which is seen or heard or thought.

snp4.6:10.1.verse: For the one who is cleansed does not conceive

snp4.6:10.2.verse: in terms of things seen, heard, or thought.

snp4.6:10.3.verse: They do not wish to be purified by another;

snp4.6:10.4.verse: they are neither passionate nor growing dispassioned.

snp4.7:1.1.verse: “For one given over to sexual intercourse,

snp4.7:2.1.verse: “In one given over to sexual intercourse,

snp4.7:3.2.verse: but then resorts to sexual intercourse

snp4.7:3.3.verse: —like a carriage out of control, in the world—

snp4.7:3.4.verse: is called vile, a person run-of-the-mill.

snp4.7:4.3.verse: Seeing this, he should train himself

snp4.7:5.2.verse: he broods like a miserable wretch.

snp4.7:6.2.verse: attacked by the words of others.

snp4.7:6.3.verse: This, for him, is a great entanglement.

snp4.7:7.2.verse: when he committed himself to the life alone,

snp4.7:7.3.verse: but now that he’s given to sexual intercourse

snp4.7:8.3.verse: stays firm in the life alone;

snp4.7:9.2.verse: this, for the noble, is highest.

snp4.7:9.3.verse: He wouldn’t, because of that, suppose himself to be better than others:

snp4.7:9.4.verse: He’s on the verge of unbinding.

snp4.7:10.1.verse: a sage remote, leading his life

snp4.7:10.3.verse: —one who’s crossed over the flood—envy him,

snp4.7:1.3.verse: “tell us, good fellow: what trouble befalls them?

snp4.7:2.5.verse: that is something ignoble in them.

snp4.7:3.3.verse: is like a chariot careening off-track;

snp4.7:3.4.verse: in the world they call them a low, ordinary person.

snp4.7:5.3.verse: When they hear what others are saying,

snp4.7:6.1.verse: Then they lash out with verbal daggers

snp4.7:6.3.verse: This is their great blind spot;

snp4.7:7.3.verse: But then they indulged in sex,

snp4.7:7.4.verse: dragged along by desire like a dullard.

snp4.7:8.2.verse: in falling from a former state here,

snp4.7:8.3.verse: a sage would firmly resolve to wander alone,

snp4.7:8.4.verse: and would not resort to sex.

snp4.7:9.1.verse: They’d train themselves only in seclusion;

snp4.7:9.2.verse: this, for the noble ones, is highest.

snp4.7:9.3.verse: One who’d not think themselves ‘best’ due to that

snp4.7:9.4.verse: has truly drawn near to extinguishment.

snp4.7:10.1.verse: People tied to sensual pleasures envy them:

snp4.8:1.1.verse: “Only here is there purity”—that’s what they say—

snp4.8:1.2.verse: “No other doctrines are pure”—so they say.

snp4.8:1.3.verse: Insisting that what they depend on is good,

snp4.8:1.4.verse: they are deeply entrenched in idiosyncratic truths.

snp4.8:2.1.verse: Seeking controversy, they plunge into an assembly,

snp4.8:2.3.verse: Relying on others’ authority, they speak in debate.

snp4.8:2.4.verse: Desiring praise, they claim to be skilled.

snp4.8:3.1.verse: Engaged in disputes in the midst of the assembly,

snp4.8:3.2.verse: —anxious, desiring praise— the one defeated is

snp4.8:3.4.verse: Shaken with criticism, he seeks for an opening.

snp4.8:4.1.verse: He whose doctrine is [judged as] demolished,

snp4.8:4.2.verse: defeated, by those judging the issue:

snp4.8:4.3.verse: He laments, he grieves—the inferior exponent.

snp4.8:5.1.verse: These disputes have arisen among contemplatives.

snp4.8:5.3.verse: Seeing this, one should abstain from disputes,

snp4.8:5.4.verse: for they have no other goal than the gaining of praise.

snp4.8:6.1.verse: While he who is praised there

snp4.8:6.2.verse: for expounding his doctrine in the midst of the assembly,

snp4.8:6.3.verse: laughs on that account & grows haughty,

snp4.8:7.1.verse: That haughtiness will be grounds for his damage,

snp4.8:7.2.verse: for he’ll speak in pride & conceit.

snp4.8:7.3.verse: Seeing this, one should abstain from debates.

snp4.8:7.4.verse: No purity is attained by them, say the skilled.

snp4.8:8.1.verse: Like a strong man nourished on royal food,

snp4.8:8.2.verse: you prowl about, roaring, searching out an opponent.

snp4.8:8.3.verse: Wherever the battle is, go there, strong man.

snp4.8:9.1.verse: Those who dispute, taking hold of a view,

snp4.8:9.2.verse: saying, “This, and this only, is true,”

snp4.8:9.4.verse: Here there is nothing—no confrontation at the birth of disputes.

snp4.8:10.1.verse: among those who live above confrontation—

snp4.8:10.3.verse: Whom would you gain as opponent, Pasūra,

snp4.8:10.4.verse: who have nothing here grasped as supreme?

snp4.8:11.3.verse: You’re paired off with a pure one

snp4.8:1.2.verse: denying that there is purification in other teachings.

snp4.8:1.3.verse: Speaking of the beauty in that which they depend on,

snp4.8:1.4.verse: each one is dogmatic about their own idiosyncratic interpretation.

snp4.8:2.1.verse: Desiring debate, they plunge into an assembly,

snp4.8:2.2.verse: where each takes the other as a fool.

snp4.8:2.3.verse: Relying on others they state their contention,

snp4.8:2.4.verse: desiring praise while claiming to be skilled.

snp4.8:3.1.verse: Addicted to debating in the midst of the assembly,

snp4.8:3.2.verse: their need for praise makes them nervous.

snp4.8:3.3.verse: But when they’re repudiated they get embarrassed;

snp4.8:3.4.verse: upset at criticism, they find fault in others.

snp4.8:4.1.verse: If their doctrine is said to be weak,

snp4.8:5.1.verse: When these disputes come up among ascetics,

snp4.8:5.4.verse: for the only purpose is praise and profit.

snp4.8:6.1.verse: But if, having declared their doctrine,

snp4.8:6.2.verse: they are praised there in the midst of the assembly,

snp4.8:6.3.verse: they laugh and gloat because of it,

snp4.8:7.2.verse: yet they speak from conceit and arrogance.

snp4.8:7.3.verse: Seeing this, one ought not dispute,

snp4.8:7.4.verse: for those who are skilled say this is no way to purity.

snp4.8:8.1.verse: As a warrior, after feasting on royal food,

snp4.8:8.2.verse: goes roaring, looking for someone to fight—

snp4.8:8.3.verse: go off and find an opponent, Sūra,

snp4.8:8.4.verse: for here, as before, there is no one to combat.

snp4.8:9.1.verse: When someone disputes about a view they’ve adopted,

snp4.8:9.3.verse: say to them, “Here you’ll have no adversary

snp4.8:9.4.verse: when a dispute has come up.”

snp4.8:10.1.verse: There are those who live far from the crowd,

snp4.8:10.3.verse: Who is there to argue with you, Pasūra,

snp4.8:10.4.verse: among those who grasp nothing here as the highest?

snp4.8:11.1.verse: And so you come along speculating,

snp4.8:11.2.verse: thinking up theories in your mind.

snp4.8:11.3.verse: Now that you’ve challenged someone who is cleansed,

snp4.8:11.4.verse: you’ll not be able to respond.

snp4.9:1.1.verse: “On seeing [the daughters of Māra] —Discontent, Craving, & Passion—

snp4.9:1.2.verse: there wasn’t even the desire for sex.

snp4.9:1.3.verse: So what would I want with this, filled with urine & excrement?

snp4.9:1.4.verse: I wouldn’t want to touch it even with my foot.”

snp4.9:2.1.verse: “If you don’t want this gem of a woman, coveted

snp4.9:2.3.verse: then for what sort of viewpoint, habit, practice, life,

snp4.9:2.4.verse: attainment of [further] becoming do you argue?”

snp4.9:3.1.verse: “‘I argue for this’ doesn’t occur to one

snp4.9:3.3.verse: when considering what’s grasped among doctrines.

snp4.9:3.4.verse: Looking for what is ungrasped with regard to views,

snp4.9:3.5.verse: and detecting inner peace, I saw.”

snp4.9:4.3.verse: Sage, you speak of not grasping.

snp4.9:4.4.verse: This ‘inner peace’: what does it mean,

snp4.9:4.5.verse: how is it, by the enlightened, proclaimed?”

snp4.9:5.1.verse: “Not by view, not by learning, not by knowledge,

snp4.9:5.3.verse: nor by habit or practice does he speak of purity;

snp4.9:5.4.verse: Nor is it found by a person through lack of view,

snp4.9:5.5.verse: of learning, of knowledge, of habit or practice.

snp4.9:5.7.verse: at peace, independent, one wouldn’t long for becoming.”

snp4.9:6.1.verse: “Well, if not by view, not by learning, not by knowledge,

snp4.9:6.3.verse: nor by habit or practice does he speak of purity;

snp4.9:6.4.verse: and it isn’t found by a person through lack of view,

snp4.9:6.5.verse: of learning, of knowledge, of habit or practice,

snp4.9:6.6.verse: it seems to me that this teaching’s simply confused,

snp4.9:6.7.verse: for some assume a purity in terms of —by means of— a view.”

snp4.9:7.3.verse: you’re confused by the things you have grasped.

snp4.9:7.4.verse: And so you don’t glimpse even the slightest notion [of what I am saying].

snp4.9:7.5.verse: That’s why you think it’s confused.

snp4.9:8.2.verse: whoever supposes this, by that he’d dispute;

snp4.9:8.3.verse: whereas to one unaffected by these three,

snp4.9:9.1.verse: Of what would the brahman say ‘true’

snp4.9:9.2.verse: or ‘false,’ with whom would he dispute?

snp4.9:9.4.verse: with whom would he join in dispute?

snp4.9:10.1.verse: Having abandoned home, living free from society,

snp4.9:10.2.verse: the sage in villages creates no intimacies.

snp4.9:10.4.verse: he wouldn’t engage with people in quarrelsome debate.

snp4.9:11.1.verse: Those things aloof from which he should go about in the world:

snp4.9:11.2.verse: The Nāga wouldn’t take them up & argue for them.

snp4.9:11.5.verse: so the sage, an exponent of peace, without greed,

snp4.9:11.6.verse: is unsmeared by sensuality & the world.

snp4.9:12.1.verse: An attainer-of-knowledge isn’t measured, made proud,

snp4.9:12.2.verse: by views or what’s thought, for he isn’t fashioned of them.

snp4.9:12.3.verse: He wouldn’t be led by action, learning;

snp4.9:12.4.verse: doesn’t reach a conclusion in any entrenchments.

snp4.9:13.1.verse: For one dispassionate toward perception there are no snares;

snp4.9:13.2.verse: for one released by discernment, no delusions.

snp4.9:13.3.verse: Those who grasp at perceptions & views

snp4.9:13.4.verse: go about clashing in the world.”

snp4.9:1.1.verse: “Even when I saw the sirens Craving, Malignancy, and Lust,

snp4.9:1.2.verse: I had no desire for sex.

snp4.9:1.3.verse: What is this body full of piss and shit?

snp4.9:1.4.verse: I wouldn’t even want to touch it with my foot.”

snp4.9:2.1.verse: “If you do not want a gem such as this,

snp4.9:2.2.verse: a lady desired by many lords of men,

snp4.9:2.3.verse: then what manner of theory, precepts and vows, livelihood,

snp4.9:2.4.verse: and rebirth in a new life do you assert?”

snp4.9:3.3.verse: “none have been adopted thinking, ‘I assert this.’

snp4.9:4.1.verse: “O sage, you speak of judgments you have formed,”

snp4.9:4.3.verse: “without having adopted any of those views.

snp4.9:4.4.verse: As to that matter of ‘inner peace’—

snp4.9:4.5.verse: how is that described by the attentive?”

snp4.9:5.1.verse: “Purity is spoken of not as due to view,”

snp4.9:5.6.verse: Having relinquished these, not adopting them,

snp4.9:5.7.verse: peaceful, independent, one would not pray for another life.”

snp4.9:6.1.verse: “It seems purity is spoken of not as due to view,”

snp4.9:6.6.verse: If so, I think this teaching is sheer folly;

snp4.9:6.7.verse: some believe that purity comes from view.”

snp4.9:7.1.verse: “Continuing to question while relying on a view,”

snp4.9:7.3.verse: “you’ve become confused by all you’ve adopted.

snp4.9:7.4.verse: From this you’ve not glimpsed the slightest idea,

snp4.9:7.5.verse: which is why you consider the teaching folly.

snp4.9:8.2.verse: special, or worse’, you’ll dispute about that.

snp4.9:8.3.verse: Not wavering due to the three discriminations,

snp4.9:8.4.verse: they have no thought, ‘I’m equal or special’.

snp4.9:9.1.verse: Why would that brahmin say, ‘It’s true’,

snp4.9:9.2.verse: or with whom would they dispute, ‘It’s false’?

snp4.9:9.3.verse: There is no equal or unequal in them,

snp4.9:9.4.verse: so who would they take on in debate?

snp4.9:10.1.verse: After leaving their bastion to migrate without abode,

snp4.9:10.2.verse: a sage doesn’t get close to anyone in town.

snp4.9:10.3.verse: Rid of sensual pleasures, not expecting,

snp4.9:10.4.verse: they wouldn’t get in arguments with people.

snp4.9:11.1.verse: A spiritual giant would not take up for debate

snp4.9:11.2.verse: the things in the world from which they live secluded.

snp4.9:11.3.verse: As a prickly lotus born in the water

snp4.9:11.4.verse: is unsullied by water and mud,

snp4.9:11.5.verse: so the greedless sage, proponent of peace,

snp4.9:11.6.verse: is unsmeared by sensuality and the world.

snp4.9:12.1.verse: A knowledge master does not become conceited

snp4.9:12.2.verse: due to view or thought, for they are not determined by that.

snp4.9:12.3.verse: They’ve no need for deeds or learning,

snp4.9:13.1.verse: There are no ties for one detached from ideas;

snp4.9:13.2.verse: there are no delusions for one freed by wisdom.

snp4.9:13.3.verse: But those who have adopted ideas and views

snp4.10:1.2.verse: is one said to be at peace?

snp4.10:2.1.verse: “Free from craving before the break-up [of the body],

snp4.10:3.4.verse: he is a sage, his speech under control.

snp4.10:4.1.verse: Free from attachment with regard to the future,

snp4.10:4.3.verse: he sees seclusion in the midst of sensory contacts.

snp4.10:4.4.verse: He can’t be led in terms of views.

snp4.10:5.4.verse: he doesn’t engage in divisive speech.

snp4.10:7.1.verse: Not in hopes of material gain does he take on the training;

snp4.10:7.2.verse: when without material gain he isn’t upset.

snp4.10:7.4.verse: he doesn’t through craving hunger for flavors.

snp4.10:8.2.verse: he doesn’t suppose himself equal, in the world;

snp4.10:8.4.verse: No swellings of pride are his.

snp4.10:9.2.verse: when, on knowing the Dhamma, he’s independent;

snp4.10:9.4.verse: in whom no craving is found:

snp4.10:10.1.verse: He is said to be at peace,

snp4.10:10.3.verse: with nothing at all to tie him down:

snp4.10:11.3.verse: In him you can’t pin down

snp4.10:12.4.verse: which is why he is unperturbed with regard to their words.

snp4.10:13.2.verse: the sage doesn’t speak of himself as among those who are higher,

snp4.10:13.4.verse: He, theory-free, goes to no theory.

snp4.10:14.1.verse: For whom nothing in the world is his own,

snp4.10:14.2.verse: who doesn’t grieve over what is not,

snp4.10:14.3.verse: who doesn’t enter into doctrines, phenomena:

snp4.10:14.4.verse: He is said to be at peace.”

snp4.10:14.5.verse: Before the Break-up (of the Body), the tenth.

snp4.10:1.2.verse: is one said to be at peace?

snp4.10:1.3.verse: When asked, Gotama, please tell me

snp4.10:2.5.verse: they are not governed by anything.

snp4.10:3.4.verse: truly that sage is controlled in speech.

snp4.10:4.1.verse: Rid of attachment to the future,

snp4.10:4.2.verse: they don’t grieve for the past.

snp4.10:4.3.verse: A seer of seclusion in the midst of contacts

snp4.10:4.4.verse: is not led astray among views.

snp4.10:7.1.verse: Not training for desire for profit,

snp4.10:7.2.verse: nor getting annoyed at lack of profit;

snp4.10:7.3.verse: they are not hostile due to craving,

snp4.10:7.4.verse: for they are not greedy for flavors.

snp4.10:8.2.verse: they never conceive themselves in the world

snp4.10:8.3.verse: as equal, special, or less than;

snp4.10:9.2.verse: understanding the teaching, they are independent.

snp4.10:9.3.verse: No craving is found in them

snp4.10:9.4.verse: to continue existence or to end it.

snp4.10:10.1.verse: I declare them to be at peace,

snp4.10:10.3.verse: No ties are found in them,

snp4.10:11.1.verse: They have no children or livestock,

snp4.10:11.3.verse: No picking up or putting down

snp4.10:12.1.verse: That by which one might describe

snp4.10:12.2.verse: an ordinary person or ascetics and brahmins

snp4.10:12.4.verse: which is why they’re unperturbed by words.

snp4.10:13.2.verse: a sage doesn’t speak of themselves as being

snp4.10:13.4.verse: One not prone to creation does not return to creation.

snp4.10:14.1.verse: They who have nothing in the world of their own

snp4.10:14.2.verse: do not grieve for that which is not,

snp4.10:14.4.verse: that’s who is said to be at peace.”

snp4.11:1.1.verse: “From where have there arisen quarrels, disputes,

snp4.11:1.4.verse: From where have they arisen? Please tell me.”

snp4.11:2.1.verse: “From what is dear there have arisen quarrels, disputes,

snp4.11:2.4.verse: Tied up with stinginess are quarrels & disputes.

snp4.11:2.5.verse: In the arising of disputes is divisiveness.”

snp4.11:3.1.verse: “Where is the cause of things dear in the world,

snp4.11:3.2.verse: along with the greeds that go about in the world?

snp4.11:3.3.verse: And where is the cause of the hopes & aims

snp4.11:3.4.verse: for the sake of a person’s next life?”

snp4.11:4.1.verse: “Desires are the cause of things dear in the world,

snp4.11:4.2.verse: along with the greeds that go about in the world.

snp4.11:4.3.verse: And here too is the cause of the hopes & aims

snp4.11:4.4.verse: for the sake of a person’s next life.”

snp4.11:5.1.verse: “Now where is the cause of desire in the world?

snp4.11:5.2.verse: And from where have there arisen decisions,

snp4.11:5.4.verse: and all the qualities described by the Contemplative?”

snp4.11:6.2.verse: In dependence on that, desire arises.

snp4.11:6.3.verse: Having seen becoming & not- with regard to forms,

snp4.11:6.4.verse: a person gives rise to decisions in the world;

snp4.11:7.2.verse: these qualities, too, when there exists that very pair.

snp4.11:7.3.verse: A person perplexed should train for the path of knowledge,

snp4.11:7.4.verse: for it’s in having known that the Contemplative has spoken of qualities/dhammas.”

snp4.11:8.1.verse: “Where is the cause of appealing & un-?

snp4.11:8.2.verse: When what isn’t do they not exist?

snp4.11:8.3.verse: And whatever is meant by becoming & not-:

snp4.11:8.4.verse: Tell me, where is their cause?”

snp4.11:9.1.verse: “Contact is the cause of appealing & un-.

snp4.11:9.2.verse: When contact isn’t, they do not exist,

snp4.11:9.3.verse: along with what’s meant by becoming & not-:

snp4.11:9.4.verse: I tell you, from here is their cause.”

snp4.11:10.1.verse: “Now where is the cause of contact in the world,

snp4.11:10.2.verse: and from where have graspings, possessions, arisen?

snp4.11:10.3.verse: When what isn’t does there not exist mine-ness?

snp4.11:10.4.verse: When what has disappeared do contacts not touch?”

snp4.11:11.2.verse: In longing do graspings, possessions have their cause.

snp4.11:11.3.verse: When longing isn’t, mine-ness doesn’t exist.

snp4.11:11.4.verse: When forms have disappeared contacts don’t touch.”

snp4.11:12.4.verse: My heart is set on knowing how they disappear.”

snp4.11:13.2.verse: not percipient of aberrant perceptions, not unpercipient, nor percipient of what’s disappeared:

snp4.11:13.4.verse: for objectification-classifications have their cause in perception.”

snp4.11:14.1.verse: “What we have asked, you’ve expounded to us.

snp4.11:14.2.verse: We ask one thing more. Please tell it.

snp4.11:14.3.verse: Do some of the wise say that just this much is the utmost,

snp4.11:14.4.verse: that purity of spirit is here;

snp4.11:14.5.verse: Or do they say that it’s other than this?”

snp4.11:15.1.verse: “Some of the wise say that just this much is the utmost,

snp4.11:15.2.verse: that purity of spirit is here.

snp4.11:15.3.verse: But some of them, who say they are skilled,

snp4.11:15.4.verse: say it’s the moment with no clinging remaining.

snp4.11:16.1.verse: But knowing, ‘Having known, they still are dependent,’

snp4.11:16.3.verse: On knowing them, released, he doesn’t get into disputes,

snp4.11:16.4.verse: doesn’t meet with becoming & not-: He’s enlightened.”

snp4.11:1.1.verse: “Where do quarrels and disputes come from?

snp4.11:1.2.verse: And lamentation and sorrow, and stinginess?

snp4.11:1.3.verse: What of conceit and arrogance, and slander too—

snp4.11:1.4.verse: tell me please, where do they come from?”

snp4.11:2.1.verse: “Quarrels and disputes come from what we hold dear,

snp4.11:2.2.verse: as do lamentation and sorrow, stinginess,

snp4.11:2.4.verse: Quarrels and disputes are linked to stinginess,

snp4.11:2.5.verse: and when disputes have arisen there is slander.”

snp4.11:3.1.verse: “So where do things held dear in the world spring from?

snp4.11:3.2.verse: And the lusts that are loose in the world?

snp4.11:3.3.verse: Where spring the hopes and aims

snp4.11:3.4.verse: a man has for lives to come?”

snp4.11:4.1.verse: “What we hold dear in the world spring from desire,

snp4.11:4.2.verse: as do the lusts that are loose in the world.

snp4.11:4.3.verse: From there spring the hopes and aims

snp4.11:4.4.verse: a man has for lives to come.”

snp4.11:5.1.verse: “So where does desire in the world spring from?

snp4.11:5.2.verse: And evaluations, too, where do they come from?

snp4.11:5.4.verse: and other things spoken of by the Ascetic?”

snp4.11:6.1.verse: “What they call pleasure and pain in the world—

snp4.11:6.2.verse: based on that, desire comes about.

snp4.11:6.3.verse: Seeing the manifestation and vanishing of forms,

snp4.11:6.4.verse: a personage makes evaluations in the world.

snp4.11:7.2.verse: these things are, too, when that pair is present.

snp4.11:7.3.verse: One who is indecisive should train in the path of knowledge;

snp4.11:7.4.verse: it is from knowledge that the Ascetic speaks of these things.”

snp4.11:8.1.verse: “Where do pleasure and pain spring from?

snp4.11:8.2.verse: When what is absent do these things not occur?

snp4.11:8.3.verse: And also, on the topic of manifesting and vanishing—

snp4.11:8.4.verse: tell me where they spring from.”

snp4.11:9.2.verse: when contact is absent they do not occur.

snp4.11:9.3.verse: And on the topic of manifesting and vanishing—

snp4.11:9.4.verse: I tell you they spring from there.”

snp4.11:10.1.verse: “So where does contact in the world spring from?

snp4.11:10.2.verse: And possessions, too, where do they come from?

snp4.11:10.3.verse: When what is absent is there no possessiveness?

snp4.11:10.4.verse: When what vanishes do contacts not strike?”

snp4.11:11.3.verse: when wishing is absent there is no possessiveness;

snp4.11:11.4.verse: when form vanishes, contacts don’t strike.”

snp4.11:12.2.verse: And how do happiness and suffering vanish?

snp4.11:12.4.verse: I think we ought to know these things.”

snp4.11:13.2.verse: not lacking perception, nor perceiving what has vanished.

snp4.11:13.3.verse: Form vanishes for one proceeding thus;

snp4.11:13.4.verse: for judgments due to proliferation spring from perception.”

snp4.11:14.1.verse: “Whatever I asked you have explained to me.

snp4.11:14.2.verse: I ask you once more, please tell me this:

snp4.11:14.3.verse: Do some astute folk here say that this is the highest extent

snp4.11:14.5.verse: Or do they say it is something else?”

snp4.11:15.1.verse: “Some astute folk do say that this is the highest extent

snp4.11:15.3.verse: But some of them, claiming to be experts,

snp4.11:15.4.verse: speak of an occasion when there is no residue.

snp4.11:16.1.verse: Knowing that these states are dependent,

snp4.11:16.2.verse: and knowing what they depend on, the inquiring sage,

snp4.11:16.3.verse: having understood, is freed, and enters no dispute.

snp4.11:16.4.verse: The attentive do not proceed to life after life.”

snp4.12:2.3.verse: Which of these statements is true

snp4.12:2.4.verse: when all of them say they are skilled?”

snp4.12:3.1.verse: “If, in not accepting an opponent’s doctrine,

snp4.12:3.2.verse: one’s a fool, a beast of inferior discernment,

snp4.12:3.3.verse: then all are fools of inferior discernment—

snp4.12:3.4.verse: all of these who dwell on their views.

snp4.12:4.1.verse: But if, in siding with a view, one’s cleansed,

snp4.12:4.2.verse: with discernment made pure, sensible, skilled,

snp4.12:4.3.verse: then none of them are of inferior discernment,

snp4.12:4.4.verse: for all of them have their own views.

snp4.12:5.1.verse: I don’t say, ‘That’s how it is,’

snp4.12:5.2.verse: the way fools tell one another.

snp4.12:5.3.verse: They each make out their views to be true

snp4.12:5.4.verse: and so regard their opponents as fools.”

snp4.12:6.1.verse: “What some say is true —‘That’s how it is’—

snp4.12:6.4.verse: Why can’t contemplatives say one thing & the same?”

snp4.12:7.2.verse: there is no second about which a person who knows it would argue with one who knows.

snp4.12:7.3.verse: Contemplatives promote their various own truths,

snp4.12:7.4.verse: that’s why they don’t say one thing & the same.”

snp4.12:8.1.verse: “But why do they say various truths,

snp4.12:8.2.verse: those who say they are skilled?

snp4.12:8.3.verse: Have they learned many various truths

snp4.12:9.2.verse: there are no many various constant truths in the world.

snp4.12:9.3.verse: Theorizing conjectures with regard to views,

snp4.12:9.4.verse: they speak of a pair: true & false.

snp4.12:10.1.verse: Dependent on what’s seen, heard, & sensed,

snp4.12:10.2.verse: dependent on habits & practices, one shows disdain [for others].

snp4.12:10.3.verse: Taking a stance on his decisions, praising himself, he says,

snp4.12:11.1.verse: That by which he regards his opponents as fools

snp4.12:11.2.verse: is that by which he says he is skilled.

snp4.12:11.4.verse: he despises another who speaks the same way.

snp4.12:12.1.verse: Agreeing on a view gone out of bounds,

snp4.12:12.2.verse: drunk with conceit, imagining himself perfect,

snp4.12:12.3.verse: he has consecrated, with his own mind,

snp4.12:12.4.verse: himself as well as his view.

snp4.12:13.1.verse: If, by an opponent’s word, one’s inferior,

snp4.12:13.2.verse: the opponent’s of inferior discernment as well.

snp4.12:13.3.verse: But if, by one’s own word one’s an attainer-of-knowledge, enlightened,

snp4.12:13.4.verse: no one among contemplatives is a fool.

snp4.12:14.1.verse: ‘Those who approve of a doctrine other than this

snp4.12:14.3.verse: That’s what the many sectarians say,

snp4.12:14.4.verse: for they’re smitten with passion for their own views.

snp4.12:15.1.verse: ‘Only here is there purity,’ that’s what they say.

snp4.12:15.2.verse: ‘In no other doctrine is purity,’ they say.

snp4.12:15.3.verse: That’s how the many sectarians are entrenched,

snp4.12:15.4.verse: speaking firmly there concerning their own path.

snp4.12:16.1.verse: Speaking firmly concerning your own path,

snp4.12:16.2.verse: what opponent here would you take as a fool?

snp4.12:16.3.verse: You’d simply bring strife on yourself

snp4.12:16.4.verse: if you said your opponent’s a fool with an impure doctrine.

snp4.12:17.1.verse: Taking a stance on your decisions,

snp4.12:17.2.verse: & yourself as your measure, you dispute further down into the world.

snp4.12:17.3.verse: But a person who’s abandoned all decisions

snp4.12:17.4.verse: creates no strife in the world.”

snp4.12:0.2.verse: The Shorter Discourse on Arrayed For Battle

snp4.12:1.2.verse: those who are skilled disagree, arguing:

snp4.12:1.3.verse: ‘Whoever sees it this way understands the teaching;

snp4.12:1.4.verse: those who reject this are inadequate.’

snp4.12:2.2.verse: saying, ‘The other is a fool, an amateur!’

snp4.12:2.3.verse: Which of these is a true statement,

snp4.12:2.4.verse: for all of them profess to be experts?”

snp4.12:3.2.verse: makes you a useless fool lacking wisdom,

snp4.12:3.3.verse: then they’re all fools lacking wisdom,

snp4.12:3.4.verse: for they all maintain their own view.

snp4.12:4.1.verse: But if having your own view makes you pristine—

snp4.12:4.2.verse: pure in wisdom, expert and thoughtful—

snp4.12:4.3.verse: then none of them lack wisdom,

snp4.12:4.4.verse: for such is the view they have all embraced.

snp4.12:5.1.verse: I do not say that it is correct

snp4.12:5.2.verse: when they call each other fools.

snp4.12:5.3.verse: Each has built up their own view to be the truth,

snp4.12:5.4.verse: which is why they take the other as a fool.”

snp4.12:6.1.verse: “What some say is true and correct,

snp4.12:6.2.verse: others say is hollow and false.

snp4.12:6.4.verse: why don’t ascetics say the same thing?”

snp4.12:7.1.verse: “The truth is one, there is no second,

snp4.12:7.2.verse: understanding which folk would not dispute.

snp4.12:7.3.verse: But those ascetics each boast of different truths;

snp4.12:7.4.verse: that’s why they don’t say the same thing.”

snp4.12:8.1.verse: “But why do they speak of different truths,

snp4.12:8.2.verse: these proponents who profess to be experts?

snp4.12:8.3.verse: Are there really so many different truths,

snp4.12:8.4.verse: or do they just follow their own lines of reasoning?”

snp4.12:9.1.verse: “No, there are not many different truths

snp4.12:9.2.verse: that, apart from perception, are lasting in the world.

snp4.12:9.3.verse: Having formed their reasoning regarding different views,

snp4.12:9.4.verse: they say there are two things: true and false.

snp4.12:10.1.verse: The seen, heard, or thought, or precepts or vows—

snp4.12:10.2.verse: based on these they show disdain.

snp4.12:10.4.verse: saying, ‘The other is a fool, an amateur!’

snp4.12:11.1.verse: They take the other as a fool on the same grounds

snp4.12:11.2.verse: that they speak of themselves as an expert.

snp4.12:11.3.verse: Professing to be expert on their own authority,

snp4.12:11.4.verse: they disdain the other while saying the same thing.

snp4.12:12.1.verse: They are perfect, according to their own extreme view;

snp4.12:12.2.verse: drunk on conceit, imagining themselves proficient.

snp4.12:12.3.verse: They have anointed themselves in their own mind,

snp4.12:12.4.verse: for such is the view they have embraced.

snp4.12:13.1.verse: If the word of your opponent makes you deficient,

snp4.12:13.2.verse: then they too are lacking wisdom.

snp4.12:13.3.verse: But if on your own authority you’re a knowledge master, an attentive one,

snp4.12:13.4.verse: then there are no fools among the ascetics.

snp4.12:14.1.verse: ‘Those who proclaim a teaching other than this

snp4.12:14.2.verse: have fallen short of purity, and are inadequate’:

snp4.12:14.3.verse: so say each one of the sectarians,

snp4.12:14.4.verse: for they are deeply attached to their own view.

snp4.12:15.2.verse: denying that there is purification in other teachings.

snp4.12:15.3.verse: Thus each one of the sectarians, being dogmatic,

snp4.12:15.4.verse: speaks forcefully within the context of their own journey.

snp4.12:16.1.verse: But in that case, so long as they are speaking forcefully of their own journey,

snp4.12:16.2.verse: how can they take the other as a fool?

snp4.12:16.3.verse: They are the ones who provoke conflict

snp4.12:16.4.verse: when they call the other a fool with an impure teaching.

snp4.12:17.1.verse: Standing in judgment, measuring by their own standard,

snp4.12:17.2.verse: they dispute with the world more and more.

snp4.12:17.3.verse: But a personage who has given up all judgments

snp4.12:17.4.verse: creates no conflict in the world.”

snp4.13:2.1.verse: “[The praise:] It’s such a small thing, not at all appeasing.

snp4.13:2.2.verse: I speak of two fruits of dispute;

snp4.13:2.3.verse: and seeing this, you shouldn’t dispute—

snp4.13:2.4.verse: seeing the state where there’s no dispute as secure.”

snp4.13:3.2.verse: any conventions born of the run-of-the mill at all.

snp4.13:3.3.verse: One who’s uninvolved: when he’s forming no predilection

snp4.13:3.4.verse: for what’s seen, for what’s heard, why would he get involved?”

snp4.13:4.1.verse: “Those for whom habits are ultimate say that purity’s a matter of self-restraint.

snp4.13:4.2.verse: Undertaking a practice, they devote themselves to it:

snp4.13:4.3.verse: ‘Let’s train just in this, and then there would be purity.’

snp4.13:4.4.verse: Those who say they are skilled are [thus] led on to becoming.

snp4.13:5.1.verse: But if one of them falls from his habits or practice,

snp4.13:5.2.verse: he trembles, having failed in his actions.

snp4.13:5.3.verse: He hopes for, longs for, purity,

snp4.13:5.4.verse: like a caravan leader lost far from home.

snp4.13:6.1.verse: But one who’s abandoned habits & practices —all—

snp4.13:6.4.verse: would live in kindness & peace, without taking up peace, detached.

snp4.13:7.2.verse: or what’s seen, heard, or sensed,

snp4.13:7.3.verse: they speak of purity through wandering further on through becoming & not-,

snp4.13:7.4.verse: their craving not gone for becoming & not-.

snp4.13:8.1.verse: For one who aspires has longings

snp4.13:8.3.verse: But one who here has no passing away & arising:

snp4.13:8.4.verse: Why would he tremble? For what would he long?”

snp4.13:9.2.verse: is the very one others call ‘lowly.’

snp4.13:9.4.verse: when all of these claim to be skilled?”

snp4.13:10.1.verse: “They say their own teaching is perfect

snp4.13:10.2.verse: while the doctrine of others is lowly.

snp4.13:10.4.verse: each saying his agreed-on opinion is true.

snp4.13:11.1.verse: If something, because of an opponent’s say-so, were lowly,

snp4.13:11.2.verse: then none among teachings would be superlative,

snp4.13:11.3.verse: for many say that another’s teaching’s inferior

snp4.13:12.1.verse: If their worship of their teaching were true,

snp4.13:12.2.verse: in line with the way they praise their own path,

snp4.13:12.3.verse: then all doctrines would be true—

snp4.13:12.4.verse: for purity’s theirs, according to each.

snp4.13:13.1.verse: The brahman has nothing led by another,

snp4.13:13.2.verse: when considering what’s grasped among doctrines.

snp4.13:13.3.verse: Thus he has gone beyond disputes,

snp4.13:13.4.verse: for he doesn’t regard as best the knowledge of a doctrine, any other doctrine.

snp4.13:14.1.verse: ‘I know. I see. That’s just how it is!’—

snp4.13:14.2.verse: Some believe purity’s in terms of view.

snp4.13:14.3.verse: But even if a person has seen, what good does it do him?

snp4.13:14.4.verse: Having slipped past, they speak of purity in connection with something or somebody else.

snp4.13:15.1.verse: A person, in seeing, sees name-&-form.

snp4.13:15.2.verse: Having seen, he’ll know only these things.

snp4.13:15.3.verse: No matter if he’s seen little, a lot,

snp4.13:15.4.verse: the skilled don’t say purity’s in connection with that.

snp4.13:16.1.verse: A person entrenched in his teachings,

snp4.13:16.2.verse: preferring a theorized view, isn’t easy to discipline.

snp4.13:16.3.verse: Whatever he depends on he describes it as lovely,

snp4.13:16.4.verse: says that it’s purity, that there he saw truth.

snp4.13:17.1.verse: The brahman, evaluating, doesn’t enter into a theory,

snp4.13:17.2.verse: doesn’t follow views, isn’t tied even to knowledge.

snp4.13:17.3.verse: And on knowing whatever’s conventional, commonplace,

snp4.13:17.4.verse: he remains equanimous: ‘That’s what others hold onto.’

snp4.13:18.1.verse: Having untied the knots here in the world,

snp4.13:18.2.verse: the sage here in the world doesn’t follow a faction when disputes have arisen.

snp4.13:18.3.verse: At peace among those not at peace, he’s equanimous,

snp4.13:18.4.verse: doesn’t hold on: ‘That’s what others hold onto.’

snp4.13:19.1.verse: Giving up old effluents, not forming new,

snp4.13:19.2.verse: neither pursuing desire, nor entrenched in his teachings,

snp4.13:19.3.verse: he’s totally released from viewpoints, enlightened.

snp4.13:19.4.verse: He doesn’t adhere to the world, is without self-rebuke;

snp4.13:20.1.verse: is enemy-free with regard to all things

snp4.13:20.3.verse: His burden laid down, the sage totally released

snp4.13:20.4.verse: is improper :: is theory-free hasn’t stopped :: isn’t impassioned isn’t worth wanting :: doesn’t desire,” the Blessed One said.

snp4.13:0.2.verse: The Longer Discourse on Arrayed for Battle

snp4.13:1.1.verse: “Regarding those who maintain their own view,

snp4.13:1.2.verse: disputing that, ‘This is the only truth’:

snp4.13:1.3.verse: are all of them subject only to criticism,

snp4.13:1.4.verse: or do some also win praise for that?”

snp4.13:2.1.verse: “That is a small thing, insufficient for peace,

snp4.13:2.2.verse: these two fruits of dispute, I say.

snp4.13:2.3.verse: Seeing this, one ought not dispute,

snp4.13:2.4.verse: looking for sanctuary in the land of no dispute.

snp4.13:3.1.verse: One who knows does not get involved

snp4.13:3.2.verse: with any of the many different conventions.

snp4.13:3.3.verse: Why would the uninvolved get involved,

snp4.13:3.4.verse: since they do not believe based on the seen or the heard?

snp4.13:4.1.verse: Those for whom ethics are the highest speak of purity through self-control;

snp4.13:4.2.verse: having undertaken a vow, they stick to it:

snp4.13:4.3.verse: ‘Let us train right here, then we will be pure.’

snp4.13:4.4.verse: Professing to be experts, they are led on to future lives.

snp4.13:5.1.verse: If they fall away from their precepts and vows,

snp4.13:5.2.verse: they tremble, having failed in their task.

snp4.13:5.3.verse: They pray and long for purity,

snp4.13:5.4.verse: like one who has lost their caravan while journeying far from home.

snp4.13:6.1.verse: But having given up all precepts and vows,

snp4.13:6.2.verse: and these deeds blameworthy or blameless;

snp4.13:7.1.verse: Relying on mortification in disgust of sin,

snp4.13:7.2.verse: or else on what is seen, heard, or thought,

snp4.13:7.3.verse: they moan that purification comes through heading upstream,

snp4.13:7.4.verse: not rid of craving for life after life.

snp4.13:8.1.verse: For one who longs there are muttered prayers,

snp4.13:8.2.verse: and trembling too over ideas they have formed.

snp4.13:8.3.verse: But one here for whom there is no passing away or reappearing:

snp4.13:8.4.verse: why would they tremble? For what would they pray?”

snp4.13:9.1.verse: “The very same teaching that some say is ‘ultimate’,

snp4.13:9.3.verse: Which of these statements is true,

snp4.13:9.4.verse: for all of them profess to be experts?”

snp4.13:10.1.verse: “They say their own teaching is perfect,

snp4.13:10.2.verse: while the teaching of others is inferior.

snp4.13:10.4.verse: each saying their own conventions are the truth.

snp4.13:11.1.verse: If someone else’s disparagement makes you inferior,

snp4.13:11.2.verse: no one in any teaching would be distinguished.

snp4.13:11.3.verse: For each of them says the other’s teaching is lacking,

snp4.13:12.1.verse: But if they honor their own teachings

snp4.13:12.2.verse: just as they praise their own journeys,

snp4.13:12.3.verse: then all doctrines would be equally valid,

snp4.13:12.4.verse: and purity would be specific to them.

snp4.13:13.1.verse: After judging among the teachings, a brahmin has adopted nothing

snp4.13:13.3.verse: That’s why they’ve gotten over disputes,

snp4.13:13.4.verse: for they see no other doctrine as best.

snp4.13:14.1.verse: Saying, ‘I know, I see, that’s how it is’,

snp4.13:14.2.verse: some believe that purity stems from view.

snp4.13:14.3.verse: But if they’ve really seen, what use is that view to them?

snp4.13:14.4.verse: Overlooking what matters, they say purity comes from another.

snp4.13:15.1.verse: When a person sees, they see name and form,

snp4.13:15.2.verse: and having seen, they will know just these things.

snp4.13:15.3.verse: Gladly let them see much or little,

snp4.13:15.4.verse: for those who are skilled say this is no way to purity.

snp4.13:16.1.verse: It’s not easy to educate someone who is dogmatic,

snp4.13:16.2.verse: promoting a view they have formulated.

snp4.13:16.3.verse: Speaking of the beauty in that on which they depend,

snp4.13:16.4.verse: they talk of purity in accord with what they saw there.

snp4.13:17.1.verse: The brahmin does not get involved with formulating and calculating;

snp4.13:17.2.verse: they’re not followers of views, nor kinsmen of notions.

snp4.13:17.3.verse: Having understood the many different conventions,

snp4.13:17.4.verse: they look on when others grasp.

snp4.13:18.1.verse: Having untied the knots here in the world,

snp4.13:18.2.verse: the sage takes no side among disputes.

snp4.13:18.4.verse: they don’t grasp when others grasp.

snp4.13:19.1.verse: Having given up former defilements and not making new ones,

snp4.13:19.2.verse: not swayed by preference, nor a proponent of dogma,

snp4.13:19.3.verse: that attentive one is released from views,

snp4.13:19.4.verse: not clinging to the world, nor reproaching themselves.

snp4.13:20.1.verse: They are remote from all things

snp4.13:20.3.verse: With burden put down, the sage is released:

snp4.13:20.4.verse: not formulating, not abstaining, not longing.”

snp4.14:1.1.verse: “I ask the Kinsman of the Sun, the Great Seer,

snp4.14:1.2.verse: about seclusion & the state of peace.

snp4.14:1.3.verse: Seeing in what way is a monk unbound,

snp4.14:1.4.verse: clinging to nothing in the world?”

snp4.14:2.1.verse: “He should put an entire stop to the root of objectification-classifications:

snp4.14:2.5.verse: to subdue any craving inside him.

snp4.14:3.3.verse: he shouldn’t, because of it, make himself hardened,

snp4.14:3.4.verse: for that isn’t called unbinding by the good.

snp4.14:4.1.verse: He shouldn’t, because of it, think himself

snp4.14:4.3.verse: Touched by contact in various ways,

snp4.14:4.4.verse: he shouldn’t keep theorizing about self.

snp4.14:5.2.verse: a monk shouldn’t seek peace from another, from anything else.

snp4.14:5.4.verse: there’s nothing embraced, so how rejected?

snp4.14:6.1.verse: As in the middle of the sea

snp4.14:6.2.verse: it is still, with no waves upwelling,

snp4.14:7.1.verse: “He whose eyes are open has described

snp4.14:7.2.verse: the Dhamma he’s witnessed, subduing danger.

snp4.14:7.3.verse: Now tell us, sir, the practice:

snp4.14:8.1.verse: “One shouldn’t be careless with his eyes,

snp4.14:8.2.verse: should close his ears to village-talk,

snp4.14:8.4.verse: or view anything in the world as mine.

snp4.14:9.3.verse: shouldn’t covet anywhere any states of becoming,

snp4.14:10.3.verse: he should not make a hoard.

snp4.14:10.4.verse: Nor should he be upset when receiving no gains.

snp4.14:11.4.verse: should live in a noise-less abode.

snp4.14:12.4.verse: laughter, sports, sexual intercourse, & all that goes with it;

snp4.14:13.4.verse: should not be devoted to doing cures or inducing fertility.

snp4.14:14.1.verse: A monk shouldn’t tremble at blame

snp4.14:15.4.verse: or flatter people in hope of gains.

snp4.14:17.3.verse: shouldn’t despise others for their life, discernment,

snp4.14:18.4.verse: for those who retaliate aren’t calm.

snp4.14:19.2.verse: a monk inquiring should always train in it mindfully.

snp4.14:19.4.verse: he shouldn’t be heedless of Gotama’s message—

snp4.14:20.2.verse: witnessed the Dhamma, not by hearsay, but directly, himself.

snp4.14:20.3.verse: So, heedful, you should always do homage & train

snp4.14:20.4.verse: in line with that Blessed One’s message,” the Blessed One said.

snp4.14:1.1.verse: “Great seer, I ask you, the Kinsman of the Sun,

snp4.14:1.2.verse: about seclusion and the state of peace.

snp4.14:1.3.verse: How, having seen, is a mendicant extinguished,

snp4.14:1.4.verse: not grasping anything in this world?”

snp4.14:2.1.verse: “They would cut off the idea, ‘I am the thinker’,”

snp4.14:2.3.verse: “which is the root of all judgments that emerge from proliferation.

snp4.14:2.4.verse: Ever mindful, they would train to remove

snp4.14:3.1.verse: Regardless of what things they know,

snp4.14:3.3.verse: they wouldn’t be proud because of that,

snp4.14:3.4.verse: for that is not quenching, say the good.

snp4.14:4.1.verse: They wouldn’t let that make them conceited,

snp4.14:4.2.verse: thinking themselves better or worse or alike.

snp4.14:5.1.verse: A mendicant would be settled internally,

snp4.14:5.2.verse: and not seek peace from another.

snp4.14:5.3.verse: For one at peace inside themselves,

snp4.14:5.4.verse: there’s no picking up, whence putting down?

snp4.14:6.1.verse: Just as, in the middle of the ocean,

snp4.14:6.2.verse: no waves arise, it stays still;

snp4.14:6.3.verse: so too one unstirred is still—

snp4.14:6.4.verse: a mendicant would make no pretension regarding anything.”

snp4.14:7.1.verse: “He whose eyes are open has explained

snp4.14:7.2.verse: the truth he witnessed, where adversities are removed.

snp4.14:7.3.verse: Please now speak of the practice, sir,

snp4.14:7.4.verse: the monastic code and immersion in samādhi.”

snp4.14:8.2.verse: they’d turn their ears from village gossip.

snp4.14:8.3.verse: They wouldn’t be greedy for flavors,

snp4.14:8.4.verse: nor possessive about anything in the world.

snp4.14:9.2.verse: a mendicant would not lament at all.

snp4.14:9.3.verse: They wouldn’t pray for another life,

snp4.14:9.4.verse: nor tremble in the face of dangers.

snp4.14:10.1.verse: When they receive food and drink,

snp4.14:10.4.verse: nor worry about not getting them.

snp4.14:11.2.verse: they’d avoid remorse and not be negligent.

snp4.14:11.4.verse: in quiet places to sit and rest.

snp4.14:12.2.verse: but, being keen, would apply themselves to wakefulness.

snp4.14:12.3.verse: They’d give up sloth, illusion, mirth, and play,

snp4.14:13.1.verse: They wouldn’t cast Artharvaṇa spells, interpret dreams

snp4.14:13.3.verse: My followers would not study ominous animal cries,

snp4.14:13.4.verse: work as a doctor, or treat an impacted fetus.

snp4.14:14.2.verse: a mendicant would not gloat when praised.

snp4.14:14.3.verse: They’d cast aside greed and stinginess,

snp4.14:15.1.verse: They’d not stand for buying and selling;

snp4.14:15.2.verse: a mendicant would not speak ill at all.

snp4.14:15.3.verse: They wouldn’t linger in the village,

snp4.14:15.4.verse: nor cajole people from desire for profit.

snp4.14:16.1.verse: A mendicant would be no boaster,

snp4.14:17.1.verse: They wouldn’t be led into lying,

snp4.14:17.3.verse: And they’d never look down on another

snp4.14:17.4.verse: because of livelihood, wisdom, or precepts and vows.

snp4.14:18.1.verse: Though provoked from hearing much talk

snp4.14:18.2.verse: from ascetics saying all different things,

snp4.14:18.4.verse: for the virtuous do not retaliate.

snp4.14:19.2.verse: inquiring, a mendicant would always train mindfully.

snp4.14:19.4.verse: they’d not be negligent in Gotama’s bidding.

snp4.14:20.1.verse: For he is the vanquisher, the unvanquished,

snp4.14:20.2.verse: seer of the truth as witness, not by legends—

snp4.14:20.3.verse: that’s why, being diligent, they would always train

snp4.15:1.1.verse: “When embraced, the rod of violence breeds danger & fear:

snp4.15:1.3.verse: I will tell how I experienced

snp4.15:2.4.verse: as I saw this, fear came into me.

snp4.15:3.1.verse: The world was entirely without substance.

snp4.15:3.2.verse: All the directions were knocked out of line.

snp4.15:3.4.verse: I saw nothing that wasn’t laid claim to.

snp4.15:4.1.verse: Seeing nothing in the end but competition,

snp4.15:4.3.verse: And then I saw an arrow here,

snp4.15:4.4.verse: so very hard to see, embedded in the heart.

snp4.15:5.3.verse: But simply on pulling it out

snp4.15:5.4.verse: you don’t run, you don’t sink.

snp4.15:6.2.verse: Whatever things are tied down in the world,

snp4.15:6.3.verse: you shouldn’t be set on them.

snp4.15:6.4.verse: Having totally penetrated sensual pleasures, sensual passions,

snp4.15:6.5.verse: you should train for your own unbinding.

snp4.15:7.3.verse: Without anger, the sage should cross over the evil

snp4.15:8.1.verse: He should conquer drowsiness, weariness, sloth;

snp4.15:8.3.verse: shouldn’t stand firm in his pride—

snp4.15:8.4.verse: the man with his heart set on unbinding.

snp4.15:10.4.verse: get entangled in what’s dazzling & bright.

snp4.15:11.1.verse: I call greed a great flood;

snp4.15:11.4.verse: sensuality, a bog hard to cross over.

snp4.15:12.1.verse: Not deviating from truth, a sage

snp4.15:12.2.verse: stands on high ground: a brahman.

snp4.15:12.4.verse: he is said to be at peace;

snp4.15:13.1.verse: having clearly known, he is an attainer-of-knowledge;

snp4.15:14.1.verse: Whoever here has gone beyond sensual passions—

snp4.15:14.2.verse: an attachment hard to transcend in the world—

snp4.15:14.4.verse: He, his stream cut, is free from bonds.

snp4.15:15.3.verse: If you don’t grasp at what’s in between,

snp4.15:16.1.verse: For whom, in name-&-form, in every way,

snp4.15:16.3.verse: and who doesn’t grieve over what is not:

snp4.15:16.4.verse: He, in the world, isn’t defeated, suffers no loss.

snp4.15:17.1.verse: To whom there doesn’t occur ‘This is mine,’

snp4.15:17.3.verse: He, feeling no sense of mine-ness,

snp4.15:17.4.verse: doesn’t grieve at the thought ‘I have nothing.’

snp4.15:18.3.verse: This is the reward —I say when asked—

snp4.15:18.4.verse: for those who are free from theorizing.

snp4.15:20.1.verse: The sage doesn’t speak of himself

snp4.15:20.2.verse: as among those who are higher, equal, or lower.

snp4.15:20.4.verse: he doesn’t embrace, doesn’t reject,” the Blessed One said.

snp4.15:1.1.verse: Peril stems from those who take up arms—

snp4.15:1.3.verse: I shall extol how I came to be

snp4.15:1.4.verse: stirred with a sense of urgency.

snp4.15:2.2.verse: like a fish in a little puddle.

snp4.15:2.3.verse: Seeing them at odds with each other,

snp4.15:4.1.verse: Yet even in their settlement they were at odds—

snp4.15:4.3.verse: Then I saw a dart there,

snp4.15:4.4.verse: so hard to see, stuck in the heart.

snp4.15:5.2.verse: you run around in all directions.

snp4.15:5.3.verse: But when that same dart has been plucked out,

snp4.15:5.4.verse: you neither run around nor sink down.

snp4.15:6.1.verse: (On that topic, the trainings are recited.)

snp4.15:6.2.verse: Whatever attachments there are in the world,

snp4.15:6.4.verse: Having pierced through sensual pleasures in every way,

snp4.15:7.2.verse: free of deceit, and rid of slander;

snp4.15:7.3.verse: without anger, a sage would cross over

snp4.15:7.4.verse: the evils of greed and avarice.

snp4.15:8.1.verse: Prevail over sleepiness, sloth, and drowsiness,

snp4.15:9.2.verse: or get caught up in affection for form.

snp4.15:10.3.verse: Don’t grieve for what is running out,

snp4.15:10.4.verse: or get attached to things that pull you in.

snp4.15:11.1.verse: Greed, I say, is the great flood,

snp4.15:11.4.verse: the swamp of sensuality so hard to get past.

snp4.15:12.1.verse: The sage never strays from the truth;

snp4.15:12.2.verse: the brahmin stands on solid ground.

snp4.15:12.4.verse: they are said to be at peace.

snp4.15:13.1.verse: They have truly known, they’re a knowledge master,

snp4.15:13.2.verse: understanding the teaching, they are independent.

snp4.15:13.3.verse: They rightly proceed in the world,

snp4.15:14.1.verse: One who has crossed over sensuality here,

snp4.15:14.2.verse: the chain in the world so hard to get past,

snp4.15:14.4.verse: they’ve cut the strings, they’re no longer bound.

snp4.15:15.1.verse: What came before, let wither away,

snp4.15:15.2.verse: and after, let there be nothing.

snp4.15:15.3.verse: If you don’t grasp at the middle,

snp4.15:16.1.verse: One who has no sense of ownership

snp4.15:16.2.verse: in the whole realm of name and form,

snp4.15:16.3.verse: does not grieve for that which is not,

snp4.15:16.4.verse: they suffer no loss in the world.

snp4.15:17.1.verse: If you don’t think of anything

snp4.15:17.2.verse: as belonging to yourself or others,

snp4.15:17.4.verse: you won’t grieve, thinking “I don’t have it”.

snp4.15:18.3.verse: when asked about one who is unwavering,

snp4.15:18.4.verse: I declare that that is the benefit.

snp4.15:20.1.verse: A sage doesn’t speak of themselves as being

snp4.15:20.4.verse: they are neither ditching nor taking up.

snp4.16:1.4.verse: of a teacher with such lovely speech

snp4.16:1.5.verse: come, together with his following from Tusita heaven,

snp4.16:2.2.verse: who appears to the world with its devas,

snp4.16:2.4.verse: having arrived at delight all alone.

snp4.16:3.1.verse: To that One Awakened— unentangled, Such,

snp4.16:3.3.verse: I have come desiring a question on behalf of the many

snp4.16:4.3.verse: the root of a tree, a cemetery,

snp4.16:4.4.verse: in mountain caves various places to stay—

snp4.16:5.2.verse: how many are the fears there

snp4.16:6.1.verse: how many the dangers in the world

snp4.16:6.2.verse: for the monk going the direction he never has gone

snp4.16:7.1.verse: What should be the ways of his speech?

snp4.16:7.2.verse: What should be his range there of action?

snp4.16:7.3.verse: What should be a resolute monk’s

snp4.16:8.3.verse: would he blow away his own impurities

snp4.16:8.4.verse: as a silver smith, those in molten silver?”

snp4.16:9.3.verse: if he’s resorting to a place remote,

snp4.16:9.4.verse: desiring self-awakening in line with the Dhamma,

snp4.16:9.5.verse: I will tell you, as one who knows.

snp4.16:10.1.verse: An enlightened monk shouldn’t fear the five fears:

snp4.16:11.1.verse: shouldn’t be fazed by those following another’s teaching

snp4.16:11.2.verse: even on seeing their manifold threats;

snp4.16:11.3.verse: should prevail over still other further dangers

snp4.16:11.4.verse: as he seeks what is skillful.

snp4.16:12.1.verse: Touched by the touch of disease, hunger,

snp4.16:12.2.verse: he should endure cold & inordinate heat.

snp4.16:12.3.verse: He with no home, in many ways touched by these things,

snp4.16:12.4.verse: striving, should make firm his persistence.

snp4.16:13.1.verse: He shouldn’t commit a theft, shouldn’t speak a lie,

snp4.16:13.2.verse: should touch with thoughts of goodwill beings firm & infirm.

snp4.16:13.3.verse: Conscious of when his mind is stirred up & turbid,

snp4.16:13.4.verse: he should dispel it: ‘It’s on the side of the Dark One.’

snp4.16:14.1.verse: He shouldn’t come under the sway of anger or pride.

snp4.16:14.2.verse: Having dug up their root he would stand firm.

snp4.16:14.4.verse: he’d prevail over notions of dear & undear.

snp4.16:15.1.verse: Deferring to discernment enraptured with what’s admirable,

snp4.16:15.3.verse: should conquer discontent in his isolated spot,

snp4.16:15.4.verse: should conquer these four thoughts of lament:

snp4.16:16.1.verse: ‘What will I eat, or where will I eat?

snp4.16:16.2.verse: How badly I slept. Tonight where will I sleep?’

snp4.16:16.4.verse: he should subdue— one under training, wandering without home.

snp4.16:17.1.verse: Receiving food & cloth at appropriate times,

snp4.16:17.2.verse: he should have a sense of enough for the sake of contentment.

snp4.16:17.3.verse: Guarded in regard to these things going restrained into a village,

snp4.16:17.4.verse: even when harassed he shouldn’t say a harsh word.

snp4.16:18.2.verse: committed to jhāna, he should be continually wakeful.

snp4.16:18.4.verse: he should cut off any penchant to conjecture or worry.

snp4.16:19.1.verse: When reprimanded with words, he should—mindful— rejoice;

snp4.16:19.2.verse: should smash any rigidity toward his fellows in the holy life;

snp4.16:19.3.verse: should utter skillful words that are not untimely;

snp4.16:19.4.verse: should give no mind to the gossip people might say.

snp4.16:20.1.verse: And then there are in the world the five kinds of dust

snp4.16:20.2.verse: for whose subduing, mindful, he should train:

snp4.16:20.3.verse: With regard to forms, sounds, tastes,

snp4.16:20.4.verse: smells, & tactile sensations he should conquer passion;

snp4.16:21.1.verse: with regard to these things he should subdue his desire.

snp4.16:21.2.verse: A monk, mindful, his mind well released,

snp4.16:21.3.verse: contemplating the right Dhamma at the right times,

snp4.16:21.4.verse: on coming to oneness should annihilate darkness,” the Blessed One said.

snp4.16:21.6.verse: The Chapter of Eights, the fourth.

snp4.16:22.1.verse: Sensuality, the Cave, and the Corrupted,

snp4.16:22.2.verse: the Pure, the Supreme, and Old Age;

snp4.16:22.4.verse: To Māgandiya, and Before the Break-up;

snp4.16:23.4.verse: and the one Asked by the Elder—sixteen.

snp4.16:1.4.verse: about a teacher of such graceful speech,

snp4.16:1.5.verse: come from Tusita heaven to lead a community.

snp4.16:2.2.verse: he appears as a Clear-eyed One

snp4.16:3.1.verse: On behalf of the many here still bound,

snp4.16:3.2.verse: I have come seeking with a question

snp4.16:3.4.verse: free of deceit, come to lead a community.

snp4.16:4.1.verse: Suppose a mendicant who loathes attachment

snp4.16:4.3.verse: the root of a tree, a charnel ground,

snp4.16:5.3.verse: at which a mendicant in their silent lodging

snp4.16:6.2.verse: how many adversities are there in the world
