snp4.16:8.3.verse: would they purge their own stains,

snp4.16:9.1.verse: “If one who loathes attachment frequents a lonely lodging,”

snp4.16:9.3.verse: “in their search for awakening—as accords with the teaching—

snp4.16:9.4.verse: I shall tell you, as I understand it,

snp4.16:10.2.verse: should not be afraid of five perils:

snp4.16:11.2.verse: even having seen the many threats they pose.

snp4.16:11.3.verse: And then one seeking the good

snp4.16:12.3.verse: Though afflicted by many such things, the homeless one

snp4.16:13.4.verse: they should dispel it as Māra’s ally.

snp4.16:14.2.verse: having dug them out by the root, they would stand firm.

snp4.16:16.3.verse: The trainee, the migrant without abode,

snp4.16:17.3.verse: Guarded in these things, walking restrained in the village,

snp4.16:17.4.verse: they wouldn’t speak harshly even when provoked.

snp4.16:18.4.verse: they should cut off worrisome habits of thought.

snp4.16:19.3.verse: They may utter skillful speech, but not for too long,

snp4.16:21.1.verse: Having removed desire for these things,

snp4.16:21.2.verse: a mindful mendicant, their heart well freed,

snp4.16:21.3.verse: rightly investigating the Dhamma in good time,

snp4.16:21.4.verse: at one, would banish the darkness.”

thag1.73:1.2.verse: and a corpse come to the end of life,

thag1.73:1.3.verse: I went forth, becoming a wanderer,

thag1.73:1.4.verse: and giving up the pleasures of the senses.

thag1.74:1.4.verse: are not found in a monk at all.

thag1.75:1.1.verse: Good is the sight of those who’ve practiced well:

thag1.75:1.2.verse: doubt is cut off and intelligence grows—

thag1.75:1.4.verse: That’s why it’s good to meet good people.

thag1.76:1.1.verse: Settle down when others spring up;

thag1.76:1.2.verse: spring up when others settle down.

thag1.77:1.1.verse: In the past my mind wandered

thag1.77:1.2.verse: how it wished, where it liked, as it pleased.

thag1.77:1.4.verse: as a trainer with a hook guides a rutting elephant.

thag1.78:1.4.verse: the mass of suffering has fallen away.

thag1.79:1.1.verse: All my lust is given up,

thag1.80:1.4.verse: now there’ll be no more future lives.

thag1.81:1.3.verse: are to be experienced right here,

thag1.82:1.3.verse: where it’s safe and free of peril—

thag1.82:1.4.verse: may you not be overcome by sorrow!

thag1.83:1.4.verse: and quickly discard this bag of bones.

thag1.85:1.1.verse: Skilled in the patterns of the mind,

thag1.85:1.4.verse: such a person would realize pleasure not of the flesh.

thag1.86:1.1.verse: Elsewhere there are many other doctrines;

thag1.86:1.2.verse: paths that, unlike this, don’t lead to extinguishment.

thag1.86:1.3.verse: For the Buddha himself instructs the Saṅgha;

thag1.86:1.4.verse: the Teacher shows the palms of his hands.

thag1.87:1.1.verse: The aggregates are seen as they truly are;

thag1.87:1.4.verse: now there’ll be no more future lives.

thag1.88:1.1.verse: I was able to lift myself up

thag1.88:1.2.verse: from the water to the shore.

thag1.88:1.3.verse: While being swept away by the great flood,

thag1.89:1.3.verse: I’m freed from floods and ties,

thag1.89:1.4.verse: and I’ve wiped out all conceit.

thag1.90:1.1.verse: The five aggregates are fully understood;

thag1.90:1.2.verse: they remain, but their root is cut.

thag1.90:1.4.verse: now there’ll be no more future lives.

thag1.91:1.1.verse: What I consumed today is considered better

thag1.91:1.2.verse: than delicious grain of a hundred flavors—

thag1.91:1.3.verse: the Dhamma taught by the Buddha,

thag1.92:1.4.verse: of the signless and the empty:

thag1.92:1.5.verse: their track is hard to trace,

thag1.93:1.5.verse: One who doesn’t enjoy sensual pleasures

thag1.94:1.4.verse: he beautifully taught the best teaching.

thag1.95:1.1.verse: I’m blind, my eyes are ruined,

thag1.95:1.3.verse: Even if I have to crawl I’ll keep going—

thag1.96:1.2.verse: and then amused myself in heavens

thag1.96:1.4.verse: with what’s left over I’ve become quenched.

thag1.97:1.1.verse: Giving up a hundred ounces of bronze,

thag1.97:1.2.verse: and a hundred grains of gold,

thag1.97:1.3.verse: I took a bowl made of clay:

thag1.98:1.1.verse: When you see a sight, mindfulness is lost

thag1.98:1.2.verse: as you focus on a pleasant feature.

thag1.98:1.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,

thag1.98:1.6.verse: leading to the root of rebirth.

thag1.99:1.1.verse: When you hear a sound, mindfulness is lost

thag1.99:1.2.verse: as you focus on a pleasant feature.

thag1.99:1.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,

thag1.100:1.1.verse: Accomplished in the four right efforts,

thag1.100:1.3.verse: festooned with the flowers of liberation,

thag1.101:1.1.verse: He’s given up the household life, but is far from perfect.

thag1.101:1.2.verse: Living for his belly, lazy, he uses his snout as a plow,

thag1.101:1.3.verse: like a great hog stuffed with grain.

thag1.101:1.4.verse: That dullard is reborn again and again.

thag1.103:1.1.verse: I have no need of this—

thag1.103:1.2.verse: I’m happy and satisfied with the sweet teaching.

thag1.103:1.3.verse: I’ve drunk the best, the supreme nectar:

thag1.104:1.2.verse: full of so much rapture and happiness.

thag1.104:1.3.verse: My body feels like it’s floating,

thag1.105:1.2.verse: and even if happy, one should leave.

thag1.105:1.3.verse: One who sees clearly wouldn’t stay

thag1.105:1.4.verse: in a place that was not conducive to the goal.

thag1.106:1.1.verse: Though the meaning has a hundred facets,

thag1.106:1.3.verse: the simpleton sees only one factor,

thag1.106:1.4.verse: while the sage sees a hundred.

thag1.107:1.2.verse: from the lay life to homelessness.

thag1.109:1.1.verse: Even on retreat he doesn’t heed the counsel

thag1.109:1.2.verse: of the one with supreme compassion for his welfare.

thag1.109:1.4.verse: like a young deer in the woods.

thag1.110:1.1.verse: The trees on the mountain tops have grown tall,

thag1.110:1.3.verse: For Usabha, who loves seclusion, and who thinks only of wilderness,

thag1.111:1.1.verse: Going forth is hard; living at home is hard;

thag1.111:1.2.verse: Dhamma is profound; money is hard to come by.

thag1.111:1.3.verse: Getting by is difficult for we who accept whatever comes,

thag1.111:1.4.verse: so we should always think about impermanence.

thag1.112:1.1.verse: I am a master of the three knowledges, I’m a great meditator,

thag1.112:1.2.verse: an expert in serenity of heart.

thag1.113:1.1.verse: The water’s clear and the rocks are broad,

thag1.113:1.2.verse: monkeys and deer are all around;

thag1.114:1.4.verse: how can you find happiness as an ascetic?

thag1.116:1.1.verse: I’ve given up the six spheres of sense-contact,

thag1.116:1.2.verse: my sense doors are guarded and well restrained;

thag1.116:1.3.verse: I’ve ejected the root of gloom

thag1.116:1.4.verse: and attained the ending of defilements.

thag1.118:1.1.verse: Old age falls like a curse;

thag1.118:1.2.verse: it’s the same body, but it seems like someone else’s.

thag1.118:1.3.verse: I remember myself as if I were someone else,

thag1.118:1.4.verse: but I’m still the same, I haven’t been away.

thag1.119:1.1.verse: You’ve left for the jungle, the root of a tree,

thag1.119:1.2.verse: having laid extinguishment in your heart.

thag1.119:1.4.verse: What use is this hullabaloo to you?

thag1.120:1.1.verse: The five aggregates are fully understood,

thag1.120:1.2.verse: they remain, but their root is cut.

thag1.120:1.3.verse: I have reached the end of suffering

thag1.120:1.4.verse: and attained the ending of defilements.

thag2.1:1.4.verse: and pass away, again and again.

thag2.1:2.2.verse: I have no need for another life.

thag2.1:2.4.verse: and attained the ending of defilements.

thag2.1:2.5.verse: That is how these verses were recited by the senior venerable Uttara.

thag2.2:1.2.verse: but food doesn’t lead to peace of heart.

thag2.2:1.3.verse: Seeing how this bag of bones is sustained by food,

thag2.2:2.1.verse: They know it’s just a swamp,

thag2.2:2.2.verse: this homage and veneration in respectable families.

thag2.2:2.3.verse: Honor is a subtle dart, hard to extract,

thag2.2:2.4.verse: and hard for a reprobate to give up.

thag2.2:2.5.verse: That is how these verses were recited by the senior venerable Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer.

thag2.3:1.1.verse: A monkey went up to the little hut

thag2.3:1.4.verse: on each door, again and again.

thag2.4:1.1.verse: My hut on the bank of the Ganges

thag2.4:1.2.verse: is made from three palm leaves.

thag2.4:1.3.verse: My alms-bowl is a funeral pot,

thag2.4:2.1.verse: In my first two rainy seasons

thag2.4:2.4.verse: the mass of darkness was shattered.

thag2.5:1.1.verse: Even a master of the three knowledges,

thag2.5:1.3.verse: is looked down upon for being unknown

thag2.5:2.4.verse: even if they are of bad character.

thag2.6:1.3.verse: I wasn’t aware of any doubt

thag2.6:2.1.verse: the caravan leader, the great hero,

thag2.7:2.1.verse: Just as rain doesn’t seep into

thag2.8:1.3.verse: what they call a “net” is given up;

thag2.8:1.4.verse: the leash to existence is eradicated.

thag2.8:2.2.verse: for the sake of which I went forth

thag2.8:2.3.verse: from the lay life to homelessness—

thag2.9:1.2.verse: when they’re not bound to women.

thag2.9:1.3.verse: For the truth is hard to find among them

thag2.9:1.4.verse: and one must always be guarded.

thag2.9:2.2.verse: We’re not in your debt any more.

thag2.10:1.4.verse: like one who kills birds using a dead bird as a decoy.

thag2.10:2.1.verse: A brahmin’s color is not on the outside;

thag2.10:2.2.verse: a brahmin is colored on the inside.

thag2.10:2.4.verse: is truly a dark one, Sujampati.

thag2.11:1.1.verse: It’s from eagerness to learn that learning grows;

thag2.11:1.3.verse: by wisdom, you know the goal;

thag2.11:2.2.verse: and practice to be released from fetters.

thag2.11:2.3.verse: If you don’t find enjoyment there,

thag2.11:2.4.verse: live in the Saṅgha, self-protected and mindful.

thag2.12:1.4.verse: hurting them in all kinds of ways—

thag2.12:1.5.verse: they’re treated in the same way;

thag2.12:2.3.verse: they are the heir to each

thag2.13:1.1.verse: The days and nights rush by,

thag2.13:1.2.verse: and then life is cut short.

thag2.13:1.3.verse: The life of mortals wastes away,

thag2.13:1.4.verse: like the water in tiny streams.

thag2.13:2.4.verse: for the result will be bad for them.

thag2.14:1.1.verse: If you’re lost in the middle of a great sea,

thag2.14:1.2.verse: and you clamber up on a little log, you’ll sink.

thag2.14:1.3.verse: So too, a person who lives well

thag2.14:1.4.verse: sinks by relying on a lazy person.

thag2.14:1.6.verse: a lazy person who lacks energy.

thag2.15:2.1.verse: So what’s the point of people,

thag2.16:1.1.verse: There’s a big black woman who looks like a crow.

thag2.16:1.2.verse: She broke off thigh-bones, first one then another;

thag2.16:1.3.verse: she broke off arm-bones, first one then another;

thag2.16:1.4.verse: she broke off a skull like a curd-bowl, and then

thag2.16:2.1.verse: When an ignorant person builds up attachments,

thag2.16:2.2.verse: that dullard returns to suffering again and again.

thag2.16:2.3.verse: So let one who understands not build up attachments:

thag2.16:2.4.verse: may I never again lie with a broken skull!

thag2.17:1.1.verse: A shaven one wrapped in the outer robe

thag2.17:1.3.verse: when they receive food and drink,

thag2.18:1.1.verse: In the Park of the East-Raftered Hall

thag2.18:1.4.verse: are happy with the scraps in their bowls.

thag2.18:2.4.verse: they enjoy the delights of the Dhamma.

thag2.19:1.1.verse: Because of focusing on the wrong things,

thag2.19:1.4.verse: racked by desire for pleasures of the senses.

thag2.19:2.1.verse: But with the help of the Buddha,

thag2.19:2.2.verse: the Kinsman of the Sun, so skilled in means,

thag2.19:2.4.verse: attachment to continued existence from my mind.

thag2.21:1.3.verse: I’ve developed the factors of awakening,

thag2.21:1.4.verse: I’ve attained the ending of defilements.

thag2.21:2.2.verse: having plucked out the weaver of the web,

thag2.21:2.3.verse: having developed the factors of awakening,

thag2.21:2.4.verse: being undefiled, I will be fully extinguished.

thag2.22:1.1.verse: There was a king named Panāda

thag2.22:1.2.verse: who had a sacrificial post all golden.

thag2.22:1.3.verse: Its height was sixteen times its width,

thag2.22:1.4.verse: and the top was a thousandfold.

thag2.22:2.1.verse: It had a thousand panels and a hundred ball-caps,

thag2.22:2.2.verse: all adorned with banners, and made of sun gold.

thag2.23:1.1.verse: As a monk, mindful and wise,

thag2.23:2.2.verse: the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold path,

thag2.24:1.1.verse: The duty of one whose energy is strong;

thag2.24:1.2.verse: the duty of one who longs to wake up:

thag2.24:1.3.verse: that I’ll do, I won’t fail—

thag2.24:2.2.verse: the direct route whose objective is freedom from death.

thag2.24:2.4.verse: as the Ganges knows the ocean.

thag2.25:2.2.verse: I once was blind, but the darkness disappeared.

thag2.25:2.3.verse: My fancy hairdo has been cut off:

thag2.25:2.4.verse: now there’ll be no more future lives.

thag2.26:1.1.verse: I gave up the five hindrances

thag2.26:1.2.verse: for the sake of sanctuary from the yoke.

thag2.26:1.3.verse: I took Dhamma as a mirror

thag2.26:2.2.verse: all of it, inside and out.

thag2.27:1.1.verse: Though a fine thoroughbred may stumble,

thag2.27:2.1.verse: Even so is one accomplished in vision,

thag2.28:2.1.verse: The sage gave us the going forth

thag2.28:2.2.verse: out of compassion, so we could realize

thag2.28:2.4.verse: now we have reached that goal.

thag2.29:1.1.verse: This is how the wise roar:

thag2.29:1.4.verse: having vanquished Māra with his legions.

thag2.29:2.2.verse: I’ve honored the Dhamma and the Saṅgha;

thag2.29:2.4.verse: because I’ve seen my son free of defilements.

thag2.30:1.1.verse: I regularly sat close by true persons

thag2.30:1.4.verse: the direct route whose objective is freedom from death.

thag2.30:2.1.verse: I’ve slain the desire for continued existence,

thag2.30:2.2.verse: it won’t be found in me again.

thag2.30:2.3.verse: It was not, and it won’t be in me,

thag2.30:2.4.verse: and it isn’t found in me now.

thag2.31:1.2.verse: in the teaching of the Buddha,

thag2.31:1.3.verse: while letting go, I rose up;

thag2.31:2.1.verse: Then, as the supreme one looked on,

thag2.31:2.4.verse: with the ending of all fetters.

thag2.32:1.2.verse: on and on, life after life.

thag2.32:1.3.verse: I’ve been searching for the house-builder—

thag2.32:1.4.verse: painful is birth again and again.

thag2.32:2.2.verse: You won’t build a house again.

thag2.32:2.6.verse: in this very life it will dissipate.

thag2.33:1.1.verse: The perfected one, the Holy One in the world,

thag2.33:1.2.verse: the sage is afflicted by winds.

thag2.33:1.4.verse: give it to the sage, brahmin.

thag2.33:2.1.verse: I wish to bring it to the one

thag2.33:2.2.verse: who is esteemed by the estimable,

thag2.34:1.1.verse: I’ve seen lay disciples who have memorized discourses,

thag2.34:1.3.verse: But they’re obsessed with jeweled earrings,

thag2.34:1.4.verse: concerned for their partners and children.

thag2.34:2.1.verse: To be honest, they don’t know Dhamma,

thag2.34:2.2.verse: even though they say “Sensual pleasures are impermanent”.

thag2.34:2.3.verse: They don’t have the power to cut their lust,

thag2.34:2.4.verse: so they cling to children, wives, and wealth.

thag2.35:1.1.verse: The heavens rain, the heavens pour,

thag2.35:1.2.verse: I’m staying alone in a frightful hole.

thag2.35:1.3.verse: But while I’m staying alone in that frightful hole,

thag2.35:1.4.verse: I’ve no fear, no dread, no goosebumps.

thag2.35:2.2.verse: while staying alone in a frightful hole:

thag2.36:1.1.verse: Whose mind is like a rock,

thag2.36:1.3.verse: free of desire for desirable things,

thag2.36:1.4.verse: not getting annoyed when things are annoying?

thag2.36:1.5.verse: From where will suffering strike one

thag2.36:1.6.verse: whose mind is developed like this?

thag2.36:2.1.verse: My mind is like a rock,

thag2.36:2.3.verse: free of desire for desirable things,

thag2.36:2.4.verse: not getting annoyed when things are annoying.

thag2.36:2.5.verse: From where will suffering strike me

thag2.36:2.6.verse: whose mind is developed like this?

thag2.37:1.1.verse: Night, with her garland of stars,

thag2.37:1.4.verse: this night is really for waking.

thag2.37:2.1.verse: Were I to fall from the back of an elephant,

thag2.37:2.2.verse: trampled by the tuskers that follow,

thag2.37:2.3.verse: better for me to die in battle,

thag2.37:2.4.verse: than to live on in defeat.

thag2.38:1.1.verse: One who’s given up the five sensual stimuli,

thag2.38:1.3.verse: and who’s left the home life out of faith—

thag2.38:1.4.verse: let them make an end to suffering!

thag2.39:1.1.verse: Arranging a robe over my shoulder,

thag2.39:1.2.verse: the color of young mango sprouts,

thag2.39:1.3.verse: I entered the village for alms

thag2.39:2.1.verse: But when I dismounted from the elephant,

thag2.39:2.2.verse: I was struck with a sense of urgency.

thag2.39:2.3.verse: I burned with shame, but then I found peace,

thag2.39:2.4.verse: and attained the ending of defilements.

thag2.40:1.1.verse: This chap, “Rag-rice”, he sure is a rag!

thag2.40:1.2.verse: Into the vase of freedom from death, polished and overflowing,

thag2.40:1.4.verse: the path to build up absorptions has been laid out.

thag2.40:2.4.verse: nodding off in the midst of the Saṅgha!

thag2.41:1.1.verse: Oh, the Buddhas! Oh, the Dhammas!

thag2.41:1.2.verse: Oh, the accomplishments of the Teacher!

thag2.41:2.5.verse: in the transmigration through births and deaths;

thag2.41:2.6.verse: now there’ll be no more future lives.

thag2.42:1.2.verse: who is devoted to the teaching of the Buddha,

thag2.42:1.4.verse: his life is not in vain.

thag2.42:2.1.verse: So let the wise devote themselves

thag2.42:2.3.verse: confidence, and insight into the teaching,

thag2.42:2.4.verse: remembering the instructions of the Buddhas.

thag2.43:1.2.verse: like horses tamed by a charioteer?

thag2.43:1.3.verse: With conceit and defilements given up,

thag2.43:1.4.verse: who is such as envied by even the gods?

thag2.43:2.2.verse: like horses tamed by a charioteer.

thag2.43:2.3.verse: With conceit and defilements given up,

thag2.43:2.4.verse: I am such as envied by even the gods.

thag2.44:1.1.verse: “Your skin is nasty but your heart is good;

thag2.44:1.2.verse: Mogharāja, you’re always immersed in samādhi.

thag2.44:1.3.verse: But in the nights of winter, so dark and cold,

thag2.44:1.4.verse: how will you get by, monk?”

thag2.44:2.3.verse: I’ll make my bed under a thatched roof,

thag2.44:2.4.verse: just like those who live in comfort.”

thag2.45:1.1.verse: One should not suspend others from the Saṅgha, nor raise objections against them;

thag2.45:1.2.verse: and neither disparage nor raise one’s voice against one who has crossed to the further shore.

thag2.45:1.3.verse: One should not praise oneself among the assemblies,

thag2.45:1.4.verse: not restless, measured in speech, and true to your vows.

thag2.45:2.1.verse: For one who sees the meaning so very subtle and fine,

thag2.45:2.2.verse: who is skilled in thought and placid in manner,

thag2.45:2.4.verse: it’s not hard to gain extinguishment.

thag2.46:1.1.verse: The peacocks cry out with their fair crests and tails,

thag2.46:1.2.verse: their lovely blue necks and fair faces, their beautiful song and their call.

thag2.46:1.3.verse: This broad earth is lush with grass and dew,

thag2.46:1.4.verse: and the firmament is full of beautiful clouds.

thag2.46:2.1.verse: One practicing absorption is happy in mind, and their appearance is uplifting;

thag2.46:2.2.verse: going forth in the teaching of the Buddha is easy for a good person.

thag2.46:2.3.verse: Realize that supreme state that does not pass,

thag2.46:2.4.verse: so very pure, subtle, and hard to see.

thag2.47:1.1.verse: The conceited mind, addicted to pleasure,

thag2.47:1.2.verse: impales itself on its own stake.

thag2.47:1.4.verse: there’s a stake, a chopping board.

thag2.47:2.1.verse: I declare you the loser mind!

thag2.47:2.2.verse: I declare you the insidious mind!

thag2.47:2.3.verse: You’ve found the Teacher so hard to find—

thag2.47:2.4.verse: don’t lead me away from the goal.

thag2.48:1.1.verse: Transmigrating for such a long time,

thag2.48:1.2.verse: I’ve cycled through various states of rebirth,

thag2.48:2.3.verse: All states of rebirth are cut off;

thag2.48:2.4.verse: now there’ll be no more future lives.

thag2.49:2.3.verse: and it’s due to that perception

thag2.49:2.4.verse: that I’ve attained the ending of defilements.

thag3.1:1.2.verse: I served the sacred fire in a grove.

thag3.1:1.3.verse: Not knowing the path to purity,

thag3.1:2.1.verse: I’ve gained this happiness by means of happiness:

thag3.1:2.2.verse: behold the clear rightness of the teaching!

thag3.1:3.1.verse: I used to be brahmin only by kin,

thag3.1:3.2.verse: but now I really am a brahmin!

thag3.1:3.3.verse: I am master of the three knowledges, I’m a bathed initiate,

thag3.1:3.4.verse: I’m a scholar and a knowledge master.

thag3.2:1.1.verse: I went forth five days ago,

thag3.2:1.2.verse: a trainee, my heart’s desire unfulfilled.

thag3.2:2.1.verse: I won’t eat; I won’t drink;

thag3.2:2.3.verse: nor will I lie down on my side—

thag3.2:2.4.verse: not until the dart of craving is plucked.

thag3.3:1.2.verse: what they should have done before

thag3.3:1.3.verse: has lost the causes for happiness,

thag3.3:1.4.verse: and afterwards they’re tormented by regrets.

thag3.3:2.1.verse: You should only say what you would do;

thag3.3:2.2.verse: you shouldn’t say what you wouldn’t do.

thag3.3:3.1.verse: Oh! Extinguishment is so very blissful,

thag3.3:3.2.verse: as taught by the fully awakened Buddha:

thag3.4:1.1.verse: If you wish to live in happiness,

thag3.4:1.3.verse: don’t look down on the Saṅgha’s robes,

thag3.4:2.1.verse: If you wish to live in happiness,

thag3.4:2.4.verse: like a snake making use of a mouse’s hole.

thag3.4:3.1.verse: If you wish to live in happiness,

thag3.4:3.4.verse: be content with whatever is offered.

thag3.5:1.3.verse: When the young neglect their work like this,

thag3.5:2.1.verse: But one who considers heat and cold

thag3.5:2.2.verse: as no more than blades of grass—

thag3.5:2.3.verse: he does his duties as a man,

thag3.5:3.1.verse: With my chest I’ll thrust aside

thag3.6:1.1.verse: “One of those monks who live in Pāṭaliputta—

thag3.6:1.2.verse: such brilliant speakers, and very learned—

thag3.6:2.1.verse: One of those monks who live in Pāṭaliputta—

thag3.6:2.2.verse: such brilliant speakers, and very learned—

thag3.6:2.4.verse: an old man, shivering in the gale.”

thag3.6:3.1.verse: “By war well fought, by sacrifice well made,

thag3.6:3.4.verse: that’s how one prospers in happiness.”

thag3.7:1.4.verse: both from this world and the next.

thag3.7:2.1.verse: But someone with a mind of love,

thag3.7:3.1.verse: You should all train to learn well-spoken words,

thag3.7:3.3.verse: to sit alone in hidden places,

thag3.8:1.1.verse: I was the only one in my family

thag3.8:1.3.verse: It’s good for my relatives that I’m

thag3.8:2.1.verse: I curbed my family out of sympathy,

thag3.8:2.2.verse: telling them off out of love

thag3.8:2.4.verse: They performed a service for the monks

thag3.8:3.2.verse: finding happiness in the Third Heaven.

thag3.8:3.4.verse: enjoy all the pleasures they desire.

thag3.9:2.2.verse: in the wilds, the formidable forest,

thag3.9:2.4.verse: like an elephant at the head of the battle.

thag3.9:3.1.verse: A monk alone is like the supreme Divinity;

thag3.9:3.2.verse: a pair of monks are like gods;

thag3.9:3.4.verse: and more than that is a rabble.”

thag3.10:1.1.verse: In the past you had faith,

thag3.10:2.4.verse: why would a sage waste away on that account?

thag3.10:3.1.verse: The meal of a sage is cooked

thag3.10:3.2.verse: bit by bit in this family or that.

thag3.11:1.2.verse: who has left their home out of faith,

thag3.11:1.4.verse: who are tireless and pure of livelihood.

thag3.11:2.2.verse: who has left their home out of faith,

thag3.11:2.3.verse: a mendicant staying in the Saṅgha,

thag3.11:2.4.verse: being wise, would train in monastic discipline.

thag3.11:3.2.verse: who has left their home out of faith,

thag3.11:3.3.verse: skilled in what is appropriate and what is not,

thag3.12:1.1.verse: I was, indeed, an astute scholar,

thag3.12:1.2.verse: competent to think on the meaning.

thag3.12:1.3.verse: The five kinds of sensual stimulation in the world,

thag3.12:2.2.verse: I was struck by a powerful dart.

thag3.12:2.3.verse: But I was able to free myself

thag3.12:2.4.verse: from the trap laid by the King of Death.

thag3.12:3.1.verse: I have given up all sensual pleasures;

thag3.12:3.4.verse: now there’ll be no more future lives.

thag3.13:1.4.verse: Painful is birth again and again.

thag3.13:2.2.verse: Devote yourselves to the instructions of the Buddha!

thag3.13:2.4.verse: as an elephant a hut of reeds.

thag3.13:3.4.verse: will make an end to suffering.

thag3.14:1.2.verse: and to the ghost realm time and again.

thag3.14:1.4.verse: in the animal realm, so full of pain.

thag3.14:2.1.verse: I was also reborn as a human,

thag3.14:2.2.verse: and from time to time I went to heaven.

thag3.14:2.3.verse: I’ve stayed in realms of luminous form and formlessness,

thag3.14:2.4.verse: among the neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient, and the non-percipient.

thag3.14:3.1.verse: I know well these created states are insubstantial—

thag3.14:3.3.verse: When I understood that this is created in myself,

thag3.15:1.2.verse: tasks they should have done before

thag3.15:1.3.verse: has lost the causes for happiness,

thag3.15:1.4.verse: and afterwards they’re tormented by regrets.

thag3.15:2.1.verse: You should only say what you would do;

thag3.15:2.2.verse: you shouldn’t say what you wouldn’t do.

thag3.15:3.1.verse: Oh! Extinguishment is so very blissful,

thag3.15:3.2.verse: as taught by the fully awakened Buddha:

thag3.16:1.3.verse: Stick to the advice he gave you,

thag3.16:2.1.verse: If you’re lost in the middle of a great sea,

thag3.16:2.2.verse: and you clamber up on a little log, you’ll sink.

thag3.16:2.3.verse: So too, a person who lives well

thag3.16:2.4.verse: sinks by relying on a lazy person.

thag3.16:2.6.verse: a lazy person who lacks energy.

thag4.1:1.1.verse: Adorned with jewelry and all dressed up,

thag4.1:1.2.verse: with garlands, and sandalwood makeup piled on,

thag4.1:1.3.verse: along the main street is a lady—

thag4.1:1.4.verse: a dancer dancing as the music plays.

thag4.1:2.2.verse: and while walking along I glanced at her,

thag4.1:2.3.verse: adorned with jewelry and all dressed up,

thag4.1:2.4.verse: set up like a snare of death.

thag4.1:4.2.verse: behold the clear rightness of the teaching!

thag4.2:1.3.verse: Stepping up to the path for walking meditation,

thag4.2:1.4.verse: I fell to the ground right there.

thag4.2:2.1.verse: I rubbed my limbs, and again

thag4.2:2.2.verse: I stepped up on the path for walking meditation.

thag4.2:2.3.verse: I walked meditation up and down the path,

thag4.2:4.2.verse: behold the clear rightness of the teaching!

thag4.3:1.2.verse: let us, who do understand this,

thag4.3:1.4.verse: for that is how conflicts are laid to rest.

thag4.3:2.1.verse: And when those who don’t understand

thag4.3:2.2.verse: behave as though they were immortal,

thag4.3:2.4.verse: are like the healthy among the sick.

thag4.3:4.3.verse: is as far from true Dhamma

thag4.3:4.4.verse: as the firmament from the earth.

thag4.4:1.1.verse: Curse you mortal frame, you stink!

thag4.4:1.2.verse: You’re on Māra’s side, you fester!

thag4.4:1.3.verse: O body, you have nine streams

thag4.4:1.4.verse: that are flowing all the time.

thag4.4:2.1.verse: Don’t think much of mortal frames;

thag4.4:2.3.verse: They’re not even aroused by heaven,

thag4.4:3.1.verse: But those who are fools and simpletons,

thag4.4:3.2.verse: with bad advisors, wrapped in delusion,

thag4.4:3.3.verse: that kind of person is aroused by bodies,

thag4.4:3.4.verse: when Māra has laid down the snare.

thag4.4:4.1.verse: Those in whom greed, hate, and ignorance

thag4.4:4.3.verse: such people are not aroused by bodies,

thag4.5:1.4.verse: I tore out my hair and beard.

thag4.5:2.4.verse: I didn’t accept food set aside for me.

thag4.5:3.1.verse: I did many deeds of this kind,

thag4.5:3.2.verse: which lead to a bad destination.

thag4.5:3.3.verse: Swept away by a great flood,

thag4.5:3.4.verse: I went to the Buddha for refuge.

thag4.5:4.2.verse: Behold the clear rightness of the teaching!

thag4.6:1.1.verse: It was so welcome for me

thag4.6:2.1.verse: He was glorious, the tutor of a community,

thag4.6:2.2.verse: a leader who had realized the highest.

thag4.6:2.3.verse: In all the world with its gods,

thag4.6:2.4.verse: he was the victor of unequaled vision.

thag4.6:3.1.verse: A great giant, a great hero,

thag4.6:3.2.verse: a great light free of defilement.

thag4.6:3.3.verse: With the utter ending of all defilements,

thag4.6:3.4.verse: the Teacher fears nothing from any quarter.

thag4.6:4.1.verse: For a long time, sadly, I was corrupted,

thag4.6:4.2.verse: fettered by the bond of wrong view.

thag4.7:1.1.verse: Hurrying when it’s time to dawdle;

thag4.7:1.2.verse: dawdling when it’s time to hurry;

thag4.7:2.2.verse: like the moon in the waning fortnight.

thag4.7:3.1.verse: Dawdling when it’s time to dawdle;

thag4.7:3.2.verse: hurrying when it’s time to hurry;

thag4.7:3.4.verse: an astute person comes into happiness.

thag4.7:4.2.verse: like the moon in the waxing fortnight.

thag4.8:1.2.verse: because I’m accomplished in both ways:

thag4.8:1.3.verse: I am the son of the Buddha,

thag4.8:1.4.verse: whose eye sees clearly in all things.

thag4.8:2.2.verse: since there are no more future lives—

thag4.8:2.4.verse: master of the three knowledges, seer of freedom from death.

thag4.8:3.1.verse: Blinded by sensual pleasures, trapped in a net,

thag4.8:3.2.verse: they are smothered over by craving;

thag4.8:3.3.verse: bound by the kinsman of the negligent,

thag4.8:3.4.verse: like a fish caught in a funnel-net trap.

thag4.8:4.1.verse: Having thrown off those sensual pleasures,

thag4.8:4.3.verse: and having plucked out craving, root and all:

thag4.9:1.3.verse: with my son upon her hip,

thag4.9:2.3.verse: adorned with jewelry and all dressed up,

thag4.9:2.4.verse: set up like a snare of death.

thag4.9:4.2.verse: behold the clear rightness of the teaching!

thag4.10:1.1.verse: “Dhamma surely protects one who practices Dhamma.

thag4.10:1.2.verse: The teaching brings happiness when practiced well.

thag4.10:1.3.verse: This is the benefit of practicing Dhamma:

thag4.10:1.4.verse: one doesn’t go to a bad destination.

thag4.10:2.1.verse: It’s not the case that Dhamma and what is not Dhamma

thag4.10:2.3.verse: What is not Dhamma leads to hell,

thag4.10:2.4.verse: while Dhamma takes you to a good place.

thag4.10:3.1.verse: So you should rouse up enthusiasm for the teachings;

thag4.10:3.2.verse: such rejoicing is owing to the Holy One, the unaffected.

thag4.10:3.3.verse: The disciples of the excellent Holy One are firm in the teaching;

thag4.10:3.4.verse: those attentive ones are led on, headed to the very best of refuges.”

thag4.10:4.1.verse: “The boil has been burst from its root,

thag4.10:4.2.verse: the net of craving is eradicated.

thag4.10:4.3.verse: He has ended transmigration, he has nothing,

thag4.10:4.4.verse: he’s like the full moon on a bright night.”

thag4.11:1.1.verse: When the crane with its beautiful white wings,

thag4.11:1.2.verse: startled by fear of the dark cloud,

thag4.11:1.4.verse: then the River Ajakaraṇī delights me.

thag4.11:2.1.verse: When the crane, so very pure and white,

thag4.11:2.2.verse: startled by fear of the dark rcloud,

thag4.11:2.3.verse: seeks a cave to shelter in, but can’t see one—

thag4.11:2.4.verse: then the River Ajakaraṇī delights me.

thag4.11:3.3.verse: that grace both banks of the river,

thag4.11:4.1.verse: Well rid of the pack of jackals, mad for the dead,

thag4.11:4.3.verse: “Today is no time to stray from mountain streams;

thag4.11:4.4.verse: Ajakaraṇī is safe, pleasant, and delightful.”

thag4.12:1.1.verse: I went forth to save my life.

thag4.12:2.1.verse: Gladly, let this body be broken!

thag4.12:2.2.verse: Let this scrap of meat disintegrate!

thag4.12:2.3.verse: Let both my legs fall off

thag4.12:3.1.verse: I won’t eat, I won’t drink,

thag4.12:3.3.verse: nor will I lie down on my side,

thag4.12:3.4.verse: until the dart of craving is plucked.

thag5.1:1.1.verse: I, a monk, went to a charnel ground

thag5.1:1.2.verse: and saw a woman’s body abandoned there,

thag5.1:2.3.verse: but sexual desire arose in me,

thag5.1:2.4.verse: I was as if blind to her oozing body.

thag5.1:3.1.verse: Quicker than the cooking of rice

thag5.1:3.4.verse: I retired to a discreet place.

thag5.1:5.2.verse: behold the clear rightness of the teaching!

thag5.2:1.1.verse: When a person, wishing for a certain outcome,

thag5.2:1.2.verse: applies themselves where they ought not;

thag5.2:1.3.verse: not achieving what they worked for,

thag5.2:1.4.verse: they say: “That’s a sign of my bad luck.”

thag5.2:2.1.verse: When a misfortune is extracted and beaten,

thag5.2:2.2.verse: to surrender it in part would be like losing at dice;

thag5.2:2.3.verse: but to surrender it all you’d have to be blind,

thag5.2:2.4.verse: not seeing the even and the uneven.

thag5.2:3.1.verse: You should only say what you would do;

thag5.2:3.2.verse: you shouldn’t say what you wouldn’t do.

thag5.2:4.4.verse: for one who does not act on it.

thag5.2:5.4.verse: for one who acts on it.

thag5.3:1.1.verse: The heavens rain like a sweet song;

thag5.3:1.2.verse: my hut is roofed and pleasant, sheltered from the wind.

thag5.3:1.4.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.

thag5.3:2.1.verse: The heavens rain like a sweet song;

thag5.3:2.2.verse: my hut is roofed and pleasant, sheltered from the wind.

thag5.3:2.3.verse: I meditate there, my mind at peace:

thag5.3:2.4.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.

thag5.3:3.1.verse: The heavens rain like a sweet song;

thag5.3:3.2.verse: my hut is roofed and pleasant, sheltered from the wind.

thag5.3:3.3.verse: I meditate there, free of greed:

thag5.3:3.4.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.

thag5.3:4.1.verse: The heavens rain like a sweet song;

thag5.3:4.2.verse: my hut is roofed and pleasant, sheltered from the wind.

thag5.3:4.3.verse: I meditate there, free of hate:

thag5.3:4.4.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.

thag5.3:5.1.verse: The heavens rain like a sweet song;

thag5.3:5.2.verse: my hut is roofed and pleasant, sheltered from the wind.

thag5.3:5.3.verse: I meditate there, free of delusion:

thag5.3:5.4.verse: so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.

thag5.4:1.1.verse: My mentor helped me to learn,

thag5.4:1.2.verse: hoping I would practice those teachings.

thag5.4:1.4.verse: I’ve done what had to be done.

thag5.4:2.2.verse: witnessing it for myself, not based on legends.

thag5.4:2.3.verse: With purified knowledge, free of doubt,

thag5.4:2.4.verse: I declare it in your presence.

thag5.4:4.4.verse: now there’ll be no more future lives.

thag5.4:5.1.verse: You advised me in noble observances;

thag5.4:5.3.verse: Your instruction was not in vain—

thag5.4:5.4.verse: I, your pupil, am fully trained.

thag5.5:1.1.verse: Oh so well was the goad

thag5.5:1.2.verse: shown to me by my mother,

thag5.5:2.2.verse: master of the three knowledges, seer of freedom from death.

thag5.5:2.3.verse: I’ve conquered the army of Namuci,

thag5.5:3.1.verse: Those defilements that were found in me,

thag5.5:3.3.verse: are all cut off without remainder,

thag5.5:5.2.verse: this bag of bones is my last

thag5.5:5.3.verse: in the transmigration through births and deaths;

thag5.5:5.4.verse: now there’ll be no more future lives.”

thag5.6:1.1.verse: It was truly for my benefit

thag5.6:1.2.verse: that the Buddha went to the Nerañjara River.

thag5.6:2.1.verse: I used to perform a diverse spectrum of sacrifices;

thag5.6:2.4.verse: I was a blind, ordinary person.

thag5.6:3.1.verse: Caught in the thicket of wrong view,

thag5.6:4.3.verse: I serve the fire for those worthy of a religious donation:

thag5.6:4.4.verse: I bow to the Realized One.

thag5.6:5.2.verse: craving for continued existence is shattered;

thag5.6:5.4.verse: now there’ll be no more future lives.

thag5.7:1.3.verse: I plunged into the water at Gayā

thag5.7:2.3.verse: I’ll now rinse away right here”—

thag5.7:2.4.verse: such was the view I used to hold.

thag5.7:4.1.verse: I’ve washed away all bad things;

thag5.7:4.3.verse: the pure heir of the pure one,

thag5.7:4.4.verse: a bosom son of the Buddha.

thag5.7:5.1.verse: When I plunged into the eightfold stream,

thag5.7:5.2.verse: all bad things were rinsed away.

thag5.8:1.2.verse: while dwelling in a forest grove,

thag5.8:1.3.verse: you’ve entered a tough place for gathering alms—

thag5.8:1.4.verse: how will you get by, monk?”

thag5.8:4.1.verse: Having seen those who are energetic, resolute,

thag5.8:5.2.verse: the best, the tamed, the serene—

thag5.9:1.2.verse: like an elephant in a stockade.

thag5.9:1.3.verse: Born of the flesh, that net of the senses,

thag5.9:1.4.verse: I won’t urge you to do bad.

thag5.9:2.2.verse: like an elephant who can’t find an open gate.

thag5.9:2.3.verse: Loser mind, you won’t wander again and again,

thag5.9:3.1.verse: Just as a strong trainer with a hook

thag5.9:3.2.verse: takes a wild, newly captured elephant

thag5.9:3.3.verse: and wins it over against its will,

thag5.9:4.1.verse: Just as a fine charioteer, skilled in the taming

thag5.9:4.2.verse: of fine horses, tames a thoroughbred,

thag5.9:4.4.verse: firmly established in the five powers.

thag5.9:5.3.verse: kept in check by harnessed energy,

thag5.9:5.4.verse: mind, you won’t go far from here.

thag5.10:1.3.verse: They’re as far from the true teaching

thag5.10:1.4.verse: as the earth is from the sky.

thag5.10:2.3.verse: They fall away from the true teaching,

thag5.10:2.4.verse: like the moon in the waning fortnight.

thag5.10:3.3.verse: They wither away in the true teaching,

thag5.10:3.4.verse: like a fish in a little puddle.

thag5.10:4.3.verse: They don’t thrive in the true teaching,

thag5.10:4.4.verse: like a rotten seed in a field.

thag5.10:5.2.verse: who listens to the victor’s instruction—

thag5.11:1.3.verse: I’ve seen the Blessed One myself,

thag5.11:1.4.verse: and even stayed together with him.

thag5.11:2.2.verse: spent much of the night in the open;

thag5.11:2.3.verse: then he, who is so skilled in meditation,

thag5.11:3.3.verse: like a lion in a rocky cave,

thag5.11:3.4.verse: with fear and dread given up.

thag5.11:4.2.verse: Soṇa, a disciple of the Buddha,

thag5.11:5.1.verse: When he has completely understood the five aggregates,

thag5.12:1.1.verse: Whatever attentive one, understanding their teacher’s words,

thag5.12:1.2.verse: stays with them, their fondness growing;

thag5.12:1.3.verse: that astute person is indeed devoted—

thag5.12:2.2.verse: one who does not tremble, but reflects instead,

thag5.12:2.3.verse: that astute person is indeed strong—

thag5.12:3.2.verse: their wisdom is deep, they see the subtle meaning;

thag5.12:3.3.verse: that astute person is indeed unfaltering—

thag5.12:4.1.verse: They’re very learned, and have memorized the teaching,

thag5.12:4.2.verse: living in line with the teaching—

thag5.12:4.3.verse: that astute person is indeed such—

thag5.12:5.1.verse: They know the meaning of what is said,

thag5.12:5.3.verse: that astute person is indeed a master of meaning—

thag6.1:1.3.verse: was not enough for me to bow to him—

thag6.1:1.4.verse: I was blinded by jealousy and conceit.

thag6.1:2.2.verse: the trainer of men scolded me.

thag6.1:2.3.verse: I was struck with a sense of urgency,

thag6.1:3.2.verse: I had before as a matted-hair ascetic,

thag6.1:4.1.verse: I used to be content with sacrifice,

thag6.1:4.2.verse: the realm of sensual pleasures was my priority.

thag6.1:5.3.verse: I have psychic powers, and know the minds of others;

thag6.1:6.2.verse: for the sake of which I went forth

thag6.1:6.3.verse: from the lay life to homelessness—

thag6.2:1.3.verse: but I don’t get any almsfood!

thag6.2:2.2.verse: Your body soaked with rapture, you’ll always be full of joy.

thag6.2:3.1.verse: In faith, recollect the immeasurable teaching!

thag6.2:3.2.verse: Your body soaked with rapture, you’ll always be full of joy.

thag6.2:4.1.verse: In faith, recollect the immeasurable Saṅgha!

thag6.2:4.2.verse: Your body soaked with rapture, you’ll always be full of joy.”

thag6.2:5.2.verse: though these winter nights are cold.

thag6.2:5.4.verse: enter your dwelling, with door shut fast.”

thag6.2:6.3.verse: I won’t perish, overcome with cold;

thag6.3:1.3.verse: falls away from the true teaching,

thag6.3:1.4.verse: like a fish in a little puddle.

thag6.3:2.3.verse: doesn’t thrive in the true teaching,

thag6.3:2.4.verse: like a rotten seed in a field.

thag6.3:3.4.verse: in the teaching of the Dhamma king.

thag6.3:4.3.verse: doesn’t fall away from the true teaching,

thag6.3:4.4.verse: like a fish in plenty of water.

thag6.3:5.4.verse: like a fine seed in a field.

thag6.3:6.4.verse: in the teaching of the Dhamma king.

thag6.4:1.1.verse: I, Kulla, went to a charnel ground

thag6.4:1.2.verse: and saw a woman’s body abandoned there,

thag6.4:3.1.verse: Taking the teaching as a mirror

thag6.4:4.1.verse: As this is, so is that;

thag6.4:4.2.verse: as that is, so is this.

thag6.4:5.1.verse: As by day, so by night;

thag6.4:5.2.verse: as by night, so by day.

thag6.4:6.1.verse: Even the music of a five-piece band

thag6.5:1.2.verse: craving grows in them like a camel’s foot creeper.

thag6.5:1.3.verse: They jump from one thing to the next, like a langur

thag6.5:1.4.verse: greedy for fruit in a forest grove.

thag6.5:2.1.verse: Whoever is beaten by this wretched craving,

thag6.5:3.1.verse: But whoever prevails over this wretched craving,

thag6.5:3.2.verse: so hard to get over in the world,

thag6.5:3.4.verse: like a drop from a lotus-leaf.

thag6.5:4.1.verse: I say this to you, good people,

thag6.5:4.2.verse: all those who have gathered here:

thag6.5:4.3.verse: dig up the root of craving,

thag6.5:4.4.verse: as you’d dig up the grass in search of roots.

thag6.5:4.5.verse: Don’t let Māra break you again and again,

thag6.5:4.6.verse: like a stream breaking a reed.

thag6.5:5.2.verse: don’t let the moment pass you by.

thag6.5:5.3.verse: For if you miss your moment

thag6.5:5.4.verse: you’ll grieve when sent to hell.

thag6.5:6.4.verse: pluck out the dart from yourself.

thag6.6:1.3.verse: I have not found peace of mind,

thag6.6:1.4.verse: even as long as a finger-snap.

thag6.6:2.1.verse: Since I couldn’t get my mind unified,

thag6.6:2.2.verse: I was racked by desire for pleasures of the senses.

thag6.6:3.3.verse: For how on earth can one such as me die

thag6.6:4.1.verse: Then I picked up a razor,

thag6.6:6.2.verse: behold the clear rightness of the teaching!

thag6.7:1.2.verse: Don’t sleep too much, be wakeful.

thag6.7:1.3.verse: Don’t be lazy and let the kinsman of the negligent,

thag6.7:1.4.verse: the King of Death, catch you in his trap.

thag6.7:2.1.verse: Like a wave in the mighty ocean,

thag6.7:2.2.verse: rebirth and old age sweep you under.

thag6.7:2.3.verse: Make a safe island of yourself,

thag6.7:2.4.verse: for you have no other shelter.

thag6.7:3.1.verse: The teacher has mastered this path,

thag6.7:3.2.verse: which transcends chains, and the fear of birth and old age.

thag6.7:3.3.verse: Be diligent in the first and final watches of the night,

thag6.7:4.1.verse: Free yourself from your former bonds!

thag6.7:4.2.verse: Wearing your outer robe, with shaven head, eating almsfood,

thag6.7:4.3.verse: don’t delight in play or sleep,

thag6.7:5.2.verse: you’re an expert in the path to sanctuary  from the yoke.

thag6.7:5.4.verse: you’ll be extinguished as a flame by water.

thag6.7:6.2.verse: is bent down by the wind, like a creeper;

thag6.8:1.1.verse: It was well-taught by the Clear-eyed One,

thag6.8:1.2.verse: the Buddha, Kinsman of the Sun,

thag6.8:2.2.verse: drying up the root of craving,

thag6.8:2.3.verse: and, having cut off the poisonous root, the slaughterhouse,

thag6.8:3.1.verse: By breaking the root of unknowing,

thag6.8:3.2.verse: it smashes the mechanism of deeds,

thag6.8:3.3.verse: and drops the thunderbolt of knowledge

thag6.8:3.4.verse: on the taking up of consciousnesses.

thag6.8:4.1.verse: It informs us of our feelings,

thag6.8:4.4.verse: all states of existence as a pit of burning coals.

thag6.8:5.1.verse: It’s very sweet and very deep,

thag6.8:5.2.verse: holding birth and death at bay;

thag6.8:5.3.verse: it is the noble eightfold path—

thag6.8:6.4.verse: as if they were in a clear light;

thag6.8:6.5.verse: leading to the great sanctuary and peace,

thag6.9:1.1.verse: I was drunk with the pride of birth

thag6.9:2.1.verse: No one was my equal or my better—

thag6.9:2.3.verse: I was such an arrogant fool,

thag6.9:2.4.verse: stuck up, waving my own flag.

thag6.9:3.1.verse: I never paid homage to anyone:

thag6.9:3.2.verse: not even my mother or father,

thag6.9:3.4.verse: I was stiff with pride, lacking regard for others.

thag6.9:4.1.verse: When I saw the foremost leader,

thag6.9:4.4.verse: at the fore of the mendicant Saṅgha,

thag6.9:5.2.verse: and, with a clear and confident heart,

thag6.9:5.3.verse: I bowed down with my head

thag6.9:5.4.verse: to the supreme among all beings.

thag6.9:6.1.verse: The conceit of superiority and the conceit of inferiority

thag6.9:6.2.verse: have been given up and eradicated.

thag6.9:6.3.verse: The conceit “I am” is cut off,

thag6.9:6.4.verse: and every kind of conceit is destroyed.

thag6.10:1.1.verse: I was only seven years old

thag6.10:1.3.verse: when I overcame the mighty serpent king

thag6.10:2.1.verse: I brought water for my mentor

thag6.10:5.1.verse: Made a thoroughbred by a thoroughbred,

thag6.10:6.3.verse: that novice Sumana has the wish:

thag6.11:1.2.verse: while dwelling in a forest grove,

thag6.11:1.3.verse: you’ve entered a tough resort for gathering alms—

thag6.11:1.4.verse: how will you get by, monk?”

thag6.11:5.1.verse: Those defilements that were found in me,

thag6.11:5.3.verse: are all cut off without remainder,

thag6.11:6.1.verse: The five aggregates are fully understood,

thag6.11:6.2.verse: they remain, but their root is cut.

thag6.11:6.3.verse: I have reached the ending of suffering,

thag6.11:6.4.verse: now there’ll be no more future lives.”

thag6.12:1.1.verse: Whence anger for one free of anger,

thag6.12:2.1.verse: When you get angry at an angry person

thag6.12:2.2.verse: you just make things worse for yourself.

thag6.12:2.3.verse: When you don’t get angry at an angry person

thag6.12:2.4.verse: you win a battle hard to win.

thag6.12:3.1.verse: When you know that the other is angry,

thag6.12:3.2.verse: you act for the good of both

thag6.12:3.4.verse: if you’re mindful and stay calm.

thag6.12:5.2.verse: reflect on the simile of the saw;

thag6.12:5.3.verse: if craving for flavors arises in you,

thag6.12:5.4.verse: remember the simile of the child’s flesh.

thag6.12:6.2.verse: to sensual pleasures and future lives,

thag6.12:6.4.verse: as one would curb a greedy cow eating grain.

thag6.13:1.1.verse: The rain saturates things that are covered up;

thag6.13:1.2.verse: it doesn’t saturate things that are open.

thag6.13:1.3.verse: Therefore you should open up a covered thing,

thag6.13:1.4.verse: so the rain will not saturate it.

thag6.13:2.1.verse: The world is beaten down by death

thag6.13:2.3.verse: The dart of craving has struck it down,

thag6.13:2.4.verse: and it’s always fuming with desire.

thag6.13:3.1.verse: The world is beaten down by death,

thag6.13:4.1.verse: Three things are coming, like a wall of flame:

thag6.13:4.3.verse: No power can stand before them,

thag6.13:4.4.verse: and no speed’s enough to flee.

thag6.13:5.4.verse: shortens your life by that much.

thag6.13:6.4.verse: you have no time to be careless.

thag6.14:1.1.verse: This two-legged body is dirty and stinking,

thag6.14:1.3.verse: and oozing all over the place—

thag6.14:2.1.verse: Like a lurking deer by a trick,

thag6.14:2.2.verse: like a fish by a hook,

thag6.14:3.3.verse: these five kinds of sensual stimulation

thag6.14:3.4.verse: are seen in a woman’s body.

thag6.14:4.1.verse: Those ordinary people, their minds full of lust,

thag6.14:4.3.verse: they swell the horrors of the charnel ground,

thag6.14:5.3.verse: like a snake’s head with their foot,

thag6.14:5.4.verse: gets over clinging to the world.

thag6.14:6.1.verse: Seeing the danger in sensual pleasures,

thag6.14:6.4.verse: and attained the ending of defilements.

thag7.1:1.1.verse: Adorned with jewelry and all dressed up,

thag7.1:1.2.verse: with her garland and her makeup on,

thag7.1:1.3.verse: and her feet so brightly rouged:

thag7.1:2.1.verse: Taking off her slippers in front of me,

thag7.1:3.5.verse: I promise this is the truth—

thag7.1:3.6.verse: I swear it by the Sacred Flame.

thag7.1:4.1.verse: And when we’ve grown old together,

thag7.1:4.2.verse: both of us leaning on staffs,

thag7.1:4.4.verse: and hold a winning hand on both counts.”

thag7.1:5.1.verse: I saw the courtesan seducing me,

thag7.1:5.3.verse: adorned with jewelry and all dressed up,

thag7.1:5.4.verse: set up like a snare of death.

thag7.1:7.2.verse: see the excellence of the Dhamma!

thag7.2:1.1.verse: Bhaddiya has plucked out craving, root and all,

thag7.2:1.3.verse: on the far side of the Wild Mango Monastery,

thag7.2:1.4.verse: he practices absorption; he is truly well-favored.

thag7.2:2.2.verse: in arched harps, and in cymbals.

thag7.2:2.3.verse: But here, at the foot of a tree,

thag7.2:2.4.verse: I delight in the Buddha’s teaching.

thag7.2:3.1.verse: If the Buddha were to grant me one wish,

thag7.2:3.2.verse: and I were to get what I wished for,

thag7.2:3.3.verse: I’d choose for the whole world

thag7.2:4.1.verse: Those who’ve judged me on appearance,

thag7.2:4.2.verse: and those swayed by my voice,

thag7.2:4.3.verse: are full of desire and greed;

thag7.2:5.3.verse: the fool shut in on every side,

thag7.2:5.4.verse: gets carried away by a voice.

thag7.2:6.4.verse: they’re also carried away by a voice.

thag7.2:7.4.verse: they don’t get carried away by a voice.

thag7.3:1.2.verse: loved by my mother and father.

thag7.3:2.2.verse: wishing me well and wanting the best for me,

thag7.3:2.4.verse: took me to see the Buddha.

thag7.3:3.3.verse: We offer him to you, Lord,

thag7.3:4.4.verse: this one will be a thoroughbred!”

thag7.3:5.1.verse: After he, the Teacher, had sent me forth,

thag7.3:6.1.verse: Consequently, the Teacher didn’t neglect me;

thag7.3:6.2.verse: when he came out from seclusion,

thag7.3:7.4.verse: oh, the clear rightness of the teaching!

thag7.4:1.2.verse: walking mindfully in the shade of the terrace,

thag7.4:1.4.verse: and bowed to the supreme among men.

thag7.4:2.1.verse: Arranging my robe over one shoulder

thag7.4:2.3.verse: I walked alongside that stainless one,

thag7.4:3.1.verse: The wise one, expert in questions,

thag7.4:4.1.verse: When all his questions were answered,

thag7.4:5.1.verse: “It is a blessing for the people of Aṅga and Magadha

thag7.4:5.6.verse: it’s a blessing for them,” he declared.

thag7.4:6.2.verse: you are invited to come and see me.

thag7.4:7.4.verse: oh, the clear rightness of the teaching!

thag7.5:1.1.verse: I broke the reeds off with my hands,

thag7.5:1.2.verse: made a hut, and stayed there.

thag7.5:2.2.verse: for me to break reeds with my hands.

thag7.5:2.3.verse: The training rules have been laid down for us

thag7.5:3.2.verse: didn’t see the disease in its entirety.

thag7.5:3.3.verse: But now I have seen the disease,

thag7.5:3.4.verse: as I’ve practiced what was taught by he who is beyond the gods.

thag7.5:4.1.verse: Gotama traveled by that direct route;

thag7.5:4.2.verse: the same path traveled by Vipassī,

thag7.5:5.1.verse: These seven Buddhas have plunged into the ending,

thag7.5:6.1.verse: out of compassion for living creatures—

thag7.5:6.3.verse: and cessation, the ending of suffering.

thag7.5:7.4.verse: and life comes to an end,

thag8.1:1.1.verse: Don’t get involved in lots of work,

thag8.1:1.2.verse: avoid people, and don’t try to acquire things.

thag8.1:1.3.verse: If you’re eager and greedy for flavors,

thag8.1:1.4.verse: you’ll miss the goal that brings such happiness.

thag8.1:2.1.verse: They know it really is a bog,

thag8.1:2.2.verse: this homage and veneration in respectable families.

thag8.1:2.3.verse: Honor is a subtle dart, hard to extract,

thag8.1:2.4.verse: and hard for a reprobate to give up.

thag8.1:3.1.verse: The deeds of a mortal aren’t bad

thag8.1:3.3.verse: You yourself should not do bad,

thag8.1:3.4.verse: for mortals have deeds as their kin.

thag8.1:4.1.verse: You’re not a bandit because of what someone says,

thag8.1:4.2.verse: you’re not a sage because of what someone says;

thag8.1:4.4.verse: so the gods will know you.

thag8.1:5.2.verse: let us, who do understand this,

thag8.1:5.4.verse: for that is how conflicts are laid to rest.

thag8.1:6.4.verse: even a rich person doesn’t really live.

thag8.1:7.1.verse: All is heard with the ear,

thag8.1:7.2.verse: all is seen with the eye;

thag8.1:7.4.verse: all that is seen and heard.

thag8.1:8.1.verse: Though you have eyes, be as if blind;

thag8.1:8.2.verse: though you have ears, be as if deaf;

thag8.1:8.3.verse: though you have wisdom, be as if dumb;

thag8.1:8.4.verse: though you have strength, be as if feeble.

thag8.1:8.6.verse: lie as still as a corpse.

thag8.2:1.2.verse: free of deceit, and rid of slander;

thag8.2:2.2.verse: free of deceit, and rid of slander;

thag8.2:2.3.verse: that’s how a mendicant with sense doors always guarded

thag8.2:3.2.verse: free of deceit, and rid of slander;

thag8.2:3.3.verse: that’s how a mendicant of good morals

thag8.2:4.2.verse: free of deceit, and rid of slander;

thag8.2:4.3.verse: that’s how a mendicant with good friends

thag8.2:5.2.verse: free of deceit, and rid of slander;

thag8.2:5.3.verse: that’s how a mendicant of good wisdom,

thag8.2:6.1.verse: Whoever has faith in the Realized One,

thag8.2:6.4.verse: praised and loved by the noble ones;

thag8.2:7.1.verse: who has confidence in the Saṅgha,

thag8.2:7.4.verse: their life is not in vain.

thag8.2:8.1.verse: So let the wise devote themselves

thag8.2:8.3.verse: confidence, and insight into the teaching,

thag8.2:8.4.verse: remembering the instructions of the Buddhas.

thag8.3:1.1.verse: When I first saw the Teacher

thag8.3:1.2.verse: who fears nothing from any quarter,

thag8.3:1.3.verse: I was struck with a sense of urgency,

thag8.3:2.1.verse: Anyone who, having found such a Teacher,

thag8.3:2.3.verse: is like one who, when approached by Lady Luck,

thag8.3:2.4.verse: would ward her off with their hands and feet.

thag8.3:3.1.verse: Then I left behind my children and wives,

thag8.3:3.3.verse: I had my hair and beard cut off,

thag8.3:4.1.verse: Endowed with the monastic training and livelihood,

thag8.3:5.1.verse: Then a wish occurred to me,

thag8.3:5.3.verse: I wouldn’t sit down, not even for a short while,

thag8.3:5.4.verse: until the dart of craving was plucked.

thag8.3:8.1.verse: Then, at the end of the night,

thag8.3:8.2.verse: as the rising of the sun drew near,

thag9.1:1.1.verse: When an astute person knows, “Old age and death are suffering;

thag9.1:1.2.verse: yet an ignorant ordinary person is bound to them”,

thag9.1:1.3.verse: completely understanding suffering, being mindful, practicing absorption:

thag9.1:1.4.verse: there is no greater pleasure than this.

thag9.1:2.1.verse: When clinging, the carrier of suffering,

thag9.1:2.2.verse: and craving, the carrier  of this painful mass of proliferation,

thag9.1:2.3.verse: are destroyed, and one is mindful, practicing absorption:

thag9.1:2.4.verse: there is no greater pleasure than this.

thag9.1:3.1.verse: When the eightfold way, so full of grace,

thag9.1:3.2.verse: the supreme path, cleanser of all corruptions,

thag9.1:3.3.verse: is seen with wisdom; and one is mindful, practicing absorption:

thag9.1:3.4.verse: there is no greater pleasure than this.

thag9.1:4.1.verse: When one develops that peaceful state,

thag9.1:4.3.verse: cleanser of all corruptions, cutter of fetters and bonds:

thag9.1:4.4.verse: there is no greater pleasure than this.

thag9.1:5.1.verse: When the thundercloud rumbles in the sky,

thag9.1:5.2.verse: while the rain pours on the path of birds all around,

thag9.1:5.3.verse: and a monk has gone to a mountain cave, practicing absorption:

thag9.1:5.4.verse: there is no greater pleasure than this.

thag9.1:6.1.verse: When sitting on a riverbank covered in flowers,

thag9.1:6.2.verse: garlanded with brightly colored forest plants,

thag9.1:6.3.verse: one is truly happy, practicing absorption:

thag9.1:6.4.verse: there is no greater pleasure than this.

thag9.1:7.1.verse: When it is midnight in a lonely forest,

thag9.1:7.2.verse: and the lions roar as the heavens pour,

thag9.1:7.3.verse: and a monk has gone to a mountain cave, practicing absorption:

thag9.1:7.4.verse: there is no greater pleasure than this.

thag9.1:8.1.verse: When one’s own thoughts have been cut off,

thag9.1:8.2.verse: between the mountains, sheltered inside a cleft,

thag9.1:8.3.verse: without stress or heartlessness, practicing absorption:

thag9.1:8.4.verse: there is no greater pleasure than this.

thag9.1:9.1.verse: When one is happy, destroyer of stains, heartlessness, and sorrow,

thag9.1:9.2.verse: free of obstructions, snarls, and thorns,

thag9.1:9.3.verse: and with all defilements annihilated, practicing absorption:

thag9.1:9.4.verse: there is no greater pleasure than this.

thag10.1:1.1.verse: “The trees are now crimson, venerable sir,

thag10.1:1.2.verse: they’ve shed their foliage, and are ready to fruit.

thag10.1:1.4.verse: great hero, this season is full of flavor.

thag10.1:2.2.verse: wafting their scent all around, in all directions.

thag10.1:2.3.verse: They’ve shed their leaves and wish to fruit,

thag10.1:2.4.verse: hero, it is time to leave here.

thag10.1:3.1.verse: It is neither too hot nor too cold,

thag10.1:3.2.verse: venerable sir, it’s a pleasant season for traveling.

thag10.1:3.3.verse: Let the Sākiyans and Koliyans see you,

thag10.1:3.4.verse: heading west across the Rohiṇī river.

thag10.1:4.1.verse: In hope, the field is plowed;

thag10.1:4.2.verse: the seed is sown in hope;

thag10.1:4.3.verse: in hope, merchants travel the seas,

thag10.1:4.5.verse: The hope that I stand for:

thag10.1:5.1.verse: Again and again, they sow the seed;

thag10.1:5.2.verse: again and again, the king of the heavens sends rain;

thag10.1:5.3.verse: again and again, farmers plow the field;

thag10.1:5.4.verse: again and again, grain is produced for the nation.

thag10.1:6.1.verse: Again and again, the beggars wander,

thag10.1:6.2.verse: again and again, the donors give.

thag10.1:6.3.verse: Again and again, when the donors have given,

thag10.1:6.4.verse: again and again, they take their place in heaven.

thag10.1:7.1.verse: A hero of vast wisdom purifies seven generations

thag10.1:7.2.verse: of the family in which they’re born.

thag10.1:7.3.verse: Sakya, I believe you’re the king of kings,

thag10.1:7.4.verse: since you fathered the one who is truly called a sage.

thag10.1:8.1.verse: The father of the great seer is named Suddhodana;

thag10.1:8.2.verse: and the Buddha’s mother is named Māyā.

thag10.1:8.3.verse: Having borne the Bodhisatta in her belly,

thag10.1:8.4.verse: she rejoices in the Third Heaven.

thag10.1:9.1.verse: When she died and passed away from here,

thag10.1:9.2.verse: she was blessed with heavenly sensual pleasures;

thag10.1:9.3.verse: enjoying the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

thag10.1:9.4.verse: Gotamī is surrounded by those hosts of gods.”

thag10.1:10.1.verse: “I’m the son of the Buddha, the incomparable Aṅgīrasa, the unaffected,

thag10.1:10.3.verse: You, Sakya, are my father’s father;

thag10.1:10.4.verse: Gotama, you are my grandfather in the Dhamma.”

thag10.2:1.1.verse: If no one else is found

thag10.2:1.4.verse: to be dwelling alone in a forest grove.

thag10.2:2.2.verse: to the wilderness praised by the Buddha.

thag10.2:2.4.verse: to be dwelling alone and resolute.

thag10.2:3.2.verse: I’ll quickly enter the delightful forest,

thag10.2:3.4.verse: and is frequented by rutting elephants.

thag10.2:4.1.verse: In the Cool Grove, so full of flowers,

thag10.2:5.3.verse: in the great wood, so delightful,

thag10.2:5.4.verse: my task complete, free of defilements?

thag10.2:6.1.verse: This is what I want to do:

thag10.2:6.4.verse: for no one can do another’s duty.

thag10.2:7.4.verse: without attaining the end of defilements.

thag10.2:9.1.verse: In a forest grove covered with blossoms,

thag10.2:9.2.verse: in a cave so very cool,

thag10.2:9.3.verse: I take pleasure in the Mountainfold,

thag10.2:9.4.verse: happy with the happiness of freedom.

thag10.2:10.1.verse: I’ve got all I wished for

thag10.2:10.2.verse: like the moon on the fifteenth day.

thag10.2:10.3.verse: With the utter ending of all defilements,

thag10.2:10.4.verse: now there’ll be no more future lives.

thag10.3:1.1.verse: If you’re prepared for the future,

thag10.3:1.2.verse: both the good and the bad,

thag10.3:1.3.verse: then those, whether enemies or well-wishers,

thag10.3:1.4.verse: who examine you for weakness will see none.

thag10.3:2.4.verse: as it was taught by the Buddha:

thag10.3:2.6.verse: like the moon freed from clouds.

thag10.3:3.3.verse: it has broken through and been uplifted—

thag10.3:4.4.verse: even a rich person doesn’t really live.

thag10.3:6.1.verse: It’s not a teaching just for today;

thag10.3:7.3.verse: Everyone who is born here dies here;

thag10.3:7.4.verse: such is the nature of living creatures.

thag10.3:8.1.verse: The things that are useful for the living

thag10.3:8.2.verse: are of no use for the dead—not fame, not celebrity,

thag10.3:8.3.verse: not praise by ascetics and brahmins.

thag10.3:8.4.verse: For the dead, there is only weeping.

thag10.3:9.1.verse: And weeping impairs the eye and the body;

thag10.3:9.4.verse: but your well-wishers are not happy.

thag10.3:10.1.verse: So you should wish that those who stay in your family

thag10.3:10.3.verse: and do their duty through the power of wisdom,

thag10.3:10.4.verse: just as you’d cross a full river by boat.

thag10.4:1.2.verse: I was despised in the past.

thag12.1:1.1.verse: One should train just in ethical conduct,

thag12.1:1.2.verse: for in this world, when ethical conduct is

thag12.1:2.1.verse: Wishing for three kinds of happiness—

thag12.1:2.3.verse: and to delight in heaven after passing away—

thag12.1:2.4.verse: the wise would take care of their ethics.

thag12.1:3.3.verse: But one lacking ethics, of bad conduct,

thag12.1:4.1.verse: A man whose ethics are bad has

thag12.1:4.3.verse: One who is ethical always has

thag12.1:4.4.verse: a good reputation, fame, and praise.

thag12.1:5.1.verse: Ethical conduct is the starting point and foundation;

thag12.1:5.4.verse: that’s why you should purify your ethics.

thag12.1:6.1.verse: Ethics provide a boundary and a restraint,

thag12.1:6.3.verse: the ford where all the Buddhas cross over:

thag12.1:6.4.verse: that’s why you should purify your ethics.

thag12.1:7.4.verse: ethics are a marvelous coat of armor.

thag12.1:8.4.verse: that float from place to place.

thag12.1:9.2.verse: ethics are the unsurpassed supply for a journey;

thag12.1:9.4.verse: that take you from place to place.

thag12.1:10.2.verse: after departing they grieve in a lower realm;

thag12.1:10.4.verse: because they are unsteady in ethics.

thag12.1:11.2.verse: after departing they’re happy in heaven;

thag12.1:11.4.verse: because they are steady in ethics.

thag12.1:12.1.verse: Ethical conduct is best in this life,

thag12.1:12.2.verse: but one with wisdom is supreme.

thag12.1:12.3.verse: Someone with both virtue and wisdom

thag12.1:12.4.verse: is victorious among men and gods.

thag12.2:1.1.verse: I was born in a low-class family.

thag12.2:1.2.verse: We were poor, with little to eat.

thag12.2:1.4.verse: I threw out the old flowers.

thag12.2:2.2.verse: I was disregarded and held in contempt.

thag12.2:2.4.verse: and paid respects to many people.

thag12.2:3.2.verse: at the fore of the mendicant Saṅgha.

thag12.2:6.2.verse: having sympathy for the whole world,

thag12.2:7.3.verse: I have completed what the Teacher taught,

thag12.2:7.4.verse: just as the victor advised me.

thag12.2:8.6.verse: I shattered the mass of darkness.

thag12.2:9.1.verse: At the end of the night,

thag12.2:9.4.verse: and revered me with joined hands.

thag12.2:10.2.verse: Homage to you, supreme among men!

thag12.2:10.4.verse: you, good fellow, are worthy of a religious donation.”

thag13.1:1.1.verse: He who was special in the kingdom,

thag13.1:8.2.verse: for the attainment of the highest goal.

thag16.3:6.3.verse: stiff as a mind beset by anger;

thag16.3:7.1.verse: propelled by the bow of craving,

thag16.3:7.2.verse: is stuck in my twice-fifteen ribcage—

thag16.3:7.3.verse: see how it stands in my breast,

thag16.3:8.2.verse: they are sharpened by memories and intentions;

thag16.3:8.3.verse: and pierced by this I tremble,

thag16.3:8.4.verse: like a leaf blowing in the gale.

thag16.3:11.2.verse: who will pull out this dart

thag16.3:11.4.verse: without harming any part of my body?

thag16.3:12.1.verse: He really would be the Lord of the Dhamma,

thag16.3:12.2.verse: the best one to cure the damage of poison;

thag16.3:12.3.verse: when I have fallen into deep waters,

thag16.3:12.4.verse: he would show me his hand and the shore.

thag16.3:13.2.verse: and I can’t wash off the mud and dirt.

thag16.3:13.3.verse: It’s full of deceit, jealousy, aggression,

thag16.3:14.1.verse: Like a thundering cloud of restlessness,

thag16.3:14.4.verse: that sweep off a person with bad views.

thag16.3:15.2.verse: a weed springs up and remains.

thag16.3:16.4.verse: cut you down suddenly like a tree.”

thag16.3:17.1.verse: That is how, when I was full of fear,

thag16.3:17.2.verse: seeking the far shore from the near,

thag16.3:17.3.verse: my shelter was the Teacher whose weapon is wisdom,

thag16.3:17.4.verse: frequented by the Saṅgha of seers.

thag16.3:18.1.verse: As I was being swept away,

thag16.3:18.2.verse: he gave me a strong, simple ladder,

thag16.3:18.3.verse: made of the heartwood of Dhamma,

thag16.3:18.4.verse: and he said to me: “Do not fear.”

thag16.3:19.1.verse: I climbed the tower of mindfulness meditation,

thag16.3:19.3.verse: at people delighting in substantial reality,

thag16.3:19.4.verse: as I had obsessed over in the past.

thag16.3:20.2.verse: as I was embarking on the ship,

thag16.3:21.1.verse: The dart that arises in oneself,

thag16.3:21.2.verse: and that which stems from the leash to existence:

thag16.3:22.1.verse: For a long time it had lain within me;

thag16.3:22.2.verse: for a long time it was fixed in me:

thag16.3:22.3.verse: the Buddha cast aside the knot,

thag16.4:1.4.verse: in which nothing lasts at all.

thag16.4:2.3.verse: it is bones swathed in skin,

thag16.4:3.3.verse: may be enough to beguile a fool,

thag16.4:3.4.verse: but not a seeker of the far shore.

thag16.4:4.3.verse: may be enough to beguile a fool,

thag16.4:4.4.verse: but not a seeker of the far shore.

thag16.4:5.2.verse: like a freshly painted makeup box

thag16.4:5.3.verse: may be enough to beguile a fool,

thag16.4:5.4.verse: but not a seeker of the far shore.

thag16.4:6.2.verse: but the deer didn’t spring the trap.

thag16.4:6.3.verse: I’ve eaten the bait and now I go,

thag16.4:7.2.verse: but the deer didn’t spring the trap.

thag16.4:7.3.verse: I’ve eaten the bait and now I go,

thag16.4:8.1.verse: “I see rich people in the world who,

thag16.4:8.2.verse: because of delusion, give not the wealth they’ve earned.

thag16.4:8.4.verse: yearning for ever more sensual pleasures.

thag16.4:9.1.verse: A king who conquered the earth by force,

thag16.4:9.2.verse: ruling the land from sea to sea,

thag16.4:9.3.verse: unsatisfied with the near shore of the ocean,

thag16.4:9.4.verse: would still yearn for the further shore.

thag16.4:10.1.verse: Not just the king, but others too,

thag16.4:10.2.verse: reach death not rid of craving.

thag16.4:10.3.verse: They leave the body still wanting,

thag16.4:10.4.verse: for in this world sensual pleasures never satisfy.

thag16.4:11.3.verse: They take out the body wrapped in a shroud,

thag16.4:11.4.verse: heap up a pyre, and burn it there.

thag16.4:12.1.verse: It’s poked with stakes while being burnt,

thag16.4:12.2.verse: in just a single cloth, all wealth gone.

thag16.4:12.4.verse: can’t help you when you’re dying.

thag16.4:13.2.verse: while beings fare on according to their deeds.

thag16.4:13.3.verse: Riches don’t follow you when you die;

thag16.4:13.4.verse: nor do children, wife, wealth, nor kingdom.

thag16.4:14.2.verse: nor does wealth banish old age;

thag16.4:14.3.verse: for the attentive say this life is short,

thag16.4:15.1.verse: The rich and the poor feel its touch;

thag16.4:15.2.verse: the fool and the attentive one feel it too.

thag16.4:15.3.verse: But the fool lies stricken by their own folly,

thag16.4:15.4.verse: while the attentive don’t tremble at the touch.

thag16.4:16.1.verse: Therefore wisdom’s much better than wealth,

thag16.4:16.2.verse: since by wisdom you reach consummation in this life.

thag16.4:16.3.verse: But if because of delusion you don’t reach consummation,

thag16.4:16.4.verse: you’ll do evil deeds in life after life.

thag16.4:17.1.verse: One who enters a womb and the world beyond,

thag16.4:17.2.verse: will transmigrate from one life to the next.

thag16.4:17.3.verse: While someone of little wisdom, placing faith in them,

thag16.4:17.4.verse: also enters a womb and the world beyond.

thag16.4:18.1.verse: As a bandit caught in a window

thag16.4:18.2.verse: is punished for his own bad deeds;

thag16.4:18.3.verse: so after departing, in the world beyond,

thag16.4:18.4.verse: people are punished for their own bad deeds.

thag16.4:19.1.verse: Sensual pleasures are diverse, sweet, delightful;

thag16.4:19.2.verse: appearing in disguise they disturb the mind.

thag16.4:20.1.verse: As fruit falls from a tree, so the sons of Manu fall,

thag16.4:20.2.verse: young and old, when the body breaks up.

thag16.4:20.3.verse: Seeing this, too, I went forth, O King;

thag16.4:20.4.verse: it’s a sure bet that the ascetic life is better.”

thag16.4:21.4.verse: I enjoy my food free of debt.

thag16.4:22.1.verse: I saw sensual pleasures as burning,

thag16.4:22.3.verse: conception in a womb as suffering,

thag16.4:22.4.verse: and the hells as very fearful.

thag16.4:23.2.verse: I was struck with a sense of urgency.

thag16.4:23.3.verse: I was stabbed, but then I found peace,

thag16.4:24.3.verse: The heavy burden is laid down,

thag16.4:24.4.verse: the leash to existence is eradicated.

thag16.4:25.2.verse: for the sake of which I went forth

thag16.4:25.3.verse: from the lay life to homelessness—

thag16.5:1.1.verse: When you see a sight, mindfulness is lost

thag16.5:1.2.verse: as you focus on a pleasant feature.

thag16.5:1.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,

thag16.5:2.6.verse: you’re said to be far from extinguishment.

thag16.5:3.1.verse: When you hear a sound, mindfulness is lost

thag16.5:3.2.verse: as you focus on a pleasant feature.

thag16.5:3.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,

thag16.5:4.6.verse: you’re said to be far from extinguishment.

thag16.5:5.1.verse: When you smell an odor, mindfulness is lost

thag16.5:5.2.verse: as you focus on a pleasant feature.

thag16.5:5.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,

thag16.5:6.6.verse: you’re said to be far from extinguishment.

thag16.5:7.1.verse: When you enjoy a taste, mindfulness is lost

thag16.5:7.2.verse: as you focus on a pleasant feature.

thag16.5:7.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,

thag16.5:8.6.verse: you’re said to be far from extinguishment.

thag16.5:9.1.verse: When you sense a touch, mindfulness is lost

thag16.5:9.2.verse: as you focus on a pleasant feature.

thag16.5:9.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,

thag16.5:10.6.verse: you’re said to be far from extinguishment.

thag16.5:11.1.verse: When you know an idea, mindfulness is lost

thag16.5:11.2.verse: as you focus on a pleasant feature.

thag16.5:11.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind full of desire,

thag16.5:12.6.verse: you’re said to be far from extinguishment.

thag16.5:13.2.verse: when you see a sight with mindfulness.

thag16.5:13.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind free of desire,

thag16.5:13.4.verse: you don’t keep clinging to it.

thag16.5:14.1.verse: Even as you see a sight

thag16.5:14.3.verse: you wear away, you don’t heap up:

thag16.5:14.6.verse: you’re said to be in the presence of extinguishment.

thag16.5:15.2.verse: when you hear a sound with mindfulness.

thag16.5:15.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind free of desire,

thag16.5:15.4.verse: you don’t keep clinging to it.

thag16.5:16.1.verse: Even as you hear a sound

thag16.5:16.3.verse: you wear away, you don’t heap up:

thag16.5:16.6.verse: you’re said to be in the presence of extinguishment.

thag16.5:17.2.verse: when you smell an odor with mindfulness.

thag16.5:17.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind free of desire,

thag16.5:17.4.verse: you don’t keep clinging to it.

thag16.5:18.1.verse: Even as you smell an odor

thag16.5:18.3.verse: you wear away, you don’t heap up:

thag16.5:18.6.verse: you’re said to be in the presence of extinguishment.

thag16.5:19.2.verse: when you enjoy a taste with mindfulness.

thag16.5:19.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind free of desire,

thag16.5:19.4.verse: you don’t keep clinging to it.

thag16.5:20.1.verse: Even as you savor a taste

thag16.5:20.3.verse: you wear away, you don’t heap up:

thag16.5:20.6.verse: you’re said to be in the presence of extinguishment.

thag16.5:21.2.verse: when you sense a touch with mindfulness.

thag16.5:21.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind free of desire,

thag16.5:21.4.verse: you don’t keep clinging to it.

thag16.5:22.1.verse: Even as you sense a touch

thag16.5:22.2.verse: and get familiar with how it feels,

thag16.5:22.3.verse: you wear away, you don’t heap up:

thag16.5:22.6.verse: you’re said to be in the presence of extinguishment.

thag16.5:23.2.verse: when you know an idea with mindfulness.

thag16.5:23.3.verse: Experiencing it with a mind free of desire,

thag16.5:23.4.verse: you don’t keep clinging to it.

thag16.5:24.1.verse: Even as you know an idea

thag16.5:24.2.verse: and get familiar with how it feels,

thag16.5:24.3.verse: you wear away, you don’t heap up:

thag16.5:24.6.verse: you’re said to be in the presence of extinguishment.

thag16.6:1.2.verse: you’re radiant, handsome, lovely to behold;

thag16.6:1.4.verse: with teeth so white; you’re strong.

thag16.6:2.3.verse: the marks of a great man,

thag16.6:2.4.verse: are all found on your body.

thag16.6:3.1.verse: Your eyes are clear, your face is fair,

thag16.6:3.3.verse: In the midst of the Saṅgha of ascetics,

thag16.6:4.1.verse: You’re a mendicant fine to see,

thag16.6:4.2.verse: with skin that shines like lustrous gold.

thag16.6:4.4.verse: what do you want with the ascetic life?

thag16.6:5.1.verse: You’re fit to be a king,

thag16.6:5.2.verse: a wheel-turning monarch, chief of charioteers,

thag16.6:5.4.verse: lord of the Black Plum Tree Land.

thag16.6:6.4.verse: as king of kings, lord of mankind!”

thag16.6:7.4.verse: By the teaching I roll forth the wheel

thag16.6:9.2.verse: the disciple who follows the Teacher’s way?

thag16.6:9.4.verse: of the teaching you rolled forth?”

thag16.6:10.1.verse: “By me the wheel was rolled forth,”

thag16.6:10.4.verse: Sāriputta, taking after the Realized One,

thag16.6:11.1.verse: I have known what should be known,

thag16.6:11.2.verse: and developed what should be developed,

thag16.6:11.3.verse: and given up what should be given up:

thag16.6:11.4.verse: and so, brahmin, I am a Buddha.

thag16.6:13.3.verse: one of those whose appearance in the world

thag16.6:14.4.verse: I rejoice, fearing nothing from any quarter.”

thag16.6:15.2.verse: is spoken by the Clear-eyed One.

thag16.6:15.4.verse: roars like a lion in the jungle.

thag16.6:16.3.verse: who would not be inspired by him,

thag16.6:16.4.verse: even one born in a dark class?

thag16.6:17.1.verse: Those who wish may follow me;

thag16.6:17.3.verse: Right here, I’ll go forth in his presence,

thag16.6:17.4.verse: the one of such outstanding wisdom.”

thag16.6:18.3.verse: we’ll also go forth in his presence,

thag16.6:18.4.verse: the one of such outstanding wisdom.”

thag16.6:19.2.verse: with cupped palms held up, ask:

thag16.6:20.3.verse: “apparent in the present life, immediately effective.

thag16.6:20.4.verse: Here the going forth isn’t in vain

thag16.6:20.5.verse: for one who trains with diligence.”

thag16.6:21.2.verse: we went for refuge, O Clear-eyed One.

thag16.6:21.3.verse: In these seven days, Blessed One,

thag16.6:21.4.verse: we’ve become tamed in your teaching.

thag16.6:22.1.verse: You are the Buddha, you are the Teacher,

thag16.6:22.2.verse: you are the sage who has overcome Māra;

thag16.6:22.3.verse: you have cut off the underlying tendencies,

thag16.6:22.4.verse: you’ve crossed over, and you bring humanity across.

thag16.6:23.3.verse: like a lion free of grasping,

thag16.6:23.4.verse: with fear and dread given up.

thag16.6:24.3.verse: Stretch out your feet, great hero:

thag16.6:24.4.verse: let these giants bow to the Teacher.”

thag16.7:2.2.verse: happy with the scraps in my bowl:
