thag16.7:21.1.verse: Giving up a hundred ounces of bronze,

thag16.7:21.2.verse: and a hundred grains of gold,

thag16.7:21.3.verse: I took a bowl made of clay:

thag16.7:22.1.verse: I used to live in a citadel with walls so high,

thag16.7:23.1.verse: Today I am fortunate, free of cowardice,

thag16.7:23.2.verse: with fear and dread given up.

thag16.7:23.4.verse: has plunged into the forest and practices absorption.

thag16.7:24.1.verse: Established in the entire spectrum of ethics,

thag16.8:1.2.verse: And I have stopped, but you tell me I’ve not.

thag16.8:1.4.verse: how is it you’ve stopped and I have not?”

thag16.8:2.2.verse: I’ve laid aside violence toward all creatures.

thag16.8:2.3.verse: But you can’t stop yourself from harming living creatures;

thag16.8:2.4.verse: that’s why I’ve stopped, but you have not.”

thag16.8:3.1.verse: “Oh, at long last a renowned great seer,

thag16.8:3.2.verse: an ascetic has followed me into this deep wood.

thag16.8:3.3.verse: Now that I’ve heard your verse on Dhamma,

thag16.8:3.4.verse: I shall discard a thousand evils.”

thag16.8:4.1.verse: With these words, the bandit hurled his sword and weapons

thag16.8:4.2.verse: down a cliff into an abyss.

thag16.8:4.3.verse: He venerated the Holy One’s feet,

thag16.8:4.4.verse: and requested the going forth from the Buddha right away.

thag16.8:5.1.verse: Then the Buddha, the compassionate great seer,

thag16.8:5.2.verse: the Teacher of the world with its gods,

thag16.8:5.4.verse: And with that he became a monk.

thag16.8:6.4.verse: like the moon freed from clouds.

thag16.8:7.4.verse: like the moon freed from clouds.

thag16.8:8.4.verse: like the moon freed from clouds.

thag16.8:9.1.verse: May even my enemies hear a Dhamma talk!

thag16.8:9.2.verse: May even my enemies devote themselves to the Buddha’s teaching!

thag16.8:9.3.verse: May even my enemies associate with those good men

thag16.8:9.4.verse: who establish others in the Dhamma!

thag16.8:10.1.verse: May even my enemies hear Dhamma at the right time,

thag16.8:10.4.verse: and may they follow that path!

thag16.8:11.1.verse: For then they’d never wish harm

thag16.8:11.4.verse: they’d look after creatures firm and frail.

thag16.8:13.1.verse: Some tame by using the rod,

thag16.8:13.2.verse: some with goads, and some with whips.

thag16.8:13.3.verse: But the unaffected one tamed me

thag16.8:14.2.verse: though I used to be harmful.

thag16.8:14.3.verse: The name I bear today is true,

thag16.8:14.4.verse: for I do no harm to anyone.

thag16.8:15.1.verse: I used to be a bandit,

thag16.8:15.3.verse: Swept away in a great flood,

thag16.8:15.4.verse: I went to the Buddha for refuge.

thag16.8:16.1.verse: I used to have blood on my hands,

thag16.8:16.4.verse: the leash to existence is eradicated.

thag16.8:17.1.verse: I’ve done many of the sort of deeds

thag16.8:17.2.verse: that lead to a bad destination.

thag16.8:17.3.verse: The result of my deeds has already struck me,

thag16.8:17.4.verse: so I enjoy my food free of debt.

thag16.8:19.3.verse: For if you’re diligent and practice absorption,

thag16.8:20.2.verse: the advice I got was good.

thag16.8:21.2.verse: the advice I got was good.

thag16.8:22.1.verse: “In the wilderness, at a tree’s root,

thag16.8:22.3.verse: it used to be that wherever I stood,

thag16.8:23.1.verse: But now I lie down happily and stand up happily,

thag16.8:23.4.verse: the Teacher had sympathy for me.

thag16.8:24.1.verse: I used to be of brahmin birth,

thag16.8:24.3.verse: now I’m a son of the Holy One,

thag16.8:25.1.verse: I am rid of craving, free of grasping,

thag16.8:25.2.verse: my sense doors are guarded and well-restrained.

thag16.8:25.3.verse: I’ve destroyed the root of gloom,

thag16.8:25.4.verse: and attained the ending of defilements.

thag16.8:26.3.verse: The heavy burden is laid down,

thag16.8:26.4.verse: the leash to existence is eradicated.”

thag16.9:1.1.verse: Leaving my mother and father behind,

thag16.9:1.2.verse: as well as sisters, kinsmen, and brothers;

thag16.9:1.3.verse: having given up the five sensual stimuli,

thag16.9:3.1.verse: But he has gone beyond all that,

thag16.9:3.2.verse: and delights in the Buddha’s teaching.

thag16.9:3.3.verse: Having crossed over the entire flood,

thag16.9:4.3.verse: having crossed over these as well,

thag16.9:5.3.verse: seeking rags from the dust heap,

thag16.9:6.2.verse: selected rags from the dust heap;

thag16.9:6.3.verse: he picked them up, washed, dyed, and wore them;

thag16.9:7.2.verse: who has many wishes and is not content,

thag16.9:8.1.verse: But someone who is mindful, few of wishes,

thag16.9:10.2.verse: the supreme Teacher in the world

thag16.9:10.3.verse: came to me in a mind-made body,

thag16.9:12.4.verse: and have fulfilled the Buddha’s instructions.

thag16.9:13.2.verse: I have not lain down to sleep.

thag16.9:14.2.verse: for the unaffected one of steady heart.

thag16.9:14.4.verse: the Clear-eyed One was fully quenched.

thag16.9:15.1.verse: He put up with painful feelings

thag16.9:15.4.verse: was like the extinguishing of a lamp.”

thag16.9:16.1.verse: “Now these touches and the other four

thag16.9:16.2.verse: are the last to be experienced by the sage;

thag16.9:16.3.verse: nor will there be other phenomena

thag16.9:16.4.verse: since the Buddha was fully quenched.

thag16.9:17.1.verse: O Penelope, weaver of the web—

thag16.9:17.2.verse: there’s no more abodes in the heavenly host.

thag16.9:17.4.verse: now there’ll be no more future lives.”

thag16.9:18.2.verse: with the age of the Divinity are known in an hour—

thag16.9:18.3.verse: that master of psychic ability sees the gods

thag16.9:18.4.verse: at the time they pass away and are reborn.”

thag16.9:20.1.verse: Then I was reborn in the Sakyan clan,

thag16.9:20.4.verse: I was awakened by cymbals and gongs.

thag16.9:21.2.verse: the Teacher, fearing nothing from any quarter;

thag16.9:21.3.verse: filling my mind with confidence in him,

thag16.9:22.2.verse: the places I used to live.

thag16.9:22.4.verse: and stayed among the thirty-three gods.

thag16.9:23.1.verse: Seven times I was a king of men

thag16.9:23.4.verse: lord of the Black Plum Tree Land.

thag16.9:24.1.verse: Seven from here, seven from there—

thag16.9:24.3.verse: I shall remember my past lives:

thag16.9:24.4.verse: at that time I stayed in the realm of the gods.

thag16.9:26.2.verse: I know the passing away and rebirth of beings,

thag16.9:26.4.verse: their lives in this state and that.

thag16.9:27.3.verse: The heavy burden is laid down,

thag16.9:27.4.verse: the leash to existence is eradicated.

thag16.9:28.1.verse: In the Vajjian village of Veḷuva,

thag16.9:28.2.verse: my life will come to an end.

thag16.9:28.4.verse: being undefiled, I will be fully extinguished.”

thag16.10:1.1.verse: This thought came to the ascetic

thag16.10:1.2.verse: in the forest full of flowers,

thag16.10:2.3.verse: from when the protector of the world,

thag16.10:2.4.verse: the best of men, was still here.

thag16.10:3.1.verse: Their robes were only for covering the private parts,

thag16.10:3.2.verse: and protection from the cold and wind.

thag16.10:3.4.verse: content with whatever they were offered.

thag16.10:4.1.verse: Whether food was fine or coarse,

thag16.10:5.3.verse: such as tonics and other necessities,

thag19.1:1.1.verse: Oh, when will I stay in a mountain cave,

thag19.1:1.3.verse: discerning all states of existence as impermanent?

thag19.1:1.4.verse: This hope of mine, when will it be?

thag19.1:2.1.verse: Oh, when will I stay happily in the forest,

thag19.1:2.2.verse: a sage wearing a torn robe, dressed in ocher,

thag19.1:2.3.verse: unselfish, with no need for hope,

thag19.1:2.4.verse: with greed, hate, and delusion destroyed?

thag19.1:3.1.verse: Oh, when will I stay alone in the wood,

thag19.1:3.2.verse: fearless, discerning this body as impermanent,

thag19.1:3.3.verse: a nest of death and disease,

thag19.1:3.4.verse: harried by death and old age; when will it be?

thag19.1:4.1.verse: Oh, when will I live, having grasped the sharp sword of wisdom

thag19.1:4.2.verse: and cut the creeper of craving that tangles around everything,

thag19.1:4.3.verse: the mother of fear, the bringer of suffering?

thag19.1:5.1.verse: Oh, when will I, seated on the lion’s throne,

thag19.1:5.2.verse: swiftly grasp the sword of the seers,

thag19.1:5.3.verse: forged by wisdom, of awesome might,

thag19.1:5.4.verse: and swiftly break Māra and his army? When will it be?

thag19.1:6.1.verse: Oh, when will I be seen in the assemblies

thag19.1:6.3.verse: seeing things as they are, with faculties subdued?

thag19.1:8.3.verse: that were realized by the great seer,

thag19.1:8.4.verse: and are so very hard to see? When will it be?

thag19.1:9.1.verse: Oh, when will I, devoted to serenity,

thag19.1:9.2.verse: see with understanding the infinite sights,

thag19.1:9.3.verse: sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas

thag19.1:9.4.verse: as burning? When will it be?

thag19.1:10.1.verse: Oh, when will I not be distraught

thag19.1:11.1.verse: Oh, when will I discern the aggregates

thag19.1:11.2.verse: and the infinite varieties of phenomena,

thag19.1:11.3.verse: those interior and exterior, as no more than

thag19.1:11.4.verse: wood, grass, and creepers? When will it be?

thag19.1:12.1.verse: Oh, when will the monsoon clouds in season

thag19.1:12.2.verse: freshly wet me in my robe in the forest,

thag19.1:12.3.verse: walking the path trodden by the seers?

thag19.1:13.1.verse: Oh, when will I rise up, intent on attaining freedom from death,

thag19.1:13.3.verse: the cry of the crested peacock in the forest?

thag19.1:14.1.verse: Oh, when will I cross by psychic power unobstructed

thag19.1:14.3.verse: and that place where one is thrown in the abyss,

thag19.1:14.4.verse: the horrifying Mare’s Mouth? When will it be?

thag19.1:15.1.verse: Oh, when will I be devoted to absorption,

thag19.1:15.2.verse: shunning all the signs of beauty,

thag19.1:15.3.verse: splitting apart desire for sensual stimulation,

thag19.1:15.4.verse: like an elephant that wanders free of ties? When will it be?

thag19.1:16.1.verse: Oh, when will I realize the teaching of the great seer

thag19.1:16.2.verse: and be content, like a pauper in debt

thag19.1:16.3.verse: harassed by creditors, who finds a hidden treasure?

thag19.1:17.1.verse: For many years you begged me,

thag19.1:17.2.verse: “Enough of living in a house for you!”

thag19.1:17.3.verse: Why do you not urge me on, mind,

thag19.1:17.4.verse: now that I’ve gone forth as an ascetic?

thag19.1:18.2.verse: “In the Mountainfold, the birds with colorful wings,

thag19.1:18.4.verse: will delight you as you meditate in the forest?”

thag19.1:19.1.verse: In my family circle, friends, loved ones, and relatives;

thag19.1:19.2.verse: and in the world, sports and play, and sensual pleasures;

thag19.1:19.3.verse: all these I gave up when I entered this life:

thag19.1:19.4.verse: and even then you’re not content with me, mind!

thag19.1:20.1.verse: This is mine alone, it doesn’t belong to others;

thag19.1:20.2.verse: when it is time to don your armor, why lament?

thag19.1:20.3.verse: Observing that all this is unstable,

thag19.1:20.4.verse: I went forth, seeking the state free of death.

thag19.1:21.1.verse: He whose words are well-composed, supreme among people,

thag19.1:21.2.verse: great physician, guide for those fit to train, said:

thag19.1:21.4.verse: so it’s very hard to control if you are not free of lust.”

thag19.1:22.1.verse: Sensual pleasures are diverse, sweet, delightful;

thag19.1:22.2.verse: an ignorant ordinary person is bound to them.

thag19.1:22.3.verse: Seeking to be reborn again, they wish for suffering;

thag19.1:22.4.verse: led on by their mind, they’re banished to hell.

thag19.1:23.1.verse: “Staying in the grove resounding with cries

thag19.1:23.2.verse: of peacocks and herons, and adorned by leopards and tigers,

thag19.1:23.3.verse: abandon concern for the body, without fail!”

thag19.1:23.4.verse: So you used to urge me, mind.

thag19.1:24.2.verse: the powers, awakening factors, and immersion;

thag19.1:24.3.verse: realize the three knowledges in the teaching of the Buddha!”

thag19.1:24.4.verse: So you used to urge me, mind.

thag19.1:25.1.verse: “Develop the eightfold path to realize freedom from death

thag19.1:25.2.verse: emancipating, its objective being the end of all suffering,

thag19.1:25.4.verse: So you used to urge me, mind.

thag19.1:26.1.verse: “Reflect rationally on the aggregates as suffering,

thag19.1:26.2.verse: and abandon that from which suffering arises;

thag19.1:26.3.verse: make an end of suffering in this very life!”

thag19.1:26.4.verse: So you used to urge me, mind.

thag19.1:27.2.verse: that emptiness is non-self, and that gloom is death.

thag19.1:27.4.verse: So you used to urge me, mind.

thag19.1:28.2.verse: seek alms amongst families, bowl in hand.

thag19.1:28.3.verse: Devote yourself to the word of the Teacher, the great seer!”

thag19.1:28.4.verse: So you used to urge me, mind.

thag19.1:29.2.verse: mentally unchained to families and sensual pleasures,

thag19.1:29.3.verse: like the full moon on a bright night!”

thag19.1:29.4.verse: So you used to urge me, mind.

thag19.1:30.2.verse: one who lives in charnel grounds, a rag-robe wearer,

thag19.1:30.3.verse: one who never lies down, always delighting in ascetic practices.”

thag19.1:30.4.verse: So you used to urge me, mind.

thag19.1:31.1.verse: Mind, when you urge me to the impermanent and unstable,

thag19.1:31.2.verse: you’re acting like someone who plants trees,

thag19.1:31.3.verse: then, when they’re about to fruit,

thag19.1:31.4.verse: wishes to cut down the very same trees.

thag19.1:32.2.verse: I won’t do your bidding any more.

thag19.1:32.3.verse: Sensual pleasures are suffering, painful, and very dangerous;

thag19.1:32.4.verse: I’ll wander with my mind focused only on extinguishment.

thag19.1:33.1.verse: I didn’t go forth due to bad luck or shamelessness,

thag19.1:33.2.verse: or due to a whim or banishment,

thag19.1:33.3.verse: nor for the sake of a livelihood;

thag19.1:33.4.verse: it was because I agreed to the promise you made, mind.

thag19.1:34.2.verse: the settling of suffering: these are praised by true persons.”

thag19.1:34.3.verse: So you used to urge me, mind,

thag19.1:34.4.verse: but now you keep on with your old habits!

thag19.1:35.1.verse: Craving, ignorance, the loved and unloved,

thag19.1:35.3.verse: and the delightful kinds of sensual stimulation:

thag19.1:35.4.verse: I’ve vomited them up, I can’t swallow them back.

thag19.1:36.1.verse: I’ve done your bidding everywhere, mind!

thag19.1:36.2.verse: For many births, I’ve done nothing to upset you.

thag19.1:36.3.verse: Yet the creation in myself is because of your ingratitude—

thag19.1:36.4.verse: for a long time I’ve transmigrated in the suffering you’ve made.

thag19.1:37.1.verse: Only you, mind, make a brahmin;

thag19.1:37.2.verse: you make an aristocrat or a royal seer.

thag19.1:37.3.verse: Sometimes we become peasants or menials;

thag19.1:37.4.verse: and life as a god is also on account of you.

thag19.1:38.2.verse: because of you we’re born in hell.

thag19.1:38.4.verse: and life as a ghost is also on account of you.

thag19.1:39.1.verse: Come what may, you won’t betray me again,

thag19.1:39.2.verse: dazzling me with your ever-changing display!

thag19.1:39.3.verse: You play with me like I’m mad—

thag19.1:39.4.verse: but how have I ever failed you, mind?

thag19.1:40.1.verse: In the past my mind wandered

thag19.1:40.2.verse: how it wished, where it liked, as it pleased.

thag19.1:40.4.verse: as a trainer with a hook guides a rutting elephant.

thag19.1:41.1.verse: The teacher willed that this world appear to me

thag19.1:41.3.verse: Mind, let me leap into the victor’s teaching,

thag19.1:41.4.verse: carry me over the great flood, so hard to pass.

thag19.1:42.2.verse: Nothing could make me return to your control!

thag19.1:42.3.verse: I’ve gone forth in the teaching of the great seer,

thag19.1:42.4.verse: those like me don’t come to ruin.

thag19.1:43.2.verse: the four quarters, the intermediate directions, below and in the sky;

thag19.1:43.3.verse: the three realms of existence are all impermanent and harried—

thag19.1:43.4.verse: where can you go to find happiness, mind?

thag19.1:44.1.verse: Mind, what will you do to someone who has made the ultimate commitment?

thag19.1:44.2.verse: Nothing could make me a follower under your control, mind;

thag19.1:44.3.verse: I’d never touch a bellows with a mouth open at each end;

thag19.1:44.4.verse: curse this mortal frame flowing with nine streams!

thag19.1:45.1.verse: You’ve ascended the mountain peak, full of nature’s beauty,

thag19.1:45.3.verse: a grove sprinkled with fresh water in the monsoon;

thag19.1:45.4.verse: and there you’ll be happy in your cave-home.

thag19.1:46.1.verse: Peacocks with beautiful necks and crests,

thag19.1:46.3.verse: crying out at the resounding thunder:

thag19.1:46.4.verse: they’ll delight you as you meditate in the forest.

thag19.1:47.1.verse: When the heavens have rained, and the grass is four inches high,

thag19.1:47.2.verse: and the grove is full of flowers like a cloud,

thag19.1:47.3.verse: between the mountains, like the fork of a tree, I’ll lie;

thag19.1:47.4.verse: it will be as soft as cotton-buds.

thag19.1:48.1.verse: I’ll act rather as a master does:

thag19.1:48.2.verse: let whatever I get be enough for me.

thag19.1:48.3.verse: And that’s why I’ll make you as supple

thag19.1:48.4.verse: as a tireless worker makes a cat-skin bag.

thag19.1:49.1.verse: I’ll act rather as a master does:

thag19.1:49.2.verse: let whatever I get be enough for me.

thag19.1:49.3.verse: I’ll control you with my energy,

thag19.1:49.4.verse: as a skilled trainer controls an elephant with a hook.

thag19.1:50.1.verse: Now that you’re well-tamed and reliable,

thag19.1:50.2.verse: I can use you, like a trainer uses a straight-running horse,

thag19.1:50.3.verse: to practice the path of grace,

thag19.1:50.4.verse: cultivated by those who take care of their minds.

thag19.1:51.1.verse: I shall strongly fasten you to a meditation subject,

thag19.1:51.2.verse: as an elephant is tied to a post with firm rope.

thag19.1:51.3.verse: You’ll be well-guarded by me, well-developed by mindfulness,

thag19.1:51.4.verse: and unattached to rebirth in all states of existence.

thag19.1:52.1.verse: With wisdom you’ll cut short the one following the wrong path,

thag19.1:52.2.verse: curb them by meditation, and settle them on the right path.

thag19.1:52.3.verse: Having seen arising and passing away with respect to the cause of suffering,

thag19.1:52.4.verse: you’ll be an heir to the greatest teacher.

thag19.1:53.1.verse: Under the sway of the four distortions, mind,

thag19.1:53.2.verse: you dragged me around like a bull in a pit;

thag19.1:53.3.verse: but now you won’t associate with the great sage of compassion,

thag19.1:53.4.verse: the cutter of fetters and bonds?

thag19.1:54.1.verse: Like a deer roaming free in the colorful forest,

thag19.1:54.2.verse: I’ll ascend the lovely mountain wreathed in monsoon clouds,

thag19.1:54.3.verse: and rejoice to be on that hill, free of folk—

thag19.1:54.4.verse: there is no doubt you’ll perish, mind.

thag19.1:55.1.verse: The men and women who live under your will and command,

thag19.1:55.3.verse: they are ignorant and fall under Māra’s control;

thag19.1:55.4.verse: loving life, they’re your disciples, mind.

thag20.1:30.2.verse: the sage in his remote lodging,

thag20.1:31.2.verse: a hundred times in the human realm,

thag20.1:31.4.verse: a student accomplished in the Vedas;

thag20.1:32.1.verse: and if he were to become a reciter,

thag20.1:32.2.verse: a master of the three Vedas:

thag20.1:32.4.verse: isn’t worth a sixteenth of that.

thag20.1:34.4.verse: in the perfected one, the unaffected;

thag20.1:34.5.verse: quickly venerate him with cupped palms:

thag20.1:35.2.verse: you don’t see the true teaching.

thag20.1:37.2.verse: It is good to see him;

thag20.1:37.3.verse: he is freed in both ways,

thag20.1:38.1.verse: free of thorns, with yoking ended,

thag20.1:38.2.verse: master of the three knowledges, conqueror of death;

thag20.1:38.4.verse: a supreme field of merit for the people.”

thag21.1:7.1.verse: Whatever here is included in form—

thag21.1:7.2.verse: on earth, in the sky, or in planet’s deep—

thag21.1:7.3.verse: wears out, it is all impermanent:

thag21.1:7.4.verse: the self-examined live having comprehended this.

thag21.1:8.1.verse: People are bound to their attachments,

thag21.1:8.2.verse: to impingement of the seen and heard, and to what is thought.

thag21.1:8.3.verse: Unstirred, dispel desire for these things;

thag21.1:8.4.verse: for one called ‘a sage’ does not cling to them.

thag21.1:9.1.verse: Trapped in the sixty wrong views, full of their own opinions,

thag21.1:9.2.verse: ordinary people are fixed in wrong principles.

thag21.1:9.3.verse: But that mendicant wouldn’t join a sect,

thag21.1:9.4.verse: still less would they utter lewd speech.

thag21.1:10.2.verse: free of deceit, alert, without envy,

thag21.1:10.3.verse: the sage has reached the state of peace;

thag21.1:11.2.verse: Completely abandon the different kinds of conceit!

thag21.1:11.3.verse: Besotted with the different kinds of conceit,

thag21.1:11.4.verse: you’ve had regrets for a long time.

thag21.1:12.1.verse: Smeared by smears and slain by conceit,

thag21.1:12.3.verse: When people slain by conceit are reborn in hell,

thag21.1:12.4.verse: they grieve for a long time.

thag21.1:13.1.verse: But a mendicant who practices rightly,

thag21.1:13.3.verse: They enjoy happiness and a good reputation,

thag21.1:13.4.verse: and they rightly call him a ‘Seer of Truth’.

thag21.1:14.1.verse: So being not hard-hearted, but energetic,

thag21.1:14.3.verse: and having completely given up conceit,

thag21.1:14.4.verse: the one who makes an end with knowledge is assuaged.”

thig11.1:14.1.verse: The Chapter of the Twelves is finished.

thig11.1:1.2.verse: though we were mother and daughter.

thig11.1:1.3.verse: I was struck with a sense of urgency,

thig11.1:2.3.verse: where we, both mother and daughter,

thig11.1:3.1.verse: Seeing the danger in sensual pleasures,

thig11.1:3.4.verse: from the lay life to homelessness.

thig11.1:4.3.verse: I encompass the minds of others;

thig11.1:5.2.verse: and attained the ending of defilements.

thig11.1:5.3.verse: I’ve realized the six kinds of direct knowledge,

thig11.1:6.3.verse: Then I bowed at the feet of the Buddha,

thig11.1:6.4.verse: the glorious protector of the world.”

thig11.1:7.1.verse: “You’ve come to this sal tree all crowned with flowers,

thig11.1:7.2.verse: and stand at its root all alone.

thig11.1:7.3.verse: But you have no male companion with you—

thig11.1:7.4.verse: silly girl, aren’t you afraid of rascals?”

thig11.1:8.3.verse: I’d stir not a hair nor tremble.

thig11.1:8.4.verse: What could you do to me all alone, Māra?

thig11.1:9.3.verse: I could stand between your eyebrows

thig11.1:9.4.verse: and you still wouldn’t see me.

thig11.1:10.1.verse: I’m the master of my own mind,

thig11.1:10.2.verse: I’ve developed the bases of psychic power well.

thig11.1:10.3.verse: I’ve realized the six kinds of direct knowledge,

thig11.1:11.1.verse: Sensual pleasures are like swords and spears;

thig11.1:11.2.verse: the aggregates are their chopping block.

thig11.1:11.4.verse: is now no delight for me.

thig11.1:12.1.verse: Relishing is banished in every respect,

thig11.1:12.2.verse: and the mass of darkness is shattered.

thig12.1:1.1.verse: “I am one who bathes in cold water,

thig12.1:1.3.verse: afraid of punishment by the masters,

thig12.1:2.2.verse: always plunging into the water frightened,

thig12.1:4.1.verse: Whether one is young or old,

thig12.1:4.3.verse: is liberated from their bad deed

thig12.1:5.4.verse: one is liberated from bad deeds’?

thig12.1:6.4.verse: and all the other marine beings will go to heaven?

thig12.1:7.1.verse: Those who slaughter sheep and pigs,

thig12.1:7.6.verse: they would be liberated from their bad deeds.

thig12.1:8.1.verse: If these rivers could carry away

thig12.1:8.2.verse: the bad deeds you made in the past,

thig12.1:8.3.verse: they would also carry away your merit,

thig12.1:8.4.verse: because it would be outside of yourself.

thig12.1:9.1.verse: Whatever you are frightened about, brahmin,

thig12.1:9.2.verse: because of which you are always going into the water,

thig12.1:9.4.verse: you do not need to let the cold hurt your skin.”

thig12.1:10.2.verse: and you have led me to the Noble Path.

thig12.1:11.2.verse: I do not wish to have it.

thig12.1:11.3.verse: If you are afraid of suffering,

thig12.1:12.1.verse: do not do any bad deeds,

thig12.1:12.3.verse: If you do a bad deed,

thig12.1:12.4.verse: or will do so in the future,

thig12.1:13.1.verse: you will not be liberated from your suffering,

thig12.1:13.2.verse: it reaches you even if you try to run away from it.

thig12.1:13.3.verse: If you are afraid of suffering,

thig12.1:14.1.verse: go for refuge to the Buddha,

thig12.1:15.1.verse: “I go for refuge to the Buddha,

thig12.1:15.3.verse: I take up the moral practices,

thig12.1:16.1.verse: Before I was a kinsman of Brahmā,

thig12.1:16.2.verse: today I am a real brahmin.

thig12.1:16.3.verse: Possessing the three knowledges and higher insight,

thig12.1:16.4.verse: I am one who has bathed, and has attained the highest knowledge.”

thig12.1:18.1.verse: The Chapter of the Sixteens is finished.

thig12.1:1.1.verse: “I used to be a water-carrier. Even when it was cold,

thig12.1:1.2.verse: I would always plunge into the water,

thig12.1:1.4.verse: harassed by fear of abuse and anger.

thig12.1:2.1.verse: Brahmin, what are you afraid of,

thig12.1:2.2.verse: that you always plunge into the water,

thig12.1:3.2.verse: Madam Puṇṇikā, when you ask me:

thig12.1:3.4.verse: to ward off the wickedness I have done.

thig12.1:4.3.verse: by ablution in water they are

thig12.1:5.3.verse: ‘Actually, by ablution in water one is

thig12.1:6.1.verse: Would not they all go to heaven, then:

thig12.1:6.2.verse: all the frogs and the turtles,

thig12.1:7.5.verse: by ablution in water they too would be

thig12.1:8.1.verse: If these rivers had carried away

thig12.1:8.2.verse: your bad deeds in the past,

thig12.1:8.3.verse: they would also carry away your good deeds,

thig12.1:9.1.verse: Brahmin, the thing that you are afraid of,

thig12.1:9.2.verse: when you always plunge into the water,

thig12.1:9.3.verse: do not do that very thing,

thig12.1:9.4.verse: don’t let the cold harm your skin.”

thig12.1:10.1.verse: “I have been on the wrong path,

thig12.1:10.2.verse: and you’ve guided me to the noble path.

thig12.1:12.3.verse: If you should do a bad deed,

thig12.1:13.1.verse: you won’t be freed from suffering,

thig12.1:13.2.verse: though you fly away and flee.

thig12.1:14.1.verse: go for refuge to the Buddha, the unaffected,

thig12.1:14.2.verse: to his teaching and to the Saṅgha.

thig12.1:14.4.verse: that will be good for you.”

thig12.1:15.1.verse: “I go for refuge to the Buddha, the unaffected,

thig12.1:15.2.verse: to his teaching and to the Saṅgha.

thig12.1:15.4.verse: that will be good for me.

thig12.1:16.1.verse: I used to be brahmin only by kin,

thig12.1:16.2.verse: today I truly am a brahmin!

thig12.1:16.3.verse: Master of the three knowledges, accomplished in wisdom,

thig12.1:16.4.verse: I’m a scholar, a bathed initiate.”

thig13.1:1.1.verse: “Curly hair, black like the color of bees,

thig13.1:1.2.verse: sprang from this head of mine.

thig13.1:1.3.verse: Because of old age it is now like hemp-bark—

thig13.1:1.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:2.1.verse: A fragrance like a sweet-scented chest full of flowers,

thig13.1:2.2.verse: sprang from this head of mine.

thig13.1:2.3.verse: Because of old age now it just smells like fur—

thig13.1:2.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:3.1.verse: Hair growing thick like a forest grove,

thig13.1:3.2.verse: made resplendent, and gathered at the top with comb and hairpins.

thig13.1:3.3.verse: Because of old age, it is now thinning here and there—

thig13.1:3.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:4.1.verse: Shining hair, adorned with plaits of black and gold,

thig13.1:4.3.verse: Because of old age my head has gone bald—

thig13.1:4.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:5.1.verse: My eyebrows were such a splendor,

thig13.1:5.2.verse: so well done, as if drawn by a painter.

thig13.1:5.3.verse: Because of old age they are sagging and wrinkly—

thig13.1:5.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:6.1.verse: My large eyes were the best shade of blue,

thig13.1:6.2.verse: as radiant and splendid as gemstones.

thig13.1:6.3.verse: Because of old age, they shine no more—

thig13.1:6.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:7.2.verse: shining at the peak of youth—

thig13.1:7.3.verse: Because of old age it has withered,

thig13.1:7.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:8.1.verse: My earlobes were such a splendor,

thig13.1:8.2.verse: like bracelets well made from start to finish.

thig13.1:8.3.verse: Because of old age they are sagging and wrinkly—

thig13.1:8.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:9.1.verse: The color of a jasmine bud,

thig13.1:9.3.verse: Because of old age they are broken and blackened—

thig13.1:9.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:10.1.verse: I had a sweet hum like a cuckoo,

thig13.1:10.2.verse: chirping in the forests and jungles.

thig13.1:10.3.verse: Because of old age it falters at times—

thig13.1:10.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:11.1.verse: My neck looked beautiful in the past,

thig13.1:11.2.verse: as smooth as a well polished conch-shell.

thig13.1:11.3.verse: Because of old age it is twisted and broken—

thig13.1:11.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:12.1.verse: My arms were of such splendor,

thig13.1:12.3.verse: Because of old age they are now like withered branches—

thig13.1:12.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:13.1.verse: My hands were of such splendor,

thig13.1:13.2.verse: smooth and adorned with gold rings.

thig13.1:13.3.verse: Because of old age they are now like gnarled roots—

thig13.1:13.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:14.1.verse: My little breasts were of such splendor,

thig13.1:14.2.verse: plump, round, close together, and perky.

thig13.1:14.3.verse: Like drops of water they now droop—

thig13.1:14.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:15.1.verse: My body was of such splendor,

thig13.1:15.3.verse: Now it’s covered with fine wrinkles—

thig13.1:15.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:16.1.verse: My thighs were of such splendor,

thig13.1:16.2.verse: both like the torso of a snake.

thig13.1:16.3.verse: Because of old age they are now like stalks of bamboo—

thig13.1:16.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:17.1.verse: My calves were of such splendor,

thig13.1:17.3.verse: Because of old age they are now like sesame twigs—

thig13.1:17.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:18.1.verse: My feet were of such splendor,

thig13.1:18.2.verse: as soft as tufts of cotton.

thig13.1:18.3.verse: Because of old age they are wrinkled and cracked—

thig13.1:18.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.

thig13.1:19.2.verse: now decrepit, an abode of much suffering,

thig13.1:19.3.verse: a house of decrepitude fallen into disrepair—

thig13.1:19.4.verse: the truth-speaker’s words are never wrong.”

thig13.1:1.1.verse: My hair was as black as bees,

thig13.1:1.3.verse: now old, it has become like hemp bark—

thig13.1:1.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:2.2.verse: my head was as fragrant as a perfume box;

thig13.1:2.3.verse: now old, it smells like dog fur—

thig13.1:2.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:3.1.verse: My hair was as thick as a well-planted forest,

thig13.1:3.2.verse: it shone, parted with brush and pins;

thig13.1:3.3.verse: now old, it’s patchy and sparse—

thig13.1:3.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:4.1.verse: With plaits of black and ribbons of gold,

thig13.1:4.2.verse: it was so pretty, graced with braids;

thig13.1:4.3.verse: now old, my head’s gone bald—

thig13.1:4.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:5.1.verse: My eyebrows used to look so nice,

thig13.1:5.2.verse: like crescents painted by an artist;

thig13.1:5.3.verse: now old, they droop with wrinkles—

thig13.1:5.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:6.1.verse: My eyes shone brilliant as gems,

thig13.1:6.3.verse: ruined by age, they shine no more—

thig13.1:6.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:7.1.verse: My nose was like a perfect peak,

thig13.1:7.2.verse: lovely in my bloom of youth;

thig13.1:7.3.verse: now old, it’s shriveled like a pepper;

thig13.1:7.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:8.3.verse: now old, they droop with wrinkles—

thig13.1:8.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:9.1.verse: My teeth used to be so pretty,

thig13.1:9.3.verse: now old, they’re broken and yellow—

thig13.1:9.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:10.1.verse: My singing was sweet as a cuckoo

thig13.1:10.3.verse: now old, it’s patchy and croaking—

thig13.1:10.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:11.1.verse: My neck used to be so pretty,

thig13.1:11.2.verse: like a polished shell of conch;

thig13.1:11.3.verse: now old, it’s bowed and bent—

thig13.1:11.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:12.1.verse: My arms used to be so pretty,

thig13.1:12.3.verse: with age, they wrinkle and sag as a patala tree—

thig13.1:12.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:13.1.verse: My hands used to be so pretty,

thig13.1:13.3.verse: now old, they’re like red radishes—

thig13.1:13.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:14.1.verse: My breasts were both once so pretty,

thig13.1:14.3.verse: now they droop like water bags—

thig13.1:14.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:15.1.verse: My body used to be so pretty,

thig13.1:15.2.verse: like a polished slab of lustrous gold;

thig13.1:15.3.verse: now it’s covered with delicate wrinkles—

thig13.1:15.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:16.1.verse: Both my thighs used to be so pretty,

thig13.1:16.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:17.1.verse: My calves used to be so pretty,

thig13.1:17.3.verse: now old, they’re like sesame sticks—

thig13.1:17.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:18.1.verse: Both my feet used to be so pretty,

thig13.1:18.3.verse: now old, they’re cracked and wrinkly—

thig13.1:18.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.1:19.1.verse: This bag of bones once was such,

thig13.1:19.2.verse: but now it’s withered, home to so much pain;

thig13.1:19.3.verse: like a house in decay with plaster crumbling—

thig13.1:19.4.verse: the word of the truthful one is confirmed.

thig13.2:1.4.verse: surely you will become a contemplative.

thig13.2:2.4.verse: what is so dear to you about contemplatives?

thig13.2:3.2.verse: living on what is given by others,

thig13.2:3.4.verse: what is so dear to you about contemplatives?”

thig13.2:4.1.verse: “For a very long time indeed, father,

thig13.2:4.2.verse: you have asked me about contemplatives.

thig13.2:4.3.verse: For you, I will speak in praise of their

thig13.2:5.3.verse: they give up passion and aversion—

thig13.2:5.4.verse: because of this, contemplatives are dear to me.

thig13.2:6.2.verse: they shake off, the ones whose actions are pure,

thig13.2:6.4.verse: because of this, contemplatives are dear to me.

thig13.2:7.4.verse: because of this, contemplatives are dear to me.

thig13.2:8.2.verse: they are pure internally and externally,

thig13.2:8.4.verse: because of this, contemplatives are dear to me.

thig13.2:9.1.verse: Very learned, knowing the Dhamma by heart,

thig13.2:9.2.verse: Noble Ones, living a life of Dhamma,

thig13.2:9.3.verse: they expound the meaning of the Dhamma—

thig13.2:9.4.verse: because of this, contemplatives are dear to me.

thig13.2:10.1.verse: Very learned, knowing the Dhamma by heart,

thig13.2:10.2.verse: Noble Ones, living a life of Dhamma,

thig13.2:10.4.verse: because of this, contemplatives are dear to me.

thig13.2:11.3.verse: they clearly know the end of suffering—

thig13.2:11.4.verse: because of this, contemplatives are dear to me.

thig13.2:12.1.verse: From whichever village they set out,

thig13.2:12.4.verse: because of this, contemplatives are dear to me.

thig13.2:13.1.verse: They do not deposit things in storerooms,

thig13.2:13.2.verse: nor do they have pots and pans,

thig13.2:13.4.verse: because of this, contemplatives are dear to me.

thig13.2:14.1.verse: They do not take up gold,

thig13.2:14.3.verse: they are nourished by the present moment—

thig13.2:14.4.verse: because of this, contemplatives are dear to me.

thig13.2:15.4.verse: because of this, contemplatives are dear to me.”

thig13.2:16.2.verse: that you were born in this clan, Rohinī.

thig13.2:16.3.verse: Very devout, and with faith in the Buddha, the Dhamma,

thig13.2:17.4.verse: will receive donations from us as well.

thig13.2:18.1.verse: Charity will be established here by us,

thig13.2:19.1.verse: go for refuge to the Buddha,

thig13.2:20.1.verse: “I go for refuge to the Buddha,

thig13.2:20.3.verse: Having taken up the moral practices,

thig13.2:20.4.verse: it will be for my sake.”

thig13.2:21.1.verse: “Before I was a kinsman of Brahmā,

thig13.2:21.3.verse: Possessing the three knowledges, I am one who has attained the highest knowledge,

thig13.2:21.4.verse: I am one who has bathed.”

thig13.2:3.1.verse: They don’t like to work, they’re lazy,

thig13.2:3.3.verse: always on the lookout, greedy for sweets—

thig13.2:3.4.verse: so why do you like ascetics?”

thig13.2:5.1.verse: They like to work, they’re not lazy;

thig13.2:5.2.verse: by giving up greed and hate,

thig13.2:5.3.verse: they do the best kind of work—

thig13.2:6.1.verse: As for the three roots of evil,

thig13.2:6.2.verse: by pure deeds they shake them off.

thig13.2:6.3.verse: They have given up all wickedness—

thig13.2:7.3.verse: their actions of mind are pure—

thig13.2:9.1.verse: They’re learned and memorize the teaching,

thig13.2:9.3.verse: teaching the text and its meaning:

thig13.2:10.1.verse: They’re learned and memorize the teaching,

thig13.2:11.3.verse: they understand the end of suffering—

thig13.2:12.2.verse: they don’t look back with longing,

thig13.2:13.1.verse: They hoard no goods in storerooms,

thig13.2:13.3.verse: They seek food prepared by others—

thig13.2:14.3.verse: feeding on whatever comes that day,

thig13.2:15.1.verse: They have gone forth from different families,

thig13.2:15.3.verse: and yet they all love one another—

thig13.2:16.1.verse: “Dear Rohinī, it was truly for our benefit

thig13.2:16.2.verse: that you were born in our family!

thig13.2:16.3.verse: You have faith and such keen respect

thig13.2:16.4.verse: for the Buddha, his teaching, and the Saṅgha.

thig13.2:18.1.verse: For there we will place our sacrifice,

thig13.2:19.1.verse: go for refuge to the Buddha, the unaffected,

thig13.2:19.2.verse: to his teaching and to the Saṅgha.

thig13.2:19.4.verse: that will be good for you.”

thig13.2:20.1.verse: “I go for refuge to the Buddha, the unaffected,

thig13.2:20.2.verse: to his teaching and to the Saṅgha.

thig13.2:20.4.verse: that will be good for me.

thig13.2:21.1.verse: I used to be brahmin only by kin,

thig13.2:21.2.verse: now I genuinely am a brahmin.

thig13.2:21.3.verse: Master of the three knowledges, I’m a scholar,

thig13.2:21.4.verse: a knowledge master, a bathed initiate.”

thig13.3:1.1.verse: “In the past I handled a staff,

thig13.3:1.2.verse: now I am a deer hunter.

thig13.3:1.3.verse: Desire held me back from passing over

thig13.3:1.4.verse: the terrible marsh to the far shore.

thig13.3:2.2.verse: sure that I am captivated by our child.

thig13.3:2.3.verse: I need to cut my bond with Cāpā

thig13.3:3.1.verse: The Great Hero will not be upset with me!

thig13.3:3.2.verse: The Great Sage will not be upset with me!

thig13.3:3.3.verse: Because how could a pure one with spiritual power

thig13.3:4.1.verse: I will escape from her claws!

thig13.3:4.2.verse: Who would want to live trapped by claws,

thig13.3:4.3.verse: that in the shape of a female capture

thig13.3:4.4.verse: contemplatives who are living a life of Dhamma?”

thig13.3:5.2.verse: enjoy sensual pleasures like you did in the past.

thig13.3:6.2.verse: of what you say to me,

thig13.3:7.1.verse: “Kālā, I am like an acacia tree

thig13.3:7.2.verse: flowering at the peak of a mountain,

thig13.3:7.4.verse: a trumpet flower tree on an island.

thig13.3:8.1.verse: My limbs are anointed in yellow sandalwood,

thig13.3:8.2.verse: and I wear the best fabrics from Kāsi.

thig13.3:8.3.verse: How can you go and leave me behind,

thig13.3:9.2.verse: who longs to capture a bird,

thig13.3:9.3.verse: but even with your attractive body

thig13.3:10.2.verse: Kāḷā, has come into existence because of you.

thig13.3:10.3.verse: How can you go and abandon me,

thig13.3:11.4.verse: like a Nāga who has cut all bonds.”

thig13.3:12.2.verse: who, with a knife or a stick,

thig13.3:12.3.verse: I will knock down on the ground,

thig13.3:12.4.verse: struck by grief after the loss of your child you will not go.”

thig13.3:13.3.verse: not even for my own child, you wretch,

thig13.3:14.2.verse: then where will you go, Kāḷa?

thig13.3:14.4.verse: to what borough or royal city?”

thig13.3:15.1.verse: “In the past we had a following,

thig13.3:15.2.verse: we thought we were contemplatives, but we actually were not.

thig13.3:15.3.verse: We wandered from village to village,

thig13.3:16.1.verse: But there is the Bhagavant, the Buddha,

thig13.3:16.3.verse: for the removal of all suffering,

thig14.1:1.1.verse: Going to the lovely mango grove

thig14.1:1.3.verse: was held up by a rascal.

thig14.1:2.1.verse: “What harm have I done to you,

thig14.1:2.2.verse: that you stand in my way?

thig14.1:2.3.verse: Respectable sir, it’s not proper that a man

thig14.1:2.4.verse: should touch a woman gone forth.

thig14.1:3.1.verse: This training was taught by the Holy One,

thig14.1:3.2.verse: it is a serious matter in my teacher’s instructions.

thig14.1:3.3.verse: I am pure and rid of blemishes,

thig14.1:3.4.verse: so why do you stand in my way?

thig14.1:4.1.verse: One whose mind is clouded against one unclouded;

thig14.1:4.2.verse: one who is lustful against one free of lust;

thig14.1:4.3.verse: unblemished, my heart is freed in every respect,

thig14.1:4.4.verse: so why do you stand in my way?”

thig14.1:5.2.verse: what will going-forth do for you?

thig14.1:5.4.verse: come and play in the blossom grove.

thig14.1:6.1.verse: Everywhere, the scent of pollen wafts sweet,

thig14.1:6.3.verse: The start of spring is a happy time—

thig14.1:6.4.verse: come and play in the blossom grove.

thig14.1:7.2.verse: cry out, as it were, in the gale.

thig14.1:7.3.verse: But what kind of fun will you have

thig14.1:7.4.verse: if you plunge into the woods all alone?

thig14.1:8.2.verse: and cow elephants aroused by rutting bulls;

thig14.1:8.3.verse: you wish to go without a friend

thig14.1:9.1.verse: Like a doll made of glittering gold,

thig14.1:9.2.verse: like a nymph wandering the park of bright vines,

thig14.1:9.4.verse: in graceful clothes of delicate Kāsian cloth.

thig14.1:10.2.verse: if we are to stay in the forest.

thig14.1:10.3.verse: I love no creature more than you,

thig14.1:10.4.verse: O pixie with such captivating eyes.

thig14.1:11.1.verse: Were you to take up my invitation—

thig14.1:11.2.verse: ‘Come, be happy, and live in a house’—

thig14.1:11.3.verse: you’ll stay in a longhouse sheltered from wind;

thig14.1:11.4.verse: let the ladies look to your needs.

thig14.1:12.2.verse: put on your garlands and your cosmetics.

thig14.1:12.3.verse: I’ll make all sorts of adornments for you,

thig14.1:12.4.verse: of lustrous gold and gems and pearls.

thig14.1:13.2.verse: its coverlet so clean and nice,

thig14.1:14.1.verse: As a blue lily risen from the water

thig14.1:14.3.verse: so too, O chaste and holy lady,

thig14.1:15.1.verse: “This carcass is full of putrefaction, it swells

thig14.1:15.2.verse: the charnel ground, for its nature is to fall apart.

thig14.1:15.3.verse: What do you think is so essential in it

thig14.1:15.4.verse: that you stare at me so crazily?”

thig14.1:16.1.verse: “Your eyes are like those of a doe,

thig14.1:16.2.verse: or a pixie in the mountains;

thig14.1:16.4.verse: swells in me all the more.

thig14.1:17.1.verse: Your eyes are like a blue lily’s bud

thig14.1:17.2.verse: in your flawless face shining like coruscant gold.

thig14.1:17.4.verse: swells in me all the more.

thig14.1:18.1.verse: Though you may wander far, I’ll still think of you,

thig14.1:18.2.verse: with lashes so long and eyes so bright.

thig14.1:18.3.verse: I love no eyes more than yours,

thig14.1:18.4.verse: O pixie with such bashful eyes.”

thig14.1:19.1.verse: “You’re setting out on the wrong road!

thig14.1:19.2.verse: You’re looking to take the moon for your toy!

thig14.1:19.3.verse: You’re trying to leap over Mount Meru!

thig14.1:19.4.verse: You, who are hunting a child of the Buddha!

thig14.1:20.1.verse: For in this world with all its gods,

thig14.1:20.2.verse: there will be no more lust anywhere in me.

thig14.1:20.3.verse: I don’t even know what kind it could be,

thig14.1:20.4.verse: it’s been smashed root and all by the path.

thig14.1:21.1.verse: Cast out like sparks from fiery coals,

thig14.1:21.2.verse: it’s worth no more than a bowl of poison.

thig14.1:21.3.verse: I don’t even see what kind it could be,

thig14.1:21.4.verse: it’s been smashed root and all by the path.

thig14.1:22.1.verse: Well may you try to seduce the type of lady

thig14.1:22.2.verse: who has not reflected on these things,

thig14.1:22.3.verse: or who has never attended the Teacher:

thig14.1:22.4.verse: but this is a lady who knows—now you’re in trouble!

thig14.1:23.1.verse: No matter if I am reviled or praised,

thig14.1:23.2.verse: or feel pleasure or pain: I stay mindful.

thig14.1:24.1.verse: I am a disciple of the Holy One,

thig14.1:24.2.verse: riding in the carriage of the eightfold path.

thig14.1:24.3.verse: The dart pulled out, free of defilements,

thig14.1:24.4.verse: I’m happy to have reached an empty place.

thig14.1:25.4.verse: and made to dance in many ways.

thig14.1:26.1.verse: But when the sticks and strings are taken off—

thig14.1:26.4.verse: on what could the mind be fixed?

thig14.1:27.1.verse: That’s what my body is really like,

thig14.1:27.2.verse: without those things it can’t go on.

thig14.1:27.4.verse: on what could the mind be fixed?

thig14.1:28.1.verse: It’s like when you saw a mural made

thig14.1:28.2.verse: by painting yellow orpiment on a wall,

thig14.1:28.3.verse: and your vision was deceived by that—

thig14.1:29.1.verse: Like an illusion cast before you,

thig14.1:29.2.verse: or a golden tree in a dream,

thig14.1:29.3.verse: you chase what is hollow, blind one,

thig14.1:29.4.verse: like a painted doll among the people.

thig14.1:30.1.verse: Like a ball in a socket,

thig14.1:30.2.verse: with a pupil in the middle, and tears,

thig14.1:30.3.verse: and mucus comes from there as well,

thig14.1:31.1.verse: Having plucked it out, the fair-eyed lady

thig14.1:31.4.verse: she said, and gave it to the man right then.

thig14.1:32.1.verse: And right then he lost his lust,

thig14.1:32.3.verse: “May you be well, O chaste and holy lady;

thig14.1:32.4.verse: such a thing will not happen again.

thig14.1:33.1.verse: Attacking a person such as this

thig14.1:33.2.verse: is like holding on to a blazing fire,

thig14.1:33.4.verse: May you be well, please forgive me.”

thig14.1:34.2.verse: she went to the presence of the excellent Buddha.

thig14.1:34.3.verse: Seeing the one with excellent marks of merit,

thig14.1:34.4.verse: her eye became just as it was before.

thig15.1:1.1.verse: In a town with the name of a flower,

thig15.1:1.2.verse: Pāṭaliputta, the blest place on earth,

thig15.1:2.1.verse: The first one is Isidāsī, the second Bodhī,

thig15.1:3.2.verse: eating their meal, and washing their bowls,

thig15.1:3.3.verse: when they were comfortably seated alone,

thig15.1:4.2.verse: and has not aged one single bit.

thig15.1:4.3.verse: What fault did you see in the world

thig15.1:4.4.verse: that made you intent upon renunciation?”

thig15.1:5.1.verse: When she was asked this question in confidence,

thig15.1:5.2.verse: the one skilled in teaching Dhamma,

thig15.1:5.4.verse: “Bodhi, listen to the story of my going forth.

thig15.1:6.1.verse: In the excellent town of Ujjeniyā,

thig15.1:6.2.verse: my father was a wealthy merchant with morality and restraint.

thig15.1:6.3.verse: I was the only daughter of his,

thig15.1:7.1.verse: Then men from the most notable families came to Sāketa

thig15.1:7.2.verse: to ask for me to marry them.

thig15.1:7.3.verse: A wealthy merchant with many jewels,

thig15.1:7.4.verse: my father gave me as a daughter-in-law to one of them.

thig15.1:8.2.verse: I bowed to both parents in-law,

thig15.1:8.4.verse: with my head at their feet.

thig15.1:9.1.verse: If I saw any of these honorable people

thig15.1:9.4.verse: I would anxiously give them a seat.

thig15.1:10.4.verse: and gave to them whatever was proper.

thig15.1:11.1.verse: I would get ready at the right time,

thig15.1:11.3.verse: and after rinsing my hands and feet,

thig15.1:11.4.verse: I would draw near my husband in añjali.

thig15.1:12.4.verse: I would beautify my own husband.

thig15.1:13.3.verse: like a mother with her only son,

thig15.1:13.4.verse: in the same way I looked after my husband.

thig15.1:14.1.verse: Thus in this way I offered service,

thig15.1:14.2.verse: a faithful servant free of pride,

thig15.1:14.4.verse: yet the husband was angry at me.

thig15.1:15.3.verse: I will not stay with Isidāsī,

thig15.1:16.4.verse: why does she displease you, son?’

thig15.1:17.1.verse: ‘She does not cause me any harm,

thig15.1:17.2.verse: but I will not stay here with Isidāsī.

thig15.1:17.3.verse: I just detest her, and I’ve had enough!

thig15.1:19.1.verse: ‘But I have not done anything wrong in any way!

thig15.1:19.2.verse: I caused no harm, I did not speak improperly!

thig15.1:20.1.verse: They led me back to my father’s house,

thig15.1:20.4.verse: we have lost the good fortune of having this beautiful woman.’

thig15.1:21.1.verse: Then my father gave me to another man

thig15.1:21.4.verse: for half the dowry of the previous one.

thig15.1:22.1.verse: I lived in his house for a month,

thig15.1:22.2.verse: I waited on him like a slave,

thig15.1:23.1.verse: My father then saw a man going about for alms -

thig15.1:23.2.verse: a tamed man who tames others - and said:

thig15.1:23.3.verse: ‘You, sage, will be my daughter’s husband:

thig15.1:23.4.verse: put down the rags and begging-bowl!’

thig15.1:24.2.verse: he told my father: ‘Give me back my rags,

thig15.1:24.4.verse: I will resume going for alms.’

thig15.1:25.2.verse: and all of my relatives, asked him:

thig15.1:25.3.verse: ‘What was not done for you here?

thig15.1:25.4.verse: Speak, and it will be quickly done for you!’

thig15.1:26.1.verse: When this was said he replied:

thig15.1:26.2.verse: ‘Enough! I am able to look after myself.

thig15.1:26.3.verse: I will not stay with Isidāsī,

thig15.1:27.3.verse: ‘After asking for permission, I will leave,

thig15.1:27.4.verse: and either die or go forth.’

thig15.1:28.3.verse: She was of my father’s clan, upholder of the vinaya,

thig15.1:29.2.verse: I got up and prepared a seat for her.

thig15.1:29.3.verse: I sat down at her feet,

thig15.1:31.2.verse: ‘My little child, go and practice the Dhamma right here!

thig15.1:31.4.verse: you will satiate contemplatives and twice-born brahmins.’

thig15.1:32.1.verse: In tears, I said to my father,

thig15.1:32.2.verse: with my hands raised in añjali:

thig15.1:32.3.verse: ‘Evil deeds were done by me in the past,

thig15.1:32.4.verse: I will grind down that karma.’

thig15.1:33.1.verse: Then my father said to me:

thig15.1:33.4.verse: which was realized by the foremost human.’

thig15.1:34.1.verse: I paid respects to mother and father,

thig15.1:35.1.verse: I know my previous seven lives,

thig15.1:35.2.verse: which this current birth is its fruit and result.

thig15.1:35.4.verse: and I will explain it to you.

thig15.1:36.1.verse: In a town in marshy lands,

thig15.1:36.2.verse: I was a goldsmith with abundant wealth.

thig15.1:36.4.verse: I had an affair with another’s wife.

thig15.1:37.1.verse: When I fell away from there,

thig15.1:37.2.verse: I was tormented in hell for a long time.

thig15.1:37.4.verse: I entered the belly of a female monkey.

thig15.1:38.1.verse: A week after I had been born,

thig15.1:38.2.verse: the leader of the monkeys castrated me.

thig15.1:38.3.verse: That is the fruit of my karma,

thig15.1:38.4.verse: because I went with another’s wife.

thig15.1:39.1.verse: When I fell away from there,

thig15.1:39.2.verse: after my death in the Sindhava forest,

thig15.1:40.2.verse: castrated, I carried children on my back.

thig15.1:40.3.verse: I was feeble, and full of worms,

thig15.1:40.4.verse: because I went with another’s wife.

thig15.1:41.1.verse: When I fell away from there,

thig15.1:41.2.verse: I was born as a cow owned by a cattle-merchant.

thig15.1:41.4.verse: I was castrated after twelve months.

thig15.1:42.4.verse: because I went with another’s wife.

thig15.1:43.1.verse: When I fell away from there,

thig15.1:43.2.verse: I was born as a man from a street-slave,

thig15.1:43.4.verse: because I went with another’s wife.

thig15.1:44.1.verse: Dead by the age of thirty,

thig15.1:44.2.verse: I was born as a girl in a family of cart-makers,

thig15.1:45.2.verse: in order to increase his already abundant wealth,

thig15.1:45.4.verse: as I was dragged away wailing.

thig15.1:46.1.verse: When he saw that I was sixteen years old,

thig15.1:46.3.verse: I was taken by his son,

thig15.1:48.1.verse: That is the fruit of my karma:

thig15.1:48.2.verse: they cast me off and left,

thig15.1:48.3.verse: setting me up as a slave.

thig15.1:48.4.verse: But I have now brought this to an end.”

thig15.1:50.1.verse: The Chapter of the Forties is finished.

thig15.1:1.1.verse: In Pāṭaliputta, the cream of the world,

thig15.1:1.2.verse: the city named for a flower,

thig15.1:1.3.verse: there were two nuns from the Sakyan clan,

thig15.1:1.4.verse: both of them ladies of quality.

thig15.1:2.1.verse: One was named Isidāsī, the second Bodhī.

thig15.1:2.2.verse: They both were accomplished in ethics,

thig15.1:3.1.verse: They wandered for alms and had their meal.

thig15.1:3.2.verse: When they had washed their bowls,

thig15.1:3.3.verse: they sat happily in a private place

thig15.1:4.2.verse: your youth has not yet faded.

thig15.1:4.3.verse: What problem did you see that made you

thig15.1:5.1.verse: Being pressed like this in private,

thig15.1:6.1.verse: In the fine town of Ujjenī,

thig15.1:6.2.verse: my father was a financier, a good and moral man.

thig15.1:7.1.verse: Then some suitors came for me

thig15.1:7.2.verse: from the top family of Sāketa.

thig15.1:7.3.verse: They were sent by a financier abounding in wealth,

thig15.1:7.4.verse: to whom my father then gave me as daughter-in-law.

thig15.1:8.2.verse: I bowed with my head to the feet

thig15.1:8.4.verse: just as I had been told.

thig15.1:9.1.verse: Whenever I saw my husband’s sisters,

thig15.1:9.3.verse: or even he, my one and only,

thig15.1:9.4.verse: I nervously gave them a seat.

thig15.1:10.2.verse: treats, or whatever was in the cupboard—

thig15.1:10.3.verse: I brought out and offered to them,

thig15.1:10.4.verse: ensuring each got what was fitting.

thig15.1:11.4.verse: and went to my husband with cupped palms.

thig15.1:12.3.verse: I myself did the makeup for my husband,

thig15.1:12.4.verse: as if I were his beautician.

thig15.1:13.4.verse: like a mother her only child.

thig15.1:14.1.verse: Thus I showed my devotion to him,

thig15.1:14.2.verse: a loyal, virtuous, and humble servant,

thig15.1:14.3.verse: getting up early, and working tirelessly:

thig15.1:14.4.verse: yet still my husband did me wrong.

thig15.1:15.1.verse: He said to his mother and father:

thig15.1:15.3.verse: I can’t stand to live together with Isidāsī

thig15.1:16.3.verse: she gets up early and works tirelessly,

thig15.1:16.4.verse: son, why doesn’t she please you?’

thig15.1:17.1.verse: ‘She hasn’t done anything to hurt me,

thig15.1:17.2.verse: but I just can’t stand to live with her.

thig15.1:17.3.verse: As far as I’m concerned, she’s just detestable.

thig15.1:17.4.verse: I’ve had enough, I’ll take my leave and go.’

thig15.1:18.2.verse: my father-in-law and mother-in-law asked me:

thig15.1:19.2.verse: I haven’t hurt him, or said anything bad.

thig15.1:19.4.verse: when my husband finds me so hateful?’

thig15.1:20.1.verse: They led me back to my father’s home,

thig15.1:20.2.verse: distraught, overcome with suffering, and said:

thig15.1:20.4.verse: we’ve lost her, so lovely and lucky!’

thig15.1:21.1.verse: Next my dad gave me to the household

thig15.1:21.3.verse: For this he got half the bride-price

thig15.1:21.4.verse: of that which the financier paid.

thig15.1:22.1.verse: In his house I also lived a month,

thig15.1:22.2.verse: before he too wanted me gone;

thig15.1:22.3.verse: though I served him like a slave,

thig15.1:23.1.verse: My father then spoke to a beggar for alms,

thig15.1:23.2.verse: a tamer of others and of himself:

thig15.1:23.4.verse: set aside your tonsure-cloth and pot.’

thig15.1:24.1.verse: He stayed a fortnight before he said to my dad:

thig15.1:25.1.verse: So then my mum and my dad

thig15.1:25.2.verse: and my whole group of relatives said:

thig15.1:25.3.verse: ‘What has not been done for you here?

thig15.1:25.4.verse: Quickly, tell us what we can do for you!’

thig15.1:26.1.verse: When they spoke to him like this he said,

thig15.1:26.2.verse: ‘If I can make do for myself, that is enough.

thig15.1:26.3.verse: I can’t stand to live together with Isidāsī

thig15.1:27.2.verse: But I sat all alone contemplating:

thig15.1:27.4.verse: either to die or to go forth.’

thig15.1:28.3.verse: who had memorized the monastic law,

thig15.1:28.4.verse: came resorting to my dad’s house for alms.

thig15.1:29.2.verse: I rose from my seat and prepared it for her.

thig15.1:29.3.verse: When she had taken her seat,

thig15.1:29.4.verse: I honored her feet and offered her a meal,

thig15.1:30.1.verse: satiating her with food and drink,

thig15.1:30.2.verse: treats, or whatever was in the cupboard.

thig15.1:31.1.verse: But my dad said to me:

thig15.1:32.1.verse: Then I said to my dad,

thig15.1:32.2.verse: crying, my cupped palms raised to him:

thig15.1:32.3.verse: ‘I’ve done bad things in the past;

thig15.1:32.4.verse: I shall wear that bad deed away.’

thig15.1:33.1.verse: And my dad said to me:

thig15.1:33.2.verse: ‘May you attain awakening, the highest state,

thig15.1:33.3.verse: and may you find the extinguishment

thig15.1:33.4.verse: that was realized by the best of men!’

thig15.1:34.1.verse: I bowed down to my mother and father,

thig15.1:34.2.verse: and my whole group of relatives;

thig15.1:34.3.verse: and then, seven days after going forth,

thig15.1:35.1.verse: I know my last seven lives;

thig15.1:35.2.verse: I shall relate to you the deeds

thig15.1:35.3.verse: of which this life is the fruit and result:

thig15.1:35.4.verse: focus your whole mind on that.

thig15.1:36.2.verse: I was a goldsmith with lots of money.

thig15.1:36.3.verse: Drunk on the pride of youth,

thig15.1:36.4.verse: I had sex with someone else’s wife.

thig15.1:37.2.verse: I burned in hell for a long time.

thig15.1:37.4.verse: I was conceived in a monkey’s womb.

thig15.1:38.1.verse: When I was only seven days old,

thig15.1:38.2.verse: I was castrated by the monkey chief.

thig15.1:38.3.verse: This was the fruit of that deed,

thig15.1:38.4.verse: because of adultery with another’s wife.

thig15.1:39.3.verse: I was conceived in the womb

thig15.1:40.1.verse: I carried children on my back for twelve years,

thig15.1:40.2.verse: and all the while I was castrated,

thig15.1:40.4.verse: because of adultery with another’s wife.

thig15.1:41.2.verse: I was reborn in a cow

thig15.1:41.4.verse: A red calf, castrated, for twelve months

thig15.1:42.4.verse: because of adultery with another’s wife.

thig15.1:43.2.verse: I was born of a slave in the street,

thig15.1:43.3.verse: with neither male nor female parts,

thig15.1:43.4.verse: because of adultery with another’s wife.

thig15.1:44.1.verse: I died at thirty years of age,

thig15.1:44.2.verse: and was reborn as a girl in a carter’s family.

thig15.1:44.3.verse: We were poor, of little wealth,

thig15.1:45.1.verse: Because of the massive interest we owed,

thig15.1:45.3.verse: taken by force from the family home

thig15.1:46.1.verse: When I was sixteen years old,

thig15.1:46.2.verse: seeing I was a girl of marriageable age,

thig15.1:46.3.verse: his son confined me as his wife—

thig15.1:47.2.verse: a virtuous and well-known lady of quality,

thig15.1:47.4.verse: yet I stirred up resentment in her.

thig15.1:48.1.verse: As the fruit of that deed,

thig15.1:48.3.verse: though I served them like a slave.

thig15.1:48.4.verse: Now I’ve made an end to this as well.”

thig16.1:4.4.verse: where they experience injury and pain.

thig16.1:5.1.verse: Those who have done evil deeds feel sorrow

thig16.1:5.2.verse: in their state of downfall, where they constantly do even more evil.

thig16.1:6.2.verse: not intending to stop the arising of suffering,

thig16.1:6.4.verse: such fools do not recognize the Noble Truths.

thig16.1:7.1.verse: Mother, most people do not understand

thig16.1:7.2.verse: the truths superbly taught by the Buddha.

thig16.1:7.3.verse: They are delighted with states of existence,

thig16.1:7.4.verse: they long for rebirth as Devas.

thig16.1:8.2.verse: is a finite and temporary state of existence.

thig16.1:8.4.verse: of being born again and again.

thig16.1:9.1.verse: From the four places of downfall,

thig16.1:9.2.verse: it is hard to obtain the two higher destinations.

thig16.1:9.3.verse: For one gone to a place of downfall,

thig16.1:9.4.verse: there is no going forth in the hell realms.

thig16.1:10.1.verse: The two of you should allow me

thig16.1:10.2.verse: to go forth in the doctrine of the one who has ten powers.

thig16.1:10.3.verse: Living at ease, I would be able to strive

thig16.1:10.4.verse: for the abandoning of birth and death.

thig16.1:11.1.verse: How can there be delight in a state of existence

thig16.1:11.2.verse: with a worthless body devoid of substance?

thig16.1:11.4.verse: so that I may bring an end to the craving for existence.

thig16.1:12.1.verse: One who is distant from the arising of the Buddhas

thig16.1:12.3.verse: I will not spoil the virtues of the spiritual life,

thig16.1:12.4.verse: for the rest of my life.”

thig16.1:13.1.verse: Then Sumedhā said to her parents:

thig16.1:13.4.verse: I will be overtaken by death.”

thig16.1:14.1.verse: Distressed, her mother and father cry,

thig16.1:14.3.verse: Together they try to convince her,

thig16.1:14.4.verse: while she is lying on the floor of the palace.

thig16.1:15.1.verse: “Rise up little child, what is this sadness?

thig16.1:15.2.verse: You are engaged to be married in Vāraṇavatī.

thig16.1:15.4.verse: and you have been given to him.

thig16.1:16.4.verse: life as an outcast— these are difficult to do, little child.

thig16.1:17.1.verse: As a queen you will have authority, wealth, sovereignty,

thig16.1:17.3.verse: You are a young lady, enjoy sensual pleasures!

thig16.1:18.2.verse: “Who would want such a worthless state of existence?

thig16.1:18.4.verse: or I will die, but I will not marry.

thig16.1:19.1.verse: What is this impure putrid body,

thig16.1:19.2.verse: a dreadful corpse with a tainted smell?

thig16.1:19.4.verse: this oozing skin-bag full of impurities?

thig16.1:20.1.verse: What do they know about this

thig16.1:20.2.verse: disgusting thing plastered in flesh and blood,

thig16.1:20.3.verse: a corpse which will be given as food

thig16.1:21.1.verse: Before long it will be taken to the cemetery,

thig16.1:21.3.verse: left there like a discarded log,

thig16.1:22.3.verse: Even one's own mother and father are disgusted and go bathe themselves—

thig16.1:22.4.verse: what can be expected from everyone else?

thig16.1:23.1.verse: Hanging on to this worthless corpse,

thig16.1:24.3.verse: would not be able to endure its smell—

thig16.1:24.4.verse: even their own mother would be disgusted.

thig16.1:25.1.verse: The khandhas, elements, and sense domains,

thig16.1:25.2.verse: are conditioned, rooted in birth, suffering.

thig16.1:25.4.verse: why would I wish to marry?

thig16.1:26.1.verse: If, day after day three hundred spears

thig16.1:26.3.verse: a hundred years of this torment

thig16.1:26.4.verse: would be good if then there was the end of suffering.

thig16.1:27.1.verse: I would consent to this torment,

thig16.1:27.2.verse: as would anyone who has heard the Teacher’s words:

thig16.1:27.3.verse: ‘Long is the cycle of birth and death

thig16.1:27.4.verse: for those who are slain again and again.’

thig16.1:28.3.verse: among petas and in the hell realms,

thig16.1:28.4.verse: no limit to torment is seen.

thig16.1:29.1.verse: There is much torment in the hell realms,

thig16.1:29.2.verse: for those who are oppressed in the lower realms.

thig16.1:29.3.verse: Even among the Devas there is no safety,

thig16.1:29.4.verse: and no happiness higher than Nirvana.

thig16.1:30.2.verse: committed to the words of the one who has ten powers;

thig16.1:31.1.verse: Today, father, I will leave behind

thig16.1:31.3.verse: I am disenchanted with sensual pleasures,

thig16.1:31.4.verse: I am at peace because I have renounced sensuality; it has been made like a palm-stump.”

thig16.1:32.1.verse: As she said this to her father,

thig16.1:32.2.verse: Anīkaratta, to whom she had been engaged to be married,

thig16.1:32.4.verse: at the time arranged for the wedding.

thig16.1:33.1.verse: Then Sumedhā cut off her thick, soft, dark hair

thig16.1:34.2.verse: when Anīkaratta came to the town.

thig16.1:34.4.verse: cultivated well the perception of impermanence.

thig16.1:35.1.verse: As she fixed the mind intently on this,

thig16.1:35.3.verse: With limbs adorned with gold and gems,

thig16.1:36.1.verse: “As a queen there is authority, wealth, sovereignty,

thig16.1:36.3.verse: You are a young lady, enjoy sensual pleasures!

thig16.1:36.4.verse: Sensual pleasures are difficult to obtain in this world!

thig16.1:37.1.verse: Royalty has been handed over to you:

thig16.1:37.4.verse: your mother and father are suffering.”

thig16.1:38.1.verse: Sumedhā, who had no need for sensual pleasures

thig16.1:38.2.verse: and was free of delusion, said to him:

thig16.1:38.4.verse: Look at the drawbacks of sensual pleasures!

thig16.1:39.2.verse: embraced the path of enjoying sensuality.

thig16.1:40.1.verse: Even if the seven kinds of gems were to pour down from the sky

thig16.1:40.2.verse: like rain in all ten directions,

thig16.1:40.3.verse: not even then would there be satisfaction in sensual pleasures:

thig16.1:41.1.verse: Sensual pleasures are like a knife on a butcher’s block,

thig16.1:41.2.verse: sensual pleasures are like a snake’s head.

thig16.1:42.4.verse: the root of calamity, resulting in suffering.

thig16.1:43.2.verse: like a piece of meat, they are suffering;

thig16.1:43.3.verse: Sensual pleasures are deceitful as a dream,

thig16.1:44.1.verse: Sensual pleasures are like the stake of a spear,

thig16.1:44.2.verse: a disease, an abscess, a calamity, an affliction.

thig16.1:44.4.verse: the root of calamity, fear, and distruction.

thig16.1:45.1.verse: In this way sensual pleasures have been declared to bring much suffering,

thig16.1:45.3.verse: Go, not to me, but to the Buddha!

thig16.1:45.4.verse: My own confidence is in him.

thig16.1:46.1.verse: What can another do for me,

thig16.1:46.2.verse: when their own head is on fire?

thig16.1:46.3.verse: When one is bound by birth and death,

thig16.1:46.4.verse: one should strive for its end.”

thig16.1:47.2.verse: and saw mother, father, and Anīkaratta

thig16.1:47.3.verse: sitting down on the ground crying,

thig16.1:48.1.verse: “Long is the cycle of birth and death for fools,

thig16.1:48.3.verse: without beginning or end for the death of the father,

thig16.1:48.4.verse: the death of the brother, and one’s own death.

thig16.1:49.2.verse: you move along in the cycle of birth and death without beginning or end.

thig16.1:49.3.verse: Bear in mind the pile of bones

thig16.1:49.4.verse: of all these sentient beings going through one life after the other.

thig16.1:50.1.verse: Bear in mind that all the tears, mother milk, and blood

thig16.1:50.3.verse: Bear in mind the pile of bones of one world cycle,

thig16.1:51.1.verse: Saṃsaric existence is without beginning or end,

thig16.1:51.2.verse: as vast as the land of Jampudīpa.

thig16.1:51.3.verse: Even if the earth was made into little balls the size of a jujube seed,

thig16.1:51.4.verse: it still would not add up to all the mothers among mothers.

thig16.1:52.1.verse: Bear in mind all the grass, wood, branches, and foliage,

thig16.1:52.3.verse: Even if they were made into twigs each only the size of four fingers,

thig16.1:52.4.verse: they would still not add up to all of fathers among fathers.

thig16.1:53.1.verse: Bear in mind the one-eyed turtle in the eastern sea,

thig16.1:53.2.verse: and, far away, a block of wood with a hole in it;

thig16.1:53.3.verse: the chance of gaining a human rebirth

thig16.1:53.4.verse: is like the chance of putting one’s head through that hole.

thig16.1:54.1.verse: Bear in mind the form of this miserable body,

thig16.1:54.2.verse: without any substance, like a lump of foam.

thig16.1:54.4.verse: bear in mind that there is much agony in hell.

thig16.1:55.1.verse: Bear in mind those filling up the cemetery,

thig16.1:55.2.verse: again and again, in all those lives.

thig16.1:55.3.verse: Bear in mind the danger of crocodiles,

thig16.1:55.4.verse: and bear in mind the four truths.

thig16.1:56.2.verse: why would you indulge in the five bitter drinks?

thig16.1:56.3.verse: For all delight in sensual pleasures,

thig16.1:56.4.verse: is more bitter than the five bitter drinks.

thig16.1:57.2.verse: why would you set yourself on fire with sensual pleasures?

thig16.1:57.3.verse: For all delight in sensual pleasures

thig16.1:58.1.verse: When one can be without enmity,

thig16.1:58.2.verse: why would you want the many enemies that come with sensual pleasures?

thig16.1:58.3.verse: Like rulers, fires, thieves, and other unpleasant things,

thig16.1:58.4.verse: sensual pleasures are common and bring many enemies.

thig16.1:59.2.verse: why would you want the imprisonment of sensual pleasures?

thig16.1:59.4.verse: and result in the suffering of imprisonment.

thig16.1:60.2.verse: burns one who holds it and does not let it go,

thig16.1:60.3.verse: sensual pleasures are like a torch:

thig16.1:60.4.verse: they burn the one who does not let go of them.

thig16.1:61.2.verse: for the sake of the minute happiness of sensual pleasure.

thig16.1:61.3.verse: Do not be like the fish who swallows the hook,

thig16.1:62.1.verse: One should willingly train oneself in regards to sensual pleasures.

thig16.1:62.2.verse: You are like a dog bound by a chain:

thig16.1:62.4.verse: like hungry savages would a dog.

thig16.1:63.4.verse: Give up these unstable sensual pleasures!

thig16.1:64.2.verse: why would you want sensual pleasures, which are subject to decay?

thig16.1:64.3.verse: All rebirths in all places are

thig16.1:65.1.verse: This is non-decay, this is non-death,

thig16.1:65.2.verse: this is non-decay and non-death, the path of sorrowlessness.

thig16.1:66.2.verse: the deathless state even today can be obtained in this way:

thig16.1:66.3.verse: it is possible by whomever wisely commits themselves,

thig16.1:67.2.verse: without desire for any conditioned things.

thig16.1:67.4.verse: Sumedhā threw her hair on the ground.

thig16.1:68.2.verse: with hands in añjali, implored her father:

thig16.1:68.4.verse: to go forth for liberation and seeking truth.”

thig16.1:69.2.verse: she went forth, leaving behind fear and sorrow.

thig16.1:69.3.verse: She realized the six special knowledges,

thig16.1:69.4.verse: the highest fruit for one who is training.

thig16.1:70.2.verse: was the Nirvana of the princess.

thig16.1:70.3.verse: This is a story of some of her past lives

thig16.1:70.4.verse: that was explained near the end of her life:

thig16.1:71.2.verse: in a new settlement in the Saṅgha’s park,

thig16.1:71.4.verse: gave the gift of a monastic dwelling.

thig16.1:72.3.verse: I was born as a Deva,

thig16.1:73.1.verse: When we were amongst the devas we had great psychic power,

thig16.1:73.3.verse: I was a queen of seven jewels,

thig16.1:74.1.verse: This is the cause, the origin,

thig16.1:74.2.verse: and root of my acceptance of the teachings.

thig16.1:75.1.verse: This is how they act, those who have faith

thig16.1:75.2.verse: in the words of superior wisdom.

thig16.1:75.3.verse: They are disenchanted with states of existence,

thig16.1:75.4.verse: and after becoming disenchanted, they become dispassionate.”

thig16.1:76.1.verse: Thus Sumedhā the Elder spoke these verses.

thig16.1:77.5.verse: The Verses of the Elder Bhikkhunīs are finished.

thig16.1:1.2.verse: the daughter of King Koñca’s chief queen,

thig16.1:2.1.verse: She was virtuous, a brilliant speaker,

thig16.1:2.2.verse: learned, and trained in the Buddha’s instructions.

thig16.1:2.3.verse: She went up to her mother and father and said:

thig16.1:3.2.verse: No state of life is eternal, not even that of the gods;

thig16.1:3.3.verse: what then of sensual pleasures, so hollow,

thig16.1:3.4.verse: offering little gratification and much distress.

thig16.1:4.1.verse: Sensual pleasures are bitter as the venom of a snake,

thig16.1:4.2.verse: yet fools are infatuated by them.

thig16.1:4.3.verse: Sent to hell for a very long time,

thig16.1:5.2.verse: ever lament in the underworld due to their own bad deeds.

thig16.1:6.2.verse: trapped by the origin of suffering,

thig16.1:6.3.verse: are ignorant, not understanding the noble truths

thig16.1:7.1.verse: Most people, mum, ignorant of the truths

thig16.1:7.3.verse: look forward to a state of life,

thig16.1:7.4.verse: longing for rebirth among the gods.

thig16.1:8.1.verse: Yet even rebirth among the gods

thig16.1:8.2.verse: in an impermanent state of life is not eternal.

thig16.1:8.4.verse: of being reborn time and again.

thig16.1:9.1.verse: Four lower realms and two other realms

thig16.1:9.2.verse: may be gained somehow or other.

thig16.1:9.3.verse: But for those who end up in a lower realm,

thig16.1:9.4.verse: there is no way to go forth in the hells.

thig16.1:10.1.verse: May you both grant me permission to go forth

thig16.1:10.2.verse: in the dispensation of him of the ten powers.

thig16.1:10.3.verse: Living at ease, I shall apply myself

thig16.1:10.4.verse: to giving up rebirth and death.

thig16.1:11.1.verse: Why look forward to a new state of life

thig16.1:11.3.verse: Grant me permission, I shall go forth

thig16.1:11.4.verse: to make an end of craving for a new life.

thig16.1:12.1.verse: A Buddha has arisen, the time has come,

thig16.1:12.3.verse: As long as I live I’ll never betray

thig16.1:12.4.verse: my ethical precepts or my chaste path.”

thig16.1:13.1.verse: Then Sumedhā said to her parents:

thig16.1:13.2.verse: “So long as I remain a layperson,

thig16.1:13.3.verse: I’ll refuse to eat any food,

thig16.1:13.4.verse: until I’ve fallen under the sway of death.”

thig16.1:14.1.verse: Upset, her mother burst into tears,

thig16.1:14.3.verse: tried his best to persuade her

thig16.1:14.4.verse: as she lay collapsed upstairs in the longhouse.

thig16.1:15.1.verse: “Get up child, why do you grieve so?

thig16.1:15.2.verse: You’re already betrothed to be married!

thig16.1:15.4.verse: is in Vāraṇavatī: he is your betrothed.

thig16.1:16.1.verse: You shall be the chief queen,

thig16.1:16.4.verse: going forth is hard to do, my child.

thig16.1:17.1.verse: As a royal there is command, wealth, authority,

thig16.1:17.3.verse: Enjoy sensual pleasures while you’re still young!

thig16.1:17.4.verse: Let your wedding take place, my child!”

thig16.1:18.2.verse: “Let this not come to pass! Existence is hollow!

thig16.1:18.3.verse: I shall either go forth or die,

thig16.1:19.1.verse: Why cling to this rotting body so foul,

thig16.1:20.1.verse: Knowing it like I do, what’s the point?

thig16.1:20.2.verse: A carcass is vile, smeared with flesh and blood,

thig16.1:20.3.verse: food for birds and swarms of worms—

thig16.1:20.4.verse: why have we been given it?

thig16.1:21.1.verse: Before long the body, bereft of consciousness,

thig16.1:21.2.verse: is carried out to the charnel ground,

thig16.1:21.3.verse: to be discarded like an old log

thig16.1:22.1.verse: When they’ve discarded it in the charnel ground,

thig16.1:22.2.verse: to be eaten by others, your own parents

thig16.1:22.4.verse: what then of people at large?

thig16.1:23.1.verse: They’re attached to this hollow carcass,

thig16.1:23.2.verse: this mass of sinews and bone;

thig16.1:23.4.verse: full of saliva, tears, feces, and pus.

thig16.1:24.1.verse: If anyone were to dissect it,

thig16.1:24.4.verse: would disgust even their own mother.

thig16.1:25.2.verse: the aggregates, elements, and sense fields

thig16.1:25.3.verse: as conditioned, rooted in birth, suffering—

thig16.1:25.4.verse: why would I wish for marriage?

thig16.1:26.3.verse: Even if the slaughter lasted a hundred years

thig16.1:26.4.verse: it’d be worth it if it led to the end of suffering.

thig16.1:27.1.verse: One who understands the Teacher’s words

thig16.1:27.2.verse: would put up with this slaughter:

thig16.1:27.4.verse: being killed time and time again.’

thig16.1:28.2.verse: in the realm of animals or that of titans,

thig16.1:28.3.verse: among the ghosts or in the hells,

thig16.1:29.1.verse: The hells are full of killing,

thig16.1:29.2.verse: for the corrupt who have fallen to the underworld.

thig16.1:29.3.verse: Even among the gods there is no shelter,

thig16.1:30.1.verse: Those who are committed to the dispensation

thig16.1:30.2.verse: of him of the ten powers attain extinguishment.

thig16.1:30.3.verse: Living at ease, they apply themselves

thig16.1:30.4.verse: to giving up rebirth and death.

thig16.1:31.1.verse: On this very day, dad, I shall renounce:

thig16.1:31.2.verse: what’s to enjoy in hollow riches?

thig16.1:31.4.verse: they’re like vomit, made like a palm stump.”
