mn24:15.1.verse: ‘So too, friend, the purification of virtue has the purification of mind as its goal; the purification of mind has the purification of view as its goal; the purification of view has the purification by overcoming doubt as its goal; the purification by overcoming doubt has the purification by knowledge and vision of what is and what is not the Path as its goal; the purification by knowledge and vision of what is and what is not the Path has the purification by knowledge and vision of the Way as its goal; the purification by knowledge and vision of the Way has the purification by knowledge and vision as its goal; the purification by knowledge and vision has Nibbāna through not clinging as its goal.

mn24:15.2.verse: It is for the goal of Nibbāna through not clinging that the life divine is lived under the Blessed One.’

mn24:16.1.verse: When this was said, the venerable Sāriputta asked the venerable Punna Mantāniputta:

mn24:16.2.verse: ‘What is the venerable one’s name, and how do his companions in the life divine know him?’

mn24:16.4.verse: and companions in the life divine know me as Mantāniputta.’

mn24:16.5.verse: ‘It is wonderful, friend, it is marvellous;

mn24:16.6.verse: each profound question has been answered point by point by the venerable Punna Mantāniputta as a learned disciple who knows the Master’s Teaching as it is.

mn24:16.7.verse: It is gain for his companions in the life divine, it is great gain for them,

mn24:16.8.verse: that they have the opportunity to see him and to honour him.

mn24:16.9.verse: And even if it were by carrying the venerable Punna Mantāniputta about on a cushion on their heads that his companions in the life divine might get the opportunity to see him and to honour him, it would be gain for them, great gain for them. And it is gain for us, great gain for us, that we have the opportunity of seeing the venerable Punna Mantāniputta and honouring him.’

mn24:17.1.verse: When this was said, the venerable Punna Mantāniputta asked the venerable Sāriputta:

mn24:17.2.verse: ‘What is the venerable one’s name, and how do his companions in the life divine know him?’

mn24:17.4.verse: and companions in the life divine know me as Sāriputta.’

mn24:17.5.verse: ‘Indeed, friend, we did not know that we were talking with the venerable Sāriputta, the disciple who is like the Master himself, saying:

mn24:17.7.verse: Had we known that it was the venerable Sāriputta, we should not have said so much.

mn24:17.8.verse: It is wonderful, friend, it is marvellous;

mn24:17.9.verse: each profound question has been put point by point by the venerable Sāriputta as a learned disciple who knows the Master’s Teaching as it is.

mn24:17.10.verse: It is gain for his companions in the life divine, it is great gain for them,

mn24:17.11.verse: that they have the opportunity to see him and to honour him.

mn24:17.12.verse: And even if it were by carrying the venerable Sāriputta about on a cushion on their heads that his companions in the life divine might get the opportunity to see him and to honour him, it would be gain for them, great gain for them. And it is gain for us, great gain for us, that we have the opportunity of seeing the venerable Sāriputta and honouring him.’

mn24:17.13.verse: Thus it was that these two great Nāgas agreed with each other’s good words,

mn24:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

mn24:2.1.verse: Then several mendicants who had completed the rainy season residence in their native land went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to them:

mn24:2.2.verse: “In your native land, mendicants, which of the native mendicants is esteemed in this way:

mn24:2.3.verse: ‘Personally having few wishes, they speak to the mendicants on having few wishes. Personally having contentment, seclusion, aloofness, energy, ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom, they speak to the mendicants on all these things. They’re an adviser and counselor, one who educates, encourages, fires up, and inspires their spiritual companions.’”

mn24:2.4.verse: “Puṇṇa son of Mantāṇī, sir, is esteemed in this way in our native land.”

mn24:3.1.verse: Now at that time Venerable Sāriputta was sitting not far from the Buddha.

mn24:3.3.verse: “Puṇṇa son of Mantāṇī is fortunate, so very fortunate,

mn24:3.4.verse: in that his sensible spiritual companions praise him point by point in the presence of the Teacher, and that the Teacher seconds that appreciation.

mn24:3.5.verse: Hopefully, some time or other I’ll get to meet Venerable Puṇṇa, and we can have a discussion.”

mn24:4.1.verse: When the Buddha had stayed in Rājagaha as long as he pleased, he set out for Sāvatthī.

mn24:4.2.verse: Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Sāvatthī,

mn24:4.3.verse: where he stayed in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn24:4.4.verse: Puṇṇa heard that the Buddha had arrived at Sāvatthī.

mn24:5.1.verse: Then he set his lodgings in order and, taking his bowl and robe, set out for Sāvatthī.

mn24:5.2.verse: Eventually he came to Sāvatthī and Jeta’s Grove. He went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side.

mn24:5.3.verse: The Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired him with a Dhamma talk.

mn24:5.4.verse: Then, having approved and agreed with what the Buddha said, Puṇṇa rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right. Then he went to the Dark Forest for the day’s meditation.

mn24:6.1.verse: Then a certain mendicant went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and said to him,

mn24:6.2.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, the mendicant named Puṇṇa, of whom you have often spoken so highly, after being inspired by a talk of the Buddha’s, left for the Dark Forest for the day’s meditation.”

mn24:7.1.verse: Sāriputta quickly grabbed his sitting cloth and followed behind Puṇṇa, keeping sight of his head.

mn24:7.2.verse: Puṇṇa plunged deep into the Dark Forest and sat at the root of a tree for the day’s meditation.

mn24:8.1.verse: Then in the late afternoon, Sāriputta came out of retreat, went to Puṇṇa, and exchanged greetings with him.

mn24:8.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Puṇṇa:

mn24:9.1.verse: “Reverend, is our spiritual life lived under the Buddha?”

mn24:9.3.verse: “Is the spiritual life lived under the Buddha for the sake of purification of ethics?”

mn24:9.5.verse: “Well, is the spiritual life lived under the Buddha for the sake of purification of mind?”

mn24:9.7.verse: “Is the spiritual life lived under the Buddha for the sake of purification of view?”

mn24:9.9.verse: “Well, is the spiritual life lived under the Buddha for the sake of purification by traversing doubt?”

mn24:9.11.verse: “Is the spiritual life lived under the Buddha for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path?”

mn24:9.13.verse: “Well, is the spiritual life lived under the Buddha for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision of the practice?”

mn24:9.15.verse: “Is the spiritual life lived under the Buddha for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision?”

mn24:10.1.verse: “When asked each of these questions, you answered, ‘Certainly not.’

mn24:10.8.verse: Then what exactly is the goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha?”

mn24:10.9.verse: “The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping.”

mn24:11.1.verse: “Reverend, is purification of ethics complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping?”

mn24:11.9.verse: purification of knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path …

mn24:11.11.verse: purification of knowledge and vision of the practice …

mn24:11.13.verse: Is purification of knowledge and vision complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping?”

mn24:11.15.verse: “Then is complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping something apart from these things?”

mn24:12.1.verse: “When asked each of these questions, you answered, ‘Certainly not.’

mn24:12.9.verse: How then should we see the meaning of this statement?”

mn24:13.1.verse: “If the Buddha had asserted purification of ethics to be complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping, he would have asserted that which grasps fuel to be complete extinguishment without grasping fuel.

mn24:13.2.verse: If the Buddha had asserted purification of mind …

mn24:13.5.verse: purification of knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path …

mn24:13.6.verse: purification of knowledge and vision of the practice …

mn24:13.7.verse: If the Buddha had asserted purification of knowledge and vision to be complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping, he would have asserted that which grasps fuel to be complete extinguishment without grasping fuel.

mn24:13.8.verse: But if complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping was something apart from these things, an ordinary person would become extinguished.

mn24:13.9.verse: For an ordinary person lacks these things.

mn24:14.1.verse: Well then, reverend, I shall give you a simile.

mn24:14.2.verse: For by means of a simile some sensible people understand the meaning of what is said.

mn24:14.3.verse: Suppose that, while staying in Sāvatthī, King Pasenadi of Kosala had some urgent business come up in Sāketa.

mn24:14.4.verse: Now, between Sāvatthī and Sāketa seven chariots were stationed at the ready for him.

mn24:14.5.verse: Then Pasenadi, exiting Sāvatthī, mounted the first chariot at the ready by the gate of the royal compound. The first chariot at the ready would bring him to the second, where he’d dismount and mount the second chariot.

mn24:14.6.verse: The second chariot at the ready would bring him to the third …

mn24:14.7.verse: The third chariot at the ready would bring him to the fourth …

mn24:14.8.verse: The fourth chariot at the ready would bring him to the fifth …

mn24:14.9.verse: The fifth chariot at the ready would bring him to the sixth …

mn24:14.10.verse: The sixth chariot at the ready would bring him to the seventh, where he’d dismount and mount the seventh chariot.

mn24:14.11.verse: The seventh chariot at the ready would bring him to the gate of the royal compound of Sāketa.

mn24:14.12.verse: And when he was at the gate, friends and colleagues, relatives and kin would ask him:

mn24:14.13.verse: ‘Great king, did you come to Sāketa from Sāvatthī by this chariot at the ready?’

mn24:14.14.verse: If asked this, how should King Pasenadi rightly reply?”

mn24:14.16.verse: ‘Well, while staying in Sāvatthī, I had some urgent business come up in Sāketa.

mn24:14.17.verse: Now, between Sāvatthī and Sāketa seven chariots were stationed at the ready for me.

mn24:14.18.verse: Then, exiting Sāvatthī, I mounted the first chariot at the ready by the gate of the royal compound.

mn24:14.19.verse: The first chariot at the ready brought me to the second, where I dismounted and mounted the second chariot. …

mn24:14.20.verse: The second chariot brought me to the third …

mn24:14.24.verse: The sixth chariot at the ready brought me to the seventh, where I dismounted and mounted the seventh chariot.

mn24:14.25.verse: The seventh chariot at the ready brought me to the gate of the royal compound of Sāketa.’

mn24:14.26.verse: That’s how King Pasenadi should rightly reply.”

mn24:15.1.verse: “In the same way, reverend, purification of ethics is only for the sake of purification of mind. Purification of mind is only for the sake of purification of view. Purification of view is only for the sake of purification by traversing doubt. Purification by traversing doubt is only for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path. Purification of knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path is only for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision of the practice. Purification of knowledge and vision of the practice is only for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision. Purification of knowledge and vision is only for the sake of extinguishment with no fuel for grasping.

mn24:15.2.verse: The spiritual life is lived under the Buddha for the sake of complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping.”

mn24:16.1.verse: When he said this, Sāriputta said to Puṇṇa,

mn24:16.2.verse: “What is the venerable’s name? And how are you known among your spiritual companions?”

mn24:16.4.verse: And I am known as ‘son of Mantāṇī’ among my spiritual companions.”

mn24:16.6.verse: Venerable Puṇṇa son of Mantāṇī has answered each deep question point by point, as a learned disciple who rightly understands the Teacher’s instructions.

mn24:16.7.verse: It is fortunate for his spiritual companions, so very fortunate,

mn24:16.8.verse: that they get to see Venerable Puṇṇa son of Mantāṇī and pay homage to him.

mn24:16.9.verse: Even if they only got to see him and pay respects to him by carrying him around on their heads on a roll of cloth, it would still be very fortunate for them! And it’s fortunate for me, so very fortunate, that I get to see the venerable and pay homage to him.”

mn24:17.1.verse: When he said this, Puṇṇa said to Sāriputta,

mn24:17.2.verse: “What is the venerable’s name? And how are you known among your spiritual companions?”

mn24:17.4.verse: And I am known as Sāriputta among my spiritual companions.”

mn24:17.5.verse: “Goodness! I had no idea I was consulting with the Venerable Sāriputta, the disciple who is fit to be compared with the Teacher himself!

mn24:17.7.verse: If I’d known, I would not have said so much.

mn24:17.9.verse: Venerable Sāriputta has asked each deep question point by point, as a learned disciple who rightly understands the Teacher’s instructions.

mn24:17.10.verse: It is fortunate for his spiritual companions, so very fortunate,

mn24:17.11.verse: that they get to see Venerable Sāriputta and pay homage to him.

mn24:17.12.verse: Even if they only got to see him and pay respects to him by carrying him around on their heads on a roll of cloth, it would still be very fortunate for them! And it’s fortunate for me, so very fortunate, that I get to see the venerable and pay homage to him.”

mn24:17.13.verse: And so these two spiritual giants agreed with each other’s fine words.

mn25:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn25:1.5.verse: “Yes, lord,” the monks responded to him.

mn25:2.1.verse: “The poison-grass sower doesn’t sow poison-grass for a herd of deer, (thinking,)

mn25:2.2.verse: ‘May the herd of deer, having enjoyed the poison-grass I have sown, be long-lived & handsome, and last for a long time.’

mn25:2.3.verse: Actually, the poison-grass sower sows poison grass for a herd of deer, (thinking,)

mn25:2.4.verse: ‘The herd of deer, venturing unwarily into the poison-grass I have sown, will eat food. Having eaten food after venturing unwarily, they will become intoxicated. Being intoxicated, they will become heedless. When they’ve become heedless, I can do with them as I like, on account of this poison-grass.’

mn25:3.1.verse: “Now, the first herd of deer, venturing unwarily into the poison-grass sown by the poison-grass sower, ate food. Having eaten food after venturing unwarily, they became intoxicated. Being intoxicated, they became heedless. When they became heedless, the poison-grass sower did with them as he liked, on account of that poison-grass.

mn25:3.2.verse: That, monks, is why that first herd of deer didn’t escape from the poison-grass sower’s power & control.

mn25:4.1.verse: “A second herd of deer reasoned thus:

mn25:4.2.verse: ‘That first herd of deer, venturing unwarily into the poison-grass sown by the poison-grass sower, ate food. Having eaten food after venturing unwarily, they became intoxicated. Being intoxicated, they became heedless. When they became heedless, the poison-grass sower did with them as he liked, on account of that poison-grass.

mn25:4.4.verse: That’s why that first herd of deer didn’t escape from the poison-grass sower’s power & control.

mn25:4.5.verse: What if we were to entirely avoid that poison-grass food, and—avoiding that dangerous enjoyment—were to dwell having plunged into a wilderness area?’

mn25:4.6.verse: “So, they entirely avoided that poison-grass food. Avoiding that dangerous enjoyment, they dwelled having plunged into a wilderness area.

mn25:4.7.verse: But in the last month of the hot season, when the grass & water were used up, their bodies became extremely gaunt.

mn25:4.8.verse: Their bodies having become extremely gaunt, they lost their strength & energy.

mn25:4.9.verse: Having lost their strength & energy, they returned to the poison-grass sown by the poison-grass sower.

mn25:4.10.verse: Venturing unwarily into the poison-grass sown by the poison-grass sower, they ate food.

mn25:4.11.verse: Having eaten food after venturing unwarily, they became intoxicated. Being intoxicated, they became heedless. When they became heedless, the poison-grass sower did with them as he liked, on account of that poison-grass.

mn25:4.12.verse: That, monks, is why that second herd of deer didn’t escape from the poison-grass sower’s power & control.

mn25:5.1.verse: “A third herd of deer reasoned thus:

mn25:5.2.verse: ‘That first herd of deer, venturing unwarily into the poison-grass sown by the poison-grass sower, ate food…

mn25:5.3.verse: …that’s why that first herd of deer didn’t escape from the poison-grass sower’s power & control.

mn25:5.4.verse: The second herd of deer reasoned thus:

mn25:5.5.verse: “That first herd of deer, venturing unwarily into the poison-grass sown by the poison-grass sower, ate food…

mn25:5.6.verse: …that’s why that first herd of deer didn’t escape from the poison-grass sower’s power & control.…

mn25:5.7.verse: What if we were to entirely avoid that poison-grass food, and—avoiding that dangerous enjoyment—were to dwell having plunged into a wilderness area?’”

mn25:5.8.verse: So, they entirely avoided that poison-grass food. Avoiding that dangerous enjoyment, they dwelled having plunged into a wilderness area.

mn25:5.9.verse: But in the last month of the hot season, when the grass & water were used up, their bodies became extremely gaunt.

mn25:5.10.verse: Their bodies having become extremely gaunt, they lost their strength & energy.

mn25:5.11.verse: Having lost their strength & energy, they returned to the poison-grass sown by the poison-grass sower.

mn25:5.12.verse: Venturing unwarily into the poison-grass sown by the poison-grass sower, they ate food.

mn25:5.13.verse: Having eaten food after venturing unwarily, they became intoxicated. Being intoxicated, they became heedless. When they became heedless, the poison-grass sower did with them as he liked, on account of that poison-grass.

mn25:5.14.verse: That’s why that second herd of deer didn’t escape from the poison-grass sower’s power & control.

mn25:5.15.verse: ‘What if we were to take up residence near where poison-grass has been sown by the poison-grass sower and—having taken up residence there—were to eat food without venturing unwarily into the poison-grass sown by the poison-grass sower?

mn25:5.16.verse: By eating food without venturing unwarily into the poison-grass sown by the poison-grass sower, we won’t become intoxicated. Not being intoxicated, we won’t become heedless. When we aren’t heedless, the poison-grass sower won’t be able to do with us as he likes on account of this poison-grass.’

mn25:5.17.verse: “So the third herd of deer took up residence near where poison-grass had been sown by the poison-grass sower

mn25:5.18.verse: and—having taken up residence there—ate food without venturing unwarily into the poison-grass sown by the poison-grass sower. When they weren’t heedless, the poison-grass sower wasn’t able to do with them as he liked on account of that poison-grass.

mn25:5.19.verse: “The thought occurred to the poison-grass sower & his followers,

mn25:5.20.verse: ‘How crafty & powerful is this third herd of deer! They must be wizards!

mn25:5.21.verse: How can they eat where the poison-grass has been sown without our knowing their coming or going!

mn25:5.22.verse: What if we were to have the sown poison-grass surrounded on all sides over a large area with stick snares? Perhaps we would see the third herd of deer’s dwelling, where they go to hide.’

mn25:5.23.verse: So they had the sown poison-grass surrounded on all sides over a large area with stick snares.

mn25:5.24.verse: The poison-grass sower & his followers saw the third herd of deer’s dwelling, where they went to hide.

mn25:5.25.verse: That, monks, is why that third herd of deer didn’t escape from the poison-grass sower’s power & control.

mn25:6.39.verse: and in that way all the herds of deer will abandon this sown poison-grass.

mn25:7.1.verse: “This simile, monks, I have given to convey a message.

mn25:7.3.verse: The poison-grass stands for the five strings of sensuality.

mn25:7.4.verse: The poison-grass sower stands for Māra, the Evil One.

mn25:7.5.verse: The poison-grass sower’s followers stand for Māra’s followers.

mn25:7.6.verse: The herds of deer stand for contemplatives & brahmans.

mn25:8.1.verse: “The first group of contemplatives & brahmans, venturing unwarily into the poison-grass & baits of the world sown by Māra, ate food.

mn25:8.2.verse: They, eating food after venturing unwarily, became intoxicated. Being intoxicated, they became heedless. When they were heedless, Māra was able to do with them as he liked, on account of that poison-grass & those baits of the world.

mn25:8.3.verse: That’s why that first group of contemplatives & brahmans didn’t escape from Māra’s power & control.

mn25:8.4.verse: “This first group of contemplatives & brahmans, I tell you, is just like the first herd of deer.

mn25:9.1.verse: “A second group of contemplatives & brahmans reasoned thus:

mn25:9.2.verse: ‘That first group of contemplatives & brahmans, venturing unwarily into the poison-grass & baits of the world sown by Māra, ate food.

mn25:9.3.verse: They, eating food after venturing unwarily, became intoxicated. Being intoxicated, they became heedless. When they were heedless, Māra was able to do with them as he liked, on account of that poison-grass & those baits of the world.

mn25:9.4.verse: That’s why that first group of contemplatives & brahmans didn’t escape from Māra’s power & control.

mn25:9.5.verse: What if we were to entirely avoid that poison-grass food, the baits of the world, and—avoiding that dangerous enjoyment—were to dwell having plunged into a wilderness area?’

mn25:9.7.verse: “So, they entirely avoided that poison-grass food, the baits of the world. Avoiding that dangerous enjoyment, they dwelled having plunged into a wilderness area.

mn25:9.8.verse: There they were eaters of greens or millet or wild rice or hide-parings or moss or rice-bran or the discarded scum of boiled rice or sesame flour or grass or cow dung or forest roots & fruits or fallen fruits.

mn25:9.9.verse: But in the last month of the hot season, when the grass & water were used up, their bodies became extremely gaunt.

mn25:9.10.verse: Their bodies having become extremely gaunt, they lost their strength & energy.

mn25:9.11.verse: Having lost their strength & energy, they lost their awareness-release.

mn25:9.12.verse: Having lost their awareness-release, they returned to the poison-grass & baits of the world sown by Māra.

mn25:9.13.verse: Venturing unwarily into the poison-grass & baits of the world sown by Māra, they ate food.

mn25:9.14.verse: Having eaten food after venturing unwarily, they became intoxicated. Being intoxicated, they became heedless. When they became heedless, Māra did with them as he liked, on account of that poison-grass and those baits of the world.

mn25:9.15.verse: That’s why that second group of contemplatives & brahmans didn’t escape from Māra’s power & control.

mn25:9.16.verse: “This second group of contemplatives & brahmans, I tell you, is just like the second herd of deer.

mn25:10.21.verse: ‘The cosmos is eternal.’ ‘The cosmos is not eternal.’

mn25:10.22.verse: ‘The cosmos is finite.’ ‘The cosmos is infinite.’

mn25:10.23.verse: ‘The soul is the same thing as the body.’ ‘The soul is one thing and the body is another.’

mn25:10.24.verse: ‘After death a Tathāgata exists.’ ‘After death a Tathāgata does not exist.’ ‘After death a Tathāgata both exists & does not exist.’ ‘After death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist.’

mn25:11.32.verse: “This fourth group of contemplatives & brahmans, I tell you, is just like the fourth herd of deer.

mn25:12.1.verse: “And how is there the place where Māra & his followers can’t go?

mn25:12.2.verse: “There is the case where a monk, quite secluded from sensuality, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters & remains in the first jhāna: rapture & pleasure born of seclusion, accompanied by directed thought & evaluation.

mn25:12.3.verse: This is said to be a monk who has blinded Māra, who has destroyed the path of Māra’s eye and has gone where Māra the Evil One can’t see him.

mn25:13.1.verse: “With the stilling of directed thoughts & evaluations, the monk enters & remains in the second jhāna: rapture & pleasure born of concentration, unification of awareness free from directed thought & evaluation—internal assurance.

mn25:13.2.verse: This is said to be a monk who has blinded Māra…

mn25:14.1.verse: “With the fading of rapture, the monk remains equanimous, mindful, & alert, and senses pleasure with the body. He enters & remains in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous & mindful, he has a pleasant abiding.’

mn25:14.2.verse: This is said to be a monk who has blinded Māra…

mn25:15.1.verse: “With the abandoning of pleasure & pain—as with the earlier disappearance of joy & distress—the monk enters & remains in the fourth jhāna: purity of equanimity & mindfulness, neither pleasure nor pain.

mn25:15.2.verse: This is said to be a monk who has blinded Māra…

mn25:16.1.verse: “With the complete transcending of perceptions of (physical) form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and not attending to perceptions of multiplicity, (perceiving,) ‘Infinite space,’ the monk enters & remains in the dimension of the infinitude of space.

mn25:16.2.verse: This is said to be a monk who has blinded Māra…

mn25:17.1.verse: “With the complete transcending of the dimension of the infinitude of space, (perceiving,) ‘Infinite consciousness,’ the monk enters & remains in the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness.

mn25:17.2.verse: This is said to be a monk who has blinded Māra…

mn25:18.1.verse: “With the complete transcending of the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness, (perceiving,) ‘There is nothing,’ the monk enters & remains in the dimension of nothingness.

mn25:18.2.verse: This is said to be a monk who has blinded Māra…

mn25:19.1.verse: “With the complete transcending of the dimension of nothingness, the monk enters & remains in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

mn25:19.2.verse: This is said to be a monk who has blinded Māra…

mn25:20.1.verse: “With the complete transcending of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, the monk enters & remains in the cessation of perception & feeling. And as he sees (that) with discernment, effluents are completely ended.

mn25:20.2.verse: This is said to be a monk who has blinded Māra, who has destroyed the path of Māra’s eye and has gone where Māra the Evil One can’t see him—and has crossed over attachment to the world.”

mn25:20.3.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

mn25:20.4.verse: Gratified, the monks delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn25:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn25:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

mn25:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, a sower does not sow seed for deer thinking,

mn25:2.2.verse: ‘May the deer, enjoying this seed, be long-lived and beautiful. May they live long and prosper!’

mn25:2.3.verse: A sower sows seed for deer thinking,

mn25:2.4.verse: ‘When these deer encroach on where I sow the seed, they’ll recklessly enjoy eating it. They’ll become indulgent, then they’ll become negligent, and then I’ll be able to do what I want with them on account of this seed.’

mn25:3.1.verse: And indeed, the first herd of deer encroached on where the sower sowed the seed and recklessly enjoyed eating it. They became indulgent, then they became negligent, and then the sower was able to do what he wanted with them on account of that seed.

mn25:3.2.verse: And that’s how the first herd of deer failed to get free from the sower’s power.

mn25:4.1.verse: So then a second herd of deer thought up a plan,

mn25:4.2.verse: ‘The first herd of deer became indulgent …

mn25:4.4.verse: and failed to get free of the sower’s power.

mn25:4.5.verse: Why don’t we refrain from eating the seed altogether? Refraining from dangerous food, we can venture deep into a wilderness region and live there.’

mn25:4.6.verse: And that’s just what they did.

mn25:4.7.verse: But when it came to the last month of summer, the grass and water ran out. Their bodies became much too thin,

mn25:4.8.verse: and they lost their strength and energy.

mn25:4.9.verse: So they returned to where the sower had sown the seed.

mn25:4.10.verse: Encroaching, they recklessly enjoyed eating it …

mn25:4.12.verse: And that’s how the second herd of deer failed to get free from the sower’s power.

mn25:5.1.verse: So then a third herd of deer thought up a plan,

mn25:5.14.verse: failed to get free of the sower’s power.

mn25:5.15.verse: Why don’t we set up our lair close by where the sower has sown the seed?

mn25:5.16.verse: Then we can encroach and enjoy eating without being reckless. We won’t become indulgent, then we won’t become negligent, and then the sower won’t be able to do what he wants with us on account of that seed.’

mn25:5.17.verse: And that’s just what they did.

mn25:5.19.verse: So the sower and his helpers thought,

mn25:5.20.verse: ‘Wow, this third herd of deer is so sneaky and devious, they must be some kind of strange spirits with magical abilities!

mn25:5.21.verse: For they eat the seed we’ve sown without us knowing how they come and go.

mn25:5.22.verse: Why don’t we surround the seed on all sides by staking out high nets? Hopefully we might get to see the lair where they go to hide out.’

mn25:5.23.verse: And that’s just what they did.

mn25:5.24.verse: And they saw the lair where the third herd of deer went to hide out.

mn25:5.25.verse: And that’s how the third herd failed to get free from the sower’s power.

mn25:6.1.verse: So then a fourth herd of deer thought up a plan,

mn25:6.27.verse: failed to get free of the sower’s power.

mn25:6.28.verse: Why don’t we set up our lair somewhere the sower and his helpers can’t go? Then we can intrude on where the sower has sown the seed and enjoy eating it without being reckless. We won’t become indulgent, then we won’t become negligent, and then the sower won’t be able to do with us what he wants on account of that seed.’

mn25:6.29.verse: And that’s just what they did.

mn25:6.31.verse: So the sower and his helpers thought,

mn25:6.32.verse: ‘Wow, this fourth herd of deer is so sneaky and devious, they must be some kind of strange spirits with magical abilities!

mn25:6.33.verse: For they eat the seed we’ve sown without us knowing how they come and go.

mn25:6.34.verse: Why don’t we surround the seed on all sides by staking out high nets? Hopefully we might get to see the lair where they go to hide out.’

mn25:6.35.verse: And that’s just what they did.

mn25:6.36.verse: But they couldn’t see the lair where the fourth herd of deer went to hide out.

mn25:6.37.verse: So the sower and his helpers thought,

mn25:6.38.verse: ‘If we disturb this fourth herd of deer, they’ll disturb others, who in turn will disturb even more.

mn25:6.39.verse: Then all of the deer will escape this seed we’ve sown.

mn25:6.40.verse: Why don’t we just keep an eye on that fourth herd?’

mn25:6.41.verse: And that’s just what they did.

mn25:6.42.verse: And that’s how the fourth herd of deer escaped the sower’s power.

mn25:7.1.verse: I’ve made up this simile to make a point.

mn25:7.2.verse: And this is what it means.

mn25:7.3.verse: ‘Seed’ is a term for the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

mn25:7.4.verse: ‘Sower’ is a term for Māra the Wicked.

mn25:7.5.verse: ‘Sower’s helpers’ is a term for Māra’s assembly.

mn25:7.6.verse: ‘Deer’ is a term for ascetics and brahmins.

mn25:8.1.verse: Now, the first group of ascetics and brahmins encroached on where the seed and the worldly pleasures of the flesh were sown by Māra and recklessly enjoyed eating it.

mn25:8.2.verse: They became indulgent, then they became negligent, and then Māra was able to do what he wanted with them on account of that seed and the worldly pleasures of the flesh.

mn25:8.3.verse: And that’s how the first group of ascetics and brahmins failed to get free from Māra’s power.

mn25:8.4.verse: This first group of ascetics and brahmins is just like the first herd of deer, I say.

mn25:9.1.verse: So then a second group of ascetics and brahmins thought up a plan,

mn25:9.2.verse: ‘The first group of ascetics and brahmins became indulgent …

mn25:9.4.verse: and failed to get free of Māra’s power.

mn25:9.5.verse: Why don’t we refrain from eating the seed and the worldly pleasures of the flesh altogether? Refraining from dangerous food, we can venture deep into a wilderness region and live there.’

mn25:9.7.verse: And that’s just what they did.

mn25:9.8.verse: They ate herbs, millet, wild rice, poor rice, water lettuce, rice bran, scum from boiling rice, sesame flour, grass, or cow dung. They survived on forest roots and fruits, or eating fallen fruit.

mn25:9.9.verse: But when it came to the last month of summer, the grass and water ran out. Their bodies became much too thin,

mn25:9.10.verse: and they lost their strength and energy.

mn25:9.11.verse: Because of this, they lost their heart’s release,

mn25:9.12.verse: so they went back to where Māra had sown the seed and the worldly pleasures of the flesh.

mn25:9.13.verse: Intruding on that place, they recklessly enjoyed eating them …

mn25:9.15.verse: And that’s how the second group of ascetics and brahmins failed to get free from Māra’s power.

mn25:9.16.verse: This second group of ascetics and brahmins is just like the second herd of deer, I say.

mn25:10.1.verse: So then a third group of ascetics and brahmins thought up a plan,

mn25:10.4.verse: and second groups of ascetics and brahmins …

mn25:10.15.verse: failed to get free of Māra’s power.

mn25:10.16.verse: Why don’t we set up our lair close by where Māra has sown the seed and those worldly pleasures of the flesh? Then we can encroach on it and enjoy eating without being reckless. We won’t become indulgent, then we won’t become negligent, and then Māra won’t be able to do what he wants with us on account of that seed and those worldly pleasures of the flesh.’

mn25:10.17.verse: And that’s just what they did.

mn25:10.20.verse: Still, they had such views as these:

mn25:10.21.verse: ‘The cosmos is eternal’ or ‘The cosmos is not eternal’;

mn25:10.22.verse: ‘The cosmos is finite’ or ‘The cosmos is infinite’;

mn25:10.23.verse: ‘The soul and the body are one and the same’ or ‘The soul is one thing, the body another’;

mn25:10.24.verse: or that after death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists.

mn25:10.25.verse: And that’s how the third group of ascetics and brahmins failed to get free from Māra’s power.

mn25:10.26.verse: This third group of ascetics and brahmins is just like the third herd of deer, I say.

mn25:11.1.verse: So then a fourth group of ascetics and brahmins thought up a plan,

mn25:11.10.verse: and third groups of ascetics and brahmins …

mn25:11.26.verse: failed to get free of Māra’s power.

mn25:11.27.verse: Why don’t we set up our lair where Māra and his assembly can’t go?

mn25:11.28.verse: Then we can encroach on where Māra has sown the seed and those worldly pleasures of the flesh, and enjoy eating without being reckless. We won’t become indulgent, then we won’t become negligent, and then Māra won’t be able to do what he wants with us on account of that seed and those worldly pleasures of the flesh.’

mn25:11.29.verse: And that’s just what they did.

mn25:11.31.verse: And that’s how the fourth group of ascetics and brahmins got free from Māra’s power.

mn25:11.32.verse: This fourth group of ascetics and brahmins is just like the fourth herd of deer, I say.

mn25:12.1.verse: And where is it that Māra and his assembly can’t go?

mn25:12.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

mn25:12.3.verse: This is called a mendicant who has blinded Māra, put out his eyes without a trace, and gone where the Wicked One cannot see.

mn25:13.1.verse: Furthermore, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, a mendicant enters and remains in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

mn25:13.2.verse: This is called a mendicant who has blinded Māra …

mn25:14.1.verse: Furthermore, with the fading away of rapture, a mendicant enters and remains in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

mn25:14.2.verse: This is called a mendicant who has blinded Māra …

mn25:15.1.verse: Furthermore, with the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, a mendicant enters and remains in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

mn25:15.2.verse: This is called a mendicant who has blinded Māra …

mn25:16.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.

mn25:16.2.verse: This is called a mendicant who has blinded Māra …

mn25:17.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

mn25:17.2.verse: This is called a mendicant who has blinded Māra …

mn25:18.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, enters and remains in the dimension of nothingness.

mn25:18.2.verse: This is called a mendicant who has blinded Māra …

mn25:19.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, enters and remains in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

mn25:19.2.verse: This is called a mendicant who has blinded Māra …

mn25:20.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, enters and remains in the cessation of perception and feeling. And, having seen with wisdom, their defilements come to an end.

mn25:20.2.verse: This is called a mendicant who has blinded Māra, put out his eyes without a trace, and gone where the Wicked One cannot see. And they’ve crossed over clinging to the world.”

mn25:20.3.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn25:20.4.verse: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

mn26:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.

mn26:2.1.verse: Then when it was morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and (outer) robe, he went into Sāvatthī for alms.

mn26:2.2.verse: Then many bhikkhus went to the venerable Ānanda and said to him:

mn26:2.3.verse: ‘Friend Ānanda, it is long since we heard a talk on the Dhamma from the Blessed One’s own lips.

mn26:2.4.verse: It would be good if we could do so, friend Ānanda.’

mn26:2.5.verse: ‘Then let the venerable ones go to Rammaka the divine’s retreat;

mn26:2.6.verse: perhaps you will hear a talk on the Dhamma from the Blessed One’s own lips.’

mn26:3.1.verse: Now when the Blessed One had wandered for alms in Sāvatthī and had returned from his alms-round after his meal, he addressed the venerable Ānanda:

mn26:3.2.verse: ‘Ānanda let us go to the Eastern Park, to the Palace of Migāra’s mother, for the day’s abiding.’

mn26:3.3.verse: ‘Even so, venerable sir,’ the venerable Ānanda replied.

mn26:3.4.verse: Then the Blessed One went with the venerable Ānanda to the Eastern Park, the Palace of Migāra’s mother, for the day’s abiding.

mn26:3.5.verse: Now when it was evening, the Blessed One rose from meditation, and he addressed the venerable Ānanda:

mn26:3.6.verse: ‘Ānanda, let us go to the Eastern bathing place and bathe our limbs.’

mn26:3.7.verse: ‘Even so, venerable sir,’ the venerable Ānanda replied.

mn26:3.8.verse: Then the Blessed One went with the venerable Ānanda to the Eastern bathing place to bathe his limbs.

mn26:3.9.verse: When he had done so, he came up out of the water and stood in one robe drying his limbs.

mn26:3.11.verse: ‘Venerable sir, Rammaka the divine’s retreat is nearby.

mn26:3.14.verse: Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One went there out of pity.’

mn26:3.15.verse: The Blessed One consented in silence.

mn26:4.1.verse: Then the Blessed One went to Rammaka the divine’s retreat.

mn26:4.2.verse: Now on that occasion many bhikkhus had gathered together there to discuss the Dhamma.

mn26:4.3.verse: The Blessed One stood outside the door waiting for the end of their discussion.

mn26:4.4.verse: When he knew that it was finished, he coughed and knocked.

mn26:4.5.verse: The bhikkhus opened the door for him.

mn26:4.6.verse: Then he went inside and sat down on a seat made ready.

mn26:4.7.verse: When he had done so he addressed the bhikkhus thus:

mn26:4.8.verse: ‘Bhikkhus, for what discussion are you gathered here now? And what was your discussion meanwhile, which was left unfinished?’

mn26:4.9.verse: ‘Venerable sir, our discussion which was left unfinished was about the Dhamma and it was about the Blessed One himself. Then the Blessed One arrived.’

mn26:4.11.verse: It becomes you that as clansmen who have gone forth from the home life into homelessness out of faith, you gather for discussion of the Dhamma.

mn26:4.12.verse: When you are gathered together there are two alternatives:

mn26:4.13.verse: discussion of the Dhamma or the Noble Ones’ silence.

mn26:5.1.verse: ‘Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of search:

mn26:5.2.verse: the noble search and the ignoble search.

mn26:5.3.verse: And what is the ignoble search?

mn26:5.4.verse: Here someone, himself subject to the birth, ageing, ailment, death, sorrow and defilement, seeks what is also subject to birth, ageing, ailment, death, sorrow and defilement.

mn26:6.1.verse: ‘And what may be said to be subject to birth?

mn26:6.2.verse: Wife and children are subject to birth, and so are bondswomen and bondsmen, goats and sheep, fowls and pigs, elephants, cattle, horses and mares, gold and silver.

mn26:6.3.verse: These essentials of existence are subject to birth;

mn26:6.4.verse: and one who is entangled with these and unwarily committed to them is one who, being himself subject to birth, seeks what is also subject to birth.

mn26:7.1.verse: ‘And what may be said to be subject to ageing?

mn26:7.2.verse: Wife and children are subject to ageing and so are … gold and silver.

mn26:7.3.verse: These essentials of existence are subject to ageing;

mn26:7.4.verse: and one who is entangled with these and unwarily committed to them is one who, being himself subject to ageing, seeks what is also subject to ageing.

mn26:8.1.verse: ‘And what may be said to be subject to ailment?

mn26:8.2.verse: Wife and children are subject to ailment and so are … gold and silver.

mn26:8.3.verse: These essentials of existence are subject to ailment …

mn26:8.4.verse: seeks what is also subject to ailment.

mn26:9.1.verse: ‘And what may be said to be subject to death?

mn26:9.2.verse: Wife and children are subject to death and so are … gold and silver

mn26:9.3.verse: These essentials of existence are subject to death …

mn26:9.4.verse: seeks what is also subject to death.

mn26:10.1.verse: ‘And what may be said to be subject to sorrow?

mn26:10.2.verse: Wife and children are subject to sorrow and so are … gold and silver.

mn26:10.3.verse: These essentials of existence are subject to sorrow …

mn26:10.4.verse: seeks what is also subject to sorrow.

mn26:11.1.verse: ‘And what may be said to be subject to defilement?

mn26:11.2.verse: Wife and children are subject to defilement and so are bondswomen and bondsmen, goats and sheep, fowls and pigs, elephants, cattle, horses and mares, gold and silver.

mn26:11.3.verse: These essentials of existence are subject to defilement,

mn26:11.4.verse: and one who is entangled with these and unwarily committed to them is one who being himself subject to defilement, seeks what is also subject to defilement.

mn26:12.2.verse: Here someone, himself subject to birth, ageing, ailment, death, sorrow and defilement, and knowing the danger in these dhammas, seeks the unborn, unageing, unailing, deathless, sorrowless, undefiled, supreme surcease of bondage, which is Nibbāna.

mn26:13.1.verse: ‘Bhikkhus, before my enlightenment, while I was still only an unenlightened Bodhisatta, I too, being myself subject to birth, ageing, ailment, death, sorrow and defilement, sought what was also subject to birth, ageing, ailment, death, sorrow and defilement.

mn26:13.3.verse: “Why, being myself subject to birth, ageing, ailment, death, sorrow and defilement, do I seek what is also subject to birth, ageing, ailment, death, sorrow and defilement?

mn26:13.4.verse: Suppose that, myself being subject to these dhammas, knowing the danger in these dhammas, I seek the unborn, unageing, unailing, deathless, sorrowless, undefiled, supreme surcease of bondage, which is Nibbāna?”’

mn26:14.1.verse: ‘Later, while still a boy, a black-haired youth endowed with the blessing of youth, in the first phase of life, I shaved off my hair and beard—though my mother and father wished otherwise and grieved with tearful faces—I put on the yellow cloth and went forth from the house life into homelessness.

mn26:15.1.verse: ‘Having gone forth in search of what is profitable, seeking the supreme state of sublime peace, I went to Āḷāra Kālāma and I said to him:

mn26:15.2.verse: “Friend Kālāma, I want to lead the life divine in this Dhamma and Discipline.”’

mn26:15.3.verse: ‘When this was said, Āḷāra Kālāma replied:

mn26:15.5.verse: This Dhamma is such that in no long time a wise man can enter upon and abide in it, himself realizing through direct knowledge his own teacher’s doctrine.”

mn26:15.7.verse: I claimed that as far as mere lip-reciting and rehearsal of his teachings went I could speak with knowledge and assurance, and that I knew and saw—and there were others that did likewise.

mn26:15.9.verse: “It is not through mere faith alone the Āḷāra Kālāma declares his Dhamma; (he does so) because he enters upon and abides in it, himself realizing it through direct knowledge.

mn26:15.10.verse: Certainly Āḷāra Kālāma abides in this Dhamma knowing and seeing.”’

mn26:15.11.verse: ‘Then I went to Ālāra Kālāma, and I said to him:

mn26:15.12.verse: “Friend Kālāma, in what way do you declare to have entered upon this Dhamma, yourself realizing it through direct knowledge?”’

mn26:15.13.verse: ‘When this was said, he declared the base consisting of nothingness.

mn26:15.15.verse: “Not only Ālāra Kālāma has faith; I too have faith.

mn26:15.16.verse: Not only Ālāra Kālāma has energy; I too have energy.

mn26:15.17.verse: Not only Ālāra Kālāma has mindfulness; I too have mindfulness.

mn26:15.18.verse: Not only Ālāra Kālāma has concentration; I too have concentration.

mn26:15.19.verse: Not only Ālāra Kālāma has understanding; I too have understanding.

mn26:15.20.verse: Suppose I exercise control in order to realize the Dhamma that he declares to have entered upon, himself realizing it through direct knowledge?”’

mn26:15.21.verse: ‘I soon entered upon and abode in that Dhamma, myself realizing it through direct knowledge.

mn26:15.22.verse: Then I went to Ālāra Kālāma, and I said to him:

mn26:15.23.verse: “Friend Kālāma, is it in this way that you declare to have entered upon this Dhamma, yourself realizing it through direct knowledge?”’

mn26:15.24.verse: ”It is in this way, friend, that I declare to have entered upon this Dhamma, myself realizing it through direct knowledge.”’

mn26:15.25.verse: ”Friend, I too in this way enter upon and abide in this Dhamma, myself realizing it through direct knowledge.”’

mn26:15.26.verse: ”It is gain for us, friend, it is great gain for us

mn26:15.27.verse: that we have such a venerable one as our companion in the life divine.

mn26:15.28.verse: So the Dhamma that I declare to have entered upon, myself realizing it through direct knowledge, that Dhamma you enter upon and abide in, yourself realizing it through direct knowledge.

mn26:15.29.verse: And the Dhamma that you enter upon and abide in, yourself realizing it through direct knowledge, that Dhamma I declare to have entered upon, myself realizing it through direct knowledge.

mn26:15.30.verse: So you know the Dhamma that I know; I know the Dhamma that you know.

mn26:15.31.verse: As I am, so you are; as you are, so am I.

mn26:15.32.verse: Come, friend, let us now lead this community together.”’

mn26:15.33.verse: ‘Thus Ālāra Kālāma, my Teacher, placed me, his pupil, on an equal footing with himself, and awarded me the highest honour.’

mn26:15.35.verse: “This Dhamma does not lead to dispassion, to fading of lust, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to full enlightenment, to Nibbāna, but only to the base consisting of nothingness.”’

mn26:15.36.verse: ‘I was not satisfied with that Dhamma. I left it and went away.

mn26:16.1.verse: ‘Still in search of what is profitable, seeking the supreme state of sublime peace, I went to Uddaka Rāmaputta, and I said to him:

mn26:16.2.verse: “Friend, I went to lead the life divine in this Dhamma and Discipline.”

mn26:16.3.verse: ‘When this was said, Uddaka Rāmaputta replied:

mn26:16.5.verse: This Dhamma is such that in no long time a wise man can enter upon and abide in it, himself realizing through direct knowledge his own teacher’s doctrine.”

mn26:16.7.verse: I claimed that as far as mere lip-reciting and rehearsal of his teaching went I could speak with knowledge and assurance, and that I knew and saw—and there were others who did likewise.

mn26:16.9.verse: “It is not through mere faith alone that Rāma declares his Dhamma, but (he does so) because he enters upon and abides in it, himself realizing it through direct knowledge.

mn26:16.10.verse: Certainly Rāma abides in this Dhamma knowing and seeing.”

mn26:16.11.verse: ‘Then I went to Uddaka Rāmaputta, and I said to him:

mn26:16.12.verse: “Friend Rāma, in what way do you declare to have entered upon this Dhamma, yourself realizing it through direct knowledge?”

mn26:16.13.verse: ‘When this was said, he declared the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

mn26:16.15.verse: “Not only Rāma has faith; I too have faith.

mn26:16.16.verse: Not only Rāma has energy; I too have energy.

mn26:16.17.verse: Not only Rāma has mindfulness; I too have mindfulness.

mn26:16.18.verse: Not only Rāma has concentration; I too have concentration.

mn26:16.19.verse: Not only Rāma has understanding; I too have understanding.

mn26:16.20.verse: Suppose I exercise control in order to realize the Dhamma that he declares to have entered upon, himself realizing it through direct knowledge?”

mn26:16.21.verse: ‘I soon entered upon and abode in that Dhamma, myself realizing it through direct knowledge.

mn26:16.22.verse: Then I went to Uddaka Rāmaputta and I said to him:

mn26:16.23.verse: “Friend Rāma, is it in this way that you declare to have entered upon the Dhamma, yourself realizing it through direct knowledge?”

mn26:16.24.verse: ”It is in this way, friend, that Rāma declares to have entered upon the Dhamma, himself realizing it through direct knowledge.”

mn26:16.25.verse: “Friend, I too in this way enter upon and abide in this Dhamma, myself realizing it through direct knowledge.”

mn26:16.26.verse: ”It is gain for us, friend, it is great gain for us,

mn26:16.27.verse: that we have such a venerable one for our companion in the life divine.

mn26:16.28.verse: So the Dhamma that Rāma declares to have entered upon, himself realizing it through direct knowledge, that Dhamma you enter upon and abide in, yourself realizing it through direct knowledge.

mn26:16.29.verse: And the Dhamma that you enter upon and abide in, yourself realizing it through direct knowledge, that Dhamma Rāma declares to have entered upon, himself realizing it through direct knowledge.

mn26:16.30.verse: So you know that Dhamma that Rāma knows; Rāma knows the Dhamma that you know.

mn26:16.31.verse: As Rāma is, so you are; as you are, so Rāma is.

mn26:16.32.verse: Come, friend, do you now lead this community.”

mn26:16.33.verse: ‘Thus Uddaka Rāmaputta, my companion in the life divine, placed me in the Teacher’s place and accorded me the highest honour.

mn26:16.35.verse: “This Dhamma does not lead to dispassion, to fading of lust, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to full enlightenment, to Nibbāna; but only to the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.”

mn26:16.36.verse: ‘I was not satisfied with that Dhamma. I left it and went away.

mn26:17.1.verse: ‘Still in search of what is profitable, seeking the supreme state of sublime peace, I wandered by stages through the Magadhan country, till at length I arrived at Senānigama near Uruvelā.

mn26:17.2.verse: There I saw an agreeable piece of ground, a delightful grove, a clear-flowing river with pleasant smooth banks, and nearby a village as alms resort.

mn26:17.4.verse: “There is this agreeable piece of ground, this delightful grove, this clear-flowing river with pleasant smooth banks, and nearby a village for alms resort.

mn26:17.5.verse: This will serve for the endeavour of a clansman who seeks endeavour.”

mn26:18.1.verse: ‘Being myself subject to birth, ageing, ailment, death, sorrow and defilement, knowing the danger in these dhammas, seeking the unborn, unageing, deathless, sorrowless, undefiled supreme surcease of bondage, which is Nibbāna, I attained the unborn, unageing, unailing, deathless, sorrowless, undefiled supreme surcease of bondage, which is Nibbāna.

mn26:18.2.verse: ‘The knowledge and vision arose in me:

mn26:18.3.verse: “My deliverance is unassailable. This my last birth. There is now no renewal of being.”’

mn26:19.2.verse: “This Dhamma that I have attained is profound, hard to see and hard to discover. It is (the most) peaceful and superior (goal of all), unattainable by (mere) ratiocination, subtle, and for the wise to experience.

mn26:19.3.verse: But this generation loves something to rely on, delights in something to rely on, is glad of something to rely on.

mn26:19.4.verse: It is hard for such a generation to see this truth, namely, specific conditionality, dependent origination.

mn26:19.5.verse: And it is hard to see this truth, namely, the stilling of all formations, relinquishing of all essentials of existence, exhaustion of craving, fading of lust, cessation, Nibbāna.

mn26:19.6.verse: And if I taught the Dhamma, others would not understand me, and that would be weariness and a bother for me.”

mn26:19.7.verse: ‘In fact, there came to me spontaneously these stanzas never heard before:

mn26:19.9.verse: That even I found hard to reach;

mn26:19.10.verse: For it will never be perceived

mn26:19.11.verse: By those who live in lust and hate.

mn26:19.12.verse: Men dyed in lust, and whom a cloud

mn26:19.13.verse: Of darkness laps, will never see

mn26:19.14.verse: What goes against the stream, is subtle,

mn26:19.15.verse: Deep, and hard to see, abstruse.

mn26:19.16.verse: ‘Considering thus, my mind favoured inaction instead of teaching the Dhamma.

mn26:20.1.verse: ‘Then the (Brahmā) Divinity Sahampati knew in mind the thought in my mind, and he (considered):

mn26:20.2.verse: “The world will be lost, the world will be utterly lost, since the mind of the Tathāgata, Arahant and Fully Enlightened One, favours inaction instead of teaching the Dhamma.”

mn26:20.3.verse: ‘Then just as soon as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm, the Divinity Sahampati vanished in the world of the Divinity and appeared before me.

mn26:20.4.verse: Then he arranged his upper robe on one shoulder and raising his hands palms together towards me, he said:

mn26:20.5.verse: “Venerable sir, let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma.

mn26:20.6.verse: There are beings with little dust in their eyes who are wasting through not hearing the Dhamma.

mn26:20.7.verse: Some of them will gain final knowledge of the Dhamma.”

mn26:20.9.verse: and having done so, he said further:

mn26:20.10.verse: In Magadha till now have Dhammas been

mn26:20.11.verse: Unpurified, thought out by those still stained.

mn26:20.12.verse: Open the Deathless gateway, let them hear

mn26:20.13.verse: The Dhamma the Immaculate has found;

mn26:20.14.verse: Who stands upon a solid pile of rock,

mn26:20.15.verse: And, just as one sees all the folk around,

mn26:20.18.verse: This human breed engulfed in sorrowing

mn26:20.19.verse: That Birth has at its mercy, and Old Age.

mn26:20.21.verse: Free from all debt, and wander in the world.

mn26:20.22.verse: Proclaim the Dhamma; there are some,

mn26:21.1.verse: ‘Then I listened to the Divinity’s pleading. Out of compassion for beings I surveyed the world with the eye of a Buddha.

mn26:21.2.verse: Surveying the world with the eye of a Buddha, I saw beings with little dust in their eyes and with much dust in their eyes, with keen faculties and with dull faculties, with good qualities and with bad qualities, easy to teach and hard to teach, and some that dwelt seeing fear in blame and in the other world.

mn26:21.3.verse: Just as in a pond of blue or red or white lotuses, some lotuses that are born and grow in the water thrive immersed in the water without rising out of it, and some other lotuses that are born and grow in water rest on the water’s surface, and some other lotuses that are born and grow in the water rise out of the water and stand clear, unwetted by it,

mn26:21.4.verse: so too, surveying the world … and some that dwelt seeing fear in blame and in the other world.

mn26:21.5.verse: ‘Then I replied to the Divinity Sahampati in stanzas:

mn26:21.6.verse: Open for them are the Deathless’ doors,

mn26:21.7.verse: Let those that hear now show their faith,

mn26:21.8.verse: Seeing the bother I spoke not for men

mn26:21.10.verse: ‘Then the Divinity Sahampati (thought): “I have made it possible for the Dhamma to be taught by the Blessed One.” And after paying homage to me, keeping me on the right, the Divinity departed.

mn26:22.2.verse: “To whom should I first teach the Dhamma?

mn26:22.3.verse: Who will soon understand this Dhamma?”

mn26:22.5.verse: “Āḷāra Kālāma is wise, learned and discerning. He has long had little dust in his eyes.

mn26:22.6.verse: Suppose I taught the Dhamma first to Āḷāra Kālāma?

mn26:22.9.verse: “Venerable sir, Āḷāra Kālāma died seven days ago.”

mn26:22.10.verse: And the knowledge and vision arose in me:

mn26:22.13.verse: “Āḷāra Kālāma’s loss is a great one.

mn26:22.14.verse: If he had heard this Dhamma, he would soon have understood it.”

mn26:23.2.verse: “To whom should I first teach the Dhamma?

mn26:23.3.verse: Who will soon understand this Dhamma?”

mn26:23.5.verse: “Uddaka Rāmaputta is wise, learned and discerning. He has long had little dust in his eyes.

mn26:23.6.verse: Suppose I taught the Dhamma first to Uddaka Rāmaputta?

mn26:23.9.verse: “Venerable sir, Uddaka Rāmaputta died last night.”

mn26:23.10.verse: And the knowledge and vision in me:

mn26:23.13.verse: “Uddaka Rāmaputta’s loss is a great one.

mn26:23.14.verse: If he had heard this Dhamma, he would soon have understood it.”

mn26:24.2.verse: “To whom should I first teach the Dhamma?

mn26:24.3.verse: Who will soon understand this Dhamma?”

mn26:24.5.verse: “The bhikkhus of the group of five, who attended me while I was engaged in the struggle for control were very helpful.

mn26:24.6.verse: Suppose I taught the Dhamma first to them?”’

mn26:24.8.verse: “Where are the bhikkhus of the group of five living now?”

mn26:24.9.verse: And with the heavenly eyesight, which is purified and surpasses the human, I saw that they were living at Benares in the Deer Park at Isipatana.

mn26:24.10.verse: ‘Then when I had stayed at Uruvela as long as I chose, I set out to go by stages to Benares.

mn26:25.1.verse: Between Gayā and the Place of Enlightenment the monk Upaka saw me on the road.

mn26:25.3.verse: “Friend, the colour of your skin is pure and bright.

mn26:25.4.verse: Under whom have you gone forth, friend? Or who is your Teacher? Or whose Dhamma do you confess?”

mn26:25.5.verse: ‘When this was said, I replied to the monk Upaka in stanzas:

mn26:25.6.verse: Transcender of all being, All-knower am I,

mn26:25.7.verse: Unsullied in all dhammas, renouncing them all

mn26:25.8.verse: By craving’s ceasing freed. And this do I owe

mn26:25.9.verse: To my own wit, to whom should I concede it?

mn26:25.10.verse: I have no Teacher, and my like

mn26:25.11.verse: Exists nowhere in all the world

mn26:25.12.verse: With all its gods, because I have

mn26:25.14.verse: I am the Teacher in the world

mn26:25.15.verse: Without a peer, an Arahant too

mn26:25.16.verse: And I alone am Full enlightened

mn26:25.17.verse: Quenched, whose fires are quite extinct.

mn26:25.18.verse: I go to Kāsi’s city now

mn26:25.19.verse: To set in motion the Dhamma’s Wheel:

mn26:25.21.verse: I go to beat the Deathless Drum.

mn26:25.22.verse: ‘“By your claims, friend, you ought to be a Victor Universal.”

mn26:25.24.verse: Are these won to exhaustion of taints.

mn26:25.26.verse: For that I am a Victor.

mn26:25.27.verse: ‘When this was said, the monk Upaka said: “May it be so, friend.” Shaking his head, he took a by-path and departed.

mn26:26.1.verse: ‘Then wandering by stages, I came at length to Benares, to the Deer Park at Isipatana, where the bhikkhus of the group of five were.

mn26:26.2.verse: ‘They saw me coming at a distance,

mn26:26.3.verse: and they agreed among themselves thus:

mn26:26.4.verse: “Friends, here comes the monk Gotama who turned self-indulgent, shirked control and reverted to luxury.

mn26:26.5.verse: We ought not to pay homage to him or rise up for him or receive his bowl and robe.

mn26:26.6.verse: But a seat can be prepared for him. If he likes, he will sit down.”

mn26:26.7.verse: ‘However, as soon as I approached, they found themselves unable to keep their pact.

mn26:26.8.verse: One came to meet me and took my bowl and (outer) robe; another prepared a seat; and another got water ready for my feet;

mn26:26.9.verse: and they addressed me by name as “friend”.

mn26:27.1.verse: ‘When this was said, I told them:

mn26:27.2.verse: “Bhikkhus, do not address a Tathāgata by name as ‘friend’.

mn26:27.3.verse: A Tathāgata is an Arahant and Fully Enlightened.

mn26:27.4.verse: Listen, bhikkhus, the Deathless has been attained. I shall instruct you; I shall teach you the Dhamma.

mn26:27.5.verse: By practising as you are instructed, you will, by realization yourselves here and now through direct knowledge enter upon and abide in that supreme goal of the life divine on account of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.”

mn26:27.6.verse: ‘When this was said, the bhikkhus of the group of five answered me thus:

mn26:27.7.verse: “Friend Gotama, with the behaviour the way, and the difficult feats, which you practised you achieved no distinction worthy of a Noble One’s knowledge and vision higher than the human state (dhamma). Since you have now turned self-indulgent, shirked control and reverted to luxury, how will you have achieved any such distinction?”

mn26:27.8.verse: ‘When this was said, I told them:

mn26:27.9.verse: “A Tathāgata is not one who has turned self-indulgent, nor has he shirked control and reverted to luxury.

mn26:27.10.verse: A Tathāgata is an Arahant and Fully Enlightened.

mn26:27.11.verse: Listen, bhikkhus, the Deathless has been attained. I shall instruct you; I shall teach you the Dhamma.

mn26:27.12.verse: By practising as you are instructed, you will, by realization yourselves here and now through direct knowledge enter upon and abide in that supreme goal of the life divine on account of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.”

mn26:27.13.verse: ‘A second time the bhikkhus of the group of five said to me:

mn26:27.14.verse: “Friend Gotama … how will you have achieved any such distinction?”

mn26:27.16.verse: “A Tathāgata is not one who has turned self-indulgent …

mn26:27.17.verse: from the home life into homelessness.”

mn26:27.18.verse: ‘A third time the bhikkhus of the group of five said to me:

mn26:27.19.verse: “Friend Gotama … how will you have achieved any such distinction?”

mn26:28.1.verse: ‘When this was said I asked them:

mn26:28.2.verse: “Bhikkhus, have you ever known me to speak like this before?”’

mn26:28.4.verse: “Bhikkhus, a Tathāgata is an Arahant and Fully Enlightened.

mn26:28.5.verse: Listen, bhikkhus, the Deathless has been attained. I shall instruct you; I shall teach you the Dhamma.

mn26:28.6.verse: By practising as you are instructed, you will, by realization yourselves here and now through direct knowledge enter upon and abide in that supreme goal of the life divine on account of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.”’

mn26:29.1.verse: ‘I was able to convince the bhikkhus of the group of five.

mn26:29.2.verse: Sometimes I instructed two bhikkhus while three went for alms;

mn26:29.3.verse: and we six lived upon what the three brought back from their alms-round.

mn26:29.4.verse: Sometimes I instructed three bhikkhus while two went for alms:

mn26:29.5.verse: and we six lived upon what the two brought back from their alms-round.

mn26:30.1.verse: ‘Then the bhikkhus of the group of five, thus taught and instructed by me, being themselves subject to birth, ageing, ailment, death, sorrow and defilement, knowing the danger in these dhammas, seeking the unborn, unageing, unailing, deathless, sorrowless, undefiled supreme surcease of bondage which is Nibbāna, attained to the unborn, unageing, unailing, deathless, sorrowless, undefiled supreme surcease of bondage which is Nibbāna.

mn26:30.2.verse: ‘The knowledge and vision arose in them:

mn26:30.3.verse: “My deliverance is unassailable. This is my last birth. There is now no renewal of being.” ‘ “

mn26:31.1.verse: ‘Bhikkhus, there are these five cords of sensual desire.

mn26:31.3.verse: Forms cognizable by the eye that are wished-for, desired, agreeable and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.

mn26:31.7.verse: Tangibles cognizable by the body … provocative of lust.

mn26:31.8.verse: These are the five cords of sensual desire.

mn26:32.1.verse: ‘When any monks and divines are entangled with and unwarily committed to these five cords of sensual desire and cultivate them with no vision of the danger in them and no understanding of the escape from them, it may be understood of them thus:

mn26:32.2.verse: “They are bound for disaster, bound for ruin, to be done with as he likes by the Evil One.”

mn26:32.3.verse: ‘Suppose a forest deer were tied to, and lay down on, a mass of snares,

mn26:32.4.verse: it might be understood of him thus:

mn26:32.5.verse: “He is bound for disaster, bound for ruin, to be done with as he likes by the hunter”,

mn26:32.7.verse: so too when any monks and divines …

mn26:32.8.verse: “… to be done with as he likes by the Evil One.”

mn26:33.1.verse: ‘When any monks and divines are not entangled with nor unwarily committed to these five cords of sensual desire and do not cultivate them, having vision of the danger in them and understanding the escape from them, it may be understood of them thus:

mn26:33.2.verse: “They are not bound for disaster, not bound for ruin, not to be done with as he likes by the Evil One.”

mn26:33.3.verse: ‘Suppose a forest deer were not tied to but lay down on a mass of snares,

mn26:33.4.verse: it might be understood of him thus.

mn26:33.5.verse: “He is not bound for disaster, not bound for ruin, not to be done with as he likes by the hunter”,

mn26:33.7.verse: so too when any monks and divines …

mn26:33.8.verse: “… not to be done with as he likes by the Evil One.”’

mn26:34.1.verse: ‘Suppose a forest deer is wandering in the forest wilds, he walks without fear, stands without fear, sits without fear, lies down without fear.

mn26:34.3.verse: Because he is out of the hunter’s sight—

mn26:34.4.verse: so too, quite secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unprofitable dhammas, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the first jhāna which is accompanied by initial and sustained application, with happiness and bliss born of seclusion.

mn26:34.5.verse: And this bhikkhu is said to have blindfolded Māra, to have become invisible to the Evil One by depriving Māra’s eye of its opportunity.

mn26:35.1.verse: ‘Again, with the stilling of initial and sustained application … second jhāna … born of concentration.

mn26:35.2.verse: And this bhikkhu is said to have blindfolded Māra, to have become invisible to the Evil One by depriving Māra’s eye of its opportunity.

mn26:36.1.verse: ‘Again, with the fading as well of happiness … third jhāna … “He has a pleasant abiding who has equanimity and is mindful.”

mn26:36.2.verse: And this bhikkhu is said to have blindfolded Māra … depriving Māra’s eye of its opportunity.

mn26:37.1.verse: ‘Again, with the abandoning of (bodily) pleasure and pain … fourth jhāna … and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.

mn26:37.2.verse: And this bhikkhu is said to have blindfolded Māra … depriving Māra’s eye of its opportunity.

mn26:38.1.verse: ‘Again, with the complete surmounting of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of the perceptions of resistance, with not giving attention to perceptions of difference, (aware that) “space is infinite”, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the base consisting of the infinity of space.

mn26:38.2.verse: And this bhikkhu is said to have blindfolded Māra … depriving Māra’s eye of its opportunity.

mn26:39.1.verse: ‘Again, by completely surmounting the base consisting of the infinity of space, (aware that) “consciousness is infinite”, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the base consisting of the infinity of consciousness.

mn26:39.2.verse: And this bhikkhu is said to have blindfolded Māra … depriving Māra’s eye of its opportunity.

mn26:40.1.verse: ‘Again, by completely surmounting the base consisting of the infinity of consciousness, (aware that) “there is nothing”, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the base consisting of nothingness.

mn26:40.2.verse: And this bhikkhu is said to have blindfolded Māra … depriving Māra’s eye of its opportunity.

mn26:41.1.verse: ‘Again, by completely surmounting the base consisting of nothingness a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

mn26:41.2.verse: And this bhikkhu is said to have blindfolded Māra … depriving Māra’s eye of its opportunity.

mn26:42.1.verse: ‘Again, by completely surmounting the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling. And his taints are exhausted by his seeing with understanding.

mn26:42.2.verse: And this bhikkhu is said to have blindfolded Māra, to have become invisible to the Evil One by depriving Māra’s eye of its opportunity,

mn26:42.3.verse: and to have crossed beyond attachment to the world.’ ‘He walks without fear, stands without fear, sits without fear, lies down without fear.

mn26:42.5.verse: He is out of the Evil One’s sight.’

mn26:42.6.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

mn26:42.7.verse: The bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn26:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn26:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

mn26:2.2.verse: Then several mendicants went up to Venerable Ānanda and said to him,

mn26:2.3.verse: “Reverend, it’s been a long time since we’ve heard a Dhamma talk from the Buddha.

mn26:2.4.verse: It would be good if we got to hear a Dhamma talk from the Buddha.”

mn26:2.5.verse: “Well then, reverends, go to the brahmin Rammaka’s hermitage.

mn26:2.6.verse: Hopefully you’ll get to hear a Dhamma talk from the Buddha.”

mn26:3.1.verse: Then, after the meal, on his return from almsround, the Buddha addressed Ānanda,

mn26:3.2.verse: “Come, Ānanda, let’s go to the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery for the day’s meditation.”

mn26:3.4.verse: So the Buddha went with Ānanda to the Eastern Monastery for the day’s meditation.

mn26:3.5.verse: In the late afternoon the Buddha came out of retreat and addressed Ānanda,

mn26:3.6.verse: “Come, Ānanda, let’s go to the eastern gate to bathe.”

mn26:3.8.verse: So the Buddha went with Ānanda to the eastern gate to bathe.

mn26:3.9.verse: When he had bathed and emerged from the water he stood in one robe drying his limbs.

mn26:3.10.verse: Then Ānanda said to the Buddha,

mn26:3.11.verse: “Sir, the hermitage of the brahmin Rammaka is nearby.

mn26:3.14.verse: Please visit it out of sympathy.”

mn26:4.1.verse: He went to the brahmin Rammaka’s hermitage.

mn26:4.2.verse: Now at that time several mendicants were sitting together in the hermitage talking about the teaching.

mn26:4.3.verse: The Buddha stood outside the door waiting for the talk to end.

mn26:4.4.verse: When he knew the talk had ended he cleared his throat and knocked on the door-panel.

mn26:4.5.verse: The mendicants opened the door for the Buddha,

mn26:4.6.verse: and he entered the hermitage, where he sat down on the seat spread out

mn26:4.8.verse: “Mendicants, what were you sitting talking about just now? What conversation was left unfinished?”

mn26:4.9.verse: “Sir, our unfinished discussion on the teaching was about the Buddha himself when the Buddha arrived.”

mn26:4.11.verse: It’s appropriate for gentlemen like you, who have gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness, to sit together and talk about the teaching.

mn26:4.12.verse: When you’re sitting together you should do one of two things:

mn26:4.13.verse: discuss the teachings or keep noble silence.

mn26:5.1.verse: Mendicants, there are these two quests:

mn26:5.2.verse: the noble quest and the ignoble quest.

mn26:5.3.verse: And what is the ignoble quest?

mn26:5.4.verse: It’s when someone who is themselves liable to be reborn seeks what is also liable to be reborn. Themselves liable to grow old, fall sick, die, sorrow, and become corrupted, they seek what is also liable to these things.

mn26:6.1.verse: And what should be described as liable to be reborn?

mn26:6.2.verse: Partners and children, male and female bondservants, goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, elephants and cattle, and gold and currency are liable to be reborn.

mn26:6.3.verse: These attachments are liable to be reborn.

mn26:6.4.verse: Someone who is tied, infatuated, and attached to such things, themselves liable to being reborn, seeks what is also liable to be reborn.

mn26:7.1.verse: And what should be described as liable to grow old?

mn26:7.2.verse: Partners and children, male and female bondservants, goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, elephants and cattle, and gold and currency are liable to grow old.

mn26:7.3.verse: These attachments are liable to grow old.

mn26:7.4.verse: Someone who is tied, infatuated, and attached to such things, themselves liable to grow old, seeks what is also liable to grow old.

mn26:8.1.verse: And what should be described as liable to fall sick?

mn26:8.2.verse: Partners and children, male and female bondservants, goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, and elephants and cattle are liable to fall sick.

mn26:8.3.verse: These attachments are liable to fall sick.

mn26:8.4.verse: Someone who is tied, infatuated, and attached to such things, themselves liable to falling sick, seeks what is also liable to fall sick.

mn26:9.1.verse: And what should be described as liable to die?

mn26:9.2.verse: Partners and children, male and female bondservants, goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, and elephants and cattle are liable to die.

mn26:9.3.verse: These attachments are liable to die.

mn26:9.4.verse: Someone who is tied, infatuated, and attached to such things, themselves liable to die, seeks what is also liable to die.

mn26:10.1.verse: And what should be described as liable to sorrow?

mn26:10.2.verse: Partners and children, male and female bondservants, goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, and elephants and cattle are liable to sorrow.

mn26:10.3.verse: These attachments are liable to sorrow.

mn26:10.4.verse: Someone who is tied, infatuated, and attached to such things, themselves liable to sorrow, seeks what is also liable to sorrow.

mn26:11.1.verse: And what should be described as liable to corruption?

mn26:11.2.verse: Partners and children, male and female bondservants, goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, elephants and cattle, and gold and currency are liable to corruption.

mn26:11.3.verse: These attachments are liable to corruption.

mn26:11.4.verse: Someone who is tied, infatuated, and attached to such things, themselves liable to corruption, seeks what is also liable to corruption.

mn26:12.1.verse: And what is the noble quest?

mn26:12.2.verse: It’s when someone who is themselves liable to be reborn, understanding the drawbacks in being liable to be reborn, seeks that which is free of rebirth, the supreme sanctuary from the yoke, extinguishment. Themselves liable to grow old, fall sick, die, sorrow, and become corrupted, understanding the drawbacks in these things, they seek that which is free of old age, sickness, death, sorrow, and corruption, the supreme sanctuary from the yoke, extinguishment.

mn26:13.1.verse: Mendicants, before my awakening—when I was still unawakened but intent on awakening—I too, being liable to be reborn, sought what is also liable to be reborn. Myself liable to grow old, fall sick, die, sorrow, and become corrupted, I sought what is also liable to these things.

mn26:13.3.verse: ‘Why do I, being liable to be reborn, grow old, fall sick, sorrow, die, and become corrupted, seek things that have the same nature?
