mn60:37.3.verse: This is called the kind of person who torments others, being interested in torturing others.

mn60:38.1.verse: What kind of person torments himself, being interested in self-torture, and torments others, being interested in torturing others ?

mn60:38.2.verse: ‘Here some person is a head-anointed warrior-noble caste king …

mn60:38.3.verse: being spurred on by threats of punishment and by fear.

mn60:38.4.verse: This is called the kind of person who torments himself, being interested in self-torture, and torments others, being interested in torturing others.

mn60:39.1.verse: ‘What kind of person does not torment himself, not being interested in self-torture, and does not torment others, not being interested in torturing others who,

mn60:39.2.verse: since he torments neither himself nor others, is here and now unparched, extinguished, cooled, and abides experiencing pleasure as one become divine in himself?

mn60:40-54.1.verse: 40-57. ‘Here a Tathāgata appears in the world …

mn60:56.1.verse: ‘This is called the kind of person … as one become divine in himself.’

mn60:56.2.verse: not being interested in self-torture, and he does not torment others, not being interested in torturing others; since he torments neither himself nor others he is here, now unparched, extinguished, cooled, he abides experiencing pleasure as one become divine in himself.

mn60:57.1.verse: When this was said, the divine-caste householders of Sālā said:

mn60:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Kosalans together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants when he arrived at a village of the Kosalan brahmins named Sālā.

mn60:2.1.verse: The brahmins and householders of Sālā heard:

mn60:2.2.verse: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—wandering in the land of the Kosalans has arrived at Sālā, together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants.

mn60:2.4.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

mn60:2.5.verse: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

mn60:2.6.verse: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

mn60:2.7.verse: It’s good to see such perfected ones.”

mn60:3.1.verse: Then the brahmins and householders of Sālā went up to the Buddha. Before sitting down to one side, some bowed, some exchanged greetings and polite conversation, some held up their cupped palms toward the Buddha, some announced their name and clan, while some kept silent. The Buddha said to them:

mn60:4.1.verse: “So, householders, is there any teacher you’re happy with, in whom you have acquired grounded faith?”

mn60:4.3.verse: “Since you haven’t found a teacher you’re happy with, you should undertake and implement this sure bet teaching.

mn60:4.4.verse: For when the sure bet teaching is undertaken, it will be for your lasting welfare and happiness.

mn60:4.5.verse: And what is the sure bet teaching?

mn60:5.1.verse: There are some ascetics and brahmins who have this doctrine and view:

mn60:5.2.verse: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

mn60:6.1.verse: And there are some ascetics and brahmins whose doctrine directly contradicts this.

mn60:6.3.verse: ‘There is meaning in giving, sacrifice, and offerings. There are fruits and results of good and bad deeds. There is an afterlife. There are such things as mother and father, and beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there are ascetics and brahmins who are rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describe the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

mn60:6.5.verse: Don’t these doctrines directly contradict each other?”

mn60:7.1.verse: “Since this is so, consider those ascetics and brahmins whose view is that

mn60:7.2.verse: there’s no meaning in giving, etc.

mn60:7.3.verse: You can expect that they will shun good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and undertake and implement bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

mn60:7.5.verse: Because those ascetics and brahmins don’t see that unskillful qualities are full of drawbacks, sordidness, and corruption, or that skillful qualities have the benefit and cleansing power of renunciation.

mn60:8.1.verse: Moreover, since there actually is another world, their view that there is no other world is wrong view.

mn60:8.2.verse: Since there actually is another world, their thought that there is no other world is wrong purpose.

mn60:8.3.verse: Since there actually is another world, their speech that there is no other world is wrong speech.

mn60:8.4.verse: Since there actually is another world, in saying that there is no other world they contradict those perfected ones who know the other world.

mn60:8.5.verse: Since there actually is another world, in persuading another that there is no other world they are persuading them to accept an untrue teaching.

mn60:8.6.verse: And on account of that they glorify themselves and put others down.

mn60:8.7.verse: So they give up their former ethical conduct and are established in unethical conduct.

mn60:8.8.verse: And that is how these many bad, unskillful qualities come to be with wrong view as condition—wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, contradicting the noble ones, persuading others to accept untrue teachings, and glorifying oneself and putting others down.

mn60:9.1.verse: A sensible person reflects on this matter in this way:

mn60:9.2.verse: ‘If there is no other world, when this individual person’s body breaks up they will keep themselves safe.

mn60:9.3.verse: And if there is another world, when their body breaks up, after death, they will be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

mn60:9.4.verse: But let us grant that those who say that there is no other world are correct.

mn60:9.5.verse: Regardless, that individual is still criticized by sensible people in this very life as being an immoral individual of wrong view, a nihilist.’

mn60:9.6.verse: But if there really is another world, they hold a losing hand on both counts.

mn60:9.7.verse: For they are criticized by sensible people in this very life, and when their body breaks up, after death, they will be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

mn60:9.8.verse: They have wrongly undertaken this sure bet teaching in such a way that it encompasses the positive outcomes of one side only, leaving out the skillful premise.

mn60:10.1.verse: Since this is so, consider those ascetics and brahmins whose view is that

mn60:10.2.verse: there is meaning in giving, etc.

mn60:10.3.verse: You can expect that they will shun bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and undertake and implement good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

mn60:10.5.verse: Because those ascetics and brahmins see that unskillful qualities are full of drawbacks, sordidness, and corruption, and that skillful qualities have the benefit and cleansing power of renunciation.

mn60:11.1.verse: Moreover, since there actually is another world, their view that there is another world is right view.

mn60:11.2.verse: Since there actually is another world, their thought that there is another world is right purpose.

mn60:11.3.verse: Since there actually is another world, their speech that there is another world is right speech.

mn60:11.4.verse: Since there actually is another world, in saying that there is another world they don’t contradict those perfected ones who know the other world.

mn60:11.5.verse: Since there actually is another world, in persuading another that there is another world they are persuading them to accept a true teaching.

mn60:11.6.verse: And on account of that they don’t glorify themselves or put others down.

mn60:11.7.verse: So they give up their former unethical conduct and are established in ethical conduct.

mn60:11.8.verse: And that is how these many skillful qualities come to be with right view as condition—right view, right purpose, right speech, not contradicting the noble ones, persuading others to accept true teachings, and not glorifying oneself or putting others down.

mn60:12.1.verse: A sensible person reflects on this matter in this way:

mn60:12.2.verse: ‘If there is another world, when this individual’s body breaks up, after death, they will be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

mn60:12.3.verse: But let us grant that those who say that there is no other world are correct.

mn60:12.4.verse: Regardless, that individual is still praised by sensible people in this very life as being a moral individual of right view, who affirms a positive teaching.’

mn60:12.5.verse: So if there really is another world, they hold a winning hand on both counts.

mn60:12.6.verse: For they are praised by sensible people in this very life, and when their body breaks up, after death, they will be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

mn60:12.7.verse: They have rightly undertaken this sure bet teaching in such a way that it encompasses the positive outcomes of both sides, leaving out the unskillful premise.

mn60:13.1.verse: There are some ascetics and brahmins who have this doctrine and view:

mn60:13.2.verse: ‘The one who acts does nothing wrong when they punish, mutilate, torture, aggrieve, oppress, intimidate, or when they encourage others to do the same. They do nothing wrong when they kill, steal, break into houses, plunder wealth, steal from isolated buildings, commit highway robbery, commit adultery, and lie.

mn60:13.3.verse: If you were to reduce all the living creatures of this earth to one heap and mass of flesh with a razor-edged chakram, no evil comes of that, and no outcome of evil.

mn60:13.4.verse: If you were to go along the south bank of the Ganges killing, mutilating, and torturing, and encouraging others to do the same, no evil comes of that, and no outcome of evil.

mn60:13.5.verse: If you were to go along the north bank of the Ganges giving and sacrificing and encouraging others to do the same, no merit comes of that, and no outcome of merit.

mn60:13.6.verse: In giving, self-control, restraint, and truthfulness there is no merit or outcome of merit.’

mn60:14.1.verse: And there are some ascetics and brahmins whose doctrine directly contradicts this. They say:

mn60:14.2.verse: ‘The one who acts does a bad deed when they punish, mutilate, torture, aggrieve, oppress, intimidate, or when they encourage others to do the same. They do a bad deed when they kill, steal, break into houses, plunder wealth, steal from isolated buildings, commit highway robbery, commit adultery, and lie.

mn60:14.3.verse: If you were to reduce all the living creatures of this earth to one heap and mass of flesh with a razor-edged chakram, evil comes of that, and an outcome of evil.

mn60:14.4.verse: If you were to go along the south bank of the Ganges killing, mutilating, and torturing, and encouraging others to do the same, evil comes of that, and an outcome of evil.

mn60:14.5.verse: If you were to go along the north bank of the Ganges giving and sacrificing and encouraging others to do the same, merit comes of that, and an outcome of merit.

mn60:14.6.verse: In giving, self-control, restraint, and truthfulness there is merit and outcome of merit.’

mn60:14.8.verse: Don’t these doctrines directly contradict each other?”

mn60:15.1.verse: “Since this is so, consider those ascetics and brahmins whose view is that

mn60:17.2.verse: ‘If there is no effective action, when this individual’s body breaks up they will keep themselves safe.

mn60:17.3.verse: And if there is effective action, when their body breaks up, after death, they will be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

mn60:21.1.verse: There are some ascetics and brahmins who have this doctrine and view:

mn60:21.2.verse: ‘There is no cause or reason for the corruption of sentient beings.

mn60:21.3.verse: Sentient beings are corrupted without cause or reason.

mn60:21.4.verse: There’s no cause or reason for the purification of sentient beings.

mn60:21.5.verse: Sentient beings are purified without cause or reason.

mn60:21.6.verse: There is no power, no energy, no human strength or vigor.

mn60:21.7.verse: All sentient beings, all living creatures, all beings, all souls lack control, power, and energy. Molded by destiny, circumstance, and nature, they experience pleasure and pain in the six classes of rebirth.’

mn60:22.1.verse: And there are some ascetics and brahmins whose doctrine directly contradicts this.

mn60:22.3.verse: ‘There is a cause and reason for the corruption of sentient beings.

mn60:22.4.verse: Sentient beings are corrupted with cause and reason.

mn60:22.5.verse: There is a cause and reason for the purification of sentient beings.

mn60:22.6.verse: Sentient beings are purified with cause and reason.

mn60:22.7.verse: There is power, energy, human strength and vigor.

mn60:22.8.verse: It is not the case that all sentient beings, all living creatures, all beings, all souls lack control, power, and energy, or that, molded by destiny, circumstance, and nature, they experience pleasure and pain in the six classes of rebirth.’

mn60:22.10.verse: Don’t these doctrines directly contradict each other?”

mn60:29.1.verse: There are some ascetics and brahmins who have this doctrine and view:

mn60:29.2.verse: ‘There are no totally formless states of meditation.’

mn60:30.1.verse: And there are some ascetics and brahmins whose doctrine directly contradicts this.

mn60:30.3.verse: ‘There are totally formless states of meditation.’

mn60:30.5.verse: Don’t these doctrines directly contradict each other?”

mn60:31.1.verse: “A sensible person reflects on this matter in this way:

mn60:31.3.verse: there are no totally formless meditations, but I have not seen that.

mn60:31.4.verse: Some ascetics and brahmins say that

mn60:31.5.verse: there are totally formless meditations, but I have not known that.

mn60:31.6.verse: Without knowing or seeing, it would not be appropriate for me to take one side and declare,

mn60:31.7.verse: ‘This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’

mn60:31.8.verse: If those ascetics and brahmins who say that

mn60:31.9.verse: there are no totally formless meditations are correct, it is possible

mn60:31.10.verse: that it’s a sure bet I will be reborn among the gods who are formed and made of mind.

mn60:31.11.verse: If those ascetics and brahmins who say that

mn60:31.12.verse: there are totally formless meditations are correct, it is possible

mn60:31.13.verse: that it’s a sure bet I will be reborn among the gods who are formless and made of perception.

mn60:31.14.verse: Now, owing to form, bad things are seen: taking up the rod and the sword, quarrels, arguments, and disputes, accusations, backbiting, and lies.

mn60:31.15.verse: But those things don’t exist where it is totally formless.’

mn60:31.16.verse: Reflecting like this, they simply practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding forms.

mn60:32.1.verse: There are some ascetics and brahmins who have this doctrine and view:

mn60:32.2.verse: ‘There is no such thing as the total cessation of continued existence.’

mn60:33.1.verse: And there are some ascetics and brahmins whose doctrine directly contradicts this.

mn60:33.3.verse: ‘There is such a thing as the total cessation of continued existence.’

mn60:33.5.verse: Don’t these doctrines directly contradict each other?”

mn60:34.1.verse: “A sensible person reflects on this matter in this way:

mn60:34.3.verse: there is no such thing as the total cessation of continued existence, but I have not seen that.

mn60:34.4.verse: Some ascetics and brahmins say that

mn60:34.5.verse: there is such a thing as the total cessation of continued existence, but I have not known that.

mn60:34.6.verse: Without knowing or seeing, it would not be appropriate for me to take one side and declare,

mn60:34.7.verse: ‘This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’

mn60:34.8.verse: If those ascetics and brahmins who say that

mn60:34.9.verse: there is no such thing as the total cessation of continued existence are correct, it is possible

mn60:34.10.verse: that it’s a sure bet I will be reborn among the gods who are formless and made of perception.

mn60:34.11.verse: If those ascetics and brahmins who say that

mn60:34.12.verse: there is such a thing as the total cessation of continued existence are correct, it is possible

mn60:34.13.verse: that I will be fully extinguished in this very life.

mn60:34.14.verse: The view of those ascetics and brahmins who say that

mn60:34.15.verse: there is no such thing as the total cessation of continued existence is close to greed, yoking, relishing, attachment, and grasping.

mn60:34.16.verse: The view of those ascetics and brahmins who say that

mn60:34.17.verse: there is such a thing as the total cessation of continued existence is close to non-greed, non-yoking, non-relishing, non-attachment, and non-grasping.’

mn60:34.18.verse: Reflecting like this, they simply practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding future lives.

mn60:35.1.verse: Householders, these four individuals are found in the world.

mn60:35.3.verse: One individual mortifies themselves, committed to the practice of mortifying themselves.

mn60:35.4.verse: One individual mortifies others, committed to the practice of mortifying others.

mn60:35.5.verse: One individual mortifies themselves and others, committed to the practice of mortifying themselves and others.

mn60:35.6.verse: One individual doesn’t mortify either themselves or others, committed to the practice of not mortifying themselves or others.

mn60:35.7.verse: They live without wishes in this very life, quenched, cooled, experiencing bliss, with self become divine.

mn60:36.1.verse: And what individual mortifies themselves, committed to the practice of mortifying themselves?

mn60:36.2.verse: It’s when a person goes naked, ignoring conventions. …

mn60:36.3.verse: And so they live committed to practicing these various ways of mortifying and tormenting the body.

mn60:36.4.verse: This is called an individual who mortifies themselves, being committed to the practice of mortifying themselves.

mn60:37.1.verse: And what individual mortifies others, committed to the practice of mortifying others?

mn60:37.2.verse: It’s when an individual is a butcher of sheep, pigs, poultry, or deer, a hunter or fisher, a bandit, an executioner, a butcher of cattle, a jailer, or has some other cruel livelihood.

mn60:37.3.verse: This is called an individual who mortifies others, being committed to the practice of mortifying others.

mn60:38.1.verse: And what individual mortifies themselves and others, being committed to the practice of mortifying themselves and others?

mn60:38.2.verse: It’s when an individual is an anointed aristocratic king or a well-to-do brahmin. He has a new ceremonial hall built to the east of the citadel. He shaves off his hair and beard, dresses in a rough antelope hide, and smears his body with ghee and oil. …

mn60:38.3.verse: His bondservants, servants, and workers do their jobs under threat of punishment and danger, weeping, with tearful faces.

mn60:38.4.verse: This is called an individual who mortifies themselves and others, being committed to the practice of mortifying themselves and others.

mn60:39.1.verse: And what individual doesn’t mortify either themselves or others, committed to the practice of not mortifying themselves or others,

mn60:39.2.verse: living without wishes in this very life, quenched, cooled, experiencing bliss, with self become divine?

mn60:40-54.1.verse: It’s when a Realized One arises in the world, perfected, a fully awakened Buddha …

mn60:40-54.2.verse: A householder hears that teaching, or a householder’s child, or someone reborn in some good family. …

mn60:40-54.3.verse: They give up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.

mn60:40-54.4.verse: Then, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, they enter and remain in the first absorption …

mn60:55.1.verse: When their mind has become immersed in samādhi like this—purified, bright, flawless, rid of corruptions, pliable, workable, steady, and imperturbable—they extend it toward recollection of past lives. …

mn60:55.2.verse: They recollect their many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

mn60:55.3.verse: When their mind has become immersed in samādhi like this—purified, bright, flawless, rid of corruptions, pliable, workable, steady, and imperturbable—they extend it toward knowledge of the death and rebirth of sentient beings.

mn60:55.4.verse: With clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. … They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

mn60:55.5.verse: When their mind has become immersed in samādhi like this—purified, bright, flawless, rid of corruptions, pliable, workable, steady, and imperturbable—they extend it toward knowledge of the ending of defilements.

mn60:55.6.verse: They truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

mn60:55.7.verse: They truly understand: ‘These are defilements’ … ‘This is the origin of defilements’ … ‘This is the cessation of defilements’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of defilements’.

mn60:55.8.verse: Knowing and seeing like this, their mind is freed from the defilements of sensuality, desire to be reborn, and ignorance.

mn60:55.9.verse: When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

mn60:55.10.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

mn60:56.1.verse: This is called an individual who neither mortifies themselves or others, being committed to the practice of not mortifying themselves or others.

mn60:56.2.verse: They live without wishes in this very life, quenched, cooled, experiencing bliss, with self become divine.”

mn60:57.1.verse: When he had spoken, the brahmins and householders of Sālā said to the Buddha,

mn60:57.3.verse: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

mn60:57.4.verse: We go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

mn60:57.5.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge for life.”

mn61:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary.

mn61:2.1.verse: Now on that occasion the venerable Rāhula[^1] was living at Ambalatthika.

mn61:2.2.verse: Then when it was evening the Blessed One rose from meditation, and went to the venerable Rāhula at Ambalatthika.

mn61:2.3.verse: The venerable Rāhula saw the Blessed One coming from afar.

mn61:2.4.verse: When he saw him, he made a seat ready and set out water for washing the feet.

mn61:2.5.verse: The Blessed One sat down on the seat made ready.

mn61:2.6.verse: Having sat down, he washed his feet.

mn61:2.7.verse: The venerable Rāhula paid homage to him and sat down at one side.

mn61:3.1.verse: Then the Blessed One poured the little remaining quantity of water into the water-dipper, and he addressed the venerable Rāhula thus:

mn61:3.2.verse: ‘Rāhula, do you see this little remaining quantity of water poured into the water-dipper?’

mn61:3.4.verse: ‘Unless people are careful not to speak falsehood knowingly, there is as little of the monk in them as this.’

mn61:4.1.verse: Then the Blessed One threw away the little remaining water, and he addressed the venerable Rāhula thus:

mn61:4.2.verse: ‘Rāhula, do you see that little remaining water thrown away?’

mn61:4.4.verse: ‘Unless people are careful not to speak falsehood knowingly, what there is of the monk in them is thrown away like that.’

mn61:5.1.verse: Then the Blessed One turned the water-dipper upside down, and he addressed the venerable Rāhula thus:

mn61:5.2.verse: ‘Rāhula, do you see this water-dipper turned upside down?’

mn61:5.4.verse: ‘Unless people are careful not to speak falsehood knowingly, what there is of the monk in them is turned upside down like that.’

mn61:6.1.verse: Then the Blessed One turned the water-dipper right way up again, and he addressed the venerable Rāhula thus:

mn61:6.2.verse: ‘Rāhula, do you see this hollow, empty water-dipper?’

mn61:6.4.verse: ‘Unless people are careful not to speak falsehood knowingly, what there is of the monk in them is as hollow and empty as that.

mn61:7.1.verse: ‘Suppose, Rāhula, there were a royal tusker elephant with tusks as long as chariot poles, full-grown in stature, highly bred, and well used to battles, and in a battle he used his fore feet and his hind feet and his fore quarters and his hind quarters and his head and his ears and his tusks and his tail, and yet he kept his trunk back;

mn61:7.2.verse: then it would occur to his mahout:

mn61:7.3.verse: “This royal tusker elephant with tusks as long as chariot poles, full-grown in stature, highly bred, and well used to battles, in a battle uses his fore feet and his hind feet … and his tail, and yet he keeps his trunk back.

mn61:7.4.verse: The royal tusker elephant has not yet given up his life to the king.”

mn61:7.5.verse: But as soon as the royal tusker elephant, in a battle, uses his fore feet and his hind feet … and his tail, and his trunk as well, then it would occur to his mahout:

mn61:7.6.verse: “This royal tusker elephant with tusks as long as chariot poles, full-grown in stature, highly bred, and well used to battles, in a battle uses his fore feet and his hind feet and his fore quarters and his hind quarters and his head and his ears and his tusks and his tail, and his trunk as well.

mn61:7.7.verse: The royal tusker elephant has given up his life to the king.

mn61:7.8.verse: There is nothing more now that the royal tusker elephant will not do.”

mn61:7.9.verse: So too, Rāhula, as long as anyone is not ashamed of speaking a deliberate lie, I say there is no evil he will not do.

mn61:7.10.verse: Therefore, Rāhula, you should train thus: “I shall not utter a falsehood even in jest” —

mn61:7.11.verse: that is how you should train, Rāhula.’

mn61:8.2.verse: what is the purpose of a looking-glass?’

mn61:8.3.verse: ‘For the purpose of reflection, venerable sir.’

mn61:8.4.verse: ‘So too, Rāhula, bodily kamma should be done with continual reflection, verbal kamma should be done with continual reflection, mental kamma should be done with continual reflection.

mn61:9.1.verse: ‘Rāhula, whatever kamma you desire to do by the body, that same bodily kamma of yours should be reviewed thus:

mn61:9.2.verse: “Would this kamma that I desire to do by the body lead to the affliction of myself, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both—

mn61:9.3.verse: is it unprofitable bodily kamma with painful consequences, with painful results?”

mn61:9.4.verse: If, when you review it, you know thus:

mn61:9.5.verse: “This kamma that I desire to do by the body would lead to the affliction of myself, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both—

mn61:9.6.verse: it is unprofitable bodily kamma with painful consequences, with painful results”, then such kamma of body is definitely not to be done by you.

mn61:9.7.verse: But if, when you review it, you know thus:

mn61:9.8.verse: “This kamma that I desire to do by the body would not lead to the affliction of myself, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both—

mn61:9.9.verse: it is profitable bodily kamma with pleasant consequences, with pleasant results”, then such kamma of body may be done by you.

mn61:10.1.verse: ‘While you are doing a kamma by the body, that same bodily kamma of yours should be reviewed thus:

mn61:10.2.verse: “Does this kamma that I am doing by the body lead to the affliction of myself, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both—

mn61:10.3.verse: is it unprofitable bodily kamma with painful consequences, with painful results?”

mn61:10.4.verse: If, when you review it, you know thus:

mn61:10.5.verse: “This kamma that I am doing by the body leads to the affliction of myself, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both—

mn61:10.7.verse: But if, when you review it, you know thus:

mn61:10.8.verse: “This kamma that I am doing by the body does not lead to the affliction of myself, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both—

mn61:10.9.verse: it is profitable bodily kamma with pleasant consequences, with pleasant results”, you may continue with such bodily kamma.

mn61:11.1.verse: ‘Having done a kamma by the body, that same bodily kamma of yours should be reviewed thus:

mn61:11.2.verse: “Did this kamma that I did by the body lead to the affliction of myself, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both—

mn61:11.3.verse: is it unprofitable bodily kamma with painful consequences, with painful results?”

mn61:12.8.verse: “This kamma that I desire to do by speech would not lead to the affliction of myself, nor to the affliction of others—

mn61:12.9.verse: it is profitable verbal kamma with pleasant consequences, with pleasant results”, then such kamma of speech may be done by you.

mn61:18.1.verse: ‘Whatever monks or divines there have been in the past who purified their bodily kamma, their verbal kamma and their mental kamma, all of them did so by repeatedly reviewing in just this way.

mn61:18.2.verse: Whatever monks or divines there will be in the future who will purify their bodily kamma, their verbal kamma and their mental kamma, all of them will do so by repeatedly reviewing in just this way.

mn61:18.3.verse: Whatever monks or divines there are now who are purifying their bodily kamma, their verbal kamma and their mental kamma, all of them do so by repeatedly reviewing in just this way.

mn61:18.4.verse: Therefore, Rāhula, you should train thus: “We shall purify our bodily kamma, our verbal kamma and our mental kamma by repeatedly reviewing them”—

mn61:18.5.verse: that is how you should train, Rāhula.’

mn61:18.6.verse: This is what the Blessed One said.

mn61:18.7.verse: The venerable Rāhula was satisfied, and he delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn61:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

mn61:2.1.verse: Now at that time Venerable Rāhula was staying at Ambalaṭṭhikā.

mn61:2.2.verse: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and went to Ambalaṭṭhika to see Venerable Rāhula.

mn61:2.3.verse: Rāhula saw the Buddha coming off in the distance.

mn61:2.4.verse: He spread out a seat and placed water for washing the feet.

mn61:2.5.verse: The Buddha sat down on the seat spread out,

mn61:2.7.verse: Rāhula bowed to the Buddha and sat down to one side.

mn61:3.1.verse: Then the Buddha, leaving a little water in the pot, addressed Rāhula,

mn61:3.2.verse: “Rāhula, do you see this little bit of water left in the pot?”

mn61:3.4.verse: “That’s how little of the ascetic’s nature is left in those who are not ashamed to tell a deliberate lie.”

mn61:4.1.verse: Then the Buddha, discarding what little water was left in the pot, said to Rāhula,

mn61:4.2.verse: “Do you see this little bit of water that was discarded?”

mn61:4.4.verse: “That’s how the ascetic’s nature is discarded in those who are not ashamed to tell a deliberate lie.”

mn61:5.1.verse: Then the Buddha, turning the pot upside down, said to Rāhula,

mn61:5.2.verse: “Do you see how this pot is turned upside down?”

mn61:5.4.verse: “That’s how the ascetic’s nature is turned upside down in those who are not ashamed to tell a deliberate lie.”

mn61:6.1.verse: Then the Buddha, turning the pot right side up, said to Rāhula,

mn61:6.2.verse: “Do you see how this pot is vacant and hollow?”

mn61:6.4.verse: “That’s how vacant and hollow the ascetic’s nature is in those who are not ashamed to tell a deliberate lie.

mn61:7.1.verse: Suppose there was a royal bull elephant with tusks like draft-poles, able to draw a heavy load, pedigree and battle-hardened. In battle it uses its fore-feet and hind-feet, its fore-quarters and hind-quarters, its head, ears, tusks, and tail, but it still protects its trunk.

mn61:7.3.verse: ‘This royal bull elephant still protects its trunk.

mn61:7.4.verse: It has not yet given its life.’

mn61:7.5.verse: But when that royal bull elephant … in battle uses its fore-feet and hind-feet, its fore-quarters and hind-quarters, its head, ears, tusks, and tail, and its trunk, its rider thinks:

mn61:7.6.verse: ‘This royal bull elephant … in battle uses its fore-feet and hind-feet, its fore-quarters and hind-quarters, its head, ears, tusks, and tail, and its trunk.

mn61:7.8.verse: Now there is nothing that royal bull elephant would not do.’

mn61:7.9.verse: In the same way, when someone is not ashamed to tell a deliberate lie, there is no bad deed they would not do, I say.

mn61:7.10.verse: So you should train like this: ‘I will not tell a lie, even for a joke.’

mn61:8.2.verse: What is the purpose of a mirror?”

mn61:8.4.verse: “In the same way, deeds of body, speech, and mind should be done only after repeated checking.

mn61:9.1.verse: When you want to act with the body, you should check on that same deed:

mn61:9.2.verse: ‘Does this act with the body that I want to do lead to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both?

mn61:9.3.verse: Is it unskillful, with suffering as its outcome and result?’

mn61:9.4.verse: If, while checking in this way, you know:

mn61:9.5.verse: ‘This act with the body that I want to do leads to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both.

mn61:9.6.verse: It’s unskillful, with suffering as its outcome and result.’ To the best of your ability, Rāhula, you should not do such a deed.

mn61:9.7.verse: But if, while checking in this way, you know:

mn61:9.8.verse: ‘This act with the body that I want to do doesn’t lead to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both.

mn61:9.9.verse: It’s skillful, with happiness as its outcome and result.’ Then, Rāhula, you should do such a deed.

mn61:10.1.verse: While you are acting with the body, you should check on that same act:

mn61:10.2.verse: ‘Does this act with the body that I am doing lead to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both?

mn61:10.3.verse: Is it unskillful, with suffering as its outcome and result?’

mn61:10.4.verse: If, while checking in this way, you know:

mn61:10.5.verse: ‘This act with the body that I am doing leads to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both.

mn61:10.6.verse: It’s unskillful, with suffering as its outcome and result.’ Then, Rāhula, you should desist from such a deed.

mn61:10.7.verse: But if, while checking in this way, you know:

mn61:10.8.verse: ‘This act with the body that I am doing doesn’t lead to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both.

mn61:10.9.verse: It’s skillful, with happiness as its outcome and result.’ Then, Rāhula, you should continue doing such a deed.

mn61:11.1.verse: After you have acted with the body, you should check on that same act:

mn61:11.2.verse: ‘Does this act with the body that I have done lead to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both?

mn61:11.3.verse: Is it unskillful, with suffering as its outcome and result?’

mn61:11.4.verse: If, while checking in this way, you know:

mn61:11.5.verse: ‘This act with the body that I have done leads to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both.

mn61:11.6.verse: It’s unskillful, with suffering as its outcome and result.’ Then, Rāhula, you should confess, reveal, and clarify such a deed to the Teacher or a sensible spiritual companion.

mn61:11.7.verse: And having revealed it you should restrain yourself in future.

mn61:11.8.verse: But if, while checking in this way, you know:

mn61:11.9.verse: ‘This act with the body that I have done doesn’t lead to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both.

mn61:11.10.verse: It’s skillful, with happiness as its outcome and result.’ Then, Rāhula, you should live in rapture and joy because of this, training day and night in skillful qualities.

mn61:12.1.verse: When you want to act with speech, you should check on that same deed:

mn61:12.2.verse: ‘Does this act of speech that I want to do lead to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both? …’ …

mn61:14.4.verse: If, while checking in this way, you know:

mn61:14.5.verse: ‘This act of speech that I have done leads to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both.

mn61:14.6.verse: It’s unskillful, with suffering as its outcome and result.’ Then, Rāhula, you should confess, reveal, and clarify such a deed to the Teacher or a sensible spiritual companion.

mn61:14.7.verse: And having revealed it you should restrain yourself in future.

mn61:14.8.verse: But if, while checking in this way, you know:

mn61:14.9.verse: ‘This act of speech that I have done doesn’t lead to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both.

mn61:14.10.verse: It’s skillful, with happiness as its outcome and result.’ Then, Rāhula, you should live in rapture and joy because of this, training day and night in skillful qualities.

mn61:15.1.verse: When you want to act with the mind, you should check on that same deed:

mn61:15.2.verse: ‘Does this act of mind that I want to do lead to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both? …’ …

mn61:17.4.verse: If, while checking in this way, you know:

mn61:17.5.verse: ‘This act of mind that I have done leads to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both.

mn61:17.6.verse: It’s unskillful, with suffering as its outcome and result.’ Then, Rāhula, you should be horrified, repelled, and disgusted by that deed.

mn61:17.7.verse: And being repelled, you should restrain yourself in future.

mn61:17.8.verse: But if, while checking in this way, you know:

mn61:17.9.verse: ‘This act with the mind that I have done doesn’t lead to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both.

mn61:17.10.verse: It’s skillful, with happiness as its outcome and result.’ Then, Rāhula, you should live in rapture and joy because of this, training day and night in skillful qualities.

mn61:18.1.verse: All the ascetics and brahmins of the past, future, and present who purify their physical, verbal, and mental actions do so after repeatedly checking.

mn61:18.4.verse: So Rāhula, you should train yourself like this: ‘I will purify my physical, verbal, and mental actions after repeatedly checking.’”

mn61:18.6.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn61:18.7.verse: Satisfied, Venerable Rāhula approved what the Buddha said.

mn62:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn62:2.1.verse: Then the Blessed One, early in the morning, adjusted his lower robe and, taking his bowl & outer robe, went into Sāvatthī for alms.

mn62:2.2.verse: And Ven. Rāhula, early in the morning, adjusted his lower robe and, taking his bowl & outer robe, went into Sāvatthī for alms following right behind the Blessed One.

mn62:3.1.verse: Then the Blessed One, looking back at Rāhula, addressed him:

mn62:3.2.verse: “Rāhula, any form whatsoever that is past, future, or present; internal or external; blatant or subtle; common or sublime; far or near: Every form is to be seen as it has come to be with right discernment as: ‘This is not mine. This is not my self. This is not what I am.’”

mn62:3.3.verse: “Just form, O Blessed One? Just form, O One Well-Gone?”

mn62:4.1.verse: Then the thought occurred to Ven. Rāhula, “Who, having been exhorted face-to-face by the Blessed One, would go into the town for alms today?” So he turned back and sat down at the foot of a tree, folding his legs crosswise, holding his body erect, & establishing mindfulness to the fore.

mn62:5.1.verse: Ven. Sāriputta saw Ven. Rāhula sitting at the foot of a tree, his legs folded crosswise, his body held erect, & with mindfulness set to the fore.

mn62:5.2.verse: On seeing him, he said to him,

mn62:5.3.verse: “Rāhula, develop the meditation [bhāvanā] of mindfulness of in-&-out breathing.

mn62:5.4.verse: The meditation of mindfulness of in-&-out breathing, when developed & pursued, is of great fruit, of great benefit.”

mn62:6.1.verse: Then Ven. Rāhula, emerging from his seclusion in the evening, went to the Blessed One and, having bowed down to him, sat to one side. As he was sitting there he said to the Blessed One,

mn62:7.1.verse: “How, lord, is mindfulness of in-&-out breathing to be developed & pursued so as to be of great fruit, or great benefit?”

mn62:8.1.verse:
{“Rāhula, any form whatsoever that is past, future, or present; internal or external; blatant or subtle; common or sublime; far or near: Every form is to be seen as it has come to be with right discernment as: ‘This is not mine. This is not my self. This is not what I am.’ There are these five properties, Rāhula. Which five? The earth property, the water property, the fire property, the wind property, & the space property.

“And what is the earth property? The earth property may be either internal or external. What is the internal earth property?} Anything internal, within oneself, that’s hard, solid, & sustained (by craving):

mn62:8.2.verse: head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, tendons, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, membranes, spleen, lungs, large intestines, small intestines, contents of the stomach, feces, or anything else internal, within oneself, that’s hard, solid, and sustained:

mn62:8.3.verse: This is called the internal earth property.

mn62:8.4.verse: Now both the internal earth property & the external earth property are simply earth property.

mn62:8.5.verse: And that should be seen as it has come to be with right discernment: ‘This is not mine, this is not what I am, this is not my self.’

mn62:8.6.verse: When one sees it thus as it has come to be with right discernment, one becomes disenchanted with the earth property and makes the earth property fade from the mind.

mn62:9.2.verse: The water property may be either internal or external.

mn62:9.3.verse: What is the internal water property?

mn62:9.4.verse: Anything internal, within oneself, that’s water, watery, & sustained:

mn62:9.5.verse: bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, oil, saliva, mucus, oil-of-the-joints, urine, or anything else internal, within oneself, that’s water, watery, & sustained:

mn62:9.6.verse: This is called the internal water property.

mn62:9.7.verse: Now both the internal water property & the external water property are simply water property.

mn62:9.8.verse: And that should be seen as it has come to be with right discernment: ‘This is not mine, this is not what I am, this is not my self.’

mn62:9.9.verse: When one sees it thus as it has come to be with right discernment, one becomes disenchanted with the water property and makes the water property fade from the mind.

mn62:10.2.verse: The fire property may be either internal or external.

mn62:10.3.verse: What is the internal fire property?

mn62:10.4.verse: Anything internal, within oneself, that’s fire, fiery, & sustained:

mn62:10.5.verse: that by which (the body) is warmed, aged, & consumed with fever; and that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, & savored gets properly digested; or anything else internal, within oneself, that’s fire, fiery, & sustained:

mn62:10.6.verse: This is called the internal fire property.

mn62:10.7.verse: Now both the internal fire property & the external fire property are simply fire property.

mn62:10.8.verse: And that should be seen as it has come to be with right discernment: ‘This is not mine, this is not what I am, this is not my self.’

mn62:10.9.verse: When one sees it thus as it has come to be with right discernment, one becomes disenchanted with the fire property and makes the fire property fade from the mind.

mn62:11.2.verse: The wind property may be either internal or external.

mn62:11.3.verse: What is the internal wind property?

mn62:11.4.verse: Anything internal, within oneself, that’s wind, windy, & sustained:

mn62:11.5.verse: up-going winds, down-going winds, winds in the stomach, winds in the intestines, winds that course through the body, in-and-out breathing, or anything else internal, within oneself, that’s wind, windy, & sustained:

mn62:11.6.verse: This is called the internal wind property.

mn62:11.7.verse: Now both the internal wind property & the external wind property are simply wind property.

mn62:11.8.verse: And that should be seen as it has come to be with right discernment: ‘This is not mine, this is not what I am, this is not my self.’

mn62:11.9.verse: When one sees it thus as it has come to be with right discernment, one becomes disenchanted with the wind property and makes the wind property fade from the mind.

mn62:12.2.verse: The space property may be either internal or external.

mn62:12.3.verse: What is the internal space property?

mn62:12.4.verse: Anything internal, within oneself, that’s space, spatial, & sustained:

mn62:12.5.verse: the holes of the ears, the nostrils, the mouth, the (passage) whereby what is eaten, drunk, consumed, & tasted gets swallowed, and where it collects, and whereby it is excreted from below, or anything else internal, within oneself, that’s space, spatial, & sustained:

mn62:12.6.verse: This is called the internal space property.

mn62:12.7.verse: Now both the internal space property & the external space property are simply space property.

mn62:12.8.verse: And that should be seen as it has come to be with right discernment: ‘This is not mine, this is not what I am, this is not my self.’

mn62:12.9.verse: When one sees it thus as it has come to be with right discernment, one becomes disenchanted with the space property and makes the space property fade from the mind.

mn62:13.1.verse: “Rāhula, develop the meditation in tune with earth.

mn62:13.2.verse: For when you are developing the meditation in tune with earth, agreeable & disagreeable sensory impressions that have arisen will not stay in charge of your mind.

mn62:13.3.verse: Just as when people throw what is clean or unclean on the earth—feces, urine, saliva, pus, or blood—the earth is not horrified, humiliated, or disgusted by it;

mn62:13.4.verse: in the same way, when you are developing the meditation in tune with earth,

mn62:13.5.verse: agreeable & disagreeable sensory impressions that have arisen will not stay in charge of your mind.

mn62:14.1.verse: “Develop the meditation in tune with water.

mn62:14.2.verse: For when you are developing the meditation in tune with water, agreeable & disagreeable sensory impressions that have arisen will not stay in charge of your mind.

mn62:14.3.verse: Just as when people wash what is clean or unclean in water—feces, urine, saliva, pus, or blood—the water is not horrified, humiliated, or disgusted by it;

mn62:14.4.verse: in the same way, when you are developing the meditation in tune with water,

mn62:14.5.verse: agreeable & disagreeable sensory impressions that have arisen will not stay in charge of your mind.

mn62:15.1.verse: “Develop the meditation in tune with fire.

mn62:15.2.verse: For when you are developing the meditation in tune with fire, agreeable & disagreeable sensory impressions that have arisen will not stay in charge of your mind.

mn62:15.3.verse: Just as when fire burns what is clean or unclean—feces, urine, saliva, pus, or blood—it is not horrified, humiliated, or disgusted by it;

mn62:15.4.verse: in the same way, when you are developing the meditation in tune with fire,

mn62:15.5.verse: agreeable & disagreeable sensory impressions that have arisen will not stay in charge of your mind.

mn62:16.1.verse: “Develop the meditation in tune with wind.

mn62:16.2.verse: For when you are developing the meditation in tune with wind, agreeable & disagreeable sensory impressions that have arisen will not stay in charge of your mind.

mn62:16.3.verse: Just as when wind blows what is clean or unclean—feces, urine, saliva, pus, or blood—it is not horrified, humiliated, or disgusted by it;

mn62:16.4.verse: in the same way, when you are developing the meditation in tune with wind,

mn62:16.5.verse: agreeable & disagreeable sensory impressions that have arisen will not stay in charge of your mind.

mn62:17.1.verse: “Develop the meditation in tune with space.

mn62:17.2.verse: For when you are developing the meditation in tune with space, agreeable & disagreeable sensory impressions that have arisen will not stay in charge of your mind.

mn62:17.3.verse: Just as space is not established anywhere,

mn62:17.4.verse: in the same way, when you are developing the meditation in tune with space,

mn62:17.5.verse: agreeable & disagreeable sensory impressions that have arisen will not stay in charge of your mind.

mn62:18.2.verse: For when you are developing the meditation of goodwill, ill-will will be abandoned.

mn62:19.2.verse: For when you are developing the meditation of compassion, harmfulness will be abandoned.

mn62:20.2.verse: For when you are developing the meditation of empathetic joy, resentment will be abandoned.

mn62:21.1.verse: For when you are developing the meditation of equanimity, irritation will be abandoned.

mn62:22.2.verse: For when you are developing the meditation of the unattractive, passion will be abandoned.

mn62:23.1.verse: “Develop the meditation of the perception of inconstancy.

mn62:23.2.verse: For when you are developing the meditation of the perception of inconstancy, the conceit ‘I am’ will be abandoned.

mn62:24.1.verse: “Develop the meditation of mindfulness of in-&-out breathing.

mn62:24.2.verse: Mindfulness of in-&-out breathing, when developed & pursued, is of great fruit, of great benefit.

mn62:24.3.verse: “And how, Rāhula, is mindfulness of in-&-out breathing developed & pursued so as to be of great fruit, of great benefit?

mn62:25.1.verse: “There is the case where a monk, having gone to the wilderness, to the shade of a tree, or to an empty building, sits down folding his legs crosswise, holding his body erect, and establishing mindfulness to the fore.

mn62:25.2.verse: Always mindful, he breathes in; mindful he breathes out.

mn62:26.1.verse: “[1] Breathing in long, he discerns, ‘I am breathing in long’; or breathing out long, he discerns, ‘I am breathing out long.’

mn62:26.2.verse: [2] Or breathing in short, he discerns, ‘I am breathing in short’; or breathing out short, he discerns, ‘I am breathing out short.’

mn62:26.3.verse: [3] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in sensitive to the entire body.’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out sensitive to the entire body.’

mn62:26.4.verse: [4] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in calming bodily fabrication.’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out calming bodily fabrication.’

mn62:27.1.verse: “[5] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in sensitive to rapture.’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out sensitive to rapture.’

mn62:27.2.verse: [6] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in sensitive to pleasure.’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out sensitive to pleasure.’

mn62:27.3.verse: [7] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in sensitive to mental fabrication.’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out sensitive to mental fabrication.’

mn62:27.4.verse: [8] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in calming mental fabrication.’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out calming mental fabrication.’

mn62:28.1.verse: “[9] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in sensitive to the mind.’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out sensitive to the mind.’

mn62:28.2.verse: [10] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in satisfying the mind.’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out satisfying the mind.’

mn62:28.3.verse: [11] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in concentrating the mind.’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out concentrating the mind.’

mn62:28.4.verse: [12] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in releasing the mind.’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out releasing the mind.’

mn62:29.1.verse: “[13] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in focusing on inconstancy.’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out focusing on inconstancy.’

mn62:29.2.verse: [14] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in focusing on dispassion [lit: fading].’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out focusing on dispassion.’

mn62:29.3.verse: [15] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in focusing on cessation.’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out focusing on cessation.’

mn62:29.4.verse: [16] He trains himself, ‘I will breathe in focusing on relinquishment.’ He trains himself, ‘I will breathe out focusing on relinquishment.’

mn62:30.1.verse: “This, Rāhula, is how mindfulness of in-&-out breathing is developed & pursued so as to be of great fruit, of great benefit.

mn62:30.2.verse: “When mindfulness of in-&-out breathing is developed & pursued in this way, even one’s final in-breaths & out-breaths are known as they cease, not unknown.”

mn62:30.3.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

mn62:30.4.verse: Gratified, Ven. Rāhula delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn62:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn62:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

mn62:2.2.verse: And Venerable Rāhula also robed up and followed behind the Buddha.

mn62:3.1.verse: Then the Buddha looked back at Rāhula and said,

mn62:3.2.verse: “Rāhula, you should truly see any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’”

mn62:3.3.verse: “Only form, Blessed One? Only form, Holy One?”

mn62:3.4.verse: “Form, Rāhula, as well as feeling and perception and choices and consciousness.”

mn62:4.1.verse: Then Rāhula thought, “Who would go to the village for alms today after being advised directly by the Buddha?” Turning back, he sat down cross-legged at the root of a certain tree, setting his body straight, and bringing mindfulness to the present.

mn62:5.1.verse: Venerable Sāriputta saw him sitting there,

mn62:5.4.verse: When mindfulness of breathing is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial.”

mn62:6.1.verse: Then in the late afternoon, Rāhula came out of retreat, went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

mn62:7.1.verse: “Sir, how is mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated to be very fruitful and beneficial?”

mn62:8.1.verse: “Rāhula, the interior earth element is anything internal, personal, that’s hard, solid, and appropriated. This includes:

mn62:8.2.verse: head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, diaphragm, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, undigested food, feces; or anything else internal, personal, that’s hard, solid, and appropriated.

mn62:8.3.verse: This is called the interior earth element.

mn62:8.4.verse: The interior earth element and the exterior earth element are just the earth element.

mn62:8.5.verse: This should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

mn62:8.6.verse: When you truly see with right understanding, you grow disillusioned with the earth element, detaching the mind from the earth element.

mn62:9.1.verse: And what is the water element?

mn62:9.2.verse: The water element may be interior or exterior.

mn62:9.3.verse: And what is the interior water element?

mn62:9.4.verse: Anything internal, personal, that’s water, watery, and appropriated. This includes:

mn62:9.5.verse: bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, urine; or anything else internal, personal, that’s water, watery, and appropriated.

mn62:9.6.verse: This is called the interior water element.

mn62:9.7.verse: The interior water element and the exterior water element are just the water element.

mn62:9.8.verse: This should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

mn62:9.9.verse: When you truly see with right understanding, you grow disillusioned with the water element, detaching the mind from the water element.

mn62:10.1.verse: And what is the fire element?

mn62:10.2.verse: The fire element may be interior or exterior.

mn62:10.3.verse: And what is the interior fire element?

mn62:10.4.verse: Anything internal, personal, that’s fire, fiery, and appropriated. This includes:

mn62:10.5.verse: that which warms, that which ages, that which heats you up when feverish, that which properly digests food and drink; or anything else internal, personal, that’s fire, fiery, and appropriated.

mn62:10.6.verse: This is called the interior fire element.

mn62:10.7.verse: The interior fire element and the exterior fire element are just the fire element.

mn62:10.8.verse: This should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

mn62:10.9.verse: When you truly see with right understanding, you grow disillusioned with the fire element, detaching the mind from the fire element.

mn62:11.1.verse: And what is the air element?

mn62:11.2.verse: The air element may be interior or exterior.

mn62:11.3.verse: And what is the interior air element?

mn62:11.4.verse: Anything internal, personal, that’s air, airy, and appropriated. This includes:

mn62:11.5.verse: winds that go up or down, winds in the belly or the bowels, winds that flow through the limbs, in-breaths and out-breaths; or anything else internal, personal, that’s air, airy, and appropriated.

mn62:11.6.verse: This is called the interior air element.

mn62:11.7.verse: The interior air element and the exterior air element are just the air element.

mn62:11.8.verse: This should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

mn62:11.9.verse: When you truly see with right understanding, you grow disillusioned with the air element, detaching the mind from the air element.

mn62:12.1.verse: And what is the space element?

mn62:12.2.verse: The space element may be interior or exterior.

mn62:12.3.verse: And what is the interior space element?

mn62:12.4.verse: Anything internal, personal, that’s space, spacious, and appropriated. This includes:

mn62:12.5.verse: the ear canals, nostrils, and mouth; and the space for swallowing what is eaten and drunk, the space where it stays, and the space for excreting it from the nether regions; or anything else internal, personal, that’s space, spacious, and appropriated.

mn62:12.6.verse: This is called the interior space element.

mn62:12.7.verse: The interior space element and the exterior space element are just the space element.

mn62:12.8.verse: This should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

mn62:12.9.verse: When you truly see with right understanding, you grow disillusioned with the space element, detaching the mind from the space element.

mn62:13.2.verse: For when you meditate like the earth, pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not occupy your mind.

mn62:13.3.verse: Suppose they were to toss both clean and unclean things on the earth, like feces, urine, spit, pus, and blood. The earth isn’t horrified, repelled, and disgusted because of this.

mn62:13.4.verse: In the same way, meditate like the earth.

mn62:13.5.verse: For when you meditate like the earth, pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not occupy your mind.

mn62:14.2.verse: For when you meditate like water, pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not occupy your mind.

mn62:14.3.verse: Suppose they were to wash both clean and unclean things in the water, like feces, urine, spit, pus, and blood. The water isn’t horrified, repelled, and disgusted because of this.

mn62:14.4.verse: In the same way, meditate like water.

mn62:14.5.verse: For when you meditate like water, pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not occupy your mind.

mn62:15.2.verse: For when you meditate like fire, pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not occupy your mind.

mn62:15.3.verse: Suppose a fire were to burn both clean and unclean things, like feces, urine, spit, pus, and blood. The fire isn’t horrified, repelled, and disgusted because of this.

mn62:15.4.verse: In the same way, meditate like fire.

mn62:15.5.verse: For when you meditate like fire, pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not occupy your mind.

mn62:16.2.verse: For when you meditate like wind, pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not occupy your mind.

mn62:16.3.verse: Suppose the wind were to blow on both clean and unclean things, like feces, urine, spit, pus, and blood. The wind isn’t horrified, repelled, and disgusted because of this.

mn62:16.4.verse: In the same way, meditate like the wind.

mn62:16.5.verse: For when you meditate like wind, pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not occupy your mind.

mn62:17.2.verse: For when you meditate like space, pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not occupy your mind.

mn62:17.3.verse: Just as space is not established anywhere,

mn62:17.4.verse: in the same way, meditate like space.

mn62:17.5.verse: For when you meditate like space, pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not occupy your mind.

mn62:18.2.verse: For when you meditate on love any ill will will be given up.

mn62:19.2.verse: For when you meditate on compassion any cruelty will be given up.

mn62:20.2.verse: For when you meditate on rejoicing any discontent will be given up.

mn62:21.2.verse: For when you meditate on equanimity any aversion will be given up.

mn62:22.2.verse: For when you meditate on ugliness any lust will be given up.

mn62:23.2.verse: For when you meditate on impermanence any conceit ‘I am’ will be given up.

mn62:24.2.verse: When mindfulness of breathing is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial.

mn62:24.3.verse: And how is mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated to be very fruitful and beneficial?

mn62:25.1.verse: It’s when a mendicant—gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut—sits down cross-legged, sets their body straight, and brings mindfulness to the present.

mn62:25.2.verse: Just mindful, they breathe in. Mindful, they breathe out.

mn62:26.1.verse: Breathing in heavily they know: ‘I’m breathing in heavily.’ Breathing out heavily they know: ‘I’m breathing out heavily.’

mn62:26.2.verse: Breathing in lightly they know: ‘I’m breathing in lightly.’ Breathing out lightly they know: ‘I’m breathing out lightly.’

mn62:26.3.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in experiencing the whole body.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out experiencing the whole body.’

mn62:26.4.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in stilling the physical process.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out stilling the physical process.’

mn62:27.1.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in experiencing rapture.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out experiencing rapture.’

mn62:27.2.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in experiencing bliss.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out experiencing bliss.’

mn62:27.3.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in experiencing the mental process.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out experiencing the mental process.’

mn62:27.4.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in stilling the mental process.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out stilling the mental process.’

mn62:28.1.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in experiencing the mind.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out experiencing the mind.’

mn62:28.2.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in gladdening the mind.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out gladdening the mind.’

mn62:28.3.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in immersing the mind in samādhi.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out immersing the mind in samādhi.’

mn62:28.4.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in freeing the mind.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out freeing the mind.’

mn62:29.1.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in observing impermanence.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out observing impermanence.’

mn62:29.2.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in observing fading away.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out observing fading away.’

mn62:29.3.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in observing cessation.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out observing cessation.’

mn62:29.4.verse: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in observing letting go.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out observing letting go.’

mn62:30.1.verse: Mindfulness of breathing, when developed and cultivated in this way, is very fruitful and beneficial.

mn62:30.2.verse: When mindfulness of breathing is developed and cultivated in this way, even as the final breaths cease they are known, not unknown.”

mn62:30.3.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn62:30.4.verse: Satisfied, Venerable Rāhula approved what the Buddha said.

mn63:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

mn63:2.1.verse: Then while the venerable Māluṅkyaputta was alone in meditation the following thought arose in his mind:

mn63:2.2.verse: ‘There are these fields of views undeclared by the Blessed One, set aside and avoided by him:

mn63:2.3.verse: “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal” or “the world is finite” or “the world is infinite” or “the soul is the same as the body” or “the soul is one and the body another” or “after death a Tathāgata is” or “after death a Tathāgata is not” or “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not” or “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—

mn63:2.4.verse: the Blessed One does not declare these to me.

mn63:2.5.verse: And it is not to my preference and liking that he does not declare them to me.

mn63:2.6.verse: So I shall go to the Blessed One and ask him the meaning of this.

mn63:2.8.verse: “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal” …

mn63:2.9.verse: … “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—

mn63:2.10.verse: then I will live the life divine under the Blessed One;

mn63:2.11.verse: but if the Blessed One does not declare to me:

mn63:2.12.verse: “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal” …

mn63:2.13.verse: … “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—

mn63:2.14.verse: then I will abandon the training and revert to the lower life.’

mn63:3.1.verse: Then when it was evening, the venerable Māluṅkyaputta rose from meditation, and went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, the venerable Māluṅkyaputta said to the Blessed One:

mn63:3.2.verse: ‘Venerable sir, while I was alone in meditation the following thought arose in my mind—

mn63:3.3.verse: there are these fields of views undeclared by the Blessed One, set aside and avoided by him:

mn63:3.4.verse: “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal” …

mn63:3.5.verse: … “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—

mn63:3.6.verse: the Blessed One does not declare these to me.

mn63:3.7.verse: And it is not to my preference and liking that he does not declare them to me.

mn63:3.8.verse: So I shall go to the Blessed One and ask him the meaning of this.

mn63:3.10.verse: “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal” …

mn63:3.11.verse: … “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—

mn63:3.12.verse: then I will live the life divine under the Blessed One.

mn63:3.13.verse: But if the Blessed One does not declare to me:

mn63:3.14.verse: “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal” …

mn63:3.15.verse: … “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—

mn63:3.16.verse: then I will abandon the training and revert to the lower life.’

mn63:3.18.verse: “the world is eternal”, let the Blessed One declare to me “the world is eternal”;

mn63:3.20.verse: “the world is not eternal”, let the Blessed One declare to me “the world is not eternal”.

mn63:3.21.verse: If the Blessed One does not know

mn63:3.22.verse: either “the world is eternal” or “the world is not eternal”, then it is straightforward for one who does not know and does not see (to say):

mn63:3.23.verse: “I do not know, I do not see.”

mn63:3.25.verse: “the world is finite”, let the Blessed One declare to me “the world is finite”;

mn63:3.27.verse: “the world is infinite”, let the Blessed One declare to me “the world is infinite”.

mn63:3.28.verse: If the Blessed One does not know

mn63:3.29.verse: either “the world is finite” or “the world is infinite”, then it is straightforward for one who does not know and does not see (to say):

mn63:3.30.verse: “I do not know, I do not see.”

mn63:3.32.verse: “the soul is the same as the body”, let the Blessed One declare to me “the soul is the same as the body”;

mn63:3.34.verse: “the soul is one and the body another”, let the Blessed One declare to me “the soul is one and the body another”.

mn63:3.35.verse: If the Blessed One does not know

mn63:3.36.verse: either “the soul is the same as the body” or “the soul is one and the body another”, then it is straightforward for one who does not know and does not see (to say):

mn63:3.37.verse: “I do not know, I do not see.”

mn63:3.39.verse: “after death a Tathāgata is”, let the Blessed One declare to me “after death a Tathāgata is”;

mn63:3.41.verse: “after death a Tathāgata is not”, let the Blessed One declare to me “after death a Tathāgata is not”.

mn63:3.42.verse: If the Blessed One does not know

mn63:3.43.verse: either “after death a Tathāgata is” or “after death a Tathāgata is not”, then it is straightforward for one who does not know and does not see (to say):

mn63:3.44.verse: “I do not know, I do not see.”

mn63:3.46.verse: “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not”, let the Blessed One declare to me “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not”;

mn63:3.48.verse: “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”, let the Blessed One declare to me “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”.

mn63:3.49.verse: If the Blessed One does not know

mn63:3.50.verse: either “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not” or “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”, then it is straightforward for one who does not know and does not see (to say):

mn63:3.51.verse: “I do not know, I do not see.”’

mn63:4.1.verse: ‘How then, Māluṅkyaputta, did I ever say to you:

mn63:4.2.verse: “Come, Māluṅkyaputta, live the life divine under me and I will declare to you:

mn63:4.3.verse: ‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’ or ‘the world is finite’ or ‘the world is infinite’ or ‘the soul is the same as the body’ or ‘the soul is one and the body another’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata is’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata is not’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata both is and is not’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not’”?’

mn63:4.6.verse: “Venerable sir, I will live the life divine under the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will declare to me:

mn63:4.7.verse: ‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’ or ‘the world is finite’ or ‘the world is infinite’ or ‘the soul is the same as the body’ or ‘the soul is one and the body another’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata is’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata is not’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata both is and is not’ or ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not’”?’

mn63:4.9.verse: ‘So then, Māluṅkyaputta, I did not say to you:

mn63:4.10.verse: “Come, Māluṅkyaputta, live the life divine under me and I will declare to you:

mn63:4.11.verse: ‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’ …

mn63:4.12.verse: … ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not’”;

mn63:4.13.verse: nor did you say to me:

mn63:4.14.verse: “Venerable sir, I will live the life divine under the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will declare to me:

mn63:4.15.verse: ‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’ …

mn63:4.16.verse: … ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not’”.

mn63:4.17.verse: That being so, misguided man, what are you and what are you forsaking?

mn63:5.2.verse: “I will not live the life divine under the Blessed One until the Blessed One declares to me:

mn63:5.3.verse: ‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’ …

mn63:5.4.verse: … ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not’”,

mn63:5.5.verse: that would still remain undeclared by the Tathāgata and meanwhile that person would die.

mn63:5.6.verse: Suppose, Māluṅkyaputta, a man were wounded by an arrow thickly smeared with poison,

mn63:5.7.verse: and his friends and companions, his relatives and kin brought a surgeon to treat him.

mn63:5.9.verse: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know the man who wounded me, whether he is a warrior-noble or a brahmin or a merchant or a worker”;

mn63:5.11.verse: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know the name and clan of the man who wounded me”;

mn63:5.13.verse: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know whether the man who wounded me is tall or short or of middle height”;

mn63:5.15.verse: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know whether the man who wounded me is dark or brown or golden-skinned”;

mn63:5.17.verse: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know whether the man who wounded me lives in such a village or town or city”;

mn63:5.19.verse: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know the bow that wounded me, whether it was a long bow or a crossbow”;

mn63:5.21.verse: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know the bowstring that wounded me, whether it was made of swallow-wort fibre, or reed, or sinew, or hemp, or bark”;[^1]

mn63:5.23.verse: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know the shaft that wounded me, whether it was wild or cultivated”;

mn63:5.25.verse: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know with whose feathers the shaft that wounded me was feathered, whether a vulture’s, or a crow’s, or a hawk’s, or a peacock’s, or a stork’s”;[^2]

mn63:5.27.verse: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know with whose sinew the shaft that wounded me was bound, whether an ox’s, or a buffalo’s, or a lion’s, or a monkey’s”;[^3]

mn63:5.29.verse: “I will not have this arrow pulled out until I know the arrowhead that wounded me, whether it was hoof-tipped, or curved, or barbed, or calf-toothed, or shaped like an oleander leaf”—[^4]

mn63:5.30.verse: that would still not be known to that man and meanwhile he would die.

mn63:5.31.verse: So too, Māluṅkyaputta, if anyone should say thus:

mn63:5.32.verse: “I will not live the life divine under the Blessed One until the Blessed One declares to me:

mn63:5.33.verse: ‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’ …

mn63:5.34.verse: … ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not’”—

mn63:5.35.verse: that would still remain undeclared by the Tathāgata and meanwhile that person would die.

mn63:6.1.verse: ‘Māluṅkyaputta, there will never be any life divine while there is the view “the world is eternal”.

mn63:6.2.verse: And there will never be any life divine while there is the view “the world is not eternal”.

mn63:6.3.verse: And while there is the view “the world is eternal” or the view “the world is not eternal”, there is still birth, there is ageing, there is death, there are sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief and despair,

mn63:6.4.verse: of which I declare the destruction here and now.

mn63:6.5.verse: ‘There will never be any life divine while there is the view “the world is finite”.

mn63:6.6.verse: And there will never be any life divine while there is the view “the world is infinite”.

mn63:6.7.verse: And while there is the view “the world is finite” or the view “the world is infinite”, there is still birth, there is ageing, there is death, there are sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief and despair,

mn63:6.8.verse: of which I declare the destruction here and now.

mn63:6.9.verse: ‘There will never be any life divine while there is the view “the soul is the same as the body”.

mn63:6.10.verse: And there will never be any life divine while there is the view “the soul is one and the body another”.

mn63:6.11.verse: And while there is the view “the soul is the same as the body” or the view “the soul is one and the body another”, there is still birth …

mn63:6.12.verse: … of which I declare the destruction.

mn63:6.13.verse: ‘There will never be any life divine while there is the view “after death a Tathāgata is”.

mn63:6.14.verse: And there will never be any life divine while there is the view “after death a Tathāgata is not”.

mn63:6.15.verse: And while there is the view “after death a Tathāgata is” or the view “after death a Tathāgata is not”, there is still birth …

mn63:6.16.verse: … of which I declare the destruction here and now.

mn63:6.17.verse: ‘There will never be any life divine while there is the view “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not”.

mn63:6.18.verse: And there will never be any life divine while there is the view “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”.

mn63:6.19.verse: And while there is the view “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not” or the view “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”, there is still birth …

mn63:6.20.verse: … of which I declare the destruction here and now.

mn63:7.1.verse: ‘Consequently, Māluṅkyaputta, remember what is undeclared by me as undeclared,

mn63:7.2.verse: and remember what is declared by me as declared.

mn63:7.3.verse: And what is undeclared by me?

mn63:7.4.verse: “The world is eternal” is undeclared by me;

mn63:7.11.verse: “the soul is the same as the body”—

mn63:7.13.verse: “the soul is one and the body another”—

mn63:7.19.verse: “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not”—

mn63:7.21.verse: “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not”—

mn63:8.1.verse: ‘And why is that undeclared by me?

mn63:8.2.verse: It is because it is unconnected with the goal, it does not belong to the fundamentals of the life divine, it does not lead to dispassion, to fading away, to cessation, to peace, to direct-knowledge, to full-enlightenment, to Nibbāna.[^5]

mn63:8.3.verse: That is why it is undeclared by me.

mn63:9.2.verse: “This is suffering” is declared by me;

mn63:9.7.verse: “this is the way leading to the cessation of suffering”—

mn63:10.1.verse: ‘And why is that declared by me?
