mn70:8.13.verse: ‘For someone feeling a pleasant feeling of this sort, unskillful qualities decrease and skillful qualities grow,’ I therefore say, ‘Enter & remain in that sort of pleasant feeling.’

mn70:8.14.verse: If it were not known by me—not seen, not observed, not realized, not touched through discernment—that

mn70:8.15.verse: ‘For someone feeling a painful feeling of this sort, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decrease,’ then would it be fitting for me, not knowing that, to say,

mn70:9.1.verse: “But because it is known by me—seen, observed, realized, touched through discernment—that

mn70:9.2.verse: ‘For someone feeling a painful feeling of this sort, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decrease,’ I therefore say, ‘Abandon that sort of painful feeling.’

mn70:9.3.verse: If it were not known by me—not seen, not observed, not realized, not touched through discernment—that

mn70:9.4.verse: ‘For someone feeling a painful feeling of this sort, unskillful qualities decrease and skillful qualities grow,’ then would it be fitting for me, not knowing that, to say,

mn70:9.5.verse: ‘Enter & remain in that sort of painful feeling’?”

mn70:9.7.verse: “But because it is known by me—seen, observed, realized, touched through discernment—that

mn70:9.8.verse: ‘For someone feeling a painful feeling of this sort, unskillful qualities decrease and skillful qualities grow,’ I therefore say, ‘Enter & remain in that sort of painful feeling.’

mn70:10.1.verse: If it were not known by me—not seen, not observed, not realized, not touched through discernment—that

mn70:10.2.verse: ‘For someone feeling a neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling of this sort, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decrease,’ then would it be fitting for me, not knowing that, to say,

mn70:10.5.verse: “But because it is known by me—seen, observed, realized, touched through discernment—that

mn70:10.6.verse: ‘For someone feeling a neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling of this sort, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decrease,’ I therefore say, ‘Abandon that sort of neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling.’

mn70:10.7.verse: If it were not known by me—not seen, not observed, not realized, not touched through discernment—that

mn70:10.8.verse: ‘For someone feeling a neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling of this sort, unskillful qualities decrease and skillful qualities grow,’ then would it be fitting for me, not knowing that, to say,

mn70:10.9.verse: ‘Enter & remain in that sort of neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling’?”

mn70:11.1.verse: “But because it is known by me—seen, observed, realized, touched through discernment—that

mn70:11.2.verse: ‘For someone feeling a neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling of this sort, unskillful qualities decrease and skillful qualities grow,’ I therefore say, ‘Enter & remain in that sort of neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling.’

mn70:12.1.verse: “Monks, I don’t say of all monks that they have a task to do with heedfulness;

mn70:12.2.verse: nor do I say of all monks that they have no task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:12.3.verse: Monks who are arahants, whose mental effluents are ended, who have reached fulfillment, done the task, laid down the burden, attained the true goal, totally destroyed the fetter of becoming, and who are released through right gnosis: I don’t say of them that they have a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:12.5.verse: They have done their task with heedfulness.

mn70:12.6.verse: They are incapable of being heedless.

mn70:13.1.verse: But as for monks in higher training, who have not yet reached their hearts’ goal, who still aspire for the unexcelled freedom from bondage: I say of them that they have a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:13.3.verse: (I think:) ‘Perhaps these venerable ones, when making use of suitable resting places, associating with admirable friends, balancing their (mental) faculties,

mn70:13.4.verse: will reach & remain in the supreme goal of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness, knowing & realizing it for themselves in the here & now.’

mn70:13.5.verse: Envisioning this fruit of heedfulness for these monks, I say that they have a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:14.1.verse: “Monks, there are these seven individuals to be found in the world.

mn70:14.3.verse: One (released) both ways, one released through discernment, a bodily witness, one attained to view, one released through conviction, a Dhamma-follower, and a conviction-follower.

mn70:15.1.verse: “And what is the individual (released) both ways?

mn70:15.2.verse: There is the case where a certain individual remains touching with his body those peaceful liberations that transcend form, that are formless, and—having seen with discernment—his effluents are ended.

mn70:15.3.verse: This is called an individual (released) both ways.

mn70:15.4.verse: Regarding this monk, I do not say that he has a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:15.6.verse: He has done his task with heedfulness.

mn70:15.7.verse: He is incapable of being heedless.

mn70:16.1.verse: “And what is the individual released through discernment?

mn70:16.2.verse: There is the case where a certain individual does not remain touching with his body those peaceful liberations that transcend form, that are formless, but—having seen with discernment—his effluents are ended.

mn70:16.3.verse: This is called an individual who is released through discernment.

mn70:16.4.verse: Regarding this monk, I do not say that he has a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:16.6.verse: He has done his task with heedfulness.

mn70:16.7.verse: He is incapable of being heedless.

mn70:17.1.verse: “And what is the individual who is a bodily witness?

mn70:17.2.verse: There is the case where a certain individual remains touching with his body those peaceful liberations that transcend form, that are formless, and—having seen with discernment—some of his effluents are ended.

mn70:17.3.verse: This is called an individual who is a bodily witness.

mn70:17.4.verse: Regarding this monk, I say that he has a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:17.6.verse: (I think:) ‘Perhaps this venerable one, when making use of suitable resting places, associating with admirable friends, balancing his (mental) faculties,

mn70:17.7.verse: will reach & remain in the supreme goal of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness, knowing & realizing it for himself in the here & now.’

mn70:17.8.verse: Envisioning this fruit of heedfulness for this monk, I say that he has a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:18.1.verse: “And what is the individual attained to view?

mn70:18.2.verse: There is the case where a certain individual does not remain touching with his body those peaceful liberations that transcend form, that are formless, but—having seen with discernment—some of his effluents are ended, and he has reviewed & examined with discernment the qualities (or: teachings) proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

mn70:18.3.verse: This is called an individual who is attained to view.

mn70:18.4.verse: Regarding this monk, I say that he has a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:18.6.verse: (I think:) ‘Perhaps this venerable one, when making use of suitable resting places, associating with admirable friends, balancing his (mental) faculties,

mn70:18.7.verse: will reach & remain in the supreme goal of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness, knowing & realizing it for himself in the here & now.’

mn70:18.8.verse: Envisioning this fruit of heedfulness for this monk, I say that he has a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:19.1.verse: “And what is the individual released through conviction?

mn70:19.2.verse: There is the case where a certain individual does not remain touching with his body those peaceful liberations that transcend form, that are formless, but—having seen with discernment—some of his effluents are ended, and his conviction in the Tathāgata is settled, rooted, and established.

mn70:19.3.verse: This is called an individual who is released through conviction.

mn70:19.4.verse: Regarding this monk, I say that he has a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:19.6.verse: (I think:) ‘Perhaps this venerable one, when making use of suitable resting places, associating with admirable friends, balancing his (mental) faculties,

mn70:19.7.verse: will reach & remain in the supreme goal of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness, knowing & realizing it for himself in the here & now.’

mn70:19.8.verse: Envisioning this fruit of heedfulness for this monk, I say that he has a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:20.1.verse: “And what is the individual who is a Dhamma-follower?

mn70:20.2.verse: There is the case where a certain individual does not remain touching with his body those peaceful liberations that transcend form, that are formless, nor—having seen with discernment—are his effluents ended. But with a (sufficient) measure of reflection through discernment he has come to an agreement with the teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata. And he has these qualities:

mn70:20.3.verse: the faculty of conviction, the faculty of persistence, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, & the faculty of discernment.

mn70:20.4.verse: This is called an individual who is a Dhamma-follower.

mn70:20.5.verse: Regarding this monk, I say that he has a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:20.7.verse: (I think:) ‘Perhaps this venerable one, when making use of suitable resting places, associating with admirable friends, balancing his (mental) faculties,

mn70:20.8.verse: will reach & remain in the supreme goal of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness, knowing & realizing it for himself in the here & now.’

mn70:20.9.verse: Envisioning this fruit of heedfulness for this monk, I say that he has a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:21.1.verse: “And what is the individual who is a conviction-follower?

mn70:21.2.verse: There is the case where a certain individual does not remain touching with his body those peaceful liberations that transcend form, that are formless, nor—having seen with discernment—are his effluents ended. But he has a (sufficient) measure of conviction in & love for the Tathāgata. And he has these qualities:

mn70:21.3.verse: the faculty of conviction, the faculty of persistence, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, & the faculty of discernment.

mn70:21.4.verse: This is called an individual who is a conviction-follower.

mn70:21.5.verse: Regarding this monk, I say that he has a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:21.7.verse: (I think:) ‘Perhaps this venerable one, when making use of suitable resting places, associating with admirable friends, balancing his (mental) faculties,

mn70:21.8.verse: will reach & remain in the supreme goal of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness, knowing & realizing it for himself in the here & now.’

mn70:21.9.verse: Envisioning this fruit of heedfulness for this monk, I say that he has a task to do with heedfulness.

mn70:22.1.verse: “Monks, I do not say that the attainment of gnosis is all at once.

mn70:22.2.verse: Rather, the attainment of gnosis is after gradual training, gradual action, gradual practice.

mn70:23.1.verse: And how is there the attainment of gnosis after gradual training, gradual action, gradual practice?

mn70:23.2.verse: There is the case where, when conviction has arisen, one visits (a teacher). Having visited, one grows close. Having grown close, one lends ear. Having lent ear, one hears the Dhamma. Having heard the Dhamma, one remembers it. Remembering, one penetrates the meaning of the teachings. Penetrating the meaning, one comes to an agreement through pondering the teachings. There being an agreement through pondering the teachings, desire arises. When desire has arisen, one is willing. When one is willing, one contemplates. Having contemplated, one makes an exertion. Having made an exertion, one realizes with the body the ultimate truth and, having penetrated it with discernment, sees it.

mn70:24.1.verse: “Now, monks, there hasn’t been that conviction,

mn70:24.3.verse: there hasn’t been that growing close…

mn70:24.7.verse: that penetration of the meaning of the teachings…

mn70:24.8.verse: that agreement through pondering the teachings…

mn70:24.13.verse: You have lost the way, monks. You have gone the wrong way, monks.

mn70:24.14.verse: How far have you strayed, foolish men, from this Dhamma & Discipline!

mn70:25.1.verse: “Monks, there is a four-phrased statement that, when it is recited, an observant man will in no long time learn the meaning through discernment.

mn70:25.2.verse: I will recite it, and you learn it from me.”

mn70:25.3.verse: “But, lord, who are we to be learners of the Dhamma?”

mn70:26.1.verse: “Monks, even with a teacher devoted to material things, an heir of material things, who lives attached to material things, this sort of haggling (by his students) wouldn’t be proper:

mn70:26.2.verse: ‘If we get this, we’ll do it; if we don’t, we won’t.’ So how could it be with regard to the Tathāgata, who dwells entirely detached from material things?

mn70:27.1.verse: “For a disciple who has conviction in the Teacher’s message & lives to penetrate it, what accords with the Dhamma is this:

mn70:27.2.verse: ‘The Blessed One is the Teacher, I am a disciple.

mn70:27.3.verse: He is the one who knows, not I.’

mn70:27.4.verse: For a disciple who has conviction in the Teacher’s message & lives to penetrate it, the Teacher’s message is healing & nourishing.

mn70:27.5.verse: For a disciple who has conviction in the Teacher’s message & lives to penetrate it, what accords with the Dhamma is this:

mn70:27.6.verse: ‘Gladly would I let the flesh & blood in my body dry up, leaving just the skin, tendons, & bones, but if I have not attained what can be reached through manly firmness, manly persistence, manly striving, there will be no relaxing my persistence.’

mn70:27.7.verse: For a disciple who has conviction in the Teacher’s message & lives to penetrate it, one of two fruits can be expected:

mn70:27.8.verse: either gnosis here & now, or—if there be any remnant of clinging-sustenance—non-return.”

mn70:27.9.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

mn70:27.10.verse: Gratified, the monks delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn70:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Kāsis together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants.

mn70:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

mn70:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, I abstain from eating at night.

mn70:2.2.verse: Doing so, I find that I’m healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.

mn70:2.3.verse: You too should never eat at night.

mn70:2.4.verse: Doing so, you’ll find that you’re healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.”

mn70:3.1.verse: Then the Buddha, traveling stage by stage in the land of the Kāsis, arrived at a town of the Kāsis named Kīṭāgiri,

mn70:4.1.verse: Now at that time the mendicants who followed Assaji and Punabbasuka were residing at Kīṭāgiri.

mn70:4.2.verse: Then several mendicants went up to them and said,

mn70:4.3.verse: “Reverends, the Buddha never eats at night, and neither does the mendicant Saṅgha.

mn70:4.4.verse: Doing so, they find that they’re healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.

mn70:4.5.verse: You too should abstain from eating at night.

mn70:4.6.verse: Doing so, you’ll find that you’re healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.”

mn70:4.7.verse: When they said this, the mendicants who followed Assaji and Punabbasuka said to them,

mn70:4.8.verse: “Reverends, we eat at dusk, at daybreak, and at the wrong time of day.

mn70:4.9.verse: Doing so, we find that we’re healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.

mn70:4.10.verse: Why should we give up what is apparent in the present to chase after what takes effect over time?

mn70:4.11.verse: We shall eat at dusk, at daybreak, and at the wrong time of day.”

mn70:5.1.verse: Since those mendicants were unable to persuade the mendicants who were followers of Assaji and Punabbasuka, they approached the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

mn70:6.1.verse: So the Buddha addressed one of the monks,

mn70:6.2.verse: “Please, monk, in my name tell the mendicants who follow Assaji and Punabbasuka that

mn70:6.4.verse: “Yes, sir,” that monk replied. He went to those mendicants and said,

mn70:6.6.verse: “Yes, reverend,” those mendicants replied. They went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side.

mn70:6.7.verse: The Buddha said to them, “Is it really true, mendicants, that several mendicants went to you and said:

mn70:6.8.verse: ‘Reverends, the Buddha never eats at night, and neither does the mendicant Saṅgha.

mn70:6.9.verse: Doing so, they find that they’re healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.

mn70:6.10.verse: You too should never eat at night.

mn70:6.11.verse: Doing so, you’ll find that you’re healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.’

mn70:6.12.verse: When they said this, did you really say to them:

mn70:6.13.verse: ‘Reverends, we eat at dusk, at daybreak, and at the wrong time of day.

mn70:6.14.verse: Doing so, we find that we’re healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.

mn70:6.15.verse: Why should we give up what is apparent in the present to chase after what takes effect over time?

mn70:6.16.verse: We shall eat at dusk, at daybreak, and at the wrong time of day.’”

mn70:6.18.verse: “Mendicants, have you ever known me to teach the Dhamma like this: no matter what this individual experiences—pleasurable, painful, or neutral—their unskillful qualities decline and their skillful qualities grow?”

mn70:7.1.verse: “Haven’t you known me to teach the Dhamma like this: ‘When someone feels this kind of pleasant feeling, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decline. But when someone feels that kind of pleasant feeling, unskillful qualities decline and skillful qualities grow. When someone feels this kind of painful feeling, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decline. But when someone feels that kind of painful feeling, unskillful qualities decline and skillful qualities grow. When someone feels this kind of neutral feeling, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decline. But when someone feels that kind of neutral feeling, unskillful qualities decline and skillful qualities grow’?”

mn70:8.2.verse: Now, suppose I hadn’t known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:

mn70:8.3.verse: ‘When someone feels this kind of pleasant feeling, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decline.’

mn70:8.4.verse: Not knowing this, would it be appropriate for me to say: ‘You should give up this kind of pleasant feeling’?”

mn70:8.6.verse: “But I have known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:

mn70:8.7.verse: ‘When someone feels this kind of pleasant feeling, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decline.’ Since this is so, that’s why I say: ‘You should give up this kind of pleasant feeling.’

mn70:8.8.verse: Now, suppose I hadn’t known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:

mn70:8.9.verse: ‘When someone feels that kind of pleasant feeling, unskillful qualities decline and skillful qualities grow.’

mn70:8.10.verse: Not knowing this, would it be appropriate for me to say: ‘You should enter and remain in that kind of pleasant feeling’?”

mn70:8.12.verse: “But I have known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:

mn70:8.13.verse: ‘When someone feels that kind of pleasant feeling, unskillful qualities decline and skillful qualities grow.’ Since this is so, that’s why I say: ‘You should enter and remain in that kind of pleasant feeling.’

mn70:8.14.verse: Now, suppose I hadn’t known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:

mn70:8.15.verse: ‘When someone feels this kind of painful feeling, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decline.’

mn70:8.16.verse: Not knowing this, would it be appropriate for me to say: ‘You should give up this kind of painful feeling’?”

mn70:9.1.verse: “But I have known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:

mn70:9.2.verse: ‘When someone feels this kind of painful feeling, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decline.’ Since this is so, that’s why I say: ‘You should give up this kind of painful feeling.’

mn70:9.3.verse: Now, suppose I hadn’t known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:

mn70:9.4.verse: ‘When someone feels that kind of painful feeling, unskillful qualities decline and skillful qualities grow.’

mn70:9.5.verse: Not knowing this, would it be appropriate for me to say: ‘You should enter and remain in that kind of painful feeling’?”

mn70:9.7.verse: “But I have known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:

mn70:9.8.verse: ‘When someone feels that kind of painful feeling, unskillful qualities decline and skillful qualities grow.’ Since this is so, that’s why I say: ‘You should enter and remain in that kind of painful feeling.’

mn70:10.1.verse: Now, suppose I hadn’t known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:

mn70:10.2.verse: ‘When someone feels this kind of neutral feeling, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decline.’

mn70:10.3.verse: Not knowing this, would it be appropriate for me to say: ‘You should give up this kind of neutral feeling’?”

mn70:10.5.verse: “But I have known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:

mn70:10.6.verse: ‘When someone feels this kind of neutral feeling, unskillful qualities grow and skillful qualities decline.’ Since this is so, that’s why I say: ‘You should give up this kind of neutral feeling.’

mn70:10.7.verse: Now, suppose I hadn’t known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:

mn70:10.8.verse: ‘When someone feels that kind of neutral feeling, unskillful qualities decline and skillful qualities grow.’

mn70:10.9.verse: Not knowing this, would it be appropriate for me to say: ‘You should enter and remain in that kind of neutral feeling’?”

mn70:11.1.verse: “But I have known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom:

mn70:11.2.verse: ‘When someone feels that kind of neutral feeling, unskillful qualities decline and skillful qualities grow.’ Since this is so, that’s why I say: ‘You should enter and remain in that kind of neutral feeling.’

mn70:12.1.verse: Mendicants, I don’t say that all these mendicants still have work to do with diligence.

mn70:12.2.verse: Nor do I say that all these mendicants have no work to do with diligence.

mn70:12.3.verse: I say that mendicants don’t have work to do with diligence if they are perfected, with defilements ended, having completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and become rightly freed through enlightenment.

mn70:12.5.verse: They’ve done their work with diligence.

mn70:13.1.verse: I say that mendicants still have work to do with diligence if they are trainees, who haven’t achieved their heart’s desire, but live aspiring to the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

mn70:13.3.verse: ‘Hopefully this venerable will frequent appropriate lodgings, associate with good friends, and control their faculties.

mn70:13.4.verse: Then they might realize the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life, and live having achieved with their own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.’

mn70:13.5.verse: Seeing this fruit of diligence for those mendicants, I say that they still have work to do with diligence.

mn70:14.1.verse: Mendicants, these seven individuals are found in the world.

mn70:14.3.verse: One freed both ways, one freed by wisdom, a direct witness, one attained to view, one freed by faith, a follower of teachings, and a follower by faith.

mn70:15.1.verse: And what individual is freed both ways?

mn70:15.2.verse: It’s an individual who has direct meditative experience of the peaceful liberations that are formless, transcending form. And, having seen with wisdom, their defilements have come to an end.

mn70:15.3.verse: This individual is called freed both ways.

mn70:15.4.verse: And I say that this mendicant has no work to do with diligence.

mn70:15.6.verse: They’ve done their work with diligence.

mn70:16.1.verse: And what individual is freed by wisdom?

mn70:16.2.verse: It’s an individual who does not have direct meditative experience of the peaceful liberations that are formless, transcending form. Nevertheless, having seen with wisdom, their defilements have come to an end.

mn70:16.3.verse: This individual is called freed by wisdom.

mn70:16.4.verse: I say that this mendicant has no work to do with diligence.

mn70:16.6.verse: They’ve done their work with diligence.

mn70:17.1.verse: And what individual is a direct witness?

mn70:17.2.verse: It’s an individual who has direct meditative experience of the peaceful liberations that are formless, transcending form. And, having seen with wisdom, some of their defilements have come to an end.

mn70:17.3.verse: This individual is called a direct witness.

mn70:17.4.verse: I say that this mendicant still has work to do with diligence.

mn70:17.6.verse: ‘Hopefully this venerable will frequent appropriate lodgings, associate with good friends, and control their faculties.

mn70:17.7.verse: Then they might realize the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life, and live having achieved with their own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.’

mn70:17.8.verse: Seeing this fruit of diligence for this mendicant, I say that they still have work to do with diligence.

mn70:18.1.verse: And what individual is attained to view?

mn70:18.2.verse: It’s an individual who doesn’t have direct meditative experience of the peaceful liberations that are formless, transcending form. Nevertheless, having seen with wisdom, some of their defilements have come to an end. And they have clearly seen and clearly contemplated with wisdom the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.

mn70:18.3.verse: This individual is called attained to view.

mn70:18.4.verse: I say that this mendicant also still has work to do with diligence.

mn70:18.6.verse: ‘Hopefully this venerable will frequent appropriate lodgings, associate with good friends, and control their faculties.

mn70:18.7.verse: Then they might realize the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life, and live having achieved with their own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.’

mn70:18.8.verse: Seeing this fruit of diligence for this mendicant, I say that they still have work to do with diligence.

mn70:19.1.verse: And what individual is freed by faith?

mn70:19.2.verse: It’s an individual who doesn’t have direct meditative experience of the peaceful liberations that are formless, transcending form. Nevertheless, having seen with wisdom, some of their defilements have come to an end. And their faith is settled, rooted, and planted in the Realized One.

mn70:19.3.verse: This individual is called freed by faith.

mn70:19.4.verse: I say that this mendicant also still has work to do with diligence.

mn70:19.6.verse: ‘Hopefully this venerable will frequent appropriate lodgings, associate with good friends, and control their faculties.

mn70:19.7.verse: Then they might realize the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life, and live having achieved with their own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.’

mn70:19.8.verse: Seeing this fruit of diligence for this mendicant, I say that they still have work to do with diligence.

mn70:20.1.verse: And what individual is a follower of teachings?

mn70:20.2.verse: It’s an individual who doesn’t have direct meditative experience of the peaceful liberations that are formless, transcending form. And having seen with wisdom, their defilements have not come to an end. And they accept the teachings proclaimed by the Realized One after deliberating them with a degree of wisdom. And they have the following qualities:

mn70:20.3.verse: the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

mn70:20.4.verse: This individual is called a follower of teachings.

mn70:20.5.verse: I say that this mendicant also still has work to do with diligence.

mn70:20.7.verse: ‘Hopefully this venerable will frequent appropriate lodgings, associate with good friends, and control their faculties.

mn70:20.8.verse: Then they might realize the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life, and live having achieved with their own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.’

mn70:20.9.verse: Seeing this fruit of diligence for this mendicant, I say that they still have work to do with diligence.

mn70:21.1.verse: And what individual is a follower by faith?

mn70:21.2.verse: It’s an individual who doesn’t have direct meditative experience of the peaceful liberations that are formless, transcending form. And having seen with wisdom, their defilements have not come to an end. And they have a degree of faith and fondness for the Realized One. And they have the following qualities:

mn70:21.3.verse: the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

mn70:21.4.verse: This individual is called a follower by faith.

mn70:21.5.verse: I say that this mendicant also still has work to do with diligence.

mn70:21.7.verse: ‘Hopefully this venerable will frequent appropriate lodgings, associate with good friends, and control their faculties.

mn70:21.8.verse: Then they might realize the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life, and live having achieved with their own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.’

mn70:21.9.verse: Seeing this fruit of diligence for this mendicant, I say that they still have work to do with diligence.

mn70:22.1.verse: Mendicants, I don’t say that enlightenment is achieved right away.

mn70:22.2.verse: Rather, enlightenment is achieved by gradual training, progress, and practice.

mn70:23.1.verse: And how is enlightenment achieved by gradual training, progress, and practice?

mn70:23.2.verse: It’s when someone in whom faith has arisen approaches a teacher. They pay homage, actively listen, hear the teachings, remember the teachings, examine their meaning, and accept them after deliberation. Then enthusiasm springs up; they make an attempt, weigh up, and strive. Striving, they directly realize the ultimate truth, and see it with penetrating wisdom.

mn70:24.1.verse: Mendicants, there has not been that faith,

mn70:24.13.verse: You’re on a bad path, mendicants! You’re practicing the wrong way!

mn70:24.14.verse: How far these futile men have strayed from this teaching and training!

mn70:25.1.verse: There is an exposition in four statements, which a sensible person would quickly understand when it is recited.

mn70:25.2.verse: I shall recite it for you, mendicants. Try to understand it.”

mn70:25.3.verse: “Sir, who are we next to those who understand the teaching?”

mn70:26.1.verse: “Even with a teacher who values things of the flesh, is an heir in things of the flesh, who lives caught up in things of the flesh, you wouldn’t get into such haggling:

mn70:26.2.verse: ‘If we get this, we’ll do that. If we don’t get this, we won’t do it.’ What then of the Realized One, who lives utterly detached from things of the flesh?

mn70:27.1.verse: For a faithful disciple who is practicing to fathom the Teacher’s instructions, this is in line with the teaching:

mn70:27.2.verse: ‘The Buddha is my Teacher, I am his disciple.

mn70:27.3.verse: The Buddha knows, I do not know.’

mn70:27.4.verse: For a faithful disciple who is practicing to fathom the Teacher’s instructions, the Teacher’s instructions are nourishing and nutritious.

mn70:27.5.verse: For a faithful disciple who is practicing to fathom the Teacher’s instructions, this is in line with the teaching:

mn70:27.6.verse: ‘Gladly, let only skin, sinews, and bones remain! Let the flesh and blood waste away in my body! I will not relax my energy until I have achieved what is possible by human strength, energy, and vigor.’

mn70:27.7.verse: For a faithful disciple who is practicing to fathom the Teacher’s instructions, one of two results can be expected:

mn70:27.8.verse: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”

mn70:27.9.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn70:27.10.verse: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

mn71:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Vesāli in the Hall with the peaked roof in the Great Wood.

mn71:2.1.verse: Now on that occasion the Wanderer Vacchagotta was staying in the Wanderers’ Park with the single White-lotus Mango tree.

mn71:3.1.verse: Then when it was morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, he went into Vesāli for alms.

mn71:3.3.verse: ‘It is still too early to wander for alms in Vesāli.

mn71:3.4.verse: Suppose I went to the Wanderer Vacchagotta in the Wanderers’ Park with the single White-lotus Mango tree?’

mn71:3.5.verse: Then the Blessed One went to the Wanderer Vacchagotta in the Wanderers’ Park with the single White-lotus Mango tree.

mn71:4.1.verse: The Wanderer Vacchagotta saw the Blessed One coming in the distance.

mn71:4.2.verse: Seeing him, he said to him:

mn71:4.3.verse: “Let the Blessed One come, venerable sir.

mn71:4.4.verse: Welcome to the Blessed One, venerable sir.

mn71:4.5.verse: It is long, venerable sir, since the Blessed One made an occasion to come here.

mn71:4.6.verse: Let the Blessed One be seated, venerable sir; this seat is ready.”

mn71:4.7.verse: The Blessed One sat down on the seat made ready.

mn71:4.8.verse: And Vacchagotta the Wanderer took another, lower, seat and sat down at one side.

mn71:4.9.verse: When he had done so, Vacchagotta the Wanderer said to the Blessed One:

mn71:5.2.verse: ‘the recluse Gotama is omniscient and all-seeing, he claims to have complete knowledge and vision thus:

mn71:5.3.verse: “whether I am walking or standing or asleep or awake, my knowledge and vision are continuously and unceasingly maintained.”’

mn71:5.4.verse: Venerable sir, when they who say that say: ‘the recluse Gotama is omniscient and all-seeing, he claims to have complete knowledge and vision thus: “whether I am walking or standing or asleep or awake, my knowledge and vision are continuously and unceasingly maintained” ’ — do they, venerable sir, say what the Blessed One says, without misrepresenting the Blessed One with what is not so, do they express a dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and does no legitimate deduction from their assertion give ground for censure?”

mn71:5.5.verse: “Vaccha, those who say thus: ‘the recluse Gotama is omniscient and all-seeing, he claims to have complete knowledge and vision thus: “whether I am walking or standing or asleep or awake, my knowledge and vision are continuously and unceasingly maintained” ’ — they do not say what I say, and they misrepresent me with what is not true and not so.”

mn71:6.1.verse: “Venerable sir, how then should we answer so as to say what the Blessed One says, without misrepresenting the Blessed One with what is not so, and express a dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, so that no legitimate deduction from our assertion would give ground for censure?”

mn71:6.2.verse: “Vaccha, if you answer thus: ‘the recluse Gotama has the three true knowledges’[^1] — you would be saying what I say, without misrepresenting me with what is not so, you would express a dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and no legitimate deduction from your assertion would give ground for censure.

mn71:7.1.verse: For, Vaccha, as far as I want, I recollect my manifold past lives,

mn71:7.2.verse: that is, one birth, two births … thus with their aspects and particulars I recollect my manifold past lives.

mn71:8.1.verse: And, Vaccha, as far as I want, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, I see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate … I understand how beings pass on according to their actions.

mn71:9.1.verse: And, Vaccha, by realizing for myself with direct knowledge, I here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints.

mn71:10.1.verse: If you answer thus: ‘the recluse Gotama has the three true knowledges’ — you would be saying what I say, without misrepresenting me with what is not so, you would express a dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and no legitimate deduction from your assertion would give ground for censure.”

mn71:11.1.verse: When this was said, the Wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One:

mn71:11.2.verse: “Master Gotama, is there any householder who, without abandoning the fetter of householdership, makes an end of suffering on the dissolution of the body?”

mn71:11.3.verse: “There is no householder, Vaccha, who, without abandoning the fetter of householdership, makes an end of suffering on the dissolution of the body.”

mn71:12.1.verse: “But, Master Gotama, is there any householder who, without abandoning the fetter of householdership, on the dissolution of the body passes on to heaven?”

mn71:12.2.verse: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the householders who, without abandoning the fetter of householdership, on the dissolution of the body pass on to heaven.”

mn71:13.1.verse: “Master Gotama, is there any Ājīvaka ascetic[^2] who on the dissolution of the body makes an end of suffering?”

mn71:13.2.verse: “There is no Ājīvaka ascetic, Vaccha, who on the dissolution of the body makes an end of suffering.”

mn71:14.1.verse: “But, Master Gotama, is there any Ājīvaka ascetic who on the dissolution of the body passes on to heaven?”

mn71:14.2.verse: “Ninety-one aeons back, Vaccha, as far as I recollect, I know of no Ājīvaka ascetic who passed on to heaven on the dissolution of the body, except for one,

mn71:14.3.verse: and he too was a teacher of the doctrine of action and the doctrine of doing.”

mn71:15.1.verse: “That being so, Master Gotama, this other sectarians’ basis is empty,

mn71:15.2.verse: even of a chance of passing on to heaven!”

mn71:15.3.verse: This is what the Blessed One said.

mn71:15.4.verse: The Wanderer Vacchagotta was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn71:0.2.verse: To Vacchagotta on the Three Knowledges

mn71:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

mn71:2.1.verse: Now at that time the wanderer Vacchagotta was residing in the Single Lotus monastery for the wanderers.

mn71:3.1.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Vesālī for alms.

mn71:3.3.verse: “It’s too early to wander for alms in Vesālī.

mn71:3.4.verse: Why don’t I visit the wanderer Vacchagotta at the Single Lotus Monastery?”

mn71:4.1.verse: Vacchagotta saw the Buddha coming off in the distance,

mn71:4.4.verse: Welcome to the Blessed One, sir!

mn71:4.5.verse: It’s been a long time since you took the opportunity to come here.

mn71:4.6.verse: Please, sir, sit down, here, a seat is ready.”

mn71:4.7.verse: The Buddha sat down on the seat spread out,

mn71:4.8.verse: while Vacchagotta took a low seat and sat to one side.

mn71:4.9.verse: Then Vacchagotta said to the Buddha:

mn71:5.2.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama claims to be all-knowing and all-seeing, to know and see everything without exception, thus:

mn71:5.3.verse: “Knowledge and vision are constantly and continually present to me, while walking, standing, sleeping, and waking.”’

mn71:5.4.verse: I trust those who say this repeat what the Buddha has said, and do not misrepresent him with an untruth? Is their explanation in line with the teaching? Are there any legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?”

mn71:5.5.verse: “Vaccha, those who say this do not repeat what I have said. They misrepresent me with what is false and untrue.”

mn71:6.1.verse: “So how should we answer so as to repeat what the Buddha has said, and not misrepresent him with an untruth? How should we explain in line with his teaching, with no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?”

mn71:6.2.verse: “‘The ascetic Gotama has the three knowledges.’ Answering like this you would repeat what I have said, and not misrepresent me with an untruth. You would explain in line with my teaching, and there would be no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism.

mn71:7.1.verse: For, Vaccha, whenever I want, I recollect my many kinds of past lives.

mn71:7.2.verse: That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. I remember: ‘There, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn somewhere else. There, too, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn here.’ And so I recollect my many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

mn71:8.1.verse: And whenever I want, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, I see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. I understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

mn71:9.1.verse: And I have realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. I live having realized it with my own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

mn71:10.1.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama has the three knowledges.’ Answering like this you would repeat what I have said, and not misrepresent me with an untruth. You would explain in line with my teaching, and there would be no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism.”

mn71:11.1.verse: When he said this, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Buddha,

mn71:11.2.verse: “Worthy Gotama, are there any laypeople who, without giving up the fetter of lay life, make an end of suffering when the body breaks up?”

mn71:12.1.verse: “But are there any laypeople who, without giving up the fetter of lay life, go to heaven when the body breaks up?”

mn71:12.2.verse: “There’s not just one hundred laypeople, Vaccha, or two or three or four or five hundred, but many more than that who, without giving up the fetter of lay life, go to heaven when the body breaks up.”

mn71:13.1.verse: “Worthy Gotama, are there any Ājīvaka ascetics who make an end of suffering when the body breaks up?”

mn71:14.1.verse: “But are there any Ājīvaka ascetics who go to heaven when the body breaks up?”

mn71:14.2.verse: “Vaccha, when I recollect the past ninety-one eons, I can’t find any Ājīvaka ascetics who have gone to heaven, except one;

mn71:14.3.verse: and he taught the efficacy of deeds and action.”

mn71:15.1.verse: “In that case, worthy Gotama, that sectarian fold is empty even of the chance to go to heaven.”

mn71:15.2.verse: “Yes, Vaccha, that sectarian fold is empty even of the chance to go to heaven.”

mn71:15.3.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn71:15.4.verse: Satisfied, the wanderer Vacchagotta approved what the Buddha said.

mn72:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

mn72:2.1.verse: Then Vacchagotta the Wanderer went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.

mn72:2.2.verse: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, he said to the Blessed One:

mn72:3.1.verse: “How is it, Master Gotama: ‘the world is eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—[^1]

mn72:3.2.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?”

mn72:3.3.verse: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:

mn72:3.4.verse: ‘the world is eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”

mn72:4.1.verse: “How then, Master Gotama: ‘the world is not eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—

mn72:4.2.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?”

mn72:4.3.verse: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:

mn72:4.4.verse: ‘the world is not eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”

mn72:5.1.verse: “How is it, Master Gotama: ‘the world is finite, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—

mn72:5.2.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?”

mn72:5.3.verse: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:

mn72:5.4.verse: ‘the world is finite, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”

mn72:6.1.verse: “How then, Master Gotama: ‘the world is infinite, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—

mn72:6.2.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?”

mn72:6.3.verse: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:

mn72:6.4.verse: ‘the world is infinite, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”

mn72:7.1.verse: “How is it, Master Gotama: ‘the soul is the same as the body, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—

mn72:7.2.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?”

mn72:7.3.verse: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:

mn72:7.4.verse: ‘the soul is the same as the body, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”

mn72:8.1.verse: “How then, Master Gotama: ‘the soul is one and the body another, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—

mn72:8.2.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?”

mn72:8.3.verse: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:

mn72:8.4.verse: ‘the soul is one and the body another, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”

mn72:9.1.verse: “How is it, Master Gotama: ‘after death a Tathāgata is,[^2] only this is true and everything else is wrong’—

mn72:9.2.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?”

mn72:9.3.verse: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:

mn72:9.4.verse: ‘after death a Tathāgata is, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”

mn72:10.1.verse: “How then, Master Gotama: ‘after death a Tathāgata is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—

mn72:10.2.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?”

mn72:10.3.verse: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:

mn72:10.4.verse: ‘after death a Tathāgata is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”

mn72:11.1.verse: “How is it, Master Gotama: ‘after death a Tathāgata both is and is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—

mn72:11.2.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?”

mn72:11.3.verse: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:

mn72:11.4.verse: ‘after death a Tathāgata both is and is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”

mn72:12.1.verse: “How then, Master Gotama: ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong’—

mn72:12.2.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?”

mn72:12.3.verse: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha:

mn72:12.4.verse: ‘after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong.’”

mn72:13.1.verse: ‘When I asked: “How is it, Master Gotama: the world is eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong—

mn72:13.2.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—

mn72:13.3.verse: the world is eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”

mn72:13.4.verse: ‘When I asked: “How then, Master Gotama: the world is not eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong—

mn72:13.5.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—

mn72:13.6.verse: the world is not eternal, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”

mn72:13.7.verse: ‘When I asked: “How is it, Master Gotama: the world is finite, only this is true and everything else is wrong—

mn72:13.8.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—

mn72:13.9.verse: the world is finite, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”

mn72:13.10.verse: ‘When I asked: “How then, Master Gotama: the world is infinite, only this is true and everything else is wrong—

mn72:13.11.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—

mn72:13.12.verse: the world is infinite, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”

mn72:13.13.verse: ‘When I asked: “How is it, Master Gotama: the soul is the same as the body, only this is true and everything else is wrong—

mn72:13.14.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—

mn72:13.15.verse: the soul is the same as the body, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”

mn72:13.16.verse: ‘When I asked: “How then, Master Gotama: the soul is one and the body another, only this is true and everything else is wrong—

mn72:13.17.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—

mn72:13.18.verse: the soul is one and the body another, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”

mn72:13.19.verse: ‘When I asked: “How is it, Master Gotama: after death a Tathāgata is, only this is true and everything else is wrong—

mn72:13.20.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—

mn72:13.21.verse: after death a Tathāgata is, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”

mn72:13.22.verse: ‘When I asked: “How then, Master Gotama: after death a Tathāgata is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong—

mn72:13.23.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—

mn72:13.24.verse: after death a Tathāgata is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”

mn72:13.25.verse: ‘When I asked: “How is it, Master Gotama: after death a Tathāgata both is and is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong—

mn72:13.26.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—

mn72:13.27.verse: after death a Tathāgata both is and is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”

mn72:13.28.verse: ‘When I asked: “How then, Master Gotama: after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong—

mn72:13.29.verse: does Master Gotama hold this view?” you, being asked thus, said: “I do not hold that view, Vaccha—

mn72:13.30.verse: after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not, only this is true and everything else is wrong.”

mn72:13.31.verse: But what danger does Master Gotama see, that he is thus altogether disassociated from all these fields of view?”

mn72:14.1.verse: ‘Vaccha, the view “the world is eternal” is a thicket of views, a wilderness of views, a contortion of views, a vacillation of views, a fetter of views; it is accompanied by suffering, by vexation, by despair, and by fever, and it does not lead to dispassion, to fading away, to cessation, to peace, to direct-knowledge, to full-enlightenment, to Nibbāna.

mn72:14.2.verse: The view “the world is not eternal” …

mn72:14.5.verse: the view “the soul is the same as the body” …

mn72:14.6.verse: the view “the soul is one and the body another” …

mn72:14.7.verse: the view “after death a Tathāgata is” …

mn72:14.8.verse: the view “after death a Tathāgata is not” …

mn72:14.9.verse: the view “after death a Tathāgata both is and is not” …

mn72:14.10.verse: … and the view “after death a Tathāgata neither is nor is not” is a thicket of views, a wilderness of views, a contortion of views, a vacillation of views, a fetter of views; it is accompanied by suffering, by vexation, by despair, and by fever, and it does not lead to dispassion, to fading away, to cessation, to peace, to direct-knowledge, to full-enlightenment, to Nibbāna.

mn72:14.11.verse: It is seeing this danger, Vaccha, that I am thus altogether disassociated from all these fields of view.”

mn72:15.1.verse: “But does Master Gotama have any view of his own?”

mn72:15.2.verse: “‘View’, Vaccha, is something a Tathāgata has done away with.

mn72:15.3.verse: For a Tathāgata has seen this:

mn72:15.4.verse: ‘such is form, such its origin, such its disappearance;

mn72:15.5.verse: such is feeling, such its origin, such its disappearance;

mn72:15.6.verse: such is perception, such its origin, such its disappearance;

mn72:15.7.verse: such are formations, such their origin, such their disappearance;

mn72:15.8.verse: such is consciousness, such its origin, such its disappearance.’

mn72:15.9.verse: Therefore I say that a Tathāgata is liberated through the exhaustion, fading away, cessation, giving up, and relinquishment of all conceiving, all excogitation, all I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit, without clinging.”

mn72:16.1.verse: “When a bhikkhu’s mind is liberated thus, Master Gotama, where does he reappear?”

mn72:16.3.verse: “Then he does not reappear, Master Gotama?”

mn72:16.4.verse: “‘Does not reappear’ does not apply, Vaccha.”

mn72:16.5.verse: “Then he both reappears and does not reappear, Master Gotama?”

mn72:16.6.verse: “‘Both reappears and does not reappear’ does not apply, Vaccha.”

mn72:16.7.verse: “Then he neither reappears nor does not reappear, Master Gotama?”

mn72:16.8.verse: “‘Neither reappears nor does not reappear’ does not apply, Vaccha.”

mn72:17.1.verse: ‘“When a bhikkhu’s mind is liberated thus, Master Gotama, where does he reappear?”—being asked thus, you said: “‘Reappears’ does not apply, Vaccha.”

mn72:17.2.verse: “Then he does not reappear, Master Gotama?”—being asked thus, you said: “‘Does not reappear’ does not apply, Vaccha.”

mn72:17.3.verse: “Then he both reappears and does not reappear, Master Gotama?”—being asked thus, you said: “‘Both reappears and does not reappear’ does not apply, Vaccha.”

mn72:17.4.verse: “Then he neither reappears nor does not reappear, Master Gotama?”—being asked thus, you said: “‘Neither reappears nor does not reappear’ does not apply, Vaccha.”

mn72:17.5.verse: Here, Master Gotama, I have fallen into unknowing, I have fallen into confusion,

mn72:17.6.verse: and whatever small measure of confidence I had through Master Gotama’s earlier conversation has now vanished.”[^3]

mn72:18.1.verse: “Enough of your unknowing, Vaccha, enough of your confusion.

mn72:18.2.verse: This Dhamma is profound, hard to see, hard to discover, peaceful, sublime, unattainable by mere reasoning, subtle, to be experienced by the wise.

mn72:18.3.verse: It is hard for you to know it since you hold a different view, favour a different acceptance, aspire to a different goal, undertake a different training, and follow a different teacher.

mn72:18.4.verse: So then, Vaccha, I shall question you about this in return; answer as you see fit.

mn72:19.2.verse: if a fire were burning before you, would you know:

mn72:19.4.verse: “If a fire were burning before me, Master Gotama, I would know:

mn72:19.6.verse: “If someone were to ask you, Vaccha, thus:

mn72:19.7.verse: ‘This fire burning before you—what does it burn dependent on?’ Being asked thus, Vaccha, how would you answer?”

mn72:19.8.verse: “If I were asked thus, Master Gotama:

mn72:19.9.verse: ‘This fire burning before you—what does it burn dependent on?’ being asked thus, Master Gotama, I would answer thus:

mn72:19.10.verse: ‘This fire burning before me burns dependent on grass and sticks as fuel.’”[^4]

mn72:19.11.verse: “If that fire before you were to go out, Vaccha, would you know:

mn72:19.12.verse: ‘this fire before me has gone out’?”

mn72:19.13.verse: “If that fire before me were to go out, Master Gotama, I would know:

mn72:19.14.verse: ‘this fire before me has gone out.’”

mn72:19.15.verse: “If someone were to ask you, Vaccha, thus:

mn72:19.16.verse: ‘This fire before you that has gone out—which direction did it go from here:

mn72:19.17.verse: east, south, west, or north?’ Being asked thus, Vaccha, how would you answer?”

mn72:19.18.verse: “That does not apply, Master Gotama. That fire burned dependent on grass and sticks as fuel, and with the exhaustion of that fuel, and no other being supplied, being without nutriment, it is reckoned as ‘gone out’.”

mn72:20.1.verse: “So too, Vaccha, the form by which one describing a Tathāgata might describe him has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, done away with, no more subject to future arising.

mn72:20.2.verse: The Tathāgata is liberated from reckoning in terms of form, Vaccha; he is profound, immeasurable, hard to fathom,

mn72:20.4.verse: ‘Reappears’ does not apply, ‘does not reappear’ does not apply, ‘both reappears and does not reappear’ does not apply, ‘neither reappears nor does not reappear’ does not apply.

mn72:20.5.verse: The feeling by which one describing a Tathāgata might describe him has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, done away with, no more subject to future arising.

mn72:20.6.verse: The Tathāgata is liberated from reckoning in terms of feeling, Vaccha; he is profound, immeasurable, hard to fathom,

mn72:20.8.verse: ‘Reappears’ does not apply, ‘does not reappear’ does not apply, ‘both reappears and does not reappear’ does not apply, ‘neither reappears nor does not reappear’ does not apply.

mn72:20.9.verse: The perception by which one describing a Tathāgata might describe him has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, done away with, no more subject to future arising.

mn72:20.10.verse: The Tathāgata is liberated from reckoning in terms of perception, Vaccha; he is profound, immeasurable, hard to fathom,

mn72:20.12.verse: ‘Reappears’ does not apply, ‘does not reappear’ does not apply, ‘both reappears and does not reappear’ does not apply, ‘neither reappears nor does not reappear’ does not apply.

mn72:20.13.verse: The formations by which one describing a Tathāgata might describe him have been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, done away with, no more subject to future arising.

mn72:20.14.verse: The Tathāgata is liberated from reckoning in terms of formations, Vaccha; he is profound, immeasurable, hard to fathom,

mn72:20.16.verse: ‘Reappears’ does not apply, ‘does not reappear’ does not apply, ‘both reappears and does not reappear’ does not apply, ‘neither reappears nor does not reappear’ does not apply.

mn72:20.17.verse: The consciousness by which one describing a Tathāgata might describe him has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, done away with, no more subject to future arising.

mn72:20.18.verse: The Tathāgata is liberated from reckoning in terms of consciousness, Vaccha; he is profound, immeasurable, hard to fathom,

mn72:20.20.verse: ‘Reappears’ does not apply, ‘does not reappear’ does not apply, ‘both reappears and does not reappear’ does not apply, ‘neither reappears nor does not reappear’ does not apply.”

mn72:21.1.verse: When this was said, Vacchagotta the Wanderer said to the Blessed One:

mn72:21.2.verse: “Master Gotama, suppose there were a great sāla tree not far from a village or town.

mn72:21.3.verse: Through impermanence its branches and foliage would fall away, its bark would fall away, its softwood would fall away;

mn72:21.4.verse: and on a later occasion, divested of branches and foliage, divested of bark, divested of softwood, it would be pure and stand established in heartwood.

mn72:21.5.verse: So too, Master Gotama’s teaching is divested of branches and foliage, divested of bark, divested of softwood, and it is pure and stands established in heartwood.

mn72:22.1.verse: ‘Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama! The Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama, as though he were righting the overthrown, revealing the hidden, showing the way to one who was lost, holding up a lamp in the darkness for those with eyesight to see forms. I go to Master Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma and to the Sangha. …

mn72:22.2.verse: … From today let Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone to him for refuge for life.”

mn72:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn72:2.1.verse: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

mn72:2.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

mn72:3.1.verse: “Worthy Gotama, is this your view: ‘The cosmos is eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”

mn72:4.1.verse: “Then is this your view: ‘The cosmos is not eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”

mn72:5.1.verse: “Then is this your view: ‘The cosmos is finite. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”

mn72:6.1.verse: “Then is this your view: ‘The cosmos is infinite. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”

mn72:7.1.verse: “Then is this your view: ‘The soul and the body are one and the same. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”

mn72:8.1.verse: “Then is this your view: ‘The soul is one thing, the body another. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”

mn72:9.1.verse: “Then is this your view: ‘A realized one still exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”

mn72:10.1.verse: “Then is this your view: ‘A realized one no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”

mn72:11.1.verse: “Then is this your view: ‘A realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”

mn72:12.1.verse: “Then is this your view: ‘A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?”

mn72:13.1.verse: “Worthy Gotama, when asked these ten questions, you say: ‘That’s not my view.’

mn72:13.31.verse: Seeing what drawback do you avoid all these convictions?”

mn72:14.1.verse: “Each of these ten convictions is the thicket of views, the desert of views, the twist of views, the dodge of views, the fetter of views. They’re beset with suffering, distress, anguish, and fever. They don’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

mn72:14.11.verse: Seeing this drawback I avoid all these convictions.”

mn72:15.1.verse: “But does the worthy Gotama have any convictions at all?”

mn72:15.2.verse: “A realized one has done away with convictions.

mn72:15.3.verse: For a realized one has seen:

mn72:15.4.verse: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the disappearance of form.

mn72:15.5.verse: Such is feeling, such is the origin of feeling, such is the disappearance of feeling.

mn72:15.6.verse: Such is perception, such is the origin of perception, such is the disappearance of perception.

mn72:15.7.verse: Such are choices, such is the origin of choices, such is the disappearance of choices.

mn72:15.8.verse: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.’

mn72:15.9.verse: That’s why a Realized One is freed by not grasping with the ending, fading away, cessation, giving up, and letting go of all conceiving, all churning, and all I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit, I say.”

mn72:16.1.verse: “But worthy Gotama, when a mendicant’s mind is freed like this, where are they reborn?”

mn72:16.5.verse: “Well then, are they both reborn and not reborn?”

mn72:16.6.verse: “‘They’re both reborn and not reborn’ doesn’t apply, Vaccha.”

mn72:16.7.verse: “Well then, are they neither reborn nor not reborn?”

mn72:16.8.verse: “‘They’re neither reborn nor not reborn’ doesn’t apply, Vaccha.”

mn72:17.1.verse: “Worthy Gotama, when asked all these questions, you say: ‘It doesn’t apply.’

mn72:17.5.verse: I fail to understand this point, worthy Gotama; I’ve fallen into confusion.

mn72:17.6.verse: And I’ve now lost even the degree of clarity I had from previous discussions with the worthy Gotama.”

mn72:18.1.verse: “No wonder you don’t understand, Vaccha, no wonder you’re confused.

mn72:18.2.verse: For this principle is deep, hard to see, hard to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of logic, subtle, comprehensible to the astute.

mn72:18.3.verse: It’s hard for you to understand, since you have a different view, creed, and belief, and another discipline and denomination.

mn72:18.4.verse: Well then, Vaccha, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.

mn72:19.2.verse: Suppose a fire was burning in front of you. Would you know:

mn72:19.3.verse: ‘This fire is burning in front of me’?”

mn72:19.6.verse: “But Vaccha, suppose they were to ask you:

mn72:19.7.verse: ‘This fire burning in front of you: what does it depend on to burn?’ How would you answer?”

mn72:19.10.verse: ‘This fire burning in front of me burns in dependence on grass and logs as fuel.’”

mn72:19.11.verse: “Suppose that fire burning in front of you was extinguished. Would you know:

mn72:19.12.verse: ‘This fire in front of me is quenched’?”

mn72:19.15.verse: “But Vaccha, suppose they were to ask you:

mn72:19.16.verse: ‘This fire in front of you that is quenched: in what direction did it go—

mn72:19.17.verse: east, south, west, or north?’ How would you answer?”

mn72:19.18.verse: “It doesn’t apply, worthy Gotama. The fire depended on grass and logs as fuel. When that runs out, and no more fuel is added, the fire is reckoned to have become quenched due to lack of fuel.”

mn72:20.1.verse: “In the same way, Vaccha, any form by which a realized one might be described has been given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

mn72:20.2.verse: A realized one is freed from reckoning in terms of form. They’re deep, immeasurable, and hard to fathom,

mn72:20.4.verse: ‘They’re reborn’, ‘they’re not reborn’, ‘they’re both reborn and not reborn’, ‘they’re neither reborn nor not reborn’—none of these apply.

mn72:20.17.verse: consciousness by which a realized one might be described has been given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

mn72:20.18.verse: A realized one is freed from reckoning in terms of consciousness. They’re deep, immeasurable, and hard to fathom,

mn72:20.20.verse: ‘They’re reborn’, ‘they’re not reborn’, ‘they’re both reborn and not reborn’, ‘they’re neither reborn nor not reborn’—none of these apply.”

mn72:21.1.verse: When he said this, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Buddha:

mn72:21.2.verse: “Worthy Gotama, suppose there was a large sal tree not far from a town or village.

mn72:21.3.verse: And because it’s impermanent, its branches and foliage, bark and shoots, and softwood would fall off.

mn72:21.4.verse: After some time it would be rid of branches and foliage, bark and shoots, and softwood, pure, and consolidated in the core.

mn72:21.5.verse: In the same way, worthy Gotama’s dispensation is rid of branches and foliage, bark and shoots, and softwood, pure, and consolidated in the core.

mn72:22.2.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

mn73:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary.

mn73:2.1.verse: Then the Wanderer Vacchagotta went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.

mn73:2.2.verse: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, he said to the Blessed One:

mn73:3.1.verse: “I have had conversations with Master Gotama for a long time.

mn73:3.2.verse: It would be good if Master Gotama would show me the profitable and the unprofitable in brief.”

mn73:3.3.verse: “I could show you the profitable and the unprofitable in brief, Vaccha, and I could show you the profitable and the unprofitable in detail;

mn73:3.4.verse: but I will show you them in brief.

mn73:3.5.verse: Listen and attend closely to what I shall say.”

mn73:4.1.verse: “Greed, Vaccha, is unprofitable, non-greed is profitable;

mn73:4.2.verse: hate is unprofitable, non-hate is profitable;

mn73:4.3.verse: delusion is unprofitable, non-delusion is profitable.

mn73:4.4.verse: So, Vaccha, these three things are unprofitable and three things are profitable.

mn73:5.1.verse: Killing living beings is unprofitable, abstention from killing living beings is profitable;

mn73:5.2.verse: taking what is not given is unprofitable, abstention from taking what is not given is profitable;

mn73:5.3.verse: misconduct in sensual desires is unprofitable, abstention from misconduct in sensual desires is profitable;

mn73:5.4.verse: false speech is unprofitable, abstention from false speech is profitable;

mn73:5.5.verse: malicious speech is unprofitable, abstention from malicious speech is profitable;

mn73:5.6.verse: harsh speech is unprofitable, abstention from harsh speech is profitable;

mn73:5.7.verse: gossip is unprofitable, abstention from gossip is profitable;

mn73:5.8.verse: covetousness is unprofitable, uncovetousness is profitable;

mn73:5.9.verse: ill will is unprofitable, non-ill-will is profitable;

mn73:5.10.verse: wrong view is unprofitable, right view is profitable.

mn73:5.11.verse: So, Vaccha, these ten things are unprofitable and ten things are profitable.

mn73:6.1.verse: When, Vaccha, a bhikkhu’s craving has been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, done away with, no more subject to future arising, that bhikkhu is an Arahant with taints destroyed, who has lived the life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, reached his own goal, destroyed the fetters of being, and is completely liberated through final knowledge.”

mn73:7.2.verse: Is there any one bhikkhu, a disciple of Master Gotama’s, who by realizing for himself with direct knowledge here and now enters upon and abides in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints?”

mn73:7.3.verse: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the bhikkhus, my disciples, who by realizing for themselves with direct knowledge here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints.”

mn73:8.1.verse: “Let Master Gotama’s own case rest, and let the bhikkhus’ case rest.

mn73:8.2.verse: Is there any one bhikkhunī, a disciple of Master Gotama’s, who by realizing for herself with direct knowledge here and now enters upon and abides in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints?”

mn73:8.3.verse: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the bhikkhunīs, my disciples, who by realizing for themselves with direct knowledge here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints.”

mn73:9.1.verse: “Let Master Gotama’s own case rest, and let the bhikkhus’ and bhikkhunīs’ case rest.

mn73:9.2.verse: Is there any one lay follower, a disciple of Master Gotama’s, a householder clothed in white, living the life divine, who with the destruction of the five lower fetters will reappear spontaneously and there attain final Nibbāna without ever returning from that world?”

mn73:9.3.verse: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the lay followers, my disciples, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, who with the destruction of the five lower fetters will reappear spontaneously and there attain final Nibbāna without ever returning from that world.”

mn73:10.1.verse: “Let Master Gotama’s own case rest, let the bhikkhus’ and bhikkhunīs’ case rest, and let the case of the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, rest.

mn73:10.2.verse: Is there any one lay follower, a disciple of Master Gotama’s, a householder clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, who carries out his instruction, responds to his advice, has crossed beyond doubt, is free from perplexity, has gained intrepidity, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s dispensation?”

mn73:10.3.verse: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the lay followers, my disciples, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, who carry out my instruction, respond to my advice, have crossed beyond doubt, are free from perplexity, have gained intrepidity, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s dispensation.”

mn73:11.1.verse: “Let Master Gotama’s own case rest, let the bhikkhus’ and bhikkhunīs’ case rest, and let the case of the lay followers, householders clothed in white, both those living the life divine and those enjoying sensual pleasures, rest.

mn73:11.2.verse: Is there any one female lay follower, a disciple of Master Gotama’s, a housewife clothed in white, living the life divine, who with the destruction of the five lower fetters will reappear spontaneously and there attain final Nibbāna without ever returning from that world?”

mn73:11.3.verse: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the female lay followers, my disciples, housewives clothed in white, living the life divine, who with the destruction of the five lower fetters will reappear spontaneously and there attain final Nibbāna without ever returning from that world.”

mn73:12.1.verse: “Let Master Gotama’s own case rest, let the bhikkhus’ and bhikkhunīs’ case rest, let the case of the lay followers, householders clothed in white, both those living the life divine and those enjoying sensual pleasures, rest, and let the case of the female lay followers, housewives clothed in white, living the life divine, rest.

mn73:12.2.verse: Is there any one female lay follower, a disciple of Master Gotama’s, a housewife clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, who carries out his instruction, responds to his advice, has crossed beyond doubt, is free from perplexity, has gained intrepidity, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s dispensation?”

mn73:12.3.verse: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the female lay followers, my disciples, housewives clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, who carry out my instruction, respond to my advice, have crossed beyond doubt, are free from perplexity, have gained intrepidity, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s dispensation.”

mn73:13.1.verse: “If, Master Gotama, only Master Gotama were accomplished in this Dhamma, and no bhikkhus were accomplished in it,

mn73:13.2.verse: then this life divine would be incomplete in that respect.

mn73:13.3.verse: But since Master Gotama is accomplished in this Dhamma and the bhikkhus too are accomplished in it,

mn73:13.4.verse: this life divine is thus complete in that respect.

mn73:13.5.verse: If Master Gotama and the bhikkhus were accomplished in this Dhamma, and no bhikkhunīs were accomplished in it,

mn73:13.6.verse: then this life divine would be incomplete in that respect.

mn73:13.7.verse: But since Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs are accomplished in this Dhamma,

mn73:13.8.verse: this life divine is thus complete in that respect.

mn73:13.9.verse: If Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs were accomplished in this Dhamma, and no lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, were accomplished in it,

mn73:13.10.verse: then this life divine would be incomplete in that respect.

mn73:13.11.verse: But since Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, are accomplished in this Dhamma,

mn73:13.12.verse: this life divine is thus complete in that respect.

mn73:13.13.verse: If Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, were accomplished in this Dhamma, and no lay followers, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, were accomplished in it,

mn73:13.14.verse: then this life divine would be incomplete in that respect.

mn73:13.15.verse: But since Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, are accomplished in this Dhamma,

mn73:13.16.verse: this life divine is thus complete in that respect.

mn73:13.17.verse: If Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, were accomplished in this Dhamma, and no female lay followers, housewives clothed in white, living the life divine, were accomplished in it,

mn73:13.18.verse: then this life divine would be incomplete in that respect.

mn73:13.19.verse: But since Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, and the female lay followers, housewives clothed in white, living the life divine, are accomplished in this Dhamma,

mn73:13.20.verse: this life divine is thus complete in that respect.

mn73:13.21.verse: If Master Gotama and the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunīs and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, living the life divine, and the lay followers, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, and the female lay followers, housewives clothed in white, living the life divine, were accomplished in this Dhamma, and no female lay followers, housewives clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, were accomplished in it,

mn73:13.22.verse: then this life divine would be incomplete in that respect.
