mn77:4.1.verse: Then the Blessed One went to the Wanderers’ Park, the Peacocks’ Sanctuary.

mn77:4.2.verse: Now on that occasion Sakuludāyī the Wanderer was sitting together with a large assembly of wanderers who were shouting and making a great uproar and noise, talking many kinds of pointless talk, such as:

mn77:4.3.verse: talk of kings, talk of robbers, talk of ministers, talk of armies, talk of dangers, talk of battles, talk of food, talk of drink, talk of clothes, talk of beds, talk of garlands, talk of scents, talk of relatives, talk of vehicles, talk of villages, talk of towns, talk of cities, talk of countries, talk of women, talk of heroes, talk of streets, talk of wells, talk of the departed, various idle tales, speculation about the world, speculation about the sea, talk of whether things are or are not, and so on.

mn77:4.4.verse: Sakuludāyī the Wanderer saw the Blessed One coming in the distance.

mn77:4.5.verse: Seeing him, he quieted his own assembly:

mn77:4.9.verse: that venerable one likes quiet and speaks in praise of quiet.

mn77:4.10.verse: Perhaps, finding our assembly quiet, he will think it fit to approach.”

mn77:5.1.verse: Then the Blessed One went up to Sakuludāyī the Wanderer.

mn77:5.2.verse: Sakuludāyī the Wanderer said to the Blessed One:

mn77:5.3.verse: “Let the Blessed One come, venerable sir.

mn77:5.4.verse: Welcome to the Blessed One, venerable sir.

mn77:5.5.verse: It is long, venerable sir, since the Blessed One made an occasion to come here.

mn77:5.6.verse: Let the Blessed One be seated, venerable sir;

mn77:5.8.verse: The Blessed One sat down on the seat made ready.

mn77:5.9.verse: And Sakuludāyī the Wanderer took a certain low seat and sat down at one side.

mn77:5.10.verse: The Blessed One then said to Sakuludāyī the Wanderer, as he sat at one side:

mn77:5.11.verse: “What talk are you gathered here for now, Udāyī? And what was your discussion that was left unfinished?”

mn77:6.1.verse: “Let that be, venerable sir, this talk for which we are now gathered here.

mn77:6.2.verse: It will not be hard for the Blessed One to hear about it later too, venerable sir.

mn77:6.3.verse: A few days ago, venerable sir, when ascetics and brahmins of various sects were gathered together, sitting in the debating hall, this discussion arose:

mn77:6.4.verse: ‘It is a gain indeed for the people of Aṅga and Magadha, it is a great gain indeed for the people of Aṅga and Magadha,

mn77:6.5.verse: that these ascetics and brahmins, heads of orders, heads of groups, teachers of groups, well known and famous ford-makers,[^1] regarded as good by many people, have entered upon the rains residence at Rājagaha.

mn77:6.6.verse: There is this Pūraṇa Kassapa, head of an order, head of a group, teacher of a group, well known and famous, a ford-maker regarded as good by many people;

mn77:6.7.verse: he too has entered upon the rains residence at Rājagaha.

mn77:6.8.verse: There is also this Makkhali Gosāla …

mn77:6.12.verse: and the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta, head of an order, head of a group, teacher of a group, well known and famous, a ford-maker regarded as good by many people;

mn77:6.13.verse: he too has entered upon the rains residence at Rājagaha.

mn77:6.14.verse: There is also this ascetic Gotama, head of an order, head of a group, teacher of a group, well known and famous, a ford-maker regarded as good by many people;

mn77:6.15.verse: he too has entered upon the rains residence at Rājagaha.

mn77:6.16.verse: Now, of these good ascetics and brahmins, heads of orders, heads of groups, teachers of groups, well known and famous ford-makers, regarded as good by many people, which one is honoured, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples, and in dependence on whom, honouring and respecting him, do his disciples live?’

mn77:6.18.verse: ‘This Pūraṇa Kassapa is head of an order, head of a group, teacher of a group, well known and famous, a ford-maker regarded as good by many people;

mn77:6.19.verse: yet he is not honoured, respected, revered, or venerated by his disciples, nor do his disciples live in dependence on Pūraṇa Kassapa, honouring and respecting him.

mn77:6.20.verse: Once, Pūraṇa Kassapa was teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred.

mn77:6.21.verse: Then a certain disciple of Pūraṇa Kassapa made a noise, saying:

mn77:6.22.verse: “Sirs, do not ask Pūraṇa Kassapa about this matter;

mn77:6.24.verse: we know it—ask us about this matter;

mn77:6.25.verse: we will answer it for you, sirs.”

mn77:6.26.verse: Once, Pūraṇa Kassapa, waving his arms about and wailing, could not obtain quiet, saying:

mn77:6.27.verse: “Be quiet, sirs, do not make a noise.

mn77:6.28.verse: They are not asking you, sirs, they are asking us;

mn77:6.30.verse: Many of Pūraṇa Kassapa’s disciples, having proved his assertion wrong, departed, saying:

mn77:6.31.verse: “You do not understand this Dhamma and Discipline; I understand this Dhamma and Discipline. How could you understand this Dhamma and Discipline? You have entered upon a wrong way; I have entered upon a right way. I am consistent; you are inconsistent. What should have been said first you said last; what should have been said last you said first. What you thought over so carefully has been overturned. Your assertion has been refuted. You are defeated. Go and try to salvage your doctrine, or disentangle yourself if you can.”

mn77:6.32.verse: So Pūraṇa Kassapa is not honoured, respected, revered, or venerated by his disciples, nor do his disciples live in dependence on Pūraṇa Kassapa, honouring and respecting him.

mn77:6.33.verse: And Pūraṇa Kassapa was reviled with the reviling of the Dhamma.’

mn77:6.39.verse: the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta is head of an order, head of a group, teacher of a group, well known and famous, a ford-maker regarded as good by many people;

mn77:6.40.verse: yet he is not honoured, respected, revered, or venerated by his disciples, nor do his disciples live in dependence on the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta, honouring and respecting him.

mn77:6.41.verse: Once, the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta was teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred.

mn77:6.42.verse: Then a certain disciple of the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta made a noise, saying:

mn77:6.43.verse: “Sirs, do not ask the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta about this matter;

mn77:6.45.verse: we know it—ask us about this matter;

mn77:6.46.verse: we will answer it for you, sirs.”

mn77:6.47.verse: Once, the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta, waving his arms about and wailing, could not obtain quiet, saying:

mn77:6.48.verse: “Be quiet, sirs, do not make a noise.

mn77:6.49.verse: They are not asking you, sirs, they are asking us;

mn77:6.51.verse: Many of the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta’s disciples, having proved his assertion wrong, departed, saying:

mn77:6.52.verse: “You do not understand this Dhamma and Discipline; I understand this Dhamma and Discipline. How could you understand this Dhamma and Discipline? You have entered upon a wrong way; I have entered upon a right way. I am consistent; you are inconsistent. What should have been said first you said last; what should have been said last you said first. What you thought over so carefully has been overturned. Your assertion has been refuted. You are defeated. Go and try to salvage your doctrine, or disentangle yourself if you can.”

mn77:6.53.verse: So the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta is not honoured, respected, revered, or venerated by his disciples, nor do his disciples live in dependence on the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta, honouring and respecting him.

mn77:6.54.verse: And the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta was reviled with the reviling of the Dhamma.’

mn77:6.56.verse: ‘This ascetic Gotama too is head of an order, head of a group, teacher of a group, well known and famous, a ford-maker regarded as good by many people;

mn77:6.57.verse: and he is honoured, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples, and his disciples live in dependence on the ascetic Gotama, honouring and respecting him.

mn77:6.58.verse: Once, the ascetic Gotama was teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred.

mn77:6.59.verse: Then a certain disciple of the ascetic Gotama cleared his throat.

mn77:6.60.verse: Thereupon a certain companion in the life divine nudged him with his knee, saying:

mn77:6.61.verse: “May the venerable one be quiet, may the venerable one not make a noise; the Teacher, the Blessed One, is teaching the Dhamma.”

mn77:6.62.verse: At the time when the ascetic Gotama is teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred, there is on that occasion no sound of coughing or clearing of throats among the ascetic Gotama’s disciples.

mn77:6.63.verse: For at that time the great crowd of people is waiting expectantly, thinking:

mn77:6.64.verse: “Let us hear the Dhamma that the Blessed One is about to speak.”

mn77:6.65.verse: Just as if a man were pressing out pure honey at a crossroads where four highways meet,

mn77:6.66.verse: and a great crowd of people were waiting expectantly for it;

mn77:6.67.verse: so too, at the time when the ascetic Gotama is teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred, there is on that occasion no sound of coughing or clearing of throats among the ascetic Gotama’s disciples.

mn77:6.68.verse: For at that time the great crowd of people is waiting expectantly, thinking:

mn77:6.69.verse: “Let us hear the Dhamma that the Blessed One is about to speak.”

mn77:6.70.verse: And even those disciples of the ascetic Gotama who quarrel with their companions in the life divine and abandon the training and revert to the lower life, even they speak in praise of the Teacher, in praise of the Dhamma, and in praise of the Sangha; they blame only themselves, not others, saying: “We are unlucky, we have little merit, for though we went forth into homelessness in such a well-proclaimed Dhamma and Discipline, we were unable to live the perfect and pure life divine for the rest of our lives.”

mn77:6.71.verse: Becoming monastery attendants or lay followers, they undertake and observe the five precepts.

mn77:6.72.verse: So the ascetic Gotama is honoured, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples, and his disciples live in dependence on the ascetic Gotama, honouring and respecting him.’”

mn77:7.1.verse: “But, Udāyī, how many things do you see in me on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me?”

mn77:8.1.verse: “I see five things in the Blessed One, venerable sir, on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

mn77:8.3.verse: First, venerable sir, the Blessed One eats little, and he speaks in praise of eating little.

mn77:8.4.verse: This, venerable sir, is the first thing I see in the Blessed One on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

mn77:8.5.verse: Again, venerable sir, the Blessed One is content with any kind of robe, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of robe.

mn77:8.6.verse: This, venerable sir, is the second thing I see in the Blessed One on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

mn77:8.7.verse: Again, venerable sir, the Blessed One is content with any kind of almsfood, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of almsfood.

mn77:8.8.verse: This, venerable sir, is the third thing I see in the Blessed One on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

mn77:8.9.verse: Again, venerable sir, the Blessed One is content with any kind of resting place, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of resting place.

mn77:8.10.verse: This, venerable sir, is the fourth thing I see in the Blessed One on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

mn77:8.11.verse: Again, venerable sir, the Blessed One is secluded, and he speaks in praise of seclusion.

mn77:8.12.verse: This, venerable sir, is the fifth thing I see in the Blessed One on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

mn77:8.13.verse: These, venerable sir, are the five things I see in the Blessed One on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.”

mn77:9.1.verse: “If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama eats little, and he speaks in praise of eating little’—

mn77:9.2.verse: there are disciples of mine, Udāyī, who live on a cupful of food, or on half a cupful, or on the amount of a bilva fruit, or on half a bilva fruit,[^2] while I sometimes eat the full contents of this bowl or even more.

mn77:9.3.verse: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama eats little, and he speaks in praise of eating little’—then those disciples of mine, Udāyī, who live on a cupful of food, or on half a cupful, or on the amount of a bilva fruit, or on half a bilva fruit, would not honour, respect, revere, or venerate me for that reason, nor live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me for that reason.

mn77:9.4.verse: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is content with any kind of robe, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of robe’—

mn77:9.5.verse: there are disciples of mine, Udāyī, who are refuse-rag wearers, wearers of coarse robes, who collect rags from charnel grounds, rubbish heaps, or shops, make them into patched outer robes, and wear them, while I sometimes wear robes given by householders that are so fine that gourd-hair[^3] would seem coarse by comparison.

mn77:9.6.verse: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is content with any kind of robe, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of robe’—then those disciples of mine, Udāyī, who are refuse-rag wearers, wearers of coarse robes, who collect rags from charnel grounds, rubbish heaps, or shops, make them into patched outer robes, and wear them, would not honour, respect, revere, or venerate me for that reason, nor live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me for that reason.

mn77:9.7.verse: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is content with any kind of almsfood, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of almsfood’—

mn77:9.8.verse: there are disciples of mine, Udāyī, who eat almsfood, walking on an uninterrupted almsround, delighting in the practice of gleaning, who, once they have entered a house, do not consent even when invited to sit down, while I sometimes eat, on invitation, fine rice with the dark grains picked out, together with many sauces and curries.

mn77:9.9.verse: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is content with any kind of almsfood, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of almsfood’—then those disciples of mine, Udāyī, who eat almsfood, walking on an uninterrupted almsround, delighting in the practice of gleaning, who, once they have entered a house, do not consent even when invited to sit down, would not honour, respect, revere, or venerate me for that reason, nor live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me for that reason.

mn77:9.10.verse: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is content with any kind of resting place, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of resting place’—

mn77:9.11.verse: there are disciples of mine, Udāyī, who are tree-root dwellers, open-air dwellers, who for eight months do not go under a roof,[^4] while I sometimes live in gabled mansions, plastered within and without, draught-free, with door-bolts fastened and windows shuttered.

mn77:9.12.verse: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is content with any kind of resting place, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of resting place’—then those disciples of mine, Udāyī, who are tree-root dwellers, open-air dwellers, who for eight months do not go under a roof, would not honour, respect, revere, or venerate me for that reason, nor live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me for that reason.

mn77:9.13.verse: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is secluded, and he speaks in praise of seclusion’—

mn77:9.14.verse: there are disciples of mine, Udāyī, who are forest-dwellers, dwelling in remote resting places in forests and woodland thickets, and who come to the midst of the Sangha only once each half-month for the recitation of the Pātimokkha, while I sometimes live surrounded by bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, male lay followers, female lay followers, kings, kings’ ministers, other sectarians, and other sectarians’ disciples.

mn77:9.15.verse: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is secluded, and he speaks in praise of seclusion’—then those disciples of mine, Udāyī, who are forest-dwellers, dwelling in remote resting places in forests and woodland thickets, who come to the midst of the Sangha only once each half-month for the recitation of the Pātimokkha, would not honour, respect, revere, or venerate me for that reason, nor live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me for that reason.

mn77:9.16.verse: So, Udāyī, it is not by these five things that my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.

mn77:10.1.verse: There are, Udāyī, five other things on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.

mn77:10.3.verse: Here, Udāyī, my disciples esteem me for the higher virtue thus:

mn77:10.4.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama has virtue; he possesses the highest aggregate of virtue.’

mn77:11.1.verse: And in that, Udāyī, my disciples esteem me for the higher virtue thus:

mn77:11.2.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama has virtue; he possesses the highest aggregate of virtue’—this, Udāyī, is the first thing on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.

mn77:12.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, my disciples esteem me for my superior knowledge and vision thus:

mn77:12.2.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama, when he knows, says “I know”;

mn77:12.3.verse: when he sees, he says “I see”;

mn77:12.4.verse: the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma by direct knowledge, not without direct knowledge;

mn77:12.5.verse: the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma with a basis, not without a basis;[^5]

mn77:12.6.verse: the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma with its own marvel, not without marvel.’[^6]

mn77:12.7.verse: And in that, Udāyī, my disciples esteem me for my superior knowledge and vision thus:

mn77:12.8.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama, when he knows, says “I know”;

mn77:12.9.verse: when he sees, he says “I see”;

mn77:12.10.verse: the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma by direct knowledge, not without direct knowledge;

mn77:12.11.verse: the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma with a basis, not without a basis;

mn77:12.12.verse: the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma with its own marvel, not without marvel’—this, Udāyī, is the second thing on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.

mn77:13.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, my disciples esteem me for the higher wisdom thus:

mn77:13.2.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama has wisdom; he possesses the highest aggregate of wisdom;

mn77:13.3.verse: it is not possible that he should not foresee a future line of argument, or should not be able to refute thoroughly, in accordance with the Dhamma, an opposing doctrine that has arisen.’

mn77:13.5.verse: would my disciples, knowing and seeing thus, break in with a question from time to time?”

mn77:13.7.verse: “I do not expect instruction from my disciples;

mn77:13.8.verse: rather, it is my disciples who expect instruction from me.

mn77:13.9.verse: And in that, Udāyī, my disciples esteem me for the higher wisdom thus:

mn77:13.10.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama has wisdom; he possesses the highest aggregate of wisdom;

mn77:13.11.verse: it is not possible that he should not foresee a future line of argument, or should not be able to refute an opposing doctrine that has arisen, in accordance with the Dhamma—

mn77:13.13.verse: This, Udāyī, is the third thing on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.

mn77:14.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, when my disciples, overcome by suffering, overwhelmed by suffering, come to me and ask about the noble truth of suffering, being asked I explain to them the noble truth of suffering, and I satisfy their minds with my explanation of the question;

mn77:14.2.verse: they ask me about the origin of suffering …

mn77:14.4.verse: the way leading to the cessation of suffering, being asked I explain to them the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering, and I satisfy their minds with my explanation of the question.

mn77:14.5.verse: And in that, Udāyī, when my disciples, overcome by suffering, overwhelmed by suffering, come to me and ask about the noble truth of suffering, being asked I explain to them the noble truth of suffering, and I satisfy their minds with my explanation of the question;

mn77:14.6.verse: they ask me about the origin of suffering …

mn77:14.8.verse: the way leading to the cessation of suffering.

mn77:14.9.verse: Being asked, I explain to them the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering.

mn77:14.10.verse: I satisfy their minds with my explanation of the question.

mn77:14.11.verse: This, Udāyī, is the fourth thing on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.

mn77:15.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the four foundations of mindfulness.

mn77:15.2.verse: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world;

mn77:15.3.verse: he dwells contemplating feelings as feelings …

mn77:15.4.verse: he dwells contemplating mind as mind …

mn77:15.5.verse: he dwells contemplating mental objects as mental objects, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.

mn77:15.6.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:16.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the four right strivings.

mn77:16.2.verse: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu arouses zeal, makes an effort, stirs up energy, exerts his mind, and strives for the non-arising of unarisen evil unwholesome states;

mn77:16.3.verse: he arouses zeal, makes an effort, stirs up energy, exerts his mind, and strives for the abandoning of arisen evil unwholesome states;

mn77:16.4.verse: he arouses zeal, makes an effort, stirs up energy, exerts his mind, and strives for the arising of unarisen wholesome states;

mn77:16.5.verse: he arouses zeal, makes an effort, stirs up energy, exerts his mind, and strives for the continuation, non-disappearance, strengthening, increase, and fulfilment by development of arisen wholesome states.

mn77:16.6.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:17.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the four bases for spiritual power.

mn77:17.2.verse: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu develops the basis for spiritual power that possesses concentration due to desire and the volitional formations of striving,

mn77:17.3.verse: he develops the basis for spiritual power that possesses concentration due to energy and the volitional formations of striving,

mn77:17.4.verse: he develops the basis for spiritual power that possesses concentration due to (purity of) mind and the volitional formations of striving,

mn77:17.5.verse: he develops the basis for spiritual power that possesses concentration due to investigation and the volitional formations of striving.

mn77:17.6.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:18.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the five faculties.

mn77:18.2.verse: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu develops the faculty of faith, which leads to peace, leads to enlightenment;

mn77:18.3.verse: he develops the faculty of energy …

mn77:18.4.verse: he develops the faculty of mindfulness …

mn77:18.5.verse: he develops the faculty of concentration …

mn77:18.6.verse: he develops the faculty of wisdom, which leads to peace, leads to enlightenment.

mn77:18.7.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:19.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the five powers.

mn77:19.2.verse: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu develops the power of faith, which leads to peace, leads to enlightenment;

mn77:19.3.verse: he develops the power of energy …

mn77:19.4.verse: he develops the power of mindfulness …

mn77:19.5.verse: he develops the power of concentration …

mn77:19.6.verse: he develops the power of wisdom, which leads to peace, leads to enlightenment.

mn77:19.7.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:20.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the seven enlightenment factors.

mn77:20.2.verse: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu develops the mindfulness enlightenment factor, which is supported by seclusion, by dispassion, by cessation, and ripens in relinquishment;

mn77:20.3.verse: he develops the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor …

mn77:20.4.verse: he develops the energy enlightenment factor …

mn77:20.5.verse: he develops the joy enlightenment factor …

mn77:20.6.verse: he develops the tranquillity enlightenment factor …

mn77:20.7.verse: he develops the concentration enlightenment factor …

mn77:20.8.verse: he develops the equanimity enlightenment factor, which is supported by seclusion, by dispassion, by cessation, and ripens in relinquishment.

mn77:20.9.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:21.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the noble eightfold path.

mn77:21.2.verse: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu develops right view, develops right intention, develops right speech, develops right action, develops right livelihood, develops right effort, develops right mindfulness, develops right concentration.

mn77:21.3.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:22.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the eight liberations.

mn77:22.4.verse: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally:

mn77:22.6.verse: One is intent only on the beautiful:

mn77:22.8.verse: With the complete surmounting of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, one enters upon and abides in the base of infinite space:

mn77:22.10.verse: By completely surmounting the base of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, one enters upon and abides in the base of infinite consciousness:

mn77:22.12.verse: By completely surmounting the base of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing’, one enters upon and abides in the base of nothingness:

mn77:22.14.verse: By completely surmounting the base of nothingness, one enters upon and abides in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception:

mn77:22.16.verse: By completely surmounting the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one enters upon and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling:

mn77:22.18.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:23.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the eight bases for transcendence.

mn77:23.2.verse: Perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, limited, fair and ugly:

mn77:23.3.verse: ‘having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.

mn77:23.4.verse: This is the first base for transcendence.

mn77:23.5.verse: Perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, measureless, fair and ugly:

mn77:23.6.verse: ‘having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.

mn77:23.7.verse: This is the second base for transcendence.

mn77:23.8.verse: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, limited, fair and ugly:

mn77:23.9.verse: ‘having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.

mn77:23.10.verse: This is the third base for transcendence.

mn77:23.11.verse: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, measureless, fair and ugly:

mn77:23.12.verse: ‘having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.

mn77:23.13.verse: This is the fourth base for transcendence.

mn77:23.14.verse: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, blue, of blue colour, blue in appearance, blue in lustre.

mn77:23.15.verse: Just as a flax flower is blue, of blue colour, blue in appearance, blue in lustre, or just as that cloth from Vārāṇasī, smoothed on both sides, is blue, of blue colour, blue in appearance, blue in lustre—

mn77:23.16.verse: so too, not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, blue, of blue colour, blue in appearance, blue in lustre.

mn77:23.17.verse: ‘Having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.

mn77:23.18.verse: This is the fifth base for transcendence.

mn77:23.19.verse: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, yellow, of yellow colour, yellow in appearance, yellow in lustre.

mn77:23.20.verse: Just as a kaṇikāra flower is yellow, of yellow colour, yellow in appearance, yellow in lustre, or just as that cloth from Vārāṇasī, smoothed on both sides, is yellow, of yellow colour, yellow in appearance, yellow in lustre—

mn77:23.21.verse: so too, not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, yellow, of yellow colour, yellow in appearance, yellow in lustre.

mn77:23.22.verse: ‘Having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.

mn77:23.23.verse: This is the sixth base for transcendence.

mn77:23.24.verse: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, red, of red colour, red in appearance, red in lustre.

mn77:23.25.verse: Just as a bandhujīvaka flower is red, of red colour, red in appearance, red in lustre, or just as that cloth from Vārāṇasī, smoothed on both sides, is red, of red colour, red in appearance, red in lustre—

mn77:23.26.verse: so too, not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, red, of red colour, red in appearance, red in lustre.

mn77:23.27.verse: ‘Having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.

mn77:23.28.verse: This is the seventh base for transcendence.

mn77:23.29.verse: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, white, of white colour, white in appearance, white in lustre.

mn77:23.30.verse: Just as the morning star[^7] is white, of white colour, white in appearance, white in lustre, or just as that cloth from Vārāṇasī, smoothed on both sides, is white, of white colour, white in appearance, white in lustre—

mn77:23.31.verse: so too, not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, white, of white colour, white in appearance, white in lustre.

mn77:23.32.verse: ‘Having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.

mn77:23.33.verse: This is the eighth base for transcendence.

mn77:23.34.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:24.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the ten bases of totality.[^8]

mn77:24.2.verse: One perceives the earth-totality, above, below, across, undivided, immeasurable;

mn77:24.11.verse: one perceives the consciousness-totality, above, below, across, undivided, immeasurable.

mn77:24.12.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:25.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the four jhānas.

mn77:25.2.verse: Here, Udāyī, quite secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome states, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial application and sustained application, with joy and pleasure born of seclusion.

mn77:25.3.verse: He drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades this very body with the joy and pleasure born of seclusion, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the joy and pleasure born of seclusion.

mn77:25.4.verse: Just as, Udāyī, a skilled bathman or his apprentice heaps bath powder in a metal basin and, sprinkling it again and again with water, kneads it together, so that the ball of bath powder is pervaded by moisture, soaked, saturated within and without, yet does not ooze;

mn77:25.5.verse: so too, Udāyī, a bhikkhu drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades this very body with the joy and pleasure born of seclusion, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the joy and pleasure born of seclusion.

mn77:26.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, with the stilling of initial and sustained application, a bhikkhu … enters upon and abides in the second jhāna …

mn77:26.2.verse: He drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades this very body with the joy and pleasure born of concentration, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the joy and pleasure born of concentration.

mn77:26.3.verse: Just as, Udāyī, there might be a lake whose water wells up from below, with no inflow from the east, west, north, or south, and not even replenished from time to time by showers of rain from the sky;

mn77:26.4.verse: then the cool spring of water welling up in that lake would drench, steep, fill, and pervade that very lake with cool water, so that there would be no part of the whole lake that was not pervaded by the cool water;

mn77:26.5.verse: so too, Udāyī, a bhikkhu drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades this very body with the joy and pleasure born of concentration, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the joy and pleasure born of concentration.

mn77:27.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, with the fading away of joy as well … a bhikkhu … enters upon and abides in the third jhāna …

mn77:27.2.verse: He drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades this very body with the pleasure divested of joy, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the pleasure divested of joy.

mn77:27.3.verse: Just as, Udāyī, in a pond of blue lotuses, or a pond of pink lotuses, or a pond of white lotuses, some lotuses that are born in the water and grow in the water do not rise up out of the water but thrive underwater, and cool water drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades them from their tips to their roots, so that there is no part of the whole of those lotuses that is not pervaded by the cool water;

mn77:27.4.verse: so too, Udāyī, a bhikkhu drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades this very body with the pleasure divested of joy, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the pleasure divested of joy.

mn77:28.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the fourth jhāna, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.

mn77:28.2.verse: He sits pervading this very body with a pure, bright mind, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the pure, bright mind.

mn77:28.3.verse: Just as, Udāyī, a man might be sitting covered from head to foot with a white cloth, so that there would be no part of his whole body not covered by the white cloth;

mn77:28.4.verse: so too, Udāyī, a bhikkhu sits pervading this very body with a pure, bright mind, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the pure, bright mind.

mn77:28.5.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:29.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples understand thus:

mn77:29.2.verse: ‘This body of mine has form, is made up of the four great elements, is procreated by mother and father, is built up out of rice and gruel, and is subject to impermanence, to being rubbed and massaged, to breaking apart and dispersal;

mn77:29.3.verse: and this consciousness of mine is supported by it and bound up with it.’

mn77:29.4.verse: Just as, Udāyī, there might be a beautiful beryl gem of pure water, eight-faceted, well cut, clear, transparent, possessed of all good qualities,

mn77:29.5.verse: and a thread—blue, yellow, red, white, or pale yellow—were strung through it;

mn77:29.6.verse: and a man with good eyes, taking it in his hand, might review it thus:

mn77:29.7.verse: ‘This beryl gem is beautiful, of pure water, eight-faceted, well cut, clear, transparent, possessed of all good qualities,

mn77:29.8.verse: and a thread—blue, yellow, red, white, or pale yellow—is strung through it.’

mn77:29.9.verse: So too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples understand thus:

mn77:29.10.verse: ‘This body of mine has form, is made up of the four great elements, is procreated by mother and father, is built up out of rice and gruel, and is subject to impermanence, to being rubbed and massaged, to breaking apart and dispersal;

mn77:29.11.verse: and this consciousness of mine is supported by it and bound up with it.’

mn77:29.12.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:30.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples create from this body another body, possessing form, mind-made, complete in all its limbs, not deficient in any faculty.

mn77:30.2.verse: Just as, Udāyī, a man might draw a reed out of its sheath;

mn77:30.4.verse: ‘This is the sheath, this is the reed; the sheath is one thing, the reed another; but the reed has been drawn out from the sheath.’

mn77:30.5.verse: Or just as, Udāyī, a man might draw a sword out of its scabbard;

mn77:30.7.verse: ‘This is the sword, this is the scabbard; the sword is one thing, the scabbard another; but the sword has been drawn out from the scabbard.’

mn77:30.8.verse: Or just as, Udāyī, a man might pull a snake out of its slough;

mn77:30.10.verse: ‘This is the snake, this is the slough; the snake is one thing, the slough another; but the snake has been pulled out from the slough.’

mn77:30.11.verse: So too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples create from this body another body, possessing form, mind-made, complete in all its limbs, not deficient in any faculty.

mn77:30.12.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:31.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples wield the various kinds of supernormal power: having been one, they become many; having been many, they become one; they appear and vanish; they go unhindered through a wall, through a rampart, through a mountain, as though through space; they dive in and out of the earth as though it were water; they walk on water without sinking as though on earth; seated cross-legged, they travel through the air like a bird on the wing; with their hands they touch and stroke the moon and sun, so mighty and powerful; they wield bodily mastery even as far as the Brahmā world.

mn77:31.2.verse: Just as, Udāyī, a skilled potter or his apprentice could make and fashion from well-prepared clay whatever kind of vessel he wished;

mn77:31.3.verse: or just as, Udāyī, a skilled ivory-carver or his apprentice could make and fashion from well-prepared ivory whatever kind of ivory-work he wished;

mn77:31.4.verse: or just as, Udāyī, a skilled goldsmith or his apprentice could make and fashion from well-prepared gold whatever kind of gold-work he wished;

mn77:31.5.verse: so too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples wield the various kinds of supernormal power: having been one, they become many; having been many, they become one; they appear and vanish; they go unhindered through a wall, through a rampart, through a mountain, as though through space; they dive in and out of the earth as though it were water; they walk on water without sinking as though on earth; seated cross-legged, they travel through the air like a bird on the wing; with their hands they touch and stroke the moon and sun, so mighty and powerful; they wield bodily mastery even as far as the Brahmā world.

mn77:31.6.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:32.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples hear, with the divine ear element, purified and surpassing the human, both kinds of sounds, the divine and the human, those that are far as well as near.

mn77:32.2.verse: Just as, Udāyī, a strong conch-blower could make himself heard without difficulty in the four quarters;

mn77:32.3.verse: so too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples hear, with the divine ear element, purified and surpassing the human, both kinds of sounds, the divine and the human, those that are far as well as near.

mn77:32.4.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:33.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples, having encompassed the minds of other beings and other persons with their own minds, understand them—

mn77:33.2.verse: they understand a mind with lust as a mind with lust,

mn77:33.3.verse: and a mind without lust as a mind without lust;

mn77:33.4.verse: they understand a mind with hate as a mind with hate,

mn77:33.5.verse: and a mind without hate as a mind without hate;

mn77:33.6.verse: they understand a mind with delusion as a mind with delusion,

mn77:33.7.verse: and a mind without delusion as a mind without delusion;

mn77:33.8.verse: they understand a contracted mind as contracted,

mn77:33.9.verse: and a distracted mind as distracted;

mn77:33.10.verse: they understand an exalted mind as exalted,

mn77:33.11.verse: and an unexalted mind as unexalted;

mn77:33.12.verse: they understand a surpassable mind as surpassable,

mn77:33.13.verse: and an unsurpassable mind as unsurpassable;

mn77:33.14.verse: they understand a concentrated mind as concentrated,

mn77:33.15.verse: and an unconcentrated mind as unconcentrated;

mn77:33.16.verse: they understand a liberated mind as liberated,

mn77:33.17.verse: and an unliberated mind as unliberated.

mn77:33.18.verse: Just as, Udāyī, a woman or a man, young, youthful, and fond of ornaments, looking at the reflection of her own face in a clean, bright mirror or in a bowl of clear water, would know if there were a blemish: ‘there is a blemish’, or would know if there were no blemish: ‘there is no blemish’;

mn77:33.19.verse: so too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples, having encompassed the minds of other beings and other persons with their own minds, understand them—

mn77:33.20.verse: they understand a mind with lust as a mind with lust,

mn77:33.35.verse: and an unliberated mind as unliberated.

mn77:33.36.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:34.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples recollect their manifold past lives, that is, one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many aeons of world-contraction, many aeons of world-expansion, many aeons of world-contraction and expansion:[^10] ‘there I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-span; and passing away from there, I reappeared elsewhere; and there too I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-span; and passing away from there, I reappeared here’—thus they recollect their manifold past lives with their aspects and particulars.

mn77:34.2.verse: Just as, Udāyī, a man might go from his own village to another village, and from that village go on to yet another village, and from that village come back again to his own village; he would think thus: ‘I went from my own village to that village, and there I stood thus, sat thus, spoke thus, was silent thus; and from that village I went on to that other village, and there too I stood thus, sat thus, spoke thus, was silent thus; and from that village I have come back again to my own village’;

mn77:34.3.verse: so too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples recollect their manifold past lives, that is, one birth … thus they recollect their manifold past lives with their aspects and particulars.

mn77:34.4.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:35.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and understand how beings pass on according to their actions: ‘these beings who were ill-conducted in body, speech, and mind, revilers of the noble ones, wrong in view, undertaking action based on wrong view, on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared in a state of deprivation, in a bad destination, in perdition, even in hell; but these beings who were well-conducted in body, speech, and mind, not revilers of the noble ones, right in view, undertaking action based on right view, on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared in a good destination, even in the heavenly world’—thus, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, they see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and understand how beings pass on according to their actions.

mn77:35.2.verse: Just as, Udāyī, there might be two houses with doors, and a man with good eyes standing between them might see people entering a house and leaving it, walking to and fro;

mn77:35.3.verse: so too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, see beings passing away and reappearing … and understand how beings pass on according to their actions …

mn77:35.4.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:36.1.verse: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples, by realizing for themselves with direct knowledge, here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints.

mn77:36.2.verse: Just as, Udāyī, there might be a lake of water in a mountain recess, clear, limpid, and undisturbed, and a man with good eyes, standing on the bank, might see shells, gravel, and pebbles, and also shoals of fish swimming about and resting; he would think thus: ‘This lake of water is clear, limpid, and undisturbed, and there are these shells, gravel, and pebbles, and also these shoals of fish swimming about and resting’;

mn77:36.3.verse: so too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples, by realizing for themselves with direct knowledge, here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints.

mn77:36.4.verse: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.

mn77:37.1.verse: This, Udāyī, is the fifth thing on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.

mn77:38.1.verse: These, Udāyī, are the five things on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.”

mn77:38.2.verse: This is what the Blessed One said.

mn77:38.3.verse: Sakuludāyī the Wanderer was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn77:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

mn77:2.1.verse: Now at that time several very well-known wanderers were residing in their monastery in the peacocks’ feeding ground.

mn77:2.2.verse: They included Annabhāra, Varadhara, Sakuludāyī, and other very well-known wanderers.

mn77:3.1.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha for alms.

mn77:3.3.verse: “It’s too early to wander for alms in Rājagaha.

mn77:3.4.verse: Why don’t I visit the wanderer Sakuludāyī at the monastery for the wanderers in the peacocks’ feeding ground?”

mn77:4.1.verse: So the Buddha went to the monastery for the wanderers.

mn77:4.2.verse: Now at that time, Sakuludāyī was sitting together with a large assembly of wanderers making an uproar, a colossal racket. They engaged in all kinds of low talk, such as

mn77:4.3.verse: talk about kings, bandits, and chief ministers; talk about armies, threats, and wars; talk about food, drink, clothes, and beds; talk about garlands and fragrances; talk about family, vehicles, villages, towns, cities, and countries; talk about women and heroes; talk at the street market and the place for water pots; talk about the departed; motley talk; tales of land and sea; and talk about being reborn in this or that place.

mn77:4.4.verse: Sakuludāyī saw the Buddha coming off in the distance,

mn77:4.6.verse: “Be quiet, good fellows, don’t make a sound.

mn77:4.9.verse: The venerable likes quiet and praises quiet.

mn77:4.10.verse: Hopefully if he sees that our assembly is quiet he’ll see fit to approach.”

mn77:5.4.verse: Welcome to the Blessed One, sir!

mn77:5.5.verse: It’s been a long time since you took the opportunity to come here.

mn77:5.6.verse: Please, sir, sit down, this seat is ready.”

mn77:5.8.verse: The Buddha sat down on the seat spread out,

mn77:5.9.verse: while Sakuludāyī took a low seat and sat to one side.

mn77:5.11.verse: “Udāyī, what were you sitting talking about just now? What conversation was left unfinished?”

mn77:6.1.verse: “Sir, leave aside what we were sitting talking about just now.

mn77:6.2.verse: It won’t be hard for you to hear about that later.

mn77:6.3.verse: Sir, a few days ago several ascetics and brahmins who follow various other religions were sitting together at the debating hall, and this discussion came up among them:

mn77:6.4.verse: ‘The people of Aṅga and Magadha are so fortunate, so very fortunate!

mn77:6.5.verse: For there are these ascetics and brahmins who lead an order and a community, and tutor a community. They’re well-known and famous religious founders, deemed holy by many people. And they have come down for the rainy season residence at Rājagaha.

mn77:6.12.verse: and the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan.

mn77:6.14.verse: This ascetic Gotama also leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people.

mn77:6.15.verse: And he too has come down for the rains residence at Rājagaha.

mn77:6.16.verse: Which of these ascetics and brahmins is honored, respected, revered, and venerated by their disciples? And how do their disciples, honoring and respecting them, remain loyal?’

mn77:6.18.verse: ‘This Pūraṇa Kassapa leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people.

mn77:6.19.verse: But he’s not honored, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples. And his disciples, not honoring and respecting him, don’t remain loyal to him.

mn77:6.20.verse: Once it so happened that he was teaching an assembly of many hundreds.

mn77:6.21.verse: Then one of his disciples made a noise,

mn77:6.22.verse: “My good fellows, don’t ask Pūraṇa Kassapa about that.

mn77:6.24.verse: I know it. Ask me about it,

mn77:6.26.verse: Once it so happened that Pūraṇa Kassapa didn’t get his way, though he called out with raised arms,

mn77:6.27.verse: “Be quiet, good fellows, don’t make a sound.

mn77:6.28.verse: They’re not asking you, they’re asking me!

mn77:6.30.verse: Indeed, many of his disciples have left him after refuting his doctrine:

mn77:6.31.verse: “You don’t understand this teaching and training. I understand this teaching and training. What, you understand this teaching and training? You’re practicing wrong. I’m practicing right. I stay on topic, you don’t. You said last what you should have said first. You said first what you should have said last. What you’ve thought so much about has been disproved. Your doctrine is refuted. Go on, save your doctrine! You’re trapped; get yourself out of this—if you can!”

mn77:6.32.verse: That’s how Pūraṇa Kassapa is not honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed by his disciples. On the contrary, his disciples, not honoring and respecting him, don’t remain loyal to him.

mn77:6.33.verse: Rather, he’s reviled, and rightly so.’

mn77:6.39.verse: This Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people.

mn77:6.40.verse: But he’s not honored, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples. And his disciples, not honoring and respecting him, don’t remain loyal to him.

mn77:6.41.verse: Once it so happened that he was teaching an assembly of many hundreds.

mn77:6.42.verse: Then one of his disciples made a noise,

mn77:6.43.verse: “My good fellows, don’t ask the Jain Ñātika about that.

mn77:6.45.verse: I know it. Ask me about it,

mn77:6.47.verse: Once it so happened that the Jain Ñātika didn’t get his way, though he called out with raised arms,

mn77:6.48.verse: “Be quiet, good fellows, don’t make a sound.

mn77:6.49.verse: They’re not asking you, they’re asking me!

mn77:6.51.verse: Indeed, many of his disciples have left him after refuting his doctrine:

mn77:6.52.verse: “You don’t understand this teaching and training. I understand this teaching and training. What, you understand this teaching and training? You’re practicing wrong. I’m practicing right. I stay on topic, you don’t. You said last what you should have said first. You said first what you should have said last. What you’ve thought so much about has been disproved. Your doctrine is refuted. Go on, save your doctrine! You’re trapped; get yourself out of this—if you can!”

mn77:6.53.verse: That’s how the Jain Ñātika is not honored, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples. On the contrary, his disciples, not honoring and respecting him, don’t remain loyal to him.

mn77:6.54.verse: Rather, he’s reviled, and rightly so.’

mn77:6.56.verse: ‘This ascetic Gotama leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people.

mn77:6.57.verse: He’s honored, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples. And his disciples, honoring and respecting him, remain loyal to him.

mn77:6.58.verse: Once it so happened that he was teaching an assembly of many hundreds.

mn77:6.59.verse: Then one of his disciples cleared their throat.

mn77:6.60.verse: And one of their spiritual companions nudged them with their knee, to indicate,

mn77:6.61.verse: “Hush, venerable, don’t make sound! Our teacher, the Blessed One, is teaching!”

mn77:6.62.verse: While the ascetic Gotama is teaching an assembly of many hundreds, there is no sound of his disciples coughing or clearing their throats.

mn77:6.63.verse: That large crowd is poised expectantly at the ready, thinking,

mn77:6.64.verse: “Whatever the Buddha teaches, we shall listen to it.”

mn77:6.65.verse: It’s like when there’s a person at the crossroads pressing out pure dwarf-bee honey,

mn77:6.66.verse: and a large crowd is poised expectantly at the ready.

mn77:6.67.verse: In the same way, while the ascetic Gotama is teaching an assembly of many hundreds, there is no sound of his disciples coughing or clearing their throats.

mn77:6.68.verse: That large crowd is poised expectantly at the ready, thinking,

mn77:6.69.verse: “Whatever the Buddha teaches, we shall listen to it.”

mn77:6.70.verse: Even when disciples of the ascetic Gotama, having clashed with their spiritual companions, resign the training and return to a lesser life, they speak only praise of the Teacher, the teaching, and the Saṅgha. They blame only themselves, not others: “We were unlucky, we had little merit. For even after going forth in such a well explained teaching and training we weren’t able to practice for life the perfectly full and pure spiritual life.”

mn77:6.71.verse: They become monastery workers or lay followers, and they proceed having undertaken the five precepts.

mn77:6.72.verse: That’s how the ascetic Gotama is honored, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples. And that’s how his disciples, honoring and respecting him, remain loyal to him.’”

mn77:7.1.verse: “But Udāyī, how many qualities do you see in me, because of which my disciples honor, respect, revere, and venerate me; and honoring and respecting me, they remain loyal to me?”

mn77:8.1.verse: “Sir, I see five such qualities in the Buddha.

mn77:8.3.verse: The Buddha eats little and praises eating little.

mn77:8.4.verse: This is the first such quality I see in the Buddha.

mn77:8.5.verse: Furthermore, the Buddha is content with any kind of robe, and praises such contentment.

mn77:8.6.verse: This is the second such quality I see in the Buddha.

mn77:8.7.verse: Furthermore, the Buddha is content with any kind of almsfood, and praises such contentment.

mn77:8.8.verse: This is the third such quality I see in the Buddha.

mn77:8.9.verse: Furthermore, the Buddha is content with any kind of lodging, and praises such contentment.

mn77:8.10.verse: This is the fourth such quality I see in the Buddha.

mn77:8.11.verse: Furthermore, the Buddha is secluded, and praises seclusion.

mn77:8.12.verse: This is the fifth such quality I see in the Buddha.

mn77:8.13.verse: These are the five qualities I see in the Buddha, because of which his disciples honor, respect, revere, and venerate him; and honoring and respecting him, they remain loyal to him.”

mn77:9.1.verse: “Suppose, Udāyī, my disciples were loyal to me because I eat little. Well, there are disciples of mine who eat a tumbler of food, or half a tumbler; they eat a wood-apple, or half a wood-apple.

mn77:9.2.verse: But sometimes I even eat this bowl full to the brim, or even more.

mn77:9.3.verse: So if it were the case that my disciples are loyal to me because I eat little, then those disciples who eat even less would not be loyal to me.

mn77:9.4.verse: Suppose my disciples were loyal to me because I’m content with any kind of robe. Well, there are disciples of mine who have rag robes, wearing shabby robes. They gather scraps from charnel grounds, rubbish dumps, and shops, make them into a patchwork robe and wear it.

mn77:9.5.verse: But sometimes I wear robes offered by householders that are strong, yet next to which bottle-gourd down is coarse.

mn77:9.6.verse: So if it were the case that my disciples are loyal to me because I’m content with any kind of robe, then those disciples who wear rag robes would not be loyal to me.

mn77:9.7.verse: Suppose my disciples were loyal to me because I’m content with any kind of almsfood. Well, there are disciples of mine who eat only almsfood, wander indiscriminately for almsfood, happy to eat whatever they glean. When they’ve entered an inhabited area, they don’t consent when invited to sit down.

mn77:9.8.verse: But sometimes I even eat by invitation boiled fine rice with the dark grains picked out, served with many soups and sauces.

mn77:9.9.verse: So if it were the case that my disciples are loyal to me because I’m content with any kind of almsfood, then those disciples who eat only almsfood would not be loyal to me.

mn77:9.10.verse: Suppose my disciples were loyal to me because I’m content with any kind of lodging. Well, there are disciples of mine who stay at the root of a tree, in the open air. For eight months they don’t go under a roof.

mn77:9.11.verse: But sometimes I even stay in bungalows, plastered inside and out, draft-free, with doors fastened and windows shuttered.

mn77:9.12.verse: So if it were the case that my disciples are loyal to me because I’m content with any kind of lodging, then those disciples who stay at the root of a tree would not be loyal to me.

mn77:9.13.verse: Suppose my disciples were loyal to me because I’m secluded and I praise seclusion. Well, there are disciples of mine who live in the wilderness, in remote lodgings. Having ventured deep into remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest, they live there, coming down to the midst of the Saṅgha each fortnight for the recitation of the monastic code.

mn77:9.14.verse: But sometimes I live crowded by monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen; by rulers and their chief ministers, and monastics of other religions and their disciples.

mn77:9.15.verse: So if it were the case that my disciples are loyal to me because I’m secluded and praise seclusion, then those disciples who live in the wilderness would not be loyal to me.

mn77:9.16.verse: So, Udāyī, it’s not because of these five qualities that my disciples honor, respect, revere, and venerate me; and honoring and respecting me, they remain loyal to me.

mn77:10.1.verse: There are five other qualities because of which my disciples honor, respect, revere, and venerate me; and honoring and respecting me, they remain loyal to me.

mn77:10.3.verse: Firstly, my disciples esteem me for the higher ethics:

mn77:10.4.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama is ethical. He possesses the entire spectrum of ethical conduct to the highest degree.’

mn77:11.2.verse: this is the first quality because of which my disciples are loyal to me.

mn77:12.1.verse: Furthermore, my disciples esteem me for my excellent knowledge and vision:

mn77:12.2.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama only claims to know when he does in fact know.

mn77:12.3.verse: He only claims to see when he really does see.

mn77:12.4.verse: He teaches based on direct knowledge, not without direct knowledge.

mn77:12.5.verse: He teaches based on reason, not without reason.

mn77:12.6.verse: He teaches with a demonstrable basis, not without it.’

mn77:12.12.verse: this is the second quality because of which my disciples are loyal to me.

mn77:13.1.verse: Furthermore, my disciples esteem me for my higher wisdom:

mn77:13.2.verse: ‘The ascetic Gotama is wise. He possesses the entire spectrum of wisdom to the highest degree.

mn77:13.3.verse: It’s not possible that he would fail to foresee grounds for future criticism, or to legitimately and completely refute the doctrines of others that come up.’

mn77:13.5.verse: Would my disciples, knowing and seeing this, break in and interrupt me?”

mn77:13.7.verse: “That’s because I don’t expect to be instructed by my disciples.

mn77:13.8.verse: Invariably, my disciples expect instruction from me.

mn77:13.13.verse: this is the third quality because of which my disciples are loyal to me.

mn77:14.1.verse: Furthermore, my disciples come to me and ask how the noble truth of suffering applies to the suffering in which they are swamped and mired. And I provide them with a satisfying answer to their question.

mn77:14.2.verse: They ask how the noble truths of the origin of suffering,

mn77:14.4.verse: and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering apply to the suffering  in which they are swamped and mired. And I provide them with satisfying answers to their questions.

mn77:14.11.verse: this is the fourth quality because of which my disciples are loyal to me.

mn77:15.1.verse: Furthermore, I have explained to my disciples a practice that they use to develop the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

mn77:15.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

mn77:15.3.verse: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

mn77:15.5.verse: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

mn77:15.6.verse: And many of my disciples meditate on that having attained perfection and consummation of insight.

mn77:16.1.verse: Furthermore, I have explained to my disciples a practice that they use to develop the four right efforts.

mn77:16.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise.

mn77:16.3.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen are given up.

mn77:16.4.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities arise.

mn77:16.5.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.

mn77:16.6.verse: And many of my disciples meditate on that having attained perfection and consummation of insight.

mn77:17.1.verse: Furthermore, I have explained to my disciples a practice that they use to develop the four bases of psychic power.

mn77:17.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort.

mn77:17.3.verse: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to energy, and active effort.

mn77:17.4.verse: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to mental development, and active effort.

mn77:17.5.verse: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to inquiry, and active effort.

mn77:17.6.verse: And many of my disciples meditate on that having attained perfection and consummation of insight.

mn77:18.1.verse: Furthermore, I have explained to my disciples a practice that they use to develop the five faculties.

mn77:18.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the faculties of faith,

mn77:18.6.verse: and wisdom, which lead to peace and awakening.

mn77:18.7.verse: And many of my disciples meditate on that having attained perfection and consummation of insight.

mn77:19.1.verse: Furthermore, I have explained to my disciples a practice that they use to develop the five powers.

mn77:19.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the powers of faith,

mn77:19.6.verse: and wisdom, which lead to peace and awakening.

mn77:19.7.verse: And many of my disciples meditate on that having attained perfection and consummation of insight.

mn77:20.1.verse: Furthermore, I have explained to my disciples a practice that they use to develop the seven awakening factors.

mn77:20.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factors of mindfulness,

mn77:20.8.verse: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

mn77:20.9.verse: And many of my disciples meditate on that having attained perfection and consummation of insight.

mn77:21.1.verse: Furthermore, I have explained to my disciples a practice that they use to develop the noble eightfold path.

mn77:21.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

mn77:21.3.verse: And many of my disciples meditate on that having attained perfection and consummation of insight.

mn77:22.1.verse: Furthermore, I have explained to my disciples a practice that they use to develop the eight liberations.

mn77:22.2.verse: Having physical form, they see forms.

mn77:22.4.verse: Not perceiving form internally, they see forms externally.

mn77:22.8.verse: Going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite space.

mn77:22.10.verse: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

mn77:22.12.verse: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness.

mn77:22.14.verse: Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, they enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

mn77:22.16.verse: Going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, they enter and remain in the cessation of perception and feeling.

mn77:22.18.verse: And many of my disciples meditate on that having attained perfection and consummation of insight.

mn77:23.1.verse: Furthermore, I have explained to my disciples a practice that they use to develop the eight dimensions of mastery.

mn77:23.2.verse: Perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limited, both pretty and ugly.

mn77:23.3.verse: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

mn77:23.4.verse: This is the first dimension of mastery.

mn77:23.5.verse: Perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limitless, both pretty and ugly.

mn77:23.6.verse: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

mn77:23.7.verse: This is the second dimension of mastery.

mn77:23.8.verse: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limited, both pretty and ugly.

mn77:23.9.verse: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

mn77:23.10.verse: This is the third dimension of mastery.

mn77:23.11.verse: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limitless, both pretty and ugly.

mn77:23.12.verse: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

mn77:23.13.verse: This is the fourth dimension of mastery.

mn77:23.14.verse: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, blue, with blue color and blue appearance.

mn77:23.15.verse: They’re like a flax flower that’s blue, with blue color and blue appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, blue, with blue color and blue appearance.

mn77:23.16.verse: In the same way, not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, blue, with blue color and blue appearance.

mn77:23.17.verse: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

mn77:23.18.verse: This is the fifth dimension of mastery.

mn77:23.19.verse: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance.

mn77:23.20.verse: They’re like a champak flower that’s yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance.

mn77:23.21.verse: In the same way, not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance.

mn77:23.22.verse: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

mn77:23.23.verse: This is the sixth dimension of mastery.

mn77:23.24.verse: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are red, with red color and red appearance.

mn77:23.25.verse: They’re like a scarlet mallow flower that’s red, with red color and red appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, red, with red color and red appearance.

mn77:23.26.verse: In the same way, not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are red, with red color and red appearance.

mn77:23.27.verse: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

mn77:23.28.verse: This is the seventh dimension of mastery.

mn77:23.29.verse: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are white, with white color and white appearance.

mn77:23.30.verse: They’re like the morning star that’s white, with white color and white appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, white, with white color and white appearance.

mn77:23.31.verse: In the same way, not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are white, with white color and white appearance.

mn77:23.32.verse: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

mn77:23.33.verse: This is the eighth dimension of mastery.

mn77:23.34.verse: And many of my disciples meditate on that having attained perfection and consummation of insight.

mn77:24.1.verse: Furthermore, I have explained to my disciples a practice that they use to develop the ten universal dimensions of meditation.

mn77:24.2.verse: Someone perceives the meditation on universal earth above, below, across, undivided and limitless.

mn77:24.3.verse: They perceive the meditation on universal water …

mn77:24.11.verse: the meditation on universal consciousness above, below, across, undivided and limitless.

mn77:24.12.verse: And many of my disciples meditate on that having attained perfection and consummation of insight.

mn77:25.1.verse: Furthermore, I have explained to my disciples a practice that they use to develop the four absorptions.

mn77:25.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

mn77:25.3.verse: They drench, steep, fill, and spread themselves with rapture and bliss born of seclusion. There’s no part of the body that’s not spread with rapture and bliss born of seclusion.

mn77:25.4.verse: It’s like when a deft bathroom attendant or their apprentice pours bath powder into a bronze dish, sprinkling it little by little with water. They knead it until the ball of bath powder is soaked and saturated with moisture, spread through inside and out; yet no moisture oozes out.

mn77:25.5.verse: In the same way, a mendicant drenches, steeps, fills, and spreads themselves with rapture and bliss born of seclusion. There’s no part of the body that’s not spread with rapture and bliss born of seclusion.

mn77:26.1.verse: Furthermore, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, a mendicant enters and remains in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

mn77:26.2.verse: They drench, steep, fill, and spread themselves with rapture and bliss born of immersion. There’s no part of the body that’s not spread with rapture and bliss born of immersion.

mn77:26.3.verse: It’s like a deep lake fed by spring water. There’s no inlet to the east, west, north, or south, and the heavens would not properly bestow showers from time to time.

mn77:26.4.verse: But the stream of cool water welling up in the lake drenches, steeps, fills, and spreads throughout the lake. There’s no part of the lake that’s not spread through with cool water.

mn77:26.5.verse: In the same way, a mendicant drenches, steeps, fills, and spreads themselves with rapture and bliss born of immersion. There’s no part of the body that’s not spread with rapture and bliss born of immersion.

mn77:27.1.verse: Furthermore, with the fading away of rapture, a mendicant enters and remains in the third absorption. They meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

mn77:27.2.verse: They drench, steep, fill, and spread themselves with bliss free of rapture. There’s no part of the body that’s not spread with bliss free of rapture.

mn77:27.3.verse: It’s like a pool with blue water lilies, or pink or white lotuses. Some of them sprout and grow in the water without rising above it, thriving underwater. From the tip to the root they’re drenched, steeped, filled, and soaked with cool water. There’s no part of them that’s not soaked with cool water.

mn77:27.4.verse: In the same way, a mendicant drenches, steeps, fills, and spreads themselves with bliss free of rapture. There’s no part of the body that’s not spread with bliss free of rapture.
