mn80:2.10.verse: “Worthy Gotama, the ultimate splendor is the splendor compared to which no other splendor is finer.”

mn80:3.1.verse: “Kaccāna, you could draw this out for a long time.

mn80:3.2.verse: You say, ‘The ultimate splendor is the splendor compared to which no other splendor is finer.’ But you don’t describe that splendor.

mn80:3.3.verse: Suppose a man was to say,

mn80:3.4.verse: ‘Whoever the finest lady in the land is, it is her that I want, her I desire!’

mn80:3.6.verse: ‘My man, that finest lady in the land who you desire—do you know whether she’s an aristocrat, a brahmin, a peasant, or a menial?’

mn80:3.9.verse: ‘My friend, that finest lady in the land who you desire—do you know her name or clan? Whether she’s tall or short or medium? Whether her skin is black, brown, or dingy? Whether she comes from such-and-such village, town, or city?’

mn80:3.12.verse: ‘My man, do you desire someone who you’ve never even known or seen?’

mn80:3.15.verse: This being so, doesn’t that man’s statement turn out to have no demonstrable basis?”

mn80:3.17.verse: “In the same way, you say, ‘The ultimate splendor is the splendor compared to which no other splendor is finer.’ But you don’t describe that splendor.”

mn80:4.1.verse: “Mister Gotama, suppose there was a beryl gem that was naturally lustrous, eight-faceted, well-worked. When placed on a cream rug it would shine and glow and dazzle. Such is the splendor of the self that is free of disease after death.”

mn80:5.2.verse: Which of these two has a finer splendor: such a beryl gem, or a firefly in the dark of night?”

mn80:5.3.verse: “A firefly in the dark of night.”

mn80:6.2.verse: Which of these two has a finer splendor: a firefly in the dark of night, or an oil lamp in the dark of night?”

mn80:6.3.verse: “An oil lamp in the dark of night.”

mn80:7.2.verse: Which of these two has a finer splendor: an oil lamp in the dark of night, or a great mass of fire in the dark of night?”

mn80:7.3.verse: “A great mass of fire in the dark of night.”

mn80:8.2.verse: Which of these two has a finer splendor: a great mass of fire in the dark of night, or the morning star in the clear and cloudless heavens at the crack of dawn?”

mn80:8.3.verse: “The morning star in the clear and cloudless heavens at the crack of dawn.”

mn80:9.2.verse: Which of these two has a finer splendor: the morning star in the clear and cloudless heavens at the crack of dawn, or the full moon at midnight in the clear and cloudless heavens on the fifteenth day sabbath?”

mn80:9.3.verse: “The full moon at midnight in the clear and cloudless heavens on the fifteenth day sabbath.”

mn80:10.2.verse: Which of these two has a finer splendor: the full moon at midnight in the clear and cloudless heavens on the fifteenth day sabbath, or the sun at midday in the clear and cloudless heavens in the last month of the rainy season, in autumn?”

mn80:10.3.verse: “The sun at midday in the clear and cloudless heavens in the last month of the rainy season, in autumn.”

mn80:11.1.verse: “Beyond this, Kaccāna, I know very many gods on whom the luminosity of the sun and moon makes no impression.

mn80:11.3.verse: ‘The splendor compared to which no other splendor is finer.’

mn80:11.4.verse: But of the splendor inferior to a firefly you say, ‘This is the ultimate splendor.’ And you don’t describe that splendor.

mn80:12.1.verse: Kaccāna, there are these five kinds of sensual stimulation.

mn80:12.3.verse: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

mn80:12.7.verse: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

mn80:12.8.verse: These are the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

mn80:13.1.verse: The pleasure and happiness that arises from these five kinds of sensual stimulation is called sensual pleasure.

mn80:13.2.verse: ‘From the senses comes sensual pleasure. Beyond sensual pleasure is the pleasure that surmounts the sensual, which is said to be the best of these.’”

mn80:14.1.verse: When he said this, Vekhanasa said to the Buddha,

mn80:14.3.verse: How well said this was by the worthy Gotama!

mn80:14.4.verse: ‘From the senses comes sensual pleasure. Beyond sensual pleasure is the pleasure that surmounts the sensual, which is said to be the best of these.’

mn80:14.5.verse: Worthy Gotama, from the senses comes sensual pleasure. Beyond sensual pleasure is the pleasure that surmounts the sensual, which is said to be the best of these.”

mn80:14.6.verse: “Kaccāna, since you have a different view, creed, and belief, and another discipline and denomination, it’s hard for you to understand

mn80:14.7.verse: the senses, sensual pleasure, and the pleasure that surmounts the sensual.

mn80:14.8.verse: There are mendicants who are perfected, who have ended the defilements, completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and are rightly freed through enlightenment. They can understand

mn80:14.9.verse: the senses, sensual pleasure, and the pleasure that surmounts the sensual.”

mn80:15.1.verse: When he said this, Vekhanasa became angry and upset. He even attacked and badmouthed the Buddha himself, saying,

mn80:15.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama will be worsted!” He said to the Buddha,

mn80:15.3.verse: “This is exactly what happens with some ascetics and brahmins. Not knowing the first beginning or seeing the final end, they nevertheless claim:

mn80:15.4.verse: ‘We understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’

mn80:15.5.verse: Their statement turns out to be a joke—mere words, vacuous and hollow.”

mn80:16.1.verse: “Kaccāna, there are some ascetics and brahmins who, not knowing the first beginning or seeing the final end, nevertheless claim:

mn80:16.2.verse: ‘We understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’

mn80:16.3.verse: There is a legitimate refutation of them.

mn80:16.4.verse: Nevertheless, Kaccāna, leave aside the first beginning and the final end.

mn80:16.5.verse: Let a sensible person come—neither devious nor deceitful, a person of integrity. I teach and instruct them.

mn80:16.6.verse: Practicing as instructed they will soon know and see for themselves,

mn80:16.7.verse: ‘So this is how to be rightly released from the bond, that is, the bond of ignorance.’

mn80:16.8.verse: Suppose there was a little baby bound with swaddling up to the neck.

mn80:16.9.verse: As they grow up and their senses mature, they’re accordingly released from those bonds.

mn80:16.10.verse: They’d know ‘I’m released,’ and there would be no more bonds.

mn80:16.11.verse: In the same way, let a sensible person come—neither devious nor deceitful, a person of integrity. I teach and instruct them.

mn80:16.12.verse: Practicing as instructed they will soon know and see for themselves,

mn80:16.13.verse: ‘So this is how to be rightly released from the bond, that is, the bond of ignorance.’”

mn80:17.1.verse: When he said this, Vekhanasa said to the Buddha,

mn80:17.3.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

mn81:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Kosalans together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants.

mn81:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha left the road, and at a certain spot he smiled.

mn81:2.3.verse: “What is the cause, what is the reason why the Buddha smiled?

mn81:2.4.verse: Realized Ones do not smile for no reason.”

mn81:2.5.verse: So Ānanda arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha, and said,

mn81:2.6.verse: “What is the cause, what is the reason why the Buddha smiled?

mn81:2.7.verse: Realized Ones do not smile for no reason.”

mn81:3.1.verse: “Once upon a time, Ānanda, there was a market town in this spot named Vebhaliṅga. It was successful and prosperous, populous and full of people.

mn81:3.2.verse: And Kassapa, a blessed one, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, lived supported by Vebhaliṅga.

mn81:3.3.verse: It was here, in fact, that he had his monastery,

mn81:3.4.verse: where he advised the mendicant Saṅgha while seated.”

mn81:4.1.verse: Then Ānanda spread out his outer robe folded in four and said to the Buddha,

mn81:4.2.verse: “Well then, sir, may the Blessed One sit here!

mn81:4.3.verse: Then this piece of land will have been occupied by two perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas.”

mn81:4.4.verse: The Buddha sat down on the seat spread out.

mn81:4.5.verse: When he was seated he said to Venerable Ānanda:

mn81:5.1.verse: “Once upon a time, Ānanda, there was a market town in this spot named Vebhaliṅga. It was successful and prosperous, populous and full of people.

mn81:5.2.verse: And Kassapa, a blessed one, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, lived supported by Vebhaliṅga.

mn81:5.3.verse: It was here, in fact, that he had his monastery,

mn81:5.4.verse: where he advised the mendicant Saṅgha while seated.

mn81:6.1.verse: The Buddha Kassapa had as chief supporter in Vebhaliṅga a potter named Ghaṭīkāra.

mn81:6.2.verse: Ghaṭīkāra had a dear friend named Jotipāla, a student.

mn81:6.4.verse: ‘Come, dear Jotipāla, let’s go to see the Blessed One Kassapa, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

mn81:6.5.verse: For I deem it holy to see that Blessed One.’

mn81:6.6.verse: When he said this, Jotipāla said to him,

mn81:6.8.verse: What’s the use of seeing that shaveling, that fake ascetic?’

mn81:6.10.verse: and a third time, Ghaṭīkāra addressed Jotipāla,

mn81:6.11.verse: ‘Come, dear Jotipāla, let’s go to see the Blessed One Kassapa, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

mn81:6.12.verse: For I deem it holy to see that Blessed One.’

mn81:6.13.verse: For a third time, Jotipāla said to him,

mn81:6.15.verse: What’s the use of seeing that shaveling, that fake ascetic?’

mn81:6.16.verse: ‘Well then, dear Jotipāla, let’s take some bathing cleanser and go to the river to bathe.’

mn81:7.2.verse: ‘Dear Jotipāla, the Buddha Kassapa’s monastery is not far away.

mn81:7.3.verse: Let’s go to see the Blessed One Kassapa, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

mn81:7.4.verse: For I deem it holy to see that Blessed One.’

mn81:7.5.verse: When he said this, Jotipāla said to him,

mn81:7.7.verse: What’s the use of seeing that shaveling, that fake ascetic?’

mn81:7.9.verse: and a third time, Ghaṭīkāra addressed Jotipāla,

mn81:7.10.verse: ‘Dear Jotipāla, the Buddha Kassapa’s monastery is not far away.

mn81:7.11.verse: Let’s go to see the Blessed One Kassapa, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

mn81:7.12.verse: For I deem it holy to see that Blessed One.’

mn81:7.13.verse: For a third time, Jotipāla said to him,

mn81:7.15.verse: What’s the use of seeing that shaveling, that fake ascetic?’

mn81:8.1.verse: Then Ghaṭīkāra grabbed Jotipāla by the skirt-hem and said,

mn81:8.2.verse: ‘Dear Jotipāla, the Buddha Kassapa’s monastery is not far away.

mn81:8.3.verse: Let’s go to see the Blessed One Kassapa, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

mn81:8.4.verse: For I deem it holy to see that Blessed One.’

mn81:8.5.verse: So Jotipāla undid his skirt-hem and said to Ghaṭīkāra,

mn81:8.7.verse: What’s the use of seeing that shaveling, that fake ascetic?’

mn81:9.1.verse: Then Ghaṭīkāra grabbed Jotipāla by the hair of his freshly-washed head and said,

mn81:9.2.verse: ‘Dear Jotipāla, the Buddha Kassapa’s monastery is not far away.

mn81:9.3.verse: Let’s go to see the Blessed One Kassapa, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

mn81:9.4.verse: For I deem it holy to see that Blessed One.’

mn81:9.7.verse: how this potter Ghaṭīkāra, though of lowly birth, should presume to grab me by the hair of my freshly-washed head!

mn81:9.8.verse: This must be no ordinary matter.’

mn81:9.10.verse: ‘You’d even milk it to this extent, dear Ghaṭīkāra?’

mn81:9.11.verse: ‘I even milk it to this extent, dear Jotipāla.

mn81:9.12.verse: For that is how holy I deem it to see that Blessed One.’

mn81:9.13.verse: ‘Well then, dear Ghaṭīkāra, release me, we shall go.’

mn81:10.1.verse: Then Ghaṭīkāra the potter and Jotipāla the student went to the Buddha Kassapa. Ghaṭīkāra bowed and sat down to one side, but Jotipāla exchanged greetings with the Buddha and sat down to one side.

mn81:10.2.verse: Ghaṭīkāra said to the Buddha Kassapa,

mn81:10.3.verse: ‘Sir, this is the student Jotipāla, my dear friend.

mn81:10.5.verse: Then the Buddha Kassapa educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired Ghaṭīkāra and Jotipāla with a Dhamma talk.

mn81:10.6.verse: Then they got up from their seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha Kassapa, keeping him on their right, before leaving.

mn81:11.2.verse: ‘Dear Ghaṭīkāra, you have heard this teaching, so why don’t you go forth from the lay life to homelessness?’

mn81:11.3.verse: ‘Don’t you know, dear Jotipāla, that I  provide for my blind old parents?’

mn81:11.4.verse: ‘Well then, dear Ghaṭīkāra, I shall go forth from the lay life to homelessness.’

mn81:12.1.verse: Then Ghaṭīkāra and Jotipāla went to the Buddha Kassapa, bowed and sat down to one side. Ghaṭīkāra said to the Buddha Kassapa,

mn81:12.2.verse: ‘Sir, this is the student Jotipāla, my dear friend.

mn81:12.3.verse: Please give him the going forth.’

mn81:12.4.verse: And Jotipāla the student received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

mn81:13.1.verse: Not long after Jotipāla’s ordination, a fortnight later, the Buddha Kassapa—having stayed in Vebhaliṅga as long as he pleased—set out for Varanasi.

mn81:13.2.verse: Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Varanasi,

mn81:13.3.verse: where he stayed near Varanasi, in the deer park at Isipatana.

mn81:14.1.verse: King Kikī of Kāsi heard that he had arrived.

mn81:14.2.verse: He had the finest carriages harnessed. He then mounted a fine carriage and, along with other fine carriages, set out in full royal pomp from Varanasi to see the Buddha Kassapa.

mn81:14.3.verse: He went by carriage as far as the terrain allowed, then descended and approached the Buddha Kassapa on foot. He bowed and sat down to one side.

mn81:14.4.verse: The Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired him with a Dhamma talk.

mn81:14.5.verse: Then King Kikī said to the Buddha,

mn81:14.6.verse: ‘Sir, would the Buddha together with the mendicant Saṅgha please accept tomorrow’s meal from me?’

mn81:14.7.verse: The Buddha Kassapa consented with silence.

mn81:15.1.verse: Then, knowing that the Buddha had consented, King Kikī rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

mn81:16.1.verse: And when the night had passed, King Kikī had delicious fresh and cooked foods prepared in his own home—soft saffron rice with the dark grains picked out, served with many soups and sauces. Then he had the Buddha informed of the time, saying,

mn81:16.2.verse: ‘Sir, it’s time. The meal is ready.’

mn81:17.1.verse: Then Kassapa Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of King Kikī, where he sat down on the seat spread out together with the Saṅgha of mendicants.

mn81:17.2.verse: Then King Kikī served and satisfied the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha with his own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

mn81:17.3.verse: When the Buddha Kassapa had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, King Kikī took a low seat and sat to one side.

mn81:17.4.verse: There he said to the Buddha Kassapa,

mn81:17.5.verse: ‘Sir, would the Buddha please accept my invitation to reside in Varanasi for the rainy season?

mn81:17.6.verse: The Saṅgha will be looked after in the same style.’

mn81:17.8.verse: I have already accepted an invitation for the rains residence.’

mn81:17.10.verse: and a third time King Kikī said to the Buddha Kassapa,

mn81:17.11.verse: ‘Sir, would the Buddha please accept my invitation to reside in Varanasi for the rainy season?

mn81:17.12.verse: The Saṅgha will be looked after in the same style.’

mn81:17.14.verse: I have already accepted an invitation for the rains residence.’

mn81:17.15.verse: Then King Kikī, thinking, ‘The Buddha does not accept my invitation to reside for the rains in Varanasi,’ became sad and upset.

mn81:17.16.verse: Then King Kikī said to the Buddha Kassapa,

mn81:17.17.verse: ‘Sir, do you have another supporter better than me?’

mn81:18.1.verse: ‘Great king, there is a market town named Vebhaliṅga,

mn81:18.2.verse: where there is a potter named Ghaṭīkāra.

mn81:18.4.verse: Now, Great King, when you thought, “The Buddha does not accept my invitation to reside for the rains in Varanasi,” you became sad and upset.

mn81:18.5.verse: But Ghaṭīkāra doesn’t get upset, nor will he.

mn81:18.6.verse: Ghaṭīkāra has gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.

mn81:18.7.verse: He doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

mn81:18.8.verse: He has experiential confidence in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and possesses the ethics loved by the noble ones.

mn81:18.9.verse: He is free of doubt regarding suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

mn81:18.10.verse: He eats in one part of the day; he’s chaste, ethical, and of good character.

mn81:18.11.verse: He has set aside gems and gold, and quit using gold and currency.

mn81:18.12.verse: He has put down the shovel and doesn’t dig the earth with his own hands.

mn81:18.13.verse: He takes what has crumbled off by a riverbank or been dug up by mice, and brings it back in a carrier. When he has made a pot, he says,

mn81:18.14.verse: “Anyone may leave bagged sesame, mung beans, or chickpeas here and take what they wish.”

mn81:18.15.verse: He provided for his blind old parents.

mn81:18.16.verse: And since he has ended the five lower fetters, Ghaṭīkāra will be reborn spontaneously and will become extinguished there, not liable to return from that world.

mn81:19.1.verse: This one time, Great King, I was staying near the market town of Vebhaliṅga.

mn81:19.2.verse: Then I robed up in the morning and, taking my bowl and robe, went to the home of Ghaṭīkāra’s parents, where I said to them,

mn81:19.4.verse: “Your supporter has gone out, sir. But take rice from the pot and sauce from the pan and eat.”

mn81:19.5.verse: So that’s what I did. And after eating I rose from my seat and left.

mn81:19.6.verse: Then Ghaṭīkāra went up to his parents and said,

mn81:19.7.verse: “Who took rice from the pot and sauce from the pan, ate it, and left?”

mn81:19.8.verse: “It was the Buddha Kassapa, my dear.”

mn81:19.11.verse: in that the Buddha Kassapa trusts me so much!”

mn81:19.12.verse: Then joy and happiness did not leave him for a fortnight, or his parents for a week.

mn81:20.1.verse: Another time, Great King, I was staying near that same market town of Vebhaliṅga.

mn81:20.2.verse: Then I robed up in the morning and, taking my bowl and robe, went to the home of Ghaṭīkāra’s parents, where I said to them,

mn81:20.4.verse: “Your supporter has gone out, sir. But take porridge from the pot and sauce from the pan and eat.”

mn81:20.5.verse: So that’s what I did. And after eating I rose from my seat and left.

mn81:20.6.verse: Then Ghaṭīkāra went up to his parents and said,

mn81:20.7.verse: “Who took porridge from the pot and sauce from the pan, ate it, and left?”

mn81:20.8.verse: “It was the Buddha Kassapa, my dear.”

mn81:20.11.verse: to be trusted so much by the Buddha Kassapa!”

mn81:20.12.verse: Then joy and happiness did not leave him for a fortnight, or his parents for a week.

mn81:21.1.verse: Another time, Great King, I was staying near that same market town of Vebhaliṅga.

mn81:21.2.verse: Now at that time my hut leaked.

mn81:21.4.verse: “Mendicants, go to Ghaṭīkāra’s home and find some grass.”

mn81:21.5.verse: When I said this, those mendicants said to me,

mn81:21.6.verse: “Sir, there’s no grass there, but his workshop has a grass roof.”

mn81:21.7.verse: “Then go to the workshop and strip the grass.”

mn81:21.9.verse: Then Ghaṭīkāra’s parents said to those mendicants,

mn81:21.10.verse: “Who’s stripping the grass from the workshop?”

mn81:21.11.verse: “It’s the mendicants, sister. The Buddha’s hut is leaking.”

mn81:21.12.verse: “Take it, sirs! Take it, dearest ones!”

mn81:21.13.verse: Then Ghaṭīkāra went up to his parents and said,

mn81:21.14.verse: “Who stripped the grass from the workshop?”

mn81:21.15.verse: “It was the mendicants, dear. It seems the Buddha’s hut is leaking.”

mn81:21.18.verse: to be trusted so much by the Buddha Kassapa!”

mn81:21.19.verse: Then joy and happiness did not leave him for a fortnight, or his parents for a week.

mn81:21.20.verse: Then the workshop remained with the atmosphere for a roof for the whole three months, but the heavens did not rain on it.

mn81:21.21.verse: And that, Great King, is what Ghaṭīkāra the potter is like.’

mn81:21.22.verse: ‘Ghaṭīkāra the potter is fortunate, very fortunate,

mn81:21.23.verse: to be so trusted by the Buddha Kassapa.’

mn81:22.1.verse: Then King Kikī sent around five hundred loads of rice, soft saffron rice, and suitable sauce to Ghaṭīkāra.

mn81:22.2.verse: Then one of the king’s men approached Ghaṭīkāra and said,

mn81:22.3.verse: ‘Sir, these five hundred loads of rice, soft saffron rice, and suitable sauce have been sent to you by King Kikī of Kāsi.

mn81:22.5.verse: ‘The king has many duties, and much to do.

mn81:22.7.verse: Let this be for the king himself.’

mn81:23.2.verse: ‘Surely the student Jotipāla must have been someone else at that time?’

mn81:23.3.verse: But you should not see it like this.

mn81:23.4.verse: I myself was the student Jotipāla at that time.”

mn81:23.5.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn81:23.6.verse: Satisfied, Venerable Ānanda approved what the Buddha said.

mn82:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering in the Kuru country together with a large Sangha of bhikkhus. He eventually arrived at Thullakoṭṭhita, a Kuru town.

mn82:2.1.verse: The divine caste householders of Thullakoṭṭhita heard:

mn82:2.2.verse: ‘The monk Gotama, it seems a son of the Sakyans who went forth from a Sakyan clan, has been wandering in the Kosalan country with a large Sangha of bhikkhus and has come to Sālā.

mn82:2.3.verse: Now a good report of Master Gotama has been spread to this effect.

mn82:2.4.verse: “That Blessed One is such since he is Arahant and Fully Enlightened, perfect in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of worlds, incomparable teacher of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and men, enlightened, blessed.

mn82:2.5.verse: He describes this world with its Māras, and its (Brahmā) Divinities, this generation with its monks and divines, with its kings and its men, which he has himself realized through direct knowledge.

mn82:2.6.verse: He teaches a Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle and good in the end with (the right) meaning and phrasing, he affirms a life divine that is utterly perfect and pure.”

mn82:2.7.verse: It is good to see such Arahants.’

mn82:3.1.verse: Then the divine caste householders of Thullakoṭṭhita went to the Blessed One and some paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at one side; some exchanged greetings with him, and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished, sat down at one side; some raised their hands palms together in salutation to the Blessed One and sat down at one side; some pronounced their name and clan in the Blessed One’s presence and sat down at one side; some kept silent and sat down at one side.

mn82:3.2.verse: When they were seated, the Blessed One instructed, urged, roused and encouraged them with talk on the Dhamma.

mn82:4.1.verse: Now at that time a clansman called Raṭṭhapāla, the son of the leading clan in that same Thullakoṭṭhita, was sitting in the assembly.

mn82:4.3.verse: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, it is not possible while living in a household to lead the life divine utterly perfect and pure as a polished shell.

mn82:4.4.verse: Suppose I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and went forth from the home life into homelessness?’

mn82:5.1.verse: Then the brahmin householders of Thullakoṭṭhita, having been instructed, urged, roused and encouraged by the Blessed One with talk on the Dhamma, and delighted in his words and agreeing, rose from their seats, and after paying homage to him, they departed keeping him on their right.

mn82:6.1.verse: Soon after they had gone the clansman Raṭṭhapāla went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, he said to the Blessed One:

mn82:6.2.verse: ‘Venerable sir, as I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, it is not possible while living in a household, to lead the life divine as perfect and pure as a polished shell.

mn82:6.3.verse: Venerable sir, I want to shave off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and go forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:6.4.verse: I would receive the Going-forth under the Blessed One and I would receive the Full Admission.’

mn82:6.6.verse: ‘Are you permitted by your parents, Raṭṭhapāla, to go forth from the home life into homelessness?’

mn82:6.8.verse: ‘Tathāgatas do not give the Going-forth without the parents’ permission, Raṭṭhapāla.’

mn82:6.9.verse: ‘Venerable sir, I shall see to it that my parents permit me to go forth from the home life into homelessness.’

mn82:7.1.verse: Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the Blessed One, (he left) keeping him on his right. He went to his parents and told them:

mn82:7.2.verse: ‘Mother and father, as I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, it is impossible while living in a household to lead the life divine as perfect and pure as a polished shell.

mn82:7.3.verse: I want to shave off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and go forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:7.4.verse: Give me permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness.’

mn82:7.5.verse: When this was said his parents replied:

mn82:7.6.verse: ‘Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you, being an only son and dear and precious to us, have been educated to pleasure, brought up to pleasure.

mn82:7.7.verse: Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you know nothing of suffering.

mn82:7.8.verse: In case of your death we should lose you willy-nilly;

mn82:7.9.verse: but why should we give you our permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?’

mn82:7.11.verse: For the third time the clansman Raṭṭhapāla said to his parents:

mn82:7.12.verse: ‘Mother and father … give me permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness.’

mn82:7.15.verse: For the third time his parents replied:

mn82:7.16.verse: ‘Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you, being an only son and dear and precious to us, have been educated to pleasure, brought up to pleasure.

mn82:7.17.verse: Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you know nothing of suffering.

mn82:7.18.verse: In case of your death we should lose you willy-nilly;

mn82:7.19.verse: but why should we give you our permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?’

mn82:7.21.verse: Then, not getting his parents’ (permission) for the Going-forth, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla lay down there on the bare floor, (thinking:)

mn82:7.22.verse: ‘Right here I shall either die or get the Going-forth’.

mn82:8.1.verse: Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla’s parents said to him:

mn82:8.2.verse: ‘Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you, being an only son and dear and precious to us, have been educated to pleasure, brought up to pleasure.

mn82:8.3.verse: Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you know nothing of suffering.

mn82:8.5.verse: but why should we give you our permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?

mn82:8.6.verse: Get up, dear Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink and be merry;

mn82:8.7.verse: enjoy eating, drinking, being merry, indulging sensual desires and making merit.

mn82:8.8.verse: We do not permit you to go forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:8.9.verse: In case of your death we should lose you willy-nilly:

mn82:8.10.verse: but why should we give you our permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?’

mn82:8.11.verse: When this was said the clansman Raṭṭhapāla was silent.

mn82:8.14.verse: For the third time his parents said to him:

mn82:8.15.verse: ‘Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you, being an only son …

mn82:9.1.verse: For the third time he was silent.

mn82:10.1.verse: Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla’s friends went to him and said to him:

mn82:10.2.verse: ‘Good Raṭṭhapāla, you, being an only son and dear and precious to your parents, have been educated to pleasure, brought up to pleasure.

mn82:10.3.verse: Good Raṭṭhapāla, you know nothing of suffering.

mn82:10.4.verse: In case of your death they would lose you willy-nilly;

mn82:10.5.verse: but why should they give you their permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?

mn82:10.6.verse: Get up, good Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink and be merry;

mn82:10.7.verse: enjoy eating, drinking, being merry, indulging sensual desires, and making merit.

mn82:10.8.verse: Your parents do not permit you to go forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:10.9.verse: In case of your death they would lose you willy-nilly;

mn82:10.10.verse: but why should they give you their permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?’

mn82:10.11.verse: When this was said, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla was silent.

mn82:10.13.verse: For the third time his friends said to him:

mn82:10.14.verse: ‘Good Raṭṭhapāla, you, being an only son …

mn82:10.16.verse: Get up, dear Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink and be merry; enjoy eating, drinking, being merry, indulging sensual desires and making merit.

mn82:10.19.verse: For the third time he was silent.

mn82:11.1.verse: Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla’s friends went to his parents and said to them:

mn82:11.2.verse: ‘Mother and father, this clansman Raṭṭhapāla has lain down there on the bare floor, (thinking:)

mn82:11.3.verse: “Right here I shall either die or get the Going-forth.”

mn82:11.4.verse: Now if you do not give him your permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness, he will die there.

mn82:11.5.verse: But if you give him your permission, you will see him after he has gone forth.

mn82:11.6.verse: And if he does not enjoy the Going-forth, what else can he do then but return here?

mn82:11.7.verse: So give him your permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness.’

mn82:11.8.verse: ‘Then we give the clansman Raṭṭhapāla permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:11.9.verse: But when he has gone forth, he must visit his parents.’

mn82:11.10.verse: So the clansman Raṭṭhapāla’s friends went to him and told him:

mn82:11.11.verse: ‘You are permitted by your parents to go forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:11.12.verse: But when you have gone forth, you must visit your parents.’

mn82:12.1.verse: The clansman Raṭṭhapāla then got up, and when he had gained strength, he went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him he sat down at one side. When he had done so, he said:

mn82:12.2.verse: ‘Venerable sir, I have my parents’ permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:12.3.verse: Let the Blessed One give me the Going-forth.’

mn82:13.1.verse: So the clansman Raṭṭhapāla received the Going-forth under the Blessed One, and he received the Full Admission.

mn82:13.2.verse: Then soon after the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s Full Admission, when he had been fully admitted a fortnight, the Blessed One, having stayed at Thullakoṭṭhita as long as he chose, set out to go by stages to Sāvatthi.

mn82:13.3.verse: Wandering by stages, he at length arrived at Sāvatthi.

mn82:13.4.verse: There he lived in Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove. Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

mn82:14.1.verse: Meanwhile, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and self-controlled, the venerable Raṭṭhapāla, by realization himself with direct knowledge here and now entered upon and abode in that supreme goal of the life divine for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:14.2.verse: He knew directly: ‘Birth is ended, the life divine has been lived, what was to be done is done, there is no more of this to come.’

mn82:14.3.verse: And the venerable Raṭṭhapāla became one of the Arahants.

mn82:15.1.verse: Then the venerable Raṭṭhapāla went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, he said:

mn82:15.2.verse: ‘Venerable sir, I wish to see my parents, if I have the Blessed One’s permission.’

mn82:15.3.verse: Then encompassing mind with mind the Blessed One directed his attention to the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s thought.

mn82:15.5.verse: ‘The clansman Raṭṭhapāla is incapable of forsaking the training and reverting to what he has abandoned,’ he told him:

mn82:15.6.verse: ‘It is time for you, Raṭṭhapāla, to do as you think fit.’

mn82:16.1.verse: The venerable Raṭṭhapāla rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the Blessed One, (he departed), keeping him on his right. Then he set his resting place in order, and taking his bowl and (outer) robe, he set out to go by stages to Thullakoṭṭhita.

mn82:16.2.verse: Wandering by stages, he eventually arrived at Thullakoṭṭhita.

mn82:16.3.verse: There he lived in Thullakoṭṭhita in King Koravya’s Migācira (Garden).

mn82:16.4.verse: Then, when it was morning, he dressed, and taking his bowl and (outer) robe, he went into Thullakoṭṭhita for alms.

mn82:16.5.verse: As was wandering from house to house he came to his own father’s house.

mn82:17.1.verse: Now on that occasion the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father was sitting in the hall of the central door having his hair dressed.

mn82:17.2.verse: He saw the venerable Raṭṭhapāla coming in the distance.

mn82:17.3.verse: When he saw him, he said:

mn82:17.4.verse: ‘Our only son who was dear and precious to us was made to go forth by these monkish shavelings.’

mn82:17.5.verse: Then the venerable Raṭṭhapāla got neither gifts nor polite refusal,

mn82:17.6.verse: and instead he got only abuse.

mn82:18.1.verse: A bondswoman belonging to one of his relatives was about to throw away some stale porridge.

mn82:18.3.verse: ‘Sister, if that is stuff to be thrown away, then pour it into my bowl here.’

mn82:18.4.verse: While she was doing so, she recognized the characteristics of his hands, his feet and his voice.

mn82:18.5.verse: Then she went to his mother and said:

mn82:18.6.verse: ‘My goodness, my lady! Do you know that

mn82:18.7.verse: my lord’s son Raṭṭhapāla has arrived?’

mn82:18.8.verse: ‘Gracious! If what you say is true, you are a bondswoman no more!’

mn82:18.9.verse: Then the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s mother went to his father and said:

mn82:18.10.verse: ‘My goodness, householder! Do you know that

mn82:18.11.verse: they say that the clansman Raṭṭhapāla has arrived?’

mn82:19.1.verse: Just then the venerable Raṭṭhapāla was eating the stale porridge by the wall of a certain (shelter).

mn82:19.2.verse: His father went to him and said:

mn82:19.3.verse: ‘Raṭṭhapāla, my dear, surely there is …  and you will be eating stale porridge!

mn82:19.4.verse: Is there not your own house to go to?’

mn82:19.5.verse: ‘How should we, householder, who have gone forth from the home life into homelessness, have a house?

mn82:19.7.verse: We went to your home but we got neither gifts nor polite refusal there,

mn82:19.9.verse: ‘Come, Raṭṭhapāla dear, let us go to the house.’

mn82:19.10.verse: ‘Enough, householder, I have finished my meal for today.’

mn82:19.12.verse: The venerable Raṭṭhapāla accepted in silence.

mn82:20.1.verse: Then knowing that his son had accepted, he went back to his own house. He had gold and bullion made into a large heap and covered with mats. Then he told the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s former wives:

mn82:20.2.verse: ‘Come, daughters-in-law, dress yourselves up in the way in which Raṭṭhapāla used to hold you most dear and precious.’

mn82:21.1.verse: When the night was ended, the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father had good food of various kinds prepared in his own house, and he had the time announced to the venerable Raṭṭhapāla:

mn82:21.2.verse: ‘It is time, dear Raṭṭhapāla, the meal is ready.’

mn82:22.1.verse: Then, it being morning, the venerable Raṭṭhapāla dressed, and taking his bowl and (outer) robe, he went to his own father’s house, and he sat down on the seat made ready. Then his father had the pile of gold and bullion uncovered, and he said:

mn82:22.2.verse: ‘Raṭṭhapāla dear, this is your maternal fortune; your paternal fortune is another and your ancestral fortune is yet another.

mn82:22.3.verse: Ratṭhapāla dear, you can use the wealth and make merit.

mn82:22.4.verse: Come then, renounce the training, return to what you have abandoned, use the wealth and make merit.’

mn82:22.5.verse: ‘Householder, if you would do as I say, then have this pile of gold and bullion loaded on carts and carried away to be dumped in the River Ganges in midstream.

mn82:22.7.verse: Because, householder, for you it will be a source of sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair.’

mn82:23.1.verse: The venerable Ratṭhapāla’s former wives clasped both his feet, saying to him:

mn82:23.2.verse: ‘What are they like, my lord, the nymphs for whose sake you lead the life divine?’

mn82:23.3.verse: ‘We do not lead the life divine for the sake of nymphs, sisters.’

mn82:23.4.verse: ‘My lord’s son Ratṭhapāla calls us “sisters”,’ (they cried) and they fell swooning on the spot.

mn82:24.1.verse: Then the venerable Ratṭhapāla told his father:

mn82:24.2.verse: ‘Householder, if there is a meal to be given, then give it.

mn82:24.4.verse: ‘Eat then, dear Ratṭhapāla. The meal is ready.’

mn82:24.5.verse: Then with his own hands the venerable Ratṭhapāla’s father served and satisfied him with the various kinds of food.

mn82:24.6.verse: When the venerable Ratṭhapāla had no longer the bowl in his hand, he stood up and uttered these stanzas:

mn82:25.2.verse: A body built up out of sores,

mn82:25.5.verse: Behold a figure here pranked out,

mn82:25.7.verse: A skeleton wrapped up in skin,

mn82:25.10.verse: And powder smeared upon its face,

mn82:25.12.verse: but not a seeker of the Further Shore.

mn82:25.13.verse: Its hair is dressed in eightfold plaits

mn82:25.14.verse: And unguent smeared upon its eyes,

mn82:25.16.verse: but not a seeker of the Further Shore.

mn82:25.20.verse: but not a seeker of the Further Shore.

mn82:25.21.verse: The deer-hunter sets well the snare

mn82:25.22.verse: But the deer springs not the trap;

mn82:25.23.verse: We ate the bait, and we depart

mn82:26.1.verse: When the venerable Raṭṭhapāla had stood up and uttered these stanzas, he went to King Koravya’s Migācira (Garden) and sat down at the root of a tree for the day’s abiding.

mn82:27.1.verse: Then King Koravya addressed Migava thus:

mn82:27.2.verse: ‘Good Migava, get the Migācira (Garden) tidied up, to the pleasure garden

mn82:27.3.verse: so that we may go to see a pleasing spot.’

mn82:27.4.verse: ‘Yes, sir,’ he replied. Now while he was having the Migācira (Garden) tidied up, he saw the venerable Raṭṭhapāla seated at the root of a tree for the day’s abiding.

mn82:27.5.verse: When he saw him, he went to the King Koravya and told him:

mn82:27.6.verse: ‘Sire, the Migācira (Garden) has been tidied up.

mn82:27.7.verse: And the clansman called Raṭṭhapāla is there, the son of the leading clan in this same Thullakoṭṭhita, of whom you have always spoken highly; he is seated at the foot of a tree for the day’s abiding.’

mn82:27.8.verse: ‘Then, good Migava, enough of the pleasure garden for today.

mn82:27.9.verse: Now we shall pay honour to that Master Raṭṭhapāla.’

mn82:28.1.verse: Then, (saying:) ‘Give away all food of any kind that has been prepared there,’ King Koravya had a number of state carriages got ready, and mounting a state carriage, he drove out from Thullakoṭṭhita with the full pomp of royalty to see the venerable Raṭṭhapāla.

mn82:28.2.verse: He went thus as far as the road was passable for carriages, and then he got down from his carriage and went forward on foot with a following of the most eminent (officials) to where the venerable Raṭṭhapāla was. He exchanged greetings with the venerable Raṭṭhapāla, and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he stood at one side. Then he said:

mn82:28.3.verse: ‘Here is an elephant rug. Let Master Raṭṭhapāla be seated on it.’

mn82:28.4.verse: ‘There is no need, great king. (Please) sit down.

mn82:28.5.verse: I am sitting on my own mat.’

mn82:28.6.verse: King Koravya sat down on a seat made ready. When he had done so, he said:

mn82:29.1.verse: ‘Master Raṭṭhapāla, there are four kinds of loss after undergoing which some people here shave off their hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth and go forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:29.3.verse: They are loss through ageing, loss through sickness, loss of property and loss of relatives.

mn82:30.2.verse: Here someone is old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life, and come to the last stage.

mn82:30.4.verse: “I am old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life and come to the last stage.

mn82:30.5.verse: It is no more possible for me to acquire unacquired properties or to augment properties already acquired.

mn82:30.6.verse: Suppose I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth and went forth from the home life into homelessness?”

mn82:30.7.verse: Undergoing that loss through ageing, he shaves off his hair and beard, puts on the yellow cloth and goes forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:30.8.verse: This is called loss through ageing.

mn82:30.9.verse: But Master Raṭṭhapāla is now still young, a black-haired boy endowed with the blessing of youth, in the first phase of life.

mn82:30.10.verse: Master Raṭṭhapāla has nothing of loss through ageing.

mn82:30.11.verse: What has he known or seen or heard that he has gone forth from the home life into homelessness?’

mn82:31.2.verse: Here someone is afflicted, suffering and gravely ill.

mn82:31.4.verse: “I am afflicted, suffering and gravely ill.

mn82:31.5.verse: It is no more possible for me to acquire unacquired properties or to augment properties already acquired.

mn82:31.6.verse: Suppose I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and went forth from the home life into homelessness?

mn82:31.7.verse: Undergoing that loss through sickness, he shaves off …

mn82:31.8.verse: This is called loss through sickness.

mn82:31.9.verse: But Master Raṭṭhapāla has now no affliction or ailment, having a good digestion that is neither too cool nor nor too warm but medium.

mn82:31.10.verse: Master Raṭṭhapāla has nothing of loss through sickness.

mn82:31.11.verse: What has he known or seen or heard that he has gone forth from the home life into homelessness?

mn82:32.2.verse: Here someone is rich with great wealth and great property.

mn82:32.3.verse: Gradually those properties of his dwindle away.

mn82:32.5.verse: “Formerly I was rich with great wealth and great property.

mn82:32.6.verse: Gradually those properties of mine have dwindled away.

mn82:32.7.verse: It is no more possible for me to acquire … into homelessness?”

mn82:32.8.verse: Suppose I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and went forth from the home life into homelessness

mn82:32.9.verse: Undergoing that loss of property, he shaves off …

mn82:32.10.verse: This is called loss of property.

mn82:32.11.verse: But Master Raṭṭhapāla is the son of the leading clan in this same Thullakoṭṭhita.

mn82:32.12.verse: Master Raṭṭhapāla has nothing of that loss of wealth.

mn82:32.13.verse: What has he known or seen or heard that he has gone forth from the home life into homelessness?

mn82:33.2.verse: Here someone has many friends and companions, relatives and kin.

mn82:33.3.verse: Gradually those relatives of his dwindle away.

mn82:33.5.verse: “Formerly I had many friends and companions, relatives and kin.

mn82:33.6.verse: Gradually those relatives of mine have dwindled away.

mn82:33.7.verse: It is no more possible for me to acquire … into homelessness?”

mn82:33.8.verse: Suppose I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and went forth from the home life into homelessness?’

mn82:33.9.verse: Undergoing that loss of relatives, he shaves off …

mn82:33.10.verse: This is called loss of relatives.

mn82:33.11.verse: But Master Raṭṭhapāla has many friends and companions, relatives and kin in this same Thullakoṭṭhita.

mn82:33.12.verse: Master Raṭṭhapāla has nothing of that loss of relatives.

mn82:33.13.verse: What has he known or seen or heard that he has gone forth from the home life into homelessness?

mn82:34.1.verse: ‘Master Raṭṭhapāla, these are four kinds of loss after undergoing which some people here shave off their hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth and go forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:34.2.verse: Master Raṭṭhapāla has none of these.

mn82:34.3.verse: What has he known or seen or heard that he has gone forth from the home life into homelessness?’

mn82:35.1.verse: ‘Great king, there are four summaries of Dhamma which have been given by the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, knowing and seeing and hearing which I went forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:36.1.verse: ‘ “(Life in) any world has no lastingness, and is led on”:

mn82:36.2.verse: this is the first summary of the Dhamma given by the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, knowing and seeing and hearing which I went forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:36.3.verse: ‘ “(Life in) any world has no shelter and no protector”:

mn82:36.4.verse: this is the second summary … into homelessness.

mn82:36.5.verse: ‘ “(Life in) any world has nothing of its own; it has to leave all and pass on”:

mn82:36.7.verse: ‘ “(Life in) any world is incomplete, insatiate and the slave of craving”:

mn82:36.8.verse: this is the fourth summary … knowing and seeing and hearing which I went forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn82:37.1.verse: ‘Great king, these are the four summaries of the Dhamma which have been given by the Blessed One … into homelessness.’

mn82:38.1.verse: ‘ “(Life in) any world has no lastingness, and is led on”,

mn82:38.3.verse: but how should the meaning of that statement be regarded?’

mn82:38.4.verse: ‘How do you conceive this, great king,

mn82:38.5.verse: when you were twenty years old and twenty-five years old, were you an expert rider of elephants, an expert horseman, an expert charioteer, an expert bowman, an expert swordsman, strong in thigh and arm, sturdy and used to wars?’

mn82:38.7.verse: Sometimes I wonder if I had supernormal power: I do not see that it was quite the same as my own power.’

mn82:38.8.verse: ‘How do you conceive this, great king,

mn82:38.9.verse: are you now as strong in thigh and arm, as sturdy and as used to wars?’

mn82:38.11.verse: Now I am old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life and come to the last stage. My years have turned eighty.

mn82:38.12.verse: Sometimes I mean to put my foot here and I put my foot somewhere else.’

mn82:38.13.verse: ‘Great king, it was on account of this that the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, said:

mn82:38.14.verse: “(Life in) any world has no lastingness and is led on”,

mn82:38.15.verse: and when I knew and saw and heard that, I went forth from the home life into homelessness.’

mn82:38.16.verse: ‘It is wonderful, Master Raṭṭhapāla, it is marvellous

mn82:38.17.verse: how well that has been expressed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened.

mn82:38.18.verse: “(Life in) any world has no lastingness and is led on”,

mn82:39.1.verse: ‘Master Raṭṭhapāla, there exist in this court elephant troops and cavalry and chariot troops and infantry, which will serve to subdue any threats to us.

mn82:39.2.verse: Now “(Life in) any world has no shelter and no protector”

mn82:39.4.verse: but how should the meaning of that statement be regarded?’

mn82:39.5.verse: ‘How do you conceive this, great king,

mn82:39.7.verse: ‘I have a latent wind sickness, Master Raṭṭhapāla.

mn82:39.8.verse: Sometimes my friends and companions, my relatives and kin, stand around me, (saying):

mn82:39.9.verse: “Now King Koravya is about to die, now King Koravya is about to die!”’

mn82:39.10.verse: ‘How do you conceive this, great king,

mn82:39.11.verse: can you have it thus with your friends and companions, your relatives and kin:

mn82:39.12.verse: “Come, my good friends and companions, my relatives and kin, do all of you present share out this feeling (of pain) so that I may feel less feeling (of pain)”,

mn82:39.13.verse: or do you have to feel that feeling (of pain) yourself alone?’

mn82:39.14.verse: ‘I cannot have it thus, Master Raṭṭhapāla,

mn82:39.16.verse: I have to feel that feeling of pain alone.’

mn82:39.17.verse: ‘Great king, it was on account of this that the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, said:

mn82:39.18.verse: “(Life in) any world has no shelter and no protector”;

mn82:39.19.verse: and when I knew and saw and heard that, I went forth from the home life into homelessness.’

mn82:39.22.verse: “(Life in) any world has no shelter and protector”,

mn82:40.1.verse: ‘Master Raṭṭhapāla, there exists in this court ample gold and bullion stored away in cellars and laid up in attics.

mn82:40.2.verse: Now “(Life in) any world has nothing of its own; it has to leave all and pass on”

mn82:40.4.verse: but how should the meaning of that statement be regarded?’

mn82:40.5.verse: ‘How do you conceive this, great king,

mn82:40.6.verse: you are now furnished and invested with the five cords of sensual desires and enjoy them, but will you be able to have it of the life to come:

mn82:40.7.verse: “May I be likewise furnished and invested with these five cords of sensual desires and enjoy them”, or will others take over this property, while you will have to pass on according to your kammas?’

mn82:40.8.verse: ‘I cannot have it thus, Master Raṭṭhapāla.

mn82:40.10.verse: On the contrary, others will take over this property, while I shall have to pass on according to my kammas.’

mn82:40.11.verse: ‘Great king, it was on account of this that the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, said:

mn82:40.12.verse: “(Life in) any world has nothing of its own; it has to leave all and pass on”;

mn82:40.13.verse: and when I knew and heard that, I went forth from the home life to homelessness.’

mn82:40.16.verse: “(Life in) any world has nothing of its own; it has to leave all and pass on”,

mn82:41.1.verse: ‘Now, “(Life in) any world is incomplete, insatiate, and the slave of craving”

mn82:41.3.verse: but how should the meaning of that statement be regarded?’

mn82:41.4.verse: ‘How do you conceive this, Great King,

mn82:41.5.verse: do you live in the rich Kuru country as its owner?’

mn82:41.7.verse: ‘How do you conceive this, great king?

mn82:41.8.verse: If a trustworthy and reliable man came to you from the east

mn82:41.10.verse: “Please to know, great king, that I come from the east,

mn82:41.11.verse: and there I saw a large country powerful and rich, very populous and crowded with men;

mn82:41.12.verse: there are plenty of elephant troops there, plenty of cavalry, plenty of chariot troops and plenty of infantry;

mn82:41.13.verse: there is plenty of ivory there,

mn82:41.14.verse: and plenty of gold and bullion both unworked and worked,

mn82:41.15.verse: and there are plenty of women for wives.

mn82:41.16.verse: With such and such a force you can conquer it.

mn82:41.17.verse: Conquer it then, great king.” How would you act?’

mn82:41.18.verse: ‘We should conquer it and live there as its owner, Master Raṭṭhapāla.’

mn82:41.19.verse: ‘How do you conceive this, great king,

mn82:41.20.verse: if a trustworthy and reliable man came to you from the west …

mn82:41.33.verse: ‘We should conquer it too and live there as its owner, Master Raṭṭhapāla.’

mn82:41.34.verse: ‘Great king, it was on account of this that the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, said:

mn82:41.35.verse: “(Life in) any world is incomplete, insatiate and the slave of craving”,

mn82:41.36.verse: and when I knew and saw and heard that, I went forth from the home life into homelessness.’

mn82:41.38.verse: ‘It is wonderful, Master Raṭṭhapāla, it is marvellous how well that has been expressed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Full Enlightened:

mn82:41.39.verse: “(Life in) any world is incomplete, insatiate and the slave of craving”,

mn82:42.1.verse: That is what the venerable Raṭṭhapāla said.

mn82:42.2.verse: And having said that he said further:

mn82:42.3.verse: I see men wealthy in the world, who yet

mn82:42.4.verse: Give not, from ignorance, their gathered riches;

mn82:42.5.verse: But greedily will hoard away their wealth,

mn82:42.6.verse: Through longing for still further sensual pleasures.

mn82:42.7.verse: A king who has by force conquered the earth

mn82:42.8.verse: And even lords the land the ocean bounds

mn82:42.9.verse: Is yet unsated with the sea’s near shore

mn82:42.10.verse: And hungers for its further shore as well.

mn82:42.11.verse: Most other men as well, not just a king,

mn82:42.13.verse: (With plans) still incomplete they leave the corpse;

mn82:42.14.verse: Desires remain unsated in the world.

mn82:42.15.verse: His relatives lament him, rend their hair,

mn82:42.16.verse: Crying “Ah me! Alas! Our love is dead!”

mn82:42.17.verse: Then bear away the body wrapped in shrouds

mn82:42.18.verse: To place it on a pyre and burn it there.

mn82:42.19.verse: and prodded with stakes he burns,

mn82:42.20.verse: Clad in single shroud, he leaves behind His property,

mn82:42.21.verse: And as he died, no relatives or kin

mn82:42.22.verse: Or friends could offer refuge to him here.

mn82:42.23.verse: The while his heirs annex his wealth,

mn82:42.24.verse: this being must now pass on according to his kammas;

mn82:42.25.verse: And as he dies no thing can follow him:

mn82:42.26.verse: Nor child nor wife nor wealth nor royal estate.

mn82:42.27.verse: Longevity is not acquired with wealth

mn82:42.28.verse: Nor can prosperity banish old age;

mn82:42.29.verse: Short is this life, as all the sages say,

mn82:42.30.verse: Eternity it knows not, only change.

mn82:42.31.verse: The rich man and the poor man both shall feel (Death’s) touch,

mn82:42.32.verse: as do the fool and sage alike;

mn82:42.33.verse: But while the fool lies stricken by his folly,

mn82:42.34.verse: No sage will ever tremble at the touch.

mn82:42.36.verse: The goal can here be gained, than any wealth;

mn82:42.37.verse: For men through different lives in ignorance

mn82:42.38.verse: Do evil, while they fail to reach the goal.

mn82:42.39.verse: As one goes to the womb and the next world,

mn82:42.40.verse: Renewing the successive round, so another

mn82:42.41.verse: With no more understanding, trusting him,

mn82:42.42.verse: Goes also to the womb and the next world.

mn82:42.43.verse: Just as robber caught in burglary

mn82:42.44.verse: By his own kamma’s marked a miscreant,

mn82:42.45.verse: So people are after death, in the next world

mn82:42.46.verse: By their own kammas marked as miscreants.

mn82:42.47.verse: For sense desires so mind-alluring, sweet,

mn82:42.48.verse: In many a different way disturb the mind;

mn82:42.49.verse: Seeing the danger in these sense desires

mn82:42.50.verse: So I went forth to homelessness, O king.

mn82:42.51.verse: Men whether young or old, like fruits of trees

mn82:42.52.verse: Fall when the body’s break-up comes about;

mn82:42.53.verse: That too I saw, and so went forth, O king,

mn82:42.54.verse: Better by far the monk’s state assured.

mn82:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Kurus together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants when he arrived at a town of the Kurus named Thullakoṭṭhika.

mn82:2.1.verse: The brahmins and householders of Thullakoṭṭhika heard:

mn82:2.2.verse: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—has arrived at Thullakoṭṭhika, together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants.

mn82:2.4.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

mn82:2.5.verse: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

mn82:2.6.verse: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

mn82:2.7.verse: It’s good to see such perfected ones.”

mn82:3.1.verse: Then the brahmins and householders of Thullakoṭṭhika went up to the Buddha. Before sitting down to one side, some bowed, some exchanged greetings and polite conversation, some held up their cupped palms toward the Buddha, some announced their name and clan, while some kept silent.

mn82:3.2.verse: When they were seated, the Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired them with a Dhamma talk.

mn82:4.1.verse: Now at that time a gentleman named Raṭṭhapāla, the son of the leading clan in Thullakoṭṭhika, was sitting in the assembly.

mn82:4.3.verse: “As I understand the Buddha’s teaching, it’s not easy for someone living at home to lead the spiritual life utterly full and pure, like a polished shell.

mn82:4.4.verse: Why don’t I shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from lay life to homelessness?”

mn82:5.1.verse: Then, having approved and agreed with what the Buddha said, the brahmins and householders of Thullakoṭṭhika got up from their seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on their right, before leaving.

mn82:6.1.verse: Soon after they left, Raṭṭhapāla went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

mn82:6.2.verse: “Sir, as I understand the Buddha’s teaching, it’s not easy for someone living at home to lead the spiritual life utterly full and pure, like a polished shell.

mn82:6.3.verse: I wish to shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

mn82:6.4.verse: Sir, may I receive the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence?

mn82:6.5.verse: May the Buddha please give me the going forth!”

mn82:6.6.verse: “But, Raṭṭhapāla, do you have your parents’ permission?”

mn82:6.8.verse: “Raṭṭhapāla, Buddhas don’t give the going forth to the child of parents who haven’t given their permission.”

mn82:6.9.verse: “I’ll make sure, sir, to get my parents’ permission.”

mn82:7.1.verse: Then Raṭṭhapāla rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha. Then he went to his parents and said,

mn82:7.2.verse: “Mum and dad, as I understand the Buddha’s teachings, it’s not easy for someone living at home to lead the spiritual life utterly full and pure, like a polished shell.

mn82:7.3.verse: I wish to shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

mn82:7.4.verse: Please give me permission to go forth.”

mn82:7.5.verse: When he said this, Raṭṭhapāla’s parents said to him,

mn82:7.6.verse: “But, dear Raṭṭhapāla, you’re our only child. You’re dear to us and we love you. You’re pampered and raised in comfort.

mn82:7.8.verse: Even when you die we will lose you against our wishes.

mn82:7.9.verse: So how can we allow you to go forth while you’re still alive?”

mn82:7.11.verse: For a third time, Raṭṭhapāla asked his parents for permission, but got the same reply.

mn82:7.21.verse: “My parents don’t allow me to go forth.” He laid down right there on the bare ground, saying,

mn82:7.22.verse: “I’ll either die right here or go forth.”

mn82:7.23.verse: And he refused to eat, up to the seventh meal.

mn82:8.1.verse: Then Raṭṭhapāla’s parents said to him,

mn82:8.2.verse: “Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you’re our only child. You’re dear to us and we love you. You’re pampered and raised in comfort.

mn82:8.4.verse: When you die we will lose you against our wishes.

mn82:8.5.verse: So how can we allow you to go forth from lay life to homelessness while you’re still living?

mn82:8.6.verse: Get up, Raṭṭhapāla! Eat, drink, and amuse yourself.

mn82:8.7.verse: While enjoying sensual pleasures, delight in making merit.

mn82:8.8.verse: We don’t allow you to go forth.

mn82:8.9.verse: When you die we will lose you against our wishes.

mn82:8.10.verse: So how can we allow you to go forth while you’re still alive?”

mn82:8.11.verse: When they said this, Raṭṭhapāla kept silent.

mn82:8.14.verse: and a third time, Raṭṭhapāla’s parents made the same request.

mn82:9.1.verse: And for a third time, Raṭṭhapāla kept silent. Raṭṭhapāla’s parents then went to see his friends. They told them of the situation and asked for their help.

mn82:10.1.verse: Then Raṭṭhapāla’s friends went to him and said,

mn82:10.2.verse: “Our dear Raṭṭhapāla, you are your parents’ only child. You’re dear to them and they love you. You’re pampered and raised in comfort.

mn82:10.4.verse: When you die your parents will lose you against their wishes.

mn82:10.5.verse: So how can they allow you to go forth while you’re still alive?

mn82:10.6.verse: Get up, Raṭṭhapāla! Eat, drink, and amuse yourself.

mn82:10.7.verse: While enjoying sensual pleasures, delight in making merit.

mn82:10.8.verse: Your parents will not allow you to go forth.

mn82:10.9.verse: Even when you die your parents will lose you against their wishes.

mn82:10.10.verse: So how can they allow you to go forth while you’re still alive?”

mn82:10.11.verse: When they said this, Raṭṭhapāla kept silent.

mn82:10.13.verse: For a third time, Raṭṭhapāla’s friends made the same request.

mn82:10.19.verse: And for a third time, Raṭṭhapāla kept silent.

mn82:11.1.verse: Then Raṭṭhapāla’s friends went to his parents and said,

mn82:11.2.verse: “Mum and dad, Raṭṭhapāla is lying there on the bare ground saying:

mn82:11.3.verse: ‘I’ll either die right here or go forth.’

mn82:11.4.verse: If you don’t allow him to go forth, he’ll die there.

mn82:11.5.verse: But if you do allow him to go forth, you’ll see him again afterwards.

mn82:11.6.verse: And if he doesn’t enjoy the renunciate life, where else will he have to go? He’ll come right back here.

mn82:11.7.verse: Please give Raṭṭhapāla permission to go forth.”

mn82:11.8.verse: “Then, dears, we give Raṭṭhapāla permission to go forth.

mn82:11.9.verse: But once gone forth he must visit his parents.”

mn82:11.10.verse: Then Raṭṭhapāla’s friends went to him and said,

mn82:11.11.verse: “Get up, Raṭṭhapāla! Your parents have given you permission to go forth from lay life to homelessness.

mn82:11.12.verse: But once gone forth you must visit your parents.”

mn82:12.1.verse: Raṭṭhapāla got up and regained his strength. He went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

mn82:12.2.verse: “Sir, I have my parents’ permission to go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

mn82:12.3.verse: May the Buddha please give me the going forth.”

mn82:13.1.verse: And Raṭṭhapāla received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

mn82:13.2.verse: Not long after Venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s ordination, a fortnight later, the Buddha—having stayed in Thullakoṭṭhika as long as he pleased—set out for Sāvatthī.

mn82:13.3.verse: Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Sāvatthī,

mn82:13.4.verse: where he stayed in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn82:14.1.verse: Then Venerable Raṭṭhapāla, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

mn82:14.2.verse: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

mn82:14.3.verse: And Venerable Raṭṭhapāla became one of the perfected.

mn82:15.1.verse: Then he went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

mn82:15.2.verse: “Sir, I would like to visit my parents, if the Buddha allows it.”

mn82:15.3.verse: Then the Buddha focused on encompassing Raṭṭhapāla’s mind.

mn82:15.5.verse: it was impossible for Raṭṭhapāla to resign the training and return to a lesser life, he said,

mn82:16.1.verse: And then Raṭṭhapāla rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right. Then he set his lodgings in order and, taking his bowl and robe, set out for Thullakoṭṭhika.

mn82:16.2.verse: Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Thullakoṭṭhika,

mn82:16.3.verse: where he stayed in King Koravya’s deer range.

mn82:16.4.verse: Then Raṭṭhapāla robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Thullakoṭṭhika for alms.

mn82:16.5.verse: Wandering indiscriminately for almsfood, he approached his own father’s house.

mn82:17.1.verse: Now at that time Raṭṭhapāla’s father was having his hair dressed in the hall of the middle gate.

mn82:17.2.verse: He saw Raṭṭhapāla coming off in the distance

mn82:17.4.verse: “Our dear and beloved only son was made to go forth by these shavelings, these fake ascetics!”

mn82:17.5.verse: And at his own father’s home Raṭṭhapāla received neither alms nor a polite refusal,

mn82:18.1.verse: Now at that time a family bondservant wanted to throw away the previous night’s porridge.

mn82:18.3.verse: “If that’s to be thrown away, sister, pour it here in my bowl.”

mn82:18.4.verse: As she was pouring the porridge into his bowl, she recognized the features of his hands, feet, and voice.

mn82:18.5.verse: She then went to his mother and said,

mn82:18.8.verse: “If you speak the truth, wench, I’ll make you a free woman!”

mn82:18.9.verse: Then Raṭṭhapāla’s mother went to his father and said,

mn82:18.11.verse: It seems our son Raṭṭhapāla has arrived.”

mn82:19.1.verse: Now at that time Raṭṭhapāla was eating last night’s porridge by a wall.

mn82:19.2.verse: Then Raṭṭhapāla’s father went up to him and said,

mn82:19.3.verse: “Dear Raṭṭhapāla! How can you be eating last night’s porridge?

mn82:19.4.verse: Why not go to your own home?”

mn82:19.5.verse: “Householder, how could those of us who have gone forth from the lay life to homelessness have a house?

mn82:19.7.verse: I came to your house, but there I received neither alms nor a polite refusal,

mn82:19.9.verse: “Come, dear Raṭṭhapāla, let’s go to the house.”

mn82:19.10.verse: “Enough, householder. My meal is finished for today.”

mn82:19.11.verse: “Well then, dear Raṭṭhapāla, please accept tomorrow’s meal from me.”

mn82:20.1.verse: Then, knowing that Raṭṭhapāla had consented, his father went back to his own house. He made a heap of gold, both coined and uncoined, and hid it under mats. Then he addressed Raṭṭhapāla’s former wives,

mn82:20.2.verse: “Please, daughters-in-law, adorn yourselves in the way that our son Raṭṭhapāla found you most adorable.”

mn82:21.1.verse: And when the night had passed Raṭṭhapāla’s father had delicious fresh and cooked foods prepared in his own home, and announced the time to the Venerable Raṭṭhapāla, saying,

mn82:21.2.verse: “Sir, it’s time. The meal is ready.”

mn82:22.1.verse: Then Raṭṭhapāla robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to his father’s home, and sat down on the seat spread out. Raṭṭhapāla’s father, revealing the heap of gold, both coined and uncoined, said to him,

mn82:22.2.verse: “Dear Raṭṭhapāla, this is your maternal fortune. There’s another paternal fortune, and an ancestral one.

mn82:22.3.verse: You can both enjoy your wealth and make merit.

mn82:22.4.verse: Come, return to a lesser life, enjoy wealth, and make merit!”

mn82:22.5.verse: “If you’d follow my advice, householder, you’d have this heap of gold, both coined and uncoined, loaded on a cart and carried away to be dumped in the middle of the Ganges River.

mn82:22.7.verse: Because this will bring you nothing but sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.”

mn82:23.1.verse: Then Raṭṭhapāla’s former wives each clasped his feet and said,

mn82:23.2.verse: “What are they like, master, the nymphs for whom you lead the spiritual life?”

mn82:23.3.verse: “Sisters, I don’t lead the spiritual life for the sake of nymphs.”

mn82:23.4.verse: Saying, “Our master Raṭṭhapāla addresses us as sisters!” they fainted right away.

mn82:24.1.verse: Then Raṭṭhapāla said to his father,

mn82:24.2.verse: “If there is food to be given, householder, please give it.

mn82:24.4.verse: “Eat, dear Raṭṭhapāla. The meal is ready.”

mn82:24.5.verse: Then Raṭṭhapāla’s father served and satisfied Venerable Raṭṭhapāla with his own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

mn82:24.6.verse: When he had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, he spoke this verse while standing right there:

mn82:25.4.verse: in which nothing lasts at all.

mn82:25.7.verse: it is bones swathed in skin,

mn82:25.11.verse: may be enough to beguile a fool,

mn82:25.12.verse: but not a seeker of the far shore.

mn82:25.15.verse: may be enough to beguile a fool,

mn82:25.16.verse: but not a seeker of the far shore.

mn82:25.18.verse: like a freshly painted makeup box

mn82:25.19.verse: may be enough to beguile a fool,

mn82:25.20.verse: but not a seeker of the far shore.

mn82:25.22.verse: but the deer didn’t spring the trap.

mn82:25.23.verse: I’ve eaten the bait and now I go,

mn82:26.1.verse: Then Raṭṭhapāla, having spoke this verse while standing, went to King Koravya’s deer range and sat at the root of a tree for the day’s meditation.

mn82:27.1.verse: Then King Koravya addressed his gamekeeper,

mn82:27.2.verse: “My good gamekeeper, tidy up the park of the deer range.

mn82:27.3.verse: We will go to see the scenery.”

mn82:27.4.verse: “Yes, Your Majesty,” replied the gamekeeper. While tidying the deer range he saw Raṭṭhapāla sitting in meditation.

mn82:27.5.verse: Seeing this, he went to the king, and said,

mn82:27.6.verse: “The deer range is tidy, Your Majesty.

mn82:27.7.verse: And the gentleman named Raṭṭhapāla, the son of the leading clan in Thullakoṭṭhika, of whom you have often spoken highly, is meditating there at the root of a tree.”

mn82:27.8.verse: “Well then, my good gamekeeper, that’s enough of the park for today.

mn82:27.9.verse: Now I shall pay homage to the worthy Raṭṭhapāla.”

mn82:28.1.verse: And then King Koravya said, “Distribute the fresh and cooked foods that have been prepared there.” He had the finest carriages harnessed. Then he mounted a fine carriage and, along with other fine carriages, set out in full royal pomp from Thullakoṭṭhika to see Raṭṭhapāla.

mn82:28.2.verse: He went by carriage as far as the terrain allowed, then descended and approached Raṭṭhapāla on foot, together with a group of eminent officials. They exchanged greetings, and, when the greetings and polite conversation were over, he stood to one side and said to Raṭṭhapāla:

mn82:28.3.verse: “Here, worthy Raṭṭhapāla, sit on this elephant rug.”

mn82:28.4.verse: “Enough, Great King, you sit on it.

mn82:28.5.verse: I’m sitting on my own seat.”

mn82:28.6.verse: So the king sat down on the seat spread out, and said:

mn82:29.1.verse: “Worthy Raṭṭhapāla, there are these four kinds of decay. Because of these, some people shave off their hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

mn82:29.3.verse: Decay due to old age, decay due to sickness, decay of wealth, and decay of relatives.

mn82:30.1.verse: And what is decay due to old age?

mn82:30.2.verse: It’s when someone is old, elderly, and senior, advanced in years, and has reached the final stage of life.

mn82:30.4.verse: ‘I’m now old, elderly, and senior. I’m advanced in years and have reached the final stage of life.

mn82:30.5.verse: It’s not easy for me to acquire more wealth or to increase the wealth I’ve already acquired.

mn82:30.6.verse: Why don’t I shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness?’

mn82:30.7.verse: So because of that decay due to old age they go forth.

mn82:30.8.verse: This is called decay due to old age.

mn82:30.9.verse: But worthy Raṭṭhapāla is now a youth, young, with pristine black hair, blessed with youth, in the prime of life.

mn82:30.10.verse: You have no decay due to old age.

mn82:30.11.verse: So what did you know or see or hear that made you go forth?

mn82:31.1.verse: And what is decay due to sickness?

mn82:31.2.verse: It’s when someone is sick, suffering, gravely ill.

mn82:31.5.verse: It’s not easy for me to acquire more wealth or to increase the wealth I’ve already acquired.

mn82:31.6.verse: Why don’t I go forth from the lay life to homelessness?’

mn82:31.7.verse: So because of that decay due to sickness they go forth.

mn82:31.8.verse: This is called decay due to sickness.

mn82:31.9.verse: But worthy Raṭṭhapāla is now rarely ill or unwell. Your stomach digests well, being neither too hot nor too cold.

mn82:31.10.verse: You have no decay due to sickness.

mn82:31.11.verse: So what did you know or see or hear that made you go forth?

mn82:32.1.verse: And what is decay of wealth?

mn82:32.2.verse: It’s when someone is rich, affluent, and wealthy.

mn82:32.3.verse: But gradually their wealth dwindles away.

mn82:32.5.verse: ‘I used to be rich, affluent, and wealthy.

mn82:32.6.verse: But gradually my wealth has dwindled away.

mn82:32.7.verse: It’s not easy for me to acquire more wealth or to increase the wealth I’ve already acquired.

mn82:32.8.verse: Why don’t I go forth from the lay life to homelessness?’

mn82:32.9.verse: So because of that decay of wealth they go forth.

mn82:32.10.verse: This is called decay of wealth.

mn82:32.11.verse: But worthy Raṭṭhapāla is the son of the leading clan here in Thullakoṭṭhika.

mn82:32.12.verse: You have no decay of wealth.

mn82:32.13.verse: So what did you know or see or hear that made you go forth?

mn82:33.1.verse: And what is decay of relatives?

mn82:33.2.verse: It’s when someone has many friends and colleagues, relatives and kin.

mn82:33.3.verse: But gradually their relatives dwindle away.

mn82:33.5.verse: ‘I used to have many friends and colleagues, relatives and kin.

mn82:33.7.verse: It’s not easy for me to acquire more wealth or to increase the wealth I’ve already acquired.

mn82:33.8.verse: Why don’t I shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness?’

mn82:33.9.verse: So because of that decay of relatives they go forth.

mn82:33.10.verse: This is called decay of relatives.

mn82:33.11.verse: But worthy Raṭṭhapāla has many friends and colleagues, relatives and kin right here in Thullakoṭṭhika.

mn82:33.12.verse: You have no decay of relatives.

mn82:33.13.verse: So what did you know or see or hear that made you go forth?

mn82:34.1.verse: There are these four kinds of decay. Because of these, some people shave off their hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

mn82:34.2.verse: Worthy Raṭṭhapāla has none of these.

mn82:34.3.verse: So what did you know or see or hear that made you go forth?”

mn82:35.1.verse: “Great king, the Blessed One who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha has taught these four summaries of the teaching for recitation. It was after knowing and seeing and hearing these that I went forth from the lay life to homelessness.

mn82:36.1.verse: ‘The world is unstable and swept away.’

mn82:36.3.verse: ‘The world has no shelter and no savior.’

mn82:36.5.verse: ‘The world has no owner—you must leave it all behind and pass on.’

mn82:36.7.verse: ‘The world is wanting, insatiable, the slave of craving.’

mn82:37.1.verse: The Blessed One who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha taught these four summaries of the teaching. It was after knowing and seeing and hearing these that I went forth from the lay life to homelessness.”

mn82:38.1.verse: “‘The world is unstable and swept away.’

mn82:38.3.verse: How should I see the meaning of this statement?”

mn82:38.5.verse: When you were twenty or twenty-five years of age, were you well-versed at riding elephants, horses, and chariots, and at archery and swordsmanship? Were you strong in thigh and arm, capable, and battle-hardened?”

mn82:38.7.verse: Sometimes it seems as if I had superpowers then. I don’t see anyone who could have equaled me in strength.”

mn82:38.9.verse: These days are you just as strong in thigh and arm, capable, and battle-hardened?”

mn82:38.11.verse: For now I am old, elderly, and senior, I’m advanced in years and have reached the final stage of life. I am eighty years old.

mn82:38.12.verse: Sometimes I intend to step in one place, but my foot goes somewhere else.”

mn82:38.13.verse: “This is what the Buddha was referring to when he said:

mn82:38.14.verse: ‘The world is unstable and swept away.’”

mn82:38.17.verse: how well said this was by the Buddha.

mn82:38.19.verse: For the world is indeed unstable and swept away.

mn82:39.1.verse: In this royal court you can find divisions of elephants, cavalry, chariots, and infantry. They will serve to defend us from any threats. Yet you said:

mn82:39.2.verse: ‘The world has no shelter and no savior.’

mn82:39.4.verse: How should I see the meaning of this statement?”

mn82:39.6.verse: Do you have any chronic ailments?”

mn82:39.8.verse: Sometimes my friends and colleagues, relatives and kin surround me, thinking:

mn82:39.9.verse: ‘Now the king will die! Now the king will die!’”

mn82:39.11.verse: Can you get your friends and colleagues, relatives and kin to help:

mn82:39.12.verse: ‘Please, my dear friends and colleagues, relatives and kin, all of you here share my pain so that I may feel less pain.’

mn82:39.13.verse: Or must you alone feel that pain?”

mn82:39.14.verse: “I can’t get my friends to share my pain.

mn82:39.16.verse: Rather, I alone must feel it.”

mn82:39.17.verse: “This is what the Buddha was referring to when he said:

mn82:39.18.verse: ‘The world has no shelter and no savior.’”

mn82:39.21.verse: how well said this was by the Buddha.

mn82:39.23.verse: For the world indeed has no shelter and no savior.

mn82:40.1.verse: In this royal court you can find abundant gold, both coined and uncoined, stored above and below ground. Yet you said:

mn82:40.2.verse: ‘The world has no owner—you must leave it all behind and pass on.’

mn82:40.4.verse: How should I see the meaning of this statement?”

mn82:40.6.verse: These days you amuse yourself, supplied and provided with the five kinds of sensual stimulation. But is there any way to ensure that in the next life
