mn91:10.1.verse: “When walking, Master Gotama steps with his right foot first.

mn91:10.2.verse: He doesn’t extend his foot too far or place it down too near.

mn91:10.3.verse: He walks neither too quickly nor too slowly.

mn91:10.4.verse: He walks without knocking his knees together or knocking his ankles together.

mn91:10.5.verse: He walks without raising or lowering his thighs, without pinching them together or spreading them apart.

mn91:10.6.verse: When he walks, only the lower part of his body moves, and he walks without bodily effort.

mn91:10.7.verse: When turning to look, he turns to look with his entire body.

mn91:10.8.verse: He doesn’t look straight up or straight down.

mn91:10.9.verse: He walks without glancing around. He gazes a plow’s length before him; beyond that, he has unhindered knowledge & vision.

mn91:11.1.verse: “When going indoors, he doesn’t raise or lower his body, bend it forward or back.

mn91:12.1.verse: He turns around neither too far from the seat nor too close. He doesn’t lean on his seat with his hand. He doesn’t plunk his body down on the seat.

mn91:12.2.verse: “Having sat down indoors, he doesn’t fidget with his hands or his feet.

mn91:12.3.verse: He doesn’t sit with his knees crossed or with his ankles crossed.

mn91:12.4.verse: He doesn’t sit with his hand holding his chin.

mn91:12.5.verse: “Having sat down indoors, he isn’t fearful, doesn’t shiver, doesn’t tremble, isn’t nervous. Being unfearful, not shivering, not trembling, not nervous, without his hair standing on end,

mn91:13.1.verse: “When receiving bowl-water, he doesn’t raise or lower the bowl, tip it forward or back.

mn91:14.1.verse: He receives neither too little nor too much bowl-water.

mn91:14.2.verse: He washes the bowl without making a sloshing sound. He washes the bowl without turning it over. He doesn’t wash his hands having put the bowl on the ground. When his hands are washed, the bowl is washed. When the bowl is washed, his hands are washed.

mn91:14.3.verse: He pours the bowl-water not too near, not too far, and without splashing.

mn91:14.4.verse: “When receiving rice, he doesn’t raise or lower the bowl, tip it forward or back.

mn91:14.5.verse: He receives neither too little nor too much rice.

mn91:14.6.verse: He also receives curry, taking curry in the proper proportion. He doesn’t put too much curry in his mouthful.

mn91:14.7.verse: Having turned the mouthful over two or three times in his mouth, he swallows it.

mn91:14.8.verse: No unchewed rice grain enters his body; no rice grain remains in his mouth.

mn91:14.10.verse: He takes his food experiencing the taste but not experiencing passion for the taste.

mn91:14.11.verse: “Master Gotama eats food endowed with eight factors:

mn91:14.12.verse: not playfully, nor for intoxication, nor for putting on bulk, nor for beautification; but simply for the survival & continuance of this body, for ending its afflictions, for the support of the holy life, thinking, ‘Thus will I destroy old feelings (of hunger) and not create new feelings (from overeating). I will maintain myself, be blameless, & live in comfort.’

mn91:15.1.verse: “When he has finished his meal and receives bowl-water, he doesn’t raise or lower the bowl, tip it forward or back.

mn91:15.2.verse: He receives neither too little nor too much bowl-water.

mn91:15.3.verse: He washes the bowl without making a sloshing sound. He washes the bowl without turning it over. He doesn’t wash his hands having put the bowl on the ground. When his hands are washed, the bowl is washed. When the bowl is washed, his hands are washed.

mn91:15.4.verse: He pours the bowl-water not too near, not too far, and without splashing. …

mn91:16.1.verse: He puts his bowl on the floor, not too near, not too far. He is neither careless of the bowl nor overly solicitous about it. …

mn91:17.1.verse: He sits in silence for a moment, but doesn’t exceed the time for the anumodanā [verses rejoicing in the merit of the donor]. …

mn91:17.2.verse: He gives the anumodanā, doesn’t criticize the meal, doesn’t expect another meal.

mn91:17.3.verse: He instructs, urges, rouses, & encourages the gathering with a talk purely on Dhamma.

mn91:17.4.verse: Having done so, he rises from his seat and departs.

mn91:18.1.verse: He walks neither too quickly nor too slowly, nor does he desire to get away.

mn91:19.1.verse: “His robe is worn not too high on his body, not too low on his body, not too tight or too loose on his body.

mn91:19.2.verse: The wind doesn’t blow his robe away from his body.

mn91:19.3.verse: Dust & dirt don’t soil his body.

mn91:20.1.verse: “Having gone to the monastery, he sits on a seat made ready. Having sat down, he washes his feet,

mn91:20.2.verse: but he doesn’t occupy himself with grooming his feet.

mn91:20.3.verse: Having washed his feet, he sits with his legs folded, sets his body erect, and brings mindfulness to the fore.

mn91:20.4.verse: He doesn’t set his mind on his own affliction, the affliction of others, or the affliction of both.

mn91:20.5.verse: He sits setting his mind on his own welfare, the welfare of others, the welfare of both—even the welfare of the entire cosmos.

mn91:21.1.verse: “Having gone to the monastery, he teaches Dhamma to the gathering. He neither flatters nor berates the gathering.

mn91:21.2.verse: He instructs, urges, rouses, & encourages the gathering with a talk purely on Dhamma.

mn91:21.3.verse: The voice that issues from his mouth is endowed with eight qualities:

mn91:21.4.verse: It is distinct, intelligible, melodious, audible, ringing, focused, deep, & resonant.

mn91:21.5.verse: But while his voice is intelligible to the gathering, the sound of his voice doesn’t extend outside the gathering.

mn91:21.6.verse: Those who have been instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged by his Dhamma talk rise from their seats and depart, looking only at him and concerned with nothing else.

mn91:22.1.verse: “We have seen Master Gotama walking, sir, we have seen him standing, we have seen him entering indoors, we have seen him sitting in silence indoors, we have seen him eating indoors, we have seen him sitting in silence after eating, we have seen him giving the anumodanā after eating, we having seen him returning to the monastery, we have seen him sitting in silence after going to the monastery, we have seen him teaching the Dhamma to a gathering in the monastery.

mn91:22.2.verse: He is like that, like that—and more than that.”

mn91:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Videhans together with a large Saṅgha of five hundred mendicants.

mn91:2.1.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Brahmāyu was residing in Mithilā. He was old, elderly, and senior, advanced in years, having reached the final stage of life; he was a hundred and twenty years old. He had mastered the three Vedas, together with their vocabularies and ritual performance, their phonology and word classification, and the testaments as fifth. He knew them word-by-word, and their grammar. He was well versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man.

mn91:3.2.verse: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—is wandering in the land of the Videhans, together with a large Saṅgha of five hundred mendicants.

mn91:3.4.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

mn91:3.5.verse: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

mn91:3.6.verse: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

mn91:3.7.verse: It’s good to see such perfected ones.”

mn91:4.1.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Brahmāyu had a pupil named Uttara. He too had mastered the Vedic curriculum.

mn91:4.2.verse: Brahmāyu told Uttara of the Buddha’s presence in the land of the Videhans, and added:

mn91:4.7.verse: “Please, dear Uttara, go to the ascetic Gotama and find out whether or not he lives up to his reputation.

mn91:4.9.verse: Through you I shall learn about the worthy Gotama.”

mn91:5.1.verse: “But sir, how shall I find out whether or not the ascetic Gotama lives up to his reputation?”

mn91:5.3.verse: “Dear Uttara, the thirty-two marks of a great man have been handed down in our hymns. A great man who possesses these has only two possible destinies, no other.

mn91:5.4.verse: If he stays at home he becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch, a just and principled king. His dominion extends to all four sides, he achieves stability in the country, and he possesses the seven treasures.

mn91:5.5.verse: He has the following seven treasures:

mn91:5.6.verse: the wheel, the elephant, the horse, the jewel, the woman, the householder, and the commander as the seventh treasure.

mn91:5.7.verse: He has over a thousand sons who are valiant and heroic, crushing the armies of his enemies.

mn91:5.8.verse: After conquering this land girt by sea, he reigns by principle, without rod or sword.

mn91:5.9.verse: But if he goes forth from the lay life to homelessness, he becomes a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, who has cast off the world’s veil.

mn91:5.10.verse: But, dear Uttara, I am the one who gives the hymns,

mn91:5.11.verse: and you are the one who receives them.”

mn91:6.1.verse: “Yes, worthy sir,” replied Uttara. He got up from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled Brahmāyu, keeping him on his right, before setting out for the land of the Videhans where the Buddha was wandering.

mn91:6.2.verse: Traveling stage by stage, he came to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

mn91:6.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side,

mn91:6.4.verse: and scrutinized his body for the thirty-two marks of a great man.

mn91:6.5.verse: He saw all of them except two,

mn91:6.7.verse: whether the private parts are sheathed in a foreskin, and the largeness of the tongue.

mn91:6.8.verse: Then it occurred to the Buddha,

mn91:6.9.verse: “This student Uttara sees all the marks except two,

mn91:6.11.verse: whether the private parts are sheathed in a foreskin, and the largeness of the tongue.”

mn91:7.1.verse: So the Buddha used his psychic power to will that Uttara would see his private parts sheathed in a foreskin.

mn91:7.2.verse: And he stuck out his tongue and stroked back and forth on his ear holes and nostrils, and covered his entire forehead with his tongue.

mn91:8.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama possesses the thirty-two marks.

mn91:8.3.verse: Why don’t I follow him and observe his deportment?”

mn91:8.4.verse: So Uttara followed the Buddha like a shadow for seven months.

mn91:8.5.verse: When seven months had passed he set out wandering toward Mithilā.

mn91:8.6.verse: There he approached the brahmin Brahmāyu, bowed, and sat down to one side. Brahmāyu said to him,

mn91:8.7.verse: “Well, dear Uttara, does the worthy Gotama live up to his reputation or not?”

mn91:8.11.verse: The worthy Gotama possesses the thirty-two marks.

mn91:9.3.verse: On the soles of his feet there are thousand-spoked wheels, with rims and hubs, complete in every detail.

mn91:9.6.verse: His hands and feet are soft and tender.

mn91:9.7.verse: He has serried hands and feet.

mn91:9.8.verse: The tops of his feet are arched.

mn91:9.9.verse: His calves are like those of an antelope.

mn91:9.10.verse: When standing upright and not bending over, the palms of both hands touch the knees.

mn91:9.11.verse: His private parts are sheathed in a foreskin.

mn91:9.12.verse: He is golden colored; his skin shines like lustrous gold.

mn91:9.13.verse: He has delicate skin, so delicate that dust and dirt don’t stick to his body.

mn91:9.14.verse: His hairs grow one per pore.

mn91:9.15.verse: His hairs stand up; they’re blue-black and curl clockwise.

mn91:9.16.verse: His body is tall and straight-limbed.

mn91:9.17.verse: He has bulging muscles in seven places.

mn91:9.18.verse: His chest is like that of a lion.

mn91:9.19.verse: He is filled out between the shoulders.

mn91:9.20.verse: He has the proportional circumference of a banyan tree: the span of his arms equals the height of his body.

mn91:9.23.verse: His jaw is like that of a lion.

mn91:9.29.verse: He has the voice of the Divinity, like a cuckoo’s call.

mn91:9.31.verse: He has eyelashes like a cow’s.

mn91:9.32.verse: Between his eyebrows there grows a tuft, soft and white like cotton-wool.

mn91:9.33.verse: The crown of his head is like a turban.

mn91:9.34.verse: These are the thirty-two marks of a great man possessed by the worthy Gotama.

mn91:10.1.verse: When he’s walking he takes the first step with the right foot.

mn91:10.2.verse: He doesn’t lift his foot too far or place it too near.

mn91:10.3.verse: He doesn’t walk too slow or too fast.

mn91:10.4.verse: He walks without knocking his knees or ankles together.

mn91:10.5.verse: When he’s walking he keeps his thighs neither too straight nor too bent, neither too tight nor too loose.

mn91:10.6.verse: When he walks, only the lower half of his body moves, and he walks effortlessly.

mn91:10.7.verse: When he turns to look he does so with the whole body.

mn91:10.8.verse: He doesn’t look directly up or down.

mn91:10.9.verse: He doesn’t look all around while walking, but focuses a plough’s length in front. Beyond that he has unhindered knowledge and vision.

mn91:11.1.verse: When entering an inhabited area he keeps his body neither too straight nor too bent, neither too tight nor too loose.

mn91:12.1.verse: He turns around neither too far nor too close to the seat. He doesn’t lean on his hand when sitting down. And he doesn’t just plonk his body down on the seat.

mn91:12.2.verse: When sitting in inhabited areas he doesn’t fidget with his hands or feet.

mn91:12.3.verse: He doesn’t sit with his knees or ankles crossed.

mn91:12.4.verse: He doesn’t sit with his hand holding his chin.

mn91:12.5.verse: When sitting in inhabited areas he doesn’t shake, tremble, quake, or get nervous, and so he is not nervous at all.

mn91:12.6.verse: When sitting in inhabited areas he still practices seclusion.

mn91:13.1.verse: When receiving water for rinsing the bowl, he holds the bowl neither too straight nor too bent, neither too tight nor too loose.

mn91:14.1.verse: He receives neither too little nor too much water.

mn91:14.2.verse: He rinses the bowl without making a sloshing noise, or spinning it around. He doesn’t put the bowl on the ground to rinse his hands; his hands and bowl are rinsed at the same time.

mn91:14.3.verse: He doesn’t throw the bowl rinsing water away too far or too near, or splash it about.

mn91:14.4.verse: When receiving rice, he holds the bowl neither too straight nor too bent, neither too close nor too loose.

mn91:14.5.verse: He receives neither too little nor too much rice.

mn91:14.6.verse: He eats sauce in a moderate proportion, and doesn’t put too much sauce on his portions.

mn91:14.7.verse: He chews over each portion two or three times before swallowing.

mn91:14.8.verse: But no grain of rice enters his body unchewed, and none remain in his mouth.

mn91:14.9.verse: Only then does he raise another portion to his lips.

mn91:14.10.verse: He eats experiencing the taste, but without experiencing greed for the taste.

mn91:14.11.verse: He eats food thinking of eight reasons:

mn91:14.12.verse: ‘Not for fun, indulgence, adornment, or decoration, but only to sustain this body, to avoid harm, and to support spiritual practice. In this way, I shall put an end to old discomfort and not give rise to new discomfort, and I will have the means to keep going, blamelessness, and a comfortable abiding.’

mn91:15.1.verse: After eating, when receiving water for washing the bowl, he holds the bowl neither too straight nor too bent, neither too tight nor too loose.

mn91:15.2.verse: He receives neither too little nor too much water.

mn91:15.3.verse: He washes the bowl without making a sloshing noise, or spinning it around. He doesn’t put the bowl on the ground to wash his hands; his hands and bowl are washed at the same time.

mn91:15.4.verse: He doesn’t throw the bowl washing water away too far or too near, or splash it about.

mn91:16.1.verse: After eating he doesn’t put the bowl on the ground too far away or too close. He’s not careless with his bowl, nor does he spend too much time on it.

mn91:17.1.verse: After eating he sits a while in silence, but doesn’t wait too long to give the verses of appreciation.

mn91:17.2.verse: After eating he expresses appreciation without criticizing the meal or expecting another one.

mn91:17.3.verse: Invariably, he educates, encourages, fires up, and inspires that assembly with a Dhamma talk.

mn91:17.4.verse: Then he gets up from his seat and leaves.

mn91:18.1.verse: He walks neither too fast nor too slow, without wanting to get out of there.

mn91:19.1.verse: He wears his robe on his body neither too high nor too low, neither too clinging nor too loose.

mn91:19.2.verse: The wind doesn’t blow his robe off his body.

mn91:19.3.verse: And dust and dirt don’t stick to his body.

mn91:20.1.verse: When he has gone to the monastery he sits on a seat spread out and washes his feet.

mn91:20.2.verse: But he doesn’t waste time with pedicures.

mn91:20.3.verse: When he has washed his feet, he sits down cross-legged, sets his body straight, and brings mindfulness to the present.

mn91:20.4.verse: He has no intention to hurt himself, hurt others, or hurt both.

mn91:20.5.verse: He only wishes for the welfare of himself, of others, of both, and of the whole world.

mn91:21.1.verse: In the monastery when he teaches Dhamma to an assembly, he neither flatters them nor rebukes them.

mn91:21.2.verse: Invariably, he educates, encourages, fires up, and inspires that assembly with a Dhamma talk.

mn91:21.3.verse: The sound of his voice has eight qualities:

mn91:21.4.verse: it is clear, comprehensible, charming, audible, lucid, undistorted, deep, and resonant.

mn91:21.5.verse: He makes sure his voice is intelligible as far as the assembly goes, but the sound doesn’t extend outside the assembly.

mn91:21.6.verse: And when they’ve been inspired with a Dhamma talk by the worthy Gotama they get up from their seats and leave looking back at him alone, and not forgetting their lesson.

mn91:22.1.verse: I have seen the worthy Gotama walking and standing; entering inhabited areas, and sitting and eating there; sitting silently after eating, and expressing appreciation; going to the monastery, sitting silently there, and teaching Dhamma to an assembly there.

mn91:22.2.verse: Such is the worthy Gotama; such he is and more than that.”

mn91:23.1.verse: When he had spoken, the brahmin Brahmāyu rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha, and uttered this aphorism three times:

mn91:23.2.verse: “Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!

mn91:23.3.verse: Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!

mn91:23.4.verse: Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!

mn91:23.5.verse: Hopefully, some time or other I’ll get to meet him, and we can have a discussion.”

mn91:24.1.verse: And then the Buddha, traveling stage by stage in the Videhan lands, arrived at Mithilā,

mn91:24.2.verse: where he stayed in the Maghadeva Mango Grove.

mn91:24.3.verse: The brahmins and householders of Mithilā heard:

mn91:24.4.verse: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—has arrived at Mithilā, where he is staying in the Maghadeva Mango Grove.

mn91:24.6.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

mn91:24.7.verse: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

mn91:24.8.verse: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

mn91:24.9.verse: It’s good to see such perfected ones.”

mn91:25.1.verse: Then the brahmins and householders of Mithilā went up to the Buddha. Before sitting down to one side, some bowed, some exchanged greetings and polite conversation, some held up their cupped palms toward the Buddha, some announced their name and clan, while some kept silent.

mn91:26.1.verse: The brahmin Brahmāyu also heard that the Buddha had arrived.

mn91:26.2.verse: So he went to the Maghadeva Mango Grove together with several disciples.

mn91:26.3.verse: Not far from the grove he thought,

mn91:26.4.verse: “It wouldn’t be appropriate for me to go to see the ascetic Gotama without letting him know beforehand.”

mn91:26.5.verse: So he addressed one of his young students:

mn91:26.6.verse: “Here, young student, go to the ascetic Gotama and in my name bow with your head to his feet. Ask him if he is healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.

mn91:26.9.verse: ‘Worthy Gotama, the brahmin Brahmāyu is old, elderly, and senior, advanced in years, having reached the final stage of life; he is a hundred and twenty years old. He has mastered the three Vedas, together with their vocabularies and ritual performance, their phonology and word classification, and the testaments as fifth. He knows them word-by-word, and their grammar. He is well versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man.

mn91:26.10.verse: Of all the brahmins and householders residing in Mithilā, Brahmāyu is said to be the foremost in

mn91:26.16.verse: He wants to see the worthy Gotama.’”

mn91:26.17.verse: “Yes, worthy sir,” that young student replied. He did as he was asked, and the Buddha said,

mn91:26.29.verse: “Please, student, let Brahmāyu come at his convenience.”

mn91:27.1.verse: The young student went back to Brahmāyu and said to him,

mn91:27.2.verse: “Your request for an audience with the ascetic Gotama has been granted.

mn91:28.1.verse: Then the brahmin Brahmāyu went up to the Buddha.

mn91:28.2.verse: The assembly saw him coming off in the distance,

mn91:28.3.verse: and made way for him, as he was well-known and famous.

mn91:28.6.verse: Please sit on your own seats.

mn91:28.7.verse: I shall sit here by the ascetic Gotama.”

mn91:29.1.verse: Then the brahmin Brahmāyu went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

mn91:29.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side,

mn91:29.3.verse: and scrutinized the Buddha’s body for the thirty-two marks of a great man.

mn91:29.4.verse: He saw all of them except two,

mn91:29.6.verse: whether the private parts are sheathed in a foreskin, and the largeness of the tongue.

mn91:29.7.verse: Then Brahmāyu addressed the Buddha in verse:

mn91:29.10.verse: There are two that I don’t see

mn91:29.11.verse: on the body of the worthy Gotama.

mn91:29.12.verse: Are the private parts sheathed in a foreskin,

mn91:29.14.verse: Though called by a word of the feminine gender,

mn91:29.15.verse: perhaps your tongue is a manly one?

mn91:29.18.verse: Please stick it out in its full extent,

mn91:29.19.verse: and so, O seer, dispel my doubt.

mn91:29.20.verse: For my welfare and benefit in this life,

mn91:29.21.verse: and happiness in lives to come.

mn91:29.22.verse: And I ask you to grant the opportunity

mn91:30.1.verse: Then it occurred to the Buddha,

mn91:30.2.verse: “Brahmāyu sees all the marks except two,

mn91:30.4.verse: whether the private parts are sheathed in a foreskin, and the largeness of the tongue.”

mn91:30.5.verse: So the Buddha used his psychic power to will that Brahmāyu would see his private parts sheathed in a foreskin.

mn91:30.6.verse: And he stuck out his tongue and stroked back and forth on his ear holes and nostrils, and covered his entire forehead with his tongue.

mn91:30.7.verse: Then the Buddha replied to Brahmāyu in verse:

mn91:31.1.verse: “The thirty-two marks of a great man

mn91:31.3.verse: are all found on my body:

mn91:31.5.verse: I have known what should be known,

mn91:31.6.verse: and developed what should be developed,

mn91:31.7.verse: and given up what should be given up:

mn91:31.8.verse: and so, brahmin, I am a Buddha.

mn91:31.9.verse: For your welfare and benefit in this life,

mn91:31.10.verse: and happiness in lives to come:

mn91:32.4.verse: what is beneficial in this life or the next?”

mn91:32.6.verse: “I’m well versed in the benefits that apply to this life,

mn91:32.7.verse: and others ask me about this.

mn91:32.8.verse: Why don’t I ask the ascetic Gotama about the benefit that specifically applies to lives to come?”

mn91:32.9.verse: So Brahmāyu addressed the Buddha in verse:

mn91:32.11.verse: And how do you become a knowledge master?

mn91:32.12.verse: How a master of the three knowledges?

mn91:32.13.verse: And how is one called a scholar?

mn91:32.14.verse: How do you become a perfected one?

mn91:32.16.verse: How do you become a sage?

mn91:32.17.verse: And how is one declared to be awakened?”

mn91:33.1.verse: Then the Buddha replied to Brahmāyu in verse:

mn91:33.3.verse: sees heaven and places of loss,

mn91:33.4.verse: and has attained the end of rebirth:

mn91:33.5.verse: such a sage has perfect insight.

mn91:33.6.verse: They know their mind is pure,

mn91:33.8.verse: they’ve given up birth and death,

mn91:33.9.verse: and have completed the spiritual journey.

mn91:33.11.verse: such a one is declared to be awakened.”

mn91:34.1.verse: When he said this, Brahmāyu got up from his seat and arranged his robe over one shoulder. He bowed with his head to the Buddha’s feet, caressing them and covering them with kisses, and pronounced his name:

mn91:34.2.verse: “I am the brahmin Brahmāyu, worthy Gotama!

mn91:35.1.verse: Then that assembly, their minds full of wonder and amazement, thought,

mn91:35.3.verse: that Brahmāyu, who is so well-known and famous, should show the Buddha such utmost deference.”

mn91:35.4.verse: Then the Buddha said to Brahmāyu,

mn91:35.5.verse: “Enough, brahmin. Get up, and sit in your own seat, since your mind has such confidence in me.”

mn91:35.6.verse: So Brahmāyu got up and sat in his own seat.

mn91:36.1.verse: Then the Buddha taught him step by step, with

mn91:36.2.verse: a talk on giving, ethical conduct, and heaven.

mn91:36.3.verse: He revealed the drawbacks of sensual pleasures, so sordid and corrupt, and the benefit of renunciation.

mn91:36.4.verse: And when the Buddha knew that Brahmāyu’s mind was ready, pliable, rid of hindrances, elated, and confident he revealed the special teaching of the Buddhas:

mn91:36.5.verse: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

mn91:36.6.verse: Just as a clean cloth rid of stains would properly absorb dye,

mn91:36.7.verse: in that very seat the stainless, immaculate vision of the Dhamma arose in the brahmin Brahmāyu:

mn91:36.8.verse: “Everything that is liable to arise is liable to cease.”

mn91:36.9.verse: Then Brahmāyu saw, attained, understood, and fathomed the Dhamma. He went beyond doubt, got rid of indecision, and became self-assured and independent of others regarding the Teacher’s instructions. He said to the Buddha:

mn91:37.2.verse: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

mn91:37.3.verse: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

mn91:37.4.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.

mn91:37.5.verse: Would you and the mendicant Saṅgha please accept tomorrow’s meal from me?”

mn91:37.7.verse: Then, knowing that the Buddha had consented, Brahmāyu rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

mn91:38.1.verse: And when the night had passed Brahmāyu had delicious fresh and cooked foods prepared in his own home. Then he had the Buddha informed of the time, saying,

mn91:38.2.verse: “It’s time, worthy Gotama, the meal is ready.”

mn91:38.3.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of the brahmin Brahmāyu, where he sat down on the seat spread out together with the Saṅgha of mendicants.

mn91:38.4.verse: For seven days, Brahmāyu served and satisfied the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha with his own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

mn91:39.1.verse: When the seven days had passed, the Buddha left to wander in the Videhan lands.

mn91:39.2.verse: Not long after the Buddha left, Brahmāyu passed away.

mn91:39.3.verse: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

mn91:39.5.verse: Where has he been reborn in his next life?”

mn91:39.6.verse: “Mendicants, the brahmin Brahmāyu was astute. He practiced in line with the teaching, and did not trouble me about the teachings.

mn91:39.7.verse: With the ending of the five lower fetters, he’s been reborn spontaneously and will become extinguished there, not liable to return from that world.”

mn91:39.8.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn91:39.9.verse: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

mn92:1.2.verse: on one occasion, while the Blessed One was wandering on a tour among the Aṅguttarāpans with a large Saṅgha of monks, approximately 1,250 monks in all, he arrived at an Aṅguttarāpan town named Āpaṇa.

mn92:2.1.verse: Keṇiya the coiled hair ascetic heard it said,

mn92:2.2.verse: “Gotama the contemplative—a son of the Sakyans, gone forth from the Sakyan clan—on a wandering tour among the Aṅguttarāpans with a large Saṅgha of monks, approximately 1,250 monks in all—has arrived at Āpaṇa.

mn92:2.3.verse: And of that Master Gotama this fine reputation has spread:

mn92:2.4.verse: ‘He is indeed a Blessed One, worthy & rightly self-awakened, consummate in clear-knowing & conduct, well-gone, an expert with regard to the cosmos, unexcelled trainer of people fit to be tamed, teacher of devas & human beings, awakened, blessed.’

mn92:2.5.verse: He makes known—having realized it through direct knowledge—this world with its devas, Māras, & Brahmās, this generation with its contemplatives & brahmans, its rulers & commonfolk;

mn92:2.6.verse: he explains the Dhamma admirable in the beginning, admirable in the middle, admirable in the end; he expounds the holy life both in its particulars & in its essence, entirely perfect, surpassingly pure.

mn92:2.7.verse: It is good to see such a worthy one.’”

mn92:3.1.verse: So Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, exchanged courteous greetings with him.

mn92:3.2.verse: After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, he sat to one side.

mn92:3.3.verse: As he was sitting there, the Blessed One instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged him with a talk on Dhamma.

mn92:3.4.verse: Then Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic—instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged with the Blessed One’s talk on Dhamma—said to him,

mn92:3.5.verse: “Master Gotama, may the Blessed One acquiesce to my meal tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha of monks.”

mn92:3.6.verse: When this was said, the Blessed One said to him,

mn92:3.7.verse: “The Saṅgha of monks is large, Keṇiya, approximately 1,250 monks in all, and you are strongly confident in brahmans.”

mn92:3.8.verse: A second time, Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic said to the Blessed One,

mn92:3.9.verse: “Even though the Saṅgha of monks is large, master Gotama, approximately 1,250 monks in all, and I am strongly confident in brahmans,

mn92:3.10.verse: may Master Gotama acquiesce to my meal tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha of monks.”

mn92:3.11.verse: A second time, the Blessed One said to Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic,

mn92:3.12.verse: “The Saṅgha of monks is large, Keṇiya, approximately 1,250 monks in all, and you are strongly confident in brahmans.”

mn92:3.13.verse: A third time, Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic said to the Blessed One,

mn92:3.14.verse: “Even though the Saṅgha of monks is large, master Gotama, approximately 1,250 monks in all, and I am strongly confident in brahmans,

mn92:3.15.verse: may Master Gotama acquiesce to my meal tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha of monks.”

mn92:3.16.verse: The Blessed One acquiesced with silence.

mn92:4.1.verse: Then Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic, understanding the Blessed One’s acquiescence, got up from his seat and returned to his own ashram. On arrival, he addressed his friends & companions, his relatives & kinsmen:

mn92:4.2.verse: “Listen to me, venerable friends & companions, relatives & kinsmen:

mn92:4.3.verse: I have invited Gotama the contemplative together with a Saṅgha of monks, approximately 1,250 monks in all, for the meal tomorrow.

mn92:4.4.verse: Give me bodily assistance for that.”

mn92:4.5.verse: “As you say, master,” his friends & companions, relatives & kinsmen responded to him. Some of them dug out ovens, some split wood, some washed dishes, some set out a water pot, some arranged seats,

mn92:4.6.verse: while Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic arranged a pavilion of garlands himself.

mn92:5.1.verse: Now on that occasion Sela the brahman was staying at Āpaṇa. He was a master of the Three Vedas with their vocabularies, liturgy, phonology, etymology, & histories as a fifth; skilled in philology & grammar, he was fully versed in cosmology and in the marks of a Great Man. He was instructing 300 young brahmans in the (Vedic) mantras.

mn92:6.1.verse: Now on that occasion Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic was strongly confident in Sela the brahman.

mn92:6.2.verse: Then, as he—surrounded by 300 young brahmans—was walking and wandering about to exercise his legs, he arrived at the ashram of Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic.

mn92:6.3.verse: He saw that some of the people in the ashram were digging out ovens, some were splitting wood, some were washing dishes, some were setting out a water pot, some were arranging seats, while Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic was arranging a pavilion of garlands himself.

mn92:7.1.verse: On seeing this, he said to Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic,

mn92:7.2.verse: “Could it be that Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic is giving a son or daughter in marriage, or is he setting up a great sacrifice, or is Seniya Bimbisāra, the king of Magadha, invited for tomorrow together with his army?”

mn92:8.1.verse: “No, Sela, it’s not that I’m giving a son or daughter in marriage, nor that Seniya Bimbisāra, the king of Magadha, is invited for tomorrow together with his army;

mn92:8.2.verse: but I am setting up a great sacrifice.

mn92:8.3.verse: There is Gotama the contemplative—a son of the Sakyans, gone forth from the Sakyan clan—who, on a wandering tour among the Aṅguttarāpans with a large Saṅgha of monks, approximately 1,250 monks in all, has arrived at Āpaṇa.

mn92:8.4.verse: And of that Master Gotama this fine reputation has spread:

mn92:8.5.verse: ‘He is indeed a Blessed One, worthy & rightly self-awakened, consummate in clear-knowing & conduct, well-gone, an expert with regard to the cosmos, unexcelled trainer of people fit to be tamed, teacher of devas & human beings, awakened, blessed.’

mn92:8.6.verse: He has been invited by me for the meal tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha of monks.”

mn92:10.1.verse: Then the thought occurred to Sela the brahman,

mn92:10.2.verse: “Even just this word is hard to come by in the world: ‘Awakened.’

mn92:10.3.verse: Now, these 32 marks of a Great Man have come down in our mantras. For a Great Man endowed with them, two future courses, and no other, exist.

mn92:10.4.verse: If he inhabits a home, he will become a wheel-turning king, righteous, a king through righteousness, a conqueror of the four quarters, a stabilizer of his countryside endowed with the seven treasures.

mn92:10.6.verse: the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the adviser-treasure as the seventh.

mn92:10.7.verse: He will have a thousand sons, valiant, heroic in body, crushers of enemy armies.

mn92:10.8.verse: He will dwell, having conquered the earth to the edge of the sea, by means of Dhamma, without rod, without sword.

mn92:10.9.verse: But if he goes forth from the home life into homelessness, he will become a worthy one, rightly self-awakened, with his roof opened in the world.”

mn92:11.1.verse: “Master Keṇiya, where is he staying now, that Master Gotama, worthy & rightly self-awakened?”

mn92:11.2.verse: When this was said, Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic lifted his right arm and said to Sela the brahman,

mn92:11.3.verse: “There, by the dark green line of the forest.”

mn92:12.1.verse: Then Sela the brahman, together with the 300 young brahmans, headed toward the Blessed One.

mn92:12.2.verse: Then he addressed the young brahmans,

mn92:12.3.verse: “Come noiselessly, masters, placing a footstep in a footstep.

mn92:12.4.verse: These Blessed Ones are hard to approach, like a lion wandering alone.

mn92:12.5.verse: And when I engage Gotama the contemplative in counsel, don’t break into the middle of my talk.

mn92:12.6.verse: Wait until the end of my talk.”

mn92:13.1.verse: Then Sela the brahman went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, exchanged courteous greetings with him.

mn92:13.2.verse: After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, he sat to one side.

mn92:13.3.verse: As he was sitting there, he looked for the 32 marks of a Great Man in the Blessed One’s body.

mn92:13.4.verse: He saw most of the 32 marks of a Great Man in the Blessed One’s body, except for two.

mn92:13.5.verse: About the two marks he was doubtful, uncertain, undecided, and wasn’t reassured:

mn92:13.6.verse: about the male organ being in a sheath, and about the size of the tongue.

mn92:13.7.verse: The thought occurred to the Blessed One,

mn92:13.8.verse: “Sela the brahman sees most of my marks of a Great Man, except for two.

mn92:13.9.verse: About the two marks he is doubtful, uncertain, undecided, and isn’t reassured:

mn92:13.10.verse: about the male organ being in a sheath, and about the size of the tongue.”

mn92:14.1.verse: So the Blessed One willed a willing of power such that Sela the brahman saw that the Blessed One’s male organ was in a sheath.

mn92:14.2.verse: And then, extending his tongue, the Blessed One licked both ear-holes and nostrils back and forth, and covered his whole forehead with his tongue.

mn92:15.1.verse: The thought occurred to Sela the brahman,

mn92:15.2.verse: “Gotama the contemplative’s 32 marks of a Great Man are complete and not incomplete.

mn92:15.3.verse: But I don’t know whether he is awakened or not.

mn92:15.4.verse: Still, I have heard the aged line of teachers, along in their years, say that

mn92:15.5.verse: Blessed Ones, worthy & rightly self-awakened, reveal themselves when their praise is spoken.

mn92:15.6.verse: What if I were to praise Gotama the contemplative face-to-face with fitting verses?”

mn92:15.7.verse: So Sela the brahman praised the Blessed One face-to-face with fitting verses:

mn92:16.3.verse: Blessed One, you have a golden complexion,

mn92:16.4.verse: you have white teeth, you’re vigorous.

mn92:16.5.verse: The characteristics of a well-born man,

mn92:16.6.verse: the marks of a Great Man,

mn92:16.7.verse: are all present in your body.

mn92:16.8.verse: Clear your eyes, good your face,

mn92:16.13.verse: A monk with skin resembling gold

mn92:16.15.verse: but what use is the contemplative state

mn92:16.16.verse: for you, so superlative in appearance?

mn92:16.17.verse: You deserve to be a king,

mn92:16.20.verse: sovereign lord of the Jambu grove.

mn92:16.23.verse: King of kings, monarch of human beings:

mn92:17.3.verse: I turn the wheel with Dhamma—

mn92:17.4.verse: the wheel whose turning can’t be stopped.”

mn92:18.5.verse: But who, master, is your general,

mn92:18.6.verse: the disciple right below the teacher?

mn92:18.8.verse: the Dhamma-wheel set rolling by you?”

mn92:19.13.verse: It’s hard often to gain sight of the Rightly Self-Awakened.

mn92:19.21.verse: I rejoice, with no fear from anywhere.”

mn92:20.2.verse: how he speaks, this One with Eyes;

mn92:20.4.verse: he roars like a lion in the forest.

mn92:20.7.verse: Who, on seeing him, would not have confidence,

mn92:20.8.verse: even one of a dark birth?

mn92:20.9.verse: Whoever wants to may follow me;

mn92:20.12.verse: in the presence of the one of foremost discernment.”

mn92:21.1.verse: “If, master, you thus delight in the message,

mn92:21.3.verse: we, too, will here go forth

mn92:21.4.verse: in the presence of the one of foremost discernment.”

mn92:22.2.verse: request, with hands palm-to-palm over the heart:

mn92:23.4.verse: where the Going-forth is not in vain

mn92:23.5.verse: for a heedful person who trains.”

mn92:24.1.verse: Then Sela the brahman, together with his following, obtained the Going-forth in the Blessed One’s presence, he obtained Acceptance.

mn92:25.1.verse: Then, as the night was ending, Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic, having had choice staple & non-staple foods prepared in his own ashram, announced the time to the Blessed One,

mn92:25.2.verse: “It is time, master Gotama. The meal is ready.”

mn92:25.3.verse: Then, early in the morning, the Blessed One—after adjusting his lower robe and carrying his bowl & outer robe—went together with a Saṅgha of monks to Keṇiya’s ashram. On arrival, he sat down on an arranged seat.

mn92:25.4.verse: Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic, with his own hand, served & satisfied the Blessed One & the Saṅgha of monks with choice staple & non-staple foods.

mn92:25.5.verse: Then, when the Blessed One had eaten and had rinsed his bowl & hands, Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic took a lower seat and sat to one side.

mn92:25.6.verse: As he was sitting there, the Blessed One expressed approval of him with these verses:

mn92:26.1.verse: “The fire oblation is the chief of sacrifices,

mn92:26.2.verse: the Sāvitti, the chief of Vedic hymns,

mn92:26.3.verse: a king, chief among human beings,

mn92:26.5.verse: The moon, chief of the zodiac stars,

mn92:26.6.verse: the sun, chief of things that burn,

mn92:26.7.verse: and for those who sacrifice, wishing for merit,

mn92:26.9.verse: Then, having expressed approval of Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic with these verses, the Blessed One got up from his seat and left.

mn92:27.1.verse: Then Ven. Sela, together with his following—dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, & resolute—in no long time reached & remained in the supreme goal of the holy life, for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness, knowing & realizing it for himself in the here-&-now.

mn92:27.2.verse: He knew: “Birth is ended, the holy life fulfilled, the task done. There is nothing further for the sake of this world.”

mn92:27.3.verse: And so Ven. Sela, together with his following, became another one of the arahants.

mn92:28.1.verse: Then Ven. Sela, together with his following, went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder and extending his hands palm-to-palm over the heart toward the Blessed One, addressed him in verse:

mn92:28.2.verse: “This is the eighth day since coming for refuge,

mn92:28.5.verse: we have tamed ourselves with your message.

mn92:28.7.verse: You : Sage who has conquered Māra;

mn92:28.9.verse: having crossed over, bring this generation across.

mn92:28.12.verse: you are a lion free of clinging,

mn92:28.15.verse: stand with hands palm-to-palm over the heart.

mn92:28.17.verse: the nāgas venerate them, the feet of the Teacher.”

mn92:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering in the country of the Anguttarāpans with a large Sangha of bhikkhus, with twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus. There is town of the Anguttarāpans called Apaṇa where the Blessed One eventually arrived.

mn92:2.2.verse: ‘The monk Gotama, it seems, the son of the Sakyans who went forth from a Sakyan clan, has been wandering in the country of the Anguttarāpans with a large Sangha of bhikkhus, with twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and he has come to Apaṇa.

mn92:2.3.verse: Now a good report of Master Gotama has been spread to this effect:

mn92:2.4.verse: “That Blessed One is such since he is Arahant, Fully Enlightened, perfect in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of worlds, incomparable leader of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and men, enlightened, blessed.”

mn92:2.5.verse: He describes this world with its gods, its Māras, and its (Brahmā) Divinities, this generation with its monks and divines, with its kings and its men, which he has himself realized through direct knowledge.

mn92:2.6.verse: He teaches a Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle and good in the end with (the right) meaning and phrasing, he affirms a life divine that is utterly perfect and pure.

mn92:2.7.verse: Now it is good to see such Arahants.’

mn92:3.1.verse: Then the matted-hair ascetic Keniya went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him,

mn92:3.2.verse: and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished he sat down at one side.

mn92:3.3.verse: When he had done so, the Blessed One instructed, urged, roused and encouraged him with talk on the Dhamma.

mn92:3.4.verse: Then delighting in the Blessed One’s words and agreeing, the matted-hair ascetic Keniya said to the Blessed One:

mn92:3.5.verse: ‘Let the Blessed One, together with the Sangha of bhikkhus, accept tomorrow’s meal from me.’

mn92:3.6.verse: When this was said, the Blessed One told him:

mn92:3.7.verse: ‘The Sangha of bhikkhus is large, Keniya, there are twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus and you place all your confidence in the divines.’

mn92:3.8.verse: A second time the matted-hair ascetic said to the Blessed One:

mn92:3.9.verse: ‘Although the Sangha of bhikkhus is large, Master Gotama, and there are twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and although I place all my confidence in the divines,

mn92:3.10.verse: still let the Blessed One, together with the Sangha of bhikkhus, accept tomorrow’s meal from me.’

mn92:3.11.verse: A second time the Blessed One told him:

mn92:3.12.verse: ‘The Sangha of bhikkhus is large, Keniya, there are twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus. And you place all your confidence in the divines.’

mn92:3.13.verse: A third time the matted-hair ascetic said to the Blessed One:

mn92:3.14.verse: ‘Although the Sangha of bhikkhus is large, Master Gotama, and there are twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and although I place all my confidence in the divines,

mn92:3.15.verse: still let the Blessed One, together with the Sangha of bhikkhus, accept tomorrow’s meal from me.’

mn92:3.16.verse: The Blessed One accepted in silence.

mn92:4.1.verse: Then, knowing that the Blessed One had accepted, he rose from his seat and went to his own hermitage where he addressed his friends and companions, relatives and kin:

mn92:4.2.verse: ‘Hear me, my friends and companions, relatives and kin;

mn92:4.3.verse: ‘The monk Gotama has been invited by me for tomorrow’s meal together with the Sangha of bhikkhus.

mn92:4.4.verse: Make the necessary purchases and preparations for me.’

mn92:4.5.verse: ‘Yes, sir,’ they replied, and some excavated ovens, some chopped wood, some washed dishes, some set out water pots, some prepared seats,

mn92:4.6.verse: while the matted-hair ascetic Keniya himself got ready a pavilion tent.

mn92:5.1.verse: Now on that occasion Sela of the divine caste was staying at Āpaṇa. An expert in the Three Vedas, he knew the text and context of the Histories, the fifth (of the divine authorities), with their invocations, liturgy, word-analysis, and he was fully versed in Natural Science and that of the Marks of the Great Man. He had three hundred divine-caste students to recite hymns.

mn92:6.1.verse: On that occasion the matted-hair ascetic Keniya placed all his confidence in Sela the divine.

mn92:6.2.verse: Then Sela of the divine caste, attended by three hundred divine-caste students, was walking and wandering for exercise, and he came to the matted-hair ascetic Keniya’s hermitage.

mn92:6.3.verse: He saw there some excavating ovens, some chopping wood, some washing dishes, some setting out water pots, some preparing seats, while the matted-hair ascetic Keniya himself was getting ready a pavilion tent.

mn92:7.1.verse: When he saw this, he asked the matted-hair ascetic Keniya:

mn92:7.2.verse: ‘What, is there a taking in marriage or a giving in marriage? Or is there some great sacrifice? Or has Seniya Bimbisāra king of Magadha been invited with a large retinue for tomorrow’s meal?’

mn92:8.1.verse: ‘I have no taking in marriage or giving in marriage, Sela; nor has Seniya Bimbisāra king of Magadha been invited with a large retinue for tomorrow’s meal.

mn92:8.2.verse: But I have a great sacrifice.

mn92:8.3.verse: The monk Gotama who went forth from the Sakyan clan has been wandering in the country of the Anguttarāpans with a large Sangha of bhikkhus, with twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and has come to Āpaṇa.

mn92:8.4.verse: Now a good report of Master Gotama has spread to this effect:

mn92:8.5.verse: “That Blessed One is such since he is Arahant, Fully Enlightened, perfect in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of worlds, incomparable leader of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and men, enlightened, blessed.”

mn92:8.6.verse: He has been invited by me for tomorrow’s meal, together with the Sangha of bhikhus.’

mn92:10.1.verse: Then it occurred to Sela of the divine caste:

mn92:10.2.verse: ‘This news “Enlightened One” is hard to get in the world.

mn92:10.3.verse: Now the thirty-two Marks of the Great Man have been handed down in our hymns, and the Great Man who is endowed with them has only two possible destinies, no other.

mn92:10.4.verse: If he lives the home life he becomes an ideal king of Dhamma, master of the four quarters, all-victorious, who has stabilized his country, and possesses seven treasures—

mn92:10.6.verse: the Wheel Treasure, the Elephant Treasure, the Horse Treasure, the Jewel Treasure, the Woman Tresure, the Householder Treasure, and the Steward Treasure as the seventh—

mn92:10.7.verse: his children who exceed a thousand, brave and heroic, crush the armies of others;

mn92:10.8.verse: over the earth bounded by this ocean he rules without a rod, without a weapon and in the Dhamma.

mn92:10.9.verse: But if he goes forth from the home life into homelessness, he becomes an Arahant, a Fully Enlightened One, who draws aside the veil in the world.’

mn92:11.1.verse: He said: ‘My good Keniya, where is Master Gotama, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, living now?’

mn92:11.2.verse: When this was said, the matted-hair ascetic Keniya extended his right arm and said:

mn92:11.3.verse: ‘There, where that green line (of trees) is, Master Sela.’

mn92:12.1.verse: Then Sela of the divine caste went with the three hundred divine-caste students to the Blessed One.

mn92:12.2.verse: Then he addressed the divine-caste students:

mn92:12.4.verse: for Blessed Ones are difficult of access, they walk alone like lions.

mn92:12.5.verse: And when I am in converse with the monk Gotama, let there be no interrupting me with talk meanwhile,

mn92:12.6.verse: but wait until our talk has been completed.’

mn92:13.1.verse: Then Sela of the divine caste went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him,

mn92:13.2.verse: and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished he sat down at one side.

mn92:13.3.verse: When had done so, he looked for the thirty-two Marks of the Great Man on the Blessed One’s body.

mn92:13.4.verse: He saw more or less, the thirty-two Marks of the Great Man on the Blessed One’s body, except for two;

mn92:13.5.verse: he was doubtful and uncertain about two of the marks, and he could not decide and make up his mind about them:

mn92:13.6.verse: about what should be hidden by a cloth being enclosed in a sheath, and about the largeness of the tongue.

mn92:13.7.verse: It occurred to the Blessed One:

mn92:13.8.verse: ‘This Sela of the divine caste sees, more or less, the thirty-two Marks of the Great Man on me, except for two;

mn92:13.9.verse: he is doubtful and uncertain about two of the marks, and he cannot decide and make up his mind about them:

mn92:13.10.verse: about what should be hidden by a cloth being enclosed in a sheath, and about the largeness of the tongue.’

mn92:14.1.verse: Then the Blessed One worked such a feat of supernormal success that Sela of the divine caste saw that in the Blessed One what should be hidden by a cloth was enclosed in a sheath.

mn92:14.2.verse: Then the Blessed One extended his tongue, and he repeatedly touched both earholes, both nostrils, and he covered the whole of his forehead with his tongue.

mn92:15.1.verse: Sela of the divine caste thought:

mn92:15.2.verse: ‘The monk Gotama is endowed with the thirty-two Marks of the Great Man, they are complete, not incomplete.

mn92:15.3.verse: But I do not know whether he is enlightened or not.

mn92:15.4.verse: However, I have heard from the elders, the aged divines, who preach according to the line of teachers,

mn92:15.5.verse: that those who are Arahant and Fully Enlightened manifest themselves as such when their praise is spoken.

mn92:15.6.verse: Suppose I eulogize the monk Gotama to his face with fitting stanzas?’

mn92:15.7.verse: Then he eulogized the Blessed One to his face with fitting stanzas:

mn92:16.2.verse: Well fashioned and good to behold;

mn92:16.3.verse: O Blessed One, golden thy colour,

mn92:16.4.verse: And white are thy teeth; thou art strong;

mn92:16.5.verse: For the features are there one and all

mn92:16.6.verse: That distinguish a man as well born;

mn92:16.7.verse: They are all to be found on thy body,

mn92:16.8.verse: These Marks that betray the Great Man.

mn92:16.9.verse: With eyes clear, with countenance bright,

mn92:16.11.verse: In the midst of this body of monks

mn92:16.12.verse: Thou shinest like unto the sun,

mn92:16.13.verse: A bhikkhu so lovely to look on

mn92:16.14.verse: With a skin of so golden a sheen—

mn92:27.2.verse: He knew directly: ‘Birth is exhausted, the life divine has been lived out, what was to be done is done, there is no more of this to come’.

mn92:27.3.verse: And the venerable Sela became one of the Arahants, together with his following.

mn92:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was wandering together with a large Saṅgha of 1,250 mendicants in the land of the Aṅguttarāpans when he arrived at a town of theirs named Āpaṇa.

mn92:2.2.verse: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—has arrived at Āpaṇa, together with a large Saṅgha of 1,250 mendicants.

mn92:2.4.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

mn92:2.5.verse: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

mn92:2.6.verse: He proclaims a teaching that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

mn92:2.7.verse: It’s good to see such perfected ones.”

mn92:3.1.verse: So Keṇiya approached the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

mn92:3.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side.

mn92:3.3.verse: The Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired him with a Dhamma talk.

mn92:3.4.verse: Then he said to the Buddha,

mn92:3.5.verse: “Would Worthy Gotama together with the mendicant Saṅgha please accept tomorrow’s meal from me?”

mn92:3.6.verse: When he said this, the Buddha said to him,

mn92:3.7.verse: “The Saṅgha is large, Keṇiya; there are 1,250 mendicants. And you are devoted to the brahmins.”

mn92:3.8.verse: For a second time, Keṇiya asked the Buddha to accept a meal offering.

mn92:3.9.verse: “Never mind that the Saṅgha is large, with 1,250 mendicants, and that I am devoted to the brahmins.

mn92:3.10.verse: Would Worthy Gotama together with the mendicant Saṅgha please accept tomorrow’s meal from me?”

mn92:3.11.verse: And for a second time, the Buddha gave the same reply.

mn92:3.13.verse: For a third time, Keṇiya asked the Buddha to accept a meal offering.

mn92:4.1.verse: Then, knowing that the Buddha had consented, Keṇiya rose from his seat and went to his own hermitage. There he addressed his friends and colleagues, relatives and kin,

mn92:4.2.verse: “My friends and colleagues, relatives and kin: please listen!

mn92:4.3.verse: The ascetic Gotama together with the mendicant Saṅgha has been invited by me for tomorrow’s meal.

mn92:4.4.verse: Please help me out with the manual preparations.”

mn92:4.5.verse: “Yes, worthy sir,” they replied. Some dug ovens, some chopped wood, some washed dishes, some set up a water jar, and some spread out seats.

mn92:4.6.verse: Meanwhile, Keṇiya set up the pavilion himself.

mn92:5.1.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Sela was residing in Āpaṇa. He had mastered the three Vedas, together with their vocabularies and ritual performance, their phonology and word classification, and the testaments as fifth. He knew them word-by-word, and their grammar. He was well versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man. And he was teaching three hundred young students to recite the hymns.

mn92:6.2.verse: Then Sela, while going for a walk escorted by the three hundred young students, approached Keṇiya’s hermitage.

mn92:8.1.verse: “There is no marriage, Worthy Sela, and the king is not coming.

mn92:10.2.verse: “It’s hard to even find the word ‘awakened one’ in the world.

mn92:10.3.verse: The thirty-two marks of a great man have been handed down in our hymns. A great man who possesses these has only two possible destinies, no other.

mn92:10.4.verse: If he stays at home he becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch, a just and principled king. His dominion extends to all four sides, he achieves stability in the country, and he possesses the seven treasures.

mn92:10.5.verse: He has the following seven treasures:

mn92:10.6.verse: the wheel, the elephant, the horse, the jewel, the woman, the householder, and the commander as the seventh treasure.

mn92:10.7.verse: He has over a thousand sons who are valiant and heroic, crushing the armies of his enemies.

mn92:10.8.verse: After conquering this land girt by sea, he reigns by principle, without rod or sword.

mn92:10.9.verse: But if he goes forth from the lay life to homelessness, he becomes a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, who casts off the veil from the world.”

mn92:14.2.verse: And he stuck out his tongue and stroked back and forth on his ear holes and nostrils, and covered his entire forehead with his tongue.

mn92:27.1.verse: Then Venerable Sela and his assembly, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. They lived having achieved with their own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

mn92:27.2.verse: They understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

mn92:27.3.verse: And Venerable Sela together with his assembly became perfected.
