mn93:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn93:2.1.verse: And on that occasion 500 brahmans from various provinces were staying at Sāvatthī on some business or other.

mn93:2.3.verse: “This Gotama the contemplative prescribes purity for the four castes.

mn93:2.4.verse: Now who is capable of disputing with him on this statement?”

mn93:3.1.verse: And on that occasion the brahman student Assalāyana was staying at Sāvatthī. Young, shaven-headed, sixteen years old, he was a master of the Three Vedas with their vocabularies, liturgy, phonology, etymology, & histories as a fifth; skilled in philology & grammar, he was fully versed in cosmology and in the marks of a Great Man.

mn93:3.2.verse: The thought occurred to the brahmans,

mn93:3.3.verse: “This brahman student Assalāyana is staying in Sāvatthī. Young, shaven-headed, sixteen years old, he was a master of the Three Vedas with their vocabularies, liturgy, phonology, etymology, & histories as a fifth; skilled in philology & grammar, he was fully versed in cosmology and in the marks of a Great Man.

mn93:3.4.verse: He is capable of disputing with Gotama the contemplative on this statement.”

mn93:4.1.verse: So the brahmans went to the brahman student Assalāyana and said to him,

mn93:4.2.verse: “Master Assalāyana, this Gotama the contemplative prescribes purity for the four castes.

mn93:4.3.verse: Come and dispute with him on this statement.”

mn93:4.4.verse: When this was said, the brahman student Assalāyana said to the brahmans,

mn93:4.5.verse: “Sirs, Gotama the contemplative is one who speaks Dhamma.

mn93:4.6.verse: And those who speak Dhamma are hard to dispute with.

mn93:4.7.verse: I can’t dispute with him on this statement.”

mn93:4.8.verse: A second time, the brahmans said to the brahman student Assalāyana,

mn93:4.9.verse: “Master Assalāyana, this Gotama the contemplative prescribes purity for the four castes.

mn93:4.10.verse: Come and dispute with him on this statement.

mn93:4.11.verse: For you have lived the life of a wanderer.”

mn93:4.12.verse: A second time the brahman student Assalāyana said to the brahmans,

mn93:4.13.verse: “Sirs, Gotama the contemplative is one who speaks Dhamma.

mn93:4.14.verse: And those who speak Dhamma are hard to dispute with.

mn93:4.15.verse: I can’t dispute with him on this statement.”

mn93:4.16.verse: A third time, the brahmans said to the brahman student Assalāyana,

mn93:4.17.verse: “Master Assalāyana, this Gotama the contemplative prescribes purity for the four castes.

mn93:4.18.verse: Come and dispute with him on this statement.

mn93:4.19.verse: For you have lived the life of a wanderer.

mn93:4.20.verse: Don’t be defeated without being defeated in battle.”

mn93:4.21.verse: When this was said, the brahman student Assalāyana said to the brahmans,

mn93:4.22.verse: “Apparently, sirs, I don’t get leave from you (to avoid the matter by saying),

mn93:4.23.verse: ‘Gotama the contemplative is one who speaks Dhamma.

mn93:4.24.verse: And those who speak Dhamma are hard to dispute with.

mn93:4.25.verse: I can’t dispute with him on this statement.’

mn93:4.26.verse: But at your bidding I will go.”

mn93:5.1.verse: Then the brahman student Assalāyana went with a large group of brahmans to the Blessed One and, on arrival, exchanged courteous greetings with him.

mn93:5.2.verse: After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, he sat to one side. As he was sitting there he said to the Blessed One:

mn93:5.4.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior.

mn93:5.5.verse: Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark.

mn93:5.6.verse: Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:5.7.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’

mn93:5.8.verse: What does Master Gotama have to say with regard to that?”

mn93:5.9.verse: “But, Assalāyana, the brahmans’ brahman-women are plainly seen having their periods, becoming pregnant, giving birth, and nursing (their children).

mn93:5.10.verse: And yet the brahmans, being born through the birth canal, say:

mn93:5.11.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior.

mn93:5.12.verse: Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark.

mn93:5.13.verse: Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:5.14.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’”

mn93:6.1.verse: “Even though Master Gotama says that, still the brahmans think,

mn93:6.2.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior. Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark. Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:6.3.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’”

mn93:6.5.verse: Have you heard that in Yona & Kamboja and other outlying countries there are only two castes—masters & slaves—and that having been a master one (can) become a slave, and that having been a slave one (can) become a master?”

mn93:6.6.verse: “Yes, Master Gotama. I have heard that in Yona & Kamboja and other outlying countries there are only two castes—masters & slaves—and that having been a master one can become a slave, and that having been a slave one can become a master.”

mn93:6.7.verse: “So what strength is there, Assalāyana, what assurance, when the brahmans say,

mn93:6.8.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior. Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark. Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:6.9.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā’?”

mn93:7.1.verse: “Even though Master Gotama says that, still the brahmans think,

mn93:7.2.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior. Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark. Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:7.3.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’”

mn93:7.5.verse: Is it only a noble warrior who—taking life, stealing, engaging in sexual misconduct, telling lies, speaking divisively, speaking harshly, engaging in idle chatter, greedy, bearing thoughts of ill will, and holding wrong views—on the break-up of the body, after death, reappears in a plane of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell, and not a brahman?

mn93:7.7.verse: Is it only a worker who—taking life, stealing, engaging in sexual misconduct, telling lies, speaking divisively, speaking harshly, engaging in idle chatter, greedy, bearing thoughts of ill will, and holding wrong views—on the break-up of the body, after death, reappears in a plane of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell, and not a brahman?”

mn93:7.9.verse: Even a noble warrior—taking life, stealing, engaging in sexual misconduct, telling lies, speaking divisively, speaking harshly, engaging in idle chatter, greedy, bearing thoughts of ill will, and holding wrong views—on the break-up of the body, after death, reappears in a plane of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell.

mn93:7.13.verse: (Members of) all four castes—if they take life, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, tell lies, speak divisively, speak harshly, engage in idle chatter, are greedy, bear thoughts of ill will, & hold wrong views—on the break-up of the body, after death, reappear in a plane of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell.”

mn93:7.14.verse: “So what strength is there, Assalāyana, what assurance, when the brahmans say,

mn93:7.15.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior. Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark. Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:7.16.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā’?”

mn93:8.1.verse: “Even though Master Gotama says that, still the brahmans think,

mn93:8.2.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior. Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark. Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:8.3.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’”

mn93:8.5.verse: Is it only a brahman who—refraining from taking life, from stealing, from sexual misconduct, from telling lies, from speaking divisive speech, from harsh speech, & from idle chatter, not greedy, bearing no thoughts of ill-will, & holding to right view—on the break-up of the body, after death, reappears in a good destination, a heavenly world, and not a noble warrior, not a merchant, not a worker?”

mn93:8.7.verse: Even a noble warrior—refraining from taking life, from stealing, from sexual misconduct, from telling lies, from speaking divisive speech, from harsh speech, & from idle chatter, not greedy, bearing no thoughts of ill-will, & holding to right view—on the break-up of the body, after death, reappears in a good destination, a heavenly world.

mn93:8.11.verse: (Members of) all four castes—if they refrain from taking life, from stealing, from sexual misconduct, from telling lies, from speaking divisive speech, from harsh speech, & from idle chatter, are not greedy, bear no thoughts of ill-will, & hold to right view—on the break-up of the body, after death, reappear in a good destination, a heavenly world.”

mn93:8.12.verse: “So what strength is there, Assalāyana, what assurance, when the brahmans say,

mn93:8.13.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior. Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark. Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:8.14.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā’?”

mn93:9.1.verse: “Even though Master Gotama says that, still the brahmans think,

mn93:9.2.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior. Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark. Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:9.3.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’”

mn93:9.5.verse: Is it only a brahman who is capable of developing in any direction a heart of good will—free from animosity, free from ill will—and not a noble warrior, not a merchant, not a worker?”

mn93:9.7.verse: Even a noble warrior is capable of developing in any direction a heart of good will—free from animosity, free from ill will;

mn93:9.11.verse: (Members of) all four castes are capable of developing in any direction a heart of good will—free from animosity, free from ill will.”

mn93:9.12.verse: “So what strength is there, Assalāyana, what assurance, when the brahmans say,

mn93:9.13.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior. Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark. Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:9.14.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā’?”

mn93:10.1.verse: “Even though Master Gotama says that, still the brahmans think,

mn93:10.2.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior. Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark. Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:10.3.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’”

mn93:10.5.verse: Is it only a brahman who is capable of taking a loofah & bath powder, going to a river, and scrubbing off dust & dirt, and not a noble warrior, not a merchant, not a worker?”

mn93:10.7.verse: Even a noble warrior is capable of taking a loofah & bath powder, going to a river, and scrubbing off dust & dirt. Even a brahman…

mn93:10.10.verse: (Members of) all four castes are capable of taking a loofah & bath powder, going to a river, and scrubbing off dust & dirt.”

mn93:10.11.verse: “So what strength is there, Assalāyana, what assurance, when the brahmans say,

mn93:10.12.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior. Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark. Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:10.13.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā’?”

mn93:11.1.verse: “Even though Master Gotama says that, still the brahmans think,

mn93:11.2.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior. Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark. Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:11.3.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’”

mn93:11.5.verse: There is the case where a consecrated noble warrior king might call together 100 men of different births (and say to them),

mn93:11.6.verse: ‘Come, masters. Those of you there born from a noble warrior clan, from a brahman clan, or from a royal clan: taking an upper fire-stick of Sal wood, salaḷa wood, sandalwood, or padumaka wood, produce fire & make heat appear.

mn93:11.7.verse: Come, masters. Those of you there born from an outcast clan, a trapper clan, a wicker workers’ clan, a cartwrights’ clan, or a scavengers’ clan: taking an upper fire-stick from a dog’s drinking trough, from a pig’s trough, from a dustbin, or of castor-oil wood, produce fire & make heat appear.’

mn93:11.9.verse: Would the fire made by those born from a noble warrior clan, a brahman clan, or a royal clan—who had produced fire & made heat appear by taking an upper fire-stick of Sal wood, salaḷa wood, sandalwood, or padumaka wood—be the only one with flame, color, & radiance, able to do whatever a fire might be needed to do?

mn93:11.10.verse: And would the fire made by those born from an outcast clan, a trapper clan, a wicker workers’ clan, a cartwrights’ clan, or a scavengers’ clan—who had produced fire & made heat appear by taking an upper fire-stick from a dog’s drinking trough, from a pig’s trough, from a dustbin, or of castor-oil wood—be without flame, color, & radiance, unable to do what a fire might be needed to do?”

mn93:11.12.verse: The fire made by those born from a noble warrior clan, a brahman clan, or a royal clan… would have flame, color, & radiance, able to do whatever a fire might be needed to do.

mn93:11.13.verse: And the fire made by those born from an outcast clan, a trapper clan, a wicker workers’ clan, a cartwrights’ clan, or a scavengers’ clan… would have flame, color, & radiance, able to do whatever a fire might be needed to do.

mn93:11.14.verse: For all fire has flame, color, & radiance, and is able to do whatever a fire might be needed to do.”

mn93:11.15.verse: “So what strength is there, Assalāyana, what assurance, when the brahmans say,

mn93:11.16.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior.

mn93:11.17.verse: Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark.

mn93:11.18.verse: Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:11.19.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā’?”

mn93:12.1.verse: “Even though Master Gotama says that, still the brahmans think,

mn93:12.2.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior. Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark. Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:12.3.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’”

mn93:12.5.verse: There is the case where a noble warrior youth might cohabit with a brahman maiden, and from their cohabitation a son would be born.

mn93:12.6.verse: Would the son born from the noble warrior youth and brahman maiden be like the father and like the mother? Should it be called a noble warrior & a brahman?”

mn93:12.7.verse: “The son born from the noble warrior youth and brahman maiden would be like the father and like the mother. He should be called a noble warrior & a brahman, Master Gotama.”

mn93:13.2.verse: There is the case where a brahman youth might cohabit with a noble warrior maiden, and from their cohabitation a son would be born.

mn93:13.3.verse: Would the son born from the brahman youth and noble warrior maiden be like the father and like the mother? Should it be called a noble warrior & a brahman?”

mn93:13.4.verse: “The son born from the brahman youth and noble warrior maiden would be like the father and like the mother. He should be called a noble warrior & a brahman, Master Gotama.”

mn93:14.2.verse: There is the case where a mare might mate with a donkey, and from their mating a foal would be born.

mn93:14.3.verse: Would the foal born from the mare & the donkey be like the father and like the mother? Should it be called a horse & a donkey?”

mn93:14.4.verse: “Master Gotama, from the mixed breeding it would be a mule.

mn93:14.5.verse: Here I see that it [the mixed breeding] makes a difference,

mn93:14.6.verse: but there [in the other two cases] I don’t see that it makes a difference.”

mn93:15.2.verse: There is the case where there might be two brahman-student brothers, born of the same mother: one learned & initiated, the other not learned & uninitiated.

mn93:15.3.verse: Which of the two would the brahmans serve first at a funeral feast, a milk-rice offering, a sacrifice, or a feast for guests?”

mn93:15.4.verse: “The brahman student who was learned & initiated—him would the brahmans serve first at a funeral feast, a milk-rice offering, a sacrifice, or a feast for guests, Master Gotama.

mn93:15.5.verse: For what great fruit would there be for what is given to one who is not learned & uninitiated?”

mn93:16.2.verse: There is the case where there might be two brahman-student brothers, born of the same mother: one learned & initiated (but) unvirtuous & of evil character, the other not learned & uninitiated, (but) virtuous & of fine character.

mn93:16.3.verse: Which of the two would the brahmans serve first at a funeral feast, a milk-rice offering, a sacrifice, or a feast for guests?”

mn93:16.4.verse: “The brahman student who was not learned & uninitiated, (but) virtuous & of fine character—him would the brahmans serve first at a funeral feast, a milk-rice offering, a sacrifice, or a feast for guests, Master Gotama.

mn93:16.5.verse: For what great fruit would there be for what is given to one who is unvirtuous & of evil character?”

mn93:17.2.verse: Then, having gone by birth, you went by mantras.

mn93:17.3.verse: Then, having gone by mantras, putting them both aside,

mn93:17.4.verse: you have come around to the purity of the four castes that I prescribe.”

mn93:17.5.verse: When this was said, the brahman student Assalāyana sat silent, abashed, his shoulders drooping, his head down, brooding, at a loss for words.

mn93:18.1.verse: Then the Blessed One—seeing that the brahman student Assalāyana was sitting silent, abashed, his shoulders drooping, his head down, brooding, at a loss for words—said to him,

mn93:18.2.verse: “Once, Assalāyana, this evil viewpoint arose in the seven brahman seers as they were consulting together in leaf huts in the wilderness:

mn93:18.3.verse: ‘Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior. Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark. Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:18.5.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’

mn93:18.6.verse: Then the seer Devala the Dark heard,

mn93:18.7.verse: ‘This evil viewpoint has arisen in the seven brahman seers as they are consulting together in leaf huts in the wilderness:

mn93:18.8.verse: Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior… Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:18.9.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’

mn93:18.10.verse: Then the seer Devala the Dark, arranging his hair & beard, putting on crimson garments, wearing multi-layered sandals, and carrying a staff made of gold, he appeared in the courtyard of the seven brahman seers.

mn93:18.11.verse: Then he walked back & forth in the courtyard of the seven brahman seers saying,

mn93:18.12.verse: “Well, now, where have these masters, the brahman seers, gone?

mn93:18.13.verse: Well, now, where have these masters, the brahman seers, gone?”

mn93:18.14.verse: Then the seven brahman seers said to the seer Devala the Dark,

mn93:18.15.verse: “Now who is this, walking back & forth in the courtyard of the seven brahman seers like a village lout, saying,

mn93:18.16.verse: ‘Well, now, where have these masters, the brahman seers, gone?

mn93:18.17.verse: Well, now, where have these masters, the brahman seers, gone?’

mn93:18.19.verse: So the seven brahman seers cursed the seer Devala the Dark:

mn93:18.22.verse: But the more they cursed him, the more beautiful, good-looking, & inspiring he became.

mn93:18.23.verse: Then the thought occurred to the seven brahman seers,

mn93:18.24.verse: ‘Our asceticism is in vain! Our holy-life is fruitless!

mn93:18.25.verse: For before, whenever we cursed anyone,

mn93:18.28.verse: But the more we curse this one, the more beautiful, good-looking, & inspiring he becomes!’”

mn93:18.29.verse: ‘Masters, your asceticism is not in vain, and your holy-life not fruitless.

mn93:18.30.verse: Please, masters, abandon your hatred toward me.’

mn93:18.31.verse: ‘We abandon our hatred toward you, master.

mn93:18.34.verse: of the seer Devala the Dark?’

mn93:18.37.verse: Then the seven brahman seers approached him to bow down to him,

mn93:18.39.verse: ‘I have heard that this evil viewpoint has arisen in the seven brahman seers as they are consulting together in leaf huts in the wilderness:

mn93:18.40.verse: “Brahmans are the superior caste; any other caste is inferior.

mn93:18.41.verse: Only brahmans are the fair caste; any other caste is dark.

mn93:18.42.verse: Only brahmans are pure, not non-brahmans.

mn93:18.43.verse: Only brahmans are the sons & offspring of Brahmā: born of his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’”

mn93:18.46.verse: if the mother who bore you went only with a brahman, and not with a non-brahman?’

mn93:18.49.verse: if the mothers of the mother who bore you—back seven generations of mothers—went only with brahmans, and not with non-brahmans?’

mn93:18.52.verse: if the father who sired you went only with a brahman woman, and not with a non-brahman woman?’

mn93:18.55.verse: if the fathers of the father who bore you—back seven generations of fathers—went only with brahman women, and not with non-brahman women?’

mn93:18.58.verse: how there is the descent of an embryo?’

mn93:18.60.verse: how there is the descent of an embryo.

mn93:18.61.verse: There is the case where the mother & father have come together, the mother is fertile, and a gandhabba [the being about to be reborn] is standing present. The coming together of these three is the descent of the embryo.’

mn93:18.63.verse: whether the gandhabba is a noble warrior, a brahman, a merchant, or a worker?’

mn93:18.67.verse: do you know who you are?’

mn93:18.69.verse: we don’t know who we are.’

mn93:18.70.verse: Now, Assalāyana, when those seven brahman seers couldn’t defend their own birth-statement when interrogated, pressed, & rebuked by the seer Devala the Dark,

mn93:18.71.verse: how can you now defend your own birth-statement when interrogated, pressed, & rebuked by me—you, their lineage holder, but not (the equal of) Puṇṇa, their ladle holder?”

mn93:19.1.verse: When this was said, the brahman student Assalāyana said to the Blessed One:

mn93:19.2.verse: “Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent! Just as if he were to place upright what was overturned, to reveal what was hidden, to show the way to one who was lost, or to carry a lamp into the dark so that those with eyes could see forms, in the same way has Master Gotama—through many lines of reasoning—made the Dhamma clear.

mn93:19.3.verse: I go to Master Gotama for refuge, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of monks. May Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone to him for refuge, from this day forward, for life.”

mn93:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn93:2.1.verse: Now at that time around five hundred brahmins from abroad were residing in Sāvatthī on some business.

mn93:2.3.verse: “This ascetic Gotama advocates purification for all four classes.

mn93:2.4.verse: Who is capable of debating with him about this?”

mn93:3.1.verse: Now at that time the student Assalāyana was residing in Sāvatthī. He was young, tonsured, and sixteen years old. He had mastered the three Vedas, together with their vocabularies and ritual performance, their phonology and word classification, and the testaments as fifth. He knew them word-by-word, and their grammar. He was well versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man.

mn93:3.4.verse: “This Assalāyana is capable of debating with the ascetic Gotama about this.”

mn93:4.1.verse: So they approached Assalāyana and said to him,

mn93:4.2.verse: “This ascetic Gotama advocates purification for all four classes.

mn93:4.3.verse: Please, worthy Assalāyana, debate with the ascetic Gotama about this.”

mn93:4.4.verse: When they said this, Assalāyana said to them,

mn93:4.5.verse: “They say that the ascetic Gotama is a speaker of principle.

mn93:4.6.verse: But speakers of principle are hard to debate.

mn93:4.7.verse: I’m not capable of debating with the ascetic Gotama about this.”

mn93:4.8.verse: For a second time, those brahmins said to him

mn93:4.9.verse: “This ascetic Gotama advocates purification for all four classes.

mn93:4.10.verse: Please, worthy Assalāyana, debate with the ascetic Gotama about this.

mn93:4.11.verse: For you have lived as a wanderer.”

mn93:4.12.verse: And for a second time, Assalāyana refused.

mn93:4.16.verse: For a third time, those brahmins said to him,

mn93:4.17.verse: “This ascetic Gotama advocates purification for all four classes.

mn93:4.18.verse: Please, worthy Assalāyana, debate with the ascetic Gotama about this.

mn93:4.19.verse: For you have lived as a wanderer.

mn93:4.20.verse: Don’t admit defeat before going into battle!”

mn93:4.21.verse: When they said this, Assalāyana said to them,

mn93:4.22.verse: “Clearly, worthy sirs, I’m not getting through to you when I say:

mn93:4.23.verse: ‘They say that the ascetic Gotama is a speaker of principle.

mn93:4.24.verse: But speakers of principle are hard to debate.

mn93:4.25.verse: I’m not capable of debating with the ascetic Gotama about this.’

mn93:4.26.verse: Nevertheless, I shall go at your bidding.”

mn93:5.1.verse: Then Assalāyana together with a large group of brahmins went to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

mn93:5.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

mn93:5.4.verse: ‘Only brahmins are the best class; other classes are inferior.

mn93:5.5.verse: Only brahmins are the light class; other classes are dark.

mn93:5.6.verse: Only brahmins are purified, not others.

mn93:5.7.verse: Only brahmins are the Divinity’s bosom sons, born from his mouth, born of the Divinity, created by the Divinity, heirs of the Divinity.’

mn93:5.8.verse: What do you say about this?”

mn93:5.9.verse: “But Assalāyana, brahmin women are seen menstruating, being pregnant, giving birth, and breastfeeding.

mn93:5.10.verse: Yet even though they’re born from a brahmin womb they say:

mn93:5.11.verse: ‘Only brahmins are the best class; other classes are inferior.

mn93:5.12.verse: Only brahmins are the light class; other classes are dark.

mn93:5.13.verse: Only brahmins are purified, not others.

mn93:5.14.verse: Only brahmins are the Divinity’s bosom sons, born from his mouth, born of the Divinity, created by the Divinity, heirs of the Divinity.’”

mn93:6.1.verse: “Even though you say this, still the brahmins maintain their belief.”

mn93:6.5.verse: Have you heard that in Greece and Persia and other foreign lands there are only two classes, masters and bonded servants; and that masters may become servants, and servants masters?”

mn93:6.7.verse: “Then what is the source of the brahmins’ certainty and forcefulness in this matter that they make this claim?”

mn93:7.1.verse: “Even though you say this, still the brahmins maintain their belief.”

mn93:7.5.verse: Suppose an aristocrat were to kill living creatures, steal, and commit sexual misconduct; to use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; and to be covetous, malicious, with wrong view. When their body breaks up, after death, they’d be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell. Would this happen only to an aristocrat, and not to a brahmin?

mn93:7.7.verse: or a menial were to act in the same way. Would that result befall only a peasant or a menial, and not to a brahmin?”

mn93:7.9.verse: If they acted the same way, the same result would befall an aristocrat, a brahmin, a peasant, or a menial.

mn93:7.13.verse: For if any of the four classes were to kill living creatures, steal, and commit sexual misconduct; to use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; and to be covetous, malicious, with wrong view, then, when their body breaks up, after death, they’d be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

mn93:7.14.verse: “Then what is the source of the brahmins’ certainty and forcefulness in this matter that they make this claim?”

mn93:8.1.verse: “Even though you say this, still the brahmins maintain their belief.”

mn93:8.5.verse: Suppose a brahmin were to refrain from killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; from using speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; and from covetousness, malice, and wrong view. When their body breaks up, after death, they’d be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm. Would this happen only to a brahmin, and not to an aristocrat, a peasant, or a menial?”

mn93:8.7.verse: If they acted the same way, the same result would befall an aristocrat, a brahmin, a peasant, or a menial.

mn93:8.11.verse: For if any of the four classes were to refrain from killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; from using speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; and from covetousness, malice, and wrong view, then, when their body breaks up, after death, they’d be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

mn93:8.12.verse: “Then what is the source of the brahmins’ certainty and forcefulness in this matter that they make this claim?”

mn93:9.1.verse: “Even though you say this, still the brahmins maintain their belief.”

mn93:9.5.verse: Is only a brahmin capable of developing a heart of love, free of enmity and ill will for this region, and not an aristocrat, peasant, or menial?”

mn93:9.7.verse: Aristocrats, brahmins, peasants, and menials can all do so.

mn93:9.11.verse: For all four classes are capable of developing a heart of love, free of enmity and ill will for this region.”

mn93:9.12.verse: “Then what is the source of the brahmins’ certainty and forcefulness in this matter that they make this claim?”

mn93:10.1.verse: “Even though you say this, still the brahmins maintain their belief.”

mn93:10.5.verse: Is only a brahmin capable of taking some bathing cleanser, going to the river, and rinsing off dust and dirt, and not an aristocrat, peasant, or menial?”

mn93:10.10.verse: All four classes are capable of doing this.”

mn93:10.11.verse: “Then what is the source of the brahmins’ certainty and forcefulness in this matter that they make this claim?”

mn93:11.1.verse: “Even though you say this, still the brahmins maintain their belief.”

mn93:11.5.verse: Suppose an anointed aristocratic king were to gather a hundred people of various births and say to them:

mn93:11.6.verse: ‘Please worthy sirs, let anyone here who was born in a family of aristocrats, brahmins, or chieftains take a drill-stick made of teak, sal, salaḷa, sandalwood, or cherry wood, light a fire and produce heat.

mn93:11.7.verse: And let anyone here who was born in a family of corpse-workers, hunters, bamboo-workers, chariot-makers, or scavengers take a drill-stick made from a mutt’s drinking trough, a pig’s trough, a dustbin, or castor-oil wood, light a fire and produce heat.’

mn93:11.9.verse: Would only the fire produced by the high class people with good quality wood have flames, color, and radiance, and be usable as fire,

mn93:11.10.verse: and not the fire produced by the low class people with poor quality wood?”

mn93:11.12.verse: The fire produced by the high class people with good quality wood would have flames, color, and radiance, and be usable as fire,

mn93:11.13.verse: and so would the fire produced by the low class people with poor quality wood.

mn93:11.14.verse: For all fire has flames, color, and radiance, and is usable as fire.”

mn93:11.15.verse: “Then what is the source of the brahmins’ certainty and forcefulness in this matter that they make this claim?”

mn93:12.1.verse: “Even though you say this, still the brahmins maintain their belief.”

mn93:12.5.verse: Suppose an aristocrat boy was to sleep with a brahmin girl, and they had a child.

mn93:12.6.verse: Would that child be called an aristocrat after the father or a brahmin after the mother?”

mn93:13.2.verse: Suppose a brahmin boy was to sleep with an aristocrat girl, and they had a child.

mn93:13.3.verse: Would that child be called an aristocrat after the mother or a brahmin after the father?”

mn93:14.2.verse: Suppose a mare were to couple with a donkey, and she gave birth to a mule.

mn93:14.3.verse: Would that mule be called a horse after the mother or a donkey after the father?”

mn93:14.4.verse: “It’s a mule, as it is a crossbreed.

mn93:14.5.verse: I see the difference in this case,

mn93:14.6.verse: but not in the previous cases.”

mn93:15.2.verse: Suppose there were two young students who were brothers who had shared a womb. One was an educated reciter, while the other was not an educated reciter.

mn93:15.3.verse: Who would the brahmins feed first at an offering of food for ancestors, an offering of a dish of milk-rice, a sacrifice, or a feast for guests?”

mn93:15.4.verse: “They’d first feed the young student who was an educated reciter.

mn93:15.5.verse: For how could an offering to someone who is not an educated reciter be very fruitful?”

mn93:16.2.verse: Suppose there were two young students who were brothers who had shared a womb. One was an educated reciter, but was unethical, of bad character, while the other was not an educated reciter, but was ethical and of good character.

mn93:16.3.verse: Who would the brahmins feed first?”

mn93:16.4.verse: “They’d first feed the young student who was not an educated reciter, but was ethical and of good character.

mn93:16.5.verse: For how could an offering to someone who is unethical and of bad character be very fruitful?”

mn93:17.3.verse: then you switched to abstemious behavior.

mn93:17.4.verse: Now you’ve come around to believing in purification for the four classes, just as I advocate.”

mn93:17.5.verse: When he said this, Assalāyana sat silent, dismayed, shoulders drooping, downcast, depressed, with nothing to say.

mn93:18.1.verse: Knowing this, the Buddha said to him:

mn93:18.2.verse: “Once upon a time, Assalāyana, seven brahmin seers settled in leaf huts in a wilderness region. They had the following harmful misconception:

mn93:18.3.verse: ‘Only brahmins are the best class; other classes are inferior.

mn93:18.4.verse: Only brahmins are the light class; other classes are dark. Only brahmins are purified, not others.

mn93:18.5.verse: Only brahmins are the Divinity’s bosom sons, born from his mouth, born of the Divinity, created by the Divinity, heirs of the Divinity.’

mn93:18.6.verse: The seer Devala the Dark heard about this.

mn93:18.10.verse: So he did up his hair and beard, dressed in magenta robes, put on his lined sandals, grasped a golden staff, and appeared in the courtyard of the seven brahmin seers.

mn93:18.11.verse: Then he wandered about the yard saying,

mn93:18.12.verse: ‘Where, oh where have those brahmin seers gone?

mn93:18.13.verse: Where, oh where have those brahmin seers gone?’

mn93:18.15.verse: ‘Who’s this wandering about our courtyard like a village lout?

mn93:18.19.verse: So they cursed Devala the Dark,

mn93:18.22.verse: But the more the seers cursed him, the more attractive, good-looking, and lovely Devala the Dark became.

mn93:18.24.verse: ‘Our fervor is in vain! Our spiritual path is fruitless!

mn93:18.25.verse: For when we used to curse someone

mn93:18.28.verse: But the more we curse this one, the more attractive, good-looking, and lovely he becomes.’

mn93:18.29.verse: ‘Worthy sirs, your fervor is not in vain; your spiritual path is not fruitless.

mn93:18.30.verse: Please let go of your malevolence toward me.’

mn93:18.31.verse: ‘We let go of our malevolence toward you.

mn93:18.32.verse: But who are you, worthy sir?’

mn93:18.37.verse: Then they approached Devala and bowed to him.

mn93:18.39.verse: ‘I heard that when the seven brahmin seers had settled in leaf huts in a wilderness region, they had the following harmful misconception:

mn93:18.40.verse: “Only brahmins are the best class; other classes are inferior.

mn93:18.41.verse: Only brahmins are the light class; other classes are dark.

mn93:18.42.verse: Only brahmins are purified, not others.

mn93:18.43.verse: Only brahmins are the Divinity’s bosom sons, born from his mouth, born of the Divinity, created by the Divinity, heirs of the Divinity.”’

mn93:18.49.verse: whether your birth mother’s mothers back to the seventh generation only had relations with brahmins and not with non-brahmins?’

mn93:18.52.verse: whether your birth father only had relations with a brahmin woman and not with a non-brahmin?’

mn93:18.55.verse: whether your birth father’s fathers back to the seventh generation only had relations with brahmins and not with non-brahmins?’

mn93:18.63.verse: for sure whether that virile spirit is an aristocrat, a brahmin, a peasant, or a menial?’

mn93:18.68.verse: ‘In that case, worthy sir, we don’t know

mn93:18.70.verse: Given that even those seven brahmin seers could not prevail when pursued, pressed, and grilled by the seer Devala on their own genealogy,

mn93:18.71.verse: how could you prevail now being grilled by me on your own genealogy when you and your denomination do not so much as pick up the last spoonful?”

mn93:19.1.verse: When he had spoken, Assalāyana said to him,

mn93:19.3.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

mn94:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Venerable Udena was living at Benares in the Khemiya Mango Grove.

mn94:2.1.verse: Now on that occasion Ghotamukha of the divine caste had arrived at Benares for some business or other.

mn94:2.2.verse: As he was walking and wandering for exercise he came to the Khemiya Mango Grove.

mn94:2.3.verse: And on that occasion the Venerable Udena was walking up and down in the open.

mn94:2.4.verse: Then Ghoṭamukha of the divine caste went up to him and exchanged greetings with him.

mn94:2.5.verse: Then when the courteous and amiable talk was finished, still walking up and down with the Venerable Udena, he said this:

mn94:2.6.verse: ‘Worthy monk, there is no true wandering:

mn94:2.7.verse: that is how it appears to me in this case.

mn94:2.8.verse: And that is either owing to (my) not seeing those such as your goodselves, or else it is (owing to not seeing that) which is the Dhamma here.’

mn94:3.1.verse: When this was said, the Venerable Udena stepped down from the walk and went into his dwelling, where he sat down on a seat made ready.

mn94:3.2.verse: And Ghoṭamukha too stepped down from the walk and went into the dwelling, where he stood at one side.

mn94:3.3.verse: Then the Venerable Udena said to him:

mn94:3.6.verse: ‘We did not sit down because we were waiting for Master Udena (to speak);

mn94:3.7.verse: for how should one like me presume to sit down on a seat uninvited?’

mn94:4.1.verse: Then he took a low seat and sat down at one side.

mn94:4.2.verse: When he had done so, he said:

mn94:4.3.verse: ‘Worthy monk, there is no true wandering:

mn94:4.4.verse: that is how it appears to me in this case.

mn94:4.5.verse: And that is either owing to (my) not seeing those such as your good selves, or else it is (owing to not seeing that) which is the Dhamma here.’

mn94:4.6.verse: ‘Divine, if you think any statement of mine is to be agreed with, then agree with it; if you think any statement is to be argued against, argue against (it); and if you should not know the meaning of any statement of mine, ask me more about it thus:

mn94:4.7.verse: “This was the statement, Master Udena; what is its meaning?” In this way there can be conversation between us on this matter.’

mn94:4.8.verse: ‘Master Udena, if I think any statement of Master Udena’s is to be agreed with, I shall agree with it; if I think any statement is to be argued against, I shall argue it; and if I should not know the meaning of any statement of Master Udena’s I shall ask Master Udena more about it thus: “This was the statement Master Udena; what is its meaning?” In this way let there be conversation between us on this matter.’

mn94:5.1.verse: ‘Divine, there are four kinds of persons to be found existing in the world.

mn94:5.3.verse: Here a certain kind of person torments himself being interested in self-torture.

mn94:5.4.verse: ‘Here a certain kind of person torments others, being interested in torturing others.

mn94:5.5.verse: ‘Here a certain kind of person torments himself, being interested in self-torture, and he torments others, being interested in torturing others.

mn94:5.6.verse: ‘Here a certain kind of person does not torment himself, not being interested in self-torture, nor does he torment others, not being interested in torturing others;

mn94:5.7.verse: since he torments neither himself nor others he is here and now unparched extinguished, cooled, he abides experiencing pleasure as one become divine in himself.

mn94:5.8.verse: ‘Which of these four kinds of person commends itself to your mind, divine?’

mn94:5.9.verse: ‘The kind of person who torments himself, being interested in self-torture, does not commend itself to my mind, Venerable sir;

mn94:5.10.verse: the kind of person who torments others, being interested in torturing others, does not commend itself to my mind;

mn94:5.11.verse: the kind of person who torments himself, being interested in self-torture, and torments others, being interested in torturing others, does not commend itself to my mind;

mn94:5.12.verse: but the kind of person who does not torment himself, not being interested in self-torture, and does not torment others, not being interested in torturing others—who, since he torments neither himself nor others, is here and now unparched, extinguished, cooled, and having become divine in himself abides experiencing pleasure—

mn94:5.13.verse: that very kind of person commends itself to my mind.’

mn94:6.1.verse: ‘But, divine why do these three kinds of persons not commend themselves to your mind?’

mn94:6.2.verse: ‘Venerable sir, the kind of person who torments himself, being interested in self-torments and tortures his own self which desires pleasure and recoils from pain;

mn94:6.3.verse: that is why that kind of person does not commend itself to my mind.

mn94:6.4.verse: And the kind of person who torments others, being interested in torturing others, torments and tortures another who desires pleasure and recoils from pain;

mn94:6.5.verse: that is why that kind of person does not commend itself to my mind.

mn94:6.6.verse: And the third kind of person who torments himself, being interested in self-torture, and torments others, being interested in torturing others, both of them desiring pleasure and recoiling from pain;

mn94:6.7.verse: that is why that kind of person does not commend itself to my mind.

mn94:6.8.verse: But the kind of person who does not torment himself, not being interested in self-torture, and does not torment others, not being interested in torturing others, since he torments neither himself nor others, he is here and now unparched, extinguished, cooled, and having become divine in himself he abides experiencing pleasure.

mn94:6.9.verse: That is why that kind of person commends itself to my mind.’

mn94:7.1.verse: ‘Divine, there are two kinds of assembly.

mn94:7.3.verse: Here a certain assembly lusts greatly after jewels and earrings, seeks bondsmen and bondswomen, seeks fields and land, seeks gold and silver.

mn94:7.4.verse: But here a certain assembly does not lust at all after jewels and earrings, but abandoning wife and children, abandoning bondsmen and bondswomen, abandoning fields and land, abandoning gold and silver, it has gone forth from home life to homelessness.

mn94:7.5.verse: Now there is this kind of person who neither torments himself, not being interested in self-torture, nor torments others, not being interested in torturing others;

mn94:7.6.verse: who, since he torments neither himself nor others, is here and now unparched, extinguished, cooled, and having become divine in himself, he abides experiencing pleasure.

mn94:7.7.verse: In which of the two kinds of assembly do you see this kind of person most often, divine—

mn94:7.8.verse: the assembly that lusts greatly after jewels and earrings, seeks bondsmen and bondswomen, seeks fields and land, seeks gold and silver, or the assembly that does not lust at all after jewels and earrings, but abandoning wife and children, abandoning bondsmen and bondswomen, abandoning fields and land, abandoning gold and silver, has gone forth from home life to homelessness?’

mn94:7.9.verse: ‘The kind of person who neither torments himself, not being interested in self-torture, nor torments others, not being interested in torturing others, who, since he torments neither himself nor others, is here and now unparched, extinguished, cooled, and having become divine in himself abides experiencing pleasure—

mn94:7.10.verse: I see this kind of person most often in the second kind of assembly, Master Udena.’

mn94:8.1.verse: ‘But only just now, divine, we understood you to say:

mn94:8.2.verse: ‘Worthy monk, there is no true wandering:

mn94:8.3.verse: that is how it appears to me in this case.

mn94:8.4.verse: And that is either owing to (my) not seeing those such as your good-selves, or else it is (owing to not seeing that) which is Dhamma here”.’

mn94:8.5.verse: ‘Certainly, Master Udena, it was in order to learn, in fact, that that statement was made by me.

mn94:8.7.verse: that is how it appears to me in this case,

mn94:8.8.verse: and may Master Udena remember me (to have spoken) thus.

mn94:8.9.verse: And now it would be good if out of compassion Master Udena would expound in detail those four kinds of persons which he mentioned in brief without expounding them in detail.’

mn94:9.1.verse: ‘Then, divine, listen and attend carefully to what I shall say.’

mn94:10.1.verse: ‘Divine, what is the kind of person who torments himself, being interested in self-torture?

mn94:10.2.verse: Here a certain person goes naked, rejecting conventions, licking his hands, not coming when asked, not stopping when asked; he does not accept a thing brought or a thing specially made or an invitation;

mn94:10.3.verse: he receives nothing from out of a pot, from out of a bowl, across a threshold, across a stick, across a pestle, from two eating together, from a woman with child, from a woman giving suck, from (where) a woman was lying with a man, from where food was advertized to be distributed, from where a dog was waiting, from where flies were buzzing; he accepts no fish or meat, he drinks no liquor, wine or besotting drink;

mn94:10.4.verse: he keeps to one house, to one morsel; he keeps to two houses, to two morsels … he keeps to seven houses, to seven morsels.

mn94:10.5.verse: He lives on one saucerful, on two saucerfuls … on seven saucerfuls, a day;

mn94:10.6.verse: he takes food once a day, once each two days … once each seven days, and so, up to once each fortnight. He dwells pursuing the practice of taking food at stated intervals.

mn94:10.7.verse: He is an eater of greens, or millet, or wild rice, or hide-parings, or moss, or ricebran, or rinsings, or sesamum flour, or grass, or cowdung; he lives on forest roots and on fruits as a feeder on windfalls.

mn94:10.8.verse: He clothes himself in hemp, in hemp mixed cloth, in shrouds, in refuse rags, in tree bark, in antelope hide, in kusa-grass fabric, in bark fabric, in wood (shavings) fabric, in head-hair wool, in animal wool, in owls’ wings.

mn94:10.9.verse: He is one who pulls out hair and beard, pursuing the practice of pulling out hair and beard.

mn94:10.10.verse: He is one who stands continuously, rejecting seats.

mn94:10.11.verse: He is one who squats continuously, devoted to maintaining the squatting position.

mn94:10.12.verse: He is one who uses a mattress of spikes; he makes a mattress of spikes his bed.

mn94:10.13.verse: He dwells pursuing the practice of bathing in water for the third time by nightfall.

mn94:10.14.verse: In fact he dwells pursuing the practice of torment and torture of the body in its main aspects.

mn94:10.15.verse: This is called the kind of person who torments himself, being interested in self-torture.

mn94:11.1.verse: ‘What kind of person torments others, being interested in torturing others?

mn94:11.2.verse: Here a certain person is a butcher of sheep, a butcher of pigs, a fowler, a trapper of wild beasts, a hunter, a fisher, an executioner of felons, a prison warder, or follows any other such bloody occupation.

mn94:11.3.verse: This is called the kind of person who torments others, being interested in torturing others.

mn94:12.1.verse: ‘What is the kind of person who torments himself, being interested in self-torture, and torments others, being interested in torturing others?

mn94:12.2.verse: Here some person is a head-anointed warrior noble, king, or a divine of great property.

mn94:12.3.verse: He has a new sacrificial temple made to the east of the city, and having shaved off his hair and beard, dressed himself in rough hide and greased his body with ghee and oil, scratching his back with a deer’s horn, he enters the sacrificial temple together with his chief queen and his high priest of the divine caste.

mn94:12.4.verse: There he lies down on the bare ground with the grass on it.

mn94:12.5.verse: The king uses any milk there is in the first teat of a cow with a calf of the same colour while the chief queen uses any milk in the second teat, and the divine high priest uses any milk in the third teat, and milk in the fourth teat they pour onto the fire: the calf uses what is left.

mn94:12.7.verse: “Let so many bulls be slaughtered for sacrifice, let so many bullocks be slaughtered for sacrifice, let so many heifers be slaughtered for sacrifice, let so many goats be slaughtered for sacrifice, let so many sheep be slaughtered for sacrifice, let so many trees be felled for the sacrificial posts, let so much grass be cut for the sacrificial grass.”

mn94:12.8.verse: And then his slaves and messengers and servants make preparations with tearful faces and weeping, being spurred on by threats of punishment and by fear.

mn94:12.9.verse: This is called the kind of person who torments himself, being interested in self-torture, and torments others, being interested in torturing others.

mn94:13.1.verse: ‘What kind of person does not torment himself, not being interested in self-torture, and does not torment others, not being interested in torturing others,

mn94:13.2.verse: who since he torments neither himself nor others, is here and now unparched, extinguished, cooled and abides experiencing pleasure having become divine in himself?

mn94:14.1.verse: ‘Here, a Tathāgata appears in the world, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, perfect in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of worlds, incomparable leader of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and men, enlightened, blessed.

mn94:14.2.verse: ‘He declares this world with its gods, its Māras and its (Brahmā) Divinities, this generation with its monks and divines, with its kings and men, which he has himself realized by direct knowledge.

mn94:14.3.verse: ‘He teaches Dhamma good in the beginning, good in the middle and good in the end, with (the right) meaning and phrasing, and he announces a life divine that is utterly perfect and pure.

mn94:15.1.verse: ‘A householder or householder’s son or one born in some clan hears that Dhamma.

mn94:15.2.verse: On hearing the Dhamma he acquires faith in the Tathāgata.

mn94:15.3.verse: Possessing that faith, he considers thus:

mn94:15.4.verse: “House life is crowded and dirty; life gone forth is wide open.

mn94:15.5.verse: It is not possible, living in a household, to lead a life divine as utterly perfect and pure as a polished shell.

mn94:15.6.verse: Suppose I shaved off hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and went forth from the home life into homelessness?”

mn94:15.7.verse: ‘And on another occasion, abandoning perhaps a small, perhaps a large fortune, abandoning perhaps a small, perhaps a large circle of relatives, he shaves off hair and beard, puts on the yellow cloth, and goes forth from the home life into homelessness.

mn94:15.8.verse: ‘Being thus gone forth and possessing the bhikkhus’ training and way of life, abandoning killing living beings, he becomes one who abstains from killing living beings; with rod and weapon laid aside, gentle and kindly, he abides compassionate to all beings.

mn94:16.1.verse: ‘Abandoning taking what is not given, he becomes one who abstains from taking what is not given; taking (only) what is given, expecting (only) what is given, he abides pure in himself by not stealing.

mn94:16.2.verse: ‘Abandoning what is not the life divine, he becomes one who lives the life divine, who lives apart, abstaining from vulgar lechery.

mn94:16.3.verse: ‘Abandoning false speech, he becomes one who abstains from false speech, he speaks truth, cleaves to truth, is trust-worthy, reliable and undeceiving of the world.

mn94:16.4.verse: ‘Abandoning malicious speech, he becomes one who abstains from malicious speech: as one who is neither a repeater elsewhere of what is heard here for the purpose of causing division from these, nor a repeater to these of what is heard elsewhere for the purpose of causing division from those, who is thus a reuniter of the divided, a promoter of friendships, and enjoying concord, rejoicing in concord, delighting in concord, he becomes a speaker of words that promote concord.

mn94:16.5.verse: ‘Abandoning harsh speech, he becomes one who abstains from harsh speech; he becomes a speaker of such words as are innocent, pleasing to the ear and lovable, as go to the heart, are civil, desired of many and dear to many.

mn94:16.6.verse: ‘Abandoning gossip, he becomes one who abstains from gossip: as one who tells in season what is true and beneficial and the Dhamma and Discipline, he becomes a speaker of timely words, worth recalling, reasoned, measured and connected with good.

mn94:16.7.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from injuring seeds and plants.

mn94:16.8.verse: ‘He becomes one who eats in only one part of the day, refusing (food) at night and late meals.

mn94:16.9.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from dancing, singing, music and theatrical shows.

mn94:16.10.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from wearing of garlands, smartening with scent and embellishment with unguents.

mn94:16.11.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from high and large couches.

mn94:16.12.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting gold and silver.

mn94:16.13.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting raw corn.

mn94:16.14.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting raw meat.

mn94:16.15.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting women and girls.

mn94:16.16.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting bondwomen and bondmen.

mn94:16.17.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting sheep and goats.

mn94:16.18.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting fowl and pigs.

mn94:16.19.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting, elephants, cattle, horses and mares.

mn94:16.20.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from accepting fields and lands.

mn94:16.21.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from going on errands.

mn94:16.22.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from buying and selling.

mn94:16.23.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from false weights, false metal and false measures.

mn94:16.24.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from cheating, deceiving, defrauding and trickery.

mn94:16.25.verse: ‘He becomes one who abstains from wounding, murdering, binding, brigandage, plunder and violence.

mn94:17.1.verse: ‘He becomes one who is content with robes to keep the body, with alms-food to keep the belly: wherever he goes he takes all with him.

mn94:17.2.verse: Just as wherever a winged bird flies it flies using its own wings,

mn94:17.3.verse: so too he becomes one who is content with robes to keep the body, with alms-food to keep the belly: wherever he goes he takes all with him.

mn94:17.4.verse: ‘Possessing this store of Noble Ones’ virtue, he feels in himself pleasure that is blameless.

mn94:18.1.verse: ‘He becomes one who, on seeing a visible form with the eye, apprehends no signs and features through which, if he left the eye faculty unguarded, evil unprofitable dhammas of covetousness and grief might invade him.

mn94:18.2.verse: He practises the way of restraint, he guards the eye faculty, undertakes the restraint of the eye faculty.

mn94:18.3.verse: On hearing a sound with the ear …

mn94:18.4.verse: On smelling an odour with the nose …

mn94:18.5.verse: On tasting a flavour with the tongue …

mn94:18.6.verse: On touching a tangible with the body …

mn94:18.7.verse: On cognizing a dhamma with the mind, he apprehends no signs and features through which, if he left the mind faculty unguarded, evil unprofitable dhammas of covetousness and grief might invade him.

mn94:18.8.verse: He practises the way of restraint, he guards the mind faculty, undertakes the restraint of the mind faculty.

mn94:18.9.verse: ‘Possessing this Noble Ones’ faculty restraint, he feels in himself pleasure that is blameless.

mn94:19.1.verse: ‘He becomes one who acts in full awareness when, moving forward and moving backward, who acts in full awareness when looking towards and looking away, who acts in full awareness when flexing and extending, who acts in full awareness when wearing the patched cloak, robes and bowl, who acts in full awareness when eating, drinking, chewing and tasting, who acts in full awareness when evacuating the bowels and making water, who acts in full awareness when walking, standing, sitting, waking up, talking and keeping silent.

mn94:20.1.verse: Possessing this store of the Noble Ones’ virtue, and possessing this Noble Ones’ faculty restraint, and possessing this Noble Ones’ mindfulness and full awareness,

mn94:20.2.verse: he resorts to a secluded resting-place—to the forest, a tree-root, a rock, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a woodland solitude, an open space, a heap of straw.

mn94:21.1.verse: On return from his alms-round after the meal, he sits down, folding his legs crosswise, setting his body erect, establishing mindfulness before him.

mn94:21.2.verse: Abandoning covetousness for the world, he abides with a mind free from covetousness; he purifies mind from covetousness.

mn94:21.3.verse: Abandoning ill-will and hatred, he abides without a mind of ill-will, compassionate for the welfare of all living beings; he purifies mind from ill-will and hatred.

mn94:21.4.verse: Abandoning lethargy and drowsiness, he abides with a mind free from lethargy and drowsiness, percipient of light, mindful and fully aware; he purifies mind from lethargy and drowsiness.

mn94:21.5.verse: Abandoning agitation and worry, he abides unagitated with a mind stilled in himself; he purifies mind from agitation and worry.

mn94:21.6.verse: Abandoning uncertainty, he abides with a mind crossed beyond uncertainty, unquestioning about profitable dhammas; he purifies mind from uncertainty.

mn94:22.1.verse: Having abandoned these five hindrances, defilements of the mind that weaken understanding,

mn94:22.2.verse: quite secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unprofitable dhammas, he enters upon and abides in the first jhāna which is accompanied by initial application and sustained application, with happiness and (bodily) pleasure born of seclusion.

mn94:23.1.verse: With the stilling of initial application and sustained application, he enters upon and abides in the second jhāna which has self-confidence and singleness of mind and is without initial application and sustained application, with happiness and (bodily) pleasure born of concentration.

mn94:24.1.verse: With the fading away of happiness as well, he abides in equanimity, mindful and fully aware, still feeling pleasure with the body, he enters upon and abides in the third jhāna, on account of which Noble Ones announce: ‘He has a pleasant abiding who has equanimity and is mindful.’

mn94:25.1.verse: With the abandoning of (bodily) pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of (mental) joy and grief, he enters upon and abides in the fourth jhāna which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.

mn94:26.1.verse: When his concentrated mind is thus purified, bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs, he inclines the mind to knowledge of the recollection of past life,

mn94:26.2.verse: that is to say, one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many aeons of (world) contraction, many aeons of (world) expansion, many aeons of (world) contraction and expansion: There he was so named, of such a race, with such (qualities of) appearance, such was his nutriment, such his experience of pleasure and pain, such his life-term; and passing away from there, he appeared elsewhere; and there too he was so-named, of such a race, with such (qualities of) appearance, such was his nutriment, such his experience of pleasure and pain, such his life-term; and passing away from there he appeared here. Thus with details and particulars he recollects his manifold past life.

mn94:27.1.verse: When his concentrated mind is thus purified, bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs, he inclines the mind to knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings.

mn94:27.2.verse: With the heavenly eyesight which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, well-behaved and ill-behaved; he understands how beings pass on according to their kammas, thus: “These worthy beings who are ill-conducted in body, speech and mind, revilers of Noble Ones, wrong in their views, giving effect to wrong view in their kammas (actions), have, on the dissolution of the body, after death, appeared in a state of deprivation, in perdition, even in hell; but these worthy beings, who are well-conducted in body, speech and mind, not revilers of Noble Ones, right in their views, giving effect to right view in their kammas (actions), have, on the dissolution of the body, after death, appeared in a good destination, even in the heavenly world”, thus with heavenly eyesight which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, well-behaved and ill-behaved. He understands how beings pass on according to their kamma.

mn94:28.1.verse: When his concentrated mind is thus purified and bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, and become malleable, wieldy, steady and attained to unperturbability, he directs, he inclines the mind to knowledge of exhaustion of taints.

mn94:28.2.verse: He has direct knowledge thus: “This is suffering”; he has direct knowledge thus: “This is the origin of suffering”; he has direct knowledge thus: “This is the cessation of suffering”; he has direct knowledge thus: “This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.”

mn94:28.3.verse: He has direct knowledge thus: “These are taints”; he has direct knowledge thus: “This is the origin of taints”; he has direct knowledge thus: “This is the cessation of taints”; he has direct knowledge thus: “This is the way leading to the cessation of taints”.

mn94:29.1.verse: When he knows and sees thus, the mind is liberated from the taints of sensual desire, from the taints of being and from the taints of ignorance.

mn94:29.2.verse: When liberated there comes the knowledge: “It is liberated”.

mn94:29.3.verse: He has direct knowledge thus: “Birth is exhausted, the life divine has been lived out, what can be done is done. There is no more of this to come.”’

mn94:30.1.verse: ‘This is called the kind of person who does not torment himself, not being interested in self torture, and does not torment others, not being interested in torturing others,

mn94:30.2.verse: who since he torments neither himself nor others, is here and now unparched, extinguished, cooled, who, become divine in himself, abides experiencing pleasure.’

mn94:31.1.verse: When this was said, Ghoṭamukha of the divine caste said to the Venerable Udena:

mn94:31.3.verse: The Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Udena as though he were righting the overthrown, revealing the hidden, showing the way to one who is lost, holding up a lamp in the dark for those with eyesight to see forms.

mn94:31.4.verse: I go to Master Udena for refuge and to the Dhamma and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.

mn94:31.5.verse: From today let Master Udena remember me as a follower who has gone for refuge for life.’

mn94:32.1.verse: ‘Do not go to me for refuge, divine.

mn94:32.2.verse: Go for refuge to that same Blessed One to whom I go for refuge.’

mn94:32.3.verse: ‘Where is he living now, that Blessed One, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, Master Udena?’

mn94:32.4.verse: ‘That Blessed One, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, has attained the final Nibbāna now, divine.’

mn94:32.5.verse: ‘If we heard that that Blessed One was within ten leagues, we would go ten leagues in order to see that Blessed One, Arahant and Fully Enlightened.

mn94:32.6.verse: If we heard that that Blessed One was within twenty …

mn94:32.9.verse: fifty leagues, we would go fifty leagues in order to see that Blessed One, Arahant and Fully Enlightened.

mn94:32.10.verse: a hundred leagues, we would go a hundred leagues in order to see that Blessed One, Arahant and Fully Enlightened.

mn94:32.11.verse: But since that Blessed One has attained the final Nibbāna, we go to that Blessed One for refuge and to the Dhamma and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.

mn94:32.12.verse: From today let Master Udena remember me as a follower who has gone for refuge for life.’

mn94:33.1.verse: ‘Now, Master Udena, there is the king of Aṅga (who) gives me a regular pension daily; from that I give Master Udena a regular pension.’

mn94:33.2.verse: ‘In what form does the king of Aṅga give you the regular pension daily, divine?’

mn94:33.3.verse: ‘It is five hundred kahāpanas, Master Udena.’

mn94:33.4.verse: ‘It is not allowed for us to accept gold and silver, divine.’

mn94:33.5.verse: ‘If that is not allowed to Master Udena, I will have a monastery built for Master Udena.’

mn94:33.6.verse: ‘If you desire to have a monastery built for me, divine, have a service hall built for the Sangha at Pāṭaliputta.’

mn94:33.7.verse: ‘I am still more satisfied and glad that Master Udena suggests to me a gift to the Sangha.

mn94:33.8.verse: So with this regular pension and another regular pension I shall have a service hall built for the Sangha at Pāṭaliputta.’

mn94:33.9.verse: Then with that regular pension (which he had offered Master Udena) and another regular pension (added to it), Ghoṭamukha of the divine caste had a service hall built for the Sangha at Pāṭaliputta.

mn94:33.10.verse: And that is now known as the Ghoṭamukhi.

mn94:1.2.verse: At one time Venerable Udena was staying near Varanasi in the Khemiya Mango Grove.

mn94:2.1.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Ghoṭamukha had arrived at Varanasi on some business.

mn94:2.2.verse: Then as he was going for a walk he went to the Khemiya Mango Grove.

mn94:2.3.verse: At that time Venerable Udena was walking mindfully in the open air.

mn94:2.4.verse: Ghoṭamukha approached and exchanged greetings with him.

mn94:2.6.verse: “My ascetic, there is no such thing as a principled renunciate life;

mn94:2.8.verse: Yet I have not seen honorable ones such as yourself, or a relevant teaching.”

mn94:3.1.verse: When he said this, Udena stepped down from the walking path, entered his dwelling, and sat down on the seat spread out.

mn94:3.2.verse: Ghoṭamukha also stepped down from the walking path and entered the dwelling, where he stood to one side.

mn94:3.6.verse: “I was just waiting for you to sit down.

mn94:3.7.verse: For how on earth could one such as I presume to sit first without being invited?”

mn94:4.1.verse: Then he took a low seat and sat to one side,

mn94:4.3.verse: “My ascetic, there is no such thing as a principled renunciate life;

mn94:4.5.verse: Yet I have not seen worthy ones such as yourself, or a relevant teaching.”

mn94:4.6.verse: “Brahmin, we can discuss this. But only if you grant what should be granted, and reject what should be rejected. And if you ask me the meaning of anything you don’t understand, saying:

mn94:4.7.verse: ‘Sir, why is this? What does that mean?’”

mn94:4.8.verse: “Let us discuss this. I will do as you say.”

mn94:5.1.verse: “Brahmin, these four individuals are found in the world.

mn94:5.3.verse: One individual mortifies themselves, committed to the practice of mortifying themselves.

mn94:5.4.verse: One individual mortifies others, committed to the practice of mortifying others.

mn94:5.5.verse: One individual mortifies themselves and others, committed to the practice of mortifying themselves and others.

mn94:5.6.verse: One individual doesn’t mortify either themselves or others, committed to the practice of not mortifying themselves or others.

mn94:5.7.verse: They live without wishes in this very life, quenched, cooled, experiencing bliss, with self become divine.

mn94:5.8.verse: Which one of these four individuals do you like the sound of?”

mn94:5.9.verse: “Worthy Udena, I don’t like the sound of the first three individuals.

mn94:5.13.verse: I only like the sound of the last individual, who doesn’t mortify either themselves or others.”

mn94:6.1.verse: “But why don’t you like the sound of those three individuals?”

mn94:6.2.verse: “Worthy Udena, the individual who mortifies themselves does so even though they want to be happy and recoil from pain.

mn94:6.3.verse: That’s why I don’t like the sound of that individual.

mn94:6.4.verse: The individual who mortifies others does so even though others want to be happy and recoil from pain.

mn94:6.5.verse: That’s why I don’t like the sound of that individual.

mn94:6.6.verse: The individual who mortifies themselves and others does so even though both themselves and others want to be happy and recoil from pain.

mn94:6.7.verse: That’s why I don’t like the sound of that individual.

mn94:6.8.verse: The individual who doesn’t mortify either themselves or others—living without wishes, quenched, cooled, experiencing bliss, with self become divine—does not torment themselves or others, both of whom want to be happy and recoil from pain.

mn94:6.9.verse: That’s why I like the sound of that individual.”

mn94:7.1.verse: “There are, brahmin, these two groups of people.

mn94:7.3.verse: There’s one group of people who, being obsessed with jeweled earrings, seeks partners and children, male and female bondservants, fields and lands, and gold and currency.

mn94:7.4.verse: And there’s another group of people who, not being obsessed with jeweled earrings, has given up partner and children, male and female bondservants, fields and lands, and gold and currency, and goes forth from the lay life to homelessness.

mn94:7.5.verse: Now, brahmin, that individual who doesn’t mortify either themselves or others—

mn94:7.7.verse: in which of these two groups of people do you usually find such an individual?”

mn94:7.9.verse: “I usually find such an individual in

mn94:7.10.verse: the group that has gone forth from the lay life to homelessness.”

mn94:8.1.verse: “Just now I understood you to say:

mn94:8.2.verse: ‘My ascetic, there is no such thing as a principled renunciate life;

mn94:8.4.verse: Yet I have not seen honorable ones such as yourself, or a relevant teaching.’”

mn94:8.5.verse: “Well, I obviously had my reasons for saying that, worthy Udena.

mn94:8.6.verse: But there is such a thing as a principled renunciate life.

mn94:8.8.verse: and that’s how you should remember me.

mn94:8.9.verse: Now, these four individuals that you’ve spoken of in a brief summary: please explain them to me in detail, out of sympathy.”

mn94:9.1.verse: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

mn94:10.1.verse: “What individual mortifies themselves, committed to the practice of mortifying themselves?

mn94:10.2.verse: It’s when an individual goes naked, ignoring conventions. They lick their hands, and don’t come or wait when called. They don’t consent to food brought to them, or food prepared on their behalf, or an invitation for a meal.

mn94:10.3.verse: They don’t receive anything from a pot or bowl; or from someone who keeps sheep, or who has a weapon or a shovel in their home; or where a couple is eating; or where there is a woman who is pregnant, breastfeeding, or who lives with a man; or where there’s a hound waiting or flies buzzing. They accept no fish or meat or beer or wine, and drink no fermented gruel.

mn94:10.4.verse: They go to just one house for alms, taking just one mouthful, or two houses and two mouthfuls, up to seven houses and seven mouthfuls.

mn94:10.5.verse: They feed on one saucer a day, two saucers a day, up to seven saucers a day.

mn94:10.6.verse: They eat once a day, once every second day, up to once a week, and so on, even up to once a fortnight. They live committed to the practice of eating food at set intervals.

mn94:10.7.verse: They eat herbs, millet, wild rice, poor rice, water lettuce, rice bran, scum from boiling rice, sesame flour, grass, or cow dung. They survive on forest roots and fruits, or eating fallen fruit.

mn94:10.8.verse: They wear robes of sunn hemp, mixed hemp, corpse-wrapping cloth, rags, lodh tree bark, antelope hide (whole or in strips), kusa grass, bark, wood-chips, human hair, horse-tail hair, or owls’ wings.

mn94:10.9.verse: They tear out their hair and beard, committed to this practice.

mn94:10.10.verse: They constantly stand, turning down seats.

mn94:10.11.verse: They squat, committed to the endeavor of squatting.

mn94:10.12.verse: They lie on a mat of thorns, making a mat of thorns their bed.

mn94:10.13.verse: They’re devoted to ritual bathing three times a day, including at dusk.

mn94:10.14.verse: And so they live committed to practicing these various ways of mortifying and tormenting the body.

mn94:10.15.verse: This is called an individual who mortifies themselves, being committed to the practice of mortifying themselves.

mn94:11.1.verse: And what individual mortifies others, committed to the practice of mortifying others?

mn94:11.2.verse: It’s when an individual is a slaughterer of sheep, pigs, poultry, or deer, a hunter or fisher, a bandit, an executioner, a butcher of cattle, a jailer, or has some other cruel livelihood.

mn94:11.3.verse: This is called an individual who mortifies others, being committed to the practice of mortifying others.

mn94:12.1.verse: And what individual mortifies themselves and others, being committed to the practice of mortifying themselves and others?

mn94:12.2.verse: It’s when an individual is an anointed aristocratic king or a well-to-do brahmin.

mn94:12.3.verse: He has a new ceremonial hall built to the east of the citadel. He shaves off his hair and beard, dresses in a rough antelope hide, and smears his body with ghee and oil. Scratching his back with antlers, he enters the hall with his chief queen and the brahmin high priest.

mn94:12.4.verse: There he lies on the bare ground strewn with grass.

mn94:12.5.verse: The king feeds on the milk from one teat of a cow that has a calf of the same color. The chief queen feeds on the milk from the second teat. The brahmin high priest feeds on the milk from the third teat. The milk from the fourth teat is served to the sacred flame. The calf feeds on the leftovers.

mn94:12.7.verse: ‘Slaughter this many bulls, bullocks, heifers, goats, rams, and horses for the sacrifice! Fell this many trees and reap this much grass for the sacrificial equipment!’

mn94:12.8.verse: His bondservants, servants, and workers do their jobs under threat of punishment and danger, weeping with tearful faces.

mn94:12.9.verse: This is called an individual who mortifies themselves and others, being committed to the practice of mortifying themselves and others.

mn94:13.1.verse: And what individual doesn’t mortify either themselves or others, committed to the practice of not mortifying themselves or others,

mn94:13.2.verse: living without wishes in this very life, quenched, cooled, experiencing bliss, with self become divine?

mn94:14.1.verse: It’s when a Realized One arises in the world, perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.

mn94:14.2.verse: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

mn94:14.3.verse: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

mn94:15.1.verse: A householder hears that teaching, or a householder’s child, or someone reborn in a good family.

mn94:15.2.verse: They gain faith in the Realized One,

mn94:15.4.verse: ‘Life at home is cramped and dirty, life gone forth is wide open.

mn94:15.5.verse: It’s not easy for someone living at home to lead the spiritual life utterly full and pure, like a polished shell.

mn94:15.6.verse: Why don’t I shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness?’
