mn129:35.8.verse: And the opposing kings in the eastern direction submit to the Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:35.9.verse: “Then the wheel-treasure plunges into the eastern ocean and emerges again. And then it turns forward rolling in the southern direction…And the opposing kings in the southern direction submit to the Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:35.10.verse: Then the wheel-treasure plunges into the southern ocean and emerges again. And then it turns forward rolling in the western direction…And the opposing kings in the western direction submit to the Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:35.11.verse: Then the wheel-treasure plunges into the western ocean and emerges again. And then it turns forward rolling in the northern direction, and the Wheel-turning Monarch follows it with his four-constituent army. Now in whatever region the wheel-treasure pauses, there the Wheel-turning Monarch takes up his abode with his four-constituent army.

mn129:35.12.verse: And opposing kings in the northern direction come to the Wheel-turning Monarch and speak thus:

mn129:35.13.verse: ‘Come, great king; welcome, great king; command, great king; advise, great king.’

mn129:35.15.verse: ‘You should not kill living beings; you should not take what has not been given; you should not misconduct yourselves in sensual pleasures; you should not speak falsehood; you should not drink intoxicants; you should eat what you are accustomed to eat.’

mn129:35.16.verse: And the opposing kings in the northern direction submit to the Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:35.17.verse: “Now when the wheel-treasure has triumphed over the earth to the ocean’s edge, it returns to the royal capital and remains as if fixed on its axle at the gate of the Wheel-turning Monarch’s inner palace, as an adornment to the gate of his inner palace.

mn129:35.18.verse: Such is the wheel-treasure that appears to a Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:36.1.verse: “Again, the elephant-treasure appears to the Wheel-turning Monarch,

mn129:36.2.verse: all white, with sevenfold stance, with supernormal power, flying through the air, the king of elephants named ‘Uposatha.’

mn129:36.3.verse: On seeing him, the Wheel-turning Monarch’s mind has confidence in him thus:

mn129:36.4.verse: ‘It would be wonderful to ride the elephant, if he would undergo taming!’

mn129:36.5.verse: Then the elephant-treasure undergoes taming just like a fine thoroughbred elephant well tamed for a long time.

mn129:36.6.verse: And it so happens that the Wheel-turning Monarch, when testing the elephant-treasure, mounts him in the morning, and after traversing the whole earth to the edge of the ocean, he returns to the royal capital to take his morning meal.

mn129:36.7.verse: Such is the elephant-treasure that appears to a Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:37.1.verse: “Again, the horse-treasure appears to the Wheel-turning Monarch,

mn129:37.2.verse: all white, with raven-black head, with mane like muñja grass, with supernormal power, flying through the air, the king of horses named ‘Valāhaka’ [‘Thundercloud’].

mn129:37.3.verse: On seeing him, the Wheel-turning Monarch’s mind has confidence in him thus:

mn129:37.4.verse: ‘It would be wonderful to ride the horse, if he would undergo taming!’

mn129:37.5.verse: Then the horse-treasure undergoes taming just like a fine thoroughbred horse well tamed for a long time.

mn129:37.6.verse: And it so happens that the Wheel-turning Monarch, when testing the horse-treasure, mounts him in the morning, and after traversing the whole earth to the edge of the ocean, he returns to the royal capital to take his morning meal.

mn129:37.7.verse: Such is the horse-treasure that appears to a Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:38.1.verse: “Again, the jewel-treasure appears to the Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:38.2.verse: The jewel is fine beryl of purest water, eight-faceted, and well cut.

mn129:38.3.verse: Now the radiance of the jewel-treasure spreads around for a whole league.

mn129:38.4.verse: And it so happens that when the Wheel-turning Monarch is testing the jewel-treasure, he draws up his four-constituent army in array, and mounting the jewel on top of his banner, he sets forth in the darkness and gloom of the night.

mn129:38.5.verse: Then all the [inhabitants of the] villages nearby begin their work by its light, thinking that it is day.

mn129:38.6.verse: Such is the jewel-treasure that appears to a Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:39.1.verse: “Again, the woman-treasure appears to the Wheel-turning Monarch,

mn129:39.2.verse: beautiful, comely and graceful, possessing the supreme beauty of complexion, neither too tall nor too short, neither too slim nor too stout, neither too dark nor too fair, surpassing human beauty without reaching divine beauty.

mn129:39.3.verse: The touch of the woman-treasure is such that it is like a tuft of kapok or a tuft of cotton-wool.

mn129:39.4.verse: When it is cool, her limbs are warm; when it is warm, her limbs are cool.

mn129:39.5.verse: From her body the scent of sandalwood comes forth, and from her mouth the scent of lotuses.

mn129:39.6.verse: She rises before the Wheel-turning Monarch and retires after him. She is eager to serve, agreeable in conduct, and sweet in speech.

mn129:39.7.verse: Since she is never unfaithful to the Wheel-turning Monarch even in thought, how could she be so in body?

mn129:39.8.verse: Such is the woman-treasure that appears to a Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:40.1.verse: “Again, the steward-treasure appears to the Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:40.2.verse: The divine eye born of past action is manifested in him whereby he sees hidden stores of treasure both with owners and ownerless.

mn129:40.3.verse: He approaches the Wheel-turning Monarch and says:

mn129:40.4.verse: ‘Sire, you remain at ease. I shall take care of your monetary affairs.’

mn129:40.5.verse: And it so happens that when the Wheel-turning Monarch is testing the steward-treasure, he boards a boat, and putting out into the river Ganges, in midstream he tells the steward-treasure:

mn129:40.7.verse: ‘Then, sire, let the boat be steered towards one bank.’

mn129:40.8.verse: ‘Steward, it is actually here that I need gold and bullion.’

mn129:40.9.verse: Then the steward-treasure plunges both hands into the water and draws up a pot full of gold and bullion, and he tells the Wheel-turning Monarch:

mn129:40.10.verse: ‘Is this enough, sire? Is enough done, enough offered?’

mn129:40.12.verse: ‘This is enough, steward, enough is done, enough offered.’

mn129:40.13.verse: Such is the steward-treasure that appears to a Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:41.1.verse: “Again, the counsellor-treasure appears to the Wheel-turning Monarch,

mn129:41.2.verse: wise, shrewd, and sagacious, capable of getting the Wheel-turning Monarch to promote that which is worthy of being promoted, to dismiss that which should be dismissed, and to establish that which should be established.

mn129:41.3.verse: He approaches the Wheel-turning Monarch and says:

mn129:41.4.verse: ‘Sire, you remain at ease. I shall govern.’

mn129:41.5.verse: Such is the counsellor-treasure that appears to a Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:41.6.verse: These are the seven treasures that a Wheel-turning Monarch possesses.

mn129:42.1.verse: “What are the four kinds of success?

mn129:42.2.verse: Here a Wheel-turning Monarch is handsome, comely, and graceful, possessing the supreme beauty of complexion, and he surpasses other human beings in that respect.

mn129:42.3.verse: This is the first kind of success that a Wheel-turning Monarch possesses.

mn129:43.1.verse: “Again, a Wheel-turning Monarch lives long and endures long, and he surpasses other human beings in that respect.

mn129:43.2.verse: This is the second kind of success that a Wheel-turning Monarch possesses.

mn129:44.1.verse: “Again, a Wheel-turning Monarch is free from illness and affliction, possessing a good digestion that is neither too cool nor too warm, and he surpasses other human beings in that respect.

mn129:44.2.verse: This is the third kind of success that a Wheel-turning Monarch possesses.

mn129:45.1.verse: “Again, a Wheel-turning Monarch is dear and agreeable to brahmins and householders.

mn129:45.2.verse: Just as a father is dear and agreeable to his children,

mn129:45.3.verse: so too a Wheel-turning Monarch is dear and agreeable to brahmins and householders.

mn129:45.4.verse: Brahmins and householders, too, are dear and agreeable to a Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:45.5.verse: Just as children are dear and agreeable to a father,

mn129:45.6.verse: so too brahmins and householders are dear and agreeable to a Wheel-turning Monarch.

mn129:45.7.verse: Once a Wheel-turning Monarch was driving in a pleasure park with his four-constituent army.

mn129:45.8.verse: Then brahmins and householders went to him and spoke thus:

mn129:45.9.verse: ‘Sire, drive slowly that we may see you longer.’

mn129:45.10.verse: And so he told his charioteer:

mn129:45.11.verse: ‘Charioteer, drive slowly that I may see the brahmins and householders longer.’

mn129:45.12.verse: This is the fourth kind of success that a Wheel-turning Monarch possesses.

mn129:45.13.verse: These are the four kinds of success that a Wheel-turning Monarch possesses.

mn129:46.2.verse: Would a Wheel-turning Monarch experience pleasure and joy because of possessing these seven treasures and these four kinds of success?”

mn129:46.3.verse: “Venerable sir, a Wheel-turning Monarch would experience pleasure and joy because of possessing even one treasure, let alone seven treasures and four kinds of success.”

mn129:47.1.verse: Then, taking a small stone the size of his hand, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:

mn129:47.3.verse: Which is the greater, this small stone that I have taken, the size of my hand, or Himalaya, the king of mountains?”

mn129:47.4.verse: “Venerable sir, the small stone that the Blessed One has taken, the size of his hand, does not count beside Himalaya, the king of mountains; it is not even a fraction, there is no comparison.”

mn129:47.5.verse: “So too, bhikkhus, the pleasure and joy that a Wheel-turning Monarch would experience because of possessing the seven treasures and the four kinds of success does not count beside the happiness of heaven; it is not even a fraction, there is no comparison.

mn129:48.1.verse: “If, some time or other, at the end of a long period, the wise man comes back to the human state, it is into a high family that he is reborn—

mn129:48.2.verse: into a family of well-to-do nobles, or well-to-do brahmins, or well-to-do householders—one that is rich, of great wealth, of great possessions, with abundant gold and silver, with abundant assets and means, and with abundant money and grain.

mn129:48.3.verse: He is handsome, comely and graceful, possessing the supreme beauty of complexion. He obtains food and drink, clothes, vehicles, garlands, scents and unguents, bed, lodging, and light.

mn129:48.4.verse: He conducts himself well in body, speech, and mind,

mn129:48.5.verse: and having done so, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world.

mn129:49.1.verse: “Bhikkhus, suppose a gambler at the very first lucky throw won a great fortune,

mn129:49.2.verse: yet a lucky throw such as that is negligible;

mn129:49.3.verse: it is a far more lucky throw when a wise man who conducts himself well in body, speech, and mind, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world.

mn129:49.4.verse: This is the complete perfection of the wise man’s grade.”

mn129:49.5.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

mn129:49.6.verse: The bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn130:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn130:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

mn130:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, suppose there were two houses with doors. A person with clear eyes standing in between them would see humans entering and leaving a house and wandering to and fro.

mn130:2.2.verse: In the same way, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, I see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. I understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds: ‘These dear beings did good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They never denounced the noble ones; they had right view; and they chose to act out of that right view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm, or among humans. These dear beings did bad things by way of body, speech, and mind. They denounced the noble ones; they had wrong view; and they chose to act out of that wrong view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in the ghost realm, the animal realm, or in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.’

mn130:3.1.verse: The wardens of hell take them by the arms and present them to King Yama, saying,

mn130:3.2.verse: ‘Your Majesty, this person did not pay due respect to their mother and father, ascetics and brahmins, or honor the elders in the family.

mn130:3.4.verse: King Yama pursues, presses, and grills them about the first messenger of the gods:

mn130:3.5.verse: ‘My man, did you not see the first messenger of the gods that appeared among human beings?’

mn130:4.2.verse: ‘My man, did you not see among human beings a little baby collapsed in their own urine and feces?’

mn130:4.6.verse: ‘My man, did it not occur to you—being sensible and mature—

mn130:4.7.verse: “I, too, am liable to be born. I’m not exempt from rebirth. I’d better do good by way of body, speech, and mind”?’

mn130:4.11.verse: ‘My man, because you were negligent, you didn’t do good by way of body, speech, and mind.

mn130:4.12.verse: Well, they’ll definitely punish you to fit your negligence.

mn130:4.13.verse: That bad deed wasn’t done by your mother, father, brother, or sister. It wasn’t done by friends and colleagues, by relatives and kin, by ascetics and brahmins, or by the deities. That bad deed was done by you alone, and you alone will experience the result.’

mn130:5.1.verse: Then King Yama grills them about the second messenger of the gods:

mn130:5.2.verse: ‘My man, did you not see the second messenger of the gods that appeared among human beings?’

mn130:5.6.verse: ‘My man, did you not see among human beings an elderly woman or a man—eighty, ninety, or a hundred years old—bent double, crooked, leaning on a staff, trembling as they walk, ailing, past their prime, with teeth broken, hair grey and scanty or bald, skin wrinkled, and limbs blotchy?’

mn130:5.10.verse: ‘My man, did it not occur to you—being sensible and mature—

mn130:5.11.verse: “I, too, am liable to grow old. I’m not exempt from old age. I’d better do good by way of body, speech, and mind”?’

mn130:5.15.verse: ‘My man, because you were negligent, you didn’t do good by way of body, speech, and mind.

mn130:5.16.verse: Well, they’ll definitely punish you to fit your negligence.

mn130:5.17.verse: That bad deed wasn’t done by your mother, father, brother, or sister. It wasn’t done by friends and colleagues, by relatives and kin, by ascetics and brahmins, or by the deities. That bad deed was done by you alone, and you alone will experience the result.’

mn130:6.1.verse: Then King Yama grills them about the third messenger of the gods:

mn130:6.2.verse: ‘My man, did you not see the third messenger of the gods that appeared among human beings?’

mn130:6.6.verse: ‘My man, did you not see among human beings a woman or a man, sick, suffering, gravely ill, collapsed in their own urine and feces, being picked up by some and put down by others?’

mn130:6.10.verse: ‘My man, did it not occur to you—being sensible and mature—

mn130:6.11.verse: “I, too, am liable to become sick. I’m not exempt from sickness. I’d better do good by way of body, speech, and mind”?’

mn130:6.15.verse: ‘My man, because you were negligent, you didn’t do good by way of body, speech, and mind.

mn130:6.16.verse: Well, they’ll definitely punish you to fit your negligence.

mn130:6.17.verse: That bad deed wasn’t done by your mother, father, brother, or sister. It wasn’t done by friends and colleagues, by relatives and kin, by ascetics and brahmins, or by the deities. That bad deed was done by you alone, and you alone will experience the result.’

mn130:7.1.verse: Then King Yama grills them about the fourth messenger of the gods:

mn130:7.2.verse: ‘My man, did you not see the fourth messenger of the gods that appeared among human beings?’

mn130:7.6.verse: ‘My man, did you not see among human beings when the rulers arrested a bandit, a criminal, and subjected them to various punishments—

mn130:7.7.verse: whipping, caning, and clubbing; cutting off hands or feet, or both; cutting off ears or nose, or both; the ‘porridge pot’, the ‘shell-shave’, the ‘Rāhu’s mouth’, the ‘garland of fire’, the ‘burning hand’, the ‘bulrush twist’, the ‘bark dress’, the ‘antelope’, the ‘meat hook’, the ‘coins’, the ‘caustic pickle’, the ‘twisting bar’, the ‘straw mat’; being splashed with hot oil, being fed to the hounds, being impaled alive, and being beheaded?’

mn130:7.11.verse: ‘My man, did it not occur to you—being sensible and mature—

mn130:7.12.verse: “It seems that one who does bad deeds receives such punishment in this very life. What must happen to them in the next? I’d better do good by way of body, speech, and mind”?’

mn130:7.16.verse: ‘My man, because you were negligent, you didn’t do good by way of body, speech, and mind.

mn130:7.17.verse: Well, they’ll definitely punish you to fit your negligence.

mn130:7.18.verse: That bad deed wasn’t done by your mother, father, brother, or sister. It wasn’t done by friends and colleagues, by relatives and kin, by ascetics and brahmins, or by the deities. That bad deed was done by you alone, and you alone will experience the result.’

mn130:8.1.verse: Then King Yama grills them about the fifth messenger of the gods:

mn130:8.2.verse: ‘My man, did you not see the fifth messenger of the gods that appeared among human beings?’

mn130:8.6.verse: ‘My man, did you not see among human beings a woman or a man, dead for one, two, or three days, bloated, livid, and festering?’

mn130:8.10.verse: ‘My man, did it not occur to you—being sensible and mature—

mn130:8.11.verse: “I, too, am liable to die. I’m not exempt from death. I’d better do good by way of body, speech, and mind”?’

mn130:8.15.verse: ‘My man, because you were negligent, you didn’t do good by way of body, speech, and mind.

mn130:8.16.verse: Well, they’ll definitely punish you to fit your negligence.

mn130:8.17.verse: That bad deed wasn’t done by your mother, father, brother, or sister. It wasn’t done by friends and colleagues, by relatives and kin, by ascetics and brahmins, or by the deities. That bad deed was done by you alone, and you alone will experience the result.’

mn130:9.1.verse: After grilling them about the fifth messenger of the gods, King Yama falls silent.

mn130:10.1.verse: The wardens of hell punish them with the five-fold crucifixion.

mn130:10.2.verse: They drive red-hot stakes through the hands and feet, and another in the middle of the chest.

mn130:10.3.verse: And there they suffer painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings—but they don’t die until that bad deed is eliminated.

mn130:11.1.verse: The wardens of hell throw them down and hack them with axes. …

mn130:12.1.verse: They hang them upside-down and hack them with hatchets. …

mn130:13.1.verse: They harness them to a chariot, and drive them back and forth across burning ground, blazing and glowing. …

mn130:14.1.verse: They make them climb up and down a big mountain of burning coals, blazing and glowing. …

mn130:15.1.verse: The wardens of hell turn them upside down and throw them in a red-hot copper pot, burning, blazing, and glowing.

mn130:15.3.verse: There they’re seared in boiling scum, and they’re swept up and down and round and round.

mn130:15.4.verse: And there they suffer painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings—but they don’t die until that bad deed is eliminated.

mn130:16.1.verse: The wardens of hell toss them into the Great Hell.

mn130:16.3.verse: ‘Four are its corners, four its doors,

mn130:16.7.verse: The ground is even made of iron,

mn130:17.1.verse: Now in the Great Hell, flames surge out of the walls and crash into the opposite wall: from east to west, from west to east, from north to south, from south to north, from bottom to top, from top to bottom.

mn130:17.2.verse: And there they suffer painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings—but they don’t die until that bad deed is eliminated.

mn130:18.1.verse: There comes a time when, after a very long period has passed, the eastern gate of the Great Hell is opened.

mn130:18.2.verse: So they run there as fast as they can.

mn130:18.3.verse: And as they run, their outer skin, inner skin, flesh, and sinews burn and even their bones smoke. Such is their escape;

mn130:18.4.verse: but when they’ve managed to make it most of the way, the gate is slammed shut.

mn130:18.5.verse: And there they suffer painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings—but they don’t die until that bad deed is eliminated.

mn130:18.6.verse: There comes a time when, after a very long period has passed, the western gate …

mn130:18.8.verse: southern gate of the Great Hell is opened.

mn130:18.9.verse: So they run there as fast as they can.

mn130:18.10.verse: And as they run, their outer skin, inner skin, flesh, and sinews burn and even their bones smoke. Such is their escape;

mn130:18.11.verse: but when they’ve managed to make it most of the way, the gate is slammed shut.

mn130:18.12.verse: And there they suffer painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings—but they don’t die until that bad deed is eliminated.

mn130:19.1.verse: There comes a time when, after a very long period has passed, the eastern gate of the Great Hell is opened.

mn130:19.2.verse: So they run there as fast as they can.

mn130:19.3.verse: And as they run, their outer skin, inner skin, flesh, and sinews burn and even their bones smoke. Such is their escape;

mn130:19.4.verse: and they make it out that door.

mn130:20.1.verse: Immediately adjacent to the Great Hell is the vast Dung Hell.

mn130:20.3.verse: In that Dung Hell there are needle-mouthed creatures that bore through the outer skin, the inner skin, the flesh, sinews, and bones, until they reach the marrow and devour it.

mn130:20.4.verse: And there they suffer painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings—but they don’t die until that bad deed is eliminated.

mn130:21.1.verse: Immediately adjacent to the Dung Hell is the vast Hell of Burning Chaff.

mn130:21.3.verse: And there they suffer painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings—but they don’t die until that bad deed is eliminated.

mn130:22.1.verse: Immediately adjacent to the Hell of Burning Chaff is the vast Red Silk-Cotton Forest. It’s a league high, full of sixteen-inch thorns, burning, blazing, and glowing.

mn130:22.2.verse: And there they make them climb up and down.

mn130:22.3.verse: And there they suffer painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings—but they don’t die until that bad deed is eliminated.

mn130:23.1.verse: Immediately adjacent to the Red Silk-Cotton Forest is the vast Sword-Leaf Forest.

mn130:23.3.verse: There the fallen leaves blown by the wind cut their hands, feet, both hands and feet; they cut their ears, nose, both ears and nose.

mn130:23.4.verse: And there they suffer painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings—but they don’t die until that bad deed is eliminated.

mn130:24.1.verse: Immediately adjacent to the Sword-Leaf Forest is the vast Acid River.

mn130:24.3.verse: There they are swept upstream, swept downstream, and swept both up and down stream.

mn130:24.4.verse: And there they suffer painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings—but they don’t die until that bad deed is eliminated.

mn130:25.1.verse: The wardens of hell pull them out with a hook and place them on solid ground, and say,

mn130:25.5.verse: The wardens of hell force open their mouth with a hot iron spike—burning, blazing, and glowing—and shove in a red-hot copper ball, burning, blazing, and glowing.

mn130:25.6.verse: It burns their lips, mouth, tongue, throat, and stomach before coming out below dragging their entrails.

mn130:25.7.verse: And there they feel painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings—but they don’t die until that bad deed is eliminated.

mn130:26.5.verse: The wardens of hell force open their mouth with a hot iron spike—burning, blazing, and glowing—and pour in molten copper, burning, blazing, and glowing.

mn130:26.6.verse: It burns their lips, mouth, tongue, throat, and stomach before coming out below dragging their entrails.

mn130:26.7.verse: And there they feel painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings—but they don’t die until that bad deed is eliminated.

mn130:27.1.verse: The wardens of hell toss them back in the Great Hell.

mn130:28.1.verse: Once upon a time, King Yama thought:

mn130:28.2.verse: ‘Those who do such bad deeds in the world receive these many different punishments.

mn130:28.3.verse: Oh, I hope I may be reborn as a human being! And that a Realized One—a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha—arises in the world! And that I may pay homage to the Buddha!

mn130:28.4.verse: Let that Buddha teach me Dhamma, so that I may understand his teaching!’

mn130:29.1.verse: Now, I don’t say this because I’ve heard it from some other ascetic or brahmin. I only say it because I’ve known, seen, and realized it for myself.”

mn130:30.1.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn130:30.2.verse: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

mn130:30.4.verse: those sons of Manu who are negligent

mn130:30.6.verse: when they go to that wretched place.

mn130:30.7.verse: When warned by the gods’ messengers,

mn130:30.8.verse: the good and true persons here

mn130:30.10.verse: the teaching of the Noble One.

mn130:30.12.verse: the origin of birth and death,

mn130:30.14.verse: with the ending of birth and death.

mn130:30.15.verse: Happy, they’ve come to a safe place,

mn130:30.17.verse: They’ve gone beyond all enmities and fears,

mn130:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

mn130:1.3.verse: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:

mn130:2.1.verse: “Bhikkhus, suppose there were two houses with doors and a man with good sight standing there between them saw people going in and coming out and passing to and fro.

mn130:2.2.verse: So too, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, I see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate. I understand how beings pass on according to their actions thus: ‘These worthy beings who were well conducted in body, speech, and mind, not revilers of noble ones, right in their views, giving effect to right views in their actions, on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world. Or these worthy beings who were well conducted in body, speech, and mind, not revilers of noble ones, right in their views, giving effect to right views in their actions, on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared among human beings. But these worthy beings who were ill conducted in body, speech, and mind, revilers of noble ones, wrong in their views, giving effect to wrong views in their actions, on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared in the realm of ghosts. Or these worthy beings who were ill conducted…on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared in the animal world. Or these worthy beings who were ill conducted…on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell.’

mn130:3.1.verse: “Now the wardens of hell seize such a being by the arms and present him to King Yama, saying:

mn130:3.2.verse: ‘Sire, this man has ill-treated his mother, ill-treated his father, ill-treated recluses, ill-treated brahmins; he has had no respect for the elders of his clan.

mn130:3.3.verse: Let the king order his punishment.’

mn130:3.4.verse: “Then King Yama presses and questions and cross-questions him about the first divine messenger:

mn130:3.5.verse: ‘Good man, did you not see the first divine messenger to appear in the world?’

mn130:4.2.verse: ‘Good man, have you never seen in the world a young tender infant lying prone, fouled in his own excrement and urine?’

mn130:4.6.verse: ‘Good man, did it never occur to you—an intelligent and mature man—

mn130:4.7.verse: “I too am subject to birth, I am not exempt from birth: surely I had better do good by body, speech, and mind”?’

mn130:4.9.verse: ‘I was unable, venerable sir, I was negligent.’

mn130:4.11.verse: ‘Good man, through negligence you have failed to do good by body, speech, and mind.

mn130:4.12.verse: Certainly they will deal with you according to your negligence.

mn130:4.13.verse: But this evil action of yours was not done by your mother or your father, or by your brother or your sister, or by your friends and companions, or by your kinsmen and relatives, or by recluses and brahmins, or by gods: this evil action was done by you yourself, and you yourself will experience its result.’

mn130:5.1.verse: “Then, after pressing and questioning and cross-questioning him about the first divine messenger, King Yama presses and questions and cross-questions him about the second divine messenger:

mn130:5.2.verse: ‘Good man, did you not see the second divine messenger to appear in the world?’

mn130:5.6.verse: ‘Good man, have you never seen in the world a man—or a woman—at eighty, ninety, or a hundred years, aged, as crooked as a roof bracket, doubled up, supported by a walking stick, tottering, frail, youth gone, teeth broken, grey-haired, scanty-haired, bald, wrinkled, with limbs all blotchy?’

mn130:5.10.verse: ‘Good man, did it never occur to you—an intelligent and mature man—

mn130:5.11.verse: “I too am subject to ageing, I am not exempt from ageing: surely I had better do good by body, speech, and mind”?’

mn130:5.13.verse: ‘I was unable, venerable sir, I was negligent.’

mn130:5.15.verse: ‘Good man, through negligence you have failed to do good by body, speech, and mind.

mn130:5.16.verse: Certainly they will deal with you according to your negligence.

mn130:5.17.verse: But this evil action of yours was not done by your mother…or by gods: this evil action was done by you yourself, and you yourself will experience its result.’

mn130:6.1.verse: “Then, after pressing and questioning and cross-questioning him about the second divine messenger, King Yama presses and questions and cross-questions him about the third divine messenger:

mn130:6.2.verse: ‘Good man, did you not see the third divine messenger to appear in the world?’

mn130:6.6.verse: ‘Good man, have you never seen in the world a man—or a woman—afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill, lying fouled in his own excrement and urine, lifted up by some and set down by others?’

mn130:6.10.verse: ‘Good man, did it never occur to you—an intelligent and mature man—

mn130:6.11.verse: “I too am subject to sickness, I am not exempt from sickness:

mn130:6.12.verse: surely I had better do good by body, speech, and mind”?’ He says:

mn130:6.13.verse: ‘I was unable, venerable sir, I was negligent.’

mn130:6.15.verse: ‘Good man, through negligence you have failed to do good by body, speech, and mind.

mn130:6.16.verse: Certainly they will deal with you according to your negligence.

mn130:6.17.verse: But this evil action of yours was not done by your mother…or by gods: this evil action was done by you yourself, and you yourself will experience its result.’

mn130:7.1.verse: “Then, after pressing and questioning and cross-questioning him about the third divine messenger, King Yama presses and questions and cross-questions him about the fourth divine messenger:

mn130:7.2.verse: ‘Good man, did you not see the fourth divine messenger to appear in the world?’

mn130:7.6.verse: ‘Good man, have you never seen in the world, when a robber culprit is caught, kings having many kinds of tortures inflicted on him:

mn130:7.7.verse: having him flogged with whips…(as Sutta 129, §4)…and having his head cut off with a sword?’

mn130:7.11.verse: ‘Good man, did it never occur to you—an intelligent and mature man—

mn130:7.12.verse: “Those who do evil actions have such tortures of various kinds inflicted on them here and now; so what in the hereafter? Surely I had better do good by body, speech, and mind”?’

mn130:7.14.verse: ‘I was unable, venerable sir, I was negligent.’

mn130:7.16.verse: ‘Good man, through negligence you have failed to do good by body, speech, and mind.

mn130:7.17.verse: Certainly they will deal with you according to your negligence.

mn130:7.18.verse: But this evil action of yours was not done by your mother…or by gods: this evil action was done by you yourself, and you yourself will experience its result.’

mn130:8.1.verse: “Then, after pressing and questioning and cross-questioning him about the fourth divine messenger, King Yama presses and questions and cross-questions him about the fifth divine messenger:

mn130:8.2.verse: ‘Good man, did you not see the fifth divine messenger to appear in the world?’

mn130:8.6.verse: ‘Good man, have you never seen in the world a man—or a woman—one-day dead, two-days dead, three-days dead, bloated, livid, and oozing with matter?’

mn130:8.10.verse: ‘Good man, did it never occur to you—an intelligent and mature man—

mn130:8.11.verse: “I too am subject to death, I am not exempt from death: surely I had better do good by body, speech, and mind”?’

mn130:8.13.verse: ‘I was unable, venerable sir, I was negligent.’

mn130:8.15.verse: ‘Good man, through negligence you have failed to do good by body, speech, and mind.

mn130:8.16.verse: Certainly they will deal with you according to your negligence.

mn130:8.17.verse: But this evil action of yours was not done by your mother…or by gods: this evil action was done by you yourself, and you yourself will experience its result.’

mn130:9.1.verse: “Then, after pressing and questioning and cross-questioning him about the fifth divine messenger, King Yama is silent.

mn130:10.1.verse: “Now the wardens of hell torture him with the fivefold transfixing.

mn130:10.2.verse: They drive a red-hot iron stake through one hand, they drive a red-hot iron stake through the other hand, they drive a red-hot iron stake through one foot, they drive a red-hot iron stake through the other foot, they drive a red-hot iron stake in the middle through his breast.

mn130:10.3.verse: There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:11.1.verse: “Next the wardens of hell throw him down and pare him with axes. There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:12.1.verse: “Next the wardens of hell set him with his feet up and his head down and pare him with adzes. There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:13.1.verse: “Next the wardens of hell harness him to a chariot and drive him back and forth across ground that is burning, blazing, and glowing. There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:14.1.verse: “Next the wardens of hell make him climb up and down a great mound of coals that are burning, blazing, and glowing. There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:15.1.verse: “Next the wardens of hell take him feet up and head down and plunge him into a red-hot metal cauldron that is burning, blazing, and glowing.

mn130:15.2.verse: He is cooked there in a swirl of froth.

mn130:15.3.verse: And as he is being cooked there in a swirl of froth, he is swept now up, now down, and now across.

mn130:15.4.verse: There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:16.1.verse: “Next the wardens of hell throw him into the Great Hell.

mn130:16.2.verse: Now as to that Great Hell, bhikkhus:

mn130:16.3.verse: It has four corners and is built

mn130:16.4.verse: With four doors, one set in each side,

mn130:16.5.verse: Walled up with iron all around

mn130:16.6.verse: And shut in with an iron roof.

mn130:16.7.verse: Its floor as well is made of iron

mn130:16.8.verse: And heated till it glows with fire.

mn130:16.9.verse: The range is a full hundred leagues

mn130:17.1.verse: “Now the flames that surge out from the Great Hell’s eastern wall dash against its western wall. The flames that surge out from its western wall dash against its eastern wall. The flames that surge out from its northern wall dash against its southern wall. The flames that surge out from its southern wall dash against its northern wall. The flames that dash out from the bottom dash against the top. And the flames that surge out from the top dash against the bottom.

mn130:17.2.verse: There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:18.1.verse: “Some time or other, bhikkhus, at the end of a long period, there comes an occasion when the Great Hell’s eastern door is opened.

mn130:18.2.verse: He runs towards it, treading quickly.

mn130:18.3.verse: As he does so, his outer skin burns, his inner skin burns, his flesh burns, his sinews burn, his bones turn to smoke; and it is the same when his foot is uplifted.

mn130:18.4.verse: When at long last he reaches the door, then it is shut.

mn130:18.5.verse: There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:18.6.verse: “Some time or other, at the end of a long period, there comes an occasion when the Great Hell’s western door is opened…

mn130:18.7.verse: when its northern door is opened…

mn130:18.8.verse: when its southern door is opened.

mn130:18.9.verse: He runs towards it, treading quickly…

mn130:18.10.verse: As he does so, his outer skin burns, his inner skin burns, his flesh burns, his sinews burn, his bones turn to smoke; and it is the same when his foot is uplifted.

mn130:18.11.verse: When at long last he reaches the door, then it is shut.

mn130:18.12.verse: There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:19.1.verse: “Some time or other, bhikkhus, at the end of a long period, there comes an occasion when the Great Hell’s eastern door is opened.

mn130:19.2.verse: He runs towards it, treading quickly.

mn130:19.3.verse: As he does so, his outer skin burns, his inner skin burns, his flesh burns, his sinews burn, his bones turn to smoke; and it is the same when his foot is uplifted.

mn130:19.4.verse: He comes out by that door.

mn130:20.1.verse: “Immediately next to the Great Hell is the vast Hell of Excrement.

mn130:20.3.verse: In that Hell of Excrement needle-mouthed creatures bore through his outer skin and bore through his inner skin and bore through his flesh and bore through his sinews and bore through his bones and devour his marrow.

mn130:20.4.verse: There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:21.1.verse: “Immediately next to the Hell of Excrement is the vast Hell of Hot Embers.

mn130:21.3.verse: There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:22.1.verse: “Immediately next to the Hell of Hot Embers is the vast Wood of Simbali Trees, a league high, bristling with thorns sixteen finger-breadths long, burning, blazing, and glowing.

mn130:22.2.verse: They make him climb up and down those trees.

mn130:22.3.verse: There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:23.1.verse: “Immediately next to the Wood of Simbali Trees is a vast Wood of Sword-leaf Trees.

mn130:23.3.verse: The leaves, stirred by the wind, cut his hands and cut his feet and cut his hands and feet; they cut his ears and cut his nose and cut his ears and nose.

mn130:23.4.verse: There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:24.1.verse: “Immediately next to the Wood of Sword-leaf Trees is a great river of caustic water.

mn130:24.3.verse: There he is swept along the stream and against the stream and both along and against the stream.

mn130:24.4.verse: There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:25.1.verse: “Next the wardens of hell pull him out with a hook, and setting him on the ground, they ask him:

mn130:25.5.verse: Then the wardens of hell prise open his mouth with red-hot iron tongs, burning, blazing, and glowing, and they throw into his mouth a red-hot metal ball, burning, blazing, and glowing.

mn130:25.6.verse: It burns his lips, it burns his mouth, it burns his throat, it burns his stomach, and it passes out below carrying with it his intestines and mesentery.

mn130:25.7.verse: There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:26.1.verse: “Next the wardens of hell ask him:

mn130:26.5.verse: Then the wardens of hell prise open his mouth with red-hot iron tongs, burning, blazing, and glowing, and they pour into his mouth molten copper, burning, blazing, and glowing.

mn130:26.6.verse: It burns his lips, it burns his mouth, it burns his throat, it burns his stomach, and it passes out below carrying with it his intestines and mesentery.

mn130:26.7.verse: There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

mn130:27.1.verse: “Then the wardens of hell throw him back again into the Great Hell.

mn130:28.1.verse: “It has happened that King Yama thought:

mn130:28.2.verse: ‘Those in the world who do evil unwholesome actions indeed have all these many kinds of tortures inflicted on them.

mn130:28.3.verse: Oh, that I might attain the human state, that a Tathāgata, accomplished and fully enlightened, might appear in the world, that I might wait on that Blessed One,

mn130:28.4.verse: that the Blessed One might teach me the Dhamma, and that I might come to understand that Blessed One’s Dhamma!’

mn130:29.1.verse: “Bhikkhus, I tell you this not as something I heard from another recluse or brahmin. I tell you this as something that I have actually known, seen, and discovered by myself.”

mn130:30.1.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

mn130:30.2.verse: When the Sublime One had said that, the Teacher said further:

mn130:30.5.verse: And people may sorrow long indeed

mn130:30.6.verse: Once gone down to the lower world.

mn130:30.7.verse: But when by the divine messengers

mn130:30.8.verse: Good people here in this life are warned,

mn130:30.9.verse: They do not dwell in negligence

mn130:30.10.verse: But practise well the noble Dhamma.

mn130:30.11.verse: Clinging they look upon with fear

mn130:30.12.verse: For it produces birth and death;

mn130:30.13.verse: And by not clinging they are freed

mn130:30.14.verse: In the destruction of birth and death.

mn130:30.15.verse: They dwell in bliss for they are safe

mn130:30.16.verse: And reach Nibbāna here and now.

mn130:30.17.verse: They are beyond all fear and hate;

mn131:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

mn131:1.3.verse: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:

mn131:2.1.verse: ‘Bhikkhus, I shall give you a summary and an exposition of one who has a single fortunate attachment.

mn131:2.2.verse: Listen and heed well what I shall say.’

mn131:3.1.verse: ‘Let not a man revive the past

mn131:3.2.verse: or on the future build his hopes;

mn131:3.5.verse: Rather with insight let him see

mn131:3.8.verse: let him know it and be sure of it.

mn131:3.9.verse: Today the effort must be made;

mn131:3.10.verse: tomorrow Death may come, who knows?

mn131:3.12.verse: can keep him and his hordes away.

mn131:3.13.verse: But one who dwells thus ardently,

mn131:3.15.verse: it is he, the peaceful sage has said,

mn131:3.16.verse: who has a single fortunate attachment.

mn131:4.1.verse: ‘And how, bhikkhus, does one revive the past?

mn131:4.2.verse: Thinking, “I had such form in the past,” he allows himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such feeling in the past,” he allows himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such perception in the past,” he allows himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such formations in the past,” he allows himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such consciousness in the past,” he allows himself to relish that—

mn131:4.3.verse: that, bhikkhus, is how one revives the past.

mn131:5.1.verse: ‘And how, bhikkhus, does one not revive the past?

mn131:5.2.verse: Thinking, “I had such form in the past,” he does not allow himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such feeling in the past,” he does not allow himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such perception in the past,” he does not allow himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such formations in the past,” he does not allow himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such consciousness in the past,” he does not allow himself to relish that—

mn131:5.3.verse: that, bhikkhus, is how one does not revive the past.

mn131:6.1.verse: ‘And how, bhikkhus, does one build up hope upon the future?

mn131:6.2.verse: Thinking, “May my form be such in the future,” he allows himself to relish that; may my feeling be such … may my perception be such … may my formations be such … thinking, “May my consciousness be such in the future,” he allows himself to relish that—

mn131:6.3.verse: that, bhikkhus, is how one builds up hope upon the future.

mn131:7.1.verse: ‘And how, bhikkhus, does one not build up hope upon the future?

mn131:7.2.verse: Thinking, “May my form be such in the future,” he does not allow himself to relish that; may my feeling be such … may my perception be such … may my formations be such … thinking, “May my consciousness be such in the future,” he does not allow himself to relish that—

mn131:7.3.verse: that, bhikkhus, is how one does not build up hope upon the future.

mn131:8.1.verse: ‘And how, bhikkhus, is one vanquished in regard to presently arisen dhammas?

mn131:8.2.verse: Here, bhikkhus, the untaught ordinary man, who has no regard for the Noble Ones and is unconversant with their Dhamma and undisciplined in it, who has no regard for True Men and is unconversant with their Dhamma and undisciplined in it,

mn131:8.3.verse: sees form as self, or self as possessed of form, or form in self, or self in form;

mn131:8.7.verse: he sees consciousness as self, or self as possessed of consciousness, or consciousness in self, or self in consciousness—

mn131:8.8.verse: that, bhikkhus, is how one is vanquished in regard to presently arisen dhammas.

mn131:9.1.verse: ‘And how, bhikkhus, is one not vanquished in regard to presently arisen dhammas?

mn131:9.2.verse: Here, bhikkhus, the well-taught disciple of the Noble Ones, who has regard for the Noble Ones and is conversant with their Dhamma and disciplined in it, who has regard for True Men and is conversant with their Dhamma and disciplined in it,

mn131:9.3.verse: does not see form as self, or self as possessed of form, or form in self, or self in form;

mn131:9.7.verse: he does not see consciousness as self, or self as possessed of consciousness, or consciousness in self, or self in consciousness—

mn131:9.8.verse: that, bhikkhus, is how one is not vanquished in regard to presently arisen dhammas.

mn131:10.1.verse: ‘Let not a man revive the past

mn131:10.2.verse: or on the future build his hopes;

mn131:10.5.verse: Rather with insight let him see

mn131:10.8.verse: let him know it and be sure of it.

mn131:10.9.verse: Today the effort must be made;

mn131:10.10.verse: tomorrow Death may come, who knows?

mn131:10.12.verse: can keep him and his hordes away.

mn131:10.13.verse: But one who dwells thus ardently,

mn132:0.2.verse: Ānanda and A Single Excellent Night

mn132:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

mn132:2.1.verse: Now on that occasion the venerable Ānanda was instructing, urging, rousing, and gladdening the bhikkhus with talk on the Dhamma in the assembly hall. He was reciting the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night.”

mn132:2.2.verse: Then, in the evening, the Blessed One rose from meditation and went to the assembly hall. He sat down on a seat made ready

mn132:2.4.verse: “Bhikkhus, who has been instructing, urging, rousing, and gladdening the bhikkhus with talk on the Dhamma in the assembly hall? Who has been reciting the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’?”

mn132:2.5.verse: “It was the venerable Ānanda, venerable sir.”

mn132:2.6.verse: Then the Blessed One asked the venerable Ānanda:

mn132:4.1.verse: ‘How, friends, does one revive the past?

mn132:5.1.verse: And how, friends, does one not revive the past?

mn132:5.2.verse: One does not nurture delight there thinking, ‘I had such material form in the past.’ One does not nurture delight there thinking, ‘I had such feeling in the past,’…‘I had such perception in the past,’…‘I had such formations in the past,’…‘I had such consciousness in the past.’

mn133:9.1.verse: “Reverends, suppose there was a person in need of heartwood. And while wandering in search of heartwood he’d come across a large tree standing with heartwood. But he’d pass over the roots and trunk, imagining that the heartwood should be sought in the branches and leaves.

mn133:9.2.verse: Such is the consequence for the venerables. Though you were face to face with the Buddha, you bypassed him, imagining that you should ask me about this matter.

mn133:9.3.verse: For he is the Buddha, the one who knows and sees. He is vision, he is knowledge, he is the manifestation of principle, he is the manifestation of divinity. He is the preacher, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the bestower of freedom from death, the lord of truth, the Realized One.

mn133:9.4.verse: That was the time to approach the Buddha and ask about this matter. You should have remembered it in line with the Buddha’s answer.”

mn133:0.2.verse: Mahā Kaccāna and A Single Excellent Night

mn133:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha in the Park of the Hot Springs.

mn133:1.3.verse: Then, when it was near dawn, the venerable Samiddhi went to the hot springs to bathe his limbs.

mn133:1.4.verse: After bathing he came up out of the water and stood dressed in one robe, drying his limbs.

mn133:1.5.verse: Then, when the night was well advanced, a certain deity of beautiful appearance who illuminated the whole of the Hot Springs, approached the venerable Samiddhi. Standing at one side, the deity said to him:

mn133:2.1.verse: “Bhikkhu, do you remember the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’?”

mn133:2.2.verse: “Friend, I do not remember the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.

mn133:2.3.verse: But, friend, do you remember the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’?”

mn133:2.4.verse: “Bhikkhu, I too do not remember the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.

mn133:2.5.verse: But, bhikkhu, do you remember the stanzas of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’?”

mn133:2.6.verse: “Friend, I do not remember the stanzas of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.

mn133:2.7.verse: But, friend, do you remember the stanzas of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’?”

mn133:2.8.verse: “Bhikkhu, I too do not remember the stanzas of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.

mn133:2.9.verse: But, bhikkhu, learn the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.

mn133:2.10.verse: Bhikkhu, master the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.

mn133:2.11.verse: Bhikkhu, remember the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.

mn133:2.12.verse: Bhikkhu, the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’ is beneficial, it belongs to the fundamentals of the holy life.”

mn133:2.13.verse: That is what was said by the deity,

mn133:3.1.verse: Then, when the night was over, the venerable Samiddhi went to the Blessed One. After paying homage to him, he sat down at one side and told the Blessed One all that had occurred:

mn133:3.2.verse: “Here, venerable sir, when it was near dawn I went to the hot springs to bathe my limbs.

mn133:3.3.verse: After bathing I came up out of the water and stood dressed in one robe, drying my limbs.

mn133:3.4.verse: Then, venerable sir, when the night was well advanced, a certain deity of beautiful appearance who illuminated the whole of the Hot Springs, approached me. Standing at one side, the deity said to me:

mn133:3.5.verse: ‘Bhikkhu, do you remember the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”?’

mn133:4.1.verse: When this was said, venerable sir, I told that deity:

mn133:4.2.verse: ‘Friend, I do not remember the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.

mn133:4.3.verse: But, friend, do you remember the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”?’

mn133:4.4.verse: ‘Bhikkhu, I too do not remember the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.

mn133:4.5.verse: But, bhikkhu, do you remember the stanzas of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”?’

mn133:4.6.verse: ‘Friend, I do not remember the stanzas of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.

mn133:4.7.verse: But, friend, do you remember the stanzas of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”?’

mn133:4.8.verse: ‘Bhikkhu, I too do not remember the stanzas of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.

mn133:4.9.verse: But, bhikkhu, learn the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.

mn133:4.10.verse: Bhikkhu, master the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.

mn133:4.11.verse: Bhikkhu, remember the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.

mn133:4.12.verse: Bhikkhu, the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night” is beneficial, it belongs to the fundamentals of the holy life.’

mn133:4.13.verse: That is what was said by the deity, venerable sir,

mn133:4.15.verse: It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would teach me the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.”

mn133:4.16.verse: “Then, bhikkhu, listen and attend closely to what I shall say.”

mn133:4.17.verse: “Yes, venerable sir,” the venerable Samiddhi replied.

mn133:5.1.verse: “Let not a person revive the past

mn133:5.2.verse: Or on the future build his hopes;

mn133:5.3.verse: For the past has been left behind

mn133:5.4.verse: And the future has not been reached.

mn133:5.5.verse: Instead with insight let him see

mn133:5.7.verse: Let him know that and be sure of it,

mn133:5.9.verse: Today the effort must be made;

mn133:5.10.verse: Tomorrow Death may come, who knows?

mn133:5.12.verse: Can keep him and his hordes away.

mn133:5.13.verse: But one who dwells thus ardently,

mn133:5.15.verse: It is he, the Peaceful Sage has said,

mn133:5.16.verse: Who has had a single excellent night.”

mn133:6.1.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

mn133:6.2.verse: Having said this, the Sublime One rose from his seat and went into his dwelling.

mn133:7.1.verse: Then, soon after the Blessed One had gone, the bhikkhus considered:

mn133:7.2.verse: “Now, friends, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and gone into his dwelling after giving a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning:

mn133:7.3.verse: ‘Let not a person revive the past

mn133:7.4.verse: Or on the future build his hopes;

mn133:7.5.verse: For the past has been left behind

mn133:7.6.verse: And the future has not been reached.

mn133:7.7.verse: Instead with insight let him see

mn133:7.9.verse: Let him know that and be sure of it,

mn133:7.11.verse: Today the effort must be made;

mn133:7.12.verse: Tomorrow Death may come, who knows?

mn133:7.14.verse: Can keep him and his hordes away.

mn133:7.15.verse: But one who dwells thus ardently,

mn133:7.17.verse: It is he, the Peaceful Sage has said,

mn133:7.18.verse: Who has had a single excellent night.’

mn133:7.19.verse: Now who will expound this in detail?”

mn133:7.21.verse: “The venerable Mahā Kaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life.

mn133:7.22.verse: The venerable Mahā Kaccāna is capable of expounding the detailed meaning.

mn133:7.23.verse: Suppose we went to him and asked him the meaning of this.”

mn133:7.24.verse: Then the bhikkhus went to the venerable Mahā Kaccāna and exchanged greetings with him.

mn133:7.25.verse: When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, they sat down to one side and told the venerable Mahā Kaccāna what had taken place:

mn133:7.26.verse: “Friend Kaccāna, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and gone into his dwelling after giving a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning:

mn133:7.27.verse: ‘Let not a person revive the past…

mn133:7.29.verse: It is he, the Peaceful Sage has said,

mn133:7.30.verse: Who has had a single excellent night.’

mn133:7.31.verse: Then, friend Kaccāna, soon after the Blessed One had gone, we considered:

mn133:7.32.verse: ‘Now, friends, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and gone into his dwelling after giving a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning:

mn133:7.33.verse: “Let not a person revive the past…

mn133:7.35.verse: It is he, the Peaceful Sage has said,

mn133:7.36.verse: Who has had a single excellent night.”

mn133:8.1.verse: Now who will expound this in detail?’

mn133:8.3.verse: ‘The venerable Mahā Kaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life.

mn133:8.4.verse: The venerable Mahā Kaccāna is capable of expounding the detailed meaning.

mn133:8.5.verse: Suppose we went to him and asked him the meaning of this.’

mn133:8.6.verse: Let the venerable Mahā Kaccāna expound it to us.”

mn133:9.1.verse: [The venerable Mahā Kaccāna replied:] “Friends, it is as though a man needing heartwood, seeking heartwood, wandering in search of heartwood, thought that heartwood should be sought for among the branches and leaves of a great tree standing possessed of heartwood, after he had passed over the root and the trunk.

mn133:9.2.verse: And so it is with you, venerable sirs, that you think that I should be asked about the meaning of this, after you passed the Blessed One by when you were face to face with the Teacher.

mn133:9.3.verse: For knowing, the Blessed One knows; seeing, he sees; he is vision, he is knowledge, he is the Dhamma, he is the holy one; he is the sayer, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the giver of the Deathless, the lord of the Dhamma, the Tathāgata.

mn133:9.4.verse: That was the time when you should have asked the Blessed One the meaning. As he told you, so you should have remembered it.”

mn133:10.1.verse: “Surely, friend Kaccāna, knowing, the Blessed One knows; seeing, he sees; he is vision…the Tathāgata.

mn133:10.2.verse: That was the time when we should have asked the Blessed One the meaning.

mn133:10.3.verse: As he told us, so we should have remembered it.

mn133:10.4.verse: Yet the venerable Mahā Kaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life.

mn133:10.5.verse: The venerable Mahā Kaccāna is capable of expounding the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One without expounding the detailed meaning.

mn133:10.6.verse: Let the venerable Mahā Kaccāna expound it without finding it troublesome.”

mn133:11.1.verse: “Then listen, friends, and attend closely to what I shall say.”

mn133:11.3.verse: The venerable Mahā Kaccāna said this:

mn133:12.1.verse: “Friends, when the Blessed One rose from his seat and went into his dwelling after giving a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning, that is:

mn133:12.2.verse: ‘Let not a person revive the past…

mn133:12.4.verse: It is he, the Peaceful Sage has said,

mn133:12.5.verse: Who has had a single excellent night,’

mn133:13.1.verse: “How, friends, does one revive the past?

mn133:13.2.verse: One’s consciousness becomes bound up with desire and lust there thinking, ‘My eye was thus in the past and forms were thus.’

mn133:13.3.verse: Because one’s consciousness is bound up with desire and lust, one delights in that. When one delights in that, one revives the past.

mn133:13.4.verse: “One’s consciousness becomes bound up with desire and lust there thinking, ‘My ear was thus in the past and sounds were thus…

mn133:13.8.verse: My mind was thus in the past and mind-objects were thus.’

mn133:13.9.verse: Because one’s consciousness is bound up with desire and lust, one delights in that. When one delights in that, one revives the past.

mn133:13.10.verse: That is how one revives the past.

mn133:14.1.verse: “How does one not revive the past?

mn133:14.2.verse: One’s consciousness does not become bound up with desire and lust there thinking, ‘My eye was thus in the past and forms were thus.’

mn133:14.3.verse: Because one’s consciousness is not bound up with desire and lust, one does not delight in that. When one does not delight in that, one does not revive the past.

mn133:14.4.verse: “One’s consciousness does not become bound up with desire and lust there thinking, ‘My ear was thus in the past and sounds were thus…

mn133:14.8.verse: My mind was thus in the past and mind-objects were thus.’

mn133:14.9.verse: Because one’s consciousness is not bound up with desire and lust, one does not delight in that. When one does not delight in that, one does not revive the past.

mn133:14.10.verse: That is how one does not revive the past.

mn133:15.1.verse: “How, friends, does one build up hope upon the future?

mn133:15.2.verse: One sets one’s heart on obtaining what has not yet been obtained, thinking, ‘May my eye be thus in the future and forms be thus!’

mn133:15.3.verse: Because one sets one’s heart thus, one delights in that. When one delights in that, one builds up hope upon the future.

mn133:15.4.verse: “One sets one’s heart on obtaining what has not yet been obtained, thinking, ‘May my ear be thus in the future and sounds be thus!…

mn133:15.8.verse: May my mind be thus in the future and mind-objects be thus!’

mn133:15.9.verse: Because one sets one’s heart thus, one delights in that. When one delights in that, one builds up hope upon the future.

mn133:15.10.verse: That is how one builds up hope upon the future.

mn133:16.1.verse: “How, friends, does one not build up hope upon the future?

mn133:16.2.verse: One does not set one’s heart on obtaining what has not yet been obtained, thinking, ‘May my eye be thus in the future and forms be thus!’

mn133:16.3.verse: Because one does not set one’s heart thus, one does not delight in that. When one does not delight in that, one does not build up hope upon the future.

mn133:16.4.verse: “One does not set one’s heart on obtaining what has not yet been obtained, thinking, ‘May my ear be thus in the future and sounds be thus!…

mn133:16.8.verse: May my mind be thus in the future and mind-objects be thus!’

mn133:16.9.verse: Because one does not set one’s heart thus, one does not delight in that. When one does not delight in that, one does not build up hope upon the future.

mn133:16.10.verse: That is how one does not build up hope upon the future.

mn133:17.1.verse: “How is one vanquished in regard to presently arisen states?

mn133:17.2.verse: In regard to the eye and forms—

mn133:17.3.verse: both of which are presently arisen—

mn133:17.4.verse: one’s consciousness is bound up with desire and lust for that which is presently arisen. Because one’s consciousness is bound up with desire and lust, one delights in that. When one delights in that, one is vanquished in regard to presently arisen states.

mn133:17.5.verse: “In regard to the ear and sounds…

mn133:17.10.verse: both of which are presently arisen—

mn133:17.11.verse: one’s consciousness is bound up with desire and lust for that which is presently arisen. Because one’s consciousness is bound up with desire and lust, one delights in that. When one delights in that, one is vanquished in regard to presently arisen states.

mn133:17.12.verse: That is how one is vanquished in regard to presently arisen states.

mn133:18.1.verse: “How is one invincible in regard to presently arisen states?

mn133:18.2.verse: In regard to the eye and forms—

mn133:18.3.verse: both of which are presently arisen—

mn133:18.4.verse: one’s consciousness is not bound up with desire and lust for that which is presently arisen. Because one’s consciousness is not bound up with desire and lust, one does not delight in that. When one does not delight in that, one is invincible in regard to presently arisen states.

mn133:18.5.verse: “In regard to the ear and sounds…

mn133:18.10.verse: both of which are presently arisen—

mn133:18.11.verse: one’s consciousness is not bound up with desire and lust for that which is presently arisen. Because one’s consciousness is not bound up with desire and lust, one does not delight in that. When one does not delight in that, one is invincible in regard to presently arisen states.

mn133:18.12.verse: That is how one is invincible in regard to presently arisen states.

mn133:19.1.verse: “Friends, when the Blessed One rose from his seat and went into his dwelling after giving a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning, that is:

mn133:19.2.verse: ‘Let not a person revive the past…

mn133:19.4.verse: It is he, the Peaceful Sage has said,

mn133:19.5.verse: Who has had a single excellent night,’

mn133:20.1.verse: Then the bhikkhus, having delighted and rejoiced in the venerable Mahā Kaccāna’s words, rose from their seats and went to the Blessed One. After paying homage to him, they sat down at one side and told the Blessed One all that had taken place after he had left:

mn133:20.2.verse: “Venerable sir, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and gone into his dwelling after giving a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning:

mn133:20.3.verse: ‘Let not a person revive the past…

mn133:20.5.verse: It is he, the Peaceful Sage has said,

mn133:20.6.verse: Who has had a single excellent night.’

mn133:20.7.verse: Then, venerable sir, soon after the Blessed One had gone, we considered:

mn133:20.8.verse: ‘Now, friends, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and gone into his dwelling after giving a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning:

mn133:20.9.verse: “Let not a person revive the past

mn133:20.10.verse: Or on the future build his hopes;

mn133:20.11.verse: For the past has been left behind

mn133:20.12.verse: And the future has not been reached.

mn133:20.13.verse: Instead with insight let him see

mn133:20.15.verse: Let him know that and be sure of it,

mn133:20.17.verse: Today the effort must be made;

mn133:20.18.verse: Tomorrow Death may come, who knows?

mn133:20.20.verse: Can keep him and his hordes away.

mn133:20.21.verse: But one who dwells thus ardently,

mn133:20.23.verse: It is he, the Peaceful Sage has said,

mn133:20.24.verse: Who has had a single excellent night.”

mn133:20.25.verse: Now who will expound this in detail?’

mn133:20.27.verse: ‘The venerable Mahā Kaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life.

mn133:20.28.verse: The venerable Mahā Kaccāna is capable of expounding the detailed meaning.

mn133:20.29.verse: Suppose we went to him and asked him the meaning of this.’

mn133:20.30.verse: Then, venerable sir, we went to the venerable Mahā Kaccāna and asked him about the meaning.

mn133:20.31.verse: The venerable Mahā Kaccāna expounded the meaning to us with these terms, statements, and phrases.”

mn133:21.1.verse: “Mahā Kaccāna is wise, bhikkhus, Mahā Kaccāna has great wisdom.

mn133:21.2.verse: If you had asked me the meaning of this, I would have explained it to you in the same way that Mahā Kaccāna has explained it.

mn133:21.3.verse: Such is its meaning, and so you should remember it.”

mn133:21.4.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

mn133:21.5.verse: The bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn134:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn134:1.3.verse: Now at that time Venerable Lomasakaṅgiya was staying in the Sakyan country at Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

mn134:2.1.verse: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Candana, lighting up the entire Banyan Tree Monastery, went up to the Venerable Lomasakaṅgiya, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, he said to Lomasakaṅgiya:

mn134:2.2.verse: “Mendicant, do you remember the summary recital and the analysis of the one who has one fine night?”

mn134:2.6.verse: But do you remember just the verses on the one who has one fine night?”

mn134:2.10.verse: “How do you remember the verses on the one who has one fine night?”

mn134:2.11.verse: “This one time, the Buddha was staying among the gods of the thirty-three at the root of the Orchid Tree on the stone spread with a cream rug.

mn134:2.12.verse: There he taught the summary recital and the analysis of the one who has one fine night to the gods of the thirty-three:

mn134:3.6.verse: you clearly discern in every case.

mn134:3.9.verse: Today’s the day to keenly work—

mn134:3.10.verse: who knows, tomorrow may bring death!

mn134:3.11.verse: For there is no bargain to be struck

mn134:3.12.verse: with Death and his mighty horde.

mn134:3.13.verse: One who keenly meditates like this,

mn134:3.15.verse: that’s who has one fine night—

mn134:4.1.verse: That’s how I remember the verses of the one who has one fine night.

mn134:4.2.verse: Learn the summary recital and the analysis of the one who has one fine night, mendicant,

mn134:4.5.verse: It is beneficial and relevant to the fundamentals of the spiritual life.”

mn134:4.6.verse: That is what the godling Candana said

mn134:5.1.verse: Then Lomasakaṅgiya set his lodgings in order and, taking his bowl and robe, set out for Sāvatthī.

mn134:5.2.verse: Eventually he came to Sāvatthī and Jeta’s Grove. He went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. Then he added:

mn134:5.28.verse: “Sir, please teach me the summary recital and the analysis of the one who has one fine night.”

mn134:6.1.verse: “But mendicant, do you know that god?”

mn134:6.4.verse: Candana pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens to the teaching.

mn134:6.5.verse: Well then, mendicant, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

mn134:7.6.verse: you clearly discern in every case.

mn134:7.9.verse: Today’s the day to keenly work—

mn134:7.10.verse: who knows, tomorrow may bring death!

mn134:7.11.verse: For there is no bargain to be struck

mn134:7.12.verse: with Death and his mighty horde.

mn134:7.13.verse: One who keenly meditates like this,

mn134:7.15.verse: that’s who has one fine night—

mn134:8-13.1.verse: And how do you run back to the past? …”

mn134:14.17.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn134:14.18.verse: Satisfied, Venerable Lomasakaṅgiya approved what the Buddha said.

mn134:0.2.verse: Lomasakangiya and A Single Excellent Night

mn134:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

mn134:1.3.verse: Now on that occasion the venerable Lomasakangiya was living in the Sakyan country at Kapilavatthu in Nigrodha’s Park.

mn134:2.1.verse: Then, when the night was well advanced, Candana, a young deity of beautiful appearance who illuminated the whole of Nigrodha’s Park, approached the venerable Lomasakangiya. Standing at one side, Candana the young deity said to him:

mn134:2.2.verse: “Bhikkhu, do you remember the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’?”

mn134:2.3.verse: “Friend, I do not remember the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.

mn134:2.4.verse: But, friend, do you remember the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’?”

mn134:2.5.verse: “Bhikkhu, I too do not remember the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.

mn134:2.6.verse: But, bhikkhu, do you remember the stanza of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’?”

mn134:2.7.verse: “Friend, I do not remember the stanza of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.

mn134:2.8.verse: But, friend, do you remember the stanza of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’?”

mn134:2.9.verse: “Bhikkhu, I remember the stanza of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.”

mn134:2.10.verse: “But, friend, in what way do you remember the stanza of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’?”

mn134:2.11.verse: “Bhikkhu, once the Blessed One was living among the gods of the heaven of the Thirty-three, on the Red Marble Stone at the root of the Pāricchattaka tree.

mn134:2.12.verse: There the Blessed One recited the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’ to the gods of the heaven of the Thirty-three:

mn134:3.1.verse: ‘Let not a person revive the past

mn134:3.2.verse: Or on the future build his hopes;

mn134:3.3.verse: For the past has been left behind

mn134:3.4.verse: And the future has not been reached.

mn134:3.5.verse: Instead with insight let him see

mn134:3.7.verse: Let him know that and be sure of it,

mn134:3.9.verse: Today the effort must be made;

mn134:3.10.verse: Tomorrow Death may come, who knows?

mn134:3.12.verse: Can keep him and his hordes away.

mn134:3.13.verse: But one who dwells thus ardently,

mn134:3.15.verse: It is he, the Peaceful Sage has said,

mn134:3.16.verse: Who has had a single excellent night.’

mn134:4.1.verse: “Bhikkhu, I remember the stanza of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’ thus.

mn134:4.2.verse: Bhikkhu, learn the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.

mn134:4.3.verse: Bhikkhu, master the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had A Single Excellent Night.’

mn134:4.4.verse: Bhikkhu, remember the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.

mn134:4.5.verse: Bhikkhu, the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’ is beneficial, it belongs to the fundamentals of the holy life.”

mn134:4.6.verse: That is what was said by Candana the young deity,

mn134:5.1.verse: Then, when the night was over, the venerable Lomasakangiya set his resting place in order, and taking his bowl and outer robe, set out to wander by stages to Sāvatthī.

mn134:5.2.verse: He at length arrived at Sāvatthī, and went to the Blessed One in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. After paying homage to him, he sat down at one side and told the Blessed One all that had occurred:

mn134:5.3.verse: “Venerable sir, on one occasion I was living in the Sakyan country at Kapilavatthu in Nigrodha’s Park.

mn134:5.4.verse: Then, venerable sir, when the night was well advanced, a certain young deity of beautiful appearance who illuminated the whole of Nigrodha’s Park, approached me. Standing at one side, that young deity said to me:

mn134:5.5.verse: ‘Bhikkhu, do you remember the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”?’

mn134:5.6.verse: When this was said, venerable sir, I told that young deity:

mn134:5.7.verse: ‘Friend, I do not remember the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.

mn134:5.8.verse: But, friend, do you remember the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”?’

mn134:5.9.verse: ‘Bhikkhu, I too do not remember the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.

mn134:5.10.verse: But, bhikkhu, do you remember the stanza of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”?’

mn134:5.11.verse: ‘Friend, I do not remember the stanza of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.

mn134:5.12.verse: But, friend, do you remember the stanza of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”?’

mn134:5.13.verse: ‘Bhikkhu, I remember the stanza of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.’

mn134:5.14.verse: ‘But, friend, in what way do you remember the stanza of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”?’

mn134:5.15.verse: ‘Bhikkhu, once the Blessed One was living among the gods of the heaven of the Thirty-three, on the Red Marble Stone at the root of the Pāricchattaka tree.

mn134:5.16.verse: There the Blessed One recited the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night” to the gods of the heaven of the Thirty-three:

mn134:5.17.verse: “Let not a person revive the past…

mn134:5.19.verse: It is he, the Peaceful Sage has said,

mn134:5.20.verse: Who has had a single excellent night.”

mn134:5.21.verse: Bhikkhu, I remember the stanza of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night” thus.

mn134:5.22.verse: Bhikkhu, learn the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.

mn134:5.23.verse: Bhikkhu, master the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.

mn134:5.24.verse: Bhikkhu, remember the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night”.

mn134:5.25.verse: Bhikkhu, the summary and exposition of “One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night” is beneficial, it belongs to the fundamentals of the holy life.’

mn134:5.26.verse: That is what was said by that young deity, venerable sir,

mn134:5.28.verse: It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would teach me the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’.”

mn134:6.1.verse: “Bhikkhu, do you know that young deity?”

mn134:6.3.verse: “Bhikkhu, that young deity is named Candana.

mn134:6.4.verse: He heeds the Dhamma, gives it attention, engages it with all his mind, hears it with eager ears.

mn134:6.5.verse: So, bhikkhu, listen and attend closely to what I shall say.”

mn134:6.6.verse: “Yes, venerable sir,” the venerable Lomasakangiya replied to the Blessed One.
