mn134:7.2.verse: Or on the future build his hopes;

mn134:7.3.verse: For the past has been left behind

mn134:7.4.verse: And the future has not been reached.

mn134:7.5.verse: Instead with insight let him see

mn134:7.7.verse: Let him know that and be sure of it,

mn134:7.9.verse: Today the effort must be made;

mn134:7.10.verse: Tomorrow Death may come, who knows?

mn134:7.12.verse: Can keep him and his hordes away.

mn134:7.13.verse: But one who dwells thus ardently,

mn134:7.15.verse: It is he, the Peaceful Sage has said,

mn134:7.16.verse: Who has had a single excellent night.

mn134:8-13.2.verse: That is how, bhikkhu, one revives the past.

mn134:8-13.3.verse: And how, bhikkhu, does one not revive the past?…

mn134:8-13.4.verse: That is how, bhikkhu, one does not revive the past.

mn134:8-13.5.verse: And how, bhikkhu, does one build up hope upon the future?…

mn134:8-13.6.verse: That is how, bhikkhu, one builds up hope upon the future.

mn134:8-13.7.verse: And how, bhikkhu, does one not build up hope upon the future?…

mn134:8-13.8.verse: That is how, bhikkhu, one does not build up hope upon the future.

mn134:8-13.9.verse: And how, bhikkhu, is one vanquished in regard to presently arisen states?…

mn134:8-13.10.verse: That is how, bhikkhu, one is vanquished in regard to presently arisen states.

mn134:8-13.11.verse: And how, bhikkhu, is one invincible in regard to presently arisen states?…

mn134:8-13.12.verse: That is how, bhikkhu, one is invincible in regard to presently arisen states.

mn134:14.2.verse: Or on the future build his hopes;

mn134:14.7.verse: Let him know that and be sure of it,

mn134:14.12.verse: Can keep him and his hordes away.

mn134:14.17.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

mn134:14.18.verse: The venerable Lomasakangiya was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn135:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

mn135:2.1.verse: Then the student Subha, Todeyya’s son, went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.

mn135:2.2.verse: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, the student Subha, Todeyya’s son, said to the Blessed One:

mn135:3.1.verse: ‘Master Gotama, what is the reason, what is the condition, why inferiority and superiority are met with among human beings, among mankind?

mn135:3.2.verse: For, Master Gotama, one meets with short-lived men, one meets with long-lived men;

mn135:3.3.verse: one meets with sickly men, one meets with healthy men;

mn135:3.4.verse: one meets with ugly men, one meets with beautiful men;

mn135:3.5.verse: one meets with insignificant men, one meets with influential men;

mn135:3.6.verse: one meets with poor men, one meets with rich men;

mn135:3.7.verse: one meets with low-born men, one meets with high-born men;

mn135:3.8.verse: one meets with stupid men, one meets with wise men.

mn135:3.9.verse: What is the reason, Master Gotama, what is the condition, why inferiority and superiority are met with among human beings, among mankind?’

mn135:4.1.verse: ‘Student, beings are owners of kammas, heirs of kammas, they have kammas as their progenitor, kammas as their kin, kammas as their homing-place.

mn135:4.2.verse: It is kammas that differentiate beings, that is to say,

mn135:4.4.verse: ‘I do not understand the detailed meaning of Master Gotama’s utterance, spoken in brief without expounding the detailed meaning.

mn135:4.5.verse: It would be good if Master Gotama taught me the Dhamma so that I might understand the detailed meaning of Master Gotama’s utterance, spoken in brief without expounding the detailed meaning.’

mn135:4.6.verse: ‘Then, student, listen and heed well what I shall say.’

mn135:4.7.verse: ‘Yes, sir,’ the student Subha, Todeyya’s son, replied to the Blessed One.

mn135:5.1.verse: ‘Here, student, some woman or man is a killer of living beings, murderous, bloody-handed, given to blows and violence, merciless to all living beings.

mn135:5.2.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn135:5.3.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is short-lived wherever he is reborn.

mn135:5.4.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to a short life, that is to say,

mn135:5.5.verse: to be a killer of living beings, murderous, bloody-handed, given to blows and violence, merciless to all living beings.

mn135:6.1.verse: ‘But here, student, some woman or man, having abandoned the killing of living beings, abstains from killing living beings; with rod and knife laid aside, conscientious and merciful, he abides compassionate for the welfare of all living beings.

mn135:6.2.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn135:6.3.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is long-lived wherever he is reborn.

mn135:6.4.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to a long life, that is to say,

mn135:6.5.verse: having abandoned the killing of living beings, to abstain from killing living beings; with rod and knife laid aside, conscientious and merciful, to abide compassionate for the welfare of all living beings.

mn135:7.1.verse: ‘Here, student, some woman or man is given to persecuting beings with the hand, or with a clod, or with a stick, or with a knife.

mn135:7.2.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn135:7.3.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is sickly wherever he is reborn.

mn135:7.4.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to sickliness, that is to say,

mn135:7.5.verse: to be given to persecuting beings with the hand, or with a clod, or with a stick, or with a knife.

mn135:8.1.verse: ‘But here, student, some woman or man is not given to persecuting beings with the hand, or with a clod, or with a stick, or with a knife.

mn135:8.2.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn135:8.3.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is healthy wherever he is reborn.

mn135:8.4.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to health, that is to say,

mn135:8.5.verse: not to be given to persecuting beings with the hand, or with a clod, or with a stick, or with a knife.

mn135:9.1.verse: ‘Here, student, some woman or man is angry and much given to rage.

mn135:9.2.verse: Even when little is said, he is furious, angered, ill-disposed, resentful, and he shows ill-temper, hatred, and bitterness.

mn135:9.3.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn135:9.4.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is ugly wherever he is reborn.

mn135:9.5.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to ugliness, that is to say,

mn135:9.6.verse: to be angry and much given to rage;

mn135:9.7.verse: even when little is said, to be furious, angered, ill-disposed, resentful, and to show ill-temper, hatred, and bitterness.

mn135:10.1.verse: ‘But here, student, some woman or man is not angry, nor much given to rage;

mn135:10.2.verse: even when much is said, he is not furious, angered, ill-disposed, resentful, nor does he show ill-temper, hatred, and bitterness.

mn135:10.3.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn135:10.4.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is beautiful wherever he is reborn.

mn135:10.5.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to beauty, that is to say,

mn135:10.6.verse: not to be angry, nor much given to rage;

mn135:10.7.verse: even when much is said, not to be furious, angered, ill-disposed, resentful, nor to show ill-temper, hatred, and bitterness.

mn135:11.1.verse: ‘Here, student, some woman or man has an envious nature;

mn135:11.2.verse: he envies, begrudges, and harbours envy about others’ gains, honour, veneration, respect, salutations, and offerings.

mn135:11.3.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn135:11.4.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is insignificant wherever he is reborn.

mn135:11.5.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to insignificance, that is to say,

mn135:11.7.verse: to envy, begrudge, and harbour envy about others’ gains, honour, veneration, respect, salutations, and offerings.

mn135:12.1.verse: ‘But here, student, some woman or man does not have an envious nature;

mn135:12.2.verse: he does not envy, begrudge, or harbour envy about others’ gains, honour, veneration, respect, salutations, and offerings.

mn135:12.3.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn135:12.4.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is influential wherever he is reborn.

mn135:12.5.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to influence, that is to say,

mn135:12.6.verse: not to have an envious nature;

mn135:12.7.verse: not to envy, begrudge, or harbour envy about others’ gains, honour, veneration, respect, salutations, and offerings.

mn135:13.1.verse: ‘Here, student, some woman or man is not a giver of food, drink, clothing, a vehicle, garlands, scent, unguent, bedding, dwelling, and lighting to ascetics or brahmins.

mn135:13.2.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn135:13.3.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is poor wherever he is reborn.

mn135:13.4.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to poverty, that is to say,

mn135:13.5.verse: not to be a giver of food, drink, clothing, a vehicle, garlands, scent, unguent, bedding, dwelling, and lighting to ascetics or brahmins.

mn135:14.1.verse: ‘But here, student, some woman or man is a giver of food, drink, clothing, a vehicle, garlands, scent, unguent, bedding, dwelling, and lighting to ascetics or brahmins.

mn135:14.2.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn135:14.3.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is rich wherever he is reborn.

mn135:14.4.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to riches, that is to say,

mn135:14.5.verse: to be a giver of food, drink, clothing, a vehicle, garlands, scent, unguent, bedding, dwelling, and lighting to ascetics or brahmins.

mn135:15.1.verse: ‘Here, student, some woman or man is obstinate and arrogant—

mn135:15.2.verse: he does not pay homage to one who should be paid homage, does not rise up for one for whom he should rise up, does not give a seat to one who deserves a seat, does not make way for one for whom he should make way, does not honour one who should be honoured, does not respect one who should be respected, does not esteem one who should be esteemed, does not revere one who should be revered.

mn135:15.3.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn135:15.4.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is low-born wherever he is reborn.

mn135:15.5.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to low birth, that is to say,

mn135:15.7.verse: not to pay homage to one who should be paid homage, not to rise up for one for whom he should rise up, not to give a seat to one who deserves a seat, not to make way for one for whom he should make way, not to honour one who should be honoured, not to respect one who should be respected, not to esteem one who should be esteemed, not to revere one who should be revered.

mn135:16.1.verse: ‘But here, student, some woman or man is not obstinate, nor arrogant;

mn135:16.2.verse: he pays homage to one who should be paid homage, rises up for one for whom he should rise up, gives a seat to one who deserves a seat, makes way for one for whom he should make way, honours one who should be honoured, respects one who should be respected, esteems one who should be esteemed, reveres one who should be revered.

mn135:16.3.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn135:16.4.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is high-born wherever he is reborn.

mn135:16.5.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to high birth, that is to say,

mn135:16.6.verse: not to be obstinate, nor arrogant;

mn135:16.7.verse: to pay homage to one who should be paid homage, to rise up for one for whom he should rise up, to give a seat to one who deserves a seat, to make way for one for whom he should make way, to honour one who should be honoured, to respect one who should be respected, to esteem one who should be esteemed, to revere one who should be revered.

mn135:17.1.verse: ‘Here, student, some woman or man, on visiting an ascetic or a brahmin, does not ask:

mn135:17.2.verse: “What, venerable sir, is profitable, what is unprofitable;

mn135:17.3.verse: what is blamable, what is blameless;

mn135:17.4.verse: what should be cultivated, what should not be cultivated;

mn135:17.5.verse: what, by my doing it, will be for my harm and suffering for a long time, or what, by my doing it, will be for my welfare and happiness for a long time?”

mn135:17.6.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn135:17.7.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is stupid wherever he is reborn.

mn135:17.8.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to stupidity, that is to say,

mn135:17.9.verse: on visiting an ascetic or a brahmin, not to ask:

mn135:17.10.verse: “What, venerable sir, is profitable, what is unprofitable;

mn135:17.11.verse: what is blamable, what is blameless;

mn135:17.12.verse: what should be cultivated, what should not be cultivated;

mn135:17.13.verse: what, by my doing it, will be for my harm and suffering for a long time, or what, by my doing it, will be for my welfare and happiness for a long time?”

mn135:18.1.verse: ‘But here, student, some woman or man, on visiting an ascetic or a brahmin, asks:

mn135:18.2.verse: “What, venerable sir, is profitable, what is unprofitable;

mn135:18.3.verse: what is blamable, what is blameless;

mn135:18.4.verse: what should be cultivated, what should not be cultivated;

mn135:18.5.verse: what, by my doing it, will be for my harm and suffering for a long time, or what, by my doing it, will be for my welfare and happiness for a long time?”

mn135:18.6.verse: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn135:18.7.verse: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is wise wherever he is reborn.

mn135:18.8.verse: This, student, is the way that leads to wisdom, that is to say,

mn135:18.9.verse: on visiting an ascetic or a brahmin, to ask:

mn135:18.10.verse: “What, venerable sir, is profitable, what is unprofitable;

mn135:18.11.verse: what is blamable, what is blameless;

mn135:18.12.verse: what should be cultivated, what should not be cultivated;

mn135:18.13.verse: what, by my doing it, will be for my harm and suffering for a long time, or what, by my doing it, will be for my welfare and happiness for a long time?”

mn135:19.1.verse: ‘So, student, the way that leads to a short life makes men short-lived, the way that leads to a long life makes men long-lived;

mn135:19.2.verse: the way that leads to sickliness makes men sickly, the way that leads to health makes men healthy;

mn135:19.3.verse: the way that leads to ugliness makes men ugly, the way that leads to beauty makes men beautiful;

mn135:19.4.verse: the way that leads to insignificance makes men insignificant, the way that leads to influence makes men influential;

mn135:19.5.verse: the way that leads to poverty makes men poor, the way that leads to riches makes men rich;

mn135:19.6.verse: the way that leads to low birth makes men low-born, the way that leads to high birth makes men high-born;

mn135:19.7.verse: the way that leads to stupidity makes men stupid, the way that leads to wisdom makes men wise.

mn135:20.1.verse: ‘Beings, student, are owners of kammas, heirs of kammas, they have kammas as their progenitor, kammas as their kin, kammas as their homing-place.

mn135:20.2.verse: It is kammas that differentiate beings, that is to say,

mn135:21.1.verse: When this was said, the student Subha, Todeyya’s son, said to the Blessed One:

mn135:21.3.verse: Master Gotama has made the Dhamma clear in many ways, as though he were turning upright what had been overthrown, revealing what was hidden, showing the way to one who was lost, or holding up a lamp in the dark for those with eyes to see forms.

mn135:21.4.verse: I go to Master Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.

mn135:21.5.verse: From today let Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone to him for refuge for life.’

mn135:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn135:2.1.verse: Then the student Subha, Todeyya’s son, approached the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

mn135:2.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

mn135:3.1.verse: “What is the cause, worthy Gotama, what is the reason why even among those who are human beings some are seen to be inferior and superior?

mn135:3.2.verse: For people are seen who are short-lived and long-lived,

mn135:3.9.verse: What is the reason why even among those who are human beings some are seen to be inferior and superior?”

mn135:4.1.verse: “Student, sentient beings are the owners of their deeds and heir to their deeds. Deeds are their womb, their relative, and their refuge.

mn135:4.2.verse: It is deeds that divide beings into

mn135:4.4.verse: “I don’t understand the meaning of what the worthy Gotama has said in brief, without explaining the details.

mn135:4.5.verse: Worthy Gotama, please teach me this matter in detail so I can understand the meaning.”

mn135:4.6.verse: “Well then, student, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

mn135:5.1.verse: “Take some woman or man who kills living creatures. They’re violent, bloody-handed, a hardened killer, merciless to living beings.

mn135:5.2.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

mn135:5.3.verse: If they’re not reborn in a place of loss, but return to the human realm, then wherever they’re reborn they’re short-lived.

mn135:5.4.verse: For killing living creatures is the path leading to a short lifespan.

mn135:6.1.verse: But take some woman or man who gives up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They’re scrupulous and kind, living full of sympathy for all living beings.

mn135:6.2.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

mn135:6.3.verse: If they’re not reborn in a heavenly realm, but return to the human realm, then wherever they’re reborn they’re long-lived.

mn135:6.4.verse: For not killing living creatures is the path leading to a long lifespan.

mn135:7.1.verse: Take some woman or man who habitually hurts living creatures with a fist, stone, rod, or sword.

mn135:7.2.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, after death they’re reborn in a place of loss …

mn135:7.3.verse: or if they return to the human realm, they’re sickly …

mn135:8.1.verse: But take some woman or man who would never hurt living creatures with a fist, stone, rod, or sword.

mn135:8.2.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, after death they’re reborn in a heavenly realm …

mn135:8.3.verse: or if they return to the human realm, they’re healthy …

mn135:9.1.verse: Take some woman or man who is irritable and bad-tempered.

mn135:9.2.verse: Even when lightly criticized they lose their temper, becoming annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, and displaying annoyance, hate, and bitterness.

mn135:9.3.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, after death they’re reborn in a place of loss …

mn135:9.4.verse: or if they return to the human realm, they’re ugly …

mn135:10.1.verse: But take some woman or man who isn’t irritable and bad-tempered.

mn135:10.2.verse: Even when heavily criticized, they don’t lose their temper, become annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, or display annoyance, hate, and bitterness.

mn135:10.3.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, after death they’re reborn in a heavenly realm …

mn135:10.4.verse: or if they return to the human realm, they’re lovely …

mn135:11.1.verse: Take some woman or man who is jealous.

mn135:11.2.verse: They envy, resent, and begrudge the possessions, honor, respect, reverence, homage, and veneration given to others.

mn135:11.3.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, after death they’re reborn in a place of loss …

mn135:11.4.verse: or if they return to the human realm, they’re insignificant …

mn135:12.1.verse: But take some woman or man who is not jealous …

mn135:12.3.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, after death they’re reborn in a heavenly realm …

mn135:12.4.verse: or if they return to the human realm, they’re illustrious …

mn135:13.1.verse: Take some woman or man who doesn’t give to ascetics or brahmins such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

mn135:13.2.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, after death they’re reborn in a place of loss …

mn135:13.3.verse: or if they return to the human realm, they’re poor …

mn135:14.1.verse: But take some woman or man who does give to ascetics or brahmins …

mn135:14.2.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, after death they’re reborn in a heavenly realm …

mn135:14.3.verse: or if they return to the human realm, they’re rich …

mn135:15.1.verse: Take some woman or man who is obstinate and arrogant.

mn135:15.2.verse: They don’t bow to those they should bow to. They don’t rise up for them, offer them a seat, make way for them, or honor, respect, esteem, or venerate those who are worthy of such.

mn135:15.3.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, after death they’re reborn in a place of loss …

mn135:15.4.verse: or if they return to the human realm, they’re reborn in a low class family …

mn135:16.1.verse: But take some woman or man who is not obstinate and arrogant …

mn135:16.3.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, after death they’re reborn in a heavenly realm …

mn135:16.4.verse: or if they return to the human realm, they’re reborn in an eminent family …

mn135:17.1.verse: Take some woman or man who doesn’t approach an ascetic or brahmin to ask:

mn135:17.2.verse: ‘Sir, what is skillful and what is unskillful?

mn135:17.3.verse: What is blameworthy and what is blameless?

mn135:17.4.verse: What should be cultivated and what should not be cultivated?

mn135:17.5.verse: What kind of action will lead to my lasting harm and suffering? Or what kind of action will lead to my lasting welfare and happiness?’

mn135:17.6.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, after death they’re reborn in a place of loss …

mn135:17.7.verse: or if they return to the human realm, they’re witless …

mn135:18.1.verse: But take some woman or man who does approach an ascetic or brahmin to ask:

mn135:18.2.verse: ‘Sir, what is skillful and what is unskillful?

mn135:18.3.verse: What is blameworthy and what is blameless?

mn135:18.4.verse: What should be cultivated and what should not be cultivated?

mn135:18.5.verse: What kind of action will lead to my lasting harm and suffering? Or what kind of action will lead to my lasting welfare and happiness?’

mn135:18.6.verse: Because of undertaking such deeds, when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

mn135:18.7.verse: If they’re not reborn in a heavenly realm, but return to the human realm, then wherever they’re reborn they’re very wise.

mn135:18.8.verse: For asking questions of ascetics or brahmins is the path leading to wisdom.

mn135:19.1.verse: So it is the way people live that makes them how they are, whether short-lived or long-lived,

mn135:19.6.verse: in a low class or eminent family,

mn135:20.1.verse: Sentient beings are the owners of their deeds and heir to their deeds. Deeds are their womb, their relative, and their refuge.

mn135:20.2.verse: It is deeds that divide beings into

mn135:21.1.verse: When he had spoken, Subha said to him,

mn135:21.3.verse: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the Teaching clear in many ways.

mn135:21.4.verse: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

mn135:21.5.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

mn136:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.

mn136:2.1.verse: Now on that occasion the venerable Samiddhi was living in a forest hut.

mn136:2.2.verse: Then the wanderer Potaliputta, while walking and wandering for exercise, went to the venerable Samiddhi and exchanged greetings with him.

mn136:2.3.verse: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, the wanderer Potaliputta said to the venerable Samiddhi:

mn136:2.4.verse: ‘I heard and learned this, friend Samiddhi, in the ascetic Gotama’s own presence:

mn136:2.5.verse: “Bodily kamma is vain, verbal kamma is vain, only mental kamma is real.”

mn136:2.6.verse: And is there that attainment, having entered upon which one feels nothing at all?’

mn136:2.7.verse: ‘Not so, friend Potaliputta, do not say that; not so, friend Potaliputta, do not say that; do not misrepresent the Blessed One. It is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One. The Blessed One would not say thus:

mn136:2.8.verse: “Bodily kamma is vain, verbal kamma is vain, only mental kamma is real.”

mn136:2.9.verse: But, friend, there is that attainment, having entered upon which one feels nothing at all.’

mn136:2.10.verse: ‘How long is it since you went forth, friend Samiddhi?’

mn136:2.12.verse: ‘What then shall we say to the elder bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu so new fancies the Teacher must be defended thus?

mn136:2.13.verse: After doing intentional kamma, friend Samiddhi, by body, by speech, or by mind, what does one feel?’

mn136:2.14.verse: ‘After doing intentional kamma, friend Potaliputta, by body, by speech, or by mind, one feels suffering.’

mn136:2.15.verse: Then the wanderer Potaliputta neither approved nor disapproved of the venerable Samiddhi’s words;

mn136:2.16.verse: neither approving nor disapproving, he got up from his seat and departed.

mn136:3.1.verse: Then, soon after the wanderer Potaliputta had gone, the venerable Samiddhi went to the venerable Ānanda and exchanged greetings with him.

mn136:3.2.verse: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side.

mn136:3.3.verse: When he had done so, the venerable Samiddhi told the venerable Ānanda all his conversation with the wanderer Potaliputta.

mn136:3.4.verse: When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the venerable Samiddhi:

mn136:3.5.verse: ‘This conversation, friend Samiddhi, is a matter to be brought to the Blessed One’s attention.

mn136:3.6.verse: Come, friend Samiddhi, let us go to the Blessed One, and, having approached, let us report this matter to him.

mn136:3.7.verse: As the Blessed One explains it to us, so we shall bear it in mind.’

mn136:3.8.verse: ‘Yes, friend,’ the venerable Samiddhi replied to the venerable Ānanda.

mn136:4.1.verse: Then the venerable Ānanda and the venerable Samiddhi went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, they sat down at one side.

mn136:4.2.verse: When they had done so, the venerable Ānanda told the Blessed One all the venerable Samiddhi’s conversation with the wanderer Potaliputta.

mn136:5.1.verse: When this was said, the Blessed One said to the venerable Ānanda:

mn136:5.2.verse: ‘I do not even recall having seen the wanderer Potaliputta, Ānanda—how, then, could there have been such a conversation?

mn136:5.3.verse: The wanderer Potaliputta’s question, which ought to have been answered after analysing it, was answered without qualification by this misguided man Samiddhi.’

mn136:6.1.verse: When this was said, the venerable Udāyī said to the Blessed One:

mn136:6.2.verse: ‘But, venerable sir, perhaps the venerable Samiddhi was referring to this when he spoke—

mn136:6.3.verse: “Whatever is felt is included in suffering.”’

mn136:6.4.verse: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda:

mn136:6.5.verse: ‘See, Ānanda, how this misguided man Udāyī interferes.

mn136:6.7.verse: that this misguided man Udāyī would unreasonably interfere just now.

mn136:6.8.verse: From the start, Ānanda, it was the three kinds of feeling that were asked about by the wanderer Potaliputta.

mn136:6.9.verse: If, Ānanda, when asked thus by the wanderer Potaliputta, this misguided man Samiddhi had answered thus:

mn136:6.10.verse: “After doing intentional kamma, friend Potaliputta, by body, by speech, or by mind, whose result is to be felt as pleasant, one feels pleasure;

mn136:6.11.verse: after doing intentional kamma, friend Potaliputta, by body, by speech, or by mind, whose result is to be felt as painful, one feels pain;

mn136:6.12.verse: after doing intentional kamma, friend Potaliputta, by body, by speech, or by mind, whose result is to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant, one feels neither pain nor pleasure”—

mn136:6.13.verse: answering thus, Ānanda, this misguided man Samiddhi would have answered the wanderer Potaliputta rightly.

mn136:6.14.verse: Besides, Ānanda, what do those foolish, incompetent wanderers of other sects know of the Tathāgata’s Great Exposition of Kamma?

mn136:6.15.verse: If you, Ānanda, were to listen to the Tathāgata expounding the Great Exposition of Kamma …’

mn136:7.1.verse: ‘This is the time, Blessed One, this is the time, Fortunate One,

mn136:7.2.verse: for the Blessed One to expound the Great Exposition of Kamma. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the bhikkhus will bear it in mind.’

mn136:7.3.verse: ‘Then, Ānanda, listen and heed well what I shall say.’

mn136:7.4.verse: ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

mn136:8.1.verse: ‘There are, Ānanda, these four kinds of persons found existing in the world.

mn136:8.3.verse: Here, Ānanda, some person kills living beings, takes what is not given, misconducts himself in sensual desires, speaks falsehood, speaks maliciously, speaks harshly, gossips, is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and has wrong view.

mn136:8.4.verse: On the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn136:8.5.verse: But here, Ānanda, some person kills living beings, takes what is not given, misconducts himself in sensual desires, speaks falsehood, speaks maliciously, speaks harshly, gossips, is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and has wrong view.

mn136:8.6.verse: On the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn136:8.7.verse: Here, Ānanda, some person abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from misconduct in sensual desires, abstains from false speech, abstains from malicious speech, abstains from harsh speech, abstains from gossip, is not covetous, has a mind free of ill will, and has right view.

mn136:8.8.verse: On the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn136:8.9.verse: But here, Ānanda, some person abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from misconduct in sensual desires, abstains from false speech, abstains from malicious speech, abstains from harsh speech, abstains from gossip, is not covetous, has a mind free of ill will, and has right view.

mn136:8.10.verse: On the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn136:9.1.verse: ‘Here, Ānanda, in consequence of ardour, endeavour, devotion, diligence, and right attention, some ascetic or brahmin attains such concentration of mind that, when his mind is concentrated, with the heavenly eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees that person—

mn136:9.2.verse: who here kills living beings, takes what is not given, misconducts himself in sensual desires, speaks falsehood, speaks maliciously, speaks harshly, gossips, is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and has wrong view—on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn136:9.4.verse: “It seems, sirs, that there are evil kammas, that there is the result of misconduct.

mn136:9.5.verse: I saw that person who here kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view; I see him, on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.”

mn136:9.7.verse: “It seems, sirs, that whoever kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view, all of them, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn136:9.8.verse: Those who know thus know rightly; those who know otherwise have wrong knowledge.”

mn136:9.9.verse: So he obstinately clings to and insists on what he has himself known, himself seen, himself found, declaring: “Only this is true, anything else is wrong.”

mn136:10.1.verse: ‘But here, Ānanda, in consequence of ardour, endeavour, devotion, diligence, and right attention, some ascetic or brahmin attains such concentration of mind that, when his mind is concentrated, with the heavenly eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees that person—

mn136:10.2.verse: who here kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view—on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn136:10.4.verse: “It seems, sirs, that there are no evil kammas, that there is no result of misconduct.

mn136:10.5.verse: I saw that person who here kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view; I see him, on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.”

mn136:10.7.verse: “It seems, sirs, that whoever kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view, all of them, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn136:11.1.verse: ‘Here, Ānanda, in consequence of ardour, endeavour, devotion, diligence, and right attention, some ascetic or brahmin attains such concentration of mind that, when his mind is concentrated, with the heavenly eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees that person—

mn136:11.4.verse: “It seems, sirs, that there are good kammas, that there is the result of good conduct.

mn136:11.5.verse: I saw that person who here abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given … has right view; I see him, on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.”

mn136:12.1.verse: ‘But here, Ānanda, in consequence of ardour, endeavour, devotion, diligence, and right attention, some ascetic or brahmin attains such concentration of mind that, when his mind is concentrated, with the heavenly eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees that person who here abstains from killing living beings … has right view—on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn136:12.3.verse: “It seems, sirs, that there are no good kammas, that there is no result of good conduct. I saw that person

mn136:12.4.verse: who here abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given … has right view; I see him, on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.”

mn136:12.5.verse: He says thus: “It seems, sirs, that whoever abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given … has right view, all of them, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn136:12.6.verse: Those who know thus know rightly; those who know otherwise have wrong knowledge.”

mn136:12.7.verse: So he obstinately clings to and insists on what he has himself known, himself seen, himself found, declaring: “Only this is true, anything else is wrong.”

mn136:13.1.verse: ‘Now, Ānanda, as to that ascetic or brahmin who says thus:

mn136:13.2.verse: “It seems, sirs, that there are evil kammas, that there is the result of misconduct”—I concede that to him.

mn136:13.4.verse: “I saw that person who here kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view; I see him, on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell”—I also concede that to him.

mn136:13.5.verse: But as to his saying thus:

mn136:13.6.verse: “It seems, sirs, that whoever kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view, all of them, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell”—that I do not concede to him.

mn136:13.8.verse: “Those who know thus know rightly; those who know otherwise have wrong knowledge”—that I do not concede to him.

mn136:13.9.verse: As to his obstinately clinging to and insisting on what he has himself known, himself seen, himself found, declaring: “Only this is true, anything else is wrong”—that I do not concede to him.

mn136:13.11.verse: Because, Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the Great Exposition of Kamma is otherwise.

mn136:14.1.verse: ‘Now, Ānanda, as to that ascetic or brahmin who says thus:

mn136:14.2.verse: “It seems, sirs, that there are no evil kammas, that there is no result of misconduct”—that I do not concede to him.

mn136:14.3.verse: But as to his saying thus:

mn136:14.4.verse: “I saw that person who here kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view; I see him, on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a happy destination, in the heavenly world”—I concede that to him.

mn136:14.8.verse: “Those who know thus know rightly; those who know otherwise have wrong knowledge”—that I do not concede to him.

mn136:14.9.verse: As to his obstinately clinging to and insisting on what he has himself known, himself seen, himself found, declaring: “Only this is true, anything else is wrong”—that I do not concede to him.

mn136:14.11.verse: Because, Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the Great Exposition of Kamma is otherwise.

mn136:15.1.verse: ‘Now, Ānanda, as to that ascetic or brahmin who says thus:

mn136:15.2.verse: “It seems, sirs, that there are good kammas, that there is the result of good conduct”—I concede that to him.

mn136:15.4.verse: “I saw that person who here abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given … has right view; I see him, on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a happy destination, in the heavenly world”—I also concede that to him.

mn136:15.5.verse: But as to his saying thus:

mn136:15.6.verse: “It seems, sirs, that whoever abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given … has right view, all of them, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a happy destination, in the heavenly world”—that I do not concede to him.

mn136:15.8.verse: “Those who know thus know rightly; those who know otherwise have wrong knowledge”—that I do not concede to him.

mn136:15.9.verse: As to his obstinately clinging to and insisting on what he has himself known, himself seen, himself found, declaring: “Only this is true, anything else is wrong”—that I do not concede to him.

mn136:15.11.verse: Because, Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the Great Exposition of Kamma is otherwise.

mn136:16.1.verse: ‘Now, Ānanda, as to that ascetic or brahmin who says thus:

mn136:16.2.verse: “It seems, sirs, that there are no good kammas, that there is no result of good conduct”—that I do not concede to him.

mn136:16.3.verse: But as to his saying thus:

mn136:16.4.verse: “I saw that person who here abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given … has right view; I see him, on the dissolution of the body, after death, having reappeared in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell”—I concede that to him.

mn136:16.6.verse: “It seems, sirs, that whoever abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given … has right view, all of them, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell”—that I do not concede to him.

mn136:16.7.verse: As to his saying thus: “Those who know thus know rightly;

mn136:16.8.verse: those who know otherwise have wrong knowledge”—that I do not concede to him.

mn136:16.9.verse: As to his obstinately clinging to and insisting on what he has himself known, himself seen, himself found, declaring: “Only this is true, anything else is wrong”—that I do not concede to him.

mn136:16.11.verse: Because, Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s knowledge of the Great Exposition of Kamma is otherwise.

mn136:17.1.verse: ‘Now, Ānanda, as to that person who here kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view, and who, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell—

mn136:17.2.verse: either an evil kamma to be felt as painful was done by him earlier, or an evil kamma to be felt as painful was done by him later, or at the time of death he undertook and held to wrong view.

mn136:17.3.verse: It is because of that, that on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn136:17.4.verse: But as to his having here killed living beings, having taken what is not given … having had wrong view—he will experience the result of that either here and now, or in his next rebirth, or in some subsequent existence.

mn136:18.1.verse: ‘Now, Ānanda, as to that person who here kills living beings, takes what is not given … has wrong view, and who, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world—

mn136:18.2.verse: either a good kamma to be felt as pleasant was done by him earlier, or a good kamma to be felt as pleasant was done by him later, or at the time of death he undertook and held to right view.

mn136:18.3.verse: It is because of that, that on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn136:18.4.verse: But as to his having here killed living beings, having taken what is not given … having had wrong view—he will experience the result of that either here and now, or in his next rebirth, or in some subsequent existence.

mn136:19.1.verse: ‘Now, Ānanda, as to that person who here abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given … has right view, and who, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world—

mn136:19.2.verse: either a good kamma to be felt as pleasant was done by him earlier, or a good kamma to be felt as pleasant was done by him later, or at the time of death he undertook and held to right view.

mn136:19.3.verse: It is because of that, that on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.

mn136:19.4.verse: But as to his having here abstained from killing living beings, having abstained from taking what is not given … having had right view—he will experience the result of that either here and now, or in his next rebirth, or in some subsequent existence.

mn136:20.1.verse: ‘Now, Ānanda, as to that person who here abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given … has right view, and who, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell—

mn136:20.2.verse: either an evil kamma to be felt as painful was done by him earlier, or an evil kamma to be felt as painful was done by him later, or at the time of death he undertook and held to wrong view.

mn136:20.3.verse: It is because of that, that on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.

mn136:20.4.verse: But as to his having here abstained from killing living beings, having abstained from taking what is not given … having had right view—he will experience the result of that either here and now, or in his next rebirth, or in some subsequent existence.

mn136:21.1.verse: ‘So, Ānanda, there is kamma that is incapable of good result and appears incapable of good result; there is kamma that is incapable of good result but appears capable of good result; there is kamma that is capable of good result and appears capable of good result; there is kamma that is capable of good result but appears incapable of good result.’

mn136:21.2.verse: This is what the Blessed One said.

mn136:21.3.verse: The venerable Ānanda was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn136:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

mn136:2.1.verse: Now at that time Venerable Samiddhi was staying in a wilderness hut.

mn136:2.2.verse: Then as the wanderer Potaliputta was going for a walk he came up to Venerable Samiddhi and exchanged greetings with him.

mn136:2.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to him:

mn136:2.4.verse: “Reverend Samiddhi, I have heard and learned this in the presence of the ascetic Gotama:

mn136:2.5.verse: ‘Deeds by way of body and speech are done in vain. Only mental deeds are real.’

mn136:2.6.verse: And: ‘There is such an attainment where the one who enters it does not feel anything at all.’”

mn136:2.7.verse: “Don’t say that, Reverend Potaliputta, don’t say that! Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say this:

mn136:2.8.verse: ‘Deeds by way of body and speech are done in vain. Only mental deeds are real.’

mn136:2.9.verse: But, reverend, there is such an attainment where the one who enters it does not feel anything at all.”

mn136:2.10.verse: “Reverend Samiddhi, how long has it been since you went forth?”

mn136:2.12.verse: “Well now, what are we to say to the senior mendicants, when even such a junior mendicant imagines their Teacher needs defending?

mn136:2.13.verse: After doing an intentional deed by way of body, speech, or mind, reverend, what does one feel?”

mn136:2.14.verse: “After doing an intentional deed by way of body, speech, or mind, reverend, one feels suffering.”

mn136:2.15.verse: Then, neither approving nor rejecting Samiddhi’s statement, Potaliputta

mn136:2.16.verse: rose from his seat and left.

mn136:3.1.verse: Soon after he had left, Venerable Samiddhi went to Venerable Ānanda, and exchanged greetings with him.

mn136:3.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side,

mn136:3.3.verse: and informed Ānanda of all they had discussed.

mn136:3.4.verse: When he had spoken, Ānanda said to him,

mn136:3.5.verse: “Reverend Samiddhi, we should see the Buddha about this matter.

mn136:3.6.verse: Come, let’s go to the Buddha and inform him about this.

mn136:3.7.verse: As he answers, so we’ll remember it.”

mn136:4.1.verse: Then Ānanda and Samiddhi went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side,

mn136:4.2.verse: and told him what had happened.

mn136:5.1.verse: When they had spoken, the Buddha said to Ānanda,

mn136:5.2.verse: “I don’t recall even seeing the wanderer Potaliputta, Ānanda, so how could we have had such a discussion?

mn136:5.3.verse: The wanderer Potaliputta’s question should have been answered after analyzing it, but this futile man answered categorically.”

mn136:6.1.verse: When he said this, Venerable Udāyī said to him,

mn136:6.2.verse: “But perhaps, sir, Venerable Samiddhi spoke in reference to the statement:

mn136:6.4.verse: But the Buddha said to Venerable Ānanda,

mn136:6.5.verse: “See what this futile man Udāyī comes up with?

mn136:6.7.verse: he was coming up with something irrational.

mn136:6.8.verse: Right from the start Potaliputta asked about the three feelings.

mn136:6.9.verse: Suppose the futile man Samiddhi had answered the wanderer Potaliputta’s question like this:

mn136:6.10.verse: ‘After doing an intentional deed to be experienced as pleasant by way of body, speech, or mind, one feels pleasure.

mn136:6.11.verse: After doing an intentional deed to be experienced as painful by way of body, speech, or mind, one feels pain.

mn136:6.12.verse: After doing an intentional deed to be experienced as neutral by way of body, speech, or mind, one feels neutral.’

mn136:6.13.verse: Answering in this way, Samiddhi would have rightly answered Potaliputta.

mn136:6.14.verse: Still, who are those foolish and incompetent wanderers of other religions to understand the Realized One’s great analysis of deeds?

mn136:6.15.verse: If you would all listen, Ānanda, I will explain the Realized One’s great analysis of deeds.”

mn136:7.1.verse: “Now is the time, Blessed One! Now is the time, Holy One!

mn136:7.2.verse: Let the Buddha explain the great analysis of deeds. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

mn136:7.3.verse: “Well then, Ānanda, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

mn136:8.1.verse: “Ānanda, these four individuals are found in the world.

mn136:8.3.verse: It’s when an individual here kills living creatures, steals, and commits sexual misconduct. They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re covetous, malicious, and have wrong view.

mn136:8.4.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

mn136:8.5.verse: But some other individual here kills living creatures, steals, and commits sexual misconduct. They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re covetous, malicious, and have wrong view.

mn136:8.6.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

mn136:8.7.verse: But some other individual here refrains from killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, or using speech that’s false, divisive, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re contented, kind-hearted, with right view.

mn136:8.8.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

mn136:8.9.verse: But some other individual here refrains from killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, or using speech that’s false, divisive, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re contented, kind-hearted, with right view.

mn136:8.10.verse: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

mn136:9.1.verse: Now, some ascetic or brahmin—by dint of keen, resolute, committed, and diligent effort, and right application of mind—experiences an immersion of the heart of such a kind that it gives rise to clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman. With that clairvoyance they see that individual

mn136:9.2.verse: here who killed living creatures, stole, and committed sexual misconduct; who used speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; and who was covetous, malicious, and had wrong view. And they see that, when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

mn136:9.4.verse: ‘It seems, worthy sir, that there is such a thing as bad deeds, and the result of bad conduct.

mn136:9.5.verse: For I have seen a individual here who killed living creatures … and had wrong view. And when their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.’

mn136:9.7.verse: ‘It seems that everyone who kills living creatures … and has wrong view is reborn in hell.

mn136:9.8.verse: Those whose notion is this have the right notion. Those whose notion is otherwise have a wrong notion.’

mn136:9.9.verse: And so they obstinately stick to what they have known, seen, and understood for themselves, insisting that: ‘This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’

mn136:10.1.verse: But some other ascetic or brahmin—by dint of keen, resolute, committed, and diligent effort, and right application of mind—experiences an immersion of the heart of such a kind that it gives rise to clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman. With that clairvoyance they see that individual

mn136:10.2.verse: here who killed living creatures … and had wrong view. And they see that they are reborn in a heavenly realm.

mn136:10.4.verse: ‘It seems that there is no such thing as bad deeds, and the result of bad conduct.

mn136:10.5.verse: For I have seen an individual here who killed living creatures … and had wrong view. And I saw that they were reborn in a heavenly realm.’

mn136:10.7.verse: ‘It seems that everyone who kills living creatures … and has wrong view is reborn in a heavenly realm.

mn136:10.8.verse: Those whose notion is this have the right notion. Those whose notion is otherwise have a wrong notion.’

mn136:10.9.verse: And so they obstinately stick to what they have known, seen, and understood for themselves, insisting that: ‘This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’

mn136:11.1.verse: Take some ascetic or brahmin who with clairvoyance sees an individual

mn136:11.2.verse: here who refrained from killing living creatures … and had right view. And they see that they are reborn in a heavenly realm.

mn136:11.4.verse: ‘It seems that there is such a thing as good deeds, and the result of good conduct.

mn136:11.5.verse: For I have seen an individual here who refrained from killing living creatures … and had right view. And I saw that they were reborn in a heavenly realm.’

mn136:11.7.verse: ‘It seems that everyone who refrains from killing living creatures … and has right view is reborn in a heavenly realm.

mn136:11.8.verse: Those whose notion is this have the right notion. Those whose notion is otherwise have a wrong notion.’

mn136:11.9.verse: And so they obstinately stick to what they have known, seen, and understood for themselves, insisting that: ‘This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’

mn136:12.1.verse: Take some ascetic or brahmin who with clairvoyance sees an individual here who refrained from killing living creatures … and had right view. And they see that they are reborn in hell.

mn136:12.3.verse: ‘It seems that there is no such thing as good deeds, and the result of good conduct. For I have seen an individual

mn136:12.4.verse: here who refrained from killing living creatures … and had right view. And I saw that they were reborn in hell.’

mn136:12.5.verse: They say: ‘It seems that everyone who refrains from killing living creatures … and has right view is reborn in hell.

mn136:12.6.verse: Those whose notion is this have the right notion. Those whose notion is otherwise have a wrong notion.’

mn136:12.7.verse: And so they obstinately stick to what they have known, seen, and understood for themselves, insisting that: ‘This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’

mn136:13.1.verse: In this case, when an ascetic or brahmin says this:

mn136:13.2.verse: ‘It seems that there is such a thing as bad deeds, and the result of bad conduct,’ I grant them that.

mn136:13.4.verse: ‘I have seen an individual here who killed living creatures … and had wrong view. And after death, they were reborn in hell,’ I also grant them that.

mn136:13.6.verse: ‘It seems that everyone who kills living creatures … and has wrong view is reborn in hell,’ I don’t grant them that.

mn136:13.8.verse: ‘Those whose notion is this have the right notion. Those whose notion is otherwise have a wrong notion.’ I also don’t grant them that.

mn136:13.9.verse: And when they obstinately stick to what they have known, seen, and understood for themselves, insisting that: ‘This is the only truth, anything else is futile,’ I also don’t grant them that.

mn136:13.11.verse: Because the Realized One’s knowledge of the great analysis of deeds is otherwise.

mn136:14.1.verse: In this case, when an ascetic or brahmin says this:

mn136:14.2.verse: ‘It seems that there is no such thing as bad deeds, and the result of bad conduct,’ I don’t grant them that.

mn136:14.4.verse: ‘I have seen an individual here who killed living creatures … and had wrong view. And I saw that they were reborn in a heavenly realm,’ I grant them that.

mn136:14.6.verse: ‘It seems that everyone who kills living creatures … and has wrong view is reborn in a heavenly realm,’ I don’t grant them that. …

mn136:14.11.verse: Because the Realized One’s knowledge of the great analysis of deeds is otherwise.

mn136:15.1.verse: In this case, when an ascetic or brahmin says this:

mn136:15.2.verse: ‘It seems that there is such a thing as good deeds, and the result of good conduct,’ I grant them that.

mn136:15.4.verse: ‘I have seen an individual here who refrained from killing living creatures … and had right view. And I saw that they were reborn in a heavenly realm,’ I also grant them that.

mn136:15.6.verse: ‘It seems that everyone who refrains from killing living creatures … and has right view is reborn in a heavenly realm,’ I don’t grant them that. …

mn136:15.11.verse: Because the Realized One’s knowledge of the great analysis of deeds is otherwise.

mn136:16.1.verse: In this case, when an ascetic or brahmin says this:

mn136:16.2.verse: ‘It seems that there is no such thing as good deeds, and the result of good conduct,’ I don’t grant them that.

mn136:16.4.verse: ‘I have seen an individual here who refrained from killing living creatures … and had right view. And after death, they were reborn in hell,’ I grant them that.

mn136:16.6.verse: ‘It seems that everyone who refrains from killing living creatures … and has right view is reborn in hell,’ I don’t grant them that.

mn136:16.7.verse: But when they say: ‘Those whose notion is this have the right notion.

mn136:16.8.verse: Those whose notion is otherwise have a wrong notion,’ I also don’t grant them that.

mn136:16.9.verse: And when they obstinately stick to what they have known, seen, and understood for themselves, insisting that: ‘This is the only truth, anything else is futile,’ I also don’t grant them that.

mn136:16.11.verse: Because the Realized One’s knowledge of the great analysis of deeds is otherwise.

mn136:17.1.verse: Now, Ānanda, take the case of the individual here who killed living creatures … and had wrong view, and who, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

mn136:17.2.verse: That bad deed of theirs that is to be experienced as painful was either done previously, or later, or else at the time of death they undertook wrong view.

mn136:17.3.verse: And that’s why, when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

mn136:17.4.verse: But anyone here who kills living creatures … and has wrong view experiences the result of that in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

mn136:18.1.verse: Now, Ānanda, take the case of the individual here who killed living creatures … and had wrong view, and who is reborn in a heavenly realm.

mn136:18.2.verse: That good deed of theirs that is to be experienced as pleasurable was either done previously, or later, or else at the time of death they undertook right view.

mn136:18.3.verse: And that’s why, when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

mn136:18.4.verse: But anyone here who kills living creatures … and has wrong view experiences the result of that in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

mn136:19.1.verse: Now, Ānanda, take the case of the individual here who refrained from killing living creatures … and had right view, and who is reborn in a heavenly realm.

mn136:19.2.verse: That good deed of theirs that is to be experienced as pleasurable was either done previously, or later, or else at the time of death they undertook right view.

mn136:19.3.verse: And that’s why, when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

mn136:19.4.verse: But anyone here who refrains from killing living creatures … and has right view experiences the result of that in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

mn136:20.1.verse: Now, Ānanda, take the case of the individual here who refrained from killing living creatures … and had right view, and who is reborn in hell.

mn136:20.2.verse: That bad deed of theirs that is to be experienced as painful was either done previously, or later, or else at the time of death they undertook wrong view.

mn136:20.3.verse: And that’s why, when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

mn136:20.4.verse: But anyone here who refrains from killing living creatures … and has right view experiences the result of that in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent period.

mn136:21.1.verse: So, Ānanda, there are deeds that are ineffective and appear ineffective. There are deeds that are ineffective but appear effective. There are deeds that are effective and appear effective. And there are deeds that are effective but appear ineffective.”

mn136:21.2.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn136:21.3.verse: Satisfied, Venerable Ānanda approved what the Buddha said.

mn137:0.2.verse: The Analysis of the Six Sense Fields

mn137:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn137:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

mn137:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, I shall teach you the analysis of the six sense fields.

mn137:2.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

mn137:3.1.verse: “‘The six interior sense fields should be understood. The six exterior sense fields should be understood. The six classes of consciousness should be understood. The six classes of contact should be understood. The eighteen mental preoccupations should be understood. The thirty-six positions of sentient beings should be understood. Therein, relying on this, give up that. The Noble One cultivates the establishment of mindfulness in three cases, by virtue of which they are a Teacher worthy to instruct a group. Of all meditation tutors, it is he that is called the supreme guide for those fit for training.’

mn137:3.2.verse: This is the summary recital for the analysis of the six sense fields.

mn137:4.1.verse: ‘The six interior sense fields should be understood.’

mn137:4.2.verse: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

mn137:4.3.verse: There are the sense fields of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

mn137:4.4.verse: ‘The six interior sense fields should be understood.’

mn137:4.5.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

mn137:5.1.verse: ‘The six exterior sense fields should be understood.’

mn137:5.2.verse: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

mn137:5.3.verse: There are the sense fields of sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

mn137:5.4.verse: ‘The six exterior sense fields should be understood.’

mn137:5.5.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

mn137:6.1.verse: ‘The six classes of consciousness should be understood.’

mn137:6.2.verse: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

mn137:6.3.verse: There are eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind consciousness.

mn137:6.4.verse: ‘The six classes of consciousness should be understood.’

mn137:6.5.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

mn137:7.1.verse: ‘The six classes of contact should be understood.’

mn137:7.2.verse: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

mn137:7.3.verse: There is contact through the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

mn137:7.4.verse: ‘The six classes of contact should be understood.’

mn137:7.5.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

mn137:8.1.verse: ‘The eighteen mental preoccupations should be understood.’

mn137:8.2.verse: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

mn137:8.3.verse: Seeing a sight with their eyes, one is preoccupied with a sight that’s a basis for happiness or sadness or equanimity.

mn137:8.4.verse: Hearing a sound with their ears …

mn137:8.5.verse: Smelling an odor with their nose …

mn137:8.6.verse: Tasting a flavor with their tongue …

mn137:8.7.verse: Encountering a touch with their body …

mn137:8.8.verse: Becoming conscious of an idea with their mind, one is preoccupied with an idea that’s a basis for happiness or sadness or equanimity.

mn137:8.9.verse: So there are six preoccupations with happiness, six preoccupations with sadness, and six preoccupations with equanimity. ‘The eighteen mental preoccupations should be understood.’

mn137:8.10.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

mn137:9.1.verse: ‘The thirty-six positions of sentient beings should be understood.’

mn137:9.2.verse: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

mn137:9.3.verse: There are six kinds of domestic happiness and six kinds of renunciate happiness. There are six kinds of domestic sadness and six kinds of renunciate sadness. There are six kinds of domestic equanimity and six kinds of renunciate equanimity.

mn137:10.1.verse: And in this context what are the six kinds of domestic happiness?

mn137:10.2.verse: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasing, connected with the worldly pleasures of the flesh. Happiness arises when you regard it as a gain to obtain such sights, or when you recollect sights you formerly obtained that have passed, ceased, and perished.

mn137:10.3.verse: Such happiness is called domestic happiness.

mn137:10.4.verse: There are sounds known by the ear …

mn137:10.8.verse: Ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasing, connected with the worldly pleasures of the flesh. Happiness arises when you regard it as a gain to obtain such ideas, or when you recollect ideas you formerly obtained that have passed, ceased, and perished.

mn137:10.9.verse: Such happiness is called domestic happiness.

mn137:10.10.verse: These are the six kinds of domestic happiness.

mn137:11.1.verse: And in this context what are the six kinds of renunciate happiness?

mn137:11.2.verse: When you’ve understood the impermanence of sights—their perishing, fading away, and cessation—happiness arises as you truly understand through right understanding that both formerly and now all those sights are impermanent, suffering, and perishable.

mn137:11.3.verse: Such happiness is called renunciate happiness.

mn137:11.4.verse: When you’ve understood the impermanence of sounds …

mn137:11.8.verse: ideas—their perishing, fading away, and cessation—happiness arises as you truly understand through right understanding that both formerly and now all those ideas are impermanent, suffering, and perishable.

mn137:11.9.verse: Such happiness is called renunciate happiness.

mn137:11.10.verse: These are the six kinds of renunciate happiness.

mn137:12.1.verse: And in this context what are the six kinds of domestic sadness?

mn137:12.2.verse: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasing, connected with the worldly pleasures of the flesh. Sadness arises when you regard it as a loss to lose such sights, or when you recollect sights you formerly lost that have passed, ceased, and perished.

mn137:12.3.verse: Such sadness is called domestic sadness.

mn137:12.4.verse: There are sounds known by the ear …

mn137:12.5.verse: There are smells known by the nose …

mn137:12.6.verse: There are tastes known by the tongue …

mn137:12.7.verse: There are touches known by the body …

mn137:12.8.verse: There are ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasing, connected with the worldly pleasures of the flesh. Sadness arises when you regard it as a loss to lose such ideas, or when you recollect ideas you formerly lost that have passed, ceased, and perished.

mn137:12.9.verse: Such sadness is called domestic sadness.

mn137:12.10.verse: These are the six kinds of domestic sadness.

mn137:13.1.verse: And in this context what are the six kinds of renunciate sadness?

mn137:13.2.verse: When you’ve understood the impermanence of sights—their perishing, fading away, and cessation—you truly understand through right understanding that both formerly and now all those sights are impermanent, suffering, and perishable. Upon seeing this, you give rise to longing for the supreme liberations:

mn137:13.3.verse: ‘Oh, when will I enter and remain in the same dimension that the noble ones enter and remain in today?’ When you give rise to longing for the supreme liberations like this, sadness arises because of the longing.

mn137:13.4.verse: Such sadness is called renunciate sadness.

mn137:13.5.verse: When you’ve understood the impermanence of sounds …

mn137:13.9.verse: ideas—their perishing, fading away, and cessation—you truly understand through right understanding that both formerly and now all those ideas are impermanent, suffering, and perishable. Upon seeing this, you give rise to longing for the supreme liberations:

mn137:13.10.verse: ‘Oh, when will I enter and remain in the same dimension that the noble ones enter and remain in today?’ When you give rise to longing for the supreme liberations like this, sadness arises because of the longing.

mn137:13.11.verse: Such sadness is called renunciate sadness.

mn137:13.12.verse: These are the six kinds of renunciate sadness.

mn137:14.1.verse: And in this context what are the six kinds of domestic equanimity?

mn137:14.2.verse: When seeing a sight with their eyes, equanimity arises for the unlearned ordinary person—a foolish ordinary person who has not overcome their limitations and the results of deeds, and is blind to the drawbacks.

mn137:14.3.verse: Such equanimity does not transcend the sight.

mn137:14.4.verse: That’s why it’s called domestic equanimity.

mn137:14.5.verse: When hearing a sound with their ears …

mn137:14.6.verse: When smelling an odor with their nose …

mn137:14.7.verse: When tasting a flavor with their tongue …

mn137:14.8.verse: When encountering a touch with their body …

mn137:14.9.verse: When knowing an idea with their mind, equanimity arises for the unlearned ordinary person—a foolish ordinary person who has not overcome their limitations and the results of deeds, and is blind to the drawbacks.

mn137:14.10.verse: Such equanimity does not transcend the idea.

mn137:14.11.verse: That’s why it’s called domestic equanimity.

mn137:14.12.verse: These are the six kinds of domestic equanimity.

mn137:15.1.verse: And in this context what are the six kinds of renunciate equanimity?

mn137:15.2.verse: When you’ve understood the impermanence of sights—their perishing, fading away, and cessation—equanimity arises as you truly understand through right understanding that both formerly and now all those sights are impermanent, suffering, and perishable.

mn137:15.4.verse: That’s why it’s called renunciate equanimity.

mn137:15.5.verse: When you’ve understood the impermanence of sounds …

mn137:15.9.verse: ideas—their perishing, fading away, and cessation—equanimity arises as you truly understand through right understanding that both formerly and now all those ideas are impermanent, suffering, and perishable.

mn137:15.11.verse: That’s why it’s called renunciate equanimity.

mn137:15.12.verse: These are the six kinds of renunciate equanimity.

mn137:15.13.verse: ‘The thirty-six positions of sentient beings should be understood.’

mn137:15.14.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

mn137:16.1.verse: ‘Therein, relying on this, give up that.’

mn137:16.2.verse: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

mn137:16.3.verse: Therein, by relying and depending on the six kinds of renunciate happiness, give up and go beyond the six kinds of domestic happiness.

mn137:16.4.verse: That’s how they are given up.

mn137:16.5.verse: Therein, by relying on the six kinds of renunciate sadness, give up the six kinds of domestic sadness.

mn137:16.6.verse: That’s how they are given up.

mn137:16.7.verse: Therein, by relying on the six kinds of renunciate equanimity, give up the six kinds of domestic equanimity.

mn137:16.8.verse: That’s how they are given up.

mn137:16.9.verse: Therein, by relying on the six kinds of renunciate happiness, give up the six kinds of renunciate sadness.

mn137:16.10.verse: That’s how they are given up.

mn137:16.11.verse: Therein, by relying on the six kinds of renunciate equanimity, give up the six kinds of renunciate happiness.

mn137:16.12.verse: That’s how they are given up.

mn137:17.1.verse: There is equanimity that is diversified, based on diversity, and equanimity that is unified, based on unity.

mn137:18.1.verse: And what is equanimity based on diversity?

mn137:18.2.verse: There is equanimity toward sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

mn137:18.3.verse: This is equanimity based on diversity.

mn137:19.1.verse: And what is equanimity based on unity?

mn137:19.2.verse: There is equanimity based on the dimensions of infinite space, infinite consciousness, nothingness, and neither perception nor non-perception.

mn137:19.3.verse: This is equanimity based on unity.

mn137:20.1.verse: Therein, relying on equanimity based on unity, give up equanimity based on diversity.

mn137:20.2.verse: That’s how it is given up.

mn137:20.3.verse: Relying on not being determined by that, give up equanimity based on unity.

mn137:20.4.verse: That’s how it is given up.

mn137:20.5.verse: ‘Therein, relying on this, give up that.’

mn137:20.6.verse: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

mn137:21.1.verse: ‘The Noble One cultivates the establishment of mindfulness in three cases, by virtue of which they are a Teacher worthy to instruct a group.’

mn137:21.3.verse: but why did I say it?

mn137:22.1.verse: The first case is when the Teacher teaches Dhamma to his disciples out of kindness and sympathy:

mn137:22.2.verse: ‘This is for your welfare. This is for your happiness.’

mn137:22.3.verse: But their disciples don’t want to listen. They don’t actively listen or try to understand. They proceed having turned away from the Teacher’s instruction.

mn137:22.4.verse: In this case the Realized One is not unhappy, he does not feel unhappiness. He remains unfestering, mindful and aware.

mn137:22.5.verse: This is the first case in which the Noble One cultivates the establishment of mindfulness.

mn137:23.1.verse: The next case is when the Teacher teaches Dhamma to his disciples out of kindness and sympathy:

mn137:23.2.verse: ‘This is for your welfare. This is for your happiness.’

mn137:23.3.verse: And some of their disciples don’t want to listen. They don’t actively listen or try to understand. They proceed having turned away from the Teacher’s instruction.

mn137:23.4.verse: But some of their disciples do want to listen. They actively listen and try to understand. They don’t proceed having turned away from the Teacher’s instruction.

mn137:23.5.verse: In this case the Realized One is not unhappy,

mn137:23.8.verse: Shunning both unhappiness and happiness, he remains equanimous, mindful and aware.

mn137:23.9.verse: This is the second case in which the Noble One cultivates the establishment of mindfulness.

mn137:24.1.verse: The next case is when the Teacher teaches Dhamma to his disciples out of kindness and sympathy:

mn137:24.2.verse: ‘This is for your welfare. This is for your happiness.’
