mn141:22.2.verse: It’s the fading away and cessation of that very same craving no residue left behind; giving it away, letting it go, releasing it, and not clinging to it.

mn141:22.3.verse: This is called the noble truth of the cessation of suffering.

mn141:23.1.verse: And what is the noble truth of the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering?

mn141:23.2.verse: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

mn141:23.3.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

mn141:24.2.verse: Knowing about suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.

mn141:25.2.verse: Purposes of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness.

mn141:26.2.verse: Refraining from lying, backbiting, harsh speech, and talking nonsense.

mn141:27.2.verse: Refraining from killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct.

mn141:28.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple gives up wrong livelihood and earns a living by right livelihood.

mn141:29.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise.

mn141:29.3.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen are given up.

mn141:29.4.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities arise.

mn141:29.5.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.

mn141:30.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

mn141:30.3.verse: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

mn141:30.5.verse: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

mn141:31.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

mn141:31.3.verse: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

mn141:31.4.verse: And with the fading away of rapture, they enter and remain in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

mn141:31.5.verse: With the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

mn141:31.7.verse: This is called the noble truth of the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.

mn141:32.1.verse: Near Varanasi, in the deer park at Isipatana, the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha rolled forth the supreme Wheel of Dhamma. And that wheel cannot be rolled back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.

mn141:32.2.verse: It is the teaching, advocating, establishing, clarifying, analyzing, and revealing of the four noble truths.”

mn141:32.3.verse: That is what Venerable Sāriputta said.

mn141:32.4.verse: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what Sāriputta said.

mn141:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Benares in the Deer Park at Isipatana.

mn141:1.3.verse: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:

mn141:2.1.verse: “At Benares, bhikkhus, in the Deer Park at Isipatana the Tathāgata, accomplished and fully enlightened, set rolling the matchless Wheel of the Dhamma, which cannot be stopped by any recluse or brahmin or god or Māra or Brahmā or anyone in the world—that is,

mn141:2.2.verse: the announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of the Four Noble Truths.

mn141:3.1.verse: “the announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of the noble truth of suffering. the announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of the noble truth of the origin of suffering…of the noble truth of the cessation of suffering…of the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering.

mn141:4.1.verse: “At Benares, bhikkhus, in the Deer Park at Isipatana the Tathāgata, accomplished and fully enlightened, set rolling the matchless Wheel of the Dhamma, which cannot be stopped by any recluse or brahmin or god or Māra or Brahmā or anyone in the world—that is,

mn141:4.2.verse: the announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of these Four Noble Truths.

mn141:5.1.verse: “Cultivate the friendship of Sāriputta and Moggallāna, bhikkhus;

mn141:5.3.verse: They are wise and helpful to their companions in the holy life.

mn141:5.6.verse: Sāriputta trains others for the fruit of stream-entry, Moggallāna for the supreme goal.

mn141:5.7.verse: Sāriputta, bhikkhus, is able to announce, teach, describe, establish, reveal, expound, and exhibit the Four Noble Truths.”

mn141:6.2.verse: Having said this, the Sublime One rose from his seat and went into his dwelling.

mn141:7.1.verse: Then, soon after the Blessed One had gone, the venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus thus:

mn141:7.3.verse: “Friend,” the bhikkhus replied to the venerable Sāriputta.

mn141:8.1.verse: “At Benares, friends, in the Deer Park at Isipatana the Tathāgata, accomplished and fully enlightened, set rolling the matchless Wheel of the Dhamma…

mn141:8.2.verse: and exhibiting of the Four Noble Truths.

mn141:9.1.verse: “The announcing…and exhibiting of the noble truth of suffering…of the noble truth of the origin of suffering…of the noble truth of the cessation of suffering…of the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering.

mn141:10.1.verse: “And what, friends, is the noble truth of suffering?

mn141:10.2.verse: Birth is suffering; ageing is suffering; death is suffering; sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are suffering; not to obtain what one wants is suffering; in short, the five aggregates affected by clinging are suffering.

mn141:11.2.verse: The birth of beings into the various orders of beings, their coming to birth, precipitation [in a womb], generation, the manifestation of the aggregates, obtaining the bases for contact—

mn141:12.2.verse: The ageing of beings in the various orders of beings, their old age, brokenness of teeth, greyness of hair, wrinkling of skin, decline of life, weakness of faculties—

mn141:13.2.verse: The passing of beings out of the various orders of beings, their passing away, dissolution, disappearance, dying, completion of time, dissolution of aggregates, laying down of the body—

mn141:14.2.verse: The sorrow, sorrowing, sorrowfulness, inner sorrow, inner sorriness, of one who has encountered some misfortune or is affected by some painful state—

mn141:15.2.verse: The wail and lament, wailing and lamenting, bewailing and lamentation, of one who has encountered some misfortune or is affected by some painful state—

mn141:16.2.verse: Bodily pain, bodily discomfort, painful, uncomfortable feeling born of bodily contact—

mn141:17.2.verse: Mental pain, mental discomfort, painful, uncomfortable feeling born of mental contact—

mn141:18.2.verse: The trouble and despair, the tribulation and desperation, of one who has encountered some misfortune or is affected by some painful state—

mn141:19.1.verse: “And what, friends, is ‘not to obtain what one wants is suffering’?

mn141:19.2.verse: To beings subject to birth there comes the wish:

mn141:19.3.verse: ‘Oh, that we were not subject to birth! That birth would not come to us!’

mn141:19.4.verse: But this is not to be obtained by wishing,

mn141:19.5.verse: and not to obtain what one wants is suffering.

mn141:19.9.verse: subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, there comes the wish:

mn141:19.10.verse: ‘Oh, that we were not subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair! That sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair would not come to us!’

mn141:19.11.verse: But this is not to be obtained by wishing,

mn141:19.12.verse: and not to obtain what one wants is suffering.

mn141:20.1.verse: “And what, friends, are the five aggregates affected by clinging that, in short, are suffering?

mn141:20.2.verse: They are: the material form aggregate affected by clinging, the feeling aggregate affected by clinging, the perception aggregate affected by clinging, the formations aggregate affected by clinging, and the consciousness aggregate affected by clinging.

mn141:20.3.verse: These are the five aggregates affected by clinging that, in short, are suffering.

mn141:20.4.verse: This is called the noble truth of suffering.

mn141:21.1.verse: “And what, friends, is the noble truth of the origin of suffering?

mn141:21.2.verse: It is craving, which brings renewal of being, is accompanied by delight and lust, and delights in this and that; that is,

mn141:21.3.verse: craving for sensual pleasures, craving for being, and craving for non-being.

mn141:21.4.verse: This is called the noble truth of the origin of suffering.

mn141:22.1.verse: “And what, friends, is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering?

mn141:22.2.verse: It is the remainderless fading away and ceasing, the giving up, relinquishing, letting go, and rejecting of that same craving.

mn141:22.3.verse: This is called the noble truth of the cessation of suffering.

mn141:23.1.verse: “And what, friends, is the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering?

mn141:23.2.verse: It is just this Noble Eightfold Path; that is,

mn141:23.3.verse: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.

mn141:24.2.verse: Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, and knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of suffering—

mn141:25.2.verse: Intention of renunciation, intention of non-ill will, and intention of non-cruelty—

mn141:26.2.verse: Abstaining from false speech, abstaining from malicious speech, abstaining from harsh speech, and abstaining from idle chatter—

mn141:27.2.verse: Abstaining from killing living beings, abstaining from taking what is not given, and abstaining from misconduct in sensual pleasures—

mn141:28.2.verse: Here a noble disciple, having abandoned wrong livelihood, earns his living by right livelihood—

mn141:29.2.verse: Here a bhikkhu awakens zeal for the non-arising of unarisen evil unwholesome states, and he makes effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives.

mn141:29.3.verse: He awakens zeal for the abandoning of arisen evil unwholesome states, and he makes effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives.

mn141:29.4.verse: He awakens zeal for the arising of unarisen wholesome states, and he makes effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives.

mn141:29.5.verse: He awakens zeal for the continuance, non-disappearance, strengthening, increase, and fulfilment by development of arisen wholesome states, and he makes effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives.

mn141:30.2.verse: Here a bhikkhu abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.

mn141:30.3.verse: He abides contemplating feelings as feelings, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.

mn141:30.4.verse: He abides contemplating mind as mind, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.

mn141:30.5.verse: He abides contemplating mind-objects as mind-objects, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.

mn141:31.2.verse: Here, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion.

mn141:31.3.verse: With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, he enters upon and abides in the second jhāna, which has self-confidence and singleness of mind without applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of concentration.

mn141:31.4.verse: With the fading away as well of rapture, he abides in equanimity, and mindful and fully aware, still feeling pleasure with the body, he enters upon and abides in the third jhāna, on account of which noble ones announce: ‘He has a pleasant abiding who has equanimity and is mindful.’

mn141:31.5.verse: With the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, he enters upon and abides in the fourth jhāna, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.

mn141:31.7.verse: “This is called the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering.

mn141:32.1.verse: “At Benares, friends, in the Deer Park at Isipatana the Tathāgata, accomplished and fully enlightened, set rolling the matchless Wheel of the Dhamma, which cannot be stopped by any recluse or brahmin or god or Māra or Brahmā or anyone in the world—that is,

mn141:32.2.verse: the announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of these Four Noble Truths.”

mn141:32.3.verse: That is what the venerable Sāriputta said.

mn141:32.4.verse: The bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words.

mn142:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

mn142:2.1.verse: Then Mahāpajāpati Gotamī approached the Buddha bringing a new pair of garments. She bowed, sat down to one side, and said to the Buddha,

mn142:2.2.verse: “Sir, I have spun and woven this new pair of garments specially for the Buddha.

mn142:2.3.verse: May the Buddha please accept this from me out of sympathy.”

mn142:2.4.verse: When she said this, the Buddha said to her,

mn142:2.6.verse: When you give to the Saṅgha, both the Saṅgha and I will be honored.”

mn142:2.13.verse: For a third time, Mahāpajāpati Gotamī said to the Buddha,

mn142:2.14.verse: “Sir, I have spun and woven this new pair of garments specially for the Buddha.

mn142:2.15.verse: May the Buddha please accept this from me out of sympathy.”

mn142:2.16.verse: And for a third time, the Buddha said to her,

mn142:2.18.verse: When you give to the Saṅgha, both the Saṅgha and I will be honored.”

mn142:3.1.verse: When he said this, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha,

mn142:3.2.verse: “Sir, please accept the new pair of garments from Mahāpajāpati Gotamī.

mn142:3.3.verse: Sir, Mahāpajāpati was very helpful to the Buddha. As his aunt, she raised him, nurtured him, and gave him her milk.

mn142:3.4.verse: When the Buddha’s birth mother passed away, she nurtured him at her own breast.

mn142:3.5.verse: And the Buddha has been very helpful to Mahāpajāpati.

mn142:3.6.verse: It is owing to the Buddha that Mahāpajāpati has gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.

mn142:3.7.verse: It’s owing to the Buddha that she refrains from killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

mn142:3.8.verse: It’s owing to the Buddha that she has experiential confidence in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and has the ethics loved by the noble ones.

mn142:3.9.verse: It’s owing to the Buddha that she is free of doubt regarding suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

mn142:3.10.verse: The Buddha has been very helpful to Mahāpajāpati.”

mn142:4.2.verse: When someone has enabled you to go for refuge, it’s not easy to repay them

mn142:4.3.verse: by bowing down to them, rising up for them, greeting them with cupped palms, and observing proper etiquette for them; or by providing them with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

mn142:4.4.verse: When someone has enabled you to refrain from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor, it’s not easy to repay them …

mn142:4.6.verse: When someone has enabled you to have experiential confidence in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and the ethics loved by the noble ones, it’s not easy to repay them …

mn142:4.8.verse: When someone has enabled you to be free of doubt regarding suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation, it’s not easy to repay them

mn142:4.9.verse: by bowing down to them, rising up for them, greeting them with cupped palms, and observing proper etiquette for them; or by providing them with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

mn142:5.1.verse: Ānanda, there are these fourteen religious donations to individuals.

mn142:5.3.verse: One gives a gift to the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

mn142:5.4.verse: This is the first religious donation to an individual.

mn142:5.5.verse: One gives a gift to an independent Buddha.

mn142:5.6.verse: This is the second religious donation to an individual.

mn142:5.7.verse: One gives a gift to a perfected one.

mn142:5.8.verse: This is the third religious donation to an individual.

mn142:5.9.verse: One gives a gift to someone practicing to realize the fruit of perfection.

mn142:5.10.verse: This is the fourth religious donation to an individual.

mn142:5.11.verse: One gives a gift to a non-returner.

mn142:5.12.verse: This is the fifth religious donation to an individual.

mn142:5.13.verse: One gives a gift to someone practicing to realize the fruit of non-return.

mn142:5.14.verse: This is the sixth religious donation to an individual.

mn142:5.15.verse: One gives a gift to a once-returner.

mn142:5.16.verse: This is the seventh religious donation to an individual.

mn142:5.17.verse: One gives a gift to someone practicing to realize the fruit of once-return.

mn142:5.18.verse: This is the eighth religious donation to an individual.

mn142:5.19.verse: One gives a gift to a stream-enterer.

mn142:5.20.verse: This is the ninth religious donation to an individual.

mn142:5.21.verse: One gives a gift to someone practicing to realize the fruit of stream-entry.

mn142:5.22.verse: This is the tenth religious donation to an individual.

mn142:5.23.verse: One gives a gift to an outsider who is free of desire for sensual pleasures.

mn142:5.24.verse: This is the eleventh religious donation to an individual.

mn142:5.25.verse: One gives a gift to an ordinary person who has good ethical conduct.

mn142:5.26.verse: This is the twelfth religious donation to an individual.

mn142:5.27.verse: One gives a gift to an ordinary person who has bad ethical conduct.

mn142:5.28.verse: This is the thirteenth religious donation to an individual.

mn142:5.29.verse: One gives a gift to an animal.

mn142:5.30.verse: This is the fourteenth religious donation to an individual.

mn142:6.1.verse: Now, Ānanda, gifts to the following persons may be expected to yield the following returns. To an animal, a hundred times. To an unethical ordinary person, a thousand. To an ethical ordinary person, a hundred thousand. To an outsider free of desire for sensual pleasures, 10,000,000,000. But a gift to someone practicing to realize the fruit of stream-entry may be expected to yield incalculable, immeasurable returns. How much more so a gift to a stream-enterer, someone practicing to realize the fruit of once-return, a once-returner, someone practicing to realize the fruit of non-return, a non-returner, someone practicing to realize the fruit of perfection, a perfected one, or an independent Buddha? How much more so a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha?

mn142:7.1.verse: But there are, Ānanda, seven religious donations bestowed on a Saṅgha.

mn142:7.3.verse: One gives a gift to the communities of both monks and nuns headed by the Buddha.

mn142:7.4.verse: This is the first religious donation bestowed on a Saṅgha.

mn142:7.5.verse: One gives a gift to the communities of both monks and nuns after the Buddha has finally become quenched.

mn142:7.6.verse: This is the second religious donation bestowed on a Saṅgha.

mn142:7.7.verse: One gives a gift to the Saṅgha of monks.

mn142:7.8.verse: This is the third religious donation bestowed on a Saṅgha.

mn142:7.9.verse: One gives a gift to the Saṅgha of nuns.

mn142:7.10.verse: This is the fourth religious donation bestowed on a Saṅgha.

mn142:7.11.verse: One gives a gift, thinking: ‘Appoint this many monks and nuns for me from the Saṅgha.’

mn142:7.12.verse: This is the fifth religious donation bestowed on a Saṅgha.

mn142:7.13.verse: One gives a gift, thinking: ‘Appoint this many monks for me from the Saṅgha.’

mn142:7.14.verse: This is the sixth religious donation bestowed on a Saṅgha.

mn142:7.15.verse: One gives a gift, thinking: ‘Appoint this many nuns for me from the Saṅgha.’

mn142:7.16.verse: This is the seventh religious donation bestowed on a Saṅgha.

mn142:8.1.verse: In times to come there will be lambs of the flock wearing a scrap of ocher cloth, unethical and of bad character.

mn142:8.2.verse: People will give gifts to those unethical people in the name of the Saṅgha.

mn142:8.3.verse: Then too, I say, a religious donation bestowed on the Saṅgha is incalculable and immeasurable.

mn142:8.4.verse: But in any case, there is no way a personal offering can be more fruitful than one bestowed on a Saṅgha, I say.

mn142:9.1.verse: Ānanda, there are these four ways of purifying a religious donation.

mn142:9.3.verse: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by the giver, not the recipient.

mn142:9.4.verse: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by the recipient, not the giver.

mn142:9.5.verse: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by neither the giver nor the recipient.

mn142:9.6.verse: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by both the giver and the recipient.

mn142:10.1.verse: And how is a religious donation purified by the giver, not the recipient?

mn142:10.2.verse: It’s when the giver is ethical, of good character, but the recipient is unethical, of bad character.

mn142:11.1.verse: And how is a religious donation purified by the recipient, not the giver?

mn142:11.2.verse: It’s when the giver is unethical, of bad character, but the recipient is ethical, of good character.

mn142:12.1.verse: And how is a religious donation purified by neither the giver nor the recipient?

mn142:12.2.verse: It’s when both the giver and the recipient are unethical, of bad character.

mn142:13.1.verse: And how is a religious donation purified by both the giver and the recipient?

mn142:13.2.verse: It’s when both the giver and the recipient are ethical, of good character.

mn142:13.4.verse: These are the four ways of purifying a religious donation.”

mn142:14.1.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn142:14.2.verse: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

mn142:14.3.verse: “When an ethical person with trusting heart

mn142:14.4.verse: gives a proper gift to unethical persons,

mn142:14.5.verse: trusting in the ample fruit of deeds,

mn142:14.6.verse: that offering is purified by the giver.

mn142:14.7.verse: When an unethical and untrusting person,

mn142:14.8.verse: gives an improper gift to ethical persons,

mn142:14.9.verse: not trusting in the ample fruit of deeds,

mn142:14.10.verse: that offering is purified by the receivers.

mn142:14.11.verse: When an unethical and untrusting person,

mn142:14.12.verse: gives an improper gift to unethical persons,

mn142:14.13.verse: not trusting in the ample fruit of deeds,

mn142:14.14.verse: I declare that gift is not very fruitful.

mn142:14.15.verse: When an ethical person with trusting heart

mn142:14.16.verse: gives a proper gift to ethical persons,

mn142:14.17.verse: trusting in the ample fruit of deeds,

mn142:14.18.verse: I declare that gift is abundantly fruitful.

mn142:14.19.verse: But when a passionless one gives to the passionless

mn142:14.20.verse: a proper gift with trusting heart,

mn142:14.21.verse: trusting in the ample fruit of deeds,

mn142:14.22.verse: that’s truly the best of material gifts.”

mn142:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living in the Sakyan country at Kapilavatthu in Nigrodha’s Park.

mn142:2.1.verse: Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī took a new pair of cloths and went to the Blessed One. After paying homage to him, she sat down at one side and said to the Blessed One:

mn142:2.2.verse: “Venerable sir, this new pair of cloths has been spun by me, woven by me, especially for the Blessed One.

mn142:2.3.verse: Venerable sir, let the Blessed One accept it from me out of compassion.”

mn142:2.4.verse: When this was said, the Blessed One told her:

mn142:2.6.verse: When you give it to the Sangha, both I and the Sangha will be honoured.”

mn142:2.7.verse: A second time Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said to the Blessed One:

mn142:2.8.verse: “Venerable sir, this new pair of cloths has been spun by me, woven by me, especially for the Blessed One.

mn142:2.9.verse: Venerable sir, let the Blessed One accept it from me out of compassion.”

mn142:2.10.verse: A second time the Blessed One told her:

mn142:2.12.verse: When you give it to the Sangha, both I and the Sangha will be honoured.”

mn142:2.13.verse: A third time Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said to the Blessed One:

mn142:2.14.verse: “Venerable sir, this new pair of cloths has been spun by me, woven by me, especially for the Blessed One.

mn142:2.15.verse: Venerable sir, let the Blessed One accept it from me out of compassion.”

mn142:2.16.verse: A third time the Blessed One told her:

mn142:2.18.verse: When you give it to the Sangha, both I and the Sangha will be honoured.”

mn142:3.1.verse: Then the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One:

mn142:3.2.verse: “Venerable sir, let the Blessed One accept the new pair of cloths from Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī.

mn142:3.3.verse: Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī has been very helpful to the Blessed One, venerable sir. As his mother’s sister, she was his nurse, his foster mother, the one who gave him milk.

mn142:3.4.verse: She suckled the Blessed One when his own mother died.

mn142:3.5.verse: The Blessed One too has been very helpful to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, venerable sir.

mn142:3.6.verse: It is owing to the Blessed One that Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī has gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha.

mn142:3.7.verse: It is owing to the Blessed One that Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī abstains from killing living beings, from taking what is not given, from misconduct in sensual pleasures, from false speech, and from wine, liquor, and intoxicants, which are the basis of negligence.

mn142:3.8.verse: It is owing to the Blessed One that Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī possesses unwavering confidence in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha, and that she possesses the virtues loved by noble ones.

mn142:3.9.verse: It is owing to the Blessed One that Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī is free from doubt about suffering, about the origin of suffering, about the cessation of suffering, and about the way leading to the cessation of suffering.

mn142:3.10.verse: The Blessed One has been very helpful to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī.”

mn142:4.1.verse: “That is so, Ānanda, that is so!

mn142:4.2.verse: When one person, owing to another, has gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha, I say that it is not easy for the former to repay the latter—that is,

mn142:4.3.verse: by paying homage to him, rising up for him, according him reverential salutation and polite services, and by providing robes, almsfood, resting places, and medicinal requisites.

mn142:4.4.verse: When one person, owing to another, has come to abstain from killing living beings, from taking what is not given, from misconduct in sensual pleasures, from false speech, and from wine, liquor, and intoxicants, which are the basis of negligence, I say that it is not easy for the former to repay the latter—that is,

mn142:4.5.verse: by paying homage to him…and medicinal requisites.

mn142:4.6.verse: When one person, owing to another, has come to possess unwavering confidence in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha, and to possess the virtues loved by noble ones, I say that it is not easy for the former to repay the latter—that is,

mn142:4.7.verse: by paying homage to him…and medicinal requisites.

mn142:4.8.verse: When one person, owing to another, has become free from doubt about suffering, about the origin of suffering, about the cessation of suffering, and about the way leading to the cessation of suffering, I say that it is not easy for the former to repay the latter—that is,

mn142:4.9.verse: by paying homage to him…and medicinal requisites.

mn142:5.1.verse: “There are fourteen kinds of personal offerings, Ānanda.

mn142:5.3.verse: One gives a gift to the Tathāgata, accomplished and fully enlightened;

mn142:5.4.verse: this is the first kind of personal offering.

mn142:5.5.verse: One gives a gift to a paccekabuddha;

mn142:5.6.verse: this is the second kind of personal offering.

mn142:5.7.verse: One gives a gift to an arahant disciple of the Tathāgata;

mn142:5.8.verse: this is the third kind of personal offering.

mn142:5.9.verse: One gives a gift to one who has entered upon the way to the realisation of the fruit of arahantship;

mn142:5.10.verse: this is the fourth kind of personal offering.

mn142:5.11.verse: One gives a gift to a non-returner;

mn142:5.12.verse: this is the fifth kind of personal offering.

mn142:5.13.verse: One gives a gift to one who has entered upon the way to the realisation of the fruit of non-return;

mn142:5.14.verse: this is the sixth kind of personal offering.

mn142:5.15.verse: One gives a gift to a once-returner;

mn142:5.16.verse: this is the seventh kind of personal offering.

mn142:5.17.verse: One gives a gift to one who has entered upon the way to the realisation of the fruit of once-return;

mn142:5.18.verse: this is the eighth kind of personal offering.

mn142:5.19.verse: One gives a gift to a stream-enterer;

mn142:5.20.verse: this is the ninth kind of personal offering.

mn142:5.21.verse: One gives a gift to one who has entered upon the way to the realisation of the fruit of stream-entry;

mn142:5.22.verse: this is the tenth kind of personal offering.

mn142:5.23.verse: One gives a gift to one outside [the Dispensation] who is free from lust for sensual pleasures;

mn142:5.24.verse: this is the eleventh kind of personal offering.

mn142:5.25.verse: One gives a gift to a virtuous ordinary person;

mn142:5.26.verse: this is the twelfth kind of personal offering.

mn142:5.27.verse: One gives a gift to an immoral ordinary person;

mn142:5.28.verse: this is the thirteenth kind of personal offering.

mn142:5.29.verse: One gives a gift to an animal;

mn142:5.30.verse: this is the fourteenth kind of personal offering.

mn142:6.1.verse: “Herein, Ānanda, by giving a gift to an animal, the offering may be expected to repay a hundredfold. By giving a gift to an immoral ordinary person, the offering may be expected to repay a thousandfold. By giving a gift to a virtuous ordinary person, the offering may be expected to repay a hundred-thousandfold. By giving a gift to one outside [the Dispensation] who is free from lust for sensual pleasures, the offering may be expected to repay a hundred-thousand times a hundred-thousandfold. By giving a gift to one who has entered upon the way to the realisation of the fruit of stream-entry, the offering may be expected to repay incalculably, immeasurably. What, then, should be said about giving a gift to a stream-enterer? What should be said about giving a gift to one who has entered upon the way to the realisation of the fruit of once-return…to a once-returner…to one who has entered upon the way to the realisation of the fruit of non-return…to a non-returner…to one who has entered upon the way to the realisation of the fruit of arahantship…to an arahant…to a paccekabuddha? What should be said about giving a gift to a Tathāgata, accomplished and fully enlightened?

mn142:7.1.verse: “There are seven kinds of offerings made to the Sangha, Ānanda.

mn142:7.3.verse: One gives a gift to a Sangha of both [bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs] headed by the Buddha;

mn142:7.4.verse: this is the first kind of offering made to the Sangha.

mn142:7.5.verse: One gives a gift to a Sangha of both [bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs] after the Tathāgata has attained final Nibbāna;

mn142:7.6.verse: this is the second kind of offering made to the Sangha.

mn142:7.7.verse: One gives a gift to a Sangha of bhikkhus;

mn142:7.8.verse: this is the third kind of offering made to the Sangha.

mn142:7.9.verse: One gives a gift to a Sangha of bhikkhunīs;

mn142:7.10.verse: this is the fourth kind of offering made to the Sangha.

mn142:7.11.verse: One gives a gift, saying: ‘Appoint so many bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs for me from the Sangha’;

mn142:7.12.verse: this is the fifth kind of offering made to the Sangha.

mn142:7.13.verse: One gives a gift, saying: ‘Appoint so many bhikkhus for me from the Sangha’;

mn142:7.14.verse: this is the sixth kind of offering made to the Sangha.

mn142:7.15.verse: One gives a gift, saying: ‘Appoint so many bhikkhunīs for me from the Sangha’;

mn142:7.16.verse: this is the seventh kind of offering made to the Sangha.

mn142:8.1.verse: “In future times, Ānanda, there will be members of the clan who are ‘yellow-necks,’ immoral, of evil character.

mn142:8.2.verse: People will give gifts to those immoral persons for the sake of the Sangha.

mn142:8.3.verse: Even then, I say, an offering made to the Sangha is incalculable, immeasurable.

mn142:8.4.verse: And I say that in no way is a gift to a person individually ever more fruitful than an offering made to the Sangha.

mn142:9.1.verse: “There are, Ānanda, four kinds of purification of offering.

mn142:9.3.verse: There is the offering that is purified by the giver, not by the receiver.

mn142:9.4.verse: There is the offering that is purified by the receiver, not by the giver.

mn142:9.5.verse: There is the offering that is purified neither by the giver nor by the receiver.

mn142:9.6.verse: There is the offering that is purified both by the giver and by the receiver.

mn142:10.1.verse: “And how is the offering purified by the giver, not by the receiver?

mn142:10.2.verse: Here the giver is virtuous, of good character, and the receiver is immoral, of evil character.

mn142:10.3.verse: Thus the offering is purified by the giver, not by the receiver.

mn142:11.1.verse: “And how is the offering purified by the receiver, not by the giver?

mn142:11.2.verse: Here the giver is immoral, of evil character, and the receiver is virtuous, of good character.

mn142:11.3.verse: Thus the offering is purified by the receiver, not by the giver.

mn142:12.1.verse: “And how is the offering purified neither by the giver nor by the receiver?

mn142:12.2.verse: Here the giver is immoral, of evil character, and the receiver is immoral, of evil character.

mn142:12.3.verse: Thus the offering is purified neither by the giver nor by the receiver.

mn142:13.1.verse: “And how is the offering purified both by the giver and by the receiver?

mn142:13.2.verse: Here the giver is virtuous, of good character, and the receiver is virtuous, of good character.

mn142:13.3.verse: Thus the offering is purified both by the giver and by the receiver.

mn142:13.4.verse: These are the four kinds of purification of offering.”

mn142:14.1.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

mn142:14.2.verse: When the Sublime One had said that, the Teacher said further:

mn142:14.3.verse: “When a virtuous person to an immoral person gives

mn142:14.4.verse: With trusting heart a gift righteously obtained,

mn142:14.5.verse: Placing faith that the fruit of action is great,

mn142:14.6.verse: The giver’s virtue purifies the offering.

mn142:14.7.verse: When an immoral person to a virtuous person gives

mn142:14.8.verse: With untrusting heart a gift unrighteously obtained,

mn142:14.9.verse: Nor places faith that the fruit of action is great,

mn142:14.10.verse: The receiver’s virtue purifies the offering.

mn142:14.11.verse: When an immoral person to an immoral person gives

mn142:14.12.verse: With untrusting heart a gift unrighteously obtained,

mn142:14.13.verse: Nor places faith that the fruit of action is great,

mn142:14.15.verse: When a virtuous person to a virtuous person gives

mn142:14.16.verse: With trusting heart a gift righteously obtained,

mn142:14.17.verse: Placing faith that the fruit of action is great,

mn142:14.18.verse: That gift, I say, will come to full fruition.

mn142:14.19.verse: When a passionless person to a passionless person gives

mn142:14.20.verse: With trusting heart a gift righteously obtained,

mn142:14.21.verse: Placing faith that the fruit of action is great,

mn142:14.22.verse: That gift, I say, is the best of worldly gifts.”

mn143:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

mn143:2.1.verse: Now on that occasion Anāthapiṇḍika the householder was afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.

mn143:2.2.verse: Then Anāthapiṇḍika the householder addressed a certain man thus:

mn143:2.3.verse: ‘Come, good man, go to the Blessed One, and in my name pay homage with your head at his feet, and say:

mn143:2.4.verse: “Venerable sir, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.

mn143:2.5.verse: He pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet.”

mn143:2.6.verse: Then go to the venerable Sāriputta, and in my name pay homage with your head at the venerable Sāriputta’s feet, and say:

mn143:2.7.verse: “Venerable sir, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.

mn143:2.8.verse: He pays homage with his head at the venerable Sāriputta’s feet.”

mn143:2.10.verse: “It would be good, venerable sir, if the venerable Sāriputta would come to the house of Anāthapiṇḍika the householder, out of compassion.”’

mn143:2.11.verse: ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ that man replied to Anāthapiṇḍika the householder, and he went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. Sitting at one side, that man said to the Blessed One:

mn143:2.12.verse: ‘Venerable sir, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.

mn143:2.13.verse: He pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet.’

mn143:2.14.verse: Then he went to the venerable Sāriputta, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. Sitting at one side, that man said to the venerable Sāriputta:

mn143:2.15.verse: ‘Venerable sir, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.

mn143:2.16.verse: He pays homage with his head at the venerable Sāriputta’s feet;

mn143:2.18.verse: “It would be good, venerable sir, if the venerable Sāriputta would come to the house of Anāthapiṇḍika the householder, out of compassion.”’

mn143:2.19.verse: The venerable Sāriputta consented in silence.

mn143:3.1.verse: Then the venerable Sāriputta dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, went with the venerable Ānanda as his attendant to the house of Anāthapiṇḍika the householder; having gone there, he sat down on the seat made ready. Sitting there, the venerable Sāriputta said to Anāthapiṇḍika the householder:

mn143:3.2.verse: ‘I hope you are getting well, householder, I hope you are comfortable. I hope your painful feelings are departing and not increasing, and that their departure and not their increase, is apparent.’

mn143:4.1.verse: ‘Venerable Sāriputta, I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not departing; their increase and not their departure is apparent.

mn143:4.2.verse: Just as if a strong man were splitting my head open with a sharp sword, so too, venerable Sāriputta, violent winds cut through my head.

mn143:4.3.verse: I am not getting well, venerable Sāriputta, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not departing; their increase and not their departure is apparent.

mn143:4.4.verse: Just as if a strong man were tightening a tough leather strap round my head as a headband, so too, venerable Sāriputta, there are violent pains in my head.

mn143:4.5.verse: I am not getting well, venerable Sāriputta, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not departing; their increase and not their departure is apparent.

mn143:4.6.verse: Just as if a clever butcher or his apprentice were carving up an ox’s belly with a sharp carving knife, so too, venerable Sāriputta, violent winds are carving up my belly.

mn143:4.7.verse: I am not getting well, venerable Sāriputta, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not departing; their increase and not their departure is apparent.

mn143:4.8.verse: Just as if two strong men had seized a weaker man by both arms and were roasting and thoroughly scorching him over a pit of hot coals, so too, venerable Sāriputta, there is a violent burning in my body.

mn143:4.9.verse: I am not getting well, venerable Sāriputta, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not departing; their increase and not their departure is apparent.’

mn143:5.2.verse: “I will not cling to the eye, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the eye.”

mn143:5.5.verse: “I will not cling to the ear, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the ear.”

mn143:5.8.verse: “I will not cling to the nose, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the nose.”

mn143:5.11.verse: “I will not cling to the tongue, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the tongue.”

mn143:5.14.verse: “I will not cling to the body, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the body.”

mn143:5.17.verse: “I will not cling to the mind, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the mind.”

mn143:6.2.verse: “I will not cling to forms, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on forms.”

mn143:6.6.verse: I will not cling to odours …

mn143:6.7.verse: I will not cling to flavours …

mn143:6.8.verse: I will not cling to tangibles …

mn143:6.9.verse: I will not cling to dhammas, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on dhammas.”

mn143:7.2.verse: “I will not cling to eye-consciousness, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on eye-consciousness.”

mn143:7.6.verse: I will not cling to nose-consciousness …

mn143:7.7.verse: I will not cling to tongue-consciousness …

mn143:7.8.verse: I will not cling to body-consciousness …

mn143:7.9.verse: I will not cling to mind-consciousness, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on mind-consciousness.”

mn143:8.2.verse: “I will not cling to eye-contact, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on eye-contact.”

mn143:8.6.verse: I will not cling to nose-contact …

mn143:8.7.verse: I will not cling to tongue-contact …

mn143:8.8.verse: I will not cling to body-contact …

mn143:8.9.verse: I will not cling to mind-contact, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on mind-contact.”

mn143:9.2.verse: “I will not cling to feeling born of eye-contact, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on feeling born of eye-contact.”

mn143:9.5.verse: “I will not cling to feeling born of ear-contact …

mn143:9.6.verse: I will not cling to feeling born of nose-contact …

mn143:9.7.verse: I will not cling to feeling born of tongue-contact …

mn143:9.8.verse: I will not cling to feeling born of body-contact …

mn143:9.9.verse: I will not cling to feeling born of mind-contact, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on feeling born of mind-contact.”

mn143:10.2.verse: “I will not cling to the earth element, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the earth element.”

mn143:10.5.verse: “I will not cling to the water element …

mn143:10.6.verse: I will not cling to the fire element …

mn143:10.7.verse: I will not cling to the air element …

mn143:10.8.verse: I will not cling to the space element …

mn143:10.9.verse: I will not cling to the consciousness element, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the consciousness element.”

mn143:11.2.verse: “I will not cling to form, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on form.”

mn143:11.6.verse: I will not cling to perception …

mn143:11.7.verse: I will not cling to formations …

mn143:11.8.verse: I will not cling to consciousness, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on consciousness.”

mn143:12.2.verse: “I will not cling to the base consisting of infinite space, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the base consisting of infinite space.”

mn143:12.5.verse: “I will not cling to the base consisting of infinite consciousness …

mn143:12.6.verse: I will not cling to the base consisting of nothingness …

mn143:12.7.verse: I will not cling to the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.”

mn143:13.2.verse: “I will not cling to this world, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on this world.”

mn143:14.2.verse: “I will not cling to the world beyond, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on the world beyond.”

mn143:14.5.verse: “Whatever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, sought after, and explored by the mind, that too I will not cling to, and there shall be no consciousness of mine based on that.”

mn143:15.1.verse: When this was said, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder wept and shed tears.

mn143:15.2.verse: Then the venerable Ānanda said to Anāthapiṇḍika the householder:

mn143:15.3.verse: ‘Are you foundering, householder, are you sinking?’

mn143:15.4.verse: ‘I am not foundering, venerable Ānanda, I am not sinking.

mn143:15.5.verse: Although I have long waited on the Teacher and on the bhikkhus worthy of esteem,

mn143:15.6.verse: yet I have never before heard such a talk on the Dhamma.’

mn143:15.7.verse: ‘Such talk on the Dhamma, householder, is not given to white-clothed laypeople;

mn143:15.8.verse: such talk on the Dhamma, householder, is given to those gone forth.’

mn143:15.9.verse: ‘Then, venerable Sāriputta, let such talk on the Dhamma be given to white-clothed laypeople as well.

mn143:15.10.verse: For there are, venerable sir, clansmen with little dust in their eyes who are wasting away through not hearing such talk on the Dhamma;

mn143:15.11.verse: there will be those who understand the Dhamma.’

mn143:16.1.verse: Then, having advised Anāthapiṇḍika the householder with this advice, the venerable Sāriputta and the venerable Ānanda rose from their seats and departed.

mn143:16.2.verse: Then, not long after the venerable Sāriputta and the venerable Ānanda had left, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder died and reappeared in the Tusita host.

mn143:17.1.verse: Then, when the night was far advanced, Anāthapiṇḍika, a son of the gods, of surpassing beauty, having illuminated the whole of Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he stood at one side.

mn143:17.2.verse: Standing at one side, Anāthapiṇḍika the son of the gods addressed the Blessed One in verses:

mn143:17.4.verse: the resort of the community of seers,

mn143:17.5.verse: dwelt in by the King of Dhamma,

mn143:17.6.verse: a place that gives rise to joy in me.

mn143:17.8.verse: virtue, the supreme way of life—

mn143:17.10.verse: not by clan or by wealth.

mn143:17.12.verse: seeing what is good for himself,

mn143:17.17.verse: even a bhikkhu who has gone beyond

mn143:17.18.verse: can at best only equal him.’

mn143:18.1.verse: This is what Anāthapiṇḍika, the son of the gods, said.

mn143:18.3.verse: Then Anāthapiṇḍika, the son of the gods, thinking:

mn143:18.4.verse: ‘The Teacher approves of me,’ paid homage to the Blessed One, and keeping him on his right, vanished right there.

mn143:19.1.verse: Then, when that night had passed, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:

mn143:19.2.verse: ‘Bhikkhus, last night, when the night was far advanced, a certain son of the gods, of surpassing beauty, having illuminated the whole of Jeta’s Grove, approached me; having approached and paid homage to me, he stood at one side.

mn143:19.3.verse: Standing at one side, that son of the gods addressed me in verses:

mn143:19.5.verse: the resort of the community of seers,

mn143:19.6.verse: dwelt in by the King of Dhamma,

mn143:19.7.verse: a place that gives rise to joy in me.

mn143:19.9.verse: virtue, the supreme way of life—

mn143:19.11.verse: not by clan or by wealth.

mn143:19.13.verse: seeing what is good for himself,

mn143:19.18.verse: even a bhikkhu who has gone beyond

mn143:19.19.verse: can at best only equal him.”

mn143:19.20.verse: This is what that son of the gods said, bhikkhus.

mn143:19.21.verse: Then, thinking: “The Teacher approves of me,” he paid homage to me, and keeping me on his right, vanished right there.’

mn143:20.1.verse: When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One:

mn143:20.2.verse: ‘Surely, venerable sir, that must have been Anāthapiṇḍika, the son of the gods.

mn143:20.3.verse: For Anāthapiṇḍika the householder had full confidence in the venerable Sāriputta.’

mn143:20.5.verse: As far as can be reached by reasoning, Ānanda, you have reached the conclusion.

mn143:20.6.verse: That son of the gods, Ānanda, was Anāthapiṇḍika, and no other.’

mn143:20.7.verse: This is what the Blessed One said.

mn143:20.8.verse: The venerable Ānanda was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn143:20.9.verse: The Discourse Giving Advice to Anāthapiṇḍika, the first, is finished.

mn143:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

mn143:2.1.verse: Now at that time the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

mn143:2.3.verse: “Please, my man, go to the Buddha, and in my name bow with your head to his feet. Say to him:

mn143:2.4.verse: ‘Sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is sick, suffering, gravely ill.

mn143:2.5.verse: He bows with his head to your feet.’

mn143:2.6.verse: Then go to Venerable Sāriputta, and in my name bow with your head to his feet. Say to him:

mn143:2.7.verse: ‘Sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is sick, suffering, gravely ill.

mn143:2.8.verse: He bows with his head to your feet.’

mn143:2.10.verse: ‘Sir, please visit him at his home out of sympathy.’”

mn143:2.11.verse: “Yes, sir,” that man replied. He did as Anāthapiṇḍika asked.

mn143:3.1.verse: Then Venerable Sāriputta robed up and, taking his bowl and robe, went with Venerable Ānanda as his second monk to Anāthapiṇḍika’s home. He sat down on the seat spread out and said to Anāthapiṇḍika,

mn143:3.2.verse: “I hope you’re keeping well, householder, I hope you’re all right. I hope your pain is fading, not growing; that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

mn143:4.1.verse: “I’m not keeping well, Honorable Sāriputta, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.

mn143:4.2.verse: The winds piercing my head are so severe, it feels like a strong man drilling into my head with a sharp point.

mn143:4.4.verse: The pain in my head is so severe, it feels like a strong man tightening a strong leather strap around my head.

mn143:4.6.verse: The winds slicing my belly are so severe, like a deft butcher or their apprentice were slicing open a cow’s belly with a sharp meat cleaver.

mn143:4.8.verse: The burning in my body is so severe, it feels like two strong men grabbing a weaker man by the arms to burn and scorch him on a pit of glowing coals. That’s how severe the burning is in my body.

mn143:4.9.verse: I’m not keeping well, Honorable Sāriputta, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.”

mn143:5.1.verse: “That’s why, householder, you should train like this:

mn143:5.2.verse: ‘I shall not grasp the eye, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on the eye.’

mn143:5.5.verse: ‘I shall not grasp the ear, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on the ear.’ …

mn143:5.8.verse: ‘I shall not grasp the nose, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on the nose.’ …

mn143:5.11.verse: ‘I shall not grasp the tongue, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on the tongue.’ …

mn143:5.14.verse: ‘I shall not grasp the body, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on the body.’ …

mn143:5.17.verse: ‘I shall not grasp the mind, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on the mind.’

mn143:6.2.verse: ‘I shall not grasp sight, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on sight.’ …

mn143:6.9.verse: idea, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on idea.’

mn143:7.2.verse: ‘I shall not grasp eye consciousness, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on eye consciousness.’ …

mn143:7.9.verse: mind consciousness, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on mind consciousness.’

mn143:8.9.verse: mind contact, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on mind contact.’

mn143:9.2.verse: ‘I shall not grasp feeling born of eye contact …

mn143:9.9.verse: feeling born of mind contact, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on the feeling born of mind contact.’

mn143:10.2.verse: ‘I shall not grasp the earth element …

mn143:10.9.verse: consciousness element, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on the consciousness element.’

mn143:11.8.verse: consciousness, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on consciousness.’

mn143:12.2.verse: ‘I shall not grasp the dimension of infinite space …

mn143:12.7.verse: the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.’

mn143:13.2.verse: ‘I shall not grasp this world, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on this world.’

mn143:14.2.verse: ‘I shall not grasp the other world, and there shall be no consciousness of mine dependent on the other world.’

mn143:14.5.verse: ‘I shall not grasp whatever is seen, heard, thought, known, attained, sought, and explored by my mind, and my consciousness will not have that as support.’

mn143:15.1.verse: When he said this, Anāthapiṇḍika cried and burst out in tears.

mn143:15.3.verse: “Are you failing, householder? Are you fading, householder?”

mn143:15.5.verse: But for a long time I have paid homage to the Buddha and the esteemed mendicants.

mn143:15.6.verse: Yet I have never before heard such a Dhamma talk.”

mn143:15.7.verse: “Householder, such Dhamma talk does not strike when teaching white-clothed laypeople.

mn143:15.8.verse: Rather, it strikes when teaching those gone forth.”

mn143:15.9.verse: “Well then, Honorable Sāriputta, let such Dhamma talk strike when teaching white-clothed laypeople as well!

mn143:15.10.verse: There are gentlemen with little dust in their eyes. They’re in decline because they haven’t heard the teaching.

mn143:15.11.verse: There will be those who understand the teaching!”

mn143:16.1.verse: And when the venerables Sāriputta and Ānanda had given the householder Anāthapiṇḍika this advice they rose from their seats and left.

mn143:16.2.verse: Not long after they had left, Anāthapiṇḍika passed away and was reborn in the host of joyful gods.

mn143:17.1.verse: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Anāthapiṇḍika, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

mn143:17.2.verse: and addressed the Buddha in verse:

mn143:17.4.verse: frequented by the Saṅgha of seers,

mn143:17.5.verse: where the King of Dhamma stayed:

mn143:17.14.verse: that’s how they become purified in that.

mn143:17.17.verse: Even a mendicant who has crossed over

mn143:18.1.verse: That is what the godling Anāthapiṇḍika said,

mn143:18.4.verse: knowing that the Teacher concurred, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

mn143:19.1.verse: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha told the mendicants all that had happened.

mn143:20.1.verse: When he had spoken, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha:

mn143:20.2.verse: “Sir, that godling must surely have been Anāthapiṇḍika.

mn143:20.3.verse: For the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was devoted to Venerable Sāriputta.”

mn143:20.5.verse: You’ve reached the logical conclusion, as far as logic goes.

mn143:20.6.verse: For that was indeed the godling Anāthapiṇḍika.”

mn143:20.7.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn143:20.8.verse: Satisfied, Venerable Ānanda approved what the Buddha said.

mn144:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

mn144:2.1.verse: Now at that time the venerables Sāriputta, Mahācunda, and Channa were staying on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

mn144:3.1.verse: Now at that time Venerable Channa was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

mn144:3.2.verse: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Sāriputta came out of retreat, went to Venerable Mahācunda and said to him,

mn144:3.3.verse: “Come, Reverend Cunda, let’s go to see Venerable Channa and ask about his illness.”

mn144:4.1.verse: And then Sāriputta and Mahācunda went to see Channa and exchanged greetings with him.

mn144:4.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side. Then Sāriputta said to Channa,

mn144:4.3.verse: “I hope you’re keeping well, Reverend Channa, I hope you’re all right. I hope your pain is fading, not growing; that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

mn144:5.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.

mn144:5.2.verse: The winds piercing my head are so severe, it feels like a strong man drilling into my head with a sharp point.

mn144:5.4.verse: The pain in my head is so severe, it feels like a strong man tightening a strong leather strap around my head.

mn144:5.6.verse: The winds slicing my belly are so severe, like a deft butcher or their apprentice were slicing open a cow’s belly with a sharp meat cleaver.

mn144:5.8.verse: The burning in my body is so severe, it feels like two strong men grabbing a weaker man by the arms to burn and scorch him on a pit of glowing coals.

mn144:5.9.verse: I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.

mn144:5.10.verse: Reverend Sāriputta, I shall commit suicide. I don’t wish to live.”

mn144:6.2.verse: Venerable Channa, keep going! We want you to keep going.

mn144:6.3.verse: If you don’t have any suitable food, we’ll find it for you.

mn144:6.4.verse: If you don’t have suitable medicine, we’ll find it for you.

mn144:6.5.verse: If you don’t have a capable carer, we’ll find one for you.

mn144:6.7.verse: Venerable Channa, keep going! We want you to keep going.”

mn144:7.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, it’s not that I don’t have suitable food,

mn144:7.4.verse: Moreover, for a long time now I have served the Teacher with love, not without love.

mn144:7.5.verse: For it is proper for a disciple to serve the Teacher with love, not without love.

mn144:7.6.verse: You should remember this: ‘The mendicant Channa will commit suicide blamelessly.’”

mn144:8.1.verse: “I’d like to ask Venerable Channa about a certain point, if you’d take the time to answer.”

mn144:8.2.verse: “Ask, Reverend Sāriputta. When I’ve heard it I’ll know.”

mn144:9.1.verse: “Reverend Channa, do you regard the eye, eye consciousness, and things knowable by eye consciousness in this way: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?

mn144:9.6.verse: mind, mind consciousness, and things knowable by mind consciousness in this way: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

mn144:9.7.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, I regard the eye, eye consciousness, and things knowable by eye consciousness in this way: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

mn144:9.12.verse: mind, mind consciousness, and things knowable by mind consciousness in this way: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self’.”

mn144:10.1.verse: “Reverend Channa, what have you seen, what have you directly known in these things that you regard them in this way: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self’?”

mn144:10.7.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, after seeing cessation, after directly knowing cessation in these things I regard them in this way: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self’.”

mn144:11.1.verse: When he said this, Venerable Mahācunda said to Venerable Channa:

mn144:11.2.verse: “So, Reverend Channa, you should regularly apply your mind to this instruction of the Buddha:

mn144:11.3.verse: ‘For the dependent there is quivering. For the independent there’s no quivering.

mn144:11.4.verse: When there’s no quivering, there is tranquility.

mn144:11.5.verse: When there is tranquility, there’s no inclination.

mn144:11.6.verse: When there’s no inclination, there’s no coming and going.

mn144:11.7.verse: When there’s no coming and going, there’s no passing away and reappearing.

mn144:11.8.verse: When there’s no passing away and reappearing, there’s no this life or the next or between the two.

mn144:11.9.verse: Just this is the end of suffering.’”

mn144:11.10.verse: And when the venerables Sāriputta and Mahācunda had given Venerable Channa this advice they rose from their seats and left.

mn144:12.1.verse: Not long after those venerables had left, Venerable Channa committed suicide.

mn144:13.1.verse: Then Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

mn144:13.3.verse: Where has he been reborn in his next life?”

mn144:13.4.verse: “Sāriputta, didn’t the mendicant Channa declare his blamelessness to you personally?”

mn144:13.5.verse: “Sir, there is a Vajjian village named Pubbajira.

mn144:13.6.verse: There Channa had families who were friendly, intimate, and hospitable.”

mn144:13.7.verse: “The mendicant Channa did indeed have such families.

mn144:13.8.verse: But, Sāriputta, this is not enough for me to call someone ‘blameworthy’.

mn144:13.9.verse: When someone lays down this body and takes up another body, I call them ‘blameworthy’.

mn144:13.10.verse: But the mendicant Channa did no such thing.

mn144:13.11.verse: You should remember this: ‘The mendicant Channa committed suicide blamelessly.’”

mn144:13.12.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn144:13.13.verse: Satisfied, Venerable Sāriputta approved what the Buddha said.

mn144:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary.

mn144:2.1.verse: Now on that occasion the venerable Sāriputta, the venerable Mahā Cunda, and the venerable Channa were living on the mountain Vulture Peak.

mn144:3.1.verse: On that occasion the venerable Channa was afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.

mn144:3.2.verse: Then, when it was evening, the venerable Sāriputta rose from meditation, went to the venerable Mahā Cunda, and said to him:

mn144:3.3.verse: “Friend Cunda, let us go to the venerable Channa and ask about his illness.”

mn144:3.4.verse: “Yes, friend,” the venerable Mahā Cunda replied.

mn144:4.1.verse: Then the venerable Sāriputta and the venerable Mahā Cunda went to the venerable Channa and exchanged greetings with him.

mn144:4.2.verse: When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, they sat down at one side and the venerable Sāriputta said to the venerable Channa:

mn144:4.3.verse: “I hope you are getting well, friend Channa, I hope you are comfortable. I hope your painful feelings are subsiding and not increasing, and that their subsiding, not their increase, is apparent.”

mn144:5.1.verse: “Friend Sāriputta, I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase and not their subsiding is apparent.

mn144:5.2.verse: Just as if a strong man were splitting my head open with a sharp sword, so too, violent winds cut through my head.

mn144:5.3.verse: I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase and not their subsiding is apparent.

mn144:5.4.verse: Just as if a strong man were tightening a tough leather strap around my head as a headband, so too, there are violent pains in my head.

mn144:5.5.verse: I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase and not their subsiding is apparent.

mn144:5.6.verse: Just as if a skilled butcher or his apprentice were to carve up an ox’s belly with a sharp butcher’s knife, so too, violent winds are carving up my belly.

mn144:5.7.verse: I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase and not their subsiding is apparent.

mn144:5.8.verse: Just as if two strong men were to seize a weaker man by both arms and roast him over a pit of hot coals, so too, there is a violent burning in my body.

mn144:5.9.verse: I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase and not their subsiding is apparent.

mn144:5.10.verse: I shall use the knife, friend Sāriputta; I have no desire to live.”

mn144:6.1.verse: “Let the venerable Channa not use the knife.

mn144:6.2.verse: Let the venerable Channa live. We want the venerable Channa to live.

mn144:6.3.verse: If he lacks suitable food, I will go in search of suitable food for him.

mn144:6.4.verse: If he lacks suitable medicine, I will go in search of suitable medicine for him.

mn144:6.5.verse: If he lacks a proper attendant, I will attend on him.

mn144:6.6.verse: Let the venerable Channa not use the knife.

mn144:6.7.verse: Let the venerable Channa live. We want the venerable Channa to live.”

mn144:7.1.verse: “Friend Sāriputta, it is not that I have no suitable food;

mn144:7.2.verse: it is not that I have no suitable medicine;

mn144:7.3.verse: it is not that I have no proper attendant.

mn144:7.4.verse: But rather, friend Sāriputta, the Teacher has long been worshipped by me with love, not without love;

mn144:7.5.verse: for it is proper for the disciple to worship the Teacher with love, not without love.

mn144:7.6.verse: Friend Sāriputta, remember this: ‘the bhikkhu Channa will use the knife blamelessly.’”

mn144:8.1.verse: “We would ask the venerable Channa certain questions, if the venerable Channa finds it opportune to reply.”

mn144:8.2.verse: “Ask, friend Sāriputta. When I have heard, I shall know.”

mn144:9.1.verse: “Friend Channa, do you regard the eye, eye-consciousness, and things cognizable [by the mind] through eye-consciousness thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?

mn144:9.2.verse: Do you regard the ear, ear-consciousness…

mn144:9.6.verse: the mind, mind-consciousness, and things cognizable [by the mind] through mind-consciousness thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

mn144:9.7.verse: “Friend Sāriputta, I regard the eye, eye-consciousness, and things cognizable [by the mind] through eye-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’.

mn144:9.12.verse: the mind, mind-consciousness, and things cognizable [by the mind] through mind-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’.”

mn144:10.1.verse: “Friend Channa, what have you seen and directly known in the eye, in eye-consciousness, and in things cognizable [by the mind] through eye-consciousness, that you regard them thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’?

mn144:10.2.verse: What have you seen and directly known in the ear, in ear-consciousness…

mn144:10.6.verse: in the mind, in mind-consciousness, and in things cognizable [by the mind] through mind-consciousness, that you regard them thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’?”

mn144:10.7.verse: “Friend Sāriputta, it is through seeing and directly knowing cessation in the eye, in eye-consciousness, and in things cognizable [by the mind] through eye-consciousness, that I regard them thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’.

mn144:10.8.verse: It is through seeing and directly knowing cessation in the ear, in ear-consciousness…

mn144:10.12.verse: in the mind, in mind-consciousness, and in things cognizable [by the mind] through mind-consciousness, that I regard them thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’.”

mn144:11.1.verse: When this was said, the venerable Mahā Cunda said to the venerable Channa:

mn144:11.2.verse: “Therefore, friend Channa, this instruction of the Blessed One’s is to be constantly given attention:

mn144:11.3.verse: ‘There is wavering in one who is dependent, there is no wavering in one who is independent;

mn144:11.4.verse: when there is no wavering, there is tranquillity;

mn144:11.5.verse: when there is tranquillity, there is no bias;

mn144:11.6.verse: when there is no bias, there is no coming and going;

mn144:11.7.verse: when there is no coming and going, there is no passing away and reappearing;

mn144:11.8.verse: when there is no passing away and reappearing, there is no here nor beyond nor in between.

mn144:11.9.verse: This is the end of suffering.’”

mn144:11.10.verse: Then when the venerable Sāriputta and the venerable Mahā Cunda had advised the venerable Channa thus, they rose from their seats and went away.

mn144:12.1.verse: Then, soon after the venerable Sāriputta and the venerable Mahā Cunda had gone, the venerable Channa used the knife.

mn144:13.1.verse: Then the venerable Sāriputta went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side and said to the Blessed One:

mn144:13.2.verse: “Venerable sir, the venerable Channa has used the knife.

mn144:13.3.verse: What is his destination, what is his future course?”

mn144:13.4.verse: “Sāriputta, didn’t the bhikkhu Channa declare to you his blamelessness?”

mn144:13.5.verse: “Venerable sir, there is a Vajjian village called Pubbajira.

mn144:13.6.verse: There the venerable Channa had friendly families, intimate families, approachable families [as his supporters].”

mn144:13.7.verse: “Indeed, Sāriputta, the bhikkhu Channa had friendly families, intimate families, approachable families [as his supporters];

mn144:13.8.verse: but I do not say that to this extent he was blameworthy.

mn144:13.9.verse: Sāriputta, when one lays down this body and takes up a new body, then I say one is blameworthy.

mn144:13.10.verse: This did not happen in the case of the bhikkhu Channa;

mn144:13.11.verse: remember this, Sāriputta: ‘the bhikkhu Channa used the knife blamelessly.’”

mn144:13.12.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

mn144:13.13.verse: The venerable Sāriputta was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn145:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

mn145:1.3.verse: Then the venerable Puṇṇa, rising from meditation in the evening, went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. Sitting at one side, the venerable Puṇṇa said to the Blessed One:

mn145:2.1.verse: ‘Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would instruct me in brief, so that, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute.’

mn145:2.2.verse: ‘Then, Puṇṇa, listen and heed well what I shall say.’

mn145:2.3.verse: ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ the venerable Puṇṇa replied.

mn145:3.1.verse: ‘Puṇṇa, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are wished for, desired, agreeable and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.

mn145:3.2.verse: If a bhikkhu relishes, welcomes, and remains holding to that,

mn145:3.3.verse: then, as he relishes, welcomes, and remains holding to it, relishing arises in him.

mn145:3.4.verse: With the arising of relishing, Puṇṇa, there is the arising of suffering, I say.

mn145:3.5.verse: There are sounds cognizable by the ear …

mn145:3.9.verse: dhammas cognizable by the mind that are wished for, desired, agreeable and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.

mn145:3.10.verse: If a bhikkhu relishes, welcomes, and remains holding to that,

mn145:3.11.verse: then, as he relishes, welcomes, and remains holding to it, relishing arises in him.

mn145:3.12.verse: With the arising of relishing, Puṇṇa, there is the arising of suffering, I say.

mn145:4.1.verse: But, Puṇṇa, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are wished for, desired, agreeable and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.

mn145:4.2.verse: If a bhikkhu does not relish, welcome, or remain holding to that,

mn145:4.3.verse: then, as he does not relish, welcome, or remain holding to it, relishing ceases in him.

mn145:4.4.verse: With the ceasing of relishing, Puṇṇa, there is the ceasing of suffering, I say.

mn145:4.5.verse: There are sounds cognizable by the ear …

mn145:4.9.verse: dhammas cognizable by the mind that are wished for, desired, agreeable and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.

mn145:4.10.verse: If a bhikkhu does not relish, welcome, or remain holding to that,

mn145:4.11.verse: then, as he does not relish, welcome, or remain holding to it, relishing ceases in him.

mn145:4.12.verse: With the ceasing of relishing, Puṇṇa, there is the ceasing of suffering, I say.

mn145:5.1.verse: ‘Now, Puṇṇa, having been given this brief instruction by me, in which country will you dwell?’

mn145:5.2.verse: ‘Venerable sir, having been given this brief instruction by the Blessed One, there is a country called Sunāparanta; I will dwell there.’

mn145:5.3.verse: ‘Fierce, Puṇṇa, are the people of Sunāparanta;

mn145:5.4.verse: rough, Puṇṇa, are the people of Sunāparanta.

mn145:5.5.verse: If the people of Sunāparanta abuse and threaten you, Puṇṇa, what will you think then?’

mn145:5.6.verse: ‘Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta abuse and threaten me, then I shall think:

mn145:5.7.verse: “These people of Sunāparanta are good indeed, truly good indeed, in that they do not give me a blow with the fist.”

mn145:5.8.verse: That, Blessed One, is what I shall think;

mn145:5.9.verse: that, Sublime One, is what I shall think.’

mn145:5.10.verse: ‘But, Puṇṇa, if the people of Sunāparanta give you a blow with the fist, what will you think then?’

mn145:5.11.verse: ‘Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta give me a blow with the fist, then I shall think:

mn145:5.12.verse: “These people of Sunāparanta are good indeed, truly good indeed, in that they do not give me a blow with a clod.”

mn145:5.13.verse: That, Blessed One, is what I shall think;

mn145:5.14.verse: that, Sublime One, is what I shall think.’

mn145:5.15.verse: ‘But, Puṇṇa, if the people of Sunāparanta give you a blow with a clod, what will you think then?’

mn145:5.16.verse: ‘Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta give me a blow with a clod, then I shall think:

mn145:5.17.verse: “These people of Sunāparanta are good indeed, truly good indeed, in that they do not give me a blow with a stick.”

mn145:5.18.verse: That, Blessed One, is what I shall think;

mn145:5.19.verse: that, Sublime One, is what I shall think.’

mn145:5.20.verse: ‘But, Puṇṇa, if the people of Sunāparanta give you a blow with a stick, what will you think then?’

mn145:5.21.verse: ‘Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta give me a blow with a stick, then I shall think:

mn145:5.22.verse: “These people of Sunāparanta are good indeed, truly good indeed, in that they do not give me a blow with a knife.”

mn145:5.23.verse: That, Blessed One, is what I shall think;

mn145:5.24.verse: that, Sublime One, is what I shall think.’

mn145:5.25.verse: ‘But, Puṇṇa, if the people of Sunāparanta give you a blow with a knife, what will you think then?’

mn145:5.26.verse: ‘Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta give me a blow with a knife, then I shall think:

mn145:5.27.verse: “These people of Sunāparanta are good indeed, truly good indeed, in that they do not deprive me of life with a sharp knife.”

mn145:5.28.verse: That, Blessed One, is what I shall think;

mn145:5.29.verse: that, Sublime One, is what I shall think.’

mn145:5.30.verse: ‘But, Puṇṇa, if the people of Sunāparanta deprive you of life with a sharp knife, what will you think then?’

mn145:5.31.verse: ‘Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta deprive me of life with a sharp knife, then I shall think:

mn145:5.32.verse: “There have been disciples of the Blessed One who, humiliated and disgusted by the body and by life, sought for a knife-bringer. I have found this knife-bringer without seeking him.”

mn145:5.33.verse: That, Blessed One, is what I shall think;

mn145:5.34.verse: that, Sublime One, is what I shall think.’

mn145:6.2.verse: Possessing such self-control and peacefulness, you will be able to dwell in the country of Sunāparanta.

mn145:6.3.verse: Now, Puṇṇa, you may go at your own convenience.’

mn145:7.1.verse: Then the venerable Puṇṇa, having delighted in and rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the Blessed One, keeping him on his right, he set his lodging in order, and taking his bowl and outer robe, set out on tour toward the country of Sunāparanta.

mn145:7.2.verse: Wandering on tour by stages, he arrived at the country of Sunāparanta.

mn145:7.3.verse: There the venerable Puṇṇa dwelt in the country of Sunāparanta.

mn145:7.4.verse: Then, within that same rainy season, the venerable Puṇṇa established about five hundred male lay followers and about five hundred female lay followers, and within that same rainy season he himself realized the three true knowledges.

mn145:7.5.verse: Then, after some time, the venerable Puṇṇa attained final Nibbāna.

mn145:8.1.verse: Then a number of bhikkhus went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, they sat down at one side. Sitting at one side, those bhikkhus said to the Blessed One:

mn145:8.2.verse: ‘Venerable sir, the clansman named Puṇṇa, to whom the Blessed One gave brief instruction, has died.

mn145:8.3.verse: What is his destination, what is his future course?’

mn145:8.4.verse: ‘Bhikkhus, the clansman Puṇṇa was wise; he practised in accordance with the Dhamma, and he did not trouble me over the interpretation of the Dhamma.

mn145:8.5.verse: The clansman Puṇṇa, bhikkhus, has attained final Nibbāna.’

mn145:8.6.verse: This is what the Blessed One said.

mn145:8.7.verse: Those bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn145:8.8.verse: The Discourse Giving Advice to Puṇṇa, the third, is finished.

mn145:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
