mn151:15.6.verse: ‘The five faculties are developed in me,’ then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

mn151:16.1.verse: “Again, Sāriputta, a bhikkhu should consider thus:

mn151:16.2.verse: ‘Are the five powers developed in me?’

mn151:16.3.verse: If, by reviewing, he knows thus:

mn151:16.4.verse: ‘The five powers are not developed in me,’ then he should make an effort to develop those five powers.

mn151:16.5.verse: But if, by reviewing, he knows thus:

mn151:16.6.verse: ‘The five powers are developed in me,’ then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

mn151:17.1.verse: “Again, Sāriputta, a bhikkhu should consider thus:

mn151:17.2.verse: ‘Are the seven enlightenment factors developed in me?’

mn151:17.3.verse: If, by reviewing, he knows thus:

mn151:17.4.verse: ‘The seven enlightenment factors are not developed in me,’ then he should make an effort to develop those seven enlightenment factors.

mn151:17.5.verse: But if, by reviewing, he knows thus:

mn151:17.6.verse: ‘The seven enlightenment factors are developed in me,’ then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

mn151:18.1.verse: “Again, Sāriputta, a bhikkhu should consider thus:

mn151:18.2.verse: ‘Is the Noble Eightfold Path developed in me?’

mn151:18.3.verse: If, by reviewing, he knows thus:

mn151:18.4.verse: ‘The Noble Eightfold Path is not developed in me,’ then he should make an effort to develop the Noble Eightfold Path.

mn151:18.5.verse: But if, by reviewing, he knows thus:

mn151:18.6.verse: ‘The Noble Eightfold Path is developed in me,’ then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

mn151:19.1.verse: “Again, Sāriputta, a bhikkhu should consider thus:

mn151:19.2.verse: ‘Are serenity and insight developed in me?’

mn151:19.3.verse: If, by reviewing, he knows thus:

mn151:19.4.verse: ‘Serenity and insight are not developed in me,’ then he should make an effort to develop them.

mn151:19.5.verse: But if, by reviewing, he knows thus:

mn151:19.6.verse: ‘Serenity and insight are developed in me,’ then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

mn151:20.1.verse: “Again, Sāriputta, a bhikkhu should consider thus:

mn151:20.2.verse: ‘Are true knowledge and deliverance realised by me?’

mn151:20.3.verse: If, by reviewing, he knows thus:

mn151:20.4.verse: ‘True knowledge and deliverance are not realised by me,’ then he should make an effort to realise true knowledge and deliverance.

mn151:20.5.verse: But if, by reviewing, he knows thus:

mn151:20.6.verse: ‘True knowledge and deliverance are realised by me,’ then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

mn151:21.1.verse: “Sāriputta, whatever recluses and brahmins in the past have purified their almsfood have all done so by repeatedly reviewing thus.

mn151:21.2.verse: Whatever recluses and brahmins in the future will purify their almsfood will all do so by repeatedly reviewing thus.

mn151:21.3.verse: Whatever recluses and brahmins in the present are purifying their almsfood are all doing so by repeatedly reviewing thus.

mn151:21.4.verse: Therefore, Sāriputta, ‘We will purify our almsfood by repeatedly reviewing thus’—

mn151:21.6.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

mn151:21.7.verse: The venerable Sāriputta was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

mn152:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kajaṅgalā in a bamboo grove.

mn152:2.1.verse: Then the student Uttara, a pupil of the brahmin Pārāsariya, approached the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

mn152:2.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

mn152:2.3.verse: “Uttara, does Pārāsariya teach his disciples the development of the faculties?”

mn152:2.6.verse: “Worthy Gotama, it’s when the eye sees no sight and the ear hears no sound.

mn152:2.7.verse: That’s how Pārāsariya teaches his disciples the development of the faculties.”

mn152:2.8.verse: “In that case, Uttara, a blind person and a deaf person will have developed faculties

mn152:2.10.verse: For a blind person sees no sight with their eyes and a deaf person hears no sound with their ears.”

mn152:2.11.verse: When he said this, Uttara sat silent, dismayed, shoulders drooping, downcast, depressed, with nothing to say.

mn152:3.1.verse: Knowing this, the Buddha addressed Venerable Ānanda,

mn152:3.2.verse: “Ānanda, the development of the faculties taught by Pārāsariya is quite different from the supreme development of the faculties in the training of the Noble One.”

mn152:3.3.verse: “Now is the time, Blessed One! Now is the time, Holy One.

mn152:3.4.verse: Let the Buddha teach the supreme development of the faculties in the training of the Noble One. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

mn152:3.5.verse: “Well then, Ānanda, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

mn152:4.1.verse: “And how, Ānanda, is there the supreme development of the faculties in the training of the Noble One?

mn152:4.2.verse: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, in them arises what is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:4.4.verse: ‘What is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable have arisen in me.

mn152:4.5.verse: That’s conditioned, crude, and dependently originated.

mn152:4.6.verse: But this is peaceful and sublime, namely

mn152:4.8.verse: Then the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease,

mn152:4.10.verse: It’s like how a person with clear eyes might open their eyes then shut them; or might shut their eyes then open them.

mn152:4.11.verse: Such is the speed, the swiftness, the ease with which anything agreeable, disagreeable, and both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease, and equanimity becomes stabilized.

mn152:4.12.verse: In the training of the Noble One this is called the supreme development of the faculties regarding sights known by the eye.

mn152:5.1.verse: Furthermore, when a mendicant hears a sound with their ears, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

mn152:5.3.verse: ‘What is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable have arisen in me.

mn152:5.4.verse: That’s conditioned, crude, and dependently originated.

mn152:5.5.verse: But this is peaceful and sublime, namely

mn152:5.7.verse: Then the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease,

mn152:5.9.verse: It’s like how a strong person can effortlessly snap their fingers.

mn152:5.10.verse: Such is the speed, the swiftness, the ease with which anything agreeable, disagreeable, and both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease, and equanimity becomes stabilized.

mn152:5.11.verse: In the training of the Noble One this is called the supreme development of the faculties regarding sounds known by the ear.

mn152:6.1.verse: Furthermore, when a mendicant smells an odor with their nose, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

mn152:6.3.verse: ‘What is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable have arisen in me.

mn152:6.4.verse: That’s conditioned, crude, and dependently originated.

mn152:6.5.verse: But this is peaceful and sublime, namely

mn152:6.7.verse: Then the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease,

mn152:6.9.verse: It’s like how a drop of water would roll off a gently sloping lotus leaf, and would not stay there.

mn152:6.10.verse: Such is the speed, the swiftness, the ease with which anything agreeable, disagreeable, and both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease, and equanimity becomes stabilized.

mn152:6.11.verse: In the training of the Noble One this is called the supreme development of the faculties regarding smells known by the nose.

mn152:7.1.verse: Furthermore, when a mendicant tastes a flavor with their tongue, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

mn152:7.3.verse: ‘What is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable have arisen in me.

mn152:7.4.verse: That’s conditioned, crude, and dependently originated.

mn152:7.5.verse: But this is peaceful and sublime, namely

mn152:7.7.verse: Then the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease,

mn152:7.9.verse: It’s like how a strong person who’s formed a glob of spit on the tip of their tongue could easily spit it out.

mn152:7.10.verse: Such is the speed, the swiftness, the ease with which anything agreeable, disagreeable, and both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease, and equanimity becomes stabilized.

mn152:7.11.verse: In the training of the Noble One this is called the supreme development of the faculties regarding tastes known by the tongue.

mn152:8.1.verse: Furthermore, when a mendicant encounters a touch with their body, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

mn152:8.3.verse: ‘What is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable have arisen in me.

mn152:8.4.verse: That’s conditioned, crude, and dependently originated.

mn152:8.5.verse: But this is peaceful and sublime, namely

mn152:8.7.verse: Then the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease,

mn152:8.9.verse: It’s like how a strong person can extend or contract their arm.

mn152:8.10.verse: Such is the speed, the swiftness, the ease with which anything agreeable, disagreeable, and both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease, and equanimity becomes stabilized.

mn152:8.11.verse: In the training of the Noble One this is called the supreme development of the faculties regarding touches known by the body.

mn152:9.1.verse: Furthermore, when a mendicant knows a thought with their mind, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

mn152:9.3.verse: ‘What is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable have arisen in me.

mn152:9.4.verse: That’s conditioned, crude, and dependently originated.

mn152:9.5.verse: But this is peaceful and sublime, namely

mn152:9.7.verse: Then the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease,

mn152:9.9.verse: It’s like how a strong person could let two or three drops of water fall onto an iron cauldron that had been heated all day.

mn152:9.10.verse: The drops would be slow to fall, but they’d quickly dry up and evaporate.

mn152:9.11.verse: Such is the speed, the swiftness, the ease with which anything agreeable, disagreeable, and both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease, and equanimity becomes stabilized.

mn152:9.12.verse: In the training of the Noble One this is called the supreme development of the faculties regarding ideas known by the mind.

mn152:9.13.verse: That’s how there is the supreme development of the faculties in the training of the Noble One.

mn152:10.1.verse: And how are they a practicing trainee?

mn152:10.2.verse: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

mn152:10.3.verse: They are horrified, repelled, and disgusted by that.

mn152:10.4.verse: When they hear a sound with their ears …

mn152:10.5.verse: When they smell an odor with their nose …

mn152:10.6.verse: When they taste a flavor with their tongue …

mn152:10.7.verse: When they feel a touch with their body …

mn152:10.8.verse: When they know a thought with their mind, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

mn152:10.9.verse: They are horrified, repelled, and disgusted by that.

mn152:10.10.verse: That’s how they are a practicing trainee.

mn152:11-15.1.verse: And how are they a noble one with developed faculties?

mn152:11-15.2.verse: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

mn152:11-15.3.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

mn152:11-15.4.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

mn152:11-15.5.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

mn152:11-15.6.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive and the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

mn152:11-15.7.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

mn152:16.1.verse: When they hear a sound with their ear …

mn152:16.2.verse: When they smell an odor with their nose …

mn152:16.3.verse: When they taste a flavor with their tongue …

mn152:16.4.verse: When they feel a touch with their body …

mn152:16.5.verse: When they know a thought with their mind, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

mn152:16.6.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

mn152:16.7.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

mn152:16.8.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

mn152:16.9.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive and the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

mn152:16.10.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

mn152:16.11.verse: That’s how they are a noble one with developed faculties.

mn152:17.1.verse: So, Ānanda, I have taught the supreme development of the faculties in the training of the Noble One, I have taught the practicing trainee, and I have taught the noble one with developed faculties.

mn152:18.1.verse: Out of sympathy, I’ve done what a teacher should do who wants what’s best for their disciples.

mn152:18.2.verse: Here are these roots of trees, and here are these empty huts. Practice absorption, Ānanda! Don’t be negligent! Don’t regret it later! This is my instruction to you.”

mn152:18.3.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

mn152:18.4.verse: Satisfied, Venerable Ānanda approved what the Buddha said.

mn152:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Kajangalā in a grove of mukhelu trees.

mn152:2.1.verse: Then the brahmin student Uttara, a pupil of the brahmin Pārāsariya, went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.

mn152:2.2.verse: When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. The Blessed One then asked him:

mn152:2.3.verse: “Uttara, does the brahmin Pārāsariya teach his disciples the development of the faculties?”

mn152:2.5.verse: “But, Uttara, how does he teach his disciples the development of the faculties?”

mn152:2.6.verse: “Here, Master Gotama, one does not see forms with the eye, one does not hear sounds with the ear—

mn152:2.7.verse: that is how the brahmin Pārāsariya teaches his disciples the development of the faculties.”

mn152:2.8.verse: “If that is so, Uttara, then a blind man and a deaf man will have developed faculties,

mn152:2.9.verse: according to what the brahmin Pārāsariya says.

mn152:2.10.verse: For a blind man does not see forms with the eye, and a deaf man does not hear sounds with the ear.”

mn152:2.11.verse: When this was said, the brahmin student Uttara, Pārāsariya’s pupil, sat silent, dismayed, with shoulders drooping and head down, glum, and without response.

mn152:3.1.verse: Then, knowing this, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda:

mn152:3.2.verse: “Ānanda, the brahmin Pārāsariya teaches his disciples the development of the faculties in one way, but in the Noble One’s Discipline the supreme development of the faculties is otherwise.”

mn152:3.3.verse: “Now is the time, Blessed One, now is the time, Sublime One,

mn152:3.4.verse: for the Blessed One to teach the supreme development of the faculties in the Noble One’s Discipline. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the bhikkhus will remember it.”

mn152:3.5.verse: “Then listen, Ānanda, and attend closely to what I shall say.”

mn152:3.6.verse: “Yes, venerable sir,” the venerable Ānanda replied.

mn152:4.1.verse: “Now, Ānanda, how is there the supreme development of the faculties in the Noble One’s Discipline?

mn152:4.2.verse: Here, Ānanda, when a bhikkhu sees a form with the eye, there arises in him what is agreeable, there arises what is disagreeable, there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:4.4.verse: ‘There has arisen in me what is agreeable, there has arisen what is disagreeable, there has arisen what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:4.5.verse: But that is conditioned, gross, dependently arisen;

mn152:4.6.verse: this is peaceful, this is sublime, that is—

mn152:4.8.verse: The agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease in him;

mn152:4.10.verse: Just as a man with good sight, having opened his eyes might shut them or having shut his eyes might open them,

mn152:4.11.verse: so too concerning anything at all, the agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease just as quickly, just as rapidly, just as easily, and equanimity is established—

mn152:4.12.verse: this is called in the Noble One’s Discipline the supreme development of the faculties regarding forms cognizable by the eye.

mn152:5.1.verse: “Again, Ānanda, when a bhikkhu hears a sound with the ear, there arises in him what is agreeable, there arises what is disagreeable, there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:5.3.verse: ‘There has arisen in me what is agreeable, there has arisen what is disagreeable, there has arisen what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:5.4.verse: But that is conditioned, gross, dependently arisen;

mn152:5.5.verse: this is peaceful, this is sublime, that is—

mn152:5.7.verse: The agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease in him;

mn152:5.9.verse: Just as a strong man might easily snap his fingers,

mn152:5.10.verse: so too concerning anything at all, the agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease just as quickly, just as rapidly, just as easily, and equanimity is established—

mn152:5.11.verse: this is called in the Noble One’s Discipline the supreme development of the faculties regarding sounds cognizable by the ear.

mn152:6.1.verse: “Again, Ānanda, when a bhikkhu smells an odour with the nose, there arises in him what is agreeable, there arises what is disagreeable, there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:6.3.verse: ‘There has arisen in me what is agreeable, there has arisen what is disagreeable, there has arisen what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:6.4.verse: But that is conditioned, gross, dependently arisen;

mn152:6.5.verse: this is peaceful, this is sublime, that is—

mn152:6.7.verse: The agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease in him;

mn152:6.9.verse: Just as raindrops on a slightly sloping lotus leaf roll off and do not remain there,

mn152:6.10.verse: so too concerning anything at all, the agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease just as quickly, just as rapidly, just as easily, and equanimity is established—

mn152:6.11.verse: this is called in the Noble One’s Discipline the supreme development of the faculties regarding odours cognizable by the nose.

mn152:7.1.verse: “Again, Ānanda, when a bhikkhu tastes a flavour with the tongue, there arises in him what is agreeable, there arises what is disagreeable, there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:7.3.verse: ‘There has arisen in me what is agreeable, there has arisen what is disagreeable, there has arisen what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:7.4.verse: But that is conditioned, gross, dependently arisen;

mn152:7.5.verse: this is peaceful, this is sublime, that is—

mn152:7.7.verse: The agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease in him;

mn152:7.9.verse: Just as a strong man might easily spit out a ball of spittle collected on the tip of his tongue,

mn152:7.10.verse: so too concerning anything at all, the agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease just as quickly, just as rapidly, just as easily, and equanimity is established—

mn152:7.11.verse: this is called in the Noble One’s Discipline the supreme development of the faculties regarding flavours cognizable by the tongue.

mn152:8.1.verse: “Again, Ānanda, when a bhikkhu touches a tangible with the body, there arises in him what is agreeable, there arises what is disagreeable, there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:8.3.verse: ‘There has arisen in me what is agreeable, there has arisen what is disagreeable, there has arisen what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:8.4.verse: But that is conditioned, gross, dependently arisen;

mn152:8.5.verse: this is peaceful, this is sublime, that is—

mn152:8.7.verse: The agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease in him;

mn152:8.9.verse: Just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm,

mn152:8.10.verse: so too concerning anything at all, the agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease just as quickly, just as rapidly, just as easily, and equanimity is established—

mn152:8.11.verse: this is called in the Noble One’s Discipline the supreme development of the faculties regarding tangibles cognizable by the body.

mn152:9.1.verse: “Again, Ānanda, when a bhikkhu cognizes a mind-object with the mind, there arises in him what is agreeable, there arises what is disagreeable, there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:9.3.verse: ‘There has arisen in me what is agreeable, there has arisen what is disagreeable, there has arisen what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:9.4.verse: But that is conditioned, gross, dependently arisen;

mn152:9.5.verse: this is peaceful, this is sublime, that is—

mn152:9.7.verse: The agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease in him;

mn152:9.9.verse: Just as if a man were to let two or three drops of water fall onto an iron plate heated for a whole day,

mn152:9.10.verse: the falling of the drops might be slow but they would quickly vaporise and vanish;

mn152:9.11.verse: so too concerning anything at all, the agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease just as quickly, just as rapidly, just as easily, and equanimity is established—

mn152:9.12.verse: this is called in the Noble One’s Discipline the supreme development of the faculties regarding ideas cognizable by the mind.

mn152:9.13.verse: That is how there is the supreme development of the faculties in the Noble One’s Discipline.

mn152:10.1.verse: “And how, Ānanda, is one a disciple in higher training, one who has entered upon the way?

mn152:10.2.verse: Here, Ānanda, when a bhikkhu sees a form with the eye, there arises in him what is agreeable, there arises what is disagreeable, there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:10.3.verse: He is repelled, humiliated, and disgusted by the agreeable that arose, by the disagreeable that arose, and by the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose.

mn152:10.4.verse: When he hears a sound with the ear…

mn152:10.5.verse: smells an odour with the nose…

mn152:10.6.verse: tastes a flavour with the tongue…

mn152:10.7.verse: touches a tangible with the body…

mn152:10.8.verse: when he cognizes a mind-object with the mind, there arises in him what is agreeable, there arises what is disagreeable, there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:10.9.verse: He is repelled, humiliated, and disgusted by the agreeable that arose, by the disagreeable that arose, and by the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose.

mn152:10.10.verse: That is how one is a disciple in higher training, one who has entered upon the way.

mn152:11-15.1.verse: “And how, Ānanda, is one a noble one with developed faculties?

mn152:11-15.2.verse: Here, Ānanda, when a bhikkhu sees a form with the eye, there arises in him what is agreeable, there arises what is disagreeable, there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:11-15.3.verse: If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive,’ he abides perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive.

mn152:11-15.4.verse: If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ he abides perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive.

mn152:11-15.5.verse: If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ he abides perceiving the unrepulsive in that.

mn152:11-15.6.verse: If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive and the repulsive,’ he abides perceiving the repulsive in that.

mn152:11-15.7.verse: If he should wish: ‘May I, avoiding both the repulsive and unrepulsive, abide in equanimity, mindful and fully aware,’ he abides in equanimity towards that, mindful and fully aware.

mn152:16.1.verse: “Again, Ānanda, when a bhikkhu hears a sound with the ear…

mn152:16.2.verse: smells an odour with the nose…

mn152:16.3.verse: tastes a flavour with the tongue…

mn152:16.4.verse: touches a tangible with the body…

mn152:16.5.verse: when he cognizes a mind-object with the mind, there arises in him what is agreeable, there arises what is disagreeable, there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

mn152:16.6.verse: If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive,’ he abides perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive.

mn152:16.7.verse: If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ he abides perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive.

mn152:16.8.verse: If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ he abides perceiving the unrepulsive in that.

mn152:16.9.verse: If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive and the repulsive,’ he abides perceiving the repulsive in that.

mn152:16.10.verse: If he should wish: ‘May I, avoiding both the repulsive and unrepulsive, abide in equanimity, mindful and fully aware,’ he abides in equanimity towards that, mindful and fully aware.

mn152:16.11.verse: That is how one is a noble one with developed faculties.

mn152:17.1.verse: “So, Ānanda, the supreme development of the faculties in the Noble One’s Discipline has been taught by me, the disciple in higher training who has entered upon the way has been taught by me, and the noble one with developed faculties has been taught by me.

mn152:18.1.verse: “What should be done for his disciples out of compassion by a Teacher who seeks their welfare and has compassion for them, that I have done for you, Ānanda.

mn152:18.2.verse: There are these roots of trees, these empty huts. Meditate, Ānanda, do not delay, or else you will regret it later. This is our instruction to you.”

mn152:18.3.verse: That is what the Blessed One said.

mn152:18.4.verse: The venerable Ānanda was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

sn1.1:1.2.verse: that on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn1.1:1.3.verse: Then a certain devatā, in the far extreme of the night, her extreme radiance lighting up the entirety of Jeta’s Grove, went to the Blessed One. On arrival, having bowed down to him, she stood to one side. As she was standing there, she said to him,

sn1.1:1.4.verse: “Tell me, dear sir, how you crossed over the flood.”

sn1.1:1.5.verse: “I crossed over the flood without pushing forward, without staying in place.”

sn1.1:1.6.verse: “But how, dear sir, did you cross over the flood without pushing forward, without staying in place?”

sn1.1:1.7.verse: “When I stayed in place, I sank.

sn1.1:1.8.verse: When I pushed forward, I was whirled about.

sn1.1:1.9.verse: And so I crossed over the flood without pushing forward, without staying in place.”

sn1.1:2.3.verse: who without staying in place, without pushing forward,

sn1.1:2.4.verse: has crossed over the entanglements of the world.”

sn1.1:3.1.verse: That is what the devatā said.

sn1.1:3.4.verse: Realizing that “The Teacher has approved of me,” she bowed down to him, circumambulated him, keeping him to her righ, and then vanished right there.

sn1.1:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn1.1:1.3.verse: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,

sn1.1:1.4.verse: “Good fellow, how did you cross the flood?”

sn1.1:1.5.verse: “Neither standing nor swimming, respectable sir, I crossed the flood.”

sn1.1:1.6.verse: “But in what way did you cross the flood neither standing nor swimming?”

sn1.1:1.8.verse: When I swam, I was swept away.

sn1.1:1.9.verse: That’s how I crossed the flood neither standing nor swimming.”

sn1.1:2.4.verse: he’s crossed over clinging to the world.”

sn1.1:3.1.verse: That is what that deity said,

sn1.1:3.4.verse: Then that deity, knowing that the Teacher concurred, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

sn1.1:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Savatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anathapiṇḍika’s Park.

sn1.1:1.3.verse: Then, when the night had advanced, a certain devatā of stunning beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One, stood to one side, and said to him:

sn1.1:1.4.verse: “How, dear sir, did you cross the flood?”

sn1.1:1.5.verse: “By not halting, friend, and by not straining I crossed the flood. ”

sn1.1:1.6.verse: “But how is it, dear sir, that by not halting and by not straining you crossed the flood?”

sn1.1:1.7.verse: “When I came to a standstill, friend, then I sank;

sn1.1:1.8.verse: but when I struggled, then I got swept away.

sn1.1:1.9.verse: It is in this way, friend, that by not halting and by not straining I crossed the flood. ”

sn1.1:2.1.verse: “After a long time at last I see

sn1.1:2.2.verse: A brahmin who is fully quenched,

sn1.1:2.3.verse: Who by not halting, not straining,

sn1.1:2.4.verse: Has crossed over attachment to the world.”

sn1.1:3.1.verse: This is what that devatā said.

sn1.1:3.4.verse: “The Teacher has approved of me, ” paid homage to the Blessed One and, keeping him on the right, disappeared right there.

sn1.2:1.2.verse: Then a certain devatā, in the far extreme of the night, her extreme radiance lighting up the entirety of Jeta’s Grove, went to the Blessed One. On arrival, having bowed down to him, she stood to one side. As she was standing there, she said to him,

sn1.2:2.1.verse: “Do you know, dear sir, freedom, liberation, seclusion for beings?”

sn1.2:3.1.verse: “Yes, friend, I know freedom, liberation, seclusion for beings.”

sn1.2:4.1.verse: “But how, dear sir, do you know freedom, liberation, seclusion for beings?”

sn1.2:5.1.verse: “From the destruction of delight in becoming,

sn1.2:5.2.verse: from the ending of perception & consciousness,

sn1.2:5.3.verse: from the cessation, stilling, of feelings:

sn1.2:1.2.verse: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,

sn1.2:2.1.verse: “Good fellow, do you know the liberation, emancipation, and seclusion of sentient beings?”

sn1.2:4.1.verse: “But how is it that you know the liberation, emancipation, and seclusion of sentient beings?”

sn1.2:5.1.verse: “Due to the ending of relish for rebirth;

sn1.2:5.2.verse: due to the finishing of perception and consciousness;

sn1.2:5.3.verse: due to the cessation and stilling of feelings—

sn1.2:5.4.verse: that, respectable sir, is how I know the liberation,

sn1.2:5.5.verse: emancipation, and seclusion of sentient beings.”

sn1.2:1.2.verse: Then, when the night had advanced, a certain devatā of stunning beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One, stood to one side, and said to him:

sn1.2:2.1.verse: “Do you know, dear sir, emancipation, release, seclusion for beings?”

sn1.2:3.1.verse: “I know, friend, emancipation, release, seclusion for beings. ”

sn1.2:4.1.verse: “But in what way, dear sir, do you know emancipation, release, seclusion for beings?”

sn1.2:5.1.verse: “By the utter destruction of delight in existence,

sn1.2:5.2.verse: By the extinction of perception and consciousness,

sn1.2:5.3.verse: By the cessation and appeasement of feelings:

sn1.2:5.4.verse: It is thus, friend, that I know for beings—

sn1.3:1.2.verse: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.3:2.1.verse: “This life, so very short, is led onward.

sn1.3:2.2.verse: One led on to old age has no shelter.

sn1.3:2.4.verse: do good deeds that bring you joy.”

sn1.3:3.1.verse: “This life, so very short, is led onward.

sn1.3:3.2.verse: One led on to old age has no shelter.

sn1.3:3.4.verse: a seeker of peace would drop the world’s bait.”

sn1.3:1.2.verse: Standing to one side, that devatā recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.3:2.1.verse: “Life is swept along,  short is the life span;

sn1.3:2.2.verse: No shelters exist for one who has reached old age.

sn1.3:2.3.verse: Seeing clearly this danger in death,

sn1.3:2.4.verse: One should do deeds of merit that bring happiness. ”

sn1.3:3.1.verse: “Life is swept along, short is the life span;

sn1.3:3.2.verse: No shelters exist for one who has reached old age.

sn1.3:3.3.verse: Seeing clearly this danger in death,

sn1.3:3.4.verse: A seeker of peace should drop the world’s bait. ”

sn1.4:1.2.verse: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.4:2.2.verse: the stages of life leave us one by one.

sn1.4:2.4.verse: do good deeds that bring you joy.”

sn1.4:3.2.verse: the stages of life leave us one by one.

sn1.4:3.4.verse: a seeker of peace would drop the world’s bait.”

sn1.4:1.2.verse: Standing to one side, that devatā recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.4:2.1.verse: “Time flies by, the nights swiftly pass;

sn1.4:2.2.verse: The stages of life successively desert us.

sn1.4:2.3.verse: Seeing clearly this danger in death,

sn1.4:2.4.verse: One should do deeds of merit that bring happiness. ”

sn1.4:3.1.verse: “Time flies by, the nights swiftly pass;

sn1.4:3.2.verse: The stages of life successively desert us.

sn1.4:3.3.verse: Seeing clearly this danger in death,

sn1.4:3.4.verse: A seeker of peace should drop the world’s bait. ”

sn1.5:1.2.verse: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.5:2.3.verse: When a mendicant slips how many chains

sn1.5:2.4.verse: are they said to have crossed the flood?”

sn1.5:3.3.verse: When a mendicant slips five chains

sn1.5:3.4.verse: they’re said to have crossed the flood.”

sn1.5:1.2.verse: Standing to one side, that devatā recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.5:2.1.verse: “How many must one cut, how many abandon,

sn1.5:2.2.verse: And how many further must one develop?

sn1.5:2.3.verse: When a bhikkhu has surmounted how many ties

sn1.5:2.4.verse: Is he called a crosser of the flood?”

sn1.5:3.1.verse: “One must cut off five, abandon five,

sn1.5:3.2.verse: And must develop a further five.

sn1.5:3.3.verse: A bhikkhu who has surmounted five ties

sn1.5:3.4.verse: Is called a crosser of the flood. ”

sn1.6:1.2.verse: Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.6:2.2.verse: How many wake among the sleeping?

sn1.6:2.3.verse: By how many do you gather dust?

sn1.6:2.4.verse: By how many are you cleansed?”

sn1.6:1.2.verse: Standing to one side, that devatā recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.6:2.1.verse: “How many are asleep when others are awake?

sn1.6:2.2.verse: How many are awake when others sleep?

sn1.6:2.3.verse: By how many does one gather dust?

sn1.6:2.4.verse: By how many is one purified?”

sn1.6:3.1.verse: “Five are asleep when others are awake;

sn1.6:3.2.verse: Five are awake when others sleep.

sn1.6:3.3.verse: By five things one gathers dust,

sn1.20:2.4.verse: Don’t let time pass you by.”

sn1.20:3.3.verse: That’s why, not having enjoyed, I go for alms:

sn1.20:3.4.verse: Don’t let my time pass me by.”

sn1.20:4.1.verse: Then the devatā, coming down to earth, said to Ven. Samiddhi,

sn1.20:4.2.verse: “You have gone forth while young, monk—black-haired, endowed with the blessings of youth in the first stage of life—without having played with sensuality.

sn1.20:4.4.verse: Don’t drop what is visible here & now in pursuit of what’s subject to time.”

sn1.20:5.3.verse: For the Blessed One has said that sensuality is subject to time, of much stress, much despair, & greater drawbacks;

sn1.20:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Hot Springs Monastery.

sn1.20:1.3.verse: Then Venerable Samiddhi rose at the crack of dawn and went to the hot springs to bathe.

sn1.20:1.5.verse: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire hot springs, went up to Samiddhi, and, standing in the air, addressed him in verse:

sn1.20:4.4.verse: Don’t give up what is apparent in the present to chase after what takes effect over time.”

sn1.20:5.3.verse: For the Buddha has said that sensual pleasures take effect over time, with much suffering and distress, and they’re all the more full of drawbacks.

sn1.20:5.4.verse: But this teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.”

sn1.20:25.1.verse: “They gave up judgment without falling into conceit;

sn1.20:25.2.verse: craving for name and form was cut off right here.

sn1.20:25.3.verse: They cut the ties, untroubled, with no need for hope.

sn1.20:25.4.verse: Though gods and humans search for them

sn1.20:25.5.verse: in this life or the next, they never find them,

sn1.20:25.6.verse: not in heaven nor in any abode.

sn1.20:26.1.verse: Tell me if you understand, spirit.”

sn1.20:27.1.verse: “This is how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement:

sn1.20:28.1.verse: You should never do anything bad

sn1.20:28.2.verse: by speech or mind or body in all the world.

sn1.20:28.3.verse: Having given up sensual pleasures, mindful and aware,

sn1.20:28.4.verse: you shouldn’t keep doing  what’s painful and pointless.”

sn1.20:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Hot Springs Park.

sn1.20:1.3.verse: Then the Venerable Samiddhi, having risen at the first flush of dawn, went to the hot springs to bathe.

sn1.20:1.4.verse: Having bathed in the hot springs and come back out, he stood in one robe drying his limbs.

sn1.20:1.5.verse: Then, when the night had advanced, a certain devatā of stunning beauty, illuminating the entire hot springs, approached the Venerable Samiddhi. Having approached, she stood in the air and addressed the Venerable Samiddhi in verse:

sn1.20:2.1.verse: “Without having enjoyed you seek alms, bhikkhu,

sn1.20:2.2.verse: You don’t seek alms after you’ve enjoyed.

sn1.20:2.3.verse: First enjoy, bhikkhu, then seek alms:

sn1.20:2.4.verse: Don’t let the time pass you by!”

sn1.20:3.1.verse: “I do not know what the time might be;

sn1.20:3.2.verse: The time is hidden and cannot be seen.

sn1.20:3.3.verse: Hence, without enjoying, I seek alms:

sn1.20:3.4.verse: Don’t let the time pass me by!”

sn1.20:4.1.verse: Then that devatā alighted on the earth and said to the Venerable Samiddhi:

sn1.20:4.2.verse: “You have gone forth while young, bhikkhu, a lad with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth, in the prime of life, without having dallied with sensual pleasures.

sn1.20:4.4.verse: bhikkhu; do not abandon what is directly visible in order to pursue what takes time. ”

sn1.20:5.1.verse: “I have not abandoned what is directly visible, friend,

sn1.20:5.2.verse: I have abandoned what takes time in order to pursue what is directly visible.

sn1.20:5.3.verse: For the Blessed One, friend, has stated that sensual pleasures are time-consuming, full of suffering, full of despair, and the danger in them is still greater,

sn1.20:5.4.verse: while this Dhamma is directly visible, immediate, inviting one to come and see, applicable, to be personally experienced by the wise. ”

sn1.20:6.1.verse: “But how is it, bhikkhu, that the Blessed One has stated that sensual pleasures are time-consuming, full of suffering, full of despair, and the danger in them is still greater?

sn1.20:6.2.verse: How is it that this Dhamma is directly visible, immediate, inviting one to come and see, applicable, to be personally experienced by the wise?”

sn1.20:7.1.verse: “I am newly ordained, friend, not long gone forth, just recently come to this Dhamma and Discipline.

sn1.20:7.2.verse: I cannot explain it in detail.

sn1.20:7.3.verse: But that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is dwelling at Rajagaha in the Hot Springs Park.

sn1.20:7.4.verse: Approach that Blessed One and ask him about this matter.

sn1.20:7.5.verse: As he explains it to you, so you should remember it. ”

sn1.20:8.1.verse: “It isn’t easy for us to approach that Blessed One, bhikkhu, as he is surrounded by other devatās of great influence.

sn1.20:8.2.verse: If you would approach him and ask him about this matter, we will come along too in order to hear the Dhamma. ”

sn1.20:8.3.verse: “Very well, friend, ” the Venerable Samiddhi replied. Then he approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported his entire discussion with that devatā, verses 44–45, included in the report, repeat verses 42–43 adding:

sn1.20:17.4.verse: “If that devatā’s statement is true, venerable sir, then that devatā should be close by. ”

sn1.20:18.1.verse: When this was said, that devatā said to the Venerable Samiddhi:

sn1.20:18.2.verse: “Ask, bhikkhu! Ask, bhikkhu! For I have arrived. ”

sn1.20:19.1.verse: Then the Blessed One addressed that devatā in verse:

sn1.20:20.1.verse: “Beings who perceive what can be expressed

sn1.20:20.2.verse: Become established in what can be expressed.

sn1.20:20.3.verse: Not fully understanding what can be expressed,

sn1.20:20.4.verse: They come under the yoke of Death.

sn1.20:21.1.verse: “But having fully understood what can be expressed,

sn1.20:21.2.verse: One does not conceive ‘one who expresses. ’

sn1.20:21.3.verse: For that does not exist for him

sn1.20:21.4.verse: By which one could describe him.

sn1.20:22.1.verse: “I do not understand in detail, venerable sir, the meaning of what was stated in brief by the Blessed One.

sn1.20:22.2.verse: Please, venerable sir, let the Blessed One explain it to me in such a way that I might understand in detail the meaning of what he stated in brief. ”

sn1.20:23.1.verse: “One who conceives ‘I am equal, better, or worse, ’

sn1.20:23.2.verse: Might on that account engage in disputes.

sn1.20:23.3.verse: But one not shaken in the three discriminations

sn1.20:23.4.verse: Does not think,  ‘I am equal or better.

sn1.20:24.1.verse: “In this case too, venerable sir, I do not understand in detail … let the Blessed One explain it to me in such a way that I might understand in detail the meaning of what he stated in brief. ”

sn1.20:25.1.verse: “He abandoned reckoning, did not assume conceit;

sn1.20:25.2.verse: He cut off craving here for name-and-form.

sn1.20:25.3.verse: The one whose knots are cut, the one untroubled, free of longing,

sn1.20:25.4.verse: For him, [they] search and do not find,

sn1.20:25.5.verse: Those devas and humans [search] here and beyond

sn1.20:25.6.verse: in the heavens and all abodes.

sn1.20:27.1.verse: “I understand in detail, venerable sir, the meaning of what was stated in brief by the Blessed One thus:

sn1.20:28.1.verse: One should do no evil, by speech, mind

sn1.20:28.2.verse: or body in all the world;

sn1.20:28.3.verse: Having abandoned sense pleasures, Mindful and clearly comprehending,

sn1.20:28.4.verse: One should not pursue a course That is painful and harmful.

sn1.21:2.2.verse: as if his head were on fire,

sn1.21:2.3.verse: a monk should live the wandering life —mindful—

sn1.21:2.4.verse: for the abandoning of sensual passion.”

sn1.21:3.2.verse: As if his head were on fire,

sn1.22:1.2.verse: It impacts one because they impact others.

sn1.22:1.3.verse: That’s why it impacts one who impacts,

sn1.22:1.4.verse: who wrongs one who’s done no wrong.”

sn1.22:2.1.verse: “Whoever wrongs a man who has done no wrong,

sn1.22:2.2.verse: a pure man who has not a blemish,

sn1.22:2.3.verse: the evil backfires on the fool,

sn1.22:1.1.verse: “It does not touch one who does not touch,

sn1.22:1.2.verse: But then will touch the one who touches.

sn1.22:1.3.verse: Therefore it touches the one who touches,

sn1.22:1.4.verse: The one who wrongs an innocent man. ”

sn1.22:2.3.verse: The evil falls back on the fool himself

sn1.22:2.4.verse: Like fine dust thrown against the wind. ”

sn1.23:1.2.verse: these people are tangled in tangles.

sn1.23:3.1.verse: Those in whom greed, hate, and ignorance

sn1.23:3.3.verse: the perfected ones with defilements ended—

sn1.23:4.2.verse: cease with no residue left behind;

sn1.23:4.3.verse: and impingement and perception of form:

sn1.23:4.4.verse: it’s here this tangle is cut.”

sn1.23:1.2.verse: This generation is entangled in a tangle.

sn1.23:1.3.verse: I ask you this, O Gotama,

sn1.23:3.2.verse: Along with ignorance have been expunged,

sn1.23:3.4.verse: For them the tangle is disentangled.

sn1.23:4.3.verse: And also impingement and perception of form:

sn1.23:4.4.verse: It is here this tangle is cut. ”

sn1.24:1.3.verse: So you should shield the mind from everything,

sn1.24:1.4.verse: then you’re freed from all suffering.”

sn1.24:2.1.verse: “You need not shield the mind from everything,

sn1.24:2.2.verse: nor has the mind gained self-control.

sn1.24:2.3.verse: The mind need only be shielded

sn1.24:2.4.verse: from where the bad things come.”

sn1.24:1.1.verse: “From whatever one reins in the mind,

sn1.24:1.2.verse: From that no suffering comes to one.

sn1.24:1.3.verse: Should one rein in the mind from everything,

sn1.24:1.4.verse: One is freed from all suffering. ”

sn1.24:2.1.verse: “One need not rein in the mind from everything

sn1.24:2.2.verse: When the mind has come under control.

sn1.24:2.3.verse: From whatever it is that evil comes,

sn1.24:2.4.verse: From this one should rein in the mind. ”

sn1.25:1.1.verse: “An arahant monk, one who is done,

sn1.25:1.4.verse: Would he say, ‘They speak to me’?”

sn1.25:2.1.verse: “An arahant monk, one who is done,

sn1.25:2.5.verse: Skillful, knowing harmonious gnosis with regard to the world,

sn1.25:2.6.verse: he uses expressions just as expressions.”

sn1.25:3.1.verse: “An arahant monk, one who is done,

sn1.25:3.5.verse: that he’d say, ‘They speak to me’?”

sn1.25:4.2.verse: whose knot of conceit is dispersed, no knots exist at all.

sn1.25:5.2.verse: Skillful, knowing harmonious gnosis with regard to the world,

sn1.25:1.2.verse: with defilements ended, bearing the final body:

sn1.25:2.2.verse: with defilements ended, bearing the final body:

sn1.25:3.3.verse: is such a mendicant drawing close to conceit

sn1.25:4.1.verse: “Someone who has given up conceit has no ties,

sn1.25:4.2.verse: the ties of conceit are all dissipated.

sn1.25:4.3.verse: Though that intelligent person has passed beyond conceiving,

sn1.25:5.3.verse: they’d use these terms as mere expressions.”

sn1.25:1.4.verse: And would he say, ‘They speak to me’?”

sn1.25:2.2.verse: Consummate, with taints destroyed, One who bears his final body,

sn1.25:2.4.verse: And he might say, ‘They speak to me. ’

sn1.25:2.6.verse: He uses such terms as mere expressions. ”

sn1.25:3.2.verse: Consummate, with taints destroyed, One who bears his final body,

sn1.25:3.3.verse: Is it because he has come upon conceit

sn1.25:3.5.verse: That he would say, ‘They speak to me’?”

sn1.25:4.1.verse: “No knots exist for one with conceit abandoned;

sn1.25:4.2.verse: For him all knots of conceit are consumed.

sn1.25:4.3.verse: Though the wise one has transcended the conceived,

sn1.25:5.1.verse: He might say too, ‘They speak to me. ’

sn1.25:5.3.verse: He uses such terms as mere expressions. ”

sn1.26:1.3.verse: We’ve come to ask the worthy sir:

sn1.26:1.4.verse: how are we to understand this?”

sn1.26:2.1.verse: “There are four lamps in the world,

sn1.26:3.3.verse: But a Buddha is the best of blazes:

sn1.26:1.1.verse: “How many sources of light are in the world

sn1.26:1.2.verse: By means of which the world is illumined?

sn1.26:1.3.verse: We have come to ask the Blessed One this:

sn1.26:1.4.verse: How are we to understand it?”

sn1.26:2.1.verse: “There are four sources of light in the world;

sn1.26:2.2.verse: A fifth one is not found here.

sn1.26:3.1.verse: And fire, both by day and at night,

sn1.26:3.3.verse: But the Buddha is the best of those that shine:

sn1.27:1.2.verse: Where does the cycle spin no more?

sn1.27:1.4.verse: cease with no residue left behind?”

sn1.27:2.2.verse: fire and air have no footing—

sn1.27:2.4.verse: here the cycle spins no more;

sn1.27:2.6.verse: cease with no residue left behind.”

sn1.27:1.1.verse: “From where do the streams turn back?

sn1.27:1.2.verse: Where does the round no longer revolve?

sn1.27:2.2.verse: fire,  and air, Do not gain a footing:

sn1.27:2.3.verse: It is from here that the streams turn back,

sn1.27:2.4.verse: Here that the round no longer revolves;

sn1.28:1.2.verse: even the aristocrats who rule the land,

sn1.28:2.1.verse: Among those of such an avid nature,

sn1.28:2.2.verse: flowing along the stream of lives,

sn1.28:2.3.verse: who here has given up craving?

sn1.28:2.4.verse: Who in the world is not avid?”

sn1.28:3.1.verse: “Having given up their home, their child, their cattle,

sn1.28:3.2.verse: and all that they love, they went forth.

sn1.28:3.3.verse: Having given up desire and hate,

sn1.28:3.5.verse: the perfected ones with defilements ended—

sn1.28:3.6.verse: they in the world are not avid.”

sn1.28:1.2.verse: Even khattiyas who rule the country,

sn1.28:1.3.verse: Look at each other with greedy eyes,

sn1.28:2.1.verse: Among these who have become so avid,

sn1.28:2.2.verse: Flowing along in the stream of existence,

sn1.28:2.4.verse: Who in the world are no longer avid?”

sn1.28:3.1.verse: “Having left their homes and gone forth,

sn1.28:3.2.verse: Having left their dear sons and cattle,

sn1.28:3.3.verse: Having left behind lust and hatred,

sn1.28:3.6.verse: Are those in the world no longer avid. ”

sn1.29:2.3.verse: and having plucked out craving, root and all:

sn1.29:2.4.verse: that’s how you will keep going.”

sn1.29:1.2.verse: Filled up and bound with greed,

sn1.29:1.3.verse: Born from a bog, O great hero!

sn1.29:1.4.verse: How does one escape from it?”

sn1.29:2.1.verse: “Having cut the thong and the strap,

sn1.30:1.3.verse: a giant, wandering alone like a lion,

sn1.30:1.4.verse: you’re not concerned for sensual pleasures.

sn1.30:1.6.verse: How is one released from all suffering?”

sn1.30:2.1.verse: “The world has five kinds of sensual stimulation,

sn1.30:2.2.verse: and the mind is said to be the sixth.

sn1.30:2.3.verse: When you’ve discarded desire for these,

sn1.30:1.1.verse: Of the slender hero with antelope calves,

sn1.30:1.3.verse: Wandering alone like a lion or naga,

sn1.30:1.5.verse: “Having approached you, we ask a question

sn1.30:1.6.verse: How is one released from suffering?”

sn1.30:2.1.verse: “Five cords of sensual pleasure in the world,

sn1.30:2.2.verse: With mind declared to be the sixth:

sn1.30:2.4.verse: One is thus released from suffering. ”

sn1.32:0.2.verse: 4. The Host of a Hundred Felicities

sn1.32:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn1.32:1.2.verse: Then, late at night, several glorious deities of the host of a hundred felicities, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side.

sn1.32:1.3.verse: Standing to one side, one deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.32:3.1.verse: Then another deity recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.32:4.1.verse: “When a miser fails to give because of fear,

sn1.32:4.2.verse: the very thing they’re afraid of comes to pass.

sn1.32:4.6.verse: in this world and the next.

sn1.32:5.2.verse: overcoming that stain, and give a gift.

sn1.32:5.3.verse: The good deeds of sentient beings

sn1.32:5.4.verse: support them in the next world.”

sn1.32:6.1.verse: Then another deity recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.32:7.1.verse: “Among the dead they do not die,

sn1.32:7.2.verse: those who, like fellow travelers on the road,

sn1.32:7.3.verse: are happy to provide, though they have but little.

sn1.32:8.1.verse: Some who have little are happy to provide,

sn1.32:8.2.verse: while some who have much don’t wish to give.

sn1.32:9.1.verse: Then another deity recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.32:10.3.verse: the wicked don’t act like this,

sn1.32:10.4.verse: for the teaching of the good is hard to follow.

sn1.32:11.1.verse: That’s why the virtuous and the wicked

sn1.32:11.4.verse: while the virtuous are bound for heaven.”

sn1.32:12.1.verse: Then another deity said to the Buddha,

sn1.32:13.1.verse: “You’ve all spoken well in your own way. However, listen to me also:

sn1.32:14.1.verse: A hundred thousand people making a thousand sacrifices

sn1.32:14.2.verse: isn’t worth a fraction of that sort,

sn1.32:14.3.verse: who lives rightly, wandering for gleanings,

sn1.32:14.4.verse: or one who supports their partner with what little they have.”

sn1.32:16.1.verse: “Why doesn’t that sacrifice of theirs, so abundant and magnificent,

sn1.32:16.2.verse: equal the value of a moral person’s gift?

sn1.32:16.3.verse: How is it that a hundred thousand people  making a thousand sacrifices

sn1.37:5.1.verse: “The mendicants there are immersed in samādhi,

sn1.37:5.3.verse: Like a charioteer holding the reins,

sn1.37:5.4.verse: the astute ones protect their senses.”

sn1.37:6.1.verse: Then another deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.37:7.1.verse: “They snapped the post and snapped the cross-bar,

sn1.37:7.2.verse: unstirred, they tore out Indra’s pillar.

sn1.37:7.4.verse: the young giants tamed by the Clear-eyed One.”

sn1.37:8.1.verse: Then another deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.37:9.1.verse: “Anyone who has gone to the Buddha for refuge

sn1.37:9.2.verse: won’t go to a plane of loss.

sn1.37:9.3.verse: After giving up this human body,

sn1.37:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Great Wood together with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with five hundred bhikkhus all of whom were arahants.

sn1.37:1.3.verse: And the devatās from ten world systems had for the most part assembled in order to see the Blessed One and the Bhikkhu Saṅgha.

sn1.37:1.4.verse: Then the thought occurred to four devatās of the host from the Pure Abodes:

sn1.37:1.5.verse: “This Blessed One is dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Great Wood together with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with five hundred bhikkhus all of whom are arahants.

sn1.37:1.6.verse: And the devatās from ten world systems have for the most part assembled in order to see the Blessed One and the Bhikkhu Saṅgha.

sn1.37:1.7.verse: Let us also approach the Blessed One and, in his presence, each speak our own verse. ”

sn1.37:2.1.verse: Then, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, those devatās disappeared from among the devas of the Pure Abodes and reappeared before the Blessed One.

sn1.37:2.2.verse: Then those devatās paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side.

sn1.37:2.3.verse: Standing to one side, one devatā recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.37:3.1.verse: “A great concourse takes place in the woods,

sn1.37:3.3.verse: We have come to this Dhamma concourse

sn1.37:4.1.verse: Then another devatā recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.37:5.2.verse: They have straightened their own minds.

sn1.37:5.3.verse: Like a charioteer who holds the reins,

sn1.37:5.4.verse: The wise ones guard their faculties. ”

sn1.37:6.1.verse: Then another devatā recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.37:7.1.verse: “Having cut through barrenness, cut the cross-bar,

sn1.37:7.3.verse: They wander about pure and stainless,

sn1.37:7.4.verse: Young nagas well tamed by the One with Vision. ”

sn1.37:8.1.verse: Then another devatā recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.37:9.1.verse: “Those who have gone to the Buddha for refuge

sn1.37:9.2.verse: Will not go to the plane of misery.

sn1.37:9.4.verse: They will fill the hosts of devas. ”

sn1.38:1.2.verse: on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Rājagaha in the Maddakucchi Deer Reserve.

sn1.38:1.3.verse: Now at that time his foot had been pierced by a stone sliver.

sn1.38:1.4.verse: Excruciating were the bodily feelings that developed within him—painful, fierce, sharp, wracking, repellent, disagreeable—

sn1.38:1.5.verse: but he endured them mindful, alert, & unperturbed.

sn1.38:1.6.verse: Having had his outer robe folded in four and laid out, he lay down on his right side in the lion’s posture, with one foot placed on top of the other, mindful & alert.

sn1.38:2.1.verse: Then 700 devatās from the Satullapa retinue, in the far extreme of the night, their extreme radiance lighting up the entirety of Maddakucchi, went to the Blessed One. On arrival, having bowed down to him, they stood to one side.

sn1.38:2.2.verse: As she was standing there, one of the devatās exclaimed in the Blessed One’s presence:

sn1.38:2.3.verse: “What a nāga is Gotama the contemplative!

sn1.38:2.4.verse: And like a nāga, when bodily feelings have arisen—painful, fierce, sharp, wracking, repellent, disagreeable—he endures them mindful, alert, & unperturbed!”

sn1.38:3.1.verse: Then another devatā exclaimed in the Blessed One’s presence:

sn1.38:3.2.verse: “What a lion is Gotama the contemplative!

sn1.38:3.3.verse: And like a lion, when bodily feelings have arisen—painful, fierce, sharp, wracking, repellent, disagreeable—he endures them mindful, alert, & unperturbed!”

sn1.38:4.1.verse: Then another devatā exclaimed in the Blessed One’s presence:

sn1.38:4.2.verse: “What a thoroughbred is Gotama the contemplative!

sn1.38:4.3.verse: And like a thoroughbred, when bodily feelings have arisen—painful, fierce, sharp, wracking, repellent, disagreeable—he endures them mindful, alert, & unperturbed!”

sn1.38:5.1.verse: Then another devatā exclaimed in the Blessed One’s presence:

sn1.38:5.2.verse: “What a peerless bull is Gotama the contemplative!

sn1.38:5.3.verse: And like a peerless bull, when bodily feelings have arisen—painful, fierce, sharp, wracking, repellent, disagreeable—he endures them mindful, alert, & unperturbed!”

sn1.38:6.1.verse: Then another devatā exclaimed in the Blessed One’s presence:

sn1.38:6.2.verse: “What a strong burden-carrier is Gotama the contemplative!

sn1.38:6.3.verse: And like a strong burden-carrier, when bodily feelings have arisen—painful, fierce, sharp, wracking, repellent, disagreeable—he endures them mindful, alert, & unperturbed!”

sn1.38:7.1.verse: Then another devatā exclaimed in the Blessed One’s presence:

sn1.38:7.2.verse: “What a tamed one is Gotama the contemplative!

sn1.38:7.3.verse: And like a tamed one, when bodily feelings have arisen—painful, fierce, sharp, wracking, repellent, disagreeable—he endures them mindful, alert, & unperturbed!”

sn1.38:8.1.verse: Then another devatā exclaimed in the Blessed One’s presence:

sn1.38:8.2.verse: “See a concentration well-developed, a mind well released—neither pressed down nor forced back, nor with mental fabrication kept blocked or suppressed.

sn1.38:8.3.verse: Whoever would think that such a nāga of a man, lion of a man, thoroughbred of a man, peerless bull of a man, strong burden-carrier of a man, such a tamed man should be violated: What else is that if not blindness?”

sn1.38:9.3.verse: Their minds are not rightly released.

sn1.38:9.4.verse: Lowly by nature, they’ve not gone beyond.

sn1.38:10.1.verse: Overpowered by craving, bound up in habits & practices,

sn1.38:10.3.verse: Their minds are not rightly released.

sn1.38:10.4.verse: Lowly by nature, they’ve not gone beyond.

sn1.38:11.1.verse: For one fond of conceit, there’s no taming;

sn1.38:11.3.verse: Though alone in the wilderness, if one lives heedlessly,

sn1.38:11.4.verse: one won’t cross over, beyond Māra’s sway.

sn1.38:12.1.verse: But having abandoned conceit, well-centered within,

sn1.38:12.2.verse: with right awareness everywhere fully released,

sn1.38:12.3.verse: alone in the wilderness, heedfully living,

sn1.38:12.4.verse: one will cross over, beyond Māra’s sway.”

sn1.38:0.2.verse: 4. The Host of a Hundred Felicities

sn1.38:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Maddakucchi deer park.

sn1.38:1.3.verse: Now at that time the Buddha’s foot had been cut by a wooden splinter.

sn1.38:1.4.verse: The Buddha was stricken by harrowing pains; physical feelings that were painful, sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, and disagreeable.

sn1.38:1.5.verse: But he endured unbothered, with mindfulness and situational awareness.

sn1.38:1.6.verse: And then he spread out his outer robe folded in four and laid down in the lion’s posture—on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other—mindful and aware.

sn1.38:2.1.verse: Then, late at night, seven hundred glorious deities of the host of a hundred felicities, lighting up the entire Maddakucchi, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side.

sn1.38:2.2.verse: Standing to one side, one deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.38:2.3.verse: “The ascetic Gotama is such an elephant, sir!

sn1.38:2.4.verse: And as an elephant, he endures painful physical feelings that have come up—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, and disagreeable—unbothered, with mindfulness and situational awareness.”

sn1.38:3.1.verse: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.38:3.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama is such a lion, sir!

sn1.38:3.3.verse: And as a lion, he endures painful physical feelings … unbothered.”

sn1.38:4.1.verse: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.38:4.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama is such a thoroughbred, sir!

sn1.38:4.3.verse: And as a thoroughbred, he endures painful physical feelings … unbothered.”

sn1.38:5.1.verse: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.38:5.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama is such a boss bull, sir!

sn1.38:5.3.verse: And as a boss bull, he endures painful physical feelings … unbothered.”

sn1.38:6.1.verse: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.38:6.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama is such a behemoth, sir!

sn1.38:6.3.verse: And as a behemoth, he endures painful physical feelings … unbothered.”

sn1.38:7.1.verse: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.38:7.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama is truly tamed, sir!

sn1.38:7.3.verse: And as someone tamed, he endures painful physical feelings … unbothered.”

sn1.38:8.1.verse: Then another deity expressed this heartfelt sentiment in the Buddha’s presence:

sn1.38:8.2.verse: “See, his immersion is so well developed, and his mind is so well freed—not leaning forward or pulling back, and not held in place by forceful suppression.

sn1.38:8.3.verse: If anyone imagines that they can overcome such an elephant of a man, a lion of a man, a thoroughbred of a man, a boss bull of a man, a behemoth of a man, a tamed man—what is that but a failure to see?”

sn1.38:9.1.verse: “Learned in the five branches of Vedic lore,

sn1.38:9.2.verse: brahmins practice fervent mortification for a full century.

sn1.38:9.3.verse: But their minds are not properly freed,

sn1.38:9.4.verse: for those of base character don’t cross to the far shore.

sn1.38:10.1.verse: Seized by craving,  attached to precept and observance,

sn1.38:10.2.verse: they practice rough and fervent mortification for a hundred years.

sn1.38:10.3.verse: But their minds are not properly freed,

sn1.38:10.4.verse: for those of base character don’t go to the far shore.

sn1.38:11.1.verse: Someone who’s fond of conceit can’t be tamed,

sn1.38:11.2.verse: and someone without immersion can’t be a sage.

sn1.38:11.3.verse: Living negligent alone in the wilderness,

sn1.38:11.4.verse: they can’t cross beyond Death’s dominion.”

sn1.38:12.1.verse: “Having given up conceit, serene within oneself,

sn1.38:12.2.verse: with a good heart, everywhere free;

sn1.38:12.3.verse: living diligent alone in the wilderness,

sn1.38:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rajagaha in the Maddakucchi Deer Park.

sn1.38:1.3.verse: Now on that occasion the Blessed One’s foot had been cut by a stone splinter.

sn1.38:1.4.verse: Severe pains assailed the Blessed One—bodily feelings that were painful, racking, sharp, piercing, harrowing, disagreeable.

sn1.38:1.5.verse: But the Blessed One endured them, mindful and clearly comprehending, without becoming distressed.

sn1.38:1.6.verse: Then the Blessed One had his outer robe folded in four, and he lay down on his right side in the lion posture with one leg overlapping the other, mindful and clearly comprehending.

sn1.38:2.1.verse: Then, when the night had advanced, seven hundred devatās belonging to the Satullapa host, of stunning beauty, illuminating the entire Maddakucchi Deer Park, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side.

sn1.38:2.2.verse: Then one devatā, standing to one side, uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.38:2.3.verse: “The ascetic Gotama is indeed a naga, sir!

sn1.38:2.4.verse: And when bodily feelings have arisen that are painful, racking, sharp, piercing, harrowing, disagreeable, through his naga-like manner he endures them, mindful and clearly comprehending, without becoming distressed. ”

sn1.38:3.1.verse: Then another devatā uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.38:3.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama is indeed a lion,

sn1.38:3.3.verse: sir! And when bodily feelings have arisen that are painful, racking, sharp, piercing, harrowing, disagreeable, through his leonine manner he endures them, mindful and clearly comprehending, without becoming distressed. ”

sn1.38:4.1.verse: Then another devatā uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.38:4.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama is indeed a thoroughbred, sir!

sn1.38:4.3.verse: And when bodily feelings have arisen that are painful … disagreeable, through his thoroughbred manner he endures them, mindful and clearly comprehending, without becoming distressed. ”

sn1.38:5.1.verse: Then another devatā uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.38:5.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama is indeed a chief bull, sir!

sn1.38:5.3.verse: mindful and clearly comprehending, without becoming distressed. ”

sn1.38:6.1.verse: Then another devatā uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.38:6.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama is indeed a beast of burden, sir!

sn1.38:6.3.verse: And when bodily feelings have arisen that are painful … disagreeable, through his beast-of-burden’s manner he endures them, mindful and clearly comprehending, without becoming distressed. ”

sn1.38:7.1.verse: Then another devatā uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.38:7.2.verse: “The ascetic Gotama is indeed tamed, sir!

sn1.38:7.3.verse: And when bodily feelings have arisen that are painful, racking, sharp, piercing, harrowing, disagreeable, through his tamed manner he endures them, mindful and clearly comprehending, without becoming distressed. ”

sn1.38:8.1.verse: Then another devatā uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn1.38:8.2.verse: “See his concentration well developed and his mind well liberated—not bent forward and not bent back, and not blocked and checked by forceful suppression!

sn1.38:8.3.verse: If anyone would think such a one could be violated—such a naga of a man, such a lion of a man, such a thoroughbred of a man, such a chief bull of a man, such a beast of burden of a man, such a tamed man—what is that due to apart from lack of vision?”

sn1.38:9.1.verse: Though brahmins learned in the five Vedas

sn1.38:9.2.verse: Practise austerities for a hundred years,

sn1.38:9.3.verse: Their minds are not rightly liberated:

sn1.38:9.4.verse: Those of low nature do not reach the far shore.

sn1.38:10.1.verse: They founder in craving, bound to vows and rules,

sn1.38:10.2.verse: Practising rough austerity for a hundred years,

sn1.38:10.3.verse: But their minds are not rightly liberated:

sn1.38:10.4.verse: Those of low nature do not reach the far shore.

sn1.38:11.1.verse: There is no taming here for one fond of conceit,

sn1.38:11.2.verse: Nor is there sagehood for the unconcentrated:

sn1.38:11.3.verse: Though dwelling alone in the forest, heedless,

sn1.38:11.4.verse: One cannot cross beyond the realm of Death.

sn1.38:12.3.verse: While dwelling alone in the forest, diligent,

sn1.38:12.4.verse: One can cross beyond the realm of Death.

sn1.40:2.1.verse: “She came here, beautiful as a flash of lightning,

sn1.40:2.3.verse: Revering the Buddha and the teaching,

sn1.40:2.4.verse: she spoke these verses full of meaning.

sn1.40:3.2.verse: I could analyze it in many different ways.

sn1.40:3.4.verse: as far as I have learned it by heart.

sn2.1:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn2.1:1.3.verse: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Kassapa, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,

sn2.1:1.4.verse: “The Buddha has revealed the mendicant, but not his instructions to a mendicant.”

sn2.1:1.5.verse: “Well then, Kassapa, clarify this matter yourself.”

sn2.1:2.1.verse: “You should all train to learn well-spoken words,

sn2.1:2.3.verse: to sit alone in hidden places,

sn2.1:3.1.verse: That is what the godling Kassapa said,

sn2.1:3.3.verse: Then Kassapa, knowing that the Teacher concurred, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

sn2.1:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

sn2.1:1.3.verse: Then, when the night had advanced, the young deva Kassapa, of stunning beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One. 141 Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One, stood to one side, and said to the Blessed One:

sn2.1:1.4.verse: “The Blessed One has revealed the bhikkhu but not the instruction to the bhikkhu. ”

sn2.1:1.5.verse: “Well then, Kassapa, clear up this point yourself. ”

sn2.1:2.2.verse: And in the exercise of an ascetic,

sn2.1:2.4.verse: And in the calming of the mind. ”

sn2.1:3.1.verse: > This is what the young deva Kassapa said.

sn2.1:3.3.verse: Then the young deva Kassapa, thinking, “The Teacher has approved of me, ” paid homage to the Blessed One and, keeping him on the right, he disappeared right there.

sn2.2:1.2.verse: Standing to one side, Kassapa the deva’s son recited this verse in the Blessed One’s presence:

sn2.2:2.1.verse: “A monk should have jhāna, be released in mind,

sn2.2:2.2.verse: if he wants the heart’s attainment:

sn2.2:2.3.verse: knowing the arising & passing away of the world,

sn2.2:2.4.verse: good in his awareness, independent, aimed at that reward.”

sn2.2:1.2.verse: Standing to one side, the godling Kassapa spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

sn2.2:2.1.verse: “If a mendicant is a meditator, freed in mind,

sn2.2:2.2.verse: and if they desire the heart’s fulfillment—

sn2.2:2.3.verse: having known the arising and passing of the world,

sn2.2:2.4.verse: good-hearted, independent, that is their reward.”

sn2.2:1.2.verse: Standing to one side, the young deva Kassapa recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn2.2:2.2.verse: One who is liberated in mind, If he desires the heart’s attainment,

sn2.2:2.3.verse: Having known the world’s rise and fall,

sn2.2:2.4.verse: Let him be lofty in mind and unattached, bent on that as his advantage.”

sn2.5:1.3.verse: As he was standing there, he recited these verses in the Blessed One’s presence:

sn2.5:2.1.verse: “This should be done by the brahman

sn2.5:2.4.verse: he should not, through that, wish for becoming.”

sn2.5:4.3.verse: Having reached the end of birth & death,

sn2.5:4.4.verse: he doesn’t strain, for he’s gone beyond.”

sn2.5:1.2.verse: Then, when the night had advanced, the young deva Dāmali, of stunning beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One.

sn2.5:1.3.verse: Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One, stood to one side, and recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn2.5:2.1.verse: “This should be done by the brahmin:

sn2.5:2.3.verse: That by his abandoning of sensual desires

sn2.5:3.1.verse: “For the brahmin there is no task to be done,

sn2.5:3.3.verse: “For the brahmin has done what should be done.

sn2.5:3.6.verse: But a footing gained, standing on the ground,

sn2.5:3.7.verse: He need not strain for he has gone beyond.

sn2.5:4.1.verse: “This is a simile for the brahmin, O Dāmali,

sn2.5:4.2.verse: For the taintless one, the discreet meditator.

sn2.5:4.3.verse: Having reached the end of birth and death,

sn2.5:4.4.verse: He need not strain for he has gone beyond. ”

sn2.6:2.4.verse: For one who has entered the homeless life,

sn2.6:4.1.verse: “They find it even though it’s hard,”

sn2.6:4.3.verse: “those who love to settle the mind;

sn2.6:5.1.verse: “But it’s hard, Blessed One, to immerse this mind in samādhi.”

sn2.6:6.1.verse: “They become immersed in samādhi even though it’s hard,”

sn2.6:6.4.verse: Having cut through the net of Death,

sn2.6:6.5.verse: the noble ones, Kāmada, go on their way.”

sn2.6:8.2.verse: the noble ones, Kāmada, go on their way.

sn2.6:8.5.verse: But the path of the noble ones is smooth,

sn2.6:8.6.verse: for the noble ones are smooth amid the rough.”

sn2.6:1.2.verse: Standing to one side, the young deva Kāmada said to the Blessed One:

sn2.6:1.3.verse: “Hard to do, Blessed One! Very hard to do, Blessed One!”

sn2.6:2.1.verse: “They do even what is hard to do,

sn2.6:2.4.verse: steadfast. For one who has entered the homeless life

sn2.6:3.1.verse: “That is hard to gain, Blessed One, namely, contentment. ”

sn2.6:4.1.verse: “They gain even what is hard to gain,

sn2.6:4.5.verse: Whose minds, Take delight in development. ”

sn2.6:5.1.verse: “That is hard to concentrate, Blessed One, namely, the mind. ”

sn2.6:6.1.verse: “They concentrate even what is hard to concentrate,

sn2.6:6.4.verse: Having cut through the net of Death,

sn2.6:6.5.verse: The noble ones, O Kāmada, go their way. ”

sn2.6:7.1.verse: “The path is impassable and uneven, Blessed One.”

sn2.6:8.1.verse: “Though the path is impassable and uneven,

sn2.6:8.2.verse: The noble ones walk it, Kāmada.

sn2.6:8.3.verse: Right there on the uneven path,

sn2.6:8.4.verse: The ignoble ones fall down head first.

sn2.6:8.5.verse: But the path of the noble ones is even,

sn2.6:8.6.verse: For the noble are even amidst the uneven. ”

sn2.7:2.1.verse: “The one of broad wisdom has indeed found
