sn3.19:1.2.verse: Then King Pasenadi of Kosala went up to the Buddha in the middle of the day, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

sn3.19:1.3.verse: “So, Great King, where are you coming from in the middle of the day?”

sn3.19:2.1.verse: “Sir, here in Sāvatthī a financier householder has passed away.

sn3.19:2.2.verse: Since he died childless, I have come after transferring his fortune to the royal compound.

sn3.19:2.3.verse: There was eight million in gold coin, not to mention the silver coin.

sn3.19:2.4.verse: And yet that financier ate meals of

sn3.19:2.5.verse: sour gruel with false black pepper.

sn3.19:2.8.verse: He traveled around in a vehicle that was

sn3.19:2.9.verse: a dilapidated little cart, holding a leaf as parasol.”

sn3.19:3.1.verse: “That’s so true, Great King! That’s so true!

sn3.19:3.2.verse: When an untrue person has acquired notable wealth they don’t make themselves happy and pleased. Nor do they make their mother and father, partners and children, bondservants, workers, and staff, and friends and colleagues happy and pleased. And they don’t establish an uplifting religious donation for ascetics and brahmins that’s conducive to heaven, ripens in happiness, and leads to heaven.

sn3.19:3.3.verse: Because they haven’t made proper use of that wealth, rulers or bandits take it, or fire consumes it, or flood sweeps it away, or unloved heirs take it.

sn3.19:3.4.verse: Since that wealth is not properly utilized, it’s wasted, not used.

sn3.19:4.1.verse: Suppose there was a lotus pond in an uninhabited region with clear, sweet, cool water, clean, with smooth banks, delightful.

sn3.19:4.2.verse: But people don’t collect it or drink it or bathe in it or use it for any purpose.

sn3.19:4.3.verse: Since that water is not properly utilized, it’s wasted, not used.

sn3.19:4.4.verse: In the same way, when an untrue person has acquired notable wealth …

sn3.19:5.1.verse: When a true person has acquired notable wealth they make themselves happy and pleased. And they make their mother and father, partners and children, bondservants, workers, and staff, and friends and colleagues happy and pleased. And they establish an uplifting religious donation for ascetics and brahmins that’s conducive to heaven, ripens in happiness, and leads to heaven.

sn3.19:5.2.verse: Because they make proper use of that wealth, rulers or bandits don’t take it, fire doesn’t consume it, flood doesn’t sweep it away, and unloved heirs don’t take it.

sn3.19:5.3.verse: Since that wealth is properly utilized, it’s used, not wasted.

sn3.19:6.1.verse: Suppose there was a lotus pond not far from a town or village with clear, sweet, cool water, clean, with smooth banks, delightful.

sn3.19:6.2.verse: And people collected it and drank it and bathed in it and used it for their own purpose.

sn3.19:6.3.verse: Since that water is properly utilized, it’s used, not wasted.

sn3.19:6.4.verse: In the same way, when a true person has acquired notable wealth …

sn3.19:7.1.verse: As cool water in an uninhabited region

sn3.19:7.3.verse: so too when a reprobate acquires wealth,

sn3.19:7.4.verse: they neither use it themselves nor give it away.

sn3.19:8.1.verse: When the attentive and sensible acquire wealth,

sn3.19:8.3.verse: That boss, having supported the family unit,

sn3.19:8.4.verse: blameless, goes to a heavenly place.”

sn3.19:1.2.verse: Then King Pasenadi of Kosala approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. The Blessed One then said to him:

sn3.19:1.3.verse: “Where are you coming from, great king, in the middle of the day?”

sn3.19:2.1.verse: “Here, venerable sir, a financier householder in Sāvatthī has died.

sn3.19:2.2.verse: I have come after conveying his heirless fortune to the palace, as he died intestate.

sn3.19:2.3.verse: There were eighty lakhs of gold, not to speak of silver,

sn3.19:2.4.verse: and yet, venerable sir, that financier householder’s meals were like this:

sn3.19:2.5.verse: he ate red rice along with sour gruel.

sn3.19:2.7.verse: he wore a three-piece hempen garment.

sn3.19:2.9.verse: he went about in a dilapidated little cart with a leaf awning. ”

sn3.19:3.1.verse: “So it is, great king! So it is, great king!

sn3.19:3.2.verse: When an inferior man gains abundant wealth, he does not make himself happy and pleased, nor does he make his mother and father happy and pleased, nor his wife and children, nor his slaves, workers, and servants, nor his friends and colleagues; nor does he establish an offering for ascetics and brahmins, one leading upwards, of heavenly fruit, resulting in happiness, conducive to heaven.

sn3.19:3.3.verse: Because his wealth is not being used properly, kings take it away, or thieves take it away, or fire burns it, or water carries it away, or unloved heirs take it.

sn3.19:3.4.verse: Such being the case, great king, that wealth, not being used properly, goes to waste, not to utilization.

sn3.19:4.1.verse: “Suppose, great king, in a place uninhabited by human beings, there was a lotus pond with clear, cool, sweet, clean water, with good fords, delightful;

sn3.19:4.2.verse: but no people would take that water, or drink it, or bathe in it, or use it for any purpose.

sn3.19:4.3.verse: In such a case, great king, that water, not being used properly, would go to waste, not to utilization.

sn3.19:4.4.verse: So too, great king, when an inferior man gains abundant wealth . . . that wealth, not being used properly, goes to waste, not to utilization.

sn3.19:5.1.verse: “But, great king, when a superior man gains abundant wealth, he makes himself happy and pleased, and he makes his mother and father happy and pleased, and his wife and children, and his slaves, workers, and servants, and his friends and colleagues;  and he establishes an offering for ascetics and brahmins, one leading upwards, of heavenly fruit, resulting in happiness, conducive to heaven.

sn3.19:5.2.verse: Because his wealth is being used properly, kings do not take it away, thieves do not take it away, fire does not burn it, water does not carry it away, and unloved heirs do not take it.

sn3.19:5.3.verse: Such being the case, great king, that wealth, being used properly, goes to utilization, not to waste.

sn3.19:6.1.verse: “Suppose, great king, not far from a village or a town, there was a lotus pond with clear, cool, sweet, clean water, with good fords, delightful;

sn3.19:6.2.verse: and people would take that water, and drink it, and bathe in it, and use it for their purposes.

sn3.19:6.3.verse: In such a case, great king, that water, being used properly, would go to utilization, not to waste.

sn3.19:6.4.verse: So too, great king, when a superior man gains abundant wealth . . . that wealth, being used properly, goes to utilization, not to waste.

sn3.19:7.1.verse: “As cool water in a desolate place

sn3.19:7.3.verse: So when a scoundrel acquires wealth

sn3.19:7.4.verse: He neither enjoys himself nor gives.

sn3.19:8.1.verse: “But when the wise man obtains wealth

sn3.19:8.2.verse: He enjoys himself and does his duty.

sn3.19:8.3.verse: Having supported his kin, free from blame,

sn3.19:8.4.verse: That noble man goes to a heavenly state. ”

sn3.20:2.1.verse: “Sir, here in Sāvatthī a financier householder has passed away.

sn3.20:2.2.verse: Since he died childless, I have come after transferring his fortune to the royal compound.

sn3.20:2.3.verse: There was ten million in gold coin, not to mention the silver coin.

sn3.20:2.4.verse: And yet that financier ate meals of

sn3.20:2.5.verse: sour gruel with false black pepper.

sn3.20:2.8.verse: He traveled around in a vehicle that was

sn3.20:2.9.verse: a dilapidated little cart, holding a leaf as parasol.”

sn3.20:3.1.verse: “That’s so true, Great King! That’s so true!

sn3.20:3.2.verse: Once upon a time, great king, that financier householder provided almsfood on behalf of an independent Buddha named Tagarasikhī.

sn3.20:3.3.verse: He instructed: ‘Give alms to that ascetic,’ before getting up from his seat and leaving.

sn3.20:3.4.verse: But after giving he regretted it:

sn3.20:3.5.verse: ‘It would have been better to feed the bondservants or workers with that almsfood.’

sn3.20:3.6.verse: What’s more, he murdered his brother’s only child for the sake of his fortune.

sn3.20:4.1.verse: Because that financier provided Tagarasikhī with almsfood, as a result of that deed he was reborn seven times in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn3.20:4.2.verse: And as a residual result of that same deed he held the position of financier seven times right here in Sāvatthī.

sn3.20:4.3.verse: But because that financier regretted giving alms,

sn3.20:4.4.verse: as a result of that deed his mind didn’t tend to enjoy nice food, clothes, vehicles, or the five refined kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn3.20:4.5.verse: And because that financier murdered his brother’s only child for the sake of his fortune, as a result of that deed he burned in hell for many years, for many hundreds, many thousands, many hundreds of thousands of years.

sn3.20:4.6.verse: And as a residual result of that same deed, he is childless for the seventh time, his fortune ending up in the royal treasury.

sn3.20:4.7.verse: Now the old merit of that financier has been used up, and he hasn’t accumulated new merit.

sn3.20:4.8.verse: Today, Great King, that financier burns in the Great Hell of Screams.”

sn3.20:4.9.verse: “Really, sir, that financier has been reborn in the Great Hell of Screams?”

sn3.20:4.2.verse: As a residual result of that same kamma, he obtained the position of financier seven times in this same city of Sāvatthī.

sn3.20:4.3.verse: But because that financier householder later felt regret about giving,

sn3.20:4.4.verse: as a result of that kamma his mind did not incline to the enjoyment of excellent food, excellent clothing, and excellent vehicles, nor to the enjoyment of excellent items among the five cords of sensual pleasure.

sn3.20:4.5.verse: And because that financier householder murdered his brother’s only son for the sake of his fortune, as a result of that kamma he was tormented in hell for many years, for many hundreds of years, for many thousands of years, for many hundreds of thousands of years.

sn3.20:4.6.verse: As a residual result of that same kamma, he has furnished the royal treasury with this seventh heirless fortune.

sn3.20:4.7.verse: “The old merit of that financier householder has been utterly exhausted, and he had not accumulated any fresh merit.

sn3.20:4.8.verse: But today, great king, the financier householder is being roasted in the Great Roruva Hell. ”

sn3.21:1.2.verse: Then King Pasenadi of Kosala approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. The Blessed One then said to him:

sn3.21:1.3.verse: “Great king, there are these four kinds of persons found existing in the world.

sn3.21:1.5.verse: The one heading from darkness to darkness,

sn3.21:1.6.verse: the one heading from darkness to light,

sn3.21:1.7.verse: the one heading from light to darkness,

sn3.21:1.8.verse: the one heading from light to light.

sn3.21:2.1.verse: “And how, great king, is a person one heading from darkness to darkness?

sn3.21:2.2.verse: Here some person has been reborn in a low family—a family of caṇḍālas, bamboo workers, hunters, cartwrights, or flower-scavengers—a poor family in which there is little food and drink and which subsists with difficulty, one where food and clothing are obtained with difficulty;

sn3.21:2.3.verse: and he is ugly, unsightly, deformed, chronically ill—purblind or cripple-handed or lame or paralyzed. He is not one who gains food, drink, clothing, and vehicles; garlands, scents, and unguents; bedding, housing, and lighting.

sn3.21:2.4.verse: He engages in misconduct of body, speech, and mind.

sn3.21:2.5.verse: Having done so, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the plane of misery, in a bad destination, in the nether world, in hell.

sn3.21:3.1.verse: “Suppose, great king, a man would go from darkness to darkness, or from gloom to gloom, or from stain to stain:

sn3.21:3.2.verse: this person, I say, is exactly similar.

sn3.21:3.3.verse: It is in this way, great king, that a person is one heading from darkness to darkness.

sn3.21:4.1.verse: “And how, great king, is a person one heading from darkness to light?

sn3.21:4.4.verse: He engages in good conduct of body, speech, and mind.

sn3.21:4.5.verse: Having done so, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.

sn3.21:5.1.verse: “Suppose, great king, a man would climb from the ground on to a palanquin, or from a palanquin on to horseback, or from horseback to an elephant mount, or from an elephant mount to a mansion:

sn3.21:5.2.verse: this person, I say, is exactly similar.

sn3.21:5.3.verse: It is in this way, great king, that a person is one heading from darkness to light.

sn3.21:6.1.verse: “And how, great king, is a person one heading from light to darkness?

sn3.21:6.2.verse: Here some person has been reborn in a high family—an affluent khattiya family, an affluent brahmin family, or an affluent householder family—one which is rich, with great wealth and property, with abundant gold and silver, abundant treasures and commodities, abundant wealth and grain;

sn3.21:6.3.verse: and he is handsome, attractive, graceful, possessing supreme beauty of complexion. He is one who gains food, drink, clothing, and vehicles; garlands, scents, and unguents; bedding, housing, and lighting.

sn3.21:6.4.verse: He engages in misconduct of body, speech, and mind.

sn3.21:6.5.verse: Having done so, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the plane of misery, in a bad destination, in the nether world, in hell.

sn3.21:7.2.verse: this person, I say, is exactly similar.

sn3.21:7.3.verse: It is in this way, great king, that a person is one heading from light to darkness.

sn3.21:8.3.verse: and he is handsome, attractive, graceful, possessing supreme beauty of complexion. He is one who gains food … and lighting.

sn3.21:8.4.verse: He engages in good conduct of body, speech, and mind.

sn3.22:1.2.verse: King Pasenadi of Kosala sat to one side, and the Buddha said to him,

sn3.22:1.3.verse: “So, Great King, where are you coming from in the middle of the day?”

sn3.22:2.1.verse: “Sir, my grandmother has passed away. She was old, elderly and senior. She was advanced in years and had reached the final stage of life; she was a hundred and twenty years old.

sn3.22:2.2.verse: But I loved my grandmother; she was dear to me.

sn3.22:2.3.verse: If by giving away the elephant-treasure I could get my grandmother back, I’d do it.

sn3.22:2.5.verse: If by giving away the horse-treasure I could get my grandmother back, I’d do it.

sn3.22:2.7.verse: If by giving away a prize village I could get my grandmother back, I’d do it.

sn3.22:2.9.verse: If by giving away the whole country I could get my grandmother back, I’d do it.”

sn3.22:2.11.verse: “Great king, all sentient beings are liable to die. Death is their end; they’re not exempt from death.”

sn3.22:2.13.verse: how well said this was by the Buddha:

sn3.22:2.14.verse: ‘All sentient beings are liable to die. Death is their end; they’re not exempt from death.’”

sn3.22:3.1.verse: “That’s so true, Great King! That’s so true!

sn3.22:3.2.verse: All sentient beings are liable to die. Death is their end; they’re not exempt from death.

sn3.22:3.3.verse: It’s like the vessels made by potters. Whatever kind they are, whether baked or unbaked, all of them are liable to break apart. Breaking is their end; they’re not exempt from breakage.

sn3.22:3.4.verse: In the same way, all sentient beings are liable to die. Death is their end; they’re not exempt from death.”

sn3.22:3.5.verse: That is what the Buddha said. …

sn3.22:4.3.verse: They pass on according to their deeds,

sn3.22:4.4.verse: reaping the fruits of good and bad.

sn3.22:4.5.verse: Those who do bad go to hell,

sn3.22:4.6.verse: and if you do good you go to heaven.

sn3.22:5.1.verse: That’s why you should do good,

sn3.22:5.3.verse: The good deeds of sentient beings

sn3.22:5.4.verse: support them in the next world.”

sn3.22:1.2.verse: Then, in the middle of the day, King Pasenadi of Kosala approached the Blessed One. The Blessed One said to him as he was sitting to one side:

sn3.22:1.3.verse: “Where are you coming from, great king, in the middle of the day?”

sn3.22:2.1.verse: “Venerable sir, my grandmother has died. She was old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life, come to the last stage, years from birth.

sn3.22:2.2.verse: Venerable sir, my grandmother was dear and beloved to me.

sn3.22:2.3.verse: If, venerable sir, by means of the elephant-gem I could have redeemed her from death, I would have given away even the elephant-gem

sn3.22:2.4.verse: so that she would not have died.

sn3.22:2.5.verse: If by means of the horse-gem I could have redeemed her from death .

sn3.22:2.7.verse: If by a prize village I could have redeemed her from death .

sn3.22:2.9.verse: If by means of the country I could have redeemed her from death, I would have given away even the country

sn3.22:2.10.verse: so that she would not have died.

sn3.22:2.11.verse: “All beings, great king, are subject to death, terminate in death, and cannot escape death. ”

sn3.22:2.12.verse: “It is wonderful, venerable sir! It is amazing, venerable sir!

sn3.22:2.13.verse: How well this has been stated by the Blessed One:

sn3.22:2.14.verse: ‘All beings, great king, are subject to death, terminate in death, and cannot escape death. ’”

sn3.22:3.1.verse: “So it is, great king! So it is, great king!

sn3.22:3.2.verse: All beings, great king, are subject to death, terminate in death, and cannot escape death.

sn3.22:3.3.verse: Just as all the potter’s vessels, whether unbaked or baked, are subject to a breakup, terminate in their breakup, and cannot escape their breakup,

sn3.22:3.4.verse: so all beings are subject to death, terminate in death, and cannot escape death.

sn3.22:4.3.verse: They will fare according to their deeds,

sn3.22:4.4.verse: Reaping the fruits of their merit and evil:

sn3.22:4.5.verse: The doers of evil go to hell,

sn3.22:4.6.verse: The doers of merit to a happy realm.

sn3.22:5.1.verse: “Therefore one should do what is good

sn3.22:5.2.verse: As a collection for the future life.

sn3.22:5.3.verse: Merits, [When they arise] in the other world,

sn3.22:5.4.verse: are the support for living beings.”

sn3.23:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, King Pasenadi said to the Buddha,

sn3.23:1.3.verse: “Sir, how many things arise in the world for its harm, suffering, and discomfort?”

sn3.23:1.4.verse: “Great king, three things arise in the world for its harm, suffering, and discomfort.

sn3.23:1.9.verse: These three things arise in the world for its harm, suffering, and discomfort.”

sn3.23:1.10.verse: That is what the Buddha said. …

sn3.23:2.3.verse: they harm a person of wicked heart,

sn3.23:2.4.verse: as a bamboo is destroyed by its own fruit.”

sn3.23:1.2.verse: Sitting to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One:

sn3.23:1.3.verse: “Venerable sir, how many things are there in the world which, when they arise, arise for one’s harm, suffering, and discomfort?”

sn3.23:1.4.verse: “There are, great king, three things in the world which, when they arise, arise for one’s harm, suffering, and discomfort.

sn3.23:1.9.verse: These are the three things in the world which, when they arise, arise for one’s harm, suffering, and discomfort.

sn3.23:2.4.verse: As its own fruit destroys the reed. ”

sn3.24:1.3.verse: “Sir, where should a gift be given?”

sn3.24:1.4.verse: “Wherever your heart feels inspired, Great King.”

sn3.24:1.5.verse: “But sir, where is a gift very fruitful?”

sn3.24:1.6.verse: “Where a gift should be given is one thing, Great King, but where a gift is very fruitful is another.

sn3.24:1.7.verse: A gift is very fruitful when it’s given to an ethical person, not so much to an unethical person.

sn3.24:1.8.verse: Well then, Great King, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.

sn3.24:1.12.verse: Would you employ such a man? Would he be of any use to you?”

sn3.24:1.13.verse: “No, sir, I would have no use for such a man.”

sn3.24:1.17.verse: “No, sir, I would have no use for such a man.”

sn3.24:2.4.verse: Would you employ such a man? Would he be of any use to you?”

sn3.24:2.5.verse: “Yes, sir, I would have a use for such a man.”

sn3.24:2.10.verse: “Yes, sir, I would have a use for such a man.”

sn3.24:3.2.verse: What are the five factors they’ve given up?

sn3.24:3.3.verse: Sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.

sn3.24:3.6.verse: The entire spectrum of an adept’s ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and knowledge and vision of freedom.

sn3.24:3.7.verse: These are the five factors they possess.

sn3.24:3.8.verse: I say that a gift to anyone who has given up these five factors and possesses these five factors is very fruitful.”

sn3.24:3.9.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn3.24:3.4.verse: What five factors does he possess?

sn3.24:3.6.verse: He possesses the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training, the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training.

sn3.24:3.8.verse: Thus what is given to one who has abandoned five factors and who possesses five factors is of great fruit.

sn3.25:1.2.verse: King Pasenadi of Kosala sat to one side, and the Buddha said to him,

sn3.25:1.3.verse: “So, Great King, where are you coming from in the middle of the day?”

sn3.25:1.4.verse: “Sir, there are anointed aristocratic kings who are infatuated with authority, and obsessed with greed for sensual pleasures. They have attained stability in the country, occupying a vast conquered territory. Today I have been busy fulfilling the duties of such kings.”

sn3.25:2.2.verse: Suppose a trustworthy and dependable man were to come from the east.

sn3.25:2.4.verse: ‘Please, Great King, you should know this. I come from the east.

sn3.25:2.5.verse: There I saw a big mountain that reached the clouds. And it was coming this way, crushing all creatures.

sn3.25:2.6.verse: So then, Great King, do what you must!’

sn3.25:2.7.verse: Then a second trustworthy and dependable man were to come from the west …

sn3.25:2.9.verse: and a fourth from the south.

sn3.25:2.11.verse: ‘Please, Great King, you should know this. I come from the south.

sn3.25:2.12.verse: There I saw a big mountain that reached the clouds. And it was coming this way, crushing all creatures.

sn3.25:2.13.verse: So then, Great King, do what you must!’

sn3.25:2.14.verse: Should such a dire threat arise—a grim loss of human life, when human birth is so rare—what would you do?”

sn3.25:3.1.verse: “Sir, what could I do but practice the teachings, practice morality, doing skillful and good actions?”

sn3.25:4.1.verse: “I tell you, Great King, I announce to you: old age and death are advancing upon you.

sn3.25:4.2.verse: Since old age and death are advancing upon you, what would you do?”

sn3.25:4.3.verse: “Sir, what can I do but practice the teachings, practice morality, doing skillful and good actions?

sn3.25:4.4.verse: Sir, there are anointed aristocratic kings who are infatuated with authority, and obsessed with greed for sensual pleasures. They have attained stability in the country, occupying a vast conquered territory. Such kings engage in battles of elephants,

sn3.25:4.10.verse: But there is no place, no domain for such battles when old age and death are advancing.

sn3.25:4.11.verse: In this royal court there are ministers of wise counsel who are capable of dividing an approaching enemy by wise counsel.

sn3.25:4.12.verse: But there is no place, no domain for such diplomatic battles when old age and death are advancing.

sn3.25:4.13.verse: In this royal court there is abundant gold, both coined and uncoined, stored above and below ground. Using this wealth we can bribe an approaching enemy.

sn3.25:4.14.verse: But there is no place, no domain for such monetary battles when old age and death are advancing.

sn3.25:4.15.verse: When old age and death are advancing, what can I do but practice the teachings, practice morality, doing skillful and good actions?”

sn3.25:5.1.verse: “That’s so true, Great King! That’s so true!

sn3.25:5.2.verse: When old age and death are advancing, what can you do but practice the teachings, practice morality, doing skillful and good actions?”

sn3.25:5.3.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn3.25:5.4.verse: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

sn3.25:1.2.verse: The Blessed One said to him as he was sitting to one side:

sn3.25:1.3.verse: “Now where are you coming from, great king, in the middle of the day?”

sn3.25:1.4.verse: “Just now, venerable sir, I have been engaged in those affairs of kingship typical for head-anointed khattiya kings, who are intoxicated with the intoxication of sovereignty, who are obsessed by greed for sensual pleasures, who have attained stable control in their country, and who rule having conquered a great sphere of territory on earth.”

sn3.25:2.2.verse: Here, a man would come to you from the east, one who is trustworthy and reliable;

sn3.25:2.3.verse: having approached, he would tell you:

sn3.25:2.4.verse: ‘For sure, great king, you should know this: I am coming from the east,

sn3.25:2.5.verse: and there I saw a great mountain high as the clouds coming this way, crushing all living beings.

sn3.25:2.6.verse: Do whatever you think should be done, great king.

sn3.25:2.7.verse: ’Then a second man would come to you from the west …

sn3.25:2.8.verse: Then a third man would come to you from the north …

sn3.25:2.9.verse: Then a fourth man would come to you from the south, one who is trustworthy and reliable;

sn3.25:2.10.verse: having approached, he would tell you:

sn3.25:2.11.verse: ‘For sure, great king, you should know this: I am coming from the south,

sn3.25:2.12.verse: and there I saw a great mountain high as the clouds coming this way, crushing all living beings.

sn3.25:2.13.verse: Do whatever you think should be done, great king.

sn3.25:2.14.verse: ’If, great king, such a great peril should arise, such a terrible destruction of human life, the human state being so difficult to obtain, what should be done?”

sn3.25:3.1.verse: “If, venerable sir, such a great peril should arise, such a terrible destruction of human life, the human state being so difficult to obtain, what else should be done but to live by the Dhamma, to live righteously, and to do wholesome and meritorious deeds?”

sn3.25:4.1.verse: “I inform you, great king, I announce to you, great king: aging and death are rolling in on you.

sn3.25:4.2.verse: When aging and death are rolling in on you, great king, what should be done?”

sn3.25:4.3.verse: “As aging and death are rolling in on me, venerable sir, what else should be done but to live by the Dhamma, to live righteously, and to do wholesome and meritorious deeds?

sn3.25:4.4.verse: “There are, venerable sir, elephant battles [fought by] head-anointed khattiya kings, who are intoxicated with the intoxication of sovereignty, who are obsessed by greed for sensual pleasures, who have attained stable control in their country, and who rule having conquered a great sphere of territory on earth;

sn3.25:4.5.verse: but there is no place for those elephant battles, no scope for them, when aging and death are rolling in.

sn3.25:4.7.verse: There are, venerable sir, cavalry battles …

sn3.25:4.12.verse: but there is no place for those battles of subterfuge, no scope for them, when aging and death are rolling in.

sn3.25:4.13.verse: In this royal court, venerable sir, there exists abundant bullion and gold stored in vaults and depositories, and with such wealth we are capable of mollifying the enemies when they come;

sn3.25:4.14.verse: but there is no place for those battles of wealth, no scope for them, when aging and death are rolling in.

sn3.25:4.15.verse: As aging and death are rolling in on me, venerable sir, what else should be done but to live by the Dhamma, to live righteously, and to do wholesome and meritorious deeds?”

sn3.25:5.1.verse: “So it is, great king! So it is, great king!

sn4.1:1.2.verse: At one time, when he was first awakened, the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the root of the goatherd’s banyan tree on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

sn4.1:1.3.verse: Then as he was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,

sn4.1:1.4.verse: “I am truly freed from that grueling work!

sn4.1:1.5.verse: Thank goodness I’m freed from that pointless grueling work.

sn4.1:1.6.verse: Thank goodness I’m freed and have attained awakening.”

sn4.1:2.1.verse: And then Māra the Wicked, knowing the Buddha’s train of thought, went up to him and addressed him in verse:

sn4.1:3.2.verse: by which sons of men purify themselves.

sn4.1:3.3.verse: You’re impure, but think yourself pure;

sn4.1:3.4.verse: you’ve strayed from the path of purity.”

sn4.1:4.1.verse: Then the Buddha, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:

sn4.1:5.4.verse: as oars and rudder on dry land.

sn4.1:6.2.verse: by developing this path to awakening

sn4.1:7.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

sn4.1:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruvelā on the bank of the river Nerañjarā at the foot of the Goatherd’s Banyan Tree just after he had become fully enlightened.

sn4.1:1.3.verse: Then, while the Blessed One was alone in seclusion, a reflection arose in his mind thus:

sn4.1:1.4.verse: “I am indeed freed from that gruelling asceticism!

sn4.1:1.5.verse: It is good indeed that I am freed from that useless gruelling asceticism!

sn4.1:1.6.verse: It is good that, steady and mindful, I have attained enlightenment!”

sn4.1:2.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, having known with his own mind the reflection in the Blessed One’s mind, approached the Blessed One and addressed him in verse:

sn4.1:3.3.verse: Being impure, you think you’re pure:

sn4.1:3.4.verse: You have missed the path to purity. ”

sn4.1:4.1.verse: Then the Blessed One, having understood, “This is Māra the Evil One, ” replied to him in verses:

sn4.1:5.3.verse: That all such penances are futile

sn4.1:5.4.verse: Like oars and rudder on dry land,

sn4.1:6.2.verse: By developing the path to enlightenment—

sn4.1:7.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, “The Blessed One knows me, the Fortunate One knows me, ” sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.

sn4.2:0.3.verse: In the Form of an Elephant King

sn4.2:1.2.verse: At one time, when he was first awakened, the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the root of the goatherd’s banyan tree on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

sn4.2:1.3.verse: Now at that time the Buddha was meditating in the open during the dark of night, while a gentle rain drizzled down.

sn4.2:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, wanting to make the Buddha feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, manifested in the form of a big elephant king and approached him.

sn4.2:1.5.verse: Its head was like a big block of soapstone.

sn4.2:1.7.verse: Its tusks were like pure silver.

sn4.2:1.9.verse: Its trunk was like a long plough pole.

sn4.2:1.11.verse: Then the Buddha, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, addressed him in verse:

sn4.2:2.2.verse: you’ve made forms beautiful and ugly.

sn4.2:3.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

sn4.6:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

sn4.6:1.3.verse: Now at that time the Buddha was meditating in the open during the dark of night, while a gentle rain drizzled down.

sn4.6:2.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, wanting to make the Buddha feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, manifested in the form of a big cobra king and approached him.

sn4.6:2.2.verse: Its body was like a big canoe carved from a single tree.

sn4.6:2.4.verse: Its hood was like a large brewer’s sieve.

sn4.6:2.6.verse: Its eyes were like big bronze cups from Kosala.

sn4.6:2.8.verse: Its tongue flickered from its mouth like lightning flashes in a thunderstorm.

sn4.6:2.10.verse: The sound of its breathing was like the puffing of a blacksmith’s bellows.

sn4.6:3.1.verse: Then the Buddha, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:

sn4.6:5.1.verse: Though there are lots of creepy crawlies,

sn4.7:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

sn4.7:1.2.verse: He spent much of the night walking mindfully in the open. At the crack of dawn he washed his feet and entered his dwelling.

sn4.7:1.3.verse: He laid down in the lion’s posture—on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other—mindful and aware, and focused on the time of getting up.

sn4.7:1.1.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary.

sn4.7:1.2.verse: Then, when the night was fading, the Blessed One, having spent much of the night walking back and forth in the open, washed his feet, entered his dwelling,

sn4.7:1.3.verse: and lay down on his right side in the lion’s posture, with one leg overlapping the other, mindful and clearly comprehending, having attended to the idea of rising.

sn4.7:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One and addressed him in verse:

sn4.7:2.1.verse: “What, you sleep? Why do you sleep?

sn4.7:3.3.verse: With the destruction of all acquisitions The Awakened One

sn4.7:3.4.verse: sleeps: Why should this concern you, Māra?”

sn4.7:4.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One … disappeared right there.

sn4.13:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Maddakucchi deer park.

sn4.13:1.3.verse: Now at that time the Buddha’s foot had been cut by a wooden splinter.

sn4.13:1.4.verse: The Buddha was stricken by harrowing pains; physical feelings that were painful, sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, and disagreeable.

sn4.13:1.5.verse: But he endured unbothered, with mindfulness and situational awareness.

sn4.13:1.6.verse: And then he spread out his outer robe folded in four and laid down in the lion’s posture—on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other—mindful and aware.

sn4.13:1.7.verse: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:

sn4.13:2.1.verse: “Are you feeble that you lie down? Or are you drunk on poetry?

sn4.13:2.2.verse: Are your goals not amply satisfied?

sn4.13:3.1.verse: “I’m not feeble that I lie down, nor am I drunk on poetry.

sn4.13:3.2.verse: Having reached the goal, I’m rid of sorrow.

sn4.13:3.4.verse: I lie down full of sympathy for all living creatures.

sn4.13:4.1.verse: Even those with a dart stuck in the breast,

sn4.13:4.2.verse: piercing the heart moment by moment,

sn4.13:4.3.verse: are able to get some sleep.

sn4.13:4.4.verse: So why not I, whose dart is drawn out?

sn4.13:5.1.verse: I don’t lie awake tense, nor do I fear to sleep.

sn4.13:5.2.verse: The days and nights don’t disturb me,

sn4.13:5.3.verse: as I see no decline for myself in the world.

sn4.13:5.4.verse: That’s why I lie down full of sympathy for all living creatures.”

sn4.13:6.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

sn4.13:1.4.verse: Severe pains assailed the Blessed One—bodily feelings that were painful, racking, sharp, piercing, harrowing, disagreeable.

sn4.13:1.5.verse: But the Blessed One endured them, mindful and clearly comprehending, without becoming distressed.

sn4.13:1.6.verse: Then the Blessed One had his outer robe folded in four, and he lay down on his right side in the lion posture with one leg overlapping the other, mindful and clearly comprehending.

sn4.13:3.2.verse: Having reached the goal, I am rid of sorrow.

sn4.13:3.4.verse: I lie down full of compassion for all beings.

sn4.13:4.1.verse: “Even those with a dart stuck in the breast

sn4.13:4.2.verse: Piercing their heart moment by moment—

sn4.13:4.3.verse: Even these here, stricken, get to sleep;

sn4.13:4.4.verse: So why should I not get to sleep When my dart has been drawn out?

sn4.13:5.1.verse: “I do not lie awake in dread, Nor am I afraid to sleep.

sn4.13:5.2.verse: The nights and days do not afflict me,

sn4.13:5.3.verse: I see for myself no decline in the world.

sn4.13:5.4.verse: Therefore I can sleep in peace, Full of compassion for all beings. ”

sn4.13:6.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One … disappeared right there.

sn4.22:1.9.verse: to have spiritual companions who are ethical and of good character.”

sn4.22:3.5.verse: And for a second time Samiddhi was meditating in that same place, diligent, ardent, and resolute.

sn4.22:3.6.verse: And for a second time he had the same thought …

sn4.22:3.7.verse: and Māra made an earth-shattering noise.

sn4.22:3.9.verse: Then Samiddhi addressed Māra the Wicked in verse:

sn4.22:4.2.verse: from the lay life to homelessness.

sn4.22:1.1.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans at Silāvatī .

sn4.22:1.2.verse: Now on that occasion the Venerable Samiddhi was dwelling not far from the Blessed One—diligent, ardent, and resolute.

sn4.22:1.3.verse: Then, while the Venerable Samiddhi was alone in seclusion, a reflection arose in his mind thus:

sn4.22:1.4.verse: “It is indeed a gain for me, it is well gained by me,

sn4.22:1.5.verse: that my teacher is the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One!

sn4.22:1.6.verse: It is indeed a gain for me, it is well gained by me,

sn4.22:1.7.verse: that I have gone forth in this well-expounded Dhamma and Discipline!

sn4.22:1.8.verse: It is indeed a gain for me, it is well gained by me,

sn4.22:1.9.verse: that my companions in the holy life are virtuous, of good character!”

sn4.22:1.10.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, having known with his own mind the reflection in the mind of the Venerable Samiddhi, approached him and, not far from him, made a loud noise, frightful and terrifying, as though the earth were splitting open.

sn4.22:2.1.verse: Then the Venerable Samiddhi approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported what had happened.

sn4.22:3.1.verse: ] “That was not the earth splitting open, Samiddhi.

sn4.22:3.2.verse: That was Māra the Evil One, who had come in order to confound you.

sn4.22:3.3.verse: Go back, Samiddhi, and dwell diligent, ardent, and resolute. ”

sn4.22:3.4.verse: “Yes, venerable sir, ” the Venerable Samiddhi replied. Then he rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, and departed, keeping him on the right.

sn4.22:3.5.verse: A second time, while the Venerable Samiddhi was alone in seclusion,

sn4.22:3.6.verse: a reflection arose in his mind …

sn4.22:3.7.verse: And a second time Māra the Evil One …

sn4.22:3.8.verse: made a loud noise, frightful and terrifying, as though the earth were splitting open.

sn4.22:3.9.verse: Then the Venerable Samiddhi, having understood, “This is Māra the Evil One, ” addressed him in verse:

sn4.22:4.1.verse: “I have gone forth out of faith

sn4.22:4.2.verse: From the home to the homeless life.

sn4.22:4.3.verse: My mindfulness and wisdom are mature,

sn4.22:4.5.verse: Conjure up whatever forms you wish,

sn4.22:4.6.verse: But you will never make me tremble. ”

sn4.22:5.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, “The bhikkhu Samiddhi knows me, ” sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.

sn4.23:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

sn4.23:1.3.verse: Now at that time Venerable Godhika was staying on the slopes of Isigili at the Black Rock.

sn4.23:1.4.verse: Then Venerable Godhika, meditating diligent, keen, and resolute, experienced temporary freedom of heart.

sn4.23:1.5.verse: But then he fell away from that temporary freedom of heart.

sn4.23:1.14.verse: sixth time Godhika experienced temporary freedom of heart.

sn4.23:1.15.verse: But for a sixth time he fell away from it.

sn4.23:3.3.verse: You’ve gone beyond all enmities and fears,

sn4.23:9.1.verse: Then the Buddha together with several mendicants went to the Black Rock on the slopes of Isigili.

sn4.23:9.2.verse: The Buddha saw Godhika off in the distance on his cot, lying with aggregates cast off.

sn4.23:9.3.verse: Now at that time a cloud of black smoke was moving east, west, north, south, above, below, and in-between.

sn4.23:10.1.verse: Then the Buddha said to the mendicants,

sn4.23:10.4.verse: “That’s Māra the Wicked searching for Godhika’s consciousness, wondering:

sn4.23:10.6.verse: But since his consciousness is not established, Godhika is quenched.”

sn4.23:10.7.verse: Then Māra, carrying his arched harp made from the pale timber of wood-apple, went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:

sn4.23:1.3.verse: Now on that occasion the Venerable Godhika was dwelling on the Black Rock on the Isigili Slope.

sn4.23:2.4.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, having known with his own mind the reflection in the Venerable Godhika’s mind, approached the Blessed One and addressed him with these verses:

sn4.23:3.2.verse: Blazing forth with power and glory!

sn4.23:3.3.verse: Who has overcome all enmity and fear.

sn4.23:3.4.verse: I worship your feet, One with Vision,

sn4.23:4.2.verse: “O great hero who has vanquished death,

sn4.23:4.3.verse: He intends [to take his own life]:

sn4.23:4.4.verse: Restrain him from this, O luminous one!

sn4.23:5.1.verse: “How, O Blessed One, can your disciple—

sn4.23:5.3.verse: A trainee seeking his mind’s ideal—

sn4.23:5.4.verse: Take his own life, O widely famed?”

sn4.23:6.2.verse: Then the Blessed One, having understood, “This is Māra the Evil One, ” addressed him in verse:

sn4.23:9.1.verse: Then the Blessed One, together with a number of bhikkhus, went to the Black Rock on the Isigili Slope.

sn4.23:9.2.verse: The Blessed One saw in the distance the Venerable Godhika lying on the bed with his shoulder turned.

sn4.23:9.3.verse: Now on that occasion a cloud of smoke, a swirl of darkness, was moving to the east, then to the west, to the north, to the south, upwards, downwards, and to the intermediate quarters.

sn4.23:10.1.verse: The Blessed One then addressed the bhikkhus thus:

sn4.23:10.2.verse: “Do you see, bhikkhus, that cloud of smoke, that swirl of darkness, moving to the east, then to the west, to the north, to the south, upwards, downwards, and to the intermediate quarters?”

sn4.23:10.4.verse: “That, bhikkhus, is Māra the Evil One searching for the consciousness of the clansman Godhika, wondering:

sn4.23:10.5.verse: ‘Where now  has the consciousness of the clansman Godhika been established?’

sn4.23:10.6.verse: However, bhikkhus, with consciousness unestablished, the clansman Godhika has attained final Nibbāna. ”

sn4.23:11.2.verse: In the four quarters and in between,

sn4.23:13.3.verse: Having drawn out craving with its root,

sn4.23:14.2.verse: That his lute dropped from his armpit.

sn4.24:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the goatherd’s banyan tree on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

sn4.24:1.3.verse: Now at that time Māra the Wicked had been pursuing the Buddha for seven years hoping to find a vulnerability without success.

sn4.24:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:

sn4.24:2.1.verse: “Are you swamped by sorrow that you meditate in the forest?

sn4.24:2.2.verse: Have you lost a fortune, or do you long for one?

sn4.24:2.3.verse: Or perhaps you’ve committed some crime in the village?

sn4.24:2.4.verse: Why don’t you get too close to people?

sn4.24:2.5.verse: And why does no one get close to you?”

sn4.24:3.1.verse: “I’ve dug out the root of sorrow completely.

sn4.24:3.2.verse: I practice absorption free of guilt or sorrow.

sn4.24:3.3.verse: I’ve cut off all greed and muttered prayer for future lives.

sn4.24:3.4.verse: Undefiled, I practice absorption, O kinsman of the negligent!”

sn4.24:5.1.verse: “The things they speak of aren’t mine;

sn4.24:5.2.verse: I’m not someone who speaks like that.

sn4.24:5.4.verse: you won’t even see the path I take.”

sn4.24:6.2.verse: that’s safe, and leads to freedom from death,

sn4.24:6.3.verse: go and walk that path alone—

sn4.24:6.4.verse: why teach it to anyone else?”

sn4.24:7.2.verse: ask what’s beyond the domain of Death.

sn4.24:7.3.verse: When I’m asked, I explain to them

sn4.24:8.1.verse: “Sir, suppose there was a lotus pond not far from a town or village,

sn4.24:8.3.verse: Then several boys or girls would leave the town or village and go to the pond, where they’d pull out the crab and put it on solid ground.

sn4.24:8.4.verse: Whenever that crab extended a claw, those boys or girls would snap, crack, and break it off with a stick or a stone.

sn4.24:8.5.verse: And when that crab’s claws had all been snapped, cracked, and broken off it wouldn’t be able to return down into that lotus pond.

sn4.24:8.6.verse: In the same way, sir, the Buddha has snapped, cracked, and broken off all my twists, ducks, and dodges.

sn4.24:8.7.verse: Now I’m not able to approach the Buddha again in hopes of finding a vulnerability.”

sn4.24:1.3.verse: Now on that occasion Māra the Evil One had been following the Blessed One for seven years, seeking to gain access to him but without success.

sn4.24:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One and addressed him in verse:

sn4.24:2.1.verse: “Is it because you are sunk in sorrow That you meditate in the woods?

sn4.24:2.3.verse: Or committed some crime in the village?

sn4.24:2.4.verse: Why don’t you make friends with people?

sn4.24:2.5.verse: Why don’t you form any intimate ties?”

sn4.24:3.1.verse: “Having dug up entirely the root of sorrow,

sn4.24:3.2.verse: Guiltless, I meditate free from sorrow.

sn4.24:3.3.verse: Having cut off all greedy urge for existence,

sn4.24:3.4.verse: I meditate taintless, O kinsman of the negligent!”

sn4.24:4.2.verse: And those who speak in terms of ‘mine’—

sn4.24:5.4.verse: Even my path you will not see. ”

sn4.24:6.2.verse: The secure way leading to the Deathless,

sn4.24:8.2.verse: in which a crab was living.

sn4.24:8.3.verse: Then a group of boys and girls would leave the village or town and go to the pond. They would pull the crab out from the water and set it down on high ground.

sn4.24:8.4.verse: Then, whenever that crab would extend one of its claws, those boys and girls would cut it off, break it, and smash it to bits with sticks and stones.

sn4.24:8.5.verse: Thus, when all its claws have been cut off, broken, and smashed to bits, that crab would be unable to return to that pond.

sn4.24:8.6.verse: So too, venerable sir, all those distortions, manoeuvres, and contortions of mine have been cut off, broken, and smashed to bits by the Blessed One.

sn4.24:8.7.verse: Now, venerable sir, I am unable to approach the Blessed One again seeking to gain access to him. ”

sn4.25:13.1.verse: “Are you swamped by sorrow that you meditate in the forest?

sn4.25:13.5.verse: And why does no one get close to you?”

sn4.25:18.1.verse: That’s how a mendicant who has crossed five floods

sn4.25:18.3.verse: That’s how they usually practice absorption so that sensual perceptions
