sn4.25:6.4.verse: Then Māra’s three daughters, each manifesting herself in the form of a hundred women who have never given birth …

sn4.25:6.6.verse: But the Blessed One paid no attention, as he was liberated in the unsurpassed extinction of acquisitions.

sn4.25:7.2.verse: in the form of a hundred women who have given birth once …

sn4.25:8.2.verse: in the form of a hundred women who have given birth twice …

sn4.25:8.7.verse: in the form of a hundred women of middle age …

sn4.25:9.2.verse: in the form of a hundred old women, approached the Blessed One and said to him:

sn4.25:9.5.verse: as he was liberated in the unsurpassed extinction of acquisitions.

sn4.25:9.6.verse: Then Māra’s daughters—Taṇhā, Aratī, and Ragā—went off to the side and said:

sn4.25:9.7.verse: “What our father told us is true:

sn4.25:10.1.verse: “‘The Arahant, the Fortunate One in the world …

sn4.25:11.1.verse: ’“If we had assailed with such tactics any ascetic or brahmin who was not devoid of lust, either his heart would have burst, or he would have vomited hot blood from his mouth, or he would have gone mad or become mentally deranged;

sn4.25:11.2.verse: Just as a green reed that has been mowed down would dry up and wither away and become shrivelled.

sn4.25:11.3.verse: In the same way, he would have dried up and withered away and become shrivelled.”

sn4.25:12.1.verse: Then Māra’s daughters—Taṇhā, Aratī, and Ragā—approached the Blessed One and stood to one side.

sn4.25:12.2.verse: Standing to one side, Māra’s daughter Taṇhā addressed the Blessed One in verse:

sn4.25:13.1.verse: “Is it because you are sunk in sorrow that you meditate in the woods?

sn4.25:13.2.verse: Because you’ve lost wealth or pine for it,

sn4.25:13.3.verse: Or committed some crime in the village?

sn4.25:13.4.verse: Why don’t you make friends with people?

sn4.25:13.5.verse: Why don’t you form any intimate ties?”

sn4.25:14.1.verse: The attainment of the goal, the peace of the heart.

sn4.25:14.2.verse: “Having conquered the army of the pleasant and agreeable,

sn4.25:14.4.verse: Therefore I don’t make friends with people,

sn4.25:14.5.verse: Nor will I form any intimate ties. ”

sn4.25:15.1.verse: Then Māra’s daughter Aratī addressed the Blessed One in verse:

sn4.25:16.1.verse: “How does a bhikkhu here often dwell

sn4.25:16.2.verse: That, five floods crossed, he here has crossed the sixth?

sn4.25:16.3.verse: How does he meditate so sensual perceptions

sn4.25:16.4.verse: Are kept at bay and fail to grip him?”

sn4.25:17.1.verse: “Tranquil in body, in mind well liberated,

sn4.25:17.4.verse: He does not erupt, or drift, or stiffen.

sn4.25:18.1.verse: “When a bhikkhu here often dwells thus,

sn4.25:18.2.verse: With five floods crossed, he here has crossed the sixth.

sn4.25:18.3.verse: When he meditates thus, sensual perceptions

sn4.25:18.4.verse: Are kept at bay and fail to grip him. ”

sn4.25:19.1.verse: Then Māra’s daughter Ragā addressed the Blessed One in verse:

sn4.25:20.1.verse: “He has cut off craving, faring with his group and order;

sn4.25:20.2.verse: Surely many other beings will cross and lead them away .

sn4.25:20.3.verse: Alas, this homeless one will snatch many people beyond the King of Death. ”

sn4.25:21.1.verse: Truly, lead by the the great heroes,

sn4.25:21.3.verse: are leading by means of the Dhamma,

sn4.25:21.4.verse: What envy can there be in those who understand?”

sn4.25:22.1.verse: Then Māra’s daughters—Taṇhā, Aratī, and Ragā—approached Māra the Evil One.

sn4.25:22.2.verse: Māra saw them coming in the distance

sn4.25:23.1.verse: “Fools! With the stalks of lotus flowers,

sn4.25:23.2.verse: You tried to batter a mountain

sn4.25:23.3.verse: To dig up a mountain with your nails,

sn4.25:23.4.verse: To chew iron with your teeth.

sn4.25:24.1.verse: “As if, having lifted a rock with your head,

sn4.25:24.2.verse: You sought a foothold in the abyss;

sn4.25:24.3.verse: As if you struck a stump with your breast,

sn4.25:25.1.verse: They had come to him glittering with beauty—

sn4.25:25.3.verse: But the Teacher swept them away right there

sn4.25:25.4.verse: As the wind, a fallen cotton tuft.

sn5.1:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn5.1:1.3.verse: Then the nun Āḷavikā robed up in the morning and, taking her bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn5.1:1.4.verse: She wandered for alms in Sāvatthī. After the meal, on her return from almsround, she went to the Dark Forest seeking seclusion.

sn5.1:1.5.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, wanting to make the nun Āḷavikā feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make her fall away from seclusion, went up to her and addressed her in verse:

sn5.1:2.2.verse: so what will seclusion do for you?

sn5.1:3.2.verse: “Who’s speaking this verse, a human or a non-human?”

sn5.1:3.4.verse: “This is Māra the Wicked, wanting to make me feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make me fall away from seclusion!”

sn5.1:3.5.verse: Then Āḷavikā, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:

sn5.1:4.1.verse: “There is an escape in the world,

sn5.1:4.2.verse: and I’ve personally experienced it with wisdom.

sn5.1:4.3.verse: O Wicked One, kinsman of the negligent,

sn5.1:5.1.verse: Sensual pleasures are like swords and spears;

sn5.1:5.2.verse: the aggregates are their chopping block.

sn5.1:5.4.verse: is now no delight for me.”

sn5.1:6.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The nun Āḷavikā knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

sn5.1:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

sn5.1:1.3.verse: Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Āḷavikā dressed and, taking bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn5.1:1.4.verse: When she had walked for alms in Sāvatthī and had returned from her alms round, after her meal she went to the Blind Men’s Grove seeking seclusion.

sn5.1:1.5.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, trepidation, and terror in the bhikkhunī Āḷavikā, desiring to make her fall away from seclusion, approached her and addressed her in verse:

sn5.1:2.1.verse: “There is no escape in the world,

sn5.1:2.2.verse: So what will you do with seclusion?

sn5.1:2.3.verse: Enjoy the delights of sensual pleasure:

sn5.1:3.1.verse: Then it occurred to the bhikkhunī Āḷavikā:

sn5.1:3.2.verse: “Now who is it that recited the verse—a human being or a nonhuman being?”

sn5.1:3.4.verse: “This is Māra the Evil One, who has recited the verse desiring to arouse fear, trepidation, and terror in me, desiring to make me fall away from seclusion. ”

sn5.1:3.5.verse: Then the bhikkhunī Āḷavikā, having understood, “This is Māra the Evil One, ” replied to him in verses:

sn5.1:4.1.verse: “There is an escape in the world

sn5.1:4.2.verse: Which I have closely touched with wisdom.

sn5.1:4.3.verse: O Evil One, kinsman of the negligent,

sn5.1:4.4.verse: You do not know that state.

sn5.1:5.1.verse: “Sensual pleasures are like swords and stakes;

sn5.1:5.2.verse: The aggregates like their chopping block.

sn5.1:6.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, “The bhikkhunī Āḷavikā knows me, ” sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.

sn5.2:1.2.verse: Then the nun Somā robed up in the morning and, taking her bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn5.2:1.3.verse: She wandered for alms in Sāvatthī. After the meal, on her return from almsround, she went to the Dark Forest for the day’s meditation,

sn5.2:1.4.verse: plunged deep into it, and sat at the root of a tree to meditate.

sn5.2:1.5.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, wanting to make the nun Somā feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make her fall away from immersion, went up to her and addressed her in verse:

sn5.2:2.2.verse: it’s for the sages to attain.

sn5.2:2.4.verse: it’s not possible for a woman.”

sn5.2:3.2.verse: “Who’s speaking this verse, a human or a non-human?”

sn5.2:3.4.verse: “This is Māra the Wicked, wanting to make me feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make me fall away from immersion!”

sn5.2:3.5.verse: Then Somā, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:

sn5.2:4.4.verse: as you rightly discern the Dhamma.

sn5.2:5.4.verse: is fit for Māra to address.”

sn5.2:6.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The nun Somā knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

sn5.2:1.2.verse: Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Somā dressed and, taking bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn5.2:1.3.verse: When she had walked for alms in Sāvatthī and had returned from her alms round, after her meal she went to the Blind Men’s Grove for the day’s abiding.

sn5.2:1.4.verse: Having plunged into the Blind Men’s Grove, she sat down at the foot of a tree for the day’s abiding.

sn5.2:1.5.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, trepidation,and terror in the bhikkhunī Somā, desiring to make her fall away from concentration, approached her and addressed her in verse:

sn5.2:2.2.verse: is that state so hard to achieve.

sn5.2:2.4.verse: it can’t be attained by a woman.”

sn5.2:3.1.verse: Then it occurred to the bhikkhunī Somā:

sn5.2:3.2.verse: “Now who is this that recited the verse—a human being or a nonhuman being?”

sn5.2:3.4.verse: “This is Māra the Evil One, who has recited the verse desiring to arouse fear, trepidation, and terror in me, desiring to make me fall away from concentration. ”

sn5.2:3.5.verse: Then the bhikkhunī Somā, having understood, “This is Māra the Evil One, ” replied to him in verses:

sn5.2:4.2.verse: When the mind is concentrated well,

sn5.2:4.4.verse: As one sees correctly into Dhamma.

sn5.2:5.4.verse: Is fit for Māra to address. ”

sn5.2:6.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, “The bhikkhunī Somā knows me, ” sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.

sn5.3:1.2.verse: Then the nun Kisāgotamī robed up in the morning and, taking her bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn5.3:1.3.verse: She wandered for alms in Sāvatthī. After the meal, on her return from almsround, she went to the Dark Forest for the day’s meditation,

sn5.3:1.4.verse: plunged deep into it, and sat at the root of a tree to meditate.

sn5.3:1.5.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, wanting to make the nun Kisāgotamī feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make her fall away from immersion, went up to her and addressed her in verse:

sn5.3:2.1.verse: “Why do you sit alone and cry

sn5.3:2.2.verse: as if your children have died?

sn5.3:2.3.verse: You’ve come to the woods all alone—

sn5.3:2.4.verse: are you looking for a man?”

sn5.3:3.2.verse: “Who’s speaking this verse, a human or a non-human?”

sn5.3:3.4.verse: “This is Māra the Wicked, wanting to make me feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make me fall away from immersion!”

sn5.3:4.1.verse: Then Kisāgotamī, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:

sn5.3:5.1.verse: “I’ve got over the death of children,

sn5.3:5.4.verse: and I’m not afraid of you, sir!

sn5.3:6.1.verse: Relishing is banished in every respect,

sn5.3:6.2.verse: and the mass of darkness is shattered.

sn5.3:6.3.verse: I’ve defeated the army of death,

sn5.3:7.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The nun Kisāgotamī knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

sn5.3:1.2.verse: Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Kisāgotamī dressed and, taking bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn5.3:1.3.verse: When she had walked for alms in Sāvatthī and had returned from her alms round, after her meal she went to the Blind Men’s Grove for the day’s abiding.

sn5.3:1.4.verse: Having plunged into the Blind Men’s Grove, she sat down at the foot of a tree for the day’s abiding.

sn5.3:1.5.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, trepidation, and terror in the bhikkhunī Kisāgotamī, desiring to make her fall away from concentration, approached her and addressed her in verse:

sn5.3:2.1.verse: “Why now, when your son is dead,

sn5.3:2.2.verse: Do you sit alone with tearful face?

sn5.3:2.3.verse: Having entered the woods all alone,

sn5.3:2.4.verse: Are you on the lookout for a man?”

sn5.3:3.1.verse: Then it occurred to the bhikkhunī Kisāgotamī:

sn5.3:3.2.verse: “Now who is this that recited the verse—a human being or a nonhuman being?”

sn5.3:3.4.verse: “This is Māra the Evil One, who has recited the verse desiring to arouse fear, trepidation, and terror in me, desiring to make me fall away from concentration. ”

sn5.3:4.1.verse: Then the bhikkhunī Kisāgotamī, having understood, “This is Māra the Evil One, ” replied to him in verses:

sn5.3:5.1.verse: “I’ve gotten past the death of sons;

sn5.3:5.2.verse: With this, the search for men has ended.

sn5.3:5.3.verse: I do not sorrow, I do not weep,

sn5.3:5.4.verse: Nor do I fear you, friend .

sn5.3:6.2.verse: The mass of darkness has been sundered.

sn5.3:6.3.verse: Having conquered the army of Death,

sn5.3:7.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, “The bhikkhunī Kisāgotamī knows me, ” sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.

sn5.4:1.2.verse: Then the nun Vijayā robed up in the morning …

sn5.4:1.3.verse: and sat at the root of a tree for the day’s meditation.

sn5.4:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, wanting to make the nun Vijayā feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make her fall away from immersion, went up to her and addressed her in verse:

sn5.4:2.2.verse: and I’m a youth in my prime.

sn5.4:2.3.verse: Come, my lady, let us enjoy

sn5.4:2.4.verse: the music of a five-piece band.”

sn5.4:3.2.verse: “Who’s speaking this verse, a human or a non-human?”

sn5.4:3.4.verse: “This is Māra the Wicked, wanting to make me feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make me fall away from immersion!”

sn5.4:3.5.verse: Then Vijayā, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:

sn5.4:4.3.verse: I hand them right back to you, Māra,

sn5.4:4.4.verse: for I have no use for them.

sn5.4:5.3.verse: I’m horrified and repelled by it,

sn5.4:6.1.verse: There are beings in the realm of luminous form,

sn5.4:6.2.verse: and others stuck in the formless.

sn5.4:7.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The nun Vijayā knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

sn5.4:1.2.verse: Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Vijayā dressed …

sn5.4:1.3.verse: … she sat down at the foot of a tree for the day’s abiding.

sn5.4:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, trepidation, and terror in the bhikkhunī Vijayā, desiring to make her fall away from concentration, approached her and addressed her in verse:

sn5.4:2.2.verse: And I too am a youth in my prime.

sn5.4:2.3.verse: With the music of a fivefold ensemble,

sn5.4:2.4.verse: Come, noble lady, let us rejoice ”

sn5.4:3.1.verse: Then it occurred to the bhikkhunī Vijayā:

sn5.4:3.4.verse: This is Māra the Evil One … desiring to make me fall away from concentration. ”

sn5.4:3.5.verse: Then the bhikkhunī Vijayā, having understood, “This is Māra the Evil One, ” replied to him in verses:

sn5.4:4.3.verse: I offer them right back to you,

sn5.4:4.4.verse: For I, O Māra, do not need them.

sn5.4:6.1.verse: “As to those beings who fare amidst form,

sn5.4:6.2.verse: And those who abide in the formless,

sn5.4:7.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, realizing “The bhikkhunī Vijayā knows me, ” sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.

sn5.5:1.2.verse: Then the nun Uppalavaṇṇā robed up in the morning …

sn5.5:1.3.verse: and stood at the root of a sal tree in full flower.

sn5.5:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, wanting to make the nun Uppalavaṇṇā feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make her fall away from immersion, went up to her and addressed her in verse:

sn5.5:2.1.verse: “You’ve come to this sal tree all crowned with flowers,

sn5.5:2.2.verse: and stand at its root all alone, O nun.

sn5.5:2.3.verse: Your beauty is second to none—

sn5.5:2.4.verse: silly girl, aren’t you afraid of rascals?”

sn5.5:3.2.verse: “Who’s speaking this verse, a human or a non-human?”

sn5.5:3.4.verse: “This is Māra the Wicked, wanting to make me feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make me fall away from immersion!”

sn5.5:3.5.verse: Then Uppalavaṇṇā, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:

sn5.5:4.3.verse: I’d stir not a hair nor panic.

sn5.5:4.4.verse: I’m not scared of you, Māra, even alone.

sn5.5:5.3.verse: I could stand between your eyebrows

sn5.5:5.4.verse: and you still wouldn’t see me.

sn5.5:6.1.verse: I’m the master of my own mind,

sn5.5:6.2.verse: I’ve developed the bases of psychic power well.

sn5.5:6.4.verse: and I’m not afraid of you, sir!”

sn5.5:7.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The nun Uppalavaṇṇā knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

sn5.5:1.2.verse: Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā dressed …

sn5.5:1.3.verse: she stood at the foot of a sal tree in full flower.

sn5.5:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, trepidation, and terror in the bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā, desiring to make her fall away from concentration, approached her and addressed her in verse:

sn5.5:2.1.verse: “Having gone to a sal tree with flowering top, bhikkhunī,

sn5.5:2.2.verse: You stand at its foot all alone.

sn5.5:2.3.verse: There is none whose beauty rivals yours:

sn5.5:2.4.verse: Foolish girl, aren’t you afraid of rogues?”

sn5.5:3.1.verse: Then it occurred to the bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā:

sn5.5:3.4.verse: This is Māra the Evil One … desiring to make me fall away from concentration. ”

sn5.5:3.5.verse: Then the bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā, having understood, “This is Māra the Evil One, ” replied to him in verses:

sn5.5:4.2.verse: Just like you might come here,

sn5.5:4.3.verse: I stir not a hair, I feel no terror;

sn5.5:4.4.verse: Even alone, Māra, I don’t fear you.

sn5.5:5.2.verse: Or I can enter inside your belly.

sn5.5:5.3.verse: I can stand between your eyebrows

sn5.5:5.4.verse: Yet you won’t catch a glimpse of me.

sn5.5:6.1.verse: “I am the master of my mind,

sn5.5:6.2.verse: The bases of power are well developed;

sn5.5:6.3.verse: I am freed from all bondage,

sn5.5:6.4.verse: Therefore I don’t fear you, friend. ”

sn5.5:7.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, “The bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā knows me, ” sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.

sn5.6:1.2.verse: Then the nun Cālā robed up in the morning …

sn5.6:1.3.verse: and sat at the root of a tree for the day’s meditation.

sn5.6:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Wicked went up to Cālā and said to her,

sn5.6:2.2.verse: When you’re born, you get to enjoy sensual pleasures.

sn5.6:2.3.verse: Who put this idea in your head:

sn5.6:3.1.verse: “Death comes to those who are born,

sn5.6:3.2.verse: when you’re born you undergo sufferings—

sn5.6:3.4.verse: that’s why you shouldn’t approve of rebirth.

sn5.6:4.1.verse: The Buddha taught me the Dhamma

sn5.6:4.4.verse: he settled me in the truth.

sn5.6:5.1.verse: There are beings in the realm of luminous form,

sn5.6:5.2.verse: and others stuck in the formless.

sn5.6:6.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The nun Cālā knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

sn5.6:1.2.verse: Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Cālā dressed …

sn5.6:1.3.verse: she sat down at the foot of a tree for the day’s abiding.

sn5.6:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Evil One approached the bhikkhunī Cālā and said to her:

sn5.6:2.2.verse: Once born, one enjoys sensual pleasures.

sn5.6:2.3.verse: Who now has persuaded you of this:

sn5.6:3.1.verse: “For one who is born there is death;

sn5.6:3.4.verse: Hence one shouldn’t approve of birth.

sn5.6:4.3.verse: For the abandoning of all suffering

sn5.6:4.4.verse: He has settled me in the truth.

sn5.6:5.1.verse: “As to those beings who fare amidst form,

sn5.6:5.2.verse: And those who abide in the formless—

sn5.6:5.4.verse: They come again to renewed existence. ”

sn5.6:6.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, “The bhikkhunī Cālā knows me, ” sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.

sn5.7:1.2.verse: Then the nun Upacālā robed up in the morning …

sn5.7:1.3.verse: and sat at the root of a tree for the day’s meditation.

sn5.7:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Wicked went up to Upacālā and said to her,

sn5.7:1.5.verse: “Nun, where do you want to be reborn?”

sn5.7:1.6.verse: “I don’t want to be reborn anywhere, sir.”

sn5.7:2.1.verse: “There are the gods of the thirty-three, and those of Yama;

sn5.7:2.3.verse: the gods who love to create,

sn5.7:2.4.verse: and the gods who control what is created by others.

sn5.7:2.5.verse: Set your heart on such places,

sn5.7:3.1.verse: “The gods of the thirty-three, and those of Yama;

sn5.7:3.3.verse: the gods who love to create,

sn5.7:3.4.verse: and the gods who control what is created by others—

sn5.7:3.5.verse: they’re bound with the bonds of sensuality;

sn5.7:3.6.verse: they fall under your sway again.

sn5.7:4.1.verse: All the world is on fire,

sn5.7:5.4.verse: and not frequented by ordinary people.”

sn5.7:6.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The nun Upacālā knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

sn5.7:1.2.verse: Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Upacālā dressed …

sn5.7:1.3.verse: she sat down at the foot of a tree for the day’s abiding.

sn5.7:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Evil One approached the bhikkhunī Upacālā and said to her:

sn5.7:1.5.verse: “Where do you wish to be reborn, bhikkhunī?”

sn5.7:1.6.verse: “I do not wish to be reborn anywhere, friend. ”

sn5.7:2.2.verse: And devatās of the Tusita realm,

sn5.7:2.3.verse: Devas who take delight in creating,

sn5.7:2.5.verse: Direct your mind there [to those realms]

sn5.7:3.2.verse: And devatās of the Tusita realm,

sn5.7:3.3.verse: Devas who take delight in creating,

sn5.7:3.5.verse: They are still bound by sensual bondage,

sn5.7:3.6.verse: They come again under Māra’s control.

sn5.7:5.1.verse: “That which does not quake or blaze,

sn5.7:5.2.verse: That to which worldlings do not resort,

sn5.7:5.3.verse: Where there is no place for Māra:

sn5.7:5.4.verse: That is where my mind delights. ”

sn5.7:6.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, “The bhikkhunī Upacālā knows me, sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.

sn5.8:1.2.verse: Then the nun Sīsupacālā robed up in the morning …

sn5.8:1.3.verse: and sat at the root of a tree for the day’s meditation.

sn5.8:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Wicked went up to Sīsupacālā and said to her,

sn5.8:1.5.verse: “Nun, whose creed do you approve of?”

sn5.8:2.1.verse: “In whose name did you shave your head?

sn5.8:2.3.verse: but you don’t approve any creed.

sn5.8:2.4.verse: Why do you wander as if lost?”

sn5.8:3.3.verse: But I don’t approve their teaching,

sn5.8:3.4.verse: for they’re no experts in the Dhamma.

sn5.8:4.1.verse: But there is one born in the Sakyan clan,

sn5.8:4.3.verse: vanquisher of all, dispeller of Māra,

sn5.8:5.3.verse: He has attained the end of all deeds,

sn5.8:5.4.verse: freed with the ending of attachments.

sn5.8:5.5.verse: That Blessed One is my Teacher,

sn5.8:6.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The nun Sīsupacālā knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

sn5.8:1.2.verse: Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Sīsupacālā dressed …

sn5.8:1.3.verse: she sat down at the foot of a tree for the day’s abiding.

sn5.8:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Evil One approached the bhikkhunī Sīsupacālā and said to her:

sn5.8:1.5.verse: “Whose creed do you approve of, bhikkhunī?”

sn5.8:1.6.verse: “I don’t approve of anyone’s creed, friend. ”

sn5.8:2.1.verse: “Under whom have you shaved your head?

sn5.8:2.2.verse: You do appear to be an ascetic,

sn5.8:2.3.verse: Yet you don’t approve of any creed,

sn5.8:2.4.verse: So why wander as if bewildered?”

sn5.8:3.3.verse: I don’t approve of their teachings;

sn5.8:3.4.verse: They are not skilled in the Dhamma.

sn5.8:4.1.verse: “But there’s one born in the Sakyan clan,

sn5.8:4.2.verse: The Enlightened One, without an equal,

sn5.8:5.2.verse: The One with Vision who sees all.

sn5.8:5.3.verse: “Attained to the end of all kamma,

sn5.8:5.4.verse: Liberated in the extinction of acquisitions,

sn5.8:5.5.verse: That Blessed One is my Teacher:

sn5.8:5.6.verse: His is the teaching I approve. ”

sn5.8:6.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, “The bhikkhunī Sīsupacālā knows me, ” sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.

sn5.9:1.2.verse: Then the nun Selā robed up in the morning …

sn5.9:1.3.verse: and sat at the root of a tree for the day’s meditation.

sn5.9:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, wanting to make the nun Selā feel fear, terror, and goosebumps …

sn5.9:3.2.verse: “Who’s speaking this verse, a human or a non-human?”

sn5.9:3.4.verse: “This is Māra the Wicked, wanting to make me feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make me fall away from immersion!”

sn5.9:3.5.verse: Then Selā, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:

sn5.9:4.2.verse: nor is this gloom made by another.

sn5.9:4.3.verse: It comes to be because of a cause,

sn5.9:4.4.verse: and ceases when the cause breaks up.

sn5.9:5.1.verse: It’s like a seed that’s sown

sn5.9:5.3.verse: relying on both the soil’s nutrients

sn5.9:6.1.verse: In the same way the aggregates and elements

sn5.9:6.3.verse: come to be because of a cause,

sn5.9:6.4.verse: and cease when the cause breaks up.”

sn5.9:7.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The nun Selā knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

sn5.9:1.2.verse: Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Selā dressed …

sn5.9:1.3.verse: she sat down at the foot of a tree for the day’s abiding.

sn5.9:1.4.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, trepidation, and terror in the bhikkhunī Selā, desiring to make her fall away from concentration, approached her and addressed her in verse:

sn5.9:2.1.verse: By whom has this puppet been created?

sn5.9:2.2.verse: Where is the maker of the puppet?

sn5.9:3.1.verse: Then it occurred to the bhikkhunī Selā:

sn5.9:3.4.verse: This is Māra the Evil One … desiring to make me fall away from concentration. ”

sn5.9:3.5.verse: Then the bhikkhunī Selā, having understood, “This is Māra the Evil One, ” replied to him in verses:

sn5.9:4.1.verse: “This puppet is not made by itself,

sn5.9:4.2.verse: Nor is this misery made by another.

sn5.9:4.3.verse: It has come to be dependent on a cause;

sn5.9:4.4.verse: With the cause’s breakup it will cease.

sn5.9:5.1.verse: “As when a seed is sown in a field

sn5.9:5.2.verse: It grows depending on a pair of factors:

sn5.9:5.3.verse: It requires both the soil’s nutrients

sn5.9:5.4.verse: And a steady supply of moisture:

sn5.9:6.2.verse: And these six bases of sensory contact,

sn5.9:6.3.verse: Have come to be dependent on a cause;

sn5.9:6.4.verse: With the cause’s breakup they will cease. ”

sn5.9:7.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, “The bhikkhunī Selā knows me, ” sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.

sn5.10:1.2.verse: Then the nun Vajirā robed up in the morning and, taking her bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn5.10:1.3.verse: She wandered for alms in Sāvatthī. After the meal, on her return from almsround, she went to the Dark Forest for the day’s meditation,

sn5.10:1.4.verse: plunged deep into it, and sat at the root of a tree to meditate.

sn5.10:1.5.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, wanting to make the nun Vajirā feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make her fall away from immersion, went up to her and addressed her in verse:

sn5.10:3.2.verse: “Who’s speaking this verse, a human or a non-human?”

sn5.10:3.4.verse: “This is Māra the Wicked, wanting to make me feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make me fall away from immersion!”

sn5.10:3.5.verse: Then Vajirā, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, replied to him in verse:

sn5.10:4.1.verse: “Why do you believe there’s such a thing as a ‘sentient being’?

sn5.10:4.3.verse: This is just a pile of conditions,

sn5.10:4.4.verse: you won’t find a sentient being here.

sn5.10:5.3.verse: So too, when the aggregates are present

sn5.10:5.4.verse: ‘sentient being’ is the convention we use.

sn5.10:6.1.verse: But it’s only suffering that comes to be,

sn5.10:6.3.verse: Naught but suffering comes to be,

sn5.10:7.1.verse: Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The nun Vajirā knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.

sn5.10:8.6.verse: The Linked Discourses on Nuns are complete.

sn5.10:1.2.verse: Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Vajirā dressed and, taking bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn5.10:1.3.verse: When she had walked for alms in Sāvatthī  and had returned from her alms round, after her meal she went to the Blind Men’s Grove for the day’s abiding.

sn5.10:1.4.verse: Having plunged into the Blind Men’s Grove, she sat down at the foot of a tree for the day’s abiding.

sn5.10:1.5.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, trepidation, and terror in the bhikkhunī Vajirā, desiring to make her fall away from concentration, approached her and addressed her in verse:

sn5.10:2.1.verse: “By whom has this being been created?

sn5.10:2.2.verse: Where is the maker of the being?

sn5.10:3.1.verse: Then it occurred to the bhikkhunī Vajirā:

sn5.10:3.2.verse: “Now who is this that recited the verse—a human being or a nonhuman being?”

sn5.10:3.4.verse: “This is Māra the Evil One, who has recited the verse desiring to arouse fear, trepidation, and terror in me, desiring to make me fall away from concentration. ”

sn5.10:3.5.verse: Then the bhikkhunī Vajirā, having understood, “This is Māra the Evil One, ” replied to him in verses:

sn5.10:4.2.verse: Māra, is that your speculative view?

sn5.10:4.3.verse: This is a heap of sheer formations:

sn5.10:5.1.verse: “Just as, with an assemblage of parts,

sn5.10:6.1.verse: “It’s only suffering that comes to be,

sn5.10:6.2.verse: Suffering that stands and falls away.

sn5.10:6.3.verse: Nothing but suffering comes to be,

sn5.10:7.1.verse: Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, “The bhikkhunī Vajirā knows me, ” sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.

sn6.1:1.2.verse: At one time, when he was first awakened, the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the root of the goatherd’s banyan tree on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

sn6.1:1.3.verse: Then as he was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,

sn6.1:1.4.verse: “This principle I have discovered is deep, hard to see, hard to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of logic, subtle, comprehensible to the astute.

sn6.1:1.5.verse: But people like clinging, they love it and enjoy it.

sn6.1:1.6.verse: It’s hard for them to see this topic; that is, specific conditionality, dependent origination.

sn6.1:1.7.verse: It’s also hard for them to see this topic; that is, the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.

sn6.1:1.8.verse: And if I were to teach this principle, others might not understand me, which would be wearying and troublesome for me.”

sn6.1:1.9.verse: And then these verses, which were neither supernaturally inspired, nor learned before in the past, occurred to the Buddha:

sn6.1:2.2.verse: there’s no need to reveal it now!

sn6.1:2.3.verse: Those mired in greed and hate

sn6.1:3.1.verse: It goes against the stream, subtle,

sn6.1:3.3.verse: Those besotted by greed cannot see,

sn6.1:3.4.verse: for they’re cloaked in a mass of darkness.”

sn6.1:4.1.verse: And as the Buddha reflected like this, his mind inclined to remaining passive, not to teaching the Dhamma.

sn6.1:5.1.verse: Then, knowing the Buddha’s train of thought, it occurred to the divinity Sahampati,

sn6.1:5.2.verse: “Oh lord! The world will be lost, the world will perish! For the mind of the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, inclines to remaining passive, not to teaching the Dhamma.”

sn6.1:5.3.verse: Then, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from the realm of divinity and reappeared in front of the Buddha.

sn6.1:5.4.verse: He arranged his robe over one shoulder, knelt on his right knee, raised his joined palms toward the Buddha, and said:

sn6.1:5.5.verse: “Sir, let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma! Let the Holy One teach the Dhamma!

sn6.1:5.6.verse: There are beings with little dust in their eyes. They’re in decline because they haven’t heard the teaching.

sn6.1:5.7.verse: There will be those who understand the teaching!”

sn6.1:5.8.verse: That is what the divinity Sahampati said. Then he went on to say:

sn6.1:6.1.verse: “Among the Magadhans there appeared in the past

sn6.1:6.2.verse: an impure teaching thought up by the stained.

sn6.1:6.3.verse: Fling open the door to freedom from death!

sn6.1:6.4.verse: Let them hear the teaching the immaculate one discovered.

sn6.1:7.1.verse: Standing high on a rocky mountain,

sn6.1:7.2.verse: you can see the people all around.

sn6.1:7.3.verse: In just the same way, All-seer, so intelligent,

sn6.1:7.4.verse: having ascended the Temple of Truth,

sn6.1:7.5.verse: rid of sorrow, look upon the people

sn6.1:7.6.verse: swamped with sorrow,  overcome by rebirth and old age.

sn6.1:8.1.verse: Rise, hero! Victor in battle, caravan leader,

sn6.1:8.2.verse: wander the world free of debt.

sn6.1:8.3.verse: Let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma!

sn6.1:8.4.verse: There will be those who understand!”

sn6.1:9.1.verse: Then the Buddha, understanding the Divinity’s invitation, surveyed the world with the eye of a Buddha, out of his compassion for sentient beings.

sn6.1:9.2.verse: And the Buddha saw sentient beings with little dust in their eyes, and some with much dust in their eyes; with keen faculties and with weak faculties, with good qualities and with bad qualities, easy to teach and hard to teach. And some of them lived seeing the danger in the fault to do with the next world, while others did not.

sn6.1:9.3.verse: It’s like a pool with blue water lilies, or pink or white lotuses. Some of them sprout and grow in the water without rising above it, thriving underwater. Some of them sprout and grow in the water reaching the water’s surface. And some of them sprout and grow in the water but rise up above the water and stand with no water clinging to them.

sn6.1:9.4.verse: In the same way, the Buddha saw sentient beings with little dust in their eyes, and some with much dust in their eyes; with keen faculties and with weak faculties, with good qualities and with bad qualities, easy to teach and hard to teach. And some of them lived seeing the danger in the fault to do with the next world, while others did not.

sn6.1:9.5.verse: When he had seen this he replied in verse to the divinity Sahampati:

sn6.1:10.1.verse: “Flung open are the doors to freedom from death!

sn6.1:10.2.verse: Let those with ears to hear commit to faith.

sn6.1:10.3.verse: Thinking it would be troublesome, Divinity, I did not teach

sn6.1:10.4.verse: the sophisticated, sublime Dhamma among mankind.”

sn6.1:11.1.verse: Then the divinity Sahampati, knowing that his request for the Buddha to teach the Dhamma had been granted, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

sn6.1:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruvelā on the bank of the river Nerañjarā at the foot of the Goatherd’s Banyan Tree just after he had become fully enlightened.

sn6.1:1.3.verse: Then, while the Blessed One was alone in seclusion, a reflection arose in his mind thus:

sn6.1:1.4.verse: “This Dhamma that I have discovered is deep, hard to see, hard to understand, peaceful and sublime, not within the sphere of reasoning, subtle, to be experienced by the wise.

sn6.1:1.5.verse: But this generation delights in adhesion, takes delight in adhesion, rejoices in adhesion.

sn6.1:1.6.verse: For such a generation this state is hard to see, that is, specific conditionality, dependent origination.

sn6.1:1.7.verse: And this state too is hard to see, that is, the stilling of all formations, the relinquishment of all acquisitions, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna.

sn6.1:1.8.verse: If I were to teach the Dhamma and if others would not understand me, that would be wearisome for me, that would be troublesome. ”

sn6.1:1.9.verse: Thereupon these astounding verses, not heard before in the past, occurred to the Blessed One:

sn6.1:2.1.verse: “What I found with so much hardship;

sn6.1:2.2.verse: Enough now with trying to teach

sn6.1:2.3.verse: By those oppressed by lust and hate.

sn6.1:3.3.verse: Those fired by lust, will never see this,

sn6.1:4.1.verse: As the Blessed One reflected thus, his mind inclined to living at ease, not to teaching the Dhamma.

sn6.1:5.1.verse: Then Brahmā Sahampati, having known with his own mind the reflection in the Blessed One’s mind, thought:

sn6.1:5.2.verse: “Alas, the world is lost! Alas, the world is to perish, in that the mind of the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, inclines to living at ease, not to teaching the Dhamma.

sn6.1:5.3.verse: ” Then, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, Brahmā Sahampati disappeared from the brahmā world and reappeared before the Blessed One.

sn6.1:5.4.verse: He arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, knelt down with his right knee on the ground, raised his joined hands in reverential salutation towards the Blessed One, and said to him:

sn6.1:5.5.verse: “Venerable sir, let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma; let the Fortunate One teach the Dhamma.

sn6.1:5.6.verse: There are beings with little dust in their eyes who are falling away because they do not hear the Dhamma.

sn6.1:5.7.verse: There will be those who will understand the Dhamma. ”

sn6.1:5.8.verse: This is what Brahmā Sahampati said. Having said this, he further said this:

sn6.1:6.1.verse: “In the past there appeared among the Magadhans

sn6.1:6.2.verse: An impure Dhamma devised by those still stained.

sn6.1:6.3.verse: Throw open this door to the Deathless!

sn6.1:6.4.verse: Let them hear The Dhamma that the Stainless One discovered.

sn6.1:7.1.verse: “Just as one standing on a mountain peak

sn6.1:7.2.verse: Might see below the people all around,

sn6.1:7.3.verse: So, made of the Dhamma, O wise one,

sn6.1:7.5.verse: Being yourself free from sorrow, these people submerged in sorrow,

sn6.1:7.6.verse: Behold beings oppressed by birth and decay. ”

sn6.1:8.1.verse: “Rise up, O hero, victor in battle!

sn6.1:8.2.verse: O caravan leader, debt-free one, wander in the world.

sn6.1:8.3.verse: Teach the Dhamma, O Blessed One:

sn6.1:8.4.verse: There will be those who will understand. ”

sn6.1:9.1.verse: Then the Blessed One, having understood Brahmā’s request, out of compassion for beings surveyed the world with the eye of a Buddha.

sn6.1:9.2.verse: As he did so, the Blessed One saw beings with little dust in their eyes and with much dust in their eyes, with keen faculties and with dull faculties, with good qualities and with bad qualities, easy to teach and difficult to teach, and a few who dwelt seeing blame and fear in the other world.

sn6.1:9.3.verse: Just as in a pond of blue or red or white lotuses, some lotuses might be born in the water, grow up in the water, and thrive while submerged in the water, without rising up from the water; some lotuses might be born in the water, grow up in the water, and stand at an even level with the water; some lotuses might be born in the water and grow up in the water, but would rise up from the water and stand without being soiled by the water,

sn6.1:9.4.verse: So too, surveying the world with the eye of a Buddha, the Blessed One saw beings with little dust in their eyes and with much dust in their eyes, with keen faculties and with dull faculties, with good qualities and with bad qualities, easy to teach and hard to teach, and a few who dwelt seeing blame and fear in the other world.

sn6.1:9.5.verse: Having seen this, he answered Brahmā Sahampati in verse:

sn6.1:10.1.verse: “Open to them are the doors to the Deathless:

sn6.1:10.2.verse: Let those who have ears release faith.

sn6.1:10.3.verse: Foreseeing trouble, O Brahmā, I did not speak

sn6.1:10.4.verse: The refined, sublime Dhamma among human beings. ”

sn6.1:11.1.verse: Then Brahmā Sahampati, thinking, “The Blessed One has given his consent [to my request] regarding the teaching of the Dhamma, ” paid homage to the Blessed One and disappeared right there.

sn6.2:1.2.verse: At one time, when he was first awakened, the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the root of the goatherd’s banyan tree on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

sn6.2:1.3.verse: Then as he was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,

sn6.2:1.4.verse: “One without respect and reverence lives in suffering. What ascetic or brahmin should I honor and respect and rely on?”

sn6.2:2.2.verse: “I’d honor and respect and rely on another ascetic or brahmin so as to complete the entire spectrum of ethics, if it were incomplete.

sn6.2:2.3.verse: But I don’t see any other ascetic or brahmin in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—who is more accomplished than myself in ethics, who I should honor and respect and rely on.

sn6.2:3.1.verse: I’d honor and respect and rely on another ascetic or brahmin so as to complete the entire spectrum of immersion, if it were incomplete.

sn6.2:3.2.verse: But I don’t see any other ascetic or brahmin … who is more accomplished than myself in immersion …

sn6.2:4.1.verse: I’d honor and respect and rely on another ascetic or brahmin so as to complete the entire spectrum of wisdom, if it were incomplete.

sn6.2:4.2.verse: But I don’t see any other ascetic or brahmin … who is more accomplished than myself in wisdom …

sn6.2:5.1.verse: I’d honor and respect and rely on another ascetic or brahmin so as to complete the entire spectrum of freedom, if it were incomplete.

sn6.2:5.2.verse: But I don’t see any other ascetic or brahmin … who is more accomplished than myself in freedom …

sn6.2:6.1.verse: I’d honor and respect and rely on another ascetic or brahmin so as to complete the entire spectrum of the knowledge and vision of freedom, if it were incomplete.

sn6.2:6.2.verse: But I don’t see any other ascetic or brahmin in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—who is more accomplished than myself in the knowledge and vision of freedom, who I should honor and respect and rely on.

sn6.2:6.3.verse: Why don’t I honor and respect and rely on the same Dhamma to which I was awakened?”

sn6.2:7.1.verse: Then the divinity Sahampati knew the Buddha’s train of thought. As easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from the realm of divinity and reappeared in front of the Buddha.

sn6.2:7.2.verse: He arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha, and said:

sn6.2:7.3.verse: “That’s so true, Blessed One! That’s so true, Holy One!

sn6.2:7.4.verse: All the perfected ones, the fully awakened Buddhas who lived in the past honored and respected and relied on this same teaching.

sn6.2:7.5.verse: All the perfected ones, the fully awakened Buddhas who will live in the future will honor and respect and rely on this same teaching.

sn6.2:7.6.verse: May the Blessed One, who is the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha at present, also honor and respect and rely on this same teaching.”

sn6.2:7.7.verse: That is what the divinity Sahampati said. Then he went on to say:

sn6.2:8.4.verse: destroyer of the sorrows of many—

sn6.2:9.2.verse: they did live, they do live,

sn6.2:9.4.verse: This is the nature of the Buddhas.

sn6.2:10.4.verse: remembering the instructions of the Buddhas.”

sn6.2:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruvelā on the bank of the river Nerañjarā at the foot of the Goatherd’s Banyan Tree just after he had become fully enlightened.

sn6.2:1.3.verse: Then, while the Blessed One was alone in seclusion, a reflection arose in his mind thus:

sn6.2:1.4.verse: “One dwells in suffering if one is without reverence and deference. Now what ascetic or brahmin can I honour and respect and dwell in dependence on?”

sn6.2:2.1.verse: Then it occurred to the Blessed One:

sn6.2:2.2.verse: “It would be for the sake of fulfilling an unfulfilled aggregate of virtue that I would honour, respect, and dwell in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin.

sn6.2:2.3.verse: However, in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, I do not see another ascetic or brahmin more perfect in virtue than myself, whom I could honour and respect and dwell in dependence on.

sn6.2:3.1.verse: “It would be for the sake of fulfilling an unfulfilled aggregate of concentration that I would honour, respect, and dwell in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin.

sn6.2:3.2.verse: However… I do not see another ascetic or brahmin more perfect in concentration than myself… .

sn6.2:4.1.verse: “It would be for the sake of fulfilling an unfulfilled aggregate of wisdom that I would honour, respect, and dwell in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin.

sn6.2:4.2.verse: However… I do not see another ascetic or brahmin more perfect in wisdom than myself… .

sn6.2:5.1.verse: “It would be for the sake of fulfilling an unfulfilled aggregate of liberation that I would honour, respect, and dwell in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin.

sn6.2:5.2.verse: However… I do not see another ascetic or brahmin more perfect in liberation than myself… .

sn6.2:6.1.verse: “It would be for the sake of fulfilling an unfulfilled aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation that I would honour, respect, and dwell in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin.

sn6.2:6.2.verse: I do not see another ascetic or brahmin more perfect in the knowledge and vision of liberation than myself, whom I could honour and respect, and on whom I could dwell in dependence. “Let me then honour, respect, and dwell in dependence on this very Dhamma to which I have fully awakened. ”

sn6.2:7.1.verse: Then, having known with his own mind the reflection in the Blessed One’s mind, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, Brahmā Sahampati disappeared from the brahmā world and reappeared before the Blessed One.

sn6.2:7.2.verse: He arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, raised his joined hands in reverential salutation towards the Blessed One, and said to him:

sn6.2:7.3.verse: “So it is, Blessed One! So it is, Fortunate One!

sn6.2:7.4.verse: Venerable sir, those who were the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the past—those Blessed Ones too honoured, respected, and dwelt in dependence just on the Dhamma itself.

sn6.2:7.5.verse: Those who will be the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the future—those Blessed Ones too will honour, respect, and dwell in dependence just on the Dhamma itself.

sn6.2:7.6.verse: Let the Blessed One too, who is at present the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, honour, respect, and dwell in dependence just on the Dhamma itself. ”

sn6.3:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn6.3:1.3.verse: Now at that time a certain brahmin lady had a son named Brahmadeva, who had gone forth from the lay life to homelessness in the presence of the Buddha.

sn6.3:2.1.verse: Then Venerable Brahmadeva, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

sn6.3:2.2.verse: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

sn6.3:2.3.verse: And Venerable Brahmadeva became one of the perfected.

sn6.3:3.1.verse: Then Brahmadeva robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn6.3:3.3.verse: Now at that time Brahmadeva’s mother, the brahmin lady, was presenting a regular oblation to the Divinity.

sn6.3:3.5.verse: “This Venerable Brahmadeva’s mother, the brahmin lady, offers up a regular oblation to the Divinity.

sn6.3:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

sn6.3:1.3.verse: Now on that occasion a certain brahmin lady had a son named Brahmadeva  who had gone forth from the household life into homelessness under the Blessed One.

sn6.3:2.1.verse: Then, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, the Venerable Brahmadeva, by realizing it for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life entered and dwelt in that unsurpassed goal of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness.

sn6.3:2.2.verse: He directly knew: “Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being. ”

sn6.3:2.3.verse: And the Venerable Brahmadeva became one of the arahants.

sn6.3:3.1.verse: Then, in the morning, the Venerable Brahmadeva dressed and, taking bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn6.3:3.2.verse: Walking on continuous alms round in Sāvatthī, he came to his own mother’s residence.

sn6.3:3.3.verse: Now on that occasion the brahmin lady, the Venerable Brahmadeva’s mother, had been offering a constant oblation to Brahmā.

sn6.3:3.5.verse: “This brahmin lady, the Venerable Brahmadeva’s mother, has been offering a constant oblation to Brahmā.

sn6.3:3.6.verse: Let me approach her and stir up a sense of urgency in her. ”

sn6.3:3.7.verse: Then, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, Brahmā Sahampati disappeared from the brahmā world and reappeared in the residence of the Venerable Brahmadeva’s mother.

sn6.4:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn6.4:1.3.verse: Now at that time Baka the Divinity had the following harmful misconception:

sn6.4:1.4.verse: “This is permanent, this is everlasting, this is eternal, this is whole, this is not liable to pass away. For this is where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn. And there’s no other escape beyond this.”

sn6.4:2.6.verse: For this is permanent, this is everlasting, this is eternal, this is whole, this is not liable to pass away. For this is where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn. And there’s no other escape beyond this.”

sn6.4:3.1.verse: When he had spoken, the Buddha said to him,

sn6.4:3.2.verse: “Alas, Baka the Divinity is lost in ignorance! Alas, Baka the Divinity is lost in ignorance!

sn6.4:3.3.verse: Because what is actually impermanent, not lasting, transient, incomplete, and liable to pass away, he says is permanent, everlasting, eternal, whole, and not liable to pass away.

sn6.4:3.5.verse: there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn.

sn6.4:3.6.verse: And although there is another escape beyond this, he says that there’s no other escape beyond this.”

sn6.4:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

sn6.4:1.3.verse: Now on that occasion the following evil speculative view had arisen in Brahmā Baka: “This is permanent, this is stable,

sn6.4:1.4.verse: this is eternal, this is complete, this is imperishable. Indeed, this is where one is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and is not reborn; and there is no other escape superior to this. ”

sn6.4:2.1.verse: Then, having known with his own mind the reflection in Brahmā Baka’s mind, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, the Blessed One disappeared from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared in that brahmā world.

sn6.4:2.2.verse: Brahmā Baka saw the Blessed One coming in the distance and said to him :

sn6.4:2.5.verse: It has been a long time, dear sir, since you took the opportunity of coming here.

sn6.4:2.6.verse: Indeed, dear sir, this is permanent, this is stable, this is eternal, this is complete, this is imperishable. Indeed, this is where one is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and is not reborn; and there is no other escape superior to this. ”

sn6.4:3.1.verse: When this was said, the Blessed One said to Brahmā Baka:

sn6.4:3.2.verse: “Alas, sir, Brahmā Baka is immersed in ignorance! Alas, sir, Brahmā Baka is immersed in ignorance,

sn6.4:3.3.verse: in so far as he will say of what is actually impermanent that it is permanent; and will say of what is actually unstable that it is stable; and will say of what is actually noneternal that it is eternal; and will say of what is actually incomplete that it is complete; and will say of what is actually perishable that it is imperishable;

sn6.4:3.4.verse: and with reference to [a realm] where one is born, ages, dies, passes away, and is reborn, will say thus:

sn6.4:3.5.verse: ‘Indeed, this is where one is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and is not reborn’;

sn6.4:3.6.verse: and when there is another escape superior to this, will say, ‘There is no other escape superior to this. ’”

sn6.4:4.2.verse: Now we wield power, beyond birth and aging.

sn6.4:4.3.verse: This, knowledge-master, is our final attainment of Brahmā.

sn6.4:4.4.verse: Many are the people who yearn for us. ”

sn6.5:10.3.verse: Who are arahants with taints destroyed,

sn6.5:10.4.verse: “Many are the disciples of the Buddha ”

sn6.5:11.1.verse: Then that member of Brahmā’s assembly, having delighted and rejoiced in the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna’s statement, approached that brahmā and told him:

sn6.5:11.2.verse: “Dear sir, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna speaks thus:

sn6.5:12.2.verse: Skilled in the course of others’ minds.

sn6.5:12.4.verse: “‘Many are the disciples of the Buddha.’”

sn6.5:13.1.verse: This is what that member of Brahmā’s assembly said.

sn6.5:13.2.verse: Elated, that brahmā delighted in his statement.

sn6.6:1.2.verse: Now at that time the Buddha had gone into retreat for the day’s meditation.

sn6.6:1.3.verse: Then the independent divinities Subrahmā and Suddhāvāsa went to the Buddha and stationed themselves one by each door-post. But Subrahmā said to Suddhāvāsa,

sn6.6:1.4.verse: “Good fellow, it’s the wrong time to pay homage to the Buddha.

sn6.6:1.5.verse: He has gone into retreat for the day’s meditation.

sn6.6:1.6.verse: But such-and-such realm of divinity is successful and prosperous, while the divinity living there is negligent.

sn6.6:1.7.verse: Come, let’s go to that realm of divinity and inspire awe in that divinity!”

sn6.6:2.1.verse: Then, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, they vanished from in front of the Buddha and appeared in that realm of divinity.

sn6.6:2.2.verse: That divinity saw those divinities coming off in the distance and said to them,

sn6.6:2.3.verse: “Well now, good fellows, where have you come from?”

sn6.6:2.4.verse: “Good fellow, we’ve come from the presence of the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

sn6.6:2.5.verse: Shouldn’t you go to attend on that Blessed One?”

sn6.6:3.1.verse: When they had spoken, that divinity refused to accept their advice. He multiplied himself a thousand times and said to Subrahmā,

sn6.6:3.2.verse: “Good fellow, can’t you see that I have such psychic power?”

sn6.6:3.4.verse: “Since I have such psychic power and might, what other ascetic or brahmin should I go to and attend upon?”

sn6.6:4.1.verse: Then Subrahmā multiplied himself two thousand times and said to that divinity,

sn6.6:4.2.verse: “Good fellow, can’t you see that I have such psychic power?”

sn6.6:4.4.verse: “That Buddha has even more psychic power and might than you or me.

sn6.6:4.5.verse: Shouldn’t you go to attend on that Blessed One?”

sn6.6:4.6.verse: Then that divinity addressed Subrahmā in verse:

sn6.6:5.1.verse: “There are three hundreds of phoenixes, four of swans,

sn6.6:5.2.verse: and five of tigerhawks. To he who practiced absorption

sn6.6:5.3.verse: belongs this palace; it shines, Divinity,

sn6.6:6.3.verse: A clever person, seeing the strife in form,

sn6.6:6.4.verse: its chronic trembling, takes no pleasure in it.”

sn6.6:7.1.verse: Then after inspiring awe in that divinity, the independent divinities Subrahmā and Suddhāvāsa vanished right there.

sn6.6:7.2.verse: And after some time that divinity went to attend on the Buddha.

sn6.6:1.2.verse: Now on that occasion the Blessed One had gone for his day’s abiding and was in seclusion.

sn6.6:1.3.verse: Then the independent brahmās Subrahmā and Suddhāvāsa approached the Blessed One and stood one at each doorpost. Then the independent brahmā Subrahmā said to the independent brahmā Suddhāvāsa:

sn6.6:1.4.verse: “It is not the right time, dear sir, to visit the Blessed One.

sn6.6:1.5.verse: The Blessed One has gone for his day’s abiding and is in seclusion.

sn6.6:1.6.verse: Such and such a brahmā world is rich and prosperous, and the brahmā there is dwelling in negligence.

sn6.6:1.7.verse: Come, dear sir, let us go to that brahmā world and stir up a sense of urgency in that brahmā. ”

sn6.6:1.8.verse: “Yes, dear sir, ” the independent brahmā Suddhāvāsa replied.

sn6.6:2.1.verse: Then, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, the independent brahmās Subrahmā and Suddhāvāsa disappeared in front of the Blessed One and reappeared in that brahmā world.

sn6.6:2.2.verse: That brahmā saw those brahmās coming in the distance and said to them:

sn6.6:2.3.verse: “Now where are you coming from, dear sirs?”

sn6.6:2.4.verse: “We have come, dear sir, from the presence of the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

sn6.6:2.5.verse: Dear sir, you should go to attend upon that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. ”

sn6.6:3.1.verse: When this was said, that brahmā refused to accept their advice. Having created a thousand transformations of himself, he said to the independent brahmā Subrahmā:

sn6.6:3.2.verse: “Do you see, dear sir, how much power and might I have?”

sn6.6:3.3.verse: “I see, dear sir, that you have so much power and might. ”

sn6.6:3.4.verse: “But, dear sir, when I am so powerful and mighty, what other ascetic or brahmin should I go to attend upon?”

sn6.6:4.1.verse: Then the independent brahmā Subrahmā, having created two thousand transformations of himself, said to that brahmā:

sn6.6:4.2.verse: “Do you see, dear sir, how much power and might I have?”

sn6.6:4.3.verse: “I see, dear sir, that you have so much power and might. ”

sn6.6:4.4.verse: “That Blessed One, dear sir, is still more powerful and mighty than both you and I.

sn6.6:4.5.verse: You should go, dear sir, to attend upon that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. ”

sn6.6:4.6.verse: Then that brahmā addressed the independent brahmā Subrahmā in verse:

sn6.6:5.3.verse: This palace, O Brahmā, of the meditator shines

sn6.6:6.1.verse: [The independent brahmā Subrahmā: ]  “Even though that palace of yours shines

sn6.6:6.3.verse: Having seen form’s flaw, its chronic trembling,

sn6.6:6.4.verse: The wise one takes no delight in form. ”

sn6.6:7.1.verse: Then the independent brahmās Subrahmā and Suddhāvāsa, having stirred up a sense of urgency in that brahmā, disappeared right there.

sn6.6:7.2.verse: And on a later occasion that brahmā went to attend upon the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

sn6.9:1.2.verse: Now at that time the mendicant Kokālika was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

sn6.9:1.3.verse: Then, late at night, the glorious independent divinity Tudu, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the mendicant Kokālika, and standing in the air he said to him,

sn6.9:1.4.verse: “Kokālika, have confidence in Sāriputta and Moggallāna,

sn6.9:1.8.verse: “Didn’t the Buddha declare you a non-returner? So what then are you doing back here?
