sn6.10:1.2.verse: Then the mendicant Kokālika went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

sn6.10:1.3.verse: “Sir, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have corrupt wishes. They’ve fallen under the sway of corrupt wishes.”

sn6.10:1.4.verse: When this was said, the Buddha said to Kokālika,

sn6.10:1.5.verse: “Don’t say that, Kokālika! Don’t say that, Kokālika!

sn6.10:1.6.verse: Have confidence in Sāriputta and Moggallāna, they’re good monks.”

sn6.10:1.7.verse: For a second time Kokālika said to the Buddha,

sn6.10:1.8.verse: “Despite my faith and trust in the Buddha, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have corrupt wishes. They’ve fallen under the sway of corrupt wishes.”

sn6.10:1.9.verse: For a second time, the Buddha said to Kokālika,

sn6.10:1.10.verse: “Don’t say that, Kokālika! Don’t say that, Kokālika!

sn6.10:1.11.verse: Have confidence in Sāriputta and Moggallāna, they’re good monks.”

sn6.10:1.12.verse: For a third time Kokālika said to the Buddha,

sn6.10:1.13.verse: “Despite my faith and trust in the Buddha, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have corrupt wishes. They’ve fallen under the sway of corrupt wishes.”

sn6.10:1.14.verse: For a third time, the Buddha said to Kokālika,

sn6.10:1.15.verse: “Don’t say that, Kokālika! Don’t say that, Kokālika!

sn6.10:1.16.verse: Have confidence in Sāriputta and Moggallāna, they’re good monks.”

sn6.10:2.1.verse: Then Kokālika rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

sn6.10:2.2.verse: Not long after he left his body erupted with boils the size of mustard seeds.

sn6.10:2.3.verse: The boils grew to the size of mung beans, then chickpeas, then jujube seeds, then jujubes, then myrobalans, then unripe wood-apples, then ripe wood-apples. Finally they burst open, and pus and blood oozed out.

sn6.10:2.4.verse: Then the mendicant Kokālika died of that illness.

sn6.10:2.5.verse: He was reborn in the Pink Lotus hell because of his resentment for Sāriputta and Moggallāna.

sn6.10:3.1.verse: Then, late at night, the glorious divinity Sahampati, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,

sn6.10:3.2.verse: “Sir, the mendicant Kokālika has passed away.

sn6.10:3.3.verse: He was reborn in the Pink Lotus hell because of his resentment for Sāriputta and Moggallāna.”

sn6.10:3.4.verse: That is what the divinity Sahampati said.

sn6.10:3.5.verse: Then he bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

sn6.10:4.1.verse: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha told the mendicants all that had happened.

sn6.10:5.1.verse: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,

sn6.10:5.2.verse: “Sir, how long is the lifespan in the Pink Lotus hell?”

sn6.10:5.5.verse: how many years, how many hundreds or thousands or hundreds of thousands of years it lasts.”

sn6.10:5.6.verse: “But sir, is it possible to give a simile?”

sn6.10:6.1.verse: “Suppose there was a Kosalan load of twenty packs of sesame seed. And at the end of every hundred years someone would remove a single seed from it.

sn6.10:6.2.verse: By this means the Kosalan load of twenty packs of sesame seed would run out faster than a single lifetime in the Abbuda hell.

sn6.10:6.3.verse: Now, twenty lifetimes in the Abbuda hell equal one lifetime in the Nirabbuda hell.

sn6.10:6.4.verse: Twenty lifetimes in the Nirabbuda hell equal one lifetime in the Ababa hell.

sn6.10:6.5.verse: Twenty lifetimes in the Ababa hell equal one lifetime in the Aṭaṭa hell.

sn6.10:6.6.verse: Twenty lifetimes in the Aṭaṭa hell equal one lifetime in the Ahaha hell.

sn6.10:6.7.verse: Twenty lifetimes in the Ahaha hell equal one lifetime in the Yellow Lotus hell.

sn6.10:6.8.verse: Twenty lifetimes in the Yellow Lotus hell equal one lifetime in the Fragrant Water Lily hell.

sn6.10:6.9.verse: Twenty lifetimes in the Fragrant Water Lily hell equal one lifetime in the Blue Water Lily hell.

sn6.10:6.10.verse: Twenty lifetimes in the Blue Water Lily hell equal one lifetime in the White Lotus hell.

sn6.10:6.11.verse: Twenty lifetimes in the White Lotus hell equal one lifetime in the Pink Lotus hell.

sn6.10:6.12.verse: The mendicant Kokālika has been reborn in the Pink Lotus hell because of his resentment for Sāriputta and Moggallāna.”

sn6.10:6.13.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn6.10:6.14.verse: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

sn6.10:7.2.verse: with an axe in their mouth.

sn6.10:7.3.verse: A fool cuts themselves with it

sn6.10:8.1.verse: When you praise someone worthy of criticism,

sn6.10:8.2.verse: or criticize someone worthy of praise,

sn6.10:8.3.verse: you choose a losing hand with your own mouth:

sn6.10:8.4.verse: you’ll never find happiness that way.

sn6.10:9.1.verse: A losing hand at dice is a trivial thing,

sn6.10:9.2.verse: if all you lose is your money

sn6.10:9.3.verse: and all you own, even yourself.

sn6.10:9.5.verse: is to hate the holy ones.

sn6.10:10.1.verse: For a hundred thousand times a hundred million,

sn6.10:10.2.verse: times five hundred and thirty-six times a thousand times ten million years

sn6.10:10.3.verse: a slanderer of noble ones goes to hell,

sn6.10:10.4.verse: having aimed bad words and thoughts at them.”

sn6.10:1.2.verse: Then the bhikkhu Kokālika approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said:

sn6.10:1.3.verse: “Venerable sir, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have evil wishes; they have come under the control of evil wishes. ”

sn6.10:1.4.verse: When this was said, the Blessed One said to the bhikkhu Kokālika:

sn6.10:1.5.verse: “Do not speak thus, Kokālika! Do not speak thus, Kokālika!

sn6.10:1.6.verse: Place confidence in Sāriputta and Moggallāna , Kokālika. Sāriputta and Moggallāna are well behaved. ”

sn6.10:1.7.verse: A second time the bhikkhu Kokālika said to the Blessed One:

sn6.10:1.8.verse: A second time the bhikkhu Kokalika said to the Blessed One:  “Venerable sir, although the Blessed One has my faith and trust, all the same I say that Sāriputta and Moggallāna have evil wishes; they have come under the control of evil wishes. ”

sn6.10:1.9.verse: And a second time the Blessed One said to the bhikkhu Kokālika:

sn6.10:1.10.verse: “Do not speak thus, Kokālika!… Sāriputta and Moggallāna are well behaved. ”

sn6.10:1.12.verse: A third time the bhikkhu Kokālika said to the Blessed One:

sn6.10:1.13.verse: “Venerable sir, although the Blessed One has my faith and trust, all the same I say that Sāriputta and Moggallāna have evil wishes; they have come under the control of evil wishes. ”

sn6.10:1.14.verse: And a third time the Blessed One said to the bhikkhu Kokālika:

sn6.10:1.15.verse: “Do not speak thus, Kokālika!… Sāriputta and Moggallāna are well behaved. ”

sn6.10:2.1.verse: Then the bhikkhu Kokālika rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, and departed, keeping him on his right.

sn6.10:2.2.verse: Not long after the bhikkhu Kokālika had left, his entire body became covered with boils the size of mustard seeds.

sn6.10:2.3.verse: These then grew to the size of mung beans; then to the size of chickpeas; then to the size of jujube stones; then to the size of jujube fruits; then to the size of myrobalans; then to the size of unripe beluva fruits; then to the size of ripe beluva fruits.

sn6.10:2.4.verse: When they had grown to the size of ripe beluva fruits, they burst open, exuding pus and blood. Then, on account of that illness,  the bhikkhu Kokālika died,

sn6.10:2.5.verse: and because he had harboured animosity towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna, after his death he was reborn in the Paduma hell.

sn6.10:3.1.verse: Then, when the night had advanced, Brahmā Sahampati, of stunning beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, stood to one side, and said to him:

sn6.10:3.2.verse: “Venerable sir,  the bhikkhu Kokālika has died,

sn6.10:3.3.verse: and because he harboured animosity towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna, after his death he has been reborn in the Paduma hell. ”

sn6.10:3.4.verse: This is what Brahmā Sahampati said.

sn6.10:3.5.verse: Having said this, he paid homage to the Blessed One and, keeping him on his right, he disappeared right there.

sn6.10:4.1.verse: Then, when the night had passed, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:

sn6.10:4.2.verse: “Bhikkhus, last night, when the night had advanced, Brahmā Sahampati approached me and said to me: … (as above) … Having said this, he paid homage to me and, keeping me on his right, he disappeared right there. ”

sn6.10:5.1.verse: When this was said, a certain bhikkhu said to the Blessed One:

sn6.10:5.2.verse: “Venerable sir, how long is the life span in the Paduma hell?”

sn6.10:5.3.verse: “The life span in the Paduma hell is long, bhikkhu.

sn6.10:5.4.verse: It is not easy to count it and say

sn6.10:5.5.verse: it is so many years, or so many hundreds of years, or so many thousands of years, or so many hundreds of thousands of years. ”

sn6.10:5.6.verse: “Then is it possible to give a simile, venerable sir?”

sn6.10:6.1.verse: Suppose, bhikkhu, there was a Kosalan cartload of twenty measures of sesamum seed. At the end of every hundred years a man would remove one seed from there.

sn6.10:6.2.verse: That Kosalan cartload of twenty measures of sesamum seed might by this effort be depleted and eliminated more quickly than a single Abbuda hell would go by.

sn6.10:6.3.verse: Twenty Abbuda hells are the equivalent of one Nirabbuda hell;

sn6.10:6.4.verse: twenty Nirabbuda hells are the equivalent of one Ababa hell;

sn6.10:6.5.verse: twenty Ababa hells are the equivalent of one Aṭaṭa hell;

sn6.10:6.6.verse: twenty Aṭaṭa hells are the equivalent of one Ahaha hell;

sn6.10:6.7.verse: twenty Ahaha hells are the equivalent of one Kumuda hell;

sn6.10:6.8.verse: twenty Kumuda hells are the equivalent of one Sogandhika hell;

sn6.10:6.9.verse: twenty Sogandhika hells are the equivalent of one Uppala hell;

sn6.10:6.10.verse: twenty Uppala hells are the equivalent of one Puṇḍarīka hell;

sn6.10:6.11.verse: and twenty Puṇḍarīka hells are the equivalent of one Paduma hell.

sn6.10:6.12.verse: Now, bhikkhu, the bhikkhu Kokālika has been reborn in the Paduma hell because he harboured animosity towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna. ”

sn6.10:6.13.verse: This is what the Blessed One said.

sn6.10:6.14.verse: Having said this, the Fortunate One, the Teacher, further said this:

sn6.10:10.4.verse: Having set evil speech and mind against them. ”

sn6.11:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the bank of the Serpentine River.

sn6.11:1.3.verse: Then, late at night, the glorious divinity Sanaṅkumāra, lighting up the entire Serpentine riverbank, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

sn6.11:1.4.verse: and spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

sn6.11:2.2.verse: who take clan as the standard.

sn6.11:2.3.verse: But one accomplished in knowledge and conduct

sn6.11:2.4.verse: is best among gods and humans.”

sn6.11:3.1.verse: That is what the divinity Sanaṅkumāra said,

sn6.11:3.3.verse: Then the divinity Sanaṅkumāra, knowing that the Teacher concurred, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

sn6.11:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha on the bank of the river Sappinī.

sn6.11:1.3.verse: Then, when the night had advanced, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra, of stunning beauty, illuminating the entire bank of the river Sappinī, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and stood to one side.

sn6.11:1.4.verse: Standing to one side, he recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn6.11:2.1.verse: “The khattiya is the best among people

sn6.11:2.2.verse: For those whose standard is the clan,

sn6.11:2.3.verse: But one accomplished in knowledge and conduct

sn6.11:2.4.verse: Is best among devas and humans. ”

sn6.11:3.1.verse: This is what Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra said.

sn6.11:3.3.verse: Then Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra, thinking, “The Teacher has approved of me, ” paid homage to the Blessed One and, keeping him on his right, he disappeared right there.

sn6.12:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain, not long after Devadatta had left.

sn6.12:1.3.verse: Then, late at night, the glorious divinity Sahampati, lighting up the entire Vulture’s Peak, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

sn6.12:1.4.verse: and spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

sn6.12:2.1.verse: “The banana plant is destroyed by its own fruit,

sn6.12:2.2.verse: as are the bamboo and the reed.

sn6.12:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha on Mount Vulture Peak not long after Devadatta had left.

sn6.12:1.3.verse: Then, when the night had advanced, Brahmā Sahampati, of stunning beauty, illuminating the entire Mount Vulture Peak, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and stood to one side.

sn6.12:1.4.verse: Standing to one side, referring to Devadatta, he recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn6.12:2.2.verse: To the plantain, bamboo, and reed,

sn6.12:2.3.verse: So do honours destroy the scoundrel,

sn6.12:2.4.verse: As its embryo destroys the mule.”

sn6.13:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Magadhans at Andhakavinda.

sn6.13:1.2.verse: Now at that time the Buddha was meditating in the open during the dark of night, while a gentle rain drizzled down.

sn6.13:1.3.verse: Then, late at night, the glorious divinity Sahampati, lighting up the entirety of Andhakavinda, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

sn6.13:1.4.verse: and recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:

sn6.13:2.2.verse: and practice to be released from fetters.

sn6.13:2.3.verse: If you don’t find enjoyment there,

sn6.13:2.4.verse: live in the Saṅgha, self-protected and mindful.

sn6.13:3.1.verse: Walking for alms from family to family,

sn6.13:3.2.verse: with senses guarded, alert and mindful.

sn6.13:3.4.verse: free of fear, freed in the fearless.

sn6.13:4.2.verse: where the lightning flashes and the heavens thunder

sn6.13:4.3.verse: in the dark of the night;

sn6.13:4.4.verse: there meditates a mendicant, free of goosebumps.

sn6.13:5.1.verse: For this is ever seen by me,

sn6.13:5.2.verse: it isn’t just the testament of hearsay.

sn6.13:5.4.verse: there are a thousand conquerors of Death.

sn6.13:6.1.verse: And of trainees, more than five hundred,

sn6.13:6.4.verse: freed from rebirth in the animal realm.

sn6.13:7.1.verse: And as for the rest of folk

sn6.13:7.2.verse: who I think have shared in merit—

sn6.13:1.1.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Magadhans at Andhakavinda.

sn6.13:1.2.verse: Now on that occasion the Blessed One was sitting out in the open in the thick darkness of the night while it was drizzling.

sn6.13:1.3.verse: Then, when the night had advanced, Brahmā Sahampati … approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and stood to one side.

sn6.13:1.4.verse: Standing to one side, he recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn6.13:2.2.verse: Practise for release from the fetters.

sn6.13:2.3.verse: But if one does not find delight there,

sn6.13:2.4.verse: Guarded and mindful, dwell in the Saṅgha.

sn6.13:3.1.verse: “Walking for alms from family to family,

sn6.13:3.3.verse: One should resort to remote lodgings,

sn6.13:3.4.verse: Freed from fear, liberated in the fearless.

sn6.13:4.2.verse: Where lightning flashes and the sky thunders,

sn6.13:4.3.verse: In the thick darkness of the night

sn6.13:4.4.verse: There sits a bhikkhu devoid of terror.

sn6.13:5.1.verse: “For this has actually been seen by me,

sn6.13:5.4.verse: A thousand have left Death behind.

sn6.13:6.2.verse: And ten times a tenfold ten:

sn6.13:6.4.verse: Never returning to the animal realm.

sn6.13:7.1.verse: “As for the other people who remain—

sn6.13:7.2.verse: Who, to my mind, partake of merit—

sn6.14:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī.

sn6.14:2.1.verse: “Once upon a time, mendicants, there was a king named Aruṇavā.

sn6.14:2.2.verse: He had a capital named Aruṇavatī.

sn6.14:2.3.verse: Sikhī the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha lived supported by Aruṇavatī.

sn6.14:2.4.verse: Sikhī had a fine pair of chief disciples named Abhibhū and Sambhava.

sn6.14:2.5.verse: Then the Buddha Sikhī addressed the mendicant Abhibhū,

sn6.14:2.6.verse: ‘Come, brahmin, let’s go to one of the realms of divinity until it’s time for our meal.’

sn6.14:2.8.verse: Then, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, they vanished from Aruṇavatī and appeared in that realm of divinity.

sn6.14:3.1.verse: Then the Buddha Sikhī addressed the mendicant Abhibhū,

sn6.14:3.2.verse: ‘Brahmin, teach the Dhamma as you feel inspired for that divinity, his assembly, and the members of his retinue.’

sn6.14:3.3.verse: ‘Yes, sir,’ replied Abhibhū. Then he educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired them with a Dhamma talk.

sn6.14:3.4.verse: But the Divinity, his assembly, and his retinue complained, grumbled, and objected,

sn6.14:3.5.verse: ‘Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing! How on earth can a disciple teach Dhamma in the presence of the Teacher?’

sn6.14:4.1.verse: Then the Buddha Sikhī addressed the mendicant Abhibhū,

sn6.14:4.2.verse: ‘Brahmin, the Divinity, his assembly, and his retinue are complaining

sn6.14:4.3.verse: that a disciple teaches Dhamma in the presence of the Teacher.

sn6.14:4.4.verse: Well then, brahmin, stir them up even more!’

sn6.14:4.5.verse: ‘Yes, sir,’ replied Abhibhū. Then he taught Dhamma with his body visible; with his body invisible; with the lower half visible and the upper half invisible; and with the upper half visible and the lower half invisible.

sn6.14:4.6.verse: And the Divinity, his assembly, and his retinue, their minds full of wonder and amazement, thought,

sn6.14:4.7.verse: ‘Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing! The ascetic has such psychic power and might!’

sn6.14:5.1.verse: Then Abhibhū said to the Buddha Sikhī,

sn6.14:5.2.verse: ‘Sir, I recall having said this in the middle of the Saṅgha:

sn6.14:5.3.verse: “Standing in the realm of divinity, I can make my voice heard throughout the thousandfold galaxy.”’

sn6.14:5.4.verse: ‘Now is the time, brahmin! Now is the time, brahmin!

sn6.14:5.5.verse: Standing in the realm of divinity, make your voice heard throughout the thousandfold galaxy.’

sn6.14:5.6.verse: ‘Yes, sir,’ replied Abhibhū. Standing in the realm of divinity, he spoke this verse:

sn6.14:6.2.verse: Devote yourselves to the teachings of the Buddha!

sn6.14:6.4.verse: as an elephant a hut of reeds.

sn6.14:7.4.verse: will make an end of suffering.’

sn6.14:8.1.verse: Having inspired that divinity, his assembly, and his retinue with a sense of awe,

sn6.14:8.2.verse: as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, Sikhī and Abhibhū vanished from that realm of divinity and appeared in Aruṇavatī.

sn6.14:8.3.verse: Then the Buddha Sikhī addressed the mendicants,

sn6.14:8.4.verse: ‘Mendicants, did you hear the mendicant Abhibhū speaking a verse while standing in a realm of divinity?’

sn6.14:9.2.verse: Devote yourselves to the teachings of the Buddha!

sn6.14:9.4.verse: as an elephant a hut of reeds.

sn6.14:10.4.verse: will make an end of suffering.”

sn6.14:11.3.verse: It’s good that you heard the mendicant Abhibhū speaking this verse while standing in a realm of divinity.’”

sn6.14:12.1.verse: That is what the Buddha said. Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

sn6.14:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī …

sn6.14:1.3.verse: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:

sn6.14:2.1.verse: “Bhikkhus, once in the past there was a king named Aruṇavā

sn6.14:2.3.verse: The Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, dwelt in dependence on the capital Aruṇavatī.

sn6.14:2.4.verse: The chief pair of disciples of the Blessed One Sikhī were named Abhibhū and Sambhava, an excellent pair.

sn6.14:2.5.verse: Then the Blessed One Sikhī addressed the bhikkhu Abhibhū:

sn6.14:2.6.verse: ‘Come, brahmin, let us go to a certain brahmā world until it is time for our meal. ’

sn6.14:2.7.verse: ‘Yes, venerable sir, ’ the bhikkhu Abhibhū replied.

sn6.14:2.8.verse: “Then, bhikkhus, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, so the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and the bhikkhu Abhibhū disappeared from the capital Aruṇavatī and reappeared in that brahmā world.

sn6.14:3.1.verse: Then the Blessed One Sikhī addressed the bhikkhu Abhibhū thus:

sn6.14:3.2.verse: ‘Give a Dhamma talk, brahmin, to Brahmā and to Brahmā’s retinue and to Brahmā’s assembly. ’

sn6.14:3.3.verse: ‘Yes, venerable sir, ’ the bhikkhu Abhibhū replied. Then, by means of a Dhamma talk, he instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened Brahmā and Brahmā’s retinue and Brahmā’s assembly.

sn6.14:3.4.verse: Thereupon Brahmā and Brahmā’s retinue and  Brahmā’s assembly found fault with this, grumbled, and complained about it, saying:

sn6.14:3.5.verse: ‘It is wonderful indeed, sir! It is amazing indeed, sir! How  can a disciple teach the Dhamma in the very presence of the Teacher?’

sn6.14:4.1.verse: “Then , bhikkhus , the Blessed One Sikhī addressed the bhikkhu Abhibhū thus:

sn6.14:4.2.verse: ‘Brahmin, Brahmā and Brahmā’s retinue and Brahmā’s assembly deplore this, saying,

sn6.14:4.3.verse: “It is wonderful indeed, sir! It is amazing indeed, sir! How can a disciple teach the Dhamma in the very presence of the Teacher?”

sn6.14:4.4.verse: Well then, brahmin, stir up an even greater sense of urgency in Brahmā and in Brahmā’s retinue and in Brahmā’s assembly. ’

sn6.14:4.5.verse: ‘Yes, venerable sir, ’ the bhikkhu Abhibhū replied. Then he taught the Dhamma with his body visible, and with his body invisible, and with the lower half of his body visible and the upper half invisible, and with the upper half of his body visible and the lower half invisible.

sn6.14:4.6.verse: Thereupon, bhikkhus, Brahmā and Brahmā’s retinue and Brahmā’s assembly were struck with wonder and amazement, saying:

sn6.14:4.7.verse: ‘It is wonderful indeed, sir! It is amazing indeed, sir! How the ascetic has such great power and might!’

sn6.14:5.1.verse: “Then, bhikkhus, the bhikkhu Abhibhū said to the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One:

sn6.14:5.2.verse: ‘I recall, venerable sir, having made such a statement as this in the midst of the Bhikkhu Saṅgha:

sn6.14:5.3.verse: “Friends, while standing in the brahmā world I can make my voice heard throughout the thousandfold world system. ’”

sn6.14:5.4.verse: ‘Now is the time for that, brahmin! Now is the time for that, brahmin!

sn6.14:5.5.verse: While standing in the brahmā world you should make your voice heard throughout the thousandfold world system. ’

sn6.14:5.6.verse: ‘Yes, venerable sir, ’ the bhikkhu Abhibhū replied. Then, while standing in the brahmā world, he recited these verses :

sn6.14:6.2.verse: Exert yourself in the Buddha’s Teaching.

sn6.14:6.3.verse: Sweep away the army of Death

sn6.14:6.4.verse: As an elephant does a hut of reeds.

sn6.14:7.3.verse: Having abandoned the wandering on in birth,

sn6.14:7.4.verse: Will make an end to suffering. ’

sn6.14:8.1.verse: “Then, bhikkhus, having stirred up a sense of urgency in Brahmā and in Brahmā’s retinue and in Brahmā’s assembly,

sn6.14:8.2.verse: just as quickly as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and the bhikkhu Abhibhū disappeared from that brahmā world and reappeared in the capital Aruṇavatī.

sn6.14:8.3.verse: Then the Blessed One Sikhī addressed the bhikkhus thus:

sn6.14:8.4.verse: ‘Bhikkhus, did you hear the verses that the bhikkhu Abhibhū recited while he was standing in the brahmā world?’

sn6.14:8.6.verse: ‘What were the verses that you heard, bhikkhus?’

sn6.14:8.7.verse: ‘We heard the verses of the bhikkhu Abhibhū thus:

sn6.14:10.4.verse: Will make an end to suffering. ”

sn6.14:11.1.verse: Such were the verses that we heard the bhikkhu Abhibhū recite while he was standing in the brahmā world. ’

sn6.14:11.3.verse: It is good that you heard the verses that the bhikkhu Abhibhū recited while he was standing in the brahmā world. ’”

sn6.14:12.1.verse: This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

sn6.15:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying between a pair of sal trees in the sal forest of the Mallas at Upavattana near Kusinārā at the time of his full extinguishment.

sn6.15:1.2.verse: Then the Buddha said to the mendicants:

sn6.15:1.3.verse: “Come now, mendicants, I say to you all:

sn6.15:1.5.verse: These were the Realized One’s last words.

sn6.15:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha entered the first absorption. Emerging from that, he entered the second absorption. Emerging from that, he successively entered into and emerged from the third absorption, the fourth absorption, the dimension of infinite space, the dimension of infinite consciousness, the dimension of nothingness, and the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. Then he entered the cessation of perception and feeling.

sn6.15:3.1.verse: Then he emerged from the cessation of perception and feeling and entered the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. Emerging from that, he successively entered into and emerged from the dimension of nothingness, the dimension of infinite consciousness, the dimension of infinite space, the fourth absorption, the third absorption, the second absorption, and the first absorption. Emerging from that, he successively entered into and emerged from the second absorption and the third absorption. Then he entered the fourth absorption. Emerging from that the Buddha immediately became fully extinguished.

sn6.15:3.2.verse: When the Buddha was fully quenched, along with the full extinguishment, the divinity Sahampati spoke this verse:

sn6.15:4.2.verse: must lay down this bag of bones.

sn6.15:4.3.verse: For even a Teacher such as this,

sn6.15:4.5.verse: the Realized One, attained to power,

sn6.15:5.1.verse: When the Buddha was fully quenched, Sakka, lord of gods, spoke this verse:

sn6.15:6.2.verse: their nature is to rise and fall;

sn6.15:7.1.verse: When the Buddha was fully quenched, Venerable Ānanda spoke this verse:

sn6.15:8.3.verse: When the Buddha, endowed with all fine qualities,

sn6.15:9.1.verse: When the Buddha was fully quenched, Venerable Anuruddha spoke this verse:

sn6.15:10.2.verse: for the unaffected one of steady heart.

sn6.15:10.4.verse: the Clear-eyed One was fully quenched.

sn6.15:11.1.verse: He put up with painful feelings

sn6.15:11.4.verse: was like the extinguishing of a lamp.”

sn6.15:12.5.verse: The Linked Discourses on the Divinity are complete.

sn6.15:1.1.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Kusinārā in Upavattana, the sal tree grove of the Mallans, between the twin sal trees, on the occasion of his final Nibbāna.

sn6.15:1.2.verse: Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:

sn6.15:1.4.verse: Formations are bound to vanish. Strive to attain the goal by diligence. ”

sn6.15:1.5.verse: This was the last utterance of the Tathāgata.

sn6.15:2.1.verse: Then the Blessed One attained the first jhāna. Having emerged from the first jhāna, he attained the second jhāna. Having emerged from the second jhāna, he attained the third jhāna. Having emerged from the third jhāna, he attained the fourth jhāna. Having emerged from the fourth jhāna, he attained the base of the infinity of space. Having emerged from the base of the infinity of space, he attained the base of the infinity of consciousness. Having emerged from the base of the infinity of consciousness, he attained the base of nothingness. Having emerged from the base of nothingness, he attained the base of neither-perception-nor-nonperception. Having emerged from the base of neither-perception-nor-nonperception, he attained the cessation of perception and feeling.

sn6.15:3.1.verse: Having emerged from the cessation of perception and feeling, he attained the base of neither-perception-nor-nonperception. Having emerged from the base of neither-perception-nor-nonperception, he attained the base of nothingness. Having emerged from the base of nothingness, he attained the base of the infinity of consciousness. Having emerged from the base of the infinity of consciousness, he attained the base of the infinity of space. Having emerged from the base of the infinity of space, he attained the fourth jhāna. Having emerged from the fourth jhāna, he attained the third jhāna. Having emerged from the third jhāna, he attained the second jhāna. Having emerged from the second jhāna, he attained the first jhāna. Having emerged from the first jhāna, he attained the second jhāna. Having emerged from the second jhāna, he attained the third jhāna. Having emerged from the third jhāna, he attained the fourth jhāna. Having emerged from the fourth jhāna, immediately after this the Blessed One attained final Nibbāna.

sn6.15:3.2.verse: When the Blessed One attained final Nibbāna, simultaneously with his final Nibbāna Brahmā Sahampati recited this verse:

sn6.15:4.2.verse: the body. All beings in the world.

sn6.15:4.3.verse: Since such a one as the Teacher,

sn6.15:4.4.verse: The peerless person in the world,

sn6.15:4.5.verse: The Tathāgata endowed with the powers,

sn6.15:4.6.verse: The Buddha, has attained final Nibbāna. ”

sn6.15:5.1.verse: When the Blessed One attained final Nibbāna, simultaneously with his final Nibbāna Sakka, lord of the devas, recited this verse:

sn6.15:6.2.verse: Their nature is to arise and vanish.

sn6.15:7.1.verse: When the Blessed One attained final Nibbāna, simultaneously with his final Nibbāna the Venerable Ānanda recited this verse:

sn6.15:8.3.verse: When the one perfect in all excellent qualities,

sn6.15:9.1.verse: When the Blessed One attained final Nibbāna, simultaneously with his final Nibbāna the Venerable Anuruddha recited these verses:

sn6.15:10.2.verse: In the Stable One of steady mind

sn6.15:10.4.verse: The One with Vision attained final Nibbāna.

sn6.15:11.3.verse: Like the quenching of a lamp

sn6.15:11.4.verse: Was the deliverance of the mind. ”

sn7.1:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

sn7.1:1.3.verse: Now at that time the wife of a certain brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, a brahmin lady named Dhanañjānī, was devoted to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.

sn7.1:1.4.verse: Once, while she was bringing her husband his meal, she tripped and expressed this heartfelt sentiment three times:

sn7.1:2.1.verse: “Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!

sn7.1:3.1.verse: Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!

sn7.1:4.1.verse: Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!”

sn7.1:5.1.verse: When she said this, the brahmin said to Dhanañjānī:

sn7.1:5.2.verse: “That’d be right. For the slightest thing this lowlife woman praises that shaven ascetic.

sn7.1:5.3.verse: Right now, lowlife woman, I’m going to refute your teacher’s doctrine!”

sn7.1:5.4.verse: “Brahmin, I don’t see anyone in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—who can refute the doctrine of the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

sn7.1:5.5.verse: But anyway, you should go. When you’ve gone you’ll understand.”

sn7.1:6.1.verse: Then the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, angry and upset, went to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

sn7.1:6.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side,

sn7.1:6.3.verse: and addressed the Buddha in verse:

sn7.1:7.1.verse: “When what is slain do you sleep at ease?

sn7.1:7.2.verse: When what is slain is there no sorrow?

sn7.1:8.1.verse: “When anger’s slain you sleep at ease.

sn7.1:8.2.verse: When anger’s slain there is no sorrow.

sn7.1:8.4.verse: and a sweet tip, O brahmin.

sn7.1:8.5.verse: The noble ones praise its killing,

sn7.1:8.6.verse: for when it’s slain there is no sorrow.”

sn7.1:9.1.verse: When he said this, the brahmin said to the Buddha,

sn7.1:9.3.verse: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

sn7.1:9.4.verse: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

sn7.1:9.5.verse: May I receive the going forth, the ordination in the worthy Gotama’s presence?”

sn7.1:10.1.verse: And the brahmin received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

sn7.1:10.2.verse: Not long after his ordination, Venerable Bhāradvāja, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

sn7.1:10.3.verse: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

sn7.1:10.4.verse: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.

sn7.1:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary.

sn7.1:1.3.verse: Now on that occasion the wife of a certain brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, a brahmin lady named Dhanañjānī, had full confidence in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha.

sn7.1:1.4.verse: Once, while the brahmin lady Dhanañjānī was bringing the brahmin his meal, she stumbled, whereupon she uttered three times this inspired utterance:

sn7.1:2.1.verse: “Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One!

sn7.1:3.1.verse: Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One!

sn7.1:4.1.verse: Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One!”

sn7.1:5.1.verse: When this was said, the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan said to her:

sn7.1:5.2.verse: “For the slightest thing this wretched woman  spouts out praise of that shaveling ascetic!

sn7.1:5.3.verse: Now, wretched woman, I am going to refute the doctrine of that teacher of yours. ʺ

sn7.1:5.4.verse: “I do not see anyone, brahmin, in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, who could refute the doctrine of the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

sn7.1:5.5.verse: But go, brahmin. When you have gone, you will understand. ”

sn7.1:6.1.verse: Then the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, angry and displeased, approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.

sn7.1:6.2.verse: When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side,

sn7.1:6.3.verse: and addressed the Blessed One in verse:

sn7.1:7.1.verse: “Having slain what does one sleep soundly?

sn7.1:7.2.verse: Having slain what does one not sorrow?

sn7.1:7.4.verse: O Gotama, Whose killing you approve?”

sn7.1:8.1.verse: [The Blessed One: ]  “Having slain anger, one sleeps soundly;

sn7.1:8.2.verse: Having slain anger, one does not sorrow;

sn7.1:8.4.verse: O brahmin, With its poisoned root and honeyed tip:

sn7.1:8.5.verse: This is the killing the noble ones praise,

sn7.1:8.6.verse: For having slain that, one does not sorrow. ”

sn7.1:9.1.verse: When this was said, the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan said to the Blessed One:

sn7.1:9.3.verse: The Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama, as though he were turning upright what had been turned upside down, revealing what was hidden, showing the way to one who was lost, or holding up a lamp in the dark for those with eyesight to see forms.

sn7.1:9.4.verse: I go for refuge to Master Gotama, and to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha.

sn7.1:9.5.verse: May I receive the going forth under Master Gotama, may I receive the higher ordination?”

sn7.1:10.1.verse: Then the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan received the going forth under the Blessed One, he received the higher ordination.

sn7.1:10.2.verse: And soon, not long after his higher ordination, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, the Venerable Bhāradvāja, by realizing it for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life entered and dwelt in that unsurpassed goal of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness.

sn7.1:10.3.verse: He directly knew: “Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being. ”

sn7.1:10.4.verse: And the Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the arahants.

sn7.2:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

sn7.2:1.2.verse: The brahmin Bhāradvāja the Rude heard a rumor that

sn7.2:2.1.verse: a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan had gone forth from the lay life to homelessness in the presence of the ascetic Gotama. Angry and displeased he went to the Buddha and abused and insulted him with rude, harsh words. When he had spoken, the Buddha said to him:

sn7.2:2.3.verse: Do friends and colleagues, relatives and kin, and guests still come to visit you?”

sn7.2:2.5.verse: “Do you then serve them with fresh and cooked foods and savories?”

sn7.2:2.7.verse: “But if they don’t accept it, brahmin, who does it belong to?”

sn7.2:2.8.verse: “In that case it still belongs to me.”

sn7.2:2.9.verse: “In the same way, brahmin, when you abuse, harass, and attack us who do not abuse, harass, and attack, we don’t accept it.

sn7.2:2.10.verse: It still belongs to you, brahmin,

sn7.2:3.1.verse: Someone who, when abused, harassed, and attacked, abuses, harasses, and attacks in return is said to eat the food and have a reaction to it.

sn7.2:3.2.verse: But we neither eat your food nor do we have a reaction to it.

sn7.2:3.3.verse: It still belongs to you, brahmin,

sn7.2:3.5.verse: “The king and his retinue believe of the worthy Gotama,

sn7.2:3.6.verse: ‘the ascetic Gotama is a perfected one’.

sn7.2:3.7.verse: And yet he still gets angry.”

sn7.2:4.1.verse: “Whence anger for one free of anger,

sn7.2:5.1.verse: When you get angry at an angry person

sn7.2:5.2.verse: you just make things worse for yourself.

sn7.2:5.3.verse: When you don’t get angry at an angry person

sn7.2:5.4.verse: you win a battle hard to win.

sn7.2:6.1.verse: When you know that the other is angry,

sn7.2:6.2.verse: you act for the good of both

sn7.2:6.4.verse: if you’re mindful and stay calm.

sn7.2:8.1.verse: When he had spoken, Bhāradvāja the Rude said to the Buddha,

sn7.2:8.3.verse: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

sn7.2:8.4.verse: Sir, may I receive the going forth, the ordination in the worthy Gotama’s presence?”

sn7.2:9.1.verse: And the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Rude received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

sn7.2:9.2.verse: Not long after his ordination, Venerable Bhāradvāja the Rude, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

sn7.2:9.3.verse: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

sn7.2:9.4.verse: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.

sn7.2:1.1.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary.

sn7.2:1.2.verse: The brahmin Akkosaka Bhāradvāja, Bhāradvāja the Abusive, heard:

sn7.2:2.1.verse: “It is said that the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan has gone forth from the household life into homelessness under the ascetic Gotama. ” Angry and displeased, he approached the Blessed One and  abused and reviled him with rude, harsh words.

sn7.2:2.2.verse: When he had finished speaking, the Blessed One said to him: “What do you think, brahmin?

sn7.2:2.3.verse: Do your friends and colleagues, kinsmen and relatives, as well as guests come to visit you?”

sn7.2:2.4.verse: “Sometimes they come to visit, Master Gotama. ”

sn7.2:2.5.verse: “Do you then offer them some food or a meal or a snack?”

sn7.2:2.7.verse: “But if they do not accept it from you, then to whom does the food belong?”

sn7.2:2.8.verse: “If they do not accept it from me, then the food still belongs to us. ”

sn7.2:2.9.verse: “So too, brahmin, we—who do not abuse anyone, who do not scold anyone, who do not rail against anyone—refuse to accept from you the abuse and scolding and tirade you let loose at us.

sn7.2:2.10.verse: It still belongs to you, brahmin!

sn7.2:2.11.verse: It still belongs to you, brahmin!

sn7.2:3.1.verse: “Brahmin, one who abuses his own abuser, who scolds the one who scolds him, who rails against the one who rails at him—he is said to partake of the meal, to enter upon an exchange.

sn7.2:3.2.verse: But we do not partake of your meal; we do not enter upon an exchange.

sn7.2:3.3.verse: It still belongs to you, brahmin!

sn7.2:3.4.verse: It still belongs to you, brahmin!”

sn7.2:3.5.verse: “The king and his retinue understand the ascetic  yet Master Gotama still gets angry.

sn7.2:4.1.verse: [The Blessed One: ]  “How can anger arise in one who is angerless,

sn7.2:4.2.verse: In the tamed one of righteous living,

sn7.2:4.3.verse: In one liberated by perfect knowledge,

sn7.2:4.4.verse: In the Stable One who abides in peace?

sn7.2:5.1.verse: Thereby makes things worse for himself.

sn7.2:5.2.verse: “One who repays an angry man with anger

sn7.2:5.3.verse: Not repaying an angry man with anger,

sn7.2:5.4.verse: One wins a battle hard to win.

sn7.2:6.1.verse: “He practises for the welfare of both:

sn7.2:6.3.verse: When, knowing that his foe is angry,

sn7.2:7.1.verse: “When he achieves the cure of both:

sn7.2:7.3.verse: The people who consider him a fool

sn7.2:8.1.verse: When this was said, the brahmin Akkosaka Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One:

sn7.2:8.3.verse: I go for refuge to Master Gotama, and to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha.

sn7.2:8.4.verse: May I receive the going forth under Master Gotama, may I receive the higher ordination?”

sn7.2:9.1.verse: Then the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan received the going forth under the Blessed One, he received the higher ordination.

sn7.2:9.2.verse: And soon, not long after his higher ordination, dwelling alone …

sn7.2:9.4.verse: the Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the arahants.

sn7.4:1.1.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary.

sn7.4:1.3.verse: “It is said that the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan has gone forth from the household life into homelessness under the ascetic Gotama. ” Angry and displeased, he approached the Blessed One and silently stood to one side.

sn7.4:1.4.verse: Then the Blessed One, having known with his own mind the reflection in the brahmin Bilaṅgika Bhāradvāja’s mind, addressed him in verse:

sn7.4:2.3.verse: The evil falls back on the fool himself

sn7.4:2.4.verse: Like fine dust thrown against the wind. ”

sn7.4:3.1.verse: When this was said, the brahmin Bilaṅgika Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One:

sn7.4:3.4.verse: And the Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the arahants.

sn7.5:1.2.verse: Then the brahmin Ahiṃsaka Bhāradvāja, Bhāradvāja the Harmless, approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk,

sn7.5:1.3.verse: he sat down to one side  and said to the Blessed One:

sn7.5:1.4.verse: “I am Ahiṃsaka the Harmless, Master Gotama. I am Ahiṃsaka the Harmless, Master Gotama. ”

sn7.5:2.1.verse: [The Blessed One: ]   “If one were as one’s name implies

sn7.5:2.2.verse: You would be a harmless one.

sn7.5:2.4.verse: But it is one who does no harm at all  or mind,

sn7.5:2.5.verse: Who really is a harmless one

sn7.5:2.6.verse: As he does not harm others. ”

sn7.5:3.1.verse: When this was said, the brahmin Ahiṃsaka Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One:

sn7.5:3.4.verse: And the Venerable Ahiṃsaka Bhāradvāja became one of the arahants.

sn7.6:1.3.verse: When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side

sn7.6:2.3.verse: I ask you this, O Gotama,

sn7.6:3.1.verse: [The Blessed One: ]  “A man established on virtue, wise,

sn7.6:4.2.verse: Along with ignorance have been expunged,

sn7.6:5.3.verse: And also impingement and perception of form:

sn7.7:1.2.verse: Then the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Pure went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

sn7.7:1.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side,

sn7.7:1.4.verse: and spoke this verse in his presence:

sn7.7:2.1.verse: “No brahmin in the world is ever purified

sn7.7:2.2.verse: even though he’s ethical and mortifies himself.

sn7.7:2.3.verse: But one accomplished in knowledge and conduct

sn7.7:2.4.verse: is purified, not these other commoners.”

sn7.7:3.3.verse: if they’re filthy and corrupt within,

sn7.7:4.1.verse: Regardless of whether you’re an aristocrat,

sn7.7:4.2.verse: a brahmin, peasant, menial, or a corpse-worker or scavenger—

sn7.7:4.6.verse: Know that for a fact, brahmin.”

sn7.7:5.1.verse: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Pure said to the Buddha,

sn7.7:5.3.verse: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.

sn7.7:1.2.verse: Then the brahmin Suddhika Bhāradvāja approached the Blessed One  and exchanged greetings with him.

sn7.7:1.3.verse: When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk,

sn7.7:1.4.verse: he sat down to one side  and recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn7.7:2.1.verse: “In the world no brahmin is ever purified

sn7.7:2.2.verse: Though he be virtuous and austere in practice;

sn7.7:2.3.verse: One accomplished in knowledge and conduct is purified,

sn7.7:2.4.verse: Not the others, the common folk. ”

sn7.7:3.1.verse: [The Blessed One: ]  “Even though one mutters many chants,

sn7.7:3.2.verse: One does not become a brahmin by birth

sn7.7:3.3.verse: If one is rotten within and defiled,

sn7.7:4.3.verse: If one is energetic and resolute,

sn7.7:4.6.verse: Know, O brahmin, that this is so. ”

sn7.7:5.1.verse: When this was said, the brahmin Suddhika Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One:

sn7.7:5.3.verse: And the Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the arahants.

sn7.8:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

sn7.8:1.2.verse: Now at that time ghee and milk-rice had been set out for the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Fire-Worshiper, who thought,

sn7.8:1.3.verse: “I will serve the sacred flame! I will perform the fire sacrifice!”

sn7.8:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha for alms.

sn7.8:2.2.verse: Wandering indiscriminately for almsfood in Rājagaha, he approached Bhāradvāja the Fire-Worshiper’s home and stood to one side.

sn7.8:2.3.verse: Bhāradvāja the Fire-Worshiper saw him standing for alms

sn7.8:3.1.verse: “One who’s accomplished in the three knowledges,

sn7.8:3.2.verse: of good birth and ample learning,

sn7.8:4.3.verse: if they’re filthy and corrupt within,

sn7.8:4.4.verse: with a following gained by fawning.

sn7.8:5.1.verse: One who knows their past lives,

sn7.8:5.2.verse: sees heaven and places of loss,

sn7.8:5.3.verse: and has attained the ending of rebirth,

sn7.8:5.4.verse: is a sage of perfect insight.

sn7.8:6.2.verse: a brahmin is a master of the three knowledges.

sn7.8:7.2.verse: The worthy one is a brahmin.”

sn7.8:8.1.verse: “Food enchanted by a verse isn’t fit for me to eat.

sn7.8:8.2.verse: That’s not the principle of those who see, brahmin.

sn7.8:8.3.verse: The Buddhas cast aside things enchanted with verses.

sn7.8:8.4.verse: Since there is such a principle, brahmin, that’s how they live.

sn7.8:9.1.verse: Serve with other food and drink

sn7.8:9.2.verse: the consummate one, the great seer,

sn7.8:9.3.verse: with defilements ended and remorse stilled.

sn7.8:9.4.verse: For he is the field for the seeker of merit.”

sn7.8:10.1.verse: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Fire-Worshiper said to the Buddha,

sn7.8:10.3.verse: And Venerable Bhāradvāja the Fire-Worshiper became one of the perfected.

sn7.8:1.1.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary.

sn7.8:1.2.verse: Now on that occasion milk-rice with ghee had been set out for the brahmin Aggika Bhāradvāja, who had thought:

sn7.8:1.3.verse: “I will offer a fire sacrifice, I will perform the fire oblation. ”

sn7.8:2.1.verse: Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed and, taking bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha for alms.

sn7.8:2.2.verse: Walking for alms on uninterrupted alms round in Rājagaha, the Blessed One approached the residence of the brahmin Aggika Bhāradvāja and stood to one side.

sn7.8:2.3.verse: The brahmin Aggika Bhāradvāja saw the Blessed One standing for alms and addressed him in verse:

sn7.8:3.2.verse: Of proper birth, of ample learning,

sn7.8:3.4.verse: Might partake of this milk-rice meal. ”

sn7.8:4.1.verse: [The Blessed One: ]  “Even though one mutters many chants,

sn7.8:4.2.verse: One does not become a brahmin by birth

sn7.8:4.3.verse: If one is rotten within and defiled,

sn7.8:4.4.verse: With followers gained by fraudulent means.

sn7.8:5.1.verse: “One who has known his past abodes,

sn7.8:5.2.verse: Who sees heaven and the plane of woe,

sn7.8:5.3.verse: Who has reached the destruction of birth,

sn7.8:5.4.verse: A sage consummate in direct knowledge:

sn7.8:6.1.verse: “By means of these three kinds of knowledge

sn7.8:6.3.verse: This one accomplished in knowledge and conduct

sn7.8:6.4.verse: Might partake of this milk-rice meal. ”

sn7.8:7.1.verse: [The brahmin Aggika Bhāradvāja: ] “Let Master Gotama eat.

sn7.8:8.1.verse: [The Blessed One: ]  “Food over which verses have been sung, is not fit to be eaten by me.

sn7.8:8.2.verse: Observed by those who see. This, brahmin, is not the principle

sn7.8:8.3.verse: The Enlightened Ones reject such food over which verses have been sung.

sn7.8:8.4.verse: As such a principle exists, O brahmin, this is their rule of conduct.

sn7.8:9.2.verse: With taints destroyed and remorse stilled,

sn7.8:9.3.verse: Serve with other food and drink.

sn7.8:9.4.verse: For he is the field for one seeking merit. ”

sn7.8:10.1.verse: When this was said, the brahmin Aggika Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One:

sn7.8:10.3.verse: And the Venerable Aggika Bhāradvāja became one of the arahants.

sn7.9:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the Kosalan lands on the bank of the Sundarikā River.

sn7.9:1.2.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā was serving the sacred flame and performing the fire sacrifice on the bank of the Sundarikā.

sn7.9:1.3.verse: Then he rose from his seat and surveyed the four quarters, wondering,

sn7.9:1.4.verse: “Now who might eat the leftovers of this oblation?”

sn7.9:1.5.verse: He saw the Buddha meditating at the root of a certain tree with his robe pulled over his head.

sn7.9:1.6.verse: Taking the leftovers of the oblation in his left hand and a pitcher in the right he approached the Buddha.

sn7.9:1.7.verse: When he heard Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā’s footsteps the Buddha uncovered his head.

sn7.9:1.8.verse: Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā thought, “This man is shaven, he is shaven!” And he wanted to turn back.

sn7.9:1.11.verse: Why don’t I go to him and ask about his birth?”

sn7.9:2.1.verse: Then the brahmin Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā went up to the Buddha, and said to him,

sn7.9:3.1.verse: “Don’t ask about birth, ask about conduct;

sn7.9:3.2.verse: for the fire of Jātaveda is born from sticks.

sn7.9:3.3.verse: A steadfast sage, even though from a low class family,

sn7.9:3.4.verse: is a thoroughbred checked by conscience.

sn7.9:4.1.verse: Tamed by truth, fulfilled by taming,

sn7.9:4.2.verse: a complete knowledge master who has completed the spiritual journey—

sn7.9:4.3.verse: that’s who a sacrificer should woo,

sn7.9:4.4.verse: and offer a timely oblation to one worthy of a religious donation.”

sn7.9:5.1.verse: “My sacrificial offering must have been well performed,

sn7.9:5.2.verse: since I have met such a knowledge master!

sn7.9:5.3.verse: It’s because I’d never met anyone like you

sn7.9:5.4.verse: that others ate the leftover oblation.

sn7.9:6.2.verse: The worthy one is a brahmin.”

sn7.9:7.1.verse: “Food enchanted by a verse isn’t fit for me to eat.

sn7.9:7.2.verse: That’s not the principle of those who see, brahmin.

sn7.9:7.3.verse: The Buddhas cast aside things enchanted with verses.

sn7.9:7.4.verse: Since there is such a principle, brahmin, that’s how they live.

sn7.9:8.1.verse: Serve with other food and drink

sn7.9:8.2.verse: the consummate one, the great seer,

sn7.9:8.3.verse: with defilements ended and remorse stilled.

sn7.9:8.4.verse: For he is the field for the seeker of merit.”

sn7.9:9.1.verse: “Then, Worthy Gotama, to whom should I give the leftovers of this oblation?”

sn7.9:9.2.verse: “Brahmin, I don’t see anyone in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—who can properly digest these leftovers, except the Realized One or one of his disciples.

sn7.9:9.3.verse: Well then, brahmin, throw out those leftovers where there is little that grows, or drop them into water that has no living creatures.”

sn7.9:10.1.verse: So Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā dropped the leftover oblation in water that had no living creatures.

sn7.9:10.2.verse: And when those leftovers were placed in the water, they sizzled and hissed, steaming and fuming.

sn7.9:10.3.verse: Suppose there was an iron cauldron that had been heated all day. If you placed it in the water, it would sizzle and hiss, steaming and fuming.

sn7.9:10.4.verse: In the same way, when those leftovers were placed in the water, they sizzled and hissed, steaming and fuming.

sn7.9:11.1.verse: Then the brahmin Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā, shocked and awestruck, went up to the Buddha, and stood to one side.

sn7.9:11.2.verse: The Buddha addressed him in verse:

sn7.9:12.2.verse: don’t imagine this is purity, for it’s just external.

sn7.9:12.3.verse: For those who are skilled say this is no way to purity,

sn7.9:12.4.verse: when one seeks purity in externals.

sn7.9:13.1.verse: I’ve given up kindling firewood, brahmin,

sn7.9:13.2.verse: now I light only the inner flame.

sn7.9:13.4.verse: I am a perfected one leading the spiritual life.

sn7.9:14.1.verse: Conceit, brahmin, is the burden of your pack,

sn7.9:14.2.verse: anger your smoke, and lies your ashes.

sn7.9:14.3.verse: The tongue is the ladle, the heart the fireplace;

sn7.9:14.4.verse: a well-tamed self is a person’s light.

sn7.9:15.1.verse: The teaching is a lake, brahmin, into which ethics are the stairs,

sn7.9:15.2.verse: unclouded, praised by the fine to the good.

sn7.9:15.3.verse: There the knowledge masters go to bathe,

sn7.9:15.4.verse: and cross to the far shore with dry limbs.

sn7.9:16.1.verse: Truth, principle, restraint, the spiritual life,

sn7.9:16.2.verse: attaining divinity based on the middle, brahmin—

sn7.9:16.3.verse: pay homage to the upright ones.

sn7.9:16.4.verse: I declare that man one who follows the teaching.”

sn7.9:17.1.verse: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja of Sundarikā said to the Buddha,

sn7.9:17.3.verse: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.

sn7.9:1.1.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Kosalans on the bank of the river Sundarika.

sn7.9:1.2.verse: Now on that occasion  the brahmin Sundarika Bhāradvāja was offering a fire sacrifice and performing the fire oblation on the bank of the river Sundarika.

sn7.9:1.3.verse: Then the brahmin Sundarika Bhāradvāja, having offered the fire sacrifice and performed the fire oblation, rose from his seat and surveyed the four quarters all around, wondering:

sn7.9:1.4.verse: “Who now might eat this sacrificial cake?”

sn7.9:1.5.verse: The brahmin Sundarika Bhāradvāja saw the Blessed One sitting at the foot of a tree with his head covered.

sn7.9:1.6.verse: Having seen him, he took the sacrificial cake in his left hand and the waterpot in his right hand and approached the Blessed One.

sn7.9:1.7.verse: When the Blessed One heard the sound of the brahmin’s footsteps, he uncovered his head.

sn7.9:1.8.verse: Then the brahmin Sundarika Bhāradvāja, thinking, “This worthy is shaven-headed, this worthy is a shaveling, ” wanted to turn back;

sn7.9:1.11.verse: Let me approach him and inquire about his birth. ”

sn7.9:2.1.verse: Then the brahmin Sundarika Bhāradvāja approached the Blessed One and said to him:

sn7.9:3.1.verse: [The Blessed One: ]  “Ask not of birth but ask of conduct:

sn7.9:3.2.verse: Fire is indeed produced from any wood.

sn7.9:3.3.verse: A resolute sage, though from low family,

sn7.9:3.4.verse: Is a thoroughbred restrained by a sense of shame.

sn7.9:4.1.verse: One tamed by truth, perfect by taming,

sn7.9:4.2.verse: Who has reached the end of knowledge, A fulfiller of the holy life.

sn7.9:4.4.verse: Then he makes a timely oblation To one worthy of offerings. ”

sn7.9:5.1.verse: [The brahmin Sundarika Bhāradvāja: ]  “Surely my sacrifice is well performed

sn7.9:5.2.verse: As I have seen such a knowledge-master.

sn7.9:5.3.verse: Because I had not seen those like yourself

sn7.9:5.4.verse: Other people ate the sacrificial cake.

sn7.9:7.1.verse: “Food over which verses have been sung

sn7.9:8.4.verse: For he is the field for one seeking merit. ”

sn7.9:9.1.verse: “Then, Master Gotama, should I give this sacrificial cake to someone else?”

sn7.9:9.2.verse: “I do not see anyone, brahmin, in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, who could eat and properly digest this sacrificial cake  except the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata.

sn7.9:9.3.verse: Therefore, brahmin, throw away the sacrificial cake in a place where there is sparse vegetation or dispose of it in water where there are no living beings. ”

sn7.9:10.1.verse: Then the brahmin Sundarika Bhāradvāja disposed of that sacrificial cake in water where there were no living beings.

sn7.9:10.2.verse: When it was disposed of in the water, that sacrificial cake sizzled and hissed and gave off steam and smoke.

sn7.9:10.3.verse: Just as a ploughshare, heated all day, sizzles and hisses and gives off steam and smoke if placed in water,

sn7.9:10.4.verse: so too that sacrificial cake, when disposed of in the water, sizzled and hissed and gave off steam and smoke.

sn7.9:11.1.verse: Then the brahmin Sundarika Bhāradvāja, shocked and terrified, approached the Blessed One and stood to one side.

sn7.9:11.2.verse: The Blessed One then addressed him with verses:

sn7.9:12.1.verse: “When kindling wood, brahmin, do not imagine

sn7.9:12.3.verse: For experts say no purity is gained

sn7.9:12.4.verse: By one who seeks it outwardly.

sn7.9:13.1.verse: “Having given up the fire made from wood, I kindle,  O brahmin,

sn7.9:13.3.verse: the inner light alone. Always ablaze, my mind always concentrated,

sn7.9:13.4.verse: I am an arahant living the holy life.

sn7.9:14.2.verse: Anger the smoke, false speech the ashes;

sn7.9:14.3.verse: The tongue is the ladle, the heart the altar,

sn7.9:14.4.verse: A well-tamed self is the light of a man.

sn7.9:15.1.verse: “The Dhamma is a lake with fords of virtue—

sn7.9:15.2.verse: Limpid, praised by the good to the good—

sn7.9:15.3.verse: Where the knowledge-masters go to bathe,

sn7.9:15.4.verse: And, dry-limbed, cross to the far shore.

sn7.9:16.2.verse: Attainment of Brahmā based on the middle:

sn7.9:16.3.verse: Pay homage, O brahmin, to the upright ones;

sn7.9:16.4.verse: I call that person one impelled by Dhamma. ”

sn7.9:17.1.verse: When this was said, the brahmin Sundarika Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One:

sn7.9:17.3.verse: And the Venerable Sundarika Bhāradvāja became one of the arahants.

sn7.10:17.2.verse: Not long after his ordination, Venerable Bhāradvāja, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

sn7.10:17.3.verse: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

sn7.10:17.4.verse: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.

There he saw the Blessed One sitting with his legs folded crosswise, holding his body erect, having set up mindfulness in front of him. Having seen him, he approached the Blessed One and recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

sn7.11:1.2.verse: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling amongst the Magadhans on the Southern Hill near the brahmin village Ekanālā.

sn7.11:1.3.verse: Then at that time the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja had about five hundred ploughs yoked up during the sowing season.

sn7.11:1.4.verse: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, approached the place where the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja was working.

sn7.11:2.1.verse: Then at that time the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja’s food distribution was proceeding.

sn7.11:2.2.verse: Then the Fortunate One approached the food distribution, and after approaching he stood on one side.

sn7.11:2.3.verse: The brahmin Kasībhāradvāja saw the Fortunate One standing for alms,

sn7.11:2.4.verse: and after seeing him he said this to the Fortunate One:

sn7.11:2.5.verse: “Ascetic, I plough and I sow, and after ploughing and sowing I eat.

sn7.11:2.6.verse: You also, ascetic, should plough and sow, and after ploughing and sowing you can eat.”

sn7.11:2.7.verse: “Brahmin, I also plough and sow, and after ploughing and sowing I eat.”

sn7.11:2.8.verse: “But we do not see the reverend Gotama’s yoke or plough or ploughshare or goad or oxen, but still the reverend Gotama said this:

sn7.11:2.9.verse: ‘Brahmin, I also plough and sow, and after ploughing and sowing I eat.’ ”

sn7.11:2.10.verse: Then the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja recited a verse to the Fortunate One:

sn7.11:3.1.verse: “You claim that you are a ploughman,

sn7.11:3.2.verse: but we do not see your ploughing.

sn7.11:3.3.verse: Please tell us about ploughing when asked

sn7.11:3.4.verse: so that we may know your ploughing.”

sn7.11:4.2.verse: wisdom is my yoke and plough,

sn7.11:4.3.verse: conscience the pole, mind is the strap,

sn7.11:4.4.verse: mindfulness is my ploughshare and goad.

sn7.11:5.4.verse: temperance the setting free (of the yoke).

sn7.11:6.4.verse: to that place where, having gone, one does not grieve.

sn7.11:7.1.verse: Thus this ploughing has been ploughed

sn7.11:7.2.verse: that produces the fruit of the deathless,

sn7.11:7.4.verse: one is set free from all suffering.”

sn7.11:8.2.verse: the reverend one is a ploughman,

sn7.11:8.3.verse: for the reverend Gotama ploughs the ploughing which has the deathless as fruit.”

sn7.11:9.1.verse: “I will not eat what is gained through chanting verses,

sn7.11:9.2.verse: that is not the Dhamma, brahmin, of those who see,

sn7.11:9.3.verse: Buddhas reject what is gained through chanting verses,

sn7.11:9.4.verse: while Dhamma lasts, brahmin, this is their way of life.

sn7.11:10.1.verse: Another great sage, who is fully adept,

sn7.11:10.2.verse: pollutant-free, at peace regarding worry (about wrong-doing),

sn7.11:10.3.verse: attend to with food and drink,

sn7.11:10.4.verse: for that is the field for those who look for merit.”

sn7.11:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Magadhans in the Southern Hills near the brahmin village of Ekanāḷa.

sn7.11:1.3.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Farmer had harnessed around five hundred plows, it being the season for sowing.

sn7.11:1.4.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to where Bhāradvāja the Farmer was working.

sn7.11:2.1.verse: Now at that time Bhāradvāja the Farmer was distributing food.

sn7.11:2.2.verse: Then the Buddha went to where the distribution was taking place and stood to one side.

sn7.11:2.3.verse: Bhāradvāja the Farmer saw him standing for alms

sn7.11:2.5.verse: “I plough and sow, ascetic, and then I eat.

sn7.11:2.6.verse: You too should plough and sow, then you may eat.”

sn7.11:2.7.verse: “I too plough and sow, brahmin, and then I eat.”

sn7.11:2.8.verse: “I don’t see the worthy Gotama with a yoke or plow or plowshare or goad or oxen, yet he says:

sn7.11:2.9.verse: ‘I too plough and sow, brahmin, and then I eat.’”

sn7.11:2.10.verse: Then Bhāradvāja the Farmer addressed the Buddha in verse:

sn7.11:3.2.verse: but I don’t see you farming.

sn7.11:3.3.verse: Tell me how you’re a farmer when asked:

sn7.11:3.4.verse: how am I to recognize your farming?”

sn7.11:4.1.verse: “Faith is my seed, fervor my rain,

sn7.11:4.2.verse: and wisdom is my yoke and plough.

sn7.11:4.3.verse: Conscience is my draft-pole, mind my strap,

sn7.11:5.2.verse: I restrict my intake of food.

sn7.11:5.3.verse: I use truth as my scythe,

sn7.11:6.2.verse: transporting me to sanctuary from the yoke.

sn7.11:6.4.verse: to where there is no sorrow.

sn7.11:7.1.verse: That’s how to do the farming

sn7.11:7.2.verse: that has freedom from death as its fruit.

sn7.11:8.2.verse: The worthy one is a farmer.

sn7.11:8.3.verse: For the worthy Gotama does the farming that has freedom from death as its fruit.”

sn7.11:9.1.verse: “Food enchanted by a verse isn’t fit for me to eat.

sn7.11:9.2.verse: That’s not the principle of those who see, brahmin.

sn7.11:9.3.verse: The Buddhas cast aside things enchanted with verses.

sn7.11:9.4.verse: Since there is such a principle, brahmin, that’s how they live.

sn7.11:10.1.verse: Serve with other food and drink

sn7.11:10.2.verse: the consummate one, the great seer,

sn7.11:10.3.verse: with defilements ended and remorse stilled.

sn7.11:10.4.verse: For he is the field for the seeker of merit.”

sn7.11:11.1.verse: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Farmer said to the Buddha,

sn7.11:11.3.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

sn7.11:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Magadhans at Dakkhiṇāgiri near the brahmin village of Ekanāḷa.

sn7.11:1.3.verse: Now on that occasion the brahmin Kasi Bhāradvāja, Bhāradvāja the Ploughman, had five hundred ploughs fastened to their yokes at the time of sowing.

sn7.11:1.4.verse: Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed and, taking bowl and robe, went to the place where the brahmin Kasi Bhāradvāja was at work.

sn7.11:2.1.verse: Now on that occasion the brahmin Kasi Bhāradvāja’s food distribution was taking place.

sn7.11:2.2.verse: Then the Blessed One approached the place of the food distribution  and stood to one side.

sn7.11:2.3.verse: The brahmin Kasi Bhāradvāja saw the Blessed One standing for alms

sn7.11:2.5.verse: “Recluse, I plough and sow, and when I have ploughed and sown I eat.

sn7.11:2.6.verse: You too, ascetic, ought to plough and sow; then, when you have ploughed and sown, you will eat. ”

sn7.11:2.7.verse: “I too, brahmin, plough and sow, and when I have ploughed and sown I eat. ”

sn7.11:2.8.verse: “But we do not see Master Gotama’s yoke or plough or ploughshare or goad or oxen; yet Master Gotama says, ‘I too, brahmin, plough and sow, and when I have ploughed and sown I eat. ’”

sn7.11:2.10.verse: Then the brahmin Kasi Bhāradvāja addressed the Blessed One in verse:

sn7.11:3.1.verse: “You claim to be a man who works the plough,

sn7.11:3.2.verse: But I do not see your ploughing.

sn7.11:3.3.verse: If you’re a ploughman, answer me:

sn7.11:3.4.verse: How should we understand your ploughing?”

sn7.11:4.1.verse: [The Blessed One: ]  “Faith is the seed, austerity the rain,

sn7.11:4.3.verse: Shame is the pole, mind the yoke-tie,

sn7.11:5.2.verse: Controlled in my appetite for food,

sn7.11:5.3.verse: I use truth as my weeding-hook,

sn7.11:6.2.verse: Carrying me to security from bondage.

sn7.11:6.4.verse: To where, having gone, one does not sorrow .

sn7.11:7.1.verse: “In such a way this ploughing is done

sn7.11:7.2.verse: Which has the Deathless as its fruit.

sn7.11:7.3.verse: Having finished this work of ploughing,

sn7.11:7.4.verse: One is released from all suffering. ”

sn7.11:8.3.verse: since Master Gotama does ploughing that has even the Deathless as its fruit. ”

sn7.11:9.1.verse: “Food over which verses have been sung

sn7.11:10.4.verse: For he is the field for one seeking merit. ”

sn7.11:11.1.verse: Having said this, the brahmin Kasi Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One:

sn7.11:11.3.verse: remember me as a lay follower who from today has gone for refuge for life. ”

sn7.12:1.2.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of the brahmin Udaya.

sn7.12:1.3.verse: Then Udaya filled the Buddha’s bowl with rice.

sn7.12:1.4.verse: The next day … Udaya again filled the Buddha’s bowl with rice.

sn7.12:1.5.verse: But when he had filled the Buddha’s bowl on the third day, he said to the Buddha,

sn7.12:1.6.verse: “This ascetic Gotama is such a drag! He keeps coming back again and again!”

sn7.12:2.1.verse: “Again and again, they sow the seed;

sn7.12:2.2.verse: again and again, the king of the heavens sends rain;

sn7.12:2.3.verse: again and again, farmers plough the field;

sn7.12:2.4.verse: again and again, grain is produced for the nation.

sn7.12:3.1.verse: Again and again, the beggars beg;

sn7.12:3.2.verse: again and again, the donors give.

sn7.12:3.3.verse: Again and again, when the donors have given,

sn7.12:3.4.verse: again and again, they take their place in heaven.

sn7.12:4.1.verse: Again and again, dairy farmers milk;

sn7.12:4.2.verse: again and again, a calf cleaves to its mother;

sn7.12:4.3.verse: again and again, oppressing and intimidating,

sn7.12:4.4.verse: that dullard returns to the womb again and again.

sn7.12:5.1.verse: Again and again, you’re reborn and die;

sn7.12:5.2.verse: again and again, you get carried to a charnel ground.

sn7.12:5.3.verse: But when they’ve gained the path for no further rebirth,

sn7.12:5.4.verse: one of vast wisdom is not reborn again and again.”

sn7.12:6.1.verse: When he had spoken, the brahmin Udaya said to the Buddha,

sn7.12:6.3.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

sn7.12:1.2.verse: Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed and, taking bowl and robe, approached the residence of the brahmin Udaya.

sn7.12:1.3.verse: Then the brahmin Udaya filled the Blessed One’s bowl with rice.

sn7.12:1.4.verse: A second time in the morning the Blessed One dressed and, taking bowl and robe, approached the residence of the brahmin Udaya…

sn7.12:1.5.verse: A third time in the morning the Blessed One dressed and, taking bowl and robe, approached the residence of the brahmin Udaya.Then a third time the brahmin Udaya filled the Blessed One’s bowl with rice, after which he said to the Blessed One:

sn7.12:1.6.verse: “This pesky ascetic Gotama keeps coming again and again.”

sn7.12:2.1.verse: [The Blessed One: ]  “Again and again, they sow the seed;

sn7.12:2.2.verse: Again and again, the sky-god sends down rain;

sn7.12:2.3.verse: Again and again, ploughmen plough the field;

sn7.12:2.4.verse: Again and again, grain comes to the realm.

sn7.12:3.1.verse: Again and again, the mendicants beg;

sn7.12:3.2.verse: Again and again, the donors give;

sn7.12:3.3.verse: When donors have given again and again,

sn7.12:3.4.verse: Again and again they go to heaven.

sn7.12:4.1.verse: Again and again, the dairy folk draw milk;

sn7.12:4.2.verse: Again and again, the calf goes to its mother;

sn7.12:4.3.verse: Again and again, one wearies and trembles;

sn7.12:4.4.verse: Again and again, the dolt enters the womb;

sn7.12:5.1.verse: Again and again, one is born and dies;

sn7.12:5.2.verse: Again and again, they take one to the cemetery.

sn7.12:5.3.verse: But when one has obtained the path That leads to no more renewed existence,

sn7.12:5.4.verse: Having become broad in wisdom, One is not born again and again!”

sn7.12:6.1.verse: When this was said, the brahmin Udaya said to the Blessed One :

sn7.12:6.3.verse: Let Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who from today has gone for refuge for life.

sn7.17:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kosalans in a certain forest grove.

sn7.17:1.2.verse: Now at that time the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Builder was having some building work done in that jungle thicket.

sn7.17:1.3.verse: He saw the Buddha sitting down cross-legged at the root of a certain sal tree, his body set straight, and mindfulness brought to the present.

sn7.17:1.4.verse: Seeing this, it occurred to him,

sn7.17:1.5.verse: “I enjoy having this building work done here in the jungle.

sn7.17:1.6.verse: I wonder what the ascetic Gotama enjoys having done?”

sn7.17:1.7.verse: Then Bhāradvāja the Builder went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:

sn7.17:2.1.verse: “What kind of works are done by you,

sn7.17:2.2.verse: a mendicant in the sal jungle?

sn7.17:3.1.verse: “There’s nothing I need do in the jungle;

sn7.17:3.2.verse: my jungle’s cut at the root, it’s withered away.

sn7.17:3.3.verse: Free of snarls and thorns in the jungle,

sn7.17:3.4.verse: I enjoy solitude, having given up discontent.”

sn7.17:4.1.verse: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Builder said to the Buddha,

sn7.17:4.3.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

sn7.17:1.1.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain woodland thicket.

sn7.17:1.2.verse: Now on that occasion the brahmin Navakammika Bhāradvāja was getting some work done in that woodland thicket.

sn7.17:1.3.verse: The brahmin Navakammika Bhāradvāja saw the Blessed One sitting at the foot of a certain sal tree with his legs folded crosswise, holding his body erect, having set up mindfulness in front of him.

sn7.17:1.5.verse: “I take delight in getting work done in this woodland thicket.

sn7.17:1.6.verse: What does this ascetic Gotama take delight in getting done?”

sn7.17:1.7.verse: Then the brahmin Navakammika Bhāradvāja approached the Blessed One and addressed him in verse:

sn7.17:2.1.verse: “With what kind of work are you engaged

sn7.17:2.2.verse: Here in this sal woods, bhikkhu,

sn7.17:2.3.verse: By reason of which you find delight

sn7.17:3.1.verse: “There is nothing in the woods I need to do;

sn7.17:3.2.verse: Cut down at the root, my woods is dried up.

sn7.17:3.3.verse: Woodless and dartless, discontent cast off,

sn7.17:3.4.verse: I find delight alone in the woods.

sn7.17:4.2.verse: Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama!…

sn7.17:4.3.verse: Let Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who from today has gone for refuge for life.

sn7.18:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kosalans in a certain forest grove.

sn7.18:1.2.verse: Then several students, pupils of one of the Bhāradvāja brahmins, approached a forest grove while collecting firewood. They saw the Buddha sitting down cross-legged at the root of a certain sal tree, his body set straight, and mindfulness brought to the present. Seeing this, they went up to Bhāradvāja and said to him,

sn7.18:1.4.verse: In such-and-such forest grove the ascetic Gotama is sitting down cross-legged, his body set straight, and mindfulness brought to the present.”

sn7.18:1.5.verse: Then Bhāradvāja together with those young students went to that forest grove

sn7.18:1.6.verse: where he saw the Buddha sitting down cross-legged, his body set straight, and mindfulness brought to the present.

sn7.18:1.7.verse: He went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:

sn7.18:2.1.verse: “Deep in the jungle so full of terrors,

sn7.18:2.2.verse: you’ve plunged into the empty, desolate wilderness.

sn7.18:3.1.verse: Where there is no song or music,

sn7.18:3.2.verse: a lonely sage resorts to the wilderness.

sn7.18:3.3.verse: This strikes me as an amazing thing,

sn7.18:3.4.verse: that you dwell so joyfully alone in the jungle.

sn7.18:4.1.verse: I suppose you wish to be reborn in the company

sn7.18:4.2.verse: of the supreme world-sovereign of the Third Heaven.

sn7.18:4.3.verse: Is that why you resort to the desolate wilderness,

sn7.18:4.4.verse: to practice fervor for attaining divinity?”

sn7.18:5.1.verse: “Any wishes and hopes that are always attached

sn7.18:5.2.verse: to the many and various realms—

sn7.18:5.3.verse: the prayers sprung from the root of unknowing—

sn7.18:5.4.verse: I’ve eliminated them all down to the root.

sn7.18:6.2.verse: amongst all things, my vision is clear.

sn7.18:6.3.verse: I’ve attained the state of grace, the supreme awakening;

sn7.18:6.4.verse: I meditate alone, brahmin, and self-assured.”

sn7.18:7.1.verse: When he had spoken, Bhāradvāja said to the Buddha,

sn7.18:7.3.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
