sn11.9:1.2.verse: “Once upon a time, mendicants, several seers who were ethical, of good character, settled in leaf huts in a wilderness region.

sn11.9:1.3.verse: Then Sakka, lord of gods, and Vepacitti, lord of titans, went to those seers.

sn11.9:1.4.verse: Vepacitti put on his lined sandals, strapped on his sword, and, carrying a sunshade, entered the hermitage through the main gate. He walked right past those seers, keeping them at arm’s length.

sn11.9:1.5.verse: Sakka took off his lined sandals, gave his sword to others, and, putting down his sunshade, entered the hermitage through the same gate. He stood downwind of those seers, revering them with cupped palms.

sn11.9:1.6.verse: Then those seers addressed Sakka in verse:

sn11.9:2.2.verse: the odor of their bodies goes with the gale.

sn11.9:2.4.verse: The odor of the seers is unclean, king of gods.’

sn11.9:3.2.verse: let the odor of their bodies go with the gale.

sn11.9:3.3.verse: We yearn for this odor, sirs,

sn11.9:3.4.verse: like a colorful crown of flowers.

sn11.9:3.5.verse: The gods don’t see it as repulsive.’”

sn11.9:1.2.verse: “Bhikkhus, once in the past a number of seers who were virtuous and of good character had settled down in leaf huts in a tract of forest.

sn11.9:1.3.verse: Then Sakka, lord of the devas, and Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, approached those seers.

sn11.9:1.4.verse: Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, put on his boots, bound his sword on tightly, and, with a parasol borne aloft, entered the hermitage through the main gate; then, having turned his left side towards them, he walked past those seers who were virtuous and of good character.

sn11.9:1.5.verse: But Sakka, lord of the devas, took off his boots, handed over his sword to others, lowered his parasol, and entered the hermitage through an [ordinary] gate; then he stood on the lee side, raising his joined hands in reverential salutation, paying homage to those seers who were virtuous and of good character.

sn11.9:1.6.verse: Then, bhikkhus, those seers addressed Sakka in verse:

sn11.9:2.1.verse: ‘The odour of the seers long bound by their vows,

sn11.9:2.2.verse: Emitted from their bodies, goes with the wind.

sn11.9:2.3.verse: Turn away from here, O thousand-eyed god,

sn11.9:2.4.verse: For the seers’ odour is foul, O deva-king.’

sn11.9:3.1.verse: ‘Let the odour of the seers long bound by their vows,

sn11.9:3.2.verse: Emitted from their bodies, go with the wind;

sn11.9:3.3.verse: We yearn for this odour, O venerable sirs,

sn11.9:3.4.verse: As for a garland of flowers on the head.

sn11.9:3.5.verse: The devas do not perceive it as repulsive.'”

sn11.10:1.2.verse: “Once upon a time, mendicants, several seers who were ethical, of good character, settled in leaf huts on the ocean shore.

sn11.10:1.5.verse: ‘The gods are principled, the titans are unprincipled.

sn11.10:1.8.verse: Then, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, those seers vanished from those leaf huts on the ocean shore and reappeared in Sambara’s presence.

sn11.10:1.9.verse: Then those seers addressed Sambara in verse:

sn11.10:2.2.verse: to beg for a pledge of safety.

sn11.10:5.1.verse: Whatever kind of seed you sow,

sn11.10:5.2.verse: that is the fruit you reap.

sn11.10:5.3.verse: A doer of good gets good,

sn11.10:5.4.verse: a doer of bad gets bad.

sn11.10:6.2.verse: But after being cursed by the seers, Sambara woke in alarm three times that night.”

sn11.10:1.2.verse: “Bhikkhus, once in the past a number of seers who were virtuous and of good character had settled down in leaf huts along the shore of the ocean.

sn11.10:1.3.verse: Now on that occasion the devas and the asuras were arrayed for a battle.

sn11.10:1.4.verse: Then it occurred to those seers who were virtuous and of good character:

sn11.10:1.5.verse: ‘The devas are righteous, the asuras unrighteous.

sn11.10:1.6.verse: There may be danger to us from the asuras.

sn11.10:1.7.verse: Let us approach Sambara, lord of the asuras, and ask him for a guarantee of safety.’

sn11.10:1.8.verse: Then, bhikkhus, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, those seers who were virtuous and of good character disappeared from their leaf huts along the shore of the ocean and reappeared in the presence of Sambara, lord of the asuras.

sn11.10:1.9.verse: Then those seers addressed Sambara in verse:

sn11.10:2.1.verse: ‘The seers who have come to Sambara

sn11.10:2.2.verse: Ask him for a guarantee of safety.

sn11.10:2.3.verse: For you can give them what you wish,

sn11.10:2.4.verse: Whether it be danger or safety.’

sn11.10:3.1.verse: ‘I'll grant no safety to the seers,

sn11.10:3.2.verse: For they are hated devotees of Sakka;

sn11.10:3.3.verse: Though you appeal to me for safety,

sn11.10:4.3.verse: We receive this at your hands:

sn11.10:4.4.verse: May ceaseless danger come to you!

sn11.10:5.1.verse: Whatever sort of seed is sown,

sn11.10:5.2.verse: That is the sort of fruit one reaps:

sn11.10:5.3.verse: The doer of good reaps good;

sn11.10:5.4.verse: The doer of evil reaps evil.

sn11.10:5.5.verse: By you, dear, has the seed been sown;

sn11.10:5.6.verse: Thus you will experience the fruit.’

sn11.10:6.1.verse: Then, bhikkhus, having put a curse on Sambara, lord of the asuras, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, those seers who were virtuous and of good character disappeared from the presence of Sambara and reappeared in their leaf huts on the shore of the ocean.

sn11.10:6.2.verse: But after being cursed by those seers who were virtuous and of good character, Sambara, lord of the asuras, was gripped by alarm three times in the course of the night.”

sn11.14:2.6.verse: ‘It is wonderful indeed, sir! It is amazing indeed, sir!

sn11.14:2.8.verse: Yet with the breakup of the body, after death, he has been reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world, in the company of the Tavatimsa devas,

sn11.14:2.9.verse: where he outshines the other devas in regard to beauty and glory.’

sn11.18:1.4.verse: ‘Harness the chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds, friend Mātali. Let us go to the park grounds to see the beautiful scenery.’

sn11.18:1.5.verse: ‘Yes, your lordship,’ Mātali the charioteer replied. Then he hamessed the chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds and announced to Sakka, lord of the devas:

sn11.18:1.6.verse: ‘The chariot has been harnessed, dear sir.

sn11.18:1.7.verse: You may come at your own convenience.’

sn11.18:1.8.verse: Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, descending from the Vejayanta Palace, raised his joined hands in reverential salutation, and worshipped the different quarters.

sn11.18:1.9.verse: Then Mātali the charioteer addressed Sakka in verse:

sn11.18:2.1.verse: ‘These all humbly worship you— those versed in the Triple Veda,

sn11.18:2.2.verse: All the khattiyas reigning on earth,

sn11.18:2.6.verse: O Sakka, to whom you bow in worship?’

sn11.18:3.1.verse: ‘These all humbly worship me, those versed in the Triple Veda,—

sn11.18:3.2.verse: All the khattiyas reigning on earth,

sn11.18:4.1.verse: But I worship those endowed with virtue,

sn11.18:4.3.verse: Those who have properly gone forth

sn11.18:4.4.verse: With the holy life their destination.

sn11.18:5.2.verse: The lay followers possessed of virtue

sn11.18:6.1.verse: ‘Those are indeed the best in the world,

sn11.18:6.2.verse: whom you worship, my lord Sakka;

sn11.18:7.4.verse: The chief, climbed into his chariot.”

sn11.20:1.3.verse: “Once upon a time, mendicants, Sakka, lord of gods, addressed his chariot handler Mātali,

sn11.20:1.9.verse: So Mātali the chariot handler addressed Sakka in verse:

sn11.20:2.2.verse: namely the humans stuck in their putrid bodies,

sn11.20:1.2.verse: There the Blessed One said this:

sn11.20:1.3.verse: “Bhikkhus, once in the past Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed his charioteer Mātali thus:

sn11.20:1.4.verse: ‘Harness the chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds, friend Mātali. Let us go to the park grounds to see the beautiful scenery.’

sn11.20:1.5.verse: ‘Yes, your lordship,’ Mātali the charioteer replied. Then he harnessed the chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds and announced to Sakka, lord of the devas:

sn11.20:1.6.verse: ‘The chariot has been harnessed, dear sir.

sn11.20:1.7.verse: You may come at your own convenience.’

sn11.20:1.8.verse: Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, descending from the Vejayanta Palace, raised his joined hands in reverential salutation and worshipped the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.

sn11.20:1.9.verse: Then Mātali the charioteer addressed Sakka, lord of the devas, in verse:

sn11.20:2.1.verse: ‘It is these that should worship you—

sn11.20:2.2.verse: The humans stuck in a putrid body,

sn11.20:3.1.verse: Why then do you envy them,

sn11.20:3.3.verse: Tell us about the seers’ conduct;

sn11.20:3.4.verse: Let us hear what you have to say.’

sn11.20:5.1.verse: ‘They do not keep their goods in storage,

sn11.20:5.2.verse: Neither in a pot nor in a box.

sn11.20:5.3.verse: Seeking what has been prepared by others,

sn11.20:5.4.verse: By this they live, firm in vows:

sn11.20:6.1.verse: Those wise ones who give good counsel,

sn11.20:6.4.verse: And people fight with one another,

sn11.20:7.2.verse: Among the violent, they are quenched;

sn11.20:7.3.verse: Among those who grasp, they do not grasp:

sn11.20:7.4.verse: These are the ones whom I worship, Mātali.’

sn11.20:8.2.verse: my lord Sakka, Are indeed the best in the world.

sn11.21:1.2.verse: And then Sakka, lord of gods, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

sn11.21:2.1.verse: “When what is slain do you sleep at ease?

sn11.21:2.2.verse: When what is slain is there no sorrow?

sn11.21:3.1.verse: “When anger’s slain you sleep at ease.

sn11.21:3.2.verse: When anger’s slain there is no sorrow.

sn11.21:3.4.verse: and a sweet tip, O Vāsava.

sn11.21:3.5.verse: The noble ones praise its killing,

sn11.21:3.6.verse: for when it’s slain there is no sorrow.”

sn11.21:1.2.verse: Then Sakka, lord of the devas, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and stood to one side.

sn11.21:1.3.verse: Standing to one side, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed the Blessed One in verse:

sn11.21:2.1.verse: “Having slain what does one sleep soundly?

sn11.21:2.2.verse: Having slain what does one not sorrow?

sn11.21:2.3.verse: What is the one thing, O Gotama,

sn11.21:3.2.verse: Having slain anger, one does not sorrow;

sn11.21:3.3.verse: Of anger, with its poisoned root

sn11.21:3.5.verse: This is the killing the noble ones praise,

sn11.21:3.6.verse: For having slain that, one does not sorrow.”

sn11.22:1.3.verse: “Once upon a time, mendicants, there was a native spirit who was ugly and deformed. He sat on the throne of Sakka, lord of gods.

sn11.22:1.4.verse: But the gods of the thirty-three complained, grumbled, and objected,

sn11.22:1.6.verse: This ugly and deformed spirit is sitting on the throne of Sakka, the lord of gods.’

sn11.22:1.7.verse: But the more the gods complained, the more attractive, good-looking, and lovely that spirit became.

sn11.22:2.1.verse: So the gods went up to Sakka and told him what had happened. He replied,

sn11.22:2.7.verse: ‘Surely, good fellow, that must be the anger-eating spirit!’

sn11.22:3.1.verse: Then Sakka went up to that spirit, arranged his robe over one shoulder, knelt on his right knee, raised his joined palms toward the anger-eating spirit, and pronounced his name three times:

sn11.22:3.2.verse: ‘Good fellow, I am Sakka, lord of gods! Good fellow, I am Sakka, the lord of gods!’

sn11.22:3.3.verse: But the more Sakka pronounced his name, the uglier and more deformed the spirit became,

sn11.22:3.4.verse: until eventually it vanished right there.

sn11.22:3.5.verse: Then Sakka, lord of gods, guiding the gods of the thirty-three, spoke this verse:

sn11.22:4.2.verse: I’m not easily drawn into the maelstrom.

sn11.22:4.3.verse: I don’t get angry for long,

sn11.22:5.1.verse: When I do get angry I don’t speak harshly,

sn11.22:5.2.verse: nor do I advertise my own virtues.

sn11.22:5.4.verse: out of regard for my own welfare.’”

sn11.22:1.3.verse: There the Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, once in the past a certain ugly deformed yakkha sat down on the seat of Sakka, lord of the devas.

sn11.22:1.4.verse: Thereupon the Tāvatiṃsa devas found fault with this, grumbled, and complained about it, saying:

sn11.22:1.5.verse: ‘It is wonderful indeed, sir! It is amazing indeed, sir!

sn11.22:1.6.verse: This ugly deformed yakkha has sat down on the seat of Sakka, lord of the devas!’

sn11.22:2.1.verse: Then, bhikkhus, the Tāvatiṃsa devas approached Sakka and said to him:

sn11.22:2.2.verse: ‘Here, dear sir, an ugly deformed yakkha has sat down on your seat….

sn11.22:2.6.verse: But to whatever extent the devas found fault with this … that yakkha became more and more handsome, more and more comely, more and more graceful.’

sn11.22:3.1.verse: Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, approached that anger-eating yakkha. Having approached, he arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, knelt down with his right knee on the ground, and, raising his joined hands in reverential salutation towards that yakkha, he announced his name three times:

sn11.22:3.2.verse: ‘I, dear sir, am Sakka, lord of the devas! I, dear sir, am Sakka, lord of the devas!’

sn11.22:3.3.verse: To whatever extent Sakka announced his name, to the same extent that yakkha became uglier and uglier and more and more deformed

sn11.22:3.5.verse: Then, bhikkhus,  Sakka, lord of the devas, having sat down on his own seat, instructing the Tāvatiṃsa devas, on that occasion recited these verses:

sn11.22:4.1.verse: ‘I am not one afflicted in mind,

sn11.22:4.2.verse: Nor easily drawn by anger's whirl.

sn11.22:4.3.verse: I never become angry for long,

sn11.22:4.4.verse: Nor does anger persist in me.

sn11.22:5.1.verse: ‘When I’m angry I don't speak harshly

sn11.22:5.2.verse: And I don't praise my virtues.

sn11.22:5.4.verse: Out of regard for my own good.’”

sn11.23:1.3.verse: “Once upon a time, mendicants, Vepacitti, lord of titans, was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

sn11.23:1.4.verse: So Sakka went to see him to ask after his illness.

sn11.23:1.5.verse: Vepacitti saw Sakka coming off in the distance,

sn11.23:1.9.verse: ‘I can’t do that, good fellow, until I have consulted with the titans.’

sn11.23:1.10.verse: Then Vepacitti, lord of titans, asked the titans,

sn11.23:1.11.verse: ‘Good fellows, may I teach the Sambari sorcery to Sakka, lord of gods?’

sn11.23:1.12.verse: ‘Do not, good fellow, teach the Sambari sorcery to Sakka!’

sn11.23:1.13.verse: So Vepacitti addressed Sakka in verse:

sn11.23:2.4.verse: into the terrible hell for a full century.’”

sn11.23:1.3.verse: “Bhikkhus, once in the past Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, was sick, afflicted, gravely ill.

sn11.23:1.4.verse: Then Sakka, lord of the devas, approached Vepacitti to inquire about his illness.

sn11.23:1.5.verse: Vepacitti saw Sakka coming in the distance

sn11.23:1.9.verse: ‘I won't teach it, dear sir, until I have asked the asuras for permission.’

sn11.23:1.10.verse: Then, bhikkhus, Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, asked the asuras:

sn11.23:1.11.verse: ‘May I teach the Sambari magic to Sakka, lord of the devas?’

sn11.23:1.12.verse: ‘Do not teach him the Sambari magic, dear sir.’

sn11.23:1.13.verse: Then, bhikkhus, Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, addressed Sakka, lord of the devas, in verse:

sn11.23:2.4.verse: Like Sambara, for a hundred years.’”

sn11.24:2.1.verse: “Bhikkhus, there are two kinds of fools:

sn11.24:2.2.verse: one who does not see a transgression as a transgression; and one who, when another is confessing a transgression, does not pardon him in accordance with the Dhamma. These are the two kinds of fools.

sn11.24:2.3.verse: There are, bhikkhus, two kinds of wise people:

sn11.24:2.4.verse: one who sees a transgression as a transgression;

sn11.24:2.5.verse: and one who, when another is confessing a transgression, pardons him in accordance with the Dhamma.

sn11.24:2.6.verse: These are the two kinds of wise people.

sn11.25:1.4.verse: “Once upon a time, mendicants, Sakka, lord of gods, guiding the gods of the thirty-three, spoke this verse:

sn11.25:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthı̄ in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park.

sn11.25:1.3.verse: There the Blessed One said this:

sn11.25:1.4.verse: “Bhikkhus, once in the past Sakka, lord of the devas, instructing the Tāvatiṃsa devas in the Sudhamma assembly hall, on that occasion recited this verse:

sn11.25:2.2.verse: Do not become angry at those who are angry.

sn11.25:2.4.verse: Within [the hearts of] the noble ones.

sn12.1:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn12.1:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

sn12.1:1.7.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you dependent origination.

sn12.1:1.8.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn12.1:2.2.verse: Ignorance is a requirement for choices.

sn12.1:2.3.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness.

sn12.1:2.4.verse: Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.

sn12.1:2.5.verse: Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.

sn12.1:2.6.verse: The six sense fields are requirements for contact.

sn12.1:2.7.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn12.1:2.8.verse: Feeling is a requirement for craving.

sn12.1:2.9.verse: Craving is a requirement for grasping.

sn12.1:2.10.verse: Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.

sn12.1:2.11.verse: Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.

sn12.1:2.12.verse: Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.

sn12.1:2.13.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.1:3.1.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, choices cease.

sn12.1:3.3.verse: When consciousness ceases, name and form cease.

sn12.1:3.4.verse: When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease.

sn12.1:3.5.verse: When the six sense fields cease, contact ceases.

sn12.1:3.9.verse: When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.

sn12.1:3.10.verse: When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.

sn12.1:3.11.verse: When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.

sn12.1:3.12.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

sn12.1:3.13.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn12.1:3.14.verse: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

sn12.1:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthı̄ in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park.

sn12.1:1.3.verse: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:

sn12.1:1.7.verse: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you dependent origination.

sn12.1:1.8.verse: Listen to that and attend closely, I will speak.”

sn12.1:2.2.verse: With ignorance as condition, volitional formations [come to be];

sn12.1:2.3.verse: with volitional formations as condition, consciousness;

sn12.1:2.5.verse: with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases;

sn12.1:2.6.verse: with the six sense bases as condition, contact;

sn12.1:2.12.verse: with birth as condition, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair come to be.

sn12.1:2.13.verse: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.

sn12.1:2.14.verse: This, bhikkhus, is called dependent origination.

sn12.1:3.1.verse: But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance, comes cessation of volitional formations;

sn12.1:3.2.verse: with the cessation of volitional formations, cessation of consciousness;

sn12.1:3.3.verse: with the cessation of consciousness, cessation of name-and-form;

sn12.1:3.4.verse: with the cessation of name-and-form, cessation of the six sense bases;

sn12.1:3.5.verse: with the cessation of the six sense bases, cessation of contact;

sn12.1:3.6.verse: with the cessation of contact, cessation of feeling;

sn12.1:3.7.verse: with the cessation of feeling, cessation of craving;

sn12.1:3.8.verse: with the cessation of craving, cessation of clinging;

sn12.1:3.9.verse: with the cessation of clinging, cessation of existence;

sn12.1:3.10.verse: with the cessation of existence, cessation of birth;

sn12.1:3.11.verse: with the cessation of birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair cease.

sn12.1:3.12.verse: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

sn12.1:3.13.verse: This is what the Blessed One said.

sn12.1:3.14.verse: Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One's statement.

sn12.1:1.2.verse: The Exalted One was once staying near Savatthi at the Jeta Grove in Anathapindika's Park.

sn12.1:1.3.verse: And there the Exalted One addressed the monks, saying:—

sn12.1:1.7.verse: “I will teach you, monks, the causal law.

sn12.1:1.8.verse: Listen to it, give your minds thoroughly and I will speak.”

sn12.1:2.2.verse: Conditioned by ignorance activities come to pass;

sn12.1:2.12.verse: conditioned by birth old age-and-death, grief, lamenting, suffering, sorrow. despair come to pass.

sn12.1:2.13.verse: Such is the uprising of this entire mass of ill.

sn12.1:3.1.verse: But from the utter fading away and ceasing of ignorance (comes] ceasing of activities;

sn12.1:3.2.verse: from ceasing of activities ceasing of consciousness;

sn12.1:3.3.verse: from ceasing of consciousness ceasing of name-and-shape;

sn12.1:3.4.verse: from ceasing of name-and-shape ceasing of sense;

sn12.1:3.5.verse: from ceasing of sense ceasing of contact;

sn12.1:3.6.verse: from ceasing of contact ceasing of feeling;

sn12.1:3.7.verse: from ceasing of feeling ceasing of craving;

sn12.1:3.8.verse: from ceasing of craving ceasing of grasping;

sn12.1:3.9.verse: from ceasing of grasping ceasing of becoming;

sn12.1:3.10.verse: from ceasing of becoming ceasing of birth;

sn12.1:3.11.verse: from ceasing of birth old age-and-death, grief, lamenting, suffering, sorrow, despair cease.

sn12.1:3.12.verse: Such is the ceasing of this entire mass of ill.”

sn12.1:3.13.verse: It is the Exalted One who had spoken this.

sn12.1:3.14.verse: Pleased in mind those monks took delight in the saying of the Exalted One.

sn12.2:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach and analyze for you dependent origination.

sn12.2:1.3.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn12.2:2.2.verse: Ignorance is a requirement for choices.

sn12.2:2.3.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness.

sn12.2:2.4.verse: Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.

sn12.2:2.5.verse: Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.

sn12.2:2.6.verse: The six sense fields are requirements for contact.

sn12.2:2.7.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn12.2:2.8.verse: Feeling is a requirement for craving.

sn12.2:2.9.verse: Craving is a requirement for grasping.

sn12.2:2.10.verse: Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.

sn12.2:2.11.verse: Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.

sn12.2:2.12.verse: Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.

sn12.2:2.13.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.2:3.1.verse: And what is old age and death?

sn12.2:3.2.verse: The old age, decrepitude, broken teeth, grey hair, wrinkly skin, diminished vitality, and failing faculties of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.

sn12.2:3.4.verse: The passing away, passing on, disintegration, demise, mortality, death, decease, breaking up of the aggregates, and laying to rest of the corpse of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.

sn12.2:3.6.verse: Such is old age, and such is death.

sn12.2:3.7.verse: This is called old age and death.

sn12.2:4.2.verse: The rebirth, inception, conception, regeneration, manifestation of the aggregates, and acquisition of the sense fields of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.

sn12.2:5.2.verse: There are these three states of existence.

sn12.2:5.3.verse: Existence in the sensual realm, the realm of luminous form, and the formless realm.

sn12.2:6.2.verse: There are these four kinds of grasping.

sn12.2:6.3.verse: Grasping at sensual pleasures, views, precepts and observances, and theories of a self.

sn12.2:7.2.verse: There are these six classes of craving.

sn12.2:7.3.verse: Craving for sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

sn12.2:8.2.verse: There are these six classes of feeling.

sn12.2:8.3.verse: Feeling born of contact through the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

sn12.2:9.2.verse: There are these six classes of contact.

sn12.2:9.3.verse: Contact through the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

sn12.2:10.1.verse: And what are the six sense fields?

sn12.2:10.2.verse: The sense fields of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

sn12.2:10.3.verse: These are called the six sense fields.

sn12.2:11.1.verse: And what are name and form?

sn12.2:11.2.verse: Feeling, perception, intention, contact, and application of mind.

sn12.2:11.4.verse: The four principal states, and form derived from the four principal states.

sn12.2:11.6.verse: Such is name and such is form.

sn12.2:11.7.verse: These are called name and form.

sn12.2:12.2.verse: There are these six classes of consciousness.

sn12.2:12.3.verse: Eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind consciousness.

sn12.2:13.2.verse: There are three kinds of choices.

sn12.2:13.3.verse: Choices by way of body, speech, and mind.

sn12.2:14.2.verse: Not knowing about suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.

sn12.2:15.1.verse: And so, ignorance is a requirement for choices.

sn12.2:15.2.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …

sn12.2:15.3.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.2:15.4.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.

sn12.2:15.6.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

sn12.2:1.2.verse: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you dependent origination and I will analyse it for you.

sn12.2:1.3.verse: Listen to that and attend closely, I will speak.”

sn12.2:2.2.verse: With ignorance as condition, volitional formations [come to be];

sn12.2:2.3.verse: with volitional formations as condition, consciousness;

sn12.2:2.5.verse: with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases;

sn12.2:2.6.verse: with the six sense bases as condition, contact;

sn12.2:2.12.verse: with birth as condition, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair come to be.

sn12.2:2.13.verse: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.

sn12.2:3.2.verse: The aging of the various beings in the various orders of beings, their growing old, brokenness of teeth, greyness of hair, wrinkling of skin, decline of vitality, degeneration of the faculties:

sn12.2:3.4.verse: The passing away of the various beings from the various orders of beings, their perishing, breakup, disappearance, mortality, death, completion of time, the breakup of the aggregates, the laying down of the carcass:

sn12.2:3.6.verse: Thus this aging and this death

sn12.2:4.2.verse: The birth of the various beings into the various orders of beings, their being born, descent [into the womb], production, the manifestation of the aggregates, the obtaining of the sense bases.

sn12.2:5.2.verse: There are these three kinds of existence:

sn12.2:5.3.verse: sense-sphere existence, form-sphere existence, formless-sphere existence.

sn12.2:6.2.verse: There are these four kinds of clinging:

sn12.2:6.3.verse: clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to rules and vows, clinging to a doctrine of self.

sn12.2:7.2.verse: There are these six classes of craving:

sn12.2:7.3.verse: craving for forms, craving for sounds, craving for odours, craving for tastes, craving for tactile objects, craving for mental phenomena.

sn12.2:8.2.verse: There are these six classes of feeling:

sn12.2:8.3.verse: feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of mind-contact.

sn12.2:9.2.verse: There are these six classes of contact:

sn12.2:9.3.verse: eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, mind-contact.

sn12.2:10.1.verse: And what, bhikkhus, are the six sense bases?

sn12.2:10.2.verse: The eye base, the ear base, the nose base, the tongue base, the body base, the mind base.

sn12.2:10.3.verse: These are called the six sense bases.

sn12.2:11.4.verse: The four great elements and the form derived from the four great elements:

sn12.2:11.6.verse: Thus this name and this form

sn12.2:12.2.verse: There are these six classes of consciousness:

sn12.2:12.3.verse: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness.

sn12.2:13.1.verse: And what, bhikkhus, are the volitional formations?

sn12.2:13.2.verse: There are these three kinds of volitional formations:

sn12.2:13.3.verse: the bodily volitional formation, the verbal volitional formation, the mental volitional formation.

sn12.2:13.4.verse: These are called the volitional formations.

sn12.2:14.2.verse: Not knowing suffering, not knowing the origin of suffering, not knowing the cessation of suffering, not knowing the way leading to the cessation of suffering.

sn12.2:15.1.verse: Thus, bhikkhus, with ignorance as condition, volitional formations [come to be];

sn12.2:15.2.verse: with volitional formations as condition, consciousness….

sn12.2:15.3.verse: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.

sn12.2:15.4.verse: But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance comes cessation of volitional formations;

sn12.2:15.5.verse: with the cessation of volitional formations, cessation of consciousness….

sn12.2:15.6.verse: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

sn12.2:1.2.verse: [the Exalted One said this]:—“I will teach you, Monks, I will analyze* the causal law.

sn12.2:1.3.verse: Listen to it, give your minds thoroughly and I will speak.’

sn12.2:2.1.verse: What, Monks, is the causal law ?

sn12.2:3.1.verse: And what, Monks, is old age-and-death?

sn12.2:3.2.verse: That which, of this and that being, in this and that group, is decay, decrepitude, breaking up, hoariness, wrinkling of the skin, shrinkage of a life-span, over-ripeness of faculties:

sn12.2:3.4.verse: That which, of this and that being from this or that group, is falling or decease, separation, disappearance, mortality or dying,* accomplishment of time: separation of component factors,> laying down of the carcase:

sn12.2:3.6.verse: Thus it is this decay and this dying

sn12.2:4.2.verse: That which, of this and that being in this and that group, is birth, continuous birth, descent,® reproduction, appearance of component factors, acquiring of sense-spheres.

sn12.2:5.3.verse: becoming in Kama-[worlds]’ becoming in Rupa-[worlds], becoming in Arupa-[worlds].

sn12.2:6.3.verse: grasping of desires, grasping of opinion, grasping of rule and ritual, grasping of soul-theory.

sn12.2:7.2.verse: There are these six groups of craving:

sn12.2:7.3.verse: craving for things seen, for things heard, for odours, for tastes, for things tangible, for ideas.

sn12.2:8.2.verse: There are these six groups of feeling:

sn12.2:8.3.verse: feeling that is born of eye-contact, feeling that is born of ear-contact, feeling that is born of nose-contact, feeling that is born of tongue-contact, feeling that 1s born of body-contact, feeling that is born of mind-contact.

sn12.2:9.2.verse: There are these six groups of contact:

sn12.2:9.3.verse: eye-contact, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, mind-contact.

sn12.2:10.1.verse: And what, Monks, is sixfold sense?

sn12.2:10.2.verse: The sense of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, mind

sn12.2:11.2.verse: Feeling, perception, will, contact, work of mind.

sn12.2:11.4.verse: The four great elements and the shape derived from them.

sn12.2:11.6.verse: This is the name, this is the shape

sn12.2:12.2.verse: These are the six groups of consciousness :

sn12.2:12.3.verse: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, smell-, taste-, touch-, and mind-consciousness.

sn12.2:14.2.verse: Nescience concerning ill, its rise, its cessation and concerning the way going to the cessation of ill.

sn12.2:15.1.verse: So thus, Monks:—‘ conditioned by ignorance activities.'

sn12.2:15.2.verse: conditioned by activities consciousness,’ and so on to 'despair'

sn12.2:15.3.verse: —such is the uprising of this entire mass of ill.

sn12.2:15.4.verse: But from the utter fading out and ceasing of ignorance, ceasing of activities,

sn12.2:15.5.verse: from the ceasing of activities ceasing of consciousness,

sn12.2:15.6.verse: such is the ceasing of this entire mass of ill.

sn12.3:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the wrong practice and the right practice.

sn12.3:1.3.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn12.3:2.2.verse: Ignorance is a requirement for choices.

sn12.3:2.3.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …

sn12.3:2.4.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.3:2.5.verse: This is called the wrong practice.

sn12.3:3.2.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.

sn12.3:3.4.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

sn12.3:3.5.verse: This is called the right practice.”

sn12.3:1.2.verse: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the wrong way and the right way.

sn12.3:1.3.verse: Listen to that and attend closely, I will speak.”

sn12.3:2.1.verse: “And what, bhikkhus, is the wrong way?

sn12.3:2.2.verse: With ignorance as condition, volitional formations [come to be];

sn12.3:2.3.verse: with volitional formations as condition, consciousness….

sn12.3:2.4.verse: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.

sn12.3:2.5.verse: This, bhikkhus, is called the wrong way.

sn12.3:3.1.verse: And what, bhikkhus, is the right way?

sn12.3:3.2.verse: With the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance comes cessation of volitional formations;

sn12.3:3.3.verse: with the cessation of volitional formations, cessation of consciousness. …

sn12.3:3.4.verse: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.

sn12.3:3.5.verse: This, bhikkhus, is called the right way.”

sn12.3:1.2.verse: [the Exalted One said]:— “I will teach you, Monks, both the wrong way and the tight way.

sn12.3:1.3.verse: Listen to it, give your minds thoroughly and I will speak.

sn12.3:2.1.verse: Which, Monks, is the wrong way?

sn12.3:2.2.verse: ‘Conditioned by ignorance activities come to pass;

sn12.3:2.4.verse: even [the way of] the uprising of this entire mass of ill.

sn12.3:2.5.verse: This is called the wrong way.

sn12.3:3.1.verse: And which is the right way?

sn12.3:3.2.verse: ‘But from the utter fading away and ceasing of ignorance [comes] the ceasing of activities ;

sn12.3:3.3.verse: from the ceasing of activities [comes] ceasing of consciousness”

sn12.3:3.4.verse: even [the way of] the ceasing of this entire mass of ill.

sn12.3:3.5.verse: This is called the right way.

sn12.4:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, Vipassī the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha had this thought before his awakening, when he was still unawakened but intent on awakening:

sn12.4:1.3.verse: ‘Alas, this world has fallen into trouble. It’s born, grows old, dies, passes away, and is reborn,

sn12.4:1.4.verse: yet it doesn’t understand how to escape from this suffering, from old age and death.

sn12.4:1.5.verse: Oh, when will an escape be found from this suffering, from old age and death?’

sn12.4:2.1.verse: Then Vipassī, the one intent on awakening, thought:

sn12.4:2.2.verse: ‘When what exists is there old age and death? What is a requirement for old age and death?’

sn12.4:2.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:2.4.verse: ‘When rebirth exists there’s old age and death. Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death.’

sn12.4:3.2.verse: ‘When what exists is there rebirth? What is a requirement for rebirth?’

sn12.4:3.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:3.4.verse: ‘When continued existence exists there’s rebirth. Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.’

sn12.4:4.2.verse: ‘When what exists is there continued existence? What is a requirement for continued existence?’

sn12.4:4.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:4.4.verse: ‘When grasping exists there’s continued existence. Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.’

sn12.4:5.2.verse: ‘When what exists is there grasping? What is a requirement for grasping?’

sn12.4:5.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:5.4.verse: ‘When craving exists there’s grasping. Craving is a requirement for grasping.’

sn12.4:6.2.verse: ‘When what exists is there craving? What is a requirement for craving?’

sn12.4:6.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:6.4.verse: ‘When feeling exists there’s craving. Feeling is a requirement for craving.’

sn12.4:7.2.verse: ‘When what exists is there feeling? What is a requirement for feeling?’

sn12.4:7.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:7.4.verse: ‘When contact exists there’s feeling. Contact is a requirement for feeling.’

sn12.4:8.2.verse: ‘When what exists is there contact? What is a requirement for contact?’

sn12.4:8.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:8.4.verse: ‘When the six sense fields exist there’s contact. The six sense fields are requirements for contact.’

sn12.4:9.2.verse: ‘When what exists are there the six sense fields? What is a requirement for the six sense fields?’

sn12.4:9.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:9.4.verse: ‘When name and form exist there are the six sense fields. Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.’

sn12.4:10.2.verse: ‘When what exists are there name and form? What is a requirement for name and form?’

sn12.4:10.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:10.4.verse: ‘When consciousness exists there are name and form. Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.’

sn12.4:11.2.verse: ‘When what exists is there consciousness? What is a requirement for consciousness?’

sn12.4:11.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:11.4.verse: ‘When choices exist there’s consciousness. Choices are a requirement for consciousness.’

sn12.4:12.2.verse: ‘When what exists are there choices? What is a requirement for choices?’

sn12.4:12.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:12.4.verse: ‘When ignorance exists there are choices. Ignorance is a requirement for choices.’

sn12.4:13.1.verse: And so, ignorance is a requirement for choices.

sn12.4:13.2.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …

sn12.4:13.3.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.4:13.4.verse: ‘Origination, origination.’ While Vipassī was intent on awakening, such was the vision, knowledge, wisdom, realization, and light that arose in him regarding teachings not learned before from another.

sn12.4:14.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no old age and death? When what ceases do old age and death cease?’

sn12.4:14.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:14.4.verse: ‘When rebirth doesn’t exist there’s no old age and death. When rebirth ceases, old age and death cease.’

sn12.4:15.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no rebirth? When what ceases does rebirth cease?’

sn12.4:15.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:15.4.verse: ‘When continued existence doesn’t exist there’s no rebirth. When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.’

sn12.4:16.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no continued existence? When what ceases does continued existence cease?’

sn12.4:16.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:16.4.verse: ‘When grasping doesn’t exist there’s no continued existence. When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.’

sn12.4:17.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no grasping? When what ceases does grasping cease?’

sn12.4:17.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:17.4.verse: ‘When craving doesn’t exist there’s no grasping. When craving ceases, grasping ceases.’

sn12.4:18.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no craving? When what ceases does craving cease?’

sn12.4:18.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:18.4.verse: ‘When feeling doesn’t exist there’s no craving. When feeling ceases, craving ceases.’

sn12.4:19.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no feeling? When what ceases does feeling cease?’

sn12.4:19.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:19.4.verse: ‘When contact doesn’t exist there’s no feeling. When contact ceases, feeling ceases.’

sn12.4:20.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no contact? When what ceases does contact cease?’

sn12.4:20.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:20.4.verse: ‘When the six sense fields don’t exist there’s no contact. When the six sense fields cease, contact ceases.’

sn12.4:21.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist are there no six sense fields? When what ceases do the six sense fields cease?’

sn12.4:21.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:21.4.verse: ‘When name and form don’t exist there are no six sense fields. When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease.’

sn12.4:22.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist are there no name and form? When what ceases do name and form cease?’

sn12.4:22.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:22.4.verse: ‘When consciousness doesn’t exist there are no name and form. When consciousness ceases, name and form cease.’

sn12.4:23.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no consciousness? When what ceases does consciousness cease?’

sn12.4:23.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:23.4.verse: ‘When choices don’t exist there’s no consciousness. When choices cease, consciousness ceases.’

sn12.4:24.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist are there no choices? When what ceases do choices cease?’

sn12.4:24.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.4:24.4.verse: ‘When ignorance doesn’t exist there are no choices. When ignorance ceases, choices cease.’

sn12.4:25.1.verse: And so, when ignorance ceases, choices cease.

sn12.4:25.3.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

sn12.4:25.4.verse: ‘Cessation, cessation.’ Such was the vision, knowledge, wisdom, realization, and light that arose in Vipassī, the one intent on awakening, regarding teachings not learned before from another.”

sn12.4:26.1.verse: (Tell in full  for each of the seven Buddhas.)

sn12.4:1.2.verse: “Bhikkhus, before his enlightenment, while he was still a bodhisatta, not yet fully enlightened, it occurred to Vipassı̄, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One:

sn12.4:1.3.verse: ‘Alas, this world has fallen into trouble, in that it is born, ages, and dies, it passes away and is reborn,

sn12.4:1.4.verse: yet it does not understand the escape from this suffering [headed by] aging-and-death.

sn12.4:1.5.verse: When now will an escape be discerned from this suffering [headed by] aging-and-death?’

sn12.4:25.4.verse: ‘Cessation, cessation’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard before there arose in the Bodhisatta Vipassı̄ vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.”

sn12.4:1.1.verse: - staying near Savatthi [the Exalted One said}]:—

sn12.4:1.2.verse: To Vipassi,+ brethren, Exalted One, Arahant, Buddha, Supreme, before his enlightenment, while he was yet unenlightened and Bodhisat, there came this thought:—

sn12.5:1.1.verse: “Sikhī, the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha …”

sn12.6:1.1.verse: “Vessabhū, the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha …”

sn12.7:1.1.verse: “Kakusandha, the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha …”

sn12.8:1.1.verse: “Koṇāgamana, the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha …”

sn12.9:1.1.verse: “Kassapa, the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha …”

sn12.10:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, before my awakening—when I was still unawakened but intent on awakening—I thought:

sn12.10:1.2.verse: ‘Alas, this world has fallen into trouble. It’s born, grows old, dies, passes away, and is reborn,

sn12.10:1.3.verse: yet it doesn’t understand how to escape from this suffering, from old age and death.

sn12.10:1.4.verse: Oh, when will an escape be found from this suffering, from old age and death?’

sn12.10:2.2.verse: ‘When what exists is there old age and death? What is a requirement for old age and death?’

sn12.10:2.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.10:2.4.verse: ‘When rebirth exists there’s old age and death. Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death.’

sn12.10:3.11.verse: ‘When what exists are there choices? What is a requirement for choices?’

sn12.10:3.12.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.10:3.13.verse: ‘When ignorance exists there are choices. Ignorance is a requirement for choices.’

sn12.10:4.1.verse: And so, ignorance is a requirement for choices.

sn12.10:4.2.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …

sn12.10:4.3.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.10:4.4.verse: ‘Origination, origination.’ Such was the vision, knowledge, wisdom, realization, and light that arose in me regarding teachings not learned before from another.

sn12.10:5.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no old age and death? When what ceases do old age and death cease?’

sn12.10:5.3.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.10:5.4.verse: ‘When rebirth doesn’t exist there’s no old age and death. When rebirth ceases, old age and death cease.’

sn12.10:6.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no rebirth? …

sn12.10:6.11.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist are there no choices? When what ceases do choices cease?’

sn12.10:6.12.verse: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:

sn12.10:6.13.verse: ‘When ignorance doesn’t exist there are no choices. When ignorance ceases, choices cease.’

sn12.10:7.1.verse: And so, when ignorance ceases, choices cease.

sn12.10:7.3.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

sn12.10:7.4.verse: ‘Cessation, cessation.’ Such was the vision, knowledge, wisdom, realization, and light that arose in me regarding teachings not learned before from another.”

sn12.10:1.1.verse: “Bhikkhus, before my enlightenment, while I was still a bodhisatta, not yet fully enlightened, it occurred to me:

sn12.10:1.2.verse: ‘Alas, this world has fallen into trouble, in that it is born, ages, and dies, it passes away and is reborn,

sn12.10:1.3.verse: yet it does not understand the escape from this suffering [headed by] aging-and-death.

sn12.10:1.4.verse: When now will an escape be discerned from this suffering [headed by] aging-and-death?’

sn12.10:2.1.verse: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me:

sn12.10:2.2.verse: ‘When what exists does aging-and-death come to be? By what is aging-and-death conditioned?’

sn12.10:2.3.verse: Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom:

sn12.10:2.4.verse: ‘When there is birth, aging-and-death comes to be; aging-and-death has birth as its condition.’

sn12.10:3.1.verse: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me:

sn12.10:3.2.verse: ‘When what exists does birth come to be? By what is birth conditioned?’Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When there is existence, birth comes to be; birth has existence as its condition.’

sn12.10:3.3.verse: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me: ‘When what exists does existence come to be? By what is existence conditioned?’ Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When there is clinging, existence comes to be; existence has clinging as its condition.’

sn12.10:3.4.verse: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me: ‘When what exists does clinging come to be? By what is clinging conditioned?’Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When there is craving, clinging comes to be; clinging has craving as its condition.’

sn12.10:3.5.verse: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me: ‘When what exists does craving come to be? By what is craving conditioned?’ Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When there is feeling, craving comes to be; craving has feeling as its condition.’

sn12.10:3.6.verse: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me: ‘When what exists does feeling come to be? By what is feeling conditioned?’ Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When there is contact, feeling comes to be; feeling has contact as its condition.’

sn12.10:3.7.verse: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me: ‘When what exists does contact come to be? By what is contact conditioned?’ Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When there are the six sense bases, contact comes to be; contact has the six sense bases as its condition.’

sn12.10:3.8.verse: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me: ‘When what exists do the six sense bases come to be? By what are the six sense bases conditioned?’ Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When there is name-and-form, the six sense bases come to be; the six sense bases have name-and-form as their condition.’

sn12.10:3.9.verse: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me: ‘When what exists does name-and-form come to be? By what is name-and-form conditioned?’ Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When there is consciousness, name-and-form comes to be; name-and-form has consciousness as its condition.’

sn12.10:3.10.verse: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me: ‘When what exists does consciousness come to be? By what is consciousness conditioned?’ Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When there are volitional formations, consciousness comes to be; consciousness has volitional formations as its condition.’

sn12.10:3.11.verse: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me: ‘When what exists do volitional formations come to be? By what are volitional formations conditioned?’

sn12.10:3.12.verse: Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom:

sn12.10:3.13.verse: ‘When there is ignorance, volitional formations come to be; volitional formations have ignorance as their condition.’

sn12.10:4.1.verse: Thus with ignorance as condition, volitional formations [come to be];

sn12.10:4.2.verse: with volitional formations as condition, consciousness….

sn12.10:4.3.verse: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.

sn12.10:4.4.verse: ‘Origination, origination’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard before there arose in me vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.

sn12.10:5.1.verse: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me:

sn12.10:5.2.verse: ‘When what does not exist does aging-and-death not come to be? With the cessation of what does the cessation of aging-and-death come about?’

sn12.10:5.3.verse: Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom:

sn12.10:5.4.verse: ‘When there is no birth, aging-and-death does not come to be; with the cessation of birth comes cessation of aging-and-death.’

sn12.10:6.1.verse: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me:

sn12.10:6.2.verse: ‘When what does not exist does birth not come to be? By the cessation of what does the cessation of birth come about?’ Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom: ‘When there is no existence, birth does not come to be; with the cessation of existence comes cessation of birth.’…

sn12.10:6.3.verse: ‘When there is no clinging, existence does not come to be; with the cessation of clinging comes cessation of existence.’…

sn12.10:6.4.verse: ‘When there is no craving, clinging does not come to be; with the cessation of craving comes cessation of clinging.’…

sn12.10:6.5.verse: ‘When there is no feeling, craving does not come to be; with the cessation of feeling comes cessation of craving.’…

sn12.10:6.6.verse: ‘When there is no contact, feeling does not come to be; with the cessation of contact comes cessation of feeling.’…

sn12.10:6.7.verse: ‘When there are no six sense bases, contact does not come to be; with the cessation of the six sense bases comes cessation of contact.’…

sn12.10:6.8.verse: ‘When there is no name-and-form, the six sense bases do not come to be; with the cessation of name-and-form comes cessation of the six sense bases.’…

sn12.10:6.9.verse: ‘When there is no consciousness, name-and-form does not come to be; with the cessation of consciousness comes cessation of name-and-form.’…

sn12.10:6.10.verse: ‘When there are no volitional formations, consciousness does not come to be; with the cessation of volitional formations comes cessation of consciousness.’…

sn12.10:6.11.verse: ‘When what does not exist does volitional formations not come to be? By the cessation of what does the cessation of volitional formations come about?’

sn12.10:6.12.verse: Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom:

sn12.10:6.13.verse: ‘When there is no ignorance, volitional formations do not come to be; with the cessation of ignorance comes cessation of volitional formations.’

sn12.10:7.1.verse: Thus with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance comes cessation of volitional formations;

sn12.10:7.2.verse: with the cessation of volitional formations, cessation of consciousness….

sn12.10:7.3.verse: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.

sn12.10:7.4.verse: ‘Cessation, cessation’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard before there arose in me vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.”

sn12.10:0.3.verse: Gotama the Great Seer of the Sakyas.

sn12.10:1.1.verse: And to me, Monks, before I was enlightened, while I was yet unenlightened and Bodhisat, there came this [same] thought: -—

sn12.10:1.2.verse: Alas! this world has fallen upon trouble. There is getting born and growing old, and dying and falling and being reborn.

sn12.10:1.3.verse: And yet from this suffering an escape is not known, even from decay-and-death.

sn12.10:1.4.verse: O when shall escape from this suffering, even from decay-and-death, be revealed?

sn12.10:2.1.verse: Then to me, Monks, came this thought:

sn12.10:2.2.verse: What now being present, does decay-and-death come to be? What conditions decay-and-death?

sn12.10:2.3.verse: Then to me thinking, according to law, came to pass, comprehension of insight:

sn12.10:2.4.verse: let there be birth, then there is decay-and-death. Decay-and-death is conditioned by birth.

sn12.10:3.1.verse: Then to me, Monks, came this thought:

sn12.10:3.2.verse: What now being present, does birth come to be? What conditions birth? Then to me, thinking, according to law, came to pass comprehension of insight: let there be becoming, then birth comes

sn12.10:3.4.verse: ...let there be grasping, then becoming comes to be. Let there be craving, then grasping comes to be.

sn12.10:3.5.verse: ...let there be feeling, then craving comes to be...

sn12.10:3.6.verse: ... let there be contact, then feeling comes to be...

sn12.10:3.7.verse: ... let there be sense, then contact comes to be...

sn12.10:3.9.verse: ... let there be name-and-shape, then sense comes to be...

sn12.10:3.10.verse: ... let there be consciousness, then name-and-shape comes to be...

sn12.10:3.11.verse: ... let there be activities, then consciousness comes to be...

sn12.10:3.13.verse: ... let there be ignorance, then activities come to be, activities are conditioned by ignorance.

sn12.10:4.1.verse: Such verily is this: activities conditioned by ignorance.

sn12.10:4.3.verse: Even so is the coming to be of this entire mass of ill.

sn12.10:4.4.verse: Coming to be! Coming to be! At the thought there arose in me, Monks, in things not taught before vision; there arose in me knowledge, insight arose, wisdom* arose, light arose.

sn12.10:5.1.verse: Then, Monks, to me came the thought:

sn12.10:5.2.verse: ‘ What now being absent, does decay-and-death not come to be? From the ceasing of what is there ceasing of decey-and-death?

sn12.10:5.3.verse: Then to me, thinking according to law, came to pass comprehension of insight:

sn12.10:5.4.verse: let there be no birth, then decay-and-death ceases. From ceasing of birth ceasing of decay-and-death.

sn12.10:6.1.verse: ‘And thus also came to me comprehension of insight into the like concerning

sn12.10:7.1.verse: Such verily is this ‘ ceasing of activities because of ceasing of ignorance,’

sn12.10:7.3.verse: Even so is the ceasing of this entire mass of ill.

sn12.10:7.4.verse: Ceasing! Ceasing! At the thought there arose in me, Monks, in things not taught before vision; there arose in me knowledge, insight arose, wisdom arose, light arose.

sn12.11:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. …

sn12.11:1.3.verse: “Mendicants, these four fuels maintain sentient beings that have been born and help those about to be born.

sn12.11:1.5.verse: Edible food, whether solid or subtle; contact is the second, mental intention the third, and consciousness the fourth.

sn12.11:1.6.verse: These are the four fuels that maintain sentient beings that have been born and help those about to be born.

sn12.11:2.1.verse: What is the source, origin, birthplace, and inception of these four fuels?

sn12.11:2.3.verse: And what is the source, origin, birthplace, and inception of craving?

sn12.11:2.5.verse: And what is the source of feeling?

sn12.11:2.7.verse: And what is the source of contact?

sn12.11:2.9.verse: And what is the source of the six sense fields?

sn12.11:2.11.verse: And what is the source of name and form?

sn12.11:2.13.verse: And what is the source of consciousness?

sn12.11:2.15.verse: And what is the source of choices?

sn12.11:3.1.verse: And so, mendicants, ignorance is a requirement for choices.

sn12.11:3.2.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …

sn12.11:3.3.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.11:3.4.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.

sn12.11:3.6.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

sn12.11:1.2.verse: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthı̄ in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. …

sn12.11:1.3.verse: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of nutriment for the maintenance of beings that have already come to be and for the assistance of those about to come to be.

sn12.11:1.5.verse: The nutriment edible food, gross or subtle; second, contact; third, mental volition; fourth, consciousness.

sn12.11:1.6.verse: These are the four kinds of nutriment for the maintenance of beings that have already come to be and for the assistance of those about to come to be.

sn12.11:2.1.verse: Bhikkhus, these four kinds of nutriment have what as their source, what as their origin, from what are they born and produced?

sn12.11:2.2.verse: These four kinds of nutriment have craving as their source, craving as their origin; they are born and produced from craving.

sn12.11:2.3.verse: And this craving has what as its source, what as its origin, from what is it born and produced?

sn12.11:2.4.verse: This craving has feeling as its source, feeling as its origin; it is born and produced from feeling.

sn12.11:2.5.verse: And this feeling has what as its source…?

sn12.11:2.6.verse: Feeling has contact as its source….

sn12.11:2.7.verse: And this contact has what as its source…?

sn12.11:2.8.verse: Contact has the six sense bases as its source….

sn12.11:2.9.verse: And these six sense bases have what as their source…?

sn12.11:2.10.verse: The six sense bases have name-and-form as their source….

sn12.11:2.11.verse: And this name-and-form has what as its source…?

sn12.11:2.12.verse: Name-and-form has consciousness as its source….

sn12.11:2.13.verse: And this consciousness has what as its source…?

sn12.11:2.14.verse: Consciousness has volitional formations as its source….

sn12.11:2.15.verse: And these volitional formations have what as their source, what as their origin, from what are they born and produced?

sn12.11:2.16.verse: Volitional formations have ignorance as their source, ignorance as their origin; they are born and produced from ignorance.

sn12.11:3.1.verse: Thus, bhikkhus, with ignorance as condition, volitional formations [come to be];

sn12.11:3.2.verse: with volitional formations as condition, consciousness….

sn12.11:3.3.verse: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.

sn12.11:3.4.verse: But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance comes cessation of volitional formations;

sn12.11:3.5.verse: with the cessation of volitional formations, cessation of consciousness….

sn12.11:3.6.verse: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

sn12.11:1.2.verse: The Exalted One was once staying near Sivatthi, at Jeta Grove, in Anathapindika’s Park:

sn12.11:1.3.verse: “There are these four sustenances, Monks, for the maintenance of beings that have come to birth or for the forwarding of them that seek to become.

sn12.11:1.5.verse: Material food, coarse or fine. Secondly, contact. Thirdly, volition, Fourthly, consciousness.

sn12.11:1.6.verse: These four are the sustenances for the maintenance of beings that have come to birth, or for the forwarding of those that seek to become.

sn12.11:2.1.verse: And of these four, Monks, what is the base, whence is the uprising? How are they produced? What causes them?

sn12.11:2.2.verse: Craving is their base, from craving is their uprising; craving produces them, causes them to be.

sn12.11:2.3.verse: What is the base, whence is the uprising of craving? What produces it? What causes it to be?

sn12.11:2.4.verse: Feeling is its base, its uprising, produces it, causes it to be.

sn12.11:2.6.verse: And contact is the base, the uprising, the producer, the cause of feeling.

sn12.11:3.1.verse: Such verily, Monks, is this: conditioned by ignorance [are] activities,

sn12.11:3.3.verse: Such is the uprising of this entire mass of ill.

sn12.11:3.4.verse: But from the utter fading away and ceasing of ignorance the ceasing of activities,

sn12.11:3.5.verse: from the ceasing of these the ceasing of consciousness...

sn12.11:3.6.verse: Such is the ceasing of this entire mass of ill.”

sn12.12:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, these four fuels maintain sentient beings that have been born and help those about to be born.

sn12.12:1.4.verse: Edible food, whether solid or subtle; contact is the second, mental intention the third, and consciousness the fourth.

sn12.12:1.5.verse: These are the four fuels that maintain sentient beings that have been born and help those that are about to be born.”

sn12.12:2.1.verse: When he said this, Venerable Phagguna of the Top-Knot said to the Buddha,

sn12.12:2.2.verse: “But sir, who consumes consciousness as fuel?”

sn12.12:2.3.verse: “That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha.

sn12.12:2.4.verse: “I don’t speak of one who consumes.

sn12.12:2.5.verse: If I were to speak of one who consumes, then it would be cogent to ask

sn12.12:2.7.verse: But I don’t speak like that.

sn12.12:2.8.verse: Hence it would be cogent to ask:

sn12.12:2.10.verse: And a cogent answer to this would be:

sn12.12:2.11.verse: ‘Consciousness as fuel is a requirement for regeneration into a new state of existence in the future. When the being is present, there are the six sense fields. The six sense fields are requirements for contact.’”

sn12.12:3.2.verse: “That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha.

sn12.12:3.3.verse: “I don’t speak of one who contacts.

sn12.12:3.4.verse: If I were to speak of one who contacts, then it would be cogent to ask

sn12.12:3.6.verse: But I don’t speak like that.

sn12.12:3.7.verse: Hence it would be cogent to ask:

sn12.12:3.9.verse: And a cogent answer to this would be:

sn12.12:3.10.verse: ‘The six sense fields are requirements for contact. Contact is a requirement for feeling.’”

sn12.12:4.2.verse: “That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha.

sn12.12:4.3.verse: “I don’t speak of one who feels.

sn12.12:4.4.verse: If I were to speak of one who feels, then it would be cogent to ask

sn12.12:4.6.verse: But I don’t speak like that.

sn12.12:4.7.verse: Hence it would be cogent to ask:

sn12.12:4.9.verse: And a cogent answer to this would be:

sn12.12:4.10.verse: ‘Contact is a requirement for feeling. Feeling is a requirement for craving.’”

sn12.12:5.2.verse: “That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha.

sn12.12:5.3.verse: “I don’t speak of one who craves.

sn12.12:5.4.verse: If I were to speak of one who craves, then it would be cogent to ask

sn12.12:5.6.verse: But I don’t speak like that.

sn12.12:5.7.verse: Hence it would be cogent to ask:

sn12.12:5.9.verse: And a cogent answer to this would be:

sn12.12:5.10.verse: ‘Feeling is a requirement for craving. Craving is a requirement for grasping.’”

sn12.12:6.2.verse: “That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha.

sn12.12:6.3.verse: “I don’t speak of one who grasps.

sn12.12:6.4.verse: If I were to speak of one who grasps, then it would be cogent to ask

sn12.12:6.6.verse: But I don’t speak like that.

sn12.12:6.7.verse: Hence it would be cogent to ask:

sn12.12:6.9.verse: And a cogent answer to this would be:

sn12.12:6.11.verse: Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.’ …

sn12.12:6.12.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.12:7.1.verse: When the six fields of contact fade away and cease with no residue left behind, contact ceases.

sn12.12:7.5.verse: When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.

sn12.12:7.6.verse: When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.

sn12.12:7.7.verse: When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.

sn12.12:7.8.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

sn12.12:1.2.verse: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of nutriment for the maintenance of beings that have already come to be and for the assistance of those about to come to be.

sn12.12:1.4.verse: The nutriment edible food, gross or subtle; second, contact; third, mental volition; fourth, consciousness.

sn12.12:1.5.verse: These are the four kinds of nutriment for the maintenance of beings that have already come to be and for the assistance of those about to come to be.”

sn12.12:2.1.verse: When this was said, the Venerable Moḷiyaphagguna said to the Blessed One:

sn12.12:2.2.verse: “Venerable sir, who consumes the nutriment consciousness?”

sn12.12:2.3.verse: “Not a valid question,” the Blessed One replied.

sn12.12:2.5.verse: If I should say, ‘One consumes,’ in that case this would be a valid question:

sn12.12:2.7.verse: But I do not speak thus.

sn12.12:2.8.verse: Since I do not speak thus, if one should ask me,

sn12.12:2.9.verse: ‘Venerable sir, for what is the nutriment consciousness [a condition]?’ this would be a valid question.

sn12.12:2.10.verse: To this the valid answer is:

sn12.12:2.11.verse: ‘The nutriment consciousness is a condition for the production of future renewed existence. When that which has come into being exists, the six sense bases [come to be]; with the six sense bases as condition, contact.’”

sn12.12:3.2.verse: “Not a valid question,” the Blessed One replied.

sn12.12:3.4.verse: If I should say, ‘One makes contact,’ in that case this would be a valid question:

sn12.12:3.6.verse: But I do not speak thus.

sn12.12:3.7.verse: Since I do not speak thus, if one should ask me,

sn12.12:3.8.verse: ‘Venerable sir, with what as condition does contact [come to be]?’

sn12.12:3.9.verse: this would be a valid question. To this the valid answer is:

sn12.12:3.10.verse: ‘With the six sense bases as condition, contact [comes to be]; with contact as condition, feeling.’”

sn12.12:4.2.verse: “Not a valid question,” the Blessed One replied.

sn12.12:4.4.verse: If I should say, ‘One feels,’ in that case this would be a valid question:

sn12.12:4.6.verse: But I do not speak thus.

sn12.12:4.7.verse: Since I do not speak thus, if one should ask me,

sn12.12:4.8.verse: ‘Venerable sir, with what as condition does feeling [come to be]?’ this would be a valid question.

sn12.12:4.9.verse: To this the valid answer is:

sn12.12:4.10.verse: ‘With contact as condition, feeling [comes to be]; with feeling as condition, craving.’”

sn12.12:5.2.verse: “Not a valid question,” the Blessed One replied.

sn12.12:5.4.verse: If I should say, ‘One craves,’ in that case this would be a valid question:

sn12.12:5.6.verse: But I do not speak thus.

sn12.12:5.7.verse: Since I do not speak thus, if one should ask me,

sn12.12:5.8.verse: ‘Venerable sir, with what as condition does craving [come to be]?’ this would be a valid question.

sn12.12:5.9.verse: To this the valid answer is:

sn12.12:5.10.verse:
‘With feeling as condition, craving [comes to be];
with craving as condition, clinging;’”

sn12.12:6.12.verse: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.’

sn12.12:7.1.verse: But, Phagguna, with the remainderless fading away and cessation of the six bases for contact comes cessation of contact;

sn12.12:7.2.verse: with the cessation of contact, cessation of feeling;

sn12.12:7.3.verse: with the cessation of feeling, cessation of craving;

sn12.12:7.4.verse: with the cessation of craving, cessation of clinging;

sn12.12:7.5.verse: with the cessation of clinging, cessation of existence;

sn12.12:7.6.verse: with the cessation of existence, cessation of birth;

sn12.12:7.7.verse: with the cessation of birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair cease.

sn12.12:7.8.verse: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

sn12.12:1.3.verse: The Exalted One was teaching the doctrine of the four sustenances.

sn12.12:2.1.verse: And when he had named them the venerable Moliya-Phagguna said to the Exalted One:

sn12.12:2.2.verse: “Who now is it, lord, who feeds on the consciousness sustenance?”

sn12.12:2.3.verse: “Not a fit question.” said the Exalted One.

sn12.12:2.5.verse: If I were saying so, to that the question would be a fit one.

sn12.12:2.7.verse: But I am not saying so. If you were to ask me:

sn12.12:2.9.verse: ‘of what now, lord, is consciousness the sustenance ?’

sn12.12:2.10.verse: this were a fit question. And the fit answer to it is:

sn12.12:2.11.verse: ‘the consciousness-sustenance is the cause of renewed becoming, of rebirth in the future. When that is come to pass, is present, the sixfold sense-sphere becomes, and conditioned by the sixfold sense-sphere contact becomes.’”

sn12.12:3.2.verse: “Not a fit question,” said the Exalted One.

sn12.12:3.4.verse: If I were saying so, the question would be a fit one.

sn12.12:3.6.verse: But I am not saying so.

sn12.12:3.7.verse: And I not saying so, if you were to ask thus:

sn12.12:3.8.verse: ‘Conditioned now by what, lord, is contact?’

sn12.12:3.9.verse: this is a fit question. And the fit answer there would be:

sn12.12:3.10.verse: ‘conditioned by the sixfold sense-sphere is contact; conditioned by contact is feeling.’”

sn12.12:4.1.verse: “Who now, lord, is it who feels?”

sn12.12:4.2.verse: “Not a fit question,” said the Exalted One.

sn12.12:4.4.verse: If I were saying so, the question would be a fit one. But I am not saying so.

sn12.12:4.6.verse: And I am not saying so,

sn12.12:4.7.verse: if you were to ask thus:

sn12.12:4.8.verse: ‘Conditioned now by what, lord, is feeling?’

sn12.12:4.9.verse: this were a fit question. And the fit answer there would be:

sn12.12:4.10.verse: ‘Conditioned by contact is feeling, conditioned by feeling is craving.’”

sn12.12:5.1.verse: “Who now, lord, is it who craves?”

sn12.12:5.2.verse: “Not a fit question,” said the Exalted One.

sn12.12:5.4.verse: If I were saying so, the question would be a fit one.

sn12.12:5.6.verse: But I am not saying so.

sn12.12:5.7.verse: And I not saying so, if you were to ask thus:

sn12.12:5.8.verse: ‘Conditioned now by what, lord, is craving ?’

sn12.12:5.9.verse: this were a fit question. And the fit answer there would be:

sn12.12:5.10.verse: ‘Conditioned by feeling is craving. Conditioned by craving is grasping.’”

sn12.12:6.1.verse: “Who now, lord, is it who grasps ?”

sn12.12:6.2.verse: “Not a fit question,” said the Exalted One

sn12.12:6.4.verse: If I were saying so, the question would be a fit one.

sn12.12:6.6.verse: But I am not saying so.

sn12.12:6.7.verse: And I not saying so, if you were to ask thus:

sn12.12:6.8.verse: ‘Conditioned now by what, lord, is there grasping?’

sn12.12:6.9.verse: this were a fit question. And the fit answer there would be:

sn12.12:6.11.verse: ‘Conditioned by grasping is becoming.’” And so on.

sn12.12:6.12.verse: “Such is the uprising of this entire mass of Ill.

sn12.12:7.1.verse: But from the utter fading away and cessation of the sixfold sphere of sense-contact, Phagguna, comes cessation of contact,

sn12.12:7.2.verse: from cessation of contact, cessation of feeling,

sn12.12:7.3.verse: from cessation of feeling, cessation of craving,

sn12.12:7.7.verse: ... of decay-and-death, of grief lamentation, suffering, unhappiness, despair.

sn12.12:7.8.verse: Such is the cessation of this entire mass of ill.”

sn12.13:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, there are ascetics and brahmins who don’t understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.13:1.12.verse: They don’t understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.13:1.13.verse: I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

sn12.13:2.1.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who do understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.13:2.11.verse: They understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.13:2.12.verse: I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

sn12.13:1.2.verse: “Bhikkhus, those ascetics or brahmins who do not understand aging-and-death, its origin, its cessation, and the way leading to its cessation;

sn12.13:1.12.verse: volitional formations, their origin, their cessation, and the way leading to their cessation:

sn12.13:1.13.verse: these I do not consider to be ascetics among ascetics or brahmins among brahmins, and these venerable ones do not, by realizing it for themselves with direct knowledge, in this very life enter and dwell in the goal of asceticism or the goal of brahminhood.

sn12.13:2.1.verse: But, bhikkhus, those ascetics and brahmins who understand aging-and-death, its origin, its cessation, and the way leading to its cessation;

sn12.13:2.11.verse: volitional formations, their origin, their cessation, and the way leading to their cessation:

sn12.13:2.12.verse: these I consider to be ascetics among ascetics and brahmins, brahmins among brahmins, and these venerable ones, by realizing it for themselves with direct knowledge, in this very life enter and dwell in the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood.”

sn12.14:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, there are ascetics and brahmins who don’t understand these things, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation. What things don’t they understand?

sn12.14:2.1.verse: They don’t understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.14:2.11.verse: They don’t understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.14:2.12.verse: They don’t understand these things, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.14:2.13.verse: I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

sn12.14:3.1.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who do understand these things, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation. What things do they understand?

sn12.14:4.1.verse: They understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.14:4.11.verse: They understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.14:4.12.verse: They understand these things, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.14:4.13.verse: I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

sn12.14:1.2.verse: “Bhikkhus, as to those ascetics and brahmins who do not understand these things, the origin of these things, the cessation of these things, and the way leading to the cessation of these things: what are those things that they do not understand, whose origin they do not understand, whose cessation they do not understand, and the way leading to whose cessation they do not understand?

sn12.14:2.1.verse: They do not understand aging-and-death, its origin, its cessation, and the way leading to its cessation.

sn12.14:2.11.verse: volitional formations, their origin, their cessation, and the way leading to their cessation.

sn12.14:2.12.verse: These are the things that they do not understand, whose origin they do not understand, whose cessation they do not understand, and the way leading to whose cessation they do not understand.
