sn12.24:2.1.verse: Now the venerable Sariputta came to those gardens, and after exchanging greetings with those heretical Wanderers and compliments of friendship and courtesy,

sn12.24:2.2.verse: sat down at one side. Then those Wanderers spoke thus to the venerable Sariputta so seated:

sn12.24:3.1.verse: “There are, friend Sariputta, certain recluses and brahmins, believers in karma, who declare that ill is self-made;

sn12.24:3.2.verse: certain others of them declare ill is made by someone other [than one’s self];

sn12.24:3.3.verse: certain others declare that ill is made by both,

sn12.24:3.4.verse: and certain others that ill is made by neither, but happens by chance.

sn12.24:3.5.verse: But the recluse Gotama—what does he declare, what does he announce?

sn12.24:3.6.verse: And how, if we were answering, should we be repeating the views of the recluse Gotama, and should not be misrepresenting him by what is not correct, but should be answering by a doctrine in conformity with his doctrine, and [one whereby] no one who is of his doctrine, a follower of his views, would render himself open to blame?”

sn12.24:4.1.verse: “Friend, the Exalted One has said that ill comes to pass through a cause.

sn12.24:4.4.verse: He who so spoke would be repeating the views of the Exalted One, and would not be misrepresenting him by what is not correct, but would be answering by a doctrine in conformity with his doctrine, and one whereby no one who is of his doctrine, a follower of his views, would render himself open to blame.

sn12.24:5.1.verse: In the case of those recluses and brahmins, friend, who believing in karma declare that ill has been made by one’s own self, this ill was caused by contact.

sn12.24:5.2.verse: In the case of those of them who declare that ill has been made by a different self, this ill too was caused by contact.

sn12.24:5.3.verse: In the case of those of them who declare that ill has been made by both one’s own self and by a different self, this ill too was caused by contact.

sn12.24:5.4.verse: In the case also of those who declare that ill has been made by neither, but has happened by chance, this ill too was caused by contact.

sn12.24:6.1.verse: In no one of these four views of those who believe in karma is it possible to show that those recluses and brahmins will experience feeling without contact.”

sn12.24:7.1.verse: Now the venerable Ananda was listening to Sariputta’s talk with the heretical Wanderers.

sn12.24:7.2.verse: And the venerable Ananda, after going his alms round in Rājagaha and eating his meal on his return, came into the presence of the Exalted One, saluted him, sat down at one side,

sn12.24:7.3.verse: and so seated told the Exalted One what that talk had been, even all of it.

sn12.24:8.1.verse: “Well done, well done, Ananda! Sariputta so answering would be answering rightly.

sn12.24:8.2.verse: I have said that ill happens through a cause.

sn12.24:8.5.verse: So saying one would be a repeater of my sayings; he would not be misrepresenting me by what is not correct, and no one who is of my doctrine, a follower of my views, would thereby render himself open to blame.

sn12.24:9.1.verse: In each of the four cases, Ananda, of those recluses and brahmins who believe in karma, ill will have been caused by contact.

sn12.24:10.1.verse: In no one of these four cases is it possible to show that those recluses and brahmins who believe in karma will experience ill without contact.

sn12.24:11.1.verse: I too, Ananda, was once staying here near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove at the Squirrels’ Feeding-ground.

sn12.24:11.4.verse: I, too, finding it too early to make my alms round,

sn12.24:11.5.verse: bethought me to go to the gardens of the heretical Wanderers.

sn12.24:12.1.verse: They told me of those four views on karma and asked me,

sn12.24:12.2.verse: What is the venerable Gotama’s view? What has he to announce to us? How answering, should we be repeating his views and should not be misrepresenting him by what is not correct?

sn12.24:13.1.verse: And I answered them even as Sariputta answered.”

sn12.24:17.2.verse: how the whole matter will have been said in one clause.

sn12.24:17.3.verse: If this matter were spoken in detail, it were deep and it would seem deep.”

sn12.24:18.1.verse: “Well then, Ananda, let just that reveal itself to you now.”

sn12.24:18.2.verse: “If, lord, they were to ask me:—

sn12.24:18.3.verse: ‘Decay-and-death, friend Ananda, what is its basis, what is its coming to pass, how is it brought to pass, what is its cause?’

sn12.24:18.5.verse: ‘Decay-and-death, friends, is based on birth, through birth it comes to pass, is brought to pass, birth is its cause.’

sn12.24:19.1.verse: Further, if they were to ask me the same concerning birth,

sn12.24:20.3.verse: And I should answer further that

sn12.24:21.9.verse: ‘And, friends, by the utter fading out and cessation of the six spheres of sense there is cessation of contact,

sn12.24:21.15.verse: from this, cessation of decay-and-death, yea, grief, lamenting, ill, sorrow and despair cease.

sn12.24:21.16.verse: Such is the ceasing of this entire mass of ill.

sn12.24:21.17.verse: So asked, lord, so should I make answer.”

sn12.25:1.2.verse: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Bhūmija came out of retreat, went to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

sn12.25:1.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to him:

sn12.25:2.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, there are ascetics and brahmins who teach the efficacy of deeds. Some of them assert that pleasure and pain are made by oneself.

sn12.25:2.2.verse: Some of them assert that pleasure and pain are made by another.

sn12.25:2.3.verse: Some of them assert that pleasure and pain are made by both oneself and another.

sn12.25:2.4.verse: Some of them assert that pleasure and pain arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another.

sn12.25:2.5.verse: What does the Buddha say about this? How does he explain it?

sn12.25:2.6.verse: How should we answer so as to repeat what the Buddha has said, and not misrepresent him with an untruth? How should we explain in line with his teaching, with no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?”

sn12.25:3.1.verse: “Reverend, the Buddha has said that pleasure and pain are dependently originated.

sn12.25:3.4.verse: In speaking like this, you would repeat what the Buddha has said, and not misrepresent him with an untruth. You would explain in line with his teaching, and there would be no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism.

sn12.25:4.1.verse: Consider the ascetics and brahmins who teach the efficacy of deeds. In the case of those who assert that pleasure and pain are made by oneself, that’s dependent on contact. …

sn12.25:4.4.verse: In the case of those who assert that pleasure and pain arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another, that’s also dependent on contact.

sn12.25:5.1.verse: Consider the ascetics and brahmins who teach the efficacy of deeds. In the case of those who assert that pleasure and pain are made by oneself, it’s impossible that they will experience that without contact. …

sn12.25:5.4.verse: In the case of those who assert that pleasure and pain arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another, it’s impossible that they will experience that without contact.”

sn12.25:6.1.verse: Venerable Ānanda heard this discussion between Venerable Sāriputta and Venerable Bhūmija.

sn12.25:6.2.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side,

sn12.25:6.3.verse: and informed the Buddha of all they had discussed.

sn12.25:7.1.verse: “Good, good, Ānanda! It’s just as Sāriputta has so rightly explained.

sn12.25:7.2.verse: I have said that pleasure and pain are dependently originated.

sn12.25:7.5.verse: In speaking like this, you would repeat what I have said, and not misrepresent me with an untruth. You would explain in line with my teaching, and there would be no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism.

sn12.25:8.1.verse: Consider the ascetics and brahmins who teach the efficacy of deeds. In the case of those who assert that pleasure and pain are made by oneself, that’s dependent on contact. …

sn12.25:8.4.verse: In the case of those who assert that pleasure and pain arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another, that’s also dependent on contact.

sn12.25:9.1.verse: Consider the ascetics and brahmins who teach the efficacy of deeds. In the case of those who assert that pleasure and pain are made by oneself, it’s impossible that they will experience that without contact. …

sn12.25:9.4.verse: In the case of those who assert that pleasure and pain arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another, it’s impossible that they will experience that without contact.

sn12.25:10.1.verse: Ānanda, as long as there’s a body, the intention that gives rise to bodily action causes pleasure and pain to arise in oneself.

sn12.25:10.2.verse: As long as there’s a voice, the intention that gives rise to verbal action causes pleasure and pain to arise in oneself.

sn12.25:10.3.verse: As long as there’s a mind, the intention that gives rise to mental action causes pleasure and pain to arise in oneself. But this is only when dependent on ignorance.

sn12.25:11.1.verse: By oneself one instigates the choice that gives rise to bodily, verbal, and mental action, conditioned by which that pleasure and pain arise in oneself.

sn12.25:11.2.verse: Or else others instigate the choice …

sn12.25:11.3.verse: One instigates the choice after deliberation …

sn12.25:11.4.verse: Or else one instigates the choice without deliberation …

sn12.25:14.1.verse: Ignorance is included in all these things.

sn12.25:14.2.verse: But when ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, that body, that voice, and that mind no longer exist dependent on which that pleasure and pain arise in oneself.

sn12.25:14.3.verse: That field does not exist, that ground does not exist, that dimension does not exist, that foundation does not exist, dependent on which that pleasure and pain arise in oneself.”

sn12.25:1.2.verse: Now the venerable Bhūmija, arising at eventide from solitary meditation, came into the presence of the venerable Sāriputta, and exchanging greetings with him and compliments of friendship and courtesy sat down at one side,

sn12.25:1.3.verse: and so seated said thus to him:—

sn12.25:2.1.verse: “There are, friend Sāriputta, certain recluses and brahmins, believers in karma, who declare that happiness and ill have been made by one's self;

sn12.25:2.2.verse: certain others who say that happiness and ill have been made by another;

sn12.25:2.3.verse: certain others who say both cases are true;

sn12.25:2.4.verse: certain others who say that neither case is true, but that happiness and ill arise by chance.

sn12.25:2.5.verse: Herein, friend Sāriputta, the Exalted One what has he to tell us?

sn12.25:2.6.verse: And how, if we were answering, should we be repeating his views correctly and not be misrepresenting him, nor rendering ourselves open to blame?”

sn12.25:3.1.verse: “The Exalted One has said, friend, that happiness and ill come to pass through a cause,

sn12.25:4.1.verse: In the case of those recluses and brahmins who believe in karma, however they say that happiness and ill have been made, it was because of contact that they came to pass.

sn12.25:5.1.verse: In no one of those four views is it possible to show that those recluses and brahmins will experience happiness or ill without contact.”

sn12.25:6.2.verse: and he went into the presence of the Exalted One

sn12.25:7.1.verse: And the Exalted One praised Sāriputta through him and confirmed all that he had said and said yet further:—

sn12.25:10.1.verse: “Where there have been deeds, Ānanda, personal happiness and suffering arise in consequence of the will there was in the deeds.

sn12.25:10.2.verse: Where there has been speech—where there has been thought, personal happiness and suffering arise in consequence of the will there was in the speech—in the thought.

sn12.25:11.1.verse: Either we of ourselves, Ānanda, plan those planned deeds conditioned by ignorance, whence so caused arises personal happiness and suffering.

sn12.25:11.2.verse: or others plan those planned deeds that we do conditioned by ignorance, whence so conditioned arises personal happiness and suffering.

sn12.25:12.1.verse: Thence both ways arises personal happiness and suffering. So also is it where there has been speech,

sn12.25:13.1.verse: Either we plan, speaking, thinking deliberately

sn12.25:13.2.verse: or others plan, so that we speak, think unwittingly.

sn12.25:13.4.verse: Thence arises personal happiness and suffering.

sn12.25:14.1.verse: In these six cases ignorance is followed after.

sn12.25:14.2.verse: But from the utter fading away and cessation of ignorance, Ānanda, those deeds are not, whence so conditioned arises personal happiness and suffering. Neither is that speech, nor that thought.

sn12.25:14.3.verse: As field they are not; as base they are not; as wherewithal they are not; as occasion they are not, that so conditioned there might arise personal happiness and suffering.”

sn12.26:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Upavāṇa went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn12.26:2.1.verse: “Sir, there are some ascetics and brahmins who assert that suffering is made by oneself.

sn12.26:2.2.verse: There are some who assert that suffering is made by another.

sn12.26:2.3.verse: There are some who assert that suffering is made by both oneself and another.

sn12.26:2.4.verse: There are some who assert that suffering arises anomalously, not made by oneself or another.

sn12.26:2.5.verse: What does the Buddha say about this? How does he explain it? How should we answer so as to repeat what the Buddha has said, and not misrepresent him with an untruth? How should we explain in line with his teaching, with no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?”

sn12.26:3.1.verse: “Upavāṇa, I have said that suffering is dependently originated.

sn12.26:3.4.verse: In speaking like this, you would repeat what I have said, and not misrepresent me with an untruth. You would explain in line with my teaching, and there would be no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism.

sn12.26:4.1.verse: In the case of those ascetics and brahmins who assert that suffering is made by oneself, that’s dependent on contact. …

sn12.26:4.4.verse: In the case of those who assert that suffering arises anomalously, not made by oneself or another, that’s also dependent on contact.

sn12.26:5.1.verse: In the case of those ascetics and brahmins who assert that suffering is made by oneself, it’s impossible that they will experience that without contact. …

sn12.26:5.4.verse: In the case of those who assert that suffering arises anomalously, not made by oneself or another, it’s impossible that they will experience that without contact.”

sn12.27:1.3.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …

sn12.27:1.4.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.27:2.1.verse: And what is old age and death?

sn12.27:2.2.verse: The old age, decrepitude, broken teeth, grey hair, wrinkly skin, diminished vitality, and failing faculties of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.

sn12.27:2.4.verse: The passing away, passing on, disintegration, demise, mortality, death, decease, breaking up of the aggregates, and laying to rest of the corpse of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.

sn12.27:2.6.verse: Such is old age, and such is death.

sn12.27:2.7.verse: This is called old age and death.

sn12.27:2.8.verse: Rebirth is the origin of old age and death.

sn12.27:2.9.verse: When rebirth ceases, old age and death cease.

sn12.27:2.10.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of old age and death is simply this noble eightfold path,

sn12.27:2.11.verse: that is: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn12.27:3.7.verse: And what are the six sense fields? …

sn12.27:3.8.verse: And what are name and form? …

sn12.27:4.2.verse: There are three kinds of choices.

sn12.27:4.3.verse: Choices by way of body, speech, and mind.

sn12.27:4.5.verse: Ignorance is the origin of choices.

sn12.27:4.7.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of choices is simply this noble eightfold path,

sn12.27:4.8.verse: that is: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn12.27:5.1.verse: When a noble disciple thus understands dependency, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation,

sn12.27:5.2.verse: that noble disciple is called: ‘one accomplished in view’, ‘one accomplished in vision’, ‘one who has come to the true teaching’, ‘one who sees this true teaching’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s insight’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s knowledge’, ‘one who has entered the stream of the teaching’, ‘a noble one with penetrative wisdom’, and also ‘one who stands pressing against the door to freedom from death’.”

sn12.28:1.3.verse: “A mendicant understands old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation. They understand rebirth …

sn12.28:1.12.verse: They understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.28:2.1.verse: And what is old age and death?

sn12.28:2.2.verse: The old age, decrepitude, broken teeth, grey hair, wrinkly skin, diminished vitality, and failing faculties of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.

sn12.28:2.4.verse: The passing away, passing on, disintegration, demise, mortality, death, decease, breaking up of the aggregates, and laying to rest of the corpse of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.

sn12.28:2.6.verse: Such is old age, and such is death.

sn12.28:2.7.verse: This is called old age and death.

sn12.28:2.8.verse: Rebirth is the origin of old age and death.

sn12.28:2.9.verse: When rebirth ceases, old age and death cease.

sn12.28:2.10.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of old age and death is simply this noble eightfold path,

sn12.28:2.11.verse: that is: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn12.28:4.2.verse: There are three kinds of choices.

sn12.28:4.3.verse: Choices by way of body, speech, and mind.

sn12.28:4.5.verse: Ignorance is the origin of choices.

sn12.28:4.7.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of choices is simply this noble eightfold path,

sn12.28:4.8.verse: that is: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn12.28:5.1.verse: A mendicant understands old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation. They understand rebirth …

sn12.28:5.13.verse: and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.28:5.14.verse: This mendicant is called: ‘one accomplished in view’, ‘one accomplished in vision’, ‘one who has come to the true teaching’, ‘one who sees this true teaching’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s insight’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s knowledge’, ‘one who has entered the stream of the teaching’, ‘a noble one with penetrative wisdom’, and also ‘one who stands pressing against the door to freedom from death’.”

sn12.29:1.3.verse: “There are ascetics and brahmins who don’t completely understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation. They don’t completely understand rebirth …

sn12.29:1.15.verse: and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.29:1.16.verse: I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

sn12.29:2.1.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who completely understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation. They completely understand rebirth …

sn12.29:2.10.verse: They completely understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.29:2.11.verse: I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

sn12.30:1.3.verse: “Mendicants, there are ascetics and brahmins who don’t understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation. It’s impossible that they will abide having transcended old age and death.

sn12.30:1.13.verse: They don’t understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation. It’s impossible that they will abide having transcended choices.

sn12.30:2.1.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who do understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation. It’s possible that they will abide having transcended old age and death.

sn12.30:2.11.verse: They understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

sn12.30:2.12.verse: It’s possible that they will abide having transcended choices.”

sn12.31:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī.

sn12.31:1.2.verse: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Sāriputta,

sn12.31:1.3.verse: “Sāriputta, this was said in ‘The Way to the Far Shore’, in ‘The Questions of Ajita’:

sn12.31:2.1.verse: ‘There are those who have appraised the teaching,

sn12.31:2.2.verse: and many kinds of trainees here.

sn12.31:2.3.verse: Now you, being alert, are asked

sn12.31:2.4.verse: to tell me their behavior, good fellow.’

sn12.31:3.1.verse: How should we see the detailed meaning of this brief statement?”

sn12.31:3.2.verse: When he said this, Sāriputta kept silent.

sn12.31:7.1.verse: “Sāriputta, do you see that this has come to be?”

sn12.31:7.2.verse: “Sir, one truly sees with right wisdom that this has come to be.

sn12.31:7.3.verse: Seeing this, one is practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding what has come to be.

sn12.31:7.4.verse: One truly sees with right wisdom that it came to be with that as fuel.

sn12.31:7.5.verse: Seeing this, one is practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding the fuel for its origination.

sn12.31:7.6.verse: One truly sees with right wisdom that when that fuel ceases, what has come to be is liable to cease.

sn12.31:7.7.verse: Seeing this, one is practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding what is liable to cease.

sn12.31:7.8.verse: In this way one is a trainee.

sn12.31:8.1.verse: And how, sir, has one appraised the teaching?

sn12.31:8.2.verse: Sir, one truly sees with right wisdom that this has come to be.

sn12.31:8.3.verse: Seeing this, one is freed by not grasping through disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding what has come to be.

sn12.31:8.4.verse: One truly sees with right wisdom that it came to be with that as fuel.

sn12.31:8.5.verse: Seeing this, one is freed by not grasping through disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding the fuel for its origination.

sn12.31:8.6.verse: One truly sees with right wisdom that when that fuel ceases, what has come to be is liable to cease.

sn12.31:8.7.verse: Seeing this, one is freed by not grasping through disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding what is liable to cease.

sn12.31:8.8.verse: In this way one has appraised the teaching.

sn12.31:8.9.verse: Sir, regarding what was said in ‘The Way to the Far Shore’, in ‘The Questions of Ajita’:

sn12.31:9.1.verse: ‘There are those who have appraised the teaching,

sn12.31:9.2.verse: and many kinds of trainees here.

sn12.31:9.3.verse: Now you, being alert, are asked

sn12.31:9.4.verse: to tell me their behavior, good fellow.’

sn12.31:10.1.verse: This is how I understand the detailed meaning of what was said in brief.”

sn12.31:11.1.verse: “Good, good, Sāriputta! (The Buddha repeated all of Sāriputta’s explanation, concluding:)

sn12.31:14.1.verse: This is how to see the detailed meaning of what was said in brief.”

sn12.32:1.2.verse: Then the mendicant Kaḷāra the Aristocrat went up to Venerable Sāriputta and exchanged greetings with him.

sn12.32:1.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to him,

sn12.32:1.4.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, the mendicant Phagguna of the Top-Knot has resigned the training and returned to a lesser life.”

sn12.32:1.5.verse: “That venerable mustn’t have gained any solace in this teaching and training.”

sn12.32:2.1.verse: “Well then, has Venerable Sāriputta found solace in this teaching and training?”

sn12.32:5.1.verse: Then Kaḷāra the Aristocrat went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

sn12.32:5.3.verse: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’”

sn12.32:6.1.verse: So the Buddha addressed one of the monks,

sn12.32:6.2.verse: “Please, monk, in my name tell Sāriputta that

sn12.32:6.4.verse: “Yes, sir,” that monk replied. He went to Sāriputta and said to him,

sn12.32:6.6.verse: “Yes, reverend,” replied Sāriputta. He went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

sn12.32:6.7.verse: “Sāriputta, is it really true that you have declared enlightenment:

sn12.32:6.8.verse: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place”’?”

sn12.32:6.9.verse: “Sir, I did not state the matter in these words and phrases.”

sn12.32:6.10.verse: “Sāriputta, no matter how a gentleman declares enlightenment, what he has declared should be regarded as such.”

sn12.32:6.11.verse: “Sir, did I not also say that

sn12.32:6.12.verse: I did not state the matter in these words and phrases?”

sn12.32:7.1.verse: “Sāriputta, suppose they were to ask you:

sn12.32:7.2.verse: ‘But Reverend Sāriputta, how have you known and seen so that you’ve declared enlightenment:

sn12.32:7.3.verse: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”’

sn12.32:8.1.verse: “Sir, if they were to ask me this,

sn12.32:8.5.verse: ‘Reverends, when the source of rebirth ended, I knew “it is ended”.

sn12.32:8.7.verse: I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’

sn12.32:8.8.verse: That’s how I’d answer such a question.”

sn12.32:9.1.verse: “But Sāriputta, suppose they were to ask you:

sn12.32:9.2.verse: ‘But what is the source, origin, birthplace, and inception of rebirth?’

sn12.32:9.4.verse: “Sir, if they were to ask me this,

sn12.32:9.7.verse: ‘Continued existence is the source, origin, birthplace, and inception of rebirth.’

sn12.32:9.8.verse: That’s how I’d answer such a question.”

sn12.32:10.1.verse: “But Sāriputta, suppose they were to ask you:

sn12.32:10.2.verse: ‘What is the source of continued existence?’

sn12.32:10.4.verse: “Sir, if they were to ask me this,

sn12.32:10.7.verse: ‘Grasping is the source of continued existence.’

sn12.32:10.8.verse: That’s how I’d answer such a question.”

sn12.32:11.1.verse: “But Sāriputta, suppose they were to ask you:

sn12.32:11.3.verse: But Sāriputta, suppose they were to ask you:

sn12.32:11.6.verse: “Sir, if they were to ask me this,

sn12.32:11.10.verse: That’s how I’d answer such a question.”

sn12.32:12.1.verse: “But Sāriputta, suppose they were to ask you:

sn12.32:12.2.verse: ‘But how have you known and seen so that the relishing of feelings is no longer present?’

sn12.32:12.4.verse: “Sir, if they were to ask me this,

sn12.32:12.11.verse: When I understood this, the relishing of feelings was no longer present.’

sn12.32:12.12.verse: That’s how I’d answer such a question.”

sn12.32:13.2.verse: The same point may also be briefly explained in this way:

sn12.32:14.1.verse: But Sāriputta, suppose they were to ask you:

sn12.32:14.2.verse: ‘But Reverend, how have you been liberated that you declare enlightenment:

sn12.32:14.3.verse: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”?’

sn12.32:14.5.verse: “Sir, if they were to ask me this,

sn12.32:14.9.verse: ‘Because of an inner release with the ending of all grasping, I live mindfully so that defilements don’t defile me and I don’t look down on myself.’

sn12.32:14.10.verse: That’s how I’d answer such a question.”

sn12.32:15.2.verse: The same point may also be briefly explained in this way:

sn12.32:15.3.verse: ‘I have no uncertainty regarding the defilements spoken of by the ascetic. I have no doubt that I’ve given them up.’”

sn12.32:15.4.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn12.32:15.5.verse: When he had spoken, the Holy One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling.

sn12.32:16.1.verse: Then, not long after the Buddha left, Venerable Sāriputta said to the mendicants,

sn12.32:16.2.verse: “Reverends, the Buddha asked me the first question without letting me know beforehand, so I hesitated.

sn12.32:16.3.verse: But when the Buddha agreed with my answer, I thought:

sn12.32:16.4.verse: ‘If the Buddha were to question me all day on this matter in different words and ways, I could answer all day with different words and ways.

sn12.32:16.5.verse: If he were to question me all night,

sn12.32:16.17.verse: or seven days and nights, I could answer in different words and ways for seven days and nights.’”

sn12.32:17.1.verse: Then Kaḷāra the Aristocrat went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

sn12.32:17.2.verse: “Sir, Venerable Sāriputta has roared his lion’s roar!”

sn12.32:17.3.verse: (And he told the Buddha all that Sāriputta had said.)

sn12.32:18.1.verse: “Mendicant, Sāriputta has clearly penetrated the principle of the teachings, so that he could answer any questions I might ask him in different words and ways up to the seventh day and night.”

sn12.33:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach forty-four grounds for knowledge.

sn12.33:1.3.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn12.33:2.1.verse: “And what are the forty-four grounds for knowledge?

sn12.33:2.2.verse: Knowledge of old age and death, knowledge of the origin of old age and death, knowledge of the cessation of old age and death, and knowledge of the practice that leads to the cessation of old age and death.

sn12.33:2.9.verse: Knowledge of the six sense fields …

sn12.33:2.12.verse: Knowledge of choices, knowledge of the origin of choices, knowledge of the cessation of choices, and knowledge of the practice that leads to the cessation of choices.

sn12.33:2.13.verse: These are called the forty-four grounds for knowledge.

sn12.33:3.1.verse: And what is old age and death?

sn12.33:3.2.verse: The old age, decrepitude, broken teeth, grey hair, wrinkly skin, diminished vitality, and failing faculties of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.

sn12.33:3.4.verse: The passing away, passing on, disintegration, demise, mortality, death, decease, breaking up of the aggregates, and laying to rest of the corpse of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.

sn12.33:3.6.verse: Such is old age, and such is death.

sn12.33:3.7.verse: This is called old age and death.

sn12.33:4.1.verse: Rebirth is the origin of old age and death.

sn12.33:4.2.verse: When rebirth ceases, old age and death cease.

sn12.33:4.3.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of old age and death is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn12.33:4.4.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn12.33:5.1.verse: A noble disciple understands old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation. This is their knowledge of the teaching.

sn12.33:5.2.verse: With this teaching that is seen, understood, immediately attained, and fathomed, they apply the method to the past and future.

sn12.33:6.1.verse: Whatever ascetics and brahmins in the past directly knew old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation, all of them directly knew these things in exactly the same way that I do now.

sn12.33:7.1.verse: Whatever ascetics and brahmins in the future will directly know old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation, all of them will directly know these things in exactly the same way that I do now.

sn12.33:8.1.verse: A noble disciple has purified and cleansed these two knowledges—

sn12.33:8.2.verse: knowledge of the teaching and inferential knowledge.

sn12.33:8.3.verse: When a noble disciple has done this, they’re one who is called ‘one accomplished in view’, ‘one accomplished in vision’, ‘one who has come to the true teaching’, ‘one who sees this true teaching’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s insight’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s knowledge’, ‘one who has entered the stream of the teaching’, ‘a noble one with penetrative wisdom’, and also ‘one who stands pressing against the door to freedom from death’.

sn12.33:9.7.verse: And what are the six sense fields? …

sn12.33:9.8.verse: And what are name and form? …

sn12.33:9.11.verse: There are three kinds of choices.

sn12.33:9.12.verse: Choices by way of body, speech, and mind.

sn12.33:10.1.verse: Ignorance is the origin of choices.

sn12.33:10.3.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of choices is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn12.33:10.4.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn12.33:11.1.verse: A noble disciple understands choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation. This is their knowledge of the teaching.

sn12.33:11.2.verse: With this teaching that is seen, understood, immediately attained, and fathomed, they apply the method to the past and future.

sn12.33:12.1.verse: Whatever ascetics and brahmins in the past directly knew choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation, all of them directly knew these things in exactly the same way that I do now.

sn12.33:13.1.verse: Whatever ascetics and brahmins in the future will directly know choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation, all of them will directly know these things in exactly the same way that I do now.

sn12.33:14.1.verse: A noble disciple has purified and cleansed these two knowledges—

sn12.33:14.2.verse: knowledge of the teaching and inferential knowledge.

sn12.33:14.3.verse: When a noble disciple has done this, they’re one who is called ‘one accomplished in view’, ‘one accomplished in vision’, ‘one who has come to the true teaching’, ‘one who sees this true teaching’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s insight’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s knowledge’, ‘one who has entered the stream of the teaching’, ‘a noble one with penetrative wisdom’, and also ‘one who stands pressing against the door to freedom from death’.”

sn12.34:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach seventy-seven grounds for knowledge.

sn12.34:1.3.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn12.34:2.1.verse: “And what are the seventy-seven grounds for knowledge?

sn12.34:2.2.verse: The knowledge that rebirth is a requirement for old age and death,

sn12.34:2.3.verse: and the knowledge that when rebirth doesn’t exist, there is no old age and death.

sn12.34:2.4.verse: Also regarding the past: the knowledge that rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, and the knowledge that when rebirth doesn’t exist, there is no old age and death.

sn12.34:2.5.verse: Also regarding the future: the knowledge that rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, and the knowledge that when rebirth doesn’t exist, there is no old age and death.

sn12.34:2.6.verse: And also their knowledge that even this knowledge of the stability of natural principles is liable to end, vanish, fade away, and cease.

sn12.34:3.1.verse: The knowledge that continued existence is a requirement for rebirth …

sn12.34:3.10.verse: The knowledge that ignorance is a requirement for choices, and the knowledge that when ignorance doesn’t exist, there are no choices.

sn12.34:3.11.verse: Also regarding the past: the knowledge that ignorance is a requirement for choices, and the knowledge that when ignorance doesn’t exist, there are no choices.

sn12.34:3.12.verse: Also regarding the future: the knowledge that ignorance is a requirement for choices, and the knowledge that when ignorance doesn’t exist, there are no choices.

sn12.34:3.13.verse: And also their knowledge that even this knowledge of the stability of natural principles is liable to end, vanish, fade away, and cease.

sn12.34:3.14.verse: These are called the seventy-seven grounds for knowledge.”

sn12.35:1.3.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …

sn12.35:1.4.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.”

sn12.35:1.5.verse: When this was said, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,

sn12.35:1.6.verse: “What are old age and death, sir, and who do they belong to?”

sn12.35:1.7.verse: “That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha. “You might say, ‘What are old age and death, and who do they belong to?’ Or you might say, ‘Old age and death are one thing, who they belong to is another.’ But both of these mean the same thing, only the phrasing differs.

sn12.35:1.8.verse: Mendicant, if you have the view that the soul and the body are one and the same, there is no living of the spiritual life.

sn12.35:1.9.verse: If you have the view that the soul is one thing, the body another, there is no living of the spiritual life.

sn12.35:1.10.verse: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:

sn12.35:1.11.verse: ‘Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death.’”

sn12.35:2.1.verse: “What is rebirth, sir, and who does it belong to?”

sn12.35:2.2.verse: “That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha. “You might say, ‘What is rebirth, and who does it belong to?’ Or you might say, ‘Rebirth is one thing, who it belongs to is another.’ But both of these mean the same thing, only the phrasing differs.

sn12.35:2.3.verse: Mendicant, if you have the view that the soul and the body are one and the same, there is no living of the spiritual life.

sn12.35:2.4.verse: If you have the view that the soul is one thing, the body another, there is no living of the spiritual life.

sn12.35:2.5.verse: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:

sn12.35:2.6.verse: ‘Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.’”

sn12.35:3.1.verse: “What is continued existence, sir, and who is it for?”

sn12.35:3.2.verse: “That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha. “You might say, ‘What is continued existence, and who does it belong to?’ Or you might say, ‘Continued existence is one thing, who it belongs to is another.’ But both of these mean the same thing, only the phrasing differs.

sn12.35:3.3.verse: Mendicant, if you have the view that the soul and the body are one and the same, there is no living of the spiritual life.

sn12.35:3.4.verse: If you have the view that the soul is one thing, the body another, there is no living of the spiritual life.

sn12.35:3.5.verse: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:

sn12.35:3.6.verse: ‘Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.’ …

sn12.35:3.10.verse: ‘The six sense fields are requirements for contact.’ …

sn12.35:3.11.verse: ‘Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.’ …

sn12.35:3.12.verse: ‘Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.’ …

sn12.35:4.1.verse: “What are choices, sir, and who do they belong to?”

sn12.35:4.2.verse: “That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha. “You might say, ‘What are choices, and who do they belong to?’ Or you might say, ‘Choices are one thing, who they belong to is another.’ But both of these mean the same thing, only the phrasing differs.

sn12.35:4.3.verse: Mendicant, if you have the view that the soul and the body are one and the same, there is no living of the spiritual life.

sn12.35:4.4.verse: If you have the view that the soul is one thing, the body another, there is no living of the spiritual life.

sn12.35:4.5.verse: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:

sn12.35:5.1.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, then any twists, ducks, and dodges are given up:

sn12.35:5.2.verse: ‘What are old age and death, and who do they belong to?’ or ‘old age and death are one thing, who they belong to is another’, or ‘the soul and the body are one and the same’, or ‘the soul is one thing, the body another.’

sn12.35:5.3.verse: These are all cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

sn12.35:6.1.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, then any twists, ducks, and dodges are given up:

sn12.35:6.2.verse: ‘What is rebirth, and who does it belong to?’ or ‘rebirth is one thing, who it belongs to is another’, or ‘the soul and the body are one and the same’, or ‘the soul is one thing, the body another.’

sn12.35:6.3.verse: These are all cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

sn12.35:7.1.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, then any twists, ducks, and dodges are given up:

sn12.35:8.1.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, then any twists, ducks, and dodges are given up:

sn12.35:8.2.verse: ‘What are choices, and who do they belong to?’ or ‘choices are one thing, who they belong to is another’, or ‘the soul and the body are one and the same’, or ‘the soul is one thing, the body another.’

sn12.35:8.3.verse: These are all cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.”

sn12.37:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, this body doesn’t belong to you or to anyone else.

sn12.37:1.3.verse: It’s old deeds, and should be seen as produced by choices and intentions, as something to be felt.

sn12.37:2.1.verse: A learned noble disciple carefully and rationally applies the mind to dependent origination itself:

sn12.37:2.2.verse: ‘So, when this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

sn12.37:2.3.verse: When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:

sn12.37:2.4.verse: Ignorance is a requirement for choices.

sn12.37:2.5.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …

sn12.37:2.6.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.37:2.7.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.

sn12.37:2.9.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’”

sn12.38:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, what you intend or plan, and what you have underlying tendencies for become a support for the continuation of consciousness.

sn12.38:1.3.verse: When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.

sn12.38:1.4.verse: When consciousness is established and grows, there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

sn12.38:1.5.verse: When there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, future rebirth, old age, and death come to be, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

sn12.38:1.6.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.38:2.1.verse: If you don’t intend or plan, but still have underlying tendencies, this becomes a support for the continuation of consciousness.

sn12.38:2.2.verse: When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.

sn12.38:2.3.verse: When consciousness is established and grows, there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

sn12.38:2.4.verse: When there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, future rebirth, old age, and death come to be, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

sn12.38:2.5.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.38:3.1.verse: If you don’t intend or plan or have underlying tendencies, this doesn’t become a support for the continuation of consciousness.

sn12.38:3.2.verse: With no support, consciousness is not established.

sn12.38:3.3.verse: When consciousness is not established and doesn’t grow, there’s no regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

sn12.38:3.4.verse: When there is no regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, future rebirth, old age, and death cease, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

sn12.38:3.5.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

sn12.39:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, what you intend or plan, and what you have underlying tendencies for become a support for the continuation of consciousness.

sn12.39:1.3.verse: When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.

sn12.39:1.4.verse: When consciousness is established and grows, name and form are conceived.

sn12.39:1.5.verse: Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.

sn12.39:1.6.verse: The six sense fields are requirements for contact.

sn12.39:1.7.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling. …

sn12.39:1.13.verse: sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress come to be.

sn12.39:1.14.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.39:2.1.verse: If you don’t intend or plan, but still have underlying tendencies, this becomes a support for the continuation of consciousness.

sn12.39:2.2.verse: When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.

sn12.39:2.3.verse: When consciousness is established and grows, name and form are conceived.

sn12.39:2.4.verse: Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields. …

sn12.39:2.5.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.39:3.1.verse: If you don’t intend or plan or have underlying tendencies, this doesn’t become a support for the continuation of consciousness.

sn12.39:3.2.verse: With no support, consciousness is not established.

sn12.39:3.3.verse: When consciousness is not established and doesn’t grow, name and form are not conceived.

sn12.39:3.4.verse: When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease. …

sn12.39:3.5.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

sn12.40:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, what you intend or plan, and what you have underlying tendencies for become a support for the continuation of consciousness.

sn12.40:1.3.verse: When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.

sn12.40:1.4.verse: When consciousness is established and grows, there is an inclination.

sn12.40:1.5.verse: When there is an inclination, there is coming and going.

sn12.40:1.6.verse: When there is coming and going, there is passing away and reappearing.

sn12.40:1.7.verse: When there is passing away and reappearing, future rebirth, old age, and death come to be, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

sn12.40:1.8.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.40:2.1.verse: If you don’t intend or plan, but still have underlying tendencies, this becomes a support for the continuation of consciousness.

sn12.40:2.2.verse: When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.

sn12.40:2.3.verse: When consciousness is established and grows, there is an inclination.

sn12.40:2.4.verse: When there is an inclination, there is coming and going.

sn12.40:2.5.verse: When there is coming and going, there is passing away and reappearing.

sn12.40:2.6.verse: When there is passing away and reappearing, future rebirth, old age, and death come to be, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

sn12.40:2.7.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.40:3.1.verse: If you don’t intend or plan or have underlying tendencies, this doesn’t become a support for the continuation of consciousness.

sn12.40:3.2.verse: With no support, consciousness is not established.

sn12.40:3.3.verse: When consciousness is not established and doesn’t grow, there’s no inclination.

sn12.40:3.4.verse: When there’s no inclination, there’s no coming and going.

sn12.40:3.5.verse: When there’s no coming and going, there’s no passing away and reappearing.

sn12.40:3.6.verse: When there’s no passing away and reappearing, future rebirth, old age, and death cease, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

sn12.40:3.7.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

sn12.41:1.2.verse: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Buddha said to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika:

sn12.41:2.1.verse: “Householder, when a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

sn12.41:2.2.verse: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’

sn12.41:3.1.verse: What are the five fears and enmities they have quelled?

sn12.41:3.2.verse: Anyone who kills living creatures brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. That fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from killing living creatures.

sn12.41:4.1.verse: Anyone who steals brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. That fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from stealing.

sn12.41:5.1.verse: Anyone who commits sexual misconduct brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. That fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from sexual misconduct.

sn12.41:6.1.verse: Anyone who lies brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. That fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from lying.

sn12.41:7.1.verse: Anyone who consumes beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. That fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants.

sn12.41:7.2.verse: These are the five fears and enmities they have quelled.

sn12.41:8.1.verse: What are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess?

sn12.41:8.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha:

sn12.41:8.3.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

sn12.41:9.1.verse: They have experiential confidence in the teaching:

sn12.41:9.2.verse: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

sn12.41:10.1.verse: They have experiential confidence in the Saṅgha:

sn12.41:10.2.verse: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

sn12.41:11.1.verse: And a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

sn12.41:11.2.verse: These are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess.

sn12.41:12.1.verse: And what is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom?

sn12.41:12.2.verse: A noble disciple carefully and rationally applies the mind to dependent origination itself:

sn12.41:12.3.verse: ‘So, when this exists, that comes to be; when this doesn’t exist, that is not.

sn12.41:12.4.verse: Due to the arising of this, that arises; due to the cessation of this, that ceases.

sn12.41:12.5.verse: Ignorance is a requirement for choices.

sn12.41:12.6.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …

sn12.41:12.7.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.41:12.8.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.

sn12.41:12.10.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’

sn12.41:12.11.verse: This is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom.

sn12.41:13.1.verse: When a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

sn12.41:13.2.verse: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

sn12.42:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

sn12.42:1.3.verse: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’

sn12.42:2.1.verse: What are the five fears and enmities they have quelled?

sn12.42:2.6.verse: consuming intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor …

sn12.42:2.7.verse: These are the five fears and enmities they have quelled.

sn12.42:3.1.verse: What are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess?

sn12.42:3.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn12.42:3.5.verse: and their ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones.

sn12.42:3.6.verse: These are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess.

sn12.42:4.1.verse: And what is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom?

sn12.42:4.2.verse: A noble disciple carefully and rationally applies the mind to dependent origination itself …

sn12.42:4.3.verse: This is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom.

sn12.42:5.1.verse: When a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

sn12.42:5.2.verse: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

sn12.43:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the origin and disappearance of suffering.

sn12.43:1.3.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn12.43:2.1.verse: “And what, mendicants, is the origin of suffering?

sn12.43:2.2.verse: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.

sn12.43:2.3.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn12.43:2.4.verse: Feeling is a requirement for craving. …

sn12.43:2.5.verse: This is the origin of suffering.

sn12.43:3.1.verse: Ear consciousness arises dependent on the ear and sounds. …

sn12.43:3.2.verse: Nose consciousness arises dependent on the nose and smells. …

sn12.43:3.3.verse: Tongue consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and tastes. …

sn12.43:3.4.verse: Body consciousness arises dependent on the body and touches. …

sn12.43:3.5.verse: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact.

sn12.43:3.6.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn12.43:3.7.verse: Feeling is a requirement for craving. …

sn12.43:3.8.verse: This is the origin of suffering.

sn12.43:4.1.verse: And what is the disappearance of suffering?

sn12.43:4.2.verse: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.

sn12.43:4.3.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn12.43:4.4.verse: Feeling is a requirement for craving.

sn12.43:4.5.verse: When that craving fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, grasping ceases.

sn12.43:4.6.verse: When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.

sn12.43:4.7.verse: When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.

sn12.43:4.8.verse: When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.

sn12.43:4.9.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

sn12.43:4.10.verse: This is the disappearance of suffering.

sn12.43:5.1.verse: Ear consciousness arises dependent on the ear and sounds. …

sn12.43:5.2.verse: Nose consciousness arises dependent on the nose and smells. …

sn12.43:5.3.verse: Tongue consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and tastes. …

sn12.43:5.4.verse: Body consciousness arises dependent on the body and touches. …

sn12.43:5.5.verse: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact.

sn12.43:5.6.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn12.43:5.7.verse: Feeling is a requirement for craving.

sn12.43:5.8.verse: When that craving fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, grasping ceases.

sn12.43:5.9.verse: When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.

sn12.43:5.10.verse: When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.

sn12.43:5.11.verse: When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.

sn12.43:5.12.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

sn12.43:5.13.verse: This is the disappearance of suffering.”

sn12.44:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the origin and disappearance of the world.

sn12.44:1.3.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn12.44:2.1.verse: “And what, mendicants, is the origin of the world?

sn12.44:2.2.verse: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.

sn12.44:2.3.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn12.44:2.4.verse: Feeling is a requirement for craving.

sn12.44:2.5.verse: Craving is a requirement for grasping.

sn12.44:2.6.verse: Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.

sn12.44:2.7.verse: Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.

sn12.44:2.8.verse: Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.

sn12.44:2.9.verse: This is the origin of the world.

sn12.44:3.1.verse: Ear consciousness arises dependent on the ear and sounds. …

sn12.44:3.2.verse: Nose consciousness arises dependent on the nose and smells. …

sn12.44:3.3.verse: Tongue consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and tastes. …

sn12.44:3.4.verse: Body consciousness arises dependent on the body and touches. …

sn12.44:3.5.verse: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact.

sn12.44:3.6.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling. …

sn12.44:3.7.verse: Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.

sn12.44:3.8.verse: This is the origin of the world.

sn12.44:4.1.verse: And what is the ending of the world?

sn12.44:4.2.verse: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.

sn12.44:4.3.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn12.44:4.4.verse: Feeling is a requirement for craving.

sn12.44:4.5.verse: When that craving fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, grasping ceases.

sn12.44:4.6.verse: When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases. …

sn12.44:4.7.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

sn12.44:4.8.verse: This is the ending of the world.

sn12.44:5.1.verse: Ear consciousness arises dependent on the ear and sounds. …

sn12.44:5.2.verse: Nose consciousness arises dependent on the nose and smells. …

sn12.44:5.3.verse: Tongue consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and tastes. …

sn12.44:5.4.verse: Body consciousness arises dependent on the body and touches. …

sn12.44:5.5.verse: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact.

sn12.44:5.6.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn12.44:5.7.verse: Feeling is a requirement for craving.

sn12.44:5.8.verse: When that craving fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, grasping ceases.

sn12.44:5.9.verse: When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases. …

sn12.44:5.10.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

sn12.44:5.11.verse: This is the ending of the world.”

sn12.45:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying at Ñātika in the brick house.

sn12.45:1.3.verse: Then while the Buddha was in private retreat he spoke this exposition of the teaching:

sn12.45:2.1.verse: “Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.

sn12.45:2.2.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn12.45:2.3.verse: Feeling is a requirement for craving.

sn12.45:2.4.verse: Craving is a requirement for grasping. …

sn12.45:2.5.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.45:3.1.verse: Ear consciousness arises dependent on the ear and sounds. …

sn12.45:3.2.verse: Nose consciousness arises dependent on the nose and smells. …

sn12.45:3.3.verse: Tongue consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and tastes. …

sn12.45:3.4.verse: Body consciousness arises dependent on the body and touches. …

sn12.45:3.5.verse: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact.

sn12.45:3.6.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn12.45:3.7.verse: Feeling is a requirement for craving.

sn12.45:3.8.verse: Craving is a requirement for grasping. …

sn12.45:3.9.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.45:4.1.verse: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.

sn12.45:4.2.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn12.45:4.3.verse: Feeling is a requirement for craving.

sn12.45:4.4.verse: When that craving fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, grasping ceases.

sn12.45:4.5.verse: When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases. …

sn12.45:5.3.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn12.45:5.4.verse: Feeling is a requirement for craving.

sn12.45:6.1.verse: Now at that time a certain monk was standing listening in on the Buddha.

sn12.45:6.4.verse: “Monk, did you hear that exposition of the teaching?”

sn12.45:6.9.verse: That exposition of the teaching is beneficial and relevant to the fundamentals of the spiritual life.”

sn12.46:1.2.verse: Then a certain brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

sn12.46:1.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

sn12.46:2.1.verse: “Worthy Gotama, are he who does the deed and he who experiences the result one and the same?”

sn12.46:2.2.verse: “‘He who does the deed and he who experiences the result are one and the same’: this is one extreme, brahmin.”

sn12.46:3.1.verse: “Then is he who does the deed one and he who experiences the result another?”

sn12.46:3.2.verse: “‘He who does the deed is one and he who experiences the result is another’: this is the second extreme.

sn12.46:3.3.verse: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:

sn12.46:3.5.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …

sn12.46:3.6.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.46:3.7.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, choices cease.

sn12.46:3.9.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’”

sn12.46:4.1.verse: When he said this, the brahmin said to the Buddha,

sn12.46:4.3.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

sn12.47:1.2.verse: Then the brahmin Jānussoṇi went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him. Seated to one side he said to the Buddha:

sn12.47:2.2.verse: “‘All exists’: this is one extreme, brahmin.”

sn12.47:3.2.verse: “‘All does not exist’: this is the second extreme.

sn12.47:3.3.verse: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:

sn12.47:3.5.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …

sn12.47:3.6.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.47:3.7.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.

sn12.47:3.9.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’”

sn12.47:4.1.verse: When he said this, the brahmin Jānussoṇi said to the Buddha,

sn12.47:4.3.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

sn12.48:1.2.verse: Then a brahmin cosmologist went up to the Buddha …

sn12.48:1.3.verse: Seated to one side he said to the Buddha:

sn12.48:2.2.verse: “‘All exists’: this is the oldest cosmology, brahmin.”

sn12.48:3.2.verse: “‘All does not exist’: this is the second cosmology.”

sn12.48:4.2.verse: “‘All is oneness’: this is the third cosmology.”

sn12.48:5.2.verse: “‘All is expansiveness’: this is the fourth cosmology.

sn12.48:6.1.verse: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:

sn12.48:6.3.verse: Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …

sn12.48:6.4.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.48:6.5.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, choices cease.

sn12.48:6.7.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’”

sn12.48:7.1.verse: When he said this, the brahmin cosmologist said to the Buddha,

sn12.48:7.3.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

sn12.49:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, a learned noble disciple doesn’t think:

sn12.49:1.4.verse: ‘When what exists, what is? Due to the arising of what, what arises?

sn12.49:1.5.verse: When what exists do name and form come to be? When what exists do the six sense fields … contact … feeling … craving … grasping … continued existence … rebirth … old age and death come to be?’

sn12.49:2.1.verse: Rather, a learned noble disciple has only knowledge about this that is independent of others:

sn12.49:2.2.verse: ‘When this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

sn12.49:2.3.verse: When ignorance exists choices come to be.

sn12.49:2.4.verse: When choices exist consciousness comes to be.

sn12.49:2.5.verse: When consciousness exists name and form come to be.

sn12.49:2.6.verse: When name and form exist the six sense fields come to be.

sn12.49:2.7.verse: When the six sense fields exist contact comes to be.

sn12.49:2.8.verse: When contact exists feeling comes to be.

sn12.49:2.9.verse: When feeling exists craving comes to be.

sn12.49:2.10.verse: When craving exists grasping comes to be.

sn12.49:2.11.verse: When grasping exists continued existence comes to be.

sn12.49:2.12.verse: When continued existence exists rebirth comes to be.

sn12.49:2.13.verse: When rebirth exists old age and death come to be.’

sn12.49:3.1.verse: A learned noble disciple doesn’t think:

sn12.49:3.3.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist, what is not? Due to the cessation of what, what ceases?

sn12.49:3.4.verse: When what doesn’t exist do choices not come to be? When what doesn’t exist do name and form not come to be? When what doesn’t exist do the six sense fields … contact … feeling … craving … grasping … continued existence … rebirth … old age and death not come to be?’

sn12.49:4.1.verse: Rather, a learned noble disciple has only knowledge about this that is independent of others:

sn12.49:4.2.verse: ‘When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases.

sn12.49:4.3.verse: When ignorance doesn’t exist choices don’t come to be.

sn12.49:4.4.verse: When choices don’t exist consciousness doesn’t come to be.

sn12.49:4.5.verse: When consciousness doesn’t exist name and form don’t come to be.

sn12.49:4.6.verse: When name and form don’t exist the six sense fields don’t come to be. …

sn12.49:4.7.verse: continued existence doesn’t come to be …

sn12.49:4.9.verse: When rebirth doesn’t exist old age and death don’t come to be.’

sn12.49:5.1.verse: A noble disciple comes to truly understand the origin and disappearance of the world. Such a noble disciple is one who is called ‘one accomplished in view’, ‘one accomplished in vision’, ‘one who has come to the true teaching’, ‘one who sees this true teaching’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s insight’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s knowledge’, ‘one who has entered the stream of the teaching’, ‘a noble one with penetrative wisdom’, and also ‘one who stands knocking at the door to freedom from death’.”

sn12.50:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, a learned noble disciple doesn’t think:

sn12.50:1.3.verse: ‘When what exists, what is? Due to the arising of what, what arises?

sn12.50:1.4.verse: When what exists do choices come to be? When what exists does consciousness come to be? When what exists do name and form … the six sense fields … contact … feeling … craving … grasping … continued existence … rebirth … old age and death come to be?’

sn12.50:2.1.verse: Rather, a learned noble disciple has only knowledge about this that is independent of others:

sn12.50:2.2.verse: ‘When this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.
