sn12.50:2.4.verse: When choices exist consciousness comes to be.

sn12.50:2.5.verse: When consciousness exists name and form come to be.

sn12.50:2.6.verse: When name and form exist the six sense fields come to be.

sn12.50:2.7.verse: When the six sense fields exist contact comes to be.

sn12.50:2.8.verse: When contact exists feeling comes to be.

sn12.50:2.9.verse: When feeling exists craving comes to be.

sn12.50:2.10.verse: When craving exists grasping comes to be.

sn12.50:2.11.verse: When grasping exists continued existence comes to be.

sn12.50:2.12.verse: When continued existence exists rebirth comes to be.

sn12.50:2.13.verse: When rebirth exists old age and death come to be.’

sn12.50:3.1.verse: A learned noble disciple doesn’t think:

sn12.50:3.2.verse: ‘When what doesn’t exist, what is not? Due to the cessation of what, what ceases?

sn12.50:3.3.verse: When what doesn’t exist do choices not come to be? When what doesn’t exist does consciousness not come to be? When what doesn’t exist do name and form … the six sense fields … contact … feeling … craving … grasping … continued existence … rebirth … old age and death not come to be?’

sn12.50:4.1.verse: Rather, a learned noble disciple has only knowledge about this that is independent of others:

sn12.50:4.2.verse: ‘When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:

sn12.50:4.3.verse: When ignorance doesn’t exists, choices don’t come to be.

sn12.50:4.4.verse: When choices don’t exist consciousness doesn’t come to be.

sn12.50:4.5.verse: When consciousness doesn’t exist name and form don’t come to be.

sn12.50:4.6.verse: When name and form don’t exist the six sense fields don’t come to be. …

sn12.50:4.7.verse: When rebirth doesn’t exist old age and death don’t come to be.’

sn12.50:5.1.verse: A noble disciple comes to truly understand the origin and disappearance of the world. Such a noble disciple is one who is called ‘one accomplished in view’, ‘one accomplished in vision’, ‘one who has come to the true teaching’, ‘one who sees this true teaching’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s insight’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s knowledge’, ‘one who has entered the stream of the teaching’, ‘a noble one with penetrative wisdom’, and also ‘one who stands pressing against the door to freedom from death’.”

sn12.51:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn12.51:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

sn12.51:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, when a mendicant is inquiring, how do you define when they are inquiring for the complete ending of suffering?”

sn12.51:2.2.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. He is our guide and our refuge. Sir, may the Buddha himself please clarify the meaning of this. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

sn12.51:2.3.verse: “Well then, mendicants, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn12.51:3.1.verse: “Mendicants, take a mendicant who makes an inquiry:

sn12.51:3.2.verse: ‘The suffering that arises in the world starting with old age and death takes many and diverse forms.

sn12.51:3.3.verse: What is the source, origin, birthplace, and inception of this suffering?

sn12.51:3.4.verse: When what exists do old age and death come to be? When what does not exist do old age and death not come to be?’

sn12.51:3.5.verse: While making an inquiry they understand:

sn12.51:3.6.verse: ‘The suffering that arises in the world starting with old age and death takes many and diverse forms. The source of this suffering is rebirth.

sn12.51:3.7.verse: When rebirth exists, old age and death come to be. When rebirth doesn’t exist, old age and death don’t come to be.’

sn12.51:4.1.verse: They understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the fitting practice for their cessation. And they practice in line with that path.

sn12.51:4.2.verse: This is called a mendicant who is practicing for the complete ending of suffering, for the cessation of old age and death.

sn12.51:5.2.verse: ‘But what is the source of this rebirth? When what exists does rebirth come to be? And when what does not exist does rebirth not come to be?’

sn12.51:5.3.verse: While making an inquiry they understand:

sn12.51:5.4.verse: ‘Continued existence is the source of rebirth.

sn12.51:5.5.verse: When continued existence exists, rebirth comes to be. When continued existence does not exist, rebirth doesn’t come to be.’

sn12.51:6.1.verse: They understand rebirth, its origin, its cessation, and the fitting practice for its cessation. And they practice in line with that path.

sn12.51:6.2.verse: This is called a mendicant who is practicing for the complete ending of suffering, for the cessation of rebirth.

sn12.51:7.2.verse: ‘But what is the source of this continued existence? …’ …

sn12.51:7.3.verse: ‘But what is the source of this grasping? …’ …

sn12.51:7.4.verse: ‘But what is the source of this craving? …’ …

sn12.51:7.5.verse: ‘But what is the source of this feeling? …’ …

sn12.51:7.6.verse: ‘But what is the source of this contact? …’ …

sn12.51:7.7.verse: ‘But what is the source of these six sense fields? …’ …

sn12.51:7.8.verse: ‘But what is the source of this name and form? …’ …

sn12.51:7.9.verse: ‘But what is the source of this consciousness? …’ …

sn12.51:7.10.verse: ‘But what is the source of these choices?

sn12.51:7.11.verse: When what exists do choices come to be? When what does not exist do choices not come to be?’

sn12.51:7.12.verse: While making an inquiry they understand:

sn12.51:7.14.verse: When ignorance exists, choices come to be. When ignorance does not exist, choices don’t come to be.’

sn12.51:8.1.verse: They understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the fitting practice for their cessation. And they practice in line with that path.

sn12.51:8.2.verse: This is called a mendicant who is practicing for the complete ending of suffering, for the cessation of choices.

sn12.51:9.1.verse: If an ignoramus makes a good choice, consciousness passes on by means of goodness.

sn12.51:9.2.verse: If they make a bad choice, consciousness passes on by means of badness.

sn12.51:9.3.verse: If they make an imperturbable choice, consciousness passes on by means of imperturbability.

sn12.51:9.4.verse: When a mendicant has given up ignorance and given rise to knowledge, with the fading away of ignorance and the arising of knowledge they don’t make a good choice, a bad choice, or an imperturbable choice.

sn12.51:9.5.verse: Not choosing or intending, they don’t grasp at anything in the world.

sn12.51:9.6.verse: Not grasping, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.

sn12.51:9.7.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

sn12.51:10.1.verse: If they feel a pleasant feeling, they understand that it’s impermanent, that they’re not attached to it, and that they don’t take pleasure in it.

sn12.51:10.2.verse: If they feel a painful feeling, they understand that it’s impermanent, that they’re not attached to it, and that they don’t take pleasure in it.

sn12.51:10.3.verse: If they feel a neutral feeling, they understand that it’s impermanent, that they’re not attached to it, and that they don’t take pleasure in it.

sn12.51:10.4.verse: If they feel a pleasant feeling, they feel it detached.

sn12.51:10.5.verse: If they feel a painful feeling, they feel it detached.

sn12.51:10.6.verse: If they feel a neutral feeling, they feel it detached.

sn12.51:11.1.verse: Feeling the end of the body draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of the body draw close.’ Feeling the end of life draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of life draw close.’

sn12.51:11.2.verse: They understand: ‘When my body breaks up and my life has come to an end, everything that’s felt, since I no longer take pleasure in it, will become cool right here. Only bodily remains will be left.’

sn12.51:12.1.verse: Suppose a person were to remove a hot clay pot from a potter’s kiln and place it down on level ground.

sn12.51:12.2.verse: Its heat would dissipate right there, and the shards would be left behind.

sn12.51:12.3.verse: In the same way, feeling the end of the body draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of the body draw close.’ Feeling the end of life draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of life draw close.’

sn12.51:12.4.verse: They understand: ‘When my body breaks up and my life has come to an end, everything that’s felt, since I no longer take pleasure in it, will become cool right here. Only bodily remains will be left.’

sn12.51:13.2.verse: Would a mendicant who has ended the defilements still make good choices, bad choices, or imperturbable choices?”

sn12.51:14.1.verse: “And when there are no choices at all, with the cessation of choices, would consciousness still be found?”

sn12.51:15.1.verse: “And when there’s no consciousness at all, would name and form still be found?”

sn12.51:16.1.verse: “And when there are no name and form at all, would the six sense fields still be found?”

sn12.51:17.1.verse: “And when there are no six sense fields at all, would contact still be found?”

sn12.51:18.1.verse: “And when there’s no contact at all, would feeling still be found?”

sn12.51:19.1.verse: “And when there’s no feeling at all, would craving still be found?”

sn12.51:20.1.verse: “And when there’s no craving at all, would grasping still be found?”

sn12.51:21.1.verse: “And when there’s no grasping at all, would continued existence still be found?”

sn12.51:22.1.verse: “And when there’s no continued existence at all, would rebirth still be found?”

sn12.51:23.1.verse: “And when there’s no rebirth at all, would old age and death still be found?”

sn12.51:24.1.verse: “Good, good, mendicants! That’s how it is, not otherwise.

sn12.51:24.2.verse: Trust me on this, mendicants; be convinced. Have no doubts or uncertainties in this matter.

sn12.51:24.3.verse: Just this is the end of suffering.”

sn12.52:1.2.verse: “There are things that fuel grasping. When you concentrate on the gratification provided by these things, your craving grows.

sn12.52:1.3.verse: Craving is a requirement for grasping.

sn12.52:1.4.verse: Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.

sn12.52:1.5.verse: Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.

sn12.52:1.6.verse: Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.

sn12.52:1.7.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.52:2.1.verse: Suppose a great mass of fire was burning with ten, twenty, thirty, or forty loads of wood.

sn12.52:2.2.verse: And from time to time someone would toss in dry grass, cow dung, or wood.

sn12.52:2.3.verse: Fed and fuelled by that, the great mass of fire would burn for a long time.

sn12.52:2.4.verse: In the same way, there are things that fuel grasping. When you concentrate on the gratification provided by these things, your craving grows.

sn12.52:2.5.verse: Craving is a requirement for grasping. …

sn12.52:2.6.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.52:3.1.verse: There are things that fuel grasping. When you concentrate on the drawbacks of these things, your craving ceases.

sn12.52:3.3.verse: When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.

sn12.52:3.4.verse: When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.

sn12.52:3.5.verse: When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.

sn12.52:3.6.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

sn12.52:4.1.verse: Suppose a great mass of fire was burning with ten, twenty, thirty, or forty loads of wood.

sn12.52:4.2.verse: And no one would toss in dry grass, cow dung, or wood from time to time.

sn12.52:4.3.verse: As the original fuel is used up and no more is added, the great mass of fire would be extinguished due to not being fed.

sn12.52:4.4.verse: In the same way, there are things that fuel grasping. When you concentrate on the drawbacks of these things, your craving ceases.

sn12.52:4.6.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

sn12.53:1.2.verse: “There are things that tighten the fetters. When you concentrate on the gratification provided by these things, your craving grows.

sn12.53:1.3.verse: Craving is a requirement for grasping.

sn12.53:1.4.verse: Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.

sn12.53:1.5.verse: Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.

sn12.53:1.6.verse: Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.

sn12.53:1.7.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.53:2.2.verse: And from time to time someone would pour oil in and adjust the wick.

sn12.53:2.3.verse: Fed and fuelled by that, the oil lamp would burn for a long time.

sn12.53:2.4.verse: In the same way, there are things that tighten the fetters. When you concentrate on the gratification provided by these things, your craving grows.

sn12.53:2.5.verse: Craving is a requirement for grasping.

sn12.53:2.9.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.53:3.3.verse: When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.

sn12.53:3.4.verse: When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.

sn12.53:3.5.verse: When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.

sn12.53:3.6.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

sn12.53:4.1.verse: Suppose an oil lamp depended on oil and a wick to burn.

sn12.53:4.2.verse: And no one would pour oil in and adjust the wick from time to time.

sn12.53:4.3.verse: As the original fuel is used up and no more is added, the oil lamp would be extinguished due to not being fed.

sn12.53:4.4.verse: In the same way, there are things that tighten the fetters. When you concentrate on the drawbacks of these things, your craving ceases.

sn12.53:4.6.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

sn12.55:2.1.verse: Suppose there was a great tree.

sn12.55:2.2.verse: And its roots going downwards and across all draw the sap upwards.

sn12.55:2.3.verse: Fed and fuelled by that, the great tree would stand for a long time.

sn12.55:2.4.verse: In the same way, there are things that fuel grasping. When you concentrate on the gratification provided by these things, your craving grows.

sn12.55:2.5.verse: Craving is a requirement for grasping. …

sn12.55:2.6.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.55:4.1.verse: Suppose there was a great tree.

sn12.55:4.2.verse: Then a person comes along with a spade and basket.

sn12.55:4.3.verse: They’d cut the tree down at the roots, dig it up, and pull the roots out, down to the fibers and stems.

sn12.55:4.4.verse: They’d cut the tree apart, cut up the parts, and chop it into splinters. They’d dry the splinters in the wind and sun, burn them with fire, and reduce them to ashes. Then they’d winnow the ashes in a strong wind, or float them away down a swift stream.

sn12.55:4.6.verse: In this way the great tree is cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

sn12.55:4.7.verse: In the same way, there are things that fuel grasping. When you concentrate on the drawbacks of these things, your craving ceases.

sn12.55:4.9.verse: When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases. …

sn12.55:4.10.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

sn12.58:1.2.verse: “There are things that tighten the fetters. When you concentrate on the gratification provided by these things, name and form are conceived.

sn12.58:1.3.verse: Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields. …

sn12.58:1.4.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn12.58:2.1.verse: Suppose there was a great tree.

sn12.58:3.1.verse: There are things that tighten the fetters. When you concentrate on the drawbacks of these things, name and form are not conceived.

sn12.58:3.2.verse: When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease. …

sn12.58:3.3.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

sn12.58:4.1.verse: Suppose there was a great tree.

sn12.60:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kurus, near the Kuru town named Kammāsadamma.

sn12.60:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn12.60:1.4.verse: in that this dependent origination is deep and appears deep, yet to me it seems as plain as can be.”

sn12.60:2.2.verse: This dependent origination is deep and appears deep.

sn12.60:2.3.verse: It is because of not understanding and not penetrating this teaching that this population has become tangled like string, knotted like a ball of thread, and matted like rushes and reeds, and it doesn’t escape the places of loss, the bad places, the underworld, transmigration.
