sn22.49:4.6.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

sn22.49:4.7.verse: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

sn22.49:4.15.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn22.49:4.17.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

sn22.49:4.18.verse: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

sn22.49:5.1.verse: “So, Soṇa, you should truly see any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

sn22.49:6.1.verse: You should truly see any kind of feeling …

sn22.49:6.4.verse: consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

sn22.49:7.1.verse: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn22.49:7.2.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

sn22.49:7.3.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.50:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

sn22.50:1.3.verse: Then the householder Soṇa went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

sn22.50:2.1.verse: “Soṇa, there are ascetics and brahmins who don’t understand form, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

sn22.50:2.5.verse: consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

sn22.50:2.6.verse: I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

sn22.50:3.1.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who do understand form, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

sn22.50:3.5.verse: consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

sn22.50:3.6.verse: I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

sn22.51:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, form really is impermanent. A mendicant sees that it is impermanent: that’s their right view.

sn22.51:1.4.verse: When relishing ends, greed ends. When greed ends, relishing ends.

sn22.51:1.5.verse: When relishing and greed end, the mind is freed, and is said to be well freed.

sn22.51:1.15.verse: Consciousness really is impermanent. A mendicant sees that it is impermanent: that’s their right view.

sn22.51:1.17.verse: When relishing ends, greed ends. When greed ends, relishing ends.

sn22.51:1.18.verse: When relishing and greed end, the mind is freed, and is said to be well freed.”

sn22.52:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, rationally apply the mind to form. Truly see the impermanence of form.

sn22.52:1.3.verse: When a mendicant does this, they grow disillusioned with form.

sn22.52:1.4.verse: When relishing ends, greed ends. When greed ends, relishing ends.

sn22.52:1.5.verse: When relishing and greed end, the mind is freed, and is said to be well freed.

sn22.52:1.6.verse: Rationally apply the mind to feeling …

sn22.52:1.15.verse: consciousness. Truly see the impermanence of consciousness.

sn22.52:1.16.verse: When a mendicant does this, they grow disillusioned with consciousness.

sn22.52:1.17.verse: When relishing ends, greed ends. When greed ends, relishing ends.

sn22.52:1.18.verse: When relishing and greed end, the mind is freed, and is said to be well freed.”

sn22.53:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, if you get involved, you’re not free. If you’re not involved, you’re free.

sn22.53:1.3.verse: Should consciousness involved with form, supported by form, established on form continue to remain, with a sprinkling of relishing it would grow, increase, and mature.

sn22.53:1.4.verse: Or should consciousness involved with feeling remain …

sn22.53:1.5.verse: Or should consciousness involved with perception remain …

sn22.53:1.6.verse: Or should consciousness involved with choices, supported by choices, established on choices continue to remain, with a sprinkling of relishing it would grow, increase, and mature.

sn22.53:2.2.verse: ‘Apart from form, feeling, perception, and choices, I will describe the coming and going of consciousness, its passing away and reappearing, its growth, increase, and maturity.’ That is not possible.

sn22.53:3.1.verse: If a mendicant has given up greed for the form element,

sn22.53:3.2.verse: the support is cut off, and there is no establishment of consciousness.

sn22.53:3.3.verse: If a mendicant has given up greed for the feeling element …

sn22.53:3.7.verse: the support is cut off, and there is no establishment of consciousness.

sn22.53:3.8.verse: Since that consciousness does not become established and does not grow, not making choices, it is freed.

sn22.53:3.9.verse: Being free, it’s stable. Being stable, it’s content. Being content, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.

sn22.53:3.10.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.54:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, there are five kinds of plants.

sn22.54:1.4.verse: Plants propagated from roots, trunks, cuttings, or joints; and those from regular seeds are the fifth.

sn22.54:1.5.verse: Suppose these five kinds of plants were intact, unspoiled, not weather-damaged, fertile, and well-kept. But there’s no earth or water.

sn22.54:1.6.verse: Then would these five kinds of plants reach growth, increase, and maturity?”

sn22.54:1.8.verse: “Suppose these five kinds of plants were intact, unspoiled, not weather-damaged, fertile, and well-kept. And there is earth and water.

sn22.54:1.9.verse: Then would these five kinds of plants reach growth, increase, and maturity?”

sn22.54:1.11.verse: “The four establishings of consciousness should be seen as like the earth element.

sn22.54:1.12.verse: Relishing and greed should be seen as like the water element.

sn22.54:1.13.verse: Consciousness with its fuel should be seen as like the five kinds of plants.

sn22.54:2.1.verse: Should consciousness involved with form, supported by form, established on form continue to remain, with a sprinkling of relishing it would grow, increase, and mature.

sn22.54:2.2.verse: Or should consciousness involved with feeling remain …

sn22.54:2.3.verse: Or should consciousness involved with perception remain …

sn22.54:2.4.verse: Or should consciousness involved with choices, supported by choices, established on choices continue to remain, with a sprinkling of relishing it would grow, increase, and mature.

sn22.54:3.2.verse: ‘Apart from form, feeling, perception, and choices, I will describe the coming and going of consciousness, its passing away and reappearing, its growth, increase, and maturity.’ That is not possible.

sn22.54:4.1.verse: If a mendicant has given up greed for the form element,

sn22.54:4.2.verse: the support is cut off, and there is no establishment of consciousness.

sn22.54:4.3.verse: If a mendicant has given up greed for the feeling element …

sn22.54:4.7.verse: the support is cut off, and there is no establishment of consciousness.

sn22.54:4.8.verse: Since that consciousness does not become established and does not grow, not making choices, it is freed.

sn22.54:4.9.verse: Being free, it’s stable. Being stable, it’s content. Being content, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.

sn22.54:4.10.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended … there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.55:1.2.verse: There the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:

sn22.55:1.3.verse: “‘It might not be, and it might not be mine. It will not be, and it will not be mine.’

sn22.55:1.4.verse: A mendicant who makes such a resolution can cut off the lower fetters.”

sn22.55:1.5.verse: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,

sn22.55:1.7.verse: can a mendicant who makes such a resolution cut off the lower fetters?”

sn22.55:2.1.verse: “Mendicant, take an unlearned ordinary person who has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in their teaching. They’ve not seen true persons, and are neither skilled nor trained in their teaching.

sn22.55:2.2.verse: They regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

sn22.55:2.6.verse: consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

sn22.55:3.1.verse: They don’t truly understand form—which is impermanent—as impermanent.

sn22.55:4.1.verse: They don’t truly understand form—which is suffering—as suffering.

sn22.55:5.1.verse: They don’t truly understand form—which is not-self—as not-self.

sn22.55:6.1.verse: They don’t truly understand form—which is conditioned—as conditioned.

sn22.55:6.6.verse: They don’t truly understand that form will vanish.

sn22.55:6.7.verse: They don’t truly understand that feeling …

sn22.55:7.1.verse: But a learned noble disciple has seen the noble ones, and is skilled and trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve seen true persons, and are skilled and trained in the teaching of the true persons.

sn22.55:7.2.verse: They don’t regard form as self …

sn22.55:8.1.verse: They truly understand form—which is impermanent—as impermanent.

sn22.55:8.6.verse: They truly understand form … feeling … perception … choices … consciousness—which is suffering—as suffering.

sn22.55:8.7.verse: They truly understand form … feeling … perception … choices … consciousness—which is not-self—as not-self.

sn22.55:8.8.verse: They truly understand form … feeling … perception … choices … consciousness—which is conditioned—as conditioned.

sn22.55:8.9.verse: They truly understand that form will vanish.

sn22.55:9.1.verse: It’s because of the vanishing of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness that a mendicant who makes such a resolution—

sn22.55:9.2.verse: ‘It might not be, and it might not be mine. It will not be, and it will not be mine’—

sn22.55:9.3.verse: can cut off the lower fetters.”

sn22.55:9.4.verse: “Sir, you say that a mendicant who makes such a resolution can cut off the lower fetters.

sn22.55:10.1.verse: But how are they to know and see in order to end the defilements without delay?”

sn22.55:10.2.verse: “Mendicant, an unlearned ordinary person worries about things that aren’t a worry.

sn22.55:10.3.verse: For an unlearned ordinary person worries:

sn22.55:10.4.verse: ‘It might not be, and it might not be mine. It will not be, and it will not be mine.’

sn22.55:11.1.verse: A learned noble disciple doesn’t worry about things that aren’t a worry.

sn22.55:11.2.verse: For a learned noble disciple doesn’t worry:

sn22.55:11.3.verse: ‘It might not be, and it might not be mine. It will not be, and it will not be mine.’

sn22.55:11.4.verse: Should consciousness involved with form, supported by form, established on form continue to remain, with a sprinkling of relishing it would grow, increase, and mature.

sn22.55:11.5.verse: Or should consciousness involved with feeling remain …

sn22.55:11.6.verse: Or should consciousness involved with perception remain …

sn22.55:11.7.verse: Or should consciousness involved with choices, supported by choices, established on choices continue to remain, with a sprinkling of relishing it would grow, increase, and mature.

sn22.55:12.1.verse: Suppose, mendicant, you were to say:

sn22.55:12.2.verse: ‘Apart from form, feeling, perception, and choices, I will describe the coming and going of consciousness, its passing away and reappearing, its growth, increase, and maturity.’ That is not possible.

sn22.55:13.1.verse: If a mendicant has given up greed for the form element, the support is cut off, and there is no establishment of consciousness.

sn22.55:13.2.verse: If a mendicant has given up greed for the feeling element …

sn22.55:13.5.verse: consciousness element, the support is cut off, and there is no establishment of consciousness.

sn22.55:13.6.verse: Since that consciousness does not become established and does not grow, not making choices, it is freed.

sn22.55:13.7.verse: Being free, it’s stable. Being stable, it’s content. Being content, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.

sn22.55:13.8.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended … there is nothing further for this place.’

sn22.55:13.9.verse: The ending of the defilements without delay is for one who knows and sees this.”

sn22.56:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five grasping aggregates.

sn22.56:1.4.verse: The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn22.56:1.5.verse: As long as I didn’t truly understand these five grasping aggregates in four rounds, I didn’t announce my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

sn22.56:1.6.verse: But when I did truly understand these five grasping aggregates in four rounds, I announced my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

sn22.56:2.1.verse: And how are there four rounds?

sn22.56:2.2.verse: I directly knew form, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

sn22.56:2.6.verse: consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

sn22.56:3.2.verse: The four principal states, and form derived from the four principal states.

sn22.56:3.6.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of form is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn22.56:3.7.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn22.56:4.1.verse: Whatever ascetics and brahmins have directly known form in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation—and are practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form: they are practicing well.

sn22.56:4.2.verse: Those who practice well have a footing in this teaching and training.

sn22.56:5.1.verse: Those ascetics and brahmins who have directly known form in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation—and due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form, are freed by not grasping: they are well freed.

sn22.56:5.2.verse: Those who are well freed are consummate ones.

sn22.56:5.3.verse: For consummate ones, there is no cycle of rebirths to be found.

sn22.56:6.2.verse: There are these six classes of feeling:

sn22.56:6.3.verse: feeling born of contact through the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

sn22.56:6.7.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of feelings is simply this noble eightfold path …

sn22.56:9.2.verse: There are these six classes of perception:

sn22.56:9.3.verse: perceptions of sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

sn22.56:9.7.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of perceptions is simply this noble eightfold path …

sn22.56:10.2.verse: There are these six classes of intention:

sn22.56:10.3.verse: intention regarding sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

sn22.56:10.7.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of choices is simply this noble eightfold path …

sn22.56:13.2.verse: There are these six classes of consciousness:

sn22.56:13.3.verse: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind consciousness.

sn22.56:13.5.verse: Consciousness originates from name and form.

sn22.56:13.6.verse: When name and form cease, consciousness ceases.

sn22.56:13.7.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of consciousness is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn22.56:13.8.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn22.56:14.1.verse: Whatever ascetics and brahmins have directly known consciousness in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation—and are practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding consciousness: they are practicing well.

sn22.56:14.2.verse: Those who practice well have a footing in this teaching and training.

sn22.56:15.1.verse: Those ascetics and brahmins who have directly known consciousness in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation—and due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding consciousness, are freed by not grasping: they are well freed.

sn22.56:15.2.verse: Those who are well freed are consummate ones.

sn22.56:15.3.verse: For consummate ones, there is no cycle of rebirths to be found.”

sn22.57:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, in this teaching and training a mendicant who is skilled in seven cases and who examines in three ways is called consummate, accomplished, a supreme person.

sn22.57:1.3.verse: And how is a mendicant skilled in seven cases?

sn22.57:1.4.verse: It’s when a mendicant understands form, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

sn22.57:1.5.verse: They understand form’s gratification, drawback, and escape.

sn22.57:1.9.verse: consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

sn22.57:1.10.verse: They understand consciousness’s gratification, drawback, and escape.

sn22.57:2.2.verse: The four principal states, and form derived from the four principal states.

sn22.57:2.6.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of form is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn22.57:2.7.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn22.57:3.1.verse: The pleasure and happiness that arise from form: this is its gratification.

sn22.57:3.3.verse: That form is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.

sn22.57:3.5.verse: Removing and giving up desire and greed for form: this is its escape.

sn22.57:4.1.verse: Those ascetics and brahmins who have directly known form in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation;

sn22.57:4.2.verse: its gratification, drawback, and escape—and are practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form: they are practicing well.

sn22.57:4.3.verse: Those who practice well have a footing in this teaching and training.

sn22.57:5.1.verse: Those ascetics and brahmins who have directly known form in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation;

sn22.57:5.2.verse: its gratification, drawback, and escape—and due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form, are freed by not grasping: they are well freed.

sn22.57:5.3.verse: Those who are well freed are consummate ones.

sn22.57:5.4.verse: For consummate ones, there is no cycle of rebirths to be found.

sn22.57:6.2.verse: There are these six classes of feeling:

sn22.57:6.8.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of feelings is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn22.57:6.9.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn22.57:7.1.verse: The pleasure and happiness that arise from feeling: this is its gratification.

sn22.57:7.3.verse: That feeling is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.

sn22.57:7.5.verse: Removing and giving up desire and greed for feeling: this is its escape. …

sn22.57:10.2.verse: There are these six classes of perception:

sn22.57:10.3.verse: perceptions of sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

sn22.57:10.7.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of perceptions is simply this noble eightfold path …

sn22.57:11.2.verse: There are these six classes of intention:

sn22.57:11.8.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of choices is simply this noble eightfold path …

sn22.57:14.2.verse: There are these six classes of consciousness:

sn22.57:14.3.verse: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind consciousness.

sn22.57:14.5.verse: Consciousness originates from name and form.

sn22.57:14.6.verse: When name and form cease, consciousness ceases.

sn22.57:14.7.verse: The practice that leads to the cessation of consciousness is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn22.57:14.8.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn22.57:15.1.verse: The pleasure and happiness that arise from consciousness: this is its gratification.

sn22.57:15.3.verse: That consciousness is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.

sn22.57:15.5.verse: Removing and giving up desire and greed for consciousness: this is its escape.

sn22.57:16.1.verse: Those ascetics and brahmins who have directly known consciousness in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation;

sn22.57:16.2.verse: its gratification, drawback, and escape—and are practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding consciousness: they are practicing well.

sn22.57:16.3.verse: Those who practice well have a footing  in this teaching and training.

sn22.57:17.1.verse: Those ascetics and brahmins who have directly known consciousness in this way—and its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation;

sn22.57:17.2.verse: its gratification, drawback, and escape—and due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding consciousness, are freed by not grasping: they are well freed.

sn22.57:17.3.verse: Those who are well freed are consummate ones.

sn22.57:17.4.verse: For consummate ones, there is no cycle of rebirths to be found.

sn22.57:17.5.verse: That’s how a mendicant is skilled in seven cases.

sn22.57:18.1.verse: And how does a mendicant examine in three ways?

sn22.57:18.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant examines by way of the elements, sense fields, and dependent origination.

sn22.57:18.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant examines in three ways.

sn22.57:18.4.verse: In this teaching and training, a mendicant who is skilled in seven cases and who examines in three ways is called consummate, accomplished, a supreme person.”

sn22.58:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha is freed by not grasping, due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form. They’re called a fully awakened Buddha.

sn22.58:1.3.verse: A mendicant freed by wisdom is also freed by not grasping, due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding form. They’re called a mendicant freed by wisdom.

sn22.58:2.1.verse: A Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha is freed by not grasping, due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding feeling …

sn22.58:3.3.verse: consciousness. They’re called a fully awakened Buddha.

sn22.58:3.4.verse: A mendicant freed by wisdom is also freed by not grasping, due to disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding consciousness. They’re called a mendicant freed by wisdom.

sn22.58:4.1.verse: What, then, is the difference between a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, and a mendicant freed by wisdom?”

sn22.58:4.2.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. He is our guide and our refuge. Sir, may the Buddha himself please clarify the meaning of this. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

sn22.58:4.3.verse: “Well then, mendicants, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn22.58:5.1.verse: “The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha gave rise to the unarisen path, gave birth to the unborn path, and explained the unexplained path. He is the knower of the path, the discoverer of the path, the expert on the path.

sn22.58:5.2.verse: And now the disciples live following the path; they acquire it later.

sn22.58:5.3.verse: This is the difference between a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, and a mendicant freed by wisdom.”

sn22.59:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

sn22.59:1.2.verse: There the Buddha addressed the group of five mendicants:

sn22.59:2.2.verse: For if form were self, it wouldn’t lead to affliction. And you could compel form:

sn22.59:2.3.verse: ‘May my form be like this! May it not be like that!’

sn22.59:2.4.verse: But because form is not-self, it leads to affliction. And you can’t compel form:

sn22.59:2.5.verse: ‘May my form be like this! May it not be like that!’

sn22.59:5.2.verse: For if consciousness were self, it wouldn’t lead to affliction. And you could compel consciousness:

sn22.59:5.3.verse: ‘May my consciousness be like this! May it not be like that!’

sn22.59:5.4.verse: But because consciousness is not-self, it leads to affliction. And you can’t compel consciousness:

sn22.59:5.5.verse: ‘May my consciousness be like this! May it not be like that!’

sn22.59:6.4.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn22.59:6.6.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

sn22.59:6.7.verse: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

sn22.59:6.14.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn22.59:6.16.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

sn22.59:6.17.verse: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

sn22.59:7.1.verse: “So you should truly see any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

sn22.59:8.1.verse: Any kind of feeling at all …

sn22.59:9.1.verse: Any kind of perception at all …

sn22.59:9.2.verse: Any kind of choices at all …

sn22.59:10.1.verse: You should truly see any kind of consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

sn22.59:11.1.verse: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn22.59:11.2.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

sn22.59:11.3.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.59:12.1.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn22.59:12.2.verse: Satisfied, the group of five mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

sn22.59:12.3.verse: And while this discourse was being spoken, the minds of the group of five mendicants were freed from defilements by not grasping.

sn22.60:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

sn22.60:1.3.verse: Then Mahāli the Licchavi went up to the Buddha … and said to him:

sn22.60:2.2.verse: ‘There is no cause or reason for the corruption of sentient beings.

sn22.60:2.3.verse: Sentient beings are corrupted without cause or reason.

sn22.60:2.4.verse: There’s no cause or reason for the purification of sentient beings.

sn22.60:2.5.verse: Sentient beings are purified without cause or reason.’

sn22.60:2.6.verse: What does the Buddha say about this?”

sn22.60:3.1.verse: “Mahāli, there is a cause and reason for the corruption of sentient beings.

sn22.60:3.2.verse: Sentient beings are corrupted with cause and reason.

sn22.60:3.3.verse: There is a cause and reason for the purification of sentient beings.

sn22.60:3.4.verse: Sentient beings are purified with cause and reason.”

sn22.60:4.1.verse: “But sir, what is the cause and reason for the corruption of sentient beings?

sn22.60:4.2.verse: How are sentient beings corrupted with cause and reason?”

sn22.60:5.1.verse: “Mahāli, if form were absolutely painful—soaked and steeped in pain and not steeped in pleasure—sentient beings wouldn’t be aroused by it.

sn22.60:5.2.verse: But because form is pleasurable—soaked and steeped in pleasure and not steeped in pain—sentient beings are aroused by it.

sn22.60:5.3.verse: Since they are aroused by it, they’re caught up in it, and so they become corrupted.

sn22.60:5.4.verse: This is a cause and reason for the corruption of sentient beings.

sn22.60:5.5.verse: This is how sentient beings are corrupted with cause and reason.

sn22.60:8.1.verse: consciousness were absolutely painful—soaked and steeped in pain and not steeped in pleasure—sentient beings wouldn’t be aroused by it.

sn22.60:8.2.verse: But because consciousness is pleasurable—soaked and steeped in pleasure and not steeped in pain—sentient beings are aroused by it.

sn22.60:8.3.verse: Since they are aroused by it, they’re caught up in it, and so they become corrupted.

sn22.60:8.4.verse: This is a cause and reason for the corruption of sentient beings.

sn22.60:8.5.verse: This is how sentient beings are corrupted with cause and reason.”

sn22.60:9.1.verse: “But sir, what is the cause and reason for the purification of sentient beings?

sn22.60:9.2.verse: How are sentient beings purified with cause and reason?”

sn22.60:9.3.verse: “Mahāli, if form was absolutely pleasurable—soaked and steeped in pleasure and not steeped in pain—sentient beings wouldn’t grow disillusioned with it.

sn22.60:9.4.verse: But because form is painful—soaked and steeped in pain and not steeped in pleasure—sentient beings do grow disillusioned with it.

sn22.60:9.5.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they are purified.

sn22.60:9.6.verse: This is a cause and reason for the purification of sentient beings.

sn22.60:9.7.verse: This is how sentient beings are purified with cause and reason.

sn22.60:10.4.verse: consciousness was absolutely pleasurable—soaked and steeped in pleasure and not steeped in pain—sentient beings wouldn’t grow disillusioned with it.

sn22.60:10.5.verse: But because consciousness is painful—soaked and steeped in pain and not steeped in pleasure—sentient beings do grow disillusioned with it.

sn22.60:10.6.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they are purified.

sn22.60:10.7.verse: This is a cause and reason for the purification of sentient beings.

sn22.60:10.8.verse: This is how sentient beings are purified with cause and reason.”

sn22.61:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are burning.

sn22.61:1.3.verse: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn22.61:1.4.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

sn22.61:1.5.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.62:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, there are these three scopes of definition, labeling, and description. They’re uncorrupted, as they have been since the beginning. They’re not being corrupted now, nor will they be. Sensible ascetics and brahmins don’t look down on them.

sn22.62:1.4.verse: When form has passed, ceased, and perished, its designation, label, and description is ‘was’.

sn22.62:4.1.verse: consciousness has passed, ceased, and perished, its designation, label, and description is ‘was’.

sn22.62:5.1.verse: When form is not yet born, and has not yet appeared, its designation, label, and description is ‘will be’.

sn22.62:8.1.verse: consciousness is not yet born, and has not yet appeared, its designation, label, and description is ‘will be’.

sn22.62:9.1.verse: When form has been born, and has appeared, its designation, label, and description is ‘is’.

sn22.62:12.1.verse: consciousness has been born, and has appeared, its designation, label, and description is ‘is’.

sn22.62:13.1.verse: These are the three scopes of definition, labeling, and description. They’re uncorrupted, as they have been since the beginning. They’re not being corrupted now, nor will they be. Sensible ascetics and brahmins don’t look down on them.

sn22.62:13.2.verse: Even those who were loud and bold advocates of the doctrines of no-cause, inaction, and nihilism, didn’t imagine that these three scopes of definition should be criticized or rejected.

sn22.62:13.4.verse: For fear of being blamed, attacked, provoked, and faulted.”

sn22.63:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn22.63:1.3.verse: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

sn22.63:1.4.verse: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

sn22.63:1.5.verse: “When you grasp, mendicant, you’re bound by Māra.

sn22.63:1.6.verse: Not grasping, you’re free from the Wicked One.”

sn22.63:2.1.verse: “But how do you see the detailed meaning of my brief statement?”

sn22.63:2.2.verse: “Sir, when you grasp form you’re bound by Māra.

sn22.63:2.3.verse: Not grasping, you’re free from the Wicked One.

sn22.63:2.9.verse: Not grasping, you’re free from the Wicked One.

sn22.63:2.10.verse: That’s how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement.”

sn22.63:3.2.verse: It’s good that you understand the detailed meaning of what I’ve said in brief like this.

sn22.63:3.3.verse: When you grasp form you’re bound by Māra.

sn22.63:3.4.verse: Not grasping, you’re free from the Wicked One.

sn22.63:3.9.verse: Not grasping, you’re free from the Wicked One.

sn22.63:3.10.verse: This is how to see the detailed meaning of what I said in brief.”

sn22.63:4.1.verse: And then that mendicant approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. He got up from his seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

sn22.63:4.2.verse: Then that mendicant, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

sn22.63:4.3.verse: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

sn22.63:4.4.verse: And that mendicant became one of the perfected.

sn22.71:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Rādha went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

sn22.71:1.3.verse: “Sir, how does one know and see so that there’s no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit for this conscious body and externally for all signs?”

sn22.71:1.4.verse: “Rādha, one truly sees any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

sn22.71:1.5.verse: One truly sees any kind of feeling …

sn22.71:1.8.verse: consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

sn22.71:1.9.verse: That’s how to know and see so that there’s no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit for this conscious body and externally for all signs.” …

sn22.71:1.10.verse: And Venerable Rādha became one of the perfected.

sn22.72:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Surādha said to the Buddha:

sn22.72:1.3.verse: “Sir, how does one know and see so that the heart is rid of I-making, mine-making, and conceit for this conscious body and externally for all signs; and going beyond discrimination, it’s peaceful and well freed?”

sn22.72:1.4.verse: “Surādha, one is freed by not grasping having truly seen any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

sn22.72:1.5.verse: One is freed by not grasping having truly seen any kind of feeling …
