sn22.136:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are burning chaff.

sn22.136:1.3.verse: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn22.136:1.4.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

sn22.136:1.5.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.137:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, you should give up desire for what is impermanent.

sn22.137:1.4.verse: Form is impermanent; you should give up desire for it.

sn22.137:1.8.verse: Consciousness is impermanent; you should give up desire for it.

sn22.137:1.9.verse: You should give up desire for what is impermanent.”

sn22.138:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, you should give up greed for what is impermanent.

sn22.138:1.4.verse: Form is impermanent; you should give up greed for it.

sn22.138:1.8.verse: Consciousness is impermanent; you should give up greed for it.

sn22.138:1.9.verse: You should give up greed for what is impermanent.”

sn22.139:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, you should give up desire and greed for what is impermanent.

sn22.139:1.4.verse: Form is impermanent; you should give up desire and greed for it.

sn22.139:1.8.verse: Consciousness is impermanent; you should give up desire and greed for it.

sn22.139:1.9.verse: You should give up desire and greed for what is impermanent.”

sn22.140:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, you should give up desire for what is suffering. …”

sn22.141:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, you should give up greed for what is suffering. …”

sn22.142:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, you should give up desire and greed for what is suffering. …”

sn22.143:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, you should give up desire for what is not-self. …”

sn22.144:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, you should give up greed for what is not-self. …”

sn22.145:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, you should give up desire and greed for what is not-self. …”

sn22.146:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith, this is what’s in line with the teaching.

sn22.146:1.3.verse: They should live full of disillusionment for form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn22.146:1.4.verse: Living in this way, they completely understand form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn22.146:1.5.verse: Completely understanding form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness, they’re freed from these things. They’re freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They’re freed from suffering, I say.”

sn22.147:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith, this is what’s in line with the teaching.

sn22.147:1.3.verse: They should meditate observing impermanence in form,

sn22.147:1.8.verse: They’re freed from suffering, I say.”

sn22.148:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith, this is what’s in line with the teaching.

sn22.148:1.3.verse: They should meditate observing suffering in form,

sn22.148:1.8.verse: They’re freed from suffering, I say.”

sn22.149:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith, this is what’s in line with the teaching.

sn22.149:1.3.verse: They should meditate observing not-self in form,

sn22.149:1.16.verse: They’re freed from suffering, I say.”

sn22.150:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what, do pleasure and pain arise in oneself?”

sn22.150:1.3.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn22.150:1.4.verse: “When form exists, because of grasping form, pleasure and pain arise in oneself.

sn22.150:1.8.verse: consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness, pleasure and pain arise in oneself.

sn22.150:1.12.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn22.150:1.14.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would pleasure and pain arise in oneself?”

sn22.150:1.21.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn22.150:1.23.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would pleasure and pain arise in oneself?”

sn22.150:1.26.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.151:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what,

sn22.151:1.3.verse: does someone regard things like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

sn22.151:1.4.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn22.151:1.5.verse: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form …

sn22.151:1.6.verse: When consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness and insisting on consciousness,

sn22.151:1.7.verse: someone regards it like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’

sn22.151:1.11.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would you regard it like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

sn22.151:1.18.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would you regard it like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

sn22.151:1.21.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.152:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, does the view arise:

sn22.152:1.3.verse: ‘The self and the cosmos are one and the same. After death I will be that, permanent, everlasting, eternal, and imperishable’?”

sn22.152:1.4.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn22.152:1.5.verse: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form, the view arises:

sn22.152:1.6.verse: ‘The self and the cosmos are one and the same. After death I will be that, permanent, everlasting, eternal, and imperishable.’

sn22.152:1.10.verse: consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness and insisting on consciousness, the view arises:

sn22.152:1.11.verse: ‘The self and the cosmos are one and the same. After death I will be that, permanent, everlasting, eternal, and imperishable.’

sn22.152:2.4.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn22.152:2.6.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would the view arise:

sn22.152:2.7.verse: ‘The self and the cosmos are one and the same. After death I will be that, permanent, everlasting, eternal, and imperishable’?”

sn22.152:2.14.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn22.152:2.16.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would the view arise:

sn22.152:2.17.verse: ‘The self and the cosmos are one and the same. After death I will be that, permanent, everlasting, eternal, and imperishable’?”

sn22.152:2.20.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.153:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, does the view arise:

sn22.153:1.3.verse: ‘I might not be, and it might not be mine. I will not be, and it will not be mine’?”

sn22.153:1.4.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn22.153:1.5.verse: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form, the view arises:

sn22.153:1.6.verse: ‘I might not be, and it might not be mine. I will not be, and it will not be mine.’

sn22.153:1.10.verse: consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness and insisting on consciousness, the view arises:

sn22.153:1.11.verse: ‘I might not be, and it might not be mine. I will not be, and it will not be mine.’

sn22.153:1.15.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn22.153:1.17.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would the view arise:

sn22.153:1.18.verse: ‘I might not be, and it might not be mine. I will not be, and it will not be mine’?”

sn22.153:1.25.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn22.153:1.27.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would the view arise:

sn22.153:1.28.verse: ‘I might not be, and it might not be mine. I will not be, and it will not be mine’?”

sn22.153:1.31.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.154:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, does wrong view arise?”

sn22.154:1.3.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn22.154:1.4.verse: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form, wrong view arises.

sn22.154:1.8.verse: consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness and insisting on consciousness, wrong view arises.

sn22.154:1.13.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would wrong view arise?”

sn22.154:1.20.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn22.154:1.22.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would wrong view arise?”

sn22.154:1.25.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.155:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, does substantialist view arise?”

sn22.155:1.3.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn22.155:1.4.verse: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form, substantialist view arises.

sn22.155:1.8.verse: consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness and insisting on consciousness, substantialist view arises.

sn22.155:1.13.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would substantialist view arise?”

sn22.155:1.21.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would substantialist view arise?”

sn22.155:1.24.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.156:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, does theory of self arise?”

sn22.156:1.3.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn22.156:1.4.verse: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form, theory of self arises.

sn22.156:1.8.verse: consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness and insisting on consciousness, theory of self arises.

sn22.156:1.13.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would theory of self arise?”

sn22.156:1.21.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would theory of self arise?”

sn22.156:1.24.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.157:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, do fetters, insistence, and shackles arise?”

sn22.157:1.3.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn22.157:1.4.verse: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form, fetters, insistence, and shackles arise.

sn22.157:1.8.verse: consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness and insisting on consciousness, fetters, insistence, and shackles arise.

sn22.157:1.13.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would fetters, insistence, and shackles arise?”

sn22.157:1.16.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.158:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, do fetters, insistence, shackles, and attachments arise?”

sn22.158:1.3.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn22.158:1.4.verse: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form, fetters, insistence, shackles, and attachments arise.

sn22.158:1.8.verse: consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness and insisting on consciousness, fetters, insistence, shackles, and attachments arise.

sn22.158:1.13.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would fetters, insistence, shackles, and attachments arise?”

sn22.159:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn22.159:1.3.verse: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

sn22.159:2.4.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn22.159:2.6.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

sn22.159:2.7.verse: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

sn22.159:2.14.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn22.159:2.16.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

sn22.159:2.17.verse: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

sn22.159:2.20.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn22.159:4.5.verse: The Linked Discourses on the aggregates are complete.

sn23.1:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Rādha went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn23.1:2.1.verse: “Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘Māra’.

sn23.1:2.3.verse: “When there is form, Rādha, there would be Māra, or the murderer, or the murdered.

sn23.1:2.4.verse: So you should see form as Māra, the murderer, the murdered, the diseased, the boil, the dart, the gloom, the gloominess.

sn23.1:2.5.verse: Those who see it like this see rightly.

sn23.1:2.9.verse: consciousness, there may be Māra, or the murderer, or the murdered.

sn23.1:2.10.verse: So you should see consciousness as Māra, the murderer, the murdered, the diseased, the boil, the dart, the gloom, the gloominess.

sn23.1:2.11.verse: Those who see it like this see rightly.”

sn23.1:3.1.verse: “But sir, what’s the purpose of seeing rightly?”

sn23.1:3.2.verse: “Disillusionment is the purpose of seeing rightly.”

sn23.1:3.9.verse: “But sir, what is the purpose of extinguishment?”

sn23.1:3.10.verse: “Your question goes too far, Rādha. You weren’t able to grasp the limit of questioning.

sn23.1:3.11.verse: For extinguishment is the objective, destination, and culmination of the spiritual life.”

sn23.2:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.2:1.3.verse: “Sir, they speak of this thing called a ‘sentient being’.

sn23.2:1.4.verse: How is a sentient being defined?”

sn23.2:1.5.verse: “Rādha, when you cling, strongly cling, to desire, greed, relishing, and craving for form, then a being is spoken of.

sn23.2:1.6.verse: When you cling, strongly cling, to desire, greed, relishing, and craving for feeling …

sn23.2:1.9.verse: consciousness, then a being is spoken of.

sn23.2:2.1.verse: Suppose some boys or girls were playing with sandcastles.

sn23.2:2.2.verse: As long as they’re not rid of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for those sandcastles, they cling to them, dally with them, treasure them, and treat them as their own.

sn23.2:2.3.verse: But when they are rid of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for those sandcastles, they scatter, smash, and destroy them with their hands and feet, making them unplayable.

sn23.2:2.4.verse: In the same way, you should scatter, smash, and destroy form, making it unplayable. And you should practice for the ending of craving.

sn23.2:2.5.verse: You should scatter, smash, and destroy feeling …

sn23.2:2.8.verse: consciousness, making it unplayable. And you should practice for the ending of craving.

sn23.2:2.9.verse: For the ending of craving is extinguishment.”

sn23.3:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.3:1.3.verse: “Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘the cessation of the leash to existence’.

sn23.3:1.4.verse: What is the leash to existence? And what is the cessation of the leash to existence?”

sn23.3:1.5.verse: “Rādha, any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for form; and any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies—

sn23.3:1.6.verse: this is called the leash to existence.

sn23.3:1.7.verse: Their cessation is the cessation of the leash to existence.

sn23.3:1.8.verse: Any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for feeling …

sn23.3:1.11.verse: consciousness; and any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies—

sn23.3:1.12.verse: this is called the leash to existence.

sn23.3:1.13.verse: Their cessation is the cessation of the leash to existence.”

sn23.4:1.2.verse: Venerable Rādha went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

sn23.4:2.1.verse: “Rādha, I will teach you the things that should be completely understood, complete understanding, and the individual who has completely understood.

sn23.4:2.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn23.4:2.5.verse: “And what things should be completely understood?

sn23.4:2.6.verse: Form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn23.4:2.7.verse: These are called the things that should be completely understood.

sn23.4:2.9.verse: The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn23.4:2.11.verse: And what is the individual who has completely understood?

sn23.4:2.12.verse: It should be said: a perfected one,

sn23.4:2.13.verse: the venerable of such name and such clan.

sn23.4:2.14.verse: This is called the individual who has completely understood.”

sn23.5:1.2.verse: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

sn23.5:1.3.verse: “Rādha, there are these five grasping aggregates.

sn23.5:1.5.verse: The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn23.5:1.6.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ gratification, drawback, and escape.

sn23.5:1.7.verse: I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

sn23.5:1.8.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who do truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ gratification, drawback, and escape.

sn23.5:1.9.verse: I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

sn23.6:1.2.verse: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

sn23.6:1.3.verse: “Rādha, there are these five grasping aggregates.

sn23.6:1.5.verse: The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn23.6:1.6.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape … Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin …

sn23.6:1.7.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who do truly understand … Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

sn23.7:1.2.verse: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

sn23.7:1.3.verse: “Rādha, there are these five grasping aggregates.

sn23.7:1.5.verse: The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn23.7:1.6.verse: When a noble disciple truly understands these five grasping aggregates’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape,

sn23.7:1.7.verse: they’re called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

sn23.8:1.2.verse: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

sn23.8:1.3.verse: “Rādha, there are these five grasping aggregates.

sn23.8:1.5.verse: The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn23.8:1.6.verse: A mendicant comes to be freed by not grasping after truly understanding these five grasping aggregates’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape.

sn23.8:1.7.verse: Such a mendicant is called a perfected one, with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment.”

sn23.9:1.2.verse: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

sn23.9:1.3.verse: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for form.

sn23.9:1.4.verse: Thus that form will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

sn23.9:1.5.verse: You should give up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for feeling …

sn23.9:1.11.verse: Thus that consciousness will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.”

sn23.10:1.2.verse: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

sn23.10:1.3.verse: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for form; and any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies.

sn23.10:1.4.verse: Thus that form will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

sn23.10:1.5.verse: You should give up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for feeling …

sn23.10:1.10.verse: consciousness; and any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies.

sn23.10:1.11.verse: Thus that consciousness will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.”

sn23.11:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.11:1.5.verse: “Rādha, form is Māra, feeling is Māra, perception is Māra, choices are Māra, consciousness is Māra.

sn23.11:1.6.verse: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn23.11:1.7.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

sn23.11:1.8.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn23.12:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.12:1.5.verse: “Rādha, form is of Māra nature. Feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are of Māra nature.

sn23.12:1.7.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn23.13:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.13:1.5.verse: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are impermanent.

sn23.13:1.7.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn23.14:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.14:1.5.verse: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are of impermanent nature.

sn23.14:1.7.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn23.15:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.15:1.5.verse: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are suffering.

sn23.15:1.7.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn23.16:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.16:1.4.verse: What is of a nature to suffer?”

sn23.16:1.5.verse: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are of a nature to suffer.

sn23.16:1.7.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn23.17:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.17:1.5.verse: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are not-self.

sn23.17:1.7.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn23.18:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.18:1.4.verse: What has a nature of not-self?”

sn23.18:1.5.verse: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a nature of not-self.

sn23.18:1.7.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn23.19:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.19:1.3.verse: “Sir, they speak of a ‘liability to end’.

sn23.19:1.4.verse: What has a liability to end?”

sn23.19:1.5.verse: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a liability to end.

sn23.19:1.7.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn23.20:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.20:1.3.verse: “Sir, they speak of a ‘liability to fall’.

sn23.20:1.4.verse: What has a liability to fall?”

sn23.20:1.5.verse: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a liability to fall.

sn23.20:1.7.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn23.21:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.21:1.3.verse: “Sir, they speak of a ‘liability to originate’.

sn23.21:1.4.verse: What has a liability to originate?”

sn23.21:1.5.verse: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a liability to originate.

sn23.21:1.7.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn23.22:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.22:1.3.verse: “Sir, they speak of a ‘liability to cease’.

sn23.22:1.4.verse: What has a liability to cease?”

sn23.22:1.5.verse: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a liability to cease.

sn23.22:1.7.verse: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn23.23:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.23:1.3.verse: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

sn23.23:2.1.verse: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is Māra.

sn23.23:2.3.verse: Form is Māra. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

sn23.23:2.7.verse: Consciousness is Māra. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

sn23.23:2.8.verse: You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is Māra.”

sn23.24:1.1.verse: “You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is of Māra nature …”

sn23.34:1.2.verse: Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

sn23.34:1.3.verse: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

sn23.34:2.1.verse: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is of a nature to cease.

sn23.34:2.2.verse: And what is of a nature to cease?

sn23.34:2.3.verse: Form is of a nature to cease. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

sn23.34:2.7.verse: Consciousness is of a nature to cease. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

sn23.34:2.8.verse: You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is of a nature to cease.”

sn23.35:1.2.verse: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

sn23.35:1.3.verse: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is Māra.

sn23.35:1.5.verse: Form is Māra. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it. …

sn23.35:1.6.verse: Consciousness is Māra. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

sn23.35:1.7.verse: You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is Māra.”

sn23.36:1.1.verse: “You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is subject to Māra …”

sn23.46:1.2.verse: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

sn23.46:1.3.verse: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is liable to cease.

sn23.46:1.4.verse: And what is liable to cease?

sn23.46:1.5.verse: Form is liable to cease. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

sn23.46:1.9.verse: Consciousness is liable to cease. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

sn23.46:1.10.verse: You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is liable to cease.”

sn23.46:2.7.verse: The Linked Discourses with Rādha are complete.

sn24.1:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove.

sn24.1:1.3.verse: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, does the view arise:

sn24.1:1.4.verse: ‘Winds don’t blow; rivers don’t flow; pregnant women don’t give birth; the moon and stars neither rise nor set, but stand firm like a pillar’?”

sn24.1:2.1.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. He is our guide and our refuge. Sir, may the Buddha himself please clarify the meaning of this. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

sn24.1:2.2.verse: “Well then, mendicants, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn24.1:3.1.verse: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form, the view arises:

sn24.1:3.2.verse: ‘Winds don’t blow; rivers don’t flow; pregnant women don’t give birth; the moon and stars neither rise nor set, but stand firm like a pillar.’

sn24.1:3.7.verse: ‘Winds don’t blow; rivers don’t flow; pregnant women don’t give birth; the moon and stars neither rise nor set, but stand firm like a pillar.’

sn24.1:3.11.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn24.1:3.13.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would the view arise:

sn24.1:3.14.verse: ‘Winds don’t blow; rivers don’t flow; pregnant women don’t give birth; the moon and stars neither rise nor set, but stand firm like a pillar’?”

sn24.1:4.6.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn24.1:4.8.verse: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would the view arise:

sn24.1:4.9.verse: ‘Winds don’t blow; rivers don’t flow; pregnant women don’t give birth; the moon and stars neither rise nor set, but stand firm like a pillar’?”

sn24.1:4.16.verse: ‘Winds don’t blow; rivers don’t flow; pregnant women don’t give birth; the moon and stars neither rise nor set, but stand firm like a pillar’?”

sn24.5:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, does the view arise:

sn24.5:1.3.verse: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.

sn24.5:1.4.verse: This person is made up of the four principal states. When they die, the earth in their body progresses and proceeds to the substance of earth. The water in their body progresses and proceeds to the substance of water. The fire in their body progresses and proceeds to the substance of fire. The air in their body progresses and proceeds to the substance of air.

sn24.5:1.5.verse: The faculties are transferred to space.

sn24.5:1.6.verse: Four men with a bier carry away the corpse.

sn24.5:1.7.verse: Their footprints show the way to the cremation ground.

sn24.5:1.9.verse: Offerings dedicated to the gods end in ashes.

sn24.5:1.10.verse: Giving is a doctrine of morons.

sn24.5:1.11.verse: When anyone affirms a positive teaching it’s just baseless, false nonsense.

sn24.5:1.12.verse: Both the foolish and the astute are annihilated and destroyed when their body breaks up, and don’t exist after death’?”

sn24.5:1.13.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn24.5:2.2.verse: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. …

sn24.5:2.3.verse: Both the foolish and the astute are annihilated and destroyed when their body breaks up, and don’t exist after death.’

sn24.6:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, does the view arise:

sn24.6:1.3.verse: ‘The one who acts does nothing wrong when they punish, mutilate, torture, aggrieve, oppress, intimidate, or when they encourage others to do the same. Nothing bad is done when they kill, steal, break into houses, plunder wealth, steal from isolated buildings, commit highway robbery, commit adultery, and lie.

sn24.6:1.4.verse: If you were to reduce all the living creatures of this earth to one heap and mass of flesh with a razor-edged chakram, no evil comes of that, and no outcome of evil.

sn24.6:1.5.verse: If you were to go along the south bank of the Ganges killing, mutilating, and torturing, and encouraging others to do the same, no evil comes of that, and no outcome of evil.

sn24.6:1.6.verse: If you were to go along the north bank of the Ganges giving and sacrificing and encouraging others to do the same, no merit comes of that, and no outcome of merit.

sn24.6:1.7.verse: In giving, self-control, restraint, and truthfulness there is no merit or outcome of merit’?”

sn24.6:1.8.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn24.6:2.2.verse: ‘The one who acts does nothing wrong …

sn24.6:2.3.verse: there is no merit or outcome of merit.’

sn24.7:1.3.verse: ‘There is no cause or reason for the corruption of sentient beings.

sn24.7:1.4.verse: Sentient beings are corrupted without cause or reason.

sn24.7:1.5.verse: There’s no cause or reason for the purification of sentient beings.

sn24.7:1.6.verse: Sentient beings are purified without cause or reason.

sn24.7:1.7.verse: There is no power, no energy, no human strength or vigor.

sn24.7:1.8.verse: All sentient beings, all living creatures, all beings, all souls lack control, power, and energy. Molded by destiny, circumstance, and nature, they experience pleasure and pain in the six classes of rebirth’?”

sn24.8:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, does the view arise:

sn24.8:1.3.verse: ‘There are these seven substances that are not made, not derived, not created, without a creator, barren, steady as a mountain peak, standing firm like a pillar.

sn24.8:1.4.verse: They don’t move or deteriorate or obstruct each other. They’re unable to cause pleasure, pain, or both pleasure and pain to each other.

sn24.8:1.6.verse: The substances of earth, water, fire, air; pleasure, pain, and the soul is the seventh.

sn24.8:1.7.verse: These seven substances are not made, not derived, not created, without a creator, barren, steady as a mountain peak, standing firm like a pillar.

sn24.8:1.8.verse: They don’t move or deteriorate or obstruct each other. They’re unable to cause pleasure, pain, or both pleasure and pain to each other.

sn24.8:1.9.verse: If you chop off someone’s head with a sharp sword, you don’t take anyone’s life.

sn24.8:1.10.verse: The sword simply passes through the gap between the seven substances.

sn24.8:1.11.verse: There are 1.4 million main wombs, and 6,000, and 600; 500 deeds, and five, and three; deeds and half-deeds; 62 paths of practice, 62 sub-eons, six classes of rebirth, and eight stages in a person’s life; 4,900 Ājīvaka ascetics, 4,900 wanderers, and 4,900 dragon abodes; 2,000 lordships, 3,000 hells, and 36 realms of dusky sky; seven percipient embryos, seven non-percipient embryos, seven knotless embryos, seven gods, seven mental heavens, seven goblins, seven streams, seven castoff incarnations and 700 castoff incarnations, seven downfalls and 700 downfalls, seven dreams and 700 dreams, and 8.4 million great eons—through all of which the foolish and the astute transmigrate before making an end of suffering.

sn24.8:1.12.verse: And here there is no such thing as this: “By this precept or observance or fervent austerity or spiritual practice I shall force unripened deeds to bear their fruit, or eliminate old deeds by experiencing their results little by little”—for that cannot be.

sn24.8:1.13.verse: Pleasure and pain are allotted. Transmigration lasts only for a limited period, so there’s no increase or decrease, no getting better or worse.

sn24.8:1.14.verse: It’s like how, when you toss a ball of string, it rolls away unraveling.

sn24.8:1.15.verse: In the same way, after transmigrating the foolish and the astute roll away unraveling as far as pleasure and pain extend’?”

sn25.1:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, the eye is impermanent, decaying, and perishing.

sn25.1:1.8.verse: Someone who has faith and confidence in these teachings is called a follower by faith. They’ve stepped into the sure path, they’ve stepped into the level of the true person, and they’ve passed beyond the level of the untrue person.

sn28.1:1.1.verse: At one time Venerable Sāriputta was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn28.1:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Sāriputta robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn28.1:1.3.verse: He wandered for alms in Sāvatthī. After the meal, on his return from almsround, he went to the Dark Forest for the day’s meditation,

sn28.1:1.4.verse: plunged deep into it, and sat at the root of a tree to meditate.

sn28.1:2.1.verse: Then in the late afternoon, Sāriputta came out of retreat and went to Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn28.1:2.2.verse: Venerable Ānanda saw him coming off in the distance,

sn28.1:2.4.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, your faculties are so very clear, and your complexion is pure and bright.

sn28.1:2.5.verse: What meditation were you practicing today?”

sn28.1:3.1.verse: “Reverend, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, I entered and remained in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn28.1:3.2.verse: But it didn’t occur to me:

sn28.1:3.3.verse: ‘I am entering the first absorption’ or ‘I have entered the first absorption’ or ‘I am emerging from the first absorption’.”

sn28.1:3.4.verse: “That must be because Venerable Sāriputta has long ago totally eradicated I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit.

sn28.1:3.5.verse: That’s why it didn’t occur to you:

sn28.1:3.6.verse: ‘I am entering the first absorption’ or ‘I have entered the first absorption’ or ‘I am emerging from the first absorption’.”

sn28.2:1.2.verse: Venerable Ānanda saw Venerable Sāriputta and said to him:

sn28.2:1.3.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, your faculties are so very clear, and your complexion is pure and bright.

sn28.2:1.4.verse: What meditation were you practicing today?”

sn28.2:2.1.verse: “Reverend, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected were stilled, I entered and remained in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn28.2:2.2.verse: But it didn’t occur to me:

sn28.2:2.3.verse: ‘I am entering the second absorption’ or ‘I have entered the second absorption’ or ‘I am emerging from the second absorption’.”

sn28.2:2.4.verse: “That must be because Venerable Sāriputta has long ago totally eradicated I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit.

sn28.2:2.5.verse: That’s why it didn’t occur to you:

sn28.2:2.6.verse: ‘I am entering the second absorption’ or ‘I have entered the second absorption’ or ‘I am emerging from the second absorption’.”

sn28.3:1.2.verse: Venerable Ānanda saw Venerable Sāriputta and said to him:

sn28.3:1.3.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, your faculties are so very clear, and your complexion is pure and bright.

sn28.3:1.4.verse: What meditation were you practicing today?”

sn28.3:2.1.verse: “Reverend, with the fading away of rapture, I entered and remained in the third absorption, where I meditated with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

sn28.3:2.2.verse: But it didn’t occur to me:

sn28.3:2.3.verse: ‘I am entering the third absorption’ or ‘I have entered the third absorption’ or ‘I am emerging from the third absorption’.”

sn28.3:2.4.verse: “That must be because Venerable Sāriputta has long ago totally eradicated I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit.

sn28.3:2.5.verse: That’s why it didn’t occur to you:

sn28.3:2.6.verse: ‘I am entering the third absorption’ or ‘I have entered the third absorption’ or ‘I am emerging from the third absorption’.”

sn28.4:1.2.verse: Venerable Ānanda saw Venerable Sāriputta and said to him:

sn28.4:1.3.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, your faculties are so very clear, and your complexion is pure and bright.

sn28.4:1.4.verse: What meditation were you practicing today?”

sn28.4:2.1.verse: “Reverend, with the giving up of pleasure and pain, and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, I entered and remained in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

sn28.4:2.2.verse: But it didn’t occur to me:

sn28.4:2.3.verse: ‘I am entering the fourth absorption’ or ‘I have entered the fourth absorption’ or ‘I am emerging from the fourth absorption’.”

sn28.4:2.4.verse: “That must be because Venerable Sāriputta has long ago totally eradicated I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit.

sn28.4:2.5.verse: That’s why it didn’t occur to you:

sn28.4:2.6.verse: ‘I am entering the fourth absorption’ or ‘I have entered the fourth absorption’ or ‘I am emerging from the fourth absorption’.”

sn28.5:1.3.verse: “Reverend, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, I entered and remained in the dimension of infinite space. …” …

sn28.6:1.3.verse: “Reverend, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, I entered and remained in the dimension of infinite consciousness. …” …

sn28.7:1.3.verse: “Reverend, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, I entered and remained in the dimension of nothingness. …” …

sn28.8:0.3.verse: The Dimension of Neither Perception Nor Non-Perception

sn28.8:1.3.verse: “Reverend, going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, I entered and remained in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. …” …

sn28.9:1.3.verse: “Reverend, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, I entered and remained in the cessation of perception and feeling.

sn28.9:1.4.verse: But it didn’t occur to me:

sn28.9:1.5.verse: ‘I am entering the cessation of perception and feeling’ or ‘I have entered the cessation of perception and feeling’ or ‘I am emerging from the cessation of perception and feeling’.”

sn28.9:1.6.verse: “That must be because Venerable Sāriputta has long ago totally eradicated I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit.

sn28.9:1.7.verse: That’s why it didn’t occur to you:

sn28.9:1.8.verse: ‘I am entering the cessation of perception and feeling’ or ‘I have entered the cessation of perception and feeling’ or ‘I am emerging from the cessation of perception and feeling’.”

sn28.10:1.1.verse: At one time Venerable Sāriputta was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

sn28.10:1.2.verse: Then he robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha for alms.

sn28.10:1.3.verse: After wandering indiscriminately for almsfood in Rājagaha, he ate his almsfood by a wall.

sn28.10:1.4.verse: Then the wanderer Sucimukhī went up to Venerable Sāriputta and said to him:

sn28.10:2.3.verse: “Well then, do you eat facing upwards?”

sn28.10:2.5.verse: “Well then, do you eat facing the cardinal directions?”

sn28.10:2.7.verse: “Well then, do you eat facing the intermediate directions?”

sn28.10:3.1.verse: “When asked if you eat facing all these directions, you answer ‘no, sister’.

sn28.10:4.1.verse: How then do you eat, ascetic?”

sn28.10:4.2.verse: “Sister, those ascetics and brahmins who earn a living by geomancy—a low lore, a wrong livelihood—are said to eat facing downwards.

sn28.10:4.3.verse: Those ascetics and brahmins who earn a living by astrology—a low lore, a wrong livelihood—are said to eat facing upwards.

sn28.10:4.4.verse: Those ascetics and brahmins who earn a living by running errands and messages—a wrong livelihood—are said to eat facing the cardinal directions.

sn28.10:4.5.verse: Those ascetics and brahmins who earn a living by limb-reading—a low lore, a wrong livelihood—are said to eat facing the intermediate directions.

sn28.10:5.1.verse: I don’t earn a living by any of these means.

sn28.10:5.2.verse: I seek alms in a principled manner,

sn28.10:5.3.verse: and I eat it in a principled manner.”

sn28.10:6.1.verse: Then Sucimukhī the wanderer went around Rājagaha from street to street and from square to square, and announced:

sn28.10:6.2.verse: “The ascetics who follow the Sakyan eat food in a principled manner!

sn28.10:6.3.verse: The ascetics who follow the Sakyan eat food blamelessly!

sn28.10:6.4.verse: Give almsfood to the ascetics who follow the Sakyan!”

sn28.10:7.7.verse: The Linked Discourses on Sāriputta are complete.

sn29.1:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, dragons reproduce in these four ways.

sn29.1:1.4.verse: Dragons are born from eggs, from a womb, from moisture, or spontaneously.

sn29.1:1.5.verse: These are the four ways that dragons reproduce.”

sn29.2:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, dragons reproduce in these four ways.

sn29.2:1.4.verse: Dragons are born from an egg, from a womb, from moisture, or spontaneously.

sn29.2:1.5.verse: Of these, dragons born from a womb, from moisture, or spontaneously are better than those born from an egg.

sn29.2:1.6.verse: Dragons born from moisture or spontaneously are better than those born from an egg or from a womb.

sn29.2:1.7.verse: Dragons born spontaneously are better than those born from an egg, from a womb, or from moisture.

sn29.2:1.8.verse: These are the four ways that dragons reproduce.”

sn29.3:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn29.3:1.2.verse: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn29.3:1.3.verse: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why some egg-born dragons keep the sabbath, having transformed their bodies?”

sn29.3:2.1.verse: “Mendicant, it’s when some egg-born dragons think:

sn29.3:2.2.verse: ‘In the past we did both kinds of deeds by body, speech, and mind.

sn29.3:2.3.verse: When the body broke up, after death, we were reborn in the company of the egg-born dragons.

sn29.3:2.4.verse: If today we do good things by body, speech, and mind, when the body breaks up, after death, we may be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn29.3:2.5.verse: Come, let us do good things by way of body, speech, and mind.’

sn29.3:2.6.verse: This is the cause, this is the reason why some egg-born dragons keep the sabbath, having transformed their bodies.”

sn32.53:1.3.verse: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why sometimes it becomes cool?”

sn33.1:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn33.1:1.2.verse: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

sn33.1:1.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

sn33.1:1.4.verse: “What is the cause, worthy Gotama, what is the reason why these various misconceptions arise in the world? That is:

sn33.1:1.5.verse: the cosmos is eternal, or not eternal, or finite, or infinite; the soul and the body are one and the same, or the soul is one thing, the body another; after death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists.”

sn33.1:1.10.verse: This is the cause, this is the reason.”

sn35.13:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, before my awakening—when I was still unawakened but intent on awakening—I thought:

sn35.13:1.3.verse: ‘What’s the gratification, the drawback, and the escape when it comes to the eye …

sn35.13:1.10.verse: ‘The pleasure and happiness that arise from the eye: this is its gratification.

sn35.13:1.11.verse: That the eye is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.

sn35.13:1.12.verse: Removing and giving up desire and greed for the eye: this is its escape.

sn35.13:1.13.verse: The pleasure and happiness that arise from the ear …

sn35.13:1.20.verse: That the mind is impermanent, suffering, and perishable: this is its drawback.

sn35.13:1.21.verse: Removing and giving up desire and greed for the mind: this is its escape.’

sn35.13:2.1.verse: As long as I didn’t truly understand these six interior sense fields’ gratification, drawback, and escape in this way for what they are, I didn’t announce my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

sn35.13:2.2.verse: But when I did truly understand these six interior sense fields’ gratification, drawback, and escape in this way for what they are, I announced my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

sn35.13:2.3.verse: Knowledge and vision arose in me:

sn35.13:2.4.verse: ‘My freedom is unshakable; this is my last rebirth; now there’ll be no more future lives.’”

sn35.17:1.18.verse: If the mind had no drawback, sentient beings wouldn’t grow disillusioned with it.

sn35.17:1.19.verse: But since the mind has a drawback, sentient beings do grow disillusioned with it.

sn35.17:1.20.verse: If there were no escape from the mind, sentient beings wouldn’t escape from it.

sn35.17:1.21.verse: But since there is an escape from the mind, sentient beings do escape from it.

sn35.17:2.1.verse: As long as sentient beings don’t truly understand these six interior sense fields’ gratification, drawback, and escape for what they are, they haven’t escaped from this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—and they don’t live detached, liberated, with mind free of boundaries.

sn35.17:2.2.verse: But when sentient beings truly understand these six interior sense fields’ gratification, drawback, and escape for what they are, they’ve escaped from this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—and they live detached, liberated, with mind free of boundaries.”

sn35.18:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, if there were no gratification in sights, sentient beings wouldn’t be aroused by them. …”

sn35.19:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, if you take pleasure in the eye, you take pleasure in suffering.

sn35.19:1.2.verse: If you take pleasure in suffering, you’re not free from suffering, I say.

sn35.19:1.3.verse: If you take pleasure in the ear …

sn35.19:1.8.verse: mind, you take pleasure in suffering.

sn35.19:1.9.verse: If you take pleasure in suffering, you’re not free from suffering, I say.

sn35.19:2.1.verse: If you don’t take pleasure in the eye, you don’t take pleasure in suffering.

sn35.19:2.2.verse: If you don’t take pleasure in suffering, you’re free from suffering, I say.

sn35.19:2.3.verse: If you don’t take pleasure in the ear …

sn35.19:2.8.verse: mind, you don’t take pleasure in suffering.

sn35.19:2.9.verse: If you don’t take pleasure in suffering, you’re free from suffering, I say.”

sn35.21:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, the arising, continuation, and manifestation and regeneration of the eye is the arising of suffering, the continuation of diseases, and the manifestation of old age and death.

sn35.21:1.2.verse: The arising, continuation, and manifestation and regeneration of the ear …

sn35.21:1.6.verse: and mind is the arising of suffering, the continuation of diseases, and the manifestation of old age and death.

sn35.21:2.1.verse: The cessation, settling, and disappearance of the eye is the cessation of suffering, the settling of diseases, and the disappearance of old age and death.

sn35.21:2.2.verse: The cessation, settling, and disappearance of the ear,

sn35.21:2.6.verse: and mind is the cessation of suffering, the settling of diseases, and the disappearance of old age and death.”

sn35.22:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, the arising, continuation, and manifestation and regeneration of sights is the arising of suffering, the continuation of diseases, and the manifestation of old age and death.

sn35.22:1.2.verse: The arising, continuation, and manifestation and regeneration of sounds,

sn35.22:1.6.verse: and ideas is the arising of suffering, the continuation of diseases, and the manifestation of old age and death.

sn35.22:2.1.verse: The cessation, settling, and disappearance of sights,

sn35.22:2.6.verse: and ideas is the cessation of suffering, the settling of diseases, and the disappearance of old age and death.”

sn35.23:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the all.

sn35.23:1.5.verse: It’s just the eye and sights, the ear and sounds, the nose and smells, the tongue and tastes, the body and touches, and the mind and ideas.

sn35.23:1.7.verse: Mendicants, suppose someone was to say:

sn35.23:1.8.verse: ‘I’ll deny this all and describe another all.’ They’d have no grounds for that claim,

sn35.23:1.9.verse: they’d be stumped by questions, and, in addition, they’d get frustrated.

sn35.23:1.11.verse: Because they’re out of their element.”

sn35.24:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the principle for giving up the all.

sn35.24:1.3.verse: And what is the principle for giving up the all?

sn35.24:1.4.verse: The eye should be given up. Sights should be given up. Eye consciousness should be given up. Eye contact should be given up. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact should also be given up.

sn35.24:1.8.verse: mind should be given up. Ideas should be given up. Mind consciousness should be given up. Mind contact should be given up. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact should be given up.

sn35.24:1.9.verse: This is the principle for giving up the all.”

sn35.28:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Gayā on Gayā Head together with a thousand mendicants.

sn35.28:1.2.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

sn35.28:1.4.verse: And what is the all that is burning?

sn35.28:1.5.verse: The eye is burning. Sights are burning. Eye consciousness is burning. Eye contact is burning. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact is also burning.

sn35.28:1.7.verse: Burning with the fires of greed, hate, and delusion. Burning with rebirth, old age, and death, with sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

sn35.28:1.11.verse: The mind is burning. Ideas are burning. Mind consciousness is burning. Mind contact is burning. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also burning.

sn35.28:1.13.verse: Burning with the fires of greed, hate, and delusion. Burning with rebirth, old age, and death, with sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress, I say.

sn35.28:1.14.verse: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact. And they grow disillusioned with the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact.

sn35.28:1.15.verse: They grow disillusioned with the ear … nose … tongue … body … mind … painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact.

sn35.28:1.16.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

sn35.28:1.17.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn35.28:2.1.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn35.28:2.2.verse: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

sn35.28:2.3.verse: And while this discourse was being spoken, the minds of the thousand mendicants were freed from defilements by not grasping.

sn35.29:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

sn35.29:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

sn35.29:1.5.verse: And what is the all that is overcome?

sn35.29:1.6.verse: The eye is overcome. Sights are overcome. Eye consciousness is overcome. Eye contact is overcome. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact is also overcome.

sn35.29:1.8.verse: Overcome by the fires of greed, hate, and delusion. Overcome by rebirth, old age, and death, by sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress, I say.

sn35.29:1.13.verse: mind is overcome. Ideas are overcome. Mind consciousness is overcome. Mind contact is overcome. The painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is also overcome.

sn35.29:1.15.verse: Overcome by greed, hate, and delusion. Overcome by rebirth, old age, and death, by sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress, I say.

sn35.30:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the practice fit for uprooting all conceiving.

sn35.30:1.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak. …

sn35.30:1.3.verse: And what is the practice fit for uprooting all conceiving?

sn35.30:1.4.verse: It’s when a mendicant does not conceive anything to be the eye, does not conceive it in the eye, does not conceive it as the eye, and does not conceive that ‘the eye is mine.’

sn35.30:1.5.verse: They don’t conceive anything to be sights, they don’t conceive it in sights, they don’t conceive it as sights, and they don’t conceive that ‘sights are mine.’

sn35.30:1.8.verse: They don’t conceive anything to be the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact. They don’t conceive it in that, they don’t conceive it as that, and they don’t conceive that ‘that is mine.’

sn35.30:1.9.verse: They don’t conceive anything to be the ear … nose … tongue …

sn35.30:1.18.verse: They don’t conceive anything to be the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact. They don’t conceive it in that, they don’t conceive it as that, and they don’t conceive that ‘that is mine.’

sn35.30:1.19.verse: They don’t conceive anything to be all, they don’t conceive it in all, they don’t conceive it as all, and they don’t conceive that ‘all is mine.’

sn35.30:1.20.verse: Not conceiving, they don’t grasp at anything in the world.

sn35.30:1.21.verse: Not grasping, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.

sn35.30:1.22.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

sn35.30:1.23.verse: This is the practice fit for uprooting all conceiving.”

sn35.31:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the practice that’s conducive to uprooting all conceiving.

sn35.31:1.3.verse: And what is the practice that’s conducive to uprooting all conceiving?

sn35.31:1.4.verse: It’s when a mendicant does not conceive anything to be the eye, does not conceive it in the eye, does not conceive it as the eye, and does not conceive that ‘the eye is mine.’

sn35.31:1.5.verse: They don’t conceive anything to be sights …

sn35.31:1.6.verse: eye consciousness … eye contact. And they don’t conceive anything to be the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact. They don’t conceive it in that, they don’t conceive it as that, and they don’t conceive that ‘that is mine.’

sn35.31:1.7.verse: For whatever you conceive it to be, whatever you conceive it in, whatever you conceive it as, and whatever you conceive to be ‘mine’: that becomes something else.

sn35.31:1.8.verse: The world is attached to being, taking pleasure only in being, yet it becomes something else.

sn35.31:1.9.verse: They don’t conceive anything to be the ear … nose … tongue …

sn35.31:1.18.verse: They don’t conceive anything to be the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact. They don’t conceive it in that, they don’t conceive it as that, and they don’t conceive that ‘that is mine.’

sn35.31:1.19.verse: For whatever you conceive it to be, whatever you conceive it in, whatever you conceive it as, and whatever you conceive to be ‘mine’: that becomes something else.

sn35.31:1.20.verse: The world is attached to being, taking pleasure only in being, yet it becomes something else.

sn35.31:1.21.verse: As far as the aggregates, elements, and sense fields extend, they don’t conceive anything to be that, they don’t conceive it in that, they don’t conceive it as that, and they don’t conceive that ‘that is mine.’

sn35.31:1.22.verse: Not conceiving, they don’t grasp at anything in the world.

sn35.31:1.23.verse: Not grasping, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.

sn35.31:1.24.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

sn35.31:1.25.verse: This is the practice that’s conducive to uprooting all conceiving.”

sn35.53:1.2.verse: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn35.53:1.3.verse: “Sir, how does one know and see so as to give up ignorance and give rise to knowledge?”

sn35.53:2.1.verse: “Mendicant, knowing and seeing the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact as impermanent, ignorance is given up and knowledge arises.

sn35.53:2.5.verse: And also knowing and seeing the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact as impermanent, ignorance is given up and knowledge arises.

sn35.53:2.10.verse: Knowing and seeing the mind, ideas, mind consciousness, and mind contact as impermanent, ignorance is given up and knowledge arises.

sn35.53:2.14.verse: And also knowing and seeing the pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact as impermanent, ignorance is given up and knowledge arises.

sn35.53:2.15.verse: That’s how to know and see so as to give up ignorance and give rise to knowledge.”

sn35.60:0.3.verse: The Complete Understanding of All Grasping

sn35.60:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the principle for the complete understanding of all grasping.

sn35.60:1.3.verse: And what is the principle for the complete understanding of all grasping?

sn35.60:1.4.verse: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.

sn35.60:1.5.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn35.60:1.6.verse: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, sights, eye consciousness, eye contact, and feeling.

sn35.60:1.7.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they are liberated, they understand: ‘I have completely understood grasping.’

sn35.60:1.8.verse: Ear consciousness arises dependent on the ear and sounds. …

sn35.60:1.9.verse: Nose consciousness arises dependent on the nose and smells. …

sn35.60:1.10.verse: Tongue consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and tastes. …

sn35.60:1.11.verse: Body consciousness arises dependent on the body and touches. …

sn35.60:1.12.verse: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact.

sn35.60:1.13.verse: Contact is a requirement for feeling.

sn35.60:1.14.verse: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the mind, ideas, mind consciousness, mind contact, and feeling.

sn35.60:1.15.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they are liberated, they understand: ‘I have completely understood grasping.’

sn35.60:1.16.verse: This is the principle for the complete understanding of all grasping.”

sn35.61:1.7.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they are liberated, they understand: ‘I have completely depleted fuel for grasping.’

sn35.61:1.12.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they are liberated, they understand: ‘I have completely depleted fuel for grasping.’

sn35.62:0.3.verse: The Depletion of All Fuel for Grasping (2nd)

sn35.62:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the principle for depleting all fuel for grasping.

sn35.62:1.3.verse: And what is the principle for depleting all fuel for grasping?

sn35.62:2.2.verse: Is the eye permanent or impermanent?”

sn35.62:4.1.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn35.62:6.1.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

sn35.62:6.2.verse: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

sn35.62:12.1.verse: The pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact: is that permanent or impermanent?”

sn35.62:14.9.verse: The pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact: is that permanent or impermanent?”

sn35.62:16.1.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn35.62:18.1.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

sn35.62:18.2.verse: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

sn35.62:20.1.verse: “Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact.

sn35.62:20.2.verse: And they grow disillusioned with the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact.

sn35.62:20.3.verse: They grow disillusioned with the ear … nose … tongue … body …

sn35.62:20.4.verse: They grow disillusioned with the mind, ideas, mind consciousness, and mind contact.

sn35.62:20.5.verse: And they grow disillusioned with the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact.

sn35.62:20.6.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

sn35.62:20.7.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

sn35.62:20.8.verse: This is the principle for depleting all fuel for grasping.”

sn35.63:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Migajāla went up to the Buddha …

sn35.63:1.4.verse: “Sir, they speak of one who lives alone.

sn35.63:1.5.verse: How is one who lives alone defined? And how is living with a partner defined?”

sn35.63:2.1.verse: “Migajāla, there are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn35.63:2.2.verse: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

sn35.63:2.5.verse: When there’s lust there is yoking.

sn35.63:2.6.verse: A mendicant who is fettered by relishing is said to live with a partner.

sn35.63:2.7.verse: There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

sn35.63:2.8.verse: There are ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn35.63:2.9.verse: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

sn35.63:2.12.verse: When there’s lust there is yoking.

sn35.63:2.13.verse: A mendicant who is fettered by relishing is said to live with a partner.

sn35.63:2.14.verse: A mendicant who lives like this is said to live with a partner, even if they frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest that are quiet and still, far from the madding crowd, remote from human settlements, and fit for retreat.

sn35.63:2.17.verse: For craving is their partner, and they haven’t given it up.

sn35.63:2.18.verse: That’s why they’re said to live with a partner.

sn35.63:3.1.verse: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn35.63:3.2.verse: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them,

sn35.63:3.4.verse: When there’s no relishing there’s no lust.

sn35.63:3.5.verse: When there’s no lust there’s no yoking.

sn35.63:3.6.verse: A mendicant who is not fettered by relishing is said to live alone.

sn35.63:3.7.verse: There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

sn35.63:3.8.verse: There are ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn35.63:3.9.verse: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them,

sn35.63:3.11.verse: When there’s no relishing there’s no lust.

sn35.63:3.12.verse: When there’s no lust there’s no yoking.

sn35.63:3.13.verse: A mendicant who is not fettered by relishing is said to live alone.

sn35.63:3.14.verse: A mendicant who lives like this is said to live alone, even if they live within a village crowded by monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen; by rulers and their chief ministers, and monastics of other religions and their disciples.

sn35.63:3.17.verse: For craving is their partner, and they have given it up.

sn35.63:3.18.verse: That’s why they’re said to live alone.”

sn35.64:1.1.verse: Then Venerable Migajāla went up to the Buddha …

sn35.64:1.3.verse: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

sn35.64:2.1.verse: “Migajāla, there are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn35.64:2.2.verse: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keep clinging to them,

sn35.64:2.4.verse: Relishing is the origin of suffering, I say.

sn35.64:2.5.verse: There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

sn35.64:2.6.verse: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn35.64:2.7.verse: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

sn35.64:2.9.verse: Relishing is the origin of suffering, I say.

sn35.64:3.1.verse: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn35.64:3.2.verse: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them, relishing ceases.

sn35.64:3.3.verse: When relishing ceases, suffering ceases, I say.

sn35.64:3.4.verse: There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

sn35.64:3.5.verse: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn35.64:3.6.verse: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them, relishing ceases.
