sn36.27:1.5.verse: I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

sn36.27:1.6.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who do truly understand these three feelings’ gratification, drawback, and escape.

sn36.27:1.7.verse: I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

sn36.28:0.2.verse: 3. The Explanation of the Hundred and Eight

sn36.28:1.4.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand these three feelings’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape. …

sn36.28:1.5.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who do truly understand …”

sn36.29:0.2.verse: 3. The Explanation of the Hundred and Eight

sn36.29:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are ascetics and brahmins who don’t understand feeling, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation. …

sn36.29:1.2.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who do understand …”

sn36.30:0.2.verse: 3. The Explanation of the Hundred and Eight

sn36.31:0.2.verse: 3. The Explanation of the Hundred and Eight

sn36.31:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there is rapture of the flesh, rapture not  of the flesh, and rapture even more spiritual than that not of the flesh.

sn36.31:1.2.verse: There is pleasure of the flesh, pleasure not of the flesh, and pleasure even more spiritual than that not of the flesh.

sn36.31:1.3.verse: There is equanimity of the flesh, equanimity not of the flesh, and equanimity even more spiritual than that not of the flesh.

sn36.31:1.4.verse: There is liberation of the flesh, liberation not of the flesh, and liberation even more spiritual than that not of the flesh.

sn36.31:1.5.verse: And what is rapture of the flesh?

sn36.31:1.6.verse: There are these five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn36.31:1.8.verse: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing. Sounds … Smells … Tastes …

sn36.31:1.9.verse: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn36.31:1.10.verse: These are the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn36.31:1.11.verse: The rapture that arises from these five kinds of sensual stimulation is called rapture of the flesh.

sn36.31:2.1.verse: And what is rapture not of the flesh?

sn36.31:2.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn36.31:2.3.verse: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn36.31:2.4.verse: This is called rapture not of the flesh.

sn36.31:3.1.verse: And what is rapture even more spiritual than that not of the flesh?

sn36.31:3.2.verse: When a mendicant who has ended the defilements reviews their mind free from greed, hate, and delusion, rapture arises. This is called rapture even more spiritual than that not of the flesh.

sn36.31:4.1.verse: And what is pleasure of the flesh?

sn36.31:4.2.verse: Mendicants, there are these five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn36.31:4.4.verse: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing. Sounds … Smells … Tastes …

sn36.31:4.5.verse: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn36.31:4.6.verse: These are the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn36.31:4.7.verse: The pleasure and happiness that arise from these five kinds of sensual stimulation is called pleasure of the flesh.

sn36.31:5.1.verse: And what is pleasure not of the flesh?

sn36.31:5.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn36.31:5.3.verse: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn36.31:5.4.verse: And with the fading away of rapture, they enter and remain in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

sn36.31:5.5.verse: This is called pleasure not of the flesh.

sn36.31:6.1.verse: And what is pleasure even more spiritual than that not of the flesh?

sn36.31:6.2.verse: When a mendicant who has ended the defilements reviews their mind free from greed, hate, and delusion, pleasure and happiness arises. This is called pleasure even more spiritual than that not of the flesh.

sn36.31:7.1.verse: And what is equanimity of the flesh?

sn36.31:7.2.verse: There are these five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn36.31:7.4.verse: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing. Sounds … Smells … Tastes …

sn36.31:7.5.verse: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn36.31:7.6.verse: These are the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn36.31:7.7.verse: The equanimity that arises from these five kinds of sensual stimulation is called equanimity of the flesh.

sn36.31:8.1.verse: And what is equanimity not of the flesh?

sn36.31:8.2.verse: It’s when, with the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, a mendicant enters and remains in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

sn36.31:8.3.verse: This is called equanimity not of the flesh.

sn36.31:9.1.verse: And what is equanimity even more spiritual than that not of the flesh?

sn36.31:9.2.verse: When a mendicant who has ended the defilements reviews their mind free from greed, hate, and delusion, equanimity arises. This is called equanimity even more spiritual than that not of the flesh.

sn36.31:10.1.verse: And what is liberation of the flesh?

sn36.31:10.2.verse: Liberation connected with form is liberation of the flesh.

sn36.31:11.1.verse: And what is liberation not of the flesh?

sn36.31:11.2.verse: Liberation connected with the formless is liberation not of the flesh.

sn36.31:12.1.verse: And what is liberation even more spiritual than that not of the flesh?

sn36.31:12.2.verse: When a mendicant who has ended the defilements reviews their mind free from greed, hate, and delusion, liberation arises. This is called liberation even more spiritual than that not of the flesh.”

sn36.31:13.5.verse: The Linked Discourses on feelings are complete.

sn37.1:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when a lady has five factors she is extremely undesirable to a man.

sn37.1:1.3.verse: She’s not attractive, wealthy, or ethical; she’s idle, and she doesn’t beget children.

sn37.1:1.4.verse: When a lady has these five factors she is extremely undesirable to a man.

sn37.1:1.5.verse: When a lady has five factors she is extremely desirable to a man.

sn37.1:1.7.verse: She’s attractive, wealthy, and ethical; she’s deft and tireless, and she begets children.

sn37.1:1.8.verse: When a lady has these five factors she is extremely desirable to a man.”

sn37.2:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when a man has five factors he is extremely undesirable to a lady.

sn37.2:1.3.verse: He’s not attractive, wealthy, or ethical; he’s idle, and he doesn’t beget children.

sn37.2:1.4.verse: When a man has these five factors he is extremely undesirable to a lady.

sn37.2:1.5.verse: When a man has five factors he is extremely desirable to a lady.

sn37.2:1.7.verse: He’s attractive, wealthy, and ethical; he’s deft and tireless, and he begets children.

sn37.2:1.8.verse: When a man has these five factors he is extremely desirable to a lady.”

sn37.3:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five kinds of suffering that particularly apply to ladies. They’re undergone by ladies and not by men.

sn37.3:1.3.verse: Firstly, a lady, while still young, goes to live with her husband’s family and is separated from her relatives.

sn37.3:1.4.verse: This is the first kind of suffering that particularly applies to ladies.

sn37.3:1.5.verse: Furthermore, a lady undergoes the menstrual cycle.

sn37.3:1.6.verse: This is the second kind of suffering that particularly applies to ladies.

sn37.3:1.8.verse: This is the third kind of suffering that particularly applies to ladies.

sn37.3:1.10.verse: This is the fourth kind of suffering that particularly applies to ladies.

sn37.3:1.11.verse: Furthermore, a lady provides services for a man.

sn37.3:1.12.verse: This is the fifth kind of suffering that particularly applies to ladies.

sn37.3:1.13.verse: These are the five kinds of suffering that particularly apply to ladies. They’re undergone by ladies and not by men.”

sn37.4:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when ladies have three qualities, when their body breaks up, after death, they are mostly reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn37.4:1.3.verse: A lady lives at home with heart full of the stain of stinginess in the morning, jealousy in the afternoon, and sexual desire in the evening.

sn37.4:1.6.verse: When ladies possess these three qualities, when their body breaks up, after death, they are mostly reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

sn37.5:1.1.verse: Then Venerable Anuruddha went up to the Buddha, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn37.5:1.2.verse: “Sometimes, sir, with my clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, I see that a female—when her body breaks up, after death—is reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn37.5:1.3.verse: How many qualities do ladies have so that they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell?”

sn37.5:2.1.verse: “Anuruddha, when ladies have five qualities, when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn37.5:2.3.verse: They’re faithless, shameless, imprudent, irritable, and witless.

sn37.5:2.4.verse: When ladies possess these five qualities, when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

sn37.6:1.3.verse: “… They’re faithless, shameless, imprudent, acrimonious, and witless. …”

sn37.7:1.3.verse: “… They’re faithless, shameless, imprudent, jealous, and witless. …”

sn37.8:1.3.verse: “… They’re faithless, shameless, imprudent, stingy, and witless. …”

sn37.9:1.3.verse: “… They’re faithless, shameless, imprudent, adulterous, and witless. …”

sn37.10:1.3.verse: “… They’re faithless, shameless, imprudent, unethical, and witless. …”

sn37.11:1.3.verse: “… They’re faithless, shameless, imprudent, unlearned, and witless. …”

sn37.12:1.3.verse: “… They’re faithless, shameless, imprudent, lazy, and witless. …”

sn37.13:1.3.verse: “… They’re faithless, shameless, imprudent, unmindful, and witless. …”

sn37.14:1.1.verse: “Anuruddha, when ladies have five qualities, when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn37.14:1.3.verse: They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, and consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

sn37.14:1.4.verse: When ladies possess these five qualities, when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

sn37.15:1.1.verse: Then Venerable Anuruddha went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

sn37.15:1.2.verse: “Sometimes, sir, with my clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, I see that a female—when her body breaks up, after death—is reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn37.15:1.3.verse: How many qualities do ladies have so that they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm?”

sn37.15:2.1.verse: “Anuruddha, when ladies have five qualities, when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn37.15:2.3.verse: They’re faithful, conscientious, prudent, loving, and wise.

sn37.15:2.4.verse: When ladies possess these five qualities, when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

sn37.16:1.3.verse: “… They’re faithful, conscientious, prudent, free of acrimony, and wise. …”

sn37.17:1.3.verse: “… They’re faithful, conscientious, prudent, free of jealousy, and wise. …”

sn37.18:1.1.verse: “… They’re faithful, conscientious, prudent, free of stinginess, and wise. …”

sn37.19:1.1.verse: “… They’re faithful, conscientious, prudent, not adulterous, and wise. …”

sn37.20:1.1.verse: “… They’re faithful, conscientious, prudent, ethical, and wise. …”

sn37.21:1.1.verse: “… They’re faithful, conscientious, prudent, learned, and wise. …”

sn37.22:1.1.verse: “… They’re faithful, conscientious, prudent, energetic, and wise. …”

sn37.23:1.1.verse: “… They’re faithful, conscientious, prudent, mindful, and wise. …”

sn37.24:1.1.verse: “Anuruddha, when ladies have five qualities, when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn37.24:1.3.verse: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

sn37.24:1.4.verse: When ladies possess these five qualities, when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

sn37.25:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five powers of a lady.

sn37.25:1.3.verse: Attractiveness, wealth, relatives, children, and ethical behavior.

sn37.25:1.4.verse: These are the five powers of a lady.

sn37.25:1.5.verse: A lady living at home with these five qualities is self-assured.”

sn37.26:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five powers of a lady.

sn37.26:1.3.verse: Attractiveness, wealth, relatives, children, and ethical behavior.

sn37.26:1.4.verse: These are the five powers of a lady.

sn37.26:1.5.verse: A lady living at home with these five powers has her husband under her thumb.”

sn37.27:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five powers of a lady.

sn37.27:1.3.verse: Attractiveness, wealth, relatives, children, and ethical behavior.

sn37.27:1.4.verse: These are the five powers of a lady.

sn37.27:1.5.verse: A lady with these five powers lives having mastered her husband.”

sn37.28:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, by means of one power a man lives having mastered a lady.

sn37.28:1.2.verse: By means of what one power?

sn37.28:1.3.verse: When a lady has been mastered by the power of authority, her powers of attractiveness, wealth, relatives, children, and ethical behavior do not avail her.”

sn37.29:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five powers of a lady.

sn37.29:1.3.verse: Attractiveness, wealth, relatives, children, and ethical behavior.

sn37.29:1.4.verse: A lady who has the power of attractiveness but not the power of wealth

sn37.29:1.6.verse: But when she has the power of attractiveness and the power of wealth

sn37.29:1.8.verse: A lady who has the powers of attractiveness and wealth, but not the power of relatives

sn37.29:1.10.verse: But when she has the powers of attractiveness, wealth, and relatives

sn37.29:1.12.verse: A lady who has the powers of attractiveness, wealth, and relatives, but not the power of children

sn37.29:1.14.verse: But when she has the powers of attractiveness, wealth, relatives, and children

sn37.29:1.16.verse: A lady who has the powers of attractiveness, wealth, relatives, and children, but not the power of ethical behavior

sn37.29:1.18.verse: But when she has the powers of attractiveness, wealth, relatives, children, and ethical behavior

sn37.29:1.20.verse: These are the five powers of a lady.”

sn37.30:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five powers of a lady.

sn37.30:1.3.verse: Attractiveness, wealth, relatives, children, and ethical behavior.

sn37.30:1.4.verse: If a lady has the power of attractiveness but not that of ethical behavior, the family will send her away, they won’t accommodate her.

sn37.30:1.5.verse: If a lady has the powers of attractiveness and wealth but not that of ethical behavior, the family will send her away, they won’t accommodate her.

sn37.30:1.6.verse: If a lady has the powers of attractiveness, wealth, and relatives, but not that of ethical behavior, the family will send her away, they won’t accommodate her.

sn37.30:1.7.verse: If a lady has the powers of attractiveness, wealth, relatives, and children, but not that of ethical behavior, the family will send her away, they won’t accommodate her.

sn37.30:1.8.verse: If a lady has the power of ethical behavior but not that of attractiveness, the family will accommodate her, they won’t send her away.

sn37.30:1.9.verse: If a lady has the power of ethical behavior but not that of wealth, the family will accommodate her, they won’t send her away.

sn37.30:1.10.verse: If a lady has the power of ethical behavior but not that of relatives, the family will accommodate her, they won’t send her away.

sn37.30:1.11.verse: If a lady has the power of ethical behavior but not that of children, the family will accommodate her, they won’t send her away.

sn37.30:1.12.verse: These are the five powers of a lady.”

sn37.31:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five powers of a lady.

sn37.31:1.3.verse: Attractiveness, wealth, relatives, children, and ethical behavior.

sn37.31:1.4.verse: It is not because of the powers of attractiveness, wealth, relatives, or children that ladies, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn37.31:1.5.verse: It is because of the power of ethical behavior that ladies, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn37.31:1.6.verse: These are the five powers of a lady.”

sn37.32:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are five things that are hard to get for ladies who have not made merit.

sn37.32:1.3.verse: ‘May I be born into a suitable family!’

sn37.32:1.5.verse: ‘Having been born in a suitable family, may I marry into a suitable family!’

sn37.32:1.7.verse: ‘Having been born in a suitable family and married into a suitable family, may I live at home without a co-wife!’

sn37.32:1.9.verse: ‘Having been born in a suitable family, and married into a suitable family, and living at home without a co-wife, may I have children!’

sn37.32:1.11.verse: ‘Having been born in a suitable family, and married into a suitable family, and living at home without a co-wife, and having had children, may I live having mastered my husband!’

sn37.32:1.13.verse: These are the five things that are hard to get for ladies who have not made merit.

sn37.32:2.1.verse: There are five things that are easy to get for ladies who have made merit.

sn37.32:2.3.verse: ‘May I be born into a suitable family!’

sn37.32:2.5.verse: ‘Having been born into a suitable family, may I marry into a suitable family!’

sn37.32:2.7.verse: ‘Having been born into a suitable family and married into a suitable family, may I live at home without a co-wife!’

sn37.32:2.9.verse: ‘Having been born into a suitable family, and married into a suitable family, and living at home without a co-wife, may I have children!’

sn37.32:2.11.verse: ‘Having been born into a suitable family, and married into a suitable family, and living at home without a co-wife, and having had children, may I live having mastered my husband!’

sn37.32:2.13.verse: These are the five things that are easy to get for ladies who have made merit.”

sn37.33:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a lady living at home with five qualities is self-assured.

sn37.33:1.3.verse: She doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

sn37.33:1.4.verse: A lady living at home with these five qualities is self-assured.”

sn37.34:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a female noble disciple who grows in five ways grows nobly, taking on what is essential and excellent in this life.

sn37.34:1.3.verse: She grows in faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

sn37.34:1.4.verse: A female noble disciple who grows in these five ways grows nobly, taking on what is essential and excellent in this life.

sn37.34:2.1.verse: When she grows in faith and ethics,

sn37.34:2.2.verse: wisdom, and both generosity and learning—

sn37.34:2.3.verse: a virtuous laywoman such as she

sn37.34:2.4.verse: takes on what is essential for herself in this life.”

sn37.34:3.5.verse: The Linked Discourses on ladies are complete.

sn38.1:1.1.verse: At one time Venerable Sāriputta was staying in the land of the Magadhans near the little village of Nālaka.

sn38.1:1.2.verse: Then the wanderer Jambukhādaka went up to Venerable Sāriputta and exchanged greetings with him.

sn38.1:1.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Sāriputta:

sn38.1:2.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘extinguishment’.

sn38.1:2.3.verse: “Reverend, the ending of greed, hate, and delusion

sn38.1:2.5.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for realizing this extinguishment?”

sn38.1:2.8.verse: “It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn38.1:2.9.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn38.1:2.10.verse: This is the path, the practice, for realizing this extinguishment.”

sn38.1:2.11.verse: “Reverend, this is a fine path, a fine practice, for realizing this extinguishment.

sn38.1:2.12.verse: Just this much is enough for diligence.”

sn38.2:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘perfection’.

sn38.2:1.3.verse: “Reverend, the ending of greed, hate, and delusion

sn38.2:1.5.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for realizing this perfection?”

sn38.2:1.8.verse: “It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn38.2:1.9.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn38.2:1.10.verse: This is the path, the practice, for realizing this perfection.”

sn38.2:1.11.verse: “Reverend, this is a fine path, a fine practice, for realizing this perfection.

sn38.2:1.12.verse: Just this much is enough for diligence.”

sn38.3:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, who in the world have principled speech? Who in the world practice well? Who are the holy ones in the world?”

sn38.3:1.2.verse: “Reverend, those who teach principles for giving up greed, hate, and delusion have principled speech in the world.

sn38.3:1.3.verse: Those who practice for giving up greed, hate, and delusion are practicing well in the world.

sn38.3:1.4.verse: Those who have given up greed, hate, and delusion—so they’re cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future—are holy ones in the world.”

sn38.3:2.1.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for giving up that greed, hate, and delusion?”

sn38.3:2.4.verse: “It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn38.3:2.5.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn38.3:2.6.verse: This is the path, this is the practice for giving up that greed, hate, and delusion.”

sn38.3:2.7.verse: “This is a fine path, a fine practice, for giving up greed, hate, and delusion.

sn38.3:2.8.verse: Just this much is enough for diligence.”

sn38.4:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, what’s the goal of leading the spiritual life under the ascetic Gotama?”

sn38.4:1.2.verse: “The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to completely understand suffering.”

sn38.4:1.3.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for completely understanding this suffering?”

sn38.5:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘gaining solace’.

sn38.5:1.2.verse: At what point do you gain solace?”

sn38.5:1.3.verse: “When a mendicant truly understands the six fields of contact’s origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape, at that point they’ve gained solace.”

sn38.5:1.4.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for realizing this solace?”

sn38.6:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘gaining ultimate solace’.

sn38.6:1.2.verse: At what point do you gain ultimate solace?”

sn38.6:1.3.verse: “When a mendicant is freed by not grasping after truly understanding the six fields of contact’s origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape, at that point they’ve gained ultimate solace.”

sn38.6:1.4.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for realizing this ultimate solace?”

sn38.7:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘feeling’.

sn38.7:1.7.verse: “But reverend, is there a path and a practice for completely understanding these three feelings?”

sn38.8:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘defilement’.

sn38.8:1.4.verse: The defilements of sensuality, desire to be reborn, and ignorance.

sn38.8:1.6.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for completely understanding these three defilements?”

sn38.9:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘ignorance’.

sn38.9:1.3.verse: “Not knowing about suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.

sn38.9:1.5.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for giving up that ignorance?”

sn38.10:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘craving’.

sn38.10:1.4.verse: Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for continued existence, and craving for nonexistence.

sn38.10:1.6.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for completely understanding these cravings?”

sn38.11:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘a flood’.

sn38.11:1.4.verse: The floods of sensuality, desire to be reborn, views, and ignorance.

sn38.11:1.6.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for completely understanding these floods?”

sn38.12:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘grasping’.

sn38.12:1.3.verse: “Reverend, there are these four kinds of grasping.

sn38.12:1.4.verse: Grasping at sensual pleasures, views, precepts and observances, and theories of a self.

sn38.12:1.5.verse: These are the four kinds of grasping.”

sn38.12:1.6.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for completely understanding these four kinds of grasping?”

sn38.13:0.3.verse: A Question About States of Existence

sn38.13:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘continued existence’.

sn38.13:1.3.verse: “Reverend, there are these three states of continued existence.

sn38.13:1.4.verse: Existence in the sensual realm, the realm of luminous form, and the formless realm.

sn38.13:1.5.verse: These are the three states of continued existence.”

sn38.13:1.6.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for completely understanding these three states of existence?”

sn38.14:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘suffering’.

sn38.14:1.3.verse: “Reverend, there are these three forms of suffering.

sn38.14:1.4.verse: The suffering inherent in painful feeling; the suffering inherent in conditions; and the suffering inherent in perishing.

sn38.14:1.5.verse: These are the three forms of suffering.”

sn38.14:1.6.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for completely understanding these forms of suffering?”

sn38.15:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘substantial reality’.

sn38.15:1.3.verse: “Reverend, the Buddha said that these five grasping aggregates are substantial reality. That is,

sn38.15:1.4.verse: form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn38.15:1.5.verse: The Buddha said that these five grasping aggregates are substantial reality.”

sn38.15:1.6.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for completely understanding this substantial reality?”

sn38.16:0.3.verse: A Question About What’s Hard to Do

sn38.16:1.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, in this teaching and training, what is hard to do?”

sn38.16:1.2.verse: “Going forth, reverend, is hard to do in this teaching and training.”

sn38.16:1.3.verse: “But what’s hard to do for someone who has gone forth?”

sn38.16:1.4.verse: “When you’ve gone forth it’s hard to be satisfied.”

sn38.16:1.5.verse: “But what’s hard to do for someone who is satisfied?”

sn38.16:1.6.verse: “When you’re satisfied, it’s hard to practice in line with the teaching.”

sn38.16:1.7.verse: “But if a mendicant practices in line with the teaching, will it take them long to become a perfected one?”

sn38.16:1.10.verse: The Linked Discourses with Jambukhādaka are complete.

sn39.1-15:1.1.verse: At one time Venerable Sāriputta was staying in the land of the Vajjis near Ukkacelā on the bank of the Ganges River.

sn39.1-15:1.2.verse: Then the wanderer Sāmaṇḍaka went up to Venerable Sāriputta and exchanged greetings with him.

sn39.1-15:1.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Sāriputta:

sn39.1-15:2.1.verse: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘extinguishment’.

sn39.1-15:2.3.verse: “Reverend, the ending of greed, hate, and delusion

sn39.1-15:2.5.verse: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for realizing this extinguishment?”

sn39.1-15:3.2.verse: “It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn39.1-15:3.3.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn39.1-15:3.4.verse: This is the path, the practice, for realizing this extinguishment.”

sn39.1-15:3.5.verse: “Reverend, this is a fine path, a fine practice, for realizing this extinguishment.

sn39.1-15:3.6.verse: Just this much is enough for diligence.”

sn40.1:0.3.verse: A Question About the First Absorption

sn40.1:1.1.verse: At one time Venerable Mahāmoggallāna was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn40.1:1.2.verse: There Venerable Mahāmoggallāna addressed the mendicants:

sn40.1:2.1.verse: “Just now, reverends, as I was in private retreat this thought came to mind:

sn40.1:2.2.verse: ‘They speak of this thing called the “first absorption”.

sn40.1:2.5.verse: ‘It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn40.1:2.6.verse: This is called the first absorption.’

sn40.1:2.7.verse: And so … I was entering and remaining in the first absorption.

sn40.1:2.8.verse: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by sensual pleasures beset me.

sn40.1:3.1.verse: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

sn40.1:3.3.verse: Don’t neglect the first absorption, brahmin! Settle your mind in the first absorption; unify your mind and immerse it in the first absorption.’

sn40.1:3.4.verse: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the first absorption.

sn40.1:3.5.verse: So if anyone should be rightly called

sn40.1:3.6.verse: a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

sn40.2:0.3.verse: A Question About the Second Absorption

sn40.2:1.1.verse: “They speak of this thing called the ‘second absorption’.

sn40.2:1.4.verse: ‘As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, a mendicant enters and remains in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn40.2:1.5.verse: This is called the second absorption.’

sn40.2:1.6.verse: And so … I was entering and remaining in the second absorption.

sn40.2:1.7.verse: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by placing the mind beset me.

sn40.2:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

sn40.2:2.3.verse: Don’t neglect the second absorption, brahmin! Settle your mind in the second absorption; unify your mind and immerse it in the second absorption.’

sn40.2:2.4.verse: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the second absorption.

sn40.2:2.5.verse: So if anyone should be rightly called

sn40.2:2.6.verse: a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

sn40.3:0.3.verse: A Question About the Third Absorption

sn40.3:1.1.verse: “They speak of this thing called the ‘third absorption’.

sn40.3:1.4.verse: ‘With the fading away of rapture, a mendicant enters and remains in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, “Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.”

sn40.3:1.5.verse: This is called the third absorption.’

sn40.3:1.6.verse: And so … I was entering and remaining in the third absorption.

sn40.3:1.7.verse: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by rapture beset me.

sn40.3:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

sn40.3:2.3.verse: Don’t neglect the third absorption, brahmin! Settle your mind in the third absorption; unify your mind and immerse it in the third absorption.’

sn40.3:2.4.verse: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the third absorption.

sn40.3:2.5.verse: So if anyone should be rightly called a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

sn40.4:0.3.verse: A Question About the Fourth Absorption

sn40.4:1.1.verse: “They speak of this thing called the ‘fourth absorption’.

sn40.4:1.4.verse: ‘It’s when, with the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, a mendicant enters and remains in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

sn40.4:1.5.verse: This is called the fourth absorption.’

sn40.4:1.6.verse: And so … I was entering and remaining in the fourth absorption.

sn40.4:1.7.verse: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by pleasure beset me.

sn40.4:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

sn40.4:2.3.verse: Don’t neglect the fourth absorption, brahmin! Settle your mind in the fourth absorption; unify your mind and immerse it in the fourth absorption.’

sn40.4:2.4.verse: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the fourth absorption.

sn40.4:2.5.verse: So if anyone should be rightly called a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

sn40.5:0.3.verse: A Question About the Dimension of Infinite Space

sn40.5:1.1.verse: “They speak of this thing called the ‘dimension of infinite space’.

sn40.5:1.2.verse: What is the dimension of infinite space?

sn40.5:1.4.verse: ‘It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that “space is infinite”, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.

sn40.5:1.5.verse: This is called the dimension of infinite space.’

sn40.5:1.6.verse: And so … I was entering and remaining in the dimension of infinite space.

sn40.5:1.7.verse: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by forms beset me.

sn40.5:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

sn40.5:2.3.verse: Don’t neglect the dimension of infinite space, brahmin! Settle your mind in the dimension of infinite space; unify your mind and immerse it in the dimension of infinite space.’

sn40.5:2.4.verse: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the dimension of infinite space.

sn40.5:2.5.verse: So if anyone should be rightly called a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

sn40.6:0.3.verse: A Question About the Dimension of Infinite Consciousness

sn40.6:1.1.verse: “They speak of this thing called the ‘dimension of infinite consciousness’.

sn40.6:1.2.verse: What is the dimension of infinite consciousness?

sn40.6:1.4.verse: ‘It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that “consciousness is infinite”, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

sn40.6:1.5.verse: This is called the dimension of infinite consciousness.’

sn40.6:1.6.verse: And so … I was entering and remaining in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

sn40.6:1.7.verse: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by the dimension of infinite space beset me.

sn40.6:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

sn40.6:2.3.verse: Don’t neglect the dimension of infinite consciousness, brahmin! Settle your mind in the dimension of infinite consciousness; unify your mind and immerse it in the dimension of infinite consciousness.’

sn40.6:2.4.verse: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

sn40.6:2.5.verse: So if anyone should be rightly called a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

sn40.7:0.3.verse: A Question About the Dimension of Nothingness

sn40.7:1.1.verse: “They speak of this thing called the ‘dimension of nothingness’.

sn40.7:1.2.verse: What is the dimension of nothingness?

sn40.7:1.4.verse: ‘It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that “there is nothing at all”, enters and remains in the dimension of nothingness.

sn40.7:1.5.verse: This is called the dimension of nothingness.’

sn40.7:1.6.verse: And so … I was entering and remaining in the dimension of nothingness.

sn40.7:1.7.verse: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by the dimension of infinite consciousness beset me.

sn40.7:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

sn40.7:2.3.verse: Don’t neglect the dimension of nothingness, brahmin! Settle your mind in the dimension of nothingness; unify your mind and immerse it in the dimension of nothingness.’

sn40.7:2.4.verse: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the dimension of nothingness.

sn40.7:2.5.verse: So if anyone should be rightly called a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

sn40.8:0.3.verse: A Question About the Dimension of Neither Perception Nor Non-Perception

sn40.8:1.1.verse: “They speak of this thing called the ‘dimension of neither perception nor non-perception’.

sn40.8:1.2.verse: What is the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception?

sn40.8:1.4.verse: ‘It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, enters and remains in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

sn40.8:1.5.verse: This is called the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.’

sn40.8:1.6.verse: And so … I was entering and remaining in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

sn40.8:1.7.verse: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by the dimension of nothingness beset me.

sn40.8:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

sn40.8:2.3.verse: Don’t neglect the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, brahmin! Settle your mind in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception; unify your mind and immerse it in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.’

sn40.8:2.4.verse: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

sn40.8:2.5.verse: So if anyone should be rightly called a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

sn40.9:1.1.verse: “They speak of this thing called the ‘signless immersion of the heart’.

sn40.9:1.2.verse: What is the signless immersion of the heart?

sn40.9:1.4.verse: ‘It’s when a mendicant, not focusing on any signs, enters and remains in the signless immersion of the heart.

sn40.9:1.5.verse: This is called the signless immersion of the heart.’

sn40.9:1.6.verse: And so … I was entering and remaining in the signless immersion of the heart.

sn40.9:1.7.verse: While I was in that meditation, my consciousness followed after signs.

sn40.9:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

sn40.9:2.3.verse: Don’t neglect the signless immersion of the heart, brahmin! Settle your mind in the signless immersion of the heart; unify your mind and immerse it in the signless immersion of the heart.’

sn40.9:2.4.verse: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the signless immersion of the heart.

sn40.9:2.5.verse: So if anyone should be rightly called

sn40.9:2.6.verse: a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

sn40.10:1.1.verse: And then Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared among the gods of the thirty-three.

sn40.10:1.2.verse: Then Sakka, lord of gods, with five hundred deities came up to Mahāmoggallāna, bowed, and stood to one side. Mahāmoggallāna said to him:
