sn42.12:14.1.verse: Now, consider the pleasure seeker who seeks wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means, and who makes themselves happy and pleased, and shares it and makes merit. But they enjoy that wealth tied, infatuated, attached, blind to the drawbacks, and not understanding the escape.

sn42.12:14.2.verse: They may be praised on three grounds and criticized on one.

sn42.12:14.3.verse: What are the three grounds for praise?

sn42.12:14.4.verse: They seek wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means. This is the first ground for praise.

sn42.12:14.5.verse: They make themselves happy and pleased. This is the second ground for praise.

sn42.12:14.6.verse: They share it and make merit. This is the third ground for praise.

sn42.12:14.7.verse: What is the one ground for criticism?

sn42.12:14.8.verse: They enjoy that wealth tied, infatuated, attached, blind to the drawbacks, and not understanding the escape. This is the one ground for criticism.

sn42.12:14.9.verse: This pleasure seeker may be praised on these three grounds, and criticized on this one.

sn42.12:15.1.verse: Now, consider the pleasure seeker who seeks wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means, and who makes themselves happy and pleased, and shares it and makes merit.

sn42.12:15.2.verse: And they enjoy that wealth untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawbacks, and understanding the escape.

sn42.12:15.3.verse: This pleasure seeker may be praised on four grounds.

sn42.12:15.4.verse: What are the four grounds for praise?

sn42.12:15.5.verse: They seek wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means. This is the first ground for praise.

sn42.12:15.6.verse: They make themselves happy and pleased. This is the second ground for praise.

sn42.12:15.7.verse: They share it and make merit. This is the third ground for praise.

sn42.12:15.8.verse: They enjoy that wealth untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawbacks, and understanding the escape. This is the fourth ground for praise.

sn42.12:15.9.verse: This pleasure seeker may be praised on these four grounds.

sn42.12:16.1.verse: These three fervent mortifiers who live rough are found in the world.

sn42.12:16.3.verse: Take a fervent mortifier who has gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness, thinking:

sn42.12:16.4.verse: ‘Hopefully I will achieve a skillful quality! Hopefully I will realize a superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones!’

sn42.12:16.5.verse: They mortify and torment themselves. But they don’t achieve any skillful quality, or realize any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.

sn42.12:17.1.verse: Take another fervent mortifier who has gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness, thinking:

sn42.12:17.2.verse: ‘Hopefully I will achieve a skillful quality! Hopefully I will realize a superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones!’

sn42.12:17.3.verse: They mortify and torment themselves. And they achieve a skillful quality, but don’t realize any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.

sn42.12:18.1.verse: Take another fervent mortifier who has gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness, thinking:

sn42.12:18.2.verse: ‘Hopefully I will achieve a skillful quality! Hopefully I will realize a superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones!’

sn42.12:18.3.verse: They mortify and torment themselves. And they achieve a skillful quality, and they realize a superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.

sn42.12:19.1.verse: In this case, the first fervent mortifier may be criticized on three grounds.

sn42.12:19.3.verse: They mortify and torment themselves. This is the first ground for criticism.

sn42.12:19.4.verse: They don’t achieve a skillful quality. This is the second ground for criticism.

sn42.12:19.5.verse: They don’t realize a superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones. This is the third ground for criticism.

sn42.12:19.6.verse: This fervent mortifier may be criticized on these three grounds.

sn42.12:20.1.verse: In this case, the second fervent mortifier

sn42.12:20.2.verse: may be criticized on two grounds, and praised on one.

sn42.12:20.3.verse: What are the two grounds for criticism?

sn42.12:20.4.verse: They mortify and torment themselves. This is the first ground for criticism.

sn42.12:20.5.verse: They don’t realize a superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones. This is the second ground for criticism.

sn42.12:20.6.verse: What is the one ground for praise?

sn42.12:20.7.verse: They achieve a skillful quality. This is the one ground for praise.

sn42.12:20.8.verse: This fervent mortifier may be criticized on these two grounds, and praised on one.

sn42.12:21.1.verse: In this case, the third fervent mortifier may be criticized on one ground, and praised on two.

sn42.12:21.2.verse: What is the one ground for criticism?

sn42.12:21.3.verse: They mortify and torment themselves. This is the one ground for criticism.

sn42.12:21.4.verse: What are the two grounds for praise?

sn42.12:21.5.verse: They achieve a skillful quality. This is the first ground for praise.

sn42.12:21.6.verse: They realize a superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones. This is the second ground for praise.

sn42.12:21.7.verse: This fervent mortifier may be criticized on this one ground, and praised on two.

sn42.12:22.1.verse: There are these three kinds of wearing away that are apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know them for themselves.

sn42.12:22.3.verse: A greedy person, because of greed, intends to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both.

sn42.12:22.4.verse: When they’ve given up greed they don’t have such intentions.

sn42.12:22.5.verse: This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

sn42.12:22.6.verse: A hateful person, because of hate, intends to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both.

sn42.12:22.7.verse: When they’ve given up hate they don’t have such intentions.

sn42.12:22.8.verse: This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

sn42.12:22.9.verse: A deluded person, because of delusion, intends to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both.

sn42.12:22.10.verse: When they’ve given up delusion they don’t have such intentions.

sn42.12:22.11.verse: This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

sn42.12:22.12.verse: These are the three kinds of wearing away that are apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know them for themselves.”

sn42.13:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Koliyans, where they have a town named Uttarakā.

sn42.13:1.2.verse: Then Pāṭaliya the chief went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn42.13:2.1.verse: I trust those who say this repeat what the Buddha has said, and do not misrepresent him with an untruth? Is their explanation in line with the teaching? Are there any legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?

sn42.13:2.2.verse: For we don’t want to misrepresent the Blessed One.”

sn42.13:2.3.verse: “Chief, those who say this repeat what I have said, and don’t misrepresent me with an untruth. Their explanation is in line with the teaching, and there are no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism.”

sn42.13:2.4.verse: “Sir, we didn’t believe that what those ascetics and brahmins said was really true.

sn42.13:2.5.verse: But it seems the ascetic Gotama is deceitful!”

sn42.13:2.6.verse: “Chief, does someone who says ‘I know deceit’ also say ‘I am deceitful’?”

sn42.13:2.7.verse: “That’s right, Blessed One! That’s right, Holy One!”

sn42.13:2.8.verse: “Well then, chief, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.

sn42.13:3.2.verse: Do you know the Koliyan officers with drooping headdresses?”

sn42.13:3.5.verse: “To put a stop to bandits and to deliver messages for the Koliyans.”

sn42.13:3.7.verse: Are the Koliyan officers with drooping headdresses moral or immoral?”

sn42.13:3.8.verse: “I know that they’re immoral, of bad character, sir. They are among those in the world who are immoral and of bad character.”

sn42.13:3.9.verse: “Would it be right to say that

sn42.13:3.10.verse: Pāṭaliya knows the Kolyian officers with drooping headdresses who are immoral, of bad character, so he too must be immoral and of bad character?”

sn42.13:3.12.verse: I’m quite different from the Koliyan officers with drooping headdresses; we have quite different characters.”

sn42.13:3.13.verse: “So if you can know those officers of bad character while you are not of bad character, why can’t the Realized One know deceit, without being deceitful?

sn42.13:3.14.verse: I understand deceit and its result. And I understand how the deceitful practice so that when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn42.13:4.1.verse: I understand killing living creatures and its result. And I understand how those who kill living creatures practice so that when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn42.13:6.1.verse: But you can see someone, garlanded and adorned, nicely bathed and anointed, hair and beard dressed, taking his pleasure with women as if he were a king.

sn42.13:6.3.verse: ‘My man, what did that man do?’

sn42.13:6.5.verse: ‘My man, that man attacked the king’s enemy and killed them.

sn42.13:6.6.verse: The king was delighted and gave him this reward.

sn42.13:6.7.verse: That’s why he’s garlanded and adorned, nicely bathed and anointed, hair and beard dressed, taking his pleasure with women as if he were a king.’

sn42.13:7.1.verse: And you can see someone else, his arms tied tightly behind his back with a strong rope. His head is shaven and he’s marched from street to street and from square to square to the beating of a harsh drum. Then he’s taken out the south gate and there, to the south of the city, they chop off his head.

sn42.13:7.3.verse: ‘My man, what did that man do?’

sn42.13:7.5.verse: ‘My man, that man is an enemy of the king, and he has murdered a man or a woman.

sn42.13:7.6.verse: That’s why the rulers arrested him and inflicted such punishment.’

sn42.13:8.2.verse: Have you seen or heard of such a thing?”

sn42.13:8.3.verse: “Sir, we have seen it and heard of it, and we will hear of it again.”

sn42.13:8.4.verse: “Since this is so, the ascetics and brahmins whose view is that

sn42.13:8.5.verse: everyone who kills living creatures experiences pain and sadness in this very life: are they right or wrong?”

sn42.13:8.7.verse: “But those who speak hollow, false nonsense: are they moral or immoral?”

sn42.13:8.9.verse: “And are those who are immoral, of bad character practicing wrongly or rightly?”

sn42.13:8.11.verse: “And do those who are practicing wrongly have wrong view or right view?”

sn42.13:8.13.verse: “But is it appropriate to have confidence in those of wrong view?”

sn42.13:15.4.verse: Whenever an ascetic or brahmin comes to stay, I share what I have as best I can.

sn42.13:15.5.verse: Once it so happened, sir, that four teachers of different views, beliefs, and opinions came to stay at my guest house.

sn42.13:16.1.verse: One teacher had this doctrine and view:

sn42.13:16.2.verse: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

sn42.13:17.1.verse: One teacher had this doctrine and view:

sn42.13:17.2.verse: ‘There is meaning in giving, sacrifice, and offerings. There are fruits and results of good and bad deeds. There is an afterlife. There are such things as mother and father, and beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there are ascetics and brahmins who are rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describe the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

sn42.13:18.1.verse: One teacher had this doctrine and view:

sn42.13:18.2.verse: ‘The one who acts does nothing wrong when they punish, mutilate, torture, aggrieve, oppress, intimidate, or when they encourage others to do the same. Nothing bad is done when they kill, steal, break into houses, plunder wealth, steal from isolated buildings, commit highway robbery, commit adultery, and lie.

sn42.13:18.3.verse: If you were to reduce all the living creatures of this earth to one heap and mass of flesh with a razor-edged chakram, no evil comes of that, and no outcome of evil.

sn42.13:18.4.verse: If you were to go along the south bank of the Ganges killing, mutilating, and torturing, and encouraging others to do the same, no evil comes of that, and no outcome of evil.

sn42.13:18.5.verse: If you were to go along the north bank of the Ganges giving and sacrificing and encouraging others to do the same, no merit comes of that, and no outcome of merit.

sn42.13:18.6.verse: In giving, self-control, restraint, and truthfulness there is no merit or outcome of merit.’

sn42.13:19.1.verse: One teacher had this doctrine and view:

sn42.13:19.2.verse: ‘The one who acts does a bad deed when they punish, mutilate, torture, aggrieve, oppress, intimidate, or when they encourage others to do the same. A bad deed is done when they kill, steal, break into houses, plunder wealth, steal from isolated buildings, commit highway robbery, commit adultery, and lie.

sn42.13:19.3.verse: If you were to reduce all the living creatures of this earth to one heap and mass of flesh with a razor-edged chakram, evil comes of that, and an outcome of evil.

sn42.13:19.4.verse: If you were to go along the south bank of the Ganges killing, mutilating, and torturing, and encouraging others to do the same, evil comes of that, and an outcome of evil.

sn42.13:19.5.verse: If you were to go along the north bank of the Ganges giving and sacrificing and encouraging others to do the same, merit comes of that, and an outcome of merit.

sn42.13:19.6.verse: In giving, self-control, restraint, and truthfulness there is merit and outcome of merit.’

sn42.13:22.1.verse: “Chief, there is immersion based on understanding of principle.

sn42.13:22.2.verse: If you gain such mental immersion, you can give up that state of uncertainty.

sn42.13:22.3.verse: And what is immersion based on understanding of principle?

sn42.13:22.4.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has given up killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, backbiting, harsh speech, talking nonsense, covetousness, ill will, and wrong view.

sn42.13:23.1.verse: Then that noble disciple is rid of desire, rid of ill will, unconfused, aware, and mindful. They meditate spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

sn42.13:23.6.verse: I hold a winning hand on both counts, since I’m restrained in body, speech, and mind, and when my body breaks up, after death, I’ll be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’

sn42.13:23.12.verse: This is that immersion based on understanding of principle.

sn42.13:28.1.verse: equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

sn42.13:31.9.verse: ‘If what this good teacher says is true, it’s a sure bet for me to not hurt any creature firm or frail.

sn42.13:31.10.verse: I hold a winning hand on both counts, since I’m restrained in body, speech, and mind, and when my body breaks up, after death, I’ll be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’

sn42.13:31.13.verse: When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil.

sn42.13:31.14.verse: When the body is tranquil, they feel bliss.

sn42.13:31.15.verse: And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.

sn42.13:31.16.verse: This is that immersion based on understanding of principle.

sn42.13:31.17.verse: If you gain such mental immersion, you can give up that state of uncertainty.”

sn42.13:32.1.verse: When he said this, Pāṭaliya the chief said to the Buddha,

sn42.13:32.3.verse: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

sn44.1:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn44.1:1.2.verse: Now at that time the nun Khemā was wandering in the land of the Kosalans between Sāvatthī and Sāketa when she took up residence in Toraṇavatthu.

sn44.1:1.3.verse: Then King Pasenadi was traveling from Sāketa to Sāvatthī, and he too stayed in Toraṇavatthu for a single night.

sn44.1:1.4.verse: Then King Pasenadi addressed a man,

sn44.1:1.5.verse: “Please, my man, check if there’s a suitable (male) ascetic or brahmin in Toraṇavatthu to whom I can pay homage.”

sn44.1:2.1.verse: “Yes, Your Majesty,” replied that man. He searched all over Toraṇavatthu, but he couldn’t see a suitable ascetic or brahmin for the king to pay homage to.

sn44.1:2.2.verse: But he saw that the nun Khemā was staying there,

sn44.1:2.3.verse: so he went to the king and said to him,

sn44.1:3.1.verse: “Your Majesty, there’s no (male) ascetic or brahmin in Toraṇavatthu for the king to pay homage to.

sn44.1:3.2.verse: But there is the nun Khemā, who’s a disciple of the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

sn44.1:3.3.verse: She has a good reputation as being

sn44.1:3.4.verse: astute, competent, intelligent, learned, a brilliant speaker, and eloquent.

sn44.1:3.5.verse: Your Majesty may pay homage to her.”

sn44.1:4.1.verse: Then King Pasenadi of Kosala went up to the nun Khemā, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to her:

sn44.1:4.2.verse: “Ma’am, does a realized one still exist after death?”

sn44.1:4.3.verse: “Great king, this has not been declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.1:4.5.verse: “Well then, does a realized one no longer exist after death?”

sn44.1:4.6.verse: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.1:4.8.verse: “Well then, does a realized one both still exist and no longer exist after death?”

sn44.1:4.9.verse: “This has not been declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.1:4.11.verse: “Well then, does a realized one neither still exist nor no longer exist after death?”

sn44.1:4.12.verse: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.1:5.1.verse: “Ma’am, when asked these questions, you say

sn44.1:5.2.verse: that this has not been declared by the Buddha.

sn44.1:5.13.verse: What’s the cause, what’s the reason why this has not been declared by the Buddha?”

sn44.1:6.1.verse: “Well then, Great King, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.

sn44.1:6.2.verse: What do you think, Great King?

sn44.1:6.3.verse: Do you have any accountant or finger-tallier or reckoner who can count the grains of sand in the Ganges, that is,

sn44.1:6.4.verse: how many grains of sand there are, how many hundreds or thousands or hundreds of thousands of grains of sand?”

sn44.1:6.6.verse: “Do you have any accountant or finger-tallier or reckoner who can count the water in the ocean, that is,

sn44.1:6.7.verse: how many gallons of water there are, how many hundreds or thousands or hundreds of thousands of gallons of water?”

sn44.1:6.10.verse: Because the ocean is deep, immeasurable, and hard to fathom.”

sn44.1:6.11.verse: “In the same way, Great King, any form by which a realized one might be described has been cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

sn44.1:6.12.verse: A realized one is freed from reckoning in terms of form. They’re deep, immeasurable, and hard to fathom,

sn44.1:6.14.verse: To say that after death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists: none of these apply.

sn44.1:9.1.verse: consciousness by which a realized one might be described has been cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

sn44.1:9.2.verse: A realized one is freed from reckoning in terms of consciousness. They’re deep, immeasurable, and hard to fathom,

sn44.1:9.4.verse: To say that after death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists: none of these apply.”

sn44.1:9.5.verse: Then King Pasenadi approved and agreed with what the nun Khemā said. Then he rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled her, keeping her on his right, before leaving.

sn44.1:10.1.verse: Then on a later occasion King Pasenadi of Kosala went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. He asked the Buddha exactly the same questions he had asked the nun Khemā, and received the same answers.

sn44.1:13.1.verse: He said, “It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!

sn44.1:13.2.verse: How the meaning and the phrasing of the Teacher and the disciple fit together and agree without contradiction when it comes to the chief matter!

sn44.1:13.3.verse: This one time I went to the nun Khemā and asked her about this matter.

sn44.1:13.4.verse: And she explained it to me with these words and phrases, just like the Buddha.

sn44.1:13.6.verse: How the meaning and the phrasing of the Teacher and the disciple fit together and agree without contradiction when it comes to the chief matter!

sn44.1:13.7.verse: Well, now, sir, I must go.

sn44.1:13.8.verse: I have many duties, and much to do.”

sn44.1:13.9.verse: “Please, Great King, go at your convenience.”

sn44.1:13.10.verse: Then King Pasenadi approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. Then he rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled him, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

sn44.2:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

sn44.2:1.2.verse: Now at that time Venerable Anurādha was staying not far from the Buddha in a wilderness hut.

sn44.2:1.3.verse: Then several wanderers of other religions went up to Venerable Anurādha and exchanged greetings with him.

sn44.2:1.4.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side and said to him:

sn44.2:1.5.verse: “Reverend Anurādha, when a realized one is describing a realized one—a supreme person, highest of people, who has reached the highest point—they describe them in these four ways:

sn44.2:1.6.verse: After death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists.”

sn44.2:1.7.verse: “Reverends, when a realized one is describing a realized one—a supreme person, highest of people, who has reached the highest point—they describe them other than these four ways:

sn44.2:1.8.verse: After death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists.”

sn44.2:1.9.verse: When he said this, the wanderers said to him,

sn44.2:1.10.verse: “This mendicant must be junior, recently gone forth, or else a foolish, incompetent senior mendicant.”

sn44.2:1.11.verse: Then, after rebuking Venerable Anurādha by calling him “junior” and “foolish”, the wanderers rose from their seats and left.

sn44.2:2.1.verse: Soon after they had left, Anurādha thought,

sn44.2:2.2.verse: “If those wanderers were to inquire further,

sn44.2:2.3.verse: how should I answer them so as to repeat what the Buddha has said, and not misrepresent him with an untruth? How should I explain in line with his teaching, so that there would be no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?”

sn44.2:2.4.verse: Then Venerable Anurādha went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

sn44.2:5.1.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

sn44.2:7.1.verse: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

sn44.2:7.2.verse: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

sn44.2:13.2.verse: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

sn44.2:15.1.verse: “So, Anurādha, you should truly see any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

sn44.2:15.5.verse: consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

sn44.2:15.6.verse: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

sn44.2:15.7.verse: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

sn44.2:15.8.verse: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

sn44.2:16.4.verse: “Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies to feeling?” …

sn44.2:16.15.verse: “Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies apart from form?”

sn44.2:16.17.verse: “Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies in relation to feeling?”

sn44.2:17.2.verse: Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies to one who has form?” … “… feeling?” … “… perception?” … “… choices?” … “… consciousness?”

sn44.2:17.5.verse: Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies to that one who is without form?” … “… feeling?” … “… perception?” … “… choices?” … “… consciousness?”

sn44.2:17.7.verse: “In that case, Anurādha, since a realized one is not found by you as a genuine fact in this very life, is it cogent for you to declare:

sn44.2:17.8.verse: ‘Reverends, when a realized one is describing a realized one—a supreme person, highest of people, who has reached the highest point—they describe them other than these four ways:

sn44.2:17.9.verse: After death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists’?”

sn44.2:17.13.verse: In the past, as today, what I describe is suffering and the cessation of suffering.”

sn44.6:2.5.verse: If you like, love, and enjoy feeling …

sn44.6:2.8.verse: consciousness, and don’t truly see the cessation of consciousness, you think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

sn44.6:2.9.verse: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

sn44.6:3.6.verse: consciousness, and you truly see the cessation of consciousness, you don’t think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

sn44.6:3.7.verse: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

sn44.6:3.8.verse: This is the cause, this is the reason why this has not been declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.6:4.1.verse: “But reverend, could there be another way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha?”

sn44.6:4.3.verse: If you like, love, and enjoy existence, and don’t truly see the cessation of continued existence, you think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

sn44.6:4.4.verse: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

sn44.6:4.5.verse: If you don’t like, love, and enjoy existence, and you truly see the cessation of continued existence, you don’t think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

sn44.6:4.6.verse: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

sn44.6:4.7.verse: This too is a way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.6:5.1.verse: “But reverend, could there be another way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha?”

sn44.6:5.3.verse: If you like, love, and enjoy grasping, and don’t truly see the cessation of grasping, you think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

sn44.6:5.4.verse: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

sn44.6:5.5.verse: If you don’t like, love, and enjoy grasping, and you truly see the cessation of grasping, you don’t think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

sn44.6:5.6.verse: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

sn44.6:5.7.verse: This too is a way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.6:6.1.verse: “But reverend, could there be another way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha?”

sn44.6:6.3.verse: If you like, love, and enjoy craving, and don’t truly see the cessation of craving, you think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

sn44.6:6.4.verse: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

sn44.6:6.5.verse: If you don’t like, love, and enjoy craving, and you truly see the cessation of craving, you don’t think ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

sn44.6:6.6.verse: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death.’

sn44.6:6.7.verse: This too is a way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.6:7.1.verse: “But reverend, could there be another way of explaining why this was not declared by the Buddha?”

sn44.6:7.2.verse: “Seriously, reverend, what more could you want?

sn44.6:7.3.verse: For one who is freed due to the ending of craving, there is no cycle of rebirths to be found.”

sn44.7:1.1.verse: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta went up to Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, and exchanged greetings with him.

sn44.7:1.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and said to Mahāmoggallāna:

sn44.7:2.1.verse: “Worthy Moggallāna, is this right: ‘the cosmos is eternal’?”

sn44.7:2.2.verse: “Vaccha, this has not been declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.7:2.4.verse: “Then is this right: ‘the cosmos is not eternal’ …

sn44.7:2.13.verse: ‘the soul and the body are one and the same’ …

sn44.7:2.16.verse: ‘the soul is one thing, the body another’ …

sn44.7:2.19.verse: ‘a realized one still exists after death’ …

sn44.7:2.22.verse: ‘a realized one no longer exists after death’ …

sn44.7:2.25.verse: ‘a realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death’ …

sn44.7:2.28.verse: ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’?”

sn44.7:2.29.verse: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.7:3.1.verse: “What’s the cause, worthy Moggallāna, what’s the reason why, when the wanderers of other religions are asked these questions, they declare one of these to be true?

sn44.7:3.3.verse: And what’s the reason why, when the ascetic Gotama is asked these questions, he does not declare one of these to be true?”

sn44.7:4.1.verse: “Vaccha, the wanderers of other religions regard the eye like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’ They regard the ear … nose …

sn44.7:4.3.verse: mind like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’

sn44.7:4.4.verse: That’s why, when asked, they declare one of those answers to be true.

sn44.7:4.7.verse: The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha regards the eye like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’ He regards the ear … nose …

sn44.7:4.9.verse: mind like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

sn44.7:4.10.verse: That’s why, when asked, he does not declare one of those answers to be true.”

sn44.7:5.1.verse: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta rose from his seat and went to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

sn44.7:5.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side. He asked the Buddha the same questions, and received the same answers.

sn44.7:8.1.verse: He said, “It’s incredible, worthy Gotama, it’s amazing!

sn44.7:8.2.verse: How the meaning and the phrasing of the Teacher and the disciple fit together and agree without contradiction when it comes to the chief matter!

sn44.7:8.3.verse: Just now I went to the ascetic Mahāmoggallāna and asked him about this matter.

sn44.7:8.4.verse: And he explained it to me with these words and phrases, just like the worthy Gotama.

sn44.7:8.5.verse: It’s incredible, worthy Gotama, it’s amazing!

sn44.7:8.6.verse: How the meaning and the phrasing of the Teacher and the disciple fit together and agree without contradiction when it comes to the chief matter!”

sn44.8:1.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and said to the Buddha:

sn44.8:1.3.verse: “Worthy Gotama, is this right: ‘the cosmos is eternal’?”

sn44.8:1.4.verse: “This has not been declared by me, Vaccha.” …

sn44.8:1.6.verse: “This too has not been declared by me.”

sn44.8:2.4.verse: And what’s the reason why, when the worthy Gotama is asked these questions, he does not declare one of these to be true?”

sn44.8:3.1.verse: “Vaccha, the wanderers of other religions regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

sn44.8:3.5.verse: consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

sn44.8:3.6.verse: That’s why, when asked, they declare one of those answers to be true.

sn44.8:3.9.verse: The Realized One doesn’t regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

sn44.8:3.13.verse: consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

sn44.8:3.14.verse: That’s why, when asked, he does not declare one of those answers to be true.”

sn44.9:1.1.verse: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

sn44.9:1.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and said to the Buddha:

sn44.9:2.1.verse: “Worthy Gotama, a few days ago several ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers who follow various other religions were sitting together in the debating hall, and this discussion came up among them:

sn44.9:2.2.verse: ‘This Pūraṇa Kassapa leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people.

sn44.9:2.3.verse: When a disciple passes away, he declares that

sn44.9:2.4.verse: this one is reborn here, while that one is reborn there.

sn44.9:2.5.verse: And as for a disciple who is a supreme person, highest of people, having reached the highest point, when they pass away he also declares that

sn44.9:2.6.verse: this one is reborn here, while that one is reborn there.

sn44.9:3.2.verse: the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan …

sn44.9:3.5.verse: Ajita of the hair blanket leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people.

sn44.9:3.6.verse: When a disciple passes away, he declares that

sn44.9:3.7.verse: this one is reborn here, while that one is reborn there.

sn44.9:3.8.verse: And as for a disciple who is a supreme person, highest of people, having reached the highest point, when they pass away he also declares that

sn44.9:3.9.verse: this one is reborn here, while that one is reborn there.

sn44.9:4.1.verse: This ascetic Gotama leads an order and a community, and tutors a community. He’s a well-known and famous religious founder, deemed holy by many people.

sn44.9:4.2.verse: When a disciple passes away, he declares that

sn44.9:4.3.verse: this one is reborn here, while that one is reborn there.

sn44.9:4.4.verse: But as for a disciple who is a supreme person, highest of people, having reached the highest point, when they pass away he doesn’t declare that

sn44.9:4.5.verse: this one is reborn here, while that one is reborn there.

sn44.9:4.6.verse: Rather, he declares that they have

sn44.9:4.7.verse: cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit have made an end of suffering.’

sn44.9:4.8.verse: I had doubt and uncertainty about that:

sn44.9:4.9.verse: ‘How on earth can I understand the ascetic Gotama’s teaching?’”

sn44.9:5.1.verse: “Vaccha, no wonder you’re doubting and uncertain.

sn44.9:5.2.verse: Doubt has come up in you about an uncertain matter.

sn44.9:5.3.verse: I describe rebirth for someone who grasps fuel, not for someone who does not.

sn44.9:5.4.verse: It’s like a fire which only burns with fuel, not without fuel.

sn44.9:5.5.verse: In the same way I describe rebirth for someone who grasps fuel, not for someone who doesn’t grasp fuel.”

sn44.9:6.1.verse: “But when a flame is blown away by the wind, what does the worthy Gotama say is its fuel then?”

sn44.9:6.2.verse: “At such a time, I say that it’s fueled by the wind.

sn44.9:6.3.verse: For the wind is its fuel then.”

sn44.9:6.4.verse: “But when someone who is attached has laid down this body and has not been reborn in one of the realms, what does the worthy Gotama say is their fuel then?”

sn44.9:6.5.verse: “When someone who is attached has laid down this body, Vaccha, and has not been reborn in one of the realms, I say they’re fueled by craving.

sn44.9:6.6.verse: For craving is their fuel then.”

sn44.10:1.1.verse: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

sn44.10:1.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

sn44.10:1.4.verse: But when he said this, the Buddha kept silent.

sn44.10:1.6.verse: But for a second time the Buddha kept silent.

sn44.10:1.7.verse: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta rose from his seat and left.

sn44.10:2.1.verse: And then, not long after Vacchagotta had left, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha:

sn44.10:2.2.verse: “Sir, why didn’t you answer Vacchagotta’s question?”

sn44.10:2.3.verse: “Ānanda, when Vacchagotta asked me whether the self survives, if I had answered that ‘the self survives’ I would have been siding with the ascetics and brahmins who are eternalists.

sn44.10:2.4.verse: When Vacchagotta asked me whether the self does not survive, if I had answered that ‘the self does not survive’ I would have been siding with the ascetics and brahmins who are annihilationists.

sn44.10:2.5.verse: When Vacchagotta asked me whether the self survives, if I had answered that ‘the self survives’, would that have facilitated the arising of the knowledge that

sn44.10:2.8.verse: “When Vacchagotta asked me whether the self does not survive, if I had answered that ‘the self does not survive’, Vacchagotta—who is already confused—would have got even more confused, thinking:

sn44.10:2.9.verse: ‘It seems that the self that I once had no longer survives.’”

sn44.11:1.1.verse: At one time Venerable Sabhiya Kaccāna was staying at Ñātika in the brick house.

sn44.11:1.2.verse: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta went up to him, and exchanged greetings with him.

sn44.11:1.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and said to Sabhiya Kaccāna:

sn44.11:1.4.verse: “Worthy Kaccāna, does a realized one still exist after death?”

sn44.11:1.5.verse: “Vaccha, this has not been declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.11:1.7.verse: “Well then, does a realized one no longer exist after death?”

sn44.11:1.8.verse: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.11:2.1.verse: “Well then, does a realized one both still exist and no longer exist after death?”

sn44.11:2.2.verse: “This has not been declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.11:2.4.verse: “Well then, does a realized one neither still exist nor no longer exist after death?”

sn44.11:2.5.verse: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

sn44.11:3.1.verse: “Worthy Kaccāna, when asked these questions, you say that this has not been declared by the Buddha.

sn44.11:3.13.verse: What’s the cause, what’s the reason why this has not been declared by the Buddha?”

sn44.11:3.14.verse: “In order to describe him as ‘formed’ or ‘formless’ or ‘percipient’ or ‘non-percipient’ or ‘neither percipient nor non-percipient’, there must be some cause or reason for doing so. But if that cause and reason were to totally and utterly cease without remainder,

sn44.11:3.15.verse: how could you describe him in any such terms?”

sn44.11:3.16.verse: “Worthy Kaccāna, how long has it been since you went forth?”

sn44.11:3.18.verse: “One who has learned this much in this time, reverend, has learned a lot, who can say what lies ahead!”

sn44.11:4.6.verse: The Linked Discourses on undeclared questions are complete.

sn44.11:5.7.verse: The Book of the Six Sense Fields is finished.

sn45.1:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn45.1:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

sn45.1:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, ignorance leads the attainment of unskillful qualities, with lack of conscience and prudence following along.

sn45.1:2.2.verse: An ignoramus, sunk in ignorance, produces wrong view.

sn45.1:3.1.verse: Knowledge leads the attainment of skillful qualities, with conscience and prudence following along.

sn45.1:3.2.verse: A knowing one, firm in knowledge, produces right view.

sn45.2:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, where they have a town named Townsville.

sn45.2:1.3.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn45.2:1.4.verse: “Sir, good friends, companions, and associates are half the spiritual life.”

sn45.2:2.2.verse: Good friends, companions, and associates are the whole of the spiritual life.

sn45.2:2.3.verse: A mendicant with good friends, companions, and associates can expect to develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path.

sn45.2:3.1.verse: And how does a mendicant with good friends develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path?

sn45.2:3.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops right view, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go.

sn45.2:3.9.verse: right immersion, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go.

sn45.2:3.10.verse: That’s how a mendicant with good friends develops and cultivates the noble eightfold path.

sn45.2:4.1.verse: And here’s another way to understand how good friends are the whole of the spiritual life.

sn45.2:4.2.verse: For, by relying on me as a good friend, sentient beings who are liable to rebirth, old age, and death, to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are freed from all these things.

sn45.2:4.3.verse: This is another way to understand how good friends are the whole of the spiritual life.”

sn45.3:1.2.verse: Then Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn45.3:1.3.verse: “Sir, good friends, companions, and associates are the whole of the spiritual life.”

sn45.3:2.2.verse: Good friends, companions, and associates are the whole of the spiritual life.

sn45.3:2.3.verse: A mendicant with good friends, companions, and associates can expect to develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path.

sn45.3:2.4.verse: And how does a mendicant with good friends develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path?

sn45.3:3.1.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn45.3:3.2.verse: That’s how a mendicant with good friends develops and cultivates the noble eightfold path.

sn45.3:4.1.verse: And here’s another way to understand how good friends are the whole of the spiritual life.

sn45.3:4.2.verse: For, by relying on me as a good friend, sentient beings who are liable to rebirth, old age, and death, to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are freed from all these things.

sn45.3:4.3.verse: This is another way to understand how good friends are the whole of the spiritual life.”

sn45.4:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn45.4:1.3.verse: He saw the brahmin Jānussoṇi driving out of Sāvatthī in an all-white chariot drawn by mares.

sn45.4:1.4.verse: The yoked horses were pure white, as were the ornaments, chariot, upholstery, reins, goad, and canopy. And his turban, robes, sandals were white, as was the chowry fanning him.

sn45.4:1.5.verse: When people saw it they exclaimed,

sn45.4:1.7.verse: It’s a vehicle fit for divinity!”

sn45.4:2.1.verse: Then Ānanda wandered for alms in Sāvatthī. After the meal, on his return from almsround, he went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened, adding,

sn45.4:3.7.verse: “Sir, can you point out a divine vehicle in this teaching and training?”

sn45.4:4.2.verse: “These are all terms for the noble eightfold path:

sn45.4:4.3.verse: ‘divine vehicle’, or else ‘vehicle of truth’, or else ‘supreme victory in battle’.

sn45.4:5.1.verse: When right view is developed and cultivated it culminates with the removal of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.4:5.8.verse: right immersion is developed and cultivated it culminates with the removal of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.4:6.1.verse: This is a way to understand how these are all terms for the noble eightfold path:

sn45.4:6.2.verse: ‘divine vehicle’, or else ‘vehicle of truth’, or else ‘supreme victory in battle’.”

sn45.4:6.3.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn45.4:7.1.verse: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

sn45.4:8.1.verse: “Of which the qualities of faith and wisdom

sn45.4:8.2.verse: are always yoked to the shaft;

sn45.4:8.3.verse: conscience its draft-pole, mind its strap,

sn45.4:9.2.verse: its axle absorption, energy its wheel;

sn45.4:10.4.verse: to sanctuary from the yoke it rolls—

sn45.4:11.3.verse: The attentive leave the world in it,

sn45.5:1.2.verse: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha … and said to him:

sn45.5:2.1.verse: “Sir, sometimes wanderers of other religions ask us:

sn45.5:2.2.verse: ‘Reverends, what’s the goal of leading the spiritual life under the ascetic Gotama?’

sn45.5:2.4.verse: ‘The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to completely understand suffering.’

sn45.5:2.5.verse: Answering this way, we trust that we repeat what the Buddha has said, and don’t misrepresent him with an untruth. We trust our explanation is in line with the teaching, and that there are no legitimate grounds for rebuttal or criticism.”

sn45.5:3.1.verse: “Indeed, in answering this way you repeat what I’ve said, and don’t misrepresent me with an untruth. Your explanation is in line with the teaching, and there are no legitimate grounds for rebuttal or criticism.

sn45.5:3.2.verse: For the goal of leading the spiritual life under me is to completely understand suffering.

sn45.5:3.3.verse: If wanderers of other religions were to ask you:

sn45.5:3.4.verse: ‘Is there a path and a practice for completely understanding that suffering?’ You should answer them like this:

sn45.5:4.2.verse: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.5:4.3.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.5:4.4.verse: This is the path and the practice for completely understanding suffering.

sn45.5:4.5.verse: When questioned by wanderers of other religions, that’s how you should answer them.”

sn45.6:1.2.verse: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

sn45.6:1.3.verse: “Sir, they speak of this thing called the ‘spiritual path’.

sn45.6:1.4.verse: What is the spiritual path? And what is the culmination of the spiritual path?”

sn45.6:2.1.verse: “Mendicant, the spiritual path is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.6:2.2.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.6:2.3.verse: The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.6:2.4.verse: This is the culmination of the spiritual path.”

sn45.7:1.2.verse: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha … and said to him:

sn45.7:2.1.verse: “Sir, they speak of ‘the removal of greed, hate, and delusion’.

sn45.7:2.2.verse: What is this a term for?”

sn45.7:2.4.verse: “Mendicant, the removal of greed, hate, and delusion is a term for an element of extinguishment.

sn45.7:2.6.verse: It’s used to speak of the ending of defilements.”

sn45.7:3.1.verse: When he said this, the mendicant said to the Buddha:

sn45.7:3.3.verse: What is freedom from death? And what is the path that leads to freedom from death?”

sn45.7:3.4.verse: “The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.7:3.5.verse: This is called freedom from death.

sn45.7:3.6.verse: The path that leads to freedom from death is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.7:3.7.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.”

sn45.8:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach and analyze for you the noble eightfold path.

sn45.8:1.3.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn45.8:2.1.verse: “And what is the noble eightfold path?

sn45.8:2.2.verse: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.8:3.2.verse: Knowing about suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.

sn45.8:4.2.verse: The purpose of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness.

sn45.8:5.2.verse: Refraining from speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.

sn45.8:6.2.verse: Refraining from killing living creatures, stealing, and unchastity.

sn45.8:7.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple gives up wrong livelihood and earns a living by right livelihood.

sn45.8:8.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise.

sn45.8:8.3.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen are given up.

sn45.8:8.4.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities arise.

sn45.8:8.5.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.

sn45.8:9.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

sn45.8:9.3.verse: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

sn45.8:9.4.verse: They meditate observing an aspect of the mind—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

sn45.8:9.5.verse: They meditate observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

sn45.8:10.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn45.8:10.3.verse: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn45.8:10.4.verse: And with the fading away of rapture, they enter and remain in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

sn45.8:10.5.verse: With the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

sn45.9:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, suppose a spike of rice or barley was pointing the wrong way. If you trod on it with hand or foot, it is impossible for it to break the skin and produce blood.

sn45.9:1.4.verse: Because the spike is pointing the wrong way.

sn45.9:1.5.verse: In the same way, a mendicant whose view and development of the path is pointing the wrong way cannot break ignorance, produce knowledge, and realize extinguishment.

sn45.9:1.7.verse: Because their view is pointing the wrong way.

sn45.9:2.1.verse: Suppose a spike of rice or barley was pointing the right way. If you trod on it with hand or foot, it’s possible it may break the skin and produce blood.

sn45.9:2.3.verse: Because the spike is pointing the right way.

sn45.9:2.4.verse: In the same way, a mendicant whose view and development of the path is pointing the right way may well break ignorance, produce knowledge, and realize extinguishment.

sn45.9:2.6.verse: Because their view is pointing the right way.

sn45.9:3.1.verse: And how does a mendicant whose view and development of the path is pointing the right way break ignorance, give rise to knowledge, and realize extinguishment?

sn45.9:3.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn45.9:3.3.verse: That’s how a mendicant whose view and development of the path is pointing the right way breaks ignorance, gives rise to knowledge, and realizes extinguishment.”

sn45.10:1.2.verse: Then the wanderer Nandiya went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

sn45.10:1.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and said to the Buddha:

sn45.10:1.4.verse: “Worthy Gotama, how many things, when developed and cultivated, have extinguishment as their target, destination, and culmination?”

sn45.10:2.1.verse: “These eight things, when developed and cultivated, have extinguishment as their target, destination, and culmination.

sn45.10:2.3.verse: They are: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.10:2.4.verse: These eight things, when developed and cultivated, have extinguishment as their target, destination, and culmination.”

sn45.10:2.5.verse: When he said this, the wanderer Nandiya said to the Buddha,

sn45.10:2.7.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

sn45.11:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I wish to go on retreat for a fortnight.

sn45.11:1.3.verse: No-one should approach me, except the one who brings my almsfood.”

sn45.11:1.4.verse: “Yes, sir,” replied those mendicants. And no-one approached him, except the one who brought the almsfood.

sn45.11:2.1.verse: Then after a fortnight had passed, the Buddha came out of retreat and addressed the mendicants:

sn45.11:2.2.verse: “Mendicants, I’ve been practicing part of the meditation I practiced when I was first awakened.

sn45.11:2.4.verse: there’s feeling conditioned by wrong view

sn45.11:2.5.verse: and feeling conditioned by right view. …

sn45.11:2.6.verse: There’s feeling conditioned by wrong immersion,

sn45.11:2.7.verse: and feeling conditioned by right immersion.

sn45.11:2.11.verse: As long as desire, thought, and perception are not stilled, there is feeling conditioned by that.

sn45.11:2.12.verse: When desire, thought, and perception are stilled, there is feeling conditioned by that.

sn45.11:2.13.verse: There is effort to attain the unattained. When that state has been attained, there is also feeling conditioned by that.”

sn45.12:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I wish to go on retreat for three months.

sn45.12:1.3.verse: No-one should approach me, except the one who brings my almsfood.”

sn45.12:1.4.verse: “Yes, sir,” replied those mendicants. And no-one approached him, except the one who brought the almsfood.

sn45.12:2.1.verse: Then after three months had passed, the Buddha came out of retreat and addressed the mendicants:

sn45.12:2.2.verse: “Mendicants, I’ve been practicing part of the meditation I practiced when I was first awakened.

sn45.12:2.4.verse: there’s feeling conditioned by wrong view

sn45.12:2.5.verse: and by the settling of wrong view,

sn45.12:2.7.verse: and by the settling of right view. …

sn45.12:2.8.verse: There’s feeling conditioned by wrong immersion

sn45.12:2.9.verse: and by the settling of wrong immersion, by right immersion

sn45.12:2.10.verse: and by the settling of right immersion.

sn45.12:2.12.verse: and by the settling of desire.

sn45.12:2.14.verse: and by the settling of thought.

sn45.12:2.16.verse: and by the settling of perception.

sn45.12:2.17.verse: As long as desire, thought, and perception are not stilled, there is feeling conditioned by that.

sn45.12:2.18.verse: When desire, thought, and perception are stilled, there is feeling conditioned by that.

sn45.12:2.19.verse: There is effort to attain the unattained. When that state has been attained, there is also feeling conditioned by that.”

sn45.13:1.2.verse: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

sn45.13:1.3.verse: “Sir, they speak of the one called ‘a trainee’.

sn45.13:2.1.verse: “Mendicant, it’s someone who has a trainee’s right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.13:2.2.verse: That’s how a trainee is defined.”

sn45.14:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, these eight things don’t arise to be developed and cultivated except when a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha has appeared.

sn45.14:1.4.verse: They are: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.14:1.5.verse: These eight things don’t arise to be developed and cultivated except when a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha has appeared.”

sn45.15:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, these eight things don’t arise to be developed and cultivated apart from the Holy One’s training.

sn45.15:1.4.verse: They are: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.15:1.5.verse: These are the eight things that don’t arise to be developed and cultivated apart from the Holy One’s training.”

sn45.16:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, these eight things don’t arise to be purified, bright, flawless, and rid of corruptions except when a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha has appeared.

sn45.16:1.4.verse: They are: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.16:1.5.verse: These eight things don’t arise to be purified, bright, flawless, and rid of corruptions except when a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha has appeared.”

sn45.17:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, these eight things don’t arise to be purified, bright, flawless, and rid of corruptions apart from the Holy One’s training.

sn45.17:1.4.verse: They are: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.17:1.5.verse: These eight things don’t arise to be purified, bright, flawless, and rid of corruptions apart from the Holy One’s training.”

sn45.18:1.2.verse: At one time the venerables Ānanda and Bhadda were staying near Pāṭaliputta, in the Chicken Monastery.

sn45.18:1.3.verse: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Bhadda came out of retreat, went to Venerable Ānanda, and exchanged greetings with him.

sn45.18:1.4.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Ānanda:

sn45.18:2.1.verse: “Reverend, they speak of this thing called ‘not the spiritual path’.

sn45.18:2.2.verse: What is not the spiritual path?”

sn45.18:2.4.verse: Your approach and eloquence are excellent, and it’s a good question.

sn45.18:2.6.verse: ‘They speak of this thing called “not the spiritual path”.

sn45.18:2.7.verse: What is not the spiritual path?’”

sn45.18:2.9.verse: “What is not the spiritual path is simply the wrong eightfold path, that is:

sn45.18:2.10.verse: wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.”

sn45.19:1.2.verse: “Reverend, they speak of this thing called the ‘spiritual path’.

sn45.19:1.3.verse: What is the spiritual path? And what is the culmination of the spiritual path?”

sn45.19:1.5.verse: Your approach and eloquence are excellent, and it’s a good question.

sn45.19:1.7.verse: ‘They speak of this thing called “the spiritual path”.

sn45.19:1.8.verse: What is the spiritual path? And what is the culmination of the spiritual path?’”

sn45.19:1.10.verse: “The spiritual path is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.19:1.11.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.19:1.12.verse: The ending of greed, hate, and delusion:

sn45.19:1.13.verse: this is the culmination of the spiritual path.”

sn45.20:1.2.verse: “Reverend, they speak of this thing called the ‘spiritual path’.

sn45.20:1.3.verse: What is the spiritual path? Who is someone on the spiritual path? And what is the culmination of the spiritual path?”

sn45.20:1.5.verse: Your approach and eloquence are excellent, and it’s a good question. …

sn45.20:1.10.verse: The spiritual path is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.20:1.11.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.20:1.12.verse: Someone who possesses this noble eightfold path

sn45.20:1.13.verse: is called someone on the spiritual path.

sn45.20:1.14.verse: The ending of greed, hate, and delusion:

sn45.20:1.15.verse: this is the culmination of the spiritual path.”

sn45.21:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the wrong way and the right way.

sn45.21:1.4.verse: And what is the wrong way?

sn45.21:1.5.verse: It is wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.21:1.6.verse: This is called the wrong way.

sn45.21:1.7.verse: And what is the right way?

sn45.21:1.8.verse: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.21:1.9.verse: This is called the right way.”

sn45.22:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you skillful and unskillful qualities.

sn45.22:1.5.verse: They are wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.22:1.8.verse: They are right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.23:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the wrong practice and the right practice.

sn45.23:1.5.verse: It is wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.23:1.6.verse: This is called the wrong practice.

sn45.23:1.8.verse: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.23:1.9.verse: This is called the right practice.”

sn45.24:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I don’t praise wrong practice for laypeople or renunciates.

sn45.24:1.3.verse: Because of wrong practice, neither laypeople nor renunciates succeed in the system of the skillful teaching.

sn45.24:2.2.verse: It is wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.24:2.3.verse: This is called the wrong practice.

sn45.24:2.4.verse: I don’t praise wrong practice for lay people or renunciates.

sn45.24:2.5.verse: Because of wrong practice, neither laypeople nor renunciates succeed in the system of the skillful teaching.

sn45.24:3.1.verse: I praise right practice for laypeople and renunciates.

sn45.24:3.2.verse: Because of right practice, both laypeople and renunciates succeed in the system of the skillful teaching.

sn45.24:3.4.verse: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.24:3.5.verse: This is called the right practice.

sn45.24:3.6.verse: I praise right practice for laypeople and renunciates.

sn45.24:3.7.verse: Because of right practice, both laypeople and renunciates succeed in the system of the skillful teaching.”

sn45.25:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you an untrue person and a true person.

sn45.25:1.4.verse: And what is an untrue person?

sn45.25:1.5.verse: It’s someone who has wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.25:1.6.verse: This is called an untrue person.

sn45.25:2.1.verse: And what is a true person?

sn45.25:2.2.verse: It’s someone who has right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.25:2.3.verse: This is called a true person.”

sn45.26:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you an untrue person and an even more untrue person,

sn45.26:1.3.verse: a true person and an even truer person.

sn45.26:1.5.verse: And what is an untrue person?

sn45.26:1.6.verse: It’s someone who has wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.26:1.7.verse: This is called an untrue person.

sn45.26:2.1.verse: And what is an even more untrue person?

sn45.26:2.2.verse: It’s someone who has wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.

sn45.26:2.3.verse: This is called an even more untrue person.

sn45.26:3.1.verse: And what is a true person?

sn45.26:3.2.verse: It’s someone who has right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.26:3.3.verse: This is called a true person.

sn45.26:4.1.verse: And what is an even truer person?

sn45.26:4.2.verse: It’s someone who has right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

sn45.26:4.3.verse: This is called an even truer person.”

sn45.27:1.2.verse: “A pot without a stand is easy to overturn, but if it has a stand it’s hard to overturn.

sn45.27:1.3.verse: In the same way, a mind without a stand is easy to overturn, but if it has a stand it’s hard to overturn.

sn45.27:1.4.verse: And what’s the stand for the mind?

sn45.27:1.5.verse: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.27:1.6.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.27:1.7.verse: This is the stand for the mind.

sn45.27:1.8.verse: A pot without a stand is easy to overturn, but if it has a stand it’s hard to overturn.

sn45.27:1.9.verse: In the same way, a mind without a stand is easy to overturn, but if it has a stand it’s hard to overturn.”

sn45.28:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you noble right immersion with its vital conditions and its prerequisites.

sn45.28:1.4.verse: And what is noble right immersion with its vital conditions and its prerequisites?

sn45.28:1.5.verse: There are right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, and right mindfulness.

sn45.28:1.6.verse: Unification of mind with these seven factors as prerequisites

sn45.28:1.7.verse: is called noble right immersion ‘with its vital conditions’ and also ‘with its prerequisites’.”

sn45.29:1.6.verse: The noble eightfold path should be developed to completely understand these three feelings.

sn45.29:1.7.verse: What is the noble eightfold path?

sn45.29:1.8.verse: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.29:1.9.verse: This noble eightfold path should be developed to completely understand these three feelings.”

sn45.30:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Uttiya went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

sn45.30:1.3.verse: “Just now, sir, as I was in private retreat this thought came to mind.

sn45.30:1.4.verse: ‘The Buddha has spoken of the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn45.30:1.7.verse: I have spoken of these five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn45.30:1.9.verse: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn45.30:1.13.verse: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn45.30:1.14.verse: These are the five kinds of sensual stimulation that I’ve spoken of.

sn45.30:1.15.verse: The noble eightfold path should be developed to give up these five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn45.30:1.16.verse: What is the noble eightfold path?

sn45.30:1.17.verse: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.30:1.18.verse: This is the noble eightfold path that should be developed to give up these five kinds of sensual stimulation.”

sn45.31:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the wrong practice and the right practice.

sn45.31:1.5.verse: It is wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.31:1.6.verse: This is called the wrong practice.

sn45.31:1.8.verse: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.31:1.9.verse: This is called the right practice.”

sn45.32:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you one practicing wrongly and one practicing rightly.

sn45.32:1.5.verse: It’s someone who has wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.32:1.6.verse: This is called one practicing wrongly.

sn45.32:1.8.verse: It’s someone who has right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.32:1.9.verse: This is called one practicing rightly.”

sn45.33:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, whoever has missed out on the noble eightfold path has missed out on the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.

sn45.33:1.3.verse: Whoever has undertaken the noble eightfold path has undertaken the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.

sn45.33:1.4.verse: And what is the noble eightfold path?

sn45.33:1.5.verse: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.33:1.6.verse: Whoever has missed out on the noble eightfold path has missed out on the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.

sn45.33:1.7.verse: Whoever has undertaken the noble eightfold path has undertaken the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.”

sn45.34:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when these eight things are developed and cultivated they lead to going from the near shore to the far shore.

sn45.34:1.4.verse: They are right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.34:1.5.verse: When these eight things are developed and cultivated they lead to going from the near shore to the far shore.”

sn45.34:2.1.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn45.34:2.2.verse: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

sn45.34:3.2.verse: who cross to the far shore.

sn45.34:4.1.verse: When the teaching is well explained,

sn45.34:4.4.verse: Death’s dominion so hard to pass.

sn45.34:5.2.verse: an astute person would develop the bright.

sn45.34:5.4.verse: in seclusion, where joy is hard,

sn45.34:6.3.verse: an astute person would cleanse themselves

sn45.34:7.1.verse: And those whose minds are rightly developed

sn45.34:7.6.verse: they are quenched in this world.”

sn45.35:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the ascetic life and the fruits of the ascetic life.

sn45.35:1.4.verse: And what is the ascetic life?

sn45.35:1.5.verse: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.35:1.6.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.35:1.7.verse: This is called the ascetic life.

sn45.35:1.8.verse: And what are the fruits of the ascetic life?

sn45.35:1.9.verse: The fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection.

sn45.35:1.10.verse: These are called the fruits of the ascetic life.”

sn45.36:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the ascetic life and the goal of the ascetic life.

sn45.36:1.4.verse: And what is the ascetic life?

sn45.36:1.5.verse: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.36:1.6.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.36:1.7.verse: This is called the ascetic life.

sn45.36:1.8.verse: And what is the goal of the ascetic life?

sn45.36:1.9.verse: The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.36:1.10.verse: This is called the goal of the ascetic life.”

sn45.37:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you life as a brahmin and the fruits of life as a brahmin.

sn45.37:1.4.verse: And what is life as a brahmin?

sn45.37:1.5.verse: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.37:1.6.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.37:1.7.verse: This is called life as a brahmin.

sn45.37:1.8.verse: And what are the fruits of life as a brahmin?

sn45.37:1.9.verse: The fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection.

sn45.37:1.10.verse: These are called the fruits of life as a brahmin.”

sn45.38:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you life as a brahmin and the goal of life as a brahmin.

sn45.38:1.4.verse: And what is life as a brahmin?

sn45.38:1.5.verse: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.38:1.6.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.38:1.7.verse: This is called life as a brahmin.

sn45.38:1.8.verse: And what is the goal of life as a brahmin?

sn45.38:1.9.verse: The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.38:1.10.verse: This is called the goal of life as a brahmin.”

sn45.39:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the spiritual path and the fruits of the spiritual path.

sn45.39:1.4.verse: And what is the spiritual path?

sn45.39:1.5.verse: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.39:1.6.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.39:1.7.verse: This is called the spiritual path.

sn45.39:1.8.verse: And what are the fruits of the spiritual path?

sn45.39:1.9.verse: The fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection.

sn45.39:1.10.verse: These are called the fruits of the spiritual path.”

sn45.40:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you the spiritual path and the goal of the spiritual path.

sn45.40:1.4.verse: And what is the spiritual path?

sn45.40:1.5.verse: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.40:1.6.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.40:1.7.verse: This is called the spiritual path.

sn45.40:1.8.verse: And what is the goal of the spiritual path?

sn45.40:1.9.verse: The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.40:1.10.verse: This is called the goal of the spiritual path.”

sn45.41:0.2.verse: 5. Abbreviated Texts on Followers of Other Religions

sn45.41:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, if wanderers who follow another religion were to ask you:

sn45.41:1.3.verse: ‘Reverends, what’s the goal of leading the spiritual life under the ascetic Gotama?’ You should answer them like this:

sn45.41:1.4.verse: ‘The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is the fading away of greed.’

sn45.41:1.5.verse: If wanderers of other religions were to ask you:

sn45.41:1.6.verse: ‘Is there a path and a practice for the fading away of greed?’ You should answer them like this:

sn45.41:1.7.verse: ‘There is a path and a practice for the fading away of greed.’

sn45.41:1.8.verse: And what is that path, what is that practice for the fading away of greed?

sn45.41:1.9.verse: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.41:1.10.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.41:1.11.verse: This is the path, this is the practice for the fading away of greed.

sn45.41:1.12.verse: When questioned by wanderers of other religions, that’s how you should answer them.”
