sn46.34:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these seven awakening factors are not obstacles, hindrances, or corruptions of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.

sn46.34:1.3.verse: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.34:1.4.verse: These seven awakening factors are not obstacles, hindrances, or corruptions of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.”

sn46.35:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when you apply the mind irrationally, sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt arise, and once arisen they increase and grow.”

sn46.35:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, when you apply the mind rationally, the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity arise, and once they’ve arisen, they’re fully developed.”

sn46.36:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when the seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they lead to growth and progress.

sn46.36:1.3.verse: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.36:1.4.verse: When these seven awakening factors are developed and cultivated they lead to growth and progress.”

sn46.37:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these five obstacles and hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.

sn46.37:1.8.verse: These are the five obstacles and hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.

sn46.37:2.1.verse: There are these seven awakening factors that are not obstacles, hindrances, or corruptions of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.

sn46.37:2.3.verse: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.37:2.4.verse: These seven awakening factors are not obstacles, hindrances, or corruptions of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.”

sn46.38:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, sometimes a noble disciple pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens to the teaching. At such a time the five hindrances are absent, and the seven awakening factors are fully developed.

sn46.38:2.1.verse: What are the five hindrances that are absent?

sn46.38:2.2.verse: Sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.

sn46.38:2.3.verse: These are the five hindrances that are absent.

sn46.38:3.1.verse: And what are the seven awakening factors that are fully developed?

sn46.38:3.2.verse: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.38:3.3.verse: These are the seven awakening factors that are fully developed.

sn46.38:3.4.verse: Sometimes a noble disciple pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens to the teaching. At such a time the five hindrances are absent, and the seven awakening factors are fully developed.”

sn46.39:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are large trees with tiny seeds and big bodies, which grow up and around other trees as parasites. The trees they engulf break apart, collapse, and fall.

sn46.39:1.2.verse: And what are those large trees with tiny seeds and big bodies?

sn46.39:1.3.verse: The peepal, banyan, wavy leaf fig, cluster fig, Moreton Bay fig, and white fig.

sn46.39:1.4.verse: These are the large trees with tiny seeds and big bodies, which grow up and around other trees as parasites. The trees they engulf break apart, collapse, and fall.

sn46.39:1.5.verse: In the same way, take a certain gentleman who has gone forth from the lay life to homelessness, abandoning sensual pleasures. But beset by sensual pleasures that are similar, or even worse, he breaks apart, collapses, and falls.

sn46.39:2.1.verse: There are these five obstacles and hindrances, parasites of the mind that weaken wisdom.

sn46.39:2.8.verse: These are the five obstacles and hindrances, parasites of the mind that weaken wisdom.

sn46.39:3.1.verse: These seven awakening factors are not obstacles, hindrances, or parasites of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.

sn46.39:3.3.verse: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.39:3.4.verse: These seven awakening factors are not obstacles, hindrances, or parasites of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.”

sn46.40:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five hindrances are destroyers of sight, vision, and knowledge. They block wisdom, they’re on the side of distress, and they don’t lead to extinguishment.

sn46.40:1.3.verse: Sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.

sn46.40:1.8.verse: These five hindrances are destroyers of sight, vision, and knowledge. They block wisdom, they’re on the side of distress, and they don’t lead to extinguishment.

sn46.40:2.1.verse: These seven awakening factors are creators of vision and knowledge. They grow wisdom, they’re on the side of solace, and they lead to extinguishment.

sn46.40:2.3.verse: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.40:2.4.verse: These seven awakening factors are creators of vision and knowledge. They grow wisdom, they’re on the side of solace, and they lead to extinguishment.”

sn46.41:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, all the ascetics and brahmins in the past who have given up the three discriminations have done so by developing and cultivating the seven awakening factors.

sn46.48:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, the dawn is the forerunner and harbinger of the sunrise.

sn46.48:1.2.verse: In the same way, for a mendicant good friendship is the forerunner and harbinger of the arising of the seven awakening factors.

sn46.48:1.3.verse: A mendicant with good friends can expect to develop and cultivate the seven awakening factors.

sn46.48:1.4.verse: And how does a mendicant with good friends develop and cultivate the seven awakening factors?

sn46.48:1.6.verse: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn46.49:1.1.verse: “Taking into account interior factors, mendicants, I do not see a single one that gives rise to the seven awakening factors like rational application of mind. …”

sn46.51:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you what fuels and what starves the five hindrances and the seven awakening factors.

sn46.51:1.4.verse: And what fuels the arising of sensual desire, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow?

sn46.51:1.5.verse: There is the feature of beauty.

sn46.51:1.6.verse: Frequent irrational application of mind to that

sn46.51:1.7.verse: fuels the arising of sensual desire, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow.

sn46.51:2.1.verse: And what fuels the arising of ill will, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow?

sn46.51:2.2.verse: There is the feature of aversion.

sn46.51:2.3.verse: Frequent irrational application of mind to that

sn46.51:2.4.verse: fuels the arising of ill will, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow.

sn46.51:3.1.verse: And what fuels the arising of dullness and drowsiness, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow?

sn46.51:3.2.verse: There is discontent, sloth, yawning, sleepiness after eating, and mental sluggishness.

sn46.51:3.3.verse: Frequent irrational application of mind to that

sn46.51:3.4.verse: fuels the arising of dullness and drowsiness, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow.

sn46.51:4.1.verse: And what fuels the arising of restlessness and remorse, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow?

sn46.51:4.3.verse: Frequent irrational application of mind to that

sn46.51:5.1.verse: And what fuels the arising of doubt, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow?

sn46.51:5.2.verse: There are things that are grounds for doubt.

sn46.51:5.3.verse: Frequent irrational application of mind to them

sn46.51:5.4.verse: fuels the arising of doubt, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow.

sn46.51:6.1.verse: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of mindfulness, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.51:6.2.verse: There are things that are grounds for the awakening factor of mindfulness.

sn46.51:6.3.verse: Frequent rational application of mind to them

sn46.51:6.4.verse: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of mindfulness, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.51:7.1.verse: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of investigation of principles, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.51:7.2.verse: There are qualities that are skillful and unskillful, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, and those with a portion of dark or bright.

sn46.51:7.3.verse: Frequent rational application of mind to them

sn46.51:7.4.verse: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of investigation of principles, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.51:8.1.verse: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of energy, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.51:8.2.verse: There are the elements of initiative, persistence, and exertion.

sn46.51:8.3.verse: Frequent rational application of mind to them

sn46.51:8.4.verse: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of energy, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.51:9.1.verse: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of rapture, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.51:9.2.verse: There are things that are grounds for the awakening factor of rapture.

sn46.51:9.3.verse: Frequent rational application of mind to them

sn46.51:9.4.verse: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of rapture, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.51:10.1.verse: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of tranquility, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.51:10.2.verse: There is tranquility of the body and of the mind.

sn46.51:10.3.verse: Frequent rational application of mind to that

sn46.51:10.4.verse: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of tranquility, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.51:11.1.verse: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of immersion, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.51:11.2.verse: There are things that are the basis of serenity and freedom from distraction.

sn46.51:11.3.verse: Frequent rational application of mind to them

sn46.51:11.4.verse: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of immersion, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.51:12.1.verse: And what fuels the arising of the awakening factor of equanimity, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it?

sn46.51:12.2.verse: There are things that are grounds for the awakening factor of equanimity.

sn46.51:12.3.verse: Frequent rational application of mind to them

sn46.51:12.4.verse: fuels the arising of the awakening factor of equanimity, or, when it has arisen, fully develops it.

sn46.51:13.2.verse: There is the feature of ugliness.

sn46.51:13.3.verse: Frequent rational application of mind to that

sn46.51:13.4.verse: starves the arising of sensual desire, or, when it has arisen, starves its increase and growth.

sn46.51:14.3.verse: Frequent rational application of mind to that

sn46.51:14.4.verse: starves the arising of ill will, or, when it has arisen, starves its increase and growth.

sn46.51:15.1.verse: And what starves the arising of dullness and drowsiness, or, when they have arisen, starves their increase and growth?

sn46.51:16.3.verse: Frequent rational application of mind to that

sn46.51:17.4.verse: starves the arising of doubt, or, when it has arisen, starves its increase and growth.

sn46.51:18.3.verse: Not frequently applying the mind to that

sn46.51:22.4.verse: starves the arising of the awakening factor of tranquility, or, when it has arisen, starves its full development.

sn46.51:23.2.verse: There are things that are the basis of serenity and freedom from distraction.

sn46.51:23.3.verse: Not frequently applying the mind to that

sn46.51:23.4.verse: starves the arising of the awakening factor of immersion, or, when it has arisen, starves its full development.

sn46.51:24.1.verse: And what starves the arising of the awakening factor of equanimity, or, when it has arisen, starves its full development?

sn46.52:1.1.verse: Then several mendicants robed up in the morning and, taking their bowls and robes, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn46.52:1.3.verse: “It’s too early to wander for alms in Sāvatthī.

sn46.52:1.4.verse: Why don’t we visit the monastery for the wanderers of other religions?”

sn46.52:2.1.verse: Then they went to the monastery for the wanderers of other religions and exchanged greetings with the wanderers there.

sn46.52:2.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side. The wanderers said to them:

sn46.52:3.1.verse: “Reverends, the ascetic Gotama teaches his disciples like this:

sn46.52:3.2.verse: ‘Mendicants, please give up the five hindrances—corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom—and truly develop the seven awakening factors.’

sn46.52:3.4.verse: ‘Reverends, please give up the five hindrances—corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom—and truly develop the seven awakening factors.’

sn46.52:3.5.verse: What, then, is the difference between the ascetic Gotama’s teaching and instruction and ours?”

sn46.52:4.1.verse: Those mendicants neither approved nor rejected that statement of the wanderers of other religions.

sn46.52:4.2.verse: They rose from their seats, thinking:

sn46.52:4.3.verse: “We will learn the meaning of this statement from the Buddha himself.”

sn46.52:4.4.verse: Then, after the meal, when they returned from almsround, they went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

sn46.52:8.1.verse: “Mendicants, when wanderers of other religions say this, you should say to them:

sn46.52:8.2.verse: ‘But reverends, is there a way in which the five hindrances become ten and the seven awakening factors become fourteen?’

sn46.52:8.3.verse: Questioned like this, the wanderers of other religions would be stumped, and, in addition, would get frustrated.

sn46.52:8.5.verse: Because they’re out of their element.

sn46.52:8.6.verse: I don’t see anyone in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—who could provide a satisfying answer to these questions except the Realized One or his disciple or someone who has heard it from them.

sn46.52:9.1.verse: And what is the way in which the five hindrances become ten?

sn46.52:9.2.verse: Sensual desire for what is internal is a hindrance; and sensual desire for what is external is also a hindrance.

sn46.52:9.3.verse: That’s how what is concisely referred to as ‘the hindrance of sensual desire’ becomes twofold.

sn46.52:9.4.verse: Ill will for what is internal is a hindrance; and ill will for what is external is also a hindrance.

sn46.52:9.5.verse: That’s how what is concisely referred to as ‘the hindrance of ill will’ becomes twofold.

sn46.52:9.6.verse: Dullness is a hindrance; and drowsiness is also a hindrance.

sn46.52:9.7.verse: That’s how what is concisely referred to as ‘the hindrance of dullness and drowsiness’ becomes twofold.

sn46.52:9.8.verse: Restlessness is a hindrance; and remorse is also a hindrance.

sn46.52:9.9.verse: That’s how what is concisely referred to as ‘the hindrance of restlessness and remorse’ becomes twofold.

sn46.52:9.10.verse: Doubt about internal things is a hindrance; and doubt about external things is also a hindrance.

sn46.52:9.11.verse: That’s how what is concisely referred to as ‘the hindrance of doubt’ becomes twofold.

sn46.52:9.12.verse: This is the way in which the five hindrances become ten.

sn46.52:10.1.verse: And what is the way in which the seven awakening factors become fourteen?

sn46.52:10.2.verse: Mindfulness of internal things is the awakening factor of mindfulness; and mindfulness of external things is also the awakening factor of mindfulness.

sn46.52:10.3.verse: That’s how what is concisely referred to as ‘the awakening factor of mindfulness’ becomes twofold.

sn46.52:11.1.verse: Investigating, exploring, and inquiring into internal things with wisdom is the awakening factor of investigation of principles; and investigating, exploring, and inquiring into external things with wisdom is also the awakening factor of investigation of principles.

sn46.52:11.2.verse: That’s how what is concisely referred to as ‘the awakening factor of investigation of principles’ becomes twofold.

sn46.52:12.1.verse: Physical energy is the awakening factor of energy; and mental energy is also the awakening factor of energy.

sn46.52:12.2.verse: That’s how what is concisely referred to as ‘the awakening factor of energy’ becomes twofold.

sn46.52:13.1.verse: Rapture while placing the mind and keeping it connected is the awakening factor of rapture; and rapture without placing the mind and keeping it connected is also the awakening factor of rapture.

sn46.52:13.2.verse: In this way what is concisely referred to as ‘the awakening factor of rapture’ becomes twofold.

sn46.52:14.1.verse: Physical tranquility is the awakening factor of tranquility; and mental tranquility is also the awakening factor of tranquility.

sn46.52:14.2.verse: In this way what is concisely referred to as ‘the awakening factor of tranquility’ becomes twofold.

sn46.52:15.1.verse: Immersion while placing the mind and keeping it connected is the awakening factor of immersion; and immersion without placing the mind and keeping it connected is also the awakening factor of immersion.

sn46.52:15.2.verse: In this way what is concisely referred to as ‘the awakening factor of immersion’ becomes twofold.

sn46.52:16.1.verse: Equanimity for internal things is the awakening factor of equanimity; and equanimity for external things is also the awakening factor of equanimity.

sn46.52:16.2.verse: In this way what is concisely referred to as ‘the awakening factor of equanimity’ becomes twofold.

sn46.52:16.3.verse: This is the way in which the seven awakening factors become fourteen.”

sn46.54:2.2.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side. The wanderers said to them:

sn46.54:3.2.verse: ‘Come, mendicants, give up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom, and meditate spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

sn46.54:3.3.verse: Meditate spreading a heart full of compassion to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. sn46.54:3.4.verse: Meditate spreading a heart full of rejoicing to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. sn46.54:3.5.verse: Meditate spreading a heart full of equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. sn46.54:5.2.verse: They rose from their seats, thinking:

sn46.54:5.3.verse: “We will learn the meaning of this statement from the Buddha himself.”

sn46.54:5.4.verse: Then, after the meal, when they returned from almsround, they went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

sn46.54:11.1.verse: “Mendicants, when wanderers of other religions say this, you should say to them:

sn46.54:11.2.verse: ‘But reverends, how is the heart’s release by love developed? What is its destination, apex, fruit, and culmination?

sn46.54:11.3.verse: How is the heart’s release by compassion developed? What is its destination, apex, fruit, and end?

sn46.54:11.4.verse: How is the heart’s release by rejoicing developed? What is its destination, apex, fruit, and end?

sn46.54:11.5.verse: How is the heart’s release by equanimity developed? What is its destination, apex, fruit, and end?’

sn46.54:11.6.verse: Questioned like this, the wanderers of other religions would be stumped, and, in addition, would get frustrated.

sn46.54:11.8.verse: Because they’re out of their element.

sn46.54:11.9.verse: I don’t see anyone in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—who could provide a satisfying answer to these questions except the Realized One or his disciple or someone who has heard it from them.

sn46.54:12.1.verse: And how is the heart’s release by love developed? What is its destination, apex, fruit, and end?

sn46.54:12.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the heart’s release by love together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

sn46.54:12.3.verse: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn46.54:12.4.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

sn46.54:12.5.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

sn46.54:12.6.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive and the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

sn46.54:12.7.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

sn46.54:12.8.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

sn46.54:12.9.verse: The apex of the heart’s release by love is the beautiful, I say, for a wise mendicant here who has not penetrated to a higher freedom.

sn46.54:13.1.verse: And how is the heart’s release by compassion developed? What is its destination, apex, fruit, and end?

sn46.54:13.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the heart’s release by compassion together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

sn46.54:13.3.verse: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn46.54:13.4.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do. …

sn46.54:13.5.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

sn46.54:13.6.verse: Or else, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite space.

sn46.54:13.7.verse: The apex of the heart’s release by compassion is the dimension of infinite space, I say, for a wise mendicant here who has not penetrated to a higher freedom.

sn46.54:14.1.verse: And how is the heart’s release by rejoicing developed? What is its destination, apex, fruit, and end?

sn46.54:14.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the heart’s release by rejoicing together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

sn46.54:14.3.verse: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn46.54:14.4.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do. …

sn46.54:14.5.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

sn46.54:14.6.verse: Or else, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

sn46.54:14.7.verse: The apex of the heart’s release by rejoicing is the dimension of infinite consciousness, I say, for a wise mendicant here who has not penetrated to a higher freedom.

sn46.54:15.1.verse: And how is the heart’s release by equanimity developed? What is its destination, apex, fruit, and end?

sn46.54:15.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the heart’s release by equanimity together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

sn46.54:15.3.verse: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn46.54:15.4.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

sn46.54:15.5.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

sn46.54:15.6.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive and the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

sn46.54:15.7.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

sn46.54:15.8.verse: If they wish: ‘May I meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

sn46.54:15.9.verse: Or else, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness.

sn46.54:15.10.verse: The apex of the heart’s release by equanimity is the dimension of nothingness, I say, for a wise mendicant here who has not penetrated to a higher freedom.”

sn46.55:1.2.verse: Then Saṅgārava the brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

sn46.55:1.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

sn46.55:2.1.verse: “What is the cause, Worthy Gotama, what is the reason why sometimes even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed?

sn46.55:2.2.verse: And why is it that sometimes even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed?”

sn46.55:3.1.verse: “Brahmin, there’s a time when your heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire and you don’t truly understand the escape from sensual desire that has arisen. At that time you don’t truly know or see what is good for yourself, good for another, or good for both. Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

sn46.55:4.1.verse: Suppose there was a bowl of water that was mixed with dye such as red lac, turmeric, indigo, or rose madder.

sn46.55:4.2.verse: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.

sn46.55:4.3.verse: In the same way, when your heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

sn46.55:5.1.verse: Furthermore, when your heart is overcome and mired in ill will … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

sn46.55:6.1.verse: Suppose there was a bowl of water that was heated by fire, boiling and bubbling.

sn46.55:6.2.verse: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.

sn46.55:6.3.verse: In the same way, when your heart is overcome and mired in ill will … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

sn46.55:7.1.verse: Furthermore, when your heart is overcome and mired in dullness and drowsiness … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

sn46.55:8.1.verse: Suppose there was a bowl of water enveloped with moss and aquatic plants.

sn46.55:8.2.verse: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.

sn46.55:8.3.verse: In the same way, when your heart is overcome and mired in dullness and drowsiness … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

sn46.55:9.1.verse: Furthermore, when your heart is overcome and mired in restlessness and remorse … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

sn46.55:10.1.verse: Suppose there was a bowl of water stirred by the wind, quivering, swirling, and rippling.

sn46.55:10.2.verse: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.

sn46.55:10.3.verse: In the same way, when your heart is overcome and mired in restlessness and remorse … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

sn46.55:11.1.verse: Furthermore, when your heart is overcome and mired in doubt … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

sn46.55:12.1.verse: Suppose there was a bowl of water that was cloudy, murky, and muddy, hidden in the darkness.

sn46.55:12.2.verse: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.

sn46.55:12.3.verse: In the same way, there’s a time when your heart is overcome and mired in doubt and you don’t truly understand the escape from doubt that has arisen. At that time you don’t truly know or see what is good for yourself, good for another, or good for both. Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

sn46.55:12.4.verse: This is the cause, brahmin, this is the reason why sometimes even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

sn46.55:13.1.verse: There’s a time when your heart is not overcome and mired in sensual desire and you truly understand the escape from sensual desire that has arisen. At that time you truly know and see what is good for yourself, good for another, and good for both. Even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.

sn46.55:14.1.verse: Suppose there was a bowl of water that was not mixed with dye such as red lac, turmeric, indigo, or rose madder.

sn46.55:14.2.verse: A person with clear eyes checking their own reflection would truly know it and see it.

sn46.55:14.3.verse: In the same way, when your heart is not overcome and mired in sensual desire … Even hymns that are long-unpracticed spring to mind, let alone those that are practiced.

sn46.55:15.1.verse: Furthermore, when your heart is not overcome and mired in ill will … Even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.

sn46.55:16.1.verse: Suppose there is a bowl of water that is not heated by a fire, boiling and bubbling.

sn46.55:16.2.verse: A person with clear eyes checking their own reflection would truly know it and see it.

sn46.55:16.3.verse: In the same way, when your heart is not overcome and mired in ill will … Even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.

sn46.55:17.1.verse: Furthermore, when your heart is not overcome and mired in dullness and drowsiness … Even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.

sn46.55:18.1.verse: Suppose there is a bowl of water that is not enveloped with moss and aquatic plants.

sn46.55:18.2.verse: A person with clear eyes checking their own reflection would truly know it and see it.

sn46.55:18.3.verse: In the same way, when your heart is not overcome and mired in dullness and drowsiness … Even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.

sn46.55:19.1.verse: Furthermore, when your heart is not overcome and mired in restlessness and remorse … Even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.

sn46.55:20.1.verse: Suppose there is a bowl of water that is not stirred by the wind, quivering, swirling, and rippling.

sn46.55:20.2.verse: A person with clear eyes checking their own reflection would truly know it and see it.

sn46.55:20.3.verse: In the same way, when your heart is not overcome and mired in restlessness and remorse … Even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.

sn46.55:21.1.verse: Furthermore, when your heart is not overcome and mired in doubt … Even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.

sn46.55:22.1.verse: Suppose there was a bowl of water that was transparent, clear, and unclouded, brought into the light.

sn46.55:22.2.verse: A person with clear eyes checking their own reflection would truly know it and see it.

sn46.55:22.3.verse: In the same way, there’s a time when your heart is not overcome and mired in doubt and you truly understand the escape from doubt that has arisen. At that time you truly know and see what is good for yourself, good for another, and good for both. Even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.

sn46.55:22.4.verse: This is the cause, brahmin, this is the reason why sometimes even hymns that are long-unrehearsed do spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.

sn46.55:23.1.verse: These seven awakening factors are not obstacles, hindrances, or corruptions of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.

sn46.55:23.3.verse: The awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

sn46.55:23.4.verse: These seven awakening factors are not obstacles, hindrances, or corruptions of the mind. When developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.”

sn46.55:24.1.verse: When he said this, Saṅgārava said to the Buddha,

sn46.55:24.3.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

sn46.56:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

sn46.56:1.3.verse: Then Prince Abhaya went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn46.56:1.5.verse: ‘There is no cause or reason for not knowing and not seeing.

sn46.56:1.6.verse: Not knowing and not seeing have no cause or reason.

sn46.56:1.7.verse: There is no cause or reason for knowing and seeing.

sn46.56:1.8.verse: Knowing and seeing have no cause or reason.’

sn46.56:1.9.verse: What does the Buddha say about this?”

sn46.56:1.10.verse: “Prince, there are causes and reasons for not knowing and not seeing.

sn46.56:1.11.verse: Not knowing and not seeing have causes and reasons.

sn46.56:1.12.verse: There are causes and reasons for knowing and seeing.

sn46.56:1.13.verse: Knowing and seeing have causes and reasons.”

sn46.56:2.1.verse: “But sir, what is the cause and reason for not knowing and not seeing?

sn46.56:2.2.verse: How do not knowing and not seeing have causes and reasons?”

sn46.56:2.3.verse: “There’s a time when the heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire, without truly knowing and seeing the escape from sensual desire that has arisen.

sn46.56:2.4.verse: This is a cause and reason for not knowing and not seeing.

sn46.56:2.5.verse: And this is how not knowing and not seeing have causes and reasons.

sn46.56:3.1.verse: Furthermore, there’s a time when the heart is overcome and mired in ill will …

sn46.56:3.4.verse: doubt, without truly knowing and seeing the escape from doubt that has arisen.

sn46.56:3.5.verse: This is a cause and reason for not knowing and not seeing.

sn46.56:3.6.verse: And this is how not knowing and not seeing have causes and reasons.”

sn46.56:4.1.verse: “Sir, what is the name of this exposition of the teaching?”

sn46.56:4.4.verse: Indeed, Holy One, these are hindrances!

sn46.56:4.5.verse: Overcome by even a single hindrance you wouldn’t truly know or see, let alone all five hindrances.

sn46.56:5.1.verse: But sir, what is the cause and reason for knowing and seeing?

sn46.56:5.2.verse: How do knowing and seeing have causes and reasons?”

sn46.56:5.3.verse: “It’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factor of mindfulness, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go.

sn46.56:5.4.verse: They truly know and see with a mind that has developed the awakening factor of mindfulness.

sn46.56:5.5.verse: This is a cause and reason for knowing and seeing.

sn46.56:5.6.verse: And this is how knowing and seeing have causes and reasons.

sn46.56:6.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant develops the awakening factor of investigation of principles … energy … rapture … tranquility … immersion …

sn46.56:6.2.verse: equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn46.56:6.3.verse: They truly know and see with a mind that has developed the awakening factor of equanimity.

sn46.56:6.4.verse: This is a cause and reason for knowing and seeing.

sn46.56:6.5.verse: And this is how knowing and seeing have causes and reasons.”

sn46.56:7.1.verse: “Sir, what is the name of this exposition of the teaching?”

sn46.56:7.3.verse: “Indeed, Blessed One, these are awakening factors!

sn46.56:7.4.verse: Indeed, Holy One, these are awakening factors!

sn46.56:7.5.verse: Endowed with even a single awakening factor you would truly know and see, let alone all seven awakening factors.

sn46.56:7.6.verse: When climbing Mount Vulture’s Peak I became fatigued in body and mind. But this has now faded away. And I’ve comprehended the teaching.”

sn46.57:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial.

sn46.57:1.4.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the perception of a skeleton together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

sn46.57:1.5.verse: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn46.57:1.6.verse: That’s how the perception of a skeleton, when developed and cultivated, is very fruitful and beneficial.”

sn46.57:2.1.verse: “When the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated you can expect one of two results: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.

sn46.57:3.1.verse: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it leads to great benefit.

sn46.57:4.1.verse: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it leads to great sanctuary from the yoke.

sn46.57:5.1.verse: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it leads to great inspiration.

sn46.57:6.1.verse: “Mendicants, when the perception of a skeleton is developed and cultivated it leads to dwelling in great ease.

sn46.60:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when the perception of a split open corpse is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

sn46.61:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when the perception of a bloated corpse is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

sn46.63:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when compassion is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

sn46.64:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when rejoicing is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

sn46.65:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when equanimity is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

sn46.69:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when the perception of repulsiveness of food is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

sn46.75:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when the perception of dispassion is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial. …”

sn46.76:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when the perception of cessation is developed and cultivated it’s very fruitful and beneficial.

sn46.76:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the perception of cessation together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

sn46.76:1.4.verse: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn46.76:1.5.verse: That’s how, when the perception of cessation is developed and cultivated, it’s very fruitful and beneficial.

sn46.76:2.1.verse: When the perception of cessation is developed and cultivated you can expect one of two results:

sn46.76:2.2.verse: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.

sn46.76:2.5.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the perception of cessation together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

sn46.76:2.6.verse: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn46.76:2.7.verse: When the perception of cessation is developed and cultivated in this way you can expect one of two results:

sn46.76:2.8.verse: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”

sn46.76:3.1.verse: “The perception of cessation, when developed and cultivated, leads to great benefit … great sanctuary from the yoke … great inspiration … great ease.

sn46.76:3.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the perception of cessation together with the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

sn46.76:3.4.verse: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn46.76:3.5.verse: That’s how the perception of cessation, when developed and cultivated, leads to great benefit … great sanctuary from the yoke … great inspiration … great ease.”

sn46.77-88:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, the Ganges River slants, slopes, and inclines to the east.

sn46.77-88:1.2.verse: In the same way, a mendicant who develops and cultivates the seven awakening factors slants, slopes, and inclines to extinguishment.

sn46.77-88:1.3.verse: And how does a mendicant who develops the seven awakening factors slant, slope, and incline to extinguishment?

sn46.77-88:1.4.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

sn46.77-88:1.5.verse: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn46.77-88:1.6.verse: That’s how a mendicant who develops and cultivates the seven awakening factors slants, slopes, and inclines to extinguishment.”

sn46.89-98:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, is said to be the best of all sentient beings—be they footless, with two feet, four feet, or many feet …”

sn46.99-110:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, all the hard work that gets done depends on the earth and is grounded on the earth. …”

sn46.111-120:1.3.verse: The search for sensual pleasures, the search for continued existence, and the search for a spiritual path. …”

sn46.121-129:1.3.verse: The floods of sensuality, desire to be reborn, views, and ignorance.”

sn46.130:1.4.verse: Desire for rebirth in the realm of luminous form, desire for rebirth in the formless realm, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance.

sn46.130:1.5.verse: These are the five higher fetters.

sn46.130:1.6.verse: The seven awakening factors should be developed for the direct knowledge, complete understanding, finishing, and giving up of these five higher fetters.

sn46.130:1.8.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

sn46.130:1.9.verse: and equanimity, which culminate in the removal of greed, hate, and delusion. …”

sn46.130:1.10.verse: “… which have freedom from death as their objective, destination, and culmination …”

sn46.130:1.11.verse: “… which slant, slope, and incline to extinguishment …

sn46.130:1.12.verse: The seven awakening factors should be developed for the direct knowledge, complete understanding, finishing, and giving up of these five higher fetters.”
