sn48.1:1.5.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.2:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.2:1.4.verse: A noble disciple comes to truly understand these five faculties’ gratification, drawback, and escape.

sn48.2:1.5.verse: Such a noble disciple is called a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

sn48.3:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.3:1.4.verse: A noble disciple comes to truly understand these five faculties’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape.

sn48.3:1.5.verse: Such a noble disciple is called a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

sn48.4:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.4:1.4.verse: A noble disciple comes to be freed by not grasping after truly understanding these five faculties’ gratification, drawback, and escape.

sn48.4:1.5.verse: Such a mendicant is called a perfected one, with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment.”

sn48.5:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.5:1.4.verse: A mendicant comes to be freed by not grasping after truly understanding these five faculties’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape.

sn48.5:1.5.verse: Such a mendicant is called a perfected one, with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment.”

sn48.6:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.6:1.4.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand the gratification, drawback, and escape when it comes to these five faculties.

sn48.6:1.5.verse: I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

sn48.6:2.1.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who do truly understand the origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape when it comes to these five faculties.

sn48.6:2.2.verse: I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

sn48.7:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are ascetics and brahmins who don’t understand the faculty of faith, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

sn48.7:1.2.verse: They don’t understand the faculty of energy …

sn48.7:1.5.verse: wisdom, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

sn48.7:1.6.verse: I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

sn48.7:2.1.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who do understand the faculty of faith, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

sn48.7:2.2.verse: They do understand the faculty of energy …

sn48.7:2.5.verse: wisdom, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

sn48.7:2.6.verse: I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

sn48.8:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.8:1.4.verse: And where should the faculty of faith be seen?

sn48.8:1.5.verse: In the four factors of stream-entry.

sn48.8:1.7.verse: And where should the faculty of energy be seen?

sn48.8:1.10.verse: And where should the faculty of mindfulness be seen?

sn48.8:1.11.verse: In the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

sn48.8:1.13.verse: And where should the faculty of immersion be seen?

sn48.8:1.16.verse: And where should the faculty of wisdom be seen?

sn48.9:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.9:1.4.verse: And what is the faculty of faith?

sn48.9:1.5.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

sn48.9:1.6.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

sn48.9:1.7.verse: This is called the faculty of faith.

sn48.9:2.1.verse: And what is the faculty of energy?

sn48.9:2.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

sn48.9:2.3.verse: This is called the faculty of energy.

sn48.9:3.1.verse: And what is the faculty of mindfulness?

sn48.9:3.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple is mindful. They have utmost mindfulness and alertness, and can remember and recall what was said and done long ago.

sn48.9:3.3.verse: This is called the faculty of mindfulness.

sn48.9:4.1.verse: And what is the faculty of immersion?

sn48.9:4.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple, relying on letting go, gains immersion, gains unification of mind.

sn48.9:4.3.verse: This is called the faculty of immersion.

sn48.9:5.1.verse: And what is the faculty of wisdom?

sn48.9:5.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

sn48.9:5.3.verse: This is called the faculty of wisdom.

sn48.10:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.10:1.4.verse: And what is the faculty of faith?

sn48.10:1.5.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

sn48.10:1.6.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

sn48.10:1.7.verse: This is called the faculty of faith.

sn48.10:2.1.verse: And what is the faculty of energy?

sn48.10:2.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

sn48.10:2.3.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise.

sn48.10:2.4.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen are given up.

sn48.10:2.5.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities arise.

sn48.10:2.6.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.

sn48.10:2.7.verse: This is called the faculty of energy.

sn48.10:3.1.verse: And what is the faculty of mindfulness?

sn48.10:3.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple is mindful. They have utmost mindfulness and alertness, and can remember and recall what was said and done long ago.

sn48.10:3.3.verse: They meditate observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

sn48.10:3.4.verse: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

sn48.10:3.6.verse: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

sn48.10:3.7.verse: This is called the faculty of mindfulness.

sn48.10:4.1.verse: And what is the faculty of immersion?

sn48.10:4.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple, relying on letting go, gains immersion, gains unification of mind.

sn48.10:4.3.verse: Quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, they enter and remain in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn48.10:4.4.verse: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn48.10:4.5.verse: And with the fading away of rapture, they enter and remain in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

sn48.10:4.6.verse: With the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

sn48.10:4.7.verse: This is called the faculty of immersion.

sn48.10:5.1.verse: And what is the faculty of wisdom?

sn48.10:5.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

sn48.10:5.3.verse: They truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

sn48.10:5.4.verse: This is called the faculty of wisdom.

sn48.11:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.11:1.4.verse: And what is the faculty of faith?

sn48.11:1.5.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

sn48.11:1.6.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

sn48.11:1.7.verse: This is called the faculty of faith.

sn48.11:2.1.verse: And what is the faculty of energy?

sn48.11:2.2.verse: The energy that’s gained owing to the four right efforts.

sn48.11:2.3.verse: This is called the faculty of energy.

sn48.11:3.1.verse: And what is the faculty of mindfulness?

sn48.11:3.2.verse: The mindfulness that’s gained owing to the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

sn48.11:3.3.verse: This is called the faculty of mindfulness.

sn48.11:4.1.verse: And what is the faculty of immersion?

sn48.11:4.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple, relying on letting go, gains immersion, gains unification of mind.

sn48.11:4.3.verse: This is called the faculty of immersion.

sn48.11:5.1.verse: And what is the faculty of wisdom?

sn48.11:5.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

sn48.11:5.3.verse: This is called the faculty of wisdom.

sn48.12:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.12:1.5.verse: Someone who has completed and fulfilled these five faculties is a perfected one. If they are weaker than that, they’re a non-returner. If they are weaker still, they’re a once-returner. If they are weaker still, they’re a stream-enterer. If they’re weaker still, they’re a follower of teachings. If they’re weaker still, they’re a follower by faith.”

sn48.13:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.13:1.5.verse: Someone who has completed and fulfilled these five faculties is a perfected one. If they are weaker than that, they’re a non-returner … a once-returner … a stream-enterer … a follower of teachings … a follower by faith.

sn48.13:1.6.verse: So from a disparity of faculties there’s a disparity of fruits. And from a disparity of fruits there’s a disparity of individuals.”

sn48.14:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.14:1.5.verse: Someone who has completed and fulfilled these five faculties is a perfected one. If they are weaker than that, they’re a non-returner … a once-returner … a stream-enterer … a follower of teachings … a follower by faith.

sn48.14:1.6.verse: So, mendicants, if you practice partially you succeed partially. If you practice fully you succeed fully.

sn48.14:1.7.verse: But in any case, these five faculties are not barren, I say.”

sn48.15:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.15:1.5.verse: Someone who has completed and fulfilled these five faculties is a perfected one. If they are weaker than that, they’re one who is extinguished between one life and the next … one who is extinguished upon landing … one who is extinguished without extra effort … one who is extinguished with extra effort … one who heads upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm … a once-returner … a stream-enterer … a follower of teachings … a follower by faith.”

sn48.16:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.16:1.5.verse: Someone who has completed and fulfilled these five faculties is a perfected one. If they are weaker than that, they’re one who is extinguished between one life and the next … one who is extinguished upon landing … one who is extinguished without extra effort … one who is extinguished with extra effort … one who heads upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm … a once-returner … a stream-enterer … a follower of teachings … a follower by faith.

sn48.16:1.6.verse: So from a disparity of faculties there’s a disparity of fruits. And from a disparity of fruits there’s a disparity of individuals.”

sn48.17:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.17:1.5.verse: Someone who has completed and fulfilled these five faculties is a perfected one. If they are weaker than that, they’re one who is extinguished between one life and the next … one who is extinguished upon landing … one who is extinguished without extra effort … one who is extinguished with extra effort … one who heads upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm … a once-returner … a stream-enterer … a follower of teachings … a follower by faith.

sn48.17:1.6.verse: So, mendicants, if you practice fully you succeed fully. If you practice partially you succeed partially.

sn48.17:1.7.verse: But in any case, these five faculties are not barren, I say.”

sn48.18:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.18:1.5.verse: Someone who has completed and fulfilled these five faculties is a perfected one. If they are weaker than that, they’re practicing to realize the fruit of perfection … a non-returner … practicing to realize the fruit of non-return … a once-returner … practicing to realize the fruit of once-return … a stream-enterer … practicing to realize the fruit of stream-entry.

sn48.18:1.6.verse: Someone who totally and utterly lacks these five faculties stands outside in the faction of ordinary persons, I say.”

sn48.19:1.1.verse: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn48.19:2.1.verse: “Sir, they speak of someone who is ‘accomplished in the faculties’.

sn48.19:2.2.verse: How is someone accomplished in the faculties defined?”

sn48.19:2.3.verse: “Mendicant, it’s when a mendicant develops the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom that lead to peace and awakening.

sn48.19:2.4.verse: This is how someone who is accomplished in the faculties is defined.”

sn48.20:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.20:1.5.verse: It’s because of developing and cultivating these five faculties that a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”

sn48.21:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.21:1.4.verse: As long as I didn’t truly understand these five faculties’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape, I didn’t announce my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

sn48.21:1.5.verse: But when I did truly understand these five faculties’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape, I announced my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

sn48.21:1.6.verse: Knowledge and vision arose in me:

sn48.21:1.7.verse: ‘My freedom is unshakable; this is my last rebirth; now there’ll be no more future lives.’”

sn48.22:1.3.verse: The faculties of femininity, masculinity, and life.

sn48.23:1.3.verse: The faculty of understanding that enlightenment is imminent. The faculty of enlightenment. The faculty of one who is enlightened.

sn48.24:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.24:1.5.verse: Someone who has completed and fulfilled these five faculties is a perfected one. If they are weaker than that, they’re one who is extinguished between one life and the next … one who is extinguished upon landing … one who is extinguished without extra effort … one who is extinguished with extra effort … one who heads upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm … a once-returner … a one-seeder … one who goes from family to family … one who has seven rebirths at most … a follower of teachings … a follower by faith.”

sn48.26:1.3.verse: The faculties of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

sn48.26:1.4.verse: A noble disciple comes to truly understand these six faculties’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape.

sn48.26:1.5.verse: Such a noble disciple is called a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

sn48.27:1.3.verse: The faculties of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

sn48.27:1.4.verse: A mendicant comes to be freed by not grasping after truly understanding these six faculties’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape.

sn48.27:1.5.verse: Such a mendicant is called a perfected one, with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment.”

sn48.28:1.3.verse: The faculties of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

sn48.28:1.4.verse: As long as I didn’t truly understand these six faculties’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape, I didn’t announce my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

sn48.28:1.5.verse: But when I did truly understand these six faculties’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape, I announced my supreme perfect awakening in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans.

sn48.28:1.6.verse: Knowledge and vision arose in me:

sn48.28:1.7.verse: ‘My freedom is unshakable; this is my last rebirth; now there’ll be no more future lives.’”

sn48.29:1.3.verse: The faculties of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

sn48.29:1.4.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand the origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape when it comes to these six faculties.

sn48.29:1.5.verse: I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

sn48.29:1.6.verse: There are ascetics and brahmins who do truly understand the origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape when it comes to these six faculties.

sn48.29:1.7.verse: I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

sn48.36:1.3.verse: The faculties of pleasure, pain, happiness, sadness, and equanimity.

sn48.36:2.1.verse: And what is the faculty of pleasure?

sn48.36:2.2.verse: Physical enjoyment, physical pleasure, the enjoyable, pleasant feeling that’s born from physical contact.

sn48.36:2.3.verse: This is called the faculty of pleasure.

sn48.36:3.1.verse: And what is the faculty of pain?

sn48.36:3.2.verse: Physical pain, physical unpleasantness, the painful, unpleasant feeling that’s born from physical contact.

sn48.36:3.3.verse: This is called the faculty of pain.

sn48.36:4.1.verse: And what is the faculty of happiness?

sn48.36:4.2.verse: Mental enjoyment, mental pleasure, the enjoyable, pleasant feeling that’s born from mind contact.

sn48.36:4.3.verse: This is called the faculty of happiness.

sn48.36:5.1.verse: And what is the faculty of sadness?

sn48.36:5.2.verse: Mental pain, mental displeasure, the painful, unpleasant feeling that’s born from mind contact.

sn48.36:5.3.verse: This is called the faculty of sadness.

sn48.36:6.1.verse: And what is the faculty of equanimity?

sn48.36:6.2.verse: Neither pleasant nor unpleasant feeling, whether physical or mental.

sn48.36:6.3.verse: This is the faculty of equanimity.

sn48.39:0.3.verse: The Simile of the Fire Sticks

sn48.39:1.3.verse: The faculties of pleasure, pain, happiness, sadness, and equanimity.

sn48.39:1.4.verse: The faculty of pleasure arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as pleasant.

sn48.39:1.5.verse: When in a state of pleasure, you understand: ‘I’m in a state of pleasure.’

sn48.39:1.6.verse: With the cessation of that contact to be experienced as pleasant, you understand that the corresponding faculty of pleasure that had arisen ceases and stops.

sn48.39:2.1.verse: The faculty of pain arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as painful.

sn48.39:2.2.verse: When in a state of pain, you understand: ‘I’m in a state of pain.’

sn48.39:2.3.verse: With the cessation of that contact to be experienced as painful, you understand that the corresponding faculty of pain that had arisen ceases and stops.

sn48.39:3.1.verse: The faculty of happiness arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as happiness.

sn48.39:3.2.verse: When in a state of happiness, you understand: ‘I’m in a state of happiness.’

sn48.39:3.3.verse: With the cessation of that contact to be experienced as happiness, you understand that the corresponding faculty of happiness that had arisen ceases and stops.

sn48.39:4.1.verse: The faculty of sadness arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as sadness.

sn48.39:4.2.verse: When in a state of sadness, you understand: ‘I’m in a state of sadness.’

sn48.39:4.3.verse: With the cessation of that contact to be experienced as sadness, you understand that the corresponding faculty of sadness that had arisen ceases and stops.

sn48.39:5.1.verse: The faculty of equanimity arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as equanimous.

sn48.39:5.2.verse: When in a state of equanimity, you understand: ‘I’m in a state of equanimity.’

sn48.39:5.3.verse: With the cessation of that contact to be experienced as equanimous, you understand that the corresponding faculty of equanimity that had arisen ceases and stops.

sn48.39:6.1.verse: When you rub two sticks together, heat is generated and fire is produced. But when you part the sticks and lay them aside, any corresponding heat ceases and stops.

sn48.39:6.2.verse: In the same way, the faculty of pleasure arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as pleasant.

sn48.39:6.3.verse: When in a state of pleasure, you understand: ‘I’m in a state of pleasure.’

sn48.39:6.4.verse: With the cessation of that contact to be experienced as pleasant, you understand that the corresponding faculty of pleasure that arises ceases and stops.

sn48.39:7.4.verse: equanimity arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as equanimous.

sn48.39:7.5.verse: When in a state of equanimity, you understand: ‘I’m in a state of equanimity.’

sn48.39:7.6.verse: With the cessation of that contact to be experienced as equanimous, you understand that the corresponding faculty of equanimity that arises ceases and stops.”

sn48.40:1.3.verse: The faculties of pain, sadness, pleasure, happiness, and equanimity.

sn48.40:1.4.verse: While a mendicant is meditating—diligent, keen, and resolute—the faculty of pain arises.

sn48.40:1.6.verse: ‘The faculty of pain has arisen in me. And that has a basis, a source, a condition, and a reason.

sn48.40:1.7.verse: It’s not possible that the faculty of pain will arise without a basis, a source, a condition, or a reason.’

sn48.40:1.8.verse: They understand the faculty of pain, its origin, its cessation, and where that faculty of pain that’s arisen ceases without remainder.

sn48.40:1.9.verse: And where does that faculty of pain that’s arisen cease without remainder?

sn48.40:1.10.verse: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn48.40:1.11.verse: That’s where the faculty of pain that’s arisen ceases without remainder.

sn48.40:1.12.verse: They’re called a mendicant who understands the cessation of the faculty of pain, and who applies their mind to that end.

sn48.40:2.1.verse: While a mendicant is meditating—diligent, keen, and resolute—the faculty of sadness arises.

sn48.40:2.3.verse: ‘The faculty of sadness has arisen in me. And that has a basis, a source, a condition, and a reason.

sn48.40:2.4.verse: It’s not possible that the faculty of sadness will arise without a basis, a source, a condition, or a reason.’

sn48.40:2.5.verse: They understand the faculty of sadness, its origin, its cessation, and where that faculty of sadness that’s arisen ceases without remainder.

sn48.40:2.6.verse: And where does that faculty of sadness that’s arisen cease without remainder?

sn48.40:2.7.verse: It’s when, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, a mendicant enters and remains in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn48.40:2.8.verse: That’s where the faculty of sadness that’s arisen ceases without remainder.

sn48.40:2.9.verse: They’re called a mendicant who understands the cessation of the faculty of sadness, and who applies their mind to that end.

sn48.40:3.1.verse: While a mendicant is meditating—diligent, keen, and resolute—the faculty of pleasure arises.

sn48.40:3.3.verse: ‘The faculty of pleasure has arisen in me. And that has a basis, a source, a condition, and a reason.

sn48.40:3.4.verse: It’s not possible that the faculty of pleasure will arise without a basis, a source, a condition, or a reason.’

sn48.40:3.5.verse: They understand the faculty of pleasure, its origin, its cessation, and where that faculty of pleasure that’s arisen ceases without remainder.

sn48.40:3.6.verse: And where does that faculty of pleasure that’s arisen cease without remainder?

sn48.40:3.7.verse: It’s when, with the fading away of rapture, a mendicant enters and remains in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

sn48.40:3.8.verse: That’s where the faculty of pleasure that’s arisen ceases without remainder.

sn48.40:3.9.verse: They’re called a mendicant who understands the cessation of the faculty of pleasure, and who applies their mind to that end.

sn48.40:4.1.verse: While a mendicant is meditating—diligent, keen, and resolute—the faculty of happiness arises.

sn48.40:4.3.verse: ‘The faculty of happiness has arisen in me. And that has a basis, a source, a condition, and a reason.

sn48.40:4.4.verse: It’s not possible that the faculty of happiness will arise without a basis, a source, a condition, or a reason.’

sn48.40:4.5.verse: They understand the faculty of happiness, its origin, its cessation, and where that faculty of happiness that’s arisen ceases without remainder.

sn48.40:4.6.verse: And where does that faculty of happiness that’s arisen cease without remainder?

sn48.40:4.7.verse: It’s when, giving up pleasure and pain, and disappearance former happiness and sadness, a mendicant enters and remains in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

sn48.40:4.8.verse: That’s where the faculty of happiness that’s arisen ceases without remainder.

sn48.40:4.9.verse: They’re called a mendicant who understands the cessation of the faculty of happiness, and who applies their mind to that end.

sn48.40:5.1.verse: While a mendicant is meditating—diligent, keen, and resolute—the faculty of equanimity arises.

sn48.40:5.3.verse: ‘The faculty of equanimity has arisen in me. And that has a basis, a source, a condition, and a reason.

sn48.40:5.4.verse: It’s not possible that the faculty of equanimity will arise without a basis, a source, a condition, or a reason.’

sn48.40:5.5.verse: They understand the faculty of equanimity, its origin, its cessation, and where that faculty of equanimity that’s arisen ceases without remainder.

sn48.40:5.6.verse: And where does that faculty of equanimity that’s arisen cease without remainder?

sn48.40:5.7.verse: It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, enters and remains in the cessation of perception and feeling.

sn48.40:5.8.verse: That’s where the faculty of equanimity that’s arisen ceases without remainder.

sn48.40:5.9.verse: They’re called a mendicant who understands the cessation of the faculty of equanimity, and who applies their mind to that end.”

sn48.41:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

sn48.41:1.3.verse: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and sat warming his back in the last rays of the sun.

sn48.41:2.1.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and while massaging the Buddha’s limbs he said:

sn48.41:2.3.verse: how the complexion of your skin is no longer pure and bright. Your limbs are flaccid and wrinkled, and your body is stooped. And it’s apparent that there has been a deterioration in your faculties

sn48.41:2.4.verse: of eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body.”

sn48.41:3.2.verse: When young you’re liable to grow old; when healthy you’re liable to get sick; and when alive you’re liable to die.

sn48.41:3.3.verse: The complexion of the skin is no longer pure and bright. The limbs are flaccid and wrinkled, and the body is stooped. And it’s apparent that there has been a deterioration in the faculties

sn48.41:3.4.verse: of eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body.”

sn48.41:4.1.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn48.41:4.2.verse: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

sn48.41:5.3.verse: That’s how much this delightful puppet

sn48.41:5.4.verse: is ground down by old age.

sn48.41:6.1.verse: Even if you live for a hundred years,

sn48.42:1.2.verse: Then Uṇṇābha the brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

sn48.42:1.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

sn48.42:2.1.verse: “Worthy Gotama, these five faculties have different domains and different ranges, and don’t experience each other’s domain and range.

sn48.42:2.3.verse: The faculties of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body.

sn48.42:2.4.verse: What do these five faculties, with their different domains and ranges, have recourse to? What experiences their domains and ranges?”

sn48.42:3.1.verse: “Brahmin, these five faculties have different domains and different ranges, and don’t experience each other’s domain and range.

sn48.42:3.3.verse: The faculties of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body.

sn48.42:3.4.verse: These five faculties, with their different domains and ranges, have recourse to the mind. And the mind experiences their domains and ranges.”

sn48.42:4.1.verse: “But worthy Gotama, what does the mind have recourse to?”

sn48.42:4.3.verse: “But what does mindfulness have recourse to?”

sn48.42:4.5.verse: “But what does freedom have recourse to?”

sn48.42:4.7.verse: “But what does extinguishment have recourse to?”

sn48.42:4.8.verse: “This question goes too far, brahmin! You weren’t able to grasp the limit of questioning.

sn48.42:4.9.verse: For extinguishment is the objective, destination, and culmination of the spiritual life.”

sn48.42:5.1.verse: And then the brahmin Uṇṇābha approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. He got up from his seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

sn48.42:6.1.verse: Then, not long after he had left, the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

sn48.42:6.2.verse: “Suppose there was a bungalow or a hall with a peaked roof, with windows on the eastern side. When the sun rises and a ray of light enters through a window, where would it land?”

sn48.42:6.4.verse: “In the same way, the brahmin Uṇṇābha’s faith in the Realized One is settled, rooted, and planted deep. It’s strong and can’t be shifted by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.

sn48.42:6.5.verse: If he were to pass away at this time, he would be bound by no fetter that might return him to this world.”

sn48.43:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāketa in the deer park at the Añjana Wood.

sn48.43:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

sn48.43:1.4.verse: “Mendicants, is there a method in which the five faculties become the five powers, and the five powers become the five faculties?”

sn48.43:2.1.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. He is our guide and our refuge. Sir, may the Buddha himself please clarify the meaning of this. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

sn48.43:3.1.verse: “Mendicants, there is a method in which the five faculties become the five powers, and the five powers become the five faculties.

sn48.43:4.2.verse: The faculty of faith is the power of faith, and the power of faith is the faculty of faith.

sn48.43:4.3.verse: The faculty of energy is the power of energy, and the power of energy is the faculty of energy.

sn48.43:4.4.verse: The faculty of mindfulness is the power of mindfulness, and the power of mindfulness is the faculty of mindfulness.

sn48.43:4.5.verse: The faculty of immersion is the power of immersion, and the power of immersion is the faculty of immersion.

sn48.43:4.6.verse: The faculty of wisdom is the power of wisdom, and the power of wisdom is the faculty of wisdom.

sn48.43:4.7.verse: Suppose there was a river slanting, sloping, and inclining to the east, and in the middle was an island.

sn48.43:4.8.verse: There’s a method in which that river can be reckoned to have just one stream.

sn48.43:4.9.verse: But there’s also a method in which that river can be reckoned to have two streams.

sn48.43:5.1.verse: And what’s the method in which that river can be reckoned to have just one stream?

sn48.43:5.2.verse: By taking into account the water to the east and the west of the island,

sn48.43:5.3.verse: that river can be reckoned to have just one stream.

sn48.43:6.1.verse: And what’s the method in which that river can be reckoned to have two streams?

sn48.43:6.2.verse: By taking into account the water to the north and the south of the island,

sn48.43:6.3.verse: that river can be reckoned to have two streams.

sn48.43:6.4.verse: By the same method, the faculty of faith is the power of faith, and the power of faith is the faculty of faith.

sn48.43:6.5.verse: The faculty of energy is the power of energy, and the power of energy is the faculty of energy.

sn48.43:6.6.verse: The faculty of mindfulness is the power of mindfulness, and the power of mindfulness is the faculty of mindfulness.

sn48.43:6.7.verse: The faculty of immersion is the power of immersion, and the power of immersion is the faculty of immersion.

sn48.43:6.8.verse: The faculty of wisdom is the power of wisdom, and the power of wisdom is the faculty of wisdom.

sn48.43:6.9.verse: It’s because of developing and cultivating the five faculties that a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”

sn48.44:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in Sāvatthī at the eastern gate.

sn48.44:1.3.verse: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Sāriputta:

sn48.44:1.5.verse: the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom, when developed and cultivated, have freedom from death as their objective, destination, and culmination?”

sn48.44:2.1.verse: “Sir, in this case I don’t rely on faith in the Buddha’s claim that

sn48.44:2.2.verse: the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom, when developed and cultivated, have freedom from death as their objective, destination, and culmination.

sn48.44:2.3.verse: There are those who have not known or seen or understood or realized or experienced this with wisdom. They may rely on faith in this matter.

sn48.44:2.5.verse: But there are those who have known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom. They have no doubts or uncertainties in this matter.

sn48.44:2.7.verse: I have known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom.

sn48.44:2.8.verse: I have no doubts or uncertainties that the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom, when developed and cultivated, have freedom from death as their objective, destination, and culmination.”

sn48.44:3.2.verse: There are those who have not known or seen or understood or realized or experienced this with wisdom. They may rely on faith in this matter.

sn48.44:3.4.verse: But there are those who have known, seen, understood, realized, and experienced this with wisdom. They have no doubts or uncertainties that

sn48.44:3.5.verse: the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom, when developed and cultivated, have freedom from death as their objective, destination, and culmination.”

sn48.45:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

sn48.45:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

sn48.45:1.4.verse: “Mendicants, how many faculties must a mendicant develop and cultivate so that they can declare enlightenment:

sn48.45:1.5.verse: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place”’?”

sn48.45:2.1.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn48.45:2.2.verse: “A mendicant must develop and cultivate one faculty so that they can declare enlightenment.

sn48.45:2.4.verse: What one? The faculty of wisdom. When a noble disciple has wisdom, the faith, energy, mindfulness, and immersion that follow along with that become stabilized.

sn48.45:2.5.verse: This is the one faculty that a mendicant must develop and cultivate so that they can declare enlightenment:

sn48.45:2.6.verse: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’”

sn48.46:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, how many faculties must a mendicant develop and cultivate so that they can declare enlightenment:

sn48.46:1.3.verse: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place”’?”

sn48.46:2.1.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn48.46:2.2.verse: “A mendicant must develop and cultivate two faculties so that they can declare enlightenment.

sn48.46:2.6.verse: For their noble wisdom is the faculty of wisdom.

sn48.46:2.7.verse: And their noble freedom is the faculty of immersion.

sn48.46:2.8.verse: These are the two faculties that a mendicant must develop and cultivate so that they can declare enlightenment:

sn48.46:2.9.verse: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’”

sn48.47:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, how many faculties must a mendicant develop and cultivate so that they can declare enlightenment:

sn48.47:1.3.verse: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place”’?”

sn48.47:2.1.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn48.47:2.2.verse: “A mendicant must develop and cultivate four faculties so that they can declare enlightenment.

sn48.47:2.5.verse: The faculties of energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.47:2.6.verse: These are the four faculties that a mendicant must develop and cultivate so that they can declare enlightenment:

sn48.47:2.7.verse: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’”

sn48.48:1.3.verse: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place”’?”

sn48.48:2.1.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn48.48:2.2.verse: “A mendicant must develop and cultivate five faculties so that they can declare enlightenment.

sn48.48:2.5.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.48:2.6.verse: These are the five faculties that a mendicant must develop and cultivate so that they can declare enlightenment:

sn48.49:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

sn48.49:1.3.verse: Now at that time Venerable Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer had declared enlightenment:

sn48.49:1.4.verse: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

sn48.49:1.5.verse: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. Then they said,

sn48.49:2.3.verse: “What reason does Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer see for doing this?”

sn48.49:3.1.verse: “It’s because Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer has developed and cultivated three faculties that he declares enlightenment:

sn48.49:3.2.verse: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’

sn48.49:3.4.verse: The faculties of mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.49:3.5.verse: It’s because Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer has developed and cultivated these three faculties that he declares enlightenment.

sn48.49:3.7.verse: What’s the culmination of these three faculties?

sn48.49:3.10.verse: Of rebirth, old age, and death.

sn48.49:3.11.verse: It’s because he sees that they culminate in the ending of rebirth, old age, and death that Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer declares enlightenment:

sn48.49:3.12.verse: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’”

sn48.50:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Aṅgas, near the Aṅgan town named Āpaṇa.

sn48.50:1.3.verse: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Sāriputta:

sn48.50:1.4.verse: “Sāriputta, would a noble disciple who is sure and devoted to the Realized One have any doubt or uncertainty about the Realized One or his instructions?”

sn48.50:2.1.verse: “Sir, a noble disciple who is sure and devoted to the Realized One would have no doubt or uncertainty about the Realized One or his instructions.

sn48.50:2.2.verse: You can expect that a faithful noble disciple will live with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

sn48.50:2.3.verse: For their energy is the faculty of energy.

sn48.50:3.1.verse: You can expect that a faithful and energetic noble disciple will be mindful, with utmost mindfulness and alertness, able to remember and recall what was said and done long ago.

sn48.50:3.2.verse: For their mindfulness is the faculty of mindfulness.

sn48.50:4.1.verse: You can expect that a faithful, energetic, and mindful noble disciple will, relying on letting go, gain immersion, gain unification of mind.

sn48.50:4.2.verse: For their immersion is the faculty of immersion.

sn48.50:5.1.verse: You can expect that a faithful, energetic, mindful noble disciple with their mind immersed in samādhi will understand this:

sn48.50:5.3.verse: No first point is found of sentient beings roaming and transmigrating, shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving.

sn48.50:5.4.verse: But when that dark mass of ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, that state is peaceful and sublime.

sn48.50:5.5.verse: That is, the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.’

sn48.50:5.6.verse: For their noble wisdom is the faculty of wisdom.

sn48.50:6.1.verse: When a noble disciple has tried again and again, recollected again and again, entered immersion again and again, and understood with wisdom again and again, they will be confident of this:

sn48.50:6.2.verse: ‘I have previously heard of these things.

sn48.50:6.3.verse: But now I have direct meditative experience of them, and see them with penetrating wisdom.’

sn48.50:6.4.verse: For their faith is the faculty of faith.”

sn48.50:7.2.verse: Sāriputta, a noble disciple who is sure and devoted to the Realized One would have no doubt or uncertainty about the Realized One or his instructions. …”

sn48.50:7.3.verse: The Buddha then repeated Sāriputta’s answer word for word.

sn48.51:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kosalans near the brahmin village of Sālā.

sn48.51:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

sn48.51:1.4.verse: “Mendicants, the lion, king of beasts, is said to be the best of animals in terms of strength, speed, and courage.

sn48.51:1.5.verse: In the same way, the faculty of wisdom is said to be the best of the qualities on the side of awakening; that is, for becoming awakened.

sn48.51:2.1.verse: And what are the qualities on the side of awakening?

sn48.51:2.6.verse: and wisdom are qualities on the side of awakening, in that they lead to becoming awakened.

sn48.51:2.7.verse: The lion, king of beasts, is said to be the best of animals in terms of strength, speed, and courage.

sn48.51:2.8.verse: In the same way, the faculty of wisdom is said to be the best of the qualities on the side of awakening; that is, for becoming awakened.”

sn48.52:0.3.verse: In the Land of the Mallas

sn48.52:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Mallas, near the Mallian town named Uruvelakappa.

sn48.52:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

sn48.52:1.4.verse: “Mendicants, as long as noble knowledge hasn’t arisen for a noble disciple the four faculties are not stable and fixed.

sn48.52:1.5.verse: But when noble knowledge has arisen for a noble disciple the four faculties become stable and fixed.

sn48.52:2.1.verse: It’s just like in a bungalow. As long as the roof peak is not lifted into place, the rafters are not stable or fixed.

sn48.52:2.2.verse: But when the roof peak is lifted into place, the rafters become stable and fixed.

sn48.52:2.3.verse: In the same way, as long as noble knowledge hasn’t arisen for a noble disciple the four faculties are not stable and fixed.

sn48.52:2.4.verse: But when noble knowledge has arisen for a noble disciple the four faculties become stable and fixed.

sn48.52:3.2.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, and immersion.

sn48.52:3.3.verse: When a noble disciple has wisdom, the faith, energy, mindfulness, and immersion that follow along with that become stabilized.”

sn48.53:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

sn48.53:1.3.verse: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

sn48.53:1.4.verse: “Mendicants, is there a way that a mendicant who is a trainee, standing at the level of a trainee, can understand that they are a trainee? And that a mendicant who is an adept, standing at the level of an adept, can understand that they are an adept?”

sn48.53:2.1.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

sn48.53:2.2.verse: “There is a way that a mendicant who is a trainee, standing at the level of a trainee, can understand that they are a trainee, and that a mendicant who is an adept, standing at the level of an adept, can understand that they are an adept.

sn48.53:3.1.verse: And what is a way that a mendicant who is a trainee can understand that they are a trainee?

sn48.53:3.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant who is a trainee truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

sn48.53:3.3.verse: This is a way that a mendicant who is a trainee can understand that they are a trainee.

sn48.53:4.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant who is a trainee reflects:

sn48.53:4.2.verse: ‘Is there any other ascetic or brahmin elsewhere whose teaching is as true, as real, as accurate as that of the Buddha?’

sn48.53:4.4.verse: ‘There is no other ascetic or brahmin elsewhere whose teaching is as true, as real, as accurate as that of the Buddha.’

sn48.53:4.5.verse: This too is a way that a mendicant who is a trainee can understand that they are a trainee.

sn48.53:5.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant who is a trainee understands the five faculties:

sn48.53:5.2.verse: faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.53:5.3.verse: And although they don’t have direct meditative experience of their destination, apex, fruit, and culmination,

sn48.53:5.4.verse: they do see them with penetrating wisdom.

sn48.53:5.5.verse: This too is a way that a mendicant who is a trainee can understand that they are a trainee.

sn48.53:6.1.verse: And what is the way that a mendicant who is an adept can understand that they are an adept?

sn48.53:6.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant who is an adept understands the five faculties:

sn48.53:6.3.verse: faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.53:6.4.verse: They have direct meditative experience of their destination, apex, fruit, and culmination,

sn48.53:6.5.verse: and they see them with penetrating wisdom.

sn48.53:6.6.verse: This is a way that a mendicant who is an adept can understand that they are an adept.

sn48.53:7.1.verse: Furthermore, a mendicant who is an adept understands the six faculties:

sn48.53:7.2.verse: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

sn48.53:7.3.verse: They understand: ‘These six faculties will totally and utterly cease without remainder. And no other six faculties will arise anywhere anyhow.’

sn48.53:7.4.verse: This too is a way that a mendicant who is an adept can understand that they are an adept.”

sn48.54:1.1.verse: “The footprints of all creatures that walk can fit inside an elephant’s footprint, so an elephant’s footprint is said to be the biggest of them all.

sn48.54:1.2.verse: In the same way, the faculty of wisdom is said to be the best of the steps that lead to awakening; that is, for becoming awakened.

sn48.54:1.3.verse: And what are the steps that lead to awakening?

sn48.54:1.8.verse: and wisdom are steps that lead to awakening, in that they lead to becoming awakened.

sn48.54:1.9.verse: The footprints of all creatures that walk can fit inside an elephant’s footprint, so an elephant’s footprint is said to be the biggest of them all.

sn48.54:1.10.verse: In the same way, the faculty of wisdom is said to be the best of the steps that lead to awakening; that is, for becoming awakened. ”

sn48.55:1.2.verse: In the same way, the faculty of wisdom is said to be the best of the qualities on the side of awakening; that is, for becoming awakened.

sn48.55:1.3.verse: And what are the qualities on the side of awakening?

sn48.55:1.8.verse: and wisdom are qualities on the side of awakening, in that they lead to becoming awakened.

sn48.56:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when a mendicant is grounded in one thing the five faculties become developed, well developed.

sn48.56:1.5.verse: It’s when a mendicant looks after their mind when it comes to defilements and things accompanied by defilements.

sn48.56:1.6.verse: As they do so the faculties of faith,

sn48.56:1.11.verse: That’s how when a mendicant is grounded in one thing the five faculties become developed, well developed.”

sn48.57:1.1.verse: At one time, when he was first awakened, the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the goatherd’s banyan tree on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

sn48.57:1.2.verse: Then as he was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,

sn48.57:1.3.verse: “When these five faculties are developed and cultivated they have freedom from death as their objective, destination, and culmination.

sn48.57:1.10.verse: When these five faculties are developed and cultivated they have freedom from death as their objective, destination, and culmination.”

sn48.57:2.1.verse: Then the divinity Sahampati knew the Buddha’s train of thought. As easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from the realm of divinity and reappeared in front of the Buddha.

sn48.57:2.2.verse: He arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha, and said:

sn48.57:2.3.verse: “That’s so true, Blessed One! That’s so true, Holy One!

sn48.57:2.4.verse: When these five faculties are developed and cultivated they have freedom from death as their objective, destination, and culmination.

sn48.57:2.6.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.57:2.7.verse: When these five faculties are developed and cultivated they have freedom from death as their objective, destination, and culmination.

sn48.57:3.1.verse: Once upon a time, sir, I lived the spiritual life under the fully awakened Buddha Kassapa.

sn48.57:3.4.verse: Because of developing and cultivating these same five faculties I lost desire for sensual pleasures. When my body broke up, after death, I was reborn in a good place, in the realm of divinity.

sn48.57:3.7.verse: That’s so true, Blessed One! That’s so true, Holy One!

sn48.57:3.8.verse: I know and see how when these five faculties are developed and cultivated they have freedom from death as their objective, destination, and culmination.”

sn48.58:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain in the Boar’s Cave.

sn48.58:1.2.verse: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Sāriputta:

sn48.58:1.3.verse: “Sāriputta, considering what benefit does a mendicant with defilements ended, in rolling forth, roll forth with utmost deference for the Realized One or his instructions?”

sn48.58:1.4.verse: “Sir, it is considering the supreme sanctuary from the yoke that a mendicant with defilements ended, in rolling forth, rolls forth with utmost deference for the Realized One or his instructions.”

sn48.58:1.6.verse: For it is considering the supreme sanctuary from the yoke that a mendicant whose defilements are ended, in rolling forth, rolls forth with utmost deference for the Realized One or his instructions.

sn48.58:2.1.verse: And what is that supreme sanctuary from the yoke?”

sn48.58:2.2.verse: “It’s when a mendicant with defilements ended develops the faculties of faith,

sn48.58:2.6.verse: and wisdom, which lead to peace and awakening.

sn48.58:2.7.verse: It is considering this supreme sanctuary from the yoke that a mendicant with defilements ended, in rolling forth, rolls forth with utmost deference for the Realized One or his instructions.”

sn48.58:2.9.verse: For this is that supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

sn48.58:3.1.verse: And what is that utmost deference that a mendicant with defilements ended, in rolling forth, shows toward the Realized One or his instructions?”

sn48.58:3.2.verse: “It’s when a mendicant with defilements ended maintains respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the training, and immersion.

sn48.58:3.5.verse: For this is that utmost deference that a mendicant with defilements ended, in rolling forth, shows toward the Realized One or his instructions.”

sn48.59:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, these five faculties don’t arise to be developed and cultivated except when a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha has appeared.

sn48.59:1.4.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.59:1.5.verse: These five faculties don’t arise to be developed and cultivated except when a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha has appeared.”

sn48.60:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these five faculties don’t arise to be developed and cultivated apart from the Holy One’s training.

sn48.60:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.60:1.4.verse: These five faculties don’t arise to be developed and cultivated apart from the Holy One’s training.”

sn48.61:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when these five faculties are developed and cultivated they lead to giving up the fetters.

sn48.61:1.4.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.61:1.5.verse: When these five faculties are developed and cultivated they lead to giving up the fetters.”

sn48.63:1.4.verse: When these five faculties are developed and cultivated they lead to the complete understanding of the course of time.”

sn48.64:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when these five faculties are developed and cultivated they lead to the ending of defilements.

sn48.64:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.64:1.4.verse: When these five faculties are developed and cultivated they lead to the ending of defilements.”

sn48.64:2.1.verse: “Mendicants, when these five faculties are developed and cultivated they lead to giving up the fetters, uprooting the underlying tendencies, completely understanding the course of time, and ending the defilements.

sn48.64:2.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.64:2.4.verse: When these five faculties are developed and cultivated they lead to giving up the fetters, uprooting the underlying tendencies, completely understanding the course of time, and ending the defilements.”

sn48.65:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.65:1.5.verse: Because of developing and cultivating these five faculties, one of two results can be expected:

sn48.65:1.6.verse: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”

sn48.66:1.3.verse: The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn48.66:1.5.verse: Because of developing and cultivating these five faculties, seven fruits and benefits can be expected.

sn48.66:1.7.verse: They attain enlightenment early on in this very life.

sn48.66:1.8.verse: If not, they attain enlightenment at the time of death.

sn48.66:1.9.verse: If not, with the ending of the five lower fetters, they’re extinguished between one life and the next …

sn48.66:1.13.verse: they head upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm.

sn48.66:1.14.verse: Because of developing and cultivating these five faculties, these seven fruits and benefits can be expected.”

sn51.10:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

sn51.10:1.3.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Vesālī for alms.

sn51.10:1.4.verse: Then, after the meal, on his return from almsround, he addressed Venerable Ānanda:

sn51.10:1.6.verse: Let’s go to the Cāpāla Shrine for the day’s meditation.”

sn51.10:1.7.verse: “Yes, sir,” replied Ānanda. Taking his sitting cloth he followed behind the Buddha.

sn51.10:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha went up to the Cāpāla Shrine, and sat down on the seat spread out.

sn51.10:2.2.verse: Ānanda bowed to the Buddha and sat down to one side.

sn51.10:3.1.verse: “Ānanda, Vesālī is lovely. And the Udena, Gotamaka, Seven Maidens, Many Sons, Sārandada, and Cāpāla Shrines are all lovely.

sn51.10:3.2.verse: Whoever has developed and cultivated the four bases of psychic power—made them a vehicle and a basis, kept them up, consolidated them, and properly implemented them—may, if they wish, live for the proper lifespan or what’s left of it.

sn51.10:3.3.verse: The Realized One has developed and cultivated the four bases of psychic power, made them a vehicle and a basis, kept them up, consolidated them, and properly implemented them. If he wished, the Realized One could live for the proper lifespan or what’s left of it.”

sn51.10:4.1.verse: But Ānanda didn’t get it, even though the Buddha dropped such an obvious hint, such a clear sign.

sn51.10:4.3.verse: “Sir, may the Blessed One please remain for the proper lifespan! May the Holy One please remain for the proper lifespan! That would be for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.” For his mind was as if possessed by Māra.

sn51.10:5.2.verse: For a third time, the Buddha said to Ānanda:

sn51.10:5.3.verse: “Ānanda, Vesālī is lovely. And the Udena, Gotamaka, Seven Maidens, Many Sons, Sārandada, and Cāpāla Shrines are all lovely.

sn51.10:5.4.verse: Whoever has developed and cultivated the four bases of psychic power—made them a vehicle and a basis, kept them up, consolidated them, and properly implemented them—may, if they wish, live for the proper lifespan or what’s left of it.

sn51.10:5.5.verse: The Realized One has developed and cultivated the four bases of psychic power, made them a vehicle and a basis, kept them up, consolidated them, and properly implemented them. If he wished, the Realized One could live for the proper lifespan or what’s left of it.”

sn51.10:6.1.verse: But Ānanda didn’t get it, even though the Buddha dropped such an obvious hint, such a clear sign.

sn51.10:6.3.verse: “Sir, may the Blessed One please remain for the proper lifespan! May the Holy One please remain for the proper lifespan! That would be for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.” For his mind was as if possessed by Māra.

sn51.10:7.1.verse: Then the Buddha said to him,

sn51.10:7.4.verse: “Yes, sir,” replied Ānanda. He rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before sitting at the root of a tree close by.

sn51.10:8.1.verse: And then, not long after Ānanda had left, Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and said to him:

sn51.10:9.1.verse: “Sir, may the Blessed One now be fully extinguished! May the Holy One now be fully extinguished! Now is the time for the full extinguishment of the Buddha.

sn51.10:9.2.verse: Sir, you once made this statement:

sn51.10:9.3.verse: ‘Wicked One, I shall not be fully extinguished until I have monk disciples who are competent, educated, assured, learned, have memorized the teachings, and practice in line with the principle of the teaching. Not until they practice properly, living in line with the teaching. Not until they’ve learned their own denomination, and explain, teach, assert, establish, disclose, analyze, and make it clear. Not until they can legitimately and completely refute the doctrines of others that come up, and teach with a demonstrable basis.’

sn51.10:10.1.verse: Today you do have such monk disciples.

sn51.10:10.2.verse: May the Blessed One now be fully extinguished! May the Holy One now be fully extinguished! Now is the time for the full extinguishment of the Buddha.

sn51.10:11.1.verse: Sir, you once made this statement:

sn51.10:11.2.verse: ‘Wicked One, I shall not be fully extinguished until I have nun disciples who are competent, educated, self-assured, learned …’ …

sn51.10:12.1.verse: Today you do have such nun disciples.

sn51.10:12.2.verse: May the Blessed One now be fully extinguished! May the Holy One now be fully extinguished! Now is the time for the full extinguishment of the Buddha.

sn51.10:13.1.verse: Sir, you once made this statement:

sn51.10:13.2.verse: ‘Wicked One, I shall not be fully extinguished until I have layman disciples …

sn51.10:13.3.verse: and laywoman disciples who are competent, educated, self-assured, learned …’ …

sn51.10:14.1.verse: Today you do have such layman

sn51.10:14.3.verse: May the Blessed One now be fully extinguished! May the Holy One now be fully extinguished! Now is the time for the full extinguishment of the Buddha.

sn51.10:15.1.verse: Sir, you once made this statement:

sn51.10:15.2.verse: ‘Wicked One, I shall not be fully extinguished until my spiritual path is successful and prosperous, extensive, popular, widespread, and fully revealed among gods and humans.’

sn51.10:15.3.verse: Today your spiritual path is successful and prosperous, extensive, popular, widespread, and fully revealed among gods and humans.

sn51.10:15.4.verse: May the Blessed One now be fully extinguished! May the Holy One now be fully extinguished! Now is the time for the full extinguishment of the Buddha.”

sn51.10:16.1.verse: When this was said, the Buddha said to Māra,

sn51.10:16.2.verse: “Relax, Wicked One. The full extinguishment of the Realized One will be soon.

sn51.10:16.3.verse: Three months from now the Realized One will be fully extinguished.”

sn51.10:17.1.verse: So at the Cāpāla Shrine the Buddha, mindful and aware, surrendered the life force.

sn51.10:17.2.verse: When he did so there was a great earthquake, awe-inspiring and hair-raising, and thunder cracked the sky.

sn51.10:17.3.verse: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha expressed this heartfelt sentiment:

sn51.10:18.1.verse: “Comparing the incomparable with the creation of prolonged life,

sn51.10:18.2.verse: the sage surrendered the life force.

sn51.10:18.4.verse: he shattered self-creation like a suit of armor.”

sn51.11:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, before my awakening—when I was still unawakened but intent on awakening—I thought:

sn51.11:1.3.verse: ‘What’s the cause, what’s the reason for the development of the bases of psychic power?’

sn51.11:1.5.verse: ‘It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort.

sn51.11:1.6.verse: They think: “My enthusiasm won’t be too lax or too tense. And it’ll be neither constricted internally nor scattered externally.”

sn51.11:1.7.verse: And they meditate perceiving before and behind:

sn51.11:1.8.verse: as before, so behind; as behind, so before;

sn51.11:1.9.verse: as below, so above; as above, so below;

sn51.11:1.10.verse: as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.

sn51.11:1.11.verse: And so, with an open and unenveloped heart, they develop a mind that’s full of radiance.

sn51.11:2.1.verse: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to energy …

sn51.11:4.2.verse: They think: “My inquiry won’t be too lax or too tense. And it’ll be neither constricted internally nor scattered externally.”

sn51.11:4.3.verse: And they meditate perceiving before and behind:

sn51.11:4.4.verse: as before, so behind; as behind, so before;

sn51.11:4.5.verse: as below, so above; as above, so below;

sn51.11:4.6.verse: as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.

sn51.11:4.7.verse: And so, with an open and unenveloped heart, they develop a mind that’s full of radiance.’

sn51.11:5.1.verse: When the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated in this way, they wield the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying themselves and becoming one again; materializing and dematerializing; going unobstructed through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; diving in and out of the earth as if it were water; walking on water as if it were earth; flying cross-legged through the sky like a bird; touching and stroking with the hand the sun and moon, so mighty and powerful; controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity.

sn51.11:6.1.verse: When the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated in this way, with clairaudience that is purified and superhuman they hear both kinds of sounds, human and heavenly, whether near or far.

sn51.11:7.1.verse: When the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated in this way, they understand the minds of other beings and individuals, having encompassed them with their own mind.

sn51.11:7.2.verse: They understand mind with greed as ‘mind with greed’,

sn51.11:7.3.verse: and mind without greed as ‘mind without greed’.

sn51.11:7.17.verse: They understand unfreed mind as ‘unfreed mind’.

sn51.11:8.1.verse: When the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated in this way, they recollect many kinds of past lives. That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. They remember: ‘There, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn somewhere else. There, too, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn here.’ And so they recollect their many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

sn51.11:9.1.verse: When the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated in this way, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds. ‘These dear beings did bad things by way of body, speech, and mind. They denounced the noble ones; they had wrong view; and they chose to act out of that wrong view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell. These dear beings, however, did good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They never denounced the noble ones; they had right view; and they chose to act out of that right view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’ And so, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

sn51.11:10.1.verse: When the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated in this way, they realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”

sn51.12:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort.

sn51.12:1.4.verse: They think: ‘My enthusiasm won’t be too lax or too tense. And it’ll be neither constricted internally nor scattered externally.’

sn51.12:1.7.verse: as below, so above; as above, so below;

sn51.12:1.8.verse: as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.

sn51.12:1.9.verse: And so, with an open and unenveloped heart, they develop a mind that’s full of radiance.

sn51.12:2.1.verse: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to energy …

sn51.12:2.4.verse: They think: ‘My inquiry won’t be too lax or too tense. And it’ll be neither constricted internally nor scattered externally.’
