sn51.12:2.9.verse: And so, with an open and unenveloped heart, they develop a mind that’s full of radiance.

sn51.12:2.10.verse: When the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated in this way they’re very fruitful and beneficial.

sn51.12:3.1.verse: When the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated in this way, a mendicant wields the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying themselves and becoming one again … controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity. …

sn51.12:4.1.verse: When the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated in this way, they realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”

sn51.13:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, if a mendicant depends on enthusiasm in order to gain immersion, gain unification of mind,

sn51.13:1.2.verse: this is called immersion due to enthusiasm.

sn51.13:1.3.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise.

sn51.13:1.4.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen are given up.

sn51.13:1.5.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities arise.

sn51.13:1.6.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.

sn51.13:1.8.verse: And so there is this enthusiasm, this immersion due to enthusiasm, and these active efforts.

sn51.13:1.9.verse: This is called the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort.

sn51.13:2.1.verse: If a mendicant depends on energy in order to gain immersion, gain unification of mind,

sn51.13:2.2.verse: this is called immersion due to energy.

sn51.13:2.3.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise …

sn51.13:2.4.verse: so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.

sn51.13:2.6.verse: And so there is this energy, this immersion due to energy, and these active efforts.

sn51.13:2.7.verse: This is called the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to energy, and active effort.

sn51.13:3.1.verse: If a mendicant depends on mental development in order to gain immersion, gain unification of mind,

sn51.13:3.2.verse: this is called immersion due to mental development.

sn51.13:3.3.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise …

sn51.13:3.4.verse: so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.

sn51.13:3.6.verse: And so there is this mental development, this immersion due to mental development, and these active efforts.

sn51.13:3.7.verse: This is called the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to mental development, and active effort.

sn51.13:4.1.verse: If a mendicant depends on inquiry in order to gain immersion, gain unification of mind,

sn51.13:4.2.verse: this is called immersion due to inquiry.

sn51.13:4.3.verse: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise …

sn51.13:4.4.verse: so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.

sn51.13:4.6.verse: And so there is this inquiry, this immersion due to inquiry, and these active efforts.

sn51.13:4.7.verse: This is called the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to inquiry, and active effort.”

sn51.14:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

sn51.14:1.3.verse: Now at that time several mendicants were staying beneath the longhouse. They were haughty, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, loose-tongued, unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying minds and undisciplined faculties.

sn51.14:2.1.verse: Then the Buddha addressed Venerable Mahāmoggallāna,

sn51.14:2.2.verse: “These spiritual companions of yours staying beneath the longhouse are haughty, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, loose-tongued, unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying minds and undisciplined faculties.

sn51.14:2.3.verse: Go, Moggallāna, and strike awe in those mendicants!”

sn51.14:3.1.verse: “Yes, sir,” replied Mahāmoggallāna. Then he used his psychic power to make the longhouse shake and rock and tremble with his big toe.

sn51.14:3.2.verse: Then those mendicants stood to one side, shocked and awestruck.

sn51.14:3.4.verse: There’s no wind at all; and this stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother has deep foundations. It’s firmly embedded, imperturbable and unshakable. And yet it shakes and rocks and quivers!”

sn51.14:4.1.verse: Then the Buddha went up to those mendicants and said:

sn51.14:4.2.verse: “Why do you, mendicants, stand to one side, shocked and awestruck?”

sn51.14:4.4.verse: There’s no wind at all; and this stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother has deep foundations. It’s firmly embedded, imperturbable and unshakable. And yet it shakes and rocks and quivers!”

sn51.14:4.5.verse: “Wanting to strike awe in you, the mendicant Moggallāna made the longhouse shake and rock and quiver with his big toe.

sn51.14:4.7.verse: What things has the mendicant Moggallāna developed and cultivated so as to have such power and might?”

sn51.14:4.8.verse: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. He is our guide and our refuge. Sir, may the Buddha himself please clarify the meaning of this. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

sn51.14:5.2.verse: The mendicant Moggallāna has become so powerful and mighty by developing and cultivating the four bases of psychic power.

sn51.14:5.4.verse: Moggallāna develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm …

sn51.14:5.8.verse: He thinks: ‘My inquiry won’t be too lax or too tense. And it’ll be neither constricted internally nor scattered externally.’

sn51.14:5.10.verse: And he meditates perceiving before and behind:

sn51.14:5.11.verse: as before, so behind; as behind, so before;

sn51.14:5.12.verse: as below, so above; as above, so below;

sn51.14:5.13.verse: as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.

sn51.14:5.14.verse: And so, with an open and unenveloped heart, he develops a mind that’s full of radiance.

sn51.14:5.15.verse: The mendicant Moggallāna has become so powerful and mighty by developing and cultivating these four bases of psychic power.

sn51.14:5.16.verse: And by developing and cultivating these four bases of psychic power, the mendicant Moggallāna wields the many kinds of psychic power … controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity. …

sn51.14:5.17.verse: And by developing and cultivating these four bases of psychic power, the mendicant Moggallāna realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And he lives having realized it with his own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”

sn51.15:1.2.verse: At one time Venerable Ānanda was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

sn51.15:1.3.verse: Then Uṇṇābha the brahmin went up to Venerable Ānanda, and exchanged greetings with him.

sn51.15:1.4.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to him,

sn51.15:1.5.verse: “Worthy Ānanda, what’s the goal of leading the spiritual life under the ascetic Gotama?”

sn51.15:1.6.verse: “The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha, brahmin, is to give up desire.”

sn51.15:2.1.verse: “But is there a path and a practice for giving up that desire?”

sn51.15:3.2.verse: “It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm …

sn51.15:3.6.verse: This is the path and the practice for giving up that desire.”

sn51.15:4.1.verse: “This being the case, worthy Ānanda, the path is endless, not finite.

sn51.15:4.2.verse: For it’s not possible to give up desire by means of desire.”

sn51.15:4.3.verse: “Well then, brahmin, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.

sn51.15:4.5.verse: Have you ever had a desire to walk to the park,

sn51.15:4.6.verse: but when you arrived at the park, the corresponding desire faded away?”

sn51.15:4.8.verse: “Have you ever had the energy to walk to the park,

sn51.15:4.9.verse: but when you arrived at the park, the corresponding energy faded away?”

sn51.15:4.11.verse: “Have you ever had the idea to walk to the park,

sn51.15:4.12.verse: but when you arrived at the park, the corresponding idea faded away?”

sn51.15:4.14.verse: “Have you ever inquired regarding a walk to the park,

sn51.15:4.15.verse: but when you arrived at the park, the corresponding inquiry faded away?”

sn51.15:5.1.verse: “In the same way, take a mendicant who is perfected—with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment. They formerly had the desire to attain perfection, but when they attained perfection the corresponding desire faded away.

sn51.15:5.2.verse: They formerly had the energy to attain perfection, but when they attained perfection the corresponding energy faded away.

sn51.15:5.3.verse: They formerly had the idea to attain perfection, but when they attained perfection the corresponding idea faded away.

sn51.15:5.4.verse: They formerly inquired regarding attaining perfection, but when they attained perfection the corresponding inquiry faded away.

sn51.15:5.6.verse: This being the case, is the path endless or finite?”

sn51.15:6.1.verse: “Clearly, worthy Ānanda, this being the case, the path is finite, not endless.

sn51.15:6.3.verse: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, the worthy Ānanda has made the teaching clear in many ways.

sn51.15:6.4.verse: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

sn51.15:6.5.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Ānanda remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

sn51.16:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, all the ascetics and brahmins in the past,

sn51.16:1.3.verse: or present who are mighty and powerful have become so by developing and cultivating the four bases of psychic power.

sn51.16:2.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm …

sn51.16:2.6.verse: All the ascetics and brahmins in the past,

sn51.16:2.8.verse: or present who are mighty and powerful have become so by developing and cultivating the four bases of psychic power.”

sn51.17:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, all the ascetics and brahmins in the past,

sn51.17:3.1.verse: or present who wield the various kinds of psychic power—multiplying themselves and becoming one again; materializing and dematerializing; going unobstructed through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; diving in and out of the earth as if it were water; walking on water as if it were earth; flying cross-legged through the sky like a bird; touching and stroking with the hand the sun and moon, so mighty and powerful; controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity—

sn51.17:3.2.verse: do so by developing and cultivating the four bases of psychic power.

sn51.17:4.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm …

sn51.17:4.6.verse: Mendicants, all the ascetics and brahmins in the past,

sn51.17:6.1.verse: or present who wield the many kinds of psychic power—multiplying themselves and becoming one again … controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity—

sn51.17:6.2.verse: do so by developing and cultivating these four bases of psychic power.”

sn51.18:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, by developing and cultivating the four bases of psychic power, a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

sn51.18:2.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm …

sn51.18:2.6.verse: By developing and cultivating these four bases of psychic power, a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”

sn51.19:0.3.verse: A Teaching on Psychic Power, Etc.

sn51.19:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, I will teach you psychic power, the bases of psychic power, the development of the bases of psychic power, and the practice that leads to the development of the bases of psychic power.

sn51.19:2.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant wields the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying themselves and becoming one again … controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity.

sn51.19:3.1.verse: And what is the basis of psychic power?

sn51.19:3.2.verse: The path and practice that leads to gaining psychic power.

sn51.19:3.3.verse: This is called the basis of psychic power.

sn51.19:4.1.verse: And what is the development of the bases of psychic power?

sn51.19:4.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm …

sn51.19:4.6.verse: This is called the development of the bases of psychic power.

sn51.19:5.1.verse: And what is the practice that leads to the development of the bases of psychic power?

sn51.19:5.2.verse: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn51.19:5.3.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn51.19:5.4.verse: This is called the practice that leads to the development of the bases of psychic power.”

sn51.20:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when the four bases of psychic power are developed and cultivated they’re very fruitful and beneficial.

sn51.20:2.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort.

sn51.20:2.3.verse: They think: ‘My enthusiasm won’t be too lax or too tense. And it’ll be neither constricted internally nor scattered externally.’

sn51.20:2.4.verse: And they meditate perceiving before and behind:

sn51.20:2.5.verse: as before, so behind; as behind, so before;

sn51.20:2.6.verse: as below, so above; as above, so below;

sn51.20:2.7.verse: as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.

sn51.20:2.8.verse: And so, with an open and unenveloped heart, they develop a mind that’s full of radiance.

sn51.20:2.9.verse: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to energy …

sn51.20:2.12.verse: They think: ‘My inquiry won’t be too lax or too tense. And it’ll be neither constricted internally nor scattered externally.’

sn51.20:2.13.verse: And they meditate perceiving before and behind:

sn51.20:2.14.verse: as before, so behind; as behind, so before;

sn51.20:2.15.verse: as below, so above; as above, so below;

sn51.20:2.16.verse: as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.

sn51.20:2.17.verse: And so, with an open and unenveloped heart, they develop a mind that’s full of radiance.

sn51.20:3.1.verse: And what is enthusiasm that’s too lax?

sn51.20:3.2.verse: It’s when enthusiasm is coupled with laziness.

sn51.20:4.1.verse: And what is enthusiasm that’s too tense?

sn51.20:4.2.verse: It’s when enthusiasm is coupled with restlessness.

sn51.20:5.1.verse: And what is enthusiasm that’s constricted internally?

sn51.20:5.2.verse: It’s when enthusiasm is coupled with dullness and drowsiness.

sn51.20:5.3.verse: This is called enthusiasm constricted internally.

sn51.20:6.1.verse: And what is enthusiasm that’s scattered externally?

sn51.20:6.2.verse: It’s when enthusiasm is frequently scattered and diffused externally on account of the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn51.20:6.3.verse: This is called enthusiasm scattered externally.

sn51.20:7.1.verse: And how does a mendicant meditate perceiving before and behind:

sn51.20:7.2.verse: as before, so behind; as behind, so before?

sn51.20:7.3.verse: It’s when the perception of before and behind is properly grasped, focused on, borne in mind, and penetrated with wisdom by a mendicant.

sn51.20:7.4.verse: That’s how a mendicant meditates perceiving before and behind:

sn51.20:7.5.verse: as before, so behind; as behind, so before.

sn51.20:8.1.verse: And how does a mendicant meditate as below, so above; as above, so below?

sn51.20:8.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant examines their own body up from the soles of the feet and down from the tips of the hairs, wrapped in skin and full of many kinds of filth.

sn51.20:8.3.verse: ‘In this body there is head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, diaphragm, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, undigested food, feces, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, urine.’

sn51.20:8.4.verse: That’s how a mendicant meditates as below, so above; as above, so below.

sn51.20:9.1.verse: And how does a mendicant meditate as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day?

sn51.20:9.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort, with the same features, attributes, and signs by day as by night.

sn51.20:9.3.verse: And they develop it with the same features, attributes, and signs by night as by day.

sn51.20:9.4.verse: That’s how a mendicant meditates as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.

sn51.20:10.1.verse: And how, with an open and unenveloped heart, does a mendicant develop a mind that’s full of radiance?

sn51.20:10.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant has properly grasped the perception of light, and has properly grasped the perception of day.

sn51.20:10.3.verse: That’s how, with an open and unenveloped heart, a mendicant develops a mind that’s full of radiance.

sn51.20:11.1.verse: And what is energy that’s too lax? …

sn51.20:16.1.verse: And what is mental development that’s too lax? …

sn51.20:20.1.verse: And what is inquiry that’s too lax?

sn51.20:20.2.verse: It’s when inquiry is coupled with laziness.

sn51.20:21.1.verse: And what is inquiry that’s too tense?

sn51.20:21.2.verse: It’s when inquiry is coupled with restlessness.

sn51.20:22.1.verse: And what is inquiry that’s constricted internally?

sn51.20:22.2.verse: It’s when inquiry is coupled with dullness and drowsiness.

sn51.20:22.3.verse: This is called inquiry constricted internally.

sn51.20:23.1.verse: And what is inquiry that’s scattered externally?

sn51.20:23.2.verse: It’s when inquiry is frequently scattered and diffused externally on account of the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn51.20:23.3.verse: This is called inquiry scattered externally. …

sn51.20:23.4.verse: That’s how, with an open and unenveloped heart, a mendicant develops a mind that’s full of radiance.

sn51.20:23.5.verse: When the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated in this way they’re very fruitful and beneficial.

sn51.20:24.1.verse: When the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated in this way, a mendicant wields the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying themselves and becoming one again … controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity. …

sn51.20:24.2.verse: When the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated in this way, they realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”

sn51.21:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, before my awakening—when I was still unawakened but intent on awakening—I thought:

sn51.21:1.3.verse: ‘What’s the path and practice for developing the bases of psychic power?’

sn51.21:1.5.verse: ‘It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort.

sn51.21:1.6.verse: They think: “My enthusiasm won’t be too lax or too tense. And it’ll be neither constricted internally nor scattered externally.”

sn51.21:1.7.verse: And they meditate perceiving before and behind:

sn51.21:1.8.verse: as before, so behind; as behind, so before;

sn51.21:1.9.verse: as below, so above; as above, so below;

sn51.21:1.10.verse: as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.

sn51.21:1.11.verse: And so, with an open and unenveloped heart, they develop a mind that’s full of radiance.

sn51.21:1.12.verse: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to energy …

sn51.21:1.15.verse: They think: “My inquiry won’t be too lax or too tense. And it’ll be neither constricted internally nor scattered externally.”

sn51.21:1.16.verse: And they meditate perceiving before and behind:

sn51.21:1.17.verse: as before, so behind; as behind, so before;

sn51.21:1.18.verse: as below, so above; as above, so below;

sn51.21:1.19.verse: as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.

sn51.21:1.20.verse: And so, with an open and unenveloped heart, they develop a mind that’s full of radiance.’

sn51.21:2.2.verse: When the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated in this way, they realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”

sn51.22:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn51.22:1.3.verse: “Sir, do you have personal experience of having gone to the realm of divinity by psychic power with a mind-made body?”

sn51.22:1.5.verse: “But do you have personal experience of having gone to the realm of divinity by psychic power with this body made up of the four principal states?”

sn51.22:2.1.verse: “It’s incredible and amazing that the Buddha is at least able to go to the realm of divinity by psychic power with a mind-made body! And that he has personal experience of going to the realm of divinity by psychic power with this body made up of the four principal states!”

sn51.22:2.2.verse: “Ānanda, the Realized Ones are incredible and have incredible qualities. They’re amazing and have amazing qualities.

sn51.22:3.1.verse: Sometimes the Realized One submerges his body in his mind and his mind in his body. He meditates after sinking into a perception of bliss and lightness in the body.

sn51.22:3.2.verse: At that time his body becomes lighter, softer, more workable, and more radiant.

sn51.22:4.1.verse: Suppose there was an iron ball that had been heated all day. It’d become lighter, softer, more workable, and more radiant.

sn51.22:4.2.verse: In the same way, sometimes the Realized One submerges his body in his mind and his mind in his body. He meditates after sinking into a perception of bliss and lightness in the body.

sn51.22:4.3.verse: At that time his body becomes lighter, softer, more workable, and more radiant.

sn51.22:5.1.verse: Sometimes the Realized One submerges his body in his mind and his mind in his body. He meditates after sinking into a perception of bliss and lightness in the body.

sn51.22:5.2.verse: At that time his body easily rises up from the ground into the air.

sn51.22:5.3.verse: He wields the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying himself and becoming one again … controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity.

sn51.22:6.1.verse: Suppose there was a light tuft of cotton-wool or kapok. Taken up by the wind, it would easily rise up from the ground into the air.

sn51.22:6.2.verse: In the same way, sometimes the Realized One submerges his body in his mind and his mind in his body. He meditates after sinking into a perception of bliss and lightness in the body.

sn51.22:6.3.verse: At that time his body easily rises up from the ground into the air.

sn51.22:6.4.verse: He wields the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying himself and becoming one again … controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity.”

sn51.23:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four bases of psychic power.

sn51.23:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm …

sn51.23:1.7.verse: These are the four bases of psychic power.

sn51.23:1.8.verse: By developing and cultivating these four bases of psychic power, a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”

sn51.25:1.8.verse: Because of developing and cultivating these four bases of psychic power, one of two results can be expected:

sn51.25:1.9.verse: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”

sn51.26:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four bases of psychic power.

sn51.26:1.3.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm …

sn51.26:1.7.verse: These are the four bases of psychic power.

sn51.26:1.8.verse: Because of developing and cultivating these four bases of psychic power, seven fruits and benefits can be expected.

sn51.26:2.2.verse: They attain enlightenment early on in this very life.

sn51.26:2.3.verse: If not, they attain enlightenment at the time of death.

sn51.26:2.4.verse: If not, with the ending of the five lower fetters, they’re extinguished between one life and the next … they’re extinguished upon landing … they’re extinguished without extra effort … they’re extinguished with extra effort … they head upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm.

sn51.26:2.5.verse: Because of developing and cultivating these four bases of psychic power, these seven fruits and benefits can be expected.”

sn51.27:1.2.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn51.27:2.1.verse: “Sir, what is psychic power? What is the basis of psychic power? What is the development of the bases of psychic power? And what is the practice that leads to the development of the bases of psychic power?”

sn51.27:2.2.verse: “Ānanda, take a mendicant who wields the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying themselves and becoming one again … controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity.

sn51.27:3.1.verse: And what is the basis of psychic power?

sn51.27:3.2.verse: The path and practice that leads to gaining psychic power.

sn51.27:3.3.verse: This is called the basis of psychic power.

sn51.27:4.1.verse: And what is the development of the bases of psychic power?

sn51.27:4.2.verse: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm …

sn51.27:4.6.verse: This is called the development of the bases of psychic power.

sn51.27:5.1.verse: And what is the practice that leads to the development of the bases of psychic power?

sn51.27:5.2.verse: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn51.27:5.3.verse: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn51.27:5.4.verse: This is called the practice that leads to the development of the bases of psychic power.”
