sn55.7:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Kosalans together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants when he arrived at a village of the Kosalan brahmins named Bamboo Gate.

sn55.7:1.3.verse: The brahmins and householders of Bamboo Gate heard:

sn55.7:1.4.verse: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—has arrived at Bamboo Gate, together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants.

sn55.7:1.6.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

sn55.7:1.7.verse: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

sn55.7:1.8.verse: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

sn55.7:1.9.verse: It’s good to see such perfected ones.”

sn55.7:2.1.verse: Then the brahmins and householders of Bamboo Gate went up to the Buddha. Before sitting down to one side, some bowed, some exchanged greetings and polite conversation, some held up their cupped palms toward the Buddha, some announced their name and clan, while some kept silent. Seated to one side they said to the Buddha:

sn55.7:2.2.verse: “Worthy Gotama, these are our wishes, desires, and hopes.

sn55.7:2.3.verse: We wish to live at home with our children; to use sandalwood imported from Kāsi; to wear garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and to accept gold and currency. And when our body breaks up, after death, we wish to be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn55.7:2.4.verse: Given that we have such wishes, may the Buddha teach us the Dhamma so that we may achieve them.”

sn55.7:3.1.verse: “Householders, I will teach you an explanation of the Dhamma that is relevant for oneself.

sn55.7:3.2.verse: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn55.7:4.1.verse: “And what is the explanation of the Dhamma that applies to oneself?

sn55.7:4.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple reflects:

sn55.7:4.3.verse: ‘I want to live and don’t want to die; I want to be happy and recoil from pain.

sn55.7:4.4.verse: Since this is so, if someone were to take my life, I wouldn’t like that.

sn55.7:4.5.verse: But others also want to live and don’t want to die; they want to be happy and recoil from pain. So if I were to take the life of someone else, they wouldn’t like that either.

sn55.7:4.6.verse: The thing that is disliked by me is also disliked by others.

sn55.7:4.7.verse: Since I dislike this thing, how can I inflict it on someone else?’

sn55.7:4.8.verse: Reflecting in this way, they give up killing living creatures themselves. And they encourage others to give up killing living creatures, praising the giving up of killing living creatures.

sn55.7:4.9.verse: So their bodily behavior is purified in three points.

sn55.7:5.2.verse: ‘If someone were to steal from me, I wouldn’t like that.

sn55.7:5.3.verse: But if I were to steal from someone else, they wouldn’t like that either.

sn55.7:5.4.verse: The thing that is disliked by me is also disliked by others.

sn55.7:5.5.verse: Since I dislike this thing, how can I inflict it on someone else?’

sn55.7:5.6.verse: Reflecting in this way, they give up stealing themselves. And they encourage others to give up stealing, praising the giving up of stealing.

sn55.7:5.7.verse: So their bodily behavior is purified in three points.

sn55.7:6.2.verse: ‘If someone were to have relations with my wives, I wouldn’t like it.

sn55.7:6.3.verse: But if I were to have relations with someone else’s wives, he wouldn’t like that either.

sn55.7:6.4.verse: The thing that is disliked by me is also disliked by others.

sn55.7:6.5.verse: Since I dislike this thing, how can I inflict it on others?’

sn55.7:6.6.verse: Reflecting in this way, they give up sexual misconduct themselves. And they encourage others to give up sexual misconduct, praising the giving up of sexual misconduct.

sn55.7:6.7.verse: So their bodily behavior is purified in three points.

sn55.7:7.2.verse: ‘If someone were to distort my meaning by lying, I wouldn’t like it.

sn55.7:7.3.verse: But if I were to distort someone else’s meaning by lying, they wouldn’t like it either.

sn55.7:7.4.verse: The thing that is disliked by me is also disliked by someone else.

sn55.7:7.5.verse: Since I dislike this thing, how can I inflict it on others?’

sn55.7:7.6.verse: Reflecting in this way, they give up lying themselves. And they encourage others to give up lying, praising the giving up of lying.

sn55.7:7.7.verse: So their verbal behavior is purified in three points.

sn55.7:8.2.verse: ‘If someone were to break me up from my friends by backbiting, I wouldn’t like it.

sn55.7:8.3.verse: But if I were to break someone else from their friends by backbiting, they wouldn’t like it either. …’

sn55.7:8.4.verse: So their verbal behavior is purified in three points.

sn55.7:9.2.verse: ‘If someone were to attack me with harsh speech, I wouldn’t like it.

sn55.7:9.3.verse: But if I were to attack someone else with harsh speech, they wouldn’t like it either. …’

sn55.7:9.5.verse: So their verbal behavior is purified in three points.

sn55.7:10.2.verse: ‘If someone were to annoy me by talking silliness and nonsense, I wouldn’t like it.

sn55.7:10.3.verse: But if I were to annoy someone else by talking silliness and nonsense, they wouldn’t like it either.’

sn55.7:10.4.verse: The thing that is disliked by me is also disliked by another.

sn55.7:10.5.verse: Since I dislike this thing, how can I inflict it on another?’

sn55.7:10.6.verse: Reflecting in this way, they give up talking nonsense themselves. And they encourage others to give up talking nonsense, praising the giving up of talking nonsense.

sn55.7:10.7.verse: So their verbal behavior is purified in three points.

sn55.7:11.1.verse: And they have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.7:11.5.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.7:11.6.verse: When a noble disciple possesses these seven good qualities and these four desirable states they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

sn55.7:11.7.verse: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

sn55.7:12.1.verse: When he had spoken, the brahmins and householders of Bamboo Gate said to the Buddha,

sn55.7:12.3.verse: We go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

sn55.7:12.4.verse: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge for life.”

sn55.8:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying at Ñātika in the brick house.

sn55.8:1.3.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn55.8:2.1.verse: “Sir, the monk named Sāḷha has passed away.

sn55.8:2.2.verse: Where has he been reborn in his next life?

sn55.8:2.7.verse: and the laywoman named Sujātā have passed away.

sn55.8:2.8.verse: Where have they been reborn in the next life?”

sn55.8:3.1.verse: “Ānanda, the monk Sāḷha passed away having realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, having realized it with his own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

sn55.8:3.2.verse: The nun Nandā passed away having ended the five lower fetters. She’s been reborn spontaneously, and will be extinguished there, not liable to return from that world.

sn55.8:3.3.verse: The layman Sudatta passed away having ended three fetters, and weakened greed, hate, and delusion. He’s a once-returner; he will come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.

sn55.8:3.4.verse: The laywoman Sujātā passed away having ended three fetters. She’s a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

sn55.8:4.1.verse: It’s no wonder that a human being should pass away.

sn55.8:4.2.verse: But if you should come and ask me about it each and every time someone dies that would be a bother for me.

sn55.8:4.3.verse: So Ānanda, I will teach you the explanation of the Dhamma named ‘the mirror of the teaching’. A noble disciple who has this may declare of themselves:

sn55.8:4.4.verse: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’

sn55.8:5.1.verse: And what is that mirror of the teaching?

sn55.8:6.1.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.8:6.4.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.8:6.5.verse: This is that mirror of the teaching.

sn55.8:6.6.verse: A noble disciple who has this may declare of themselves:

sn55.8:6.7.verse: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

sn55.8:6.9.verse: (The following two discourses have the same setting.)

sn55.9:1.2.verse: “Sir, the monk named Asoka has passed away.

sn55.9:1.3.verse: Where has he been reborn in his next life?

sn55.9:1.6.verse: and the laywoman named Asokā have passed away.

sn55.9:1.7.verse: Where have they been reborn in the next life?”

sn55.9:2.1.verse: “Ānanda, the monk Asoka passed away having realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom … in this very life …

sn55.9:2.2.verse: (And all is explained as in SN 55.8.)

sn55.9:3.1.verse: This is that mirror of the teaching.

sn55.9:3.2.verse: A noble disciple who has this may declare of themselves:

sn55.9:3.3.verse: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

sn55.10:1.2.verse: “Sir, the layman named Kakkaṭa has passed away in Ñātika.

sn55.10:1.3.verse: Where has he been reborn in his next life?

sn55.10:1.10.verse: Subhadda have passed away in Ñātika.

sn55.10:1.11.verse: Where have they been reborn in the next life?”

sn55.10:2.8.verse: and Subhadda passed away having ended the five lower fetters. They’ve been reborn spontaneously, and will be extinguished there, not liable to return from that world.

sn55.10:3.1.verse: Over fifty laymen in Ñātika have passed away having ended the five lower fetters. They’ve been reborn spontaneously, and will be extinguished there, not liable to return from that world.

sn55.10:3.2.verse: More than ninety laymen in Ñātika have passed away having ended three fetters, and weakened greed, hate, and delusion. They’re once-returners, who will come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.

sn55.10:3.3.verse: More than five hundred laymen in Ñātika have passed away having ended three fetters. They’re stream-enterers, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

sn55.10:4.1.verse: It’s no wonder that a human being should pass away.

sn55.10:4.2.verse: But if you should come and ask me about it each and every time someone passes away, that would be a bother for me.

sn55.10:4.3.verse: So Ānanda, I will teach you the explanation of the Dhamma named ‘the mirror of the teaching’. A noble disciple who has this may declare of themselves:

sn55.10:4.4.verse: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’

sn55.10:5.1.verse: And what is that mirror of the teaching?

sn55.10:6.1.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.10:6.4.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.10:6.5.verse: This is that mirror of the teaching.

sn55.10:6.6.verse: A noble disciple who has this may declare of themselves:

sn55.10:6.7.verse: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

sn55.11:0.3.verse: A Saṅgha of a Thousand Nuns

sn55.11:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the Royal Monastery.

sn55.11:1.2.verse: Then a Saṅgha of a thousand nuns went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side. The Buddha said to them:

sn55.11:2.1.verse: “Nuns, a noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

sn55.11:2.3.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.11:2.7.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.11:2.8.verse: A noble disciple who has these four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

sn55.12:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, the brahmins advocate a practice called ‘get up and go’.

sn55.12:1.4.verse: ‘Please, my man, rising early you should face east and walk.

sn55.12:1.5.verse: Do not avoid a pit, a cliff, a stump, thorny ground, a swamp, or a sewer.

sn55.12:1.6.verse: You should await death in the place that you fall.

sn55.12:1.7.verse: And when your body breaks up, after death, you’ll be reborn in a good place, a heaven realm.’

sn55.12:2.1.verse: But this practice of the brahmins is a foolish procedure, a stupid procedure. It doesn’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, or extinguishment.

sn55.12:2.2.verse: But in the training of the Noble One I advocate a ‘get up and go’ practice

sn55.12:2.3.verse: which does lead solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

sn55.12:3.1.verse: And what is that ‘get up and go’ practice?

sn55.12:3.3.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.12:3.7.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.12:3.8.verse: This is that ‘get up and go’ practice

sn55.12:3.9.verse: which does lead solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.”

sn55.13:1.1.verse: At one time the venerables Ānanda and Sāriputta were staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn55.13:1.2.verse: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Sāriputta came out of retreat, went to Venerable Ānanda, and exchanged greetings with him.

sn55.13:1.3.verse: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to him:

sn55.13:1.4.verse: “Reverend, how many things do people have to give up and how many do they have to possess in order for the Buddha to declare that they’re a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening?”

sn55.13:1.5.verse: “Reverend, people have to give up four things and possess four things in order for the Buddha to declare that they’re a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

sn55.13:2.2.verse: They don’t have the distrust in the Buddha that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn55.13:2.3.verse: And they do have the experiential confidence in the Buddha that causes a learned noble disciple to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn55.13:2.4.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

sn55.13:3.1.verse: They don’t have the distrust in the teaching that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn55.13:3.2.verse: And they do have the experiential confidence in the teaching that causes a learned noble disciple to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn55.13:3.3.verse: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

sn55.13:4.1.verse: They don’t have the distrust in the Saṅgha that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn55.13:4.2.verse: And they do have the experiential confidence in the Saṅgha that causes a learned noble disciple to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn55.13:4.3.verse: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, and worthy of veneration with cupped palms.’

sn55.13:5.1.verse: They don’t have the unethical conduct that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn55.13:5.2.verse: And they do have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones that causes a learned noble disciple to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn55.13:5.3.verse: Their ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

sn55.13:5.4.verse: People have to give up these four things and possess these four things in order for the Buddha to declare that they’re a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

sn55.14:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a noble disciple who has four things has gone beyond all fear of being reborn in a bad place.

sn55.14:1.3.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.14:1.7.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.14:1.8.verse: A noble disciple who has these four things has gone beyond all fear of being reborn in a bad place.”

sn55.15:0.3.verse: Fear of the Bad Place, the Underworld

sn55.15:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a noble disciple who has four things has gone beyond all fear of being reborn in a bad place, the underworld.

sn55.15:1.3.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.15:1.7.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.15:1.8.verse: A noble disciple who has these four things has gone beyond all fear of being reborn in a bad place, the underworld.”

sn55.16:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who you have sympathy for, and those worth listening to—friends and colleagues, relatives and family—should be encouraged, supported, and established by you in the four factors of stream-entry.

sn55.16:1.7.verse: And the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.16:1.8.verse: Those who you have sympathy for, and those worth listening to—friends and colleagues, relatives and family—should be encouraged, supported, and established by you in these four factors of stream-entry.”

sn55.17:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, those who you have sympathy for, and those worth listening to—friends and colleagues, relatives and family—should be encouraged, supported, and established by you in the four factors of stream-entry.

sn55.17:2.1.verse: There might be change in the four principal states—the elements of earth, water, fire, and air—but a noble disciple with experiential confidence in the Buddha would never change.

sn55.17:2.2.verse: In this context, ‘change’ means that such a noble disciple will be reborn in hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm: this is quite impossible.

sn55.17:2.5.verse: The ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.17:2.6.verse: There might be change in the four principal states—the elements of earth, water, fire, and air—but a noble disciple with the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones would never change.

sn55.17:2.7.verse: In this context, ‘change’ means that such a noble disciple will be reborn in hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm: this is quite impossible.

sn55.17:2.8.verse: Those who you have sympathy for, and those worth listening to—friends and colleagues, relatives and family—should be encouraged, supported, and established by you in these four factors of stream-entry.”

sn55.18:1.2.verse: And then Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared among the gods of the thirty-three.

sn55.18:1.3.verse: Then several deities of the company of the thirty-three went up to Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, bowed, and stood to one side. Moggallāna said to them:

sn55.18:2.1.verse: “Reverends, it’s good to have experiential confidence in the Buddha. …

sn55.18:2.3.verse: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn55.18:2.4.verse: It’s good to have experiential confidence in the teaching. …

sn55.18:2.6.verse: and to have the ethical conduct that’s loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.18:2.7.verse: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

sn55.18:3.1.verse: “My good fellow Moggallāna, it’s good to have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.18:3.3.verse: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn55.18:3.4.verse: It’s good to have experiential confidence in the teaching. …

sn55.18:3.7.verse: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

sn55.21:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

sn55.21:1.3.verse: Then Mahānāma the Sakyan went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn55.21:1.4.verse: “Sir, this Kapilavatthu is successful and prosperous, populous and full of people, with cramped cul-de-sacs.

sn55.21:1.5.verse: In the late afternoon, after paying homage to the Buddha or an esteemed mendicant, I enter Kapilavatthu.

sn55.21:1.11.verse: At that time I lose mindfulness regarding the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.

sn55.21:1.13.verse: ‘If I were to die at this time, where would I be reborn in my next life?’”

sn55.21:2.1.verse: “Do not fear, Mahānāma, do not fear!

sn55.21:2.2.verse: Your death will not be a bad one; your passing will not be a bad one.

sn55.21:2.3.verse: Take someone whose mind has for a long time been imbued with faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom. Their body is formed, made up of the four principal states, produced by mother and father, built up from rice and porridge, liable to impermanence, to wearing away and erosion, to breaking up and destruction.

sn55.21:2.4.verse: Right here the crows, vultures, hawks, hounds, jackals, and many kinds of little creatures devour it.

sn55.21:2.5.verse: But their mind rises up, headed for a higher place.

sn55.21:3.1.verse: Suppose a person was to sink a pot of ghee or oil into a deep lake and break it open.

sn55.21:3.2.verse: Its shards and chips would sink down, while the ghee or oil in it would rise up, headed for a higher place.

sn55.21:3.3.verse: In the same way, take someone whose mind has for a long time been imbued with faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom. Their body is formed, made up of the four principal states, produced by mother and father, built up from rice and porridge, liable to impermanence, to wearing away and erosion, to breaking up and destruction.

sn55.21:3.4.verse: Right here the crows, vultures, hawks, hounds, jackals, and many kinds of little creatures devour it.

sn55.21:3.5.verse: But their mind rises up, headed for a higher place.

sn55.21:3.6.verse: Your mind, Mahānāma, has for a long time been imbued with faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

sn55.21:3.7.verse: Do not fear, Mahānāma, do not fear!

sn55.21:3.8.verse: Your death will not be a bad one; your passing will not be a bad one.”

sn55.22:1.2.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

sn55.22:1.3.verse: Then Mahānāma the Sakyan went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn55.22:1.4.verse: “Sir, this Kapilavatthu is successful and prosperous, populous and full of people, with cramped cul-de-sacs.

sn55.22:1.5.verse: In the late afternoon, after paying homage to the Buddha or an esteemed mendicant, I enter Kapilavatthu.

sn55.22:1.11.verse: At that time I lose mindfulness regarding the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.

sn55.22:1.13.verse: ‘If I were to die at this time, where would I be reborn in my next life?’”

sn55.22:2.1.verse: “Do not fear, Mahānāma, do not fear!

sn55.22:2.2.verse: Your death will not be a bad one; your passing will not be a bad one.

sn55.22:2.3.verse: A noble disciple who has four things slants, slopes, and inclines toward extinguishment.

sn55.22:2.5.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.22:2.9.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.22:3.1.verse: Suppose there was a tree that slants, slopes, and inclines to the east. If it was cut off at the root where would it fall?”

sn55.22:3.2.verse: “Sir, it would fall in the direction that it slants, slopes, and inclines.”

sn55.22:3.3.verse: “In the same way, a noble disciple who has four things slants, slopes, and inclines toward extinguishment.”

sn55.23:1.2.verse: Then Mahānāma the Sakyan went up to Godhā the Sakyan, and said to her,

sn55.23:1.3.verse: “Godhā, how many things must an individual have for you to recognize them as a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening?”

sn55.23:2.1.verse: “Mahānāma, an individual must have three things for me to recognize them as a stream-enterer.

sn55.23:2.3.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.23:2.8.verse: When an individual has these three things I recognize them as a stream-enterer.

sn55.23:3.1.verse: But Mahānāma, how many things must an individual have for you to recognize them as a stream-enterer?”

sn55.23:3.2.verse: “Godhā, an individual must have four things for me to recognize them as a stream-enterer.

sn55.23:3.4.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.23:3.8.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.23:3.9.verse: When an individual has these four things I recognize them as a stream-enterer.”

sn55.23:4.2.verse: Only the Buddha would know whether or not they have these things.”

sn55.23:4.3.verse: “Come, Godhā, let’s go to the Buddha and inform him about this.”

sn55.23:4.4.verse: Then Mahānāma and Godhā went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. Mahānāma told the Buddha all that had happened, and then said:

sn55.23:8.4.verse: “Sir, some instigation of a legal proceeding might come up. The Buddha might take one side, and the Saṅgha of monks the other.

sn55.23:8.6.verse: May the Buddha remember me as having such confidence.

sn55.23:8.7.verse: Some instigation of a legal proceeding might come up. The Buddha might take one side, and the Saṅgha of monks and the Saṅgha of nuns the other. …

sn55.23:8.10.verse: The Buddha might take one side, and the Saṅgha of monks and the Saṅgha of nuns and the laymen the other. …

sn55.23:8.13.verse: The Buddha might take one side, and the Saṅgha of monks and the Saṅgha of nuns and the laymen and the laywomen the other. …

sn55.23:8.16.verse: The Buddha might take one side, and the Saṅgha of monks and the Saṅgha of nuns and the laymen and the laywomen and the world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—the other.

sn55.23:8.18.verse: May the Buddha remember me as having such confidence.”

sn55.23:8.19.verse: “Godhā, what do you have to say to Mahānāma when he speaks like this?”

sn55.23:8.20.verse: “Sir, I have nothing to say to Mahānāma when he speaks like this, except what is good and wholesome.”

sn55.24:1.2.verse: Now at that time Sarakāni the Sakyan had passed away.

sn55.24:1.3.verse: The Buddha declared that he was

sn55.24:1.4.verse: a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

sn55.24:1.5.verse: At that, several Sakyans came together complaining, grumbling, and objecting,

sn55.24:1.7.verse: Who can’t become a stream-enterer these days?

sn55.24:1.8.verse: For the Buddha even declared Sarakāni to be a stream-enterer after he passed away.

sn55.24:1.11.verse: Sarakāni was too weak for the training; he used to drink liquor.”

sn55.24:2.1.verse: Then Mahānāma the Sakyan went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. The Buddha said:

sn55.24:3.1.verse: “Mahānāma, when a lay follower has for a long time gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, how could they go to the underworld?

sn55.24:3.2.verse: And if anyone should rightly be said to

sn55.24:3.3.verse: have for a long time gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, it’s Sarakāni the Sakyan.

sn55.24:3.4.verse: Sarakāni the Sakyan has for a long time gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.

sn55.24:3.5.verse: How could he go to the underworld?

sn55.24:4.1.verse: Take a certain individual who has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.24:4.5.verse: They have laughing wisdom and swift wisdom, and are endowed with freedom.

sn55.24:4.6.verse: They’ve realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

sn55.24:4.7.verse: This individual is exempt from hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They’re exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

sn55.24:5.1.verse: Take another individual who has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.24:5.5.verse: They have laughing wisdom and swift wisdom, but are not endowed with freedom.

sn55.24:5.6.verse: With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re reborn spontaneously. They are extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.

sn55.24:5.7.verse: This individual, too, is exempt from hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They’re exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

sn55.24:6.1.verse: Take another individual who has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.24:6.5.verse: But they don’t have laughing wisdom or swift wisdom, nor are they endowed with freedom.

sn55.24:6.6.verse: With the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, they’re a once-returner. They come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.

sn55.24:6.7.verse: This individual, too, is exempt from hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They’re exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

sn55.24:7.1.verse: Take another individual who has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.24:7.5.verse: But they don’t have laughing wisdom or swift wisdom, nor are they endowed with freedom.

sn55.24:7.6.verse: With the ending of three fetters they’re a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

sn55.24:7.7.verse: This individual, too, is exempt from hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They’re exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

sn55.24:8.1.verse: Take another individual who doesn’t have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.24:8.4.verse: They don’t have laughing wisdom or swift wisdom, nor are they endowed with freedom.

sn55.24:8.6.verse: the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn55.24:8.7.verse: And they accept the teachings proclaimed by the Realized One after deliberating them with a degree of wisdom.

sn55.24:8.8.verse: This individual, too, doesn’t go to hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They don’t go to places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

sn55.24:9.1.verse: Take another individual who doesn’t have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.24:9.4.verse: They don’t have laughing wisdom or swift wisdom, nor are they endowed with freedom.

sn55.24:9.6.verse: the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn55.24:9.7.verse: And they have a degree of faith and fondness for the Buddha.

sn55.24:9.8.verse: This individual, too, doesn’t go to hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They don’t go to places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

sn55.24:9.9.verse: If these great sal trees could understand what was well said and poorly said, I’d declare them to be stream-enterers.

sn55.24:9.10.verse: Why can’t this apply to Sarakāni?

sn55.24:9.11.verse: Mahānāma, Sarakāni the Sakyan undertook the training at the time of his death.”

sn55.25:1.2.verse: Now at that time Sarakāni the Sakyan had passed away.

sn55.25:1.3.verse: The Buddha declared that he was

sn55.25:1.4.verse: a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

sn55.25:1.5.verse: At that, several Sakyans came together complaining, grumbling, and objecting,

sn55.25:1.7.verse: Who can’t become a stream-enterer these days?

sn55.25:1.8.verse: For the Buddha even declared Sarakāni to be a stream-enterer after he passed away.

sn55.25:1.12.verse: Then Mahānāma the Sakyan went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. The Buddha said:

sn55.25:3.1.verse: “Mahānāma, when a lay follower has for a long time gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, how could they go to the underworld?

sn55.25:3.2.verse: And if anyone should rightly be said to

sn55.25:3.3.verse: have for a long time gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, it’s Sarakāni the Sakyan.

sn55.25:3.4.verse: Sarakāni the Sakyan has for a long time gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.

sn55.25:4.1.verse: Take a certain individual who is sure and devoted to the Buddha …

sn55.25:4.5.verse: They have laughing wisdom and swift wisdom, and are endowed with freedom.

sn55.25:4.6.verse: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

sn55.25:4.7.verse: This individual is exempt from hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They’re exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

sn55.25:5.1.verse: Take another individual who is sure and devoted to the Buddha …

sn55.25:5.5.verse: They have laughing wisdom and swift wisdom, but are not endowed with freedom.

sn55.25:5.6.verse: With the ending of the five lower fetters, they’re extinguished between one life and the next … they’re extinguished upon landing … they’re extinguished without extra effort … they’re extinguished with extra effort … they head upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm.

sn55.25:5.7.verse: This individual, too, is exempt from hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They’re exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

sn55.25:6.1.verse: Take another individual who is sure and devoted to the Buddha …

sn55.25:6.5.verse: But they don’t have laughing wisdom or swift wisdom, nor are they endowed with freedom.

sn55.25:6.6.verse: With the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, they’re a once-returner. They come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.

sn55.25:6.7.verse: This individual, too, is exempt from hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They’re exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

sn55.25:7.1.verse: Take another individual who is sure and devoted to the Buddha …

sn55.25:7.5.verse: But they don’t have laughing wisdom or swift wisdom, nor are they endowed with freedom.

sn55.25:7.6.verse: With the ending of three fetters they’re a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

sn55.25:7.7.verse: This individual, too, is exempt from hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They’re exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

sn55.25:8.1.verse: Take another individual who isn’t sure or devoted to the Buddha …

sn55.25:8.4.verse: They don’t have laughing wisdom or swift wisdom, nor are they endowed with freedom.

sn55.25:8.6.verse: the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn55.25:8.7.verse: And they accept the teachings proclaimed by the Realized One after deliberating them with a degree of wisdom.

sn55.25:8.8.verse: This individual, too, doesn’t go to hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They don’t go to places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

sn55.25:9.1.verse: Take another individual who isn’t sure or devoted to the Buddha …

sn55.25:9.4.verse: They don’t have laughing wisdom or swift wisdom, nor are they endowed with freedom.

sn55.25:9.6.verse: the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

sn55.25:9.7.verse: And they have a degree of faith and love for the Buddha.

sn55.25:9.8.verse: This individual, too, doesn’t go to hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They don’t go to places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

sn55.25:10.1.verse: Suppose there was a barren field, a barren ground, with uncleared stumps. And you had seeds that were broken, spoiled, weather-damaged, infertile, and ill kept. And the heavens didn’t provide enough rain.

sn55.25:10.2.verse: Would those seeds grow, increase, and mature?”

sn55.25:10.4.verse: “In the same way, take a teaching that’s badly explained and badly propounded, not emancipating, not leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is not a fully awakened Buddha.

sn55.25:10.5.verse: This is what I call a barren field.

sn55.25:10.6.verse: A disciple remains in such a teaching, practicing in line with that teaching, practicing it properly, living in line with that teaching.

sn55.25:10.7.verse: This is what I call a bad seed.

sn55.25:11.1.verse: Suppose there was a fertile field, a fertile ground, well-cleared of stumps. And you had seeds that were intact, unspoiled, not weather-damaged, fertile, and well-kept. And there’s plenty of rainfall.

sn55.25:11.3.verse: Would those seeds grow, increase, and mature?”

sn55.25:11.5.verse: “In the same way, take a teaching that’s well explained and well propounded, emancipating, leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is a fully awakened Buddha.

sn55.25:11.6.verse: This is what I call a fertile field.

sn55.25:11.7.verse: A disciple remains in such a teaching, practicing in line with that teaching, practicing it properly, living in line with that teaching.

sn55.25:11.8.verse: This is what I call a good seed.

sn55.25:11.9.verse: Why can’t this apply to Sarakāni?

sn55.25:11.10.verse: Mahānāma, Sarakāni the Sakyan fulfilled the training at the time of his death.”

sn55.26:1.2.verse: Now at that time the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

sn55.26:1.4.verse: “Please, my man, go to Venerable Sāriputta, and in my name bow with your head to his feet. Say to him:

sn55.26:1.5.verse: ‘Sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is sick, suffering, gravely ill.

sn55.26:1.6.verse: He bows with his head to your feet.’

sn55.26:1.8.verse: ‘Sir, please visit him at his home out of sympathy.’”

sn55.26:2.1.verse: “Yes, sir,” that man replied. He did as Anāthapiṇḍika asked.

sn55.26:4.1.verse: Then Venerable Sāriputta robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went with Venerable Ānanda as his second monk to Anāthapiṇḍika’s home. He sat down on the seat spread out and said to Anāthapiṇḍika,

sn55.26:4.2.verse: “I hope you’re keeping well, householder; I hope you’re all right. I hope your pain is fading, not growing; that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

sn55.26:4.3.verse: “Sir, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.”

sn55.26:5.1.verse: “Householder, you don’t have the distrust in the Buddha that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn55.26:5.2.verse: And you have experiential confidence in the Buddha:

sn55.26:5.3.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

sn55.26:5.4.verse: Seeing in yourself that experiential confidence in the Buddha, that pain may die down on the spot.

sn55.26:6.1.verse: You don’t have the distrust in the teaching that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn55.26:6.2.verse: And you have experiential confidence in the teaching:

sn55.26:6.3.verse: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

sn55.26:6.4.verse: Seeing in yourself that experiential confidence in the teaching, that pain may die down on the spot.

sn55.26:7.1.verse: You don’t have the distrust in the Saṅgha that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn55.26:7.2.verse: And you have experiential confidence in the Saṅgha:

sn55.26:7.3.verse: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, and worthy of veneration with cupped palms. It is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

sn55.26:7.4.verse: Seeing in yourself that experiential confidence in the Saṅgha, that pain may die down on the spot.

sn55.26:8.1.verse: You don’t have the unethical conduct that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn55.26:8.2.verse: Your ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

sn55.26:8.3.verse: Seeing in yourself that ethical conduct loved by the noble ones, that pain may die down on the spot.

sn55.26:9.1.verse: You don’t have the wrong view that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

sn55.26:9.3.verse: Seeing in yourself that right view, that pain may die down on the spot.

sn55.26:10.1.verse: You don’t have the wrong purpose …

sn55.26:18.3.verse: Seeing in yourself that right freedom, that pain may die down on the spot.”

sn55.26:19.1.verse: And then Anāthapiṇḍika’s pain died down on the spot.

sn55.26:19.2.verse: Then he served Sāriputta and Ānanda from his own dish.

sn55.26:19.3.verse: When Sāriputta had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, Anāthapiṇḍika took a low seat and sat to one side.

sn55.26:19.4.verse: Venerable Sāriputta expressed his appreciation to him with these verses.

sn55.26:20.1.verse: “Whoever has faith in the Realized One,

sn55.26:20.4.verse: praised and loved by the noble ones;

sn55.26:21.1.verse: who has confidence in the Saṅgha,

sn55.26:21.4.verse: their life is not in vain.

sn55.26:22.1.verse: So let the wise devote themselves

sn55.26:22.3.verse: confidence, and insight into the teaching,

sn55.26:22.4.verse: remembering the instructions of the Buddhas.”

sn55.26:23.1.verse: After expressing his appreciation to Anāthapiṇḍika with these verses, Sāriputta rose from his seat and left.

sn55.26:24.1.verse: Then Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

sn55.26:24.2.verse: “So, Ānanda, where are you coming from in the middle of the day?”

sn55.26:24.3.verse: “Sir, Venerable Sāriputta advised the householder Anāthapiṇḍika in this way and that.”

sn55.26:24.5.verse: He has great wisdom, since he can analyze the four factors of stream-entry in ten respects.”

sn55.27:1.2.verse: Now at that time the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

sn55.27:1.4.verse: “Please, my man, go to Venerable Ānanda, and in my name bow with your head to his feet. Say to him:

sn55.27:1.5.verse: ‘Sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is sick, suffering, gravely ill.

sn55.27:1.6.verse: He bows with his head to your feet.’

sn55.27:1.8.verse: ‘Sir, please visit him at his home out of sympathy.’”

sn55.27:2.1.verse: “Yes, sir,” that man replied. He did as Anāthapiṇḍika asked.

sn55.27:3.1.verse: Then Venerable Ānanda robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika. He sat down on the seat spread out and said to Anāthapiṇḍika,

sn55.27:3.2.verse: “I hope you’re keeping well, householder, I hope you’re all right. I hope your pain is fading, not growing; that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

sn55.27:3.3.verse: “Sir, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.”

sn55.27:4.1.verse: “Householder, when an unlearned ordinary person has four things, they’re frightened and terrified, and fear what awaits them after death.

sn55.27:4.3.verse: Firstly, an unlearned ordinary person distrusts the Buddha.

sn55.27:4.4.verse: Seeing in themselves that distrust of the Buddha, they’re frightened and terrified, and fear what awaits them after death.

sn55.27:5.1.verse: Furthermore, an unlearned ordinary person distrusts the teaching …

sn55.27:6.1.verse: Furthermore, an unlearned ordinary person distrusts the Saṅgha …

sn55.27:7.1.verse: Furthermore, an unlearned ordinary person has unethical conduct.

sn55.27:7.2.verse: Seeing in themselves that unethical conduct, they’re frightened and terrified, and fear what awaits them after death.

sn55.27:7.3.verse: When an unlearned ordinary person has these four things, they’re frightened and terrified, and fear what awaits them after death.

sn55.27:8.1.verse: When a learned noble disciple has four things, they’re not frightened or terrified, and don’t fear what awaits them after death.

sn55.27:8.3.verse: Firstly, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.27:8.5.verse: Seeing in themselves that experiential confidence in the Buddha, they’re not frightened or terrified, and don’t fear what awaits them after death.

sn55.27:9.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the teaching …

sn55.27:10.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Saṅgha …

sn55.27:11.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

sn55.27:11.2.verse: Seeing in themselves that ethical conduct loved by the noble ones, they’re not frightened or terrified, and don’t fear what awaits them after death.

sn55.27:11.3.verse: When a learned noble disciple has these four things, they’re not frightened or terrified, and don’t fear what awaits them after death.”

sn55.27:12.3.verse: For I have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.27:12.8.verse: And of the training rules appropriate for laypeople taught by the Buddha, I don’t see any that I have broken.”

sn55.27:12.10.verse: You have declared the fruit of stream-entry.”

sn55.28:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, the Buddha said to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika:

sn55.28:1.3.verse: “Householder, when a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

sn55.28:1.4.verse: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’

sn55.28:2.1.verse: What are the five fears and enmities they have quelled?

sn55.28:2.2.verse: Anyone who kills living creatures brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness.

sn55.28:2.3.verse: So that fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from killing living creatures.

sn55.28:2.7.verse: Anyone who consumes beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness.

sn55.28:2.8.verse: So that fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants.

sn55.28:2.9.verse: These are the five fears and enmities they have quelled.

sn55.28:3.1.verse: What are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess?

sn55.28:3.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.28:3.6.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.28:3.7.verse: These are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess.

sn55.28:4.1.verse: And what is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom?

sn55.28:4.2.verse: A noble disciple rationally applies the mind to dependent origination itself:

sn55.28:4.3.verse: ‘So, when this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

sn55.28:4.4.verse: So, when this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:

sn55.28:4.5.verse: Ignorance is a requirement for choices. Choices are a requirement for consciousness. Consciousness is a requirement for name and form. Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields. The six sense fields are requirements for contact. Contact is a requirement for feeling. Feeling is a requirement for craving. Craving is a requirement for grasping. Grasping is a requirement for continued existence. Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth. Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.

sn55.28:4.6.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

sn55.28:4.7.verse: When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, choices cease. When choices cease, consciousness ceases. When consciousness ceases, name and form cease. When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease. When the six sense fields cease, contact ceases. When contact ceases, feeling ceases. When feeling ceases, craving ceases. When craving ceases, grasping ceases. When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases. When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases. When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.

sn55.28:4.8.verse: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’

sn55.28:4.9.verse: This is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom.

sn55.28:5.1.verse: When a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

sn55.28:5.2.verse: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

sn55.29:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, when a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

sn55.29:1.3.verse: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

sn55.30:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

sn55.30:1.2.verse: Then Nandaka the Licchavi chief minister went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

sn55.30:2.1.verse: “Nandaka, a noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

sn55.30:2.3.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.30:2.7.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.30:2.8.verse: A noble disciple who has these four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

sn55.30:3.1.verse: A noble disciple who has these four things is endowed with long life, both human and heavenly …

sn55.30:3.5.verse: and sovereignty, both human and heavenly.

sn55.30:3.6.verse: Now, I don’t say this because I’ve heard it from some other ascetic or brahmin. I only say it because I’ve known, seen, and realized it for myself.”

sn55.30:4.1.verse: When he had spoken, a certain person said to Nandaka:

sn55.30:4.3.verse: “Enough now, lad, with that exterior bath.

sn55.30:4.4.verse: This interior bathing will do for me, that is,

sn55.31:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.

sn55.31:1.4.verse: Firstly, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.31:1.6.verse: This is the first kind of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

sn55.31:2.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the teaching …

sn55.31:2.3.verse: This is the second kind of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

sn55.31:3.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Saṅgha …

sn55.31:3.3.verse: This is the third kind of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

sn55.31:4.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

sn55.31:4.2.verse: This is the fourth kind of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

sn55.31:4.3.verse: These are the four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.”

sn55.32:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.

sn55.32:1.3.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.32:3.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

sn55.32:3.2.verse: This is the fourth kind of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

sn55.32:3.3.verse: These are the four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.”

sn55.33:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.

sn55.33:1.3.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.33:3.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

sn55.33:3.2.verse: This is the fourth kind of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

sn55.33:3.3.verse: These are the four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.”

sn55.34:1.2.verse: “Mendicants, these four footprints of the gods are in order to purify unpurified beings and cleanse unclean beings.

sn55.34:2.2.verse: Firstly, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.34:2.4.verse: This is the first footprint of the gods in order to purify unpurified beings and cleanse unclean beings.

sn55.34:3.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the teaching …

sn55.34:4.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

sn55.34:4.2.verse: This is the fourth footprint of the gods in order to purify unpurified beings and cleanse unclean beings.

sn55.34:4.3.verse: These four footprints of the gods are in order to purify unpurified beings and cleanse unclean beings.”

sn55.35:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, these four footprints of the gods are in order to purify unpurified beings and cleanse unclean beings.

sn55.35:2.2.verse: Firstly, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha:

sn55.35:2.3.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

sn55.35:2.5.verse: ‘What now is the footprint of the gods?’

sn55.35:2.7.verse: ‘I hear that these days the gods consider non-harming to be supreme.

sn55.35:2.8.verse: But I don’t hurt any creature firm or frail.

sn55.35:2.9.verse: I definitely live in possession of a footprint of the gods.’

sn55.35:2.10.verse: This is the first footprint of the gods in order to purify unpurified beings and cleanse unclean beings.

sn55.35:3.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the teaching …

sn55.35:4.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

sn55.35:4.3.verse: ‘What now is the footprint of the gods?’

sn55.35:4.5.verse: ‘I hear that these days the gods consider non-harming to be supreme.

sn55.35:4.6.verse: But I don’t hurt any creature firm or frail.

sn55.35:4.7.verse: I definitely live in possession of a footprint of the gods.’

sn55.35:4.8.verse: This is the fourth footprint of the gods in order to purify unpurified beings and cleanse unclean beings.

sn55.35:4.9.verse: These four footprints of the gods are in order to purify unpurified beings and cleanse unclean beings.”

sn55.36:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, when someone possesses four things the gods are pleased and speak of what they have in common.

sn55.36:1.3.verse: Firstly, a noble disciple possesses experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.36:1.5.verse: There are deities who possess experiential confidence in the Buddha who passed away from here and were reborn there. They think:

sn55.36:1.6.verse: ‘Possessing such experiential confidence in the Buddha, we passed away from there and were reborn here. That noble disciple possesses the same kind of experiential confidence in the Buddha, so they will come into the presence of the gods.’

sn55.36:2.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple possesses experiential confidence in the teaching …

sn55.36:2.3.verse: And they possess the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.36:2.4.verse: There are deities who possess the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones who passed away from here and were reborn there. They think:

sn55.36:2.5.verse: ‘Possessing such ethical conduct loved by the noble ones, we passed away from there and were reborn here. That noble disciple possesses the same kind of ethical conduct loved by the noble ones, so they will come into the presence of the gods.’

sn55.36:2.6.verse: When someone possesses four things the gods are pleased and speak of what they have in common.”

sn55.37:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

sn55.37:1.2.verse: Then Mahānāma the Sakyan went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn55.37:2.1.verse: “Sir, how is a lay follower defined?”

sn55.37:2.2.verse: “Mahānāma, when you’ve gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha,

sn55.37:2.3.verse: you’re considered to be a lay follower.”

sn55.37:3.1.verse: “But how is an ethical lay follower defined?”

sn55.37:3.2.verse: “When a lay follower doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor,

sn55.37:3.3.verse: they’re considered to be an ethical lay follower.”

sn55.37:4.1.verse: “But how is a faithful lay follower defined?”

sn55.37:4.2.verse: “It’s when a lay follower has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

sn55.37:4.3.verse: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

sn55.37:4.4.verse: Then they’re considered to be a faithful lay follower.”

sn55.37:5.1.verse: “But how is a generous lay follower defined?”

sn55.37:5.2.verse: “It’s when a lay follower lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

sn55.37:5.3.verse: Then they’re considered to be a generous lay follower.”

sn55.37:6.1.verse: “But how is a wise lay follower defined?”

sn55.37:6.2.verse: “It’s when a lay follower is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

sn55.37:6.3.verse: Then they’re considered to be a wise lay follower.”

sn55.38:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, suppose the heavens rain heavily on a mountain top, and the water flows downhill to fill the hollows, crevices, and creeks. As they become full, they fill up the pools. The pools fill up the lakes, the lakes fill up the streams, and the streams fill up the rivers. And as the rivers become full, they fill up the ocean.

sn55.38:1.2.verse: In the same way, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and the ethics loved by the noble ones.

sn55.38:1.3.verse: These things flow onwards; and, after crossing to the far shore, they lead to the ending of defilements.”

sn55.39:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

sn55.39:1.2.verse: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of Kāḷigodhā the Sakyan lady, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

sn55.39:1.3.verse: Then Kāḷigodhā went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to her:

sn55.39:2.1.verse: “Godhā, a female noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

sn55.39:2.3.verse: It’s when a female noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.39:2.7.verse: And she lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

sn55.39:2.8.verse: A female noble disciple who has these four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

sn55.39:3.1.verse: “Sir, these four factors of stream-entry that were taught by the Buddha are found in me, and I exhibit them.

sn55.39:3.2.verse: For I have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.39:3.6.verse: And I share without reservation all the gifts available to give in our family with those who are ethical and of good character.”

sn55.39:3.8.verse: You have declared the fruit of stream-entry.”

sn55.40:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

sn55.40:1.2.verse: Then Nandiya the Sakyan went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn55.40:1.3.verse: “Sir, if a noble disciple were to totally and utterly lack the four factors of stream-entry, would they live negligently?”

sn55.40:2.1.verse: “Nandiya, someone who totally and utterly lacks these four factors of stream-entry stands outside in the faction of ordinary persons, I say.

sn55.40:2.2.verse: Neverthless, Nandiya, as to how a noble disciple lives negligently and how they live diligently,

sn55.40:2.3.verse: listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

sn55.40:3.1.verse: “And how does a noble disciple live negligently?

sn55.40:3.2.verse: Firstly, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.40:3.4.verse: They’re content with that confidence, and don’t make a further effort for solitude by day or retreat by night.

sn55.40:3.5.verse: When they live negligently, there’s no joy.

sn55.40:3.6.verse: When there’s no joy, there’s no rapture.

sn55.40:3.7.verse: When there’s no rapture, there’s no tranquility.

sn55.40:3.8.verse: When there’s no tranquility, there’s suffering.

sn55.40:3.9.verse: When one is suffering, the mind does not become immersed in samādhi.

sn55.40:3.10.verse: When the mind is not immersed in samādhi, principles do not become clear.

sn55.40:3.11.verse: Because principles have not become clear, they’re reckoned to live negligently.

sn55.40:4.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the teaching …

sn55.40:4.3.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.40:4.4.verse: They’re content with that ethical conduct loved by the noble ones, and don’t make a further effort for solitude by day or retreat by night.

sn55.40:4.5.verse: When they live negligently, there’s no joy.

sn55.40:4.6.verse: When there’s no joy, there’s no rapture.

sn55.40:4.7.verse: When there’s no rapture, there’s no tranquility.

sn55.40:4.8.verse: When there’s no tranquility, there’s suffering.

sn55.40:4.9.verse: When one is suffering, the mind does not become immersed in samādhi.

sn55.40:4.10.verse: When the mind is not immersed in samādhi, principles do not become clear.

sn55.40:4.11.verse: Because principles have not become clear, they’re reckoned to live negligently.

sn55.40:4.12.verse: That’s how a noble disciple lives negligently.

sn55.40:5.1.verse: And how does a noble disciple live diligently?

sn55.40:5.2.verse: Firstly, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.40:5.4.verse: But they’re not content with that confidence, and make a further effort for solitude by day and retreat by night.

sn55.40:5.5.verse: When they live diligently, joy springs up.

sn55.40:5.7.verse: When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil.

sn55.40:5.8.verse: When the body is tranquil, they feel bliss.

sn55.40:5.9.verse: And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.

sn55.40:5.10.verse: When the mind is immersed in samādhi, principles become clear.

sn55.40:5.11.verse: Because principles have become clear, they’re reckoned to live diligently.

sn55.40:6.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the teaching …

sn55.40:6.3.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.40:6.4.verse: But they’re not content with that ethical conduct loved by the noble ones, and make a further effort for solitude by day and retreat by night.

sn55.40:6.5.verse: When they live diligently, joy springs up.

sn55.40:6.7.verse: When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil.

sn55.40:6.8.verse: When the body is tranquil, they feel bliss.

sn55.40:6.9.verse: And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.

sn55.40:6.10.verse: When the mind is immersed in samādhi, principles become clear.

sn55.40:6.11.verse: Because principles have become clear, they’re reckoned to live diligently.

sn55.40:6.12.verse: That’s how a noble disciple lives diligently.”

sn55.41:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.

sn55.41:1.3.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.41:3.1.verse: Furthermore, they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion. …

sn55.41:3.3.verse: These are the four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.

sn55.41:4.1.verse: When a noble disciple has these four kinds of overflowing merit and goodness, it’s not easy to count how much merit they have by saying that

sn55.41:4.2.verse: this is the extent of their overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

sn55.41:4.3.verse: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.

sn55.41:5.1.verse: It’s like trying to count how much water is in the ocean. It’s not easy to say

sn55.41:5.2.verse: how many gallons, how many hundreds, thousands, hundreds of thousands of gallons there are.

sn55.41:5.3.verse: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of water.

sn55.41:5.4.verse: In the same way, when a noble disciple has these four kinds of overflowing merit and goodness, it’s not easy to count how much merit they have by saying that

sn55.41:5.5.verse: this is the extent of their overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

sn55.41:5.6.verse: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.”

sn55.41:6.1.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn55.41:6.2.verse: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

sn55.41:7.2.verse: and though the rivers are many,

sn55.41:7.3.verse: all reach the great deep, the boundless ocean,

sn55.41:7.4.verse: the cruel sea that’s home to precious gems.

sn55.41:8.1.verse: So too, when a person gives food, drink, and clothes;

sn55.41:8.2.verse: and they’re a giver of beds, seats, and mats—

sn55.41:8.3.verse: the streams of merit reach that astute person,

sn55.41:8.4.verse: as the rivers bring their waters to the sea.”

sn55.42:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.

sn55.42:1.3.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.42:3.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

sn55.42:3.2.verse: This is the fourth kind of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

sn55.42:3.3.verse: These are the four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.

sn55.42:4.1.verse: When a noble disciple has these four kinds of overflowing merit and goodness, it’s not easy to count how much merit they have by saying that

sn55.42:4.2.verse: this is the extent of their overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

sn55.42:4.3.verse: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.

sn55.42:5.1.verse: There are places where the great rivers—the Ganges, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—join together and converge.

sn55.42:5.2.verse: It’s not easy to count how much water is in such places by saying

sn55.42:5.3.verse: how many gallons, how many hundreds, thousands, hundreds of thousands of gallons there are.

sn55.42:5.4.verse: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of water.

sn55.42:5.5.verse: In the same way, when a noble disciple has these four kinds of overflowing merit and goodness, it’s not easy to count how much merit they have by saying that

sn55.42:5.6.verse: this is the extent of their overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

sn55.42:5.7.verse: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.”

sn55.42:5.8.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn55.42:5.9.verse: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

sn55.42:6.2.verse: and though the rivers are many,

sn55.42:6.3.verse: all reach the great deep, the boundless ocean,

sn55.42:6.4.verse: the cruel sea that’s home to precious gems.

sn55.42:7.1.verse: So too, when a person gives food, drink, and clothes;

sn55.42:7.2.verse: and they’re a giver of beds, seats, and mats—

sn55.42:7.3.verse: the streams of merit reach that astute person,

sn55.42:7.4.verse: as the rivers bring their waters to the sea.”

sn55.43:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.

sn55.43:1.3.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.43:3.1.verse: Furthermore, a noble disciple is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

sn55.43:3.2.verse: This is the fourth kind of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

sn55.43:3.3.verse: These are the four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.

sn55.43:4.1.verse: When a noble disciple has these four kinds of overflowing merit and goodness, it’s not easy to count how much merit they have by saying that

sn55.43:4.2.verse: this is the extent of their overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

sn55.43:4.3.verse: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.”

sn55.43:4.4.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn55.43:4.5.verse: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

sn55.43:5.1.verse: “One who desires merit, grounded in the skillful,

sn55.43:5.2.verse: develops the path to realize freedom from death.

sn55.43:5.3.verse: Once they’ve reached the heart of the teaching, delighting in ending,

sn55.43:5.4.verse: they don’t tremble at the approach of the King of Death.”

sn55.44:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a noble disciple who has four things is said to be rich, affluent, and wealthy.

sn55.44:2.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.44:2.6.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.44:2.7.verse: A noble disciple who has these four things is said to be rich, affluent, and wealthy.”

sn55.45:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a noble disciple who has four things is said to be rich, affluent, wealthy, and famous.

sn55.45:2.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.45:2.6.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.45:2.7.verse: A noble disciple who has these four things is said to be rich, affluent, wealthy, and famous.”

sn55.46:2.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.46:2.6.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.46:2.7.verse: A noble disciple who has these four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

sn55.47:1.3.verse: “Nandiya, a noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

sn55.47:2.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.47:2.6.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.
