sn55.48:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, the Buddha said to Bhaddiya the Sakyan:

sn55.48:1.3.verse: “Bhaddiya, a noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer …”

sn55.49:1.2.verse: Seated to one side, the Buddha said to Mahānāma the Sakyan:

sn55.49:1.3.verse: “Mahānāma, a noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer …”

sn55.50:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, there are these four factors for stream-entry.

sn55.50:1.3.verse: Associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, rational application of mind, and practicing in line with the teaching.

sn55.50:1.4.verse: These are the four factors for stream-entry.”

sn55.51:1.1.verse: “Mendicants, a noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

sn55.51:2.2.verse: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.51:2.6.verse: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

sn55.51:2.7.verse: A noble disciple who has these four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

sn55.51:2.8.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

sn55.51:2.9.verse: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

sn55.51:3.1.verse: “Whoever has faith in the Realized One,

sn55.51:3.4.verse: praised and loved by the noble ones;

sn55.51:4.1.verse: who has confidence in the Saṅgha,

sn55.51:4.4.verse: their life is not in vain.

sn55.51:5.1.verse: So let the wise devote themselves

sn55.51:5.3.verse: confidence, and insight into the teaching,

sn55.51:5.4.verse: remembering the instructions of the Buddhas.”

sn55.52:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

sn55.52:1.2.verse: Now at that time a certain mendicant who had completed the rainy season residence in Sāvatthī arrived at Kapilavatthu on some business.

sn55.52:1.3.verse: The Sakyans of Kapilavatthu heard about this.

sn55.52:2.1.verse: They went to that mendicant, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

sn55.52:2.2.verse: “Sir, we hope that the Buddha is healthy and strong.”

sn55.52:3.1.verse: “And we hope that Sāriputta and Moggallāna are healthy and strong.”

sn55.52:4.1.verse: “And we hope that the mendicant Saṅgha is healthy and strong.”

sn55.52:5.1.verse: “But sir, during this rains residence did you hear and learn anything in the presence of the Buddha?”

sn55.52:5.2.verse: “Respectable sirs, I heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

sn55.52:5.3.verse: ‘There are fewer mendicants who realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

sn55.52:5.4.verse: There are more mendicants who, having ended the five lower fetters, are reborn spontaneously, and will be extinguished there, not liable to return from that world.’

sn55.52:6.1.verse: In addition, I heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

sn55.52:6.2.verse: ‘There are fewer mendicants who, having ended the five lower fetters, are reborn spontaneously, and will be extinguished there, not liable to return from that world.

sn55.52:6.3.verse: There are more mendicants who, with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, are once-returners, who come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.’

sn55.52:7.1.verse: In addition, I heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

sn55.52:7.2.verse: ‘There are fewer mendicants who, with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, are once-returners, who come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.

sn55.52:7.3.verse: There are more mendicants who, with the ending of three fetters are stream-enterers, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.’”

sn55.53:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

sn55.53:1.2.verse: Then the lay follower Dhammadinna, together with five hundred lay followers, went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn55.53:1.4.verse: and instruct us. It will be for our lasting welfare and happiness.”

sn55.53:2.1.verse: “So, Dhammadinna, you should all train like this:

sn55.53:2.2.verse: ‘From time to time we will undertake and dwell upon the discourses spoken by the Realized One that are deep, profound, transcendent, dealing with emptiness.’

sn55.53:2.3.verse: That’s how you should train yourselves.”

sn55.53:2.4.verse: “Sir, we live at home with our children, using sandalwood imported from Kāsi, wearing garlands, fragrance, and makeup, and accepting gold and currency.

sn55.53:2.5.verse: It’s not easy for us to undertake and dwell from time to time upon the discourses spoken by the Realized One that are deep, profound, transcendent, dealing with emptiness.

sn55.53:2.6.verse: Since we are established in the five training rules, please teach us further.”

sn55.53:3.1.verse: “So, Dhammadinna, you should all train like this:

sn55.53:3.2.verse: ‘We will have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.53:3.6.verse: And we will have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.’

sn55.53:3.7.verse: That’s how you should train yourselves.”

sn55.53:4.1.verse: “Sir, these four factors of stream-entry that were taught by the Buddha are found in us, and we embody them.

sn55.53:4.2.verse: For we have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.53:4.6.verse: And we have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.”

sn55.53:4.7.verse: “You’re all fortunate, Dhammadinna, so very fortunate!

sn55.53:4.8.verse: You’ve all declared the fruit of stream-entry.”

sn55.54:1.1.verse: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

sn55.54:1.2.verse: At that time several mendicants were making a robe for the Buddha, thinking that

sn55.54:1.3.verse: when his robe was finished and the three months of the rains residence had passed the Buddha would set out wandering.

sn55.54:1.4.verse: Mahānāma the Sakyan heard about this.

sn55.54:1.7.verse: Then he went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him that he had heard that the Buddha was leaving. He added,

sn55.54:1.11.verse: “Sir, I haven’t heard and learned it in the presence of the Buddha

sn55.54:1.12.verse: how a wise lay follower should advise another wise lay follower who is sick, suffering, gravely ill.”

sn55.54:2.1.verse: “Mahānāma, a wise lay follower should put at ease another wise lay follower who is sick, suffering, gravely ill with four consolations.

sn55.54:2.3.verse: You have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

sn55.54:2.7.verse: And you have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.’

sn55.54:3.1.verse: When a wise lay follower has put at ease another wise lay follower who is sick, suffering, gravely ill with these four consolations, they should say:

sn55.54:3.2.verse: ‘Are you concerned for your mother and father?’

sn55.54:3.5.verse: ‘But sir, it’s your nature to die.

sn55.54:3.6.verse: Whether or not you are concerned for your mother and father,

sn55.54:3.8.verse: It would be good to give up concern for your mother and father.’

sn55.54:4.2.verse: ‘I have given up concern for my mother and father,’ they should say:

sn55.54:4.3.verse: ‘But are you concerned for your partners and children?’

sn55.54:4.6.verse: ‘But sir, it’s your nature to die.

sn55.54:4.7.verse: Whether or not you are concerned for your partners and children,

sn55.54:4.9.verse: It would be good to give up concern for your partners and children.’

sn55.54:5.2.verse: ‘I have given up concern for my partners and children,’ they should say:

sn55.54:5.3.verse: ‘But are you concerned for the five kinds of human sensual stimulation?’

sn55.54:5.6.verse: ‘Respectable sir, heavenly sensual pleasures are better than human sensual pleasures.

sn55.54:5.7.verse: It would be good to turn your mind away from human sensual pleasures and focus it on the gods of the four great kings.’

sn55.54:6.2.verse: ‘I have done so,’ they should say:

sn55.54:6.3.verse: ‘Respectable sir, the gods of the thirty-three are better than the gods of the four great kings …

sn55.54:7.3.verse: Respectable sir, the gods of Yama …

sn55.54:7.5.verse: the gods who love to create …

sn55.54:7.6.verse: the gods who control what is created by others …

sn55.54:7.7.verse: the gods of the realm of divinity are better than the gods who control what is created by others.

sn55.54:7.8.verse: It would be good to turn your mind away from the gods who control what is created by others and focus it on the gods of the realm of divinity.’

sn55.54:7.10.verse: ‘I have done so,’ they should say:

sn55.54:7.11.verse: ‘Respectable sir, the realm of divinity is impermanent, not lasting, and included within substantial reality.

sn55.54:7.12.verse: It would be good to turn your mind away from the realm of divinity and apply it to the cessation of substantial reality.’

sn55.54:8.3.verse: then there is no difference between a lay follower whose mind is freed in this way and a mendicant whose mind is freed from defilements; that is,

sn55.54:8.4.verse: between the freedom of one and the other.”

sn55.55:1.3.verse: Associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, rational application of mind, and practicing in line with the teaching.

sn55.55:1.4.verse: When these four things are developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry.”

sn56.1:1.4.verse: A mendicant who has immersion truly understands.

sn56.1:1.6.verse: They truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

sn56.1:1.8.verse: A mendicant who has immersion truly understands.

sn56.1:2.1.verse: That’s why you should practice meditation to understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.”

sn56.2:1.2.verse: A mendicant in retreat truly understands.

sn56.2:1.4.verse: They truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

sn56.2:1.6.verse: A mendicant in retreat truly understands.

sn56.2:2.1.verse: That’s why you should practice meditation to understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.”

sn56.3:1.3.verse: or present—rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness, all of them do so in order to truly comprehend the four noble truths.

sn56.3:2.2.verse: The noble truths of suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.

sn56.3:2.5.verse: or present—rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness, all of them do so in order to truly comprehend the four noble truths.

sn56.3:3.1.verse: That’s why you should practice meditation to understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.”
